twi: Ɔbea no de awo akyi ade ne abofra a wawo no foforo no besie wɔn sɛnea obetumi awe ne nyinaa wɔ kokoa mu, esiane ɔhaw ne abɛbrɛsɛ a mo atamfo de bɛba mo so, bere a wɔatua mo nkuropɔn ano no nti.
english: the afterbirth from her womb and the children she bears. For in her dire need she intends to eat them secretly because of the suffering your enemy will inflict on you during the siege of your cities.

twi: Sɛ moanni mmara a wɔakyerɛw wɔ saa nhoma yi mu no nyinaa so pɛpɛɛpɛ, na moanni saa onuonyamfo ne ɔnwonwani Awurade, mo Nyankopɔn no, no din ni a,
english: If you do not carefully follow all the words of this law, which are written in this book, and do not revere this glorious and awesome name—the Lord your God—

twi: Awurade de ɔyaredɔm a ɛyɛ hu bɛba mo ne mo asefo. Ɛbɛyɛ atoyerɛnkyɛm a ano yɛ den ne ɔyaredɔm a ano yɛ den na ɛbɛtena hɔ akyɛ.
english: the Lord will send fearful plagues on you and your descendants, harsh and prolonged disasters, and severe and lingering illnesses.

twi: Ɔde ɔyaredɔm ahorow a ɛbaa wɔ Misraim a ɛbɔɔ mo hu no bɛba bɛtena mo so.
english: He will bring on you all the diseases of Egypt that you dreaded, and they will cling to you.

twi: Awurade de nyarewa ahorow bebree ne atoyerɛnkyɛm a wɔnkyerɛw wɔ Mmara Nhoma yi mu no bɛbrɛ mo akosi sɛ mobɛsɛe.
english: The Lord will also bring on you every kind of sickness and disaster not recorded in this Book of the Law, until you are destroyed.

twi: Mo a na modɔɔso te sɛ ɔsoro nsoromma no, mo so bɛtew koraa, efisɛ moantie Awurade, mo Nyankopɔn no.
english: You who were as numerous as the stars in the sky will be left but few in number, because you did not obey the Lord your God.

twi: Sɛnea na ɛyɛ Awurade anisɔ sɛ ɔbɛma mo adi yiye na moadɔɔso no, saa ara nso na ɛbɛyɛ no anisɔ sɛ ɔbɛdwerɛw mo na wasɛe mo. Obetutu mo ase afi asase a morekɔ so akɔfa no so.
english: Just as it pleased the Lord to make you prosper and increase in number, so it will please him to ruin and destroy you. You will be uprooted from the land you are entering to possess.

twi: Na Awurade bɛbɔ mo apansam afra aman nyinaa afi asase ano akosi asase ano. Ɛhɔ na mobɛsom ahɔho anyame a mo anaa mo agyanom nhuu bi da; anyame a wɔde nnua ne abo ayɛ!
english: Then the Lord will scatter you among all nations, from one end of the earth to the other. There you will worship other gods—gods of wood and stone, which neither you nor your ancestors have known.

twi: Morennya guankɔbea anaa homebea mma mo anantin wɔ saa aman no so. Ɛhɔ na Awurade bɛma mo adwene a ɛpere, aniwa a ayɛ siamoo ne koma a apa abawa.
english: Among those nations you will find no repose, no resting place for the sole of your foot. There the Lord will give you an anxious mind, eyes weary with longing, and a despairing heart.

twi: Mo asetena bedi nsensɛnmu daa, na ehu bɛhyɛ mo so anadwo ne awia a munnim nea ɛrekɔ so wɔ mo asetena mu.
english: You will live in constant suspense, filled with dread both night and day, never sure of your life.

twi: Anɔpa mobɛka se, “Sɛ ɛyɛɛ anwummere a!” Na anwummere nso mobɛka se, “Sɛ ɛyɛɛ anɔpa a!” Mobɛka saa, esiane ehu a ɛbɛhyɛ mo koma amaama ne nea atwa mo ho ahyia a mo ani behu no.
english: In the morning you will say, “If only it were evening!” and in the evening, “If only it were morning!”—because of the terror that will fill your hearts and the sights that your eyes will see.

twi: Na Awurade bɛma mo atenatena ahyɛn mu asan akɔ Misraim, akwantu a mehyɛɛ sɛ ɛnsɛ sɛ mutu bio no. Ɛhɔ na mode mo ho bɛma mo atamfo sɛ wɔntɔ mo sɛ nkoa, nanso obiara rempɛ sɛ ɔbɛtɔ mo.
english: The Lord will send you back in ships to Egypt on a journey I said you should never make again. There you will offer yourselves for sale to your enemies as male and female slaves, but no one will buy you.

twi: Apam No NtimuEyinom ne nhyehyɛe a ɛwɔ apam a Awurade hyɛɛ Mose sɛ ɔne Israelfo no nyɛ wɔ Moab nka apam a ɔne wɔn yɛɛ no wɔ Horeb no mu no ho.
english: These are the terms of the covenant the Lord commanded Moses to make with the Israelites in Moab, in addition to the covenant he had made with them at Horeb.

twi: Mose frɛɛ Israelfo no nyinaa ka kyerɛɛ wɔn se:Moahu nea Awurade yɛɛ Farao ne ne mpanyimfo ne ne man nyinaa wɔ Misraim no.
english:
Moses summoned all the Israelites and said to them:
Your eyes have seen all that the Lord did in Egypt to Pharaoh, to all his officials and to all his land.

twi: Mo ankasa muhuu sɔhwɛ akɛse, nsɛnkyerɛnne a ɛyɛ hu ne anwonwade akɛse no.
english: With your own eyes you saw those great trials, those signs and great wonders.

twi: Nanso de besi nnɛ yi, Awurade mmaa mo adwene a ɛte asɛm ase anaa ani a ehu ade anaa aso a ɛte asɛm.
english: But to this day the Lord has not given you a mind that understands or eyes that see or ears that hear.

twi: Nanso Awurade se, mfe aduanan a midii mo anim faa sare so no mu no, mo ntama antetew, na mo mpaboa a ɛhyehyɛ mo anan nso anhwere.
english: Yet the Lord says, “During the forty years that I led you through the wilderness, your clothes did not wear out, nor did the sandals on your feet.

twi: Moanni brodo, annom nsa anaa nsa a ano yɛ den. Meyɛɛ saa sɛnea mubehu sɛ mene Awurade, mo Nyankopɔn no.
english: You ate no bread and drank no wine or other fermented drink. I did this so that you might know that I am the Lord your God.”

twi: Yeduu ha no, Hesbonhene Sihon ne Basanhene Og ba bɛko tiaa yɛn, nanso yedii wɔn so.
english: When you reached this place, Sihon king of Heshbon and Og king of Bashan came out to fight against us, but we defeated them.

twi: Yɛfaa wɔn asase de maa Ruben ne Gad mmusuakuw ne Manase abusuakuw no fa sɛ wɔn agyapade.
english: We took their land and gave it as an inheritance to the Reubenites, the Gadites and the half-tribe of Manasseh.

twi: Ɛno nti, munni saa apam yi so sɛnea ɛbɛyɛ a biribiara a mobɛyɛ no bɛyɛ yiye.
english: Carefully follow the terms of this covenant, so that you may prosper in everything you do.

twi: Mo nyinaa—mo mmusuakuw mpanyimfo, mo atemmufo, mo ahwɛfo ne Israel mmarima nyinaa, nnɛ mugyina Awurade, mo Nyankopɔn no, anim;
english: All of you are standing today in the presence of the Lord your God—your leaders and chief men, your elders and officials, and all the other men of Israel,

twi: mo ne mo mma ne mo yerenom ne ahɔho a wɔte mo mu a wobu mo nnua, soa mo nsu.
english: together with your children and your wives, and the foreigners living in your camps who chop your wood and carry your water.

twi: Mugyina ha sɛ mo ne Awurade, mo Nyankopɔn no, rebɛyɛ apam; apam a Awurade ne mo reyɛ nnɛ na ɔde ntam resɔw ano
english: You are standing here in order to enter into a covenant with the Lord your God, a covenant the Lord is making with you this day and sealing with an oath,

twi: na wasi so gyinae sɛ nnɛ, moyɛ ne nkurɔfo na ɔno nso bɛyɛ mo Nyankopɔn, sɛnea ɔhyɛɛ mo bɔ no na ɔkaa ntam kyerɛɛ mo agyanom Abraham, Isak ne Yakob no.
english: to confirm you this day as his people, that he may be your God as he promised you and as he swore to your fathers, Abraham, Isaac and Jacob.

twi: Mereyɛ saa apam yi a ne ntam bata ho a, ɛnyɛ mo nko a,
english: I am making this covenant, with its oath, not only with you

twi: mo ne yɛn gyina ha nnɛ wɔ Awurade, mo Nyankopɔn no, anim na mmom, wɔn a wonni ha nnɛ nso ka ho bi.
english: who are standing here with us today in the presence of the Lord our God but also with those who are not here today.

twi: Mo ankasa munim sɛnea yɛtenaa Misraim ne sɛnea yɛreba ha no yɛfaa aman so besii ha.
english: You yourselves know how we lived in Egypt and how we passed through the countries on the way here.

twi: Muhuu akyiwade ahoni a wɔde nnua ne abo ne dwetɛ ne sikakɔkɔɔ ayɛ wɔ wɔn nkyɛn.
english: You saw among them their detestable images and idols of wood and stone, of silver and gold.

twi: Monhwɛ yiye sɛ ɔbarima anaa ɔbea anaa abusua biara a ɛwɔ mo mu nnɛ no mu biara koma rennan mfi Awurade, mo Nyankopɔn no, ho nkɔsom saa aman yi anyame; monhwɛ sɛ ntin biara nni mo mu a epuw bɔre a ɛyɛ nwen saa.
english: Make sure there is no man or woman, clan or tribe among you today whose heart turns away from the Lord our God to go and worship the gods of those nations; make sure there is no root among you that produces such bitter poison.

twi: Sɛ saa onipa no te ntam yi mu nsɛm na ohyira ne ho, na ɔka wɔ ne tirim se, “Me ho sɔnn, ɛmfa ho sɛ menam asoɔden kwan so.” Eyi de atoyerɛnkyɛm bɛba asase a so afɔw ne nea so awo no nyinaa so.
english: When such a person hears the words of this oath and they invoke a blessing on themselves, thinking, “I will be safe, even though I persist in going my own way,” they will bring disaster on the watered land as well as the dry.

twi: Awurade remfa nkyɛ saa onipa no. Nʼabufuw ne ne ninkunu bɛdɛw atia no. Nnome a wɔakyerɛw no saa nhoma yi mu no nyinaa bɛba ne so na Awurade bɛpepa ne din afi ɔsoro ase.
english: The Lord will never be willing to forgive them; his wrath and zeal will burn against them. All the curses written in this book will fall on them, and the Lord will blot out their names from under heaven.

twi: Awurade bɛtwe no afi Israel mmusuakuw nyinaa mu na wahwie apam no mu nnome nyinaa a wɔakyerɛw wɔ saa mmara nhoma no mu no agu ne so.
english: The Lord will single them out from all the tribes of Israel for disaster, according to all the curses of the covenant written in this Book of the Law.

twi: Mo mma a wɔbɛba wɔ daakye awo ntoatoaso mu no ne wɔn a wofi ahɔho ase a wofi akyirikyiri asase so behu asase no sɛe ne nyarewa a Awurade de bɛbrɛ asase no.
english: Your children who follow you in later generations and foreigners who come from distant lands will see the calamities that have fallen on the land and the diseases with which the Lord has afflicted it.

twi: Wobehu sɛ, wɔn asase no nyinaa adan sufre ne nkyene a wonnua so hwee, na hwee mfifi wɔ so na ahabammono biara nnyina so, a ɛnyɛ yiye na hwee nso nnyin wɔ so; sare ahaban mpo. Ɛbɛyɛ sɛ Sodom ne Gomora, Adma ne Seboim a Awurade sɛee no nʼabufuwhyew mu no.
english: The whole land will be a burning waste of salt and sulfur—nothing planted, nothing sprouting, no vegetation growing on it. It will be like the destruction of Sodom and Gomorrah, Admah and Zeboyim, which the Lord overthrew in fierce anger.

twi: Aman a atwa ahyia no bebisa se, “Adɛn nti na Awurade ayɛ saa asase yi saa? Adɛn nti na ne bo fu dennen saa?”
english: All the nations will ask: “Why has the Lord done this to this land? Why this fierce, burning anger?”

twi: Na wɔbɛka akyerɛ wɔn se, “Saa asɛm yi sii, efisɛ nnipa a wɔwɔ asase no so buu apam a wɔne Awurade, wɔn agyanom Nyankopɔn no, yɛe bere a oyii wɔn fii Misraim asase so no.
english: And the answer will be: “It is because this people abandoned the covenant of the Lord, the God of their ancestors, the covenant he made with them when he brought them out of Egypt.

twi: Wɔdan kɔsom anyame afoforo wɔkotow wɔn, anyame a wonnim wɔn, anyame a Awurade nkyerɛɛ wɔn sɛ wɔnsom.
english: They went off and worshiped other gods and bowed down to them, gods they did not know, gods he had not given them.

twi: Ɛno nti Awurade abufuw dɛw tiaa saa asase yi, nam so de nnome a wɔakyerɛw wɔ saa nhoma yi mu no nyinaa baa wɔn so no.
english: Therefore the Lord’s anger burned against this land, so that he brought on it all the curses written in this book.

twi: Abufuwhyew mu, Awurade tutuu ne nkurɔfo ase fii wɔn asase so twaa wɔn asu de wɔn koguu asase foforo so, sɛnea ɛte mprempren yi.”
english: In furious anger and in great wrath the Lord uprooted them from their land and thrust them into another land, as it is now.”

twi: Kokoamsɛm yɛ Awurade, yɛn Nyankopɔn no, dea, nanso nneɛma a wɔda no adi no yɛ yɛn ne yɛn asefo dea daa, sɛnea ɛbɛyɛ a yebedi saa mmara yi mu nsɛm so.
english: The secret things belong to the Lord our God, but the things revealed belong to us and to our children forever, that we may follow all the words of this law.

twi: Awurade Nkyɛn Ba Mu YiyediSɛ nhyira ne nnome a mede ato mo anim no nyinaa ba mo so, na mode hyɛ mo koma mu wɔ baabiara a Awurade, mo Nyankopɔn no, bɛfa mo akɔ, wɔ aman no mu,
english: When all these blessings and curses I have set before you come on you and you take them to heart wherever the Lord your God disperses you among the nations,

twi: na mo ne mo mma san ba Awurade, mo Nyankopɔn no, nkyɛn, na mode mo koma ne mo kra nyinaa yɛ osetie ma no sɛnea merekyerɛ mo nnɛ yi a,
english: and when you and your children return to the Lord your God and obey him with all your heart and with all your soul according to everything I command you today,

twi: ɛno de, Awurade, mo Nyankopɔn no, de mo siade bɛma mo, na wahu mo mmɔbɔ, na waboaboa mo ano bio afi amanaman a ɔbɔɔ mo hwete kɔɔ so no nyinaa so, asan de mo aba.
english: then the Lord your God will restore your fortunes and have compassion on you and gather you again from all the nations where he scattered you.

twi: Sɛ mpo, wɔapam mo kɔ akyirikyiri asase bi a ɛwɔ ɔsoro ase a, efi hɔ no, Awurade, mo Nyankopɔn no, bɛboaboa mo ano asan de mo aba.
english: Even if you have been banished to the most distant land under the heavens, from there the Lord your God will gather you and bring you back.

twi: Ɔde mo bɛba asase a ɛyɛ mo agyanom de no so na moafa sɛ agyapade. Ɔbɛma mo adi yiye na moadɔɔso asen mo agyanom.
english: He will bring you to the land that belonged to your ancestors, and you will take possession of it. He will make you more prosperous and numerous than your ancestors.

twi: Awurade, mo Nyankopɔn no, beyi fi a ɛwɔ mo ne mo asefo koma mu no sɛnea ɛbɛyɛ a mode mo koma ne mo kra nyinaa bɛdɔ no na moanya nkwa.
english: The Lord your God will circumcise your hearts and the hearts of your descendants, so that you may love him with all your heart and with all your soul, and live.

twi: Awurade, mo Nyankopɔn no, de saa nnome yi nyinaa begu mo atamfo a wɔtaa mo no so.
english: The Lord your God will put all these curses on your enemies who hate and persecute you.

twi: Mobɛsan atie, adi Awurade ahyɛde a mede rema mo nnɛ no nyinaa so.
english: You will again obey the Lord and follow all his commands I am giving you today.

twi: Awurade, mo Nyankopɔn no, bɛma biribiara a moyɛ no asi mo yiye. Ɔbɛma mo yafunu mu aba asi yiye pii. Mo nyɛmmoa bɛdɔɔso. Na mo mfuw mu nnɔbae nso bebu so, efisɛ Awurade, mo Nyankopɔn no, ani begye sɛ ɔbɛma mo adi yiye sɛnea na ɔyɛ mo agyanom no.
english: Then the Lord your God will make you most prosperous in all the work of your hands and in the fruit of your womb, the young of your livestock and the crops of your land. The Lord will again delight in you and make you prosperous, just as he delighted in your ancestors,

twi: Sɛ mutie Awurade, mo Nyankopɔn no, nne, na mudi nʼahyɛde ne ne mmara a wɔakyerɛw wɔ saa Mmara Nhoma no mu no so, na mode mo koma ne mo kra dɔ no a, nʼani begye mo yiyedi ho.
english: if you obey the Lord your God and keep his commands and decrees that are written in this Book of the Law and turn to the Lord your God with all your heart and with all your soul.

twi: Owu Ne NkwaNokware, saa mmara a merehyɛ ama mo nnɛ yi sodi nyɛ den na ɛnyɛ ade a morentumi nyɛ nso.
english: Now what I am commanding you today is not too difficult for you or beyond your reach.

twi: Enni ɔsoro a enti mobɛka se, “Hena na ɔbɛkɔ ɔsoro ama yɛn na wakogye abrɛ yɛn, na yɛate adi so?”
english: It is not up in heaven, so that you have to ask, “Who will ascend into heaven to get it and proclaim it to us so we may obey it?”

twi: Saa ara nso na enni po agya a enti mobɛka se, “Hena na obetwa akɔ ɛpo fa nohɔ ama yɛn na wakogye abrɛ yɛn, na yɛate adi so?”
english: Nor is it beyond the sea, so that you have to ask, “Who will cross the sea to get it and proclaim it to us so we may obey it?”

twi: Dabi, asɛm no abɛn wo. Ɛda wʼano na ɛwɔ wo koma mu sɛ mudi so.
english: No, the word is very near you; it is in your mouth and in your heart so you may obey it.

twi: Muntie, nnɛ, mede nkwa ne yiyedi, owu ne ɔsɛe asi mo anim.
english: See, I set before you today life and prosperity, death and destruction.

twi: Na Sɛ mutie Awurade, mo Nyankopɔn no, mmara a merehyɛ ama mo nnɛ yi, nam so dɔ Awurade, mo Nyankopɔn, nantew nʼakwan mu, di ne mmara so a, mubenya nkwa na mo ase adɔ, na Awurade, mo Nyankopɔn behyira mo wɔ asase a morekɔ akɔtena so no so.
english: For I command you today to love the Lord your God, to walk in obedience to him, and to keep his commands, decrees and laws; then you will live and increase, and the Lord your God will bless you in the land you are entering to possess.

twi: Nanso sɛ mo koma dan, sɛ moanyɛ osetie, na sɛ wɔtwe mo kɔkotow anyame afoforo, na mosom wɔn a,
english: But if your heart turns away and you are not obedient, and if you are drawn away to bow down to other gods and worship them,

twi: mepae mu ka kyerɛ mo nnɛ sɛ, nea ɛte biara no wɔbɛsɛe mo; morentena asase a moretwa Yordan akɔ so akɔfa sɛ agyapade no so nkyɛ.
english: I declare to you this day that you will certainly be destroyed. You will not live long in the land you are crossing the Jordan to enter and possess.

twi: Nnɛ mede nkwa ne owu, nhyira ne nnome, asi mo anim sɛ munyi nea mopɛ. Mefrɛ ɔsoro ne asase sɛ nnansefo. Momfa nkwa sɛnea ɛbɛyɛ a mo ne mo asefo benya nkwa!
english: This day I call the heavens and the earth as witnesses against you that I have set before you life and death, blessings and curses. Now choose life, so that you and your children may live

twi: Monnɔ Awurade, mo Nyankopɔn no, monyɛ osetie mma no, na momfa mo ho mma no, efisɛ ɔno ne mo nkwa. Ɛno na mobɛtena ase akyɛ wɔ asase a Awurade kaa ntam sɛ ɔde bɛma mo tete agyanom; Abraham, Isak ne Yakob no.
english: and that you may love the Lord your God, listen to his voice, and hold fast to him. For the Lord is your life, and he will give you many years in the land he swore to give to your fathers, Abraham, Isaac and Jacob.

twi: Yosua Di Mose AdeBere a Mose kaa saa nsɛm yi kyerɛɛ Israelfo wiee no,
english: Then Moses went out and spoke these words to all Israel:

twi: ɔkaa bio se, “Mprempren madi mfe ɔha ne aduonu, nti merentumi nni mo anim bio. Awurade aka akyerɛ me sɛ merentwa Asubɔnten Yordan.
english: “I am now a hundred and twenty years old and I am no longer able to lead you. The Lord has said to me, ‘You shall not cross the Jordan.’

twi: Nanso Awurade, mo Nyankopɔn no, ankasa bedi mo anim atwa. Ɔbɛsɛe aman a wɔte hɔ na mobɛfa wɔn asase no. Yosua ne onipa foforo a obedi mo anim sɛnea Awurade hyɛɛ mo bɔ no.
english: The Lord your God himself will cross over ahead of you. He will destroy these nations before you, and you will take possession of their land. Joshua also will cross over ahead of you, as the Lord said.

twi: Awurade bɛsɛe aman aman a wɔte asase no so no sɛnea ɔsɛee Sihon ne Og a na wɔyɛ Amorifo ahemfo no.
english: And the Lord will do to them what he did to Sihon and Og, the kings of the Amorites, whom he destroyed along with their land.

twi: Awurade de nnipa a wɔte hɔ no bɛhyɛ mo nsa na ɛsɛ sɛ mo ne wɔn di no sɛnea mahyɛ mo no.
english: The Lord will deliver them to you, and you must do to them all that I have commanded you.

twi: Monyɛ den na mo bo nyɛ duru! Munnsuro wɔn! Awurade, mo Nyankopɔn no, bedi mo anim. Ɔrenni mo huammɔ na ɔrennyaw mo nso.”
english: Be strong and courageous. Do not be afraid or terrified because of them, for the Lord your God goes with you; he will never leave you nor forsake you.”

twi: Afei, Mose frɛɛ Yosua ka kyerɛɛ no wɔ Israelfo no nyinaa anim se, “Yɛ den na yɛ nnam, na wo na wode ɔman yi bɛkɔ asase a Awurade kaa wɔn agyanom ntam sɛ ɔde bɛma wɔn no so; na wo na wobɛkyɛ ama wɔn.
english: Then Moses summoned Joshua and said to him in the presence of all Israel, “Be strong and courageous, for you must go with this people into the land that the Lord swore to their ancestors to give them, and you must divide it among them as their inheritance.

twi: Awurade na ɔredi wʼanim. Ɔbɛka wo ho; ɔrenni wo huammɔ na ɔrennyaw wo nti nsuro na mma wo koma ntu!”
english: The Lord himself goes before you and will be with you; he will never leave you nor forsake you. Do not be afraid; do not be discouraged.”

twi: Mmara No KenkanAfei, Mose kyerɛw mmara yi too hɔ; ɔde maa Lewifo asɔfo a wɔsoaa Awurade apam adaka no ne Israel mpanyimfo nyinaa.
english: So Moses wrote down this law and gave it to the Levitical priests, who carried the ark of the covenant of the Lord, and to all the elders of Israel.

twi: Mose hyɛɛ wɔn se, “Mfe ason biara awiei, Asese Afahyɛ mu no, wɔmfa obiara ka a ɔde no nkyɛ no.
english: Then Moses commanded them: “At the end of every seven years, in the year for canceling debts, during the Festival of Tabernacles,

twi: Israelfo nyinaa nhyia wɔ Awurade mo Nyankopɔn no, anim wɔ faako a ɔbɛkyerɛ no, na moakenkan saa mmara yi wɔ wɔn anim ama wɔate.
english: when all Israel comes to appear before the Lord your God at the place he will choose, you shall read this law before them in their hearing.

twi: Frɛ nnipa no nyinaa, mmarima, mmea, mmofra ne ahɔho a wɔte mo nkurow so nso sɛnea ɛbɛyɛ a wɔbɛte na wobesua sɛ, ɛsɛ sɛ wosuro Awurade, mo Nyankopɔn no, na wobedi mmara no so pɛpɛɛpɛ
english: Assemble the people—men, women and children, and the foreigners residing in your towns—so they can listen and learn to fear the Lord your God and follow carefully all the words of this law.

twi: na ama wɔn mma a wonnim mmara no ate na wɔasua sɛnea ɛsɛ sɛ wosuro Awurade, mo Nyankopɔn no, mmere dodow a mote asase a moretwa Yordan akɔfa sɛ agyapade no so.”
english: Their children, who do not know this law, must hear it and learn to fear the Lord your God as long as you live in the land you are crossing the Jordan to possess.”

twi: Wɔka Israel Asoɔden Ho AsɛmAwurade ka kyerɛɛ Mose se, “Wo wu bere aso. Frɛ Yosua na fa no kɔ Ahyiae Ntamadan no mu, faako a mede nʼadwuma bɛhyɛ ne nsa no.” Enti Mose ne Yosua kɔdaa wɔn ho adi wɔ Ahyiae Ntamadan no mu.
english: The Lord said to Moses, “Now the day of your death is near. Call Joshua and present yourselves at the tent of meeting, where I will commission him.” So Moses and Joshua came and presented themselves at the tent of meeting.

twi: Na Awurade yii ne ho adi kyerɛɛ wɔn wɔ omununkum fadum mu, na omununkum no gyinaa ntamadan no abobow ano.
english: Then the Lord appeared at the tent in a pillar of cloud, and the cloud stood over the entrance to the tent.

twi: Awurade ka kyerɛɛ Mose se, “Ɛrenkyɛ wubewu na woakɔka wʼagyanom ho, na ɛrenkyɛ na saa nnipa yi de wɔn ho bɛma anyame hɔho a wɔwɔ asase a wɔrekɔ so no so no. Wobegyaw me na wɔabu apam a me ne wɔn hyehyɛɛ no so.
english: And the Lord said to Moses: “You are going to rest with your ancestors, and these people will soon prostitute themselves to the foreign gods of the land they are entering. They will forsake me and break the covenant I made with them.

twi: Na saa da no, me bo befuw wɔn na mapo wɔn; mede mʼanim behintaw wɔn na wɔbɛsɛe wɔn. Ɔhaw a emu yɛ den ahorow pii bɛba wɔn so ama wɔabisa se, ‘So ɛnsɛ sɛ saa ɔhaw yi ba, esiane sɛ Onyankopɔn nni yɛn nkyɛn bio no nti?’
english: And in that day I will become angry with them and forsake them; I will hide my face from them, and they will be destroyed. Many disasters and calamities will come on them, and in that day they will ask, ‘Have not these disasters come on us because our God is not with us?’

twi: Saa bere no mede mʼanim behintaw wɔn esiane wɔn bɔne ahorow a wɔayɛ wɔ anyame afoforo a wɔsom no nti.
english: And I will certainly hide my face in that day because of all their wickedness in turning to other gods.

twi: “Afei, monkyerɛw saa dwom yi mu nsɛm mfa na monkyerɛ Israelfo no, na wɔnto sɛnea ɛbɛyɛ adansede ama me na mede atia wɔn.
english: “Now write down this song and teach it to the Israelites and have them sing it, so that it may be a witness for me against them.

twi: Mede wɔn bɛba asase a nufusu ne ɛwo resen wɔ so sɛnea mekaa ntam hyɛɛ wɔn agyanom bɔ no. Na wodidi mee yɛ akɛse a, afei, wɔbɛdan wɔn ani akɔsom anyame afoforo apo me, nam so abu mʼapam no so.
english: When I have brought them into the land flowing with milk and honey, the land I promised on oath to their ancestors, and when they eat their fill and thrive, they will turn to other gods and worship them, rejecting me and breaking my covenant.

twi: Afei, ɔhaw ne akwanside bebree ba wɔn so a, dwom yi bedi adanse atia wɔn, efisɛ wɔn asefo werɛ remfi da. Minim nea wotumi yɛ koraa ansa na mede wɔn bɛba asase a maka ho ntam ahyɛ bɔ no so.”
english: And when many disasters and calamities come on them, this song will testify against them, because it will not be forgotten by their descendants. I know what they are disposed to do, even before I bring them into the land I promised them on oath.”

twi: Enti Mose kyerɛw dwom no guu hɔ saa da no na ɔkyerɛɛ Israelfo no.
english: So Moses wrote down this song that day and taught it to the Israelites.

twi: Afei, Awurade hyɛɛ Nun babarima Yosua sɛ, “Yɛ den na yɛ nnam, efisɛ wo na wode Israelfo no bɛba asase a mekaa ntam hyɛɛ ho bɔ no so na mʼankasa mɛka mo ho.”
english: The Lord gave this command to Joshua son of Nun: “Be strong and courageous, for you will bring the Israelites into the land I promised them on oath, and I myself will be with you.”

twi: Bere a Mose kyerɛw mmara nsɛm no nyinaa fi mfiase kosii awiei no guu nhoma mu wiei no,
english: After Moses finished writing in a book the words of this law from beginning to end,

twi: ɔde saa ahyɛde yi maa Lewifo a na wɔsoa Awurade apam adaka no:
english: he gave this command to the Levites who carried the ark of the covenant of the Lord:

twi: “Momfa saa Mmara Nhoma yi nkɔto Awurade, mo Nyankopɔn, apam adaka no nkyɛn. Ɛhɔ na ɛbɛda sɛ adansede a etia Israelfo.
english: “Take this Book of the Law and place it beside the ark of the covenant of the Lord your God. There it will remain as a witness against you.

twi: Efisɛ minim sɛnea moyɛ atuatewfo ne asoɔden. Mpo, me ne mo da so wɔ hɔ yi, moatew Awurade so atua. Na me wu akyi no, atua bɛn na morentew!
english: For I know how rebellious and stiff-necked you are. If you have been rebellious against the Lord while I am still alive and with you, how much more will you rebel after I die!

twi: Momfrɛ mo mpanyimfo nyinaa ne mo mmusuakuw ntuanofo nyinaa sɛnea metumi akasa akyerɛ wɔn na mafrɛ ɔsoro ne asase de adi adanse atia wɔn.
english: Assemble before me all the elders of your tribes and all your officials, so that I can speak these words in their hearing and call the heavens and the earth to testify against them.

twi: Minim sɛ me wu akyi no, mobɛsɛe koraa na moaman afi ɔkwan a makyerɛ mo sɛ momfa so no so. Mmere a ɛreba no, amanehunu bɛba mo so, efisɛ monam bɔne a mobɛyɛ wɔ Awurade anim no so no bɛhwanyan nʼabufuw.”
english: For I know that after my death you are sure to become utterly corrupt and to turn from the way I have commanded you. In days to come, disaster will fall on you because you will do evil in the sight of the Lord and arouse his anger by what your hands have made.”

twi: Mose DwomEnti Mose kaa dwom no mu nsɛm nyinaa fi ti kosi ti kyerɛɛ Israelfo a wɔahyia hɔ no.
english: And Moses recited the words of this song from beginning to end in the hearing of the whole assembly of Israel:

twi: Monyɛ aso, mo ɔsoro na mɛkasa;tie, wo asase, nsɛm a efi mʼanom.
english:
Listen, you heavens, and I will speak;
    hear, you earth, the words of my mouth.

twi: Ma me nkyerɛkyerɛ ntɔ sɛ osu;na me nsɛm nsian sɛ obosu,sɛ osu a ɛpete gu sare foforo so,sɛ osu mmoroso wɔ afifide foforo so.
english:
Let my teaching fall like rain
    and my words descend like dew,
like showers on new grass,
    like abundant rain on tender plants.

twi: Mɛbɔ Awurade din.O, monkamfo yɛn Nyankopɔn kɛseyɛ!
english:
I will proclaim the name of the Lord.
    Oh, praise the greatness of our God!

twi: Ɔne Ɔbotan no, ne nnwuma so nni,na nʼakwan nyinaa ye.Onyankopɔn nokwafo a ɔnyɛ mfomso,Ɔtreneeni ne ɔnokwafo ne no.
english:
He is the Rock, his works are perfect,
    and all his ways are just.
A faithful God who does no wrong,
    upright and just is he.

twi: Porɔwee adidi wɔn mu na wɔnyɛ ne mma;wɔyɛ awo ntoatoaso akɔntɔnkyefo aniwufo.
english:
They are corrupt and not his children;
    to their shame they are a warped and crooked generation.

twi: Saa ne ɔkwan a ɛsɛ sɛ mofa so tua Awurade ka ni ana,mo nkwaseafo ne adwenharefo?Ɛnyɛ ɔno ne mo Agya, mo yɛfo no?Ɛnyɛ ɔno na ɔbɔɔ mo na ɔmaa mo nnyinaso?
english:
Is this the way you repay the Lord,
    you foolish and unwise people?
Is he not your Father, your Creator,
    who made you and formed you?

twi: Monkae tete nna;munnwen tete awo ntoatoaso no ho.Mummisa mo agya na ɔbɛkyerɛ mo.Mummisa mo mpanyimfo na wɔbɛkyerɛ mo ase.
english:
Remember the days of old;
    consider the generations long past.
Ask your father and he will tell you,
    your elders, and they will explain to you.

twi: Bere a Ɔsorosoroni no maa amanaman no agyapade,na ɔkyekyɛɛ adesamma nyinaa mu no,ɔtotoo ahye maa nnipa nosɛnea Israelmma no dodow te.
english:
When the Most High gave the nations their inheritance,
    when he divided all mankind,
he set up boundaries for the peoples
    according to the number of the sons of Israel.

twi: Efisɛ Israelfo yɛ Awurade kyɛfa;Yakob yɛ nʼagyapade wɔde maa no.
english:
For the Lord’s portion is his people,
    Jacob his allotted inheritance.

twi: Ohuu no wɔ sare asase so,asase kesee a hwee nni so so.Ɔde no sie hwɛɛ ne so;ɔbɔɔ ne ho ban sɛ nʼaniwa kurutiayisi,
english:
In a desert land he found him,
    in a barren and howling waste.
He shielded him and cared for him;
    he guarded him as the apple of his eye,

twi: sɛ ɔkɔre a ɔhwanyan ne berebuw muna ɔbɔ mfamfia fa ne mma ho,na ɔtrɛw ne ntaban mu buma no,soaa no kɔɔ no.
english:
like an eagle that stirs up its nest
    and hovers over its young,
that spreads its wings to catch them
    and carries them aloft.

twi: Awurade nkutoo na ɔkyerɛɛ no kwan;na ananafo nyame biara nka ne ho.
english:
The Lord alone led him;
    no foreign god was with him.

twi: Ɔma no nantew faa asase no nkoko so;na ɔde mfuw so nnuaba bɔɔ no akɔnhama;Ɔde ɔbotan mu wone ngo a efi abohemaa mu,
english:
He made him ride on the heights of the land
    and fed him with the fruit of the fields.
He nourished him with honey from the rock,
    and with oil from the flinty crag,

twi: nyɛmmoa mu nufusu ne srade,nguamma ne mmirekyi a wɔadɔ srade,Basan adwennini a wɔpawne atoko muhumuhu siesiee no.Monom nsa papa a efi bobe mu.
english:
with curds and milk from herd and flock
    and with fattened lambs and goats,
with choice rams of Bashan
    and the finest kernels of wheat.
You drank the foaming blood of the grape.

twi: Yeshurun dɔɔ srade na onyaa ahoɔden;aduan ma wɔyɛɛ duru, yɛɛ pemee.Wɔtoo Onyankopɔn a ɔbɔɔ wɔn no asaworam;wɔpoo wɔn Nkwagye Botan no.
english:
Jeshurun grew fat and kicked;
    filled with food, they became heavy and sleek.
They abandoned the God who made them
    and rejected the Rock their Savior.

twi: Wɔma ɔtwee ninkunu wɔ wɔn ananafo anyame no hona wɔde wɔn abosom a okyi no hyɛɛ no abufuw.
english:
They made him jealous with their foreign gods
    and angered him with their detestable idols.

twi: Wɔbɔɔ afɔre maa atoro anyame a wɔnyɛ Onyankopɔn,anyame a na wonnim wɔn,anyame a wɔbaa nnansa yi ara,anyame a na mo agyanom nsuro wɔn.
english:
They sacrificed to false gods, which are not God—
    gods they had not known,
    gods that recently appeared,
    gods your ancestors did not fear.

twi: Mopaa Ɔbotan a ɔyɛɛ mo agya no.Mo werɛ fii Onyankopɔn a ɔwoo mo no.
english:
You deserted the Rock, who fathered you;
    you forgot the God who gave you birth.

twi: Awurade huu eyi na ɔpoo wɔnefisɛ ne mmabarima ne ne mmabea hyɛɛ no abufuw.
english:
The Lord saw this and rejected them
    because he was angered by his sons and daughters.

twi: Ɔkae se, “Mede mʼanim behintaw wɔnna wɔahu sɛnea wɔn awiei bɛyɛEfisɛ, wɔyɛ awo ntoatoaso akɔntɔnkyefo;mma a wonni nokware.
Wɔde nea ɛnyɛ Onyame ahyɛ me ninkutwena wɔde wɔn ahoni ahuhuw no ahyɛ me abufuw.Mɛma wɔn ani abere nnipa a wɔnyɛ me nkurɔfo.Mɛma ɔman a wonni ntease no ahyɛ wɔn abufuw.
english:
They made me jealous by what is no god
    and angered me with their worthless idols.
I will make them envious by those who are not a people;
    I will make them angry by a nation that has no understanding.

twi: Efisɛ mʼabufuwhyew befita ogya mu,nea ɛhyew kɔka awufo a wɔwɔ asase ase no.Ɛbɛsɛe asase ne so nnɔbaena ɛpaapae mmepɔw fapem.
english:
For a fire will be kindled by my wrath,
    one that burns down to the realm of the dead below.
It will devour the earth and its harvests
    and set afire the foundations of the mountains.

twi: “Mɛhɔre amanehunu ahorow no siw wɔ wɔn sona matow me bɛmma awowɔ wɔn.
english:
“I will heap calamities on them
    and spend my arrows against them.

twi: Mede ɔkɔm kɛse,atiridiinini ne owuyare a ɛsɛe ade;mɛsoma nkekammoa se aba wɔn so;nhurutoa a wɔtow si wɔ mfutuma mu no ano bɔre.
english:
I will send wasting famine against them,
    consuming pestilence and deadly plague;
I will send against them the fangs of wild beasts,
    the venom of vipers that glide in the dust.

twi: Afoa bɛma wɔahwere wɔn mma wɔ abɔnten so;wɔn afi mu, ehu bɛtɔ wɔn so.Mmerante ne mmabaa,mmofra ne nkwakoraa ase bɛhyew.
english:
In the street the sword will make them childless;
    in their homes terror will reign.
The young men and young women will perish,
    the infants and those with gray hair.

twi: Mekae se mɛbɔ wɔn ahwetena mapepa wɔn din afi nnipa adwene mu.
english:
I said I would scatter them
    and erase their name from human memory,

twi: Nanso misuroo ɔtamfo fɛwdi,anyɛ a na ɔtamfo ante ase aka se,‘Yɛn nsa adi nkonim;Ɛnyɛ Awurade na ɔyɛɛ eyinom nyinaa.’ ”
english:
but I dreaded the taunt of the enemy,
    lest the adversary misunderstand
and say, ‘Our hand has triumphed;
    the Lord has not done all this.’”

twi: Israel yɛ ɔman a wonni adwene.Obi nni wɔn mu a ɔwɔ nhumu.
english:
They are a nation without sense,
    there is no discernment in them.

twi: Sɛ anka wɔyɛ anyansafo na wɔbɛte eyi ase,na wɔahu nea wɔn awiei bɛyɛ ɛ!
english:
If only they were wise and would understand this
    and discern what their end will be!

twi: Ɛbɛyɛ dɛn na onipa baako ataa nnipa apem,na baanu bɛma mpem du aguan,gye sɛ wɔn Botan atɔn wɔngye sɛ Awurade ayi wɔn ama.
english:
How could one man chase a thousand,
    or two put ten thousand to flight,
unless their Rock had sold them,
    unless the Lord had given them up?

twi: Efisɛ wɔn botan nte sɛ yɛn Botan,sɛnea yɛn atamfo mpo gye to mu no.
english:
For their rock is not like our Rock,
    as even our enemies concede.

twi: Wɔn bobe fi Sodom bobe muna efi Gomora mfuw mu.Awuduru ahyɛ wɔn bobe aba mma,na bɔnwoma ahyɛ wɔn kasiaw amaama.
english:
Their vine comes from the vine of Sodom
    and from the fields of Gomorrah.
Their grapes are filled with poison,
    and their clusters with bitterness.

twi: Wɔn bobesa yɛ awɔ ano bɔre;aprammiri ano bɔrewerɛmfo.
english:
Their wine is the venom of serpents,
    the deadly poison of cobras.

twi: “So menkoraa eyi mmoroso,na mensɔw ano wɔ mʼademude mu ana
english:
“Have I not kept this in reserve
    and sealed it in my vaults?

twi: Mɛtɔ were; metua so ka.Wɔn nan bɛwatiri bere a ɛsɛ mu;wɔn atoyerɛnkyɛm no abɛnna wɔn sɛe taa wɔn.”
english:
It is mine to avenge; I will repay.
    In due time their foot will slip;
their day of disaster is near
    and their doom rushes upon them.”

twi: Awurade bebu ne nkurɔfo atɛnna wasesa nʼadwene wɔ ne nkoa ho,bere a wahu sɛ wɔn ahoɔden asa,na ɛnkaa obiara, akoa anaa ɔdehye.
english:
The Lord will vindicate his people
    and relent concerning his servants
when he sees their strength is gone
    and no one is left, slave or free.

twi: Obebisa se, “Afei wɔn anyame no wɔ he,ɔbotan a wɔde yɛɛ wɔn guankɔbea,
english:
He will say: “Now where are their gods,
    the rock they took refuge in,

twi: anyame a wodii wɔn afɔrebɔde mu sradena wɔnom wɔn ɔnom afɔrebɔ mu nsa no?Ma wɔnsɔre mmɛboa mo!Ma womegye mo!
english:
the gods who ate the fat of their sacrifices
    and drank the wine of their drink offerings?
Let them rise up to help you!
    Let them give you shelter!

twi: “Afei, munhu sɛ, me ara me ne no!Onyame biara nni hɔ sɛ me!Me na mikum na mema nkwa:Me na mipira, na mɛkyekye,na obi rentumi nnye mfi me nsam.
english:
“See now that I myself am he!
    There is no god besides me.
I put to death and I bring to life,
    I have wounded and I will heal,
    and no one can deliver out of my hand.

twi: Mema me nsa so kyerɛ ɔsoro de nidi sua sɛ:Sɛ mete ase daa yi,
english:
I lift my hand to heaven and solemnly swear:
    As surely as I live forever,

twi: sɛ mesew me afoa a ɛpa yerɛwyerɛw nona mifi atemmu mu so mu kuaw a,mɛtɔ mʼatamfo so werena matua wɔn a wokyi me ka.
english:
when I sharpen my flashing sword
    and my hand grasps it in judgment,
I will take vengeance on my adversaries
    and repay those who hate me.

twi: Mɛma me bɛmma anom mogya abow,na mʼafoa adi ɔhonam,atɔfo ne nnommumfo mogya,atamfo ntuanofo no ti.”
english:
I will make my arrows drunk with blood,
    while my sword devours flesh:
the blood of the slain and the captives,
    the heads of the enemy leaders.”

twi: Mo aman, mo ne ne nkurɔfo nni ahurusi,efisɛ ɔbɛtɔ ne nkoa mogya so were;ɔbɛtɔ were wɔ nʼatamfo sona wapata ama nʼasase ne ne nkurɔfo.
english:
Rejoice, you nations, with his people,
    for he will avenge the blood of his servants;
he will take vengeance on his enemies
    and make atonement for his land and people.

twi: Mose ne Nun babarima Hosea ba bɛkaa dwom yi mu nsɛm nyinaa kyerɛɛ nnipa no.
english: Moses came with Joshua son of Nun and spoke all the words of this song in the hearing of the people.

twi: Mose woroo saa dwom no mu nsɛm no kyerɛɛ Israelfo no wiee no,
english: When Moses finished reciting all these words to all Israel,

twi: ɔka kaa ho se, “Momfa nsɛm a maka akyerɛ mo no nyinaa nsie mo koma mu. Monka nkyerɛ mo mma nso, sɛnea ɛbɛyɛ a wobedi saa mmara yi mu nsɛm nyinaa so pɛpɛɛpɛ.
english: he said to them, “Take to heart all the words I have solemnly declared to you this day, so that you may command your children to obey carefully all the words of this law.

twi: Saa nkyerɛkyerɛ yi nyɛ nsɛm bi a wɔde rema mo kwa, ɛyɛ mo nkwa! Sɛ mudi so a, mubenyin akyɛ wɔ asase a moretwa Asubɔnten Yordan akɔfa no so.”
english: They are not just idle words for you—they are your life. By them you will live long in the land you are crossing the Jordan to possess.”

twi: Mose WuDa no ara, Awurade ka kyerɛɛ Mose se,
english: On that same day the Lord told Moses,

twi: “Kɔ Moab, kɔ mmepɔw a ɛwɔ asu no apuei no so, na foro Nebo bepɔw a ɛne Yeriko di nhwɛanim no. To wʼani hwɛ Kanaan asase no, asase a mede rema Israelfo sɛ wɔn agyapade no.
english: “Go up into the Abarim Range to Mount Nebo in Moab, across from Jericho, and view Canaan, the land I am giving the Israelites as their own possession.

twi: Bepɔw a woaforo no so hɔ na wobɛkɔ akɔka wʼagyanom ho, sɛnea wo nua Aaron wuu wɔ Hor bepɔw so kɔkaa nʼagyanom ho no.
english: There on the mountain that you have climbed you will die and be gathered to your people, just as your brother Aaron died on Mount Hor and was gathered to his people.

twi: Efisɛ mo baanu dii me huammɔ wɔ Israelfo mu wɔ Meriba ne Kades asu ho wɔ Sin sare so. Moanni me kronkronyɛ ho adanse ankyerɛ Israelfo no wɔ hɔ.
english: This is because both of you broke faith with me in the presence of the Israelites at the waters of Meribah Kadesh in the Desert of Zin and because you did not uphold my holiness among the Israelites.

twi: Ɛno nti, mubehu asase no afi akyiri, nanso morenkɔ asase a mede rema Israelfo no so.”
english: Therefore, you will see the land only from a distance; you will not enter the land I am giving to the people of Israel.”

twi: Mose Hyira Mmusuakuw NoEyi ne nhyira a Onyankopɔn nipa Mose de hyiraa Israelfo no ansa na ɔrewu:
english: This is the blessing that Moses the man of God pronounced on the Israelites before his death.

twi: Ose, “Awurade fi Sinai baeofi Seir baa wɔn so;ɔhran fi Paran bepɔw so.Ɔde akronkronfo pii baefi anafo fam ne mmepɔw nsian so.
english:
He said:
“The Lord came from Sinai
    and dawned over them from Seir;
    he shone forth from Mount Paran.
He came with myriads of holy ones
    from the south, from his mountain slopes.

twi: Nokware ni, wo na wodɔ nnipa no,akronkronfo nyinaa wɔ wo nsam.Wɔn nyinaa kotow wo nan ase,na wonya nkyerɛkyerɛ fi wo hɔ,
english:
Surely it is you who love the people;
    all the holy ones are in your hand.
At your feet they all bow down,
    and from you receive instruction,

twi: mmara a Mose de maa yɛn no;Yakob nkurɔfo agyapade.
english:
the law that Moses gave us,
    the possession of the assembly of Jacob.

twi: Ɔyɛɛ ɔhene wɔ Yeshurunbere a nnipa no ntuanofo hyiae,wɔne Israel mmusuakuw no.
english:
He was king over Jeshurun
    when the leaders of the people assembled,
    along with the tribes of Israel.

twi: “Ma Ruben nya nkwa na onwu,na mma ne nkurɔfo so nhuan.”
english:
“Let Reuben live and not die,
    nor his people be few.”

twi: Na ɔkaa eyi faa Yuda ho:“Tie, Awurade, tie Yuda sufrɛ;fa no brɛ ne nkurɔfo.Ɔde nʼankasa nsa bɔ ne ho ban.Ao, yɛ ne boafo tia nʼatamfo!”
english:
And this he said about Judah:
“Hear, Lord, the cry of Judah;
    bring him to his people.
With his own hands he defends his cause.
    Oh, be his help against his foes!”

twi: Asɛm a ɔka faa Lewi abusuakuw ho:“Awurade, wode ade kronkronama wʼasomfo nokwafo Lewifo.Wosɔɔ wɔn hwɛe wɔ Masawɔne wɔn koe wɔ Meriba asu ho.
english:
About Levi he said:
“Your Thummim and Urim belong
    to your faithful servant.
You tested him at Massah;
    you contended with him at the waters of Meribah.

twi: Lewifo tiee wʼasɛmbɔɔ wʼapam no ho ban.Wodii wo nokwaresen sɛnea wodii wɔn awofo,abusuafo ne wɔn mma nokware.
english:
He said of his father and mother,
    ‘I have no regard for them.’
He did not recognize his brothers
    or acknowledge his own children,
but he watched over your word
    and guarded your covenant.

twi: Afei, ma wɔnkyerɛ Yakob wo mmara no.Ma wɔmfa wo nkyerɛkyerɛ no mma Israelfo.Wɔde aduhuam bɛba wʼanimAbɛbɔ ɔhyew afɔre wɔ afɔremuka so.
english:
He teaches your precepts to Jacob
    and your law to Israel.
He offers incense before you
    and whole burnt offerings on your altar.

twi: Hyira Lewifo, Ao Awuradena ma wɔn nsa ano nnwuma nsɔ wʼani.Bubu wɔn atamfo;bɔ wɔn atamfo hwe fam a wɔnsɔre bio.”
english:
Bless all his skills, Lord,
    and be pleased with the work of his hands.
Strike down those who rise against him,
    his foes till they rise no more.”

twi: Asɛm a Mose ka faa Benyamin abusuakuw ho:“Ma Awurade dɔ nnye ntin wɔ Benyamin nkurɔfo mu,efisɛ ɔbɔ wɔn ho ban daa nyinaa,na nea Awurade dɔ no no nhome wɔ ne nwini ase daa.”
english:
About Benjamin he said:
“Let the beloved of the Lord rest secure in him,
    for he shields him all day long,
    and the one the Lord loves rests between his shoulders.”

twi: Asɛm a Mose ka faa Yosef mmusuakuw ho:“Awurade mfa ne sorosoro bosu a ɛsom bone bun mu nsu a efi asase ase no,nhyira wɔn nsase.
english:
About Joseph he said:
“May the Lord bless his land
    with the precious dew from heaven above
    and with the deep waters that lie below;

twi: Ɔmfa ne nnepa efi owia mu bane adonne a ebetumi apue afi ɔsram so;
english:
with the best the sun brings forth
    and the finest the moon can yield;

twi: ne nnɔbae pa a efi tete mmepɔw mune nea abu so wɔ nkoko a etim hɔ daa mu
english:
with the choicest gifts of the ancient mountains
    and the fruitfulness of the everlasting hills;

twi: ne akyɛde a ɛso nni a efi asase ne ne mayɛ mu,ne adom a efi nea na ɔte nwura a ɛhyew mu no.Saa nhyira yi nyinaa mmra Yosef ti so,nea ɔyɛ ne nuanom mu ɔheneba no anintɔn mu.
english:
with the best gifts of the earth and its fullness
    and the favor of him who dwelt in the burning bush.
Let all these rest on the head of Joseph,
    on the brow of the prince among his brothers.

twi: Yosef sɛ nantwinini a ɔyɛ abakan wɔ ahenni mu.Ne ahoɔden te sɛ ɔtrɔm mmɛn.Ɔde bɛwowɔ aman no,wɔn a wɔwɔ asase ano no mpo.Eyinom ne Efraim mpem du du no;eyinom ne Manase mpempem no.”
Asɛm a Mose ka faa Sebulon ne Isakar mmusuakuw ho:“Sebulon asefo, munni anigye wɔ mo adifi mu.Isakar asefo, munni anigye wɔ mo ntamadan mu.
english:
About Zebulun he said:
“Rejoice, Zebulun, in your going out,
    and you, Issachar, in your tents.

twi: Wɔbɛfrɛ nnipa ahorow akɔ bepɔw no sokɔbɔ trenee afɔre wɔ hɔ;wobefi po mu adenya mmoroso mu ato ponafi ademude a ahintaw wɔ nwea mu.”
english:
They will summon peoples to the mountain
    and there offer the sacrifices of the righteous;
they will feast on the abundance of the seas,
    on the treasures hidden in the sand.”

twi: Asɛm a Mose ka faa Gad abusuakuw ho:“Nhyira nka obi a ɔtrɛw Gad mantam mu!Gad te hɔ sɛ gyataa ɔretetew abasa anaa eti.
english:
About Gad he said:
“Blessed is he who enlarges Gad’s domain!
    Gad lives there like a lion,
    tearing at arm or head.

twi: Gad nkurɔfo paw asase pa no maa wɔn ho;ɔkannifo kyɛfa na wɔde maa wɔn.Bere a nkurɔfo no mpanyimfo hyiae no,wɔyɛɛ Awurade atɛntrenee apɛde no,ne nʼatemmu a ɛfa Israelfo ho no.”
english:
He chose the best land for himself;
    the leader’s portion was kept for him.
When the heads of the people assembled,
    he carried out the Lord’s righteous will,
    and his judgments concerning Israel.”

twi: Asɛm a Mose ka faa Dan abusuakuw ho:“Dan yɛ gyata ba a,ɔrepue afi Basan.”
english:
About Dan he said:
“Dan is a lion’s cub,
    springing out of Bashan.”

twi: Asɛm a Mose ka faa Naftali abusuakuw ho:“Naftali wɔ adom bebreena Awurade nhyira ayɛ wo ma;ɔtare no anafo fam bɛyɛ wo kyɛfa.”
english:
About Naphtali he said:
“Naphtali is abounding with the favor of the Lord
    and is full of his blessing;
    he will inherit southward to the lake.”

twi: Asɛm a Mose ka faa Aser abusuakuw ho:“Mma no mu nea wɔahyira no koraa ne Aser;wɔmma ne nuanom mpɛ nʼasɛm,na ɔmfa ngo nguare nʼanan ase.
Wʼapon ho nkyerewa nyɛ dade ne kɔbere mfrafrae;wʼahoɔden ne wo nkwanna bɛsae so.
english:
The bolts of your gates will be iron and bronze,
    and your strength will equal your days.

twi: “Onyankopɔn biara nni hɔ sɛ Yeshurun Nyankopɔn;a ɔnam ɔsorosoro ne nʼahenni mu mununkumso ba bɛboa wo.
english:
“There is no one like the God of Jeshurun,
    who rides across the heavens to help you
    and on the clouds in his majesty.

twi: Onyankopɔn a ɔwɔ hɔ daa yɛ wo guankɔbea;nea ɛwɔ ase no ne abasa a ɛwɔ hɔ daa no.Ɔbɛpam wʼatamfo afi wʼanim;ɔbɛka se, ‘Sɛe wɔn!’
english:
The eternal God is your refuge,
    and underneath are the everlasting arms.
He will drive out your enemies before you,
    saying, ‘Destroy them!’

twi: Enti, Israel bɛtena ase dwoodwoo;Yakob benya bammɔwɔ asase a atoko ne nsa foforo wɔ so,faako a ɔsoro bosu gugu.
english:
So Israel will live in safety;
    Jacob will dwell secure
in a land of grain and new wine,
    where the heavens drop dew.

twi: Nhyira nka mo, Israel!Hena na ɔte sɛ mo,nnipa a Awurade agye mo nkwa.Ɔyɛ mo nkatabo ne boafone mo anuonyam afoa!Mo atamfo bɛkotow mo anim,na moatiatia wɔn sorɔnsorɔmmea.”
english:
Blessed are you, Israel!
    Who is like you,
    a people saved by the Lord?
He is your shield and helper
    and your glorious sword.
Your enemies will cower before you,
    and you will tread on their heights.”

twi: Mose WuNa Mose fi Moab asase tataw so foro kɔɔ Nebo Bepɔw so, san foroo Pisga a etwa Yeriko. Ɛhɔ na Awurade kyerɛɛ no asase no nyinaa, efi Gilead kosi Dan;
english: Then Moses climbed Mount Nebo from the plains of Moab to the top of Pisgah, across from Jericho. There the Lord showed him the whole land—from Gilead to Dan,

twi: Naftali nsase nyinaa; Efraim ne Manase nsase; Yuda nsase nyinaa kosi Ntam Po no ho;
english: all of Naphtali, the territory of Ephraim and Manasseh, all the land of Judah as far as the Mediterranean Sea,

twi: Negeb; ne nsase a efi Yeriko Bon, ne Mmɛ Kuropɔn no de kosi Soar tɔnn.
english: the Negev and the whole region from the Valley of Jericho, the City of Palms, as far as Zoar.

twi: Na Awurade ka kyerɛɛ Mose se, “Eyi ne asase a mekaa ntam hyɛɛ ho bɔ kyerɛɛ Abraham, Isak ne Yakob se mede bɛma wɔn asefo no. Afei, mama wo de wʼani ahu, nanso worentwa nkɔ so.”
english: Then the Lord said to him, “This is the land I promised on oath to Abraham, Isaac and Jacob when I said, ‘I will give it to your descendants.’ I have let you see it with your eyes, but you will not cross over into it.”

twi: Na Mose, Awurade somfo no wuu wɔ Moab asase so sɛnea Awurade kae no.
english: And Moses the servant of the Lord died there in Moab, as the Lord had said.

twi: Wosiee no wɔ obon bi a ɛne Bet-Peor di nhwɛanim, nanso ebesi nnɛ, obiara nnim faako a ne da wɔ.
english: He buried him in Moab, in the valley opposite Beth Peor, but to this day no one knows where his grave is.

twi: Mose dii mfirihyia ɔha ne aduonu na owui, nanso na nʼani hu ade yiye na ne ho nso yɛ den.
english: Moses was a hundred and twenty years old when he died, yet his eyes were not weak nor his strength gone.

twi: Israelfo suu no nnafua aduasa wɔ Moab tataw so ara kosii sɛ nʼayiyɛ kɔɔ awiei.
english: The Israelites grieved for Moses in the plains of Moab thirty days, until the time of weeping and mourning was over.

twi: Afei, Nun babarima Yosua nyaa nyansa honhom, efisɛ Mose de ne nsa guu ne so. Enti Israelfo yɛɛ osetie maa no na wɔyɛɛ biribiara sɛnea Awurade hyɛɛ Mose no ara pɛ.
english: Now Joshua son of Nun was filled with the spirit of wisdom because Moses had laid his hands on him. So the Israelites listened to him and did what the Lord had commanded Moses.

twi: Mose akyi no, odiyifo biara mmaa Israel a Awurade nim no anim ne anim
english: Since then, no prophet has risen in Israel like Moses, whom the Lord knew face to face,

twi: a Awurade somaa no ma ɔkɔyɛɛ anwonwade ne nsɛnkyerɛnne a ɛyɛ hu wɔ Misraim asase so de tiaa Farao ne ne mpanyimfo nyinaa wɔ asase no so nyinaa.
english: who did all those signs and wonders the Lord sent him to do in Egypt—to Pharaoh and to all his officials and to his whole land.

twi: Na obiara nnaa tumi kɛse anaa ahodwiriw nneyɛe adi te sɛnea Mose yɛɛ wɔ Israel nyinaa ani so no.
english: For no one has ever shown the mighty power or performed the awesome deeds that Moses did in the sight of all Israel.

twi: Biribiara Yɛ AdehuhuwEyinom ne nsɛm a Ɔsɛnkafo, ɔhene Dawid babarima a ɔyɛ ɔhene wɔ Yerusalem se:
english: The words of the Teacher, son of David, king in Jerusalem:

twi: “Ahuhude! Ahuhude!”Ɔsɛnkafo no na ose.“Ahuhude mu ahuhudeBiribiara yɛ ahuhude.”
english:
“Meaningless! Meaningless!”
    says the Teacher.
“Utterly meaningless!
    Everything is meaningless.”

twi: Dɛn na onipa nya fi nʼadwumayɛ nyinaa mu,nea okum ne ho yɛ no owia so no?
english:
What do people gain from all their labors
    at which they toil under the sun?

twi: Awo ntoatoaso ba na ɛkɔ,nanso asase tim hɔ daa.
english:
Generations come and generations go,
    but the earth remains forever.

twi: Owia pue na owia kɔtɔ,na ɛyɛ ntɛm kɔ nea epue fii hɔ no.
english:
The sun rises and the sun sets,
    and hurries back to where it rises.

twi: Mframa bɔ kɔ anafo famna ɛdan hwɛ atifi fam;ekyinkyin kɔ baabiara,na ɛsan bɔ fa ne kwan so.
english:
The wind blows to the south
    and turns to the north;
round and round it goes,
    ever returning on its course.

twi: Nsubɔnten nyinaa sen kogu po mu,nanso po nyɛ ma da.Faako a nsubɔnten no fi nohɔ na wɔsan kɔ bio.
english:
All streams flow into the sea,
    yet the sea is never full.
To the place the streams come from,
    there they return again.

twi: Biribiara yɛ ɔbrɛa ɛboro nea obi bɛka so.Ani nhwɛ ade nwie dana aso nso ntie nsɛm mma ɛnyɛ mma da.
english:
All things are wearisome,
    more than one can say.
The eye never has enough of seeing,
    nor the ear its fill of hearing.

twi: Nea aba no bɛba bio,nea wɔayɛ no, wɔbɛyɛ bio;ade foforo biara nni owia yi ase.
Biribi wɔ hɔ a wobetumi aka wɔ ho se:“Hwɛ! eyi yɛ ade foforo” ana?Ɛwɔ hɔ dedaw fi tete nteredee;ɛwɔ hɔ ansa na wɔwoo yɛn.
english:
Is there anything of which one can say,
    “Look! This is something new”?
It was here already, long ago;
    it was here before our time.

twi: Wɔnkae tetefo no,na wɔn a wonnya nnwoo wɔn no nso,wɔn a wobedi wɔn akyi norenkae wɔn.
english:
No one remembers the former generations,
    and even those yet to come
will not be remembered
    by those who follow them.

twi: Nimdeɛ Yɛ AhuhudeMe, Ɔsɛnkafo, na meyɛ Israelhene wɔ Yerusalem.
english: I, the Teacher, was king over Israel in Jerusalem.

twi: Mituu me ho sii hɔ sɛ mede nimdeɛ besua ayɛ nhwehwɛmu wɔ biribiara a wɔyɛ no owia yi ase ho. Adesoa duruduru a Onyankopɔn de ato adesamma so!
english: I applied my mind to study and to explore by wisdom all that is done under the heavens. What a heavy burden God has laid on mankind!

twi: Mahu biribiara a wɔyɛ no owia yi ase; ne nyinaa nka hwee, ɛte sɛnea obi tu mmirika taa mframa.
english: I have seen all the things that are done under the sun; all of them are meaningless, a chasing after the wind.

twi: Nea akyea no wontumi nteɛ;na nea enni hɔ no wontumi nkan.
english:
What is crooked cannot be straightened;
    what is lacking cannot be counted.

twi: Mekaa wɔ me tirim se, “Hwɛ, manyin na manya nimdeɛ bebree asen obiara a watena Yerusalem ahengua so ansa na merebedi ade. Manya nhumu ne nimdeɛ mu osuahu.”
english: I said to myself, “Look, I have increased in wisdom more than anyone who has ruled over Jerusalem before me; I have experienced much of wisdom and knowledge.”

twi: Afei meyɛɛ mʼadwene sɛ mɛhwehwɛ na mate nimdeɛ, ne adammɔsɛm ne nkwaseasɛm ase. Nanso mihuu sɛ eyi nso te sɛnea obi tu mmirika taa mframa.
english: Then I applied myself to the understanding of wisdom, and also of madness and folly, but I learned that this, too, is a chasing after the wind.

twi: Nimdeɛ bebree de awerɛhow na ɛba;nyansa dɔɔso a, awerɛhowdi dɔɔso.
english:
For with much wisdom comes much sorrow;
    the more knowledge, the more grief.

twi: Anigye Ne Adwuma Yɛ Ade HuhuwMekaa wɔ me koma mu se, “Afei bra, mede anigye bɛsɔ wo ahwɛ na yɛahu nea eye.” Nanso ankosi hwee.
english: I said to myself, “Come now, I will test you with pleasure to find out what is good.” But that also proved to be meaningless.

twi: Mekae se, “Ɔserew yɛ nkwaseade. Na dɛn na anigye tumi yɛ?”
english: “Laughter,” I said, “is madness. And what does pleasure accomplish?”

twi: Mepɛɛ sɛ mihu nea eye pa ara ma yɛn wɔ bere tiaa a yɛwɔ wɔ asase yi so no. Enti meyɛɛ mʼadwene sɛ mede nsa bɛsɛpɛw me ho na mahwehwɛ, ahu nkwaseasɛm nkyerɛase, a na nyansa da so bɔ mʼankasa mʼadwene ho ban.
english: I tried cheering myself with wine, and embracing folly—my mind still guiding me with wisdom. I wanted to see what was good for people to do under the heavens during the few days of their lives.

twi: Mede me nsa hyɛɛ nnwuma akɛse ase; misisii adan yɛɛ bobe nturo.
english: I undertook great projects: I built houses for myself and planted vineyards.

twi: Meyɛɛ nturo ne ahomegyebea na miduaduaa nnuaba ahorow bebree wɔ mu.
english: I made gardens and parks and planted all kinds of fruit trees in them.

twi: Misisii nsukorae a mɛtwe nsu afi mu, de agugu nnua a ɛrenyin no so.
english: I made reservoirs to water groves of flourishing trees.

twi: Metɔɔ nkoa ne mfenaa, na minyaa ebinom nso a wɔwoo wɔn wɔ me fi. Afei nso, minyaa anantwi ne nguan bebree sen obiara a wadi mʼanim wɔ Yerusalem.
english: I bought male and female slaves and had other slaves who were born in my house. I also owned more herds and flocks than anyone in Jerusalem before me.

twi: Mepɛɛ dwetɛ ne sikakɔkɔɔ, gyigyee ahemfo ne amantam no ademude kaa ho. Mefaa mmarima ne mmea nnwontofo, pɛɛ mmea atenae nso; nea ɛyɛ ɔbarima koma anigyede biara.
english: I amassed silver and gold for myself, and the treasure of kings and provinces. I acquired male and female singers, and a harem as well—the delights of a man’s heart.

twi: Migyee din sen obiara a wadi mʼanim wɔ Yerusalem. Eyinom nyinaa mu no me nimdeɛ kɔɔ so yɛɛ adwuma.
english: I became greater by far than anyone in Jerusalem before me. In all this my wisdom stayed with me.

twi: Nea mʼani hwehwɛe biara mamfa ankame no;mansiw me koma anigye ho kwan.Me koma ani gyee me nnwuma nyinaa ho,na eyi yɛ mʼadwumayɛ so akatua.
english:
I denied myself nothing my eyes desired;
    I refused my heart no pleasure.
My heart took delight in all my labor,
    and this was the reward for all my toil.

twi: Nanso sɛ mehwɛ nea me nsa ayɛ nyinaane nea mabrɛ anya a,ne nyinaa nka hwee, ɛte sɛnea wotu mmirika taa mframamannya mfaso biara wɔ owia yi ase.
english:
Yet when I surveyed all that my hands had done
    and what I had toiled to achieve,
everything was meaningless, a chasing after the wind;
    nothing was gained under the sun.

twi: Nimdeɛ Ne Nkwaseade Yɛ Ade HuhuwMede mʼadwene kɔɔ nimdeɛ,adammɔsɛm ne nkwaseasɛm so.Dɛn bio na nea wadi ɔhene ade betumi ayɛasen nea wɔayɛ dedaw no?
english:
Then I turned my thoughts to consider wisdom,
    and also madness and folly.
What more can the king’s successor do
    than what has already been done?

twi: Mihuu sɛ nimdeɛ ye sen nkwaseasɛm,sɛnea hann yɛ sen sum no.
english:
I saw that wisdom is better than folly,
    just as light is better than darkness.

twi: Onyansafo ani wɔ ne tirim,na ɔkwasea de, ɔnantew sum mu;nanso mihuu sɛwɔn nyinaa nkrabea yɛ pɛ.
english:
The wise have eyes in their heads,
    while the fool walks in the darkness;
but I came to realize
    that the same fate overtakes them both.

twi: Afei misusuw wɔ me koma mu se,“Ɔkwasea nkrabea bɛto me nso.Enti sɛ mihu nyansa a mfaso bɛn na minya?”Mekaa wɔ me koma mu se,“Eyi nso nka hwee.”
english:
Then I said to myself,
“The fate of the fool will overtake me also.
    What then do I gain by being wise?”
I said to myself,
    “This too is meaningless.”

twi: Te sɛ ɔkwasea no, onyansafo nso, wɔrenkae no daa;nna a ɛreba no mu, wɔrenkae wɔn baanu no.Te sɛ ɔkwasea no, onyansafo nso bewu!
Adwumayɛ Nka HweeƐno nti asetena fonoo me, na adwuma a yɛyɛ wɔ owia yi ase no haw me. Ne nyinaa yɛ ahuhude, te sɛnea wotu mmirika taa mframa.
english: So I hated life, because the work that is done under the sun was grievous to me. All of it is meaningless, a chasing after the wind.

twi: Mikyii nea mayɛ adwuma apɛ nyinaa wɔ owia yi ase, efisɛ ɛsɛ sɛ migyaw hɔ ma nea obedi mʼade.
english: I hated all the things I had toiled for under the sun, because I must leave them to the one who comes after me.

twi: Na hena na onim sɛ onipa ko no bɛyɛ onyansafo anaa ɔkwasea? Nanso nea mabiri me mogya ani apɛ wɔ owia yi ase nyinaa bɛkɔ ne nsam. Eyi nso yɛ ahuhude.
english: And who knows whether that person will be wise or foolish? Yet they will have control over all the fruit of my toil into which I have poured my effort and skill under the sun. This too is meaningless.

twi: Enti mepaa abaw wɔ owia yi ase adwumaden ho.
english: So my heart began to despair over all my toilsome labor under the sun.

twi: Na onipa befi ne nimdeɛ, nyansa ne adwumayɛ ho nimdeɛ mu ayɛ nʼasɛde, na afei ɛsɛ sɛ ogyaw nʼadwumayɛ so aba ma obi a ɔnyɛɛ adwuma biara. Eyi nso yɛ ahuhude, na ɛhaw adwene.
english: For a person may labor with wisdom, knowledge and skill, and then they must leave all they own to another who has not toiled for it. This too is meaningless and a great misfortune.

twi: Dɛn na onipa nya fi ne brɛ ne dadwen a ɔde yɛ adwuma wɔ owia yi ase mu?
english: What do people get for all the toil and anxious striving with which they labor under the sun?

twi: Ne nkwanna nyinaa, nʼadwumayɛ yɛ ɔyaw ne ɔhaw; anadwo mpo nʼadwene yɛ adwuma. Eyi nso yɛ ahuhude.
english: All their days their work is grief and pain; even at night their minds do not rest. This too is meaningless.

twi: Biribiara nsen sɛ onipa bedidi na wanom na wanya ahotɔ wɔ adwumayɛ mu. Eyi nso mihuu sɛ efi Onyankopɔn,
english: A person can do nothing better than to eat and drink and find satisfaction in their own toil. This too, I see, is from the hand of God,

twi: efisɛ ɛnyɛ ɔno a anka hena na obetumi adidi anaasɛ obenya ahotɔ?
english: for without him, who can eat or find enjoyment?

twi: Onipa a ɔsɔ Onyankopɔn ani no, ɔma no nimdeɛ, nyansa ne anigye, nanso omumɔyɛfo de, ɔma ɔboaboa ahonyade ano ma nea ɔsɔ Onyankopɔn ani. Eyi nso yɛ ahuhude, sɛnea wɔde mmirikatu taa mframa no.
english: To the person who pleases him, God gives wisdom, knowledge and happiness, but to the sinner he gives the task of gathering and storing up wealth to hand it over to the one who pleases God. This too is meaningless, a chasing after the wind.

twi: Biribiara Wɔ Ne BereBiribiara wɔ ne bere,na dwumadi biara a ɛwɔ ɔsoro ase wɔ ne bere.
english:
There is a time for everything,
    and a season for every activity under the heavens:

twi: Awo wɔ ne bere, na owu wɔ ne bere,ogu wɔ ne bere na otwa nso wɔ ne bere,
english:
a time to be born and a time to die,
    a time to plant and a time to uproot,

twi: okum wɔ ne bere na ayaresa wɔ ne bere,obubu wɔ ne bere, na osi nso wɔ ne bere,
english:
a time to kill and a time to heal,
    a time to tear down and a time to build,

twi: agyaadwotwa wɔ ne bere, na ɔserew nso wɔ ne bere,awerɛhow wɔ ne bere na asaw wɔ ne bere,
english:
a time to weep and a time to laugh,
    a time to mourn and a time to dance,

twi: abo hwete wɔ ne bere na abo anoboa wɔ ne bere,atuuyɛ wɔ ne bere na ne ntetewmudi nso wɔ ne bere,
english:
a time to scatter stones and a time to gather them,
    a time to embrace and a time to refrain from embracing,

twi: adehwehwɛ wɔ ne bere na adehwere wɔ ne bere,adekora wɔ ne bere na adetowgu wɔ ne bere,
english:
a time to search and a time to give up,
    a time to keep and a time to throw away,

twi: ade mu sunsuane wɔ ne bere na ne pempam wɔ ne bere,kommyɛ wɔ ne bere na kasa wɔ ne bere,
english:
a time to tear and a time to mend,
    a time to be silent and a time to speak,

twi: ɔdɔ wɔ ne bere na ɔtan wɔ ne bere,ɔko wɔ ne bere na asomdwoe wɔ ne bere.
english:
a time to love and a time to hate,
    a time for war and a time for peace.

twi: Mfaso bɛn na odwumayɛni nya fi nʼadwumaden mu?
english: What do workers gain from their toil?

twi: Mahu adesoa a Onyankopɔn de ato nnipa so.
english: I have seen the burden God has laid on the human race.

twi: Wayɛ biribiara fɛfɛ wɔ ne bere mu. Ɔde nkwa a ɛnsa da ahyɛ nnipa koma mu, nanso wontumi nte nea Onyankopɔn ayɛ fi mfiase kosi awiei no ase.
english: He has made everything beautiful in its time. He has also set eternity in the human heart; yet no one can fathom what God has done from beginning to end.

twi: Minim sɛ biribiara nni hɔ a eye ma nnipa kyɛn sɛ wobegye wɔn ani na wɔayɛ nea eye bere a wɔte ase.
english: I know that there is nothing better for people than to be happy and to do good while they live.

twi: Sɛ obiara bedidi na wanom na wanya anigye wɔ ne dwumadi nyinaa mu, eyi ne Onyankopɔn akyɛde.
english: That each of them may eat and drink, and find satisfaction in all their toil—this is the gift of God.

twi: Minim sɛ biribiara a Onyankopɔn yɛ no bɛtena hɔ daa, wɔrentumi mfa biribi nka ho na wɔrentumi nyi biribi mfi mu. Onyankopɔn yɛ eyi sɛnea nnipa de nidi bɛma no.
english: I know that everything God does will endure forever; nothing can be added to it and nothing taken from it. God does it so that people will fear him.

twi: Biribiara a ɛwɔ hɔ nnɛ no, aba pɛn,na nea ɛbɛba no nso aba dedaw;na Onyankopɔn bɛfrɛ nea asi dedaw no ama akontaabu.
Na mihuu biribi foforo wɔ owia yi ase sɛ:Amumɔyɛsɛm wɔ nea atemmu wɔ,atɛntreneebea no, amumɔyɛsɛm wɔ hɔ.
english:
And I saw something else under the sun:
In the place of judgment—wickedness was there,
    in the place of justice—wickedness was there.

twi: Medwenee wɔ me koma mu se,“Onyankopɔn bebuatreneefo ne amumɔyɛfo nyinaa atɛn,efisɛ adwuma biara benya ne bere,nneyɛe biara ne ne bere.”
english:
I said to myself,
“God will bring into judgment
    both the righteous and the wicked,
for there will be a time for every activity,
    a time to judge every deed.”

twi: Afei medwenee se, “Nnipa de, Onyankopɔn sɔ wɔn hwɛ ma wohu sɛ wɔte sɛ mmoa.
english: I also said to myself, “As for humans, God tests them so that they may see that they are like the animals.

twi: Onipa nkrabea te sɛ mmoa de na ɛda hɔ ma wɔn nyinaa. Sɛnea ɔbaako wu no, saa ara na ɔfoforo nso wu. Wɔn nyinaa wɔ ɔhome baako; onipa nni biribi a ɔde kyɛn aboa. Biribiara yɛ ahuhude.
english: Surely the fate of human beings is like that of the animals; the same fate awaits them both: As one dies, so dies the other. All have the same breath; humans have no advantage over animals. Everything is meaningless.

twi: Wɔn nyinaa kɔ faako; wɔn nyinaa fi dɔte mu na wɔsan kɔ dɔte mu.
english: All go to the same place; all come from dust, and to dust all return.

twi: Hena na onim sɛ onipa honhom foro soro na aboa de sian kɔ asase mu ana?”
english: Who knows if the human spirit rises upward and if the spirit of the animal goes down into the earth?”

twi: Enti mihuu sɛ biribiara nni hɔ a eye ma onipa kyɛn sɛ nʼani bɛka nʼadwuma ho, efisɛ ɛno ne ne kyɛfa. Na hena na obetumi de no asan aba sɛ ɔmmɛhwɛ nea ebesi ne wu nʼakyi?
english: So I saw that there is nothing better for a person than to enjoy their work, because that is their lot. For who can bring them to see what will happen after them?

twi: Nhyɛso, Adwumaden, AnkonamBio, mehwɛ mihuu nhyɛso a ɛrekɔ so wɔ owia yi ase:Mihuu wɔn a wɔredi wɔn nya no nusuna wonni ɔwerɛkyekyefo biara;tumi no wɔ wɔn nhyɛsofo no nsamna wonni ɔwerɛkyekyefo biara.
english:
Again I looked and saw all the oppression that was taking place under the sun:
I saw the tears of the oppressed—
    and they have no comforter;
power was on the side of their oppressors—
    and they have no comforter.

twi: Na mekae se: Awufo awɔawuwu dedaw no,ani gye sen ateasefo;wɔn a wɔda so wɔ nkwa mu no.
english:
And I declared that the dead,
    who had already died,
are happier than the living,
    who are still alive.

twi: Na nea oye sen baanu yine nea onnya mmae,nea onnya nhuu bɔne awɔyɛ wɔ owia yi ase.
english:
But better than both
    is the one who has never been born,
who has not seen the evil
    that is done under the sun.

twi: Na mihuu sɛ adwumayɛ mu ɔbrɛ ne nea onipa tumi yɛ nyinaa nnyinaso ne sɛ nʼani bere ne yɔnko. Eyi nso yɛ ahuhude, mmirika a wotu taa mframa.
english: And I saw that all toil and all achievement spring from one person’s envy of another. This too is meaningless, a chasing after the wind.

twi: Ɔkwasea bobɔw ne nsa gu ne hona ɔsɛe ne ho.
english:
Fools fold their hands
    and ruin themselves.

twi: Nsammua baako a asomdwoe wɔ muye sen nsammua abien a ɔbrɛ bata ho;ɛte sɛ nea wotaa mframa.
english:
Better one handful with tranquillity
    than two handfuls with toil
    and chasing after the wind.

twi: Afei nso mihuu biribi a ɛnka hwee wɔ owia yi ase:
english: Again I saw something meaningless under the sun:

twi: Na ɔbarima bi wɔ hɔ a ɔyɛ ankonam;onni ɔbabarima anaa onuabarima.Nʼadwumaden amma nʼawie da,nanso nʼani ansɔ nʼahonya.Obisaa ne ho se, “Na hena na merebrɛ ama no,na adɛn nti na mede anigye kame me kra?”Eyi nso yɛ ahuhude,ɛyɛ ɔhaw kwa.
english:
There was a man all alone;
    he had neither son nor brother.
There was no end to his toil,
    yet his eyes were not content with his wealth.
“For whom am I toiling,” he asked,
    “and why am I depriving myself of enjoyment?”
This too is meaningless—
    a miserable business!

twi: Baanu ye sen ɔbaakofo,efisɛ wonya wɔn brɛ so mfaso a ɛsɔ ani:
english:
Two are better than one,
    because they have a good return for their labor:

twi: Sɛ ɔbaako hwe ase ane yɔnko betumi aboa no.Nanso onipa a ɔhwe ase aonni ɔboafo no, yɛ mmɔbɔ.
english:
If either of them falls down,
    one can help the other up.
But pity anyone who falls
    and has no one to help them up.

twi: Bio, sɛ baanu da bɔ mu a wɔka wɔn ho hyew.Na ɛbɛyɛ dɛn na ankonam bɛka ne ho hyew?
english:
Also, if two lie down together, they will keep warm.
    But how can one keep warm alone?

twi: Ɔbaakofo de, wobetumi aka no ahyɛnanso baanu tumi pere wɔn ti.Hama a wɔawɔ no mmɛsa no, wontumi ntetew mu ntɛm.
english:
Though one may be overpowered,
    two can defend themselves.
A cord of three strands is not quickly broken.

twi: Nkɔso Yɛ AdehunuƆbabun nyansafo a odi hia ye sen ɔhene akwakoraa a ɔyɛ ɔkwasea na ontie kɔkɔbɔ bio.
english: Better a poor but wise youth than an old but foolish king who no longer knows how to heed a warning.

twi: Ebia na ɔbabun no fi afiase na obedii ade anaasɛ wɔwoo no too ohia mu wɔ adehye abusua mu.
english: The youth may have come from prison to the kingship, or he may have been born in poverty within his kingdom.

twi: Mihuu sɛ wɔn a wɔtenaa ase na wɔnantew owia yi ase nyinaa dii ɔbabun no akyi, nea odii ɔhene no ade no.
english: I saw that all who lived and walked under the sun followed the youth, the king’s successor.

twi: Nnipadɔm a wontumi nkan wɔn dii nʼakyi. Nanso nkyirimma no ani annye ne ho. Eyi nso yɛ ahuhude, ɛte sɛ wotaa mframa.
english: There was no end to all the people who were before them. But those who came later were not pleased with the successor. This too is meaningless, a chasing after the wind.

twi: Suro OnyankopɔnSɛ wokɔ Onyankopɔn fi a, hwɛ wʼanammɔntu yiye. Bɛn no na tie no sen sɛ wobɛbɔ nkwaseafo afɔre, wɔn a wonnim mfomso a wɔyɛ no.
english: Guard your steps when you go to the house of God. Go near to listen rather than to offer the sacrifice of fools, who do not know that they do wrong.

twi: Mpɛ ntɛm nkasa.Mpere wo ho wɔ wo koma musɛ wobɛka asɛm bi wɔ Onyankopɔn anim.Onyankopɔn te ɔsorona wo de, wowɔ asase so,enti ma wo nsɛm nyɛ kakraa bi.
english:
Do not be quick with your mouth,
    do not be hasty in your heart
    to utter anything before God.
God is in heaven
    and you are on earth,
    so let your words be few.

twi: Adaeso fi adwennwen bebree mu ba,na nsɛm dodow da adi wɔ ɔkwasea kasa mu.
english:
A dream comes when there are many cares,
    and many words mark the speech of a fool.

twi: Sɛ wohyɛ Onyankopɔn bɔ a, ntwentwɛn wo nan ase wɔ ho. Onni anigye wɔ nkwaseafo mu; enti di wo bɔhyɛ so.
english: When you make a vow to God, do not delay to fulfill it. He has no pleasure in fools; fulfill your vow.

twi: Sɛ woanhyɛ bɔ koraa a eye sen sɛ wobɛhyɛ bɔ na wunni so.
english: It is better not to make a vow than to make one and not fulfill it.

twi: Mma wʼano mfa wo nkɔ bɔne mu. Nyi wʼano nkyerɛ asɔredan mu somfo se, “Me bɔhyɛ no yɛ mfomso.” Adɛn nti na ɛsɛ sɛ Onyankopɔn bo fuw nea woka na ɔsɛe wo nsa ano adwuma?
english: Do not let your mouth lead you into sin. And do not protest to the temple messenger, “My vow was a mistake.” Why should God be angry at what you say and destroy the work of your hands?

twi: Adaeso ne nsɛnkeka bebree nka hwee. Enti suro Onyankopɔn.
english: Much dreaming and many words are meaningless. Therefore fear God.

twi: Ahonya Yɛ AhuhudeSɛ wuhu ohiani a wɔhyɛ ne so wɔ ɔmansin bi mu, na atɛntrenee ne ahofadi abɔ no a, mma eyinom nyɛ wo nwonwa, efisɛ nea ɔso sen no hwɛ no so, na nea ɔso sen wɔn baanu no nso hwɛ wɔn so.
english: If you see the poor oppressed in a district, and justice and rights denied, do not be surprised at such things; for one official is eyed by a higher one, and over them both are others higher still.

twi: Wɔn nyinaa fa asase no so siade; na ɔhene no ankasa nya mfuw no so mfaso.
english: The increase from the land is taken by all; the king himself profits from the fields.

twi: Nea nʼani bere sika no nnya nea ɛdɔɔso da;na nea ɔpɛ ahonyade dodow no ani nsɔ nea onya.Eyi nso yɛ ahuhude.
Adetɔnnne bu so a,saa ara na atɔfo no nso dɔɔso.Na mfaso bɛn na nea ɛwɔ no no nyasen sɛ ɔde nʼani bɛhwɛ?
english:
As goods increase,
    so do those who consume them.
And what benefit are they to the owners
    except to feast their eyes on them?

twi: Ɔpaani da ma nʼani kum,sɛ wadidi amee, anaasɛ wammee,nanso ɔdefo ahonya dodow ntiontumi nna.
english:
The sleep of a laborer is sweet,
    whether they eat little or much,
but as for the rich, their abundance
    permits them no sleep.

twi: Mahu bɔne kɛse wɔ owia yi ase:wɔde ahode sie de haw ne wuranom,
english:
I have seen a grievous evil under the sun:
wealth hoarded to the harm of its owners,

twi: anaasɛ ahode fa atoyerɛnkyɛm bi so hweresɛ ɛbɛyɛ na wonya mma awɔremmɛto hwee mfa.
english:
or wealth lost through some misfortune,
so that when they have children
    there is nothing left for them to inherit.

twi: Adagyaw na onipa de fi ne na yafunu mu bae,na sɛnea ɔbae no, saa ara na ɔbɛkɔ.Ɔremfa nʼadwumayɛ so mfaso biara aobetumi akita wɔ ne nsa mu no nkɔ.
english:
Everyone comes naked from their mother’s womb,
    and as everyone comes, so they depart.
They take nothing from their toil
    that they can carry in their hands.

twi: Eyi nso yɛ ɔhaw kɛse:Sɛnea onipa ba no, saa ara na ɔkɔ,na mfaso bɛn na onyawɔ bere a ɔyɛ adwuma ma mframa?
english:
This too is a grievous evil:
As everyone comes, so they depart,
    and what do they gain,
    since they toil for the wind?

twi: Ne nna nyinaa mu no, odidi a nʼanom nyɛ no dɛ,efisɛ abawpa, ateetee ne abufuw wɔ no so.
english:
All their days they eat in darkness,
    with great frustration, affliction and anger.

twi: Afei mihuu sɛ eye ma onipa sɛ obedidi na wanom na wama nʼani agye nʼadwumaden ho wɔ owia yi ase, wɔ mmere kakra a Onyankopɔn de ama no yi mu, efisɛ eyi ne ne kyɛfa.
english: This is what I have observed to be good: that it is appropriate for a person to eat, to drink and to find satisfaction in their toilsome labor under the sun during the few days of life God has given them—for this is their lot.

twi: Nea ɛka ho ne sɛ, sɛ Onyankopɔn ma onipa bi ahonyade ne adenya, na onya ahotɔ, de anigye yɛ nʼadwuma, na ohu sɛ ne kyɛfa ne no a, ɔnkae sɛ ɛyɛ Onyankopɔn akyɛde.
english: Moreover, when God gives someone wealth and possessions, and the ability to enjoy them, to accept their lot and be happy in their toil—this is a gift of God.

twi: Ɔntaa ntena ase nnwen ne nkwanna ho, efisɛ Onyankopɔn de koma mu anigye ama no.
english: They seldom reflect on the days of their life, because God keeps them occupied with gladness of heart.

twi: Mahu bɔne foforo bi wɔ owia yi ase a ɛhyɛ nnipa so yiye:
english: I have seen another evil under the sun, and it weighs heavily on mankind:

twi: Onyankopɔn ma onipa ahonyade, adenya ne anuonyam sɛnea biribiara a ne koma pɛ no ɛremmɔ no, nanso Onyankopɔn amma no kwan sɛ ɔmfa nnye nʼani, na ɔhɔho mmom na ɔde gye nʼani. Eyi yɛ ahuhude, ɔhaw a ɛyɛ yaw.
english: God gives some people wealth, possessions and honor, so that they lack nothing their hearts desire, but God does not grant them the ability to enjoy them, and strangers enjoy them instead. This is meaningless, a grievous evil.

twi: Onipa betumi anya mma ɔha na wanyin akyɛ; nanso ne mfe dodow yi akyi no, nʼahonya no amma nʼani annye na ne sie nso anyɛ fɛ a, ɔpɔn ba so wɔ mfaso sen no.
english: A man may have a hundred children and live many years; yet no matter how long he lives, if he cannot enjoy his prosperity and does not receive proper burial, I say that a stillborn child is better off than he.

twi: Ne ba no yɛ ade hunu, sum mu na ɔkɔ, na sum akata ne din so.
english: It comes without meaning, it departs in darkness, and in darkness its name is shrouded.

twi: Ɛwɔ mu sɛ wanhu owia na onnim hwee de, nanso obenya ahomegye bebree sen nea saa ɔbarima no benya,
english: Though it never saw the sun or knew anything, it has more rest than does that man—

twi: mpo sɛ ɔtena ase mfe apem mmɔho na wamfa nʼahonyade annye nʼani a, wɔn nyinaa nkɔ faako ana?
english: even if he lives a thousand years twice over but fails to enjoy his prosperity. Do not all go to the same place?

twi: Onipa brɛ nyinaa yɛ nʼano ntia,nanso nʼakɔnnɔde mmee no da.
english:
Everyone’s toil is for their mouth,
    yet their appetite is never satisfied.

twi: Na dɛn na onyansafo wɔ de sen ɔkwasea?Sɛ ohiani yɛ nʼakwan yiye wɔ afoforo anim amfaso bɛn na obenya?
english:
What advantage have the wise over fools?
What do the poor gain
    by knowing how to conduct themselves before others?

twi: Nea aniwa hu noye sen nea akɔnnɔ kyin hwehwɛ.Eyi nso yɛ ahuhude,ɛte sɛ wotaa mframa.
english:
Better what the eye sees
    than the roving of the appetite.
This too is meaningless,
    a chasing after the wind.

twi: Nea ɛwɔ hɔ biara, wɔato din dedaw,na sɛnea onipa te nso, wonim dedaw;onipa biara rentumi ne nea ɔwɔ ahoɔdensen no nnye eyi ho akyinnye.
english:
Whatever exists has already been named,
    and what humanity is has been known;
no one can contend
    with someone who is stronger.

twi: Nsɛm dɔɔso a,mu ntease sua,na so wɔ mfaso ma onipa ana?
english:
The more the words,
    the less the meaning,
    and how does that profit anyone?

twi: Na hena na onim nea eye ma onipa wɔ ne nkwanna kakraa bi a ɛyɛ ahuhude na ɔfa mu kɔ sɛ sunsuma no mu? Hena na obetumi aka nea ebesi wɔ owia yi ase akyerɛ no bere a ɔkɔ no?
english: For who knows what is good for a person in life, during the few and meaningless days they pass through like a shadow? Who can tell them what will happen under the sun after they are gone?

twi: NimdeɛDin pa yɛ sen aduhuam papa,na owuda yɛ sen awoda.
english:
A good name is better than fine perfume,
    and the day of death better than the day of birth.

twi: Eye sɛ obi bɛkɔ ayi asesen sɛ ɔbɛkɔ aponto ase,efisɛ owu yɛ onipa biara nkrabeana ɛsɛ sɛ ateasefo hyɛ eyi nsow.
english:
It is better to go to a house of mourning
    than to go to a house of feasting,
for death is the destiny of everyone;
    the living should take this to heart.

twi: Awerɛhow ye sen ɔserew,efisɛ anim a ayɛ mmɔbɔmmɔbɔ de koma mu nsiesie pa ba.
english:
Frustration is better than laughter,
    because a sad face is good for the heart.

twi: Onyansafo koma wɔ ayi ase,nanso nkwaseafo koma wɔ ahosɛpɛwfo fi.
english:
The heart of the wise is in the house of mourning,
    but the heart of fools is in the house of pleasure.

twi: Eye sɛ wobetie onyansafo animkasen sɛ wobetie nkwaseafo dwom.
english:
It is better to heed the rebuke of a wise person
    than to listen to the song of fools.

twi: Sɛnea nsɔe turuturuw wɔ ɔsɛn ase nosaa ara na nkwaseafo serew te.Eyi nso yɛ ahuhude.
english:
Like the crackling of thorns under the pot,
    so is the laughter of fools.
    This too is meaningless.

twi: Asisi ma onyansafo dan ɔkwasea,na kɛtɛasehyɛ sɛe koma.
english:
Extortion turns a wise person into a fool,
    and a bribe corrupts the heart.

twi: Asɛm awiei ye sen ne mfiase,na ntoboase ye sen ahantan.
english:
The end of a matter is better than its beginning,
    and patience is better than pride.

twi: Mma wo koma nsɔre ntɛmntɛm,na abufuw da nkwaseafo srɛ so.
english:
Do not be quickly provoked in your spirit,
    for anger resides in the lap of fools.

twi: Nka se, “Adɛn nti na tete nna no ye sen nnɛ mmere yi?”Onyansafo mmisa nsɛm sɛɛ.
english:
Do not say, “Why were the old days better than these?”
    For it is not wise to ask such questions.

twi: Nimdeɛ, ɛyɛ ade pa sɛ agyapade ara pɛ,so wɔ mfaso ma wɔn a wohu owia.
english:
Wisdom, like an inheritance, is a good thing
    and benefits those who see the sun.

twi: Sɛnea nimdeɛ yɛ bammɔ no,saa ara na sika nso te;nanso nhumu ho ade a eye ne sɛ:nea ɔwɔ nimdeɛ no bɔ ne nkwa ho ban.
english:
Wisdom is a shelter
    as money is a shelter,
but the advantage of knowledge is this:
    Wisdom preserves those who have it.

twi: Dwene nea Onyankopɔn ayɛ ho:Hena na obetumi ateɛnea wɔama akyea?
english:
Consider what God has done:
Who can straighten
    what he has made crooked?

twi: Mmere pa mu, ma wʼani nnye;nanso mmere bɔne mu, hu sɛOnyankopɔn na wayɛ ne nyinaa.Ɛno nti onipa rentumi nhunea ɛbɛto no daakye.
english:
When times are good, be happy;
    but when times are bad, consider this:
God has made the one
    as well as the other.
Therefore, no one can discover
    anything about their future.

twi: Me nkwanna a ɛyɛ ahuhude yi mu, mahu nneɛma abien:Ɔtreneeni a owu wɔ ne trenee mu,ne omumɔyɛfo a ɔtena ase kyɛ wɔ nʼamumɔyɛ mu.
english:
