twi: “Monnhyɛ ɔnanani so; mo ankasa munim sɛnea ɔnananiyɛ te, efisɛ na moyɛ ananafo wɔ Misraim.
english: “Do not oppress a foreigner; you yourselves know how it feels to be foreigners, because you were foreigners in Egypt.

twi: Homeda Ho Mmara“Munnua na muntwa no nnɔbae ntoatoa so saa ara nkosi mfe asia,
english: “For six years you are to sow your fields and harvest the crops,

twi: nanso afe a ɛto so ason so de, momma asase no nna hɔ kwa mma ahiafo ntwa nnɔbae biara a ebenyin wɔ so no; nkae no, munnyaw mma mmoa nwe. Saa ara na monyɛ mo bobeturo ne wo ngonnua turo nso.
english: but during the seventh year let the land lie unplowed and unused. Then the poor among your people may get food from it, and the wild animals may eat what is left. Do the same with your vineyard and your olive grove.

twi: “Nnansia na momfa nyɛ adwuma na monhome ne nnanson so. Eyi bɛma mo anantwi, mo mfurum, mo fifo, mo asomfo ne mo ahɔho nso ahome.
english: “Six days do your work, but on the seventh day do not work, so that your ox and your donkey may rest, and so that the slave born in your household and the foreigner living among you may be refreshed.

twi: “Munni asɛm biara a maka no so. Monnkankye mmɔ onyame foforo biara din; momma wɔnnte bi mmfi mo ano.”
english: “Be careful to do everything I have said to you. Do not invoke the names of other gods; do not let them be heard on your lips.

twi: Afe Mu Afahyɛ Abiɛsa No Ho Mmara“Afe biara mu, monhyɛ fa mprɛnsa mfa nhyɛ me anuonyam.
english: “Three times a year you are to celebrate a festival to me.

twi: “Nea edi kan no, munni Apiti Afahyɛ no. Sɛ edu so a, munnni brodo a mmɔkaw wɔ mu nnanson, sɛnea mehyɛɛ mo no. Ɛsɛ sɛ afe biara mohyɛ saa fa yi wɔ ɔsram Abib mu, ɔsram a mode tu fii Misraim no mu.“Edu saa bere no a, obiara mmrɛ me afɔrebɔde.
english:
“Celebrate the Festival of Unleavened Bread; for seven days eat bread made without yeast, as I commanded you. Do this at the appointed time in the month of Aviv, for in that month you came out of Egypt.
“No one is to appear before me empty-handed.

twi: “Ɛno akyi no, Otwabere Afahyɛ na edi so. Saa afahyɛ yi du so a, momfa mo aduankan mmrɛ me.“Nea etwa to yɛ nnɔbae anoboa afahyɛ a ɛsɛ sɛ wodi no otwa bere no akyi.
english:
“Celebrate the Festival of Harvest with the firstfruits of the crops you sow in your field.
“Celebrate the Festival of Ingathering at the end of the year, when you gather in your crops from the field.

twi: “Afahyɛ ahorow abiɛsa yi mu nyinaa, ɛsɛ sɛ Israel mmarima nyinaa ba Awurade Nyankopɔn anim.
english: “Three times a year all the men are to appear before the Sovereign Lord.

twi: “Mommfa biribiara a mmɔkaw wɔ mu mmɔ mogya afɔre mma me.“Saa ara na ɛnsɛ sɛ mʼafahyɛ afɔrebɔde mu srade no tena hɔ ma ade kye so.
english:
“Do not offer the blood of a sacrifice to me along with anything containing yeast.
“The fat of my festival offerings must not be kept until morning.

twi: “Sɛ mutwa mo nnɔbae a, Momfa mo nnɔbae mu nea ɛsɔ ani koraa no mmra Awurade mo Nyankopɔn fi.“Monnoa abirekyi ba wɔ ne na nufusu mu.
english:
“Bring the best of the firstfruits of your soil to the house of the Lord your God.
“Do not cook a young goat in its mother’s milk.

twi: Onyankopɔn Bammɔ Ho Bɔhyɛ“Meresoma ɔbɔfo na wadi mo anim de mo akɔ asase a masiesie ama mo no so dwoodwoo.
english: “See, I am sending an angel ahead of you to guard you along the way and to bring you to the place I have prepared.

twi: Momfa nidi mma no na munni ne nsɛm so; monnsɔre ntia no, efisɛ ɔremfa mo amumɔyɛ nkyɛ mo. Ɔyɛ me nsiananmu, na me din na ɛda ne so.
english: Pay attention to him and listen to what he says. Do not rebel against him; he will not forgive your rebellion, since my Name is in him.

twi: Na sɛ motɔ mo bo ase, na mutie no, di me nsɛm nyinaa so a, mɛyɛ ɔtamfo atia mo atamfo.
english: If you listen carefully to what he says and do all that I say, I will be an enemy to your enemies and will oppose those who oppose you.

twi: Me bɔfo bedi mo anim de mo aba Amorifo, Hetifo, Perisifo, Kanaanfo, Hewifo ne Yebusifo asase so na moatena hɔ. Na mɛsɛe saa nnipa no nyinaa wɔ mo anim.
english: My angel will go ahead of you and bring you into the land of the Amorites, Hittites, Perizzites, Canaanites, Hivites and Jebusites, and I will wipe them out.

twi: Monnsom anyame a saa aman yi som wɔn no bi, na mommmɔ afɔre mma wɔn da biara da. Munnni saa abosonsomfo yi akyi. Munni wɔn so na mummubu wɔn ahoni a ɛyɛ animguasede no ngu.
english: Do not bow down before their gods or worship them or follow their practices. You must demolish them and break their sacred stones to pieces.

twi: Mo Awurade, mo Nyankopɔn nko ara na monsom no. Na mehyira mo ama moanya aduan ne nsu na meyi nyarewa nyinaa afi mo so.
english: Worship the Lord your God, and his blessing will be on your food and water. I will take away sickness from among you,

twi: Ɔpɔn anaa abonin remma mo asase no so na mɛma mo nna amee mo.
english: and none will miscarry or be barren in your land. I will give you a full life span.

twi: “Awurade ho hu bɛka aman a mubedi wɔn so no so nnipa nyinaa na wɔaguan wɔ mo anim.
english: “I will send my terror ahead of you and throw into confusion every nation you encounter. I will make all your enemies turn their backs and run.

twi: Mɛma kotokurodu abɛpam Hewifo, Kanaanfo ne Hetifo afi mo anim.
english: I will send the hornet ahead of you to drive the Hivites, Canaanites and Hittites out of your way.

twi: Merenyɛ eyinom nyinaa afe baako pɛ mu na asase no annan sare amma nkekaboa ammu amfa mo so.
english: But I will not drive them out in a single year, because the land would become desolate and the wild animals too numerous for you.

twi: Mɛpam wɔn nkakrankakra kosi sɛ mobɛdɔɔso, atumi ahyɛ asase no so ma.
english: Little by little I will drive them out before you, until you have increased enough to take possession of the land.

twi: “Mɛto mo ahye afi Po Kɔkɔɔ no ano akosi Filistifo mpoano, na mede afi sare a ɛwɔ anafo fam no so akosi Asu Eufrate, na mɛma mo adi nnipa a wɔte asase no so no so, na moapam wɔn afi mo anim.
english: “I will establish your borders from the Red Sea to the Mediterranean Sea, and from the desert to the Euphrates River. I will give into your hands the people who live in the land, and you will drive them out before you.

twi: Mo ne wɔn nnyɛ apam biara, na saa ara nso na mo ne wɔn anyame no nnyɛ biribiara.
english: Do not make a covenant with them or with their gods.

twi: Mommma wɔmmɛtena mo mu, anyɛ saa a wɔbɛma mo ayɛ bɔne atia me; esiane sɛ ɛnyɛ dɛn ara a, wɔn abosonsom no som bɛyɛ afiri a ebeyi mo.”
english: Do not let them live in your land or they will cause you to sin against me, because the worship of their gods will certainly be a snare to you.”

twi: Israelfo Gye Apam No To MuAfei, Awurade ka kyerɛɛ Mose se, “Wo ne Aaron, Nadab, Abihu ne Israelfo mpanyimfo aduɔson mforo mmra ha. Mo nyinaa, momma me ne mo ntam ntwe na monsom me.
english: Then the Lord said to Moses, “Come up to the Lord, you and Aaron, Nadab and Abihu, and seventy of the elders of Israel. You are to worship at a distance,

twi: Mose nko ara na ɔbɛbɛn Awurade; na monkae nso sɛ, ɛnsɛ sɛ wɔn a wɔaka no twiw bɛn bepɔw no koraa.”
english: but Moses alone is to approach the Lord; the others must not come near. And the people may not come up with him.”

twi: Mose kaa mmara a Awurade hyɛɛ no no nyinaa kyerɛɛ nnipa no ma wɔn nyinaa bɔ gyee so se, “Yebedi ne nyinaa so.”
english: When Moses went and told the people all the Lord’s words and laws, they responded with one voice, “Everything the Lord has said we will do.”

twi: Mose kyerɛw Awurade mmara no nyinaa guu hɔ.Ade kyee anɔpa no, osii afɔremuka wɔ bepɔw no ase. Ɔde adum dumien twaa ho hyiae, efisɛ na Israel mmusuakuw no yɛ dumien.
english:
Moses then wrote down everything the Lord had said.
He got up early the next morning and built an altar at the foot of the mountain and set up twelve stone pillars representing the twelve tribes of Israel.

twi: Afei, ɔsomaa mmabun a wɔwɔ wɔn mu no bi sɛ wɔnkɔbɔ ɔhyew afɔre ne asomdwoe afɔre mma Awurade.
english: Then he sent young Israelite men, and they offered burnt offerings and sacrificed young bulls as fellowship offerings to the Lord.

twi: Mose sɔn mmoa no mogya no fa de guu nkankyee mu, na ɔtow fa a aka no petee afɔremuka no so.
english: Moses took half of the blood and put it in bowls, and the other half he splashed against the altar.

twi: Ɔkenkan nhoma a wakyerɛw a ɛyɛ Apam Nhoma a Awurade akwankyerɛ ne ne mmara wɔ mu no kyerɛɛ nnipa no. Nnipa no bɔ gyee so bio se, “Yɛhyɛ bɔ sɛ, yebedi mmara no nyinaa so.”
english: Then he took the Book of the Covenant and read it to the people. They responded, “We will do everything the Lord has said; we will obey.”

twi: Afei, Mose de mogya a ɛwɔ nkankye no mu no petee nnipa no so kae se, “Saa mogya yi hyɛ apam a mo ne Awurade ayɛ ne mmara a ɔde ama mo no mu den.”
english: Moses then took the blood, sprinkled it on the people and said, “This is the blood of the covenant that the Lord has made with you in accordance with all these words.”

twi: Mose, Aaron, Nadab, Abihu ne Israelfo mpanyimfo aduɔson no foro kɔɔ bepɔw no so
english: Moses and Aaron, Nadab and Abihu, and the seventy elders of Israel went up

twi: na wohuu Israel Nyankopɔn. Na nʼanan ntiaso hyerɛn te sɛ hoabo a ne hyerɛn te sɛ wim ahosu.
english: and saw the God of Israel. Under his feet was something like a pavement made of lapis lazuli, as bright blue as the sky.

twi: Ɛwɔ mu sɛ mpanyimfo no huu Onyankopɔn de, nanso wansɛe wɔn. Nokwarem, wɔn nyinaa bɔɔ mu didii wɔ Awurade anim.
english: But God did not raise his hand against these leaders of the Israelites; they saw God, and they ate and drank.

twi: Na Awurade ka kyerɛɛ Mose se, “Foro bra me nkyɛn wɔ bepɔw so ha na tena ha, na mede mmaransɛm a makyerɛw agu ɔbo so no bɛma wo, na woafa so akyerɛkyerɛ nnipa no.”
english: The Lord said to Moses, “Come up to me on the mountain and stay here, and I will give you the tablets of stone with the law and commandments I have written for their instruction.”

twi: Enti Mose ne ne boafo Yosua foro kɔɔ Onyankopɔn bepɔw no so.
english: Then Moses set out with Joshua his aide, and Moses went up on the mountain of God.

twi: Ɔka kyerɛɛ mpanyimfo no se, “Montena ha ntwɛn yɛn kosi sɛ yɛbɛba. Sɛ asɛm bi kyere obi so a, obetumi akɔ Aaron ne Hur nkyɛn.”
english: He said to the elders, “Wait here for us until we come back to you. Aaron and Hur are with you, and anyone involved in a dispute can go to them.”

twi: Mose foro kɔɔ bepɔw no so hɔ na ɔyeraa wɔ omununkum mu.
english: When Moses went up on the mountain, the cloud covered it,

twi: Na Awurade anuonyam hyɛɛ Sinai bepɔw no so ma. Na omununkum sii bepɔw no so nnansia. Ne nnanson so no, ɔfrɛɛ Mose fii omununkum no mu.
english: and the glory of the Lord settled on Mount Sinai. For six days the cloud covered the mountain, and on the seventh day the Lord called to Moses from within the cloud.

twi: Wɔn a wɔwɔ bepɔw no ase no huu anwonwade no. Na Awurade anuonyam a ɛwɔ bepɔw no so no te sɛ ogya a ɛredɛw.
english: To the Israelites the glory of the Lord looked like a consuming fire on top of the mountain.

twi: Na Mose yeraa wɔ bepɔw no so mununkum no mu. Odii bepɔw no so adaduanan.
english: Then Moses entered the cloud as he went on up the mountain. And he stayed on the mountain forty days and forty nights.

twi: Hyiadan AfɔrebɔAwurade ka kyerɛɛ Mose se,
english: The Lord said to Moses,

twi: “Ka kyerɛ Israelfo no se, wɔmmɔ afɔre mma me.
english: “Tell the Israelites to bring me an offering. You are to receive the offering for me from everyone whose heart prompts them to give.

twi: “Saa nneɛma a edidi so yi mu na womfi mmɔ me afɔre no:“sikakɔkɔɔ, dwetɛ, kɔbere,
english: These are the offerings you are to receive from them: gold, silver and bronze;

twi: ntama tuntum, koogyan bibiri tam; koogyan tam, sirikyi,abirekyi ho nwi,
english: blue, purple and scarlet yarn and fine linen; goat hair;

twi: odwennini nhoma a wɔahyɛ no kɔkɔɔ, mmirekyi nhoma,ɔkanto dua,
english: ram skins dyed red and another type of durable leather; acacia wood;

twi: kanea ngo,ɔsra ngo, nnuhuam a wɔhyewee,
english: olive oil for the light; spices for the anointing oil and for the fragrant incense;

twi: abo a nʼahosu te sɛ apopobibiri, abo a wɔde betuatua asɔfotade ne nkatabo mu.
english: and onyx stones and other gems to be mounted on the ephod and breastpiece.

twi: “Afei monyɛ kronkronbea mma me, na mɛtena wɔn mu.
english: “Then have them make a sanctuary for me, and I will dwell among them.

twi: Monyɛ ntamadan yi ne ne nsiesiemu nyinaa sɛnea mɛkyerɛ mo no pɛpɛɛpɛ.
english: Make this tabernacle and all its furnishings exactly like the pattern I will show you.

twi: Apam Adaka No Yɛbea“Momfa ɔkanto dua nyɛ Apam Adaka a ne ntwemu yɛ anammɔn abiɛsa ne fa, ne trɛw nyɛ anammɔn abien ne fa na ne sorokɔ nso nyɛ anammɔn abien ne fa.
english: “Have them make an ark of acacia wood—two and a half cubits long, a cubit and a half wide, and a cubit and a half high.

twi: Na momfa sikakɔkɔɔ ankasa nnura ho ne mu nyinaa.
english: Overlay it with pure gold, both inside and out, and make a gold molding around it.

twi: Momfa sikakɔkɔɔ nkaa anan nhyehyɛ adaka no anan anan no ho, wɔ fam pɛɛ. Ma nkaa no abien nkɔ ɔfa baako na abien a aka no nso nkɔ fa.
english: Cast four gold rings for it and fasten them to its four feet, with two rings on one side and two rings on the other.

twi: Fa ɔkanto sen mmaa, na fa sikakɔkɔɔ duradura ho.
english: Then make poles of acacia wood and overlay them with gold.

twi: Fa mmaa no hyehyɛ nkaa no mu na wɔde asoa apam adaka no.
english: Insert the poles into the rings on the sides of the ark to carry it.

twi: Munnyiyi nnua a wɔde soa adaka no mfi nkaa no mu. Momma ɛnhyehyɛ mu afebɔɔ.
english: The poles are to remain in the rings of this ark; they are not to be removed.

twi: Muwie adaka no a, momfa ɔbo a makyerɛw Mmaransɛm Du no agu so no nto mu.
english: Then put in the ark the tablets of the covenant law, which I will give you.

twi: “Momfa sikakɔkɔɔ nyɛ adaka no ti a ne ntwemu yɛ basafa abien ne fa na ne trɛw nso yɛ anammɔn abien ne kakra. Ɛha ne baabi a mubenya mo bɔne so ahummɔbɔ afi.
english: “Make an atonement cover of pure gold—two and a half cubits long and a cubit and a half wide.

twi: Momfa sikakɔkɔɔ a wɔaboro nyɛ kerubim abien. Momfa ɔbaako nsi adaka no nkataso atifi na momfa ɔbaako nsi anafo.
english: And make two cherubim out of hammered gold at the ends of the cover.

twi: Fa kerubim no tetare adaka no ti ne nʼanafo na ɛne adaka no nkataso no nyɛ mua.
english: Make one cherub on one end and the second cherub on the other; make the cherubim of one piece with the cover, at the two ends.

twi: Kerubim a wɔyɛ abɔfo no bedi nhwɛanim a wɔasisi wɔn ti ase rehwɛ mpata agua no na wɔatrɛtrɛw wɔn ntaban mu akata so.
english: The cherubim are to have their wings spread upward, overshadowing the cover with them. The cherubim are to face each other, looking toward the cover.

twi: Momfa ɔbo kyerɛwpon a mede bɛma mo no nto adaka no mu, na momfa ne ti no nkata so.
english: Place the cover on top of the ark and put in the ark the tablets of the covenant law that I will give you.

twi: Na mehyia mo wɔ hɔ na makasa afi mpata agua wɔ soro hɔ afa abɔfo no ntam. Na adaka no mu na wɔbɛkora mʼapam no ho mmara. Ɛhɔ na mɛda me mmaransɛm a mode bɛma Israelfo no adi akyerɛ mo.
english: There, above the cover between the two cherubim that are over the ark of the covenant law, I will meet with you and give you all my commands for the Israelites.

twi: Ɔpon No Yɛbea“Momfa ɔkanto dua nyɛ ɔpon a ne ntwemu mu yɛ anammɔn abiɛsa, ne trɛw yɛ ɔnammɔn baako ne fa na ne sorokɔ yɛ anammɔn abien ne fa.
english: “Make a table of acacia wood—two cubits long, a cubit wide and a cubit and a half high.

twi: Momfa sikakɔkɔɔ nnura ho na momfa sikakɔkɔɔ hankare ntwa ho nhyia.
english: Overlay it with pure gold and make a gold molding around it.

twi: Yɛ adaka no ho ntetareho a ne trɛw yɛ nsateaa anan twa ɔpon no ano ho hyia, na fa sikakɔkɔɔ hankare fa ho.
english: Also make around it a rim a handbreadth wide and put a gold molding on the rim.

twi: Yɛ sikakɔkɔɔ nkaa anan na fa nkaa anan no tuatua nʼanan anan no biara akyi
english: Make four gold rings for the table and fasten them to the four corners, where the four legs are.

twi: twɔtwɔw so wɔ soro. Wɔde nnua no bɛhyehyɛ saa nkaa a wɔde bɛma ɔpon no so asoa no mu.
english: The rings are to be close to the rim to hold the poles used in carrying the table.

twi: Fa ɔkanto yɛ nnua no, na fa sikakɔkɔɔ dura ho.
english: Make the poles of acacia wood, overlay them with gold and carry the table with them.

twi: Momfa sikakɔkɔɔ nyɛ nsanka, mprɛte, ntere, nhina ne nsatoa.
english: And make its plates and dishes of pure gold, as well as its pitchers and bowls for the pouring out of offerings.

twi: Da biara, fa brodo to ɔpon no so wɔ mʼanim.
english: Put the bread of the Presence on this table to be before me at all times.

twi: Kaneadua Yɛbea“Momfa sikakɔkɔɔ a wɔaboro nyɛ kaneadua. Kaneadua no ase, nʼabaa, akanea no nhwiren ne ɛho asiesie no nyinaa nyɛ ade baako.
english: “Make a lampstand of pure gold. Hammer out its base and shaft, and make its flowerlike cups, buds and blossoms of one piece with them.

twi: Kaneadua a ɛhyɛ mfimfini no benya nkorata asia a abiɛsa wɔ fa na abiɛsa nso wɔ fa.
english: Six branches are to extend from the sides of the lampstand—three on one side and three on the other.

twi: Momfa nhwiren abiɛsa nsiesie nkorata biara ho.
english: Three cups shaped like almond flowers with buds and blossoms are to be on one branch, three on the next branch, and the same for all six branches extending from the lampstand.

twi: Na kaneadua no, momfa nhwiren a ɛyɛ fɛ nni adwinni mfa nsiesie no.
english: And on the lampstand there are to be four cups shaped like almond flowers with buds and blossoms.

twi: Nhwiren no bi bɛwɔ ne dua no ase wɔ nkorata abien biara ase. Afei, nhwiren no bi bɛwɔ nkorata abien a ɛwɔ ase no ase, na bi nso bɛwɔ nkorata abien a ɛwɔ soro no so.
english: One bud shall be under the first pair of branches extending from the lampstand, a second bud under the second pair, and a third bud under the third pair—six branches in all.

twi: Saa nneɛma a wɔde siesie kaneadua no ne ne nkorabata no nyinaa nyɛ ade baako a wɔde sikakɔkɔɔ ankasa a wɔaboro ayɛ.
english: The buds and branches shall all be of one piece with the lampstand, hammered out of pure gold.

twi: “Monyɛ akanea dua ntuatuaho ason wɔ kaneadua no ho wɔ ɔkwan bi so a ne hyerɛn no bɛtow hann agu nʼanim.
english: “Then make its seven lamps and set them up on it so that they light the space in front of it.

twi: Kanea ntamabamma adabaw no ne ne mpampaa no nso, momfa sikakɔkɔɔ ankasa nyɛ.
english: Its wick trimmers and trays are to be of pure gold.

twi: Sikakɔkɔɔ kilogram aduasa anan na ɛho behia sɛ mode bɛyɛ kaneadua no ne ɛho nneɛma nyinaa.
english: A talent of pure gold is to be used for the lampstand and all these accessories.

twi: Biribiara a mobɛyɛ no nso, monyɛ no pɛpɛɛpɛ sɛnea makyerɛ mo wɔ bepɔw so ha yi no.
english: See that you make them according to the pattern shown you on the mountain.

twi: Ahyiae Ntamadan Ho Nhyehyɛe“Fa asaawa a ɛyɛ fɛ a woafura bamma du ne ntama a wɔahyɛ no aduru tuntum, ɔtam bibiri, koogyan a wɔanwen kerubim sɛso agu mu si Ahyiae Ntamadan no.
english: “Make the tabernacle with ten curtains of finely twisted linen and blue, purple and scarlet yarn, with cherubim woven into them by a skilled worker.

twi: Ɛsɛ sɛ nkataano du no nyinaa kɛse yɛ pɛ. Emu biara tenten yɛ anammɔn aduanan abien na ne trɛw nso yɛ anammɔn asia.
english: All the curtains are to be the same size—twenty-eight cubits long and four cubits wide.

twi: Mompam saa ntama no anum mmɔ mu mma ɛnyɛ baako. Anum a aka no nso, monyɛ no saa ara.
english: Join five of the curtains together, and do the same with the other five.

twi: Momfa ntama bibiri bamma aduonum nwurawura ntama no afa abien a ɛsensɛn hɔ no mu.
english: Make loops of blue material along the edge of the end curtain in one set, and do the same with the end curtain in the other set.

twi: Ɛsɛ sɛ mobɔ nkɔtɔkoro aduonum ma edi nhwɛanim wɔ ɔfa biara.
english: Make fifty loops on one curtain and fifty loops on the end curtain of the other set, with the loops opposite each other.

twi: Bɔ sikakɔkɔɔ nkɔtɔkoro aduonum na fa kyekyere nkɔtɔkoro no bɔ mu, sɛnea ɛbɛyɛ na Ahyiae Ntamadan hɔ no bɛyɛ ɔdan baako.
english: Then make fifty gold clasps and use them to fasten the curtains together so that the tabernacle is a unit.

twi: “Monwen mmirekyi nwi mfa nkuru Ahyiae Ntamadan no so. Ɛsɛ sɛ nkuruso no dodow yɛ dubaako.
english: “Make curtains of goat hair for the tent over the tabernacle—eleven altogether.

twi: Nkurusotam dubaako no nyinaa tenten ne ne trɛw nyɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ. Ne tenten nyɛ anammɔn aduanan anum na ne trɛw nyɛ anammɔn asia.
english: All eleven curtains are to be the same size—thirty cubits long and four cubits wide.

twi: Ka saa nkataso yi anum bɔ mu na ɛnyɛ ade tɛtrɛɛ baako; na fa asia a aka no bɔ mu na ɛno nso nyɛ ade tɛtrɛɛ baako. Wobebu nkuruso a ɛto so asia no ato so ama asensɛn fam sɛ ɔdan kronkron no nhiniano.
english: Join five of the curtains together into one set and the other six into another set. Fold the sixth curtain double at the front of the tent.

twi: Yɛ nkɔtɔkoro aduonum aduonum a wɔabobɔ hyehyɛ ntama asinasin akuw abien no biara ano.
english: Make fifty loops along the edge of the end curtain in one set and also along the edge of the end curtain in the other set.

twi: Na yɛ nsusomu aduonum na fa saa nsusomu no hyehyɛ nkɔtɔkoro no mu na ɛnka asɔredan no mmɔ mu na ɛnyɛ mua.
english: Then make fifty bronze clasps and put them in the loops to fasten the tent together as a unit.

twi: Ɔdan no nkurusotam anammɔn baako ne fa bɛsensɛn Ahyiae Ntamadan no akyi,
english: As for the additional length of the tent curtains, the half curtain that is left over is to hang down at the rear of the tabernacle.

twi: na anammɔn baako ne fa nso asensɛn anim.
english: The tent curtains will be a cubit longer on both sides; what is left will hang over the sides of the tabernacle so as to cover it.

twi: Momfa nneɛma ahorow abien mmɔ ɔdan no so. Nea edi kan no nyɛ odwennini were a wɔahyɛ no kɔkɔɔ, nea ɛto so abien nyɛ abirekyi were a ɛsɔ.
english: Make for the tent a covering of ram skins dyed red, and over that a covering of the other durable leather.

twi: “Fa ɔkanto yɛ ntaaboo na fa twa Ahyiae Ntamadan no ho.
english: “Make upright frames of acacia wood for the tabernacle.

twi: Mpuran biara sorokɔ nyɛ anammɔn dunum na ne trɛw nyɛ anammɔn abien ne kakra.
english: Each frame is to be ten cubits long and a cubit and a half wide,

twi: Ɛsɛ sɛ nkɔtɔkoro abien wɔ mpuran biara ase, na mpuran biara yɛ pɛ.
english: with two projections set parallel to each other. Make all the frames of the tabernacle in this way.

twi: Mobɛyɛ Ahyiae Ntamadan no ntaaboo ama emu aduonu akyerɛ nʼanafo.
english: Make twenty frames for the south side of the tabernacle

twi: Wɔde besisi dwetɛ nnyinaso aduanan so; nnyinaso no abien abien nhyehyɛ mpuran biara ase.
english: and make forty silver bases to go under them—two bases for each frame, one under each projection.

twi: Ahyiae Ntamadan no atifi fam nso, wɔbɛyɛ ntaaboo aduonu atwa ho.
english: For the other side, the north side of the tabernacle, make twenty frames

twi: Ɛno nso wɔde besisi dwetɛ nnyinaso aduanan so a mpuran baako besi nnyinaso abien so.
english: and forty silver bases—two under each frame.

twi: Ahyiae Ntamadan no fa a ɛkyerɛ atɔe fam no bɛyɛ nʼakyi. Ɛno nso wɔde ntaaboo asia na ebetwa ho
english: Make six frames for the far end, that is, the west end of the tabernacle,

twi: a ntaaboo abien sisi twea biara.
english: and make two frames for the corners at the far end.

twi: Wɔde nkɔtɔkoro besuso ntaaboo abien no soro ne ne fam.
english: At these two corners they must be double from the bottom all the way to the top and fitted into a single ring; both shall be like that.

twi: Wɔka ne nyinaa bɔ mu a, ntaaboo awotwe na wɔde bɛyɛ ɔdan no fa hɔ a wɔde besisi dwetɛ nsisiso dunsia so. Mpuran biara bɛfa nsisiso abien.
english: So there will be eight frames and sixteen silver bases—two under each frame.

twi: “Fa ɔkanto sen mmeamu nnua bi na fa bea ntaaboo no mu. Mmeamu nnua no anum nkɔ ntaaboo no fa baako
english: “Also make crossbars of acacia wood: five for the frames on one side of the tabernacle,

twi: na anum a aka no nso nkɔ ɔfa baako. Fa mmeamu nnua no anum bobɔ ntaaboo a ɛwɔ ntamadan no akyi, a ani kyerɛ atɔe fam no.
english: five for those on the other side, and five for the frames on the west, at the far end of the tabernacle.

twi: Ma mmeamu dua a ɛbea mfimfini no nkɔ ntaaboo no soro kakra mma emfi ti nkɔka ti.
english: The center crossbar is to extend from end to end at the middle of the frames.

twi: Fa sikakɔkɔɔ dura ntaaboo no ho na fa sikakɔkɔɔ nkaa suso mmeamu dua no mu na ennyina. Fa sikakɔkɔɔ dura mmeamu dua no nso ho.
english: Overlay the frames with gold and make gold rings to hold the crossbars. Also overlay the crossbars with gold.

twi: “Fa hyehyɛbea a mekyerɛɛ wo wɔ bepɔw no so hɔ no so pɛpɛɛpɛ si Ahyiae Ntamadan no.
english: “Set up the tabernacle according to the plan shown you on the mountain.

twi: “Fa ntama tuntum, koogyan bibiri, koogyan ne asaawatam a ɛyɛ fɛ yɛ ntwamtam a wɔanwen kerubim sɛso agu mu no.
english: “Make a curtain of blue, purple and scarlet yarn and finely twisted linen, with cherubim woven into it by a skilled worker.

twi: Fa sɛn ɔkanto nnua fadum anan a wɔde sikakɔkɔɔ adura ho a sikakɔkɔɔ nsusomu anan suso ano no so. Ma ɔfadum anan no mu biara nsi dwetɛ nnyinaso anan no baako so.
english: Hang it with gold hooks on four posts of acacia wood overlaid with gold and standing on four silver bases.

twi: Fa ntwamtam no sensɛn nsusomu no so na fa twa ɔdan no mu. Fa adaka a ɔbo a wɔakyerɛw Onyankopɔn mmara agu so no da mu no si ntama ntwamu no akyi. Ntama ntwamu no betwa kronkronbea hɔ ne kronkron mu kronkron no ntam.
english: Hang the curtain from the clasps and place the ark of the covenant law behind the curtain. The curtain will separate the Holy Place from the Most Holy Place.

twi: Afei, fa adaka no mmuaso a wɔde sikakɔkɔɔ ayɛ no bua so na fa si kronkron mu kronkron hɔ.
english: Put the atonement cover on the ark of the covenant law in the Most Holy Place.

twi: Fa ɔpon no ne kaneadua no twa dan no mu wɔ ntwamtam no akyi. Kaneadua no besi kronkronbea no anafo, na ɔpon no asi nʼatifi.
english: Place the table outside the curtain on the north side of the tabernacle and put the lampstand opposite it on the south side.

twi: “Fa ntama foforo a ɛyɛ ɔtam bibiri ne koogyan asaawatam yɛ Ahyiae Ntamadan no ano nkataanim.
english: “For the entrance to the tent make a curtain of blue, purple and scarlet yarn and finely twisted linen—the work of an embroiderer.

twi: Fa saa ntwamtam no sɛn ɔkanto mpuran anum a wɔde sikakɔkɔɔ adura ho no nsusomu no so. Wɔde saa mpuran no besisi ayowa ntaease anum no mu.
english: Make gold hooks for this curtain and five posts of acacia wood overlaid with gold. And cast five bronze bases for them.

twi: Ɔhyew Afɔrebɔ Afɔremuka Ho Nhyehyɛe“Fa ɔkanto yɛ afɔremuka ma enyi ahinanan a nʼafanan no mu biara yɛ anammɔn ason ne fa na ne sorokɔ nso yɛ anammɔn anan ne fa.
english: “Build an altar of acacia wood, three cubits high; it is to be square, five cubits long and five cubits wide.

twi: Yɛ mmɛn anan tuatua afɔremuka no ntwea anan no nyinaa so, na fa kɔbere dura ne nyinaa ho. Ɔkanto a wode bɛyɛ afɔremuka no, ɛno ara bi na wode bɛyɛ mmɛn no.
english: Make a horn at each of the four corners, so that the horns and the altar are of one piece, and overlay the altar with bronze.

twi: Bokiti a nsõ begu mu, sofi, hweaseammɔ, adinam ne nsramma nkankye nyinaa, kɔbere na fa yɛ.
english: Make all its utensils of bronze—its pots to remove the ashes, and its shovels, sprinkling bowls, meat forks and firepans.

twi: Fa kɔbere yɛ ntwitae na fa dade nkaa hyehyɛ ne ntwea anan no so.
english: Make a grating for it, a bronze network, and make a bronze ring at each of the four corners of the network.

twi: Fa ntwitae no hyɛ nsramma kuruwa no mu na fa si afɔremuka no basa a wɔayɛ no so.
english: Put it under the ledge of the altar so that it is halfway up the altar.

twi: Fa ɔkanto sen nnua a wɔde kɔbere adura ho a wɔde bɛsoa afɔremuka no.
english: Make poles of acacia wood for the altar and overlay them with bronze.

twi: Sɛ moresoa a, momfa nnua no nhyehyɛ nkaa a mode atuatua afɔremuka no ho no mu.
english: The poles are to be inserted into the rings so they will be on two sides of the altar when it is carried.

twi: Ntaaboo na momfa nyɛ afɔremuka no. Momma emu nna kwan sɛnea mede kyerɛɛ mo wɔ bepɔw no so no.
english: Make the altar hollow, out of boards. It is to be made just as you were shown on the mountain.

twi: “Twa adiwo ma Ahyiae Ntamadan no na fa ntama a wɔde asaawa a ɛyɛ fɛ ayɛ sensɛn ho. Nkataano a ɛsɛn anafo no tenten no nyɛ anammɔn ɔha aduonum
english: “Make a courtyard for the tabernacle. The south side shall be a hundred cubits long and is to have curtains of finely twisted linen,

twi: a kɔbere nnua aduonu a esisi kɔbere nnyinaso aduonu mu no suso mu. Dwetɛ nkɔtɔkoro ne dwetɛ ntwea a ɛtetare dwetɛ afadum no ho no na ebesuso nsɛnanim no mu.
english: with twenty posts and twenty bronze bases and with silver hooks and bands on the posts.

twi: Adiwo a ɛkyerɛ atifi fam no nso, saa ara na wɔnyɛ no. Nsɛnanim a ne tenten yɛ anammɔn ɔha aduonum, na nnua aduonu sisi kɔbere nnyinaso mu a dwetɛ nkɔtɔkoro ne ne ntwea tetare ho na ebegyina no.
english: The north side shall also be a hundred cubits long and is to have curtains, with twenty posts and twenty bronze bases and with silver hooks and bands on the posts.

twi: “Adiwo no fa a ɛkyerɛ atɔe fam no trɛw bɛyɛ anammɔn aduɔson anum a ekura nnua du a ntokuru du deda mu.
english: “The west end of the courtyard shall be fifty cubits wide and have curtains, with ten posts and ten bases.

twi: Apuei fam nso bɛyɛ anammɔn aduɔson anum saa ara.
english: On the east end, toward the sunrise, the courtyard shall also be fifty cubits wide.

twi: Baabi a ne kwan da nʼapuei fam no, wɔmfa nsɛnanotam a ne tenten yɛ anammɔn aduonu abien ne fa a nnua abiɛsa a esisi ntokuru abiɛsa mu suso mu no nsɛn ano.
english: Curtains fifteen cubits long are to be on one side of the entrance, with three posts and three bases,

twi: Baabi a ne kwan da wɔ nʼatɔe fam no nso, wɔmfa nsɛnanotam a ne tenten yɛ anammɔn aduonu abien ne fa nsɛn ano. Nnua abiɛsa a esisi ntokuru abiɛsa mu na ebesuso nsɛnanotam no mu.
english: and curtains fifteen cubits long are to be on the other side, with three posts and three bases.

twi: “Adiwo hɔ no ano kwan nyɛ ntama nsɛnanim a ne trɛw yɛ anammɔn aduasa. Wɔde asaawa tuntum, bibiri ne koogyan bedi mu adwinni fɛfɛɛfɛ. Wɔde nnua anan a esisi ne nnyinaso mu no nso besuso nsɛnanotam no mu.
english: “For the entrance to the courtyard, provide a curtain twenty cubits long, of blue, purple and scarlet yarn and finely twisted linen—the work of an embroiderer—with four posts and four bases.

twi: Ɛsɛ sɛ nnua a ɛwɔ adiwo hɔ no nyinaa wɔde dwetɛ ntwea a dwetɛ suso mu, na nʼase no nso wɔde hyehyɛ kɔbere nnyinaso apipiripi mu.
english: All the posts around the courtyard are to have silver bands and hooks, and bronze bases.

twi: Enti adiwo hɔ tenten mu bɛyɛ anammɔn ɔha ne aduonum, na ne trɛw nso ayɛ anammɔn aduɔson anum. Wɔde nkataano a wɔde asaawatam bɛyɛ ne fasu, a ne sorokɔ nso bɛyɛ anammɔn ason ne fa. Ɛsɛ sɛ wɔde nnua a atwa adiwo hɔ no ho ahyia no sisi kɔbere nnyinaso no mu.
english: The courtyard shall be a hundred cubits long and fifty cubits wide, with curtains of finely twisted linen five cubits high, and with bronze bases.

twi: Kɔbere na ɛsɛ sɛ wɔde yɛ Ahyiae Ntamadan mu hɔ nkankye a wɔde nneɛma gu mu, ne nnyinaso a wɔde nkankyee bɛsensɛn so wɔ ɔfasu ho no wɔ hɔ.
english: All the other articles used in the service of the tabernacle, whatever their function, including all the tent pegs for it and those for the courtyard, are to be of bronze.

twi: “Ka kyerɛ Israelfo no na wɔmfa ngo kronkron a wɔde begu akanea a daa nyinaa ebesi so no mmrɛ wo.
english: “Command the Israelites to bring you clear oil of pressed olives for the light so that the lamps may be kept burning.

twi: Aaron ne ne mmabarima na wɔde akanea a ennum da no besi Ahyiae Ntamadan no mu. Wɔbɛhwɛ so daa ama Awurade, sɛnea ɛbɛyɛ a ɛrennum. Eyi yɛ mmara a ɛsɛ sɛ Israelfo di so daa.
english: In the tent of meeting, outside the curtain that shields the ark of the covenant law, Aaron and his sons are to keep the lamps burning before the Lord from evening till morning. This is to be a lasting ordinance among the Israelites for the generations to come.

twi: Asɔfotade“Yi wo nua Aaron ne ne mmabarima Nadab, Abihu, Eleasar ne Itamar na tew wɔn ho na wɔnyɛ asɔfo nsom me.
english: “Have Aaron your brother brought to you from among the Israelites, along with his sons Nadab and Abihu, Eleazar and Ithamar, so they may serve me as priests.

twi: Pam atade kronkron ma wo nua Aaron na ama anuonyam aba nʼadwuma no ho. Pam atade no na ɛnyɛ fɛ, sɛnea ɛbɛma afata nʼadwuma no.
english: Make sacred garments for your brother Aaron to give him dignity and honor.

twi: Ka kyerɛ nnipa a mama wɔn adepam ho nyansa na wɔmpam atade no. Ɛno na ɛbɛma no ada nsow wɔ ne mfɛfo mu na ama watumi asom me.
english: Tell all the skilled workers to whom I have given wisdom in such matters that they are to make garments for Aaron, for his consecration, so he may serve me as priest.

twi: Ntade ahorow a wɔbɛpam no ni: adɛbo asɔfotade, atade yuu, atade kɔnsin a ɛyɛ adamadam, abotiri ne nkyekyeremu. Wɔbɛpam ntade kronkron bi nso de ama Aaron mmabarima no.
english: These are the garments they are to make: a breastpiece, an ephod, a robe, a woven tunic, a turban and a sash. They are to make these sacred garments for your brother Aaron and his sons, so they may serve me as priests.

twi: Wɔde ntama tuntum, bibiri ne koogyan a wɔde asaawatam pa na anwen na ɛbɛpam.
english: Have them use gold, and blue, purple and scarlet yarn, and fine linen.

twi: “Ma ntamanwen mu adwumfo papa mfa sikakɔkɔɔ ne bibiri ne asaawa a ɛbere dum ne koogyan ne asaawa fitaa a wɔafura nyɛ asɔfotade no.
english: “Make the ephod of gold, and of blue, purple and scarlet yarn, and of finely twisted linen—the work of skilled hands.

twi: Wɔbɛpam no asinasin abien a ɛyɛ anim ne akyi a wɔapam ne mmati no so abɔ mu.
english: It is to have two shoulder pieces attached to two of its corners, so it can be fastened.

twi: Nkyekyeremu no bɛyɛ ntama koro no ara bi. Ɛbɛyɛ asaawatam a ɛyɛ akokɔsrade, tuntum, bibiri ne koogyan.
english: Its skillfully woven waistband is to be like it—of one piece with the ephod and made with gold, and with blue, purple and scarlet yarn, and with finely twisted linen.

twi: “Fa apopobibiri abo abien na kyerɛw Israelfo mmusuakuw no din gu so.
english: “Take two onyx stones and engrave on them the names of the sons of Israel

twi: Ɔbo biara, wɔnkyerɛw din asia ngu so, sɛnea ɛbɛyɛ a, wɔn nyinaa din bedidi so mpanyin mu.
english: in the order of their birth—six names on one stone and the remaining six on the other.

twi: Fa ɔkwan a aboɔdemmotwafo si fa twa din gu adwinne so no so kyerɛw din ahorow no sɛnea Israel mma no din te, na fa sika mmuano twa ho hyia.
english: Engrave the names of the sons of Israel on the two stones the way a gem cutter engraves a seal. Then mount the stones in gold filigree settings

twi: Fa abo abien no sisi asɔfotade no mmati so na ɛnyɛ nkae ade mma Israelfo. Na daa Aaron nso nam so akae, abɔ wɔn din akyerɛ Awurade.
english: and fasten them on the shoulder pieces of the ephod as memorial stones for the sons of Israel. Aaron is to bear the names on his shoulders as a memorial before the Lord.

twi: Yɛ sikakɔkɔɔ ntweaban a wɔakyinkyim
english: Make gold filigree settings

twi: ne ntweaban abien a wɔde sikakɔkɔɔ ayɛ tetare ntetareho a ɛwɔ asɔfotade no mmati so no mu.
english: and two braided chains of pure gold, like a rope, and attach the chains to the settings.

twi: “Momma odwumfo a nʼadwinni yɛ fɛ na ɔnyɛ atemmu adɛbo no. Momfa asaawatam a ɛyɛ akokɔsrade, tuntum, bibiri ne koogyan na ɛmpam adɛbo no sɛnea mode pam asɔfotade no.
english: “Fashion a breastpiece for making decisions—the work of skilled hands. Make it like the ephod: of gold, and of blue, purple and scarlet yarn, and of finely twisted linen.

twi: Mummu adɛbo no nto so na ɛnyɛ sɛ ntama nkotoku.
english: It is to be square—a span long and a span wide—and folded double.

twi: Momfa abo a ɛsom bo a ɛsesa so anan mmobɔ mu. Nea a edi kan no nyɛ bogyanambo, nea ɛto so abien no nyɛ akraatebo na nea etwa to no nyɛ ɔbo a ɛte sɛ ahabammono.
english: Then mount four rows of precious stones on it. The first row shall be carnelian, chrysolite and beryl;

twi: Nsaso a ɛto so abien no nyɛ nsrammabo, hoabo ne dɛnkyɛmmo.
english: the second row shall be turquoise, lapis lazuli and emerald;

twi: Nsaso a ɛto so abiɛsa no nso bɛyɛ akutuhonobo, mfrafraebo ne beredumbo.
english: the third row shall be jacinth, agate and amethyst;

twi: Nsaso a ɛto so anan no bɛyɛ sikabereɛbo, apopobibiribo ne ahwehwɛbo. Sikakɔkɔɔ mmuano ntwa ne nyinaa ho nhyia.
english: the fourth row shall be topaz, onyx and jasper. Mount them in gold filigree settings.

twi: Ɔbo no baako biara begyina hɔ ama Israel mmusuakuw no baako. Na wɔbɛkyerɛw abusua ko no din agu so sɛ nsɔwanode.
english: There are to be twelve stones, one for each of the names of the sons of Israel, each engraved like a seal with the name of one of the twelve tribes.

twi: “Ɔkwan a mobɛfa so de adɛbo no afam asɔfotade no mu ni: yɛ sikakɔkɔɔ ntweaban.
english: “For the breastpiece make braided chains of pure gold, like a rope.

twi: Yɛ sikakɔkɔɔ nkaa abien, na fa tetare adɛbo no twɔtwɔw so.
english: Make two gold rings for it and fasten them to two corners of the breastpiece.

twi: Fa sikakɔkɔɔ ntweaban abien no hyehyɛ adɛbo no nkaa abien no twɔtwɔw so,
english: Fasten the two gold chains to the rings at the corners of the breastpiece,

twi: ntweaban abien a aka no fa biara nso, wɔmfa ntare ɔbo a ɛte sɛ apopobibiri no apɔw abien no so nsan mfa ntare asɔfotade no mmati so.
english: and the other ends of the chains to the two settings, attaching them to the shoulder pieces of the ephod at the front.

twi: Yɛ sika nkaa abien na fa hyehyɛ adɛbo ntwea abien a ɛwɔ fam no mu.
english: Make two gold rings and attach them to the other two corners of the breastpiece on the inside edge next to the ephod.

twi: San yɛ sikakɔkɔɔ nkaa abien hyehyɛ asɔfotade no ntwea so wɔ fam ma ɛnka nkyekyeremu no.
english: Make two more gold rings and attach them to the bottom of the shoulder pieces on the front of the ephod, close to the seam just above the waistband of the ephod.

twi: Fa bibiri hama kyekyere adɛbo no ase na fa hyehyɛ nkaa a ɛwɔ asɔfotade no ase no mu. Eyi remma adɛbo no mfi asɔfotade no ho ntew nsensɛn.
english: The rings of the breastpiece are to be tied to the rings of the ephod with blue cord, connecting it to the waistband, so that the breastpiece will not swing out from the ephod.

twi: “Aaron bɛfa saa kwan yi so na ɔde Israel mmusuakuw no din a ɛwɔ adɛbo no so no bɛkɔ kronkronbea hɔ; na eyi na ɛbɛma Awurade akae Israelman bere nyinaa mu.
english: “Whenever Aaron enters the Holy Place, he will bear the names of the sons of Israel over his heart on the breastpiece of decision as a continuing memorial before the Lord.

twi: Sɛ Aaron rekɔ Awurade anim a, ɔmfa Urim ne Tumim a ase ne hann ne pɛyɛ nhyɛ adɛbo a ɛda ne koko so no kotoku mu. Saa ara na daa Aaron bɛsoa nneɛma a wɔnam so kyerɛ Awurade apɛde de ma ne nkurɔfo no bere biara a ɔbɛkɔ Awurade anim no.
english: Also put the Urim and the Thummim in the breastpiece, so they may be over Aaron’s heart whenever he enters the presence of the Lord. Thus Aaron will always bear the means of making decisions for the Israelites over his heart before the Lord.

twi: “Wɔde ntama tuntum na ɛbɛpam asɔfotade no
english: “Make the robe of the ephod entirely of blue cloth,

twi: na wɔagyaw ɔkwan bi a Aaron de ne ti bewura mu. Ɛsɛ sɛ wɔde ntama a wɔanwen to atade no kɔn mu hyia, na ansuane amfa mu.
english: with an opening for the head in its center. There shall be a woven edge like a collar around this opening, so that it will not tear.

twi: Wɔde ntama tuntum, bibiri ne koogyan na ɛbɛpam ato ano.
english: Make pomegranates of blue, purple and scarlet yarn around the hem of the robe, with gold bells between them.

twi: Ɛsɛ sɛ wɔde sikakɔkɔɔ adɔmma ne atoaa aba a edi afrafra twa asɔfotade no mmuano ho hyia.
english: The gold bells and the pomegranates are to alternate around the hem of the robe.

twi: Bere biara a Aaron bɛkɔ Awurade anim akɔsɔre no, saa asɔfotade yi na ɔbɛhyɛ. Ɔredi akɔneaba wɔ Awurade anim hɔ wɔ kronkronbea hɔ no, na dɔn no rewosow sɛnea ɛbɛyɛ a ɔrenwu.
english: Aaron must wear it when he ministers. The sound of the bells will be heard when he enters the Holy Place before the Lord and when he comes out, so that he will not die.

twi: “Afei, boro sikakɔkɔɔ ankasa ma ɛnyɛ tratraa sɛ prɛte na kyerɛw so sɛnea wokurukyerɛw nsɔwanode so no se:Kronkron Ma Awurade.
english: “Make a plate of pure gold and engrave on it as on a seal: holy to the Lord.

twi: Wɔde ntama tuntum beso mu asensɛn Aaron abotiri no anim.
english: Fasten a blue cord to it to attach it to the turban; it is to be on the front of the turban.

twi: Aaron de saa ade no bɛbɔ ne moma so sɛnea ɛbɛyɛ a, sɛ Israelfo no bɔ afɔre biara na mfomso ba ho a, ɛho asodi bɛda ne so, na Awurade agye nnipa no, na ɔde wɔn bɔne nso akyɛ wɔn.
english: It will be on Aaron’s forehead, and he will bear the guilt involved in the sacred gifts the Israelites consecrate, whatever their gifts may be. It will be on Aaron’s forehead continually so that they will be acceptable to the Lord.

twi: “Fa asaawatam a ɛyɛ fɛ nwen Aaron atade kɔnsin no. Ma ɛnyɛ adamadam na fa ntama koro no ara bi pam abotiri na nwen biribi gu ne nkatakɔnmu no nso mu.
english: “Weave the tunic of fine linen and make the turban of fine linen. The sash is to be the work of an embroiderer.

twi: Pam atade yuu ne nkyekyeremu ne abotiri ma Aaron mmabarima na momfa obu ne nidi mma wɔn.
english: Make tunics, sashes and caps for Aaron’s sons to give them dignity and honor.

twi: Saa ntade yi na momfa nhyɛ Aaron ne ne mmabarima na momfa ngo ngu wɔn tirim mfa nhyɛ wɔn asɔfo wɔ ɔsom no mu, na momfa ntew wɔn ho sɛ asɔfo a wɔyɛ me dea.
english: After you put these clothes on your brother Aaron and his sons, anoint and ordain them. Consecrate them so they may serve me as priests.

twi: “Mompam sirikyi ntade a efi wɔn sisi kɔka wɔn nan ase, na wɔhyɛ ansa a, wɔahyɛ wɔn ntade no agu so.
english: “Make linen undergarments as a covering for the body, reaching from the waist to the thigh.

twi: Bere biara a Aaron ne ne mmabarima no rekɔ Ahyiae Ntamadan mu hɔ anaasɛ wɔrekɔ afɔremuka no anim wɔ kronkronbea hɔ no, wɔnhyɛ. Anyɛ saa a afɔbu bɛba wɔn so ama wɔawuwu.“Eyi yɛ daa apam a wɔahyɛ ama Aaron ne ne mmabarima.
english:
Aaron and his sons must wear them whenever they enter the tent of meeting or approach the altar to minister in the Holy Place, so that they will not incur guilt and die.
“This is to be a lasting ordinance for Aaron and his descendants.

twi: Asɔfohyɛ“Ɔkwan a ɛsɛ sɛ mofa so hyɛ Aaron ne ne mma asɔfo ni: Momfa nantwi ba ne adwennini abien a wɔn ho nni dɛm.
english: “This is what you are to do to consecrate them, so they may serve me as priests: Take a young bull and two rams without defect.

twi: Na momfa esiam muhumuhu a mmɔkaw nni mu nyɛ brodo a ɛyɛ dɛ ne tetare a wɔde ngo afra ne ɔfam a wɔde ngo agu so.
english: And from the finest wheat flour make round loaves without yeast, thick loaves without yeast and with olive oil mixed in, and thin loaves without yeast and brushed with olive oil.

twi: Fa brodo no gu kɛntɛn mu na fa nantwi ba no ne odwennini no ka ho bra Ahyiae Ntamadan no ano.
english: Put them in a basket and present them along with the bull and the two rams.

twi: Momfa Aaron ne ne mmabarima no mmra Ahyiae Ntamadan no kwan ano hɔ, na momfa nsu nguare wɔn.
english: Then bring Aaron and his sons to the entrance to the tent of meeting and wash them with water.

twi: Momfa Aaron atade yuu no nhyɛ no. Monhyɛ no atade kɔnsin no, nʼasɔfotade no ne adɛbo no ne nkyekyeremu no,
english: Take the garments and dress Aaron with the tunic, the robe of the ephod, the ephod itself and the breastpiece. Fasten the ephod on him by its skillfully woven waistband.

twi: na momfa abotiri a sikakɔkɔɔ bobɔ mu no mmɔ no.
english: Put the turban on his head and attach the sacred emblem to the turban.

twi: Momfa ɔsrango no na munhwie ngu ne ti so.
english: Take the anointing oil and anoint him by pouring it on his head.

twi: Ne mmabarima no nso, momfa wɔn ntade yuu no nhyehyɛ wɔn.
english: Bring his sons and dress them in tunics

twi: Momfa wɔn nkyekyeremu no nka wɔn ho. Saa kwan yi so na momfa nhyɛ Aaron ne ne mma ne wɔn asefo mma wɔnyɛ asɔfo daa nyinaa.
english:
and fasten caps on them. Then tie sashes on Aaron and his sons. The priesthood is theirs by a lasting ordinance.
“Then you shall ordain Aaron and his sons.

twi: “Mode nantwi ba no bɛba Ahyiae Ntamadan no anim na Aaron ne ne mmabarima de wɔn nsa agu aboa no apampam.
english: “Bring the bull to the front of the tent of meeting, and Aaron and his sons shall lay their hands on its head.

twi: Munkum no wɔ Awurade anim wɔ Ahyiae Ntamadan no kwan ano.
english: Slaughter it in the Lord’s presence at the entrance to the tent of meeting.

twi: Momfa ne mogya nsrasra mmɛn a etuatua afɔremuka no ho no so. Momfa mo nsateaa na ɛnyɛ, na munhwie mogya a ɛbɛka no ngu afɔremuka no ase.
english: Take some of the bull’s blood and put it on the horns of the altar with your finger, and pour out the rest of it at the base of the altar.

twi: Munyi ne mu srade no ne ne bɔnwoma kotoku no ne ne asaabo abien no ne srade a ɛwɔ ho no na monhyew no wɔ afɔremuka no so.
english: Then take all the fat on the internal organs, the long lobe of the liver, and both kidneys with the fat on them, and burn them on the altar.

twi: Mmom momfa aboa no ne ne were ne nʼagyanan no mfi hɔ nkɔ afikyiri na monkɔhyew no sɛ bɔne ho afɔrebɔ.
english: But burn the bull’s flesh and its hide and its intestines outside the camp. It is a sin offering.

twi: “Sɛ wɔrebekum adwennini no nso a, Aaron ne ne mmabarima no mfa wɔn nsa ngu aboa no baako apampam
english: “Take one of the rams, and Aaron and his sons shall lay their hands on its head.

twi: na wonkum no. Wɔnsɔw ne mogya no na wɔmfa mpete afɔremuka no ho nyinaa.
english: Slaughter it and take the blood and splash it against the sides of the altar.

twi: Twitwa odwennini no asinasin na hohoro nʼayamde no mu ne nʼanan no ho; fa ne ti no ne nea moatwitwa no gu faako
english: Cut the ram into pieces and wash the internal organs and the legs, putting them with the head and the other pieces.

twi: na monhyew no wɔ afɔremuka no so; ɛyɛ ɔhyew afɔre a ɛsɔ Awurade ani.
english: Then burn the entire ram on the altar. It is a burnt offering to the Lord, a pleasing aroma, a food offering presented to the Lord.

twi: “Momfa odwennini a aka no na Aaron ne ne mmabarima mfa wɔn nsa ngu nʼapampam,
english: “Take the other ram, and Aaron and his sons shall lay their hands on its head.

twi: Munkum no na monsɔw mogya no bi na momfa ketewaa bi nsosɔ Aaron ne ne mmabarima no aso nifa, wɔn kokurobeti nifa ne wɔn anan nifa kokurobeti so. Afei mompete nkae no ngu afɔremuka no ho nyinaa.
english: Slaughter it, take some of its blood and put it on the lobes of the right ears of Aaron and his sons, on the thumbs of their right hands, and on the big toes of their right feet. Then splash blood against the sides of the altar.

twi: Montworɔw mogya a ɛwɔ afɔremuka no so no bi na momfa mfra ɔsrango na momfa mpete Aaron ne ne mmabarima no so ne wɔn ntade mu. Ɛnam saa so bɛma wɔn ne wɔn ntade ho atew wɔ Awurade anim.
english: And take some blood from the altar and some of the anointing oil and sprinkle it on Aaron and his garments and on his sons and their garments. Then he and his sons and their garments will be consecrated.

twi: “Momfa odwennini no srade ne ne dua ne ne mu srade ne ne bɔnwoma kotoku ne nʼasaabo abien ne ɛho srade ne ne srɛ nifa. Eyi ne odwennini a wɔde bɛhyɛ Aaron ne ne mmabarima asɔfo no.
english: “Take from this ram the fat, the fat tail, the fat on the internal organs, the long lobe of the liver, both kidneys with the fat on them, and the right thigh. (This is the ram for the ordination.)

twi: Momfa brodo mua baako ne tetare a wɔde ɔsrango afra, na munyi ɔfam baako mfi kɛntɛn a wɔde brodo a mmɔkaw nni mu agu mu a wɔde asi Awurade anim no mu.
english: From the basket of bread made without yeast, which is before the Lord, take one round loaf, one thick loaf with olive oil mixed in, and one thin loaf.

twi: Momfa eyinom nhyɛ Aaron ne ne mmabarima nsam na wɔmfa nkyerɛ sɛ afɔrebɔde mma Awurade.
english: Put all these in the hands of Aaron and his sons and have them wave them before the Lord as a wave offering.

twi: Ɛno akyi no, munnye mfi wɔn nsam na monhyew no wɔ afɔremuka no so sɛ ohuam afɔre mma no.
english: Then take them from their hands and burn them on the altar along with the burnt offering for a pleasing aroma to the Lord, a food offering presented to the Lord.

twi: Momfa Aaron asɔfohyɛguan no yan no a munhim wɔ Awurade anim sɛ ohim afɔrebɔ, na ɛbɛyɛ mo kyɛfa.
english: After you take the breast of the ram for Aaron’s ordination, wave it before the Lord as a wave offering, and it will be your share.

twi: “Montew asɔfohyɛ dwennini no akwaa, ne koko a wohimii ne ne srɛ a wɔde mae a ɛyɛ Aaron ne ne mmabarima de no ho.
english: “Consecrate those parts of the ordination ram that belong to Aaron and his sons: the breast that was waved and the thigh that was presented.

twi: Ɛsɛ sɛ eyi yɛ Israelfo asɛde sɛ wɔbɛyɛ ama Aaron ne ne mmabarima. Ɛyɛ Israelfo no fam asomdwoe afɔre a ɛsɛ sɛ wɔbɔ ma Awurade.
english: This is always to be the perpetual share from the Israelites for Aaron and his sons. It is the contribution the Israelites are to make to the Lord from their fellowship offerings.

twi: “Aaron ntade kronkron yi bɛyɛ nʼasefo de na wɔatumi ahyɛ ama wɔasra wɔn ngo ahyɛ wɔn asɔfo.
english: “Aaron’s sacred garments will belong to his descendants so that they can be anointed and ordained in them.

twi: Ɔsɔfopanyin biara a obedi Aaron ade no bɛhyɛ saa ntade yi nnanson ansa na wafi nʼasɔfodwuma ase wɔ Ahyiae Ntamadan no mu ne kronkronbea hɔ.
english: The son who succeeds him as priest and comes to the tent of meeting to minister in the Holy Place is to wear them seven days.

twi: “Fa odwennini no nam a wɔatew ho no ne odwennini nam a wɔde hyɛɛ ɔsɔfo no na monnoa no wɔ baabi a ɛhɔ tew.
english: “Take the ram for the ordination and cook the meat in a sacred place.

twi: Aaron ne ne mmabarima bedi brodo a ɛwɔ kɛntɛn no mu no, na wɔde nam no abɔ so wɔ Ahyiae Ntamadan no ano.
english: At the entrance to the tent of meeting, Aaron and his sons are to eat the meat of the ram and the bread that is in the basket.

twi: Wɔn nko ara na wɔbɛwe nam no adi nnuan a wɔde tew wɔn ho no. Nnipa a wɔmfra asɔfo abusua no mu no renni bi, efisɛ wɔatew ho.
english: They are to eat these offerings by which atonement was made for their ordination and consecration. But no one else may eat them, because they are sacred.

twi: Sɛ ade kye asɔfohyɛ dwennini anaa brodo no bi so a, monhyew. Ɛnsɛ sɛ wodi, efisɛ ɛyɛ kronkron.
english: And if any of the meat of the ordination ram or any bread is left over till morning, burn it up. It must not be eaten, because it is sacred.

twi: “Eyi ne ɔkwan a momfa so nhyɛ Aaron ne ne mmabarima no asɔfo. Nnanson na wɔmfa nni saa asɔfohyɛ no ho dwuma.
english: “Do for Aaron and his sons everything I have commanded you, taking seven days to ordain them.

twi: Da biara, mode nantwi ba bɛbɔ afɔre de adwira mo ho. Ɛno akyi no, mompra afɔremuka no ho bɔne nyinaa na monyɛ no kronkron na monhwie ngo ngu so mfa ntew ho.
english: Sacrifice a bull each day as a sin offering to make atonement. Purify the altar by making atonement for it, and anoint it to consecrate it.

twi: Montew afɔremuka no ho na daa monyɛ no kronkron saa ara nnanson mma Onyankopɔn. Ɛno akyi no, afɔremuka no ho bɛtew yiye sɛnea biribiara a wɔde bɛka no no bɛyɛ Onyankopɔn dea.
english: For seven days make atonement for the altar and consecrate it. Then the altar will be most holy, and whatever touches it will be holy.

twi: “Da biara, momfa nguanten mma abien a wɔadi afe mmɔ afɔre wɔ afɔremuka no so.
english: “This is what you are to offer on the altar regularly each day: two lambs a year old.

twi: Momfa oguamma no baako mmɔ afɔre no anɔpa na momfa baako nso mmɔ afɔre anwummere.
english: Offer one in the morning and the other at twilight.

twi: Afɔrebɔ a edi kan no, momfa asikresiam lita abien ne fa a wɔayam no muhumuhu mfra ngo a wɔakyi afi ngodua mu lita baako; saa ara na momfa bobesa lita baako nyɛ ahwiesa.
english: With the first lamb offer a tenth of an ephah of the finest flour mixed with a quarter of a hin of oil from pressed olives, and a quarter of a hin of wine as a drink offering.

twi: Momfa oguan no baako a waka no mmɔ anwummere afɔre a asikresiam ne nsa ka ho te sɛ anɔpa de no ara. Ɛbɛyɛ ɔhyew afɔrehuam ama Awurade.
english: Sacrifice the other lamb at twilight with the same grain offering and its drink offering as in the morning—a pleasing aroma, a food offering presented to the Lord.

twi: “Saa afɔrebɔ yi bɛkɔ so da biara wɔ Ahyiae Ntamadan no pon ano wɔ Awurade anim. Ɛhɔ na mehyia mo ne mo akasa.
english: “For the generations to come this burnt offering is to be made regularly at the entrance to the tent of meeting, before the Lord. There I will meet you and speak to you;

twi: Na mehyia Israelmma wɔ hɔ na mʼanuonyam atew Ahyiae Ntamadan no ho.
english: there also I will meet with the Israelites, and the place will be consecrated by my glory.

twi: “Ampa ara, mɛtew Ahyiae Ntamadan no ne afɔremuka no ho ne Aaron ne ne mmabarima a wɔyɛ mʼasɔfo no ho.
english: “So I will consecrate the tent of meeting and the altar and will consecrate Aaron and his sons to serve me as priests.

twi: Na mɛtena Israelfo mu na mayɛ wɔn Nyankopɔn,
english: Then I will dwell among the Israelites and be their God.

twi: na wobehu sɛ mene Awurade, wɔn Nyankopɔn. Mede wɔn fi Misraim bae sɛnea ɛbɛyɛ a, mɛtena wɔn mu. Mene Awurade wɔn Nyankopɔn.
english: They will know that I am the Lord their God, who brought them out of Egypt so that I might dwell among them. I am the Lord their God.

twi: Aduhuam Afɔremuka“Fa ɔkanto yɛ afɔremuka ketewa bi a wobɛhyew aduhuam wɔ so.
english: “Make an altar of acacia wood for burning incense.

twi: Ma ɛnyɛ ahinanan a ne fa biara susuw nsateaa dunwɔtwe, na ne sorokɔ nso nyɛ anammɔn abiɛsa a wɔasen; ne mmɛn a baako tua ho.
english: It is to be square, a cubit long and a cubit wide, and two cubits high—its horns of one piece with it.

twi: Fa sikakɔkɔɔ dura ne soro, ne nkyɛn ne ne mmɛn a ɛwɔ afɔremuka no ho no nyinaa. Na fa sikakɔkɔɔ mmuano twa afɔremuka no ho nyinaa hyia.
english: Overlay the top and all the sides and the horns with pure gold, and make a gold molding around it.

twi: Fa sikakɔkɔɔ nkaa abien hyehyɛ mmuano no a ɛwɔ afanu no ase na wɔde nnua a wɔde bɛsoa no awurawura mu.
english: Make two gold rings for the altar below the molding—two on each of the opposite sides—to hold the poles used to carry it.

twi: Wɔmfa ɔkanto na ɛnyɛ nnua no, na wɔmfa sikakɔkɔɔ nnura ho nyinaa.
english: Make the poles of acacia wood and overlay them with gold.

twi: Fa afɔremuka no si ntwamtam no akyi wɔ mpatabea hɔ a ɛbɔ faako a Apam Adaka a Mmaransɛm Du no wɔ no ho ban. Mehyia mo wɔ hɔ.
english: Put the altar in front of the curtain that shields the ark of the covenant law—before the atonement cover that is over the tablets of the covenant law—where I will meet with you.

twi: “Da biara anɔpa, sɛ Aaron resiesie kanea no a, ɔbɛhyew aduhuam wɔ afɔremuka no so.
english: “Aaron must burn fragrant incense on the altar every morning when he tends the lamps.

twi: Anwummere biara, sɛ ɔsɔ kanea no a, ɔbɛhyew aduhuam wɔ Awurade anim ama awo ntoatoaso a ɛbɛba nyinaa.
english: He must burn incense again when he lights the lamps at twilight so incense will burn regularly before the Lord for the generations to come.

twi: Monhyew aduhuam a wɔama ho kwan wɔ afɔremuka no so. Mommmɔ ɔhyew afɔre ne aduan afɔre wɔ so, na mommfa ahwiesa ngu so.
english: Do not offer on this altar any other incense or any burnt offering or grain offering, and do not pour a drink offering on it.

twi: Afe biara, ɛsɛ sɛ Aaron dwira afɔremuka no ho yɛ no kronkron. Ɔde mogya bɛsrasra mmɛn a etuatua ho no so sɛ mpata. Ɛsɛ sɛ afe biara wɔtew afɔremuka no ho yɛ no kronkron ma awo ntoatoaso a ɛbɛba no so kosi awo ntoatoaso so. Ɛyɛ kronkron ma Awurade.”
english: Once a year Aaron shall make atonement on its horns. This annual atonement must be made with the blood of the atoning sin offering for the generations to come. It is most holy to the Lord.”

twi: Awurade ka kyerɛɛ Mose se,
english: Then the Lord said to Moses,

twi: “Bere biara a wobɛkan Israelfo no, obiara a wɔbɛkan no no mfa ne kra ho mpata mmrɛ Awurade, sɛnea ɛbɛyɛ a ɔyaredɔm biara remma wɔn mu bi so.
english: “When you take a census of the Israelites to count them, each one must pay the Lord a ransom for his life at the time he is counted. Then no plague will come on them when you number them.

twi: Ɛsɛ sɛ obiara a wɔkan no no ma dwetɛbona fa, a emu duru yɛ gram asia (sɛnea kronkronbea mu dwetɛbona bo te no.)
english: Each one who crosses over to those already counted is to give a half shekel, according to the sanctuary shekel, which weighs twenty gerahs. This half shekel is an offering to the Lord.

twi: Obiara a wadi mfe aduonu rekɔ no na ɔbɛbɔ saa afɔre yi.
english: All who cross over, those twenty years old or more, are to give an offering to the Lord.

twi: Ɛnsɛ sɛ adefo ma ma ɛboro sika a wɔatwa ato hɔ no so. Ɛnsɛ sɛ ahiafo nso ma nea esua sen saa, efisɛ ɛyɛ Awurade afɔre a ɔde retew yɛn ho ama yɛn.
english: The rich are not to give more than a half shekel and the poor are not to give less when you make the offering to the Lord to atone for your lives.

twi: Momfa saa sika yi nsiesie Ahyiae Ntamadan no. Sɛ moyɛ saa a, ɛbɛma Awurade ani aba mo, Israelfo, so na ayɛ mpata nso ama mo.”
english: Receive the atonement money from the Israelites and use it for the service of the tent of meeting. It will be a memorial for the Israelites before the Lord, making atonement for your lives.”

twi: Awurade ka kyerɛɛ Mose se.
english: Then the Lord said to Moses,

twi: “Fa kɔbere yɛ hweaseammɔ a ne nnyinaso nso yɛ kɔbere. Fa si Ahyiae Ntamadan no ne afɔremuka no ntam na fa nsu gu mu.
english: “Make a bronze basin, with its bronze stand, for washing. Place it between the tent of meeting and the altar, and put water in it.

twi: Ɛhɔ na Aaron ne ne mmabarima bɛhohoro wɔn nsa ne wɔn anan ho
english: Aaron and his sons are to wash their hands and feet with water from it.

twi: bere a wɔrekɔ Ahyiae Ntamadan no mu de wɔn ho akɔkyerɛ Awurade, anaasɛ wɔrekɔ akɔbɔ afɔre wɔ afɔremuka no so ama Awurade no. Saa ara na bere biara a wɔrekodi saa dwuma yi no,
english: Whenever they enter the tent of meeting, they shall wash with water so that they will not die. Also, when they approach the altar to minister by presenting a food offering to the Lord,

twi: ɛsɛ sɛ wɔhohoro wɔn ho na wɔanwuwu. Ɛsɛ sɛ eyi yɛ mmara a ɛbɛtena hɔ daa ama Aaron ne nʼasefo, awo ntoatoaso a ɛbɛba nyinaa.”
english: they shall wash their hands and feet so that they will not die. This is to be a lasting ordinance for Aaron and his descendants for the generations to come.”

twi: Afei, Awurade ka kyerɛɛ Mose se,
english: Then the Lord said to Moses,

twi: “Hwehwɛ nnuhuam papa sɛ kurobow a ɛyɛ kilogram asia, sinamon kilogram abiɛsa ne mmetire huamhuam kilogram abiɛsa.
english: “Take the following fine spices: 500 shekels of liquid myrrh, half as much (that is, 250 shekels) of fragrant cinnamon, 250 shekels of fragrant calamus,

twi: Kurobow dodow a mobɛfa no nyɛ sɛ sinamon no dodow na momfa ngodua mu ngo lita anan.
english: 500 shekels of cassia—all according to the sanctuary shekel—and a hin of olive oil.

twi: Awurade ahyɛ nnuhuamfrafo a wakwadaw ne yɛ mu yiye, sɛ wɔmfra saa nnuhuam yi mma ɛnyɛ ngo kronkron a wɔde tew onipa ho.
english: Make these into a sacred anointing oil, a fragrant blend, the work of a perfumer. It will be the sacred anointing oil.

twi: Na momfa eyi ntew Ahyiae Ntamadan ne Apam Adaka,
english: Then use it to anoint the tent of meeting, the ark of the covenant law,

twi: ɔpon no ne ɛho nkankyee nyinaa, kaneadua no ɛho nneɛma, nnuhuam afɔremuka no,
english: the table and all its articles, the lampstand and its accessories, the altar of incense,

twi: ɔhyew afɔre ne ho nkankyee, ne hweaseammɔ ne nea esi so.
english: the altar of burnt offering and all its utensils, and the basin with its stand.

twi: Montew ho na ɛnyɛ kronkron na biribiara a ɛbɛka saa nneɛma yi no ho atew.
english: You shall consecrate them so they will be most holy, and whatever touches them will be holy.

twi: “Monsra Aaron ne ne mmabarima no sɛnea ɛbɛyɛ a wɔn ho bɛtew na wɔatumi ayɛ asɔfodwuma de asom me.
english: “Anoint Aaron and his sons and consecrate them so they may serve me as priests.

twi: Na monka nkyerɛ Israelfo se, ‘Eyi bɛyɛ me srango kronkron ama awo ntoatoaso a ɛbɛba no.
english: Say to the Israelites, ‘This is to be my sacred anointing oil for the generations to come.

twi: Ɛnsɛ sɛ wohwie gu obiara so kwa, na ɛnsɛ sɛ mo ankasa nso moyɛ bi, efisɛ ɛyɛ kronkron enti ɛsɛ sɛ mo nso moyɛ no kronkron.
english: Do not pour it on anyone else’s body and do not make any other oil using the same formula. It is sacred, and you are to consider it sacred.

twi: Obiara a ɔbɛfra aduhuam a ɛte sɛ ɛno na obehwie bi agu obi a ɔnyɛ ɔsɔfo so no, sɛ sɛ wo twa no asu.’ ”
english: Whoever makes perfume like it and puts it on anyone other than a priest must be cut off from their people.’”

twi: Awurade hyɛɛ mmara a ɛfa aduhuam no ho maa Mose se, “Fa nnuhuam atomude ne nworahuam ne prɛkɛsɛ huamhuam ne ohuamfufu gyenennyenen na wonsusuw ne nyinaa mu duru mma ɛnyɛ pɛ,
english: Then the Lord said to Moses, “Take fragrant spices—gum resin, onycha and galbanum—and pure frankincense, all in equal amounts,

twi: na fa yɛ aduhuam a wɔhyewee a aduhuamfrani a waben yɛ no bi, na wɔmfa nkyene mfra mu; na ɛbɛyɛ aduhuam kronkron.
english: and make a fragrant blend of incense, the work of a perfumer. It is to be salted and pure and sacred.

twi: Monyam bi mma ɛnyɛ muhumuhu na momfa bi nsi Apam Adaka no anim faako a mehyia mo wɔ Ahyiae Ntamadan no mu hɔ no. Saa aduhuam yi ne nea ɛyɛ kronkron koraa wɔ ne nyinaa mu.
english: Grind some of it to powder and place it in front of the ark of the covenant law in the tent of meeting, where I will meet with you. It shall be most holy to you.

twi: Monnyɛ bi mfa, efisɛ wɔakora ama Awurade enti ɛsɛ sɛ moyɛ no kronkron.
english: Do not make any incense with this formula for yourselves; consider it holy to the Lord.

twi: Obiara a ɔbɛyɛ bi afa no, wontwa no asu.”
english: Whoever makes incense like it to enjoy its fragrance must be cut off from their people.”

twi: Onyankopɔn Yi Besaleel Ne OholiabAwurade ka kyerɛɛ Mose se,
english: Then the Lord said to Moses,

twi: “Mapaw Besaleel a ɔyɛ Uri babarima na ɔyɛ Hur nena a ofi Yuda abusua mu no
english: “See, I have chosen Bezalel son of Uri, the son of Hur, of the tribe of Judah,

twi: de Onyankopɔn Honhom, nyansa, ntease, nimdeɛ ne nnepa ahorow nyinaa ahyɛ no mma
english: and I have filled him with the Spirit of God, with wisdom, with understanding, with knowledge and with all kinds of skills—

twi: sɛ ɔmfa nyɛ sika, dwetɛ ne kɔbere nnwinne ahorow,
english: to make artistic designs for work in gold, silver and bronze,

twi: sɛ ɔmfa nyɛ abo ne dua dwumfo ne adwinni ahorow nyinaa.
english: to cut and set stones, to work in wood, and to engage in all kinds of crafts.

twi: Bio, mayi Ahisamak ba Oholiab a ofi Dan abusua mu sɛ ɔnyɛ ne boafo.“Ɛno akyi no, mama adwumayɛfo no nyinaa nimdeɛ sononko bi sɛnea ɛbɛyɛ a, wobetumi adi dwuma biara a makyerɛ sɛ munni no:
english: Moreover, I have appointed Oholiab son of Ahisamak, of the tribe of Dan, to help him. Also I have given ability to all the skilled workers to make everything I have commanded you:

twi: “Ahyiae Ntamadan,Apam Adaka ne mpata agua neAhyiae Ntamadan no mu ahyehyɛde nkae no nyinaa;
english: the tent of meeting, the ark of the covenant law with the atonement cover on it, and all the other furnishings of the tent—

twi: ɔpon no ne so nneɛma,sikakɔkɔɔ kaneadua ne ho nneɛma,ohuam afɔremuka;
english: the table and its articles, the pure gold lampstand and all its accessories, the altar of incense,

twi: ɔhyew afɔremuka ne ho nneɛma,nsankason ne ne nnyinaso;
english: the altar of burnt offering and all its utensils, the basin with its stand—

twi: ɔsɔfo Aaron ntade kronkron fɛɛfɛ none ne mma ntade bere a wɔsom sɛ asɔfo no;
english: and also the woven garments, both the sacred garments for Aaron the priest and the garments for his sons when they serve as priests,

twi: ne ɔsra ngo ne Kronkronbea hɔ aduhuam no.“Ɛsɛ sɛ wɔfa kwan a mɛkyerɛ wo no so na wɔyɛ eyinom nyinaa.”
english: and the anointing oil and fragrant incense for the Holy Place. They are to make them just as I commanded you.”

twi: Afei, Awurade ka kyerɛɛ Mose se,
english: Then the Lord said to Moses,

twi: “Ka kyerɛ Israelfo no se, ‘Sɛ edu Homeda a, monhome. Eyi ne nsɛnkyerɛnne a ɛda me ne mo ne awo ntoatoaso a ɛbɛba no ntam, na moahu sɛ mene Awurade a meyɛ mo kronkron no.’
english: “Say to the Israelites, ‘You must observe my Sabbaths. This will be a sign between me and you for the generations to come, so you may know that I am the Lord, who makes you holy.

twi: “ ‘Munni Homeda no, efisɛ ɛyɛ da kronkron. Obiara a obebu saa mmara yi so no, obewu. Na nea ɔbɛyɛ adwuma saa da no nso, wobekum no.
english: “‘Observe the Sabbath, because it is holy to you. Anyone who desecrates it is to be put to death; those who do any work on that day must be cut off from their people.

twi: Nnansia na mode bɛyɛ adwuma. Na nnanson so no yɛ Homeda a wɔntoto no ase a ɛyɛ kronkron ma Awurade. Ɛsɛ sɛ wokum obiara a ɔbɛyɛ adwuma Homeda no.
english: For six days work is to be done, but the seventh day is a day of sabbath rest, holy to the Lord. Whoever does any work on the Sabbath day is to be put to death.

twi: Ɛsɛ sɛ Israelfo no di Homeda no, wonni mma awo ntoatoaso no nhu sɛ ɛyɛ apam afebɔɔ.
english: The Israelites are to observe the Sabbath, celebrating it for the generations to come as a lasting covenant.

twi: Ɛbɛyɛ daa apam a ɛda me ne Israelfo ntam no ho nsɛnkyerɛnne. Efisɛ nnansia mu na Awurade de bɔɔ ɔsoro ne asase, na ɔhomee da a ɛto so ason no.’ ”
english: It will be a sign between me and the Israelites forever, for in six days the Lord made the heavens and the earth, and on the seventh day he rested and was refreshed.’”

twi: Onyankopɔn kasa kyerɛɛ Mose wɔ Sinai Bepɔw so wiee no, ɔde abo pon abien a ɔde ne nsa akyerɛw Mmaransɛm Du no wɔ so no maa no.
english: When the Lord finished speaking to Moses on Mount Sinai, he gave him the two tablets of the covenant law, the tablets of stone inscribed by the finger of God.

twi: Sika Nantwi BaMose kyɛe wɔ bepɔw no so saa no, nnipa no nyinaa kɔɔ Aaron so kɔka kyerɛɛ no se, “Ntɛm, yɛ anyame a wobedi yɛn anim ma yɛn, efisɛ yenhu baabi a Mose a odii yɛn anim de yɛn fi Misraim asase so baa ha no afa; ebia na biribi ayɛ no.”
english: When the people saw that Moses was so long in coming down from the mountain, they gathered around Aaron and said, “Come, make us gods who will go before us. As for this fellow Moses who brought us up out of Egypt, we don’t know what has happened to him.”

twi: Aaron nso ka kyerɛɛ wɔn se, “Munyiyi mo sika nsonkaa nyinaa mmra.”
english: Aaron answered them, “Take off the gold earrings that your wives, your sons and your daughters are wearing, and bring them to me.”

twi: Wɔn nyinaa yiyii wɔn nsonkaa brɛɛ Aaron.
english: So all the people took off their earrings and brought them to Aaron.

twi: Aaron nan sikakɔkɔɔ nsonkaa no, na ɔde oguu nantwi ba ohoni. Nnipa no nyinaa kae se, “Israel, oyi ne mo nyame a oyii mo fii Misraim asase so bae no.”
english: He took what they handed him and made it into an idol cast in the shape of a calf, fashioning it with a tool. Then they said, “These are your gods, Israel, who brought you up out of Egypt.”

twi: Aaron huu sɛ nnipa no ani agye sika nantwi ba ohoni no ho no, osii afɔremuka sii nantwi ba no anim kae se, “Ɔkyena yɛbɛhyɛ fa ama Awurade.”
english: When Aaron saw this, he built an altar in front of the calf and announced, “Tomorrow there will be a festival to the Lord.”

twi: Wɔsɔree anɔpahema fii ase bɔɔ ɔhyew afɔre ne asomdwoe afɔre de maa nantwi ba ohoni no. Ɛno akyi no, wɔtoo pon kɛse, didi nomee, goruu abosongoru, yɛɛ ahuhude.
english: So the next day the people rose early and sacrificed burnt offerings and presented fellowship offerings. Afterward they sat down to eat and drink and got up to indulge in revelry.

twi: Afei, Awurade ka kyerɛɛ Mose se, “Yɛ ntɛm na sian kɔ wo nkurɔfo a wode wɔn fi Misraim asase so bae no nkyɛn, efisɛ wɔagu wɔn ho fi,
english: Then the Lord said to Moses, “Go down, because your people, whom you brought up out of Egypt, have become corrupt.

twi: na wɔabu me mmara nyinaa nso so. Wɔabɔ sika nantwi ba a wɔsom no, asan abɔ afɔre nso ama no aka se, ‘Israel, oyi ne mo nyame a oyii mo fii Misraim asase so bae no.’ ”
english: They have been quick to turn away from what I commanded them and have made themselves an idol cast in the shape of a calf. They have bowed down to it and sacrificed to it and have said, ‘These are your gods, Israel, who brought you up out of Egypt.’

twi: Awurade kae se, “Mahu sɛnea saa nnipa yi si yɛ asoɔden na wɔsan yɛ atuatewfo fa.
english: “I have seen these people,” the Lord said to Moses, “and they are a stiff-necked people.

twi: Afei, ma me kwan na memma mʼabufuw nnɛw ntia wɔn mma mensɛe wɔn. Na mɛyɛ wo ɔman kɛse.”
english: Now leave me alone so that my anger may burn against them and that I may destroy them. Then I will make you into a great nation.”

twi: Nanso Mose srɛɛ Onyankopɔn sɛ ɔnyɛ saa. Ɔkɔɔ so se, “Awurade, adɛn nti na ɛsɛ sɛ wʼabufuw dɛw atia wo ara wo nkurɔfo a wonam anwonwakwan ne wo tumi so yii wɔn fii Misraim asase so yi?
english: But Moses sought the favor of the Lord his God. “Lord,” he said, “why should your anger burn against your people, whom you brought out of Egypt with great power and a mighty hand?

twi: Adɛn nti na ɛsɛ sɛ Misraimfo no ka se, ‘Onyankopɔn daadaa wɔn sɛ wɔmmra bepɔw no so sɛnea obenya wɔn akum wɔn, atɔre wɔn ase afi asase so?’ Ma wo bo ntɔ wo yam na gyae ɔsɛe a wopɛ sɛ wode ba wo nkurɔfo no so no.
english: Why should the Egyptians say, ‘It was with evil intent that he brought them out, to kill them in the mountains and to wipe them off the face of the earth’? Turn from your fierce anger; relent and do not bring disaster on your people.

twi: Kae bɔ a wohyɛɛ wʼasomfo Abraham, Isak ne Israel no. Wo ara wokaa ntam se, ‘Mɛma mo asefo adɔɔso sɛ ɔsoro nsoromma na mede saa asase a mahyɛ mo ho bɔ yi nyinaa bɛma mo asefo na wɔatena so afebɔɔ.’ ”
english: Remember your servants Abraham, Isaac and Israel, to whom you swore by your own self: ‘I will make your descendants as numerous as the stars in the sky and I will give your descendants all this land I promised them, and it will be their inheritance forever.’”

twi: Na Awurade sesaa nʼadwene de wɔn ho kyɛɛ wɔn.
english: Then the Lord relented and did not bring on his people the disaster he had threatened.

twi: Afei, Mose sian fii bepɔw no so bae a okura Mmaransɛm Du no a wɔakyerɛw agu abo apon abien akyi ne anim no.
english: Moses turned and went down the mountain with the two tablets of the covenant law in his hands. They were inscribed on both sides, front and back.

twi: Onyankopɔn no ankasa na ɔkyerɛw mmaransɛm no wɔ apon no so.
english: The tablets were the work of God; the writing was the writing of God, engraved on the tablets.

twi: Bere a Yosua tee sɛ nnipa bi reyɛ gyegyeegye no, ɔka kyerɛɛ Mose se, “Ɛyɛ me sɛ wɔreboaboa wɔn ho akɔ ɔko!”
english: When Joshua heard the noise of the people shouting, he said to Moses, “There is the sound of war in the camp.”

twi: Ɛnna Mose nso buaa no se, “Ɛnyɛ nkonimdi mu nnyigyei na ɛnyɛ nkogu de, na mmom, ɛyɛ nnwonto nnyigyei na mete.”
english:
Moses replied:
“It is not the sound of victory,
    it is not the sound of defeat;
    it is the sound of singing that I hear.”

twi: Wobeduu atenae hɔ, Mose huu nantwi ba no ne asaw a wɔresaw. Enti ɔde abufuwhyew tow kyerɛwapon no hwehwee fam ma ebubuu wɔ bepɔw no ase.
english: When Moses approached the camp and saw the calf and the dancing, his anger burned and he threw the tablets out of his hands, breaking them to pieces at the foot of the mountain.

twi: Ɔfaa nantwi ba no nan no wɔ ogya mu na edwoe no, ɔyam no muhumuhu de guu nsu mu maa nnipa no nomee.
english: And he took the calf the people had made and burned it in the fire; then he ground it to powder, scattered it on the water and made the Israelites drink it.

twi: Obisaa Aaron se, “Dɛn nko ara na saa nnipa no yɛɛ wo a enti wudii wɔn anim ma wɔyɛɛ saa bɔne kɛse yi?”
english: He said to Aaron, “What did these people do to you, that you led them into such great sin?”

twi: Aaron buaa no se, “Mma wo bo mmfuw. Wo ara wunim sɛnea wo nkurɔfo yi yɛ nnipa bɔne fa.
english: “Do not be angry, my lord,” Aaron answered. “You know how prone these people are to evil.

twi: Wɔn ara na wɔka kyerɛɛ me se, ‘Yɛ onyame bi ma yɛn na ɔnkyerɛ yɛn kwan na yennim nea ayɛ saa Mose a odii yɛn anim fii Misraim no.’
english: They said to me, ‘Make us gods who will go before us. As for this fellow Moses who brought us up out of Egypt, we don’t know what has happened to him.’

twi: Enti me nso mekae se, ‘Munyiyi mo sikakɔkɔɔ nsonkaa mma me.’ Woyiyi de maa me na mede guu gya mu. Ɛne saa nantwi ba no!”
english: So I told them, ‘Whoever has any gold jewelry, take it off.’ Then they gave me the gold, and I threw it into the fire, and out came this calf!”

twi: Mose huu sɛ Aaron ama nnipa no adan aguamammɔfo ama wɔn atamfo anya wɔn no,
english: Moses saw that the people were running wild and that Aaron had let them get out of control and so become a laughingstock to their enemies.

twi: ogyinaa wɔn atenae hɔ pon no ano teɛɛ mu se, “Mo a mowɔ Awurade afa no, mommra me nkyɛn.” Lewifo no nyinaa kɔɔ ne nkyɛn.
english: So he stood at the entrance to the camp and said, “Whoever is for the Lord, come to me.” And all the Levites rallied to him.

twi: Ɔka kyerɛɛ wɔn se, “Awurade Israel Nyankopɔn se, ‘Momfa mo afoa nhyehyɛ mo ho na munni mo atenae hɔ akɔneaba, na munkunkum mo nuanom, mo nnamfonom ne mo afipamfo.’ ”
english: Then he said to them, “This is what the Lord, the God of Israel, says: ‘Each man strap a sword to his side. Go back and forth through the camp from one end to the other, each killing his brother and friend and neighbor.’”

twi: Enti wɔyɛɛ saa maa nnipa bɛyɛ mpensa totɔɔ da no.
english: The Levites did as Moses commanded, and that day about three thousand of the people died.

twi: Afei, Mose ka kyerɛɛ Lewifo no se, “Nnɛ, moatu mo ho asi hɔ sɛ mobɛsom Awurade, efisɛ moayɛ osetie ama no ama mpo, monam so akunkum mo mma ne mo nuanom, enti obehyira mo bebree.”
english: Then Moses said, “You have been set apart to the Lord today, for you were against your own sons and brothers, and he has blessed you this day.”

twi: Ade kyee anɔpa no, Mose ka kyerɛɛ nkurɔfo no se, “Moayɛ bɔne a ɛso bi mmaa da, nanso mɛsan akɔ Awurade nkyɛn wɔ bepɔw no so akɔhwɛ sɛ ebia, menya bɔnefakyɛ ama mo ana.”
english: The next day Moses said to the people, “You have committed a great sin. But now I will go up to the Lord; perhaps I can make atonement for your sin.”

twi: Enti Mose san kɔɔ Awurade nkyɛn kɔka kyerɛɛ no se, “Ao, saa nnipa yi ayɛ bɔne a ɛso bi mmaa da, na wɔde sikakɔkɔɔ ayɛ wɔn anyame.
english: So Moses went back to the Lord and said, “Oh, what a great sin these people have committed! They have made themselves gods of gold.

twi: Enti meredi ama wɔn sɛ, fa wɔn bɔne kyɛ wɔn, na sɛ ɛnte saa nso a, pepa me din fi nhoma a woakyerɛw no mu.”
english: But now, please forgive their sin—but if not, then blot me out of the book you have written.”

twi: Awurade buaa Mose se, “Obiara a wayɛ me bɔne no, mɛpepa no afi me nhoma mu.
english: The Lord replied to Moses, “Whoever has sinned against me I will blot out of my book.

twi: Enti afei, kɔ na di nkurɔfo no anim kɔ baabi a mekyerɛɛ wo no na mehyɛ wo bɔ sɛ mɛma me bɔfo adi wʼanim; nanso sɛ mebɛsra nkurɔfo no a, mɛtwe wɔn aso wɔ wɔn bɔne no ho.”
english: Now go, lead the people to the place I spoke of, and my angel will go before you. However, when the time comes for me to punish, I will punish them for their sin.”

twi: Na esiane sɛ nnipa no som Aaron nantwi ba no nti, ɔtew ɔyare guu wɔn so.
english: And the Lord struck the people with a plague because of what they did with the calf Aaron had made.

twi: Awurade ka kyerɛɛ Mose se, “Di saa nnipa a wode wɔn fi Misraim asase so no anim kɔ asase a mede hyɛɛ Abraham, Isak ne Yakob bɔ no so, efisɛ mekae se, ‘Mede saa asase yi bɛma wʼasefo.’
english: Then the Lord said to Moses, “Leave this place, you and the people you brought up out of Egypt, and go up to the land I promised on oath to Abraham, Isaac and Jacob, saying, ‘I will give it to your descendants.’

twi: Mɛsoma ɔbɔfo adi wʼanim na wapam Kanaanfo, Amorifo, Hetifo, Perisifo, Hewifo ne Yebusifo.
english: I will send an angel before you and drive out the Canaanites, Amorites, Hittites, Perizzites, Hivites and Jebusites.

twi: Ɛyɛ asase a ɛwo ne nufusu sen wɔ so. Na me ne mo rentu saa kwan no efisɛ moyɛ nnipa a mo aso yɛ den, na anyɛ a na makɔsɛe mo wɔ ɔkwan so.”
english: Go up to the land flowing with milk and honey. But I will not go with you, because you are a stiff-necked people and I might destroy you on the way.”

twi: Nnipa yi tee saa nsɛnhyew yi no, wotwaa agyaadwo na wɔworɔworɔw wɔn ho nkaa ne nnwinne nyinaa.
english: When the people heard these distressing words, they began to mourn and no one put on any ornaments.

twi: Awurade ka kyerɛɛ Mose se ɔnka nkyerɛ wɔn se, “Moyɛ nnipa a mo aso yɛ den. Na sɛ me ne mo tena bɛyɛ simma baako pɛ koraa mpo a, anyɛ a na matɔre mo ase. Monworɔworɔw mo nkaa ne mo nnwinne a mohyehyɛ no nyinaa na mehu nea mɛyɛ mo.”
english: For the Lord had said to Moses, “Tell the Israelites, ‘You are a stiff-necked people. If I were to go with you even for a moment, I might destroy you. Now take off your ornaments and I will decide what to do with you.’”

twi: Eyi akyi no, obiara worɔw ne nnwinne wɔ Bepɔw Horeb so.
english: So the Israelites stripped off their ornaments at Mount Horeb.

twi: Na Mose sii ahyiae ntamadan wɔ nsraban no akyi a obiara a ɔpɛ sɛ ɔne Awurade di nkitaho no kɔ hɔ. Wɔtoo dan no din Ahyiae.
english: Now Moses used to take a tent and pitch it outside the camp some distance away, calling it the “tent of meeting.” Anyone inquiring of the Lord would go to the tent of meeting outside the camp.

twi: Bere biara a Mose bɛkɔ Ahyiae Ntamadan no mu no, nnipa no nyinaa sɔre begyina wɔn ntamadan no ano hwɛ no kosi sɛ obedu ɔdan no ano.
english: And whenever Moses went out to the tent, all the people rose and stood at the entrances to their tents, watching Moses until he entered the tent.

twi: Ɔrewura mu a, omununkum fadum behyia no wɔ ɔkwan no ano na Awurade nam mu ne Mose akasa.
