english: As Moses went into the tent, the pillar of cloud would come down and stay at the entrance, while the Lord spoke with Moses.

twi: Bere biara a nnipa no behu omununkum fadum no sɛ egyina ntamadan no pon ano no, wɔn nyinaa bɛsɔre akotow nea wobehu wɔ wɔn ntamadan no pon ano no.
english: Whenever the people saw the pillar of cloud standing at the entrance to the tent, they all stood and worshiped, each at the entrance to their tent.

twi: Ɔdan no mu, na Awurade kasa kyerɛ Mose anim ne anim, sɛnea obi ne nʼadamfo di nkɔmmɔ. Na sɛ Mose san kɔ nsraban no hɔ a, aberante a ɔboa no a wɔfrɛ no Yosua (Nun ba) no de, ɔtena Ahyiae Ntamadan no mu ara kosi sɛ Mose bɛsan aba.
english: The Lord would speak to Moses face to face, as one speaks to a friend. Then Moses would return to the camp, but his young aide Joshua son of Nun did not leave the tent.

twi: Mose ka kyerɛɛ Awurade se, “Daa woka kyerɛ me se, ‘Fa saa nnipa yi kɔ bɔhyɛ asase no so, nanso wonkyerɛɛ me onipa a ɔnka me ho ne me nkɔ. Wuse woyɛ mʼadamfo a woayɛ me adɔe bebree.’
english: Moses said to the Lord, “You have been telling me, ‘Lead these people,’ but you have not let me know whom you will send with me. You have said, ‘I know you by name and you have found favor with me.’

twi: Na sɛ saa na ɛte a, di mʼanim kyerɛ me faako a ɛyɛ wo pɛ sɛ mefa na ama mate wo ase na mafa wo kwan so pɛpɛɛpɛ. Na mma wo werɛ mfi sɛ saa ɔman yi yɛ wo nkurɔfo.”
english: If you are pleased with me, teach me your ways so I may know you and continue to find favor with you. Remember that this nation is your people.”

twi: Na Awurade buaa no se, “Mʼankasa me ne wo bɛkɔ na woadi nkonim.”
english: The Lord replied, “My Presence will go with you, and I will give you rest.”

twi: Nanso Mose kae se, “Sɛ wo ne yɛn renkɔ de a, mma yemmfi ha nnkɔ.
english: Then Moses said to him, “If your Presence does not go with us, do not send us up from here.

twi: Sɛ wo ne yɛn ankɔ a, hena na obehu sɛ me ne me nkurɔfo anya wo hɔ adom a ama nsonoe abɛda yɛn ne asase sofo a wɔaka no ntam?”
english: How will anyone know that you are pleased with me and with your people unless you go with us? What else will distinguish me and your people from all the other people on the face of the earth?”

twi: Awurade buaa Mose se, “Ampa ara, mɛyɛ wʼabisade ama wo, efisɛ woanya ahummɔbɔ afi me nkyɛn na woyɛ mʼadamfo.”
english: And the Lord said to Moses, “I will do the very thing you have asked, because I am pleased with you and I know you by name.”

twi: Na Mose srɛɛ sɛ ɔpɛ sɛ ohu Onyankopɔn anuonyam.
english: Then Moses said, “Now show me your glory.”

twi: Awurade buae se, “Mɛma mo ahu mʼadɔe, na mɛbɔ me din Awurade no akyerɛ mo. Nea mepɛ sɛ mihu no mmɔbɔ no, mehu no mmɔbɔ, na nea mepɛ sɛ meyɛ no adɔe nso, mɛyɛ no adɔe.
english: And the Lord said, “I will cause all my goodness to pass in front of you, and I will proclaim my name, the Lord, in your presence. I will have mercy on whom I will have mercy, and I will have compassion on whom I will have compassion.

twi: Nanso morenhu mʼanuonyam, efisɛ obiara renhu mʼanim ntena nkwa mu.
english: But,” he said, “you cannot see my face, for no one may see me and live.”

twi: “Nanso gyina ɔbotan yi so wɔ me nkyɛn ha.
english: Then the Lord said, “There is a place near me where you may stand on a rock.

twi: Na sɛ mʼanuonyam resen a, mede wo bɛhyɛ ɔbotan no mu na mede me nsa akata wo so akosi sɛ metwa mu.
english: When my glory passes by, I will put you in a cleft in the rock and cover you with my hand until I have passed by.

twi: Afei, meyi me nsa na woahu mʼakyi, na mʼanim de, ɛnsɛ sɛ wohu.”
english: Then I will remove my hand and you will see my back; but my face must not be seen.”

twi: Onyankopɔn Kyerɛw Apam No BioAwurade ka kyerɛɛ Mose se, “Yɛ abo kyerɛw apon abien te sɛ nea woyɛɛ kan no na mɛkyerɛw mmara koro no ara sɛnea na ɛwɔ nea wububuu mu no so ara pɛ ama wo.
english: The Lord said to Moses, “Chisel out two stone tablets like the first ones, and I will write on them the words that were on the first tablets, which you broke.

twi: Siesie wo ho na bra Sinai Bepɔw so anɔpa na fa wo ho bɛkyerɛ me.
english: Be ready in the morning, and then come up on Mount Sinai. Present yourself to me there on top of the mountain.

twi: Mfa obiara nka wo ho na ɛnsɛ sɛ obiara bɛn bepɔw no ho baabiara. Mma mmoa biara nkɔ adidi mmɛn bepɔw no.”
english: No one is to come with you or be seen anywhere on the mountain; not even the flocks and herds may graze in front of the mountain.”

twi: Enti Mose twaa kyerɛw apon abien te sɛ kan de no de kɔɔ Sinai Bepɔw so anɔpahema sɛnea Awurade hyɛe no no.
english: So Moses chiseled out two stone tablets like the first ones and went up Mount Sinai early in the morning, as the Lord had commanded him; and he carried the two stone tablets in his hands.

twi: Awurade sian baa sɛ omununkum fadum begyinaa Mose ho bɔɔ ne din kronkron Awurade no.
english: Then the Lord came down in the cloud and stood there with him and proclaimed his name, the Lord.

twi: Awurade faa Mose anim frɛɛ no kae se, “Me, Awurade, Onyankopɔn mmɔborɔhunufo ne ɔdomfo a me bo kyɛ fuw na mewɔ ɔdɔ na midi nokware nso;
english: And he passed in front of Moses, proclaiming, “The Lord, the Lord, the compassionate and gracious God, slow to anger, abounding in love and faithfulness,

twi: me Awurade, medɔ nnipa mpempem na mede atirimɔden, atuatew ne bɔne kyɛ. Nanso metwe afɔdi aso na metwe Agyanom, mma ne nananom aso kosi awo ntoatoaso abiɛsa ne anan aso.”
english: maintaining love to thousands, and forgiving wickedness, rebellion and sin. Yet he does not leave the guilty unpunished; he punishes the children and their children for the sin of the parents to the third and fourth generation.”

twi: Mose kotow Awurade som no.
english: Moses bowed to the ground at once and worshiped.

twi: Ɔkae se, “Sɛ ɛyɛ nokware pa ara sɛ woagye me ato mu de a, Awurade, wo ne yɛnkɔ bɔhyɛ asase no so. Saa nnipa yi aso yɛ den de, nanso fa yɛn bɔne kyɛ yɛn na gye yɛn sɛ wo ara wo nnipa.”
english: “Lord,” he said, “if I have found favor in your eyes, then let the Lord go with us. Although this is a stiff-necked people, forgive our wickedness and our sin, and take us as your inheritance.”

twi: Awurade buae se, “Eye, me ne wo bɛyɛ nhyehyɛe bi. Merebɛyɛ anwonwade bi a bi nsii asase so da, na ɛnam so ama Israelfo nyinaa ahu tumi a Awurade wɔ. Menam wo so na mɛyɛ saa tumide no.
english: Then the Lord said: “I am making a covenant with you. Before all your people I will do wonders never before done in any nation in all the world. The people you live among will see how awesome is the work that I, the Lord, will do for you.

twi: Wo fam de a wobɛyɛ ara ne sɛ, wubetie nsɛm a mɛhyɛ wo no na woayɛ ne nyinaa; na sɛ ɛba saa a, mɛpam Amorifo, Kanaanfo, Hetifo, Perisifo, Hewifo ne Yebusifo no nyinaa afi wʼanim.
english: Obey what I command you today. I will drive out before you the Amorites, Canaanites, Hittites, Perizzites, Hivites and Jebusites.

twi: Hwɛ wo ho so yiye pa ara na wo ne ɔman a worekɔ mu no mufo ampam, anyɛ saa a, wɔbɛyɛ mfiri wɔ mo mu a ebeyiyi mo.
english: Be careful not to make a treaty with those who live in the land where you are going, or they will be a snare among you.

twi: Bubu wɔn abosonsom afɔremuka no. Sɛe wɔn abo adum no na muntutu wɔn abosom no ngu.
english: Break down their altars, smash their sacred stones and cut down their Asherah poles.

twi: Na monnsom onyame foforo biara nka Awurade ho, na ɔno nko ara ne Onyankopɔn a ɛsɛ sɛ mosom no.
english: Do not worship any other god, for the Lord, whose name is Jealous, is a jealous God.

twi: “Wo ne onipa biara a ɔte asase no so nnyɛ asomdwoe apam biara, efisɛ wonni me nokware, na wɔbɔ afɔre ma wɔn anyame de tia me. Sɛ wo ne wɔn yɛ adwene a, wɔbɛto nsa afrɛ wo ama woakodi wɔn abosom so nnuan.
english: “Be careful not to make a treaty with those who live in the land; for when they prostitute themselves to their gods and sacrifice to them, they will invite you and you will eat their sacrifices.

twi: Afei nso, ɛyɛ saa a, mubegye wɔn mmabea aware ama mo mmabarima no akɔsom wɔn yerenom no anyame bi de atia me.
english: And when you choose some of their daughters as wives for your sons and those daughters prostitute themselves to their gods, they will lead your sons to do the same.

twi: “Monnyɛ ahoni biara.
english: “Do not make any idols.

twi: “Munni Apiti Afahyɛ no. Munni brodo a mmɔkaw nni mu nnanson sɛnea meka kyerɛɛ mo no. Monyɛ eyi afe biara mu ɔsram Abib (Yudafo ɔsram a edi kan) mu, efisɛ saa ɔsram no mu na mutu fii Misraim.
english: “Celebrate the Festival of Unleavened Bread. For seven days eat bread made without yeast, as I commanded you. Do this at the appointed time in the month of Aviv, for in that month you came out of Egypt.

twi: “Abakan biara yɛ me dea, sɛ ɛyɛ nantwi, oguan anaa abirekyi.
english: “The first offspring of every womb belongs to me, including all the firstborn males of your livestock, whether from herd or flock.

twi: Afurum ba a ɔyɛ abakan de, wɔmfa no nsesa oguamma. Na sɛ wompɛ sɛ wode no di nsesa de a, bu ne kɔn mu. Mo mmabarima de, munnye wɔn nyinaa.“Obiara mma mʼanim a onkura akyɛde bi.
english:
Redeem the firstborn donkey with a lamb, but if you do not redeem it, break its neck. Redeem all your firstborn sons.
“No one is to appear before me empty-handed.

twi: “Nnansia pɛ na momfa nyɛ adwuma. Da a ɛto so ason no de, munnni dwuma biara. Ofuntumbere anaa otwabere mpo, momfa nnansia nyɛ adwuma. Da a ɛto so ason no, monhome.
english: “Six days you shall labor, but on the seventh day you shall rest; even during the plowing season and harvest you must rest.

twi: “Monkae na munni saa afahyɛ abiɛsa a ɛwɔ afe mu no nyinaa. Eyinom ne: Otwabere Afahyɛ (anaasɛ Pentekoste), Atoko a edi kan Afahyɛ ne Asese Afahyɛ.
english: “Celebrate the Festival of Weeks with the firstfruits of the wheat harvest, and the Festival of Ingathering at the turn of the year.

twi: Saa afahyɛ abiɛsa yi mu biara du so a, ɛsɛ sɛ Israelfo mmarima ne mmarimaa nyinaa ba Awurade anim.
english: Three times a year all your men are to appear before the Sovereign Lord, the God of Israel.

twi: Sɛ mokɔ Awurade mo Nyankopɔn anim saa mprɛnsa no nyinaa afe biara mu a, obiara nni hɔ a ɔbɛtoa mo abedi mo asase no so. Mɛpam saa aman no wɔ mo anim na matrɛw mo ahye mu.
english: I will drive out nations before you and enlarge your territory, and no one will covet your land when you go up three times each year to appear before the Lord your God.

twi: “Mommfa brodo a mmɔkaw wɔ mu mmɔ me afɔre. Na Twam Afahyɛ nam no nso, mommfa bi nsi hɔ mma ade nkye so.
english: “Do not offer the blood of a sacrifice to me along with anything containing yeast, and do not let any of the sacrifice from the Passover Festival remain until morning.

twi: “Sɛ mutwa mo nnɔbae a, Momfa mo nnɔbae mu nea ɛsɔ ani koraa no mmra Awurade mo Nyankopɔn fi.“Monnoa abirekyi ba wɔ ne na nufusu mu.”
english:
“Bring the best of the firstfruits of your soil to the house of the Lord your God.
“Do not cook a young goat in its mother’s milk.”

twi: Na Awurade ka kyerɛɛ Mose se, “Kyerɛw saa mmara a mede ama wo yi nyinaa gu hɔ, efisɛ ɛyɛ me ne wo, Israel ntam apam.”
english: Then the Lord said to Moses, “Write down these words, for in accordance with these words I have made a covenant with you and with Israel.”

twi: Mose ne Awurade de adaduanan, awia ne anadwo, dii nkitaho wɔ bepɔw no so, na saa bere no, Mose annidi, annom. Saa bere no, Onyankopɔn kyerɛw Mmaransɛm Du no guu ɔbo kyerɛwpon no so.
english: Moses was there with the Lord forty days and forty nights without eating bread or drinking water. And he wrote on the tablets the words of the covenant—the Ten Commandments.

twi: Bere a Mose de kyerɛw apon no fi Onyankopɔn nkyɛn resian bepɔw no, na onnim sɛ nʼanim rehyerɛn.
english: When Moses came down from Mount Sinai with the two tablets of the covenant law in his hands, he was not aware that his face was radiant because he had spoken with the Lord.

twi: Esiane nʼanim hyerɛn a na ɛhyerɛn no nti, Aaron ne Israelfo no huu Mose no, wosuroe sɛ wɔbɛbɛn no.
english: When Aaron and all the Israelites saw Moses, his face was radiant, and they were afraid to come near him.

twi: Nanso Mose frɛɛ wɔn baa ne nkyɛn maa Aaron ne ɔman no mu ntuanofo ne no bɛkasae.
english: But Moses called to them; so Aaron and all the leaders of the community came back to him, and he spoke to them.

twi: Akyiri no, nnipa no nyinaa baa ne nkyɛn ma ɔde mmaransɛm a Awurade de maa no wɔ bepɔw no so hɔ no maa wɔn.
english: Afterward all the Israelites came near him, and he gave them all the commands the Lord had given him on Mount Sinai.

twi: Mose ne wɔn kasa wiee no, ɔde nkataanim kataa nʼanim,
english: When Moses finished speaking to them, he put a veil over his face.

twi: na bere biara a ɔbɛkɔ Ahyiae Ntamadan mu hɔ ne Awurade akɔkasa no, oyi nkataanim no kosi sɛ ɔbɛsan aba bio; ɔba saa a, asɛm biara a Onyankopɔn aka akyerɛ no no, na ɔno nso ka kyerɛ nnipa no
english: But whenever he entered the Lord’s presence to speak with him, he removed the veil until he came out. And when he came out and told the Israelites what he had been commanded,

twi: a wohu sɛ nʼanim ayɛ hyerɛnn no. Akyiri no, ɔde nkataanim no kata nʼanim bio kosi sɛ ɔbɛkɔ Onyankopɔn nkyɛn na ɔne no akɔkasa.
english: they saw that his face was radiant. Then Moses would put the veil back over his face until he went in to speak with the Lord.

twi: Homeda Ho MmaraAfei, Mose frɛɛ Israelmma nyinaa ne wɔn yɛɛ nhyiamu ka kyerɛɛ wɔn se, “Eyi ne Awurade mmara a ɛsɛ sɛ mudi so.
english: Moses assembled the whole Israelite community and said to them, “These are the things the Lord has commanded you to do:

twi: Monyɛ adwuma nnansia. Na da a ɛto so ason no de, momfa nhome; ɛyɛ da kronkron a ɛsɛ sɛ mode som Awurade. Obiara a ɔbɛyɛ adwuma biara saa da no, ɛsɛ sɛ wokum no.
english: For six days, work is to be done, but the seventh day shall be your holy day, a day of sabbath rest to the Lord. Whoever does any work on it is to be put to death.

twi: Da no, ogya mpo, monnsɔ bi ano wɔ mo afi mu.”
english: Do not light a fire in any of your dwellings on the Sabbath day.”

twi: Mose ka kyerɛɛ nnipa no nyinaa se, “Nsɛm a Awurade ahyɛ sɛ monyɛ ni:
english: Moses said to the whole Israelite community, “This is what the Lord has commanded:

twi: Obiara a ɔpɛ no mfa saa afɔrebɔde yi mu biara mmrɛ Awurade:“Sikakɔkɔɔ, dwetɛ, kɔbere mfrafrae;
english: From what you have, take an offering for the Lord. Everyone who is willing is to bring to the Lord an offering of gold, silver and bronze;

twi: ntama a wɔde asaawa tuntum, bibiri ne koogyan ayɛ neabirekyi nwi,
english: blue, purple and scarlet yarn and fine linen; goat hair;

twi: odwennini nwoma a wɔahyɛ no aduru kɔkɔɔ ne abirekyi nwoma a wɔahyɛ,ɔkanto dua;
english: ram skins dyed red and another type of durable leather; acacia wood;

twi: ngo a wɔde begu akanea no mu, ɔhyew nnuhuam a wɔde bɛyɛ ɔsrango ne;ɔhyew aduhuam;
english: olive oil for the light; spices for the anointing oil and for the fragrant incense;

twi: abo a ɛte sɛ apopobibiri ne abo a wɔde bɛhyehyɛ asɔfotade no ne nʼadɛbo no mu.
english: and onyx stones and other gems to be mounted on the ephod and breastpiece.

twi: “Mo a mowɔ nimdeɛ wɔ biribiyɛ ho no, mo nyinaa mommra na monyɛ nea Awurade aka no nyinaa te sɛ:
english: “All who are skilled among you are to come and make everything the Lord has commanded:

twi: “Ahyiae Ntamadan no so ntama ne ne nkataso, nkɔtɔkoro, mpuran nnua a esisi mu, adum ne nnyinaso;
english: the tabernacle with its tent and its covering, clasps, frames, crossbars, posts and bases;

twi: Apam Adaka no ne nnua a esisi ho; Mpata agua ntwamtam a ɛkata kronkronbea hɔ,
english: the ark with its poles and the atonement cover and the curtain that shields it;

twi: ɔpon ne nnua a wɔde soa ne ɛho nneɛma nyinaa, Ɔkyerɛ Brodo;
english: the table with its poles and all its articles and the bread of the Presence;

twi: akanea nnua ne nʼakanea ne ngo;
english: the lampstand that is for light with its accessories, lamps and oil for the light;

twi: aduhuam afɔremuka ne nnua a wɔde bɛsoa; ɔsrango ne aduhuam a eyi hua pa,nsɛnanim a wɔde bɛsɛn Ahyiae Ntamadan no pon ano;
english: the altar of incense with its poles, the anointing oil and the fragrant incense; the curtain for the doorway at the entrance to the tabernacle;

twi: kɔbere Afɔremuka a wɔde bɛbɔ ɔhyew afɔre, kɔbere ntwitae ne nnua a wɔde bɛsoa ho nneɛma,ne nea wɔhoro mu nneɛma ne ne ntaamu,
english: the altar of burnt offering with its bronze grating, its poles and all its utensils; the bronze basin with its stand;

twi: adiwo hɔ no ntwamtam, adum ne ne nnyinaso, ntama a wɔde bɛkata adiwo hɔ kwan ano,
english: the curtains of the courtyard with its posts and bases, and the curtain for the entrance to the courtyard;

twi: Ahyiae Ntamadan no adiwo hɔ nnua ne ne ntampehama,
english: the tent pegs for the tabernacle and for the courtyard, and their ropes;

twi: asɔfotade a ɛyɛ fɛ a ɔsɔfo no bɛhyɛ asɔre wɔ kronkronbea hɔ ne Aaron ntade kronkron a sɛ ne mmabarima no yɛ asɔfodwuma a, wɔbɛhyɛ bi.”
english: the woven garments worn for ministering in the sanctuary—both the sacred garments for Aaron the priest and the garments for his sons when they serve as priests.”

twi: Na Israelmma nyinaa fii Mose anim,
english: Then the whole Israelite community withdrew from Moses’ presence,

twi: na wɔn a Onyankopɔn honhom kaa wɔn koma no de wɔn akyɛde a wɔde besi Ahyiae Ntamadan no ne ɛho nneɛma ne nea wɔde bɛpam atade kronkron no bae.
english: and everyone who was willing and whose heart moved them came and brought an offering to the Lord for the work on the tent of meeting, for all its service, and for the sacred garments.

twi: Mmea ne mmarima a asɛm no kaa wɔn koma no nyinaa bae. Wɔde sikakɔkɔɔ, agude, nsonkaa, nkaa, kɔnmuade ne sika adwinne bebree brɛɛ Awurade.
english: All who were willing, men and women alike, came and brought gold jewelry of all kinds: brooches, earrings, rings and ornaments. They all presented their gold as a wave offering to the Lord.

twi: Wɔn a wɔwɔ ntama pa, kuntu a ɛyɛ tuntum, bibiri, abirekyi nwoma a wɔahyɛ, odwennini nwoma a wɔahyɛ no kɔkɔɔ anaa aboa nwoma a ɛyɛ fɛ nso de bae.
english: Everyone who had blue, purple or scarlet yarn or fine linen, or goat hair, ram skins dyed red or the other durable leather brought them.

twi: Afoforo nso de dwetɛ ne kɔbere brɛɛ Awurade sɛ wɔn akyɛde. Ebinom de ɔkanto nnua nso bae.
english: Those presenting an offering of silver or bronze brought it as an offering to the Lord, and everyone who had acacia wood for any part of the work brought it.

twi: Mmea no bi a wonim adepam yiye no too asaawa tuntum, bibiri ne koogyan de yɛɛ ntama a ɛyɛ fɛ de brɛɛ Awurade.
english: Every skilled woman spun with her hands and brought what she had spun—blue, purple or scarlet yarn or fine linen.

twi: Afoforo nso de anigye nam wɔn dom akyɛde so de abirekyi nwi yɛɛ ntama.
english: And all the women who were willing and had the skill spun the goat hair.

twi: Mpanyimfo a wodi wɔn anim no de abo a ɛte sɛ apopobibiri bae sɛ wɔmfa nyɛ asɔfotade no ne nʼadɛbo.
english: The leaders brought onyx stones and other gems to be mounted on the ephod and breastpiece.

twi: Wɔde nnuhuam ne ngo a wɔde begu akanea mu ne nea wɔde bɛfra ɔsrango no ne nnuhuam no ama adi mu no nso bae.
english: They also brought spices and olive oil for the light and for the anointing oil and for the fragrant incense.

twi: Eyi di ho adanse sɛ Israel mmarima ne mmea a na wɔpɛ sɛ wɔboa dwumadi a Awurade nam Mose so de hyɛɛ wɔn nsa no fi wɔn pɛ mu de wɔn akyɛde brɛɛ no.
english: All the Israelite men and women who were willing brought to the Lord freewill offerings for all the work the Lord through Moses had commanded them to do.

twi: Mose ka kyerɛɛ Israelfo no se, “Awurade ayi Besaleel, Uri ba a ɔyɛ Hur a ofi Yuda abusua mu nena
english: Then Moses said to the Israelites, “See, the Lord has chosen Bezalel son of Uri, the son of Hur, of the tribe of Judah,

twi: no sɛ ɔno Onyankopɔn Honhom ahyɛ no ma. Wama no nyansa, tumi ne adwene a ɔde besi Ahyiae Ntamadan no ayɛ biribiara a ɛwɔ mu.
english: and he has filled him with the Spirit of God, with wisdom, with understanding, with knowledge and with all kinds of skills—

twi: Obetumi adi adwinni afi sikakɔkɔɔ, dwetɛ, ne kɔbere mu.
english: to make artistic designs for work in gold, silver and bronze,

twi: Obetumi adi abo adwinni na obetumi asen nnua nso; nokware mu, ɔwɔ ɔdom akyɛde bebree.
english: to cut and set stones, to work in wood and to engage in all kinds of artistic crafts.

twi: Na Onyankopɔn ama ɔno ne Oholiab a ɔyɛ Ahisamak a ofi Dan abusuakuw mu babarima ɔdom akyɛde a wɔnam so kyerɛ afoforo ade.
english: And he has given both him and Oholiab son of Ahisamak, of the tribe of Dan, the ability to teach others.

twi: Onyankopɔn ama wɔn baanu akyɛde sononko sɛ adwumfo, duadwumfo, adenwenfo a wotumi nwen nneɛma a ɛyɛ fɛ gu ntama pa a ɛyɛ tuntum, bibiri ne koogyan mu. Wonim saa adwinne yi nyinaa di ma ɛboro so.
english: He has filled them with skill to do all kinds of work as engravers, designers, embroiderers in blue, purple and scarlet yarn and fine linen, and weavers—all of them skilled workers and designers.

twi: Adwumfo a wɔaka a Onyankopɔn ama wɔn ɔdom akyɛde no nyinaa bɛboa Besaleel ne Oholiab na wɔasi asiesie Ahyiae Ntamadan no mu sɛnea Awurade ahyɛ no.”
english: So Bezalel, Oholiab and every skilled person to whom the Lord has given skill and ability to know how to carry out all the work of constructing the sanctuary are to do the work just as the Lord has commanded.”

twi: Enti Mose ka kyerɛɛ Besaleel ne Oholiab ne wɔn a wɔaka na wɔte nka sɛ ɛsɛ sɛ wɔboa dwumadi no sɛ womfiti ase.
english: Then Moses summoned Bezalel and Oholiab and every skilled person to whom the Lord had given ability and who was willing to come and do the work.

twi: Mose de nneɛma a nnipa no de bɛkyɛɛ no maa wɔn, na adekyee biara nso, na wonya akyɛde foforo.
english: They received from Moses all the offerings the Israelites had brought to carry out the work of constructing the sanctuary. And the people continued to bring freewill offerings morning after morning.

twi: Akyiri no, adwumayɛfo no nyinaa gyaee wɔn adwumayɛ no
english: So all the skilled workers who were doing all the work on the sanctuary left what they were doing

twi: kɔɔ Mose nkyɛn kɔka kyerɛɛ no se, “Nneɛma a yɛn nsa aka no dɔɔso sen nea yehia.”
english: and said to Moses, “The people are bringing more than enough for doing the work the Lord commanded to be done.”

twi: Enti Mose somaa obi maa ɔkɔɔ wɔn nyinaa so kɔka kyerɛɛ wɔn se, afei de, obiara mmmɛkyɛ wɔn ade bio. Na obiara amfa hwee amma bio.
english: Then Moses gave an order and they sent this word throughout the camp: “No man or woman is to make anything else as an offering for the sanctuary.” And so the people were restrained from bringing more,

twi: Efisɛ na nneɛma a wɔwɔ no bɛso dwuma no di ama aboro so mpo.
english: because what they already had was more than enough to do all the work.

twi: Wɔn a wonim adwinni pa ara no de asaawa a wɔanwen yɛɛ Ntamadan no nsɛnanotam du a emu bi yɛ tuntum, bibiri ne koogyan a wɔayɛ kerubim agu mu.
english: All those who were skilled among the workers made the tabernacle with ten curtains of finely twisted linen and blue, purple and scarlet yarn, with cherubim woven into them by expert hands.

twi: Nkataano du no nyinaa kɛse yɛ pɛ. Emu biara tenten yɛ anammɔn aduanan abien na ne trɛw nso yɛ anammɔn asia.
english: All the curtains were the same size—twenty-eight cubits long and four cubits wide.

twi: Wɔkekaa ntama bamma anum sisii anim nyaa nkataano baako. Na wɔkekaa ntama bamma anum a aka no nso sisii anim nyaa nkataano foforo.
english: They joined five of the curtains together and did the same with the other five.

twi: Wɔde ntama bibiri bamma aduonum wurawuraa nkataano a wɔkeka sisii anim no mu biara ano
english: Then they made loops of blue material along the edge of the end curtain in one set, and the same was done with the end curtain in the other set.

twi: a hentia baako biara ne baako di nhwɛanim.
english: They also made fifty loops on one curtain and fifty loops on the end curtain of the other set, with the loops opposite each other.

twi: Afei, wɔyɛɛ sika nkɔtɔkoro aduonum de susoo nkɔtɔkoro no mu maa nkataano ahorow abien no yɛɛ nkataano baako.
english: Then they made fifty gold clasps and used them to fasten the two sets of curtains together so that the tabernacle was a unit.

twi: Wɔde ntama nkataso dubaako a wɔde mmirekyi nwi na ayɛ
english: They made curtains of goat hair for the tent over the tabernacle—eleven altogether.

twi: a ne nyinaa tenten yɛ anammɔn aduanan anum na ne trɛw yɛ anammɔn asia kataa Ntamadan no so.
english: All eleven curtains were the same size—thirty cubits long and four cubits wide.

twi: Besaleel kekaa saa nkataso yi anum sisii anim ma ɛyɛɛ bamma tenten baako na ɔsan de afoforo asia sisii anim maa ɛno nso yɛɛ bamma tenten baako.
english: They joined five of the curtains into one set and the other six into another set.

twi: Afei, ɔbobɔɔ nkɔtɔkoro aduonum wɔ emu biara ano
english: Then they made fifty loops along the edge of the end curtain in one set and also along the edge of the end curtain in the other set.

twi: na ɔyɛɛ kɔbere nkɔtɔkoro aduonum de koakoaa nkɔtɔkoro no, sɛnea ɛbɛma nkataho no akyere pintinn.
english: They made fifty bronze clasps to fasten the tent together as a unit.

twi: Wosiesiee nneɛma ahorow abien de bɔɔ ɔdan no so. Nea edi kan no yɛ odwennini were a wahyɛ no kɔkɔɔ, nea ɛto so abien yɛ abirekyi were a ɛsɔ.
english: Then they made for the tent a covering of ram skins dyed red, and over that a covering of the other durable leather.

twi: Wɔde ɔkanto yɛɛ ntaaboo de twaa Ahyiae Ntamadan no ho.
english: They made upright frames of acacia wood for the tabernacle.

twi: Mpuran biara sorokɔ nyɛ anammɔn dunum na ne trɛw nyɛ anammɔn abien ne kakra,
english: Each frame was ten cubits long and a cubit and a half wide,

twi: nkɔtɔkoro abien wɔ mpuran biara ase, na mpuran biara yɛ pɛ.
english: with two projections set parallel to each other. They made all the frames of the tabernacle in this way.

twi: Na Ahyiae Ntamadan no ntaaboo aduonu kyerɛ nʼanafo
english: They made twenty frames for the south side of the tabernacle

twi: a wɔn ase sisi dwetɛ nnyinaso aduanan so. Nnyinaso no abien abien hyehyɛ mpuran biara ase.
english: and made forty silver bases to go under them—two bases for each frame, one under each projection.

twi: Ahyiae Ntamadan no atifi fam nso, na wɔde ntaaboo aduonu atwa ho
english: For the other side, the north side of the tabernacle, they made twenty frames

twi: a esisi dwetɛ nnyinaso aduanan so a mpuran baako besi nnyinaso abien so.
english: and forty silver bases—two under each frame.

twi: Ahyiae Ntamadan no fa a ɛkyerɛ atɔe fam no yɛ nʼakyi. Ɛno nso, wɔde ntaaboo asia na atwa ho,
english: They made six frames for the far end, that is, the west end of the tabernacle,

twi: na ne twɔtwɔw biara so nso ntaaboo abien sisi hɔ.
english: and two frames were made for the corners of the tabernacle at the far end.

twi: Na mpuran a ɛbobɔ so abien abien sisi twɔtwɔw abien no biara so fi ase de kosi soro a wɔde nkaa asuso mu a ne nyinaa yɛ pɛ.
english: At these two corners the frames were double from the bottom all the way to the top and fitted into a single ring; both were made alike.

twi: Enti mpuran awotwe ne dwetɛ nnyinaso dunsia a abien wɔ mpuran biara ase na wɔde yɛe.
english: So there were eight frames and sixteen silver bases—two under each frame.

twi: Afei, ɔyɛɛ ɔkanto nnua bi de beabeaa ntaaboo no mu. Mmeamu nnua no anum kɔ mpuran no fa baako.
english: They also made crossbars of acacia wood: five for the frames on one side of the tabernacle,

twi: Wɔyɛɛ afoforo anum nso kɔɔ ɔfa baako. Na mmeamu nnua no anum bɔ ntaaboo a ɛwɔ ntamadan no akyi a ani kyerɛ atɔe fam.
english: five for those on the other side, and five for the frames on the west, at the far end of the tabernacle.

twi: Wɔbɔɔ mmeamu dua baako de bɔɔ ntaaboo no mfimfini. Wɔde twaa mu fi ti kɔkaa ti.
english: They made the center crossbar so that it extended from end to end at the middle of the frames.

twi: Na wɔde sikakɔkɔɔ adura ntaaboo no ho, na wɔde sikakɔkɔɔ nkaa asuso mmeamu dua no mu ama no agyina. Na sikakɔkɔɔ dura mmeamu dua no nso ho.
english: They overlaid the frames with gold and made gold rings to hold the crossbars. They also overlaid the crossbars with gold.

twi: Wɔde ntama pa a ɛyɛ tuntum, bibiri ne koogyan a wɔanwen kerubim agu mu fɛfɛɛfɛ na ayɛ ntwamtam no wɔ Ntamadan no mu.
english: They made the curtain of blue, purple and scarlet yarn and finely twisted linen, with cherubim woven into it by a skilled worker.

twi: Na wɔyɛɛ ɔkanto nnua afadum anan a wɔde sikakɔkɔɔ adura ho ne sikakɔkɔɔ nsusomu anan maa ntwamtam no. Na afadum anan no mu biara si dwetɛ nnyinaso anan no baako so.
english: They made four posts of acacia wood for it and overlaid them with gold. They made gold hooks for them and cast their four silver bases.

twi: Afei, wɔyɛɛ Ahyiae Ntamadan no ano nkataanim. Wɔde asaawatam a ɛyɛ fɛ a wɔde tuntum, bibiri ne koogyan adi mu adwinni na ɛyɛe.
english: For the entrance to the tent they made a curtain of blue, purple and scarlet yarn and finely twisted linen—the work of an embroiderer;

twi: Wɔde nkɔtɔkoro anum na asuso saa nkataanim yi mu de akyekyere nnua anum no. Nnua no ne ɛho nneɛma ne pema no nyinaa, wɔde sikakɔkɔɔ adura ho na ne nnyinaso anum no nso, wɔde kɔbere na ɛyɛe.
english: and they made five posts with hooks for them. They overlaid the tops of the posts and their bands with gold and made their five bases of bronze.

twi: Apam Adaka No YɛAfei, Besaleel yɛɛ Apam Adaka no. Ɔde ɔkanto na ɛyɛe. Na ne tenten yɛ anammɔn abiɛsa ne fa, ne trɛw nso yɛ anammɔn abien ne fa ne ntwemu ne sorokɔ nso yɛ anammɔn abien ne fa.
english: Bezalel made the ark of acacia wood—two and a half cubits long, a cubit and a half wide, and a cubit and a half high.

twi: Na wɔde sikakɔkɔɔ duraa ho ne emu nyinaa na wɔde bi beabea ho nyinaa.
english: He overlaid it with pure gold, both inside and out, and made a gold molding around it.

twi: Na wɔde sikakɔkɔɔ nkaa hyehyɛɛ nʼanan anan no a nkaa abien wɔ ɔfa biara.
english: He cast four gold rings for it and fastened them to its four feet, with two rings on one side and two rings on the other.

twi: Osen ɔkanto nnua bi de sikakɔkɔɔ duraa ho.
english: Then he made poles of acacia wood and overlaid them with gold.

twi: Na wɔde nnua no hyehyɛɛ adaka no nkyɛn nkaa no mu wɔde bɛsoa.
english: And he inserted the poles into the rings on the sides of the ark to carry it.

twi: Afei, ɔde sikakɔkɔɔ ankasa yɛɛ ne mmuaso a wɔfrɛ no Mpata Agua. Na ne ntwemu yɛ anammɔn abiɛsa ne fa, na ne trɛw nso yɛ anammɔn abien ne fa.
english: He made the atonement cover of pure gold—two and a half cubits long and a cubit and a half wide.

twi: Ɔboroo sikakɔkɔɔ ma ɛyɛɛ tratraa de yɛɛ kerubim abien na ɔde tetaree adaka no mmuaso no ti ne ti.
english: Then he made two cherubim out of hammered gold at the ends of the cover.

twi: Wɔde kerubim no tetaree adaka no atifi ne nʼanafo na ɛne adaka no nkataso no yɛɛ baako.
english: He made one cherub on one end and the second cherub on the other; at the two ends he made them of one piece with the cover.

twi: Na kerubim no di nhwɛanim a wɔasisi wɔn ti ase rehwɛ Mpata Agua no na wɔatrɛtrɛw wɔn ntaban mu akata so.
english: The cherubim had their wings spread upward, overshadowing the cover with them. The cherubim faced each other, looking toward the cover.

twi: Afei, ɔde ɔkanto yɛɛ ɔpon a ne ntwemu yɛ anammɔn abiɛsa; ne trɛw yɛ ɔnammɔn baako ne fa na ne sorokɔ yɛ anammɔn abien ne fa.
english: They made the table of acacia wood—two cubits long, a cubit wide and a cubit and a half high.

twi: Na wɔde sikakɔkɔɔ duraa ho na woguu bi wɔ ne ntwea so nyinaa.
english: Then they overlaid it with pure gold and made a gold molding around it.

twi: Wɔyɛɛ adaka no ho ntetareho a ne trɛw yɛ nsateaa anan twaa ɔpon no ano ho hyiae, na wɔde sikakɔkɔɔ hankare faa ho.
english: They also made around it a rim a handbreadth wide and put a gold molding on the rim.

twi: Afei, wɔyɛɛ sikakɔkɔɔ nkaa anan, na ɔde hyehyɛɛ ɔpon no anan anan no nyinaa ase.
english: They cast four gold rings for the table and fastened them to the four corners, where the four legs were.

twi: Wɔde nnua no hyehyɛɛ saa nkaa no mu a wɔde bɛma ɔpon no so asoa.
english: The rings were put close to the rim to hold the poles used in carrying the table.

twi: Wɔde ɔkanto nnua a wɔde sikakɔkɔɔ agu ho yɛɛ nnua a wɔde bɛsoa.
english: The poles for carrying the table were made of acacia wood and were overlaid with gold.

twi: Wɔde sikakɔkɔɔ yɛɛ nsanka, mprɛte, nsukuruwa ne nkoraa. Saa nneɛma yi na wɔde bedi ahwiesa afɔrebɔ ho dwuma.
english: And they made from pure gold the articles for the table—its plates and dishes and bowls and its pitchers for the pouring out of drink offerings.

twi: Bio, wɔde sikakɔkɔɔ a wɔaboro yɛɛ kaneadua. Ne nnyinaso, nʼabaa, nea wɔde akanea no hyehyɛ mu ne nhwiren a wɔde siesiee no nyinaa bɔ mu yɛ ade baako.
english: They made the lampstand of pure gold. They hammered out its base and shaft, and made its flowerlike cups, buds and blossoms of one piece with them.

twi: Kaneadua a ɛhyɛ mfimfini no wɔ nkorata asia a abiɛsa wɔ fa na abiɛsa nso wɔ fa.
english: Six branches extended from the sides of the lampstand—three on one side and three on the other.

twi: Wɔde nhwiren abiɛsa siesiee nkorata biara ho.
english: Three cups shaped like almond flowers with buds and blossoms were on one branch, three on the next branch and the same for all six branches extending from the lampstand.

twi: Na saa ara nso na kaneadua no, wodii nhwiren a ɛyɛ fɛ bi adwinni de siesiee no.
english: And on the lampstand were four cups shaped like almond flowers with buds and blossoms.

twi: Nhwiren no bi wɔ ne dua no ase wɔ nkorata abien biara ase. Afei, nhwiren no bi wɔ nkorata abien a ɛwɔ ase no ase, na bi nso wɔ nkorata abien a ɛwɔ soro no so. Ne nyinaa yɛ asia.
english: One bud was under the first pair of branches extending from the lampstand, a second bud under the second pair, and a third bud under the third pair—six branches in all.

twi: Nea wɔde siesiee kaneadua no ne ne nkorata no nyinaa yɛ ade baako a sikakɔkɔɔ ankasa a wɔaboro na wɔde yɛe.
english: The buds and the branches were all of one piece with the lampstand, hammered out of pure gold.

twi: Afei, ɔyɛɛ akanea ason, adaban adabaw, ne apampaa. Ne nyinaa wɔde sikakɔkɔɔ ankasa na ɛyɛe.
english: They made its seven lamps, as well as its wick trimmers and trays, of pure gold.

twi: Na kaneadua no ne ho nneɛma no mu duru yɛ kilogram aduasa anan a ne nyinaa yɛ sikakɔkɔɔ.
english: They made the lampstand and all its accessories from one talent of pure gold.

twi: Wɔde ɔkanto na ɛyɛɛ aduhuam afɔremuka no. Wɔyɛɛ no ahinanan a ne fa biara susuw nsateaa dunwɔtwe. Na ne sorokɔ yɛ basafa baako a mmɛn a etuatua ne ntwea so ntwea so no nso nyinaa ka bɔ mu ma ɛyɛ ade baako.
english: They made the altar of incense out of acacia wood. It was square, a cubit long and a cubit wide and two cubits high—its horns of one piece with it.

twi: Wɔde sikakɔkɔɔ duraa ne nyinaa ho, na oguu bi nso wɔ ne ntwea so nyinaa.
english: They overlaid the top and all the sides and the horns with pure gold, and made a gold molding around it.

twi: Wɔde sika nkaa abien abien susoo afanu no mu wɔ nea wɔyɛɛ nguguho no ase a wɔde besuso nnua a wɔde bɛsoa no mu.
english: They made two gold rings below the molding—two on each of the opposite sides—to hold the poles used to carry it.

twi: Nnua a na wɔde soa no yɛ ɔkanto nnua a wɔde sikakɔkɔɔ adura ho.
english: They made the poles of acacia wood and overlaid them with gold.

twi: Wɔfaa nnuhuamyɛfo mu abenfo kwan so fii nnuhuam mu yɛɛ ɔsrango kronkron a wɔde sra asɔfo ne ɔhyew nnuhuam no nso.
english: They also made the sacred anointing oil and the pure, fragrant incense—the work of a perfumer.

twi: Ɔhyew AfɔremukaƆhyew afɔremuka no nso, ɔkanto na wɔde yɛe. Woyii no ahinanan a ne fa biara susuw anammɔn ason ne fa na ne sorokɔ nso yɛ anammɔn anan ne fa.
english: They built the altar of burnt offering of acacia wood, three cubits high; it was square, five cubits long and five cubits wide.

twi: Na ne ntwea so anan no nyinaa mmɛn tuatua ho a ne nyinaa ka bɔ mu ma ɛyɛ ade baako a wɔde kɔbere adura ho.
english: They made a horn at each of the four corners, so that the horns and the altar were of one piece, and they overlaid the altar with bronze.

twi: Wɔyɛɛ afɔremuka no ho nneɛma te sɛ nkuku, sofi, hweaseammɔ, adinam ne nkankyee a wɔbɛnoa mu de kaa ho.
english: They made all its utensils of bronze—its pots, shovels, sprinkling bowls, meat forks and firepans.

twi: Afei, wɔde kɔbere nwenee afɔremuka no ho twitae a ɛte sɛ atena de sii adaka a ɛbɛdeda ogya adaka no mfimfini.
english: They made a grating for the altar, a bronze network, to be under its ledge, halfway up the altar.

twi: Wɔde nkaa anan anan sensɛn twaa ne fa biara ma wɔde nnua a wɔde bɛsoa no hyehyɛɛ mu.
english: They cast bronze rings to hold the poles for the four corners of the bronze grating.

twi: Ɔkanto nnua a wɔde kɔbere adura ho na wɔde yɛɛ nnua a wɔde bɛsoa no.
english: They made the poles of acacia wood and overlaid them with bronze.

twi: Wɔde nnua a wɔde soa no hyehyɛɛ nkaa no a ɛbobɔ afɔremuka no nkyɛn no mu. Ntaaboo na wɔde yɛe. Na emu da kwan nso.
english: They inserted the poles into the rings so they would be on the sides of the altar for carrying it. They made it hollow, out of boards.

twi: Wɔde kɔbere a wɔatwa afi kɔbere ahwehwɛ a mmea a wɔsom wɔ Ahyiae Ntamadan no ano no de kyɛe no na ɛyɛɛ ade a wɔhoro mu nneɛma ne ne ntaease no.
english: They made the bronze basin and its bronze stand from the mirrors of the women who served at the entrance to the tent of meeting.

twi: Afei, wɔyɛɛ adiwo. Na ɔfasu a ɛwɔ nʼanafo no ne tenten yɛ anammɔn ɔha aduonum a wɔde nnurahotam a wɔde asaawatam a ɛyɛ fɛ na ɛyɛe.
english: Next they made the courtyard. The south side was a hundred cubits long and had curtains of finely twisted linen,

twi: Nnua aduonu na wɔde besuso nnurahotam no mu. Ne nnyinaso yɛ kɔbere a dwetɛ nkɔtɔkoro ne pema ka ho.
english: with twenty posts and twenty bronze bases, and with silver hooks and bands on the posts.

twi: Na atifi ɔfasu no tenten yɛ anammɔn ɔha ne aduonum a kɔbere nnua aduonu ne ne nnyinaso a dwetɛ nkɔtɔkoro ne pema ka ho.
english: The north side was also a hundred cubits long and had twenty posts and twenty bronze bases, with silver hooks and bands on the posts.

twi: Atɔe fam fasu no trɛw yɛ anammɔn aduɔson anum. Wɔde nnurahotam faa ɔfasu no ho. Nnua du, ne nnyinaso ne dwetɛ nkɔtɔkoro ne ntwea na na ɛma saa ɔfasu no gyina.
english: The west end was fifty cubits wide and had curtains, with ten posts and ten bases, with silver hooks and bands on the posts.

twi: Na apuei fam no nso trɛw yɛ anammɔn aduɔson anum.
english: The east end, toward the sunrise, was also fifty cubits wide.

twi: Na adiwo hɔ kwan no wɔ apuei fam a wɔde nkataanim abien akata hɔ. Na nkataanim a ɛwɔ nifa so no tenten yɛ anammɔn aduonu abien ne fa, na nnua abiɛsa a esisi nnyinasode abiɛsa so na ekura mu,
english: Curtains fifteen cubits long were on one side of the entrance, with three posts and three bases,

twi: na nkataanim a ɛwɔ benkum so no nso tenten yɛ anammɔn aduonu abien ne fa a nnua abiɛsa a esisi nnyinasode abiɛsa so kura mu.
english: and curtains fifteen cubits long were on the other side of the entrance to the courtyard, with three posts and three bases.

twi: Asaawatam a ɛyɛ fɛ na wɔde nwenee nnurahotam a wɔde twaa adiwo hɔ no ho.
english: All the curtains around the courtyard were of finely twisted linen.

twi: Na dua biara wɔ ne kɔbere nnyinasode, nanso ɛho nkɔtɔkoro ne mfɛnsere no yɛ dwetɛ; nnua no atifi nyinaa na wɔde dwetɛ agu, na mfɛnsere a wɔde besuso nnurahotam no mu no nso, na ne nyinaa yɛ dwetɛ ankasa.
english: The bases for the posts were bronze. The hooks and bands on the posts were silver, and their tops were overlaid with silver; so all the posts of the courtyard had silver bands.

twi: Asaawatam a wɔde tuntum, bibiri ne koogyan anwen mu fɛfɛɛfɛ na wɔde yɛɛ nnurahotam kataa adiwo hɔ kwan no ano. Na ne tenten yɛ anammɔn aduasa na ne trɛw nso yɛ anammɔn ason ne fa te sɛ nnurahotam a wɔde duraa adiwo hɔ afasu no ho no.
english: The curtain for the entrance to the courtyard was made of blue, purple and scarlet yarn and finely twisted linen—the work of an embroiderer. It was twenty cubits long and, like the curtains of the courtyard, five cubits high,

twi: Nnua anan na na ɛsensɛn so, na nnua no nso gyina kɔbere nnyinasode anan a dwetɛ nkɔtɔkoro ne mfɛnsere ka ho nso. Nnua no so nyinaa yɛ dwetɛ.
english: with four posts and four bronze bases. Their hooks and bands were silver, and their tops were overlaid with silver.

twi: Nnadewa a wɔde sii Ahyiae Ntamadan no ne adiwo hɔ no nyinaa yɛ kɔbere.
english: All the tent pegs of the tabernacle and of the surrounding courtyard were bronze.

twi: Eyi ne ɔkwan a wɔfaa so sii Ahyiae Ntamadan a wɔde Apam Adaka no besi mu no sɛnea ɛbɛyɛ a Lewifo no betumi ayɛ wɔn asɔfodwuma. Ɔkwan a Mose kyerɛɛ wɔn sɛ wɔmfa so nsi no ara so na wɔfae. Ɔsɔfo Aaron ba Itamar na ɔhwɛɛ dwumadi no so.
english: These are the amounts of the materials used for the tabernacle, the tabernacle of the covenant law, which were recorded at Moses’ command by the Levites under the direction of Ithamar son of Aaron, the priest.

twi: Odwumfo dansifo a na ɔwɔ ho nso ne Uri ba Besaleel a ɔyɛ Hur a ofi Yuda abusua mu no nena.
english: (Bezalel son of Uri, the son of Hur, of the tribe of Judah, made everything the Lord commanded Moses;

twi: Ne boafo ne Oholiab a ɔyɛ Ahisamak a ofi Dan abusua mu ba. Na ɔno nso yɛ odwumfo a otumi twa nkyerɛw gu nneɛma mu. Afei na ɔyɛ adenwenfo a otumi de asaawatam tuntum, bibiri ne koogyan di adwinni gu ntama mu.
english: with him was Oholiab son of Ahisamak, of the tribe of Dan—an engraver and designer, and an embroiderer in blue, purple and scarlet yarn and fine linen.)

twi: Nnipa no de sikakɔkɔɔ kilogram apem bae. Wɔde ne nyinaa nso yɛɛ Ahyiae Ntamadan no ho adwuma.
english: The total amount of the gold from the wave offering used for all the work on the sanctuary was 29 talents and 730 shekels, according to the sanctuary shekel.

twi: Dwetɛ a asafo no mu nnipa no de bae yɛ kilogram mpem abiɛsa ne ahannan (,).
english: The silver obtained from those of the community who were counted in the census was 100 talents and 1,775 shekels, according to the sanctuary shekel—

twi: Saa dwetɛ yi fi tow a wotwa maa mmarima a wɔadi mfe aduonu rekɔ a wɔkan wɔn no. Wogye fii mmarima mpem ahansia ne abiɛsa, ahannum ne aduonum hɔ.
english: one beka per person, that is, half a shekel, according to the sanctuary shekel, from everyone who had crossed over to those counted, twenty years old or more, a total of 603,550 men.

twi: Kronkronbea hɔ nnyinaso ɔha ne mpuran a esuso ntwamtam no mu no behia dwetɛ kilogram mpem abiɛsa ne ahannan Enti nnyinaso biara bɛyɛ dwetɛ kilogram aduasa anan.
english: The 100 talents of silver were used to cast the bases for the sanctuary and for the curtain—100 bases from the 100 talents, one talent for each base.

twi: Dwetɛ kilogram aduonu no a ɛkae no nso, wɔde yɛɛ nnua no de bi duraa apampamu, de bi yɛɛ mfɛnsere no ne nkɔtɔkoro no.
english: They used the 1,775 shekels to make the hooks for the posts, to overlay the tops of the posts, and to make their bands.

twi: Kɔbere mfrafrae a wɔde bae no nso, na ɛyɛ kilogram mpem abien ne ahannan (,).
english: The bronze from the wave offering was 70 talents and 2,400 shekels.

twi: Ɛno na wɔde yɛɛ adum no nnyinaso wɔ Ahyiae Ntamadan no kwan ano. Ɛno bi ara na wɔde yɛɛ kɔbere mfrafrae afɔremuka, kɔbere mfrafrae ntwitae,
english: They used it to make the bases for the entrance to the tent of meeting, the bronze altar with its bronze grating and all its utensils,

twi: afɔremuka no so nneɛma, adum no nnyinasode a ekura nnurahotam a etwa adiwo no ho hyia no ne nnadewa a wɔde si Ahyiae Ntamadan no de yɛɛ adiwo hɔ adwuma nyinaa.
english: the bases for the surrounding courtyard and those for its entrance and all the tent pegs for the tabernacle and those for the surrounding courtyard.

twi: AsɔfotadeNnipa no de ntama tuntum, bibiri ne koogyan a ɛyɛ fɛ pam asɔfotade maa asɔfo no a wɔde bɛsom wɔ kronkronbea hɔ. Saa ntadetam no ara bi na wɔde pam Aaron ntade kronkron no sɛnea Awurade hyɛɛ Mose no.
english: From the blue, purple and scarlet yarn they made woven garments for ministering in the sanctuary. They also made sacred garments for Aaron, as the Lord commanded Moses.

twi: Wɔde asaawatam bi a wɔanwen afi asaawa a wɔato mu na ɛpam asɔfotade nkataase no.
english: They made the ephod of gold, and of blue, purple and scarlet yarn, and of finely twisted linen.

twi: Besaleel boroo sikakɔkɔɔ ma ɛyɛɛ tratraa, ɛnna otwitwaa no nteanteaa sɛ hama na ɔde bobɔɔ ntama tuntum, bibiri ne koogyan no mu. Ɛyɛ nsaanoadwuma a ɛte apɔw yiye.
english: They hammered out thin sheets of gold and cut strands to be worked into the blue, purple and scarlet yarn and fine linen—the work of skilled hands.

twi: Wɔde nwoma a wɔapam susoo nkataase no mu fi ase besii mmati ahama abien no mu.
english: They made shoulder pieces for the ephod, which were attached to two of its corners, so it could be fastened.

twi: Na wɔde ntama tuntum, bibiri, koogyan ne sikakɔkɔɔ yɛɛ nkyekyeremu sɛnea Onyankopɔn hyɛɛ Mose no.
english: Its skillfully woven waistband was like it—of one piece with the ephod and made with gold, and with blue, purple and scarlet yarn, and with finely twisted linen, as the Lord commanded Moses.

twi: Abo apopobibiri abien a wotwa de femfam mmati ahama abien no a eso asɔfotade no nkataase no mu no, sikakɔkɔɔ na wɔde kyerɛw Israelfo mmusuakuw no nyinaa din guu so sɛnea wɔkyerɛw nsateaa so kaa so no.
english: They mounted the onyx stones in gold filigree settings and engraved them like a seal with the names of the sons of Israel.

twi: Saa abo yi yɛ nkae ade de ma Awurade fa Israelfo ho, na wɔyɛɛ ne nyinaa sɛnea Awurade hyɛɛ Mose sɛ wɔnyɛ no no ara pɛ.
english: Then they fastened them on the shoulder pieces of the ephod as memorial stones for the sons of Israel, as the Lord commanded Moses.

twi: Wɔpam adɛbo no te sɛ asɔfotade a wɔde nwera ankasa yɛe, na wɔde sikakɔkɔɔ hama ne asaawa tuntum, bibiri ne koogyan na ɛnwen mu.
english: They fashioned the breastpiece—the work of a skilled craftsman. They made it like the ephod: of gold, and of blue, purple and scarlet yarn, and of finely twisted linen.

twi: Na ɛyɛ ahinanan a ne fa biara susuw nsateaa akron a wɔabu abɔ so.
english: It was square—a span long and a span wide—and folded double.

twi: Na wɔhyehyɛɛ abo a ɛsom bo sesaa so nnidiso nnidiso anan wɔ mu. Nnidiso a edi kan no yɛ bogyanambo, akraatebo ne ahabammono bo;
english: Then they mounted four rows of precious stones on it. The first row was carnelian, chrysolite and beryl;

twi: nnidiso a ɛto so abien no yɛ nsrammabo, hoabo ne dɛnkyɛmmo;
english: the second row was turquoise, lapis lazuli and emerald;

twi: nea ɛto so abiɛsa no yɛ akutuhonobo, mfrafraebo ne beredumbo;
english: the third row was jacinth, agate and amethyst;

twi: na nea ɛto so anan no yɛ sikabereɛbo, apopobibiribo ne ahwehwɛbo a wɔde sikakɔkɔɔ atwa emu biara ho ahyia.
english: the fourth row was topaz, onyx and jasper. They were mounted in gold filigree settings.

twi: Wɔyɛɛ abo no te sɛ nsɔwanode bi kyerɛw Israel mmusuakuw dumien no din guu so.
english: There were twelve stones, one for each of the names of the sons of Israel, each engraved like a seal with the name of one of the twelve tribes.

twi: Sɛnea ɛbɛyɛ a wobetumi de adɛbo no aso asɔfotade no mu no, wɔde sikakɔkɔɔ nkaa hyehyɛɛ asɔfotade no mmati ntareso abien no so.
english: For the breastpiece they made braided chains of pure gold, like a rope.

twi: Wɔsan yɛɛ sikakɔkɔɔ nkaa abien de hyehyɛɛ adɛbo no ntwɔtwɔw so wɔ soro.
english: They made two gold filigree settings and two gold rings, and fastened the rings to two of the corners of the breastpiece.

twi: Wɔde sikakɔkɔɔ ahama abien no hyehyɛɛ sikakɔkɔɔ nkaa a ɛwɔ adɛbo no mu no mu.
english: They fastened the two gold chains to the rings at the corners of the breastpiece,

twi: Wɔde ahama no ti no bobɔɔ sikakɔkɔɔ no a esuso asɔfotade no mu no mu.
english: and the other ends of the chains to the two settings, attaching them to the shoulder pieces of the ephod at the front.

twi: Wɔde sikakɔkɔɔ nkaa abien nso hyehyɛɛ adɛbo no ntwea abien no a egu asɔfotade no so pɛɛ no so.
english: They made two gold rings and attached them to the other two corners of the breastpiece on the inside edge next to the ephod.

twi: Wɔde sikakɔkɔɔ nkaa abien susoo asɔfotade no mmati ntareso no mu ma ɛbɛn nkyekyeremu a wɔanwen no fɛfɛɛfɛ ne asɔfotade no ahyiae so no.
english: Then they made two more gold rings and attached them to the bottom of the shoulder pieces on the front of the ephod, close to the seam just above the waistband of the ephod.

twi: Sɛnea ɛbɛyɛ na adɛbo no begyina pɛpɛɛpɛ wɔ nkyekyeremu fɛfɛ no so nti, wɔde ntama tuntum kyekyeree nkaa a esuso adɛbo no ne asɔfotade no mu. Eyinom nyinaa, Awurade na ɔhyɛɛ Mose sɛ wɔnyɛ.
english: They tied the rings of the breastpiece to the rings of the ephod with blue cord, connecting it to the waistband so that the breastpiece would not swing out from the ephod—as the Lord commanded Moses.

twi: Asɔfotade no fa kɛse no ara de, wɔde ntama tuntum na ɛnwenee
english: They made the robe of the ephod entirely of blue cloth—the work of a weaver—

twi: na wotwaa mfimfini tokuru pempam bi faa so maa ano no yɛɛ den sɛnea wɔhyɛ a ɛrentetew.
english: with an opening in the center of the robe like the opening of a collar, and a band around this opening, so that it would not tear.

twi: Na wɔde bibiri ne asaawa a ɛbere dum ne koogyan a wɔanwen yɛɛ biribi te sɛ atoaa aba de sensɛn batakari no ase mmuano no ano.
english: They made pomegranates of blue, purple and scarlet yarn and finely twisted linen around the hem of the robe.

twi: Na wɔde sikakɔkɔɔ yɛɛ nnɔnnɔmma na wɔde biribi te sɛ atoaa aba no hyehyɛɛ ntam ne ntam wɔ batakari no ase mmuano no ano de twaa ho hyiae.
english: And they made bells of pure gold and attached them around the hem between the pomegranates.

twi: Sɛ Aaron hyɛ asɔfotade yi a, na ɛkyerɛ sɛ ɔrekɔsom Awurade sɛnea Awurade hyɛɛ Mose sɛ ɔnyɛ no.
english: The bells and pomegranates alternated around the hem of the robe to be worn for ministering, as the Lord commanded Moses.

twi: Wɔde asaawatam a ɛyɛ fɛ pam asɔfotade no bi maa Aaron ne ne mmabarima.
english: For Aaron and his sons, they made tunics of fine linen—the work of a weaver—

twi: Wɔde ntama a ɛyɛ fɛ na ɛpam adɛbo, abotiri, kyɛw ne nhyɛasetam ahorow no.
english: and the turban of fine linen, the linen caps and the undergarments of finely twisted linen.

twi: Bio, wɔde ntama a ɛyɛ fɛ na ɛpam nkyekyeremu no na wɔde asaawa tuntum, bibiri ne koogyan dii mu adwinni sɛnea Awurade hyɛɛ Mose sɛ ɔnyɛ no.
english: The sash was made of finely twisted linen and blue, purple and scarlet yarn—the work of an embroiderer—as the Lord commanded Moses.

twi: Na afei, wɔde sikakɔkɔɔ yɛɛ abɔanim a wɔakyerɛw so:Kronkron Ma Awurade.
english: They made the plate, the sacred emblem, out of pure gold and engraved on it, like an inscription on a seal: holy to the Lord.

twi: Wɔde ntama tuntum na asina abɔanim no abɔ abotiri no mu sɛnea Awurade hyɛe no.
english: Then they fastened a blue cord to it to attach it to the turban, as the Lord commanded Moses.

twi: Eyi nyinaa akyi no, wowiee Ahyiae Ntamadan no si sɛnea Awurade kyerɛɛ Mose sɛ wonsi no no.
english: So all the work on the tabernacle, the tent of meeting, was completed. The Israelites did everything just as the Lord commanded Moses.

twi: Afei, wɔde Ahyiae Ntamadan no ne emu nneɛma nyinaa brɛɛ Mose:Nkyerewa, nnyinaso, mmeamu nnua, mpuran ne nsisiso;
english: Then they brought the tabernacle to Moses: the tent and all its furnishings, its clasps, frames, crossbars, posts and bases;

twi: adwennini nwoma a wɔahyɛ no kɔkɔɔ, abirekyi nwoma a wɔahyɛ, nkataano,
english: the covering of ram skins dyed red and the covering of another durable leather and the shielding curtain;

twi: adaka no a Mmaransɛm Du no wɔ mu no, nnua a wɔde soa Mpata agua;
english: the ark of the covenant law with its poles and the atonement cover;

twi: ɔpon no ne ɛho nneɛma, Ɔkyerɛ Brodo,
english: the table with all its articles and the bread of the Presence;

twi: sika akaneadua ne nʼakanea, ɛho nneɛma ne ngo wɔde sɔ kanea;
english: the pure gold lampstand with its row of lamps and all its accessories, and the olive oil for the light;

twi: sikakɔkɔɔ afɔremuka, ɔsrango, aduhuam ne Ahyiae Ntamadan no nkataano,
english: the gold altar, the anointing oil, the fragrant incense, and the curtain for the entrance to the tent;

twi: kɔbere Afɔremuka, kɔbere ntwitae, nnua no ne ɛho nneɛma,nea wɔhoro mu nneɛma ne ne ntaamu,
english: the bronze altar with its bronze grating, its poles and all its utensils; the basin with its stand;

twi: ntwahotam a wɔde twa adiwo hɔ fasu ho, ne ɛho nnua a esuso mu,nnyinasode ne ntwahotam a ɛwɔ adiwo pon ano,ntampehama ne nnadewa ne biribiara a wɔde boaa Ahyiae Ntamadan no si.
english: the curtains of the courtyard with its posts and bases, and the curtain for the entrance to the courtyard; the ropes and tent pegs for the courtyard; all the furnishings for the tabernacle, the tent of meeting;

twi: Wɔde asɔfotade a wɔapam no fɛfɛɛfɛ a wɔhyɛ kɔ kronkronbea hɔ no brɛɛ no ma ɔhwɛe. Afei, wɔde Aaron asɔfotade kronkron no nso ne ne mmabarima de a wɔbɛhyɛ de ayɛ asɔfodwuma no bɛkyerɛɛ no.
english: and the woven garments worn for ministering in the sanctuary, both the sacred garments for Aaron the priest and the garments for his sons when serving as priests.

twi: Enti Israelfo no dii nsɛm a Awurade hyɛɛ Mose sɛ ɔnka nkyerɛ wɔn no nyinaa so.
english: The Israelites had done all the work just as the Lord had commanded Moses.

twi: Na Mose hwɛɛ nnwuma no nyinaa huu sɛ biribiara ntɔ kyima wɔ ho no, ohyiraa wɔn, efisɛ sɛnea Awurade hyɛe no ara pɛ na wɔyɛe.
english: Moses inspected the work and saw that they had done it just as the Lord had commanded. So Moses blessed them.

twi: Afei Awurade ka kyerɛɛ Mose se,
english: Then the Lord said to Moses:

twi: “Ɔsram a edi kan no da a edi kan no na si Ahyiae Ntamadan no.
english: “Set up the tabernacle, the tent of meeting, on the first day of the first month.

twi: Wusi wie a, fa Apam Adaka a Mmaransɛm Du no wɔ mu no si mu. Na fa ntwamtam no twa Apam Adaka no anim ma ɛnhyɛ kronkron mu kronkron hɔ.
english: Place the ark of the covenant law in it and shield the ark with the curtain.

twi: Afei, fa ɔpon no besi hɔ na fa ɛho nneɛma nyinaa gu so na fa kaneadua no bra na sɔ kanea no.
english: Bring in the table and set out what belongs on it. Then bring in the lampstand and set up its lamps.

twi: Fa sikakɔkɔɔ afɔremuka a wɔbɛhyew aduhuam wɔ so no besi Apam Adaka no anim na fa ɔpon no nkataanim sɛn Ahyiae Ntamadan no ano.
english: Place the gold altar of incense in front of the ark of the covenant law and put the curtain at the entrance to the tabernacle.

twi: “Fa ɔhyew afɔremuka no si Ahyiae Ntamadan no kwan ano.
english: “Place the altar of burnt offering in front of the entrance to the tabernacle, the tent of meeting;

twi: Fa hweaseammɔ no si Ahyiae Ntamadan no ne afɔremuka no ntam na hyɛ no nsu ma.
english: place the basin between the tent of meeting and the altar and put water in it.

twi: Siesie adiwo twa Ahyiae Ntamadan no ho hyia na fa nsɛnanim no sɛn ne kwan no ano.
english: Set up the courtyard around it and put the curtain at the entrance to the courtyard.

twi: “Fa ɔsrango no na pete gu Ahyiae Ntamadan no so baabiara ne biribiara a ɛwɔ mu ne nneɛma a ɛwɔ hɔ nyinaa ne nkongua so, na fa tew ho.
english: “Take the anointing oil and anoint the tabernacle and everything in it; consecrate it and all its furnishings, and it will be holy.

twi: Ɔhyew afɔremuka no ne ɛho nneɛma nyinaa nso, pete ɔsra ngo no bi gu so na tew ho na ɛnyɛ kronkron.
english: Then anoint the altar of burnt offering and all its utensils; consecrate the altar, and it will be most holy.

twi: Sra hweaseammɔ no ne ne ntaease no ngo na fa tew ho.
english: Anoint the basin and its stand and consecrate them.

twi: “Fa Aaron ne ne mmabarima no bra Ahyiae Ntamadan no kwan ano na fa nsu hohoro wɔn ho.
english: “Bring Aaron and his sons to the entrance to the tent of meeting and wash them with water.

twi: Na fa atade kronkron no hyɛ Aaron, na sra no ngo na ne ho ntew na ɔmmɛyɛ me sɔfo.
english: Then dress Aaron in the sacred garments, anoint him and consecrate him so he may serve me as priest.

twi: Fa ne mmabarima no bra na fa wɔn ntade hyehyɛ wɔn.
english: Bring his sons and dress them in tunics.

twi: Sra wɔn ngo sɛnea woyɛɛ wɔn agya no, sɛnea wɔbɛsom me sɛ asɔfo. Wɔn ngosra no bɛyɛ asɔfodi wɔ wɔn awo ntoatoaso nyinaa mu.”
english: Anoint them just as you anointed their father, so they may serve me as priests. Their anointing will be to a priesthood that will continue throughout their generations.”

twi: Mose yɛɛ biribiara sɛnea Awurade hyɛɛ no no.
english: Moses did everything just as the Lord commanded him.

twi: Afe a ɛto so abien no mu ɔsram a edi kan no da a edi kan no, wɔkekaa Ahyiae Ntamadan no sisii anim.
english: So the tabernacle was set up on the first day of the first month in the second year.

twi: Mose sii Ahyiae Ntamadan no; ɔde nsisiso no sisii wɔn afa, de nnyinaso no hyehyɛɛ mu de mmeamu nnua beabea mu de mpuran sisii wɔn afa.
english: When Moses set up the tabernacle, he put the bases in place, erected the frames, inserted the crossbars and set up the posts.

twi: Afei, ɔde nkuruso no kuruu mpuran no so de ne nguguso guguu so san de nguguso a edi akyi kuruu so sɛnea Awurade hyɛɛ no no.
english: Then he spread the tent over the tabernacle and put the covering over the tent, as the Lord commanded him.

twi: Ɔde abo a wɔakyerɛw Mmaransɛm Du no wɔ so no guu Apam Adaka no mu de nnua a wɔde bɛsoa no susoo mu. Ɔde ne nkataso a wɔde sikakɔkɔɔ ayɛ a ɛyɛ mpata nkataso no kataa so.
english: He took the tablets of the covenant law and placed them in the ark, attached the poles to the ark and put the atonement cover over it.

twi: Afei, ɔde Apam Adaka no besii Ahyiae Ntamadan no mu de ntwamtam no twaa mu, sɛnea Awurade hyɛɛ no no.
english: Then he brought the ark into the tabernacle and hung the shielding curtain and shielded the ark of the covenant law, as the Lord commanded him.

twi: Afei, ɔde ɔpon no sii atifi fam wɔ ɔdan no mu wɔ ntwamtam no akyi,
english: Moses placed the table in the tent of meeting on the north side of the tabernacle outside the curtain

twi: de Ɔkyerɛ Brodo no too so wɔ Awurade anim sɛnea Awurade hyɛe no.
english: and set out the bread on it before the Lord, as the Lord commanded him.

twi: Ɔde kaneadua no sii ɔpon no nkyɛn wɔ Ahyiae Ntamadan no anafo fam.
english: He placed the lampstand in the tent of meeting opposite the table on the south side of the tabernacle

twi: Afei, ɔsɔɔ kanea no wɔ Awurade anim sɛnea Awurade hyɛɛ no no.
english: and set up the lamps before the Lord, as the Lord commanded him.

twi: Mose de sikakɔkɔɔ afɔremuka sii ntwamtam no ho pɛɛ wɔ Ahyiae Ntamadan no mu
english: Moses placed the gold altar in the tent of meeting in front of the curtain

twi: na ɔhyew nnuhuam wɔ so sɛnea Awurade hyɛe no.
english: and burned fragrant incense on it, as the Lord commanded him.

twi: Ɔde Ahyiae Ntamadan no ano nkataano sɛn ano.
english: Then he put up the curtain at the entrance to the tabernacle.

twi: Ɔde afɔremuka a esi akyi a wɔbɔ ɔhyew afɔre wɔ so no si bɛn ɔkwan no ano, na ɔbɔɔ so ɔhyew afɔre ne aduan afɔre sɛnea Awurade hyɛe no.
english: He set the altar of burnt offering near the entrance to the tabernacle, the tent of meeting, and offered on it burnt offerings and grain offerings, as the Lord commanded him.

twi: Ɔde hweaseammɔ sii Ahyiae Ntamadan no ne afɔremuka no ntam na wɔhyɛɛ no nsu ma, sɛnea asɔfo no benya bi ahohoro wɔn ho,
english: He placed the basin between the tent of meeting and the altar and put water in it for washing,

twi: na Mose ne Aaron ne Aaron mmabarima hohoroo wɔn nsa ho ne wɔn anan ase wɔ hɔ.
english: and Moses and Aaron and his sons used it to wash their hands and feet.

twi: Bere biara a wɔbɛfa afɔremuka no ho akɔ Ahyiae Ntamadan no mu no, wogyina hohoroo wɔn ho sɛnea Awurade hyɛɛ Mose no.
english: They washed whenever they entered the tent of meeting or approached the altar, as the Lord commanded Moses.

twi: Na Mose sii biribi twaa Ahyiae Ntamadan no ne afɔremuka no ho hyiae na wɔde nsɛnanotam sɛn ano. Ɛnna Mose wiee nʼadwuma.
english: Then Moses set up the courtyard around the tabernacle and altar and put up the curtain at the entrance to the courtyard. And so Moses finished the work.

twi: Omununkum no bɛkataa Ahyiae Ntamadan no so maa Awurade anuonyam hyɛɛ no ma.
english: Then the cloud covered the tent of meeting, and the glory of the Lord filled the tabernacle.

twi: Esiane sɛ na omununkum no asi wɔ hɔ no nti, Mose antumi ankɔ mu na Awurade anuonyam hyɛɛ Ahyiae Ntamadan no ma.
english: Moses could not enter the tent of meeting because the cloud had settled on it, and the glory of the Lord filled the tabernacle.

twi: Bere biara a omununkum no bɛma ne ho so no, na Israelfo no nso di akyi.
english: In all the travels of the Israelites, whenever the cloud lifted from above the tabernacle, they would set out;

twi: Na sɛ egyina a, na wɔn nso agyina akosi sɛ ɛbɛma ne ho so bio.
english: but if the cloud did not lift, they did not set out—until the day it lifted.

twi: Awia de, omununkum no gyina Ahyiae Ntamadan no so na sɛ edu anadwo a, na ogya asɔ wɔ omununkum no mu sɛnea Israelfo no nyinaa behu. Eyi toaa so saa ara wɔ wɔn akwantu no nyinaa mu.
english: So the cloud of the Lord was over the tabernacle by day, and fire was in the cloud by night, in the sight of all the Israelites during all their travels.

twi: Ateasefo No Ne Awurade AnuonyamAfe a ɛto so aduasa no, ɔsram a ɛto so anan no da a ɛto so anum no, na meka wɔn a wɔatwa wɔn asu akɔ amannɔne no ho. Mewɔ Asubɔnten Kebar ho no, ɔsoro buei, na mihuu Onyankopɔn wɔ anisoadehu mu.
english: In my thirtieth year, in the fourth month on the fifth day, while I was among the exiles by the Kebar River, the heavens were opened and I saw visions of God.

twi: Ɔsram no da a ɛto so anum no na ɔhene Yehoiakin adi mfe anum wɔ asutwa mu.
english: On the fifth of the month—it was the fifth year of the exile of King Jehoiachin—

twi: Awurade asɛm baa Busi babarima Hesekiel a ɔyɛ ɔsɔfo no nkyɛn wɔ Asubɔnten Kebar ho wɔ Babilonia asase so. Ɛhɔ na Onyankopɔn nsa baa ne so.
english: the word of the Lord came to Ezekiel the priest, the son of Buzi, by the Kebar River in the land of the Babylonians. There the hand of the Lord was on him.

twi: Mehwɛe, na mihuu sɛ ahum kɛse bi fi atifi fam reba, omununkum kɛse bi a ɛretwa anyinam na hann bi a ano yɛ den atwa ho ahyia. Ogya no mfimfini te sɛ dade a asɔ kɔɔ.
english: I looked, and I saw a windstorm coming out of the north—an immense cloud with flashing lightning and surrounded by brilliant light. The center of the fire looked like glowing metal,

twi: Na ogya no mu na na wohu biribi te sɛ ateasefo baanan. Na wɔn su te sɛ onipa,
english: and in the fire was what looked like four living creatures. In appearance their form was human,

twi: wɔn mu biara anim yɛ anan na wɔwowɔ ntaban anan anan.
english: but each of them had four faces and four wings.

twi: Wɔn anan yɛ kirebenn, wɔn anammɔn te sɛ nantwi ba de na ɛhyerɛn te sɛ kɔbere mfrafrae a wɔahoa ho.
english: Their legs were straight; their feet were like those of a calf and gleamed like burnished bronze.

twi: Wɔwowɔ nnipa nsa wɔ ntaban a ɛwowɔ afaafa anan no ase. Wɔn mu biara wɔ nnipa nsa anan a baako wɔ ntaban biara ase,
english: Under their wings on their four sides they had human hands. All four of them had faces and wings,

twi: na wɔn ntaban keka sisi anim. Wɔn nyinaa kɔ wɔn anim tee a wɔnnan wɔn ho.
english: and the wings of one touched the wings of another. Each one went straight ahead; they did not turn as they moved.

twi: Na sɛɛ na wɔn anim tete: Wɔn mu biara wɔ onipa anim, wɔwɔ gyata anim wɔ nifa so, wɔwɔ nantwi anim wɔ benkum so; na wɔn mu biara nso wɔ ɔkɔre anim.
english: Their faces looked like this: Each of the four had the face of a human being, and on the right side each had the face of a lion, and on the left the face of an ox; each also had the face of an eagle.

twi: Saa na na wɔn anim tete. Wɔatrɛtrɛw wɔn ntaban mu kɔ soro; na wɔn mu biara wɔ ntaban abien abien, a mu biara si ɔfoforo de anim wɔ benkum ne nifa, na ntaban abien nso katakata wɔn ho.
english: Such were their faces. They each had two wings spreading out upward, each wing touching that of the creature on either side; and each had two other wings covering its body.

twi: Obiara kɔ nʼanim tee. Baabiara a honhom no bɛkɔ no, hɔ na wɔbɛkɔ a wɔnnan wɔn ho.
english: Each one went straight ahead. Wherever the spirit would go, they would go, without turning as they went.

twi: Ateasefo no suban te sɛ nnyansramma a ɛredɛw anaa ogyatɛn. Ogya di akɔneaba wɔ ateasefo no mu; ɛhyerɛn na mu na anyinam fi twitwa.
english: The appearance of the living creatures was like burning coals of fire or like torches. Fire moved back and forth among the creatures; it was bright, and lightning flashed out of it.

twi: Na ateasefo no de mmirika di akɔneaba te sɛ anyinam a ɛretwitwa.
english: The creatures sped back and forth like flashes of lightning.

twi: Bere a merehwɛ ateasefo no, mihuu sɛ nkyimii si fam wɔ ateasefo a wɔn mu biara anim yɛ anan no nkyɛn mu.
english: As I looked at the living creatures, I saw a wheel on the ground beside each creature with its four faces.

twi: Sɛɛ na na nkyimii no bɔbea te: Etwa yerɛw yerɛw te sɛ sikabereɛbo, na anan no nyinaa sesɛ. Wɔayɛ mu biara te sɛ nkyimii a ɛtoa nkyimii foforo mu.
english: This was the appearance and structure of the wheels: They sparkled like topaz, and all four looked alike. Each appeared to be made like a wheel intersecting a wheel.

twi: Sɛ nkyimii no nam a wɔkɔ faako a ateasefo no ani kyerɛ; nkyimii no nnan wɔn ho bere a ateasefo no nam no.
english: As they moved, they would go in any one of the four directions the creatures faced; the wheels did not change direction as the creatures went.

twi: Wɔn hankare no korɔn, na ɛyɛ hu, na aniwa tuatua hankare anan no nyinaa ho.
english: Their rims were high and awesome, and all four rims were full of eyes all around.

twi: Sɛ ateasefo no nantew a nkyimii a ɛbatabata wɔn ho no nso kɔ saa ara; sɛ ateasefo no ma wɔn ho so fi fam a nkyimii no nso ma wɔn ho so.
english: When the living creatures moved, the wheels beside them moved; and when the living creatures rose from the ground, the wheels also rose.

twi: Baabiara a honhom no bɛkɔ no, ateasefo no nso bɛkɔ, na nkyimii no bɛka wɔn ho ama wɔn ho so, efisɛ ateasefo no honhom wɔ nkyimii no mu.
english: Wherever the spirit would go, they would go, and the wheels would rise along with them, because the spirit of the living creatures was in the wheels.

twi: Sɛ ateasefo no tu teɛ a nkyimii no nso kɔ saa ara; sɛ ateasefo no gyina a, wɔn nso gyina; sɛ ateasefo no pagyaw wɔn ho a nkyimii no ne wɔn pagyaw wɔn ho, efisɛ ateasefo no honhom wɔ nkyimii no mu.
english: When the creatures moved, they also moved; when the creatures stood still, they also stood still; and when the creatures rose from the ground, the wheels rose along with them, because the spirit of the living creatures was in the wheels.

twi: Na ntrɛwmu bi wɔ ateasefo no atifi a etwa yerɛw yerɛw te sɛ sukyerɛmma, na ɛyɛ hu.
english: Spread out above the heads of the living creatures was what looked something like a vault, sparkling like crystal, and awesome.

twi: Na wɔatrɛtrɛw wɔn ntaban no mu asisi anim wɔ ntrɛwmu no ase, na ateasefo no mu biara wɔ ntaban abien a ɛkata ne ho.
english: Under the vault their wings were stretched out one toward the other, and each had two wings covering its body.

twi: Ateasefo no tu teɛe no, metee wɔn ntaban no nnyigyei a ɛte sɛ asu a ɛworo, te sɛ Otumfo no nne, anaa asraafo huuyɛ. Sɛ wogyina a wɔatrɛtrɛw wɔn ntaban mu.
english: When the creatures moved, I heard the sound of their wings, like the roar of rushing waters, like the voice of the Almighty, like the tumult of an army. When they stood still, they lowered their wings.

twi: Na nne bi fi ntrɛwmu a ɛkata wɔn so no atifi bae, bere a wɔatrɛtrɛw wɔn ntaban mu na wogyinagyina hɔ no.
english: Then there came a voice from above the vault over their heads as they stood with lowered wings.

twi: Na biribi a ɛte sɛ aboɔdemmo ahengua wɔ ntrɛwmu a ɛkata ateasefo no atifi no so, na biribi a ɛte sɛ onipa te ahengua so wɔ ɔsoro hɔ.
english: Above the vault over their heads was what looked like a throne of lapis lazuli, and high above on the throne was a figure like that of a man.

twi: Mihuu sɛ efi nea ayɛ sɛ nʼasen mu rekɔ ne soro no na ɔte sɛ dade a adɔ kɔɔ sɛ ogya a ano asɔ, na efi hɔ reba ne fam no na ɔte sɛ ogyaframa; na hann a ɛhyerɛn atwa ne ho ahyia.
english: I saw that from what appeared to be his waist up he looked like glowing metal, as if full of fire, and that from there down he looked like fire; and brilliant light surrounded him.

twi: Sɛnea nyankontɔn to wɔ omununkum mu osutɔ da no, saa ara na hann a atwa ne ho ahyia no te.Eyi yɛ Awurade anuonyam ahoyi no sɛso. Na mihui no, mede mʼanim butuw fam, na metee obi a ɔrekasa nne.
english:
Like the appearance of a rainbow in the clouds on a rainy day, so was the radiance around him.
This was the appearance of the likeness of the glory of the Lord. When I saw it, I fell facedown, and I heard the voice of one speaking.

twi: Hesekiel FrɛƆka kyerɛɛ me se, “Onipa ba, sɔre gyina hɔ na me ne wo nkasa.”
english: He said to me, “Son of man, stand up on your feet and I will speak to you.”

twi: Ɔrekasa no, Honhom no bɛhyɛɛ me mu maa me so gyinaa hɔ, na metee se ɔrekasa kyerɛ me.
english: As he spoke, the Spirit came into me and raised me to my feet, and I heard him speaking to me.

twi: Ɔkae se, “Onipa ba, meresoma wo akɔ Israelfo mu, atuatew man a wayɛ dɔm atia me; wɔne wɔn agyanom ayɛ dɔm atia me abesi nnɛ.
english: He said: “Son of man, I am sending you to the Israelites, to a rebellious nation that has rebelled against me; they and their ancestors have been in revolt against me to this very day.

twi: Nnipa a meresoma wo wɔn nkyɛn no yɛ nnipa a wɔasen wɔn kɔn na wɔn aso awu. Ka kyerɛ wɔn se, ‘Sɛɛ na Otumfo Awurade se.’
english: The people to whom I am sending you are obstinate and stubborn. Say to them, ‘This is what the Sovereign Lord says.’

twi: Na sɛ wotie anaa wɔantie a, esiane sɛ wɔyɛ atuatewfo nti, wobehu ampa ara sɛ odiyifo bi aba wɔn mu.
english: And whether they listen or fail to listen—for they are a rebellious people—they will know that a prophet has been among them.

twi: Na wo, onipa ba, nsuro wɔn anaasɛ wɔn nsɛm. Nsuro, ɛwɔ mu sɛ nsasono ne nsɔe atwa wo ho ahyia na wote nkekantwɛre mu de, nanso nsuro nea wɔka, na mma wɔmmɔ wo hu, ɛwɔ mu sɛ wɔyɛ atuatewfo.
english: And you, son of man, do not be afraid of them or their words. Do not be afraid, though briers and thorns are all around you and you live among scorpions. Do not be afraid of what they say or be terrified by them, though they are a rebellious people.

twi: Wɔyɛ atuatewfo ankasa nanso sɛ wobetie oo, sɛ wɔrentie oo, ɛsɛ sɛ woka me nsɛm kyerɛ wɔn.
english: You must speak my words to them, whether they listen or fail to listen, for they are rebellious.

twi: Nanso wo onipa ba, tie asɛm a meka kyerɛ wo no. Ntew atua te sɛ saa atuatewfo no; bue wʼanom na di nea mede ma wo no.”
english: But you, son of man, listen to what I say to you. Do not rebel like that rebellious people; open your mouth and eat what I give you.”

twi: Afei mehwɛe, na mihuu nsa bi a ateɛ wɔ me so, na mu na nhoma mmobɔwee bi wɔ.
english: Then I looked, and I saw a hand stretched out to me. In it was a scroll,

twi: Ɔtrɛw mu wɔ mʼanim. Nʼafanu no mu, na wɔakyerɛw kwadwom, awerɛhowdi ne nnome nsɛm.
english: which he unrolled before me. On both sides of it were written words of lament and mourning and woe.

twi: Awurade ka kyerɛɛ me se, “Onipa ba, di nea wuhu wɔ wʼanim no, di saa nhoma mmobɔwee yi, na afei kɔ na kɔkasa kyerɛ Israelfo.”
english: And he said to me, “Son of man, eat what is before you, eat this scroll; then go and speak to the people of Israel.”

twi: Enti mibuee mʼanom na ɔde nhoma mmobɔwee no maa me dii.
english: So I opened my mouth, and he gave me the scroll to eat.

twi: Afei ɔka kyerɛɛ me se, “Onipa ba, di saa nhoma mmobɔwee a mede rema wo yi fa hyɛ wo yafunu ma.” Enti midii na na ɛyɛ dɛ te sɛ ɛwo wɔ mʼanom.
english: Then he said to me, “Son of man, eat this scroll I am giving you and fill your stomach with it.” So I ate it, and it tasted as sweet as honey in my mouth.

twi: Na ɔka kyerɛɛ me se, “Onipa ba, afei kɔ Israelfo nkyɛn na kɔka me nsɛm kyerɛ wɔn.
english: He then said to me: “Son of man, go now to the people of Israel and speak my words to them.

twi: Ɛnyɛ nnipa bi a wɔn kasa mu nna hɔ anaa ntease nni mu nkyɛn na meresoma wo, mmom meresoma wo Israelfo hɔ.
english: You are not being sent to a people of obscure speech and strange language, but to the people of Israel—

twi: Ɛnyɛ nnipa bebree a wɔn kasa mu nna hɔ na ɛyɛ den, wɔn a wonte wɔn kasa ase nkyɛn. Ampa, sɛ mesomaa wo wɔ saa nnipa yi nkyɛn a, anka wotiee wo.
english: not to many peoples of obscure speech and strange language, whose words you cannot understand. Surely if I had sent you to them, they would have listened to you.

twi: Nanso Israelfo mpɛ sɛ wotie wo, efisɛ wɔmpɛ sɛ wotie me. Israel nyinaa ayɛ komapirim ne asoɔden.
english: But the people of Israel are not willing to listen to you because they are not willing to listen to me, for all the Israelites are hardened and obstinate.

twi: Ɛno nti mɛma woayɛ asoɔden ne komapirim te sɛ wɔn.
english: But I will make you as unyielding and hardened as they are.

twi: Mɛyɛ wo moma dennen sɛ apemmo, nea ɛyɛ den sen ɔtwɛrebo. Nsuro wɔn na mma wɔmmɔ wo hu, ɛwɔ mu sɛ wɔyɛ atuatewfo de.”
english: I will make your forehead like the hardest stone, harder than flint. Do not be afraid of them or terrified by them, though they are a rebellious people.”

twi: Na ɔka kyerɛɛ me se, “Onipa ba, tie me nsɛm a meka kyerɛ wo no yiye na dwene ho wɔ wo koma mu.
english: And he said to me, “Son of man, listen carefully and take to heart all the words I speak to you.

twi: Afei kɔ wo nkurɔfo a wɔwɔ nnommum mu na kasa kyerɛ wɔn. Se wɔn sɛ, ‘Sɛɛ na Otumfo Awurade se,’ sɛ wobetie oo, sɛ wɔrentie oo.”
english: Go now to your people in exile and speak to them. Say to them, ‘This is what the Sovereign Lord says,’ whether they listen or fail to listen.”

twi: Na Honhom no maa me so kɔɔ soro na metee sɛ nnyigyei dennen bi reworo so wɔ mʼakyi bere a na Awurade anuonyam rema ne ho so wɔ ne gyinabea hɔ no
english: Then the Spirit lifted me up, and I heard behind me a loud rumbling sound as the glory of the Lord rose from the place where it was standing.

twi: Na ɛyɛ nnyigyei a efi ateasefo no ntaban a ɛkeka twiw ho ne nkyimii a ɛwowɔ wɔn ho no. Nnyigyei dennen a ɛworo so.
english: It was the sound of the wings of the living creatures brushing against each other and the sound of the wheels beside them, a loud rumbling sound.

twi: Honhom no maa me so kɔɔ soro de me kɔɔ baabi, mekɔɔ no nweenwen ne honhom mu abufuw so, a na Awurade tumi yɛ kɛse wɔ me so.
english: The Spirit then lifted me up and took me away, and I went in bitterness and in the anger of my spirit, with the strong hand of the Lord on me.

twi: Mebaa nnommum a wɔtete Tel Abib a ɛbɛn Asubɔnten Kebar no nkyɛn. Na hɔ na me ne wɔn tenaa nnanson, na me ho dwiriw me.
english: I came to the exiles who lived at Tel Aviv near the Kebar River. And there, where they were living, I sat among them for seven days—deeply distressed.

twi: Israel KɔkɔbɔNnanson akyi no, Awurade asɛm baa me nkyɛn se,
english: At the end of seven days the word of the Lord came to me:

twi: “Onipa ba, mayɛ wo ɔwɛmfo ama Israel; ɛno nti tie asɛm a meka no, na bɔ wɔn kɔkɔ a efi me.
english: “Son of man, I have made you a watchman for the people of Israel; so hear the word I speak and give them warning from me.

twi: Sɛ meka kyerɛ omumɔyɛfo se, ‘Ampa ara wubewu’ na sɛ woammɔ no kɔkɔ anaasɛ woankasa ankyerɛ no amma wantwe ne ho amfi nʼakwammɔne ho annya nkwa a, saa omumɔyɛfo no bewu wɔ ne bɔne mu, na mɛma woabu ne mogya ho akontaa.
english: When I say to a wicked person, ‘You will surely die,’ and you do not warn them or speak out to dissuade them from their evil ways in order to save their life, that wicked person will die for their sin, and I will hold you accountable for their blood.

twi: Nanso sɛ wobɔ omumɔyɛfo no kɔkɔ na sɛ wansakra amfi nʼamumɔyɛ anaa nʼakwammɔne ho a, obewu wɔ ne bɔne mu, nanso na woagye wo ho nkwa.
english: But if you do warn the wicked person and they do not turn from their wickedness or from their evil ways, they will die for their sin; but you will have saved yourself.

twi: “Bio, sɛ ɔtreneeni dan fi trenee ho kɔyɛ bɔne a, mede hintidua bɛto nʼanim ama no ahwe ase, na wawu. Sɛ woammɔ no kɔkɔ nti, obewu wɔ ne bɔne mu. Adetrenee ahorow a ɔyɛe no, wɔrenkae na mɛma woabu ne mogya ho akontaa.
english: “Again, when a righteous person turns from their righteousness and does evil, and I put a stumbling block before them, they will die. Since you did not warn them, they will die for their sin. The righteous things that person did will not be remembered, and I will hold you accountable for their blood.

twi: Nanso sɛ wobɔ ɔtreneeni no kɔkɔ sɛ onnyae bɔneyɛ na ogyae a, obenya nkwa efisɛ otiee kɔkɔbɔ, na wo nso wubegye wo ho nkwa.”
english: But if you do warn the righteous person not to sin and they do not sin, they will surely live because they took warning, and you will have saved yourself.”

twi: Na Awurade tumi baa me so wɔ hɔ, na ɔka kyerɛɛ me se, “Sɔre na kɔ tataw no so, na hɔ na mɛkasa akyerɛ wo.”
english: The hand of the Lord was on me there, and he said to me, “Get up and go out to the plain, and there I will speak to you.”

twi: Enti mesɔre kɔɔ tataw no so. Na Awurade anuonyam te sɛ nea mihuu wɔ Asubɔnten Kebar ho no gyina hɔ, na mede mʼanim butuw fam.
english: So I got up and went out to the plain. And the glory of the Lord was standing there, like the glory I had seen by the Kebar River, and I fell facedown.

twi: Afei Honhom no bɛhyɛɛ me mu na ɔmaa me so gyinaa hɔ. Ɔka kyerɛɛ me se, “Kɔ na kɔto wo ho pon mu wɔ wo fi.
english: Then the Spirit came into me and raised me to my feet. He spoke to me and said: “Go, shut yourself inside your house.

twi: Na wo, onipa ba, wɔde ntampehama bɛkyekyere wo sɛnea worentumi mpue nkɔ nnipa no mu.
english: And you, son of man, they will tie with ropes; you will be bound so that you cannot go out among the people.

twi: Na mɛma wo tɛkrɛma atare wʼanom sɛnea wobɛyɛ komm a worentumi nka wɔn anim, efisɛ wɔyɛ atuatewfo.
english: I will make your tongue stick to the roof of your mouth so that you will be silent and unable to rebuke them, for they are a rebellious people.

twi: Nanso sɛ mekasa kyerɛ wo a, mebue wʼano ama woaka akyerɛ wɔn se, ‘Sɛnea Otumfo Awurade se ni!’ Nea obetie no ma no ntie, na nea ɔmpɛ sɛ otie no mma no ntie; na wɔyɛ atuatewfo.
english: But when I speak to you, I will open your mouth and you shall say to them, ‘This is what the Sovereign Lord says.’ Whoever will listen let them listen, and whoever will refuse let them refuse; for they are a rebellious people.

twi: Yerusalem Tua Ho Mfonitwa“Na afei, onipa ba, fa ntayaa bi to wʼanim na kurukyerɛw Yerusalem kuropɔn mfoni wɔ so.
