english: and I will inflict punishment on Moab. Then they will know that I am the Lord.’”

twi: Nkɔmhyɛ A Etia Edom“Sɛɛ na Otumfo Awurade se: Esiane sɛ Edom tɔɔ were wɔ Yudafi so na ɔnam so dii fɔ no nti,
english: “This is what the Sovereign Lord says: ‘Because Edom took revenge on Judah and became very guilty by doing so,

twi: nea Otumfo Awurade se ni: ‘Mɛteɛ me nsa atia Edom na makum ne mmarima ne ne mmoa, mɛma asase a ɛda Teman kosi Dedan ada mpan, na wɔbɛtotɔ wɔ afoa ano.
english: therefore this is what the Sovereign Lord says: I will stretch out my hand against Edom and kill both man and beast. I will lay it waste, and from Teman to Dedan they will fall by the sword.

twi: Me nkurɔfo Israelfo bɛyɛ nsa a mɛfa so atɔ Edom so were na wɔne no bedi no sɛnea mʼabufuw ne mʼabufuwhyew te; wobehu mʼaweretɔ, Otumfo Awurade asɛm ni.’ ”
english: I will take vengeance on Edom by the hand of my people Israel, and they will deal with Edom in accordance with my anger and my wrath; they will know my vengeance, declares the Sovereign Lord.’”

twi: Nkɔmhyɛ A Etia Filistia“Sɛɛ na Otumfo Awurade se: ‘Esiane sɛ Filistifo tɔɔ were, na wɔde koma mu nsusuw bɔne na ɛyɛɛ saa, na wɔde ɔtan a efi tete sɛee Yuda nti,
english: “This is what the Sovereign Lord says: ‘Because the Philistines acted in vengeance and took revenge with malice in their hearts, and with ancient hostility sought to destroy Judah,

twi: sɛnea Otumfo Awurade se ni: Merebɛteɛ me nsa atia Filistifo, na matwa Keretifo no agu na masɛe wɔn a wɔaka wɔ mpoano hɔ no.
english: therefore this is what the Sovereign Lord says: I am about to stretch out my hand against the Philistines, and I will wipe out the Kerethites and destroy those remaining along the coast.

twi: Mɛtɔ wɔn so were a ɛso na matwe wɔn aso wɔ mʼabufuwhyew mu. Na sɛ metɔ wɔn so were a, wobehu sɛ mene Awurade no.’ ”
english: I will carry out great vengeance on them and punish them in my wrath. Then they will know that I am the Lord, when I take vengeance on them.’”

twi: Nkɔmhyɛ A Etia TiroAfe a ɛto so dubaako no sram da a edi kan no, Awurade asɛm baa me nkyɛn se:
english: In the eleventh month of the twelfth year, on the first day of the month, the word of the Lord came to me:

twi: “Onipa ba, esiane sɛ Tiro aka afa Yerusalem ho se, ‘Ɛhɛɛ! Amanaman no ano pon abubu na nʼapon no abuebue ama me; mprempren a kuropɔn yi asɛe yi, menya nkɔso.’
english: “Son of man, because Tyre has said of Jerusalem, ‘Aha! The gate to the nations is broken, and its doors have swung open to me; now that she lies in ruins I will prosper,’

twi: Ɛno nti, sɛɛ na Otumfo Awurade se: Me ne wo anya, Tiro, mede aman bebree bɛba abetia wo te sɛ po a ɛrebɔ nʼasorɔkye.
english: therefore this is what the Sovereign Lord says: I am against you, Tyre, and I will bring many nations against you, like the sea casting up its waves.

twi: Wɔbɛsɛe Tiro afasu na wɔadwiriw nʼabantenten no. Mɛpa so dɔte agu ama ayɛ ɔbotan kwaboo.
english: They will destroy the walls of Tyre and pull down her towers; I will scrape away her rubble and make her a bare rock.

twi: Obefi po mu abɛyɛ beae a wɔhata asau, efisɛ makasa. Otumfo Awurade asɛm ni. Ɔbɛyɛ amanaman no asade,
english: Out in the sea she will become a place to spread fishnets, for I have spoken, declares the Sovereign Lord. She will become plunder for the nations,

twi: na afoa bɛsɛe nʼatenae a ɛwɔ asase kesee so no pasaa. Afei wobehu sɛ, mene Awurade no.
english: and her settlements on the mainland will be ravaged by the sword. Then they will know that I am the Lord.

twi: “Na sɛɛ na Otumfo Awurade se: Merekɔfa Babiloniahene Nebukadnessar, ahene mu hene, ne ne apɔnkɔ ne nteaseɛnam, ne apɔnkɔsotefo ne nsraadɔm kɛse afi atifi fam aba wo so.
english: “For this is what the Sovereign Lord says: From the north I am going to bring against Tyre Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon, king of kings, with horses and chariots, with horsemen and a great army.

twi: Ɔde afoa bɛsɛe wʼatenae a ɛwɔ asase kesee no so no pasaa; obesisi mpampim ayɛ mpempe wɔ wʼafasu ho na wama ne nkatabo so atia wo.
english: He will ravage your settlements on the mainland with the sword; he will set up siege works against you, build a ramp up to your walls and raise his shields against you.

twi: Ɔde oburuw nnua bɛpempem wʼafasu no, na ɔde akode abubu wʼabantenten no asɛe no.
english: He will direct the blows of his battering rams against your walls and demolish your towers with his weapons.

twi: Nʼapɔnkɔ no bɛdɔɔso yiye, na wɔbɛbɔ mfutuma akata wo so. Ɔsa apɔnkɔ no, nkyimii ne nteaseɛnam nnyigyei bɛma wʼafasu awosow, bere a wɔahyɛn wo apon mu, sɛnea mmarima hyɛn kuropɔn a nʼafasu mu adeda akwan no.
english: His horses will be so many that they will cover you with dust. Your walls will tremble at the noise of the warhorses, wagons and chariots when he enters your gates as men enter a city whose walls have been broken through.

twi: Nʼapɔnkɔ no tɔte betiatia wo mmɔnten nyinaa so, ɔde afoa bekunkum wo nkurɔfo na wʼafadum dennen no bebubu agu fam.
english: The hooves of his horses will trample all your streets; he will kill your people with the sword, and your strong pillars will fall to the ground.

twi: Wɔbɛfom wʼahode na wɔawia wʼaguade, wobebubu wʼafasu, na wɔadwiriw wʼadan fɛfɛ no na wɔatotow wʼabo, wo nnua ne wo dɔte agu po mu.
english: They will plunder your wealth and loot your merchandise; they will break down your walls and demolish your fine houses and throw your stones, timber and rubble into the sea.

twi: Mɛma wo nnwonto gyegyeegye no aba awiei na wɔrente wo sanku so nnwonto no bio.
english: I will put an end to your noisy songs, and the music of your harps will be heard no more.

twi: Mɛyɛ wo ɔbotan kwaboo na wo so na wɔbɛhata asau. Wɔrenkyekyere wo bio.
english: I will make you a bare rock, and you will become a place to spread fishnets. You will never be rebuilt, for I the Lord have spoken, declares the Sovereign Lord.

twi: “Sɛɛ na Otumfo Awurade ka kyerɛ Tiro: Sɛ wo mpoano nkurow no te wʼasehwe ho apinisi ne akunkumakunkum a asi wɔ wo mu a, wɔn ho rempopo ana?
english: “This is what the Sovereign Lord says to Tyre: Will not the coastlands tremble at the sound of your fall, when the wounded groan and the slaughter takes place in you?

twi: Afei mpoano mmapɔmma no nyinaa befi wɔn nhengua so, ayiyi wɔn nguguso ne ntade a wɔadi mu adwinni agu hɔ. Ehu bɛbɔ wɔn ama wɔatenatena fam, wɔn ho bɛpopo na wɔn ho adwiriw wɔn wɔ wo nti.
english: Then all the princes of the coast will step down from their thrones and lay aside their robes and take off their embroidered garments. Clothed with terror, they will sit on the ground, trembling every moment, appalled at you.

twi: Afei wɔbɛma kwadwom a ɛfa wo ho so se:“‘Hwɛ sɛnea wɔasɛe wo, kuropɔn a woagye din,wo a po sofo na ɛte wo mu,na anka wowɔ tumi wɔ po so!Wo ne wo manfo;wode hu hyɛɛwɔn a wɔte hɔ nyinaa mu.
english:
Then they will take up a lament concerning you and say to you:
“‘How you are destroyed, city of renown,
    peopled by men of the sea!
You were a power on the seas,
    you and your citizens;
you put your terror
    on all who lived there.

twi: Mprempren, mpoano nsase no ho popowɔ wʼasehwe da no;asupɔw a ɛwɔ po mu noabɔ hu wɔ wʼasehwe no ho.’
english:
Now the coastlands tremble
    on the day of your fall;
the islands in the sea
    are terrified at your collapse.’

twi: “Sɛɛ na Otumfo Awurade se: Sɛ mema woyɛ kuropɔn a ada mpan te sɛ nkuropɔn a nnipa ntete so, na sɛ mema po bun ba wo so na sɛ ne mu nsu bebrebe no bɛkata wo so a,
english: “This is what the Sovereign Lord says: When I make you a desolate city, like cities no longer inhabited, and when I bring the ocean depths over you and its vast waters cover you,

twi: mede wo ne wɔn a wɔkɔ amoa mu no besian akɔ teteetefo no nkyɛn. Mɛma woatena asase ase hɔ te sɛ tete mmubui, wo ne wɔn a wosian kɔ amoa mu no, na worensan anaa worennya kyɛfa wɔ ateasefo asase so.
english: then I will bring you down with those who go down to the pit, to the people of long ago. I will make you dwell in the earth below, as in ancient ruins, with those who go down to the pit, and you will not return or take your place in the land of the living.

twi: Mede wo bɛba awiei a ɛyɛ hu mu na worenhu bio. Wɔbɛhwehwɛ wo nanso wɔrenhu wo bio da, Otumfo Awurade asɛm ni.”
english: I will bring you to a horrible end and you will be no more. You will be sought, but you will never again be found, declares the Sovereign Lord.”

twi: Tiro Ho KwadwomAwurade asɛm baa me nkyɛn se:
english: The word of the Lord came to me:

twi: “Onipa ba, ma kwadwom a ɛfa Tiro ho so.
english: “Son of man, take up a lament concerning Tyre.

twi: Ka kyerɛ Tiro a ɔda po abobow ano, na ɔne aguadifo bebree a wɔwɔ mpoano nkurow so di gua se, eyi ne asɛm a Otumfo Awurade ka:“ ‘Woka se, Tiro,“Me ho yɛ fɛ yiye.”
english:
Say to Tyre, situated at the gateway to the sea, merchant of peoples on many coasts, ‘This is what the Sovereign Lord says:
“‘You say, Tyre,
    “I am perfect in beauty.”

twi: Wo tumidi wɔ po so akyirikyiri;wʼadansifo maa wʼahoɔfɛ wiee pɛyɛ.
english:
Your domain was on the high seas;
    your builders brought your beauty to perfection.

twi: Wo nnua a wɔpaee nyinaayɛ ɔpepaw a efi Senir.Wɔde Lebanon sidana ɛyɛɛ ahyɛn so nnua maa wo.
english:
They made all your timbers
    of juniper from Senir;
they took a cedar from Lebanon
    to make a mast for you.

twi: Odum nnua a efi Basanna wɔde yɛɛ wʼatabon;Kwabɔhɔre nnua a efi Kipro mpoanona wɔde yɛɛ wʼahyɛn abrannaa, a wɔde asonse asɛw so.
english:
Of oaks from Bashan
    they made your oars;
of cypress wood from the coasts of Cyprus
    they made your deck, adorned with ivory.

twi: Misraim nwera papa bi a wɔadi mu adwinina wɔde yɛɛ wʼahyɛn so mframatama ɛyɛɛ wo frankaa nso;wʼapon ne mfɛnsere ano ntama yɛ abibitam ne beredum ntamaa efi Elisa mpoano.
english:
Fine embroidered linen from Egypt was your sail
    and served as your banner;
your awnings were of blue and purple
    from the coasts of Elishah.

twi: Sidonfo ne Arwadfo na wɔhare wʼahyɛn;wo mmarima anyansafo. Tiro,na wɔyɛ adwumayɛfo wɔ wʼahyɛn mu.
english:
Men of Sidon and Arvad were your oarsmen;
    your skilled men, Tyre, were aboard as your sailors.

twi: Gebal adwumfo adedaw tenaa wʼahyɛn musɛ dua dwumfo a wotuatua ahyɛn no mu ntokuru.Po so ahyɛn ne wɔn hyɛnmufo nyinaabaa wo nkyɛn ne wo bedii nsesagua.
english:
Veteran craftsmen of Byblos were on board
    as shipwrights to caulk your seams.
All the ships of the sea and their sailors
    came alongside to trade for your wares.

twi: “ ‘Persia, Lidia ne Put mmarimasomee sɛ asraafo wɔ wo nsraadɔm mu.Wɔde wɔn nkatabo ne dade kyɛwsensɛn wʼafasu ho,de hyɛɛ wo anuonyam.
english:
“‘Men of Persia, Lydia and Put
    served as soldiers in your army.
They hung their shields and helmets on your walls,
    bringing you splendor.

twi: Arwad ne Helek mmarimawɛn wʼafasu ho nyinaaGammad mmarimatenaa wʼabantenten mu.Wɔde wɔn nkatabo sensɛn wʼafasu homaa wʼahoɔfɛ dii mu.
“ ‘Wʼaguade a ɛma wonyaa wo ho bebree nti, Tarsis ne wo dii gua, wɔde dwetɛ, dade, sanyaa ne sumpii sesaa wʼaguade.
english: “‘Tarshish did business with you because of your great wealth of goods; they exchanged silver, iron, tin and lead for your merchandise.

twi: “ ‘Helafo, Tubalfo ne Mesekfo ne wo dii gua, wɔde nkoa ne kɔbere nneɛma sesaa wʼaguade.
english: “‘Greece, Tubal and Meshek did business with you; they traded human beings and articles of bronze for your wares.

twi: “ ‘Bet Togarma mmarima de adwumayɛ apɔnkɔ, ɔsa apɔnkɔ ne mfurum mma bɛsesaa wʼaguade.
english: “‘Men of Beth Togarmah exchanged chariot horses, cavalry horses and mules for your merchandise.

twi: “ ‘Roda mmarima ne wo dii gua, na mpoano nkurow bebree yɛɛ wʼadetɔfo a wɔde asonse ne duabo nnua tuaa wo ka.
english: “‘The men of Rhodes traded with you, and many coastlands were your customers; they paid you with ivory tusks and ebony.

twi: “ ‘Aram ne wo dii gua esiane wo nneɛma bebrebe a woyɛ nti; wɔde nsrammabo, ntama a ɛberedum, nea wɔadi mu adwinni, nwera pa, nnɛnkyerema ne bota bɛsesaa wʼaguade.
english: “‘Aram did business with you because of your many products; they exchanged turquoise, purple fabric, embroidered work, fine linen, coral and rubies for your merchandise.

twi: “ ‘Yuda ne Israel ne wo dii gua; wɔde awi a efi Minit ne brodo, ɛwo, ngo ne ahyehyesrade sesaa wʼaguade.
english: “‘Judah and Israel traded with you; they exchanged wheat from Minnith and confections, honey, olive oil and balm for your wares.

twi: “ ‘Damasko ne wo dii gua wɔ nsa a efi Helbon ne nguan ho nwi a efi Sahar mu, esiane nneɛma a woyɛ ne wʼaguade a ama woanya wo ho bebree no nti.
english: “‘Damascus did business with you because of your many products and great wealth of goods. They offered wine from Helbon, wool from Zahar

twi: Danfo ne Helafo a wofi Usal tɔɔ wʼaguade na wɔde dade a wɔaboro, sesadua ne ahunuanyankwa sesaa wʼaguade.
english: and casks of wine from Izal in exchange for your wares: wrought iron, cassia and calamus.

twi: “ ‘Dedan de apɔnkɔnguasotam ne wo dii gua.
english: “‘Dedan traded in saddle blankets with you.

twi: “ ‘Arabfo ne Kedar mmapɔmma nyinaa yɛɛ wʼaguadifo a wɔde nguantenmma, adwennini ne mpapo ne wo dii gua.
english: “‘Arabia and all the princes of Kedar were your customers; they did business with you in lambs, rams and goats.

twi: “ ‘Seba ne Raama aguadifo ne wo dii gua; wɔde nnuhuam ahorow a ɛte apɔw, aboɔden abo ne sikakɔkɔɔ ne wo bedii nsesagua.
english: “‘The merchants of Sheba and Raamah traded with you; for your merchandise they exchanged the finest of all kinds of spices and precious stones, and gold.

twi: “ ‘Haran, Kan ne Eden, aguadifo a wofi Seba, Asur ne Kilmad ne wo dii gua.
english: “‘Harran, Kanneh and Eden and merchants of Sheba, Ashur and Kilmad traded with you.

twi: Wo gua so hɔ, wɔde ntama a ɛyɛ fɛ, nnɛmmatam a ɛyɛ tuntum, adwinne ahorow ne ntama fɛfɛ a ɛwɔ ahosu ahorow a wɔde nhoma a wɔakyinkyim abobɔ no apɔwapɔw na ayɛ ne wo bedii gua.
english: In your marketplace they traded with you beautiful garments, blue fabric, embroidered work and multicolored rugs with cords twisted and tightly knotted.

twi: “ ‘Tarsis ahyɛn yɛ adwumasɛ asoafo ma wʼaguade.Adesoa duruduru ayɛ wo mawɔ po no mfimfini.
english:
“‘The ships of Tarshish serve
    as carriers for your wares.
You are filled with heavy cargo
    as you sail the sea.

twi: Wʼaharefo no fa wode wo kɔ po so akyirikyirinanso apuei ahum bebubu wo mu nketenketewɔ po no mfimfini.
english:
Your oarsmen take you
    out to the high seas.
But the east wind will break you to pieces
    far out at sea.

twi: Wʼahonya, aguade ne adetɔnnnewʼahyɛn akwankyerɛfo, wʼahyɛn mufo newɔn a wotuatua wʼahyɛn mu ntokuru,wʼaguadifo ne wʼasraafo nyinaa,ne obiara a ɔwɔ hyɛn no mubɛmem akɔ po ase tɔnn,da a wo hyɛn no bɛbɔ.
english:
Your wealth, merchandise and wares,
    your mariners, sailors and shipwrights,
your merchants and all your soldiers,
    and everyone else on board
will sink into the heart of the sea
    on the day of your shipwreck.

twi: Mpoano asase bɛwosowbere a wo hyɛn mufo no reteɛteɛ mu.
english:
The shorelands will quake
    when your sailors cry out.

twi: Wɔn a wokurakura atabon no nyinaabegyaw wɔn ahyɛn hɔ;hyɛn akwankyerɛfo ne hyɛn mufo nyinaabegyinagyina mpoano.
english:
All who handle the oars
    will abandon their ships;
the mariners and all the sailors
    will stand on the shore.

twi: Wɔbɛma wɔn nne soasu osu yaayaw ama wo;wɔbɛpete mfutuma agu wɔn ti sona wɔayantayantam nsõ mu.
english:
They will raise their voice
    and cry bitterly over you;
they will sprinkle dust on their heads
    and roll in ashes.

twi: Wo nti wɔbɛbobɔ tikwawna wɔafurafura atweaatam.Wɔde ɔkra mu ahoyerawne awerɛhow a mu yɛ denbegyam wo.
english:
They will shave their heads because of you
    and will put on sackcloth.
They will weep over you with anguish of soul
    and with bitter mourning.

twi: Bere a wɔretwa adwo redi awerɛhow nowɔbɛma kwadwom bi a ɛfa wo ho so se:“Hena na wama no atɔ mumte sɛ Tiro a po atwa ne ho ahyia yi?”
english:
As they wail and mourn over you,
    they will take up a lament concerning you:
“Who was ever silenced like Tyre,
    surrounded by the sea?”

twi: Bere a wʼaguade kɔɔ po ahorow so nowoboaa aman bebree;Wʼahonyade ne wʼaguademaa asase so ahemfo nyaa wɔn ho.
english:
When your merchandise went out on the seas,
    you satisfied many nations;
with your great wealth and your wares
    you enriched the kings of the earth.

twi: Afei po abubu wo mu nketenketewɔ asu no bun muwʼaguade ne wʼadwumayɛfo nyinaane wo amem kɔ asu ase.
english:
Now you are shattered by the sea
    in the depths of the waters;
your wares and all your company
    have gone down with you.

twi: Wɔn a wɔtete mpoano nyinaaho adwiriw wɔn wɔ wo ho;ehu ma wɔn ahemfo ho popona wɔn anim sinsiam.
english:
All who live in the coastlands
    are appalled at you;
their kings shudder with horror
    and their faces are distorted with fear.

twi: Aman no mu aguadifo bɔ ntwɔm gu wo sowoaba awiei a ɛyɛ huna wɔrenhu wo bio.’ ”
Nkɔmhyɛ A Etia TiroheneAwurade asɛm baa me nkyɛn se:
english: The word of the Lord came to me:

twi: “Onipa ba, ka kyerɛ Tiro sodifo no se: ‘Sɛɛ na Otumfo Awurade se:“ ‘Wufi wʼahantan koma mu ka se,“Meyɛ onyame;mete onyame bi ahengua sowɔ po mfimfini.”Nanso woyɛ onipa, wonyɛ onyame,ɛwɔ mu, wudwen sɛ wunim nyansa sɛ onyame bi.
english:
“Son of man, say to the ruler of Tyre, ‘This is what the Sovereign Lord says:
“‘In the pride of your heart
    you say, “I am a god;
I sit on the throne of a god
    in the heart of the seas.”
But you are a mere mortal and not a god,
    though you think you are as wise as a god.

twi: Wunim nyansa sen Daniel ana?Wunim kokoamsɛm biara ana?
english:
Are you wiser than Daniel?
    Is no secret hidden from you?

twi: Wonam wo nyansa ne nhumu soanya ahode ama wo ho,woapɛ sikakɔkɔɔ ne dwetɛ bebreeagu wʼadekoradan mu.
english:
By your wisdom and understanding
    you have gained wealth for yourself
and amassed gold and silver
    in your treasuries.

twi: Wonam wʼaguadi mu nyansa soama wʼahonya adɔɔso,na wʼahonya ntiwoahoran wɔ wo koma mu.
english:
By your great skill in trading
    you have increased your wealth,
and because of your wealth
    your heart has grown proud.

twi: “ ‘Ɛno nti sɛɛ na Otumfo Awurade se:“ ‘Esiane sɛ wudwen sɛ wunim nyansate sɛ Onyame nti,
english:
“‘Therefore this is what the Sovereign Lord says:
“‘Because you think you are wise,
    as wise as a god,

twi: mede ananafo reba abetia wo,amanaman no mu ɔdesɛefo pa ara;wɔbɛtwetwe wɔn afoawɔ wʼahoɔfɛ ne wo nyansa sona wɔahwirew wʼanuonyam no.
english:
I am going to bring foreigners against you,
    the most ruthless of nations;
they will draw their swords against your beauty and wisdom
    and pierce your shining splendor.

twi: Wɔde wo bɛto amoa no mu,na wubewu owu yaayawwɔ ɛpo mfimfini.
english:
They will bring you down to the pit,
    and you will die a violent death
    in the heart of the seas.

twi: Afei wobɛka se, “Meyɛ onyame,”wɔ wɔn a wokum wo no anim ana?Wobɛyɛ onipa na ɛnyɛ onyame,wɔ wɔn a wokum wo no nsam.
english:
Will you then say, “I am a god,”
    in the presence of those who kill you?
You will be but a mortal, not a god,
    in the hands of those who slay you.

twi: Wubewu momonotofo wuwɔ ananafo nsam.Me na maka, Otumfo Awurade asɛm ni.’ ”
english:
You will die the death of the uncircumcised
    at the hands of foreigners.
I have spoken, declares the Sovereign Lord.’”

twi: Awurade asɛm baa me nkyɛn se:
english: The word of the Lord came to me:

twi: “Onipa ba, ma kwadwom a ɛfa Tirohene ho so na ka kyerɛ no se: ‘Sɛɛ na Otumfo Awurade se:“ ‘Na anka woyɛ pɛyɛ nhwɛso,na wowɔ nyansa na woyɛ ahoɔfɛdua.
english:
“Son of man, take up a lament concerning the king of Tyre and say to him: ‘This is what the Sovereign Lord says:
“‘You were the seal of perfection,
    full of wisdom and perfect in beauty.

twi: Na anka wowɔ EdenOnyankopɔn turo no mu.Wɔde abohemaa nyinaa siesie wo:bogyanambo, akraatebo ne bɔwerɛbosikabereɛbo, apopobibiribo ne ahwehwɛbo,hoabo, nsrammabo ne ahabammono bo;wɔde sika kɔkɔɔ na ayɛ wʼahyehyɛde,wosiesiee ne nyinaa da a wɔbɔɔ wo.
english:
You were in Eden,
    the garden of God;
every precious stone adorned you:
    carnelian, chrysolite and emerald,
    topaz, onyx and jasper,
    lapis lazuli, turquoise and beryl.
Your settings and mountings were made of gold;
    on the day you were created they were prepared.

twi: Wɔsraa wo ngo sɛ ɔhwɛfo kerub,efisɛ saa na mehyɛɛ wo.Na wowɔ Onyankopɔn bepɔw kronkron no so;wonantew ogya abo mu.
english:
You were anointed as a guardian cherub,
    for so I ordained you.
You were on the holy mount of God;
    you walked among the fiery stones.

twi: Na anka wʼakwan ho nni asɛmefi da a wɔbɔɔ wo nokosii sɛ wohuu amumɔyɛ wɔ wo mu.
english:
You were blameless in your ways
    from the day you were created
    till wickedness was found in you.

twi: Wʼaguadi a mu trɛw no ntiwɔde akakabensɛm hyɛɛ wo mana woyɛɛ bɔne.Ɛno nti mepam wo fiiOnyankopɔn bepɔw no so wɔ animguase mu,na miyii wo adi, ɔhwɛfo kerub,fii ogya abo no mu.
english:
Through your widespread trade
    you were filled with violence,
    and you sinned.
So I drove you in disgrace from the mount of God,
    and I expelled you, guardian cherub,
    from among the fiery stones.

twi: Wohyerɛn wɔ wo koma muwʼahoɔfɛ ntina womaa wo nyansa porɔwee,wʼanuonyam no nti.Enti metow wo kyenee fam;na mede wo yɛɛ ahwɛde wɔ ahemfo anim.
english:
Your heart became proud
    on account of your beauty,
and you corrupted your wisdom
    because of your splendor.
So I threw you to the earth;
    I made a spectacle of you before kings.

twi: Wode wo nnebɔne ne aguadi mu asisiagu wo kronkrommea ho fiɛno nti memaa ogya fii wo muna ɛhyew wo,na memaa wo dan nsõ wɔ famwɔ wɔn a na wɔrehwɛ no nyinaa anim.
english:
By your many sins and dishonest trade
    you have desecrated your sanctuaries.
So I made a fire come out from you,
    and it consumed you,
and I reduced you to ashes on the ground
    in the sight of all who were watching.

twi: Aman a na wonim wo nyinaaho adwiriw wɔn wɔ wo ho:wʼawiei ayɛ ahometewna wɔrenhu wo bio.’ ”
english:
All the nations who knew you
    are appalled at you;
you have come to a horrible end
    and will be no more.’”

twi: Nkɔmhyɛ A Etia SidonAwurade asɛm baa me nkyɛn se:
english: The word of the Lord came to me:

twi: “Onipa ba, fa wʼani kyerɛ Sidon na hyɛ nkɔm tia no
english: “Son of man, set your face against Sidon; prophesy against her

twi: na ka se: ‘Sɛɛ na Otumfo Awurade se:“ ‘Me ne wo anya, Sidonna mɛda mʼanuonyam adi wɔ mo mu.Wubehu sɛ mene Awurade no,bere a mede asotwe aba ne sona mada me ho adi sɛ ɔkronkronni wɔ ne mu no.
english:
and say: ‘This is what the Sovereign Lord says:
“‘I am against you, Sidon,
    and among you I will display my glory.
You will know that I am the Lord,
    when I inflict punishment on you
    and within you am proved to be holy.

twi: Mɛma ɔyaredɔm aba ne sona mama mogya ateɛ wɔ ne mmɔnten so.Apirafo bɛtotɔ wɔ ne mu,bere a afoa redi ahim wɔ ne ho nyinaa.Afei na wobehu sɛ mene Awurade no.
english:
I will send a plague upon you
    and make blood flow in your streets.
The slain will fall within you,
    with the sword against you on every side.
Then you will know that I am the Lord.

twi: “ ‘Na Israelfo rennya yɔnkonom a wɔwɔ adwemmɔne, wɔn a wɔwowɔ yayaayaw sɛ ohwirem ne nsɔe bio. Afei na wobehu sɛ mene Otumfo Awurade no.
english: “‘No longer will the people of Israel have malicious neighbors who are painful briers and sharp thorns. Then they will know that I am the Sovereign Lord.

twi: “ ‘Sɛɛ na Otumfo Awurade se: Sɛ meboa Israelfo ano fi aman a wabɔ wɔn apete no so a, mɛda me kronkronyɛ adi wɔ wɔn mu, ama amanaman no ahu. Afei wɔbɛtena wɔn ankasa asase a mede maa me somfo Yakob no so.
english: “‘This is what the Sovereign Lord says: When I gather the people of Israel from the nations where they have been scattered, I will be proved holy through them in the sight of the nations. Then they will live in their own land, which I gave to my servant Jacob.

twi: Wɔbɛtena hɔ asomdwoe mu na wobesisi adan, ayeyɛ bobe nturo; Wɔbɛtena ase asomdwoe mu wɔ bere a matwe ne yɔnkonom a wɔkasa tiaa no no nyinaa aso. Afei wobehu sɛ mene Awurade, wɔn Nyankopɔn no.’ ”
english: They will live there in safety and will build houses and plant vineyards; they will live in safety when I inflict punishment on all their neighbors who maligned them. Then they will know that I am the Lord their God.’”

twi: Nkɔmhyɛ A Etia MisraimMfe du so ɔsram a ɛto so du no da a ɛto so dumien no, Awurade asɛm baa me nkyɛn se:
english: In the tenth year, in the tenth month on the twelfth day, the word of the Lord came to me:

twi: “Onipa ba, fa wʼani kyerɛ Misraimhene Farao so na hyɛ nkɔm tia no ne Misraim nyinaa.
english: “Son of man, set your face against Pharaoh king of Egypt and prophesy against him and against all Egypt.

twi: Kasa kyerɛ no na ka se: ‘Sɛɛ na Otumfo Awurade se.“ ‘Me ne wo anya, Misraimhene Faraoasuboa kɛse a woda wo nsuwansuwa mu.’ ”Woka se, “Nil yɛ mede;meyɛ maa me ho.”
english:
Speak to him and say: ‘This is what the Sovereign Lord says:
“‘I am against you, Pharaoh king of Egypt,
    you great monster lying among your streams.
You say, “The Nile belongs to me;
    I made it for myself.”

twi: Na mede nnarewa besuso wʼabogye muna mama mpataa a wɔwɔ wo nsuwansuwa mu noatetare wʼabon ho.Mɛtwe wo afi wo nsuwansuwa no mu,a mpataa no nyinaa tetare wo ho.
english:
But I will put hooks in your jaws
    and make the fish of your streams stick to your scales.
I will pull you out from among your streams,
    with all the fish sticking to your scales.

twi: Megyaw wo hɔ wɔ sare no so,wo ne mpataa a wɔwɔ wo nsuwansuwa mu no nyinaa.Mobɛhwe ase wɔ asase petee mua wɔremma mo so bio.Mede wo bɛma asase so mmoane wim nnomaa sɛ wɔn aduan.
english:
I will leave you in the desert,
    you and all the fish of your streams.
You will fall on the open field
    and not be gathered or picked up.
I will give you as food
    to the beasts of the earth and the birds of the sky.

twi: Afei wɔn a wɔte Misraim nyinaa behu sɛ mene Awurade no.“ ‘Woayɛ sɛ demmire pema ama Israelfi.
english:
Then all who live in Egypt will know that I am the Lord.
“‘You have been a staff of reed for the people of Israel.

twi: Wɔde wɔn nsa soo wo mu no, wo mu bukaw ma wuhuruwii, wotwerii wo no, wo mu bu ma wobɔɔ pemmɔ.
english: When they grasped you with their hands, you splintered and you tore open their shoulders; when they leaned on you, you broke and their backs were wrenched.

twi: “ ‘Ɛno nti sɛɛ na Otumfo Awurade se: Mede afoa bɛba abɛko atia wo na makunkum wo mmarima ne wɔn mmoa.
english: “‘Therefore this is what the Sovereign Lord says: I will bring a sword against you and kill both man and beast.

twi: Misraim bɛda mpan na asɛe. Ɛno na wobehu sɛ mene Awurade.“ ‘Efisɛ wokae se, “Nil yɛ me de; me na meyɛe,” enti
english:
Egypt will become a desolate wasteland. Then they will know that I am the Lord.
“‘Because you said, “The Nile is mine; I made it,”

twi: me ne wo ne wo nsuwansuwa na anya, na mɛma Misraim asase asɛe na ada mpan, efi Migdol kosi Aswan twa mu de kɔka Kus hye so.
english: therefore I am against you and against your streams, and I will make the land of Egypt a ruin and a desolate waste from Migdol to Aswan, as far as the border of Cush.

twi: Onipa anaa aboa biara nan rensi so, obiara rentena so mfe aduanan.
english: The foot of neither man nor beast will pass through it; no one will live there for forty years.

twi: Mɛma Misraim asase no ada mpan wɔ nsase a asɛe mu na ne nkuropɔn bɛda mpan mfe aduanan wɔ wɔn nkuropɔn a asɛe no mu. Na mɛbɔ Misraimfo apete wɔ amanaman mu, na mahwete wɔn wɔ nsase so.
english: I will make the land of Egypt desolate among devastated lands, and her cities will lie desolate forty years among ruined cities. And I will disperse the Egyptians among the nations and scatter them through the countries.

twi: “ ‘Nanso sɛɛ ne nea Otumfo Awurade se: Mfe aduanan akyi no, mɛboaboa Misraimfo ano afi aman a mebɔɔ wɔn petee so no so.
english: “‘Yet this is what the Sovereign Lord says: At the end of forty years I will gather the Egyptians from the nations where they were scattered.

twi: Mede wɔn befi nnommumfa mu aba na mede wɔn akɔ Misraim Atifi, wɔn nenanom asase. Ɛhɔ na wɔbɛyɛ ahenni mu kumaa bi.
english: I will bring them back from captivity and return them to Upper Egypt, the land of their ancestry. There they will be a lowly kingdom.

twi: Ɛbɛyɛ ahenni a ɛnyɛ den na ɛrentumi mma ne ho so wɔ aman a aka no mu. Mɛyɛ no ahenni a ɛrentumi nni aman afoforo so.
english: It will be the lowliest of kingdoms and will never again exalt itself above the other nations. I will make it so weak that it will never again rule over the nations.

twi: Misraim renyɛ ɔman a Israelfo de wɔn ho bɛto no so bio, mmom ɛbɛkae wɔn bɔne a wɔyɛɛ sɛ wɔde wɔn ho kɔdan no de pɛɛ mmoa. Afei, wobehu sɛ mene Otumfo Awurade no.’ ”
english: Egypt will no longer be a source of confidence for the people of Israel but will be a reminder of their sin in turning to her for help. Then they will know that I am the Sovereign Lord.’”

twi: Mfe aduonu ason so, ɔsram a edi kan no da a edi kan no, Awurade asɛm baa me nkyɛn se:
english: In the twenty-seventh year, in the first month on the first day, the word of the Lord came to me:

twi: “Onipa ba, Babiloniahene Nebukadnessar ne nʼasraafo tuu Tiro so sa abran so, eti biara so pepae, na ɔbati nso so popɔree. Nanso ɔne nʼasraafo no annya hwee amfi adwumaden a wɔyɛ de tiaa Tiro no mu.
english: “Son of man, Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon drove his army in a hard campaign against Tyre; every head was rubbed bare and every shoulder made raw. Yet he and his army got no reward from the campaign he led against Tyre.

twi: Ɛno nti, sɛɛ na Otumfo Awurade se: Mede Misraim rebɛhyɛ Babiloniahene Nebukadnessar nsa na ɔbɛsoa nʼahode akɔ. Ɔbɛfom asase no de ayɛ akatua ama nʼasraafo.
english: Therefore this is what the Sovereign Lord says: I am going to give Egypt to Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon, and he will carry off its wealth. He will loot and plunder the land as pay for his army.

twi: Mede Misraim ama no sɛ nʼadwumayɛ so akatua, efisɛ ɔne nʼakofo yɛ maa me, Otumfo Awurade asɛm ni.
english: I have given him Egypt as a reward for his efforts because he and his army did it for me, declares the Sovereign Lord.

twi: “Saa da no mɛma abɛn bi afifi ama Israelfi, na mebue wʼano wɔ wɔn mu. Afei wobehu sɛ mene Awurade no.”
english: “On that day I will make a horn grow for the Israelites, and I will open your mouth among them. Then they will know that I am the Lord.”

twi: Misraim Ho KwadwomAwurade asɛm baa me nkyɛn se:
english: The word of the Lord came to me:

twi: “Onipa ba, hyɛ nkɔm na ka se: ‘Sɛɛ na Otumfo Awurade se:“ ‘Twa adwo na ka se,“Ao da no!”
english:
“Son of man, prophesy and say: ‘This is what the Sovereign Lord says:
“‘Wail and say,
    “Alas for that day!”

twi: Na da no abɛn,Awurade da no abɛn,omununkum da,amanaman no atemmu bere.
english:
For the day is near,
    the day of the Lord is near—
a day of clouds,
    a time of doom for the nations.

twi: Afoa bi bɛsɔre atia Misraim,na ahoyeraw bɛba Kus so.Sɛ apirafo totɔ wɔ Misraim awɔbɛsoa nʼahonyade akɔna wɔabubu ne fapem agu fam.
english:
A sword will come against Egypt,
    and anguish will come upon Cush.
When the slain fall in Egypt,
    her wealth will be carried away
    and her foundations torn down.

twi: Kus ne Put, Lidia ne Arabia nyinaa, Libia ne bɔhyɛ asase no so nnipa ne Misraim bɛtotɔ wɔ afoa ano.
english: Cush and Libya, Lydia and all Arabia, Kub and the people of the covenant land will fall by the sword along with Egypt.

twi: “ ‘Sɛɛ na Awurade se:“ ‘Misraim nnamfonom bɛtotɔna nʼahomaso ahoɔden bedi no huammɔ.Efi Migdol kosi Aswanwɔbɛtotɔ wɔ afoa a ɛwɔ ne mu no ano,Otumfo Awurade asɛm ni.
english:
“‘This is what the Lord says:
“‘The allies of Egypt will fall
    and her proud strength will fail.
From Migdol to Aswan
    they will fall by the sword within her,
declares the Sovereign Lord.

twi: Wɔbɛdeda mpanwɔ nsase a ada mpan mu,na wɔn nkuropɔn bebubu akankuropɔn a abubu ho.
english:
“‘They will be desolate
    among desolate lands,
and their cities will lie
    among ruined cities.

twi: Afei wobehu sɛ mene Awurade no,bere a mede ogya ato Misraim muna madwerɛw nʼaboafo nyinaa no.
english:
Then they will know that I am the Lord,
    when I set fire to Egypt
    and all her helpers are crushed.

twi: “ ‘Saa da no, asomafo de ahyɛn befi me nkyɛn akohunahuna Kus a ne tirim yɛ no dɛ no. Ne ho bɛyeraw no wɔ Misraim atemmuda no, na ampa ara ɛbɛba mu.
english: “‘On that day messengers will go out from me in ships to frighten Cush out of her complacency. Anguish will take hold of them on the day of Egypt’s doom, for it is sure to come.

twi: “ ‘Sɛɛ na Otumfo Awurade se:“ ‘Mede Misraim dɔm bebrebe no bɛba awieimɛfa Babiloniahene Nebukadnessar so.
english:
“‘This is what the Sovereign Lord says:
“‘I will put an end to the hordes of Egypt
    by the hand of Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon.

twi: Ɔno ne nʼasraafo; amanaman no mu anuɔdenfo,wɔde wɔn bɛba abɛsɛe asase no.Wɔbɛtwe wɔn afoa atia Misraimna wɔde afunu ahyɛ asase no so ma.
english:
He and his army—the most ruthless of nations—
    will be brought in to destroy the land.
They will draw their swords against Egypt
    and fill the land with the slain.

twi: Mɛma Nil mu nsu ayowna matɔn asase no ama nnipa bɔne;menam ananafo sobɛsɛe asase no ne nea ɛwɔ mu nyinaa.Me Awurade na maka.
english:
I will dry up the waters of the Nile
    and sell the land to an evil nation;
by the hand of foreigners
    I will lay waste the land and everything in it.
I the Lord have spoken.

twi: “ ‘Sɛɛ na Otumfo Awurade se:“ ‘Mɛsɛe ahoni nona mede Memfis nsɛsode ahorow no aba awiei.Misraim rennya mmapɔmma bio,na mɛma hu aba asase no so nyinaa.
english:
“‘This is what the Sovereign Lord says:
“‘I will destroy the idols
    and put an end to the images in Memphis.
No longer will there be a prince in Egypt,
    and I will spread fear throughout the land.

twi: Mɛsɛe Misraim Atifi,ato Soan mu gyana matwe Tebes aso.
english:
I will lay waste Upper Egypt,
    set fire to Zoan
    and inflict punishment on Thebes.

twi: Mehwie mʼabufuwhyew agu Pɛlusum so,Misraim bammɔ dennen no,na matwa Tebes nnipa bebrebe no agu.
english:
I will pour out my wrath on Pelusium,
    the stronghold of Egypt,
    and wipe out the hordes of Thebes.

twi: Mɛto Misraim mu gya;Pɛlusum de ɔyaw bebubu ne mu.Ahum bebu afa Tebes so;na Memfis bedi abooboo da biara.
Heliopolis ne Bubastis mmerantebɛtotɔ wɔ afoa ano,na nkuropɔn no ankasa bɛkɔ nnommum mu.
english:
The young men of Heliopolis and Bubastis
    will fall by the sword,
    and the cities themselves will go into captivity.

twi: Sum kabii beduru Tapanhes, da nosɛ mibubu Misraim konnua no a;hɔ na nʼahomaso ahoɔden bɛba awiei.Omununkum bɛkata no so,na ne nkuraa bɛkɔ nnommum mu.
english:
Dark will be the day at Tahpanhes
    when I break the yoke of Egypt;
    there her proud strength will come to an end.
She will be covered with clouds,
    and her villages will go into captivity.

twi: Ɛno nti mɛtwe Misraim aso,na wobehu sɛ mene Awurade no.’ ”
english:
So I will inflict punishment on Egypt,
    and they will know that I am the Lord.’”

twi: Afe a ɛto so dubaako no, ɔsram a edi kan no da a ɛto so ason no, Awurade asɛm baa me nkyɛn se:
english: In the eleventh year, in the first month on the seventh day, the word of the Lord came to me:

twi: “Onipa ba, mabu Misraimhene Farao basa mu. Wɔnkyekyeree, na atoa bio; na wɔmfa nhyɛɛ ntama bamma mu na anya ahoɔden a ɔde beso afoa mu.
english: “Son of man, I have broken the arm of Pharaoh king of Egypt. It has not been bound up to be healed or put in a splint so that it may become strong enough to hold a sword.

twi: Ɛno nti, Otumfo Awurade na ose: Mene Misraimhene Farao anya; mebubu nʼabasa abien no mu; basa a eye ne nea mu abu no, na mama afoa afi ne nsam atɔ fam.
english: Therefore this is what the Sovereign Lord says: I am against Pharaoh king of Egypt. I will break both his arms, the good arm as well as the broken one, and make the sword fall from his hand.

twi: Mede Misraimfo bɛkɔ amanaman mu na mahwete wɔn agu nsase so.
english: I will disperse the Egyptians among the nations and scatter them through the countries.

twi: Mɛhyɛ Babiloniahene basa mu den na mede mʼafoa ahyɛ ne nsa, nanso Farao de, mebu nʼabasa mu, na wasi apini wɔ nʼanim sɛ obi a wapira opirabɔne.
english: I will strengthen the arms of the king of Babylon and put my sword in his hand, but I will break the arms of Pharaoh, and he will groan before him like a mortally wounded man.

twi: Mɛma Babiloniahene abasa mu ayɛ den, nanso Farao abasa bedwudwo asensɛn ne ho. Sɛ mede mʼafoa hyɛ Babiloniahene nsa na ɔma so tia Misraim a, wobehu sɛ mene Awurade no.
english: I will strengthen the arms of the king of Babylon, but the arms of Pharaoh will fall limp. Then they will know that I am the Lord, when I put my sword into the hand of the king of Babylon and he brandishes it against Egypt.

twi: Mede Misraimfo bɛkɔ amanaman mu na mahwete wɔn agu nsase no so. Ɛno na wobehu sɛ mene Awurade no.”
english: I will disperse the Egyptians among the nations and scatter them through the countries. Then they will know that I am the Lord.”

twi: Sida Bi A Ɛwɔ LebanonMfe dubaako mu, ɔsram a ɛto so abiɛsa no da a edi kan no, Awurade asɛm baa me nkyɛn se,
english: In the eleventh year, in the third month on the first day, the word of the Lord came to me:

twi: “Onipa ba, ka kyerɛ Misraimhene Farao ne ne dɔm se:“ ‘Hena ho na wɔde wo kɛseyɛ bɛtoto?
english:
“Son of man, say to Pharaoh king of Egypt and to his hordes:
“‘Who can be compared with you in majesty?

twi: Dwene Asiria ho, sida bi a bere bi na ɛwɔ Lebanon,Ɔde mman a ɛyɛ fɛ, na ɛhyɛ kwae sonyin kɔɔ soro yiye,ma ne nkɔn mu boro nhaban a ayɛ kusuu no so.
english:
Consider Assyria, once a cedar in Lebanon,
    with beautiful branches overshadowing the forest;
it towered on high,
    its top above the thick foliage.

twi: Nsu no maa no aduan,mmura a mu dɔ ma enyin kɔɔ soro;wɔn nsuwansuwa sen faa nʼase nyinaade kɔɔ mfuw no so nnua nyinaa ho.
english:
The waters nourished it,
    deep springs made it grow tall;
their streams flowed
    all around its base
and sent their channels
    to all the trees of the field.

twi: Enti ɛkɔɔ sorosorosen mfuw no so nnua nyinaa;ne dubaa dɔɔsone mman nyin yɛɛ atenten,na nsu dodow a enyaa no nti ɛdennanee.
english:
So it towered higher
    than all the trees of the field;
its boughs increased
    and its branches grew long,
    spreading because of abundant waters.

twi: Wim nnomaa nyinaayɛɛ wɔn berebuw wɔ ne dubaa no mu,wuram mmoa nyinaawowoo mma wɔ ne mman no aseaman akɛse nyinaatenaa ne nwini ase.
english:
All the birds of the sky
    nested in its boughs,
all the animals of the wild
    gave birth under its branches;
all the great nations
    lived in its shade.

twi: Na ne kɛseyɛ no yɛ fɛ,ne dubaa a adennan no nti,na ne ntin nyin kɔɔ famkoduu nsu bebree mu.
english:
It was majestic in beauty,
    with its spreading boughs,
for its roots went down
    to abundant waters.

twi: Sida a ɛwɔ Onyankopɔn turo munto no,na ɔpepaw nnua nsodubaa ne no nyɛ pɛ,na wontumi mfa ɔfo nnua nsontoto ne mman ho,dua biara nni Onyankopɔn turono mu a nʼahoɔfɛ te sɛ no.
english:
The cedars in the garden of God
    could not rival it,
nor could the junipers
    equal its boughs,
nor could the plane trees
    compare with its branches—
no tree in the garden of God
    could match its beauty.

twi: Mebɔɔ no ahoɔfɛmaa no mman bebree,na nnua a ɛwɔ Eden nyinaaOnyankopɔn turo no mu noani beree no.
english:
I made it beautiful
    with abundant branches,
the envy of all the trees of Eden
    in the garden of God.

twi: “ ‘Ɛno nti, sɛɛ na Otumfo Awurade se: Esiane sɛ enyin kɔɔ soro, maa ne nkɔn mu hyɛɛ nhaban a abunkam so, na afei ɔyɛɛ ahantan wɔ ne tentenyɛ ho nti,
english: “‘Therefore this is what the Sovereign Lord says: Because the great cedar towered over the thick foliage, and because it was proud of its height,

twi: mede no hyɛɛ amanaman sodifo nsa, sɛ ɔne no nni no sɛnea nʼamumɔyɛ te. Mepoo no,
english: I gave it into the hands of the ruler of the nations, for him to deal with according to its wickedness. I cast it aside,

twi: na ananafo aman no mu anuɔdenfo twaa no hwee fam, na ogyaw no hɔ. Ne dubaa no hwehwee mmepɔw ne aku mu; ne mman mu bubuu wɔ subon mu. Asase so aman nyinaa fii ne nwini ase, na wogyaw no hɔ.
english: and the most ruthless of foreign nations cut it down and left it. Its boughs fell on the mountains and in all the valleys; its branches lay broken in all the ravines of the land. All the nations of the earth came out from under its shade and left it.

twi: Wim nnomaa nyinaa sisii dua a abu no so, na wuram mmoa kɔhyehyɛɛ ne mman mu.
english: All the birds settled on the fallen tree, and all the wild animals lived among its branches.

twi: Ɛno nti, nnua a ɛwɔ nsu ho no mu biara renyɛ ahantan, nnyin nkɔ sorosoro, mmoro nhaban a abunkam so no so. Nnua afoforo biara a enya nsu bebree no rennyin nkɔ soro saa bio. Wɔahyɛ sɛ wɔn nyinaa bewu akɔ asase ase, wɔ nnipamma a wosian kɔ amoa mu no nkyɛn.
english: Therefore no other trees by the waters are ever to tower proudly on high, lifting their tops above the thick foliage. No other trees so well-watered are ever to reach such a height; they are all destined for death, for the earth below, among mortals who go down to the realm of the dead.

twi: “ ‘Sɛɛ na Otumfo Awurade se: Da a wɔde no too ɔda mu no, mede awerɛhow kataa nsuwansuwa a mu dɔ no so maa no, na amma ne nsuten no ansen, na misiw ne nsu dodow no kwan. Ne nti mede kusuuyɛ furaa Lebanon, na nnua a ɛwɔ sare no so nyinaa botowee.
english: “‘This is what the Sovereign Lord says: On the day it was brought down to the realm of the dead I covered the deep springs with mourning for it; I held back its streams, and its abundant waters were restrained. Because of it I clothed Lebanon with gloom, and all the trees of the field withered away.

twi: Memaa aman no ho popoo wɔ nʼasehwe nnyigyei no ho, bere a mede no baa ɔda mu ne wɔn a wɔasian kɔ amoa mu no. Afei Eden nnua nyinaa, nea ɛte apɔw na ɛyɛ papa wɔ Lebanon, nnua a enya nsu yiye nyinaa nyaa awerɛkyekye wɔ asase ase.
english: I made the nations tremble at the sound of its fall when I brought it down to the realm of the dead to be with those who go down to the pit. Then all the trees of Eden, the choicest and best of Lebanon, the well-watered trees, were consoled in the earth below.

twi: Wɔn a wɔtenaa ne nwini ase, ne ne dɔm a wɔwɔ amanaman no mu nso ne no kɔ ɔda mu, akɔka wɔn a wɔtotɔɔ wɔ afoa ano no ho.
english: They too, like the great cedar, had gone down to the realm of the dead, to those killed by the sword, along with the armed men who lived in its shade among the nations.

twi: “ ‘Nnua a ɛwɔ Eden no mu de, ɛwɔ he na ebetumi de ne ho atoto wo ho wɔ anuonyam ne kɛseyɛ mu? Nanso wo nso wobesian wo akɔ fam, wo ne Eden nnua no. Wobɛfra momonotofo mu, wɔn a wɔatotɔ wɔ afoa ano no.“ ‘Eyi yɛ Farao ne ne dɔm no, Otumfo Awurade asɛm ni.’ ”
english:
“‘Which of the trees of Eden can be compared with you in splendor and majesty? Yet you, too, will be brought down with the trees of Eden to the earth below; you will lie among the uncircumcised, with those killed by the sword.
“‘This is Pharaoh and all his hordes, declares the Sovereign Lord.’”

twi: Farao Ho KwadwomMfe dumien mu, ɔsram a ɛto so dumien no da a edi kan no, Awurade asɛm baa me nkyɛn se:
english: In the twelfth year, in the twelfth month on the first day, the word of the Lord came to me:

twi: “Onipa ba, to kwadwom fa Misraimhene Farao ho na ka kyerɛ no se:“ ‘Wote sɛ gyata wɔ aman no mu:wote sɛ po mu aboa a ne ho yɛ huwububu dikyi wɔ wo nsuten mu,wode wo nan boro nsuten node fono nsu no.
english:
“Son of man, take up a lament concerning Pharaoh king of Egypt and say to him:
“‘You are like a lion among the nations;
    you are like a monster in the seas
thrashing about in your streams,
    churning the water with your feet
    and muddying the streams.

twi: “ ‘Sɛɛ na Otumfo Awurade se:“ ‘Mede dɔm bɛbaabɛtow mʼasau agu wo so,na wɔbɛtwe wo afi mʼasau mu.
english:
“‘This is what the Sovereign Lord says:
“‘With a great throng of people
    I will cast my net over you,
    and they will haul you up in my net.

twi: Mɛtow wo akyene asase no sona mahiri wo ato sare so.Mɛma wim nnomaa nyinaa abesisi wo sona asase so mmoa nyinaa adi wo nam afrɛ so.
english:
I will throw you on the land
    and hurl you on the open field.
I will let all the birds of the sky settle on you
    and all the animals of the wild gorge themselves on you.

twi: Mɛhata wo nam wɔ mmepɔw no sona mede wo funu ahyɛ aku ma.
english:
I will spread your flesh on the mountains
    and fill the valleys with your remains.

twi: Mede wo mogya a ɛresen noafɔw asase no de akɔka mmepɔw nona wo nam bɛhyɛ abon nketewa no ma.
english:
I will drench the land with your flowing blood
    all the way to the mountains,
    and the ravines will be filled with your flesh.

twi: Sɛ mitwa wo fi hɔ a, mɛkata ɔsoro anina madunnum wɔn nsoromma;mede omununkum bɛkata owia ani,na ɔsram renhyerɛn.
english:
When I snuff you out, I will cover the heavens
    and darken their stars;
I will cover the sun with a cloud,
    and the moon will not give its light.

twi: Ɔsoro akanea a ɛhyerɛn nyinaamɛma aduru sum wɔ wo so;mɛma sum aduru wʼasase, Otumfo Awurade asɛm ni.
english:
All the shining lights in the heavens
    I will darken over you;
    I will bring darkness over your land,
declares the Sovereign Lord.

twi: Mɛma nnipa bebree koma atutubere a mede wo sɛe aba aman no mu,nsase a wunnya nhuu mu.
english:
I will trouble the hearts of many peoples
    when I bring about your destruction among the nations,
    among lands you have not known.

twi: Mɛma nnipa bebree ho adwiriw wɔn wɔ wo ho,wo nti, hu bɛma wɔn ahene ho apopobere a merehim mʼafoa wɔ wɔn anim no.Da a wobɛhwe ase nowɔn mu biara ho bɛwosowbere nyinaa mu wɔ wɔn nkwa nti.
english:
I will cause many peoples to be appalled at you,
    and their kings will shudder with horror because of you
    when I brandish my sword before them.
On the day of your downfall
    each of them will tremble
    every moment for his life.

twi: “ ‘Na sɛɛ na Otumfo Awurade se:“ ‘Babiloniahene afoabɛsɔre wɔ wo so.
english:
“‘For this is what the Sovereign Lord says:
“‘The sword of the king of Babylon
    will come against you.

twi: Mɛma wo dɔm no atotɔwɔ dɔmmarima afoa ano,wɔ aman a wɔyɛ anuɔdenfo mu.Wɔbɛsɛe Misraim ahomaso pasaana ne dɔm no nyinaa bedi nkogu.
english:
I will cause your hordes to fall
    by the swords of mighty men—
    the most ruthless of all nations.
They will shatter the pride of Egypt,
    and all her hordes will be overthrown.

twi: Mekunkum nʼanantwi nyinaaafi nsu bebree no hona onipa nan rentiatia mu biona anantwi tɔte nso remfono no.
english:
I will destroy all her cattle
    from beside abundant waters
no longer to be stirred by the foot of man
    or muddied by the hooves of cattle.

twi: Afei mɛma ne nsu ani atewna mama ne nsuten ateɛ sɛ ngo,Otumfo Awurade asɛm ni.
english:
Then I will let her waters settle
    and make her streams flow like oil,
declares the Sovereign Lord.

twi: Sɛ mema Misraim da mpanna miyi biribiara fi asase no so,sɛ mikum wɔn a wɔte so nyinaa a,afei na wobehu sɛ mene Awurade no.’
english:
When I make Egypt desolate
    and strip the land of everything in it,
when I strike down all who live there,
    then they will know that I am the Lord.’

twi: “Eyi ne kwadwom a wɔbɛto ama no. Amanaman no mmabea bɛto ama Misraim ne ne dɔm nyinaa, Otumfo Awurade asɛm ni.”
english: “This is the lament they will chant for her. The daughters of the nations will chant it; for Egypt and all her hordes they will chant it, declares the Sovereign Lord.”

twi: Afe a ɛto so dumien no ne sram da a ɛto so dunum no, Awurade asɛm baa me nkyɛn se:
english: In the twelfth year, on the fifteenth day of the month, the word of the Lord came to me:

twi: “Onipa ba, twa adwo ma Misraim dɔm na ma ɔne amanaman akɛse no mmabea nsian nkɔ asase ase nkɔka wɔn a wɔasian kɔ amoa mu no ho.
english: “Son of man, wail for the hordes of Egypt and consign to the earth below both her and the daughters of mighty nations, along with those who go down to the pit.

twi: Ka kyerɛ wɔn se, ‘Wadom mo dodo sen wɔn a aka no ana? Munsian nkɔ na mo ne momonotofo no nkɔda.’
english: Say to them, ‘Are you more favored than others? Go down and be laid among the uncircumcised.’

twi: Wɔbɛka wɔn a wowuwuu wɔ afoa ano no ho. Wɔatwe afoa no, ma wɔntwe ne nnipadɔm no ase nkɔ.
english: They will fall among those killed by the sword. The sword is drawn; let her be dragged off with all her hordes.

twi: Akannifo akɛse a wɔwɔ ɔda mu bɛka afa Misraim ne ne dɔm ho se, ‘Wɔasian aba na wɔdeda momonotofo mu, wɔn a wowuwuu wɔ afoa ano no.’
english: From within the realm of the dead the mighty leaders will say of Egypt and her allies, ‘They have come down and they lie with the uncircumcised, with those killed by the sword.’

twi: “Asiria ne nʼasraafo nyinaa wɔ hɔ, wɔn a wɔakunkum wɔn no nna atwa ne ho ahyia, wɔn a wɔatotɔ wɔ afoa ano no.
english: “Assyria is there with her whole army; she is surrounded by the graves of all her slain, all who have fallen by the sword.

twi: Wɔn nna no wɔ amoa no ase tɔnn na nʼasraafo deda ne nna ho nyinaa. Wɔn a na wohunahuna afoforo wɔ ateasefo asase so no nyinaa awuwu, wɔatotɔ wɔ afoa ano.
english: Their graves are in the depths of the pit and her army lies around her grave. All who had spread terror in the land of the living are slain, fallen by the sword.

twi: “Elam wɔ hɔ, ne nnipadɔm nyinaa atwa ne da ho ahyia. Wɔn nyinaa awuwu, wɔatotɔ wɔ afoa ano. Wɔn a na wohunahuna afoforo wɔ ateasefo asase so nyinaa sian kɔɔ asase ase sɛ momonotofo. Wɔde wɔn animguase kɔka wɔn a wosian kɔ amoa mu no ho.
english: “Elam is there, with all her hordes around her grave. All of them are slain, fallen by the sword. All who had spread terror in the land of the living went down uncircumcised to the earth below. They bear their shame with those who go down to the pit.

twi: Wɔato mpa ama no wɔ atɔfo no mu, na ne dɔm atwa ne da ho ahyia. Wɔn nyinaa yɛ momonotofo a wɔatotɔ wɔ afoa ano. Esiane sɛ wɔn ahunahuna trɛw wɔ ateasefo asase so no nti, wɔne wɔn a wosian kɔ amoa mu no nyinaa anim agu ase. Wɔadeda wɔn wɔ atɔfo no mu.
english: A bed is made for her among the slain, with all her hordes around her grave. All of them are uncircumcised, killed by the sword. Because their terror had spread in the land of the living, they bear their shame with those who go down to the pit; they are laid among the slain.

twi: “Mesek ne Tubal wɔ hɔ a wɔn dɔm atwa wɔn nna ho ahyia. Wɔn nyinaa yɛ momonotofo a wɔatotɔ wɔ afoa ano efisɛ wɔtrɛtrɛw wɔn ahunahuna mu wɔ ateasefo asase so.
english: “Meshek and Tubal are there, with all their hordes around their graves. All of them are uncircumcised, killed by the sword because they spread their terror in the land of the living.

twi: Ɛnyɛ wɔn ne akofo momonotofo foforo a wɔatotɔ na wɔdeda hɔ no ana? Wɔn a wɔne wɔn akode sian kɔɔ nna mu na wɔn ti deda wɔn afoa so no. Wɔn amumɔyɛ so asotwe daa wɔn nnompe so, mmom saa akofo yi ahunahuna atrɛtrɛw wɔ ateasefo asase so.
english: But they do not lie with the fallen warriors of old, who went down to the realm of the dead with their weapons of war—their swords placed under their heads and their shields resting on their bones—though these warriors also had terrorized the land of the living.

twi: “Farao, wo nso wobebubu wo mu na woakɔda momonotofo mu, wo ne wɔn a wɔtotɔɔ wɔ afoa ano no.
english: “You too, Pharaoh, will be broken and will lie among the uncircumcised, with those killed by the sword.

twi: “Edom wɔ hɔ, nʼahemfo ne ne mmapɔmma nyinaa deda wɔn a wɔatotɔ wɔ afoa ano no mu, wɔn tumi nyinaa akyi. Wɔdeda momonotofo mu, wɔne wɔn a wosian kɔ amoa mu no.
english: “Edom is there, her kings and all her princes; despite their power, they are laid with those killed by the sword. They lie with the uncircumcised, with those who go down to the pit.

twi: “Mmapɔmma a wofi atifi fam nyinaa ne Sidonfo nyinaa wɔ hɔ, wɔne atɔfo kɔɔ wɔ animguase mu, wɔn tumi a wɔde hunahuna no nyinaa akyi. Wɔdeda hɔ sɛ momonotofo, wɔne wɔn a wokum wɔn wɔ afoa ano, na wɔne wɔn a wosian kɔ amoa mu no asoa wɔn animguase.
english: “All the princes of the north and all the Sidonians are there; they went down with the slain in disgrace despite the terror caused by their power. They lie uncircumcised with those killed by the sword and bear their shame with those who go down to the pit.

twi: “Farao, ɔne nʼasraafo nyinaa behu wɔn na ne werɛ bɛkyekye wɔ ne dɔm a wokunkum wɔn wɔ afoa ano no ho, Otumfo Awurade asɛm ni.
english: “Pharaoh—he and all his army—will see them and he will be consoled for all his hordes that were killed by the sword, declares the Sovereign Lord.

twi: Mmom me na memaa Farao ne ne nnipadɔm de ahunahuna trɛtrɛw wɔ ateasefo asase so de, nanso wɔbɛdeda momonotofo mu, wɔn a wɔde afoa kunkum wɔn, Otumfo Awurade asɛm ni.”
english: Although I had him spread terror in the land of the living, Pharaoh and all his hordes will be laid among the uncircumcised, with those killed by the sword, declares the Sovereign Lord.”

twi: Ɔwɛmfo HesekielAwurade asɛm baa me nkyɛn se:
english: The word of the Lord came to me:

twi: “Onipa ba, kasa kyerɛ wo manmma na ka kyerɛ wɔn se: ‘Sɛ metwe mʼafoa wɔ asase bi so, na sɛ asase no so nnipa yi wɔn mmarima no mu baako sɛ ɔnyɛ ɔwɛmfo mma wɔn,
english: “Son of man, speak to your people and say to them: ‘When I bring the sword against a land, and the people of the land choose one of their men and make him their watchman,

twi: na ohu sɛ afoa reba abɛko atia asase no a, ɔhyɛn torobɛnto de bɔ nnipa no kɔkɔ.
english: and he sees the sword coming against the land and blows the trumpet to warn the people,

twi: Na sɛ obi te torobɛnto no nnyigyei na wanna ne ho so, na sɛ afoa no bekum no a, ne mogya bɛbɔ ɔno ankasa ti so.
english: then if anyone hears the trumpet but does not heed the warning and the sword comes and takes their life, their blood will be on their own head.

twi: Esiane sɛ ɔtee torobɛnto no nnyigyei na wantie kɔkɔbɔ no nti, ne mogya bɛbɔ nʼankasa ti so. Sɛ otiee kɔkɔbɔ no a, anka onyaa ne ti didii mu.
english: Since they heard the sound of the trumpet but did not heed the warning, their blood will be on their own head. If they had heeded the warning, they would have saved themselves.

twi: Nanso sɛ ɔwɛmfo no hu sɛ afoa no reba na wanhyɛn torobɛnto no ammɔ nnipa no kɔkɔ, na sɛ afoa no ba bekum wɔn mu baako a, wɔbɛfa saa onipa no akɔ wɔ ne bɔne nti, nanso mɛma ɔwɛmfo no abu owufo no mogya ho akontaa.’
english: But if the watchman sees the sword coming and does not blow the trumpet to warn the people and the sword comes and takes someone’s life, that person’s life will be taken because of their sin, but I will hold the watchman accountable for their blood.’

twi: “Onipa ba, mayɛ wo ɔwɛmfo ama Israelfi, ɛno nti tie mʼanom nsɛm na fa kɔkɔbɔ a efi me nkyɛn ma wɔn.
english: “Son of man, I have made you a watchman for the people of Israel; so hear the word I speak and give them warning from me.

twi: Sɛ meka kyerɛ omumɔyɛfo se, ‘Wo omumɔyɛfo, owu na wubewu,’ na sɛ woankasa ankyerɛ no amma wamfi nʼakwan so a, saa omumɔyɛfo no bewu ne bɔne mu, na mɛma woabu ne mogya ho akontaa.
english: When I say to the wicked, ‘You wicked person, you will surely die,’ and you do not speak out to dissuade them from their ways, that wicked person will die for their sin, and I will hold you accountable for their blood.

twi: Nanso sɛ wobɔ omumɔyɛfo no kɔkɔ sɛ omfi nʼakwan so na sɛ wanyɛ a, ne bɔne nti, obewu, nanso worenni ne mogya ho fɔ.
english: But if you do warn the wicked person to turn from their ways and they do not do so, they will die for their sin, though you yourself will be saved.

twi: “Onipa ba, ka kyerɛ Israelfi se: ‘Sɛɛ ne nea moreka: “Yɛn mfomso ne yɛn nnebɔne hyɛ yɛn so, yɛresɛe, esiane eyinom nti. Na dɛn na yɛbɛyɛ na yɛanya nkwa?” ’
english: “Son of man, say to the Israelites, ‘This is what you are saying: “Our offenses and sins weigh us down, and we are wasting away because of them. How then can we live?”’

twi: Ka kyerɛ wɔn se, ‘Sɛ mete ase yi, Otumfo Awurade asɛm ni, mʼani nnye amumɔyɛfo wu ho, na mmom mepɛ sɛ wɔdan fi wɔn akwan so na wonya nkwa. Monnan! Monnan mfi mo amumɔyɛ akwan no so! Adɛn nti na ɛsɛ sɛ muwuwu, Israelfi?’
english: Say to them, ‘As surely as I live, declares the Sovereign Lord, I take no pleasure in the death of the wicked, but rather that they turn from their ways and live. Turn! Turn from your evil ways! Why will you die, people of Israel?’

twi: “Ɛno nti onipa ba, ka kyerɛ wo manmma se, ‘Ɔtreneeni trenee rentumi nnye no nkwa wɔ bere a ɔnyɛ osetie; na omumɔyɛfo amumɔyɛ remma ɔnhwe ase wɔ bere a ɔdan fi ho. Sɛ ɔtreneeni yɛ bɔne a, ɔrennya nkwa wɔ ne kan treneeyɛ nti.’
english: “Therefore, son of man, say to your people, ‘If someone who is righteous disobeys, that person’s former righteousness will count for nothing. And if someone who is wicked repents, that person’s former wickedness will not bring condemnation. The righteous person who sins will not be allowed to live even though they were formerly righteous.’

twi: Sɛ meka kyerɛ ɔtreneeni sɛ obenya nkwa, na afei ɔde ne ho to ne treneeyɛ so na ɔyɛ bɔne a, wɔrenkae ne kan trenee nneyɛe biara. Obewu wɔ ne bɔne a wayɛ nti.
english: If I tell a righteous person that they will surely live, but then they trust in their righteousness and do evil, none of the righteous things that person has done will be remembered; they will die for the evil they have done.

twi: Na sɛ meka kyerɛ omumɔyɛfo se, ‘Owu na wubewu,’ na afei ɔdan fi ne nnebɔne ho na ɔyɛ nea eye na ɛteɛ,
english: And if I say to a wicked person, ‘You will surely die,’ but they then turn away from their sin and do what is just and right—

twi: na sɛ ɔsan de bosea ho awowaside ma, na ɔsan de nea wawia ma, na odi ahyɛde a ɛma nkwa so, na wanyɛ bɔne a, ampa ara obenya nkwa, na ɔrenwu.
english: if they give back what they took in pledge for a loan, return what they have stolen, follow the decrees that give life, and do no evil—that person will surely live; they will not die.

twi: Wɔrenkae bɔne a wayɛ no mu biara ntia no. Wayɛ nea eye na ɛteɛ, ampa ara obenya nkwa.
english: None of the sins that person has committed will be remembered against them. They have done what is just and right; they will surely live.

twi: “Nanso wo manmma ka se, ‘Awurade akwan nteɛ.’ Nanso ɛyɛ wɔn akwan mmom na ɛnteɛ.
english: “Yet your people say, ‘The way of the Lord is not just.’ But it is their way that is not just.

twi: Sɛ ɔtreneeni fi ne trenee ho na ɔyɛ bɔne a, ɛno nti obewu.
english: If a righteous person turns from their righteousness and does evil, they will die for it.

twi: Na sɛ omumɔyɛfo dan fi ne nnebɔne ho na ɔyɛ nea eye na ɛteɛ a, obenya nkwa.
english: And if a wicked person turns away from their wickedness and does what is just and right, they will live by doing so.

twi: Nanso Israelfi, moka se, ‘Awurade akwan nteɛ.’ Nanso mebu obiara atɛn sɛnea nʼakwan te.”
english: Yet you Israelites say, ‘The way of the Lord is not just.’ But I will judge each of you according to your own ways.”

twi: Wɔkyerɛ Yerusalem Asehwe AseYɛn asutwa afe a ɛto so dumien no sram a ɛto so du no nnaanum so, ɔbarima bi a waguan afi Yerusalem baa me nkyɛn bɛkae se, “Kuropɔn no ahwe ase!”
english: In the twelfth year of our exile, in the tenth month on the fifth day, a man who had escaped from Jerusalem came to me and said, “The city has fallen!”

twi: Na anwummere a ade rebɛkye ama ɔbarima no aba no, na Awurade nsa wɔ me so na obuee mʼano ansa na ɔbarima no baa anɔpa. Enti na mʼano abue a mitumi kasa.
english: Now the evening before the man arrived, the hand of the Lord was on me, and he opened my mouth before the man came to me in the morning. So my mouth was opened and I was no longer silent.

twi: Afei Awurade asɛm baa me nkyɛn se,
english: Then the word of the Lord came to me:

twi: “Onipa ba, nnipa a wɔtete saa nnwiriwii so wɔ Israel asase no so no reka se, ‘Abraham yɛ onipa baako, nanso onyaa asase no nyinaa. Nanso yɛdɔɔso, na nokware wɔde asase no ama yɛn sɛ yɛn agyapade.’
english: “Son of man, the people living in those ruins in the land of Israel are saying, ‘Abraham was only one man, yet he possessed the land. But we are many; surely the land has been given to us as our possession.’

twi: Ɛno nti, ka kyerɛ wɔn se, ‘Sɛɛ na Otumfo Awurade se: Sɛ mowe nam a mogya wɔ mu, mosom mo anyame na muhwie mogya gu nti, ɛsɛ sɛ mofa asase no ana?
english: Therefore say to them, ‘This is what the Sovereign Lord says: Since you eat meat with the blood still in it and look to your idols and shed blood, should you then possess the land?

twi: Mode mo ho to mo afoa so. Moyɛ akyiwade na mo mu biara gu ne yɔnko yere ho fi. Ɛsɛ sɛ munya asase no ana?’
english: You rely on your sword, you do detestable things, and each of you defiles his neighbor’s wife. Should you then possess the land?’

twi: “Ka eyi kyerɛ wɔn se, ‘Nea Otumfo Awurade se ni: Ampa ara sɛ mete ase yi, wɔn a wɔaka wɔ kurow no nnwiriwii mu no bɛtotɔ wɔ afoa ano. Wɔn a wɔwɔ wuram no mede wɔn bɛma nkekaboa ama wɔawe wɔn na wɔn a wɔwɔ abandennen ne abodan mu no, ɔyaredɔm bekunkum wɔn.
english: “Say this to them: ‘This is what the Sovereign Lord says: As surely as I live, those who are left in the ruins will fall by the sword, those out in the country I will give to the wild animals to be devoured, and those in strongholds and caves will die of a plague.

twi: Mɛsɛe asase no ama ayɛ amamfo, na nʼahomaso ahoɔden no bɛba awiei na Israel mmepɔw no bɛda mpan a obiara rentwa mu wɔ hɔ.
english: I will make the land a desolate waste, and her proud strength will come to an end, and the mountains of Israel will become desolate so that no one will cross them.

twi: Afei wobehu sɛ mene Awurade no, bere a mama asase no ada mpan wɔ akyiwade a wɔayɛ nyinaa nti.’
english: Then they will know that I am the Lord, when I have made the land a desolate waste because of all the detestable things they have done.’

twi: “Wo de, onipa ba, wo manmma reka wo ho nsɛm wɔ afasu ho ne afi apon ano kyerɛ wɔn ho wɔn ho se, ‘Mommra mmetie asɛm a efi Awurade nkyɛn aba.’
english: “As for you, son of man, your people are talking together about you by the walls and at the doors of the houses, saying to each other, ‘Come and hear the message that has come from the Lord.’

twi: Me nkurɔfo ba wo nkyɛn, sɛnea wɔyɛ daa no, bɛtenatena wʼanim betie wo nsɛm, nanso wɔmmfa nyɛ adwuma. Wɔde wɔn ano ka ahofama, nanso wɔn koma mu de, wɔn ani bere asisi mu adenya.
english: My people come to you, as they usually do, and sit before you to hear your words, but they do not put them into practice. Their mouths speak of love, but their hearts are greedy for unjust gain.

twi: Nokware, wɔn de, wote sɛ obi a ne nne yɛ dɛ, na ɔde nnwontode to ɔdɔ nnwom, efisɛ wɔte wo nsɛm nanso wɔmmfa nyɛ adwuma.
english: Indeed, to them you are nothing more than one who sings love songs with a beautiful voice and plays an instrument well, for they hear your words but do not put them into practice.

twi: “Sɛ eyinom nyinaa ba mu a, na nokware ɛbɛba mu nso, na afei wobehu sɛ odiyifo bi baa wɔn mu.”
english: “When all this comes true—and it surely will—then they will know that a prophet has been among them.”

twi: Nguanhwɛfo Ne NguanAwurade asɛm baa me nkyɛn se:
english: The word of the Lord came to me:

twi: “Onipa ba, hyɛ nkɔm tia Israel nguanhwɛfo: hyɛ nkɔm na ka kyerɛ wɔn se: Sɛɛ na Otumfo Awurade se: Nnome nka Israel nguanhwɛfo a wɔhwɛ wɔn ankasa nko ara so. Ɛnsɛ sɛ nguanhwɛfo hwɛ nguankuw no ana?
english: “Son of man, prophesy against the shepherds of Israel; prophesy and say to them: ‘This is what the Sovereign Lord says: Woe to you shepherds of Israel who only take care of yourselves! Should not shepherds take care of the flock?

twi: Monom nufusu, mode mmoa no ho nwi fura mo ho na mukum mmoa a wɔadodɔ nanso monhwɛ nguankuw no.
english: You eat the curds, clothe yourselves with the wool and slaughter the choice animals, but you do not take care of the flock.

twi: Monhyɛɛ wɔn a wɔyɛ mmerɛw no den, nsaa ayarefo yare na monkyekyeree apirafo akuru. Momfaa wɔn a wɔabɔ ko mmae, na monhwehwɛɛ wɔn a wɔayera. Mode ɔhyɛ ne atirimɔden na ahwɛ wɔn so.
english: You have not strengthened the weak or healed the sick or bound up the injured. You have not brought back the strays or searched for the lost. You have ruled them harshly and brutally.

twi: Ɛno nti wɔbɔ ahwete, efisɛ wonni ɔhwɛfo bi, na wɔbɔ ahwete no, wɔbɛyɛɛ hanam maa wuram mmoa nyinaa.
english: So they were scattered because there was no shepherd, and when they were scattered they became food for all the wild animals.

twi: Me nguan kyinkyin mmepɔw ne nkoko nyinaa so. Wɔbɔɔ wɔn petee asase so baabiara, na obiara anhwehwɛ wɔn.
english: My sheep wandered over all the mountains and on every high hill. They were scattered over the whole earth, and no one searched or looked for them.

twi: “Enti, mo nguanhwɛfo, muntie Awurade asɛm:
english: “‘Therefore, you shepherds, hear the word of the Lord:

twi: Nokware, sɛ mete ase yi, Otumfo Awurade asɛm ni, esiane sɛ me nguankuw nni ɔhwɛfo nti wɔawiawia wɔn na wɔayɛ hanam ama wuram mmoa, na esiane sɛ nguanhwɛfo no anhwehwɛ me nguan no na mmom wɔhwɛɛ wɔn ankasa ho na wɔtoo me nguan no asaworam
english: As surely as I live, declares the Sovereign Lord, because my flock lacks a shepherd and so has been plundered and has become food for all the wild animals, and because my shepherds did not search for my flock but cared for themselves rather than for my flock,

twi: nti, nguanhwɛfo, muntie Awurade asɛm:
english: therefore, you shepherds, hear the word of the Lord:

twi: Sɛɛ na Otumfo Awurade se: Me ne nguanhwɛfo no anya na mɛma wɔabu me nguankuw no ho akontaa. Meremma wɔnhwɛ nguankuw no bio sɛnea ɛbɛyɛ a wɔrenkum nguan no nnwe; megye me nguankuw afi wɔn anom na wɔrenyɛ wɔn aduan bio.
english: This is what the Sovereign Lord says: I am against the shepherds and will hold them accountable for my flock. I will remove them from tending the flock so that the shepherds can no longer feed themselves. I will rescue my flock from their mouths, and it will no longer be food for them.

twi: “ ‘Na sɛɛ na Otumfo Awurade se: Me ara mɛhwehwɛ me nguan na mahwɛ wɔn so.
english: “‘For this is what the Sovereign Lord says: I myself will search for my sheep and look after them.

twi: Sɛnea oguanhwɛfo hwɛ ne nguan a wɔahwete bere a ɔwɔ wɔn nkyɛn no, saa ara na mɛhwɛ me nguan so. Meyi wɔn afi mmeae a wɔhwete kɔɔ wɔ omununkum ne sum kabii da no.
english: As a shepherd looks after his scattered flock when he is with them, so will I look after my sheep. I will rescue them from all the places where they were scattered on a day of clouds and darkness.

twi: Mede wɔn befi amanaman so aba na maboaboa wɔn ano afi nsase so na mede wɔn aba wɔn ankasa asase so. Mɛma wɔadidi wɔ Israel mmepɔw so, subon ne asase no so atenae nyinaa.
english: I will bring them out from the nations and gather them from the countries, and I will bring them into their own land. I will pasture them on the mountains of Israel, in the ravines and in all the settlements in the land.

twi: Mehwɛ wɔn so wɔ adidibea papa, na Israel mmepɔw atenten so bɛyɛ wɔn adidibea. Ɛhɔ na wɔbɛdeda adidibea asase papa so, na hɔ na wɔbɛwe sare frɔmfrɔm wɔ Israel mmepɔw so.
english: I will tend them in a good pasture, and the mountain heights of Israel will be their grazing land. There they will lie down in good grazing land, and there they will feed in a rich pasture on the mountains of Israel.

twi: Me ara mɛhwɛ me nguan na mama wɔadeda hɔ. Awurade asɛm ni.
english: I myself will tend my sheep and have them lie down, declares the Sovereign Lord.

twi: Mɛhwehwɛ nea wayera na mede nea wabɔ ko asan aba. Mɛkyekyere nea wapira no akuru, na mahyɛ nea ɔyɛ mmerɛw no den, nanso nea wadɔ ne nea ne ho yɛ den no, mɛsɛe wɔn. Mede trenee bɛhwɛ nguankuw no.
english: I will search for the lost and bring back the strays. I will bind up the injured and strengthen the weak, but the sleek and the strong I will destroy. I will shepherd the flock with justice.

twi: “ ‘Na mo, me nguankuw, sɛɛ na Otumfo Awurade se: Mebu oguan baako ne ɔfoforo ntam atɛn ne mpapo ne adwennini ntam.
english: “‘As for you, my flock, this is what the Sovereign Lord says: I will judge between one sheep and another, and between rams and goats.

twi: Adidibea papa a mudidi so no, ɛyɛ ade ketewa ma mo ana? Ɛsɛ sɛ mode mo anan tiatia mo adidibea a aka no nso so ana? Ɛnsɔ mo ani sɛ monom nsu a ani yɛ kurunnyenn ana? Ɛsɛ sɛ mode mo anan fono nkae no ana?
english: Is it not enough for you to feed on the good pasture? Must you also trample the rest of your pasture with your feet? Is it not enough for you to drink clear water? Must you also muddy the rest with your feet?

twi: Ɛsɛ sɛ me nguankuw di nea moatiatia so na wɔnom nea mode mo anan afon ana?
english: Must my flock feed on what you have trampled and drink what you have muddied with your feet?

twi: “ ‘Ɛno nti sɛɛ na Otumfo Awurade ka kyerɛ wɔn: Monhwɛ, me ara mebu nguan a wɔadodɔ ne nguan a wɔafonfɔn ntam atɛn.
english: “‘Therefore this is what the Sovereign Lord says to them: See, I myself will judge between the fat sheep and the lean sheep.

twi: Esiane sɛ, mode mo nkyɛn mu ne mmati puapua nguan a wonni ahoɔden na mode mo mmɛn pempem wɔn kosi sɛ mobɛpam wɔn akɔ akyirikyiri nti,
english: Because you shove with flank and shoulder, butting all the weak sheep with your horns until you have driven them away,

twi: megye me nguankuw na wɔremfom wɔn bio. Mebu oguan baako ne ɔfoforo ntam atɛn.
english: I will save my flock, and they will no longer be plundered. I will judge between one sheep and another.

twi: Mɛma oguanhwɛfo baako, me somfo Dawid, ahwɛ wɔn so, na ɔbɛyɛn wɔn na wayɛ wɔn hwɛfo.
english: I will place over them one shepherd, my servant David, and he will tend them; he will tend them and be their shepherd.

twi: Na me, Awurade, mɛyɛ wɔn Nyankopɔn na me somfo Dawid ayɛ wɔn mu obirɛmpɔn. Me Awurade na maka.
english: I the Lord will be their God, and my servant David will be prince among them. I the Lord have spoken.

twi: “ ‘Me ne wɔn bɛyɛ asomdwoe apam na matɔre nkekaboa ase wɔ asase no so sɛnea wobetumi atena sare so na wɔadeda kwae mu asomdwoe mu.
english: “‘I will make a covenant of peace with them and rid the land of savage beasts so that they may live in the wilderness and sleep in the forests in safety.

twi: Mehyira wɔn ne mmeae a atwa me pampa ho ahyia. Mɛtɔ obosu wɔ ne bere mu, na ɛbɛyɛ nhyira bosu.
english: I will make them and the places surrounding my hill a blessing. I will send down showers in season; there will be showers of blessing.

twi: Mfuw so nnua bɛsow wɔn aba na asase no nso abɔ nʼaduan. Nnipa no bɛtena wɔn asase so dwoodwoo. Mibubu wɔn konnua na migye wɔn fi wɔn a wɔde wɔn yɛɛ nkoa nsam a wobehu sɛ mene Awurade no.
english: The trees will yield their fruit and the ground will yield its crops; the people will be secure in their land. They will know that I am the Lord, when I break the bars of their yoke and rescue them from the hands of those who enslaved them.

twi: Amanaman no remfow wɔn bio, na wuram mmoa nso renkyere wɔn nnwe. Wɔbɛtena asomdwoe mu na obiara renhunahuna wɔn.
english: They will no longer be plundered by the nations, nor will wild animals devour them. They will live in safety, and no one will make them afraid.

twi: Na mɛma wɔn asase a ɛsow nnɔbae ama agye din, na aduankɔm renne wɔn wɔ asase no so na wɔrenyɛ ahohora mma amanaman no.
english: I will provide for them a land renowned for its crops, and they will no longer be victims of famine in the land or bear the scorn of the nations.

twi: Afei wobehu sɛ me Awurade, wɔn Nyankopɔn ne wɔn wɔ hɔ, na wɔn, Israelfi, yɛ me nkurɔfo; Otumfo Awurade asɛm ni.
english: Then they will know that I, the Lord their God, am with them and that they, the Israelites, are my people, declares the Sovereign Lord.

twi: Mo, me nguan, mʼadidibea nguan yɛ me nkurɔfo, na mene mo Nyankopɔn, Otumfo Awurade asɛm ni.’ ”
english: You are my sheep, the sheep of my pasture, and I am your God, declares the Sovereign Lord.’”

twi: Nkɔmhyɛ A Etia EdomAwurade asɛm baa me nkyɛn se:
english: The word of the Lord came to me:

twi: “Onipa ba, fa wʼani kyerɛ Bepɔw Seir; hyɛ nkɔm tia no,
english: “Son of man, set your face against Mount Seir; prophesy against it

twi: na ka se, ‘Sɛɛ na Otumfo Awurade se: Me ne wo anya, Bepɔw Seir, na mɛteɛ me basa atia wo na mɛma wo ada mpan.
english: and say: ‘This is what the Sovereign Lord says: I am against you, Mount Seir, and I will stretch out my hand against you and make you a desolate waste.

twi: Mɛdan wo nkurow ama ayɛ mmubui na wobɛda mpan. Afei wubehu sɛ mene Awurade no.
english: I will turn your towns into ruins and you will be desolate. Then you will know that I am the Lord.

twi: “ ‘Esiane sɛ wode tete nitan hyɛɛ wo mu na wuyii Israelfo maa afoa wɔ wɔn amanehunu mu, bere a wɔn asotwe duu ne mpɔmpɔnso no
english: “‘Because you harbored an ancient hostility and delivered the Israelites over to the sword at the time of their calamity, the time their punishment reached its climax,

twi: nti, sɛ mete ase yi de, Otumfo Awurade asɛm ni, mede wo bɛma mogyahwiegu na ebedi wʼakyi. Esiane sɛ woansuro mogyahwiegu no nti, mogyahwiegu bɛtaa wo.
english: therefore as surely as I live, declares the Sovereign Lord, I will give you over to bloodshed and it will pursue you. Since you did not hate bloodshed, bloodshed will pursue you.

twi: Mɛma bepɔw Seir ada mpan, na mayi wɔn a wodi so akɔneaba no afi hɔ.
english: I will make Mount Seir a desolate waste and cut off from it all who come and go.

twi: Mede atɔfo bɛhyɛ wo mmepɔw so ma; wɔn a wɔbɛtotɔ wɔ afoa ano bɛtotɔ ase wɔ wo nkoko so, aku mu ne wo subon mu.
english: I will fill your mountains with the slain; those killed by the sword will fall on your hills and in your valleys and in all your ravines.

twi: Mɛma woada mpan afebɔɔ, na obiara rentena wo nkurow so. Afei wubehu sɛ mene Awurade no.
english: I will make you desolate forever; your towns will not be inhabited. Then you will know that I am the Lord.

twi: “ ‘Woaka se, “Saa aman abien ne nsase yi bɛyɛ yɛn dea, na yɛbɛfa,” wɔ bere a me Awurade mete hɔ;
english: “‘Because you have said, “These two nations and countries will be ours and we will take possession of them,” even though I the Lord was there,

twi: enti sɛ mete ase yi, Otumfo Awurade asɛm ni, me ne wo bedi no sɛnea abufuw ne ninkunu a wodaa no adi wɔ ɔtan a wotan wɔn no mu no te, na mɛda me ho adi wɔ wɔn mu, bere a mebu wo atɛn.
english: therefore as surely as I live, declares the Sovereign Lord, I will treat you in accordance with the anger and jealousy you showed in your hatred of them and I will make myself known among them when I judge you.

twi: Afei wubehu sɛ me Awurade, mate animtiaabu nsɛm a woaka atia Israel mmepɔw no. Wokae se, “Wɔama ada mpan na wɔadan ama yɛn sɛ yɛmfa.”
english: Then you will know that I the Lord have heard all the contemptible things you have said against the mountains of Israel. You said, “They have been laid waste and have been given over to us to devour.”

twi: Mohoahoaa mo ho tiaa me na mokasa tiaa me a moanto sɛbe, na metee.
english: You boasted against me and spoke against me without restraint, and I heard it.

twi: Sɛɛ na Otumfo Awurade se: Bere a wiase nyinaa redi ahurusi no, mɛma wo ada mpan.
english: This is what the Sovereign Lord says: While the whole earth rejoices, I will make you desolate.

twi: Sɛnea wudii ahurusi bere a Israelfi agyapade daa mpan no, saa ɔkwan no na mede wo bɛfa so. Wobɛda mpan, Bepɔw Seir, wo ne Edom nyinaa. Afei wobehu sɛ mene Awurade no.’ ”
english: Because you rejoiced when the inheritance of Israel became desolate, that is how I will treat you. You will be desolate, Mount Seir, you and all of Edom. Then they will know that I am the Lord.’”

twi: Israel Mmepɔw Ho Nkɔmhyɛ“Onipa ba, hyɛ nkɔm kyerɛ Israel mmepɔw na ka se: ‘Israel mmepɔw, muntie Awurade asɛm.
english: “Son of man, prophesy to the mountains of Israel and say, ‘Mountains of Israel, hear the word of the Lord.

twi: Sɛɛ na Otumfo Awurade se: Sɛɛ na ɔtamfo no ka faa wo ho, “Aaa! Tete sorɔnsorɔmmea no abɛyɛ yɛn dea.” ’
english: This is what the Sovereign Lord says: The enemy said of you, “Aha! The ancient heights have become our possession.”’

twi: Ɛno nti, hyɛ nkɔm na ka se, ‘Sɛɛ na Otumfo Awurade se: Esiane sɛ wɔasɛe mo na wɔataataa mo wɔ afa nyinaa, na ɛno nti mobɛyɛɛ aman a aka no agyapade ne nnipa no ahohora nsɛnka ne atwetwesi,
english: Therefore prophesy and say, ‘This is what the Sovereign Lord says: Because they ravaged and crushed you from every side so that you became the possession of the rest of the nations and the object of people’s malicious talk and slander,

twi: ɛno nti, Israel mmepɔw, muntie Otumfo Awurade asɛm: Sɛɛ na Otumfo Awurade ka kyerɛ mmepɔw ne nkoko, nsubon ne abon, nnwiriwii a ada mpan ne nea ayɛ amamfo, nkurow amamfo a wɔadwiriw agu na aman no nkae a atwa wɔn ho ahyia no di wɔn ho fɛw.
english: therefore, mountains of Israel, hear the word of the Sovereign Lord: This is what the Sovereign Lord says to the mountains and hills, to the ravines and valleys, to the desolate ruins and the deserted towns that have been plundered and ridiculed by the rest of the nations around you—

twi: Sɛɛ na Otumfo Awurade se: Mifi anem a emu yɛ den mu akasa atia amanaman a aka no ne Edom nyinaa, efisɛ wɔde fɛwdi ne adwemmɔne ayɛ me man wɔn agyapade, sɛnea wobetumi afom ne didibea.’
english: this is what the Sovereign Lord says: In my burning zeal I have spoken against the rest of the nations, and against all Edom, for with glee and with malice in their hearts they made my land their own possession so that they might plunder its pastureland.’

twi: Ɛno nti, hyɛ nkɔm a ɛfa Israel asase ho, na ka kyerɛ mmepɔw ne nkoko, subon ne abon se, ‘Sɛɛ na Otumfo Awurade se: Mede ninkutwe mu anibere kasa, efisɛ amanaman no abu wo animtiaa.
english: Therefore prophesy concerning the land of Israel and say to the mountains and hills, to the ravines and valleys: ‘This is what the Sovereign Lord says: I speak in my jealous wrath because you have suffered the scorn of the nations.

twi: Enti sɛɛ na Otumfo Awurade se: Mema me nsa so ka ntam sɛ amanaman a atwa wo ho ahyia no nso, wobebu wɔn animtiaa.
english: Therefore this is what the Sovereign Lord says: I swear with uplifted hand that the nations around you will also suffer scorn.

twi: “ ‘Nanso mo, Israel mmepɔw, mubenya mman, asow aba ama me nkurɔfo Israelfo, efisɛ ɛrenkyɛ wɔbɛba fie.
english: “‘But you, mountains of Israel, will produce branches and fruit for my people Israel, for they will soon come home.

twi: Mo ho hia me na mehu mo mmɔbɔ; wobefuntum mo na wɔadua mo so aba,
english: I am concerned for you and will look on you with favor; you will be plowed and sown,

twi: na mɛma wo so nnipa adɔɔso, Israelfi nyinaa mpo, nnipa bɛtena wo nkurow no so bio, na wobesisi nnwiriwii no nso.
english: and I will cause many people to live on you—yes, all of Israel. The towns will be inhabited and the ruins rebuilt.

twi: Mɛma mmarima ne mmoa adɔɔso wɔ mo so na wɔbɛwowo na wɔadodɔ, mɛma nnipa atena wo mu te sɛ kan no na wɔbɛma woadi yiye asen kan no. Na afei mubehu sɛ mene Awurade no.
english: I will increase the number of people and animals living on you, and they will be fruitful and become numerous. I will settle people on you as in the past and will make you prosper more than before. Then you will know that I am the Lord.

twi: Mɛma nkurɔfo, me nkurɔfo Israelfo, anantew wo so. Wɔbɛfa wo na wobɛyɛ wɔn agyapade na woremma wonni mmakɔm bio.
