twi: Na mefɛree sɛ mebisa ɔhene no sɛ ɔmma yɛn asraafo ne apɔnkɔsotefo na wɔnka yɛn ho mmɔ yɛn ho ban wɔ ɔkwan so, efisɛ na yɛaka akyerɛ ɔhene no se, “Yɛn Nyankopɔn bɔ wɔn a wɔsom no no ho ban, na nʼabufuwhyew no tia wɔn a wɔpo no.”
english: I was ashamed to ask the king for soldiers and horsemen to protect us from enemies on the road, because we had told the king, “The gracious hand of our God is on everyone who looks to him, but his great anger is against all who forsake him.”

twi: Enti yedii mmuada, bɔɔ mpae srɛɛ yɛn Nyankopɔn wɔ eyi ho, na otiee yɛn mpaebɔ.
english: So we fasted and petitioned our God about this, and he answered our prayer.

twi: Na miyii asɔfo no ntuanofo dumien a wɔne Serebia, Hasabia ne asɔfo afoforo du a wɔka wɔn ho
english: Then I set apart twelve of the leading priests, namely, Sherebiah, Hashabiah and ten of their brothers,

twi: sɛ wɔnhwɛ dwetɛ, sikakɔkɔɔ, sikakɔkɔɔ hweaseammɔ ne nneɛma a ɛka ho a ɔhene no nʼagyinatufo, ne ntuanofo ne Israelfo de ama Onyankopɔn fi no so.
english: and I weighed out to them the offering of silver and gold and the articles that the king, his advisers, his officials and all Israel present there had donated for the house of our God.

twi: Mede agude no rema wɔn no, mekarii na mihuu sɛ emu duru yɛ: dwetɛ nkaribo tɔn aduonu anan, sikakɔkɔɔ nkuku ne nkaka nkaribo pɔn mpem ahanson ne ahannum, sikakɔkɔɔ nkaribo pɔn mpem ahanson ne ahannum,
english: I weighed out to them 650 talents of silver, silver articles weighing 100 talents, 100 talents of gold,

twi: sikakɔkɔɔ hweaseammɔ aduonu a ɛne sikakɔkɔɔ nnwetɛbona apem bo yɛ pɛ, kɔbere nneɛma abien a wɔabere ho ma ɛrekɔyɛ sɛ sikakɔkɔɔ ankasa.
english: 20 bowls of gold valued at 1,000 darics, and two fine articles of polished bronze, as precious as gold.

twi: Na meka kyerɛɛ saa asɔfo yi se, “Wɔayi mo ne saa agyapade yi nyinaa asi nkyɛn sɛ ade kronkron ama Awurade. Saa dwetɛ ne sikakɔkɔɔ yi yɛ koma pa mu afɔrebɔde a wɔde rema Awurade, yɛn agyanom Nyankopɔn.
english: I said to them, “You as well as these articles are consecrated to the Lord. The silver and gold are a freewill offering to the Lord, the God of your ancestors.

twi: Monhwɛ saa agyapade yi so yiye, na momfa mma asɔfo mpanyin, Lewifo ne Israel ntuanofo wɔ adekorae a ɛwɔ Yerusalem asɔredan no mu no.”
english: Guard them carefully until you weigh them out in the chambers of the house of the Lord in Jerusalem before the leading priests and the Levites and the family heads of Israel.”

twi: Enti asɔfo no ne Lewifo no gye too wɔn ho so sɛ wɔde saa Onyankopɔn asɔre sika no bɛkɔ Yerusalem.
english: Then the priests and Levites received the silver and gold and sacred articles that had been weighed out to be taken to the house of our God in Jerusalem.

twi: Yefii Ahawa Suka atenae hɔ Ab ɔsram (bɛyɛ Oforisuo) da a ɛto so dunkron, sii mu kɔɔ Yerusalem. Na Onyankopɔn nsa no bɔɔ yɛn ho ban, gyee yɛn fii atamfo ne akwamukafo nsam.
english: On the twelfth day of the first month we set out from the Ahava Canal to go to Jerusalem. The hand of our God was on us, and he protected us from enemies and bandits along the way.

twi: Enti yekoduu Yerusalem dwoodwoo, homee wɔ hɔ nnansa.
english: So we arrived in Jerusalem, where we rested three days.

twi: Yeduu no, ne nnaanan so no, wɔkarii dwetɛ, sikakɔkɔɔ ne aboɔdenne a aka no wɔ Onyankopɔn asɔredan no mu, na wɔde hyɛɛ Uria babarima ɔsɔfo Meremot ne Pinehas babarima Eleasar ne Yesua babarima Yosabad ne Binui babarima Noadia a wɔn baanu no yɛ Lewifo no nsa.
english: On the fourth day, in the house of our God, we weighed out the silver and gold and the sacred articles into the hands of Meremoth son of Uriah, the priest. Eleazar son of Phinehas was with him, and so were the Levites Jozabad son of Jeshua and Noadiah son of Binnui.

twi: Wɔkan biribiara dodow, karii mu duru, kyerɛw biribiara.
english: Everything was accounted for by number and weight, and the entire weight was recorded at that time.

twi: Na wɔn a wofi nnommum mu bae no de anantwi dumien, adwennini aduɔkron asia ne nguantenmma aduɔson ason, bɔɔ ɔhyew afɔre, maa Israel Nyankopɔn. Afei, wɔmaa mmirekyi dumien sɛ bɔne ho afɔrebɔde. Wɔde eyinom nyinaa bae sɛ ɔhyew afɔre maa Awurade.
english: Then the exiles who had returned from captivity sacrificed burnt offerings to the God of Israel: twelve bulls for all Israel, ninety-six rams, seventy-seven male lambs and, as a sin offering, twelve male goats. All this was a burnt offering to the Lord.

twi: Wɔde ɔhene no mmara no maa ne mpanyimfo ne amradofo a wɔwɔ asu Eufrate agya no, na wɔn nyinaa yɛɛ baako boaa Onyankopɔn asɔredan no si.
english: They also delivered the king’s orders to the royal satraps and to the governors of Trans-Euphrates, who then gave assistance to the people and to the house of God.

twi: Ɛsra Bɔ Ahɔhoware Ho MpaeNa Yudafo ntuanofo no baa me nkyɛn bɛkae se, “Israelfo bebree, na mpo, asɔfo ne Lewifo ntwee wɔn ho mfii nnipa afoforo bi a wɔte asase no so no ho. Wodi akyiwade a na Kanaanfo, Hetifo, Perisifo, Yebusifo, Amonfo, Moabfo, Misraimfo ne Amorifo yɛ no akyi.
english: After these things had been done, the leaders came to me and said, “The people of Israel, including the priests and the Levites, have not kept themselves separate from the neighboring peoples with their detestable practices, like those of the Canaanites, Hittites, Perizzites, Jebusites, Ammonites, Moabites, Egyptians and Amorites.

twi: Na Israelfo mmarima ware fi saa nnipa no mu, na wɔpɛ yerenom fi wɔn mu, ma wɔn mmabarima. Enti ananafo aware no ama nnipa kronkron no ho agu fi. Nea ɛsɛee asɛm no koraa ne sɛ, mpanyimfo ne ntuanofo no koraa na wodi ho fɔ kɛse.”
english: They have taken some of their daughters as wives for themselves and their sons, and have mingled the holy race with the peoples around them. And the leaders and officials have led the way in this unfaithfulness.”

twi: Metee saa asɛm no, misunsuan me ntade mu, tutuu me tinwi fii me ti so, tutuu mʼabogyesɛ nso, tew tenaa fam ahodwiriw so.
english: When I heard this, I tore my tunic and cloak, pulled hair from my head and beard and sat down appalled.

twi: Na wɔn a na wonya ayamhyehye wɔ Israel Nyankopɔn asɛm ho no bɛtenaa me nkyɛn wɔ ne nkurɔfo nokware a wɔanni no ho. Metenaa ase ahodwiriw so kosii anwummere afɔrebɔbere.
english: Then everyone who trembled at the words of the God of Israel gathered around me because of this unfaithfulness of the exiles. And I sat there appalled until the evening sacrifice.

twi: Eduu afɔrebɔbere no, mesɔre gyinaa faako a na mete hɔ awerɛhow mu a masunsuan mʼatade mu no, na mibuu nkotodwe, maa me nsa so kyerɛɛ Awurade, me Nyankopɔn no.
english: Then, at the evening sacrifice, I rose from my self-abasement, with my tunic and cloak torn, and fell on my knees with my hands spread out to the Lord my God

twi: Mebɔɔ mpae se:“Me Nyankopɔn, mʼani awu yiye, na mafɛre sɛ merema mʼani so kyerɛ wo. Na yɛn bɔne akɔ soro sen yɛn ti, na yɛn afɔdi adu ɔsorosoro.
english:
and prayed:
“I am too ashamed and disgraced, my God, to lift up my face to you, because our sins are higher than our heads and our guilt has reached to the heavens.

twi: Yɛn abakɔsɛm nyinaa yɛ bɔne kɛse. Ɛno nti na yɛn ne yɛn ahemfo ne yɛn asɔfo de yɛn ho akɔhyɛ abosonsomfo ahemfo a wɔwɔ asase no so ase no. Wɔakunkum yɛn, wɔakyere yɛn nnommum, wɔabɔ yɛn korɔn, agu yɛn anim ase sɛnea yɛte nnɛ yi
english: From the days of our ancestors until now, our guilt has been great. Because of our sins, we and our kings and our priests have been subjected to the sword and captivity, to pillage and humiliation at the hand of foreign kings, as it is today.

twi: “Nanso mprempren, Awurade, yɛn Nyankopɔn, ayɛ yɛn adom ama yɛn mu kakra atena nkwa mu sɛ nkaase. Wabɔ yɛn ho ban wɔ beae kronkron ha. Yɛn Nyankopɔn abue yɛn ani, ama yɛn ahomegye kakra afi yɛn nkoasom mu.
english: “But now, for a brief moment, the Lord our God has been gracious in leaving us a remnant and giving us a firm place in his sanctuary, and so our God gives light to our eyes and a little relief in our bondage.

twi: Efisɛ na yɛyɛ nkoa, nanso ne dɔ a ɔde dɔ yɛn daa no nti, Onyankopɔn annyaa yɛn wɔ yɛn nkoasom mu. Mmom, ɔmaa Persiahene hwɛɛ yɛn yiye. Ɔkanyan yɛn, sɛnea yebetumi asan asi yɛn Nyankopɔn asɔredan no, asiesie nʼamamfo no. Wama yɛn bammɔ afasu wɔ Yuda ne Yerusalem.
english: Though we are slaves, our God has not forsaken us in our bondage. He has shown us kindness in the sight of the kings of Persia: He has granted us new life to rebuild the house of our God and repair its ruins, and he has given us a wall of protection in Judah and Jerusalem.

twi: “Na mprempren, yɛn Nyankopɔn, asɛm bɛn na yɛwɔ ka wɔ eyinom nyinaa akyi? Efisɛ yɛapo wo mmara nsɛm
english: “But now, our God, what can we say after this? For we have forsaken the commands

twi: a wonam wʼasomfo adiyifo no so bɔɔ yɛn kɔkɔ sɛ, ‘Asase a mobɛfa no, nnipa a wɔte so no nam wɔn nneyɛe bɔne so agu ho fi koraa. Porɔwee ahyɛ asase no so ma, fi ti kosi ti.
english: you gave through your servants the prophets when you said: ‘The land you are entering to possess is a land polluted by the corruption of its peoples. By their detestable practices they have filled it with their impurity from one end to the other.

twi: Enti mommma mo mmabea nware wɔn mmabarima, na mo mmabarima nso nware wɔn mmabea, na ɛnsɛ sɛ moboa saa aman no wɔ ɔkwan biara so, na yɛayɛ ɔman kɛse, adi asase no so nnepa, na yɛagyaw ama yɛn mma sɛ daapem agyapade.’
english: Therefore, do not give your daughters in marriage to their sons or take their daughters for your sons. Do not seek a treaty of friendship with them at any time, that you may be strong and eat the good things of the land and leave it to your children as an everlasting inheritance.’

twi: “Nea ato yɛn yi fi yɛn amumɔyɛsɛm ne yɛn afɔdi. Nanso asotwe a wode ama yɛn no sua koraa sen sɛnea ɛfata yɛn, efisɛ wo Awurade, yɛn Nyankopɔn ama yɛn mu bi atena sɛ nkaase.
english: “What has happened to us is a result of our evil deeds and our great guilt, and yet, our God, you have punished us less than our sins deserved and have given us a remnant like this.

twi: Nanso mprempren, yɛresan abu wo mmara nsɛm so, na yɛne wɔn a wɔyɛ saa akyiwade no redi aware. Nokware, wʼabufuw bɛsɛe yɛn ara akosi sɛ, nkaefo kakra no ase bɛtɔre koraa.
english: Shall we then break your commands again and intermarry with the peoples who commit such detestable practices? Would you not be angry enough with us to destroy us, leaving us no remnant or survivor?

twi: Awurade, Israel Nyankopɔn, woyɛ ɔtreneeni. Yɛnka hwee sɛ nkaefo a wɔafi nkoasom mu. Yɛde yɛn afɔdi gyina wʼanim a anka yɛn mu biara rentumi nnyina wʼanim wɔ saa tebea yi mu.”
english: Lord, the God of Israel, you are righteous! We are left this day as a remnant. Here we are before you in our guilt, though because of it not one of us can stand in your presence.”

twi: BɔnekaBere a Ɛsra rebɔ mpae, reka saa bɔne yi no, na ɔresu, de ne ho toto fam wɔ Onyankopɔn Asɔredan no anim, na nnipadɔm a wɔyɛ Israelfo, mmarima, mmea ne mmofra bɛkaa ne ho ne no twaa adwo.
english: While Ezra was praying and confessing, weeping and throwing himself down before the house of God, a large crowd of Israelites—men, women and children—gathered around him. They too wept bitterly.

twi: Na Yehiel babarima Sekania a ɔyɛ Elam aseni no ka kyerɛɛ Ɛsra se, “Yɛpae mu ka sɛ yɛanni yɛn Nyankopɔn nokware, efisɛ yɛawareware abosonsomfo mmea a wɔwɔ asase no so. Nanso eyi akyi no, anidaso wɔ hɔ ma Israel.
english: Then Shekaniah son of Jehiel, one of the descendants of Elam, said to Ezra, “We have been unfaithful to our God by marrying foreign women from the peoples around us. But in spite of this, there is still hope for Israel.

twi: Afei, momma yɛne yɛn Nyankopɔn nyɛ apam, na yennyaa yɛn yerenom abosonsomfo no aware, na yɛmpam wɔne wɔn mma. Yebetie afotu a wo ne afoforo a wodi yɛn Nyankopɔn mmara so no de ama yɛn. Yebedi Onyankopɔn mmara no so.
english: Now let us make a covenant before our God to send away all these women and their children, in accordance with the counsel of my lord and of those who fear the commands of our God. Let it be done according to the Law.

twi: Sɔre, na nya akokoduru, efisɛ ɛyɛ wʼasɛde sɛ wokyerɛ yɛn ɔkwan a yɛbɛfa so ama biribiara akɔ so tee, na yɛde yɛn ahoɔden nyinaa bɛboa.”
english: Rise up; this matter is in your hands. We will support you, so take courage and do it.”

twi: Na Ɛsra sɔre gyinae, na ɔhyɛɛ sɛ asɔfo no ntuanofo, Lewifo ne Israelfo nyinaa nka ntam sɛ wɔbɛyɛ nea Sekania aka no. Na wɔn nyinaa kaa ntam a ano yɛ den.
english: So Ezra rose up and put the leading priests and Levites and all Israel under oath to do what had been suggested. And they took the oath.

twi: Na Ɛsra sɔre fii Onyankopɔn Asɔredan no anim kɔɔ Eliasib babarima Yehohanan dan mu. Ɔdaa hɔ, nanso wannidi annom. Na ɔda so di awerɛhow esiane nnommum a wɔasan aba no nokware a wɔanni no nti.
english: Then Ezra withdrew from before the house of God and went to the room of Jehohanan son of Eliashib. While he was there, he ate no food and drank no water, because he continued to mourn over the unfaithfulness of the exiles.

twi: Afei, wɔbɔɔ dawuru wɔ Yuda ne Yerusalem nyinaa se, nnommum a wɔasan aba no nyinaa mmra Yerusalem.
english: A proclamation was then issued throughout Judah and Jerusalem for all the exiles to assemble in Jerusalem.

twi: Na wɔn a wɔamma nnansa ntam no, sɛ ntuanofo ne mpanyimfo pɛ a, wɔde wɔn nsa bɛto wɔn agyapade so, na wɔapam wɔn afi wɔn mu.
english: Anyone who failed to appear within three days would forfeit all his property, in accordance with the decision of the officials and elders, and would himself be expelled from the assembly of the exiles.

twi: Nnansa ntam no, na Yudafo ne Benyaminfo aboa wɔn ho ano wɔ Yerusalem. Asɛm yi sii wɔ Kislev ɔsram (bɛyɛ Ɔpɛnimma) da a ɛto so dunkron, na wɔn nyinaa tenatenaa aguabɔbea hɔ wɔ Onyankopɔn Asɔredan no anim. Na wɔn ho repopo, efisɛ nea edi kan no, na asɛm no mu yɛ duru, na nea ɛto so abien no, na osu nso retɔ.
english: Within the three days, all the men of Judah and Benjamin had gathered in Jerusalem. And on the twentieth day of the ninth month, all the people were sitting in the square before the house of God, greatly distressed by the occasion and because of the rain.

twi: Na ɔsɔfo Ɛsra sɔre gyina kae se, “Moayɛ bɔne, efisɛ moawareware mmea abosonsomfo. Enti mprempren, yɛwɔ afɔbu a ano yɛ den mu sen kan de no.
english: Then Ezra the priest stood up and said to them, “You have been unfaithful; you have married foreign women, adding to Israel’s guilt.

twi: Mompae mu nka mo bɔne nkyerɛ Awurade, mo agyanom Nyankopɔn, na monyɛ nʼapɛde. Montwe mo ho mfi nnipa a wɔwɔ asase no so ne mmea abosonsomfo no ho.”
english: Now honor the Lord, the God of your ancestors, and do his will. Separate yourselves from the peoples around you and from your foreign wives.”

twi: Afei bagua no nyinaa maa wɔn nne so ka se, “Ampa, wʼasɛm no yɛ nokware. Ɛsɛ sɛ yɛyɛ nea woaka no.
english: The whole assembly responded with a loud voice: “You are right! We must do as you say.

twi: Nanso nnipa bebree wɔ ha na ɛyɛ asusow bere, enti yɛrentumi ntena mfikyiri. Bio, yɛrentumi mfa da koro anaa nnaanu nni saa asɛm yi, efisɛ, yɛn mu bebree na saa bɔne kɛse yi ka yɛn.
english: But there are many people here and it is the rainy season; so we cannot stand outside. Besides, this matter cannot be taken care of in a day or two, because we have sinned greatly in this thing.

twi: Momma yɛn mpanyimfo nsi yɛn anan nyɛ biribiara. Obiara a ɔware ɔbea bosonsomni no ne ntuanofo ne atemmufo a wɔwɔ kurow yi mu behyia bere a wɔahyɛ no sɛnea ɛbɛyɛ a Onyankopɔn abufuwhyew a ɛfa saa asɛm yi ho no befi yɛn so.”
english: Let our officials act for the whole assembly. Then let everyone in our towns who has married a foreign woman come at a set time, along with the elders and judges of each town, until the fierce anger of our God in this matter is turned away from us.”

twi: Asahel babarima Yonatan ne Tikwa babarima Yahasia na wotiaa saa asɛm yi mu, na Mesulam ne Sabetai a ɔyɛ Lewini no foaa wɔn so.
english: Only Jonathan son of Asahel and Jahzeiah son of Tikvah, supported by Meshullam and Shabbethai the Levite, opposed this.

twi: Enti eyi ne nhyehyɛe a wɔfaa so. Ɛsra yii ntuanofo ma wosii wɔn mmusua no anan, na ɔde din bi too ntuanoni biara so. Ɔsram Kislev (bɛyɛ Ɔpɛnimma) da a ɛto so aduonu akron no, ntuanofo no tenaa ase hwehwɛɛ asɛm no mu.
english: So the exiles did as was proposed. Ezra the priest selected men who were family heads, one from each family division, and all of them designated by name. On the first day of the tenth month they sat down to investigate the cases,

twi: Afe a edi so no mu, Abib ɔsram (bɛyɛ Ɔbɛnem) da a ɛto so aduonu ason no na wɔawie mmarima a wɔawareware mmea abosonsomfo no nyinaa ho asɛnka.
english: and by the first day of the first month they finished dealing with all the men who had married foreign women.

twi: Asɔfo a na wɔawareware abosonsomfo no din ni:Yosadak babarima Yesua ne ne nuabarimanom:Maaseia, Elieser, Yarib ne Gedalia.
english:
Among the descendants of the priests, the following had married foreign women:
From the descendants of Joshua son of Jozadak, and his brothers: Maaseiah, Eliezer, Jarib and Gedaliah.

twi: Wɔkaa ntam sɛ wobegyaa wɔn yerenom, wɔn mu biara gyee nʼafɔdi too mu, na wɔde adwennini bɛbɔɔ afɔdi ho afɔre.
english: (They all gave their hands in pledge to put away their wives, and for their guilt they each presented a ram from the flock as a guilt offering.)

twi: Imer asefo mu no:Hanani ne Sebadia.
english:
From the descendants of Immer:
Hanani and Zebadiah.

twi: Harim asefo mu no:Maaseia, Elia, Semaia, Yehiel ne Usia.
english:
From the descendants of Harim:
Maaseiah, Elijah, Shemaiah, Jehiel and Uzziah.

twi: Pashur asefo mu no:Elioenai, Maaseia, Ismael, Netanel, Yosabad ne Elasa.
english:
From the descendants of Pashhur:
Elioenai, Maaseiah, Ishmael, Nethanel, Jozabad and Elasah.

twi: Eyinom ne Lewifo a na afɔdi da wɔn so:Yosabad, Simei, Kelaia, a ɛyɛ Kelita, Petahia, Yuda ne Elieser.
english:
Among the Levites:
Jozabad, Shimei, Kelaiah (that is, Kelita), Pethahiah, Judah and Eliezer.

twi: Nnwontofo a na afɔdi da ne so no yɛ:Eliasib.Eyinom ne aponanohwɛfo a na afɔdi da wɔn so:Salum, Telem ne Uri.
english:
From the musicians:
Eliashib.
From the gatekeepers:
Shallum, Telem and Uri.

twi: Eyinom ne nnipa bi a wɔyɛ Israelfo a na afɔdi da wɔn so:Paros asefo mu no:Ramia, Yisia, Malkia, Miamin, Eleasar, Malkia ne Benaia.
english:
And among the other Israelites:
From the descendants of Parosh:
Ramiah, Izziah, Malkijah, Mijamin, Eleazar, Malkijah and Benaiah.

twi: Elam asefo mu no:Matania, Sakaria, Yehiel, Abdi, Yeremot ne Elia.
english:
From the descendants of Elam:
Mattaniah, Zechariah, Jehiel, Abdi, Jeremoth and Elijah.

twi: Satu asefo mu no:Elioenai, Eliasib, Matania, Yeremot, Sabad ne Asisa.
english:
From the descendants of Zattu:
Elioenai, Eliashib, Mattaniah, Jeremoth, Zabad and Aziza.

twi: Bebai asefo mu no:Yehohanan, Hanania, Sabai ne Atlai.
english:
From the descendants of Bebai:
Jehohanan, Hananiah, Zabbai and Athlai.

twi: Bani asefo mu no:Mesulam, Maluk, Adaia, Yasub, Seal ne Yeremot.
english:
From the descendants of Bani:
Meshullam, Malluk, Adaiah, Jashub, Sheal and Jeremoth.

twi: Pahat-Moab asefo mu no:Adna, Kelal, Benaia, Maaseia, Matania, Basaleel, Binui ne Manase.
english:
From the descendants of Pahath-Moab:
Adna, Kelal, Benaiah, Maaseiah, Mattaniah, Bezalel, Binnui and Manasseh.

twi: Harim asefo mu no:Elieser, Yisia, Malkia Semaia ne Simeon.
english:
From the descendants of Harim:
Eliezer, Ishijah, Malkijah, Shemaiah, Shimeon,

twi: Benyamin, Maluk ne Semaria.
english: Benjamin, Malluk and Shemariah.

twi: Hasum asefo mu no:Matenai, Matata, Sabad, Elifelet, Yeremai, Manase ne Simei.
english:
From the descendants of Hashum:
Mattenai, Mattattah, Zabad, Eliphelet, Jeremai, Manasseh and Shimei.

twi: Bani asefo mu no:Maadai, Amram ne Uel,
english:
From the descendants of Bani:
Maadai, Amram, Uel,

twi: Benaia, Bedeia, Keluhi,
english: Benaiah, Bedeiah, Keluhi,

twi: Wania, Meremot, Eliasib,
english: Vaniah, Meremoth, Eliashib,

twi: Matania, Matenai ne Yaasu.
english: Mattaniah, Mattenai and Jaasu.

twi: Binui asefo mu no:Simei,
english:
From the descendants of Binnui:
Shimei,

twi: Selemia, Natan, Adaia,
english: Shelemiah, Nathan, Adaiah,

twi: Maknadebai, Sasai, Sarai,
english: Maknadebai, Shashai, Sharai,

twi: Asarel, Selemia, Semaria,
english: Azarel, Shelemiah, Shemariah,

twi: Salum, Amaria ne Yosef.
english: Shallum, Amariah and Joseph.

twi: Nebo asefo mu no:Yeiel, Matitia, Sabad, Sebina, Yadau, Yoel ne Benaia.
english:
From the descendants of Nebo:
Jeiel, Mattithiah, Zabad, Zebina, Jaddai, Joel and Benaiah.

twi: Na mmarima yi mu biara aware ɔbea bosonsomni a na wɔn mu bi mpo ne wɔn yerenom yi wɔ mma.
english: All these had married foreign women, and some of them had children by these wives.

twi: Adebɔ MfiaseMfiase no Onyankopɔn bɔɔ ɔsoro ne asase.
english: In the beginning God created the heavens and the earth.

twi: Na asase yɛ basaa a na ɛda mpan, na sum kata bun no ani, na Onyankopɔn Honhom butuw nsu no ani.
english: Now the earth was formless and empty, darkness was over the surface of the deep, and the Spirit of God was hovering over the waters.

twi: Onyankopɔn hyɛe se, “Ɛnyɛ hann,” na ɛyɛɛ hann.
english: And God said, “Let there be light,” and there was light.

twi: Onyankopɔn huu sɛ hann no ye, na ɔtew hann no fii sum no ho.
english: God saw that the light was good, and he separated the light from the darkness.

twi: Onyankopɔn frɛɛ hann no se, “adekyee,” na sum no nso se, “adesae.” Ade sae na ade kyee, da a edi kan ne no.
english: God called the light “day,” and the darkness he called “night.” And there was evening, and there was morning—the first day.

twi: Onyankopɔn kae se, “Nkyemu mmra nsu no ntam, na ɛnkyekyɛ nsu no mu.”
english: And God said, “Let there be a vault between the waters to separate water from water.”

twi: Enti Onyankopɔn yɛɛ nkyɛmu no, de kyekyɛɛ nsu a ɛwɔ nkyɛmu no ase fii nsu a ɛwɔ nkyɛmu no atifi no mu. Na ɛyɛɛ saa.
english: So God made the vault and separated the water under the vault from the water above it. And it was so.

twi: Onyankopɔn too atifi nkyɛmu no din wim. Na ade sae, na ade kyee; eyi ne da a ɛto so abien.
english: God called the vault “sky.” And there was evening, and there was morning—the second day.

twi: Na Onyankopɔn kae se, “Nsu a ɛwɔ nkyɛmu no ase no ano mmoa wɔ faako, na asase kesee nna ne ho adi.” Na ɛyɛɛ saa.
english: And God said, “Let the water under the sky be gathered to one place, and let dry ground appear.” And it was so.

twi: Onyankopɔn too beae kesee ne din “asase.” Na nsu a ɛboaa ne ho ano no nso, ɔtoo no din “ɛpo.” Onyankopɔn hui sɛ eye.
english: God called the dry ground “land,” and the gathered waters he called “seas.” And God saw that it was good.

twi: Afei Onyankopɔn kae se, “Afifide mfifi wɔ asase so; afifide a ɛsow aba, nnuaba ahorow a ɛsow aba ne nea nʼaba hyehyɛ mu nyinaa mfifi wɔ asase so.” Na ɛyɛɛ saa.
english: Then God said, “Let the land produce vegetation: seed-bearing plants and trees on the land that bear fruit with seed in it, according to their various kinds.” And it was so.

twi: Afifide a ɛsow aba ne nnua fifii wɔ asase so na nʼaba no nyin yɛɛ nnua ne afifide sɛ ne sɛso. Onyankopɔn hui sɛ eye.
english: The land produced vegetation: plants bearing seed according to their kinds and trees bearing fruit with seed in it according to their kinds. And God saw that it was good.

twi: Na ade sae, na ade kyee. Eyi ne da a ɛto so abiɛsa.
english: And there was evening, and there was morning—the third day.

twi: Na Onyankopɔn kae se, “Hann mmra nkyɛmu a ɛwɔ wim no mu, na ɛmmɛpae adekyee ne adesae mu. Na ɛmmɛyɛ nnyinaso mma bere nkyekyɛmu, nna ne mfe,
english: And God said, “Let there be lights in the vault of the sky to separate the day from the night, and let them serve as signs to mark sacred times, and days and years,

twi: na ɛmma hann mmra nkyɛmu a ɛwɔ wim no mu, na ahyerɛn wɔ asase so.” Na ɛyɛɛ saa.
english: and let them be lights in the vault of the sky to give light on the earth.” And it was so.

twi: Onyankopɔn yɛɛ akanea akɛse abien a ɛyɛ owia ne ɔsram sɛ, owia no nni adekyee so na ɔsram no nni anadwo so. Ɔbɔɔ nsoromma nso.
english: God made two great lights—the greater light to govern the day and the lesser light to govern the night. He also made the stars.

twi: Onyankopɔn de akanea akɛse abien yi sii nkyɛmu a ɛwɔ wim no mu sɛ ɛnhyerɛn wɔ asase so,
english: God set them in the vault of the sky to give light on the earth,

twi: na wonni adekyee ne adesae no so, na ɛntew hann no mfi sum no ho. Na Onyankopɔn hui sɛ eye.
english: to govern the day and the night, and to separate light from darkness. And God saw that it was good.

twi: Na ade sae, na ade kyee. Da a ɛto so anan ne no.
english: And there was evening, and there was morning—the fourth day.

twi: Onyankopɔn kae se, “Abɔde a nkwa wɔ mu nhyɛ nsu no ma, na nnomaa ntu mfa asase ne nkyɛmu a ɛwɔ wim no so.”
english: And God said, “Let the water teem with living creatures, and let birds fly above the earth across the vault of the sky.”

twi: Enti Onyankopɔn bɔɔ po mu mmoa akɛse ne mmoa ahorow nyinaa a wɔwɔ nkwa na wɔkeka wɔn ho ne nnomaa ahorow nyinaa. Na Onyankopɔn hui sɛ eye.
english: So God created the great creatures of the sea and every living thing with which the water teems and that moves about in it, according to their kinds, and every winged bird according to its kind. And God saw that it was good.

twi: Onyankopɔn hyiraa abɔde no nyinaa so, kae se, “Monwo na monyɛ bebree na monhyɛ po no mu nsu no ma, na nnomaa ase ntrɛw wɔ asase so.”
english: God blessed them and said, “Be fruitful and increase in number and fill the water in the seas, and let the birds increase on the earth.”

twi: Na ade sae, na ade kyee. Da a ɛto so anum ne no.
english: And there was evening, and there was morning—the fifth day.

twi: Onyankopɔn kae se, “Abɔde a nkwa wɔ mu ahorow nyinaa ne wɔn sɛso, anantwi ne mmoa a wɔwea wɔn afuru so ne mmoa ahorow a wɔyɛ keka a wɔwɔ asase so nyinaa mmra asase so.” Na ɛyɛɛ saa.
english: And God said, “Let the land produce living creatures according to their kinds: the livestock, the creatures that move along the ground, and the wild animals, each according to its kind.” And it was so.

twi: Onyankopɔn bɔɔ mmoa ahorow, anantwi ahorow ne wɔn sɛso ne mmoa a wɔwea wɔn afuru so ne wɔn sɛso. Na Onyankopɔn hui sɛ eye.
english: God made the wild animals according to their kinds, the livestock according to their kinds, and all the creatures that move along the ground according to their kinds. And God saw that it was good.

twi: Onyankopɔn kae se, “Momma yɛmmɔ onipa sɛ yɛn sɛso, na onni po mu mpataa, wim nnomaa, anantwi ne mmoa a wɔyɛ keka ne biribiara a ɛwea nʼafuru so wɔ asase so no so.”
english: Then God said, “Let us make mankind in our image, in our likeness, so that they may rule over the fish in the sea and the birds in the sky, over the livestock and all the wild animals, and over all the creatures that move along the ground.”

twi: Enti Onyankopɔn bɔɔ onipa sɛ ne sɛso;Onyankopɔn sɛso so na ɔbɔɔ wɔn;ɔbarima ne ɔbea na ɔbɔɔ wɔn.
Onyankopɔn hyiraa wɔn, ka kyerɛɛ wɔn se, “Monwo na monyɛ asase so ma, na munni biribiara so. Munni po mu mpataa ne wim nnomaa ne abɔde biara a nkwa wɔ mu a ɛwɔ asase so no nyinaa so.”
english: God blessed them and said to them, “Be fruitful and increase in number; fill the earth and subdue it. Rule over the fish in the sea and the birds in the sky and over every living creature that moves on the ground.”

twi: Afei Onyankopɔn kae se, “Mede asase so afifide a ɛsow aba nyinaa, afifide biara a aba hyɛ ne nnuaba mu wɔ asase yi so nyinaa hyɛ wo nsa. Ɛbɛyɛ wʼaduan.
english: Then God said, “I give you every seed-bearing plant on the face of the whole earth and every tree that has fruit with seed in it. They will be yours for food.

twi: Mede nhabammono nyinaa ama aboa biara a ɔwɔ asase so, anomaa biara a ɔwɔ wim, biribiara a ɛwea nʼafuru so, biribiara a nkwa wɔ mu wɔ asase so sɛ wɔn aduan.” Na ɛyɛɛ saa.
english: And to all the beasts of the earth and all the birds in the sky and all the creatures that move along the ground—everything that has the breath of life in it—I give every green plant for food.” And it was so.

twi: Onyankopɔn hwɛɛ nea wayɛ nyinaa huu sɛ ɛyɛ papa. Na ade sae, na ade kyee. Eyi ne da a ɛto so asia.
english: God saw all that he had made, and it was very good. And there was evening, and there was morning—the sixth day.

twi: Eyi ne ɔkwan a Onyankopɔn faa so bɔɔ ɔsoro ne asase ne nea ɛwɔ mu nyinaa.
english: Thus the heavens and the earth were completed in all their vast array.

twi: Eduu da a ɛto so ason no, na Onyankopɔn awie nnwuma a ofii ase yɛe no nyinaa. Enti da a ɛto so ason no, ogyee nʼahome.
english: By the seventh day God had finished the work he had been doing; so on the seventh day he rested from all his work.

twi: Enti Onyankopɔn hyiraa da a ɛto so ason no, na ɔtew ho, efisɛ saa da no na Onyankopɔn gyee nʼahome fii adebɔ nnwuma no nyinaa mu.
english: Then God blessed the seventh day and made it holy, because on it he rested from all the work of creating that he had done.

twi: Eyi ne ɔsoro ne asasebɔ ho asɛm. Bere a Awurade Nyankopɔn bɔɔ ɔsoro ne asase no.
english: This is the account of the heavens and the earth when they were created, when the Lord God made the earth and the heavens.

twi: Na afifide biara nni asase so, na wuram nnua biara nso nni hɔ. Efisɛ, na Awurade Nyankopɔn mmaa osu ntɔɔ wɔ asase so, na onipa nso nni asase so a ɔbɛyɛ so adwuma.
english: Now no shrub had yet appeared on the earth and no plant had yet sprung up, for the Lord God had not sent rain on the earth and there was no one to work the ground,

twi: Nanso nsuti puepue fifii asase mu bɛfɔw asase ani nyinaa.
english: but streams came up from the earth and watered the whole surface of the ground.

twi: Awurade Nyankopɔn de asase no so dɔte nwen onipa, na ɔhomee nkwa home guu ne hwenem, maa onipa no bɛyɛɛ ɔteasefo.
english: Then the Lord God formed a man from the dust of the ground and breathed into his nostrils the breath of life, and the man became a living being.

twi: Afei Awurade Nyankopɔn yɛɛ turo wɔ Eden apuei fam, na ɛhɔ na ɔde onipa a ɔnwen no no tenae.
english: Now the Lord God had planted a garden in the east, in Eden; and there he put the man he had formed.

twi: Awurade Nyankopɔn maa nnua ahorow nyinaa fifi fii asase no mu; nnua a ɛyɛ fɛ na wodi. Na nkwa dua ne papa ne bɔnehu dua sisi turo no mfimfini.
english: The Lord God made all kinds of trees grow out of the ground—trees that were pleasing to the eye and good for food. In the middle of the garden were the tree of life and the tree of the knowledge of good and evil.

twi: Na asu sen fii Eden bɛfɔw turo no mu afifide no; efi hɔ a, na saa asu no mu apaapae ayɛ nsubɔnten anan.
english: A river watering the garden flowed from Eden; from there it was separated into four headwaters.

twi: Wɔtoo asu a apaapae no mu nea edi kan no din Pison. Na ɛkɔntɔn fa Hawila asase a sikakɔkɔɔ wɔ so no so nyinaa.
english: The name of the first is the Pishon; it winds through the entire land of Havilah, where there is gold.

twi: Na saa asase no so sikakɔkɔɔ ye. Na ɛhyɛ a ɛyɛ huam ne apopobibiribo nso wɔ hɔ.
english: (The gold of that land is good; aromatic resin and onyx are also there.)

twi: Asubɔnten a ɛto so abien no din de Gihon. Na ɛno ara na ɛkɔntɔnkɔntɔn fa Kus asase ho nyinaa.
english: The name of the second river is the Gihon; it winds through the entire land of Cush.

twi: Asu a ɛto so abiɛsa no, na wɔfrɛ no Tigris a ɛsen kɔ asase kɛse Asiria apuei fam no. Asu a ɛto so anan no nso, na wɔfrɛ no Eufrate.
english: The name of the third river is the Tigris; it runs along the east side of Ashur. And the fourth river is the Euphrates.

twi: Awurade Nyankopɔn faa onipa no de no kɔtenaa Eden turo mu hɔ sɛ ɔnyɛ mu adwuma, na ɔnhwɛ so.
english: The Lord God took the man and put him in the Garden of Eden to work it and take care of it.

twi: Na Awurade Nyankopɔn bɔɔ onipa no kɔkɔ se, “Wowɔ ho kwan sɛ wudi dua biara so aba wɔ turo yi mu ha;
english: And the Lord God commanded the man, “You are free to eat from any tree in the garden;

twi: nanso wunni ho kwan sɛ wudi papa ne bɔnehu dua no so aba. Da a wubedi no, nea ɛbɛyɛ biara no, wubewu.”
english: but you must not eat from the tree of the knowledge of good and evil, for when you eat from it you will certainly die.”

twi: Onyankopɔn Bɔ HawaAfei Awurade Nyankopɔn kae se, “Enye sɛ onipa nko tena; mɛbɔ ɔboafo a ɔfata no ama no.”
english: The Lord God said, “It is not good for the man to be alone. I will make a helper suitable for him.”

twi: Saa bere no na Awurade Nyankopɔn de mfutuma abɔ wuram mmoa ne wim nnomaa nyinaa. Enti, ɔde wɔn brɛɛ onipa sɛ ɔnhwehwɛ din ko a ɔde bɛtoto wɔn; na din a onipa de too abɔde a nkwa wɔ mu biara no, ɛno ara na ɛyɛɛ din a wɔde frɛɛ no.
english: Now the Lord God had formed out of the ground all the wild animals and all the birds in the sky. He brought them to the man to see what he would name them; and whatever the man called each living creature, that was its name.

twi: Enti onipa totoo nyɛmmoa, wim nnomaa ne wuram mmoa no nyinaa din.Nanso onipa de, wannya ɔboafo a ɔfata.
english:
So the man gave names to all the livestock, the birds in the sky and all the wild animals.
But for Adam no suitable helper was found.

twi: Enti Awurade Nyankopɔn maa onipa daa nnahɔɔ. Bere a onipa daa saa no, oyii ne mfe mu mparow baako, na ɔde honam taree baabi a oyii mparow hɔ no.
english: So the Lord God caused the man to fall into a deep sleep; and while he was sleeping, he took one of the man’s ribs and then closed up the place with flesh.

twi: Afei Awurade Nyankopɔn de mfe mu mparow baako a oyi fii onipa mu no bɔɔ ɔbea, de no maa onipa no.
english: Then the Lord God made a woman from the rib he had taken out of the man, and he brought her to the man.

twi: Na Adam kae se,“Mʼankasa me dompene me honam bi ni.Wɔbɛfrɛ oyi ɔbea efisɛɔbarima mu na woyii no fii.”
english:
The man said,
“This is now bone of my bones
    and flesh of my flesh;
she shall be called ‘woman,’
    for she was taken out of man.”

twi: Eyi nti na ɔbarima gyaw nʼagya ne ne na de ne ho kɔbɔ ne yere ho sɛnea wɔn baanu no bɛyɛ nnipa koro.
english: That is why a man leaves his father and mother and is united to his wife, and they become one flesh.

twi: Saa bere no, na ɔbarima ne ne yere nyinaa ho da hɔ, nanso na wɔmfɛre.
english: Adam and his wife were both naked, and they felt no shame.

twi: Bɔne A Adam Yɛe Ne Akyi AsɛmNa ɔwɔ yɛ ɔdaadaafo wɔ wuram mmoadoma a Awurade Nyankopɔn abɔ wɔn no nyinaa mu. Ɔwɔ no kɔɔ ɔbea no nkyɛn kobisaa no se, “Enti ɛyɛ ampa ara sɛ, Onyankopɔn se, ‘Munnni turo yi mu aduaba biara?’ ”
english: Now the serpent was more crafty than any of the wild animals the Lord God had made. He said to the woman, “Did God really say, ‘You must not eat from any tree in the garden’?”

twi: Ɔbea no buaa ɔwɔ se, “Yetumi di nnua a ɛwɔ turo yi mu no so aduaba biara,
english: The woman said to the serpent, “We may eat fruit from the trees in the garden,

twi: nanso Onyankopɔn kae se, ‘Ɛnsɛ sɛ yedi dua a esi turo no mfimfini no so aduaba, na ɛnsɛ sɛ yɛde yɛn nsa mpo ka, anyɛ saa a yebewu.’ ”
english: but God did say, ‘You must not eat fruit from the tree that is in the middle of the garden, and you must not touch it, or you will die.’”

twi: Na ɔwɔ no ka kyerɛɛ ɔbea no se, “Morenwuwu.
english: “You will not certainly die,” the serpent said to the woman.

twi: Mmom, Onyankopɔn nim sɛ, da a mubedi no ara pɛ, mo ani bɛba mo ho so, ama moayɛ sɛ Onyankopɔn, na moahu papa ne bɔne.”
english: “For God knows that when you eat from it your eyes will be opened, and you will be like God, knowing good and evil.”

twi: Bere a ɔbea no huu sɛ dua a esi mfimfini no so aba no wodi a, ɛbɛyɛ yie, na ɛyɛ akɔnnɔ, na afei ɛtew ani no, ɔtew bi dii, de bi maa ne kunu a na ɔne no wɔ hɔ no, maa ɔno nso dii.
english: When the woman saw that the fruit of the tree was good for food and pleasing to the eye, and also desirable for gaining wisdom, she took some and ate it. She also gave some to her husband, who was with her, and he ate it.

twi: Wodi wiee no, wɔn baanu ani baa wɔn ho so, na wohuu sɛ wɔn nyinaa da adagyaw. Enti wɔkekaa nhaban sisii anim, de kataa wɔn adagyaw so.
english: Then the eyes of both of them were opened, and they realized they were naked; so they sewed fig leaves together and made coverings for themselves.

twi: Da no anwummere, wɔtee Awurade Nyankopɔn nka sɛ ɔnam turo no mu; enti Adam ne ne yere Hawa de wɔn ho kosiee nnua a ɛwɔ turo mu hɔ no mu sɛnea Awurade Nyankopɔn renhu wɔn.
english: Then the man and his wife heard the sound of the Lord God as he was walking in the garden in the cool of the day, and they hid from the Lord God among the trees of the garden.

twi: Na Awurade Nyankopɔn frɛɛ Adam bisaa no se, “Mowɔ he?”
english: But the Lord God called to the man, “Where are you?”

twi: Adam buae se, “Metee wo nka wɔ turo no mu hɔ, nanso na misuro, efisɛ na meda adagyaw nti mekɔtɛwee.”
english: He answered, “I heard you in the garden, and I was afraid because I was naked; so I hid.”

twi: Na Onyankopɔn bisaa no se, “Hena na ɔka kyerɛɛ wo se na woda adagyaw? Woadi dua a meka kyerɛɛ wo se nni so aba no bi ana?”
english: And he said, “Who told you that you were naked? Have you eaten from the tree that I commanded you not to eat from?”

twi: Adam kae se, “Yiw, nanso ɔbea no a wode no maa me sɛ me ne no ntena no na ɔde aduaba a ɔtew fii dua no so no brɛɛ me maa midii.”
english: The man said, “The woman you put here with me—she gave me some fruit from the tree, and I ate it.”

twi: Enti Awurade Nyankopɔn bisaa ɔbea no se, “Dɛn na woayɛ yi?”Ɔbea no buae se, “Ɔwɔ no na ɔdaadaa me ma midii.”
english:
Then the Lord God said to the woman, “What is this you have done?”
The woman said, “The serpent deceived me, and I ate.”

twi: Enti Awurade Nyankopɔn ka kyerɛɛ ɔwɔ no se, “Esiane saa ade a woayɛ yi nti,“Wɔadome wo wɔ mmoanyinaa ne nkekaboa mu.Wobɛwea wʼafuru so,na wo nkwannanyinaa woadi mfutuma.
english:
So the Lord God said to the serpent, “Because you have done this,
“Cursed are you above all livestock
    and all wild animals!
You will crawl on your belly
    and you will eat dust
    all the days of your life.

twi: Mede ɔtan bɛtowo ne ɔbea none wʼasefo ne nʼasefo ntam.Ɔno na ɔbɛbɔ wo ti,na wo nso woaka ne nantin.”
english:
And I will put enmity
    between you and the woman,
    and between your offspring and hers;
he will crush your head,
    and you will strike his heel.”

twi: Afei, Awurade Nyankopɔn ka kyerɛɛ ɔbea no nso se,“Wobɛte ɔyaw pa ara wɔ wʼawo mu;ɔyaw mu na wobɛwo mma.Eyi nyinaa akyi no,wʼani begyina wo kunu na obedi wo so.”
english:
To the woman he said,
“I will make your pains in childbearing very severe;
    with painful labor you will give birth to children.
Your desire will be for your husband,
    and he will rule over you.”

twi: Onyankopɔn ka kyerɛɛ Adam nso se, “Esiane sɛ wutiee wo yere asɛm, na wudii dua a mehyɛɛ wo se, ‘nni so aba no’ nti,“Madome asase,na ɔbrɛ ne ɔhaw mu na wubedidi sowo nkwanna nyinaa.
english:
To Adam he said, “Because you listened to your wife and ate fruit from the tree about which I commanded you, ‘You must not eat from it,’
“Cursed is the ground because of you;
    through painful toil you will eat food from it
    all the days of your life.

twi: Ebefifi nsɔe ne nkyɛkyerɛama wo na woadi wuram nhaban.
english:
It will produce thorns and thistles for you,
    and you will eat the plants of the field.

twi: Wubesiam wʼanim fifiriansa na woanya aduan adi,kosi sɛ wubewu akɔ dɔte mu,efisɛ dɔte no mu na menwen wo fii;woyɛ dɔte,na dɔte mu na wobɛsan akɔ.”
english:
By the sweat of your brow
    you will eat your food
until you return to the ground,
    since from it you were taken;
for dust you are
    and to dust you will return.”

twi: Adam too ne yere no din Hawa, efisɛ ɔno na ɔbɛyɛ ateasefo nyinaa na.
english: Adam named his wife Eve, because she would become the mother of all the living.

twi: Awurade Nyankopɔn de aboa nhoma yɛɛ ntade maa Adam ne ne yere Hawa de kataa wɔn ho.
english: The Lord God made garments of skin for Adam and his wife and clothed them.

twi: Awurade Nyankopɔn kae se, “Afei, onipa no abɛyɛ sɛ yɛn ara a, wahu papa ne bɔne. Ɛnsɛ sɛ yɛma no kwan na ɔteɛ ne nsa kɔtew nkwa dua no so aba no bi di, na ɔtena ase afebɔɔ.”
english: And the Lord God said, “The man has now become like one of us, knowing good and evil. He must not be allowed to reach out his hand and take also from the tree of life and eat, and live forever.”

twi: Enti Awurade Nyankopɔn pam no fii Eden turo no mu sɛ ɔnkɔyɛ adwuma wɔ asase a wɔnwenee no fii mu no so.
english: So the Lord God banished him from the Garden of Eden to work the ground from which he had been taken.

twi: Ɔpam onipa no, ɔde Kerubim ne afoa a ɛdɛw twaa ne ho fa baabiara no sii Eden turo no apuei fam sɛ ɛnwɛn ɔkwan a ɛkɔ nkwa dua no ho no.
english: After he drove the man out, he placed on the east side of the Garden of Eden cherubim and a flaming sword flashing back and forth to guard the way to the tree of life.

twi: Kain Ne Habel AfɔrebɔAdam de ne ho kaa ne yere Hawa ma onyinsɛn, woo abarimaa a wɔfrɛ no Kain. Na ɔkae se, Awurade adaworoma, mawo ɔbabarima.
english: Adam made love to his wife Eve, and she became pregnant and gave birth to Cain. She said, “With the help of the Lord I have brought forth a man.”

twi: Akyiri no, ɔsan woo nʼakyi babarima too no din Habel.Na Habel bɛyɛɛ oguanhwɛfo, na Kain nso bɛyɛɛ okuafo.
english:
Later she gave birth to his brother Abel.
Now Abel kept flocks, and Cain worked the soil.

twi: Nna bi akyi no, Kain de nʼafum nnɔbae bi kɔbɔɔ Awurade afɔre.
english: In the course of time Cain brought some of the fruits of the soil as an offering to the Lord.

twi: Habel nso de ne nyɛmmoa no mu mmakan a wɔadodɔ srade kɔbɔɔ Onyankopɔn afɔre. Awurade ani sɔɔ Habel afɔrebɔ no.
english: And Abel also brought an offering—fat portions from some of the firstborn of his flock. The Lord looked with favor on Abel and his offering,

twi: Nanso Kain afɔrebɔ no de, nʼani ansɔ. Asɛm no anyɛ Kain dɛ, na ne bo fuwii.
english: but on Cain and his offering he did not look with favor. So Cain was very angry, and his face was downcast.

twi: Awurade bisaa Kain se, “Adɛn nti na wo bo afuw? Adɛn nti na woamuna saa?
english: Then the Lord said to Cain, “Why are you angry? Why is your face downcast?

twi: Sɛ woyɛ ade pa a, anka wɔrennye wo nto mu ana? Sɛ wonyɛ ade pa de a, bɔne gyina wo pon ano, ɛrehwehwɛ wo ako atia wo, nanso ɛsɛ sɛ wudi no so.”
english: If you do what is right, will you not be accepted? But if you do not do what is right, sin is crouching at your door; it desires to have you, but you must rule over it.”

twi: Kain Kum HabelDa bi Kain ka kyerɛɛ ne nua Habel se, “Ma yɛnkɔ afum.” Bere a wɔwɔ afum hɔ no, Kain tow hyɛɛ ne nua Habel so, kum no.
english: Now Cain said to his brother Abel, “Let’s go out to the field.” While they were in the field, Cain attacked his brother Abel and killed him.

twi: Awurade bisaa Kain se, “Wo nua Habel wɔ he?”Kain buae se, “Minnim. Mɛyɛ dɛn ahu? Me na mehwɛ me nua so ana?”
english:
Then the Lord said to Cain, “Where is your brother Abel?”
“I don’t know,” he replied. “Am I my brother’s keeper?”

twi: Awurade bisaa Kain se, “Dɛn na woayɛ yi? Tie! Wo nua mogya su fi asase so frɛ me.
english: The Lord said, “What have you done? Listen! Your brother’s blood cries out to me from the ground.

twi: Mprempren, wɔadome wo, apam wo afi asase a ebuee nʼano gyee wo nua mogya fii wo nsam no so.
english: Now you are under a curse and driven from the ground, which opened its mouth to receive your brother’s blood from your hand.

twi: Sɛ woyɛ asase no so adwuma sɛ dɛn ara a, worennya nnɔbae biara mfi so. Wobɛyɛ ɔkobɔfo, akyinkyin asase so.”
english: When you work the ground, it will no longer yield its crops for you. You will be a restless wanderer on the earth.”

twi: Kain kae se, “Awurade mʼasotwe boro me so.
english: Cain said to the Lord, “My punishment is more than I can bear.

twi: Nnɛ, woapam me afi asase so ne wʼanim. Mɛyɛ ɔkobɔfo akyinkyin asase so na obiara a obenya me no bekum me.”
english: Today you are driving me from the land, and I will be hidden from your presence; I will be a restless wanderer on the earth, and whoever finds me will kill me.”

twi: Nanso Awurade ka kyerɛɛ no se, “Ɛnte saa koraa! Obiara a obekum Kain no benya Kain asotwe no mpɛn ason.” Afei, Awurade hyɛɛ Kain agyirae bi sɛnea ɛbɛyɛ a, obiara a obehyia no no renkum no.
english: But the Lord said to him, “Not so; anyone who kills Cain will suffer vengeance seven times over.” Then the Lord put a mark on Cain so that no one who found him would kill him.

twi: Enti Kain guan fii Awurade anim, kɔtenaa Nod asase so wɔ Eden apuei fam.
english: So Cain went out from the Lord’s presence and lived in the land of Nod, east of Eden.

twi: Anibue MfiaseKain de ne ho kaa ne yere na onyinsɛn, woo ɔbabarima, too no din Henok. Saa bere no, Kain kyekyeree kurow bi de too ne ba Henok.
english: Cain made love to his wife, and she became pregnant and gave birth to Enoch. Cain was then building a city, and he named it after his son Enoch.

twi: Henok woo Irad. Irad woo Mehuyael. Mehuyael woo Metusael. Metusael woo Lamek.
english: To Enoch was born Irad, and Irad was the father of Mehujael, and Mehujael was the father of Methushael, and Methushael was the father of Lamech.

twi: Lamek waree mmea baanu a wɔn din de Ada ne Sila.
english: Lamech married two women, one named Adah and the other Zillah.

twi: Ada woo Yabal a nʼasefo yɛ wɔn a wɔte ntamadan mu yɛn mmoa.
english: Adah gave birth to Jabal; he was the father of those who live in tents and raise livestock.

twi: Na Yabal nuabarima din de Yubal a nʼasefo yɛ mmɛnhyɛnfo ne sankubɔfo.
english: His brother’s name was Jubal; he was the father of all who play stringed instruments and pipes.

twi: Sila woo ɔbabarima a wɔfrɛ no Tubal-Kain. Na ɔyɛ kɔbere atomfo ne nnade ahorow nyinaa atomfo agya. Na Tubal-Kain wɔ nuabea bi a ne din de Naama.
english: Zillah also had a son, Tubal-Cain, who forged all kinds of tools out of bronze and iron. Tubal-Cain’s sister was Naamah.

twi: Da bi, Lamek ka kyerɛɛ ne yerenom Ada ne Sila se,“Muntie me, me yerenommakum aberante bi a,ɔtow hyɛɛ me so, piraa me.
english:
Lamech said to his wives,
“Adah and Zillah, listen to me;
    wives of Lamech, hear my words.
I have killed a man for wounding me,
    a young man for injuring me.

twi: Sɛ Kain so aweretɔ bɛyɛ mpɛn ason a,ɛno de, me Lamek de, nea obekum me no, nʼasotwe bɛyɛ mpɛn aduɔson ason.”
english:
If Cain is avenged seven times,
    then Lamech seventy-seven times.”

twi: Akyiri no, Adam de ne ho kaa ne yere Hawa. Na ɔwoo ɔbabarima bio. Na wɔtoo no din Set kae se, “Onyankopɔn ama me ɔba foforo asi Habel a Kain kum no no anan mu.”
english: Adam made love to his wife again, and she gave birth to a son and named him Seth, saying, “God has granted me another child in place of Abel, since Cain killed him.”

twi: Set nso woo ɔbabarima na ɔtoo no din Enos.Saa bere no mu na nnipa fitii ase bɔɔ Awurade din.
english:
Seth also had a son, and he named him Enosh.
At that time people began to call on the name of the Lord.

twi: Adam AsefoSɛnea Adam asefo nnidiso te ni.Bere a Onyankopɔn nwen onipa no, ɔnwen no sɛ ɔno ara ne sɛso.
english:
This is the written account of Adam’s family line.
When God created mankind, he made them in the likeness of God.

twi: Ɔbɔɔ ɔbea ne ɔbarima, na ohyiraa wɔn. Ɔbɔɔ wɔn wiee no, ɔtoo wɔn din onipa.
english: He created them male and female and blessed them. And he named them “Mankind” when they were created.

twi: Adam dii mfe ɔha aduasa no, ɔwoo ɔbabarima sɛ ɔno ara ne bɔbea ne ne sɛso. Ɔtoo ne din Set.
english: When Adam had lived 130 years, he had a son in his own likeness, in his own image; and he named him Seth.

twi: Ɔwoo Set no, Adam tenaa ase mfe ahanwɔtwe a ɔwowoo mmabarima ne mmabea kaa ho.
english: After Seth was born, Adam lived 800 years and had other sons and daughters.

twi: Sɛ wɔka Adam mfe nyinaa bɔ mu a, odii mfe ahankron aduasa, ansa na ɔrewu.
english: Altogether, Adam lived a total of 930 years, and then he died.

twi: Set dii mfe ɔha ne anum no, ɔwoo Enos.
english: When Seth had lived 105 years, he became the father of Enosh.

twi: Set woo Enos akyi no, ɔtenaa ase, dii mfe ahanwɔtwe ne ason, wowoo mmabarima ne mmabea kaa ho.
english: After he became the father of Enosh, Seth lived 807 years and had other sons and daughters.

twi: Sɛ wɔka Set mfe dodow bɔ mu a, odii mfe ahankron ne dumien, ansa na ɔrewu.
english: Altogether, Seth lived a total of 912 years, and then he died.

twi: Enos dii mfe aduɔkron no, ɔwoo Kenan.
english: When Enosh had lived 90 years, he became the father of Kenan.

twi: Enos woo Kenan akyi no, ɔtenaa ase mfe ahanwɔtwe ne dunum, wowoo mmabarima ne mmabea kaa ho.
english: After he became the father of Kenan, Enosh lived 815 years and had other sons and daughters.

twi: Sɛ wɔka Enos mfe dodow bɔ mu a, odii mfe ahankron ne anum, ansa na ɔrewu.
english: Altogether, Enosh lived a total of 905 years, and then he died.

twi: Kenan dii mfe aduɔson no, ɔwoo Mahalalel.
english: When Kenan had lived 70 years, he became the father of Mahalalel.

twi: Kenan woo Mahalalel akyi no, ɔtenaa ase mfe ahanwɔtwe aduanan, wowoo mmabarima ne mmabea kaa ho.
english: After he became the father of Mahalalel, Kenan lived 840 years and had other sons and daughters.

twi: Sɛ wɔka Kenan mfe dodow bɔ mu a, odii mfe ahankron ne du, ansa na ɔrewu.
english: Altogether, Kenan lived a total of 910 years, and then he died.

twi: Mahalalel dii mfe aduosia anum no, ɔwoo Yared.
english: When Mahalalel had lived 65 years, he became the father of Jared.

twi: Mahalalel woo Yared akyi no, ɔtenaa ase, dii mfe ahanwɔtwe aduasa, wowoo mmabarima ne mmabea kaa ho.
english: After he became the father of Jared, Mahalalel lived 830 years and had other sons and daughters.

twi: Sɛ wɔka Mahalalel mfe dodow bɔ mu a, odii mfe ahanwɔtwe aduɔkron anum, ansa na ɔrewu.
english: Altogether, Mahalalel lived a total of 895 years, and then he died.

twi: Yared dii mfe ɔha aduosia abien no, ɔwoo Henok.
english: When Jared had lived 162 years, he became the father of Enoch.

twi: Yared woo Henok akyi no, ɔtenaa ase mfe ahanwɔtwe, wowoo mmabarima ne mmabea kaa ho.
english: After he became the father of Enoch, Jared lived 800 years and had other sons and daughters.

twi: Sɛ wɔka Yared mfe dodow bɔ mu a, odii mfe ahankron aduosia abien, ansa na ɔrewu.
english: Altogether, Jared lived a total of 962 years, and then he died.

twi: Henok dii mfe aduosia anum no, ɔwoo Metusela.
english: When Enoch had lived 65 years, he became the father of Methuselah.

twi: Henok woo Metusela akyi no, Henok de ne ho bataa Awurade ho mfe ahaasa, na ɔwowoo mmabarima ne mmabea kaa ho.
english: After he became the father of Methuselah, Enoch walked faithfully with God 300 years and had other sons and daughters.

twi: Sɛ wɔka Henok mfe dodow bɔ mu a, odii mfe ahaasa aduosia anum.
english: Altogether, Enoch lived a total of 365 years.

twi: Henok de ne ho bataa Onyankopɔn; afei, obi anhu no bio, efisɛ Onyankopɔn faa no kɔe.
english: Enoch walked faithfully with God; then he was no more, because God took him away.

twi: Metusela dii mfe ɔha aduɔwɔtwe ason no, ɔwoo Lamek.
english: When Methuselah had lived 187 years, he became the father of Lamech.

twi: Metusela woo Lamek akyi no, ɔtenaa ase mfe ahanson aduɔwɔtwe abien, wowoo mmabarima ne mmabea kaa ho.
english: After he became the father of Lamech, Methuselah lived 782 years and had other sons and daughters.

twi: Sɛ wɔka Metusela mfe dodow bɔ mu a, odii mfe ahankron aduosia akron, ansa na ɔrewu.
english: Altogether, Methuselah lived a total of 969 years, and then he died.

twi: Lamek dii mfe ɔha ne aduɔwɔtwe abien no, ɔwoo ɔbabarima.
english: When Lamech had lived 182 years, he had a son.

twi: Ɔtoo no din Noa, na ɔkae se, “Ɔno na ɔbɛma yɛanya ahomegye afi kuayɛ mu adwumaden wɔ asase a Awurade adome no so.”
english: He named him Noah and said, “He will comfort us in the labor and painful toil of our hands caused by the ground the Lord has cursed.”

twi: Lamek woo Noa akyi no, ɔtenaa ase mfe ahannum aduɔkron anum, wowoo mmabarima ne mmabea kaa ho.
english: After Noah was born, Lamech lived 595 years and had other sons and daughters.

twi: Sɛ wɔka Lamek mfe dodow bɔ mu a, odii mfe ahanson aduɔson ason, ansa na ɔrewu.
english: Altogether, Lamech lived a total of 777 years, and then he died.

twi: Noa dii mfe ahannum no, ɔwoo mmabarima baasa a wɔfrɛ wɔn Sem, Ham ne Yafet.
english: After Noah was 500 years old, he became the father of Shem, Ham and Japheth.

twi: Nnipa Ne BɔneBere a nnipa dɔɔso wɔ asase so na wɔwoo mmabea no,
english: When human beings began to increase in number on the earth and daughters were born to them,

twi: Onyankopɔn mmabarima no huu sɛ nnipa mmabea no ho yɛ fɛ, nti nea obiara pɛ no no, ɔfaa no waree.
english: the sons of God saw that the daughters of humans were beautiful, and they married any of them they chose.

twi: Na Awurade kae se, “Me honhom rentena nnipa mu nkosi daa, efisɛ wɔyɛ ɔhonam; na wɔn nkwa nna bɛyɛ mfe ɔha aduonu.”
english: Then the Lord said, “My Spirit will not contend with humans forever, for they are mortal; their days will be a hundred and twenty years.”

twi: Saa bere no, na nnipa abran wɔ asase no so. Bere a Onyankopɔn mmabarima yi kɔɔ nnipa mmabea yi ho no, wɔne wɔn wowoe. Saa nnipa yi ne kan tete nnipa atitiriw a wogyee din no.
english: The Nephilim were on the earth in those days—and also afterward—when the sons of God went to the daughters of humans and had children by them. They were the heroes of old, men of renown.

twi: Awurade Nyankopɔn huu sɛ adesamma amumɔyɛ adɔɔso wɔ asase so, na nnipa nsusuwii nyinaa yɛ bɔne nko ara.
english: The Lord saw how great the wickedness of the human race had become on the earth, and that every inclination of the thoughts of the human heart was only evil all the time.

twi: Awurade Nyankopɔn nuu ne ho sɛ ɔbɔɔ wɔn bɛtenaa asase so. Saa bɔne no yɛɛ Awurade Nyankopɔn awerɛhow.
english: The Lord regretted that he had made human beings on the earth, and his heart was deeply troubled.

twi: Awurade kae se, “Mɛpepa nnipa a mabɔ wɔn no afi asase so; mmoa ne mmoa a wɔwea asase so ne wim nnomaa, efisɛ manu me ho sɛ mebɔɔ wɔn.”
english: So the Lord said, “I will wipe from the face of the earth the human race I have created—and with them the animals, the birds and the creatures that move along the ground—for I regret that I have made them.”

twi: Nanso Noa de, onyaa adom Awurade anim.
english: But Noah found favor in the eyes of the Lord.

twi: Noa awo ntoatoaso ni.Na Noa yɛ onipa ɔtreneeni a ne ho nni asɛm wɔ ne bere sofo no mu. Ɔyɛɛ Onyankopɔn apɛde.
english:
This is the account of Noah and his family.
Noah was a righteous man, blameless among the people of his time, and he walked faithfully with God.

twi: Noa woo mmabarima baasa na wɔn din de Sem, Ham ne Yafet.
english: Noah had three sons: Shem, Ham and Japheth.

twi: Na bɔne ahyɛ asase so ma a, amumɔyɛsɛm adɔɔso.
english: Now the earth was corrupt in God’s sight and was full of violence.

twi: Onyankopɔn huu saa bɔne yi nyinaa wɔ asase so, huu awurukasɛm ne amumɔyɛsɛm wɔ mmaa nyinaa nso.
english: God saw how corrupt the earth had become, for all the people on earth had corrupted their ways.

twi: Enti Onyankopɔn ka kyerɛɛ Noa se, “Esiane sɛ nnipa ama basabasa aba asase so nti, mɛsɛe nnipa ne asase a wɔte so no nyinaa.
english: So God said to Noah, “I am going to put an end to all people, for the earth is filled with violence because of them. I am surely going to destroy both them and the earth.

twi: Fa ɔwawa dua yɛ adaka. Yɛ adan wɔ Adaka no mu, na fa ama ka mu ne akyi nyinaa.
english: So make yourself an ark of cypress wood; make rooms in it and coat it with pitch inside and out.

twi: Sɛɛ na ɛsɛ sɛ woyɛ no: ma ne tenten nyɛ anammɔn ahannan aduonum, ne trɛw anammɔn aduɔson anum, na ne sorokɔ nso nyɛ anammɔn aduanan anum.
english: This is how you are to build it: The ark is to be three hundred cubits long, fifty cubits wide and thirty cubits high.

twi: Bɔ adaka no so. Ma ne sorokɔ nyɛ bɛyɛ sɛ nsateaa dunwɔtwe. Fa ɔpon to adaka no nkyɛn, na yɛ nsɛmso abiɛsa; nea edi kan, nea ɛda ntam ne nea ɛwɔ soro.
english: Make a roof for it, leaving below the roof an opening one cubit high all around. Put a door in the side of the ark and make lower, middle and upper decks.

twi: Tie! Mede nsuyiri rebɛkata asase so nyinaa, na mede asɛe abɔde a nkwa wɔ mu; biribiara a nkwa wɔ mu no, ne nyinaa bewuwu.
english: I am going to bring floodwaters on the earth to destroy all life under the heavens, every creature that has the breath of life in it. Everything on earth will perish.

twi: Na wo de, me ne wo bɛyɛ apam; na wo, wo mmabarima, wo yere ne wo mmabarima yerenom nyinaa ne wo bɛba Adaka no mu.
english: But I will establish my covenant with you, and you will enter the ark—you and your sons and your wife and your sons’ wives with you.

twi: Ɛsɛ sɛ wode abɔde a nkwa wɔ mu nyinaa, abien abien a ɛyɛ onini ne ɔbere, a wo ne wɔn bɛtena adaka no mu nsuyiri bere no a wonnwuwu.
english: You are to bring into the ark two of all living creatures, male and female, to keep them alive with you.

twi: Nnomaa ahorow biara abien, mmoa biara abien, ne abɔde biara a ɛwea asase so abien bɛba wo nkyɛn, na woahwɛ wɔn, na wɔanwuwu.
english: Two of every kind of bird, of every kind of animal and of every kind of creature that moves along the ground will come to you to be kept alive.

twi: Afei, fa nnuan ahorow a wodi na kora. Ɛno na ɛbɛyɛ wo ne wɔn nnuan a mubedi.”
english: You are to take every kind of food that is to be eaten and store it away as food for you and for them.”

twi: Noa yɛɛ biribiara pɛpɛɛpɛ, sɛnea Onyankopɔn ka kyerɛɛ no sɛ ɔnyɛ no.
english: Noah did everything just as God commanded him.

twi: Afei, Awurade ka kyerɛɛ Noa se, “Wo ne wo fifo nyinaa nkɔ Adaka no mu, efisɛ asase so nnipa nyinaa mu no, wo na mahu sɛ woyɛ ɔtreneeni.
english: The Lord then said to Noah, “Go into the ark, you and your whole family, because I have found you righteous in this generation.

twi: Fa mmoa a wɔn ho tew biara, anini ason ne abere ason ka wo ho. Na fa mmoa biara a wɔn ho ntew nso abien, onini ne ɔbere.
english: Take with you seven pairs of every kind of clean animal, a male and its mate, and one pair of every kind of unclean animal, a male and its mate,

twi: Na fa nnomaa biara anini ason ne abere, sɛnea ɛbɛyɛ a nsuyiri no akyi no, wɔn ase bɛfɛe.
english: and also seven pairs of every kind of bird, male and female, to keep their various kinds alive throughout the earth.

twi: Nnanson akyi no mɛma osu atɔ wɔ asase so awia ne anadwo adaduanan. Mɛpepa abɔde biara a nkwa wɔ mu a mabɔ afi asase so.”
english: Seven days from now I will send rain on the earth for forty days and forty nights, and I will wipe from the face of the earth every living creature I have made.”

twi: Noa dii nsɛm a Awurade ka kyerɛɛ no no nyinaa so.
english: And Noah did all that the Lord commanded him.

twi: Bere a nsuyiri baa asase so no, na Noa adi mfe ahansia.
english: Noah was six hundred years old when the floodwaters came on the earth.

twi: Noa ne ne mmabarima ne ne yere ne ne nsenom mmea kɔhyɛɛ adaka no mu sɛnea ɛbɛyɛ a nsuyiri no renka wɔn.
english: And Noah and his sons and his wife and his sons’ wives entered the ark to escape the waters of the flood.

twi: Mmoa a wɔn ho tew ne wɔn a wɔn ho ntew, nnomaa ne mmoa a wɔwea fam,
english: Pairs of clean and unclean animals, of birds and of all creatures that move along the ground,

twi: abien abien a wɔyɛ anini ne abere kɔkaa Noa ho wɔ adaka no mu, sɛnea Onyankopɔn ka kyerɛɛ Noa sɛ ɔnyɛ no.
english: male and female, came to Noah and entered the ark, as God had commanded Noah.

twi: Na nnanson no akyi no, nsuyiri no fii ase.
english: And after the seven days the floodwaters came on the earth.

twi: Noa dii mfe ahansia no mu no, ɔsram a ɛto so abien no da a ɛto so dunson no, nsuti a ɛwɔ asase mu no nyinaa bobɔe, na ɔsoro mfɛnsere nso buebuei.
english: In the six hundredth year of Noah’s life, on the seventeenth day of the second month—on that day all the springs of the great deep burst forth, and the floodgates of the heavens were opened.

twi: Osu tɔɔ wɔ asase so awia ne anadwo adaduanan.
english: And rain fell on the earth forty days and forty nights.

twi: Saa da no ara, Noa ne ne mmabarima Sem, Ham ne Yafet ne ne yere ne ne mmabarima baasa no yerenom kɔhyɛɛ adaka no mu.
english: On that very day Noah and his sons, Shem, Ham and Japheth, together with his wife and the wives of his three sons, entered the ark.

twi: Na wuram mmoa ahorow ne nyɛmmoa ahorow ne aboa biara a ɔnam asase so ne anomaa biara ne abɔde biara a ɛwɔ ntaban ka wɔn ho wɔ Adaka no mu.
english: They had with them every wild animal according to its kind, all livestock according to their kinds, every creature that moves along the ground according to its kind and every bird according to its kind, everything with wings.

twi: Abɔde biara a nkwa wɔ wɔn mu abien abien baa Noa nkyɛn bewuraa Adaka no mu.
english: Pairs of all creatures that have the breath of life in them came to Noah and entered the ark.

twi: Mmoa a wowuraa mu no nyinaa, na wɔyɛ anini ne abere, sɛnea Onyankopɔn ka kyerɛɛ Noa no. Afei, Awurade kaa Noa hyɛɛ adaka no mu, too no mu.
english: The animals going in were male and female of every living thing, as God had commanded Noah. Then the Lord shut him in.

twi: Nsuyiri no toaa so adaduanan wɔ asase so. Ɛmaa Adaka no so maa ɛtɛn nsu no ani.
english: For forty days the flood kept coming on the earth, and as the waters increased they lifted the ark high above the earth.

twi: Nsu no kɔɔ so yirii tɛnn wɔ asase so, maa Adaka no tɛn nsu no ani.
english: The waters rose and increased greatly on the earth, and the ark floated on the surface of the water.

twi: Nsu no yirii tɛnn wɔ asase so ara kosii sɛ ɛkataa mmepɔw atenten akɛse a ɛwɔ asase so nyinaa so.
english: They rose greatly on the earth, and all the high mountains under the entire heavens were covered.

twi: Nsu no yirii ara kosii sɛ ɛkataa mmepɔw no so boroo so anammɔn aduonu.
english: The waters rose and covered the mountains to a depth of more than fifteen cubits.

twi: Abɔde biara a nkwa wɔ mu a ɛnam asase so te sɛ nnomaa, wuram mmoa a wɔwea asase so ne adesamma ase hyewee.
english: Every living thing that moved on land perished—birds, livestock, wild animals, all the creatures that swarm over the earth, and all mankind.

twi: Biribiara a ɛte asase ani no nso ase hyewee.
english: Everything on dry land that had the breath of life in its nostrils died.

twi: Wɔpepaa biribiara a nkwa wɔ mu a ɛte asase so no. Nnipa ne mmoa ne abɔde a wɔnam asase so ne wim nnomaa nyinaa nso wɔpepaa wɔn fii asase so. Ɛkaa Noa ne wɔn a na wɔka ne ho wɔ adaka no mu no nko ara.
english: Every living thing on the face of the earth was wiped out; people and animals and the creatures that move along the ground and the birds were wiped from the earth. Only Noah was left, and those with him in the ark.

twi: Nsuyiri no toaa so wɔ asase so nnafua ɔha aduonum.
english: The waters flooded the earth for a hundred and fifty days.

twi: Nanso Onyankopɔn kaee Noa ne wuram mmoa a na wɔne no wɔ Adaka no mu no, na ɔmaa mframa bɔ faa asase so, na nsu no twee.
english: But God remembered Noah and all the wild animals and the livestock that were with him in the ark, and he sent a wind over the earth, and the waters receded.

twi: Asuti a ɛwowɔ asase ase no mu nsu a ɛbobɔe no gyaee ba, na ɔsoro mfɛnsere no nso mu toto maa osu no gyaee tɔ.
english: Now the springs of the deep and the floodgates of the heavens had been closed, and the rain had stopped falling from the sky.

twi: Nsu no toaa so twe fii asase so. Nnafua ɔha ne aduonum akyi no, na nsu no atwe koraa.
english: The water receded steadily from the earth. At the end of the hundred and fifty days the water had gone down,

twi: Ɔsram a ɛto so ason no da a ɛto so dunson so, Adaka no kɔtaa Ararat mmepɔw so.
english: and on the seventeenth day of the seventh month the ark came to rest on the mountains of Ararat.

twi: Nsu no toaa so, twee ara kosii ɔsram a ɛto so du no so. Na ɔsram no da a edi kan no, mmepɔw no atifi daa adi.
english: The waters continued to recede until the tenth month, and on the first day of the tenth month the tops of the mountains became visible.

twi: Adaduanan akyi no, Noa buee mfɛnsere a otwa too Adaka no ho no,
english: After forty days Noah opened a window he had made in the ark

twi: na ɔsomaa kwaakwaadabi ma odii akɔneaba kosii sɛ nsu no nyinaa yow fii asase no so.
english: and sent out a raven, and it kept flying back and forth until the water had dried up from the earth.

twi: Afei, ɔsomaa aborɔnoma sɛ ɔnkɔhwɛ sɛ asase no so awo ana.
english: Then he sent out a dove to see if the water had receded from the surface of the ground.

twi: Nanso aborɔnoma no annya baabi ansi, efisɛ na nsu no akata asase no so nyinaa. Enti ɔsan baa Noa nkyɛn ma Noa teɛɛ ne nsa soo ne mu de no baa Adaka no mu.
english: But the dove could find nowhere to perch because there was water over all the surface of the earth; so it returned to Noah in the ark. He reached out his hand and took the dove and brought it back to himself in the ark.

twi: Noa twɛn nnanson, na ɛno akyi no, ɔsan somaa aborɔnoma no bio.
english: He waited seven more days and again sent out the dove from the ark.

twi: Bere a aborɔnoma no san baa ne nkyɛn anwummere no, na ngodua ahabammono a watew tua nʼano. Ɛno na ɛmaa Noa huu sɛ nsu no atwe afi asase no so.
english: When the dove returned to him in the evening, there in its beak was a freshly plucked olive leaf! Then Noah knew that the water had receded from the earth.

twi: Noa twɛn nnanson bio, na ɔsan somaa aborɔnoma no, nanso wansan amma ne nkyɛn bio.
english: He waited seven more days and sent the dove out again, but this time it did not return to him.

twi: Na ɛbaa sɛ Noa dii mfe ahansia ne baako, ɔsram a edi kan no mu da a edi kan no, na nsu no atwe afi asase no so. Enti Noa yii Adaka no suhyɛ no, na ohuu sɛ asase so awo.
english: By the first day of the first month of Noah’s six hundred and first year, the water had dried up from the earth. Noah then removed the covering from the ark and saw that the surface of the ground was dry.

twi: Ɔsram a ɛto so abien no da a ɛto so aduonu ason so no na asase no so woo koraa.
english: By the twenty-seventh day of the second month the earth was completely dry.

twi: Onyankopɔn ka kyerɛɛ Noa se,
english: Then God said to Noah,

twi: “Wo ne wo yere ne wo mmabarima ne wɔn yerenom mfi Adaka no mu mpue.
english: “Come out of the ark, you and your wife and your sons and their wives.

twi: Yi abɔde biara a nkwa wɔ mu a wɔwɔ wo nkyɛn, a ɛyɛ nnomaa, mmoa ne mmoa a wɔnam asase so nyinaa fi Adaka no mu sɛnea ɛbɛyɛ a, wɔn ase bɛdɔ wɔ asase so.”
english: Bring out every kind of living creature that is with you—the birds, the animals, and all the creatures that move along the ground—so they can multiply on the earth and be fruitful and increase in number on it.”

twi: Enti Noa ne ne mmabarima ne ne yere ne ne mmabarima yerenom fii Adaka no mu.
english: So Noah came out, together with his sons and his wife and his sons’ wives.

twi: Mmoa no nyinaa ne abɔde a wɔnam asase so nyinaa ne nnomaa nyinaa ne biribiara a ɛnam asase so nyinaa fii Adaka no mu saa ara mmaako mmaako.
english: All the animals and all the creatures that move along the ground and all the birds—everything that moves on land—came out of the ark, one kind after another.

twi: Onyankopɔn Bɔ A Ɔhyɛɛ NoaNa Noa sii afɔremuka maa Awurade. Ɔfaa mmoa ne nnomaa a wɔn ho tew, de bɔɔ ɔhyew afɔre wɔ afɔremuka no so.
english: Then Noah built an altar to the Lord and, taking some of all the clean animals and clean birds, he sacrificed burnt offerings on it.

twi: Awurade tee afɔre a Noa bɔe no huam no, ɔkaa wɔ ne koma mu se, “Ɛwɔ mu sɛ bɔne ahyɛ onipa koma ma fi ne mmofraase de, nanso merenni onipa akyi nnome asase bio. Na merensɛe abɔde a nkwa wɔ mu bio sɛnea mayɛ yi.
english: The Lord smelled the pleasing aroma and said in his heart: “Never again will I curse the ground because of humans, even though every inclination of the human heart is evil from childhood. And never again will I destroy all living creatures, as I have done.

twi: “Mmere dodow a asase da so wɔ hɔ yi,ogu ne otwa,awɔw ne ahuhuru,asusow ne ɔpɛ,awia ne anadwoto rentwa da.”
english:
“As long as the earth endures,
seedtime and harvest,
cold and heat,
summer and winter,
day and night
will never cease.”

twi: Apam A Onyankopɔn Ne Noa YɛeAfei, Onyankopɔn hyiraa Noa ne ne mmabarima no ka kyerɛɛ wɔn se, “Monwo, na monyɛ bebree nhyɛ asase so ma.
english: Then God blessed Noah and his sons, saying to them, “Be fruitful and increase in number and fill the earth.

twi: Mo ho hu ne mo ho suro bɛtɔ mmoa a wɔwɔ asase so nyinaa ne wim nnomaa nyinaa ne abɔde a wɔwɔ asase so ne nsu mu mpataa nyinaa so. Wɔn nyinaa hyɛ mo nsa.
english: The fear and dread of you will fall on all the beasts of the earth, and on all the birds in the sky, on every creature that moves along the ground, and on all the fish in the sea; they are given into your hands.

twi: Biribiara a nkwa wɔ mu, na ɛkeka ne ho no bɛyɛ mo aduan. Sɛnea mede nhabammono hyɛɛ mo nsa no, afei de, mede biribiara ma mo.
english: Everything that lives and moves about will be food for you. Just as I gave you the green plants, I now give you everything.

twi: “Nanso ɛnsɛ sɛ mowe aboa a wontwaa ne mene mmaa ne mogya no ngui no nam.
english: “But you must not eat meat that has its lifeblood still in it.

twi: Na wo nkwa de, nea ɛbɛyɛ biara, mebisa ho akontaabu. Onipa a okum ne yɔnko nipa no, mebisa no ho asɛm. Mpo, aboa biara a obekum onipa no, mewɔ saa aboa no nso asɛmmisa. Mebisa onipa kra ho asɛm.
english: And for your lifeblood I will surely demand an accounting. I will demand an accounting from every animal. And from each human being, too, I will demand an accounting for the life of another human being.

twi: “Obiara a ohwie onipa mogya gu no,onipa so na wɔnam behwie ɔno nso mogya agu,efisɛ Onyankopɔn no ara sɛso na ɔbɔɔ onipa.
english:
“Whoever sheds human blood,
    by humans shall their blood be shed;
for in the image of God
    has God made mankind.

twi: Mo de, monwo, na monyɛ bebree. Mo ase mfɛe wɔ asase so, na monnɔɔso.”
english: As for you, be fruitful and increase in number; multiply on the earth and increase upon it.”

twi: Afei, Onyankopɔn ka kyerɛɛ Noa ne ne mmabarima a wɔka ne ho no se,
english: Then God said to Noah and to his sons with him:

twi: “Nnɛ, me ne mo ne mo asefo a wɔbɛwo wɔn no
english: “I now establish my covenant with you and with your descendants after you

twi: ne abɔde biara a nkwa wɔ mu a na wɔwɔ mo nkyɛn wɔ Adaka no mu yɛ apam: nnomaa, nyɛmmoa ne wuram mmoa a wɔne mo fi Adaka no mu bae no nyinaa, ne abɔde biara a nkwa wɔ mu a wɔwɔ asase so.
english: and with every living creature that was with you—the birds, the livestock and all the wild animals, all those that came out of the ark with you—every living creature on earth.

twi: Me ne mo yɛ mʼapam sɛ: Meremfa nsuyiri nsɛe abɔde biara a nkwa wɔ mu a ɛwɔ asase so. Saa ara nso na meremfa nsuyiri nsɛe asase bio da.”
english: I establish my covenant with you: Never again will all life be destroyed by the waters of a flood; never again will there be a flood to destroy the earth.”

twi: Na Onyankopɔn kae se, “Eyi ne apam a me, Onyankopɔn, ne mo ne abɔde a nkwa wɔ mu biara a wɔka mo ho no ne nkyirimma nyinaa reyɛ no ho nsɛnkyerɛnne.
english: And God said, “This is the sign of the covenant I am making between me and you and every living creature with you, a covenant for all generations to come:

twi: Mato me nyankontɔn wɔ omununkum mu. Ɛno na ɛbɛyɛ apam a ɛbɛda me ne asase ntam.
english: I have set my rainbow in the clouds, and it will be the sign of the covenant between me and the earth.

twi: Bere biara a mede omununkum bɛba asase ani, na sɛ nyankontɔn pue wɔ omununkum no mu a,
english: Whenever I bring clouds over the earth and the rainbow appears in the clouds,

twi: mɛkae mʼapam a ɛda me ne mo ne abɔde a nkwa wɔ mu ahorow no nyinaa ntam. Nsuyiri a ɛbɛsɛe abɔde a nkwa wɔ mu no nyinaa remma da biara da bio.
english: I will remember my covenant between me and you and all living creatures of every kind. Never again will the waters become a flood to destroy all life.

twi: Bere biara a nyankontɔn bɛto wɔ omununkum mu no, mehu na makae apam a ɛwɔ hɔ daa a ɛda me, Onyankopɔn, ne abɔde a nkwa wɔ mu ahorow nyinaa a wɔwɔ asase yi so no ntam no.”
english: Whenever the rainbow appears in the clouds, I will see it and remember the everlasting covenant between God and all living creatures of every kind on the earth.”

twi: Enti Onyankopɔn ka kyerɛɛ Noa se, “Eyi ne apam a me ne abɔde biara a nkwa wɔ mu a wɔwɔ asase yi so ayɛ no ho nsɛnkyerɛnne.”
english: So God said to Noah, “This is the sign of the covenant I have established between me and all life on the earth.”

twi: Noa MmabarimaEyinom ne Noa mmabarima a wofi Adaka no mu bae: Sem, Ham ne Yafet. Ham na ɔwoo Kanaan.
english: The sons of Noah who came out of the ark were Shem, Ham and Japheth. (Ham was the father of Canaan.)

twi: Eyinom ne Noa mmabarima. Wɔn mu na nnipa a wɔahwete wɔ asase so nyinaa fi bae.
english: These were the three sons of Noah, and from them came the people who were scattered over the whole earth.

twi: Noa yɛ okuafo a odii kan. Ɔyɛɛ bobeturo.
english: Noah, a man of the soil, proceeded to plant a vineyard.

twi: Da bi, ɔnom bobesa no bi bow ma ɔdaa ne ntamadan mu adagyaw.
english: When he drank some of its wine, he became drunk and lay uncovered inside his tent.

twi: Ham a ɔwoo Kanaan no kɔtoo nʼagya Noa sɛ ɔda adagyaw. Ofii hɔ no, ɔkɔbɔɔ ne nuabarimanom baanu no amanneɛ.
english: Ham, the father of Canaan, saw his father naked and told his two brothers outside.

twi: Enti Sem ne Yafet faa atade de guu wɔn mmati so, kɔɔ nkyirinkyiri de kɔkataa wɔn agya adagyaw so. Na wɔn ani nkyerɛ wɔn agya nti, wɔanhu nʼadagyaw mu.
english: But Shem and Japheth took a garment and laid it across their shoulders; then they walked in backward and covered their father’s naked body. Their faces were turned the other way so that they would not see their father naked.

twi: Bere a Noa ani so tetew no, na ohuu sɛnea ne kaakyiri no ayɛ no,
english: When Noah awoke from his wine and found out what his youngest son had done to him,

twi: ɔkae se,“Nnome nka Ham asefo a wɔyɛ Kanaanfo.Wɔbɛyɛ wɔn nuanommu nkoa mu nkoa.”
english:
he said,
“Cursed be Canaan!
    The lowest of slaves
    will he be to his brothers.”

twi: Noa kaa bio se,“Me nhyira a efi Awurade, me Nyankopɔn, nkyɛn no nka Sem!Kanaan nyɛ Sem akoa.
english:
He also said,
“Praise be to the Lord, the God of Shem!
    May Canaan be the slave of Shem.

twi: Onyankopɔn ntrɛw Yafet ase ne nʼasase mu.Yafet ntena Sem ntamadan mu,na Kanaan nyɛ nʼakoa.”
Nsuyiri no akyi no, Noa tenaa ase mfe ahaasa ne aduonum.
english: After the flood Noah lived 350 years.

twi: Noa dii mfe ahankron ne aduonum, ansa na ɔrewu.
english: Noah lived a total of 950 years, and then he died.

twi: Noa Awo NtoatoasoEyinom ne Noa mmabarima: Wɔne Sem, Ham ne Yafet asefo. Wɔwowoo mmabarima nsuyiri no akyi.
english: This is the account of Shem, Ham and Japheth, Noah’s sons, who themselves had sons after the flood.

twi: Yafet AsefoYafet asefo ni:Gomer, Magog, Media, Yawan, Tubal, Mesek ne Tiras.
english:
The sons of Japheth:
Gomer, Magog, Madai, Javan, Tubal, Meshek and Tiras.

twi: Gomer asefo ni:Askenas, Rifat ne Togarma.
english:
The sons of Gomer:
Ashkenaz, Riphath and Togarmah.

twi: Yawan asefo ni:Elisa, Tarsis, Kitim ne Rodanim.
english:
The sons of Javan:
Elishah, Tarshish, the Kittites and the Rodanites.

twi: Na wɔn asefo bɛyɛɛ po so adwumayɛfo wɔ nsase ahorow so a na abusuakuw biara ka ne kasa nko.
english: (From these the maritime peoples spread out into their territories by their clans within their nations, each with its own language.)

twi: Ham AsefoHam asefo ni:Kus, Misraim, Put ne Kanaan.
english:
The sons of Ham:
Cush, Egypt, Put and Canaan.

twi: Kus asefo ni:Seba, Hawila, Sabta, Raama ne Sabteka.Na Raama asefo nso ne:Saba ne Dedan.
english:
The sons of Cush:
Seba, Havilah, Sabtah, Raamah and Sabteka.
The sons of Raamah:
Sheba and Dedan.

twi: Kus woo Nimrod. Na Nimrod bɛyɛɛ ɔkofo kɛse wɔ asase so.
english: Cush was the father of Nimrod, who became a mighty warrior on the earth.

twi: Na ɔyɛ ɔbɔmmɔfo kɛse a Awurade ahyira no, na wɔbɔ ne din ka asɛm. Na obiara a ɔyɛ akokodurusɛm no, wɔde no toto Nimrod a na ɔyɛ ɔbɔmmɔfo kɛse a Awurade ahyira no no ho.
english: He was a mighty hunter before the Lord; that is why it is said, “Like Nimrod, a mighty hunter before the Lord.”

twi: Nʼahenni fii ase wɔ Babilonia, Erek, Akad ne Kalne a ne nyinaa wɔ Sinear asase so.
english: The first centers of his kingdom were Babylon, Uruk, Akkad and Kalneh, in Shinar.

twi: Ofii saa asase no so trɛw nʼahenni mu kɔɔ Asiria, kɔkyekyeree Ninewe. Rehobot-Ir, Kala ne
english: From that land he went to Assyria, where he built Nineveh, Rehoboth Ir, Calah

twi: Resen a ɛda Ninewe ne Kala ntam; ɛno na ɛyɛ kurow kɛse wɔ saa ahemman no mu.
english: and Resen, which is between Nineveh and Calah—which is the great city.

twi: Na Misraim wooLudfo, Anamfo, Lehabfo, Naftuhfo,
english:
Egypt was the father of
the Ludites, Anamites, Lehabites, Naphtuhites,

twi: Patrusfo, Kasluhfo ne Kaftorfo a wɔn ase na Filistifo fi.
english: Pathrusites, Kasluhites (from whom the Philistines came) and Caphtorites.

twi: Na Kanaan woo nʼabakanSidon ne Het.
english:
Canaan was the father of
Sidon his firstborn, and of the Hittites,

twi: Yebusifo, Amorifo, Girgasifo,
english: Jebusites, Amorites, Girgashites,

twi: Hewifo, Arkifo, Sinifo,
english: Hivites, Arkites, Sinites,

twi: Arwadfo, Semarifo ne Hematifo.Akyiri no, Kanaanfo mmusua no petee.
english:
Arvadites, Zemarites and Hamathites.
Later the Canaanite clans scattered

twi: Kanaan nsase ahye trɛw fii Sidon koduu Gerar de kosii Gasa koduu Sodom ne Gomora, Adma, Seboim de kosi Lasa.
english: and the borders of Canaan reached from Sidon toward Gerar as far as Gaza, and then toward Sodom, Gomorrah, Admah and Zeboyim, as far as Lasha.

twi: Eyinom ne Ham asefo a wɔn mmusuakuw, wɔn kasa, wɔn nsase ne wɔn aman da wɔn adi.
english: These are the sons of Ham by their clans and languages, in their territories and nations.

twi: Sem AsefoSem a na ne nua panyin ne Yafet no nso woo mmabarima. Sem nananom ne Eber mma.
english: Sons were also born to Shem, whose older brother was Japheth; Shem was the ancestor of all the sons of Eber.

twi: Sem asefo ni:Elam, Asur, Arfaksad, Lud ne Aram.
english:
The sons of Shem:
Elam, Ashur, Arphaxad, Lud and Aram.

twi: Aram asefo ni:Us, Hul, Geter ne Mas.
english:
The sons of Aram:
Uz, Hul, Gether and Meshek.

twi: Na Arfaksad woo Sela,na Sela woo Eber.
english:
Arphaxad was the father of Shelah,
and Shelah the father of Eber.

twi: Eber woo mmabarima baanu.Wɔtoo ɔbaako din Peleg a ase kyerɛ Nkyekyɛmu, efisɛ nʼawobere mu na kasa ahorow nti, nnipa a wɔwɔ asase so mu kyekyɛe ma wɔhwetee. Na wɔtoo ne nua a ɔka ne ho no din Yoktan.
english:
Two sons were born to Eber:
One was named Peleg, because in his time the earth was divided; his brother was named Joktan.

twi: Yoktan wooAlmodada, Selef, Hasarmawet, Yera,
english:
Joktan was the father of
Almodad, Sheleph, Hazarmaveth, Jerah,

twi: Hadoram, Usal, Dikla,
english: Hadoram, Uzal, Diklah,

twi: Obal, Abimael, Seba,
english: Obal, Abimael, Sheba,

twi: Ofir, Hawila ne Yobab.
english: Ophir, Havilah and Jobab. All these were sons of Joktan.
