english: In that day five cities in Egypt will speak the language of Canaan and swear allegiance to the Lord Almighty. One of them will be called the City of the Sun.

twi: Saa da no, wobesi afɔremuka wɔ Misraim mfimfini ama Awurade, na wɔasi nkaedum wɔ ne hye so nso ama Awurade.
english: In that day there will be an altar to the Lord in the heart of Egypt, and a monument to the Lord at its border.

twi: Ɛbɛyɛ nsɛnkyerɛnne ne adansede ama Asafo Awurade wɔ Misraim asase so. Sɛ wɔn nhyɛsofo nti wosu frɛ Awurade a, ɔbɛsoma ogyefo ne bammɔni, na obegye wɔn.
english: It will be a sign and witness to the Lord Almighty in the land of Egypt. When they cry out to the Lord because of their oppressors, he will send them a savior and defender, and he will rescue them.

twi: Enti Awurade bɛda ne ho adi akyerɛ Misraimfo, na saa da no wobehu Awurade. Wɔde afɔrebɔ ne nnuan bɛsom, wɔbɛhyɛ Awurade bɔ, na wɔadi so.
english: So the Lord will make himself known to the Egyptians, and in that day they will acknowledge the Lord. They will worship with sacrifices and grain offerings; they will make vows to the Lord and keep them.

twi: Awurade de ɔyaredɔm bɛbɔ Misraim; ɔde bɛbɔ wɔn na wasa wɔn yare. Wɔbɛdan akɔ Awurade nkyɛn, na obetie wɔn sufrɛ, na wasa wɔn yare.
english: The Lord will strike Egypt with a plague; he will strike them and heal them. They will turn to the Lord, and he will respond to their pleas and heal them.

twi: Saa da no, ɔtempɔn befi Misraim ne Asiria. Asiriafo bɛkɔ Misraim na Misraimfo akɔ Asiria. Misraimfo ne Asiriafo bɛbɔ mu asom.
english: In that day there will be a highway from Egypt to Assyria. The Assyrians will go to Egypt and the Egyptians to Assyria. The Egyptians and Assyrians will worship together.

twi: Saa da no Israel bɛto Misraim ne Asiria so sɛ abiɛsa, a ayɛ nhyira wɔ asase so.
english: In that day Israel will be the third, along with Egypt and Assyria, a blessing on the earth.

twi: Na Asafo Awurade behyira wɔn, aka se, “Nhyira nka Misraim, me nkurɔfo, Asiria me nsa ano adwuma ne Israel mʼagyapade.”
english: The Lord Almighty will bless them, saying, “Blessed be Egypt my people, Assyria my handiwork, and Israel my inheritance.”

twi: Nkɔmhyɛ A Etia Misraim Ne KusAfe a Asiriahene Sargon somaa ne man no sahene kɔɔ Asdod kɔtow hyɛɛ no so na odii ne so nkonim no,
english: In the year that the supreme commander, sent by Sargon king of Assyria, came to Ashdod and attacked and captured it—

twi: saa bere no Awurade faa Yesaia, Amos babarima so kasae se, “Yi atweaatam no fi wo ho ne mpaboa no fi wo nan ase.” Ɔyɛɛ saa de adagyaw a nʼanan nso sisi fam dii akɔneaba.
english: at that time the Lord spoke through Isaiah son of Amoz. He said to him, “Take off the sackcloth from your body and the sandals from your feet.” And he did so, going around stripped and barefoot.

twi: Na Awurade kae se, “Sɛnea me somfo Yesaia de adagyaw anantew mfe abiɛsa a nʼanan nso sisi fam yi de, ayɛ ɔhaw nsɛnkyerɛnne a etia Misraim ne Kus no,
english: Then the Lord said, “Just as my servant Isaiah has gone stripped and barefoot for three years, as a sign and portent against Egypt and Cush,

twi: saa ara na Asiriahene bedi Misraim nneduafo ne Kus nnommum a wɔdeda adagyaw na wɔn nan sisi fam, mmabun ne mpanyin a wɔn to deda so no anim, de agu Misraim anim ase.
english: so the king of Assyria will lead away stripped and barefoot the Egyptian captives and Cushite exiles, young and old, with buttocks bared—to Egypt’s shame.

twi: Wɔn a wɔde wɔn ho too Kus so, na wɔde Misraim hoahoaa wɔn ho no besuro na wɔn ani awu.
english: Those who trusted in Cush and boasted in Egypt will be dismayed and put to shame.

twi: Saa da no nnipa a wɔtete mpoano ha bɛka se, ‘Monhwɛ asɛm a ato wɔn a yɛde yɛn ho too wɔn so no, wɔn a yeguan kɔɔ wɔn nkyɛn kɔpɛɛ mmoa sɛ wobegye yɛn afi Asiriahene nsam no! Yɛbɛyɛ dɛn na yɛaguan?’ ”
english: In that day the people who live on this coast will say, ‘See what has happened to those we relied on, those we fled to for help and deliverance from the king of Assyria! How then can we escape?’”

twi: Nkɔmhyɛ A Etia BabiloniaNkɔmhyɛ a ɛfa Nweatam a ɛda Po ho no ho:Te sɛ mfɛtɛ a ɛbɔ fa anafo fam asase so no,ɔtamfo bi fi nweatam so reba,ofi asase a ɛyɛ ahuabɔbrim so.
english:
A prophecy against the Desert by the Sea:
Like whirlwinds sweeping through the southland,
    an invader comes from the desert,
    from a land of terror.

twi: Wɔde adaeso a ɛyɛ nwonwa akyerɛ me:Ɔfatwafo di huammɔ, ɔfomfo fa asade.Elam tow hyɛ so! Media bɔ pampim!Mede apinisi a ɔde bae no nyinaa bɛba awiei.
english:
A dire vision has been shown to me:
    The traitor betrays, the looter takes loot.
Elam, attack! Media, lay siege!
    I will bring to an end all the groaning she caused.

twi: Eyi ama ɔyaw bi abɛhyɛ me mu,ɔyaw aka me, te sɛ ɔbea a awo aka no;nea metee no nti mintumi nnyina me nan so,nea mihu no ama me ho adwiriw me.
english:
At this my body is racked with pain,
    pangs seize me, like those of a woman in labor;
I am staggered by what I hear,
    I am bewildered by what I see.

twi: Me koma bɔ kitirikitiri,ehu ma me ho popo;na hann a mepɛɛ sɛ mihu noabɛyɛ aninyanne ama me.
english:
My heart falters,
    fear makes me tremble;
the twilight I longed for
    has become a horror to me.

twi: Wɔto pon,wɔde kuntu akɛtɛ sesɛw fam,wodidi, na wɔnom!Monsɔre, mo asraafo mpanyimfo,momfa ngo nsrasra mo akatabo ho!
english:
They set the tables,
    they spread the rugs,
    they eat, they drink!
Get up, you officers,
    oil the shields!

twi: Sɛɛ na Awurade ka kyerɛ me:“Fa ɔwɛmfo kogyina hɔna ɔnka nea ohu nkyerɛ wo.
english:
This is what the Lord says to me:
“Go, post a lookout
    and have him report what he sees.

twi: Sɛ ohu nteaseɛnamne apɔnkɔ akuwakuw,wɔn a wɔtete mfurum sone wɔn a wɔtete yoma so a,ɔnwɛn nʼaso,nwɛn no pa ara.”
english:
When he sees chariots
    with teams of horses,
riders on donkeys
    or riders on camels,
let him be alert,
    fully alert.”

twi: Na ɔwɛmfo no teɛɛ mu se,“Me wura, da biara migyina ɔwɛn aban no soAnadwo biara, migyina hɔ.
Hwɛ, ɔbarima bi a ɔte teaseɛnam mu na ɔreba yiɔne apɔnkɔ dɔm.Na ɔwɛmfo no kae se,‘Babilon ahwe ase, wahwe ase!Nʼanyame ne nʼahoni nyinaaabubu agu fam!’ ”
english:
Look, here comes a man in a chariot
    with a team of horses.
And he gives back the answer:
    ‘Babylon has fallen, has fallen!
All the images of its gods
    lie shattered on the ground!’”

twi: Ao, me nkurɔfo a, wɔadwerɛw mo wɔ awiporowbea asemeka nea mate kyerɛ monea efi Asafo Awurade,nea efi Israel Nyankopɔn hɔ.
english:
My people who are crushed on the threshing floor,
    I tell you what I have heard
from the Lord Almighty,
    from the God of Israel.

twi: Nkɔmhyɛ A Etia EdomAdehu a ɛfa Duma ho:Obi frɛ me fi Seir,“Ɔwɛmfo, bere bɛn na ade bɛkyɛ?Ɔwɛmfo, aka nnɔnhwerew ahe ansa na ade akye?”
english:
A prophecy against Dumah:
Someone calls to me from Seir,
    “Watchman, what is left of the night?
    Watchman, what is left of the night?”

twi: Ɔwɛmfo no bua se,“Ade rekye, nanso ade bɛsa.Sɛ wubebisa bio asan bra bebisa.”
english:
The watchman replies,
    “Morning is coming, but also the night.
If you would ask, then ask;
    and come back yet again.”

twi: Nkɔmhyɛ A Etia ArabiaAdehu a ɛfa Arabia ho:Mo Dedan akwantufo amosoɛ wɔ Arabia adɔtɔ ase,
english:
A prophecy against Arabia:
You caravans of Dedanites,
    who camp in the thickets of Arabia,

twi: Momfa nsu mmrɛ wɔn a osukɔm de wɔn;mo a motete Tema,mommrɛ aguanfo no aduan.
Woguan fi afoa a watwetadua a wɔakuntun mune ɔko a egyina mu ano.
english:
They flee from the sword,
    from the drawn sword,
from the bent bow
    and from the heat of battle.

twi: Sɛɛ na Awurade ka kyerɛ me, “Afe baako mu, sɛnea ɔsomfo a wayɛ nhyehyɛe bebubu nna no, Kedar kɛseyɛ to betwa.
english: This is what the Lord says to me: “Within one year, as a servant bound by contract would count it, all the splendor of Kedar will come to an end.

twi: Na agyantowfo a wɔbɛka ne Kedar akofo bɛyɛ kakraa bi.” Nea Awurade, Israel Nyankopɔn, aka ni.
english: The survivors of the archers, the warriors of Kedar, will be few.” The Lord, the God of Israel, has spoken.

twi: Nkɔmhyɛ A Ɛfa Yerusalem HoNkɔmhyɛ a etia Anisoadehu Bon no:Dɛn na ɛhaw mo mprempren,a mo nyinaa aforo kɔ adan atifi yi,
english:
A prophecy against the Valley of Vision:
What troubles you now,
    that you have all gone up on the roofs,

twi: kurow a basabasayɛ ahyɛ no ma,huuyɛ ne ahosɛpɛw kuropɔn?Ɛnyɛ afoa ano na wʼatɔfo hweree wɔn nkwa,na wɔanwuwu wɔ ɔko ano nso.
english:
you town so full of commotion,
    you city of tumult and revelry?
Your slain were not killed by the sword,
    nor did they die in battle.

twi: Mo akannifo nyinaa abɔ mu aguan;wɔamfa tadua ankyekye wɔn.Mo a wɔkyeree mo nyinaa wɔfaa mo nneduafomo a muguan wɔ bere a na atamfo no wɔ akyirikyiri.
english:
All your leaders have fled together;
    they have been captured without using the bow.
All you who were caught were taken prisoner together,
    having fled while the enemy was still far away.

twi: Enti mekae se, “Mumfi me sona mintwa adwo.Monnkyekye me werɛwɔ me nkurɔfo sɛe ho.”
english:
Therefore I said, “Turn away from me;
    let me weep bitterly.
Do not try to console me
    over the destruction of my people.”

twi: Awurade, Asafo Awurade wɔ da bima huuyɛ, ntiatiaso ne ehuwɔ Anisoadehu Bon no mu,da a wɔde bubu afasuna wɔde su kyerɛ mmepɔw.
english:
The Lord, the Lord Almighty, has a day
    of tumult and trampling and terror
    in the Valley of Vision,
a day of battering down walls
    and of crying out to the mountains.

twi: Elam fa bɛmma noka ne nteaseɛnamkafo ne apɔnkɔ ho;Kir ama kyɛm no so.
Nteaseɛnam ayɛ mo bon fɛfɛ no ma,na wɔde apɔnkɔsotefo agyinagyina kuropɔn apon no ano.
english:
Your choicest valleys are full of chariots,
    and horsemen are posted at the city gates.

twi: Wɔayi Yuda ho bammɔ no.Na da no wode wʼani tooakode a ɛwɔ Kwae mu Ahemfi no so;
english:
The Lord stripped away the defenses of Judah,
    and you looked in that day
    to the weapons in the Palace of the Forest.

twi: wuhuu sɛ Dawid Kuropɔn no,akwan bebree deda ne bammɔ muwoboaa nsu anowɔ Ase Abura mu.
english:
You saw that the walls of the City of David
    were broken through in many places;
you stored up water
    in the Lower Pool.

twi: Wokan adan a ɛwɔ Yerusalem nona wudwiriw afi de boaa ɔfasu no ahoɔden.
english:
You counted the buildings in Jerusalem
    and tore down houses to strengthen the wall.

twi: Woyɛɛ nsukorae wɔ afasu abien no ntammaa nsu a ɛwɔ Abura Dedaw mu no,nanso woanhwehwɛ Onipa ko a ɔyɛe,na woammu Onipa a ɔhyehyɛe dedaada no.
english:
You built a reservoir between the two walls
    for the water of the Old Pool,
but you did not look to the One who made it,
    or have regard for the One who planned it long ago.

twi: Awurade, Asafo Awurade,frɛɛ wo saa da nosɛ su na twa adwo,sɛ yi wo tinwi na fura atweaatam.
english:
The Lord, the Lord Almighty,
    called you on that day
to weep and to wail,
    to tear out your hair and put on sackcloth.

twi: Nanso hwɛ, anigye ne ahosɛpɛw wɔ hɔ;wokunkum anantwi ne nguan;wɔwe nam na wɔbow nsa!Wɔka se, “Momma yennidi na yɛnnom,efisɛ, ɔkyena yebewu!”
english:
But see, there is joy and revelry,
    slaughtering of cattle and killing of sheep,
    eating of meat and drinking of wine!
“Let us eat and drink,” you say,
    “for tomorrow we die!”

twi: Awurade, Asafo Awurade ayi me asotiw se, “Wɔremfa saa bɔne yi nkyɛ wo da kosi wo wuda,” sɛnea Awurade, Asafo Awurade se ni.
english: The Lord Almighty has revealed this in my hearing: “Till your dying day this sin will not be atoned for,” says the Lord, the Lord Almighty.

twi: Sɛɛ na Awurade, Asafo Awurade se,“Kɔ, kɔka kyerɛ saa ɔsomfo yi,Sebna a, ɔhwɛ ahemfi no so se,
english:
This is what the Lord, the Lord Almighty, says:
“Go, say to this steward,
    to Shebna the palace administrator:

twi: Dɛn na woreyɛ wɔ ha na hena na ɔmaa wo kwansɛ bɔ wo da wɔ ha,worebɔ wo da wɔ baabi a ɛkorɔnna woretwa wo homebea wɔ ɔbotan mu?
english:
What are you doing here and who gave you permission
    to cut out a grave for yourself here,
hewing your grave on the height
    and chiseling your resting place in the rock?

twi: “Hwɛ yiye, na Awurade rebeso wo mu denatow wo akyene, wo ɔhoɔdenfo.
english:
“Beware, the Lord is about to take firm hold of you
    and hurl you away, you mighty man.

twi: Ɔbɛbobɔw wo, ama woayɛ kurukuruwa,na watow wo akyene ɔman kɛse bi sohɔ na wubewuna wo teaseɛnam fɛfɛ no aka hɔ,wo a woyɛ ahohora ma wo wura fi!
english:
He will roll you up tightly like a ball
    and throw you into a large country.
There you will die
    and there the chariots you were so proud of
    will become a disgrace to your master’s house.

twi: Megye wʼadwuma afi wo nsa muna wɔayi wo afi wo dibea so.
english:
I will depose you from your office,
    and you will be ousted from your position.

twi: “Saa da no, mɛfrɛ me somfo Eliakim a ɔyɛ Hilkia babarima.
english: “In that day I will summon my servant, Eliakim son of Hilkiah.

twi: Mede wʼatade yuu bɛhyɛ no na mede wʼabɔso abebare nʼasen mu na mede wo tumi ahyɛ ne nsa. Ɔbɛyɛ agya ama wɔn a wɔtete Yerusalem ne Yuda fi.
english: I will clothe him with your robe and fasten your sash around him and hand your authority over to him. He will be a father to those who live in Jerusalem and to the people of Judah.

twi: Mede Dawid fi safe bɛma no; nea obebue no obiara rentumi nto mu; na nea ɔbɛto mu nso a obiara rentumi mmue.
english: I will place on his shoulder the key to the house of David; what he opens no one can shut, and what he shuts no one can open.

twi: Mɛbɔ ne so sɛ pɛe ama watim, ɔbɛyɛ anuonyam agua ama nʼagya fi.
english: I will drive him like a peg into a firm place; he will become a seat of honor for the house of his father.

twi: Nʼabusua anuonyam nyinaa begyina ne so: nʼasefo ne ne nenanom, ne nkuku ne nkaka, fi nsanka, mprɛte so kosi nhina nyinaa so.
english: All the glory of his family will hang on him: its offspring and offshoots—all its lesser vessels, from the bowls to all the jars.

twi: “Saa da no,” sɛnea Asafo Awurade se ni, “pɛe a wɔabɔ so ama atim no, betu ahwe fam na nʼadesoa no nso asɛe, Awurade, akasa!”
english: “In that day,” declares the Lord Almighty, “the peg driven into the firm place will give way; it will be sheared off and will fall, and the load hanging on it will be cut down.” The Lord has spoken.

twi: Nkɔmhyɛ A Ɛfa Tiro HoNkɔmhyɛ a ɛfa Tiro ho:Tarsis ahyɛn, muntwa adwo!Efisɛ wɔasɛe Tirona wɔannyaw no ofi anaa hyɛngyinabea.Wufi Kipro asase soabɛka asɛm akyerɛ wɔn.
english:
A prophecy against Tyre:
Wail, you ships of Tarshish!
    For Tyre is destroyed
    and left without house or harbor.
From the land of Cyprus
    word has come to them.

twi: Monyɛ komm, mo nnipa a mowɔ supɔw no sone mo Sidon aguadifo apo so adwumayɛfo ama mo ayɛ adefo.
english:
Be silent, you people of the island
    and you merchants of Sidon,
    whom the seafarers have enriched.

twi: Nsu akɛse no sona aduan fi Sihor nam bae;Nil ho nnɔbae na ɛyɛɛ Tiro foto,na ɔbɛyɛɛ amanaman aguadibea.
english:
On the great waters
    came the grain of the Shihor;
the harvest of the Nile was the revenue of Tyre,
    and she became the marketplace of the nations.

twi: Animguase nka wo, Sidon, ne wo, po so abandennen,efisɛ po akasa se,“Menkyemee da, na menwoo da;mentetew mmabarima anaa mmabea da.”
Sɛ asɛm no du Misraim a,wobedi yaw wɔ nkra a efi Tiro no ho.
english:
When word comes to Egypt,
    they will be in anguish at the report from Tyre.

twi: Muntwa nkɔ Tarsis;muntwa adwo, mo a mowɔ supɔw no so.
english:
Cross over to Tarshish;
    wail, you people of the island.

twi: Eyi ne mo ahosɛpɛw kuropɔn no,teteete kuropɔn no,nea wɔatu akɔtenaakyirikyiri nsase so no ana?
english:
Is this your city of revelry,
    the old, old city,
whose feet have taken her
    to settle in far-off lands?

twi: Hena na ɔbɔɔ atirimpɔw yi de tiaa Tiro,nea ɔkyekyɛ ahenkyɛw,nea nʼaguadifo yɛ ahenemma,na nʼadetɔnfo agye din wɔ asase so?
english:
Who planned this against Tyre,
    the bestower of crowns,
whose merchants are princes,
    whose traders are renowned in the earth?

twi: Asafo Awurade na ɔbɔɔ ne tirimpɔw se,ɔbɛbrɛ anuonyam mu ahomaso asena wabrɛ wɔn a wɔagye din wɔ asase yi so nyinaa ase.
english:
The Lord Almighty planned it,
    to bring down her pride in all her splendor
    and to humble all who are renowned on the earth.

twi: Yɛ wʼasase so adwuma te sɛnea wɔyɛ wɔ Nil ho noTarsis Babea,efisɛ wunni hyɛngyinabea bio.
english:
Till your land as they do along the Nile,
    Daughter Tarshish,
    for you no longer have a harbor.

twi: Awurade ama ne nsa so wɔ po no soama ahenni ahorow a ɛwɔ hɔ no repopo.Wahyɛ Kanaan ho mmara se,wɔnsɛe nʼaban.
english:
The Lord has stretched out his hand over the sea
    and made its kingdoms tremble.
He has given an order concerning Phoenicia
    that her fortresses be destroyed.

twi: Ɔkae se, “Wʼahurisidi no nso ha ara,Sidon Babea Ɔbabun a wɔadwerɛw wo!“Sɔre, twa kɔ Kipro;hɔ mpo worennya ahotɔ.”
english:
He said, “No more of your reveling,
    Virgin Daughter Sidon, now crushed!
“Up, cross over to Cyprus;
    even there you will find no rest.”

twi: Monhwɛ Babiloniafo asase nosaa nnipa a mprempren wɔnka hwee no!Asiriafo ayɛ nobaabi a nweatam so mmoa te;wosisii wɔn anotua aban bebree,wodwiriw nʼaban guima ɛdan nnwiriwii.
english:
Look at the land of the Babylonians,
    this people that is now of no account!
The Assyrians have made it
    a place for desert creatures;
they raised up their siege towers,
    they stripped its fortresses bare
    and turned it into a ruin.

twi: Muntwa adwo, Tarsis ahyɛn;wɔasɛe wʼaban!
english:
Wail, you ships of Tarshish;
    your fortress is destroyed!

twi: Saa bere no wɔrenkae Tiro mfe aduɔson a ɛyɛ ɔhene nkwanna. Nanso mfe aduɔson akyi no, nea ɛbɛto Tiro no bɛyɛ sɛnea ɛwɔ oguamanfo no dwom mu no:
english: At that time Tyre will be forgotten for seventy years, the span of a king’s life. But at the end of these seventy years, it will happen to Tyre as in the song of the prostitute:

twi: “Ma sankuten no so, pase fa kuropɔn no mu,oguamanfo a wɔnnkae wo;bɔ sankuten no yiye, to nnwom bebree,sɛnea wɔbɛkae wo.”
english:
“Take up a harp, walk through the city,
    you forgotten prostitute;
play the harp well, sing many a song,
    so that you will be remembered.”

twi: Mfe aduɔson akyi, Awurade ne Tiro bedi. Ɔbɛsan akodi ne paa sɛ oguamanfo na ɔne ahenni a ɛwɔ asase so nyinaa adi gua.
english: At the end of seventy years, the Lord will deal with Tyre. She will return to her lucrative prostitution and will ply her trade with all the kingdoms on the face of the earth.

twi: Nanso nea obenya ne ne mfaso nyinaa wɔde bɛto hɔ ama Awurade; wɔremmoaboa ano na wɔremfa nsie. Ne mfaso no bɛkɔ wɔn a wɔsom wɔ Awurade anim no nkyɛn, na wɔanya aduan bebree ne ntade pa.
english: Yet her profit and her earnings will be set apart for the Lord; they will not be stored up or hoarded. Her profits will go to those who live before the Lord, for abundant food and fine clothes.

twi: Asase Sɛe A Efi AwuradeHwɛ, Awurade rebɛma asase ada mpanna wasɛe no;ɔbɛsɛe asase anina wabɔ sotefo ahwete,
english:
See, the Lord is going to lay waste the earth
    and devastate it;
he will ruin its face
    and scatter its inhabitants—

twi: ɛbɛyɛ saa araama ɔsɔfo sɛnea ɛbɛyɛ ama nnipa,ama owura sɛnea ɛbɛyɛ ama asomfo,ama awuraa sɛnea ɛbɛyɛ ama afenaa,ama nea ɔtɔn sɛnea ɛbɛyɛ ama nea ɔtɔ,ama nea ogye bosea sɛnea ɛbɛyɛ ama nea ɔma bosea,ama ɔkafo sɛnea ɛbɛyɛ ama nea ɔde ma.
Asase bɛda mpan koraa,na wɔafom so nneɛma.Awurade, na waka saa asɛm yi.
english:
The earth will be completely laid waste
    and totally plundered.
The Lord has spoken this word.

twi: Asase so yɛ wosee, na ekisawiase kɔ ahoyeraw mu, na ekisa,nea wɔama no so wɔ asase so ho yeraw no.
english:
The earth dries up and withers,
    the world languishes and withers,
    the heavens languish with the earth.

twi: Asase so nnipa agu ne ho fi;wɔanni mmara no so,wɔabu ahyɛde no sona wɔasɛe apam a ɛwɔ hɔ daa no.
english:
The earth is defiled by its people;
    they have disobeyed the laws,
violated the statutes
    and broken the everlasting covenant.

twi: Enti nnome amene asase noɛsɛ sɛ so nnipa nya wɔn afɔdi so akatuane saa nti wɔahyew asase no so nnipa,na kakraa bi pɛ na wɔaka.
english:
Therefore a curse consumes the earth;
    its people must bear their guilt.
Therefore earth’s inhabitants are burned up,
    and very few are left.

twi: Nsa foforo no ho yow na bobe no guan;wɔn a wogye wɔn ani no si apini.
english:
The new wine dries up and the vine withers;
    all the merrymakers groan.

twi: Akasaebɔ mu anigye no agyae,ahosɛpɛwfo no nteɛteɛmu no agyae.Sankuten so nnwom dɛdɛ no ayɛ dinn.
english:
The joyful timbrels are stilled,
    the noise of the revelers has stopped,
    the joyful harp is silent.

twi: Wɔnnto dwom mfa nnom nsa bio;mmorɔsa ayɛ nwen ama anomfo.
english:
No longer do they drink wine with a song;
    the beer is bitter to its drinkers.

twi: Kuropɔn a wɔasɛe no ada mpan;wɔatoto ofi biara apon mu.
english:
The ruined city lies desolate;
    the entrance to every house is barred.

twi: Wɔpere nsa wɔ mmɔnten so;ahosɛpɛw nyinaa adan bosooyɛ,anigye nyinaa atu ayera wɔ asase no so.
Kuropɔn no asɛe,wɔabubu nʼapon mu nketenkete.
english:
The city is left in ruins,
    its gate is battered to pieces.

twi: Saa ara na ɛbɛyɛ wɔ asase no sone amanaman no mu,sɛnea wɔboro ngodua a ɛyɛ no,anaa sɛnea wogyaw mpɛpɛ wɔ bobe twabere akyi no.
english:
So will it be on the earth
    and among the nations,
as when an olive tree is beaten,
    or as when gleanings are left after the grape harvest.

twi: Wɔma wɔn nne so, wɔde anigye teɛteɛ mu;efi atɔe fam, wɔkamfo Awurade kɛseyɛ.
english:
They raise their voices, they shout for joy;
    from the west they acclaim the Lord’s majesty.

twi: Enti apuei fam, monhyɛ Awurade anuonyam;momma Awurade din so, Israel Nyankopɔn no,wɔ supɔw a ɛwɔ po so no so.
Yɛte nnwonto fi asase ano yɛte se,“Anuonyam nka Ɔtreneeni no.”Nanso mekae se, “Matɔ beraw, mapa abaw!Minnue!Ɔfatwafo di huammɔ!Ɔnam nnaadaa so di huammɔ.”
english:
From the ends of the earth we hear singing:
    “Glory to the Righteous One.”
But I said, “I waste away, I waste away!
    Woe to me!
The treacherous betray!
    With treachery the treacherous betray!”

twi: Ehu, amoa ne afiri retwɛn mo,nnipa a mote asase so.
english:
Terror and pit and snare await you,
    people of the earth.

twi: Nea ehu nti oguan nobɛtɔ amoa mu;nea ɔforo fi amoa mu noafiri beyi no.Wɔabue nsu apon wɔ ɔsoro,na asase nnyinaso wosow.
english:
Whoever flees at the sound of terror
    will fall into a pit;
whoever climbs out of the pit
    will be caught in a snare.
The floodgates of the heavens are opened,
    the foundations of the earth shake.

twi: Wɔadwiriw asase nona emu apaapae,na asase awosow ankasa.
english:
The earth is broken up,
    the earth is split asunder,
    the earth is violently shaken.

twi: Asase tɔ ntintan te sɛ ɔsabowfo.Ehinhim biribiri te sɛ ntamadan wɔ mframa ano;nʼatuatew ho afɔdi ayɛ adesoa ama nona ɛhwe ase a ɛrensɔre bio.
english:
The earth reels like a drunkard,
    it sways like a hut in the wind;
so heavy upon it is the guilt of its rebellion
    that it falls—never to rise again.

twi: Saa da no, Awurade bɛtweɔsoro atumfone ahemfo a wɔwɔ asase so aso.
english:
In that day the Lord will punish
    the powers in the heavens above
    and the kings on the earth below.

twi: Wɔbɛka wɔn nyinaa abɔ musɛ nneduafo ahyɛ afiase amoa mu;wɔbɛto wɔn mu wɔ afiasena nna bebree akyi no wɔatwe wɔn aso.
english:
They will be herded together
    like prisoners bound in a dungeon;
they will be shut up in prison
    and be punished after many days.

twi: Ɔsram anim begu ase na owia ani awu;na Asafo Awurade bedi henewɔ Sion bepɔw so ne Yerusalem,ne wɔn mpanyimfo anim, wɔ anuonyam mu.
english:
The moon will be dismayed,
    the sun ashamed;
for the Lord Almighty will reign
    on Mount Zion and in Jerusalem,
    and before its elders—with great glory.

twi: Ayeyi Nka AwuradeAwurade, wo ne me Nyankopɔn;mɛma wo so na mayi wo din ayɛ,efisɛ wufi nokwaredi mu,ayɛ anwonwade bebree,nneɛma a wɔahyehyɛ fi teteete.
english:
Lord, you are my God;
    I will exalt you and praise your name,
for in perfect faithfulness
    you have done wonderful things,
    things planned long ago.

twi: Woayɛ kuropɔn no nnwiriwii siw,kurow no a ɛwɔ bammɔ no asɛe;ananafo abandennen no nyɛ kuropɔn bio;na wɔrensi bio.
english:
You have made the city a heap of rubble,
    the fortified town a ruin,
the foreigners’ stronghold a city no more;
    it will never be rebuilt.

twi: Enti aman a wɔyɛ den bedi wo niatutuwpɛfo aman bɛhyɛ wo anuonyam.
english:
Therefore strong peoples will honor you;
    cities of ruthless nations will revere you.

twi: Woayɛ ahiafo guankɔbea,ohiani mmɔborɔni guankɔbea,ahum ano ahintaweeɔhyew mu nwinina atirimɔdenfo homete sɛ ahum a ɛrebɔ dwira ɔfasu
english:
You have been a refuge for the poor,
    a refuge for the needy in their distress,
a shelter from the storm
    and a shade from the heat.
For the breath of the ruthless
    is like a storm driving against a wall

twi: ne ɔhyew a ɛwɔ nweatam so.Wobrɛ ananafo huuyɛ ase;sɛnea omununkum brɛ owia hyew ano ase no,saa ara na atirimɔdenfo nnwom nso begyae.
english:
and like the heat of the desert.
You silence the uproar of foreigners;
    as heat is reduced by the shadow of a cloud,
    so the song of the ruthless is stilled.

twi: Asafo Awurade bɛto pon wɔ saa bepɔw yi soobesiesie nnuan pa ne nsa a adi nna;nam pa ne nsa pa ama nnipa nyinaa.
english:
On this mountain the Lord Almighty will prepare
    a feast of rich food for all peoples,
a banquet of aged wine—
    the best of meats and the finest of wines.

twi: Wɔ bepɔw yi so, ɔbɛsɛentama a ɛkata nnipa nyinaa hone nkataso a ɛkata aman nyinaa so no;
Ɔbɛmene owu afebɔɔ.Asafo Awurade bɛpepaani so nusu nyinaa.Obeyi ne nkurɔfo ahohora,afi nsase nyinaa so.Awurade, na waka.
english:
he will swallow up death forever.
The Sovereign Lord will wipe away the tears
    from all faces;
he will remove his people’s disgrace
    from all the earth.
The Lord has spoken.

twi: Saa da no, wɔbɛka se,“Ampa ara yɛn Nyankopɔn ni;yɛde yɛn ho too no so na ogyee yɛn;Awurade no ni, yegyee no dii;momma yenni ahurusi na yɛn ani nnye wɔ ne nkwagye no mu.”
Awurade nsa bɛda saa bepɔw yi so;nanso obetiatia Moab sote sɛ sare a wotiatia so de fra sumina.
Wɔbɛtrɛtrɛw wɔn nsa mu wɔ so,sɛnea asuguarefo trɛtrɛw wɔn nsa mu de guare.Onyankopɔn bɛbrɛ wɔn ahomaso asea ɔrenhwɛ wɔn nsa ano dwumadi ho.
english:
They will stretch out their hands in it,
    as swimmers stretch out their hands to swim.
God will bring down their pride
    despite the cleverness of their hands.

twi: Obebubu mo bammɔ afasu atenten no agu,obebubu agu famama ayɛ mfutuma.
english:
He will bring down your high fortified walls
    and lay them low;
he will bring them down to the ground,
    to the very dust.

twi: Ayeyi DwomSaa da no, wɔbɛto saa dwom yi wɔ Yuda asase so:Yɛwɔ kuropɔn dennen;Onyankopɔn de nkwagyeayɛ nʼafasu ne ne hankare a ɛkorɔn.
english:
In that day this song will be sung in the land of Judah:
We have a strong city;
    God makes salvation
    its walls and ramparts.

twi: Mummuebue apon nona atreneefo man no nhyɛn mu,ɔman nokwafo no.
english:
Open the gates
    that the righteous nation may enter,
    the nation that keeps faith.

twi: Wobɛkora no so asomdwoe munea wasi nʼadwene pi,efisɛ ɔde ne ho to wo so.
english:
You will keep in perfect peace
    those whose minds are steadfast,
    because they trust in you.

twi: Fa wo ho to Awurade so afebɔɔ,efisɛ, Awurade, Awurade yɛ daa Botan.
english:
Trust in the Lord forever,
    for the Lord, the Lord himself, is the Rock eternal.

twi: Ɔbrɛ wɔn a wɔtete soro ase,na ɔbrɛ kuropɔn a ɛkorɔn no ase;obubu gu fam pasaama ɛda mfutuma mu.
english:
He humbles those who dwell on high,
    he lays the lofty city low;
he levels it to the ground
    and casts it down to the dust.

twi: Anammɔn tiatia so,wɔn a wɔhyɛ wɔn so anammɔnahiafo anammɔntu.
english:
Feet trample it down—
    the feet of the oppressed,
    the footsteps of the poor.

twi: Ɔtreneeni kwan so yɛ tamaa;wo, Ɔnokwafo, woma ɔtreneeni kwan so yɛ trontrom.
english:
The path of the righteous is level;
    you, the Upright One, make the way of the righteous smooth.

twi: Yiw, Awurade, yɛnam wo mmara kwan so yi,yɛretwɛn wo;na wo din ne ne kɛseyɛyɛ nea yɛn koma pɛ.
english:
Yes, Lord, walking in the way of your laws,
    we wait for you;
your name and renown
    are the desire of our hearts.

twi: Me kra pere hwehwɛ wo anadwo;anɔpa nso me honhom ani gyina wo.Sɛ wʼatemmu ba asase yi so a,nnipa a wɔwɔ wiase sua treneeyɛ.
english:
My soul yearns for you in the night;
    in the morning my spirit longs for you.
When your judgments come upon the earth,
    the people of the world learn righteousness.

twi: Ɛwɔ mu sɛ wuyi adom adi kyerɛ amumɔyɛfo de,nanso wonsua treneeyɛ;na mpo atreneefo asase so no, wɔkɔ so yɛ bɔnena wommu Awurade kɛseyɛ.
english:
But when grace is shown to the wicked,
    they do not learn righteousness;
even in a land of uprightness they go on doing evil
    and do not regard the majesty of the Lord.

twi: Ao Awurade, wɔama wo nsa so kɔ soro,nanso wonhu.Ma wonhu wo mmɔdemmɔ wɔ wo nkurɔfo ho na ɛnhyɛ wɔn aniwu;ma ogya a wɔasɔ ama wʼatamfo no nhyew wɔn.
english:
Lord, your hand is lifted high,
    but they do not see it.
Let them see your zeal for your people and be put to shame;
    let the fire reserved for your enemies consume them.

twi: Awurade, woama yɛn asomdwoe;nea yɛatumi ayɛ nyinaa wo na woayɛ ama yɛn.
english:
Lord, you establish peace for us;
    all that we have accomplished you have done for us.

twi: Awurade yɛn Nyankopɔn, awuranom afoforo bi adi yɛn so,nanso wo din nko ara na yɛ kamfo.
english:
Lord our God, other lords besides you have ruled over us,
    but your name alone do we honor.

twi: Afei wɔawuwu, na wɔnte ase bio;ahonhom a wɔafi mu no wɔrensɔre.Wotwee wɔn aso na wosɛee wɔnwɔama yɛn werɛ afi wɔn.
Woama ɔman no ayɛ kɛse, Awurade;woama ɔman no ayɛ kɛse;woahyɛ wo ho anuonyam;woatrɛtrɛw asase no ahye nyinaa mu.
Awurade, wofi ahohia mu baa wo nkyɛn;bere a wotwee wɔn aso no,na wontumi mmue wɔn ano mpo mmɔ mpae.
Sɛnea ɔpemfo a awo aka nofi ɔyaw mu bukabukaw ne mu na osu no,saa ara na yɛyɛe wɔ wʼanim, Awurade.
english:
As a pregnant woman about to give birth
    writhes and cries out in her pain,
    so were we in your presence, Lord.

twi: Yenyinsɛnee, yɛkyemee wɔ ɔyaw munanso yɛwoo mframa.Yɛamfa nkwagye amma asase so;wɔanwo nnipa amma asase so.
english:
We were with child, we writhed in labor,
    but we gave birth to wind.
We have not brought salvation to the earth,
    and the people of the world have not come to life.

twi: Nanso wʼawufo benya nkwa;wɔn nipadua bɛsɔre.Ma wɔn a wɔtete mfutuma mu no,nsɔre mfa anigye nteɛ mu.Mo bosu te sɛ anɔpa bosu;asase beyi nʼafunu apue.
Monkɔ, me nkurɔfo, monhyɛnhyɛn mo adan muna montoto apon no mu;momfa mo ho nsie bere tiaa bikosi sɛ nʼabufuwhyew ano bedwo.
english:
Go, my people, enter your rooms
    and shut the doors behind you;
hide yourselves for a little while
    until his wrath has passed by.

twi: Hwɛ, Awurade refi nʼatenaeabɛtwe nnipa a wɔte asase so aso wɔ wɔn bɔne ho.Asase bɛda mogya a wɔahwie agu no so no adi;ɔrentumi mfa nʼatɔfo nsie bio.
english:
See, the Lord is coming out of his dwelling
    to punish the people of the earth for their sins.
The earth will disclose the blood shed on it;
    the earth will conceal its slain no longer.

twi: Israel OgyeSaa da no,Awurade de nʼafoa bɛtwe aso,ɔde nʼafoa a ɛyɛ hu na ɛso na ɛyɛ nnam no,ɔwɔ Lewiatan a ɔde ahoɔhare tu hoo,ɔwɔ Lewiatan a ɔbobɔw ne ho;obekum po mu aboa kɛse a ne ho yɛ hu no.
english:
In that day,
the Lord will punish with his sword—
    his fierce, great and powerful sword—
Leviathan the gliding serpent,
    Leviathan the coiling serpent;
he will slay the monster of the sea.

twi: Saa da no,“To dwom fa bobeturo a ɛsow no ho se:
english:
In that day—
“Sing about a fruitful vineyard:

twi: Me, Awurade, mehwɛ so;migugu so nsu bere biara.Mebɔ ho ban awia ne anadwosɛnea obiara rensɛe no.
english:
I, the Lord, watch over it;
    I water it continually.
I guard it day and night
    so that no one may harm it.

twi: Me bo mfuw ɛ.Sɛ ɛkaa nware ne nsɔe nko ara na ɛko tia me aanka me ne wɔn de bɛbɔ ani;na mahyew wɔn nyinaa.
english:
I am not angry.
If only there were briers and thorns confronting me!
    I would march against them in battle;
    I would set them all on fire.

twi: Sɛ ɛnte saa a, ma wɔmmra me nkyɛn mmehintaw;ne me mmɛdwene asomdwoe hoYiw, asomdwoe ho na mo ne me mmɛdwene.”
Nna a ɛreba no mu no, Yakob ase betim,Israel begu nhwiren na anyin fɛfɛɛfɛna ɔde ne nnuaba ahyɛ wiase nyinaa ma.
english:
In days to come Jacob will take root,
    Israel will bud and blossom
    and fill all the world with fruit.

twi: Awurade abɔ Israelsɛnea ɔbɔɔ wɔn a wɔbɔɔ Israel hwee fam no ana?Awurade akum Israelsɛnea okum wɔn a wokum Israel no ana?
english:
Has the Lord struck her
    as he struck down those who struck her?
Has she been killed
    as those were killed who killed her?

twi: Wode ɔko ne asutwa twe nʼaso,wode mframa a ano yɛ den pam note sɛ da a apuei mframa bɔ no.
english:
By warfare and exile you contend with her—
    with his fierce blast he drives her out,
    as on a day the east wind blows.

twi: Eyi na ɛbɛyɛ mpata ama Yakob afɔdi,eyi na ɛbɛyɛ ne bɔne asetu so aba a edi mu:bere a ɔyɛ afɔremuka so abosɛ hyirew a wɔabubu mu nketenkete,na Asera nnuane nnuhuam afɔremuka nsisi hɔ bio no.
english:
By this, then, will Jacob’s guilt be atoned for,
    and this will be the full fruit of the removal of his sin:
When he makes all the altar stones
    to be like limestone crushed to pieces,
no Asherah poles or incense altars
    will be left standing.

twi: Kuropɔn a wɔabɔ ho ban no ada mpanwɔagyaw atenae a wɔafi so no te sɛ nweatamhɔ na nantwimma didi,hɔ na wɔdeda;wɔwe so nnua no mman ma ho yɛ kokwakokwa.
Sɛ nnubaa no wo a, wobubuna mmea bɛfa de kɔsɔ ogya.Na saa nnipa yi nni nteaseenti wɔn yɛfo nhu wɔn mmɔbɔ,na wonnya adom mfi nea ɔbɔɔ wɔn no nkyɛn.
english:
When its twigs are dry, they are broken off
    and women come and make fires with them.
For this is a people without understanding;
    so their Maker has no compassion on them,
    and their Creator shows them no favor.

twi: Saa da no, Awurade bɛporow afi asuten Eufrate akosi Misraim Bon Wosee mu, na mo, Israelfo de, wɔbɛfa mo mmaako mmaako aboaboa mo ano.
english: In that day the Lord will thresh from the flowing Euphrates to the Wadi of Egypt, and you, Israel, will be gathered up one by one.

twi: Saa da no, wɔbɛhyɛn torobɛnto kɛse no. Wɔn a na wɔrewuwu wɔ Asiria ne wɔn a na wɔwɔ nnommum mu wɔ Misraim bɛba abɛsom Awurade wɔ Yerusalem bepɔw kronkron no so.
english: And in that day a great trumpet will sound. Those who were perishing in Assyria and those who were exiled in Egypt will come and worship the Lord on the holy mountain in Jerusalem.

twi: Efraim Ne Yuda Akannifo NnueNnome nka nhwiren abotiri a ɛyɛ Efraim asabowfo ahohoahoade nonhwiren a ɛrepa, nʼahoɔfɛ a ɛho wɔ nyam,a ɛda asasebere bon so.Nnome nka kuropɔn no, nea nnipa a nsa asɛe wɔn no de hoahoa wɔn ho no.
english:
Woe to that wreath, the pride of Ephraim’s drunkards,
    to the fading flower, his glorious beauty,
set on the head of a fertile valley—
    to that city, the pride of those laid low by wine!

twi: Hwɛ, Awurade wɔ obi a ɔwɔ tumi ne ahoɔden.Ɔte sɛ mparuwbo ne mframa a ɛsɛe adeɔte sɛ osu a ɛne mframa nam, ne osuhweam a ɛhyɛ suka maɔbɛtow no ahwe fam ahoɔden so.
english:
See, the Lord has one who is powerful and strong.
    Like a hailstorm and a destructive wind,
like a driving rain and a flooding downpour,
    he will throw it forcefully to the ground.

twi: Saa nhwiren abotiri no a ɛyɛ Efraim asabowfo ahohoahoade no,wobetiatia so.
english:
That wreath, the pride of Ephraim’s drunkards,
    will be trampled underfoot.

twi: Saa nhwiren a ɛrepa, nʼahoɔfɛ a ɛho wɔ nyam,a ɛda asasebere bon so no,bɛyɛ sɛ borɔdɔma a ɛbere ansa na otwabere adu,sɛ obi hu na ɔte aodi no ntɛm so.
english:
That fading flower, his glorious beauty,
    set on the head of a fertile valley,
will be like figs ripe before harvest—
    as soon as people see them and take them in hand,
    they swallow them.

twi: Saa da no Asafo Awuradebɛyɛ Anuonyam ahenkyɛw,nhwiren abotiri fɛfɛama ne nkurɔfo nkae no.
english:
In that day the Lord Almighty
    will be a glorious crown,
a beautiful wreath
    for the remnant of his people.

twi: Ɔbɛyɛ atɛntrenee honhomama otemmufo a ɔte agua mu.Ɔbɛyɛ ahoɔden farebaeama wɔn a wɔpam atamfo wɔ nkurow apon ano.
english:
He will be a spirit of justice
    to the one who sits in judgment,
a source of strength
    to those who turn back the battle at the gate.

twi: Na eyinom nso nsa ma wɔtɔ ntintanna bobesa ma wohinhim;bobesa ma asɔfo ne adiyifo tɔ ntintanna nsa ma wɔn ani so yɛ wɔn totɔtotɔ;na wohinhimwɔtɔ ntintan bere a wɔrenya anisoadehu,na wɔn ano fomfom wɔ adwenkyerɛ mu.
english:
And these also stagger from wine
    and reel from beer:
Priests and prophets stagger from beer
    and are befuddled with wine;
they reel from beer,
    they stagger when seeing visions,
    they stumble when rendering decisions.

twi: Ɔfe agugu apon nyinaa so,na baabiara ayɛ fi.
english:
All the tables are covered with vomit
    and there is not a spot without filth.

twi: “Hena na ɔpɛ sɛ ɔkyerɛkyerɛ no?Na hena nso na ɔrekyerɛ nʼasɛm ase akyerɛ no?Mmofra a wɔatwa wɔn nufu,wɔn a wotwaa wɔn nufu nkyɛe no ana?
english:
“Who is it he is trying to teach?
    To whom is he explaining his message?
To children weaned from their milk,
    to those just taken from the breast?

twi: Na ɛyɛ:Yɛ eyi, anaa eyimmara foforo akyi mmara;ɛha kakra, ɛhɔ kakra.”
english:
For it is:
    Do this, do that,
    a rule for this, a rule for that;
    a little here, a little there.”

twi: Eye, na afei ananafo ano ne kasa foforona Onyankopɔn de bɛkasa akyerɛ saa nkurɔfo yi,
english:
Very well then, with foreign lips and strange tongues
    God will speak to this people,

twi: Ɔka kyerɛɛ wɔn se,“Ha ne ahomegyebea no, momma abrɛfo no nhome;ahodwobea nso ni,”nanso wɔantie no.
english:
to whom he said,
    “This is the resting place, let the weary rest”;
and, “This is the place of repose”—
    but they would not listen.

twi: Enti afei wɔbɛfa Awurade asɛm a ɔde ma wɔn no sɛ:Yɛ eyi anaa eyi,mmara foforo akyi mmara;ha kakra, hɔ kakra,sɛnea wɔrekɔ no ɛbɛma wɔapini wɔn akyi;wobepirapira, na wɔatɔ afiri mu, na wɔakyere wɔn.
Ɛno nti, muntie Awurade asɛm, mo fɛwdifoa mudi saa nkurɔfo yi so wɔ Yerusalem.
english:
Therefore hear the word of the Lord, you scoffers
    who rule this people in Jerusalem.

twi: Mohoahoa mo ho se, “Yɛne owu ayɛ apam,yɛne ɔda ayɛ nhyehyɛesɛ asotwe a ano yɛ den ba a,ɛrentumi nka yɛn,efisɛ yɛde atoro ayɛ yɛn guankɔbeane nnaadaa ayɛ yɛn hintabea.”
english:
You boast, “We have entered into a covenant with death,
    with the realm of the dead we have made an agreement.
When an overwhelming scourge sweeps by,
    it cannot touch us,
for we have made a lie our refuge
    and falsehood our hiding place.”

twi: Enti nea Otumfo Awurade se ni,“Hwɛ! Mede ɔbo bi retim Sion,ɔbo a wɔasɔ ahwɛ,tweatibo a ɛsom bo ama fapem a ɛyɛ den;nea ɔde ne ho to so no remmɔ hu.
english:
So this is what the Sovereign Lord says:
“See, I lay a stone in Zion, a tested stone,
    a precious cornerstone for a sure foundation;
the one who relies on it
    will never be stricken with panic.

twi: Mede atɛntrenee bɛyɛ susuhamana treneeyɛ ayɛ ɔfasu kirebennyɛ susuhamamparuwbo bɛsɛe wo guankɔbea a ɛyɛ atoro no,na nsu abɛkata wo hintabea hɔ.
english:
I will make justice the measuring line
    and righteousness the plumb line;
hail will sweep away your refuge, the lie,
    and water will overflow your hiding place.

twi: Wobetwa apam a wo ne owu ayɛ no mu;nhyehyɛe a wo ne ɔda ayɛ no nso rennyinasɛ asotwe a ano yɛ den no ba a,ebetwiw afa mo so.
english:
Your covenant with death will be annulled;
    your agreement with the realm of the dead will not stand.
When the overwhelming scourge sweeps by,
    you will be beaten down by it.

twi: Mpɛn dodow biara a ɛbɛba no ɛbɛsoa mo akɔ;anɔpa, awia ne anadwo biara,ɛbɛfa mu akɔ.”Saa nkra yi nteasede ehu bɛba.
english:
As often as it comes it will carry you away;
    morning after morning, by day and by night,
    it will sweep through.”
The understanding of this message
    will bring sheer terror.

twi: Mpa no yɛ tia dodo ma sɛ wɔteɛ wɔn mu wɔ so,kuntu no yɛ hiahiaa sɛ ɛbɛso wɔn ho kata.
english:
The bed is too short to stretch out on,
    the blanket too narrow to wrap around you.

twi: Awurade bɛsɔre sɛnea ɔsɔree wɔ Perasim bepɔw so no,ɔbɛkanyan ne ho sɛnea ɔyɛɛ wɔ Gibeon Bon mu,yɛɛ nʼadwuma, nʼadwuma nwonwaso nodii ne dwuma, dwumadi a bi mmaa da.
english:
The Lord will rise up as he did at Mount Perazim,
    he will rouse himself as in the Valley of Gibeon—
to do his work, his strange work,
    and perform his task, his alien task.

twi: Afei gyae wo fɛwdi no,anyɛ saa a wo nkɔnsɔnkɔnsɔn mu bɛyɛ duru;Awurade, Asafo Awurade aka akyerɛ meɔsɛe ho mmaraden a wɔahyɛ atia asase no nyinaa.
english:
Now stop your mocking,
    or your chains will become heavier;
the Lord, the Lord Almighty, has told me
    of the destruction decreed against the whole land.

twi: Muntie na monte me nne;monwɛn mo aso na muntie nea meka.
english:
Listen and hear my voice;
    pay attention and hear what I say.

twi: Sɛ okuafo funtum asase sɛ ɔrebedua so a, ɔyɛ no daa ana?Ɔkɔ so tutu, fɛntɛm asase no ana?
english:
When a farmer plows for planting, does he plow continually?
    Does he keep on breaking up and working the soil?

twi: Sɛ osiesie asase no ani a,onnua ɛme, na ɔmpete ntɛtɛ wɔ so ana?Onnua awi ne atoko mu biara wɔ nʼafa ana?
english:
When he has leveled the surface,
    does he not sow caraway and scatter cumin?
Does he not plant wheat in its place,
    barley in its plot,
    and spelt in its field?

twi: Ne Nyankopɔn ma no akwankyerɛna ɔkyerɛ no ɔkwan pa.
english:
His God instructs him
    and teaches him the right way.

twi: Wɔmfa asae mpo ɛme ho,wɔmfa teaseɛnam hankare mfa ntɛtɛ so;wɔde pema na ɛboro ɛme,na wɔde abaa aboro ntɛtɛ.
english:
Caraway is not threshed with a sledge,
    nor is the wheel of a cart rolled over cumin;
caraway is beaten out with a rod,
    and cumin with a stick.

twi: Wɔyam aburow de to brodonti obi nkɔ so nyam a onnwie da.Ɛwɔ mu, ɔde nʼawiporowee teaseɛnam hankare fa so de,nanso ɛnyɛ nʼapɔnkɔ na wɔyam.
english:
Grain must be ground to make bread;
    so one does not go on threshing it forever.
The wheels of a threshing cart may be rolled over it,
    but one does not use horses to grind grain.

twi: Eyinom nyinaa fi Asafo Awurade,afotu mu nwonwani,na ne nyansa boro so.
english:
All this also comes from the Lord Almighty,
    whose plan is wonderful,
    whose wisdom is magnificent.

twi: Nnome Nka Dawid KuropɔnDue wo Ariel,Ariel, kuropɔn a Dawid tenaa mu!Fa afe ka afe hona ma wo mfirihyia mu afahyɛ ahorow no nkɔ so.
english:
Woe to you, Ariel, Ariel,
    the city where David settled!
Add year to year
    and let your cycle of festivals go on.

twi: Nanso metua Ariel ano;obedi awerɛhow na wato kwadwom,ɔbɛyɛ sɛ afɔremuka so gya.
Mede dɔm betwa wo ho ahyia;mesisi abantenten atwa wo ho ahyiana madi ntuano dwuma atia wo.
Wɔasie wo no, wobɛkasa afi asase mu;wo kasa a mu ntew no befi mfutuma mu aba.Wo nne befi asase no mu aba te sɛ ɔsaman de;wo kasa befi mfutuma mu aka asomsɛm.
Nanso wʼatamfo bebrebe no bɛyɛ sɛ mfutuma muhumuhu,na atirimɔdenfo bebrebe no ayɛ sɛ ntɛtɛ a mframa abɔ.Ɛbɛba prɛko pɛ, amono mu hɔ ara.
english:
But your many enemies will become like fine dust,
    the ruthless hordes like blown chaff.
Suddenly, in an instant,

twi: Asafo Awurade bɛba.Ɔde aprannaa ne asasewosow ne huuyɛ kɛse,mframahweam ne ahum ne ogyaframa a ɛhyew ade bɛba.
english:
the Lord Almighty will come
with thunder and earthquake and great noise,
    with windstorm and tempest and flames of a devouring fire.

twi: Afei amanaman bebrebe a wotu Ariel so sa nyinaa,wɔn a wɔtow hyɛ ɔne nʼaban so na wotua nʼano no,ɛbɛyɛ wɔn sɛ adaeso,anaa anadwo mu anisoadehu.
english:
Then the hordes of all the nations that fight against Ariel,
    that attack her and her fortress and besiege her,
will be as it is with a dream,
    with a vision in the night—

twi: Sɛnea obi a ɔkɔm de no so dae sɛ ɔredidi,na sɛ onyan a ɔte sɛ ɔkɔm de no no;sɛnea obi a osukɔm de no so dae sɛ ɔrenom nsu,nanso onyan a na watɔ beraw, na osukɔm de no ara no.Saa ara na ɛbɛyɛ ama amanaman dodow awɔko tia Bepɔw Sion no.
english:
as when a hungry person dreams of eating,
    but awakens hungry still;
as when a thirsty person dreams of drinking,
    but awakens faint and thirsty still.
So will it be with the hordes of all the nations
    that fight against Mount Zion.

twi: Mo ho nnwiriw mo na ɛnyɛ mo nwonwa,mo ani mfura a munhu ade;mommobow a emfi nsa,montotɔ ntintan a emfi bobesa.
english:
Be stunned and amazed,
    blind yourselves and be sightless;
be drunk, but not from wine,
    stagger, but not from beer.

twi: Awurade de nnahɔɔ ato mo so:Wakata mo ani (adiyifo no);wakata mo ti so (adehufo no).

Mo de, saa anisoadehu yi nyinaa nka hwee mma mo, ɛte sɛ nsɛm a wɔasɔw ano wɔ nhoma mmobɔwee mu. Sɛ mode nhoma mmobɔwee no ma obi a, otumi kenkan, na moka kyerɛ no se, “Mesrɛ wo kenkan eyi” a, obebua se, “Merentumi, efisɛ wɔasɔw ano.”
english: For you this whole vision is nothing but words sealed in a scroll. And if you give the scroll to someone who can read, and say, “Read this, please,” they will answer, “I can’t; it is sealed.”

twi: Sɛ nso, mode nhoma mmobɔwee no ma nea onnim akenkan, na moka kyerɛ no se, “Mesrɛ wo kenkan eyi” a, obebua se, “Minnim akenkan.”
english: Or if you give the scroll to someone who cannot read, and say, “Read this, please,” they will answer, “I don’t know how to read.”

twi: Awurade ka se,“Saa nnipa yi de anohunu twiw bɛn mena wɔde wɔn anofafa hyɛ me anuonyam,nanso wɔn koma mmɛn me.Som a wɔsom me noyɛ mmara a nnipa akyerɛ wɔn no nko ara.
english:
The Lord says:
“These people come near to me with their mouth
    and honor me with their lips,
    but their hearts are far from me.
Their worship of me
    is based on merely human rules they have been taught.

twi: Enti mɛma nnipa yi ho adwiriw wɔn biomede anwonwade ntoatoaso bɛyɛ;mɛsɛe anyansafo nyansa,na mɛma nimdefo adenim ayɛ ɔkwa.”
english:
Therefore once more I will astound these people
    with wonder upon wonder;
the wisdom of the wise will perish,
    the intelligence of the intelligent will vanish.”

twi: Wonnue, wɔn a wɔyɛ biribiara sɛwɔde wɔn atirimpɔw behintaw Awurade,wɔn a wɔyɛ wɔn nnwuma wɔ sum ase na wosusuw sɛ,“Hena na ohu yɛn? Hena na ɔbɛte ase?”
english:
Woe to those who go to great depths
    to hide their plans from the Lord,
who do their work in darkness and think,
    “Who sees us? Who will know?”

twi: Musisi nneɛma ti ase,sɛnea modwene sɛ ɔnwemfo te sɛ dɔte no!Nea wayɛ betumi aka akyerɛ nea ɔyɛe no se,“Ɛnyɛ wo na woyɛɛ me ana”?Kuku betumi aka afa ɔnwemfo ho se“Onnim hwee ana”?
english:
You turn things upside down,
    as if the potter were thought to be like the clay!
Shall what is formed say to the one who formed it,
    “You did not make me”?
Can the pot say to the potter,
    “You know nothing”?

twi: Ɛrenkyɛ koraa, wɔrennan Lebanon nyɛ no asaseberena asasebere no nso nyɛ sɛ kwae ana?
english:
In a very short time, will not Lebanon be turned into a fertile field
    and the fertile field seem like a forest?

twi: Saa da no, ɔsotifo bɛte nsɛm a ɛwɔ nhoma mmobɔwee no muna kusuuyɛ ne esum mu mpoonifuraefo ani behu ade.
english:
In that day the deaf will hear the words of the scroll,
    and out of gloom and darkness
    the eyes of the blind will see.

twi: Ahobrɛasefo bedi ahurusi wɔ Awurade mu bio;ahiafo ho bɛsɛpɛw wɔn wɔ Israel Ɔkronkronni no mu.
english:
Once more the humble will rejoice in the Lord;
    the needy will rejoice in the Holy One of Israel.

twi: Atutuwpɛfo bɛyera,wɔrenhu fɛwdifo bio,na wɔn a wodwen bɔne nyinaa, wobetwa wɔn agu,
english:
The ruthless will vanish,
    the mockers will disappear,
    and all who have an eye for evil will be cut down—

twi: wɔn a wɔka asɛm baako ma obi di fɔ,wɔn a wosum nea ɔreyi ne ho ano afiri wɔ asenniina wodi adansekurum ma wobu nea odi bem no fɔ no nso wobetwa wɔn agu.
english:
those who with a word make someone out to be guilty,
    who ensnare the defender in court
    and with false testimony deprive the innocent of justice.

twi: Enti sɛɛ na Awurade a ogyee Abraham nkwa noka kyerɛ Yakob fifo:“Yakob anim rengu ase bio;wɔn anim rehoa bio.
Sɛ wohu wɔn mma wɔ wɔn mu,wɔn a wɔyɛ me nsa ano adwuma no awɔbɛyɛ me din no kronkron;wobegye Yakob ɔkronkronni no kronkronyɛ ato mu,na wɔde fɛre agyina Israel Nyankopɔn no anim.
english:
When they see among them their children,
    the work of my hands,
they will keep my name holy;
    they will acknowledge the holiness of the Holy One of Jacob,
    and will stand in awe of the God of Israel.

twi: Wɔn a wɔfom kwan wɔ honhom mu benya ntease;wɔn a wonwiinwii nso begye nkyerɛkyerɛ ato mu.”
english:
Those who are wayward in spirit will gain understanding;
    those who complain will accept instruction.”

twi: Munnue, Ɔman Asoɔdenfo“Munnue mmofra asoɔdenfo,”sɛɛ na Awurade se,“Wɔn a wɔde nhyehyɛe a emfi me yɛ adwuma,na wɔyɛ apam a emfi me honhom mu,na wɔboaboa bɔne ano;
english:
“Woe to the obstinate children,”
    declares the Lord,
“to those who carry out plans that are not mine,
    forming an alliance, but not by my Spirit,
    heaping sin upon sin;

twi: wɔn a wɔkɔ Misraima wommisa me ansa;wɔhwehwɛ mmoa a ɛyɛ bammɔ fi Farao nkyɛn,wɔkɔ Misraim kɔhwehwɛ hintabea.
english:
who go down to Egypt
    without consulting me;
who look for help to Pharaoh’s protection,
    to Egypt’s shade for refuge.

twi: Nanso Farao bammɔ bɛyɛ animguase ama mo,Misraim nwini de ahohora bɛbrɛ mo.
english:
But Pharaoh’s protection will be to your shame,
    Egypt’s shade will bring you disgrace.

twi: Ɛwɔ mu, wɔwɔ adwumayɛfo wɔ Soanna wɔn ananmusifo adu Hanes de,
english:
Though they have officials in Zoan
    and their envoys have arrived in Hanes,

twi: nanso wɔn nyinaa anim begu asennipa bi a wɔn so nni wɔn mfaso nti,wɔmmfa mmoa anaa mfaso mma,na mmom animguase ne ahohora.”
english:
everyone will be put to shame
    because of a people useless to them,
who bring neither help nor advantage,
    but only shame and disgrace.”

twi: Adehunu a ɛfa Negeb mmoa ho:wɔfa ahokyere ne ahohiahia asase so,nea gyata ne gyatabere,nhurutoa ne awɔ a wɔn ho yɛ hare wɔ,ananmusifo no de wɔn ahonyade soa mfurumne wɔn ademude wɔ yoma afu so,de kɔ saa ɔman a ne so nni mfaso no so,
english:
A prophecy concerning the animals of the Negev:
Through a land of hardship and distress,
    of lions and lionesses,
    of adders and darting snakes,
the envoys carry their riches on donkeys’ backs,
    their treasures on the humps of camels,
to that unprofitable nation,

twi: de kɔ Misraim a ne mmoa so nni mfaso,enti mefrɛ noRahab nea Onsi Hwee.
english:
to Egypt, whose help is utterly useless.
Therefore I call her
    Rahab the Do-Nothing.

twi: Kɔ afei, kyerɛw wɔ kyerɛwpon so ma wɔn,kurukyerɛw wɔ nhoma mmobɔwee sosɛnea nna a ɛreba no mu noɛbɛyɛ adansede a ɛbɛtena hɔ afebɔɔ.
english:
Go now, write it on a tablet for them,
    inscribe it on a scroll,
that for the days to come
    it may be an everlasting witness.

twi: Saa nnipa yi yɛ atuatewfo, mma asisifo,mma a wɔmpɛ sɛ wotie Awurade nkyerɛkyerɛ.
english:
For these are rebellious people, deceitful children,
    children unwilling to listen to the Lord’s instruction.

twi: Wɔka kyerɛ adehufo se,“Munhu mo ani so ade bio!”ne adiyifo no nso se,“Monnka anisoadehu a ɛyɛ nokware no nkyerɛ yɛn bio!Monka abodwosɛm nkyerɛ yɛn,monhyɛ nnaadaa nkɔm.
english:
They say to the seers,
    “See no more visions!”
and to the prophets,
    “Give us no more visions of what is right!
Tell us pleasant things,
    prophesy illusions.

twi: Mumfi saa ɔtempɔn yi so,momman mfi saa ɔkwan yi hona munnyae Israel Kronkronnia mode no haw yɛn yi!”
english:
Leave this way,
    get off this path,
and stop confronting us
    with the Holy One of Israel!”

twi: Enti sɛɛ na Israel Ɔkronkronni no se:“Esiane sɛ moapo saa nkra yi,na mode mo ho ato nhyɛsone nnaadaa so nti,
english:
Therefore this is what the Holy One of Israel says:
“Because you have rejected this message,
    relied on oppression
    and depended on deceit,

twi: saa bɔne yi bɛyɛ sɛɔfasu tenten bi a ahyɛ kam na akyeana ebu mpofirim, ama mo.
english:
this sin will become for you
    like a high wall, cracked and bulging,
    that collapses suddenly, in an instant.

twi: Ebebubu nketenkete ayɛ sɛ kuku.Ɛbɛyam pasaa a,sin koraa renka awobetumi de asɔ gya afi muka muanaa wɔde bɛsaw nsu afi ahina mu.”
english:
It will break in pieces like pottery,
    shattered so mercilessly
that among its pieces not a fragment will be found
    for taking coals from a hearth
    or scooping water out of a cistern.”

twi: Sɛɛ na Otumfo Awurade, Israel Kronkronni no se:“Ahonu mu ne ntoboase mu na mo nkwagye wɔkommyɛ ne ahotoso mu na mo ahoɔden wɔ,nanso, morennya mu biara.
english:
This is what the Sovereign Lord, the Holy One of Israel, says:
“In repentance and rest is your salvation,
    in quietness and trust is your strength,
    but you would have none of it.

twi: Mokaa se, ‘Dabi da, yɛbɛtena apɔnkɔ so aguan.’Enti mubeguan!Mokaa se, ‘yɛbɛtena apɔnkɔ a wɔn ho yɛ hare so akɔ.’Enti wɔn a wɔtaa mo no ho bɛyɛ hare!
english:
You said, ‘No, we will flee on horses.’
    Therefore you will flee!
You said, ‘We will ride off on swift horses.’
    Therefore your pursuers will be swift!

twi: Apem beguanɔbaako ho hu nti;baanum ho hu ntimo nyinaa beguan akɔ,akosi sɛ wobegyaw mote sɛ frankaa dua a esi bepɔw atifi,te sɛ frankaa a esi koko so.”
english:
A thousand will flee
    at the threat of one;
at the threat of five
    you will all flee away,
till you are left
    like a flagstaff on a mountaintop,
    like a banner on a hill.”

twi: Nanso Awurade pɛ sɛ ɔdom mo;ɔma ne ho so, kyerɛ wo nʼahummɔbɔ.Efisɛ Awurade yɛ ɔtreneeni Nyankopɔn.Nhyira ne wɔn a wɔtwɛn no nyinaa!
english:
Yet the Lord longs to be gracious to you;
    therefore he will rise up to show you compassion.
For the Lord is a God of justice.
    Blessed are all who wait for him!

twi: Sionfo a mote Yerusalem, morentwa adwo bio. Sɛ musu frɛ no hwehwɛ mmoa a, ɔbɛdom mo! Sɛ ɔte a obegye mo so prɛko pɛ.
english: People of Zion, who live in Jerusalem, you will weep no more. How gracious he will be when you cry for help! As soon as he hears, he will answer you.

twi: Ɛwɔ mu, Awurade brɛ mo amanehunu sɛ aduan ne ɔhaw sɛ nsu de, nanso, afei mubehu Awurade, mo kyerɛkyerɛfo no bio, na ɔbɛkyerɛ mo kwan.
english: Although the Lord gives you the bread of adversity and the water of affliction, your teachers will be hidden no more; with your own eyes you will see them.

twi: Sɛ mofa nifa anaa benkum a, mobɛte nne bi wɔ mo akyi a ɛka se, “Ɔkwan no ni na momfa so.”
english: Whether you turn to the right or to the left, your ears will hear a voice behind you, saying, “This is the way; walk in it.”

twi: Afei mobɛtow mo ahoni a mode dwetɛ adura ho ne nsɛsode a mode sikakɔkɔɔ afa ho no nyinaa agu. Mobɛtow wɔn agu sɛ ntamagow fi, na moaka kyerɛ wɔn se, “Mumfi yɛn so nkɔ.”
english: Then you will desecrate your idols overlaid with silver and your images covered with gold; you will throw them away like a menstrual cloth and say to them, “Away with you!”

twi: Afei ɔde osu behyira mo bere a mudua nnuaba, na aduan a asase no bɛbɔ no bɛyɛ papa na ɛbɛdɔɔso nso. Da no, mo anantwi bedidi wɔ adidibea a ɛtrɛw so.
english: He will also send you rain for the seed you sow in the ground, and the food that comes from the land will be rich and plentiful. In that day your cattle will graze in broad meadows.

twi: Mo anantwi ne mo mfurum a wofuntum asase no bɛwe atoko pa ne ne ntɛtɛ a, wɔde sofi ne nkorata trɛtrɛw mu.
english: The oxen and donkeys that work the soil will eat fodder and mash, spread out with fork and shovel.

twi: Saa okum kɛse da no a abantenten ahwehwe ase no, nsuwa bɛteɛ wɔ bepɔw tenten ne koko a ɛkorɔn biara so.
english: In the day of great slaughter, when the towers fall, streams of water will flow on every high mountain and every lofty hill.

twi: Ɔsram bɛhyerɛn sɛ owia, na owia hyerɛn no bɛyɛ mpɛn ason, te sɛ nnafua ason mu hyerɛn, bere a Awurade kyekyere ne nkurɔfo akuru na ɔsa apirakuru a ɔde ama wɔn no.
english: The moon will shine like the sun, and the sunlight will be seven times brighter, like the light of seven full days, when the Lord binds up the bruises of his people and heals the wounds he inflicted.

twi: Hwɛ! Awurade fi akyirikyiri reba,ɔde abufuwhyew ne wusiw kumɔnn;abufuw ahyɛ nʼanom ma,na ne tɛkrɛma yɛ ogya a ɛhyew nneɛma.
english:
See, the Name of the Lord comes from afar,
    with burning anger and dense clouds of smoke;
his lips are full of wrath,
    and his tongue is a consuming fire.

twi: Ne home te sɛ asuworoe a ɛsen ntɛmntɛm,na ɛforo kɔdeda kɔn mu.Ɔwosow aman no wɔ ɔsɛe sɔnee so;ɔde nnareka a ɛma wɔfom kwanhyehyɛ nnipa no nnyepi.
english:
His breath is like a rushing torrent,
    rising up to the neck.
He shakes the nations in the sieve of destruction;
    he places in the jaws of the peoples
    a bit that leads them astray.

twi: Na mobɛto dwomte sɛ anadwo a mudi afahyɛ kronkron no;mo koma bedi ahurusite sɛ bere a nnipa de atɛntɛbɛn forokɔ Awurade bepɔw no so,kɔ Israel Ɔbotan no nkyɛn.
english:
And you will sing
    as on the night you celebrate a holy festival;
your hearts will rejoice
    as when people playing pipes go up
to the mountain of the Lord,
    to the Rock of Israel.

twi: Awurade bɛma nnipa ate nʼabrɛmpɔnnnena ɔbɛma wɔahu ne basa a ɛresianna ɛde abufuwhyew ne ogya a ɛhyew nneɛmaosu dennen, aprannaa ne mparuwbo reba.
english:
The Lord will cause people to hear his majestic voice
    and will make them see his arm coming down
with raging anger and consuming fire,
    with cloudburst, thunderstorm and hail.

twi: Awurade nne bɛhwe Asiria;ɔde nʼabaa bɛbɔ wɔn ahwe fam.
english:
The voice of the Lord will shatter Assyria;
    with his rod he will strike them down.

twi: Ɔbɛbɔ wɔn wɔ ɔko mu,na bere biara a ɔbɛbɔ wɔn noɛbɛyɛ sɛ akasae ne sankuten so nnwonto koro.
english:
Every stroke the Lord lays on them
    with his punishing club
will be to the music of timbrels and harps,
    as he fights them in battle with the blows of his arm.

twi: Wɔasiesie Topet dedaada;wɔayɛ no krado ama ɔhene no.Wɔahyehyɛ ogya ne nnyentia bebreewɔ ne gya amoa no a emu dɔ na ɛtrɛw no mu;Awurade homete sɛ sufre asuten nobɛsɔ mu gya.
english:
Topheth has long been prepared;
    it has been made ready for the king.
Its fire pit has been made deep and wide,
    with an abundance of fire and wood;
the breath of the Lord,
    like a stream of burning sulfur,
    sets it ablaze.

twi: Wɔn A Wɔde Wɔn Ho To Misraim So No NnueWonnue, wɔn a wɔkɔ Misraim kɔhwehwɛ mmoa,wɔn a wɔde wɔn ho to apɔnkɔ so,wɔn a wogye wɔn nteaseɛnam dodowne wɔn apɔnkɔsotefo ahoɔden mmoroso no di,na wɔnhwɛ Israel Kronkronni no,anaasɛ wɔmpɛ mmoa mfi Awurade hɔ.
english:
Woe to those who go down to Egypt for help,
    who rely on horses,
who trust in the multitude of their chariots
    and in the great strength of their horsemen,
but do not look to the Holy One of Israel,
    or seek help from the Lord.

twi: Nanso Awurade yɛ onyansafo a obetumi de ɔhaw aba;ɔnsesa nʼano.Ɔbɛsɔre atia amumɔyɛfo fi,ne wɔn a wɔboa nnebɔneyɛfo.
english:
Yet he too is wise and can bring disaster;
    he does not take back his words.
He will rise up against that wicked nation,
    against those who help evildoers.

twi: Na Misraimfo yi yɛ nnipa kɛkɛ, wɔnyɛ Onyankopɔn.Wɔn apɔnkɔ yɛ ɔhonam na wɔnyɛ honhom.Sɛ Awurade teɛ ne nsa a,ɔboafo bɛwatirina nea wɔboa no no bɛhwe ase;wɔn baanu bɛbɔ mu asɛe.

Sɛɛ na Awurade ka kyerɛ me:“Sɛnea gyata woro so,sɛnea gyata kokroo woro so gu ne hanam so noa mpo sɛ wɔfrɛ nguanhwɛfo dɔm kɔ no so a,wɔn nteɛteɛmu mmɔ no huna wɔn huuyɛ nso nhaw no no,saa ara na Asafo Awurade besianabɛko wɔ Sion Bepɔw ne ne sorɔnsorɔmmea so.
english:
This is what the Lord says to me:
“As a lion growls,
    a great lion over its prey—
and though a whole band of shepherds
    is called together against it,
it is not frightened by their shouts
    or disturbed by their clamor—
so the Lord Almighty will come down
    to do battle on Mount Zion and on its heights.

twi: Sɛnea nnomaa tu gyina faako wɔ wim nosaa ara na Asafo Awurade bɛbɔ Yerusalem ho ban;ɔbɛbɔ ne ho ban na wagye no,obegyaa no na wagye no asi hɔ.”
english:
Like birds hovering overhead,
    the Lord Almighty will shield Jerusalem;
he will shield it and deliver it,
    he will ‘pass over’ it and will rescue it.”

twi: Monsan nkɔ nea moayɛ dɔm atia no no nkyɛn, Israelfo.
english: Return, you Israelites, to the One you have so greatly revolted against.

twi: Da no mo mu biara bɛpo dwetɛ ne sikakɔkɔɔ ahoni a mode mo nsa a ɛho agu fi ayɛ no.
english: For in that day every one of you will reject the idols of silver and gold your sinful hands have made.

twi: “Asiria bɛhwe ase wɔ afoa a ɛnyɛ onipa de ano;afoa a ɛnyɛ onipa de bɛsɛe wɔn.Wobeguan afi afoa no anona wɔbɛma wɔn mmerante ayɛ ɔhyɛ adwuma.
english:
“Assyria will fall by no human sword;
    a sword, not of mortals, will devour them.
They will flee before the sword
    and their young men will be put to forced labor.

twi: Wɔn abandennen bebubu, ehu nti;wohu akofo frankaa a, wɔn asraafo mpanyimfo bɛbɔ huboa,”sɛɛ na Awurade se,nea ne gya wɔ Sion,na ne fononoo si Yerusalem no.
english:
Their stronghold will fall because of terror;
    at the sight of the battle standard their commanders will panic,”
declares the Lord,
    whose fire is in Zion,
    whose furnace is in Jerusalem.

twi: Trenee AhenniHwɛ, ɔhene bi bedi hene wɔ trenee muna ahemfo de atɛntrenee adi nnipa so.
english:
See, a king will reign in righteousness
    and rulers will rule with justice.

twi: Onipa biara bɛyɛ mframa ano hintabeane ahum mu guankɔbea,ɔbɛyɛ sɛ nsuwansuwa a ɛwɔ nweatam sone ɔbotan kɛse sunsuma a ɛwɔ osukɔm asase so.
english:
Each one will be like a shelter from the wind
    and a refuge from the storm,
like streams of water in the desert
    and the shadow of a great rock in a thirsty land.

twi: Wɔn a wohu no ani renkata bio,na wɔn a wɔte asɛm no aso betie.
english:
Then the eyes of those who see will no longer be closed,
    and the ears of those who hear will listen.

twi: Nea ɔyɛ adwene mu hare behu na wate ase,wɔn a wɔpo dodow bɛkasa na mu ada hɔ.
english:
The fearful heart will know and understand,
    and the stammering tongue will be fluent and clear.

twi: Wɔremfrɛ ɔkwasea sɛ onuonyamfo biona wɔremfa nidi mma apapahwekwa.
english:
No longer will the fool be called noble
    nor the scoundrel be highly respected.

twi: Ɔkwasea ka nkwaseasɛmna osusuw bɔne ho:ɔyɛ anyame apɛdeɔka Awurade ho nsɛm a enye;ɔmma nea ɔkɔm de no no aduanɔde nsu kame nea osukɔm de no.
english:
For fools speak folly,
    their hearts are bent on evil:
They practice ungodliness
    and spread error concerning the Lord;
the hungry they leave empty
    and from the thirsty they withhold water.

twi: Apapahwekwa akwan yɛ amumɔyɛ,ɔyɛ bɔne ho nhyehyɛede atoro sɛe ohiani,wɔ bere a ohiani asɛm yɛ nokware mpo.
english:
Scoundrels use wicked methods,
    they make up evil schemes
to destroy the poor with lies,
    even when the plea of the needy is just.

twi: Nanso onuonyamfo yɛ nhyehyɛe a ɛho wɔ nyamna nneyɛe pa no nti ɔda nsow.
english:
But the noble make noble plans,
    and by noble deeds they stand.

twi: Yerusalem MmabaaMo mmea a mugye mo ho di,monsɔre na muntie me;mo mmabea a mususuw sɛ mowɔ bammɔmonyɛ aso mma nea mewɔ ka!
english:
You women who are so complacent,
    rise up and listen to me;
you daughters who feel secure,
    hear what I have to say!

twi: Afe akyi nna kakra bi nomo a mugye di sɛ mowɔ bammɔ ho bɛpopo;bobe twabere no bedi mo huammɔ,nnuaba no twabere nso remma.
english:
In little more than a year
    you who feel secure will tremble;
the grape harvest will fail,
    and the harvest of fruit will not come.

twi: Mo ho mpopo, mo mmea a mugye mo ho dimommɔ hu, mo mmabea a mugye di sɛ mowɔ bammɔ!Mompa mo ho ntamana momfa atweaatam mmɔ mo asen.
english:
Tremble, you complacent women;
    shudder, you daughters who feel secure!
Strip off your fine clothes
    and wrap yourselves in rags.

twi: Mommobɔ mo koko so sɛ mowɔ mfuw afɛfɛne bobe a ɛso no nti,
english:
Beat your breasts for the pleasant fields,
    for the fruitful vines

twi: ne me nkurɔfo asase,asase a nsɔe ne nnɛnkyɛnse agye afa.Yiw, montwa adwo mma afi a wogye wɔn ani wɔ mune saa ahosɛpɛw kuropɔn yi.
english:
and for the land of my people,
    a land overgrown with thorns and briers—
yes, mourn for all houses of merriment
    and for this city of revelry.

twi: Wobegyaw aban no hɔ,na gyegyeegye kuropɔn no ada mpan;abanwa ne ɔwɛn aban bɛdan asasehunu afebɔɔ,nea mfurum pɛ ne nguankuw didibea,
english:
The fortress will be abandoned,
    the noisy city deserted;
citadel and watchtower will become a wasteland forever,
    the delight of donkeys, a pasture for flocks,

twi: kosi sɛ wobehwie honhom afi ɔsoro agu yɛn so,na nweatam bɛdan asaseberena asasebere ayɛ sɛ kwae.
english:
till the Spirit is poured on us from on high,
    and the desert becomes a fertile field,
    and the fertile field seems like a forest.

twi: Trenee bɛtena nweatam sona adetreneeyɛ atena asasebere so.
english:
The Lord’s justice will dwell in the desert,
    his righteousness live in the fertile field.

twi: Adetreneeyɛ bɛsow asomdwoe aba;nea adetreneeyɛ de ba no bɛyɛ kommyɛ ne ahotoso a enni awiei.
english:
The fruit of that righteousness will be peace;
    its effect will be quietness and confidence forever.

twi: Me nkurɔfo bɛtenatena mmeae a asomdwoe wɔafi a wɔabɔ ho banhomebea a ɔhaw biara nni hɔ.
english:
My people will live in peaceful dwelling places,
    in secure homes,
    in undisturbed places of rest.

twi: Mpo sɛ mparuwbo sɛe kwae nona kuropɔn no sɛe koraa a,
english:
Though hail flattens the forest
    and the city is leveled completely,

twi: wobehyira wo,wubedua wʼaba wɔ nsuwa biara ho,na wama wʼanantwi ne wo mfurum anantew baabiara.
english:
how blessed you will be,
    sowing your seed by every stream,
    and letting your cattle and donkeys range free.

twi: Ahohia Ne MmoaDue, ɔdesɛefo,wo a wɔnsɛee wo!Due, ɔfatwafo,wo a wonnii wo huammɔ!sɛ wugyae adesɛe a,wɔbɛsɛe wo;sɛ wuwie huammɔdi a,wobedi wo huammɔ.
english:
Woe to you, destroyer,
    you who have not been destroyed!
Woe to you, betrayer,
    you who have not been betrayed!
When you stop destroying,
    you will be destroyed;
when you stop betraying,
    you will be betrayed.

twi: Ao Awurade, hu yɛn mmɔbɔ;yɛn ani da wo so.Yɛ yɛn ahoɔden anɔpa biara,ne yɛn nkwagye wɔ ahohia mu.
english:
Lord, be gracious to us;
    we long for you.
Be our strength every morning,
    our salvation in time of distress.

twi: Aman no te wo nne mmubomu a, woguan;sɛ woma wo ho so a amanaman no bɔ ahwete.
english:
At the uproar of your army, the peoples flee;
    when you rise up, the nations scatter.

twi: Wɔtase mo asade, Ao amanaman, sɛnea mmoadabimma yɛ;nnipa tow hyɛ so te sɛ mmoadabi dɔm.
english:
Your plunder, O nations, is harvested as by young locusts;
    like a swarm of locusts people pounce on it.

twi: Wɔama Awurade so, na ɔte ɔsorosoro;ɔde trenee ne adetreneeyɛ bɛhyɛ Sion ma.
english:
The Lord is exalted, for he dwells on high;
    he will fill Zion with his justice and righteousness.

twi: Ɔbɛyɛ fapem a atim yiye wɔ mo mmere so,nkwagye, nyansa ne nhumu mmoroso akorae;Awurade suro ne ademude yi akorae ano safe.
Monhwɛ, wɔn mmarima akokodurufo su teɛteɛɛ mu wɔ mmɔnten so;asomdwoe ho abɔfo su yayaayaw.
english:
Look, their brave men cry aloud in the streets;
    the envoys of peace weep bitterly.

twi: Atempɔn no so da hɔ kwa,akwantufo biara nni akwan no so.Wɔabu apam no so,wobu nʼadansefo animtiaawommu obiara.
english:
The highways are deserted,
    no travelers are on the roads.
The treaty is broken,
    its witnesses are despised,
    no one is respected.

twi: Asase no wo kesee na ɛsɛe,Lebanon agyigya na nʼanim agu ase;Saron ayɛ sɛ Araba,Basan ne Karmel porow wɔn nhaban.
english:
The land dries up and wastes away,
    Lebanon is ashamed and withers;
Sharon is like the Arabah,
    and Bashan and Carmel drop their leaves.

twi: “Afei na mɛsɔre,” sɛɛ na Awurade se.“Afei na wɔbɛpagyaw me ɛ;afei na wɔbɛma me so.
Munyinsɛn ntɛtɛ,na mowo sare;mo home yɛ ogya a ɛhyew mo.
Wɔbɛhyew aman no ama wɔatɔ nso;wɔbɛto wɔn mu gya te sɛ nsɔe a wɔatwa.”
english:
The peoples will be burned to ashes;
    like cut thornbushes they will be set ablaze.”

twi: Mo a mowɔ akyirikyiri no, muntie nea mayɛ;mo a mobɛn no, monkamfo me kɛseyɛ!
english:
You who are far away, hear what I have done;
    you who are near, acknowledge my power!

twi: Nnebɔneyɛfo a wɔwɔ Sion abɔ huboa;ahopopo aka wɔn a wonnim Onyame:“Yɛn mu hena na obetumi ne ogya a ɛhyew ade atena?Yɛn mu hena na obetumi ne daa ogyatannaa atena?”
english:
The sinners in Zion are terrified;
    trembling grips the godless:
“Who of us can dwell with the consuming fire?
    Who of us can dwell with everlasting burning?”

twi: Nea ɔnantew trenee muna odi nokwarenea ɔpo mfaso a asisi de bana onnye adanmude,nea ontie awudi ho pɔwbɔnea ɔmpɛ sɛ ohu bɔneyɛ ho agyinatu,
english:
Those who walk righteously
    and speak what is right,
who reject gain from extortion
    and keep their hands from accepting bribes,
who stop their ears against plots of murder
    and shut their eyes against contemplating evil—

twi: saa onipa yi na ɔbɛtena ɔsorosoro hɔ,ne guankɔbea bɛyɛ bepɔw aban no.Wɔde nʼaduan bɛma nona ne nsu remmɔ no.
english:
they are the ones who will dwell on the heights,
    whose refuge will be the mountain fortress.
Their bread will be supplied,
    and water will not fail them.

twi: Mo ani behu ɔhene no wɔ nʼanuonyam muna ahwɛ asase a ɛtrɛw kɔ akyirikyiri no.
english:
Your eyes will see the king in his beauty
    and view a land that stretches afar.

twi: Mo adwennwen mu, mobɛbooboo nea na ohunahuna mo no ho:“Odwumayɛni panyin no wɔ he?Nea na ogyigye tow no wɔ he?Nea na ɔhwɛ abantenten so no wɔ he?”
english:
In your thoughts you will ponder the former terror:
    “Where is that chief officer?
Where is the one who took the revenue?
    Where is the officer in charge of the towers?”

twi: Morenhu saa ahantanfo no bio,wɔn a wɔn kasa mu nna hɔ,na monte nea wɔka no ase no.
english:
You will see those arrogant people no more,
    people whose speech is obscure,
    whose language is strange and incomprehensible.

twi: Monhwɛ Sion, yɛn afahyɛ kuropɔn no;mo ani behu Yerusalem,asomdwoe tenabea, ntamadan a wontutu;wɔrentutu ne nnyinaso da,na wɔrentetew ne ntampehama mu nso.
Ɛhɔ na Awurade bɛyɛ yɛn Tumfo.Ɛbɛyɛ sɛ faako a nsu akɛse ne nsuwansuwa wɔ.Akorow a wɔhare remfa soahyɛn akɛse rennantew so.
english:
There the Lord will be our Mighty One.
    It will be like a place of broad rivers and streams.
No galley with oars will ride them,
    no mighty ship will sail them.

twi: Na Awurade ne yɛn temmufo,Awurade ne yɛn mmarahyɛfo,Awurade ne yɛn hene;na ɔno na obegye yɛn nkwa.
english:
For the Lord is our judge,
    the Lord is our lawgiver,
the Lord is our king;
    it is he who will save us.

twi: Wo ntampehama mu agowenti hyɛn dua no nni nnyinaso,na wɔntrɛw hyɛn so ntama no mu.Afei wɔbɛkyɛ asade bebree no muna mpakye mpo bɛsoa asade akɔ.
english:
Your rigging hangs loose:
    The mast is not held secure,
    the sail is not spread.
Then an abundance of spoils will be divided
    and even the lame will carry off plunder.

twi: Obiara nni Sion a ɔbɛka se, “Meyare;”na wɔde wɔn a wɔte hɔ no bɔne bɛkyɛ wɔn.
english:
No one living in Zion will say, “I am ill”;
    and the sins of those who dwell there will be forgiven.

twi: Atemmu A Etia Amanaman NoMuntwiw mmɛn, mo amanaman, na muntie;monyɛ aso, mo ɔmanfo!Momma asase ne nea ɛwɔ so nyinaa ntie,wiase ne nea efi mu ba nyinaa!
english:
Come near, you nations, and listen;
    pay attention, you peoples!
Let the earth hear, and all that is in it,
    the world, and all that comes out of it!

twi: Awurade bo afuw amanaman nyinaa;nʼabufuwhyew no tia wɔn asraafo nyinaa.Ɔbɛsɛe wɔn pasaa,ɔbɛma wɔakunkum wɔn.
english:
The Lord is angry with all nations;
    his wrath is on all their armies.
He will totally destroy them,
    he will give them over to slaughter.

twi: Wɔbɛtow wɔn mu atɔfo no agu,wɔn afunu no beyi hua;wɔn mogya afɔw mmepɔw no.
Ɔsoro nsoromma nyinaa bɛyerana wɔbɛbobɔw ɔsoro te sɛ nhoma mmobɔwee;ɔsoro atumfo bɛhwe asesɛnea nhaban tew fi bobe so,sɛnea mman a awo pan fi borɔdɔma dua ho.
english:
All the stars in the sky will be dissolved
    and the heavens rolled up like a scroll;
all the starry host will fall
    like withered leaves from the vine,
    like shriveled figs from the fig tree.

twi: Mʼafoa anom nea ɛmee no no wɔ ɔsoro;hwɛ, ɛresian de atemmu aba Edom so,wɔn a masɛe wɔn koraa no.
Mogya aguare Awurade afoa ho,wɔde srade asra ho,nguantenmma ne mmirekyi mogya,adwennini asaabo mu srade.Awurade wɔ afɔre bi bɔ wɔ Bosrane okum kɛse wɔ Edom.
english:
The sword of the Lord is bathed in blood,
    it is covered with fat—
the blood of lambs and goats,
    fat from the kidneys of rams.
For the Lord has a sacrifice in Bozrah
    and a great slaughter in the land of Edom.

twi: Anantwi anuɔdenfo ne wɔn bɛtotɔ,anantwinini nketewa ne akɛse.Mogya afɔw wɔn asase no,na srade ayɛ so dɔte no sɔkyee.
english:
And the wild oxen will fall with them,
    the bull calves and the great bulls.
Their land will be drenched with blood,
    and the dust will be soaked with fat.

twi: Na Awurade wɔ aweretɔ daananmuhyɛ afe, a obedi ama Sion.
english:
For the Lord has a day of vengeance,
    a year of retribution, to uphold Zion’s cause.

twi: Edom nsuwansuwa bɛdan agodibea,ne dɔte bɛdan sufre a ɛdɛwnʼasase bɛyɛ agoprama a ɛdɛw!
Ɛrennum awia anaa anadwo;ne wusiw befi a ɛto rentwa da.Ɛbɛda mpan fi awo ntoatoaso akosi awo ntoatoaso;obiara remfa ho bio koraa.
Nweatam so patu ne ɔbonsamnomabegye hɔ afa;patu ne kwaakwaadabi bɛtena hɔ.Onyankopɔn bɛtwe wɔ Edom sobasabasayɛ susuhamane amamfoyɛ kirebennyɛ susudua.
english:
The desert owl and screech owl will possess it;
    the great owl and the raven will nest there.
God will stretch out over Edom
    the measuring line of chaos
    and the plumb line of desolation.

twi: Nʼatitiriw rennya biribiara a ɛbɛma wɔafrɛ no ahenni,nʼahenemma mmarima nyinaa betu ayera.
english:
Her nobles will have nothing there to be called a kingdom,
    all her princes will vanish away.

twi: Nsɔe begye nʼabankɛse afa,nsansono ne nsɔe befuw wɔ nʼabankɛse hɔ.Hɔ bɛyɛ adompo atu,ne mpatu tenabea.
english:
Thorns will overrun her citadels,
    nettles and brambles her strongholds.
She will become a haunt for jackals,
    a home for owls.

twi: Nweatam so mmoa ne mpataku behyia adi afra,mmirekyi anuɔdenfo besu akyerɛ wɔn ho wɔn ho;hɔ na anadwommoa bɛdedana wɔde ayɛ wɔn homebea.
english:
Desert creatures will meet with hyenas,
    and wild goats will bleat to each other;
there the night creatures will also lie down
    and find for themselves places of rest.

twi: Ɛhɔ na patu bɛyɛ ne berebuw, na watow ne nkesua.Obesow ne mma, na ɔde ne ntaban akata wɔn so;ɛhɔ na nkorɔma bɛboaboa wɔn ho ano,obiara ne nea ɔka ne ho.
english:
The owl will nest there and lay eggs,
    she will hatch them, and care for her young
    under the shadow of her wings;
there also the falcons will gather,
    each with its mate.

twi: Hwɛ Awurade nhoma mmobɔwee no mu, na kenkan:Eyinom mu biara renyera,obiara benya nea ɔka ne ho.Efisɛ nʼanom na ɔhyɛ asɛm no fi,na ne honhom bɛboaboa wɔn ano.
english:
Look in the scroll of the Lord and read:
None of these will be missing,
    not one will lack her mate.
For it is his mouth that has given the order,
    and his Spirit will gather them together.

twi: Ɔde wɔn kyɛfa ma wɔn;ɔde ne nsa yɛ susudua kyekyɛ.Wɔbɛfa no sɛ wɔn de afebɔɔna wofi awo ntoatoaso akosi awo ntoatoaso atena hɔ.
english:
He allots their portions;
    his hand distributes them by measure.
They will possess it forever
    and dwell there from generation to generation.

twi: Wɔn A Wɔagye Wɔn No AhosɛpɛwNweatam ne asase a awo no ani begye;sare bedi ahurusi na ayɛ frɔmfrɔm.Te sɛ nhwiren no,
ɛbɛpae ayɛ fɛfɛɛfɛebedi ahurusi na ɛde anigye ateɛ mu,wɔde Lebanon anuonyam bɛma noKarmel ne Saron ahoɔfɛ;wobehu Awurade anuonyam,yɛn Nyankopɔn tumi no.
Hyɛ nsa a emu agow no mu den,hyɛ nkotodwe a ahodwow no mu den;
english:
Strengthen the feeble hands,
    steady the knees that give way;

twi: Ka kyerɛ wɔn a wɔn koma atu no se,“Monhyɛ mo ho den, na munnsuro;mo Nyankopɔn bɛba,ɔde aweretɔ bɛba;ananmuhyɛ a efi ɔsorobɛba abegye mo nkwa.”
Ɛno na wobebue anifuraefo ani,na wɔama asotifo aso ate asɛm.
english:
Then will the eyes of the blind be opened
    and the ears of the deaf unstopped.

twi: Ɛno na mpakye behuruw te sɛ ɔforote,na mum tɛkrɛma de anigye ateɛ mu.Nsu betue wɔ sare so,na nsuwansuwa apue wɔ nweatam so.
english:
Then will the lame leap like a deer,
    and the mute tongue shout for joy.
Water will gush forth in the wilderness
    and streams in the desert.

twi: Nwea a so yɛ hyew no bɛdan ɔtare,na nsuwansuwa atue wɔ asase wosee so.Atu a anka sakraman te mu no,ɛhɔ na sare ne demmire ne paparɔso befifi.
english:
The burning sand will become a pool,
    the thirsty ground bubbling springs.
In the haunts where jackals once lay,
    grass and reeds and papyrus will grow.

twi: Na ɔtempɔn bɛda hɔ;wɔbɛfrɛ no Ahotefo Kwan.Wɔn a wɔn ho ntew rentu kwan wɔ so;ɛbɛda hɔ ama wɔn a wɔnantew saa Kwan no so;amumɔyɛfo nkwaseafo rennantenantew so.
Gyata biara rentena hɔ,na akekaboa biara rensi so;wɔrenhu wɔn wɔ hɔ.Na wɔn a wɔagye wɔn nko ara na wɔbɛfa so,
english:
No lion will be there,
    nor any ravenous beast;
    they will not be found there.
But only the redeemed will walk there,

twi: na wɔn a Awurade agye wɔn no bɛsan aba.Wɔde nnwonto bɛhyɛn Sion;anigye a ɛnsa da bɛyɛ wɔn ahenkyɛw.Wobenya anigye ne ahosɛpɛw mmoroso,na awerɛhow ne apinisi beguan akɔ.
english:
and those the Lord has rescued will return.
They will enter Zion with singing;
    everlasting joy will crown their heads.
Gladness and joy will overtake them,
    and sorrow and sighing will flee away.

twi: Sanaherib Hunahuna YerusalemƆhene Hesekia adedi mfe dunan so no, Asiriahene Sanaherib bɛtow hyɛɛ Yuda nkuropɔn a wɔabɔ ho ban no so dii so.
english: In the fourteenth year of King Hezekiah’s reign, Sennacherib king of Assyria attacked all the fortified cities of Judah and captured them.

twi: Afei Asiriahene somaa nʼananmusifo fi Lakis a asraafo dɔm kɛse ka ne ho kohyiaa Ɔhene Hesekia wɔ Yerusalem. Bere a ɔsahene begyinaa nsudorobɛn bi a efi Atifi Tare de kɔ Ntamahorofo Atenae hɔ no,
english: Then the king of Assyria sent his field commander with a large army from Lachish to King Hezekiah at Jerusalem. When the commander stopped at the aqueduct of the Upper Pool, on the road to the Launderer’s Field,

twi: Hilkia babarima Eliakim a na ɔhwɛ ahemfi no ntotoe so; Sebna a na ɔyɛ ɔkyerɛwfo ne Asaf babarima Yoa a na ɔno nso yɛ ɔkyerɛwfo kohyiaa no.
english: Eliakim son of Hilkiah the palace administrator, Shebna the secretary, and Joah son of Asaph the recorder went out to him.

twi: Na ɔsahene no ka kyerɛɛ wɔn se, “Monka nkyerɛ Hesekia se,“ ‘Asɛm a otumfo, Asiriahene ka ni: Dɛn na wode wo ho to so a ɛma wugye wo ho di saa?
english:
The field commander said to them, “Tell Hezekiah:
“‘This is what the great king, the king of Assyria, says: On what are you basing this confidence of yours?

twi: Woka se wowɔ akodi ho nyansa ne nʼahoɔden, nanso woka nsɛm hunu. Hena na ɔtaa wʼakyi a enti wotew mʼanim atua?
