english: You say you have counsel and might for war—but you speak only empty words. On whom are you depending, that you rebel against me?

twi: Hwɛ wʼani da Misraim so, demmire a emu abu a ɛte sɛ pema a wutweri a ɛbɛwɔ wo nsa mu apira wo no! Saa na Misraimhene Farao te ma wɔn a wɔde wɔn ho to ne so no nyinaa.
english: Look, I know you are depending on Egypt, that splintered reed of a staff, which pierces the hand of anyone who leans on it! Such is Pharaoh king of Egypt to all who depend on him.

twi: Ebia wobɛka se, “Yɛde yɛn ho to Awurade, yɛn Nyankopɔn so!” Ɛnyɛ ɔno na ɔhene Hesekia atutu nʼabosonnan ne afɔremuka nyinaa, ahyɛ Yudafo sɛ wɔnsom wɔ afɔremuka a ɛwɔ Yerusalem ha nko ara so no?
english: But if you say to me, “We are depending on the Lord our God”—isn’t he the one whose high places and altars Hezekiah removed, saying to Judah and Jerusalem, “You must worship before this altar”?

twi: “ ‘Mɛka asɛm bi akyerɛ wo! Me wura Asiriahene ne wo bɛyɛ nhyehyɛe bi. Sɛ wubenya apɔnkɔsotefo mpenu, afi wo asraafo mu a, ɔbɛma wɔn apɔnkɔ mpenu ama wɔatenatena wɔn so.
english: “‘Come now, make a bargain with my master, the king of Assyria: I will give you two thousand horses—if you can put riders on them!

twi: Na wʼasraafo ketewa sɛɛ yi, ɛbɛyɛ dɛn na woaso dae, sɛ wubetumi ne me wura asraafo no mu fa bi a wɔyɛ mmerɛw no mpo adi asi. Minim sɛ wode wo ho ato Misraim nteaseɛnam ne apɔnkɔsotefo mmoa so.
english: How then can you repulse one officer of the least of my master’s officials, even though you are depending on Egypt for chariots and horsemen?

twi: Bio, wugye di sɛ, maba sɛ merebɛtow ahyɛ asase yi so asɛe no kwa a Awurade nsa nni mu? Awurade ankasa ka kyerɛɛ me se menkɔko ntia saa asase yi na mensɛe no.’ ”
english: Furthermore, have I come to attack and destroy this land without the Lord? The Lord himself told me to march against this country and destroy it.’”

twi: Na Eliakim, Sebna ne Yoa ka kyerɛɛ ɔsahene no se, “Yɛsrɛ mo, monka Arameike kasa nkyerɛ mo asomfo, efisɛ, yɛte ase yiye. Monnka Hebri na nnipa a wɔwɔ ɔfasu no so no bɛte ase.”
english: Then Eliakim, Shebna and Joah said to the field commander, “Please speak to your servants in Aramaic, since we understand it. Don’t speak to us in Hebrew in the hearing of the people on the wall.”

twi: Na Senaherib nanmusini no buae se, “Me wura pɛ sɛ obiara a ɔwɔ Yerusalem te saa asɛm yi, na ɛnyɛ mo nko. Ɔpɛ sɛ wɔte sɛ, sɛ moamma mo nsa so a, wobetua kuropɔn yi. Ɔkɔm ne osukɔm werɛmfo bɛde nkurɔfo no ara kosi sɛ, wobedi wɔn ara agyanan, anom wɔn dwonsɔ.”
english: But the commander replied, “Was it only to your master and you that my master sent me to say these things, and not to the people sitting on the wall—who, like you, will have to eat their own excrement and drink their own urine?”

twi: Afei ɔsahene no sɔre gyina kasaa wɔ Hebri mu se, “Muntie saa nkra yi a efi ɔhempɔn, Asiriahene nkyɛn no!
english: Then the commander stood and called out in Hebrew, “Hear the words of the great king, the king of Assyria!

twi: Sɛnea ɔhene no se ni: Mommma Hesekia nnaadaa mo. Ɔrentumi nnye mo!
english: This is what the king says: Do not let Hezekiah deceive you. He cannot deliver you!

twi: Mommma Hesekia mfa saa asɛm a ɔkae se, ‘Awurade begye yɛn! Wɔremfa saa kurow yi mma Asiriahene’ no mma mo tirim nyɛ mo dɛ.
english: Do not let Hezekiah persuade you to trust in the Lord when he says, ‘The Lord will surely deliver us; this city will not be given into the hand of the king of Assyria.’

twi: “Munntie Hesekia. Nea Asiriahene ka ni: Mo ne me nyɛ asomdwoe nhyehyɛe na mommra me nkyɛn. Na afei, mɛma mo mu biara adi ɔno ankasa bobe ne borɔdɔma na woanom nsu afi ɔno ankasa abura mu,
english: “Do not listen to Hezekiah. This is what the king of Assyria says: Make peace with me and come out to me. Then each of you will eat fruit from your own vine and fig tree and drink water from your own cistern,

twi: kosi sɛ mɛba abɛfa mo akɔ asase a ɛte sɛ mo de yi so, awi ne nsa foforo asase, aduan ne bobe mfuw asase.
english: until I come and take you to a land like your own—a land of grain and new wine, a land of bread and vineyards.

twi: “Mommma Hesekia nka se, ‘Awurade begye yɛn,’ mfa nnaadaa mo. Ɔman bi so nyame atumi agye ne man afi Asiriahene nsam pɛn ana?
english: “Do not let Hezekiah mislead you when he says, ‘The Lord will deliver us.’ Have the gods of any nations ever delivered their lands from the hand of the king of Assyria?

twi: Ɛhe na Hamat ne Arpad anyame no wɔ? Na Sefarwaim anyame no nso wɔ he? Wɔagye Samaria afi me nsam ana?
english: Where are the gods of Hamath and Arpad? Where are the gods of Sepharvaim? Have they rescued Samaria from my hand?

twi: Ɔman bɛn so nyame na watumi agye ne manfo afi me tumi ase? Na afei ɛbɛyɛ dɛn na Awurade betumi agye Yerusalem afi me nsam.”
english: Who of all the gods of these countries have been able to save their lands from me? How then can the Lord deliver Jerusalem from my hand?”

twi: Na nnipa no yɛɛ komm a wɔamma mmuae biara, efisɛ na Hesekia aka akyerɛ wɔn se wɔnnkasa.
english: But the people remained silent and said nothing in reply, because the king had commanded, “Do not answer him.”

twi: Afei Hilkia babarima Eliakim a na ɔhwɛ ahemfi no ntotoe so, Sebna a na ɔyɛ ɔkyerɛwfo ne Asaf babarima Yoa a ɔno nso yɛ ɔkyerɛwfo kɔɔ Hesekia nkyɛn a wɔasunsuane wɔn ntade mu, kɔkaa nea ɔsahene no aka akyerɛ no no.
english: Then Eliakim son of Hilkiah the palace administrator, Shebna the secretary and Joah son of Asaph the recorder went to Hezekiah, with their clothes torn, and told him what the field commander had said.

twi: Wɔhyɛ Yerusalem Gye Ho NkɔmBere a ɔhene Hesekia tee eyinom no, osunsuan ne ntade mu, na ofuraa atweaatam, na ɔkɔɔ Awurade asɔredan mu.
english: When King Hezekiah heard this, he tore his clothes and put on sackcloth and went into the temple of the Lord.

twi: Na ɔsomaa Eliakim a ɔhwɛ ahemfi ntotoe so, Sebna, a ɔyɛ ɔkyerɛwfo ne asɔfo akunini a wɔn nyinaa furafura atweaatam, kɔɔ Amos babarima Odiyifo Yesaia nkyɛn.
english: He sent Eliakim the palace administrator, Shebna the secretary, and the leading priests, all wearing sackcloth, to the prophet Isaiah son of Amoz.

twi: Wɔka kyerɛɛ no se, “Sɛnea ɔhene Hesekia ka ni: Saa da yi yɛ ɔhaw, animka ne animguase da. Ayɛ te sɛ nea mmofra awo du so, na ahoɔden a wɔde bɛwo wɔn nni hɔ.
english: They told him, “This is what Hezekiah says: This day is a day of distress and rebuke and disgrace, as when children come to the moment of birth and there is no strength to deliver them.

twi: Nanso ebia Awurade, mo Nyankopɔn ate sɛ Asiria nanmusini no regu Onyankopɔn teasefo no anim ase, na wɔbɛtwe nʼaso wɔ ne nsɛnkeka no ho. Enti bɔ mpae ma yɛn a yɛaka no!”
english: It may be that the Lord your God will hear the words of the field commander, whom his master, the king of Assyria, has sent to ridicule the living God, and that he will rebuke him for the words the Lord your God has heard. Therefore pray for the remnant that still survives.”

twi: Bere a Ɔhene Hesekia mpanyimfo no de ɔhene no nkra brɛɛ Yesaia no,
english: When King Hezekiah’s officials came to Isaiah,

twi: Yesaia ka kyerɛɛ wɔn se, “Ka kyerɛ wo wura se, ‘Sɛnea Awurade se ni: Mma abususɛm a Asiriahene asomafo no ka tiaa me no nhaw wo.
english: Isaiah said to them, “Tell your master, ‘This is what the Lord says: Do not be afraid of what you have heard—those words with which the underlings of the king of Assyria have blasphemed me.

twi: Muntie! Mede honhom bi rebɛhyɛ ne mu, sɛnea ɛbɛyɛ a sɛ ɔte asɛm bi a ɔbɛsan akɔ ne man mu na hɔ na mɛma wɔde afoa akum no.’ ”
english: Listen! When he hears a certain report, I will make him want to return to his own country, and there I will have him cut down with the sword.’”

twi: Bere a ɔsahene no tee sɛ Asiriahene afi Lakis no, ɔsan nʼakyi kohuu sɛ ɔhene no ne Libna reko.
english: When the field commander heard that the king of Assyria had left Lachish, he withdrew and found the king fighting against Libnah.

twi: Ankyɛ, ɔhene Sanaherib nyaa nkra se, Tirhaka Etiopiani a ɔyɛ Misraimhene di asraafo anim rebɛko atia no. Bere a ɔtee no, ɔsomaa abɔfo kɔɔ Hesekia nkyɛn de nkra kɔmaa no se,
english: Now Sennacherib received a report that Tirhakah, the king of Cush, was marching out to fight against him. When he heard it, he sent messengers to Hezekiah with this word:

twi: “Monka nkyerɛ Yudahene Hesekia se: Mma onyame a wode wo ho ato no so no nnaadaa mo nka se, ‘Wɔremfa Yerusalem mma Asiriahene.’
english: “Say to Hezekiah king of Judah: Do not let the god you depend on deceive you when he says, ‘Jerusalem will not be given into the hands of the king of Assyria.’

twi: Moate nea Asiria ahemfo ayɛ amanaman no nyinaa. Wɔasɛe wɔn pasaa. Na mo de, wobegye mo ana?
english: Surely you have heard what the kings of Assyria have done to all the countries, destroying them completely. And will you be delivered?

twi: Anyame a wɔwɔ aman a me nenanom sɛee wɔn no, aman te sɛ, Gosan, Haran, Resef ne Edenfo a na wɔwɔ Talasar no anyame gyee wɔn ana?
english: Did the gods of the nations that were destroyed by my predecessors deliver them—the gods of Gozan, Harran, Rezeph and the people of Eden who were in Tel Assar?

twi: Nsɛm bɛn na ɛtotoo Hamathene ne Arpadhene? Nsɛm bɛn nso na ɛtotoo Sefarwaim, Hena ne Iwa ahemfo?”
english: Where is the king of Hamath or the king of Arpad? Where are the kings of Lair, Sepharvaim, Hena and Ivvah?”

twi: Hesekia MpaebɔHesekia nsa kaa krataa a abɔfo no de bae no, ɔkenkanee. Afei ɔforo kɔɔ Awurade asɔredan no mu kɔtrɛw mu wɔ Awurade anim.
english: Hezekiah received the letter from the messengers and read it. Then he went up to the temple of the Lord and spread it out before the Lord.

twi: Na Hesekia bɔɔ mpae kyerɛɛ Awurade se,
english: And Hezekiah prayed to the Lord:

twi: “Asafo Awurade, Israel Nyankopɔn a wɔasi wo hene wɔ Kerubim ntam. Wo nko ara na woyɛ Onyankopɔn wɔ asase so ahenni nyinaa so. Wo na wobɔɔ ɔsoro ne asase.
english: “Lord Almighty, the God of Israel, enthroned between the cherubim, you alone are God over all the kingdoms of the earth. You have made heaven and earth.

twi: Brɛ wʼaso ase, Awurade, na tie! Bue wʼani, Awurade, na hwɛ. Tie nsɛm a Sanaherib asoma de abɛsopa Onyankopɔn teasefo no.
english: Give ear, Lord, and hear; open your eyes, Lord, and see; listen to all the words Sennacherib has sent to ridicule the living God.

twi: “Awurade, ɛyɛ nokware sɛ Asiria ahemfo asɛe aman yi nyinaa, sɛnea nkra no ka no.
english: “It is true, Lord, that the Assyrian kings have laid waste all these peoples and their lands.

twi: Na wɔatow anyame a wɔwɔ saa aman yi so no agu gya mu, ahyew wɔn, efisɛ wɔnyɛ anyame, na mmom wɔyɛ nnua ne abo a nnipa de wɔn nsa ayɛ.
english: They have thrown their gods into the fire and destroyed them, for they were not gods but only wood and stone, fashioned by human hands.

twi: Afei Awurade, yɛn Nyankopɔn, gye yɛn fi ne nsam, na ama ahenni a ɛwɔ asase so nyinaa ahu sɛ, wo nko ara, Awurade, ne Onyankopɔn.”
english: Now, Lord our God, deliver us from his hand, so that all the kingdoms of the earth may know that you, Lord, are the only God.”

twi: Sanaherib AsehweNa Amos babarima Yesaia de saa nkra yi kɔmaa Hesekia se, “Sɛɛ na Awurade, Israel Nyankopɔn se: Esiane sɛ woabɔ me mpae afa Asiriahene Sanaherib ho nti,
english: Then Isaiah son of Amoz sent a message to Hezekiah: “This is what the Lord, the God of Israel, says: Because you have prayed to me concerning Sennacherib king of Assyria,

twi: eyi ne asɛm a Awurade aka atia no:“Ɔbabeabun Sion sopa wo,na ɔserew wo.Ɔbabea Yerusalem di wo ho fɛw,na ɔwosow ne ti bere a woreguan.
english:
this is the word the Lord has spoken against him:
“Virgin Daughter Zion
    despises and mocks you.
Daughter Jerusalem
    tosses her head as you flee.

twi: Hena na wugye di sɛ woyeyaw no, di ne ho fɛw nso?Hena na womaa wo nne so tiaa nona wohwɛɛ no ahantan so?Ɛyɛ Israel ɔkronkronni no!
english:
Who is it you have ridiculed and blasphemed?
    Against whom have you raised your voice
and lifted your eyes in pride?
    Against the Holy One of Israel!

twi: Wonam wʼasomafo soadi Awurade ho fɛw.Na woaka se,‘Me nteaseɛnam dodow ntimaforo mmepɔw atenten.Yiw Lebanon mmepɔw a ɛwoware pa ara no.Matwitwa ne sida atenten no,ne nʼapepaw a ɛyɛ fɛ no agu fam.Madu ne mmepɔw a ɛwɔ akyirikyiri no so,ne ne kwaeberentuw mu.
english:
By your messengers
    you have ridiculed the Lord.
And you have said,
    ‘With my many chariots
I have ascended the heights of the mountains,
    the utmost heights of Lebanon.
I have cut down its tallest cedars,
    the choicest of its junipers.
I have reached its remotest heights,
    the finest of its forests.

twi: Matutu mmura wɔ ahɔho nsase bebree sode ne nsu pa no adwudwo me ho.Mpo, mepaee Misraim nsubɔnten musɛnea mʼakofo betumi atwa!’
english:
I have dug wells in foreign lands
    and drunk the water there.
With the soles of my feet
    I have dried up all the streams of Egypt.’

twi: “Na Montee ɛ?Bere tenten a atwam, na mehyɛ too hɔ.Bere bi a atwam no na medwenee ho;afei mama aba mu sɛ,moadan ɔman a mosɛe nkuropɔn a wɔabɔho ban.
english:
“Have you not heard?
    Long ago I ordained it.
In days of old I planned it;
    now I have brought it to pass,
that you have turned fortified cities
    into piles of stone.

twi: Wɔn nkurɔfo a tumi afi wɔn nsa noho adwiriw wɔn, na animguase aka wɔn.Wɔte sɛ afuw so nnua,ne afifide foforo a ɛyɛ mmrɛw.Wɔte sɛ sare a efifi ɔdan atifia ɛhyew ansa na anyin.
english:
Their people, drained of power,
    are dismayed and put to shame.
They are like plants in the field,
    like tender green shoots,
like grass sprouting on the roof,
    scorched before it grows up.

twi: “Nanso minim nea wotebere a woba ne bere a wokɔne sɛnea wo bo huru tia me.
english:
“But I know where you are
    and when you come and go
    and how you rage against me.

twi: Na esiane sɛ wo bo huru tia mena wʼahantan adu mʼasom nti,mede me darewa bɛhyɛ wo hwenem,na mede akwankyerɛ dade ahyɛ wʼanom,mɛma wo afa ɔkwan a wofaa so bae no soasan wʼakyi.
english:
Because you rage against me
    and because your insolence has reached my ears,
I will put my hook in your nose
    and my bit in your mouth,
and I will make you return
    by the way you came.

twi: “Eyi na ɛbɛyɛ nsɛnkyerɛnne ama wo, Hesekia:“Saa afe yi wubedi nea ɛno ankasa fifii.Afe a ɛto so abien no, wubedi nea efi mu ba.Nanso afe a ɛto so abiɛsa no de, wo ara dua na twa,yɛ bobe nturo na di so aba.
english:
“This will be the sign for you, Hezekiah:
“This year you will eat what grows by itself,
    and the second year what springs from that.
But in the third year sow and reap,
    plant vineyards and eat their fruit.

twi: Bio, nkae bi a ofi Yuda fibegye ntin wɔ fam na wasow aba wɔ soro.
english:
Once more a remnant of the kingdom of Judah
    will take root below and bear fruit above.

twi: Na nkae bi befi Yerusalem aba,na nkae dɔm afi Bepɔw Sion so.Asafo Awurade pɛ mu na eyi bɛyɛ.
english:
For out of Jerusalem will come a remnant,
    and out of Mount Zion a band of survivors.
The zeal of the Lord Almighty
    will accomplish this.

twi: “Eyi ne asɛm a Awurade ka fa Asiriahene ho:“Ɔrenhyɛn saa kuropɔn yi muna ɔrentow bɛmma wɔ ha.Ɔremfa nkatabo mmegyina kuropɔn no akyina ɔrensi pie ntua nʼano.
english:
“Therefore this is what the Lord says concerning the king of Assyria:
“He will not enter this city
    or shoot an arrow here.
He will not come before it with shield
    or build a siege ramp against it.

twi: Ɔhene no kwan a ɔfaa so bae no ara so na ɔbɛsan afa akɔ nʼankasa man mu.”Awurade ka se,“Ɔrenwura saa kurow yi mu.
Esiane mʼankasa mʼanuonyam ne mʼakoa Dawid nti,mɛbɔ ho ban.”
english:
“I will defend this city and save it,
    for my sake and for the sake of David my servant!”

twi: Afei Awurade bɔfo fii adi na okunkum asraafo mpem ɔha aduɔwɔtwe anum wɔ Asiria nsraban mu. Bere a nnipa no sɔree anɔpa no, wohuu sɛ amu gugu baabiara!
english: Then the angel of the Lord went out and put to death a hundred and eighty-five thousand in the Assyrian camp. When the people got up the next morning—there were all the dead bodies!

twi: Enti Asiriahene Sanaherib pɔn nʼakofo. Ɔsan kɔɔ Ninewe kɔtenaa hɔ.
english: So Sennacherib king of Assyria broke camp and withdrew. He returned to Nineveh and stayed there.

twi: Da bi a na ɔresɔre ne nyame Nisrok wɔ abosonnan mu no, ne mma mmarima baanu, Adramelek ne Sareser de afoa kokum no, na woguan kɔɔ Ararat asase so. Na ne babarima Esarhadon bedii nʼade sɛ Asiriahene.
english: One day, while he was worshiping in the temple of his god Nisrok, his sons Adrammelek and Sharezer killed him with the sword, and they escaped to the land of Ararat. And Esarhaddon his son succeeded him as king.

twi: Hesekia YareSaa nna no mu no, Hesekia yaree owuyare, na Amos babarima Odiyifo Yesaia kɔɔ ne nkyɛn kɔkae se, “Sɛnea Awurade se ni: Toto wʼakwan yiye, efisɛ worebewu; na wo ho renyɛ wo den bio.”
english: In those days Hezekiah became ill and was at the point of death. The prophet Isaiah son of Amoz went to him and said, “This is what the Lord says: Put your house in order, because you are going to die; you will not recover.”

twi: Bere a Hesekia tee asɛm yi, otwaa nʼani hwɛɛ ɔfasu, bɔɔ Awurade mpae se,
english: Hezekiah turned his face to the wall and prayed to the Lord,

twi: “Kae, Awurade, sɛnea manantew wʼanim nokware mu na mede me koma ayɛ nea ɛfata wɔ wʼanim.” Na Hesekia suu bebree.
english: “Remember, Lord, how I have walked before you faithfully and with wholehearted devotion and have done what is good in your eyes.” And Hezekiah wept bitterly.

twi: Na saa asɛm yi fii Awurade nkyɛn kɔɔ Yesaia hɔ se,
english: Then the word of the Lord came to Isaiah:

twi: “San kɔ Hesekia nkyɛn, na kɔka kyerɛ no se, ‘Sɛɛ na Awurade, wʼagya Dawid Nyankopɔn, ka: Mate wo mpaebɔ no, na mahu wo nisu. Mede mfe dunum bɛka wo nkwanna ho.
english: “Go and tell Hezekiah, ‘This is what the Lord, the God of your father David, says: I have heard your prayer and seen your tears; I will add fifteen years to your life.

twi: Na megye wo ne kuropɔn yi afi Asiriahene nsam. Mɛbɔ kuropɔn yi ho ban.
english: And I will deliver you and this city from the hand of the king of Assyria. I will defend this city.

twi: “ ‘Na eyi ne nsɛnkyerɛnne a Awurade bɛyɛ de adi ho adanse sɛ, obedi ne bɔhyɛ so:
english: “‘This is the Lord’s sign to you that the Lord will do what he has promised:

twi: Mɛma owia ano sunsuma atwe akɔ nʼakyi anammɔn du wɔ Ahas antweri so.’ ” Ɛno nti, owiahyerɛn no kɔɔ nʼakyi anammɔn du.
english: I will make the shadow cast by the sun go back the ten steps it has gone down on the stairway of Ahaz.’” So the sunlight went back the ten steps it had gone down.

twi: Nea Yudahene Hesekia kyerɛw wɔ ne yare ne nʼayaresa akyi ni:
english: A writing of Hezekiah king of Judah after his illness and recovery:

twi: Mekae se, “Mʼasetena mu nnapa yi muɛsɛ sɛ mefa owu apon muna wogye me mfe a aka yi ana?”
english:
I said, “In the prime of my life
    must I go through the gates of death
    and be robbed of the rest of my years?”

twi: Mekae se, “Merenhu Awurade Nyankopɔn bioAwurade a ɔwɔ ateasefo asase so.Merenhu adesamma bio,anaa merenka wɔn a wɔte wiase yi ho bio.
english:
I said, “I will not again see the Lord himself
    in the land of the living;
no longer will I look on my fellow man,
    or be with those who now dwell in this world.

twi: Wɔadwiriw me fi agu agye afi me nsam,te sɛ, oguanhwɛfo ntamadan.Matwa me nkwa so sɛnea ɔnwemfotwa me fi asadua so;awia ne anadwo wutwaa me nkwa so.
english:
Like a shepherd’s tent my house
    has been pulled down and taken from me.
Like a weaver I have rolled up my life,
    and he has cut me off from the loom;
    day and night you made an end of me.

twi: Mede ntoboase twɛn kosii ahemadakye,nanso wɔbobɔɔ me nnompe mu te sɛ gyata;awia ne anadwo wutwaa me nkwa so.
Misuu sɛ asomfena anaa asukɔnkɔn;mitwaa adwo sɛ, aborɔnoma a ɔredi awerɛhow.Mʼani yɛɛ siamoo bere a mehwɛɛ soro.Mewɔ ɔhaw mu, Awurade, bra bɛboa me!”
english:
I cried like a swift or thrush,
    I moaned like a mourning dove.
My eyes grew weak as I looked to the heavens.
    I am being threatened; Lord, come to my aid!”

twi: Na dɛn na metumi aka?Wakasa akyerɛ me, na ɔno ankasa na wayɛ eyi.Mede ahobrɛase bɛnantew mʼasetena nyinaa mume kra ahoyeraw yi nti.
english:
But what can I say?
    He has spoken to me, and he himself has done this.
I will walk humbly all my years
    because of this anguish of my soul.

twi: Awurade, ɛnam saa nneɛma yi so na nnipa nya nkwana me honhom nso nya nkwa wɔ mu.Wode mʼakwahosan asan ama menam so ama manya nkwa.
english:
Lord, by such things people live;
    and my spirit finds life in them too.
You restored me to health
    and let me live.

twi: Yiw, ɛyɛ me yiyeyɛ ntina mekɔɔ saa ahoyeraw yi mu.Wo dɔ nti, wode me sieina mankɔ ɔsɛe amoa mu;na wode me bɔne nyinaa akyɛ me.
english:
Surely it was for my benefit
    that I suffered such anguish.
In your love you kept me
    from the pit of destruction;
you have put all my sins
    behind your back.

twi: Ɔda rentumi nkamfo wo;owu rentumi nto wo ayeyi nnwom;wɔn a wosian kɔ amoa mu norentumi nnya anidaso wɔ wo nokware mu bio.
english:
For the grave cannot praise you,
    death cannot sing your praise;
those who go down to the pit
    cannot hope for your faithfulness.

twi: Ateasefo nko na wobetumi akamfo wo,sɛnea mereyɛ nnɛ yi;agyanom ka wo nokwaredi ho asɛmkyerɛ wɔn mma.
english:
The living, the living—they praise you,
    as I am doing today;
parents tell their children
    about your faithfulness.

twi: Awurade begye me nkwa,na yɛde asanku bɛto nnwomyɛn nkwanna nyinaawɔ Awurade fi.
english:
The Lord will save me,
    and we will sing with stringed instruments
all the days of our lives
    in the temple of the Lord.

twi: Na Yesaia kae se, “Momfa borɔdɔma nyɛ nku mfa nsra pɔmpɔ no so, na ne ho bɛtɔ no.”
english: Isaiah had said, “Prepare a poultice of figs and apply it to the boil, and he will recover.”

twi: Na Hesekia bisae se, “Dɛn nsɛnkyerɛnne na ɛbɛda no adi sɛ, mɛkɔ Awurade asɔredan mu?”
english: Hezekiah had asked, “What will be the sign that I will go up to the temple of the Lord?”

twi: Asomafo A Wofi BabiloniaSaa bere no Merodak-Baladan a ɔyɛ Babiloniahene Baladan babarima soma ma wɔde krataa ne akyɛde kɔmaa Hesekia, efisɛ na wate sɛ wayare ama ne ho atɔ no.
english: At that time Marduk-Baladan son of Baladan king of Babylon sent Hezekiah letters and a gift, because he had heard of his illness and recovery.

twi: Hesekia gyee asomafo no fɛw so, na afei ɔde nea ɔwɔ wɔ ne adekoradan mu kyerɛɛ wɔn; dwetɛ, sikakɔkɔɔ, nnuhuam, ngohuam, nʼakode akorae ne biribiara a ɛka nʼademude ho. Biribiara nni nʼahemfi ne nʼahenni mu a Hesekia amfa ankyerɛ wɔn.
english: Hezekiah received the envoys gladly and showed them what was in his storehouses—the silver, the gold, the spices, the fine olive oil—his entire armory and everything found among his treasures. There was nothing in his palace or in all his kingdom that Hezekiah did not show them.

twi: Afei Odiyifo Yesaia kɔɔ ɔhene Hesekia nkyɛn, kobisaa no se, “Asɛm bɛn na saa mmarima no kae na he na wofi bae?”Hesekia buae se, “Wofi akyirikyiri asase bi so. Wofi Babilonia, na wɔbaa me nkyɛn.”
english:
Then Isaiah the prophet went to King Hezekiah and asked, “What did those men say, and where did they come from?”
“From a distant land,” Hezekiah replied. “They came to me from Babylon.”

twi: Odiyifo no bisae se, “Dɛn na wohuu wɔ wʼahemfi hɔ?”Hesekia buae se, “Wohuu biribiara a ɛwɔ mʼahemfi ha. Biribiara nni mʼademude mu a mamfa ankyerɛ wɔn.”
english:
The prophet asked, “What did they see in your palace?”
“They saw everything in my palace,” Hezekiah said. “There is nothing among my treasures that I did not show them.”

twi: Afei Yesaia ka kyerɛɛ Hesekia se, “Tie asɛm a efi Asafo Awurade nkyɛn:
english: Then Isaiah said to Hezekiah, “Hear the word of the Lord Almighty:

twi: Nokware, bere bi bɛba a, wɔbɛsoa biribiara a ɛwɔ wʼahemfi ne agyapade a wʼagyanom akora de abedu nnɛ no akɔ Babilonia. Biribiara renka, sɛɛ na Awurade se.
english: The time will surely come when everything in your palace, and all that your predecessors have stored up until this day, will be carried off to Babylon. Nothing will be left, says the Lord.

twi: Wʼankasa wʼasefo bi mpo, wɔbɛfa wɔn nnommum. Wɔbɛyɛ piamfo a wɔbɛsom wɔ Babiloniahene ahemfi.”
english: And some of your descendants, your own flesh and blood who will be born to you, will be taken away, and they will become eunuchs in the palace of the king of Babylon.”

twi: Na Hesekia ka kyerɛɛ Yesaia se, “Saa asɛm yi a efi Awurade nkyɛn a woaka akyerɛ me yi yɛ asɛm papa.” Nanso na ɔhene no redwene sɛ, ne bere so de, obenya asomdwoe ne bammɔ.
english: “The word of the Lord you have spoken is good,” Hezekiah replied. For he thought, “There will be peace and security in my lifetime.”

twi: Onyankopɔn Nkurɔfo AwerɛkyekyeMonkyekye, monkyekye me nkurɔfo werɛ.Saa na mo Nyankopɔn se.
english:
Comfort, comfort my people,
    says your God.

twi: Monka asomdwoesɛm nkyerɛ Yerusalem,na mompae mu nka nkyerɛ no sene som dennen no aba awiei,wɔatua ne bɔne no so ka,na wɔanya ne bɔne nyinaa so akatua mmɔhoafi Awurade nsam.
english:
Speak tenderly to Jerusalem,
    and proclaim to her
that her hard service has been completed,
    that her sin has been paid for,
that she has received from the Lord’s hand
    double for all her sins.

twi: Nne bi reteɛ mu se,“Munsiesie ɔkwan mma Awuradewɔ nweatam no so.Monteɛ ɔtempɔn wɔ sare no somma yɛn Nyankopɔn.
english:
A voice of one calling:
“In the wilderness prepare
    the way for the Lord;
make straight in the desert
    a highway for our God.

twi: Obon biara bɛyɛ ma,bepɔw ne nkoko nyinaa bɛkɔ fam,asase a ɛyɛ abonkyiabonkyi no bɛyɛ tamaa,na mmeae a ɛyɛ akɔntɔnkye no ayɛ tataw.
english:
Every valley shall be raised up,
    every mountain and hill made low;
the rough ground shall become level,
    the rugged places a plain.

twi: Na Awurade anuonyam bɛda adi,na nnipa nyinaa behu.Efisɛ Awurade na waka!”
english:
And the glory of the Lord will be revealed,
    and all people will see it together.
For the mouth of the Lord has spoken.”

twi: Nne bi kae se, “Teɛ mu.”Na mekae se, “Menteɛ mu nka dɛn?”“Nnipa nyinaa te sɛ sare,na wɔn anuonyam nyinaa te sɛ afuw so nhwiren.
english:
A voice says, “Cry out.”
    And I said, “What shall I cry?”
“All people are like grass,
    and all their faithfulness is like the flowers of the field.

twi: Sare hyew, na nhwiren twintwamefisɛ Awurade ahomegu fa wɔn so.Nokware, nnipa no yɛ sare.
english:
The grass withers and the flowers fall,
    because the breath of the Lord blows on them.
    Surely the people are grass.

twi: Sare hyew, na nhwiren twintwam,nanso yɛn Nyankopɔn asɛm no tim hɔ daa.”
english:
The grass withers and the flowers fall,
    but the word of our God endures forever.”

twi: Wo a wode asɛm pa reba Sion,foro kɔ bepɔw tenten bi so.Wo a wode asɛm pa reba Yerusalem,ma wo nne so na teɛ mu,ma so, nsuro;ka kyerɛ Yuda nkurow se,“Mo Nyankopɔn ni!”
english:
You who bring good news to Zion,
    go up on a high mountain.
You who bring good news to Jerusalem,
    lift up your voice with a shout,
lift it up, do not be afraid;
    say to the towns of Judah,
    “Here is your God!”

twi: Hwɛ, Asafo Awurade de tumi reba,na nʼabasa bedi hene ama no.Hwɛ, nʼakatua ka ne ho,na ɔde nʼabasobɔde nam.
english:
See, the Sovereign Lord comes with power,
    and he rules with a mighty arm.
See, his reward is with him,
    and his recompense accompanies him.

twi: Ɔhwɛ ne nguankuw sɛ oguanhwɛfo.Ɔboa nguantenmma no wɔ nʼabasa sooturu wɔn ne koko so;na nguan a wɔwɔ mma no, ɔka wɔn brɛoo.
english:
He tends his flock like a shepherd:
    He gathers the lambs in his arms
and carries them close to his heart;
    he gently leads those that have young.

twi: Hena na wasusuw obon mu nsu wɔ ne nsamanaa ɔde ne nsateaa asusuw ɔsoro?Hena na ɔde asase so mfutuma agu kɛntɛn mu,anaa wakari mmepɔw wɔ nsania sone nkoko wɔ nsania apampaa so?
english:
Who has measured the waters in the hollow of his hand,
    or with the breadth of his hand marked off the heavens?
Who has held the dust of the earth in a basket,
    or weighed the mountains on the scales
    and the hills in a balance?

twi: Hena na wate Awurade ase,anaa wakyerɛkyerɛ no sɛ ne fotufo?
english:
Who can fathom the Spirit of the Lord,
    or instruct the Lord as his counselor?

twi: Hena na Awurade abisa no sɛ ɔnkyerɛ no biribi ase,na hena na ɔkyerɛɛ no ɔkwan pa no?Hena na ɔmaa no nimdeɛanaa ɔkyerɛɛ no nhumu kwan?
english:
Whom did the Lord consult to enlighten him,
    and who taught him the right way?
Who was it that taught him knowledge,
    or showed him the path of understanding?

twi: Ampa ara aman no te sɛ nsu sope wɔ bokiti mu;wɔde wɔn toto mfutuma a egu nsania so ho;ɔkari nsupɔw te sɛnea ɛyɛ mfutuma muhumuhu.
Lebanon nnɔɔso mma afɔremuka so gya,na ne mmoa renso mma ɔhyew afɔrebɔde.
english:
Lebanon is not sufficient for altar fires,
    nor its animals enough for burnt offerings.

twi: Aman nyinaa nsɛ hwee wɔ nʼanim;obu wɔn adehunu bia wɔnka hwee.
Afei hena ho na wode Onyankopɔn bɛtoto?Nsɛsode bɛn ho na wode no bɛto?
english:
With whom, then, will you compare God?
    To what image will you liken him?

twi: Ohoni de, odwumfo na ɔyɛ,na sikadwumfo de sikakɔkɔɔ agu hona wasiesie dwetɛ nkɔnsɔnkɔnsɔn ama no.
english:
As for an idol, a metalworker casts it,
    and a goldsmith overlays it with gold
    and fashions silver chains for it.

twi: Ohiani a ɔrentumi mfa saa ayɛyɛde yi mma nokɔhwehwɛ dua a ɛremporɔw.Ɔhwehwɛ odwumfo nyansafona wayɛ ohoni a ɛremmunum nhwe fam asi hɔ.
english:
A person too poor to present such an offering
    selects wood that will not rot;
they look for a skilled worker
    to set up an idol that will not topple.

twi: Wunnim ana?Wontee ana?Wɔnnka nkyerɛɛ wo mfii mfiase no ana?Efi bere a wɔbɔɔ asase no, wontee ase ana?
english:
Do you not know?
    Have you not heard?
Has it not been told you from the beginning?
    Have you not understood since the earth was founded?

twi: Ɔte ahengua so wɔ asase dantaban no atifiɛso nnipa te sɛ tɛwtɛwɔtwe ɔsoro mu te sɛ bamkyinii,na ɔtrɛw mu sɛ ntamadan tena mu.
english:
He sits enthroned above the circle of the earth,
    and its people are like grasshoppers.
He stretches out the heavens like a canopy,
    and spreads them out like a tent to live in.

twi: Ɔma ahemmea yɛ nnipahununa wiase yi sodifo nso, ɔbrɛ wɔn ase.
english:
He brings princes to naught
    and reduces the rulers of this world to nothing.

twi: Wɔtɛw wɔn ara pɛ,woduaa wɔn ara pɛ,wogyee ntin wɔ asase mu pɛ,na wahome agu wɔn so ama wɔakisa,na mframa abɔ wɔn kɔ te sɛ ntɛtɛ.
english:
No sooner are they planted,
    no sooner are they sown,
    no sooner do they take root in the ground,
than he blows on them and they wither,
    and a whirlwind sweeps them away like chaff.

twi: “Hena ho na wode me bɛto?Anaasɛ hena na ɔne me sɛ?” Ɔkronkronni no na ose.
english:
“To whom will you compare me?
    Or who is my equal?” says the Holy One.

twi: Momma mo ani so nhwɛ ɔsoro:Hena na ɔbɔɔ eyinom nyinaa?Nea oyiyi ɔsoro nsoromma mmaako mmaako,na ɔbɔ obiara din frɛ no.Nʼahoɔden ne ne tumi ntiwɔn mu baako mpo nyera.
english:
Lift up your eyes and look to the heavens:
    Who created all these?
He who brings out the starry host one by one
    and calls forth each of them by name.
Because of his great power and mighty strength,
    not one of them is missing.

twi: Adɛn na wunwiinwii, Yakob,na woka se, Israel,“Mʼakwan ahintaw Awurade;na me Nyankopɔn abɔ mʼasɛm agu”?
english:
Why do you complain, Jacob?
    Why do you say, Israel,
“My way is hidden from the Lord;
    my cause is disregarded by my God”?

twi: Wunnim ana?Wontee ana?Awurade yɛ daapem Nyankopɔn,na ɔyɛ asase nyinaa yɛfo.Ɔremmrɛ na ɔrentɔ beraw,na ne nhumu nni nhwehwɛmu.
english:
Do you not know?
    Have you not heard?
The Lord is the everlasting God,
    the Creator of the ends of the earth.
He will not grow tired or weary,
    and his understanding no one can fathom.

twi: Ɔma nea watɔ beraw ahoɔdennea wayɛ mmerɛw nso, ɔto nʼahoɔden so.
english:
He gives strength to the weary
    and increases the power of the weak.

twi: Mpo, mmabun brɛ, na wɔtɔ beraw,na mmerante hintihintiw hwehwe ase;
english:
Even youths grow tired and weary,
    and young men stumble and fall;

twi: Nanso, wɔn a wɔn ani da Awurade sobenya ahoɔden foforo.Wɔde ntaban sɛ akɔre de betu akɔ wim;wobetu mmirika, na wɔrentɔ beraw.Wɔbɛnantew, na wɔrentɔ piti.
english:
but those who hope in the Lord
    will renew their strength.
They will soar on wings like eagles;
    they will run and not grow weary,
    they will walk and not be faint.

twi: Israel Boafo“Monyɛ komm wɔ mʼanim, mo nsupɔw!Ma aman no nhyɛ wɔn ho den!Ma wɔmmra ha mmɛkasa;momma yɛmmɔ mu nhyia wɔ asennii hɔ.
english:
“Be silent before me, you islands!
    Let the nations renew their strength!
Let them come forward and speak;
    let us meet together at the place of judgment.

twi: “Hena na wakanyan nea ofi apuei no,afrɛ no trenee mu sɛ ɔmmɛsom no?Ɔde aman hyɛ ne nsana ɔbrɛ ahemfo ase wɔ nʼanim.Ɔde nʼafoa ma wɔdan mfutuma,ɔde ne bɛmma ma wɔdan ntɛtɛ a mframa bɔ hwete.
english:
“Who has stirred up one from the east,
    calling him in righteousness to his service?
He hands nations over to him
    and subdues kings before him.
He turns them to dust with his sword,
    to windblown chaff with his bow.

twi: Ɔtaa wɔn na ɔkɔ nʼanim a biribiara nti ne ho,wɔ kwan a ɔmfaa so da no so.
english:
He pursues them and moves on unscathed,
    by a path his feet have not traveled before.

twi: Hena na wayɛ eyi akosi awiei,afrɛ awo ntoatoaso afi mfiase?Me Awurade, meka adikanfone akyikafo ho, Mene ɔno ara.”
english:
Who has done this and carried it through,
    calling forth the generations from the beginning?
I, the Lord—with the first of them
    and with the last—I am he.”

twi: Nsupɔw no ahu na wɔbɔ hu;nsase ano ho popo.Wotwiw bɛn, na wɔba anim;
na obiara boa ne yɔnkona ɔka kyerɛ ne nua se, “Yɛ den!”
english:
they help each other
    and say to their companions, “Be strong!”

twi: Odwumfo hyɛ sikadwumfo nkuran,na nea ɔde asae yɛ no trontromboa nea ɔbɔ atommo so.Ɔka fa nea ɔsɔw no ho se, “Eye pa ara.”Ɔbobɔ ohoni no mu nnadewa sɛnea ɛrentu nhwe fam.
english:
The metalworker encourages the goldsmith,
    and the one who smooths with the hammer
    spurs on the one who strikes the anvil.
One says of the welding, “It is good.”
    The other nails down the idol so it will not topple.

twi: “Nanso wo, Israel, me somfo,Yakob, nea mayi no no,mo, mʼadamfo Abraham asefo.
english:
“But you, Israel, my servant,
    Jacob, whom I have chosen,
    you descendants of Abraham my friend,

twi: Mefaa wo fii nsase ano,fii nʼakyirikyiri ntwea so, na mefrɛɛ wo.Mekae se, ‘Woyɛ me somfo’;mapaw wo na mempoo wo ɛ.
english:
I took you from the ends of the earth,
    from its farthest corners I called you.
I said, ‘You are my servant’;
    I have chosen you and have not rejected you.

twi: Enti nsuro, na mene wo wɔ hɔ;mma wo werɛ nhow, na mene wo Nyankopɔn.Mɛhyɛ wo den, na mɛboa wo;mede me trenee nsa nifa bɛma wo so.
“Wɔn a wɔn bo afuw wo no nyinaa, ampa arawɔn ani bewu na wɔn anim agu ase;wɔn a wɔsɔre tia wo norensɛ hwee na wobewuwu.
english:
“All who rage against you
    will surely be ashamed and disgraced;
those who oppose you
    will be as nothing and perish.

twi: Ɛwɔ mu sɛ wobɛhwehwɛ wʼatamfo de,nanso worenhu wɔn.Wɔn a wotu wo so sa norensɛ hwee koraa.
english:
Though you search for your enemies,
    you will not find them.
Those who wage war against you
    will be as nothing at all.

twi: Na mene Awurade, wo Nyankopɔn,nea okura wo nsa nifa muna ɔka kyerɛ wo se, Nsuro;mɛboa wo.
english:
For I am the Lord your God
    who takes hold of your right hand
and says to you, Do not fear;
    I will help you.

twi: Nsuro, osunson Yakob,Israel a wusua,na me ankasa mɛboa wo,” Awurade na ose,wo gyefo, Israel Ɔkronkronni no.
english:
Do not be afraid, you worm Jacob,
    little Israel, do not fear,
for I myself will help you,” declares the Lord,
    your Redeemer, the Holy One of Israel.

twi: “Hwɛ, mede wo bɛyɛ nhuwso apa,a ɛyɛ amono, ano yɛ nnam na ɛwɔ ɛse bebree.Wubehuhuw mmepɔw no so na woadwiriw wɔn,na woama nkoko ayɛ sɛ ntɛtɛ.
english:
“See, I will make you into a threshing sledge,
    new and sharp, with many teeth.
You will thresh the mountains and crush them,
    and reduce the hills to chaff.

twi: Wubehuhuw wɔn so, mframa bɛma wɔn so,na ahum abɔ wɔn akɔ.Nanso wʼani begye wɔ Awurade muna woahyɛ Israel Ɔkronkronni no anuonyam.
english:
You will winnow them, the wind will pick them up,
    and a gale will blow them away.
But you will rejoice in the Lord
    and glory in the Holy One of Israel.

twi: “Ohiani ne mmɔborɔni kyin pɛ nsu,nanso bi nni hɔ;osukɔm ama wɔn tɛkrɛma so ayow.Nanso me Awurade, mɛma wɔn mmuae.Me, Israel Nyankopɔn, merennyaw wɔn.
Mɛma nsubɔnten ateɛ wɔ sorɔnsorɔmmea a awu no so,na nsuti apue wɔ abon mu.Mɛdan nweatam ayɛ no mmura,na nsase a awo adan nsuti bebree.
english:
I will make rivers flow on barren heights,
    and springs within the valleys.
I will turn the desert into pools of water,
    and the parched ground into springs.

twi: Meduadua wɔ nweatam so,sida, ɔkanto, ohuam ne ngonnua.Meduadua ɔpepaw wɔ asase wosee soasɛsɛ ne kwabɔhɔre abɔ mu,
english:
I will put in the desert
    the cedar and the acacia, the myrtle and the olive.
I will set junipers in the wasteland,
    the fir and the cypress together,

twi: sɛnea nnipa behu na wɔate,na wɔasusuw ho na wɔate ase sɛ,Awurade nsa na ayɛ saa ade yi,Israel ɔkronkronni no na ɔma ɛbae.
english:
so that people may see and know,
    may consider and understand,
that the hand of the Lord has done this,
    that the Holy One of Israel has created it.

twi: “Bɔ wo nkuro,” Awurade na ose.“Kyerɛkyerɛ wʼasɛm mu,” Yakob Hene na ose.
english:
“Present your case,” says the Lord.
    “Set forth your arguments,” says Jacob’s King.

twi: “Fa wʼahoni no brana wɔmmɛka nea ebesi nkyerɛ yɛn.Wɔmmɛka sɛnea na kan nneɛma no te nkyerɛ yɛn,sɛnea yebedwen ho afana yɛahu nea ebefi mu aba.Anaasɛ wɔmpae mu nka nneɛma a ebesi nkyerɛ yɛn.
english:
“Tell us, you idols,
    what is going to happen.
Tell us what the former things were,
    so that we may consider them
    and know their final outcome.
Or declare to us the things to come,

twi: Monka yɛn nea ebesi daakye,na ama yɛahu sɛ moyɛ anyame.Monyɛ biribi, sɛ eye anaa enye,sɛnea ɛbɛyɛ a yɛn werɛ bɛhow na ehu aka yɛn.
english:
tell us what the future holds,
    so we may know that you are gods.
Do something, whether good or bad,
    so that we will be dismayed and filled with fear.

twi: Nanso, monnka hwee,na mo nnwuma so nni mfaso;nea ɔfa mo no yɛ akyiwade.
“Makanyan obi a ofi atifi fam na ɔreba,nea ofi owia apuei na ɔbɔ me din.Otiatia ahemfo so te sɛ dɔte a wɔde si dan,te sɛ ɔnwemfo a ɔrewɔw dɔte.
english:
“I have stirred up one from the north, and he comes—
    one from the rising sun who calls on my name.
He treads on rulers as if they were mortar,
    as if he were a potter treading the clay.

twi: Hena na ɔkaa eyi ho asɛm fii mfiase, sɛnea anka ɛbɛma yɛahu,anaa waka ato hɔ, sɛnea yebetumi aka se, ‘Ne de no ye’?Obiara anka eyi,obiara anni kan anka,obiara ante nsɛm biara amfi wo nkyɛn.
english:
Who told of this from the beginning, so we could know,
    or beforehand, so we could say, ‘He was right’?
No one told of this,
    no one foretold it,
    no one heard any words from you.

twi: Me na midii kan ka kyerɛɛ Sion, ‘Hwɛ, woni!’Memaa Yerusalem ɔsomafo a ɔde asɛmpa ba.
english:
I was the first to tell Zion, ‘Look, here they are!’
    I gave to Jerusalem a messenger of good news.

twi: Mehwɛ, nanso obiara nni hɔ,obiara nni wɔn mu a obetu wɔn fo,sɛ mibisa wɔn a, obiara ntumi mma mmuae.
english:
I look but there is no one—
    no one among the gods to give counsel,
    no one to give answer when I ask them.

twi: Hwɛ, wɔn nyinaa yɛ atorofo!Wɔn nneyɛe nka hwee;wɔn nsɛsode yɛ mframa ne basabasayɛ nko ara.
Awurade Somfo No“Me somfo a mahyɛ no den ni,nea mayi no na ɔsɔ mʼani;mede me Honhom begu no sona ɔde atɛntrenee bɛbrɛ aman no.
english:
“Here is my servant, whom I uphold,
    my chosen one in whom I delight;
I will put my Spirit on him,
    and he will bring justice to the nations.

twi: Ɔrenteɛ mu anaa ɔremma ne nne so.Ɔremma ne nne so wɔ mmɔnten so.
english:
He will not shout or cry out,
    or raise his voice in the streets.

twi: Demmire a ayɛ mmerɛw no, ɔremmu mu.Kanea ntamabamma a ɛnnɛw yiye no, ɔrennum.Nokware mu na ɔbɛda trenee adi;
ɔrenhinhim na ɔrempa abawkosi sɛ ɔde trenee bɛba asase so.Ne mmara so na amanaman no de wɔn ani bɛto.”
english:
he will not falter or be discouraged
till he establishes justice on earth.
    In his teaching the islands will put their hope.”

twi: Sɛɛ na Onyankopɔn, Awurade no se,nea ɔbɔɔ ɔsoro na ɔtrɛw mu,nea ɔtwee asase mu ne nea efi mu nyinaa,nea ɔma wɔn a wɔte so home,na ɔma wɔn a wɔnantew so no nkwa:
english:
This is what God the Lord says—
the Creator of the heavens, who stretches them out,
    who spreads out the earth with all that springs from it,
    who gives breath to its people,
    and life to those who walk on it:

twi: “Me, Awurade, mafrɛ wo trenee mu;meso wo nsa.Mɛhwɛ wo so na mede wo ayɛapam ama nkurɔfo none kanea ama amanamanmufo,
english:
“I, the Lord, have called you in righteousness;
    I will take hold of your hand.
I will keep you and will make you
    to be a covenant for the people
    and a light for the Gentiles,

twi: na woabue ani a afura,na woayi nneduafo afi afiasena woagye wɔn a wɔda afiase amoa mu, wɔn a wɔte sum kabii mu no.
english:
to open eyes that are blind,
    to free captives from prison
    and to release from the dungeon those who sit in darkness.

twi: “Mene Awurade; me din ne no!Meremfa mʼanuonyam mma obianaa mʼayeyi mma ahoni.
english:
“I am the Lord; that is my name!
    I will not yield my glory to another
    or my praise to idols.

twi: Hwɛ, nneɛma dedaw no asisi,na nneɛma foforo no mepae mu ka;ansa na ɛbɛba mu no,meka kyerɛ mo.”
english:
See, the former things have taken place,
    and new things I declare;
before they spring into being
    I announce them to you.”

twi: Awurade Ayeyi DwomMonto dwom foforo mma Awurade!Nʼayeyi mfi asase ano,mo a mokɔ po so ne nea ɛwo mu nyinaa,mo asupɔw ne wɔn a wɔtete so nyinaa.
english:
Sing to the Lord a new song,
    his praise from the ends of the earth,
you who go down to the sea, and all that is in it,
    you islands, and all who live in them.

twi: Ma nweatam ne so nkurow mma wɔn nne so;ma atenae a Kedar te so no nsɛpɛw wɔn ho.Ma nnipa a wɔwɔ Sela nto nnwom nnye wɔn ani;ma wɔnteɛ mu mfi mmepɔw no atifi!
Ma wɔnhyɛ Awurade anuonyam;na wɔmpae mu nka nʼayeyi no wɔ asupɔw no so.
english:
Let them give glory to the Lord
    and proclaim his praise in the islands.

twi: Awurade bepue aba sɛ ɔkatakyi,te sɛ ɔkofo no, ɔbɛhyɛ ne mmɔdemmɔ mu den;ɔde nteɛmu bɛyɛ ɔkofo nkanyanna obedi nʼatamfo so nkonim.
english:
The Lord will march out like a champion,
    like a warrior he will stir up his zeal;
with a shout he will raise the battle cry
    and will triumph over his enemies.

twi: “Mayɛ komm akyɛ,mayɛ dinn na mahyɛ me ho so.Nanso afei, te sɛ ɔbea a ɔrewo no,meteɛ mu, mehome a ensi so na mehome afrɛ so.
english:
“For a long time I have kept silent,
    I have been quiet and held myself back.
But now, like a woman in childbirth,
    I cry out, I gasp and pant.

twi: Mɛsɛe mmepɔw ne nkoko nona mahyew so afifide nyinaa.Mɛdan nsubɔnten ama ayɛ asupɔw,na mama atare ayoyow.
english:
I will lay waste the mountains and hills
    and dry up all their vegetation;
I will turn rivers into islands
    and dry up the pools.

twi: Medi anifuraefo anim afa akwan a wonnim so so,akwan a wonnim so papa so na mɛkyerɛ wɔn kwan.Mɛma sum no ayɛ hann wɔ wɔn anim,na mayɛ mmeae a ɛyɛ abonkyiabonkyi no trontrom.Eyinom ne nneɛma a mɛyɛ;merennyaw wɔn mu.
Na wɔn a wɔde wɔn ho to ahoni so,na wɔka kyerɛ nsɛsode se, ‘Moyɛ yɛn anyame’ no,wɔbɛpam wɔn wɔ animguase mu.”
english:
But those who trust in idols,
    who say to images, ‘You are our gods,’
    will be turned back in utter shame.

twi: Israel, Onifuraefo Ne Ɔsotifo“Tie, wo ɔsotifo;hwɛ, wo onifuraefo na hu!
english:
“Hear, you deaf;
    look, you blind, and see!

twi: Hena ne onifuraefo sɛ me somfo,na ɔyɛ ɔsotifo sɛ ɔbɔfo a mesoma no?Hena na nʼani afura sɛ nea ɔde ne werɛ ahyɛ me mu,nʼani afura sɛ Awurade somfo?
english:
Who is blind but my servant,
    and deaf like the messenger I send?
Who is blind like the one in covenant with me,
    blind like the servant of the Lord?

twi: Woahu nneɛma bebree, nanso amfa wo ho;Ɔkwan da wʼasom, nanso wonte hwee.”
english:
You have seen many things, but you pay no attention;
    your ears are open, but you do not listen.”

twi: Ɛsɔɔ Awurade ani,ne trenee ntisɛ ɔbɛma ne mmara ayɛ kɛse na anya anuonyam.
english:
It pleased the Lord
    for the sake of his righteousness
    to make his law great and glorious.

twi: Nanso saa nnipa a wɔawia wɔn na wɔafow wɔn yi,wɔn nyinaa aka amoa muanaa wɔde wɔn asie wɔ afiase.Wɔayɛ wɔn asadena wonni obi a obegye wɔn;wɔayɛ wɔn akorɔnnena wonni obi a ɔbɛka se, “Momfa wɔn nsan nkɔ.”
english:
But this is a people plundered and looted,
    all of them trapped in pits
    or hidden away in prisons.
They have become plunder,
    with no one to rescue them;
they have been made loot,
    with no one to say, “Send them back.”

twi: Mo mu hena na obetie eyianaa nʼani beku ho yiye akyiri yi?
english:
Which of you will listen to this
    or pay close attention in time to come?

twi: Hena na ɔde Yakob maa sɛ ɔmmɛyɛ akorɔnne,na ɔde Israel maa afowfo?Ɛnyɛ Awurade ayɛayɛ bɔne atia no no?Efisɛ wɔannantew nʼakwan so;na wɔanni ne mmara so.
english:
Who handed Jacob over to become loot,
    and Israel to the plunderers?
Was it not the Lord,
    against whom we have sinned?
For they would not follow his ways;
    they did not obey his law.

twi: Enti ohwiee nʼabufuwhyew guu wɔn so,akodi mu basabasayɛ.Ɛde ogyaframa bunkam wɔn so, nanso wɔante ase.Ɛhyew wɔn, nanso amfa wɔn ho.
english:
So he poured out on them his burning anger,
    the violence of war.
It enveloped them in flames, yet they did not understand;
    it consumed them, but they did not take it to heart.

twi: Israel Agyenkwa KoroNa afei, sɛɛ na Awurade se,nea ɔbɔɔ wo, Yakobnea ɔnwen wo, Israel;“Nsuro na magye wo;mabɔ wo din afrɛ wo; woyɛ me dea.
english:
But now, this is what the Lord says—
    he who created you, Jacob,
    he who formed you, Israel:
“Do not fear, for I have redeemed you;
    I have summoned you by name; you are mine.

twi: Sɛ wofa nsu mu a,mɛka wo ho;na sɛ wutwa nsubɔnten no a,ɛremmu mfa wo so.Sɛ wonantew ogya no mu a,worenhyew;ogyaframa no renhye wo.
english:
When you pass through the waters,
    I will be with you;
and when you pass through the rivers,
    they will not sweep over you.
When you walk through the fire,
    you will not be burned;
    the flames will not set you ablaze.

twi: Na mene Awurade, wo Nyankopɔn,Israel Kronkronni, wo Agyenkwa.Mede Misraim yɛ mpata ma wona mede Kus ne Seba si wʼanan mu.
english:
For I am the Lord your God,
    the Holy One of Israel, your Savior;
I give Egypt for your ransom,
    Cush and Seba in your stead.

twi: Sɛ wosom bo ma me na wowɔ anuonyam wɔ mʼanimna medɔ wo nti,mede nnipa bɛsesa wo,na mede nkurɔfo asesa wo nkwa.
english:
Since you are precious and honored in my sight,
    and because I love you,
I will give people in exchange for you,
    nations in exchange for your life.

twi: Nsuro, efisɛ meka mo ho;mede wo mma befi apuei fam abana maboa wɔn ano afi atɔe fam.
Mɛka akyerɛ atifi fam se, ‘Munnyaa wɔn!’ne anafo fam se, ‘Munnye wɔn ntena ha.’Momfa me mmabarima mfi akyirikyiri mmrana me mmabea mfi asase ano mmra,
english:
I will say to the north, ‘Give them up!’
    and to the south, ‘Do not hold them back.’
Bring my sons from afar
    and my daughters from the ends of the earth—

twi: obiara a me din da no so,nea mebɔɔ no de hyɛɛ me ho anuonyam,nea menwen no na meyɛɛ no.”
english:
everyone who is called by my name,
    whom I created for my glory,
    whom I formed and made.”

twi: Momfa wɔn a wɔwɔ ani, nanso wonhu adewɔn a wɔwɔ aso nanso asisiw no mmra.
english:
Lead out those who have eyes but are blind,
    who have ears but are deaf.

twi: Aman no nyinaa boa wɔn ho ano,na nnipa no hyia mu.Wɔn mu hena na ɔkaa eyi fii mfiasena ɔpaee mu kaa nneɛma a atwam no kyerɛɛ yɛn?Ma wɔmmfa wɔn nnansefo mmra mmedi adanse sɛ wodi bem,sɛnea afoforo bɛte na wɔaka se, “Ɛyɛ nokware.”
english:
All the nations gather together
    and the peoples assemble.
Which of their gods foretold this
    and proclaimed to us the former things?
Let them bring in their witnesses to prove they were right,
    so that others may hear and say, “It is true.”

twi: “Mone me nnansefo, ne mʼasomfo a mapaw no,”sɛɛ na Awurade se,“Sɛnea mubehu na moagye me adina moate ase sɛ me ne no.Wɔammɔ onyame bi anni mʼanim,na mʼakyi nso obiara remma.
english:
“You are my witnesses,” declares the Lord,
    “and my servant whom I have chosen,
so that you may know and believe me
    and understand that I am he.
Before me no god was formed,
    nor will there be one after me.

twi: Me, Me ara, Mene Awurade,na agyenkwa biara nni hɔ sɛ me.
english:
I, even I, am the Lord,
    and apart from me there is no savior.

twi: Mada no adi na magye nkwa na mapae mu aka se,Me, na ɛnyɛ onyame nanani bi a ɔwɔ mo mu.Mone me nnansefo,” Awurade na ose sɛ, “Mene Onyankopɔn.
english:
I have revealed and saved and proclaimed—
    I, and not some foreign god among you.
You are my witnesses,” declares the Lord, “that I am God.

twi: Yiw, na efi teteete no me ne no.Obiara rentumi nnye mfi me nsamsɛ meyɛ biribi a, hena na obetumi adan no?”
english:
Yes, and from ancient days I am he.
No one can deliver out of my hand.
    When I act, who can reverse it?”

twi: Onyankopɔn Ahummɔbɔ Ne Israel HuammɔdiSɛɛ na Awurade se,wʼAgyenkwa, Israel Kronkronni no:“Mo nti, mɛsoma akɔ Babilonia,na mede Babiloniafo nyinaa bɛba sɛ aguanfowɔ ahyɛn a wɔde hoahoa wɔn ho no mu.
english:
This is what the Lord says—
    your Redeemer, the Holy One of Israel:
“For your sake I will send to Babylon
    and bring down as fugitives all the Babylonians,
    in the ships in which they took pride.

twi: Mene Awurade, wo Kronkronni no,Israel Yɛfo, wo Hene.”
english:
I am the Lord, your Holy One,
    Israel’s Creator, your King.”

twi: Sɛɛ na Awurade se,nea ɔbɔɔ kwan wɔ po mu,kwan a ɛda asubun mu,
english:
This is what the Lord says—
    he who made a way through the sea,
    a path through the mighty waters,

twi: nea ɔtwee nteaseɛnam ne apɔnkɔ,asraafo ne ne nkekaho nyinaa,na wɔkaa hɔ a wɔansɔre bio,wɔadum wɔn te sɛ kanea mu ntamabamma:
english:
who drew out the chariots and horses,
    the army and reinforcements together,
and they lay there, never to rise again,
    extinguished, snuffed out like a wick:

twi: “Momma mo werɛ mfi kan nneɛma nomonntɔ nnkɔ nea atwam no so.
english:
“Forget the former things;
    do not dwell on the past.

twi: Hwɛ, mereyɛ ade foforo!Mprempren, ɛrepue; na munhu ana?Merebɔ kwan afa nweatam sona mereyɛ nsuwansuwa wɔ asase wosee so.
english:
See, I am doing a new thing!
    Now it springs up; do you not perceive it?
I am making a way in the wilderness
    and streams in the wasteland.

twi: Mmoa a wɔyɛ keka hyɛ me anuonyam,adompo ne mpatu,efisɛ mema nsu wɔ nweatam sone nsuwansuwa wɔ asase wosee so,de ma me nkurɔfo, wɔn a mapaw wɔn no nsu,
english:
The wild animals honor me,
    the jackals and the owls,
because I provide water in the wilderness
    and streams in the wasteland,
to give drink to my people, my chosen,

twi: nnipa a meyɛɛ wɔn maa me hosɛ wɔmpae mu nka mʼayeyi.
english:
the people I formed for myself
    that they may proclaim my praise.

twi: “Nanso, womfrɛɛ me, Yakob,wonhaw wo ho wɔ me ho, Israel.
english:
“Yet you have not called on me, Jacob,
    you have not wearied yourselves for me, Israel.

twi: Momfaa nguan mmrɛɛ me sɛ ɔhyew afɔrebɔde,na momfaa mo afɔrebɔ nhyɛɛ me anuonyam nso.Memmaa aduan afɔre nyɛɛ mo adesoana memfaa nnuhuamgye nhaw mo.
english:
You have not brought me sheep for burnt offerings,
    nor honored me with your sacrifices.
I have not burdened you with grain offerings
    nor wearied you with demands for incense.

twi: Montɔɔ nnuhuam mmrɛɛ me,na mommaa mo afɔrebɔde mu srade mmuu me so.Mmom, mode mo bɔne asoa mena mode mo mfomso ho haw abɛto me so.
english:
You have not bought any fragrant calamus for me,
    or lavished on me the fat of your sacrifices.
But you have burdened me with your sins
    and wearied me with your offenses.

twi: “Me, me ara, mene nea ɔpepamo bɔne, me nti,na menkae mo amumɔyɛ bio.
english:
“I, even I, am he who blots out
    your transgressions, for my own sake,
    and remembers your sins no more.

twi: Monhwehwɛ nea atwa mu no mu bio mma me,momma yɛmmɔ mu nnye asɛm no ho akyinnye;ka wʼasɛm a ɛkyerɛ sɛ wunni fɔ no.
Mo agya a odii kan no yɛɛ bɔne;mo kasamafo tew mʼanim atua.
english:
Your first father sinned;
    those I sent to teach you rebelled against me.

twi: Enti magu mo asɔredan mu atitiriw anim ase,na mede Yakob ama ɔsɛena mede Israel ama ahohora.
Israel, Nea Wɔapaw No“Na afei tie, Yakob me somfo,Israel, nea mapaw no.
english:
“But now listen, Jacob, my servant,
    Israel, whom I have chosen.

twi: Sɛɛ na Awurade se,nea ɔnwen wo, na ɔyɛɛ wo wɔ awotwaa mu,ɔno na ɔbɛboa wo:Nsuro Yakob, me somfo,Yeshurun, a mapaw no.
english:
This is what the Lord says—
    he who made you, who formed you in the womb,
    and who will help you:
Do not be afraid, Jacob, my servant,
    Jeshurun, whom I have chosen.

twi: Na mehwie nsu agu asase a awo no so,ne nsuten wɔ asase kesee so;mehwie me Honhom agu wo mma so,ne me nhyira agu wʼasefo so.
english:
For I will pour water on the thirsty land,
    and streams on the dry ground;
I will pour out my Spirit on your offspring,
    and my blessing on your descendants.

twi: Wobefifi sɛnea sare fifi wɔ mmoa adidibea,te sɛ mpampuro a ɛwɔ asuten ho.
english:
They will spring up like grass in a meadow,
    like poplar trees by flowing streams.

twi: Obi bɛka se, ‘Meyɛ Awurade de’;ɔfoforo bɛfrɛ ne ho se Yakob;afoforo bɛkɔ so akyerɛw wɔn nsa ho se, ‘Awurade de,’na wɔafa din Israel.
Ɛyɛ Awurade, Ɛnyɛ Ahoni“Sɛɛ na AwuradeIsraelhene ne Ogyefo, Asafo Awurade se:Mene odikanfo ne okyikafo;Onyankopɔn biara nni hɔ sɛ me.
english:
“This is what the Lord says—
    Israel’s King and Redeemer, the Lord Almighty:
I am the first and I am the last;
    apart from me there is no God.

twi: Hena na ɔne me sɛ? Ma ɔmpae mu nka.Ma ɔnka na ɔnkyerɛ wɔ mʼanimnea asisi fi bere a migyee me tete nkurɔfo sii hɔ,ne nea ɛrebɛba.Yiw, ma ɔnhyɛ nea ɛreba ho nkɔm.
english:
Who then is like me? Let him proclaim it.
    Let him declare and lay out before me
what has happened since I established my ancient people,
    and what is yet to come—
    yes, let them foretell what will come.

twi: Mommma mo ho mpopo, munnsuro.Mampae mu anka eyi, manhyɛ ho amfi teteete ana?Mone me nnansefo. Onyankopɔn foforo bi ka me ho ana?Dabi, Ɔbotan foforo bi nni hɔ; minnim baako mpo.”
english:
Do not tremble, do not be afraid.
    Did I not proclaim this and foretell it long ago?
You are my witnesses. Is there any God besides me?
    No, there is no other Rock; I know not one.”

twi: Wɔn a wɔyɛ ahoni nyinaa nka hwee,na nneɛma a ɛsom wɔn bo no so nni mfaso.Wɔn a anka wɔkasa ma wɔn no ani afura;wonnim wɔn ankasa animguase ho hwee.
english:
All who make idols are nothing,
    and the things they treasure are worthless.
Those who would speak up for them are blind;
    they are ignorant, to their own shame.

twi: Hena na ɔbɔ onyame na ogu ohoni,a ne so mma no mfaso biara?
english:
Who shapes a god and casts an idol,
    which can profit nothing?

twi: Ɔno ne wɔn a wɔte sɛ no nyinaa anim begu ase;adwumfo nyɛ hwee sɛ nnipa.Momma wɔn nyinaa mmɔ mu nsɔre nnyina,ehu ne animguase na ɛbɛka wɔn.
Ɔtomfo fa nʼatonnadeɔde hyehyɛ nnyansramma mu;ɔde asae bobɔ so yɛ no ohoni,ɔde nʼabasa mu ahoɔden mmoroso na ɛyɛ;ɔkɔm de no na ɔyɛ mmrɛw;ɔnnom nsu nti ɔtɔ beraw.
Duadwumfo de hama susuwna ɔde kyerɛwdua sensan;na ɔde pɛe yiyi hoafei ɔde kɔmpaase hyɛ no agyirae.Osen na ɛyɛ sɛ onipa sɛso,ɛyɛ sɛ onipa wɔ nʼanuonyam nyinaa mu,sɛ wɔde besi abosonnan mu.
english:
The carpenter measures with a line
    and makes an outline with a marker;
he roughs it out with chisels
    and marks it with compasses.
He shapes it in human form,
    human form in all its glory,
    that it may dwell in a shrine.

twi: Otwitwaa sida,anaasɛ ebia ɔfaa kwabɔhɔre anaa odum.Ɔma enyinii wɔ kwae mu,anaa oduaa ɔpepaw, na osu ma enyinii.
english:
He cut down cedars,
    or perhaps took a cypress or oak.
He let it grow among the trees of the forest,
    or planted a pine, and the rain made it grow.

twi: Ɛyɛ nea onipa de sɔ ogya;ɔde bi ka ne ho hyew,ɔde bi sɔ ogya to brodo.Nanso ɔde bi sen onyame na ɔsɔre no;ɔyɛ ohoni na ɔkotow no.
Ɔde dua no mu fa sɔ ogya;so na ɔnoa nʼaduan,ɔtoto ne nam wɔ so na wawe amee.Afei ɔka ne ho hyew na ɔka se,Aa! mahu ogya; me ho ayɛ me hyew.
english:
Half of the wood he burns in the fire;
    over it he prepares his meal,
    he roasts his meat and eats his fill.
He also warms himself and says,
    “Ah! I am warm; I see the fire.”

twi: Nkae no ɔde yɛ onyame, ne ohoni;ɔkotow no na ɔsɔre no.Ɔbɔ no mpae se,“Gye me; wo ne me nyame.”
english:
From the rest he makes a god, his idol;
    he bows down to it and worships.
He prays to it and says,
    “Save me! You are my god!”

twi: Wonnim hwee, na wɔnte hwee ase;wɔatare wɔn ani so nti wonhu ade,wɔato wɔn adwene mu nti wɔnte hwee ase.

Obiara nna nnwen ho,obiara nni nimdeɛ anaa nhumu a ɔde bɛka se,“Mede fa sɔɔ ogya;na mpo metoo brodo wɔ ne nnyansramma so;metotoo nam wɔ so wee.Ɛsɛ sɛ mede nkae no yɛ akyiwade ana?Ɛsɛ sɛ mekotow gyentia ana?”
english:
No one stops to think,
    no one has the knowledge or understanding to say,
“Half of it I used for fuel;
    I even baked bread over its coals,
    I roasted meat and I ate.
Shall I make a detestable thing from what is left?
    Shall I bow down to a block of wood?”

twi: Saa onipa no di nsõ, nnaadaa koma ma no to kwan;ɔrentumi nnye ne ho, anaa nka se,“Nea mikura wɔ me nsa nifa yi nyɛ atoro ana?”
“Kae saa nneɛma yi, Yakob,efisɛ, woyɛ me somfo, Israel.Me na meyɛɛ wo, woyɛ me somfo;Ao Israel, me werɛ remfi wo.
english:
“Remember these things, Jacob,
    for you, Israel, are my servant.
I have made you, you are my servant;
    Israel, I will not forget you.

twi: Mapra wo mfomso agu te sɛ omununkumne wo bɔne te sɛ anɔpa bosu.San bra me nkyɛn,efisɛ magye wo.”
english:
I have swept away your offenses like a cloud,
    your sins like the morning mist.
Return to me,
    for I have redeemed you.”

twi: Momfa ahosɛpɛw nto dwom, ɔsorosoro,na Awurade na wayɛ eyi.Mommɔ ose, asase ase.Momma nnwonto so, mo mmepɔw,mo kwae ne emu nnua nyinaa,na Awurade agye Yakob,wada nʼanuonyam adi wɔ Israel.
Wɔbɛtena Yerusalem“Sɛɛ na Awurade se,wo Gyefo a ɔnwen wo wɔ awotwaa mu no:“Mene Awurade,nea wayɛ nneɛma nyinaa,nea ɔno nko ara trɛw ɔsoro munea ɔno nko ara twee asase mu,
english:
“This is what the Lord says—
    your Redeemer, who formed you in the womb:
I am the Lord,
    the Maker of all things,
    who stretches out the heavens,
    who spreads out the earth by myself,

twi: nea ɔsɛe atoro adiyifo nsɛnkyerɛnnena ɔma nkɔmhyɛfo yɛ nkwaseafo,nea otutu anyansafo adenim guna ɔdan no nkwaseasɛm,
english:
who foils the signs of false prophets
    and makes fools of diviners,
who overthrows the learning of the wise
    and turns it into nonsense,

twi: nea ɔma nʼasomfo nsɛm ba munea ɔhyɛ nʼasomafo nkɔmhyɛ mu ma,“nea ɔka fa Yerusalem ho se, ‘Wɔbɛtena mu,’ne Yuda nkurow ho se, ‘Wɔbɛkyekye,’ne mmubui ho se, ‘Mɛyɛ no foforo,’
english:
who carries out the words of his servants
    and fulfills the predictions of his messengers,
who says of Jerusalem, ‘It shall be inhabited,’
    of the towns of Judah, ‘They shall be rebuilt,’
    and of their ruins, ‘I will restore them,’

twi: nea ɔka kyerɛ asubun se, ‘Yow,na mɛma wo nsuwa ayoyow,’
english:
who says to the watery deep, ‘Be dry,
    and I will dry up your streams,’

twi: nea ɔka wɔ Kores ho se, ‘Ɔyɛ me guanhwɛfona obewie nea mepɛ nyinaa yɛ;ɔbɛka afa Yerusalem ho se, “Ma wɔnkyekyere bio,”na waka afa asɔredan no ho se, “Ma wɔnto ne fapem.” ’ ”
english:
who says of Cyrus, ‘He is my shepherd
    and will accomplish all that I please;
he will say of Jerusalem, “Let it be rebuilt,”
    and of the temple, “Let its foundations be laid.”’

twi: “Sɛɛ na Awurade ka kyerɛ nea wasra no ngo,Kores a maso ne nsa nifa musɛ ɔmmrɛ aman ase wɔ nʼanimna onnye ahemfo akode mfi wɔn nsamsɛ ommuebue apon a ɛwɔ nʼanimsɛnea kurow apon no mu rentoto.
english:
“This is what the Lord says to his anointed,
    to Cyrus, whose right hand I take hold of
to subdue nations before him
    and to strip kings of their armor,
to open doors before him
    so that gates will not be shut:

twi: Medi wʼanimmɛyɛ mmepɔw tamaa;mebubu kɔbere mfrafrae apon aguna matwitwa nnade adaban mu.
english:
I will go before you
    and will level the mountains;
I will break down gates of bronze
    and cut through bars of iron.

twi: Mede sum mu ademude bɛma woahonyade a wɔde asie kokoa musɛnea wubehu sɛ, mene Awurade,Israel Nyankopɔn, a ɔbɔ wo din frɛ wo no.
english:
I will give you hidden treasures,
    riches stored in secret places,
so that you may know that I am the Lord,
    the God of Israel, who summons you by name.

twi: Me somfo Yakob nti,Israel a mapaw no nti,mebɔ wo din frɛ wona mɛma wo anuonyamhyɛ abodin,ɛwɔ mu sɛ wunnyee me ntoo mu de.
english:
For the sake of Jacob my servant,
    of Israel my chosen,
I summon you by name
    and bestow on you a title of honor,
    though you do not acknowledge me.

twi: Mene Awurade, obiara nni hɔ bio;Onyankopɔn biara nni hɔ ka me ho.Mɛhyɛ wo den,ɛwɔ mu sɛ wunnyee me ntoo mu de,
english:
I am the Lord, and there is no other;
    apart from me there is no God.
I will strengthen you,
    though you have not acknowledged me,

twi: sɛnea ɛbɛyɛ a efi nea owia puekosi beae a ɛtɔ nonnipa behu sɛ obiara nka me ho.Mene Awurade, na obiara nni hɔ bio.
english:
so that from the rising of the sun
    to the place of its setting
people may know there is none besides me.
    I am the Lord, and there is no other.

twi: Meyɛ hann, na mebɔ sum.Mede yiyedi ba na mede ɔhaw ba;Me, Awurade, na meyɛ eyinom nyinaa.
“Mo ɔsorosoro munhwie trenee ngu fam;momma emfi omununkum mu ntɔmomma asase mu mmue kɛse,na nkwagye mpue mfi mu,na trenee ne no nnyin;Me, Awurade na mayɛ.
“Nnome nka nea ɔne ne Yɛfo hamɛnka nea ɔmfra te sɛ kyɛmfɛre a ɛfra nea egugu fam mu.Dɔte betumi abisa ɔnwemfo se,‘Dɛn na woreyɛ yi?’Wʼadwuma betumi abisa wo se‘Wunni nsa’?
english:
“Woe to those who quarrel with their Maker,
    those who are nothing but potsherds
    among the potsherds on the ground.
Does the clay say to the potter,
    ‘What are you making?’
Does your work say,
    ‘The potter has no hands’?

twi: Nnome nka nea ose nʼagya se‘Dɛn na woawo yi?’Anaa obisa ne na se,‘Dɛn na wokyem woe?’
english:
Woe to the one who says to a father,
    ‘What have you begotten?’
or to a mother,
    ‘What have you brought to birth?’

twi: “Sɛɛ na Awurade se,Israel Ɔkronkronni ne ne Yɛfo;Nea ɛfa nneɛma a ɛreba ho no,wubisa me nsɛm a ɛfa me mma ho,anaa wohyɛ me wɔ me nsa ano adwuma ho?
english:
“This is what the Lord says—
    the Holy One of Israel, and its Maker:
Concerning things to come,
    do you question me about my children,
    or give me orders about the work of my hands?

twi: Ɛyɛ me na meyɛɛ asasena mebɔɔ adesamma guu so.Me ara me nsa na mede trɛw ɔsoro mu;nsoromma ahorow nyinaa hyɛ mʼase.
english:
It is I who made the earth
    and created mankind on it.
My own hands stretched out the heavens;
    I marshaled their starry hosts.

twi: Mɛma Kores so wɔ me trenee mu;meteɛteɛ nʼakwan nyinaa.Ɔbɛsan akyekyere me kuropɔnna wagyaa me nnommumfo,nanso ɔrennye akatua anaa akyɛde,Asafo Awurade na ose.”
english:
I will raise up Cyrus in my righteousness:
    I will make all his ways straight.
He will rebuild my city
    and set my exiles free,
but not for a price or reward,
    says the Lord Almighty.”

twi: Sɛɛ na Awurade se:“Nneɛma a efi Misraim ne aguade a efi Kus,ne Sebafo atenten no,wɔbɛba wo nkyɛnabɛyɛ wo dea;wobedi wʼakyi brɛoo aba awogu nkɔnsɔnkɔnsɔn mu.Wobebu nkotodwe wʼanimna wɔasrɛ wo aka se,‘Ampa ara, Onyankopɔn ka wo ho, na obi nni hɔ;onyame biara nni hɔ.’ ”
english:
This is what the Lord says:
“The products of Egypt and the merchandise of Cush,
    and those tall Sabeans—
they will come over to you
    and will be yours;
they will trudge behind you,
    coming over to you in chains.
They will bow down before you
    and plead with you, saying,
‘Surely God is with you, and there is no other;
    there is no other god.’”

twi: Ampa ara, woyɛ Onyankopɔn a ɔde ne ho sie,Ao Onyankopɔn ne Israel Agyenkwa.
english:
Truly you are a God who has been hiding himself,
    the God and Savior of Israel.

twi: Wɔn a wɔyɛ ahoni nyinaa bɛfɛre na wɔn anim agu ase;wɔbɛbɔ mu akɔ animguase mu.
english:
All the makers of idols will be put to shame and disgraced;
    they will go off into disgrace together.

twi: Nanso Awurade begye Israel nkwa,ɔde daapem nkwagye;wɔremma wʼani nwu na wʼanim rengu ase biokosi daapem.
english:
But Israel will be saved by the Lord
    with an everlasting salvation;
you will never be put to shame or disgraced,
    to ages everlasting.

twi: Na sɛɛ na Awurade se,nea ɔbɔɔ ɔsorosoro noɔno ne Onyankopɔn;nea ɔmaa asase, ne tebea na ɔbɔe no,ɔno na ɔtoo ne fapem;wammɔ no sɛ so nna hɔ kwa,mmom, ɔyɛe se nnipa ntena so,ɔka se:“Mene Awurade,na obi nni hɔ.
english:
For this is what the Lord says—
he who created the heavens,
    he is God;
he who fashioned and made the earth,
    he founded it;
he did not create it to be empty,
    but formed it to be inhabited—
he says:
“I am the Lord,
    and there is no other.

twi: Menkasaa wɔ kokoa mu,mfi asase so baabi a aduru sum;menka nkyerɛɛ Yakob asefo se,‘Monhwehwɛ me na munhu me.’Me Awurade, meka nokware no;meka nea eye.
“Mommoaboa mo ho ano na mommra;munhyia mu, mo aguanfo a mufi amanaman so.Wɔn a wonnim de na wɔsoa nnua ahoni de kyinkyinwɔn a wɔbɔ anyame a wontumi nnye nkwa no mpae.
english:
“Gather together and come;
    assemble, you fugitives from the nations.
Ignorant are those who carry about idols of wood,
    who pray to gods that cannot save.

twi: Mompae mu nka nea ebesi, momfa nto gua,ma wɔmmɔ mu ntu agyina.Hena na odii kan kaa no teteete,hena na ɔdaa no adi fi tete nteredee?Ɛnyɛ me Awurade ana?Onyankopɔn bi nni hɔ ka me ho,trenee Nyankopɔn ne Agyenkwa;obiara nni hɔ sɛ me.
english:
Declare what is to be, present it—
    let them take counsel together.
Who foretold this long ago,
    who declared it from the distant past?
Was it not I, the Lord?
    And there is no God apart from me,
a righteous God and a Savior;
    there is none but me.

twi: “Monnan mmra me nkyɛn na munnya nkwa,mo a mowɔ asase ano nyinaa;efisɛ mene Onyankopɔn, na obiara nni hɔ.
Maka me ho ntam,mʼano aka wɔ nokwaredi nyinaa muasɛm a wɔntwe nsan sɛ:obiara bebu nkotodwe wɔ mʼanim.Na obiara bɛpae mu aka se, mene Onyankopɔn.
english:
By myself I have sworn,
    my mouth has uttered in all integrity
    a word that will not be revoked:
Before me every knee will bow;
    by me every tongue will swear.

twi: Wɔbɛka me ho asɛm se, ‘Awurade nko ara muna trenee ne ahoɔden wɔ.’ ”Wɔn a wɔn bo huru tia no nyinaabɛba ne nkyɛn na wɔn anim begu ase.
english:
They will say of me, ‘In the Lord alone
    are deliverance and strength.’”
All who have raged against him
    will come to him and be put to shame.

twi: Nanso Awurade mu, Israel asefo nyinaawobebu wɔn bem, na wɔahoahoa wɔn ho.
english:
But all the descendants of Israel
    will find deliverance in the Lord
    and will make their boast in him.

twi: Babilonia AnyameBel bɔ ne mu ase, Nebo brɛ ne dibea ase;mfurum soa wɔn ahoni.Nsɛsode a wɔso nenam no mu yɛ duru,ɛyɛ adesoa ma nea wabrɛ.
english:
Bel bows down, Nebo stoops low;
    their idols are borne by beasts of burden.
The images that are carried about are burdensome,
    a burden for the weary.

twi: Wɔbɔ mu kotow, bɔ wɔn mu ase;wontumi nsiw amanehunu ano,wɔn ankasa kɔ nkoasom mu.
“Muntie me, Yakobfifo,mo a moaka wɔ Israelfi nyinaa,mo a maso mo mu fi mo nyinsɛn mu,na maturu mo afi bere a wɔwoo mo.
english:
“Listen to me, you descendants of Jacob,
    all the remnant of the people of Israel,
you whom I have upheld since your birth,
    and have carried since you were born.

twi: Mpo kosi mo nkwakoraa bere ne bere a mubefuw dwen mu,Me ne no, Me ne nea obeso mo mu.Mabɔ mo na meturu mo;mɛwowaw mo na megye mo.
english:
Even to your old age and gray hairs
    I am he, I am he who will sustain you.
I have made you and I will carry you;
    I will sustain you and I will rescue you.

twi: “Hena ho na mode me bɛto, anaa mubebu no me sɛso?Hena na mode me besusuw no, na mode no atoto me ho?
english:
“With whom will you compare me or count me equal?
    To whom will you liken me that we may be compared?

twi: Ebinom hwie sikakɔkɔɔ fi wɔn nkotoku muna wɔkari dwetɛ wɔ nsania so;wɔbɔ sika dwumfo paa, ma ɔde yɛ onyame bi,na wɔkotow sɔre no.
english:
Some pour out gold from their bags
    and weigh out silver on the scales;
they hire a goldsmith to make it into a god,
    and they bow down and worship it.

twi: Wɔsoa no wɔ wɔn mmati so,wɔde kosi nʼafa, na ɛka hɔ ara.Ɛrentumi mfi faako a esi.Obi teɛ mu frɛ no de, nanso ommua;ɛrentumi nyi no mfi ne haw mu.
“Monkae yiye, momma ɛnka mo tirim,munnwen ho mo atuatewfo.
english:
“Remember this, keep it in mind,
    take it to heart, you rebels.

twi: Monkae nneɛma a atwam no, teteete nneɛma no;Mene Onyankopɔn, na obi nni hɔ;Mene Onyankopɔn, na obiara nte sɛ me.
Meda awiei adi fi mfiase,efi tete, meka nea ɛbɛba.Meka se: ‘Mʼatirimpɔw begyina,na mɛyɛ nea mepɛ nyinaa.’
english:
I make known the end from the beginning,
    from ancient times, what is still to come.
I say, ‘My purpose will stand,
    and I will do all that I please.’

twi: Mɛfrɛ anomaa a ɔkyere mmoa afi apuei fam;afi akyirikyiri asase so, onipa a ɔbɛhyɛ me botae ma.Nea maka no, ɛno na mɛma aba mu;nea madwen ho no, ɛno na mɛyɛ.
Muntie me, mo a moyɛ akokodurufo,mo a mo ne trenee ntam kwan ware;
english:
Listen to me, you stubborn-hearted,
    you who are now far from my righteousness.

twi: Mede me trenee rebɛn,enni akyirikyiri;na me nkwagye nso renkyɛ.Mɛma Sion nkwagye,na mede mʼanuonyam ama Israel.
english:
I am bringing my righteousness near,
    it is not far away;
    and my salvation will not be delayed.
I will grant salvation to Zion,
    my splendor to Israel.

twi: Babilonia Asehwe“Sian kɔ, tena mfutuma mu,Ɔbabea Babilonia;tena fam na mfa ahengua,Babiloniafo hemmea kuropɔn.Wɔremfrɛ wo bio se,nsiforo anaa nea ne ho yɛ na.
english:
“Go down, sit in the dust,
    Virgin Daughter Babylon;
sit on the ground without a throne,
    queen city of the Babylonians.
No more will you be called
    tender or delicate.

twi: Fa awiyammo na yam esiam;yi wo nkataanim no.Ma wʼatade so kɔ soro, na wo nan ho ngu hɔ,na fa nsuwansuwa no mu.
english:
Take millstones and grind flour;
    take off your veil.
Lift up your skirts, bare your legs,
    and wade through the streams.

twi: Wʼadagyaw bɛda adina wʼanimguase so renkata.Mɛtɔ were;meremfa obiara ho nkyɛ no.”
english:
Your nakedness will be exposed
    and your shame uncovered.
I will take vengeance;
    I will spare no one.”

twi: Yɛn Gyefo, Asafo Awurade ne ne din,ɔno ne Israel Kronkronni.
english:
Our Redeemer—the Lord Almighty is his name—
    is the Holy One of Israel.

twi: “Tena ase dinn, kɔhyɛ sum mu,Babiloniafo hemmea kurow;wɔremfrɛ wo bio seahenni ahorow so hemmea.
english:
“Sit in silence, go into darkness,
    queen city of the Babylonians;
no more will you be called
    queen of kingdoms.

twi: Me bo fuw me nkurɔfo,na miguu mʼagyapade ho fi;mede wɔn hyɛɛ wo nsa,na woanhu wɔn mmɔbɔ.Nkwakoraa koraa mpo,wosoaa wɔn konnua duruduru.
english:
I was angry with my people
    and desecrated my inheritance;
I gave them into your hand,
    and you showed them no mercy.
Even on the aged
    you laid a very heavy yoke.

twi: Wokae se, ‘Mɛkɔ so daa,ayɛ ɔhemmea afebɔɔ.’Nanso woannwen saa nneɛma yi hona woansusuw nea ebetumi asi ho.
english:
You said, ‘I am forever—
    the eternal queen!’
But you did not consider these things
    or reflect on what might happen.

twi: “Afei tie, wo oguamanfo,woredwudwo wo ho wɔ wo bammɔ muna woka kyerɛ wo ho se,‘me ne no, na obiara nni hɔ sɛ me.Merenyɛ okunafo dana merenni awommawu.’
english:
“Now then, listen, you lover of pleasure,
    lounging in your security
and saying to yourself,
    ‘I am, and there is none besides me.
I will never be a widow
    or suffer the loss of children.’

twi: Saa nneɛma abien yi bɛto woprɛko pɛ, da koro pɛ:awommawu ne kunayɛ.Saa nneɛma yi bɛba wo so pa ara,wʼabayisɛm bebrebe yine ntafowayi a mu yɛ den nyinaa akyi.
english:
Both of these will overtake you
    in a moment, on a single day:
    loss of children and widowhood.
They will come upon you in full measure,
    in spite of your many sorceries
    and all your potent spells.

twi: Wode wo ho ato wʼamumɔyɛ sona waka se, ‘Obiara nhu me.’Wo nyansa ne nimdeɛ ma wo fom kwanbere a woka kyerɛ wo ho se,‘Me ne no, obiara nni hɔ ka me ho.’
english:
You have trusted in your wickedness
    and have said, ‘No one sees me.’
Your wisdom and knowledge mislead you
    when you say to yourself,
    ‘I am, and there is none besides me.’

twi: Amanehunu bɛto wo,na worenhu ɔkwan ko a wobɛfa so ayi afi hɔ.Ɔhaw bi bɛba wo soa worentumi mfa mpata nyi mfi hɔ;atoyerɛnkyɛm a ɛnnaa ne ho adi nkyerɛɛ wobɛba wo so mpofirim.
english:
Disaster will come upon you,
    and you will not know how to conjure it away.
A calamity will fall upon you
    that you cannot ward off with a ransom;
a catastrophe you cannot foresee
    will suddenly come upon you.

twi: “Kɔ so yɛ wo ntafowayine wʼabayisɛm bebrebea wode adi dwuma fi wo mmofraase no.Ebia wubedi nkonim,ebia wode ehu bɛba.
english:
“Keep on, then, with your magic spells
    and with your many sorceries,
    which you have labored at since childhood.
Perhaps you will succeed,
    perhaps you will cause terror.

twi: Woabrɛ wɔ afotufo bebrebe a woanya no mu!Ma wo nsoromma ho anyansafo mmra anim,wɔn a wɔhwɛ nsoromma mu no, ka nea ɛreba ɔsram biara mu no,ma wonnye wo mfi nea ɛreba wo so no mu.
english:
All the counsel you have received has only worn you out!
    Let your astrologers come forward,
those stargazers who make predictions month by month,
    let them save you from what is coming upon you.

twi: Nokwarem, wɔte sɛ gyentia;ogya bɛhyew wɔn.Na wontumi nnye wɔn ankasa homfi ogyaframa anoden no ho.Nnyansramma biara nni ha a ɛbɛka obiara hyew;ogya biara nni ha a wɔbɛtena ho ato.
Nea wobetumi ayɛ ama wo ara ne no,eyinom na wo ne wɔn abrɛna wo ne wɔn anantew fi mmofraase.Wɔn mu biara kɔ so yɛ ne mfomso;ɔbaako mpo nni hɔ a obetumi agye wo.
english:
That is all they are to you—
    these you have dealt with
    and labored with since childhood.
All of them go on in their error;
    there is not one that can save you.

twi: Israel Ɔsoɔdenfo“Muntie eyi, Yakobfifomo a wɔde Israel din frɛ mo,na moyɛ Yuda asefo,mo a mobɔ Awurade din ka ntam,na mofrɛ Israel Nyankopɔn,nanso ɛnyɛ nokware anaa trenee mu,
english:
“Listen to this, you descendants of Jacob,
    you who are called by the name of Israel
    and come from the line of Judah,
you who take oaths in the name of the Lord
    and invoke the God of Israel—
    but not in truth or righteousness—

twi: mo a mofrɛ mo ho kurow kronkron no mmana mode mo ho to Israel Nyankopɔn so,Asafo Awurade ne ne din.
english:
you who call yourselves citizens of the holy city
    and claim to rely on the God of Israel—
    the Lord Almighty is his name:

twi: Mehyɛɛ nneɛma a atwa mu no ho nkɔm dedaada,mebɔɔ nkae, na medaa no adi;afei mpofirim mekekaa me ho na ɛbaa mu.
Na minim sɛnea moyɛ asoɔden famo kɔn ho ntin yɛ dadena mo moma yɛ kɔbere mfrafrae.
Enti, mekaa saa nsɛm yi kyerɛɛ mo dedaadaansa na ɛrebesisi no, mebɔɔ mo nkaesɛnea morentumi nka se,‘Mʼahoni na wɔyɛe:me dua nsɛsode ne me dade nyame na ɔhyɛe.’
Moate eyinom nyinaa; monhwɛ wɔn nyinaa.Morennye wɔn nto mu ana?“Efi saa bere yi de rekɔ mɛka nsɛm foforo akyerɛ mo,ɛfa nneɛma a ahintaw a munnim ho.
english:
You have heard these things; look at them all.
    Will you not admit them?
“From now on I will tell you of new things,
    of hidden things unknown to you.

twi: Afei na wɔayɛ koraa, ɛnkyɛe;ebesi nnɛ no na anka montee ho hwee.Enti morentumi nka se,‘Yiw na minim dedaw!’
english:
They are created now, and not long ago;
    you have not heard of them before today.
So you cannot say,
    ‘Yes, I knew of them.’

twi: Wontee, na wontee ase;efi tete nyinaa wʼaso asiw.Na minim sɛ woyɛ ɔfatwafo;wɔfrɛɛ wo otuatewfo fi ɔyafunu mu.
Me din nti metwentwɛn mʼabufuw so;mʼayeyi nti miyi fi wo so,sɛnea merensɛe wo koraa.
Hwɛ mahoa mo ho, ɛnyɛ sɛnea wɔnan dwetɛ ho;mmom, masɔ wo ahwɛ wɔ amanehunu fononoo mu.
english:
See, I have refined you, though not as silver;
    I have tested you in the furnace of affliction.

twi: Me nti, me nti, na meyɛ eyi.Adɛn nti na ɛsɛ sɛ mema ho kwan na wɔsɛe me din?Memma obi nnye mʼanuonyam.
english:
For my own sake, for my own sake, I do this.
    How can I let myself be defamed?
    I will not yield my glory to another.

twi: Israel Ahofadi“Tie me, Yakob,Israel a mafrɛ no;Me ne no;Me ne odikanfo ne okyikafo.
english:
“Listen to me, Jacob,
    Israel, whom I have called:
I am he;
    I am the first and I am the last.

twi: Me ara me nsa na ɛtoo asase fapem,na me nsa na ɛtrɛw ɔsorosoro mu;sɛ mefrɛ wɔn a,wɔn nyinaa bɔ mu sɔre.
english:
My own hand laid the foundations of the earth,
    and my right hand spread out the heavens;
when I summon them,
    they all stand up together.

twi: “Mo nyinaa mommɔ mu mmra mmetie:ahoni no mu nea ɔwɔ he na waka saa nsɛm yi dedaw?Awurade boafo a wapaw nobɛma nʼatirimpɔw a etia Babilonia aba mu;ne basa betia Babiloniafo.
english:
“Come together, all of you, and listen:
    Which of the idols has foretold these things?
The Lord’s chosen ally
    will carry out his purpose against Babylon;
    his arm will be against the Babylonians.

twi: Me, me na makasa.Yiw, mafrɛ no.Mede no bɛba,na obewie nʼadwuma nkonimdi so.
english:
I, even I, have spoken;
    yes, I have called him.
I will bring him,
    and he will succeed in his mission.

twi: “Montwiw mmɛn me na muntie eyi:“Efi nkaebɔ a edi kan no, menkasaa wɔ kokoa mu;bere biara a ebesi no, na mewɔ hɔ.”Na afei Asafo Awuradede ne Honhom asoma me.
english:
“Come near me and listen to this:
“From the first announcement I have not spoken in secret;
    at the time it happens, I am there.”
And now the Sovereign Lord has sent me,
    endowed with his Spirit.

twi: Sɛɛ na Awurade se,mo gyefo, Israel Kronkronni no:“Mene Awurade mo Nyankopɔn,nea ɔkyerɛ mo nea eye ma mo,na ɔkyerɛ mo ɔkwan a ɛsɛ sɛ mofa so.
english:
This is what the Lord says—
    your Redeemer, the Holy One of Israel:
“I am the Lord your God,
    who teaches you what is best for you,
    who directs you in the way you should go.

twi: Sɛ mudii mʼahyɛde so a,anka mo asomdwoe ayɛ sɛ asubɔnten,na mo trenee ayɛ sɛ po asorɔkye.
english:
If only you had paid attention to my commands,
    your peace would have been like a river,
    your well-being like the waves of the sea.

twi: Anka mo asefo ayɛ sɛ nwea,na mo mma ayɛ sɛ ne mmosea a wontumi nkan;wɔn din rempepa dawɔrensɛe mfi mʼanim.”
english:
Your descendants would have been like the sand,
    your children like its numberless grains;
their name would never be blotted out
    nor destroyed from before me.”

twi: Mumfi Babilonia,munguan mfi Babiloniafo nkyɛn!Momfa osebɔ nteɛmu mmɔ nkaena mompae mu nka eyi.Momfa nkɔ nsase ano;monka se, “Awurade abegye ne somfo Yakob.”
english:
Leave Babylon,
