    and wail in brokenness of spirit.

twi: Wubegyaw din bi a ɛbɛyɛ mmusuama wɔn a mapaw wɔn;Otumfo Awurade bekum wona nʼasomfo de, mɛma wɔn din foforo.
english:
You will leave your name
    for my chosen ones to use in their curses;
the Sovereign Lord will put you to death,
    but to his servants he will give another name.

twi: Obiara a ɔsrɛ nhyira wɔ asase no so no,bɛyɛ wɔ nokware Nyankopɔn koro no mu;obiara a ɔka ntam wɔ asase no sobɛka no wɔ nokware Nyankopɔn koro no mu.Na ɔhaw a atwa mu no wɔn werɛ befina wɔde behintaw me.
english:
Whoever invokes a blessing in the land
    will do so by the one true God;
whoever takes an oath in the land
    will swear by the one true God.
For the past troubles will be forgotten
    and hidden from my eyes.

twi: “Hwɛ! Mɛbɔɔsorosoro foforo ne asase foforo.Wɔrenkae nneɛma a atwam no bio,na ɛremma adwene mu nso.
english:
“See, I will create
    new heavens and a new earth.
The former things will not be remembered,
    nor will they come to mind.

twi: Nanso momma mo ani nnye na munni ahurusi afebɔɔwɔ nea merebɛbɔ ho,efisɛ mɛbɔ Yerusalem ama ayɛ anigye,na mu nnipa ayɛ anigye farebae.
english:
But be glad and rejoice forever
    in what I will create,
for I will create Jerusalem to be a delight
    and its people a joy.

twi: Mɛsɛpɛw me ho wɔ Yerusalem mu,na madi ahurusi wɔ me nkurɔfo ho.Na wɔrente agyaadwo ne osu nnyigyeiwɔ mu bio.
english:
I will rejoice over Jerusalem
    and take delight in my people;
the sound of weeping and of crying
    will be heard in it no more.

twi: “Ɛrensi bio wɔ muabofra a ne nkwanna yɛ kakraa bi,anaa akwakoraa a onni ne mfe nwie;nea odi mfe ɔha na owu nowɔbɛfa no sɛ ɔbabun bi kɛkɛ;na nea wannya mfe ɔha nowɔbɛfa no sɛ wɔadome no.
english:
“Never again will there be in it
    an infant who lives but a few days,
    or an old man who does not live out his years;
the one who dies at a hundred
    will be thought a mere child;
the one who fails to reach a hundred
    will be considered accursed.

twi: Wobesisi afi na wɔatena mu,wɔbɛyɛ bobe nturo na wɔadi mu aba.
english:
They will build houses and dwell in them;
    they will plant vineyards and eat their fruit.

twi: Wɔrensisi afi mma afoforo mmɛtena mu bio,na wɔrennua mma afoforo mmedi.Na nna a dua di no,saa ara na me nkurɔfo nna bɛyɛ;me nkurɔfo a mapaw wɔn no bediwɔn nsa ano adwuma so aba akyɛ.
english:
No longer will they build houses and others live in them,
    or plant and others eat.
For as the days of a tree,
    so will be the days of my people;
my chosen ones will long enjoy
    the work of their hands.

twi: Wɔremmrɛ nguna wɔrenwo mma a wɔn nkrabea nye;efisɛ wɔbɛyɛ nnipa a Awurade ahyira wɔn,wɔne wɔn asefo.
Mebua wɔn ansa, mpo, na wɔafrɛ me.Bere a wogu so rekasa no metie.
english:
Before they call I will answer;
    while they are still speaking I will hear.

twi: Pataku ne oguamma bedidi abɔ mugyata bɛwe sare sɛ nantwi,nanso mfutuma bɛyɛ ɔwɔ aduan.Wɔrempira obi anaa wɔrensɛe obiwɔ me bepɔw kronkron so nyinaa,”sɛnea Awurade se ni.
english:
The wolf and the lamb will feed together,
    and the lion will eat straw like the ox,
    and dust will be the serpent’s food.
They will neither harm nor destroy
    on all my holy mountain,”
says the Lord.

twi: Atemmu Ne AnidasoSɛɛ na Awurade se:“Ɔsoro yɛ mʼahengua,na asase yɛ me nan ntiaso.Ofi a wubesi ama me no wɔ he?Ɛhe na ɛbɛyɛ me homebea?
english:
This is what the Lord says:
“Heaven is my throne,
    and the earth is my footstool.
Where is the house you will build for me?
    Where will my resting place be?

twi: Ɛnyɛ me nsa na ɛyɛɛ eyinom nyinaa,na ɛma ɛbae ana?”Awurade na ose.“Obi a mʼani sɔ no ni:nea ɔwɔ ahobrɛase ne ahonu honhom,na ne ho popo wɔ mʼasɛm ho.
english:
Has not my hand made all these things,
    and so they came into being?”
declares the Lord.
“These are the ones I look on with favor:
    those who are humble and contrite in spirit,
    and who tremble at my word.

twi: Nanso obi a ɔde nantwinini bɔ afɔre nosaa onipa no ara kum nnipa,na nea ɔma oguamma no,saa onipa no ara bu ɔkraman kɔn mu;nea ɔbɔ aduan afɔre nosaa onipa no ara de prako mogya bɔ afɔre,nea ɔhyew nnuhuam a ɛwɔ din nosaa onipa no ara som ɔbosom.Wɔafa wɔn ankasa akwanna wɔn akra ani gye wɔn akyiwade ho;
english:
But whoever sacrifices a bull
    is like one who kills a person,
and whoever offers a lamb
    is like one who breaks a dog’s neck;
whoever makes a grain offering
    is like one who presents pig’s blood,
and whoever burns memorial incense
    is like one who worships an idol.
They have chosen their own ways,
    and they delight in their abominations;

twi: enti me nso mɛpɛ ayayade ayɛ wɔnna mede nea wosuro bɛba wɔn so.Efisɛ mefrɛe no, obiara annye so,mekasae no, obiara antie.Wɔyɛɛ bɔne wɔ mʼani sona wɔyɛɛ nea mempɛ.”
english:
so I also will choose harsh treatment for them
    and will bring on them what they dread.
For when I called, no one answered,
    when I spoke, no one listened.
They did evil in my sight
    and chose what displeases me.”

twi: Muntie Awurade asɛm,mo a mote nʼasɛm a mo ho popo:“Mo nuanom mmarima a wɔtan mo,na me din nti wotwa mo gyaw no, aka se,‘Momma wɔnhyɛ Awurade anuonyam,na yɛahu mo anigye!’Nanso wɔn anim begu ase.
english:
Hear the word of the Lord,
    you who tremble at his word:
“Your own people who hate you,
    and exclude you because of my name, have said,
‘Let the Lord be glorified,
    that we may see your joy!’
    Yet they will be put to shame.

twi: Muntie huuyɛ a efi kuropɔn no mu,muntie gyegyeegye a efi asɔredan no mu!Ɛyɛ Awurade nnyigyeia ɔde retua nʼatamfo ka sɛnea ɛfata wɔn.
english:
Hear that uproar from the city,
    hear that noise from the temple!
It is the sound of the Lord
    repaying his enemies all they deserve.

twi: “Ansa na ɔbea bɛkyem no,ɔwo;ansa na ɔbɛte awoyaw noɔwo ɔbabarima.
english:
“Before she goes into labor,
    she gives birth;
before the pains come upon her,
    she delivers a son.

twi: Hena na wate biribi sɛɛ ho asɛm pɛn?Hena na wahu biribi sɛɛ pɛn?Wobetumi de da koro akyekyere ɔmansin,anaa ɔman mu, bere sin bi mu ana?Nanso awo ka Sion ara pɛ aɔwo ne mma.
english:
Who has ever heard of such things?
    Who has ever seen things like this?
Can a country be born in a day
    or a nation be brought forth in a moment?
Yet no sooner is Zion in labor
    than she gives birth to her children.

twi: Mede obi bedu awoko ano amemma no nwo ana?” Sɛnea Awurade se ni.“Misiw awotwaa anobere a awo adu so ana?” Wo Nyankopɔn na ose.
english:
Do I bring to the moment of birth
    and not give delivery?” says the Lord.
“Do I close up the womb
    when I bring to delivery?” says your God.

twi: Mo ne Yerusalem ani nnye na munni ahurusi mma no,mo a modɔ no nyinaa;mo ne no nsɛpɛw mo ho yiye,mo a mudi ne ho awerɛhow nyinaa.
english:
“Rejoice with Jerusalem and be glad for her,
    all you who love her;
rejoice greatly with her,
    all you who mourn over her.

twi: Mubenum nʼawerɛkyekye nufuno amee;mobɛnom aboro sona mo ani begye nea abu so atra so no ho.
english:
For you will nurse and be satisfied
    at her comforting breasts;
you will drink deeply
    and delight in her overflowing abundance.”

twi: Na sɛɛ na Awurade se:“Mede asomdwoe bɛma no sɛ asubɔnten,ne amanaman no ahonya nso sɛ asuten a ayiri.Mubenum na waturu mo wɔ ne basa sona obegyigye mo agoru wɔ nʼanankoroma so.
english:
For this is what the Lord says:
“I will extend peace to her like a river,
    and the wealth of nations like a flooding stream;
you will nurse and be carried on her arm
    and dandled on her knees.

twi: Sɛnea ɛna kyekye ne ba werɛ nosaa ara na mɛkyekye mo werɛ;na mubenya awerɛkyekye wɔ Yerusalem.”
Sɛ muhu eyi a, mo koma ani begyena mobɛyɛ frɔmfrɔm sɛ sare;wobehu Awurade nsa wɔ ne nkoa so,nanso wobehu nʼabufuwhyew wɔ nʼatamfo so.
english:
When you see this, your heart will rejoice
    and you will flourish like grass;
the hand of the Lord will be made known to his servants,
    but his fury will be shown to his foes.

twi: Hwɛ, Awurade de ogya reba,na ne nteaseɛnam te sɛ mfɛtɛ;ɔde nʼabufuw bɛba wɔ anibere so,na ɔde gyaframa ayɛ nʼanimka.
english:
See, the Lord is coming with fire,
    and his chariots are like a whirlwind;
he will bring down his anger with fury,
    and his rebuke with flames of fire.

twi: Ogya ne nʼafoa,na Awurade de bebu nnipa nyinaa atɛn,na wɔn a wɔbɛtotɔ wɔ Awurade nsa ano bɛyɛ bebree.
english:
For with fire and with his sword
    the Lord will execute judgment on all people,
    and many will be those slain by the Lord.

twi: “Wɔn a wɔtew wɔn ho na wodwira wɔn ho de kɔ nturo mu, na wodi ɔbaako a ɔfra wɔn a wɔwe mprakonam ne akisi ne nneɛma a ɛyɛ akyiwade akyi no, wɔbɛbɔ mu ahu wɔn awiei,” sɛnea Awurade se ni.
english: “Those who consecrate and purify themselves to go into the gardens, following one who is among those who eat the flesh of pigs, rats and other unclean things—they will meet their end together with the one they follow,” declares the Lord.

twi: “Esiane wɔn nneyɛe ne wɔn nsusuwii nti, Me, mereba abɛboaboa amanaman ne ɔkasa ahorow ano, na wɔbɛba abehu mʼanuonyam.
english: “And I, because of what they have planned and done, am about to come and gather the people of all nations and languages, and they will come and see my glory.

twi: “Na mɛyɛ nsɛnkyerɛnne bi wɔ wɔn mu, na mede nkae no mu bi bɛkɔ amanaman no mu: Tarsis, Libiafo ne Lidiafo (wɔn a wɔagye din wɔ agyantow mu), Tubal ne Helafo, ne asupɔw a ɛwɔ akyirikyiri a wɔntee me din a ahyeta na wonhuu mʼanuonyam no. Wɔbɛpae mu aka mʼanuonyam wɔ amanaman mu.
english: “I will set a sign among them, and I will send some of those who survive to the nations—to Tarshish, to the Libyans and Lydians (famous as archers), to Tubal and Greece, and to the distant islands that have not heard of my fame or seen my glory. They will proclaim my glory among the nations.

twi: Na wɔde mo nuabarimanom nyinaa befi amanaman nyinaa so bɛba me bepɔw kronkron a ɛwɔ Yerusalem no so sɛ, afɔrebɔde ama Awurade. Wɔtete apɔnkɔ so ne nteaseɛnam mu ne asako mu ne mfurumpɔnkɔ ne yoma so bɛba,” sɛɛ na Awurade se. “Wɔde wɔn bɛba sɛnea Israelfo de wɔn aduan afɔre kɔ Awurade asɔredan mu, wɔ afahyɛ nkuruwa a ho tew mu.
english: And they will bring all your people, from all the nations, to my holy mountain in Jerusalem as an offering to the Lord—on horses, in chariots and wagons, and on mules and camels,” says the Lord. “They will bring them, as the Israelites bring their grain offerings, to the temple of the Lord in ceremonially clean vessels.

twi: Na meyi wɔn mu bi ayɛ asɔfo ne Lewifo,” Awurade, na ose!
english: And I will select some of them also to be priests and Levites,” says the Lord.

twi: “Sɛnea ɔsorosoro foforo ne asase foforo bɛtena hɔ no, saa ara na mo din ne mo asefo bɛtena hɔ,” sɛnea Awurade se ni.
english: “As the new heavens and the new earth that I make will endure before me,” declares the Lord, “so will your name and descendants endure.

twi: “Efi Ɔsram Foforo baako kɔpem foforo, efi Homeda baako kosi foforo no, adesamma nyinaa bɛba abɛkotow me,” sɛnea Awurade se ni.
english: From one New Moon to another and from one Sabbath to another, all mankind will come and bow down before me,” says the Lord.

twi: “Na wobefi adi akohu wɔn a wɔtew atua tiaa me no afunu; wɔn asunson renwu, na wɔn gya nso rennum, na wɔn ho bɛyɛ adesamma nyinaa nwini.”
english: “And they will go out and look on the dead bodies of those who rebelled against me; the worms that eat them will not die, the fire that burns them will not be quenched, and they will be loathsome to all mankind.”

twi: Saa krataa yi fi me Yakobo a meyɛ Onyankopɔn ne Awurade Yesu Kristo somfo nkyɛn,Mikyia mmusuakuw dumien a wɔahwete no nyinaa.
english:
James, a servant of God and of the Lord Jesus Christ,
To the twelve tribes scattered among the nations:
Greetings.

twi: Gyidi Ne NyansaAnuanom, sɛ sɔhwɛ bi ba mo akwan mu a, momma mo ani nnye
english: Consider it pure joy, my brothers and sisters, whenever you face trials of many kinds,

twi: efisɛ sɛ mo gyidi tumi gyina sɔhwɛ no ano a, ɛno ansa na munya ntoboase.
english: because you know that the testing of your faith produces perseverance.

twi: Momma ntoboase no ntena mo mu daa nyinaa sɛnea ɛbɛyɛ a mobɛyɛ pɛ a biribiara ho renhia mo.
english: Let perseverance finish its work so that you may be mature and complete, not lacking anything.

twi: Sɛ nyansa ho hia mo mu bi a, ɛsɛ sɛ ɔbɔ mpae srɛ Onyankopɔn na ɔbɛma no bi, efisɛ Onyankopɔn fi ayamye ne adom mu ma obiara nea ehia no no kwa.
english: If any of you lacks wisdom, you should ask God, who gives generously to all without finding fault, and it will be given to you.

twi: Na sɛ worebɔ mpae a, ɛsɛ sɛ wugye di a wunnye ho akyinnye. Obiara a ogye akyinnye no te sɛ po asorɔkye a mframa bɔ no kɔ baabiara a ɛpɛ.
english: But when you ask, you must believe and not doubt, because the one who doubts is like a wave of the sea, blown and tossed by the wind.

twi: Ɛnsɛ sɛ saa onipa no susuw sɛ obenya biribiara afi Awurade nkyɛn;
english: That person should not expect to receive anything from the Lord.

twi: nʼadwene yɛ no ntanta a ontumi nsi biribiara pi.
english: Such a person is double-minded and unstable in all they do.

twi: Ohia Ne AhonyaSɛ Onyankopɔn ma onua hiani so a, ɛsɛ sɛ nʼani gye,
english: Believers in humble circumstances ought to take pride in their high position.

twi: na adefo a wabrɛ wɔn ase no nso saa ara. Efisɛ, adefo no twam kɔ sɛ wuram afifide bi.
english: But the rich should take pride in their humiliation—since they will pass away like a wild flower.

twi: Owia pue de ne hyew no hyew afifide no ma nʼahoɔfɛ sɛe. Saa ara na wɔbɛsɛe adefo no wɔ bere a wogu so redi wɔn nnwuma no.
english: For the sun rises with scorching heat and withers the plant; its blossom falls and its beauty is destroyed. In the same way, the rich will fade away even while they go about their business.

twi: SɔhwɛNhyira nka onipa a onya gyidi wɔ amanehunu mu, efisɛ ɔno na obenya akyɛde a Onyankopɔn ahyɛ ho bɔ ama wɔn a wɔdɔ no no.
english: Blessed is the one who perseveres under trial because, having stood the test, that person will receive the crown of life that the Lord has promised to those who love him.

twi: Sɛ wɔsɔ obi hwɛ a, ɛnsɛ sɛ ɔka se, “Saa sɔhwɛ yi fi Onyankopɔn.” Efisɛ bɔne rentumi nsɔ Onyankopɔn nhwɛ, na ɔno Onyankopɔn nso nsɔ obi nhwɛ.
english: When tempted, no one should say, “God is tempting me.” For God cannot be tempted by evil, nor does he tempt anyone;

twi: Na sɛ onipa twe ne ho na ɔno ara nʼakɔnnɔ yi no a, na ayɛ sɔhwɛ ama no.
english: but each person is tempted when they are dragged away by their own evil desire and enticed.

twi: Na sɛ akɔnnɔ no nyinsɛn a, ɛwo bɔne, na bɔne no nyin a ɛwo owu.
english: Then, after desire has conceived, it gives birth to sin; and sin, when it is full-grown, gives birth to death.

twi: Me nuanom adɔfo, mommma wɔnnnaadaa mo.
english: Don’t be deceived, my dear brothers and sisters.

twi: Akyɛde pa ne akyɛde a ɛyɛ pɛ nyinaa fi ɔsoro; efi Onyankopɔn a ɔbɔɔ ɔsoro hann no nkyɛn na ɛba. Ɔno na ɔnsesa sɛ sunsuma.
english: Every good and perfect gift is from above, coming down from the Father of the heavenly lights, who does not change like shifting shadows.

twi: Ofi ne pɛ mu nam nokware a ɛwɔ asɛm no mu no so woo yɛn sɛnea ɛbɛyɛ a, yebedi kan wɔ abɔde nyinaa mu.
english: He chose to give us birth through the word of truth, that we might be a kind of firstfruits of all he created.

twi: Otie Ne ƆyɛMe nuanom adɔfo, monhyɛ eyinom nsow: monyɛ ntɛm ntie, monyɛ nyaa nkasa na monyɛ nyaa mfa abufuw;
english: My dear brothers and sisters, take note of this: Everyone should be quick to listen, slow to speak and slow to become angry,

twi: efisɛ onipa abufuw no mma onnya Onyankopɔn trenee no.
english: because human anger does not produce the righteousness that God desires.

twi: Ɛno nti, montwe mo ho mfi afide ne atirimɔden ho. Momfa mo ho mma Onyankopɔn na munnye asɛm a odua wɔ mo koma mu a ebegye mo nkwa no.
english: Therefore, get rid of all moral filth and the evil that is so prevalent and humbly accept the word planted in you, which can save you.

twi: Munntie asɛm no sɛ atiefo kwa nsisi mo ho, na mmom monyɛ asɛm no yɛfo.
english: Do not merely listen to the word, and so deceive yourselves. Do what it says.

twi: Obiara a otie asɛm no na ɔmfa nni dwuma no te sɛ obi a ɔhwɛ ahwehwɛ mu, na ohu sɛnea ɔte.
english: Anyone who listens to the word but does not do what it says is like someone who looks at his face in a mirror

twi: Ɔhwɛ ne ho wɔ ahwehwɛ no mu hu ne ho yiye na sɛ ofi ahwehwɛ no anim ara pɛ a, ne werɛ fi nea ohuu no nyinaa.
english: and, after looking at himself, goes away and immediately forgets what he looks like.

twi: Nanso obiara a ɔhwɛ mmara a ɛyɛ pɛ, na ɛma onipa de ne ho no mu yiye, na odi so, na otie, na ne werɛ mfi, na ɔde di dwuma no, Onyankopɔn behyira saa onipa no wɔ biribiara a ɔyɛ mu.
english: But whoever looks intently into the perfect law that gives freedom, and continues in it—not forgetting what they have heard, but doing it—they will be blessed in what they do.

twi: Sɛ obi susuw sɛ ɔyɛ Onyamesomni na wanto ne tɛkrɛma nnareka a, ne nyamesom no so nni mfaso na ɔdaadaa ne ho nso.
english: Those who consider themselves religious and yet do not keep a tight rein on their tongues deceive themselves, and their religion is worthless.

twi: Nea Agya Onyankopɔn fa no sɛ ɛyɛ onyamesom pa no ni: Ɔhwɛ nyisaa ne akunafo wɔ wɔn ahohia mu, na oyi ne ho fi wiase porɔwee ho.
english: Religion that God our Father accepts as pure and faultless is this: to look after orphans and widows in their distress and to keep oneself from being polluted by the world.

twi: KɔkɔbɔMe nuanom, sɛ moyɛ agyidifo wɔ Awurade Kristo anuonyam mu yi, monnyɛ nhwɛanim.
english: My brothers and sisters, believers in our glorious Lord Jesus Christ must not show favoritism.

twi: Sɛ muhyia a, ɔdefo a ɔhyɛ mpɛtea ne ntade pa ne ohiani bi nso a ɔhyɛ ntadegow nyinaa tumi ba bi.
english: Suppose a man comes into your meeting wearing a gold ring and fine clothes, and a poor man in filthy old clothes also comes in.

twi: Sɛ wode nidi ma nea wasiesie ne ho yiye no, na woka kyerɛ no se, “Tena saa akongua pa yi so,” na woka kyerɛ ohiani no nso se, “Sɔre gyina hɔ anaa tena fam wɔ me nan ase ha” a,
english: If you show special attention to the man wearing fine clothes and say, “Here’s a good seat for you,” but say to the poor man, “You stand there” or “Sit on the floor by my feet,”

twi: wudi fɔ sɛ wugyina atemmu a efi adwemmɔne mu de nyiyimu abɛto mo mu no ho.
english: have you not discriminated among yourselves and become judges with evil thoughts?

twi: Me nuanom adɔfo, muntie! Onyankopɔn yii wiase yi mu ahiafo sɛ wɔnyɛ adefo wɔ gyidi mu na wɔanya ahenni a ɔhyɛɛ wɔn a wɔdɔ no no ho bɔ no.
english: Listen, my dear brothers and sisters: Has not God chosen those who are poor in the eyes of the world to be rich in faith and to inherit the kingdom he promised those who love him?

twi: Nanso moammu ahiafo! Ɛhefo na wodi mo nya twe mo kɔ atemmufo anim? Adefo!
english: But you have dishonored the poor. Is it not the rich who are exploiting you? Are they not the ones who are dragging you into court?

twi: Wɔne nnipa a wɔkasa tia din pa a wɔde ama mo no.
english: Are they not the ones who are blaspheming the noble name of him to whom you belong?

twi: Eye sɛ mudi yɛn Awurade mmara a ɛka se, “Dɔ wo yɔnko sɛ wo ho” no so.
english: If you really keep the royal law found in Scripture, “Love your neighbor as yourself,” you are doing right.

twi: Na sɛ mohwɛ nnipa anim de gye wɔn a, mudi ho fɔ na mmara no di tia mo sɛ mmaratofo.
english: But if you show favoritism, you sin and are convicted by the law as lawbreakers.

twi: Obiara a obu mmara no mu baako pɛ so no bu ne nyinaa so.
english: For whoever keeps the whole law and yet stumbles at just one point is guilty of breaking all of it.

twi: Efisɛ nea ɔkae se, “Nsɛe aware” no, ɔno ara nso na ɔkae se, “Nni awu.” Na sɛ woansɛe aware na wudi awu a, woabu mmara so.
english: For he who said, “You shall not commit adultery,” also said, “You shall not murder.” If you do not commit adultery but do commit murder, you have become a lawbreaker.

twi: Sɛ woyɛ Kristo apɛde o, sɛ woanyɛ nʼapɛde o, wubebu wo ho atɛn. Enti hwɛ asɛm a woka ne nea woyɛ biara yiye.
english: Speak and act as those who are going to be judged by the law that gives freedom,

twi: Efisɛ obi a wanhu mmɔbɔ no, Onyankopɔn atemmu mu no, wɔrenhu no mmɔbɔ. Nanso mmɔborɔhunu bunkam atemmu so.
english: because judgment without mercy will be shown to anyone who has not been merciful. Mercy triumphs over judgment.

twi: Me nuanom, sɛ obi ka se, “Mewɔ gyidi” na onni gyidi no ho dwuma a, mfaso bɛn na ɛwɔ so? Saa gyidi no betumi agye no nkwa ana?
english: What good is it, my brothers and sisters, if someone claims to have faith but has no deeds? Can such faith save them?

twi: Sɛ anuanom bi wɔ hɔ a ntama ho hia wɔn na wonni aduan dodow nso a wobedi,
english: Suppose a brother or a sister is without clothes and daily food.

twi: na sɛ wokɔka kyerɛ wɔn se, “Onyame nhyira mo! Mo ho nyɛ mo hyew na munnidi yiye” na sɛ woamma wɔn asetena yi mu nea ehia wɔn a, papa bɛn na woayɛ wɔn?
english: If one of you says to them, “Go in peace; keep warm and well fed,” but does nothing about their physical needs, what good is it?

twi: Saa ara na gyidi te. Sɛ nneyɛe nka ho a, na awu.
english: In the same way, faith by itself, if it is not accompanied by action, is dead.

twi: Nanso obi betumi aka se, “Obi wɔ gyidi na afoforo nso wɔ nneyɛe.”Me mmuae ne sɛ, “Kyerɛ me sɛnea obi tumi nya gyidi a nneyɛe mmata ho ase. Me de, menam me nneyɛe so bɛkyerɛ wo me gyidi.”
english:
But someone will say, “You have faith; I have deeds.”
Show me your faith without deeds, and I will show you my faith by my deeds.

twi: Wugye di sɛ Onyankopɔn baako pɛ na ɔwɔ hɔ? Eye! Ahonhommɔne nso gye di saa ara na wɔn ho popo wɔ osuro mu.
english: You believe that there is one God. Good! Even the demons believe that—and shudder.

twi: Ɔkwasea! Wopɛ sɛ wɔka kyerɛ wo sɛ gyidi a nneyɛe mmata ho no so nni mfaso ana?
english: You foolish person, do you want evidence that faith without deeds is useless?

twi: Ɛyɛɛ dɛn na Onyankopɔn buu Abraham bem? Ɛnam ne nneyɛe so sɛ ɔde ne ba Isak maa wɔ afɔremuka so no.
english: Was not our father Abraham considered righteous for what he did when he offered his son Isaac on the altar?

twi: Wuhu sɛ ne gyidi ne ne nneyɛe nyinaa redi dwuma na ne nneyɛe no maa ne gyidi no dii mu.
english: You see that his faith and his actions were working together, and his faith was made complete by what he did.

twi: Na Kyerɛwsɛm no baa mu se, Abraham gyee Onyankopɔn dii na esiane ne gyidi no nti, Onyankopɔn gyee no sɛ ɔtreneeni. Enti wɔfrɛ Abraham Onyankopɔn adamfo.
english: And the scripture was fulfilled that says, “Abraham believed God, and it was credited to him as righteousness,” and he was called God’s friend.

twi: Eyi da no adi pefee sɛ Onyankopɔn nam onipa nneyɛe so na obu no bem, na ɛnnam ne gyidi nko so.
english: You see that a person is considered righteous by what they do and not by faith alone.

twi: Saa ara na ɛte wɔ aguaman Rahab ho. Ne nneyɛe maa Onyankopɔn buu no bem, efisɛ ogyee Yudafo bi a wɔsomaa wɔn, boaa wɔn ma woguan faa ɔkwan foforo bi so.
english: In the same way, was not even Rahab the prostitute considered righteous for what she did when she gave lodging to the spies and sent them off in a different direction?

twi: Sɛnea onipadua a honhom nni mu awu no, saa ara nso na gyidi a nneyɛe mmata ho no nso awu.
english: As the body without the spirit is dead, so faith without deeds is dead.

twi: TɛkrɛmaMe nuanom, ɛnyɛ mo nyinaa na ɛsɛ sɛ moyɛ mo ho akyerɛkyerɛfo, efisɛ munim sɛ yɛn akyerɛkyerɛfo de, sɛ yɛfom a, wobebu yɛn atɛn a mu yɛ den sen afoforo.
english: Not many of you should become teachers, my fellow believers, because you know that we who teach will be judged more strictly.

twi: Yɛn nyinaa taa yɛ mfomso. Onipa a ɔnyɛ mfomso wɔ nea ɔka mu no yɛ pɛ a obetumi ahyɛ ne nipadua no so.
english: We all stumble in many ways. Anyone who is never at fault in what they say is perfect, able to keep their whole body in check.

twi: Yɛde nnareka to ɔpɔnkɔ anom sɛnea obetie yɛn na yɛatumi ama wakɔ baabiara a yɛpɛ sɛ ɔkɔ.
english: When we put bits into the mouths of horses to make them obey us, we can turn the whole animal.

twi: Anaasɛ dwene hyɛn ho; sɛnea ne kɛse te a mframa a ano yɛ den na ɛbɔ no, nanso wotumi de sitia ketewaa bi na ɛdannan no ma ɛkɔ baabi a hyɛnkafo no pɛ sɛ ɛkɔ no.
english: Or take ships as an example. Although they are so large and are driven by strong winds, they are steered by a very small rudder wherever the pilot wants to go.

twi: Saa ara na tɛkrɛma te; sua a esua nyinaa akyi no, etumi hoahoa ne ho. Hwɛ sɛnea ogya ketewaa bi si tumi hyew kwae kɛse.
english: Likewise, the tongue is a small part of the body, but it makes great boasts. Consider what a great forest is set on fire by a small spark.

twi: Tɛkrɛma nso yɛ ogya, onipa akwaa mu nnebɔne wiase. Ɛsɛe nipadua no nyinaa; ɛsɔ onipa abrabɔ nyinaa so gya na nʼankasa nso ɔsɛe sɔ ne so gya.
english: The tongue also is a fire, a world of evil among the parts of the body. It corrupts the whole body, sets the whole course of one’s life on fire, and is itself set on fire by hell.

twi: Onipa tumi dwudwo mmoadoma, nnomaa, mmoa a wɔwea, po mu mmoa nyinaa,
english: All kinds of animals, birds, reptiles and sea creatures are being tamed and have been tamed by mankind,

twi: nanso obiara rentumi nnwudwo tɛkrɛma da. Ɔyɛ ɔbɔnefo a ɔyɛ hagyahagya a awuduru ahyɛ no ma.
english: but no human being can tame the tongue. It is a restless evil, full of deadly poison.

twi: Yɛde tɛkrɛma kamfo yɛn Awurade ne yɛn Agya na yɛde ɛno ara nso adome nnipa a wɔbɔɔ wɔn Onyankopɔn sɛso so no.
english: With the tongue we praise our Lord and Father, and with it we curse human beings, who have been made in God’s likeness.

twi: Ano koro no ara mu na nkamfo ne nnome fi ba. Me nuanom, ɛnsɛ sɛ ɛba saa.
english: Out of the same mouth come praise and cursing. My brothers and sisters, this should not be.

twi: Nsu pa ne nsu a ɛyɛ nkyenenkyene betumi afi asuti baako mu aba ana?
english: Can both fresh water and salt water flow from the same spring?

twi: Me nuanom, borɔdɔma dua betumi asow ngodua aba ana? Anaasɛ bobe betumi asow borɔdɔma? Saa ara na asuti a ɛyɛ nkyenenkyene remma nsu pa.
english: My brothers and sisters, can a fig tree bear olives, or a grapevine bear figs? Neither can a salt spring produce fresh water.

twi: Nyansa A Efi ƆsoroObi wɔ mo mu a onim nyansa na ɔwɔ ntease? Ɛsɛ sɛ ɔnam abrabɔ pa, nnwuma pa a wɔnam ahobrɛase ne nyansa so, da no adi.
english: Who is wise and understanding among you? Let them show it by their good life, by deeds done in the humility that comes from wisdom.

twi: Na sɛ mowɔ nitan, mansotwe ne pɛsɛmenkominya wɔ mo koma mu a, ɛno de ɛnsɛ sɛ mohoahoa mo ho, na mofa so ka nkontompo tia nokware.
english: But if you harbor bitter envy and selfish ambition in your hearts, do not boast about it or deny the truth.

twi: Saa nyansa yi mfi ɔsoro na ɛbae. Ɛyɛ wiase nyansa na ɛyɛ honhommɔne nso.
english: Such “wisdom” does not come down from heaven but is earthly, unspiritual, demonic.

twi: Baabiara a nitan ne pɛsɛmenkominya wɔ no, basabasa ne bɔne ahorow nyinaa bi wɔ hɔ.
english: For where you have envy and selfish ambition, there you find disorder and every evil practice.

twi: Nanso nyansa a efi ɔsoro no yɛ kronkron; asomdwoe wɔ mu, edwo na ɛpɛ asomdwoe; ɛwɔ ahummɔbɔ na nneyɛe pa fi mu ba; ennye akyinnye na ɛnyɛ nyaatwom nso.
english: But the wisdom that comes from heaven is first of all pure; then peace-loving, considerate, submissive, full of mercy and good fruit, impartial and sincere.

twi: Na ɛsow aba pa a efi aba a asomdwoefo duaa no asomdwoe mu no mu.
english: Peacemakers who sow in peace reap a harvest of righteousness.

twi: Brɛ Wo Ho Ase Ma OnyankopɔnƆko ne akasakasa a asi mo mu yi fi he? Efi mo ara mo akɔnnɔ a ɛne mo nipadua di asi no.
english: What causes fights and quarrels among you? Don’t they come from your desires that battle within you?

twi: Morepɛ nneɛma bi nanso morentumi nnya, ɛno nti moayɛ mo adwene sɛ mubedi awu. Mo ani abere denneennen rehwehwɛ nneɛma bi, nanso mo nsa nka, enti akasakasa ne ɔko nam so ba. Mo nsa renka nea morehwehwɛ no efisɛ mummisa Onyankopɔn.
english: You desire but do not have, so you kill. You covet but you cannot get what you want, so you quarrel and fight. You do not have because you do not ask God.

twi: Na sɛ mubisa koraa nso a, mo nsa renka, efisɛ mowɔ adwemmɔne, sɛ ɛbɛyɛ a mode nea munya no begye mo ani.
english: When you ask, you do not receive, because you ask with wrong motives, that you may spend what you get on your pleasures.

twi: Nnipa a munni gyidi! Munnim sɛ, sɛ mofa wiase adamfo a, na moyɛ Onyankopɔn atamfo? Obiara a ɔpɛ sɛ ɔyɛ wiase adamfo no bɛyɛ Onyankopɔn tamfo.
english: You adulterous people, don’t you know that friendship with the world means enmity against God? Therefore, anyone who chooses to be a friend of the world becomes an enemy of God.

twi: Mususuw sɛ Kyerɛwsɛm a ɛka se, “Ninkutwe ahyɛ honhom a Onyankopɔn de ahyɛ yɛn mu no ma” no wɔkaa no kwa ana?
english: Or do you think Scripture says without reason that he jealously longs for the spirit he has caused to dwell in us?

twi: Nanso adom a Onyankopɔn dom yɛn no dɔɔso yiye. Na Kyerɛwsɛm no ka se,“Onyankopɔn siw ahantanfo kwan,na ɔdom ahobrɛasefo.”
english:
But he gives us more grace. That is why Scripture says:
“God opposes the proud
    but shows favor to the humble.”

twi: Enti momfa mo ho nhyɛ Onyankopɔn ase. Munsiw ɔbonsam kwan, na obeguan afi mo ho.
english: Submit yourselves, then, to God. Resist the devil, and he will flee from you.

twi: Mommɛn Onyankopɔn, na ɔno nso bɛbɛn mo. Monhohoro mo nsa ho, mo nnebɔneyɛfo! Montew mo koma mu, mo a mo adwene yɛ ntanta!
english: Come near to God and he will come near to you. Wash your hands, you sinners, and purify your hearts, you double-minded.

twi: Munni awerɛhow, munsu, na muntwa agyaadwo; momma mo serew nnan osu, na mo anigye nnan awerɛhow.
english: Grieve, mourn and wail. Change your laughter to mourning and your joy to gloom.

twi: Mommrɛ mo ho ase mma Awurade, na ɔbɛma mo so.
english: Humble yourselves before the Lord, and he will lift you up.

twi: Atemmu Ho KɔkɔbɔMe nuanom, munnnidi mo ho nseku. Obiara a ɔkasa tia ne nua anaa obu no atɛn no, kasa tia mmara no. Na sɛ wubu mmara no atɛn a, na ɛkyerɛ sɛ afei de, wunni mmara no so.
english: Brothers and sisters, do not slander one another. Anyone who speaks against a brother or sister or judges them speaks against the law and judges it. When you judge the law, you are not keeping it, but sitting in judgment on it.

twi: Onyankopɔn nko na ɔma mmara na obu atɛn. Ɔno nko na ogye nkwa na ɔsɛe. Wone hena a wubu wo yɔnko atɛn?
english: There is only one Lawgiver and Judge, the one who is able to save and destroy. But you—who are you to judge your neighbor?

twi: Ahohoahoa Ho KɔkɔbɔMo a moka se, “Nnɛ anaa ɔkyena yebetu kwan akɔ kurow bi so akodi afe akɔyɛ adwuma, apɛ sika” no, muntie me.
english: Now listen, you who say, “Today or tomorrow we will go to this or that city, spend a year there, carry on business and make money.”

twi: Munnim nea ɛbɛto mo ɔkyena. Mote sɛ omununkum a ɛba bere tiaa bi na ɛyera.
english: Why, you do not even know what will happen tomorrow. What is your life? You are a mist that appears for a little while and then vanishes.

twi: Asɛm a ɛsɛ sɛ moka ne se, “Sɛ Awurade pɛ a, yɛbɛyɛ eyi anaa eyi.”
english: Instead, you ought to say, “If it is the Lord’s will, we will live and do this or that.”

twi: Nanso mprempren mohoahoa mo ho de mo nsa si mo bo. Saa ahohoahoa no nyinaa yɛ bɔne.
english: As it is, you boast in your arrogant schemes. All such boasting is evil.

twi: Enti nea onim papa yɛ na ɔnyɛ no, ɛyɛ bɔne ma no.
english: If anyone, then, knows the good they ought to do and doesn’t do it, it is sin for them.

twi: Ahonya Ho KɔkɔbɔAfei mo adefo nso muntie! Munsu na muntwa agyaadwo wɔ amanehunu a ɛreba mo so no ho.
english: Now listen, you rich people, weep and wail because of the misery that is coming on you.

twi: Mo ahonya no aporɔw na nwewee awe mo ntama.
english: Your wealth has rotted, and moths have eaten your clothes.

twi: Mo sika ne mo dwetɛ agye nkannare na saa nkannare no bedi adanse atia mo, na ahyew mo honam sɛ ogya. Moahyehyɛ agyapade wɔ nna a edi akyiri no mu.
english: Your gold and silver are corroded. Their corrosion will testify against you and eat your flesh like fire. You have hoarded wealth in the last days.

twi: Muntuaa nnipa a wɔyɛɛ adwuma wɔ mo mfuw mu no ka enti wɔresi apini. Na wɔn apinisi no adu Onyankopɔn, Asafo Awurade no aso mu.
english: Look! The wages you failed to pay the workers who mowed your fields are crying out against you. The cries of the harvesters have reached the ears of the Lord Almighty.

twi: Mo asetena wɔ asase so ha yɛ afɛfɛde ne anigye. Moadɔ srade ama okum da.
english: You have lived on earth in luxury and self-indulgence. You have fattened yourselves in the day of slaughter.

twi: Moabu nea ɔnnsɔre ntia mo no na onni fɔ no kumfɔ akum no.
english: You have condemned and murdered the innocent one, who was not opposing you.

twi: Boasetɔ Ne MpaebɔMe nuanom, montɔ mo bo ase nkosi sɛ Awurade bɛba. Monhwɛ sɛnea okuafo nya boasetɔ twɛn asusow bere.
english: Be patient, then, brothers and sisters, until the Lord’s coming. See how the farmer waits for the land to yield its valuable crop, patiently waiting for the autumn and spring rains.

twi: Ɛsɛ sɛ mo nso motɔ mo bo ase. Momma mo anidaso mu nyɛ den, efisɛ da a Awurade bɛba no abɛn.
english: You too, be patient and stand firm, because the Lord’s coming is near.

twi: Anuanom, munnni nseku ntia mo ho mo ho, na Onyankopɔn ammu mo atɛn. Hwɛ, Otemmufo no gyina ɔpon no ano.
english: Don’t grumble against one another, brothers and sisters, or you will be judged. The Judge is standing at the door!

twi: Me nuanom, monkae adiyifo a wɔde Awurade din kasae no. Momfa wɔn sɛ nhwɛso wɔ wɔn boasetɔ ne tumi a wotumi de tenaa amanehunu mu no.
english: Brothers and sisters, as an example of patience in the face of suffering, take the prophets who spoke in the name of the Lord.

twi: Yɛde nidi ma wɔn, efisɛ wonyaa boasetɔ. Moate Hiob boasetɔ no na munim nea Awurade de dom no awiei no; efisɛ Awurade yɛ ɔdomfo ne mmɔborɔhunufo.
english: As you know, we count as blessed those who have persevered. You have heard of Job’s perseverance and have seen what the Lord finally brought about. The Lord is full of compassion and mercy.

twi: Ne nyinaa akyi no, anuanom, sɛ mohyɛ bɔ a, monnka ntam nsi so. Mommfa ɔsoro anaa asase anaa biribiara nka ntam. Sɛ mopɛ sɛ moka “Yiw” a, monka “Yiw.” Sɛ nso mopɛ sɛ moka “Dabi” a, monka “Dabi” na moamma Onyankopɔn atemmu ase.
english: Above all, my brothers and sisters, do not swear—not by heaven or by earth or by anything else. All you need to say is a simple “Yes” or “No.” Otherwise you will be condemned.

twi: Mo mu bi wɔ ɔhaw bi mu ana? Ɛsɛ sɛ saa onipa no bɔ mpae. Mo mu bi wɔ ahotɔ mu ana? Ɛsɛ sɛ ɔto ayeyi nnwom.
english: Is anyone among you in trouble? Let them pray. Is anyone happy? Let them sing songs of praise.

twi: Mo mu bi yare ana? Ɛsɛ sɛ saa onipa no frɛ asafo mpanyimfo na wɔde Awurade din bɔ mpae ma no na wɔsra no ngo.
english: Is anyone among you sick? Let them call the elders of the church to pray over them and anoint them with oil in the name of the Lord.

twi: Sɛ wɔbɔ saa mpae no gyidi mu a, ɛbɛsa ɔyarefo no yare, na Awurade bɛma no anya ahoɔden, na ne bɔne a wayɛ nyinaa, wɔde bɛkyɛ no.
english: And the prayer offered in faith will make the sick person well; the Lord will raise them up. If they have sinned, they will be forgiven.

twi: Enti afei, monkeka mo bɔne nkyerɛ mo ho mo ho, na mommobɔ mpae mma mo ho mo ho sɛnea ɛbɛyɛ a wɔbɛsa mo yare. Onipa trenee mpaebɔ tumi yɛ nneɛma bebree.
english: Therefore confess your sins to each other and pray for each other so that you may be healed. The prayer of a righteous person is powerful and effective.

twi: Yɛte sɛ Elia a ɔbɔɔ mpae nokware mu sɛ osu nntɔ, na ampa ara osu antɔ wɔ asase no so mfe abiɛsa ne fa.
english: Elijah was a human being, even as we are. He prayed earnestly that it would not rain, and it did not rain on the land for three and a half years.

twi: Ɔsan bɔɔ mpae bio maa osu tɔ maa asase nyaa nnɔbae.
english: Again he prayed, and the heavens gave rain, and the earth produced its crops.

twi: Me nuanom, sɛ mo mu bi guan fi nokware ho na ɔfoforo de no ba bio a,
english: My brothers and sisters, if one of you should wander from the truth and someone should bring that person back,

twi: monkae sɛ, nea ɔdan ɔdebɔneyɛni fi nʼakwammɔne ho no gye no nkwa fi owu mu ma wɔde ne bɔne dodow no nyinaa kyɛ no.
english: remember this: Whoever turns a sinner from the error of their way will save them from death and cover over a multitude of sins.

twi: Nsɛm a efi Yeremia nkyɛn ni. Yeremia yɛ Hilkia babarima a na ɔyɛ Anatot asɔfo no mu baako wɔ Benyamin asase so.
english: The words of Jeremiah son of Hilkiah, one of the priests at Anathoth in the territory of Benjamin.

twi: Awurade asɛm baa ne nkyɛn wɔ Yosia a ɔyɛ Yuda hene Amon babarima adedi afe a ɛto so dumiɛnsa no mu.
english: The word of the Lord came to him in the thirteenth year of the reign of Josiah son of Amon king of Judah,

twi: Ɛtoaa so wɔ Yuda hene Yosia babarima Yehoiakim bere so, kosii Yuda hene Yosia babarima Sedekia bere so a nnipa a wɔte Yerusalem kɔɔ nkoasom mu wɔ adedi no afe a ɛto so dubaako no ɔsram a ɛto so anum no mu.
english: and through the reign of Jehoiakim son of Josiah king of Judah, down to the fifth month of the eleventh year of Zedekiah son of Josiah king of Judah, when the people of Jerusalem went into exile.

twi: Yeremia FrɛAwurade asɛm baa me nkyɛn se,
english: The word of the Lord came to me, saying,

twi: “Ansa na mereyɛ wo wɔ awotwaa mu no na minim wo;ansa na wɔrebɛwo wo no, miyii wo sii nkyɛn;meyɛɛ wo odiyifo maa aman no.”
Mekae se, “Aa, Otumfo Awurade minnim kasa; meyɛ abofra.”
english: “Alas, Sovereign Lord,” I said, “I do not know how to speak; I am too young.”

twi: Awurade ka kyerɛɛ me se, “Nka se ‘meyɛ abofra.’ Ɛsɛ sɛ wokɔ obiara a mɛsoma wo no nkyɛn na woka asɛm biara a mɛhyɛ wo sɛ ka no.
english: But the Lord said to me, “Do not say, ‘I am too young.’ You must go to everyone I send you to and say whatever I command you.

twi: Nsuro wɔn, efisɛ meka wo ho, na magye wo,” nea Awurade se ni.
english: Do not be afraid of them, for I am with you and will rescue you,” declares the Lord.

twi: Na Awurade teɛɛ ne nsa de kaa mʼano na ɔka kyerɛɛ me se, “Mprempren mede me nsɛm ahyɛ wʼanom.
english: Then the Lord reached out his hand and touched my mouth and said to me, “I have put my words in your mouth.

twi: Hwɛ, nnɛ, mede wo asi aman ne ahenni so sɛ, tutu na dwiriw gu, sɛe na tu gu, kyekyere na dua.”
english: See, today I appoint you over nations and kingdoms to uproot and tear down, to destroy and overthrow, to build and to plant.”

twi: Na Awurade asɛm baa me nkyɛn se, “Dɛn na wuhu yi, Yeremia?”Na mibuae se, “Mihu ɔsonkoran dubaa.”
english:
The word of the Lord came to me: “What do you see, Jeremiah?”
“I see the branch of an almond tree,” I replied.

twi: Na Awurade ka kyerɛɛ me se, “Wahu no yiye, na merehwɛ anim sɛ mʼasɛm bɛba mu.”
english: The Lord said to me, “You have seen correctly, for I am watching to see that my word is fulfilled.”

twi: Awurade asɛm baa me nkyɛn bio se, “Dɛn na wuhu yi?”Mibuae se, “Mihu kuku a ɛrehuru sɛ ano rekyea akyerɛ yɛn fi atifi fam.”
english:
The word of the Lord came to me again: “What do you see?”
“I see a pot that is boiling,” I answered. “It is tilting toward us from the north.”

twi: Awurade ka kyerɛɛ me se, “Wobefi atifi fam de amanehunu aba wɔn a wɔte asase no so nyinaa so.
english: The Lord said to me, “From the north disaster will be poured out on all who live in the land.

twi: Merebɛfrɛ atifi ahenni mu nnipa nyinaa,” nea Awurade se ni.“Wɔn ahemfo de wɔn ahengua bɛbaabesisi Yerusalem kuropɔn apon ano;wɔbɛtow ahyɛ nʼafasu a atwa ahyiane Yuda nkurow nyinaa so.
english:
I am about to summon all the peoples of the northern kingdoms,” declares the Lord.
“Their kings will come and set up their thrones
    in the entrance of the gates of Jerusalem;
they will come against all her surrounding walls
    and against all the towns of Judah.

twi: Mebu me nkurɔfo atɛnwɔ wɔn amumɔyɛ sɛ wɔagyaw me,sɛ wɔhyew nnuhuam ma anyame afoforona wɔkotow sɔre nea wɔde wɔn nsa ayɛ.
english:
I will pronounce my judgments on my people
    because of their wickedness in forsaking me,
in burning incense to other gods
    and in worshiping what their hands have made.

twi: “Siesie wo ho! Sɔre na ka nea mɛka akyerɛ wo biara kyerɛ wɔn. Mma wɔmmmɔ wo hu, anyɛ saa a mɛma woabɔ hu wɔ wɔn anim.
english: “Get yourself ready! Stand up and say to them whatever I command you. Do not be terrified by them, or I will terrify you before them.

twi: Nnɛ, mayɛ wo kuropɔn a ɛwɔ bammɔ, dadedum ne kɔbere fasu sɛ wobɛsɔre atia asase no nyinaa, Yuda ahemfo, nʼadwumayɛfo, asɔfo ne nnipa a wɔwɔ asase no so.
english: Today I have made you a fortified city, an iron pillar and a bronze wall to stand against the whole land—against the kings of Judah, its officials, its priests and the people of the land.

twi: Wɔbɛko atia wo, nanso wɔrentumi nni wo so nkonim, efisɛ meka wo ho na megye wo,” sɛnea Awurade se ni.
english: They will fight against you but will not overcome you, for I am with you and will rescue you,” declares the Lord.

twi: Israel Pa Onyankopɔn AkyiAwurade asɛm baa me so:
english: The word of the Lord came to me:

twi: “Kɔpae mu ka ma Yerusalem nte:“ ‘Mekae sɛnea wode wo ho maa me wo mmabun bere mu,sɛnea wodɔɔ me wɔ wʼayeforo bere muna wudii mʼakyi wɔ sare so,asase a wonnuaa hwee wɔ so no.
english:
“Go and proclaim in the hearing of Jerusalem:
“This is what the Lord says:
“‘I remember the devotion of your youth,
    how as a bride you loved me
and followed me through the wilderness,
    through a land not sown.

twi: Na Israel yɛ kronkron ma Awurade,ne twabere mu aduankan;wɔn a wodii nʼani no wobuu wɔn fɔ,na amanehunu baa wɔn so,’ ”sɛnea Awurade, se ni.
english:
Israel was holy to the Lord,
    the firstfruits of his harvest;
all who devoured her were held guilty,
    and disaster overtook them,’”
declares the Lord.

twi: Muntie Awurade asɛm, mo Yakob asefo,mo Israel mmusuakuw nyinaa.
english:
Hear the word of the Lord, you descendants of Jacob,
    all you clans of Israel.

twi: Eyi ne nea Awurade se:“Mfomso bɛn na mo agyanom huu wɔ me ho aɛma wɔtwee wɔn ho kɔɔ akyirikyiri sɛɛ?Wodii ahoni a wɔn so nni mfaso akyi,maa wɔn ankasa bɛyɛɛ ahuhufo.
english:
This is what the Lord says:
“What fault did your ancestors find in me,
    that they strayed so far from me?
They followed worthless idols
    and became worthless themselves.

twi: Wɔammisa se, ‘Ɛhe na Awurade wɔ?Nea oyii yɛn fii Misraimna ɔde yɛn faa sare wosee so,nweatam ne abonabon asasea awo na ayɛ owubon no.Asase a obiara mfa so na obiara nte so no.’
english:
They did not ask, ‘Where is the Lord,
    who brought us up out of Egypt
and led us through the barren wilderness,
    through a land of deserts and ravines,
a land of drought and utter darkness,
    a land where no one travels and no one lives?’

twi: Mede mo beduaa asasebere sosɛ munni so nnuaba ne ɛso nnepa.Nanso mubeguu mʼasase ho fi,na moyɛɛ mʼagyapade akyiwade.
english:
I brought you into a fertile land
    to eat its fruit and rich produce.
But you came and defiled my land
    and made my inheritance detestable.

twi: Asɔfo no ammisa se,‘Ɛhe na Awurade wɔ?’Wɔn a wɔde mmara yɛ adwuma no anhwehwɛ me;ntuanofo sɔre tiaa me.Adiyifo no de Baal hyɛɛ nkɔm,na wodii ahoni huhuw akyi.
english:
The priests did not ask,
    ‘Where is the Lord?’
Those who deal with the law did not know me;
    the leaders rebelled against me.
The prophets prophesied by Baal,
    following worthless idols.

twi: “Ɛno nti, merebɔ mo kwaadu bio,”nea Awurade se ni.“Na mɛbɔ mo mma mma kwaadu.
english:
“Therefore I bring charges against you again,”
declares the Lord.
    “And I will bring charges against your children’s children.

twi: Muntwa nkɔ Kitim mpoano nkɔhwɛ,monsoma nkɔ Kedar nkɔhwehwɛ mu yiye;monhwɛ sɛ biribi a ɛte sɛɛ asi wɔ hɔ:
Ɔman bi asesa wɔn anyame pɛn ana?Nso wɔnnyɛ anyame mpo.Nanso me nkurɔfo de wɔn anuonyamasesa ahoni huhuw.
english:
Has a nation ever changed its gods?
    (Yet they are not gods at all.)
But my people have exchanged their glorious God
    for worthless idols.

twi: Mo ɔsorosoro, momma mo ho nnwiriw mo wɔ eyi ho,na mo ho nwosow wɔ akomatu mu,”nea Awurade se ni.
english:
Be appalled at this, you heavens,
    and shudder with great horror,”
declares the Lord.

twi: “Me nkurɔfo ayɛ bɔne ahorow abien:Wɔapa me,me a meyɛ nkwa asubura no,na wɔatutu wɔn ankasa mmura amoa,mmura a apaapae a entumi nkora nsu.
english:
“My people have committed two sins:
They have forsaken me,
    the spring of living water,
and have dug their own cisterns,
    broken cisterns that cannot hold water.

twi: Israel yɛ akoa anaa ɔsomfo fi awo mu ana?Adɛn nti na wayɛ asade yi?
english:
Is Israel a servant, a slave by birth?
    Why then has he become plunder?

twi: Gyata abobɔ mu;wɔaworo so akyerɛ no.Wɔama nʼasase ada mpan;wɔahyehyew ne nkurow ayɛ no amamfo.
Afei Memfis ne Tapanhes mmarimaayi wo ti so nwi.
english:
Also, the men of Memphis and Tahpanhes
    have cracked your skull.

twi: Ɛnyɛ wo na woama eyi aba wo sosɛ wopaa Awurade wo Nyankopɔn akyi,wɔ bere a ɔrekyerɛ wo kwan no?
english:
Have you not brought this on yourselves
    by forsaking the Lord your God
    when he led you in the way?

twi: Afei adɛn nti na wokɔ Misraimkɔnom Sihor mu nsu?Na adɛn nti na wokɔ Asiriakɔnom Asubɔnten no mu nsu?
english:
Now why go to Egypt
    to drink water from the Nile?
And why go to Assyria
    to drink water from the Euphrates?

twi: Wo amumɔyɛ bɛtwe wʼaso;wo nsanakyi bɛka wʼanim.Enti dwene ho na hu sɛ,sɛ wopa Awurade wo Nyankopɔn akyina woannya ne ho suro a,ɛyɛ bɔne ne ɔyaw ma wo.”Awurade, Asafo Awurade na ose.
english:
Your wickedness will punish you;
    your backsliding will rebuke you.
Consider then and realize
    how evil and bitter it is for you
when you forsake the Lord your God
    and have no awe of me,”
declares the Lord, the Lord Almighty.

twi: “Tete mmere no, wububuu wo konnua mu,na wotetew wo nkɔnsɔnkɔnsɔn mu;na wokae se, ‘Merensom wo!’Ampa, wɔ koko biara sone dua biara a adennan asena wotena bɔɔ aguaman.
english:
“Long ago you broke off your yoke
    and tore off your bonds;
    you said, ‘I will not serve you!’
Indeed, on every high hill
    and under every spreading tree
    you lay down as a prostitute.

twi: Miduaa wo sɛ bobe ankasaa efi bobe a ase ye pa ara mu.Na ɛyɛɛ dɛn na wodan wʼakyi kyerɛɛ mebɛyɛɛ bobe a anyin asɛe wɔ wura mu yi?
english:
I had planted you like a choice vine
    of sound and reliable stock.
How then did you turn against me
    into a corrupt, wild vine?

twi: Sɛ wode sodane samina bebree guare mpo a,wʼafɔdi nkekae da so wɔ mʼanim ara,”sɛnea Otumfo Awurade se ni.
english:
Although you wash yourself with soap
    and use an abundance of cleansing powder,
    the stain of your guilt is still before me,”
declares the Sovereign Lord.

twi: “Ɛbɛyɛ dɛn na woaka se, ‘Me ho nguu fi ɛ;minnii Baalnom akyi ɛ’?Hwɛ sɛnea woyɛɛ wo ho wɔ obon no mu;dwene nea woayɛ no ho.Woyɛ yomabere hoɔharefoa wutu mmirika kɔ ha ba ha,

wura mu afurum a nweatam so tena akokwaw no,ohuahua bere a ɔpɛ sɛ onini hyia no.Sɛ nʼakɔnnɔ no ano yɛ den a hena na obesianka no?Anini biara a wɔtaa no no nhaw wɔn ho bebree;edu bere a ɛsɛ sɛ wohyia no a wobenya no.
english:
a wild donkey accustomed to the desert,
    sniffing the wind in her craving—
    in her heat who can restrain her?
Any males that pursue her need not tire themselves;
    at mating time they will find her.

twi: Ntu mmirika nkosi sɛ wʼanan ase bɛyɛ kwaterekwa,na wo mene mu bɛyow.Nanso wokae se, ‘So nni mfaso!Mepɛ ananafo anyame,na ɛsɛ sɛ midi wɔn akyi.’
english:
Do not run until your feet are bare
    and your throat is dry.
But you said, ‘It’s no use!
    I love foreign gods,
    and I must go after them.’

twi: “Sɛnea wɔkyere ɔkorɔmfo a wogu nʼanim ase no,saa na wɔagu Israelfi anim ase,wɔn ankasa, wɔn ahemfo ne wɔn adwumayɛfo,wɔn asɔfo ne wɔn adiyifo.
english:
“As a thief is disgraced when he is caught,
    so the people of Israel are disgraced—
they, their kings and their officials,
    their priests and their prophets.

twi: Wɔka kyerɛ dua se, ‘Woyɛ mʼagya,’ne ɔbo se, ‘Wo na wowoo me.’Wɔadan wɔn akyi akyerɛ mena ɛnyɛ wɔn anim;nanso sɛ amanehunu bi ba wɔn so a, wɔka se,‘Bra begye yɛn!’
english:
They say to wood, ‘You are my father,’
    and to stone, ‘You gave me birth.’
They have turned their backs to me
    and not their faces;
yet when they are in trouble, they say,
    ‘Come and save us!’

twi: Anyame a moyɛ maa mo ho no wɔ he?Momma wɔmmra sɛ wobetumi agye mobere a mowɔ amanehunu mu!Efisɛ mowɔ anyame bebreete sɛ nea mowɔ nkurow bebree no, Yuda.
english:
Where then are the gods you made for yourselves?
    Let them come if they can save you
    when you are in trouble!
For you, Judah, have as many gods
    as you have towns.

twi: “Adɛn nti na mobɔ me sobo?Mo nyinaa ayɛ dɔm atia me,”Awurade na ose.
english:
“Why do you bring charges against me?
    You have all rebelled against me,”
declares the Lord.

twi: “Metwee mo nkurɔfo aso kwa;wɔamfa me nteɛso.Wʼafoa akunkum wʼadiyifote sɛ gyata a nʼani abere.
english:
“In vain I punished your people;
    they did not respond to correction.
Your sword has devoured your prophets
    like a ravenous lion.

twi: “Mo nnɛmmafo, munnwen Awurade asɛm ho:“Mayɛ sɛ, nweatam ama Israel ana?Anaasɛ asase a so aduru sum kabii ana?Adɛn nti na me nkurɔfo ka se, ‘Yɛwɔ ho kwan sɛ yekyinkyin;yɛremma wo nkyɛn bio.’
english:
“You of this generation, consider the word of the Lord:
“Have I been a desert to Israel
    or a land of great darkness?
Why do my people say, ‘We are free to roam;
    we will come to you no more’?

twi: Ɔbabun werɛ fi ne mpempranne,ayeforo werɛ befi nʼahyehyɛde ana?Nanso me nkurɔfo werɛ afi menna a wontumi nkan.
english:
Does a young woman forget her jewelry,
    a bride her wedding ornaments?
Yet my people have forgotten me,
    days without number.

twi: Hwɛ nyansa a mowɔ de pɛ mo adɔfo!Mmea a wɔnsɛ hwee koraa tumi sua mo akwan.
english:
How skilled you are at pursuing love!
    Even the worst of women can learn from your ways.

twi: Mo adurade mu wɔahiafo a wodi bem mogya,nanso moankyere wɔn sɛ wɔrebubu akɔ mu.Eyinom nyinaa akyi
english:
On your clothes is found
    the lifeblood of the innocent poor,
    though you did not catch them breaking in.
Yet in spite of all this

twi: woka se, ‘Midi bem;ne bo mfuw me.’Nanso mebu wo atɛnefisɛ woka se, ‘Menyɛɛ bɔne biara ɛ.’
english:
you say, ‘I am innocent;
    he is not angry with me.’
But I will pass judgment on you
    because you say, ‘I have not sinned.’

twi: Adɛn nti na wukyinkyin sɛɛ,sesa wʼakwan?Misraim bedi wo huammɔsɛnea Asiria yɛe no.
english:
Why do you go about so much,
    changing your ways?
You will be disappointed by Egypt
    as you were by Assyria.

twi: Afei wubefi saa beae hɔa wo nsa gu wo ti so.Efisɛ Awurade apo wɔn a wode wo ho too wɔn so no;wɔremmoa wo.
english:
You will also leave that place
    with your hands on your head,
for the Lord has rejected those you trust;
    you will not be helped by them.

twi: “Sɛ ɔbarima gyaa ne yerena ɔbea no kɔware ɔbarima foforo a,ɛsɛ sɛ ɔbarima no san kɔ ɔbea no nkyɛn ana?Ɛremma asase no ho ngu fi koraa ana?Nanso wo ne adɔfo bebree abɔ aguaman,na mprempren de wobɛsan aba me nkyɛn ana?”Awurade na ose.
english:
“If a man divorces his wife
    and she leaves him and marries another man,
should he return to her again?
    Would not the land be completely defiled?
But you have lived as a prostitute with many lovers—
    would you now return to me?”
declares the Lord.

twi: “Ma wʼani so hwɛ nkoko no so.Baabi wɔ hɔ a wɔntoo wo mmonnaa da ana?Wotenaa kwankyɛn twɛn adɔfo,wotenaa sɛ mmoahwɛfo a wodi atutena wɔ nweatam so.Woagu asase no ho fi,wode wʼaguamammɔ ne wʼamumɔyɛ na ayɛ.
english:
“Look up to the barren heights and see.
    Is there any place where you have not been ravished?
By the roadside you sat waiting for lovers,
    sat like a nomad in the desert.
You have defiled the land
    with your prostitution and wickedness.

twi: Enti wɔatwe obosu asan,na asusowbere su antɔ.Nanso wʼanim ayɛ sɛ oguamanfo a ɔmfɛre hwee;wʼani nwu hwee.
english:
Therefore the showers have been withheld,
    and no spring rains have fallen.
Yet you have the brazen look of a prostitute;
    you refuse to blush with shame.

twi: Nnansa yi ara, woamfrɛ me se:‘Mʼagya, me mmabunmmere mu adamfo,
english:
Have you not just called to me:
    ‘My Father, my friend from my youth,

twi: wo bo befuw biribiara ana?Wʼabufuwhyew no bɛkɔ so daa ana?’Sɛɛ na wokasa,nanso woyɛ bɔne nyinaa sɛnea wutumi.”
english:
will you always be angry?
    Will your wrath continue forever?’
This is how you talk,
    but you do all the evil you can.”

twi: Israel A Onni NokwareƆhene Yosia adedi bere so no, Awurade ka kyerɛɛ me se, “Woahu nea Israel a onni nokware no ayɛ? Wakɔ nkoko nyinaa so ne dua a adennan biara ase akɔsɛe aware wɔ hɔ.
english: During the reign of King Josiah, the Lord said to me, “Have you seen what faithless Israel has done? She has gone up on every high hill and under every spreading tree and has committed adultery there.

twi: Misusuwii sɛ anka wayɛ eyinom nyinaa akyi no, ɔbɛsan aba me nkyɛn nanso wamma, na ne nuabea Yuda a ɔno nso nka nokware no hui.
english: I thought that after she had done all this she would return to me but she did not, and her unfaithful sister Judah saw it.

twi: Memaa Israel a onni nokware no awaregyae nhoma na mepam no esiane nʼawaresɛe abrabɔ nti. Nanso mihuu sɛ ne nuabea Yuda a onni nokware no ansuro; ɔno nso kɔbɔɔ aguaman bra.
english: I gave faithless Israel her certificate of divorce and sent her away because of all her adulteries. Yet I saw that her unfaithful sister Judah had no fear; she also went out and committed adultery.

twi: Esiane sɛ Israel aguamammɔ anyɛ no asɛnhia nti, ɔde fi kaa asase no na ɔne abo ne nnua bɔɔ aguaman.
english: Because Israel’s immorality mattered so little to her, she defiled the land and committed adultery with stone and wood.

twi: Eyinom nyinaa akyi no, ne nuabea Yuda amfi ne koma nyinaa mu ansan amma me nkyɛn, ɔyɛ de kyerɛɛ kɛkɛ,” sɛnea Awurade se ni.
english: In spite of all this, her unfaithful sister Judah did not return to me with all her heart, but only in pretense,” declares the Lord.

twi: Awurade ka kyerɛɛ me se, “Israel a onni nokware no teɛ sen Yuda okontomponi no.
english: The Lord said to me, “Faithless Israel is more righteous than unfaithful Judah.

twi: Kɔ, fa wʼani kyerɛ atifi fam kɔka saa nsɛm yi kyerɛ wɔn:“ ‘San wʼakyi, Israel a onni nokware,’ Sɛɛ na Awurade se,‘Meremmuna nkyerɛ wo bio,efisɛ meyɛ mmɔborɔhunufo,’ sɛɛ na Awurade se,‘Me bo remfuw afebɔɔ.
english:
Go, proclaim this message toward the north:
“‘Return, faithless Israel,’ declares the Lord,
    ‘I will frown on you no longer,
for I am faithful,’ declares the Lord,
    ‘I will not be angry forever.

twi: Gye wo afɔdi to mu,woatew Awurade, wo Nyankopɔn anim atua,woakyekyɛ wʼadɔe mu ama ananafo anyamewɔ dua biara a adennan ase,na woanyɛ osetie amma me,’ ”sɛnea Awurade se ni.
english:
Only acknowledge your guilt—
    you have rebelled against the Lord your God,
you have scattered your favors to foreign gods
    under every spreading tree,
    and have not obeyed me,’”
declares the Lord.

twi: “Monsan mo akyi, mo akyirisanfo,” sɛnea Awurade se ni, “efisɛ meyɛ mo kunu. Meyi wo; ɔbaako befi kurow mu na baanu afi abusuakuw mu, na mede mo aba Sion.
english: “Return, faithless people,” declares the Lord, “for I am your husband. I will choose you—one from a town and two from a clan—and bring you to Zion.

twi: Afei mɛma mo nguanhwɛfo a wɔda me koma so, wɔn a wɔde nimdeɛ ne ntease bɛkyerɛ mo ɔkwan.
english: Then I will give you shepherds after my own heart, who will lead you with knowledge and understanding.

twi: Saa nna no mu, sɛ mo dɔɔso bebree wɔ asase no so a,” Awurade na ose, “nnipa renka bio se, ‘Awurade apam adaka no.’ Ɛremma wɔn adwene mu anaa wɔrenkae da; wɔn kɔn rennɔ na wɔrenyɛ foforo nso.
english: In those days, when your numbers have increased greatly in the land,” declares the Lord, “people will no longer say, ‘The ark of the covenant of the Lord.’ It will never enter their minds or be remembered; it will not be missed, nor will another one be made.

twi: Saa bere no wɔbɛfrɛ Yerusalem Awurade Ahengua, na amanaman nyinaa behyia wɔ Yerusalem abɛkamfo Awurade din. Na wɔrenni wɔn koma bɔne a ɛma wɔyɛ asoɔden no akyi bio.
english: At that time they will call Jerusalem The Throne of the Lord, and all nations will gather in Jerusalem to honor the name of the Lord. No longer will they follow the stubbornness of their evil hearts.

twi: Saa nna no mu, Yuda fi bɛka Israelfi ho, na wɔabɔ mu afi atifi fam asase bi so aba asase a mede maa mo agyanom sɛ agyapade no so.
english: In those days the people of Judah will join the people of Israel, and together they will come from a northern land to the land I gave your ancestors as an inheritance.

twi: “Mʼankasa mekae se,‘Anka ɛbɛyɛ me anigye sɛ mɛyɛ mo sɛ mmana mama mo asase a eye,agyapade a edi mu ma ɔman biara.’Misusuwii sɛ mobɛfrɛ me ‘Agya’na monnan mo ho mfi mʼakyi.
english:
“I myself said,
“‘How gladly would I treat you like my children
    and give you a pleasant land,
    the most beautiful inheritance of any nation.’
I thought you would call me ‘Father’
    and not turn away from following me.

twi: Nanso te sɛ ɔbea a onni ne kunu nokware no,saa ara na moanni me nokware, Israelfi,”sɛnea Awurade se ni.
english:
But like a woman unfaithful to her husband,
    so you, Israel, have been unfaithful to me,”
declares the Lord.

twi: Wɔte osu bi wɔ nkoko no so,ɛyɛ Israelfo agyaadwotwa ne nkotosrɛ,efisɛ wɔakyeakyea wɔn akwanna wɔn werɛ afi Awurade, wɔn Nyankopɔn.
english:
A cry is heard on the barren heights,
    the weeping and pleading of the people of Israel,
because they have perverted their ways
    and have forgotten the Lord their God.

twi: “Monsan mmra, ɔyera mma;mɛsa mo akyirisan yare no.”“Yiw, yɛbɛba wo nkyɛn,efisɛ wo ne Awurade, yɛn Nyankopɔn no.
english:
“Return, faithless people;
    I will cure you of backsliding.”
“Yes, we will come to you,
    for you are the Lord our God.

twi: Ampa, ahoni huuyɛ wɔ nkokone mmepɔw so no yɛ nnaadaa;nokware Awurade yɛn Nyankopɔn muna Israel nkwagye wɔ.
english:
Surely the idolatrous commotion on the hills
    and mountains is a deception;
surely in the Lord our God
    is the salvation of Israel.

twi: Efi yɛn mmofraase, anyame huhuw adiyɛn agyanom nsa ano adwuma so aba,wɔn nguankuw ne anantwi,wɔn mmabarima ne wɔn mmabea.
english:
From our youth shameful gods have consumed
    the fruits of our ancestors’ labor—
their flocks and herds,
    their sons and daughters.

twi: Momma yɛmfa yɛn aniwu nneda famna yɛn ahohora nkata yɛn so.Yɛayɛ bɔne atia Awurade yɛn Nyankopɔn,yɛn ne yɛn agyanom;efi yɛn mmofraase besi nnɛyɛanyɛ osetie amma Awurade, yɛn Nyankopɔn no.”
english:
Let us lie down in our shame,
    and let our disgrace cover us.
We have sinned against the Lord our God,
    both we and our ancestors;
from our youth till this day
    we have not obeyed the Lord our God.”

twi: “Sɛ wo, Israel, wobɛsan wʼakyi a,san bra me nkyɛn,”sɛɛ na Awurade se.“Sɛ wuyi wʼahoni a ɛyɛ akyiwade fi mʼani sona sɛ woamman bio,
english:
“If you, Israel, will return,
    then return to me,”
declares the Lord.
“If you put your detestable idols out of my sight
    and no longer go astray,

twi: na sɛ wufi nokware, pɛpɛyɛ ne trenee muka ntam se, ‘Sɛ Awurade te ase yi,’ aafei wobehyira aman nona ne mu na wobenya anuonyam.”
english:
and if in a truthful, just and righteous way
    you swear, ‘As surely as the Lord lives,’
then the nations will invoke blessings by him
    and in him they will boast.”

twi: Eyi ne asɛm a, Awurade ka kyerɛ Yuda mmarima ne Yerusalem:“Munsiesie mo asase a womfuntum da,na munnnua wɔ nsɔe mu.
english:
This is what the Lord says to the people of Judah and to Jerusalem:
“Break up your unplowed ground
    and do not sow among thorns.

twi: Muntwitwa mo ho twetia mma Awurademuntwitwa mo koma twetia,mo Yuda mmarima ne Yerusalemfo,anyɛ saa a mʼabufuwhyew bɛsɔre na adɛw sɛ ogyamo bɔne a moayɛ nti,ɛbɛhyew a obiara rennum.”
english:
Circumcise yourselves to the Lord,
    circumcise your hearts,
    you people of Judah and inhabitants of Jerusalem,
or my wrath will flare up and burn like fire
    because of the evil you have done—
    burn with no one to quench it.

twi: Amanehunu A Efi Atifi Fam“Bɔ nkae wɔ Yuda na pae mu ka wɔ Yerusalem se‘Hyɛn torobɛnto no wɔ asase no nyinaa so!’Teɛ mu dennen se:‘Mommoaboa mo ho ano!Momma yenguan nkɔ nkuropɔn a wɔabɔ ho ban no mu!’
english:
“Announce in Judah and proclaim in Jerusalem and say:
    ‘Sound the trumpet throughout the land!’
Cry aloud and say:
    ‘Gather together!
    Let us flee to the fortified cities!’

twi: Momma frankaa so na monkɔ Sionmunguan nkɔbɔ mo ho aguaa!Efisɛ mede amanehunu fi atifi fam reba,ɔsɛe a ɛyɛ hu.”
english:
Raise the signal to go to Zion!
    Flee for safety without delay!
For I am bringing disaster from the north,
    even terrible destruction.”

twi: Gyata bi afi ne tu mu;ɔbɔɔaman bi asi mu.Wafi ne tenabeasɛ ɔrebɛsɛe wʼasase.Wo nkurow bebubuna ada mpan.
english:
A lion has come out of his lair;
    a destroyer of nations has set out.
He has left his place
    to lay waste your land.
Your towns will lie in ruins
    without inhabitant.

twi: Enti fura atweaatam,di awerɛhow na twa adwo,efisɛ Awurade abufuwhyew nonnan mfii yɛn so.
english:
So put on sackcloth,
    lament and wail,
for the fierce anger of the Lord
    has not turned away from us.

twi: “Saa da no,” Awurade na ose,“ɔhene no ne adwumayɛfo no bɛbɔ hu,asɔfo no bo betu,na adiyifo no ho bedwiriw wɔn.”
english:
“In that day,” declares the Lord,
    “the king and the officials will lose heart,
the priests will be horrified,
    and the prophets will be appalled.”

twi: Afei, mekae se, “Aa, Otumfo Awurade, woadaadaa nnipa yi ne Yerusalem, wokae se, ‘Mubenya asomdwoe,’ wɔ bere a afoa da yɛn mene mu.”
english: Then I said, “Alas, Sovereign Lord! How completely you have deceived this people and Jerusalem by saying, ‘You will have peace,’ when the sword is at our throats!”

twi: Saa bere no wɔbɛka akyerɛ nnipa yi ne Yerusalem se, “Mframa a emu yɛ hyew bɛbɔ afi nkoko wosee a ɛwɔ nweatam so aba me nkurɔfo so, ɛnyɛ nea ɛpo ho anaa ehuhuw so;
english: At that time this people and Jerusalem will be told, “A scorching wind from the barren heights in the desert blows toward my people, but not to winnow or cleanse;

twi: mframa a ano yɛ den boro saa no fi me nkyɛn. Afei mepae mu ka mʼatemmu a etia wɔn.”
english: a wind too strong for that comes from me. Now I pronounce my judgments against them.”

twi: Hwɛ! ɔreba sɛ omununkum,ne nteaseɛnam reba sɛ mfɛtɛ,nʼapɔnkɔ ho yɛ hare sen akɔre.Yennue! Yɛawu!
english:
Look! He advances like the clouds,
    his chariots come like a whirlwind,
his horses are swifter than eagles.
    Woe to us! We are ruined!

twi: Yerusalem, yi bɔne fi wo koma mu na woanya nkwa.Wode adwemmɔne bɛhyɛ wo mu akosi da bɛn?
english:
Jerusalem, wash the evil from your heart and be saved.
    How long will you harbor wicked thoughts?

twi: Nne bi rebɔ amanneɛ fi Dan,ɛrebɔ amanehunu ho dawuru fi Efraim nkoko so.
english:
A voice is announcing from Dan,
    proclaiming disaster from the hills of Ephraim.

twi: “Monka eyi nkyerɛ aman no,mommɔ no dawuru nkyerɛ Yerusalem se,‘Atuafo dɔm fi akyirikyiri asase bi so reba,wɔma ɔko nteɛmu so de tia Yuda nkuropɔn.
english:
“Tell this to the nations,
    proclaim concerning Jerusalem:
‘A besieging army is coming from a distant land,
    raising a war cry against the cities of Judah.

twi: Wotwa ne ho hyia sɛ mmarima a wɔrewɛn afuw,efisɛ watew me so atua,’ ”sɛɛ na Awurade se.
english:
They surround her like men guarding a field,
    because she has rebelled against me,’”
declares the Lord.

twi: “Wo ankasa abrabɔ ne nneyɛe,na ɛde eyi aba wo so.Eyi yɛ wʼasotwe.Ɛyɛ nwen!Ɛwowɔ koma!”
english:
“Your own conduct and actions
    have brought this on you.
This is your punishment.
    How bitter it is!
    How it pierces to the heart!”

twi: Ao, mʼahoyeraw, mʼahoyeraw!midi me mu yaw.Me koma mu yawdi!Me koma bɔ kitirikitiri wɔ me mu,mintumi nyɛ komm.Efisɛ, mate torobɛnto no nnyigye;mate ɔko frɛ no.
english:
Oh, my anguish, my anguish!
    I writhe in pain.
Oh, the agony of my heart!
    My heart pounds within me,
    I cannot keep silent.
For I have heard the sound of the trumpet;
    I have heard the battle cry.

twi: Amanehunu di amanehunu akyi;asase no nyinaa asɛe.Wɔasɛe me ntamadan prɛko pɛ,ne me hintabea mpofirim.
english:
Disaster follows disaster;
    the whole land lies in ruins.
In an instant my tents are destroyed,
    my shelter in a moment.

twi: Ɛsɛ sɛ mehwɛ ɔko frankaa nona mitie torobɛnto no nnyigye kosi da bɛn?
english:
How long must I see the battle standard
    and hear the sound of the trumpet?

twi: “Me nkurɔfo yɛ nkwaseafo;wonnim me.Wɔyɛ mma a wonni adwene;wɔnte hwee ase.Wɔwɔ bɔneyɛ ho nyansa;na wonnim sɛnea wɔyɛ papa.”
Mehwɛɛ asase no,na enni bɔbea, na ɛda mpan;mehwɛɛ ɔsorosoro, na wɔn hann no nni hɔ.
english:
I looked at the earth,
    and it was formless and empty;
and at the heavens,
    and their light was gone.

twi: Mehwɛɛ mmepɔw no,na wɔrewosowosow,na nkoko no nyinaa rehinhim.
Mehwɛe, na nnipa nni hɔ;wim anomaa biara atu kɔ.
english:
I looked, and there were no people;
    every bird in the sky had flown away.

twi: Mehwɛe, na nsasebere no adan nweatamna ne nkurow nyinaa asɛewɔ Awurade anim, wɔ nʼabufuwhyew ano.
Sɛnea Awurade se:“Wɔbɛsɛe asase no nyinaa;mmom, merensɛe no korakora.
english:
This is what the Lord says:
“The whole land will be ruined,
    though I will not destroy it completely.

twi: Enti asase bedi awerɛhowna ɔsorosoro beduru sum,efisɛ makasa na merentwe nsan;masi gyinae na merennan no.”
english:
Therefore the earth will mourn
    and the heavens above grow dark,
because I have spoken and will not relent,
    I have decided and will not turn back.”

twi: Apɔnkɔsotefo ne agyantowfo nnyigyeima kurow biara sofo guan.Ebinom kɔhyɛ nkyɛkyerɛ mu,ebinom foro kɔ abotan mu.Nkurow no nyinaa so adeda mpan;na obiara nte so.
Dɛn na woreyɛ, wo a wɔasɛe wo?Adɛn na wufura ɔkɔbende sikakɔkɔɔ agude asiesie wo ho?Adɛn na wode nnuru keka wʼani?Wohyehyɛ wo ho kwa.Wʼadɔfo bu wo animtiaa;wɔrehwehwɛ wo akum wo.
english:
What are you doing, you devastated one?
    Why dress yourself in scarlet
    and put on jewels of gold?
Why highlight your eyes with makeup?
    You adorn yourself in vain.
Your lovers despise you;
    they want to kill you.

twi: Mete osu bi te sɛ ɔbea a ɔwɔ awoko mu,apinisi te sɛ ɔbea a ɔrewo nʼabakan,Ɔbabea Sion resu te sɛ nea osi apini,ɔtrɛw ne nsa mu na ɔreka se,“Afei de meretɔ piti;wɔde me nkwa ama awudifo.”
english:
I hear a cry as of a woman in labor,
    a groan as of one bearing her first child—
the cry of Daughter Zion gasping for breath,
    stretching out her hands and saying,
“Alas! I am fainting;
    my life is given over to murderers.”

twi: Obiara Nyɛ Ɔtreneeni“Munni akɔneaba wɔ Yerusalem mmɔnten so,monhwɛ mo ho nhyia nhwɛ,monhwehwɛ guabɔbea nyinaa.Sɛ muhu onipa baako mpo aɔyɛ pɛ na odi nokware a,mede kuropɔn yi ho bɛkyɛ no.
english:
“Go up and down the streets of Jerusalem,
    look around and consider,
    search through her squares.
If you can find but one person
    who deals honestly and seeks the truth,
    I will forgive this city.

twi: Ɛwɔ mu wɔka se, ‘Sɛ Awurade te ase yi,’nanso wɔda so ka ntam hunu.”
english:
Although they say, ‘As surely as the Lord lives,’
    still they are swearing falsely.”

twi: Awurade, wʼani mpɛ nokware ahu ana?Wobɔɔ wɔn hwee fam, nanso wɔante yaw biara;wodwerɛw wɔn, nanso wɔpoo nteɛso.Wɔyɛɛ wɔn anim dennen sen ɔbona wɔansakra wɔn adwene.
english:
Lord, do not your eyes look for truth?
    You struck them, but they felt no pain;
    you crushed them, but they refused correction.
They made their faces harder than stone
    and refused to repent.

twi: Misusuw se, “Eyinom nko ara ne ahiafo no;wɔyɛ nkwaseafo nso,efisɛ wonnim Awurade akwan,nea wɔn Nyankopɔn hwehwɛ.
Enti mɛkɔ ntuanofo no nkyɛnakɔkasa akyerɛ wɔn;ampa ara wonim Awurade akwannea wɔn Onyankopɔn hwehwɛ.”Nanso wɔn nso de adwene koro abubu konnua noatetew nkyehama no mu.
english:
So I will go to the leaders
    and speak to them;
surely they know the way of the Lord,
    the requirements of their God.”
But with one accord they too had broken off the yoke
    and torn off the bonds.

twi: Ɛno nti gyata bi a ofi kwae mu bɛtow ahyɛ wɔn so,pataku bi a ofi nweatam so bɛtetew wɔn mu.Ɔsebɔ bi bɛtɛw abɛn wɔn nkurow,na obiara a obeyi ne ti no ɔbɛtetew ne mu nketenkete,efisɛ wɔn atuatew no ano yɛ denna wɔn akyirisan aboro so.
english:
Therefore a lion from the forest will attack them,
    a wolf from the desert will ravage them,
a leopard will lie in wait near their towns
    to tear to pieces any who venture out,
for their rebellion is great
    and their backslidings many.

twi: “Adɛn nti na ɛsɛ sɛ mede mo ho kyɛ mo?Mo mma apo me,wɔde anyame a wɔnyɛ anyame aka ntam.Memaa wɔn nea wohia nyinaa,nanso wɔbɔɔ aguamanna wɔbɔɔ yuu kɔɔ nguamanfo afi mu.
english:
“Why should I forgive you?
    Your children have forsaken me
    and sworn by gods that are not gods.
I supplied all their needs,
    yet they committed adultery
    and thronged to the houses of prostitutes.

twi: Mpɔnkɔnini aniberefo a wɔhwɛ wɔn yiye,wɔn mu biara su di ne yɔnko yere akyi.
english:
They are well-fed, lusty stallions,
    each neighing for another man’s wife.

twi: Ɛnsɛ sɛ metwe wɔn aso wɔ eyi ho?”Sɛɛ na Awurade se.“Ɛnsɛ sɛ, mʼankasa metɔɔman a ɛte sɛɛ so were ana?
english:
Should I not punish them for this?”
    declares the Lord.
“Should I not avenge myself
    on such a nation as this?

twi: “Momfa ne bobe nturo no mu na monsɛe no,nanso monnsɛe no koraa.Mompempan ne mman no,efisɛ saa nnipa yi nyɛ Awurade dea.
english:
“Go through her vineyards and ravage them,
    but do not destroy them completely.
Strip off her branches,
    for these people do not belong to the Lord.

twi: Israelfi ne Yudafianni me nokware koraa,”Awurade na ose.
english:
The people of Israel and the people of Judah
    have been utterly unfaithful to me,”
declares the Lord.

twi: Wɔadi atoro afa Awurade ho,wɔkae se, “Ɔrenyɛ hwee!Ɔhaw biara remma yɛn so;yɛrenhu afoa anaa ɔkɔm da.
Adiyifo no yɛ mframa bi kɛkɛna asɛm no nte wɔn mu;enti momma nea wɔka no mmra wɔn so.”
Enti eyi ne nea Asafo Awurade, Nyankopɔn se:“Esiane sɛ, nnipa no aka saa nsɛm yi nti,mɛyɛ me nsɛm a ɛwɔ wʼanom no ogyana saa nnipa yi ayɛ nnyina a ogya no bɛhyew.
english:
Therefore this is what the Lord God Almighty says:
“Because the people have spoken these words,
    I will make my words in your mouth a fire
    and these people the wood it consumes.

twi: Israelfi,” Awurade na ose,“Mede ɔman bi a ɛwɔ akyirikyiri rebetia wo,tete man a ɛyɛ ɔmantease,nnipa a munnim wɔn kasa,na monnte wɔn kasa ase.
english:
People of Israel,” declares the Lord,
    “I am bringing a distant nation against you—
an ancient and enduring nation,
    a people whose language you do not know,
    whose speech you do not understand.

twi: Wɔn agyan mmɔtɔwa te sɛ ɔda a ano da hɔ;wɔn nyinaa yɛ dɔmmarima.
english:
Their quivers are like an open grave;
    all of them are mighty warriors.

twi: Wɔbɛsɛe mo nnɔbae ne mo nnuan,asɛe mo mmabarima ne mo mmabea;wɔbɛsɛe mo nguankuw ne mo anantwikuw,asɛe mo bobe ne mo mmrɔdɔma.Wɔde afoa bɛsɛenkuropɔn a ɛwɔ bammɔ a mode mo werɛ ahyɛ mu no.
english:
They will devour your harvests and food,
    devour your sons and daughters;
they will devour your flocks and herds,
    devour your vines and fig trees.
With the sword they will destroy
    the fortified cities in which you trust.

twi: “Afei saa nna no mu mpo,” sɛɛ na Awurade se, “Merensɛe mo korakora.
english: “Yet even in those days,” declares the Lord, “I will not destroy you completely.

twi: Na sɛ nnipa no bisa se, ‘Adɛn nti na Awurade, yɛn Nyankopɔn, ayɛ yɛn sɛɛ’ a, mobɛka akyerɛ wɔn se, ‘Sɛnea moagyaw me hɔ akɔsom ananafo anyame wɔ mo ankasa mo asase so no, saa ara na mprempren mobɛsom ananafo wɔ asase a ɛnyɛ mo dea no so.’
english: And when the people ask, ‘Why has the Lord our God done all this to us?’ you will tell them, ‘As you have forsaken me and served foreign gods in your own land, so now you will serve foreigners in a land not your own.’

twi: “Monka eyi nkyerɛ Yakobfina mo mpae mu nka wɔ Yuda se:
english:
“Announce this to the descendants of Jacob
    and proclaim it in Judah:

twi: Muntie, mo nkwaseafo ne nnipa a munni adwene,mowɔ ani nso munhu ade,na mowɔ aso nso monte asɛm:
english:
Hear this, you foolish and senseless people,
    who have eyes but do not see,
    who have ears but do not hear:

twi: Ɛnsɛ sɛ musuro me ana?” Sɛɛ na Awurade se.“Ɛnsɛ sɛ mo ho popo wɔ mʼanim ana?Mede nwea ato ɔhye ama po,ɔhye a ɛwɔ hɔ daa a ɛrentumi ntra.Asorɔkye bɛbɔ nanso ɛrentumi mmu mfa so;ebehuru so nanso ɛrentumi ntra.
english:
Should you not fear me?” declares the Lord.
    “Should you not tremble in my presence?
I made the sand a boundary for the sea,
    an everlasting barrier it cannot cross.
The waves may roll, but they cannot prevail;
    they may roar, but they cannot cross it.

twi: Nanso saa nnipa yi wɔ asoɔden ne atuatew koma;wɔatwe wɔn ho afi me ho kɔ.
english:
But these people have stubborn and rebellious hearts;
    they have turned aside and gone away.

twi: Wɔnnka nkyerɛ wɔn ho wɔn ho se,‘Momma yensuro Awurade yɛn Nyankopɔn,a ɔma osu tɔ wɔ ne mmere mu,nea ɔma yɛn awerehyɛmu wɔ otwabere nnapɛn a wahyɛ no ho.’
english:
They do not say to themselves,
    ‘Let us fear the Lord our God,
who gives autumn and spring rains in season,
    who assures us of the regular weeks of harvest.’

twi: Mo amumɔyɛ abɔ eyinom agu;mo bɔne ama ade pa abɔ mo.
english:
Your wrongdoings have kept these away;
    your sins have deprived you of good.

twi: “Amumɔyɛfo bi wɔ me nkurɔfo yi mua wɔtɛw sɛ nnipa a wosum nnomaa afiri,na wɔte sɛ wɔn a wosum mfiri yi nnipa.
english:
“Among my people are the wicked
    who lie in wait like men who snare birds
    and like those who set traps to catch people.

twi: Sɛnea nnomaa ahyɛ kɛntɛn ma nosaa ara na asisi ahyɛ wɔn afi amaama;wɔayeyɛ adefo anyinya tumi,
na wɔadodɔ srade ama wɔn ho ayɛ hanahana.Wɔn amumɔyɛsɛm no nni awiei;wɔnnka ayisaa asɛm mma wonni bem,na wɔmmɔ ahiafo tumi ho ban.
Ɛnsɛ sɛ metwe wɔn aso wɔ eyinom ho ana?”Sɛɛ na Awurade se.“Ɛnsɛ sɛ, mʼankasa metɔɔman a ɛte sɛɛ so were ana?
english:
Should I not punish them for this?”
    declares the Lord.
“Should I not avenge myself
    on such a nation as this?

twi: “Ade a ɛyɛ hu ne ahodwiriwasi wɔ asase no so:
english:
“A horrible and shocking thing
    has happened in the land:

twi: Adiyifo no hyɛ akɔntoro,asɔfo no de wɔn dibea di tumi,na me nkurɔfo no pɛ no saa ara.Nanso awiei no dɛn na wobɛyɛ?”
english:
The prophets prophesy lies,
    the priests rule by their own authority,
and my people love it this way.
    But what will you do in the end?

twi: Atamfo Atwa Yerusalem Ho Ahyia“Benyaminfo, munguan nkɔbɔ mo ho aguaa!Munguan mfi Yerusalem!Monhyɛn torobɛnto no wɔ Tekoa!Munsi frankaa no wɔ Bet-Hakerem!Efisɛ amanehunu bobɔw fi atifi fam,ɔsɛe bi a ɛyɛ hu.
english:
“Flee for safety, people of Benjamin!
    Flee from Jerusalem!
Sound the trumpet in Tekoa!
    Raise the signal over Beth Hakkerem!
For disaster looms out of the north,
    even terrible destruction.

twi: Mɛsɛe Ɔbabea Sion,ɔhoɔfɛfo sɔɔnɔ no.
english:
I will destroy Daughter Zion,
    so beautiful and delicate.

twi: Nguanhwɛfo ne wɔn nguankuw bɛba abetia no;wobesisi wɔn ntamadan atwa ne ho ahyia,wɔn mu biara bɛhwɛ ne kyɛfa so.”
“Munsiesie mo ho ne no nkɔko!Monsɔre, momma yɛnkɔtow nhyɛ ne so owigyinae!Nanso hwɛ, onwini redwo,na anwummere sunsuma reware.
english:
“Prepare for battle against her!
    Arise, let us attack at noon!
But, alas, the daylight is fading,
    and the shadows of evening grow long.

twi: Enti monsɔre, momma yɛnkɔtow nhyɛ ne so anadwona yɛnsɛe nʼaban ahorow!”
english:
So arise, let us attack at night
    and destroy her fortresses!”

twi: Nea Asafo Awurade se ni:“Muntwitwa nnua no ngu famna muntwa Yerusalem ho dantaban.Ɛsɛ sɛ wɔtwe kuropɔn yi aso;nhyɛso ahyɛ no ma.
english:
This is what the Lord Almighty says:
“Cut down the trees
    and build siege ramps against Jerusalem.
This city must be punished;
    it is filled with oppression.

twi: Sɛnea abura puw ne nsu no,saa ara na opuw nʼamumɔyɛ.Wɔte awurukasɛm ne ɔsɛe nka wɔ ne mu;ne yare ne nʼapirakuru wɔ mʼanim daa.
english:
As a well pours out its water,
    so she pours out her wickedness.
Violence and destruction resound in her;
    her sickness and wounds are ever before me.

twi: Fa kɔkɔbɔ, Yerusalem,anyɛ saa metwe me ho afi wo hona mama wʼasase ada mpana obiara ntumi ntena so.”
english:
Take warning, Jerusalem,
    or I will turn away from you
and make your land desolate
    so no one can live in it.”

twi: Nea Asafo Awurade se ni:“Ma wonyiyi Israel nkae no mu yiyesɛnea woyiyi bobe mu yiye no;fa wo nsa fa mman no so bio,sɛ obi a ɔretetew bobe aba.”
english:
This is what the Lord Almighty says:
“Let them glean the remnant of Israel
    as thoroughly as a vine;
pass your hand over the branches again,
    like one gathering grapes.”

twi: Hena na metumi akasa akyerɛ no na mabɔ no kɔkɔ?Hena na obetie me?Wɔn aso asisiwenti wɔnte asɛm.Awurade asɛm yɛ akyiwade ma wɔn,na wɔn ani nnye ho.
english:
To whom can I speak and give warning?
    Who will listen to me?
Their ears are closed
    so they cannot hear.
The word of the Lord is offensive to them;
    they find no pleasure in it.

twi: Nanso Awurade abufuwhyew ahyɛ me ma,na mintumi nkora so.“Hwie gu mmofra a wɔwɔ mmɔnten sone mmerante a wɔahyia;ɛbɛka okunu ne ɔyere,mmasiriwa, wɔn a onyin ahunhuan wɔn no so.
english:
But I am full of the wrath of the Lord,
    and I cannot hold it in.
“Pour it out on the children in the street
    and on the young men gathered together;
both husband and wife will be caught in it,
    and the old, those weighed down with years.

twi: Wɔbɛdan wɔn afi ama afoforo,wɔn mfuw ne wɔn yerenom bɛka ho;sɛ meteɛ me nsawɔ wɔn a wɔte asase no so a,”sɛnea Awurade se ni.
english:
Their houses will be turned over to others,
    together with their fields and their wives,
when I stretch out my hand
    against those who live in the land,”
declares the Lord.

twi: “Efi akumaa so kosi ɔkɛse so,wɔn nyinaa yɛ adifudepɛfo de pɛ ahonya;adiyifo ne asɔfo te saa,wɔn nyinaa yɛ asisifo.
english:
“From the least to the greatest,
    all are greedy for gain;
prophets and priests alike,
    all practice deceit.

twi: Wɔtoto me nkurɔfo apirakurute sɛnea ɛnyɛ hu.Wɔka se, ‘Asomdwoe, asomdwoe’wɔ mmere a asomdwoe nni hɔ.
english:
They dress the wound of my people
    as though it were not serious.
‘Peace, peace,’ they say,
    when there is no peace.

twi: Wɔn ani wu wɔ wɔn animguase nneyɛe no ho ana?Dabi da, wɔn ani nnwu koraa;wonnim fɛre mpo.Enti wɔbɛtotɔ wɔ atɔfo mu;wɔbɛhwehwe ase, sɛ metwe wɔn aso a,”sɛnea Awurade se ni.
Eyi ne nea Awurade se,“Munnyina nkwantanan no so na monhwɛ;mummisa tete akwan no,mummisa faako a ɔkwan pa no da na monnantew so,na mubenya home ama mo akra.Nanso mokae se, ‘yɛnnantew so.’
english:
This is what the Lord says:
“Stand at the crossroads and look;
    ask for the ancient paths,
ask where the good way is, and walk in it,
    and you will find rest for your souls.
    But you said, ‘We will not walk in it.’
