“for your day has come,
    the time for you to be punished.

twi: Ɔhantanni no behintiw na wahwe ase,obiara remmoa no mma ɔnnsɔre;mɛto ne nkurow mu gyana ahyew wɔn a atwa ne ho ahyia nyinaa.”
english:
The arrogant one will stumble and fall
    and no one will help her up;
I will kindle a fire in her towns
    that will consume all who are around her.”

twi: Sɛɛ na Asafo Awurade se:“Wɔhyɛ Israelfo so,na Yudafo nso saa ara.Wɔn nnommumfafo no kura wɔn dennena wɔmpɛ sɛ wogyaa wɔn ma wɔkɔ.
english:
This is what the Lord Almighty says:
“The people of Israel are oppressed,
    and the people of Judah as well.
All their captors hold them fast,
    refusing to let them go.

twi: Nanso wɔn Gyefo yɛ ɔhoɔdenfo;ne din ne Asafo Awurade.Obedi wɔn asɛm ama wɔn anibere so,sɛnea ɔde ahotɔ bɛba wɔn asase no so,na wɔn a wɔte Babilonia no nea wahyɛ wɔn ahometew.
english:
Yet their Redeemer is strong;
    the Lord Almighty is his name.
He will vigorously defend their cause
    so that he may bring rest to their land,
    but unrest to those who live in Babylon.

twi: “Afoa a etia Babiloniafo!”Awurade na ose,“etia wɔn a wɔte Babiloniana etia nʼadwumayɛfo ne nʼanyansafo!
english:
“A sword against the Babylonians!”
    declares the Lord—
“against those who live in Babylon
    and against her officials and wise men!

twi: Afoa a etia nʼatoro adiyifo!Wɔbɛdan nkwaseafo.Afoa a etia nʼakofo!Ehu bɛhyɛ wɔn ma.
english:
A sword against her false prophets!
    They will become fools.
A sword against her warriors!
    They will be filled with terror.

twi: Afoa a etia nʼapɔnkɔ ne ne nteaseɛnamne ananafo a wɔwɔ wɔn mu nyinaa!Wɔbɛdan mmea.Afoa a etia nʼademude!Wɔbɛfom.
english:
A sword against her horses and chariots
    and all the foreigners in her ranks!
    They will become weaklings.
A sword against her treasures!
    They will be plundered.

twi: Ɔyow wɔ nʼasu ahorow so!Ɛbɛyoyow.Efisɛ ɛyɛ ahoni asase,ahoni a ehu bɛma wɔabobɔ adam.
english:
A drought on her waters!
    They will dry up.
For it is a land of idols,
    idols that will go mad with terror.

twi: “Enti sare so mmoa ne mpataku bɛtena hɔ,na ɛhɔ na patu bɛtena.Obiara rentena so bioefi awo ntoatoaso kosi awo ntoatoaso.
english:
“So desert creatures and hyenas will live there,
    and there the owl will dwell.
It will never again be inhabited
    or lived in from generation to generation.

twi: Sɛnea Onyankopɔn tuu Sodom ne Gomorane wɔn nkurow gui no,”Awurade na ose,“saa ara na obiara rentena hɔ;onipa biara rentena mu.
english:
As I overthrew Sodom and Gomorrah
    along with their neighboring towns,”
declares the Lord,
“so no one will live there;
    no people will dwell in it.

twi: “Monhwɛ! Asraafo bi fi atifi fam reba;ɔman kɛse ne ahemfo bebree,wɔrehwanyan wɔn afi nsase ano.
Wokurakura bɛmma ne mpeaw;wɔn tirim yɛ den, na wonni ahummɔbɔ.Wɔn nnyigyei te sɛ po a ɛworo so.Sɛ wɔtete wɔn apɔnkɔ so a,wɔba sɛ mmarima a wɔrekɔ saabɛtow ahyɛ wo so, Ɔbabea Babilonia.
Babiloniahene ate wɔn ho nsɛm,ne nsa sesa ne ho kwa.Ahohiahia akyekyere noɔyaw a ɛte sɛ ɔbea a ɔrekyem wɔ awo so.
english:
The king of Babylon has heard reports about them,
    and his hands hang limp.
Anguish has gripped him,
    pain like that of a woman in labor.

twi: Sɛnea gyata a ofi Yordan nkyɛkyerɛ murekɔ adidibea frɔmfrɔm no,saa ara na mɛtaa Babilonia fi nʼasase so wɔ bere tiaa bi mu.Hena ne nea mayi no sɛ ɔnyɛ eyi?Hena na ɔte sɛ me, na hena na obetumi ne me adi asi?Na oguanhwɛfo bɛn na obetumi asɔre atia me?”
english:
Like a lion coming up from Jordan’s thickets
    to a rich pastureland,
I will chase Babylon from its land in an instant.
    Who is the chosen one I will appoint for this?
Who is like me and who can challenge me?
    And what shepherd can stand against me?”

twi: Enti tie nea Awurade ahyehyɛ atia Babilonia,nea wabɔ ne tirim sɛ ɔbɛyɛ de atia Babiloniafo asase ni:Nguankuw no mu nkumaa no wɔbɛtwe wɔn akɔ;wɔn nti ɔbɛsɛe adidibea no koraa.
english:
Therefore, hear what the Lord has planned against Babylon,
    what he has purposed against the land of the Babylonians:
The young of the flock will be dragged away;
    their pasture will be appalled at their fate.

twi: Babilonia nnommumfa nnyigyei bɛma asase awosow;ne nteɛteɛmu gyegyeegye wɔ amanaman no mu.
english:
At the sound of Babylon’s capture the earth will tremble;
    its cry will resound among the nations.

twi: Sɛɛ na Awurade se:“Monhwɛ, mɛkanyan ɔsɛefo bi honhomatia Babilonia ne nnipa a wɔwɔ Leb Kamai.
english:
This is what the Lord says:
“See, I will stir up the spirit of a destroyer
    against Babylon and the people of Leb Kamai.

twi: Mɛsoma ananafo akɔ Babiloniasɛ wonkohuhuw ne so na wɔnsɛe nʼasase;wobetia no wɔ afanan nyinaawɔ nʼamanehunu da no.
english:
I will send foreigners to Babylon
    to winnow her and to devastate her land;
they will oppose her on every side
    in the day of her disaster.

twi: Mma agyantowni pema nʼagyan,mma ɔnhyɛ ne nkatabo.Mma ne mmerante mfa wɔn ho nni;sɛe nʼasraafo no pasaa.
english:
Let not the archer string his bow,
    nor let him put on his armor.
Do not spare her young men;
    completely destroy her army.

twi: Wɔbɛhwehwe ase a wɔatotɔ wɔ Babilonia,a wɔapirapira yiye wɔ ne mmɔnten so.
english:
They will fall down slain in Babylon,
    fatally wounded in her streets.

twi: Na Israel Nyankopɔn, Asafo Awurade no,nnyaw Israel ne Yuda hɔ ɛ,ɛwɔ mu, afɔdi ahyɛ wɔn asase no so mawɔ Israel Ɔkronkronni no anim.
english:
For Israel and Judah have not been forsaken
    by their God, the Lord Almighty,
though their land is full of guilt
    before the Holy One of Israel.

twi: “Munguan mfi Babilonia!Muntu mmirika mpere mo nkwa!Mommma wɔnnsɛe mo esiane ne bɔne nti.Awurade aweretɔbere aso;ɔde nea ɛfata no betua no ka.
english:
“Flee from Babylon!
    Run for your lives!
    Do not be destroyed because of her sins.
It is time for the Lord’s vengeance;
    he will repay her what she deserves.

twi: Na Babilonia yɛ sikakɔkɔɔ kuruwa wɔ Awurade nsam;ɔmaa asase nyinaa bow nsa.Aman no nom ne nsa;ɛno nti, afei wɔabobɔ adam.
Babilonia bɛhwe ase abubu mpofirim.Muntwa ne ho agyaadwo!Mompɛ ne yaw no ano aduru;ebia ne ho bɛtɔ no.
english:
Babylon will suddenly fall and be broken.
    Wail over her!
Get balm for her pain;
    perhaps she can be healed.

twi: “ ‘Anka yɛbɛsa Babilonia yare,nanso wontumi nsa no yare;momma yennyaw no hɔ na obiara nkɔ nʼankasa asase so,efisɛ nʼatemmu du sorosoro;ɛforo soro te sɛ omununkum.’
“ ‘Awurade abu yɛn bem.Mommra, momma yɛnka wɔ Sion,nea Awurade, yɛn Nyankopɔn ayɛ.’
“Monsew agyan no ano!Momfa nkatabo no!Awurade ahwanyan Mede ahemfo no,efisɛ ne botae ne sɛ ɔbɛsɛe Babilonia.Awurade bɛtɔ were,ɔbɛtɔ were ama nʼasɔrefi no.
english:
“Sharpen the arrows,
    take up the shields!
The Lord has stirred up the kings of the Medes,
    because his purpose is to destroy Babylon.
The Lord will take vengeance,
    vengeance for his temple.

twi: Mompagyaw frankaa bi ntia Babilonia afasu!Mummia bammɔ mu,momma awɛmfo no nnyinagyina.Munsiesie ahintawee!Awurade bɛma nʼatirimpɔw aba mu,nea wahyɛ atia Babilonia no.
english:
Lift up a banner against the walls of Babylon!
    Reinforce the guard,
station the watchmen,
    prepare an ambush!
The Lord will carry out his purpose,
    his decree against the people of Babylon.

twi: Mo a motete nsuwansuwa bebree hona nnwetɛbona abu mo so,mo awiei aba,bere a ɛsɛ sɛ wotwa mo kyene no.
english:
You who live by many waters
    and are rich in treasures,
your end has come,
    the time for you to be destroyed.

twi: Asafo Awurade, aka ne ho ntam sɛ:mede nnipa bɛhyɛ wo ma sɛ tɛwtɛw,na wɔabɔ ose wɔ wo so.
english:
The Lord Almighty has sworn by himself:
    I will surely fill you with troops, as with a swarm of locusts,
    and they will shout in triumph over you.

twi: “Ɔde ne tumi bɔɔ asase;ɔtoo wiase fapem wɔ ne nyansa muna ɔde ne nhumu trɛw ɔsorosoro mu.
Sɛ ɔbobɔ mu a, ɔsoro nsu woro so;ɔma omununkum ma ne ho so fi nsase ano.Ɔsoma anyinam ka osu hona ɔma mframa bɔ fi ne koradan mu.
english:
When he thunders, the waters in the heavens roar;
    he makes clouds rise from the ends of the earth.
He sends lightning with the rain
    and brings out the wind from his storehouses.

twi: “Onipa biara nnim nyansa, na onni nimdeɛ;sikadwumfo biara anim gu ase, esiane nʼahoni nti.Ne nsɛsode yɛ atoro;wonni ɔhome biara wɔ wɔn mu.
Wɔn so nni mfaso, wɔn ho yɛ serew;sɛ wɔn atemmu du so a, wɔbɛyera.
english:
They are worthless, the objects of mockery;
    when their judgment comes, they will perish.

twi: Nea ɔyɛ Yakob Kyɛfa no nte sɛ eyinom,efisɛ ɔno ne ade nyinaa Yɛfoa Israel, abusua a ɛyɛ nʼagyapade nso ka ho.Asafo Awurade ne ne din.
english:
He who is the Portion of Jacob is not like these,
    for he is the Maker of all things,
including the people of his inheritance—
    the Lord Almighty is his name.

twi: “Woyɛ me ko abaa,mʼakode a mede kɔ samede wo dwerɛw amanaman,mede wo sɛe ahenni bebree,
english:
“You are my war club,
    my weapon for battle—
with you I shatter nations,
    with you I destroy kingdoms,

twi: mede wo bobɔ ɔpɔnkɔ ne ne sotefo,teaseɛnam ne ne kafo,
english:
with you I shatter horse and rider,
    with you I shatter chariot and driver,

twi: mede wo dwerɛw ɔbarima ne ɔbea,mede wo dwerɛw akwakoraa ne ɔbabun,mede wo dwerɛw aberante ne ababaa,
english:
with you I shatter man and woman,
    with you I shatter old man and youth,
    with you I shatter young man and young woman,

twi: mede wo dwerɛw oguanhwɛfo ne nguankuw,mede wo dwerɛw okuafo ne anantwi,mede wo dwerɛw amradofo ne adwumayɛfo.
english:
with you I shatter shepherd and flock,
    with you I shatter farmer and oxen,
    with you I shatter governors and officials.

twi: “Metua Babilonia ne wɔn a wɔtete Babilonia ka wɔ mfomso a, wɔayɛ wɔ Sion nyinaa, wɔ wʼanim,” Awurade na ose.
english: “Before your eyes I will repay Babylon and all who live in Babylonia for all the wrong they have done in Zion,” declares the Lord.

twi: “Bepɔw sɛefo, me ne wo anya,wo a wosɛe asase nyinaa no,”Awurade na ose.“Mɛteɛ me nsa wɔ wo somepia wo afi abotan no so,na mayɛ wo sɛ bepɔw a ɛnka hwee.
english:
“I am against you, you destroying mountain,
    you who destroy the whole earth,”
declares the Lord.
“I will stretch out my hand against you,
    roll you off the cliffs,
    and make you a burned-out mountain.

twi: Wɔremfa ɔbo biara mfi wo so nyɛ tweatiboanaasɛ fapem mpo,efisɛ wobɛda mpan afebɔɔ,”Awurade na ose.
english:
No rock will be taken from you for a cornerstone,
    nor any stone for a foundation,
    for you will be desolate forever,”
declares the Lord.

twi: “Momma frankaa so wɔ asase no so!Monhyɛn torobɛnto no wɔ amanaman no mu!Munsiesie amanaman no mma wontu no so sa;Momfrɛfrɛ saa ahenni ahorow yi mma wɔnko ntia no:Ararat, Mini ne Askenas.Munnyi ɔsahene ntia no;momfa apɔnkɔ manyamanya te sɛ tɛwtɛw mmra.
english:
“Lift up a banner in the land!
    Blow the trumpet among the nations!
Prepare the nations for battle against her;
    summon against her these kingdoms:
    Ararat, Minni and Ashkenaz.
Appoint a commander against her;
    send up horses like a swarm of locusts.

twi: Munsiesie amanaman no mma wontu no so sa,mo Mede ahemfo,wɔn amradofo ne wɔn adwumayɛfo nyinaa,ne aman a wodi so nyinaa.
english:
Prepare the nations for battle against her—
    the kings of the Medes,
their governors and all their officials,
    and all the countries they rule.

twi: Asase no wosow, na onukunuku ne mu,efisɛ Awurade atirimpɔw a etia Babiloniasɛ ɔbɛsɛe Babilonia asase aobiara rentumi ntena so no nsakraa ɛ.
english:
The land trembles and writhes,
    for the Lord’s purposes against Babylon stand—
to lay waste the land of Babylon
    so that no one will live there.

twi: Babilonia dɔmmarima agyae kowɔhyehyɛ wɔn aban mu.Wɔn ahoɔden asa;wɔayɛ sɛ mmea.Wɔatoto nʼatenae ahorow no mu gya,na wɔabubu nʼapon akyi adaban.
Abɔfo didi sona asomafo didi so awɔrekɔbɔ Babiloniahene amanneɛ se,wɔafa ne kuropɔn no,
english:
One courier follows another
    and messenger follows messenger
to announce to the king of Babylon
    that his entire city is captured,

twi: wɔagye asutwabea ahorow a ɛdeda asubɔnten no ano no afa,na wɔde ogya ato ɔwora no mu,na asraafo no abɔ huboa.”
english:
the river crossings seized,
    the marshes set on fire,
    and the soldiers terrified.”

twi: Sɛɛ na Asafo Awurade, Israel Nyankopɔn, se:“Babilonia Babea ayɛ sɛ, awiporowbeawɔ bere a wɔretiatia hɔ.Aka kakraa bi, na bere a ɛsɛ sɛ wotwa no sɛ nnɔbae no adu.”
english:
This is what the Lord Almighty, the God of Israel, says:
“Daughter Babylon is like a threshing floor
    at the time it is trampled;
    the time to harvest her will soon come.”

twi: “Babiloniahene Nebukadnessar adwerɛw yɛn,ɔde yɛn ato ɔhaw mu,wayɛ yɛn sɛ ahina a hwee nni mu.Wamene yɛn sɛ ɔwɔ nona ɔde yɛn nneɛma a ɛyɛ dɛ ahyɛ ne yafunu ma,na wapuw yɛn afi nʼanom agu.
english:
“Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon has devoured us,
    he has thrown us into confusion,
    he has made us an empty jar.
Like a serpent he has swallowed us
    and filled his stomach with our delicacies,
    and then has spewed us out.

twi: Ma ayakayakade a wɔde dii yɛn honam no mmra Babilonia so,”nnipa a wɔtete Sion na wɔka.“Ma yɛn mogya ngu wɔn a wɔtete Babilonia so,”Yerusalem na ɔka.
english:
May the violence done to our flesh be on Babylon,”
    say the inhabitants of Zion.
“May our blood be on those who live in Babylonia,”
    says Jerusalem.

twi: Enti sɛɛ na Awurade se:“Hwɛ, medi mo asɛm ama mona matɔ were ama mo;Mɛma po a ɛyɛ ne de no ayowna mama ne nsubɔnten ayoyow.
english:
Therefore this is what the Lord says:
“See, I will defend your cause
    and avenge you;
I will dry up her sea
    and make her springs dry.

twi: Babilonia bɛyɛ mmubui siw,sakraman atuahodwiriwde ne fɛwdi,baabi a obiara nte.
english:
Babylon will be a heap of ruins,
    a haunt of jackals,
an object of horror and scorn,
    a place where no one lives.

twi: Ne nkurɔfo nyinaa bobɔ mu sɛ gyata,wɔbobɔ mu te sɛ gyatamma.
english:
Her people all roar like young lions,
    they growl like lion cubs.

twi: Nanso bere a wɔahwanyan wɔn ho no,mɛto pon ama wɔnna mama wɔabobow nsa,sɛnea wɔde nteɛteɛmu bedi ahurusi,na wɔadeda a wɔrennyan bio,”Awurade na ose.
english:
But while they are aroused,
    I will set out a feast for them
    and make them drunk,
so that they shout with laughter—
    then sleep forever and not awake,”
declares the Lord.

twi: “Mede wɔn bɛbate sɛ nguantenmma a wɔrekokum wɔn,te sɛ adwennini ne mpapo.
english:
“I will bring them down
    like lambs to the slaughter,
    like rams and goats.

twi: “Sɛnea wɔbɛfa Sesak,wɔbɛfa asase nyinaa so ahohoahoa!Babilonia bɛyɛ ahodwiriwdewɔ amanaman no mu!
english:
“How Sheshak will be captured,
    the boast of the whole earth seized!
How desolate Babylon will be
    among the nations!

twi: Po bebunkam afa Babilonia so;na nʼasorɔkye bɛkata ne so.
english:
The sea will rise over Babylon;
    its roaring waves will cover her.

twi: Ne nkurow bɛda mpan,nweatam a so awo,asase a obiara nte so,na obiara ntu kwan mfa so.
english:
Her towns will be desolate,
    a dry and desert land,
a land where no one lives,
    through which no one travels.

twi: Mɛtwe Bel aso wɔ Babiloniana mama wapuw nea wamene agu.Amanaman no rento santen nkɔ ne nkyɛn bio.Na Babilonia fasu bebubu.
english:
I will punish Bel in Babylon
    and make him spew out what he has swallowed.
The nations will no longer stream to him.
    And the wall of Babylon will fall.

twi: “Me nkurɔfo, mumfi ne mu!Muntu mmirika mpere mo nkwa!Munguan mfi Awurade abufuwhyew ano.
english:
“Come out of her, my people!
    Run for your lives!
    Run from the fierce anger of the Lord.

twi: Mommma mo koma ntu na munnsurosɛ mote huhuhuhu wɔ asase no so a;huhuhuhu ba afe yi na foforo ba afe a ɛbɛba,basabasayɛ ho huhuhuhu wɔ asase no soɛfa ɔhene a ɔsɔre tia ɔfoforo ho.
english:
Do not lose heart or be afraid
    when rumors are heard in the land;
one rumor comes this year, another the next,
    rumors of violence in the land
    and of ruler against ruler.

twi: Na ampa ara bere no bɛbaa mɛtwe Babilonia ahoni aso;nʼasase no nyinaa anim begu asena nʼatɔfo nyinaa bɛtotɔ ase wɔ ne so.
english:
For the time will surely come
    when I will punish the idols of Babylon;
her whole land will be disgraced
    and her slain will all lie fallen within her.

twi: Ɔsoro ne asase ne nea ɛwɔ mu nyinaade ahosɛpɛw bɛteɛ mu agu Babilonia so,efisɛ ɔsɛefo befi atifi famabɛtow ahyɛ ne so,”Awurade na ose.
english:
Then heaven and earth and all that is in them
    will shout for joy over Babylon,
for out of the north
    destroyers will attack her,”
declares the Lord.

twi: “Ɛsɛ sɛ Babilonia hwe ase, esiane Israel atɔfo ntisɛnea atɔfo a wɔwɔ wiase nyinaa ahwehwe aseesiane Babilonia nti no.
english:
“Babylon must fall because of Israel’s slain,
    just as the slain in all the earth
    have fallen because of Babylon.

twi: Mo a mo aguan afi afoa ano,monkɔ, na monntwentwɛn mo nan ase!Monkae Awurade wɔ akyirikyiri asase so,na munnwen Yerusalem ho.”
english:
You who have escaped the sword,
    leave and do not linger!
Remember the Lord in a distant land,
    and call to mind Jerusalem.”

twi: “Wɔagu yɛn anim ase,efisɛ wayeyaw yɛnna fɛre akata yɛn anim,efisɛ ananafo ahyɛnAwurade fi kronkronbea ahorow hɔ.”
english:
“We are disgraced,
    for we have been insulted
    and shame covers our faces,
because foreigners have entered
    the holy places of the Lord’s house.”

twi: “Nanso nna bi reba,” Awurade na ose,“a mɛtwe nʼahoni aso,na nʼasase so nyinaaapirafo besi apini.
english:
“But days are coming,” declares the Lord,
    “when I will punish her idols,
and throughout her land
    the wounded will groan.

twi: Sɛ Babilonia kɔka soro mpo,na omiamia nʼaban tenten bammɔ mu a,mɛsoma ɔsɛefo ne no abedi asi,”Awurade na ose.
english:
Even if Babylon ascends to the heavens
    and fortifies her lofty stronghold,
    I will send destroyers against her,”
declares the Lord.

twi: “Osu nnyigyei bi fi Babilonia,ɔsɛe kɛse bi nnyigyeifi Babiloniafo asase so.
english:
“The sound of a cry comes from Babylon,
    the sound of great destruction
    from the land of the Babylonians.

twi: Awurade bɛsɛe Babilonia;ɔbɛma nʼasotuatua nnyigyei no agyae.Atamfo a wɔte sɛ ahum betu sɛ nsu akɛse;wɔn mmubomu bɛyɛ gyegyeegye.
Ɔsɛefo bi bɛsɔre atia Babilonia;wɔbɛfa ne dɔmmarima nnommumna wobebubu wɔn tadua mu.Efisɛ Awurade yɛ Onyankopɔn a ɔhyɛ anan mu;obetua so ka pɛpɛɛpɛ.
Mɛma nʼadwumayɛfo ne nʼanyansafo abow nsanʼamradonom, ne mpanyimfo ne dɔmmarima nso saa ara;wɔbɛdeda afebɔɔ a wɔrennyan,”sɛɛ na ɔhempɔn a ne din ne Asafo Awurade, no se.
english:
I will make her officials and wise men drunk,
    her governors, officers and warriors as well;
they will sleep forever and not awake,”
    declares the King, whose name is the Lord Almighty.

twi: Sɛɛ na Asafo Awurade, se:“Wobedwiriw Babilonia afasu a ɛtrɛw no agu famna wɔbɛto nʼapon atenten no mu gya;nnipa no haw wɔn ho kwa,ɔman no adwumayɛ ma ogya no dɛw mmom.”
english:
This is what the Lord Almighty says:
“Babylon’s thick wall will be leveled
    and her high gates set on fire;
the peoples exhaust themselves for nothing,
    the nations’ labor is only fuel for the flames.”

twi: Eyi ne asɛm a Yeremia ka kyerɛɛ Neria babarima Seraia a ɔyɛ adwumayɛfo panyin na ɔyɛ Maseia nena no, bere a ɔne Yudahene Sedekia kɔɔ Babilonia wɔ nʼadedi afe a ɛto so anan no mu.
english: This is the message Jeremiah the prophet gave to the staff officer Seraiah son of Neriah, the son of Mahseiah, when he went to Babylon with Zedekiah king of Judah in the fourth year of his reign.

twi: Na Yeremia akyerɛw amanehunu a ɛbɛba Babilonia so no nyinaa agu nhoma mmobɔwee so, nea wakyerɛw a ɛfa Babilonia ho nyinaa.
english: Jeremiah had written on a scroll about all the disasters that would come upon Babylon—all that had been recorded concerning Babylon.

twi: Ɔka kyerɛɛ Seraia se, “Sɛ wudu Babilonia a, hwɛ sɛ wobɛkenkan saa nsɛm yi nyinaa sɛnea obiara bɛte.
english: He said to Seraiah, “When you get to Babylon, see that you read all these words aloud.

twi: Afei ka se, ‘Awurade, woaka se wobɛsɛe beae yi sɛnea onipa anaa aboa biara rentumi ntena so; na ɛbɛda mpan afebɔɔ.’
english: Then say, ‘Lord, you have said you will destroy this place, so that neither people nor animals will live in it; it will be desolate forever.’

twi: Sɛ wokenkan nhoma mmobɔwee yi wie a, kyekyere fam ɔbo ho, na tow kyene Asubɔnten Eufrate mu.
english: When you finish reading this scroll, tie a stone to it and throw it into the Euphrates.

twi: Afei ka se, ‘Sɛɛ na Babilonia ne ne nkurɔfo bɛmem a wɔrensɔre bio, esiane amanehunu a mede bɛba ne so no nti.’ ”Yeremia nsɛm no awiei ni.
english:
Then say, ‘So will Babylon sink to rise no more because of the disaster I will bring on her. And her people will fall.’”
The words of Jeremiah end here.

twi: Yerusalem AsehweSedekia dii ade no, na wadi mfirihyia aduonu baako. Odii ade wɔ Yerusalem mfirihyia dubaako. Na ne na din de Hamutal a ɔyɛ Yeremia a ofi Libna no babea.
english: Zedekiah was twenty-one years old when he became king, and he reigned in Jerusalem eleven years. His mother’s name was Hamutal daughter of Jeremiah; she was from Libnah.

twi: Ɔyɛɛ bɔne wɔ Awurade ani so, sɛnea Yehoiakim yɛe no.
english: He did evil in the eyes of the Lord, just as Jehoiakim had done.

twi: Awurade abufuw nti na eyinom nyinaa baa Yerusalem ne Yuda so, na akyiri no, oyii nʼani fii wɔn so.Afei, Sedekia sɔre tiaa Babiloniahene.
english:
It was because of the Lord’s anger that all this happened to Jerusalem and Judah, and in the end he thrust them from his presence.
Now Zedekiah rebelled against the king of Babylon.

twi: Ɔsram Tebet (bɛyɛ Ɔpɛpɔn) da a ɛto so dunum wɔ Sedekia ahenni mfe akron so no, ɔhene Nebukadnessar dii nʼakofo nyinaa anim, bɛko tiaa Yerusalem. Wotwaa kuropɔn no ho hyiae. Wɔbobɔɔ mpampim wɔ kuropɔn no afasu ho.
english: So in the ninth year of Zedekiah’s reign, on the tenth day of the tenth month, Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon marched against Jerusalem with his whole army. They encamped outside the city and built siege works all around it.

twi: Wotuaa kuropɔn no kosii Ɔhene Sedekia adedi afe a ɛto so dubaako no mu.
english: The city was kept under siege until the eleventh year of King Zedekiah.

twi: Eduu ɔsram a ɛto so anan no da a ɛto so akron no, na ɔkɔm a asi kuropɔn no mu no ano ayɛ den a mu nnipa no nnya aduan nni.
english: By the ninth day of the fourth month the famine in the city had become so severe that there was no food for the people to eat.

twi: Na wɔpaee kuropɔn no fasu mu, na asraafo no nyinaa guanee. Wɔfaa ɔhene turo mu fii kuropɔn no mu anadwo, kɔfaa ɔpon a ɛwɔ afasu abien no ntam, de wɔn ani kyerɛɛ Araba.
english: Then the city wall was broken through, and the whole army fled. They left the city at night through the gate between the two walls near the king’s garden, though the Babylonians were surrounding the city. They fled toward the Arabah,

twi: Nanso Babilonia asraafo no taa Ɔhene Sedekia kɔtoo no wɔ Yeriko tataw so. Na nʼasraafo no nyinaa afi ne ho abɔ ahwete,
english: but the Babylonian army pursued King Zedekiah and overtook him in the plains of Jericho. All his soldiers were separated from him and scattered,

twi: na wɔkyeree no.Wɔfaa no dommum de no kɔmaa Babiloniahene wɔ Ribla a ɛwɔ Hamat asase so, na hɔ na obuu no atɛn.
english:
and he was captured.
He was taken to the king of Babylon at Riblah in the land of Hamath, where he pronounced sentence on him.

twi: Ribla hɔ na Babiloniahene kunkum Sedekia mmabarima wɔ nʼanim na okum Yudafo adwumayɛfo nyinaa nso.
english: There at Riblah the king of Babylon killed the sons of Zedekiah before his eyes; he also killed all the officials of Judah.

twi: Afei otutuu Sedekia ani, de kɔbere mfrafrae mpokyerɛ guu no sɛ ɔde no rekɔ Babilonia, hɔ na ɔde no too afiase kosii ne wuda.
english: Then he put out Zedekiah’s eyes, bound him with bronze shackles and took him to Babylon, where he put him in prison till the day of his death.

twi: Ab ɔsram (bɛyɛ Ɔsannaa) da ɛto so dunan wɔ afe a ɛyɛ Nebukadnessar mfe dunkron adedi mu no, Nebusaradan a ɔyɛ awɛmfo so panyin a ɔyɛ Babiloniahene mpanyimfo no mu baako no kɔɔ Yerusalem.
english: On the tenth day of the fifth month, in the nineteenth year of Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon, Nebuzaradan commander of the imperial guard, who served the king of Babylon, came to Jerusalem.

twi: Ɔde ogya too Awurade asɔredan, ahemfi ne afi a ɛwɔ Yerusalem nyinaa mu. Ɔhyew ofi biara a edi mu.
english: He set fire to the temple of the Lord, the royal palace and all the houses of Jerusalem. Every important building he burned down.

twi: Awɛmfo so panyin no hwɛ maa Babilonia asraafo no bubuu Yerusalem afasu no.
english: The whole Babylonian army, under the commander of the imperial guard, broke down all the walls around Jerusalem.

twi: Ɔsahene Nebusaradan a na otua awɛmfo no ano no faa wɔn a wodi hia no mu bi, wɔn a wɔkaa kuropɔn no mu, adwumfo a wɔaka ne wɔn a wɔkɔdɔm Babiloniahene no kɔɔ nnommum mu.
english: Nebuzaradan the commander of the guard carried into exile some of the poorest people and those who remained in the city, along with the rest of the craftsmen and those who had deserted to the king of Babylon.

twi: Nanso Nebusaradan gyaa wɔn a wodi hia wɔ asase no so no nkae sɛ wɔnhwɛ bobe nturo ne mfuw no.
english: But Nebuzaradan left behind the rest of the poorest people of the land to work the vineyards and fields.

twi: Babiloniafo no bubuu kɔbere mfrafrae afadum, nnyinasode a wotumi moma so ne kɔbere mfrafrae Po a na ɛwɔ Awurade asɔredan mu, na wɔde kɔbere mfrafrae no nyinaa kɔɔ Babilonia.
english: The Babylonians broke up the bronze pillars, the movable stands and the bronze Sea that were at the temple of the Lord and they carried all the bronze to Babylon.

twi: Afei wɔfaa nkuku, nsofi, kanea ntamabamma ntwitwaso, ɔpete nkuruwa, nsanka, mprɛte ne kɔbere mfrafrae nneɛma a wɔde yɛ ɔsom adwuma wɔ asɔredan mu no nso kɔe.
english: They also took away the pots, shovels, wick trimmers, sprinkling bowls, dishes and all the bronze articles used in the temple service.

twi: Ɔhene awɛmfo sahene no faa nkankyee, nkankyee ntrantraa, ɔpete nkuruwa, nkuku, kaneannua, nsanka, mprɛte ne nkuruwa a wɔde di ɔnom afɔrebɔ ho dwuma no kɔe; wɔde sikakɔkɔɔ ankasa anaa dwetɛ na ɛyɛɛ eyinom nyinaa.
english: The commander of the imperial guard took away the basins, censers, sprinkling bowls, pots, lampstands, dishes and bowls used for drink offerings—all that were made of pure gold or silver.

twi: Kɔbere mfrafrae a wɔde yɛɛ afadum abien no, Po no ne anantwinini dumien a ɛwɔ nʼase ne nnyinaso a wɔmema so, na wontumi nkari saa nneɛma a Ɔhene Salomo yɛɛ wɔ Awurade asɔredan mu yi mu duru.
english: The bronze from the two pillars, the Sea and the twelve bronze bulls under it, and the movable stands, which King Solomon had made for the temple of the Lord, was more than could be weighed.

twi: Na afadum no biara sorokɔ yɛ anammɔn aduonu ason na ne dantaban mu nso yɛ anammɔn dunwɔtwe. Emu da tokuru na ne hankare no mu piw yɛ nsateaa anan.
english: Each pillar was eighteen cubits high and twelve cubits in circumference; each was four fingers thick, and hollow.

twi: Na kɔbere mfrafrae ntaaso a esi ɔfadum baako so no sorokɔ yɛ anammɔn ason ne fa a, wɔde kɔbere mfrafrae atoaa ahyehyɛ ho nyinaa ahyia. Afadum a aka no nso a wɔde kɔbere mfrafrae atoaa ahyehyɛ ho no te sɛ baako no.
english: The bronze capital on top of one pillar was five cubits high and was decorated with a network and pomegranates of bronze all around. The other pillar, with its pomegranates, was similar.

twi: Na Kɔbere mfrafrae atoaa aba a ɛsensɛn ntaaso no ano no yɛ aduɔkron asia, na nea ɛkata ntaaso no ho yɛ ɔha.
english: There were ninety-six pomegranates on the sides; the total number of pomegranates above the surrounding network was a hundred.

twi: Awɛmfo no sahene no faa ɔsɔfopanyin Seraia, abediakyiri Sefania ne ɔponanoahwɛfo baasa no nnommum.
english: The commander of the guard took as prisoners Seraiah the chief priest, Zephaniah the priest next in rank and the three doorkeepers.

twi: Ɔfaa ɔpanyin a otua asraafo no ano, ne adehye afotufo baason fii nnipa a na wɔda so wɔ kuropɔn no mu no mu. Afei ɔfaa ɔkyerɛwfo a na ɔyɛ adwumayɛfo panyin ma wɔn a wɔfa nnipa ma wɔkɔyɛ asraafo wɔ asase no so, ne nʼadwumayɛfo no mu aduosia a ohuu wɔn wɔ kuropɔn no mu no.
english: Of those still in the city, he took the officer in charge of the fighting men, and seven royal advisers. He also took the secretary who was chief officer in charge of conscripting the people of the land, sixty of whom were found in the city.

twi: Ɔsahene Nebusaradan de wɔn nyinaa kɔɔ Babiloniahene anim wɔ Ribla.
english: Nebuzaradan the commander took them all and brought them to the king of Babylon at Riblah.

twi: Ɔhene no ma wokunkum wɔn wɔ Ribla a ɛwɔ Hamat.Enti wotwaa Yuda asu fii nʼasase so.
english:
There at Riblah, in the land of Hamath, the king had them executed.
So Judah went into captivity, away from her land.

twi: Nnipa dodow a Nebukadnessar de wɔn kɔɔ nkoasom mu ni:nʼahenni afe a ɛto so ason mu,Yudafo ,;
english:
This is the number of the people Nebuchadnezzar carried into exile:
in the seventh year, 3,023 Jews;

twi: Nebukadnessar ahenni afe a ɛto so dunwɔtwe mu,nnipa a wofi Yerusalem, ;
english:
in Nebuchadnezzar’s eighteenth year,
832 people from Jerusalem;

twi: nʼahenni afe a ɛto so aduonu abiɛsa mu,ɔsahene Nebusaradan, a otua ɔhene awɛmfo ano no de Yudafo  kɔɔ nnommum mu.Nnipa no nyinaa dodow yɛ ,.
english:
in his twenty-third year,
745 Jews taken into exile by Nebuzaradan the commander of the imperial guard.
There were 4,600 people in all.

twi: Wogyaa YehoiakyinYudahene Yehoiakyin nnommumfa afe a ɛto so aduasa ason mu a Ewil-Merodak bɛyɛɛ Babiloniahene no, oyii Yudahene Yehoiakyin fii afiase wɔ ɔsram a ɛto so dumien no da a ɛto so aduonu anum.
english: In the thirty-seventh year of the exile of Jehoiachin king of Judah, in the year Awel-Marduk became king of Babylon, on the twenty-fifth day of the twelfth month, he released Jehoiachin king of Judah and freed him from prison.

twi: Ɔkaa abodwosɛm kyerɛɛ no, na ɔmaa no dibea a ɛwɔ anuonyam sen ahemfo a wɔne no wɔ Babilonia no de.
english: He spoke kindly to him and gave him a seat of honor higher than those of the other kings who were with him in Babylon.

twi: Enti Yehoiakin yii nʼafiase ntade guu nkyɛn, na efi saa da no odidii wɔ ɔhene didipon so bere biara, kosii ne wuda.
english: So Jehoiachin put aside his prison clothes and for the rest of his life ate regularly at the king’s table.

twi: Na Babiloniahene no san maa Yehoiakin sika bere ano bere ano, ma ɔde tuatua ne ho aka, kosii ne wuda.
english: Day by day the king of Babylon gave Jehoiachin a regular allowance as long as he lived, till the day of his death.

twi: Ɔbarima bi tenaa ase wɔ Us asase so a na ne din de Hiob. Na ne ho nni asɛm na ɔyɛ pɛ; na osuro Onyankopɔn, na ɔtwe ne ho fi bɔne ho.
english: In the land of Uz there lived a man whose name was Job. This man was blameless and upright; he feared God and shunned evil.

twi: Na ɔwɔ mmabarima baason ne mmabea baasa,
english: He had seven sons and three daughters,

twi: na ɔwɔ nguan mpem ason, yoma mpem abiɛsa, anantwi mpamho ahannum ne mfurumbere ahannum, na ɔwɔ asomfo bebree. Na ɔyɛ onipa kɛse pa ara wɔ nnipa a wɔwɔ Apuei fam nyinaa no mu.
english: and he owned seven thousand sheep, three thousand camels, five hundred yoke of oxen and five hundred donkeys, and had a large number of servants. He was the greatest man among all the people of the East.

twi: Na ne mmabarima no to pon nnidiso nnidiso wɔ wɔn afi mu, na wɔto nsa frɛ wɔn nuabeanom baasa no ne wɔn bɔ mu didi, nom.
english: His sons used to hold feasts in their homes on their birthdays, and they would invite their three sisters to eat and drink with them.

twi: Sɛ aponto nna no twa mu a, Hiob soma kɔfrɛ wɔn na wodwira wɔn ho. Ɔsɔre anɔpahema bɔ ɔhyew afɔre ma wɔn mu biara, efisɛ na osusuw sɛ, “Ebia na me mma no ayɛ bɔne na wɔadome Onyankopɔn wɔ wɔn koma mu.” Eyi yɛ dwuma a na Hiob di no bere ano bere ano.
english: When a period of feasting had run its course, Job would make arrangements for them to be purified. Early in the morning he would sacrifice a burnt offering for each of them, thinking, “Perhaps my children have sinned and cursed God in their hearts.” This was Job’s regular custom.

twi: Hiob Sɔhwɛ A Edi KanDa bi, abɔfo no de wɔn ho bɛkyerɛɛ Awurade, na Satan kaa wɔn ho bae.
english: One day the angels came to present themselves before the Lord, and Satan also came with them.

twi: Awurade bisaa Satan se, “Wufi he na wobaa ha?”Satan buaa Awurade se, “Mifi asase so akyinkyinakyinkyin ne emu akɔneabadi mu.”
english:
The Lord said to Satan, “Where have you come from?”
Satan answered the Lord, “From roaming throughout the earth, going back and forth on it.”

twi: Na Awurade bisaa Satan se, “Woadwene me somfo Hiob ho ana? Obiara nte sɛ ɔno wɔ asase so, ne ho nni asɛm na ɔteɛ, ɔyɛ onipa a osuro Onyankopɔn na okyi bɔne.”
english: Then the Lord said to Satan, “Have you considered my servant Job? There is no one on earth like him; he is blameless and upright, a man who fears God and shuns evil.”

twi: Satan buaa Awurade se, “Hiob suro Onyankopɔn kwa ana?
english: “Does Job fear God for nothing?” Satan replied.

twi: Wunnyee ban mfaa ɔno, ne fie ne biribiara a ɔwɔ ho ana? Woahyira ne nsa ano adwuma so, enti ne nguan ne nʼanantwi ase atrɛw asase no so.
english: “Have you not put a hedge around him and his household and everything he has? You have blessed the work of his hands, so that his flocks and herds are spread throughout the land.

twi: Na wo de, teɛ wo nsa na sɛe nea ɔwɔ nyinaa, na obegyina wʼanim na wadome wo.”
english: But now stretch out your hand and strike everything he has, and he will surely curse you to your face.”

twi: Awurade ka kyerɛɛ Satan se, “Eye, nea ɔwɔ nyinaa wɔ wo nsam, nanso ɔno ankasa de, mfa wo nsateaa nka no.”Na Satan fii Awurade anim kɔe.
english:
The Lord said to Satan, “Very well, then, everything he has is in your power, but on the man himself do not lay a finger.”
Then Satan went out from the presence of the Lord.

twi: Da bi a Hiob mmabarima ne ne mmabea redidi na wɔrenom bobesa wɔ wɔn nuabarima panyin fi no,
english: One day when Job’s sons and daughters were feasting and drinking wine at the oldest brother’s house,

twi: ɔbɔfo bi baa Hiob hɔ bɛkae se, “Anantwi no refuntum na mfurum no redidi wɔ wɔn nkyɛn no,
english: a messenger came to Job and said, “The oxen were plowing and the donkeys were grazing nearby,

twi: Sabiafo bɛtow hyɛɛ yɛn so, sesaw wɔn kɔe. Wɔde afoa kunkum apaafo no, na me nko ara na miguanee a merebɛbɔ wo saa amanneɛ yi.”
english: and the Sabeans attacked and made off with them. They put the servants to the sword, and I am the only one who has escaped to tell you!”

twi: Bere a ogu so rekasa no, ɔbɔfo foforo bi ba bɛkae se, “Onyankopɔn gya fi soro abɛhyew wo nguan ne wo nguanhwɛfo no nyinaa, na me nko ara na miguanee a merebɛbɔ wo amanneɛ yi.”
english: While he was still speaking, another messenger came and said, “The fire of God fell from the heavens and burned up the sheep and the servants, and I am the only one who has escaped to tell you!”

twi: Ogu so rekasa no, ɔbɔfo foforo bi bɛkae se, “Kaldeafo de akorɔmfo akuw abiɛsa baa wo yoma so bɛsoaa wɔn kɔe. Wɔde afoa kunkum asomfo no na me nko ara na miguanee a merebɛbɔ wo amanneɛ yi.”
english: While he was still speaking, another messenger came and said, “The Chaldeans formed three raiding parties and swept down on your camels and made off with them. They put the servants to the sword, and I am the only one who has escaped to tell you!”

twi: Bere a ogu so rekasa no, ɔbɔfo foforo bi ba bɛkae se, “Na wo mmabarima ne wo mmabea redidi na wɔrenom bobesa wɔ wɔn nuabarima panyin fi,
english: While he was still speaking, yet another messenger came and said, “Your sons and daughters were feasting and drinking wine at the oldest brother’s house,

twi: na prɛko pɛ, ahum bi bɔ fii sare no so bedwiraa ofi no ntwea anan no. Ofi no dwiriw guu wɔn so na akunkum wɔn, na me nko ara na miguanee a merebɛbɔ wo amanneɛ yi.”
english: when suddenly a mighty wind swept in from the desert and struck the four corners of the house. It collapsed on them and they are dead, and I am the only one who has escaped to tell you!”

twi: Eyi maa Hiob sɔre gyinaa hɔ, sunsuan nʼatade mu na oyii ne tinwi. Afei ɔtenaa fam sɔree Awurade
english: At this, Job got up and tore his robe and shaved his head. Then he fell to the ground in worship

twi: kae se,“Adagyaw na mede fi me na yam bae,na adagyaw na mede bɛsan akɔ.Awurade de mae, na Awurade afa;nhyira nka Awurade din!”
english:
and said:
“Naked I came from my mother’s womb,
    and naked I will depart.
The Lord gave and the Lord has taken away;
    may the name of the Lord be praised.”

twi: Eyi nyinaa mu no, Hiob anyɛ bɔne sɛ ɔbɛbɔ Onyankopɔn sobo.
english: In all this, Job did not sin by charging God with wrongdoing.

twi: Hiob Sɔhwɛ A Ɛto So AbienDa foforo bi, abɔfo no baa Awurade anim bio na Satan nso kaa wɔn ho bae.
english: On another day the angels came to present themselves before the Lord, and Satan also came with them to present himself before him.

twi: Awurade bisaa Satan se, “Wufi he na wobaa ha?”Satan buaa Awurade se, “Mifi asase so akyinkyinakyinkyin ne emu akɔneabadi mu.”
english:
And the Lord said to Satan, “Where have you come from?”
Satan answered the Lord, “From roaming throughout the earth, going back and forth on it.”

twi: Na Awurade bisaa Satan se, “Woadwene mʼakoa Hiob ho ana? Obiara nte sɛ ɔno wɔ asase so, ne ho nni asɛm na ɔteɛ. Ɔyɛ onipa a osuro Onyankopɔn na okyi bɔne. Ɛwɔ mu sɛ wohyɛɛ me sɛ mensɛe no a minni nnyinaso biara de, nanso ɔda so gyina ne pɛpɛyɛ no mu.”
english: Then the Lord said to Satan, “Have you considered my servant Job? There is no one on earth like him; he is blameless and upright, a man who fears God and shuns evil. And he still maintains his integrity, though you incited me against him to ruin him without any reason.”

twi: Satan buaa Awurade sɛ, “Were pere were. Onipa de nea ɔwɔ nyinaa bɛma de apere ne nkwa.
english: “Skin for skin!” Satan replied. “A man will give all he has for his own life.

twi: Sɛ ebetumi a teɛ wo nsa fa ka ne honam ne ne nnompe, na ɔbɛdome wo wɔ wʼanim!”
english: But now stretch out your hand and strike his flesh and bones, and he will surely curse you to your face.”

twi: Awurade ka kyerɛɛ Satan se, “Eye, ɔwɔ wo nsam na ne nkwa de gyaa mu ma no.”
english: The Lord said to Satan, “Very well, then, he is in your hands; but you must spare his life.”

twi: Enti Satan fii Awurade anim, na ɔmaa akuru a ɛyɛ yaw totɔɔ Hiob ho fi ne nʼanan ase kosii nʼapampam.
english: So Satan went out from the presence of the Lord and afflicted Job with painful sores from the soles of his feet to the crown of his head.

twi: Afei, na kyɛmfɛre na Hiob de twiw ne ho, bere a ɔte nsõ mu.
english: Then Job took a piece of broken pottery and scraped himself with it as he sat among the ashes.

twi: Ne yere bisaa no se, “Woda so kura wo pɛpɛyɛ no mu ara? Dome Onyankopɔn, na wu!”
english: His wife said to him, “Are you still maintaining your integrity? Curse God and die!”

twi: Na Hiob buaa no sɛ, “Wokasa sɛ ɔbea a ɔyɛ ɔkwasea. Ade pa de yɛagye afi Onyankopɔn nsam na ade bɔne na yɛmpo ana?”Eyi nyinaa mu no, Hiob anka asɛm bɔne.
english:
He replied, “You are talking like a foolish woman. Shall we accept good from God, and not trouble?”
In all this, Job did not sin in what he said.

twi: Hiob Nnamfo Baasa NoBere a Hiob nnamfo baasa bi a wɔne Temanni Elifas, Suhini Bildad ne Naamani Sofar tee amanehunu a aba Hiob so no, wofii wɔn afi mu, hyia yɛɛ adwene sɛ wɔbɛkɔ akɔhwɛ no na wɔakyekye ne werɛ.
english: When Job’s three friends, Eliphaz the Temanite, Bildad the Shuhite and Zophar the Naamathite, heard about all the troubles that had come upon him, they set out from their homes and met together by agreement to go and sympathize with him and comfort him.

twi: Wohuu Hiob fii akyiri no, wɔanhu sɛ ɛyɛ ɔno; wɔhyɛɛ ase twaa agyaadwo, sunsuan wɔn ntade mu, tuu mfutuma guu wɔn ti so.
english: When they saw him from a distance, they could hardly recognize him; they began to weep aloud, and they tore their robes and sprinkled dust on their heads.

twi: Na wɔne no tenaa fam nnanson, awia ne anadwo. Na obiara ankasa, efisɛ wohuu sɛ nʼamanehunu no nyɛ adewa.
english: Then they sat on the ground with him for seven days and seven nights. No one said a word to him, because they saw how great his suffering was.

twi: Hiob KasaAkyiri no Hiob kasae, na ɔdomee da a wɔwoo no.
english: After this, Job opened his mouth and cursed the day of his birth.

twi: Ɔkae se,
english: He said:

twi: “Ma da a wɔwoo me no nyera,ne anadwo a wɔkae se, ‘Wɔawo ɔbabarima no!’
english:
“May the day of my birth perish,
    and the night that said, ‘A boy is conceived!’

twi: Saa da no nnuru sum;mma Ɔsoro Nyankopɔn nhwehwɛ akyi kwan;mma hann biara ntɔ ngu so.
Ma sum ne owusum nnye no mfa;ma omununkum nkata so;na sum mmunkam ne hann so.
Ma sum kabii nnye saa anadwo no mfa;ma wonyi saa anadwo no mfi asranna sona wɔmmfa nhyɛ ɔsram biara mu.
Saa anadwo no nyɛ obonin;mma wɔnnte anigye nteɛmu wɔ mu.
english:
May that night be barren;
    may no shout of joy be heard in it.

twi: Ma wɔn a wɔdome nna no nnome saa da no;wɔn a wɔayɛ krado sɛ wɔbɛkanyan dɛnkyɛmmirampɔn no.
english:
May those who curse days curse that day,
    those who are ready to rouse Leviathan.

twi: Ma nʼanɔpa nsoromma nnuru sum;na ɔntwɛn adekyee kwaa onhu anɔpawia nsensanee a edi kan no,
efisɛ anto nea ɔwoo me no awotwaa mu ama wawo mena anka mʼani renhu saa abɛbrɛsɛ yi.
english:
for it did not shut the doors of the womb on me
    to hide trouble from my eyes.

twi: “Adɛn nti na manwu awoe hɔ,bere a mifi me na awotwaa mu no?
english:
“Why did I not perish at birth,
    and die as I came from the womb?

twi: Adɛn nti na nkotodwe gyee mene nufu sɛ minnum?
english:
Why were there knees to receive me
    and breasts that I might be nursed?

twi: Anka sesɛɛ meda hɔ asomdwoe mu;anka mada regye mʼahome
english:
For now I would be lying down in peace;
    I would be asleep and at rest

twi: me ne wiase ahemfo ne fotufo,wɔn a wosisii adan maa wɔn ho na nnɛ yi abubu no,
english:
with kings and rulers of the earth,
    who built for themselves places now lying in ruins,

twi: me ne ahenemma a na wɔwɔ sika kɔkɔɔ,wɔn a wɔde dwetɛ hyɛɛ wɔn afi mu ma.
english:
with princes who had gold,
    who filled their houses with silver.

twi: Anaasɛ adɛn nti na wɔansie me sɛ ɔpɔnba,te sɛ akokoaa a wanhu adekyee hann da?
english:
Or why was I not hidden away in the ground like a stillborn child,
    like an infant who never saw the light of day?

twi: Ɛhɔ na amumɔyɛfo gyae basabasayɛ,na abrɛfo nya ahomegye.
english:
There the wicked cease from turmoil,
    and there the weary are at rest.

twi: Nneduafo nso nya wɔn ahofadi;na wɔnte nnommumfo wuranom ateɛteɛ bio.
english:
Captives also enjoy their ease;
    they no longer hear the slave driver’s shout.

twi: Nketewa ne akɛse wɔ hɔ,na akoa de ne ho fi ne wura nsam.
english:
The small and the great are there,
    and the slaves are freed from their owners.

twi: “Adɛn nti na wɔma mmɔborɔfo hann,na ɔkra mu ahohiahiafo nya nkwa,
english:
“Why is light given to those in misery,
    and life to the bitter of soul,

twi: wɔn a wɔn kɔn dɔ owu nanso ɛmma,wɔn a wɔbrɛ hwehwɛ owu sen sɛnea wɔhwehwɛ nnwetɛbona,
english:
to those who long for death that does not come,
    who search for it more than for hidden treasure,

twi: wɔn a anigye ahyɛ wɔn mana wodu ɔda mu a wodi ahurusi.
english:
who are filled with gladness
    and rejoice when they reach the grave?

twi: Adɛn nti na wɔde nkwa ma onipa ane kwan ahintaw,nea Onyankopɔn aka no ahyɛ mu?
english:
Why is life given to a man
    whose way is hidden,
    whom God has hedged in?

twi: Ahomekokogu adan mʼaduan;na mʼapinisi gu te sɛ nsu.
english:
For sighing has become my daily food;
    my groans pour out like water.

twi: Nea na misuro no aba me so;nea na ɛbɔ me hu no ato me.
english:
What I feared has come upon me;
    what I dreaded has happened to me.

twi: Minni ahotɔ, minni asomdwoe;minni ahomegye na mmom, ɔhaw nko ara.”
english:
I have no peace, no quietness;
    I have no rest, but only turmoil.”

twi: Elifas Mmuae A Edi KanNa Temanni Elifas buaa Hiob se,
english: Then Eliphaz the Temanite replied:

twi: “Sɛ obi pɛ sɛ ɔne wo kasa a, worennya ntoboase ana?Hena na wobetumi aka nʼano ato mu?
english:
“If someone ventures a word with you, will you be impatient?
    But who can keep from speaking?

twi: Dwene sɛnea wakyerɛkyerɛ nnipa bebree,sɛnea woahyɛ nsa a emu ayɛ mmerɛw no den.
english:
Think how you have instructed many,
    how you have strengthened feeble hands.

twi: Wo nsɛm ahyɛ wɔn a wɔahintiw no den;woahyɛ nkotodwe a ayɛ mmerɛw mu den.
english:
Your words have supported those who stumbled;
    you have strengthened faltering knees.

twi: Na afei a ɔhaw aba no, wʼaba mu abu;adwira wo, na wo werɛ ahow.
english:
But now trouble comes to you, and you are discouraged;
    it strikes you, and you are dismayed.

twi: So ɛnsɛ sɛ wo nyamesuro yɛ wʼahotosona wʼakwan a ɛho nni asɛm no yɛ wʼanidaso ana?
english:
Should not your piety be your confidence
    and your blameless ways your hope?

twi: “Dwene ho: Wɔasɛe obi a ne ho nni asɛm pɛn ana?Ɛhefa na wɔsɛee obi a ɔyɛ pɛ?
english:
“Consider now: Who, being innocent, has ever perished?
    Where were the upright ever destroyed?

twi: Sɛnea mahu no, wɔn a wofuntum bɔnene wɔn a wodua ɔhaw no twa so aba.
english:
As I have observed, those who plow evil
    and those who sow trouble reap it.

twi: Onyankopɔn home ano, wɔsɛe;nʼabufuw turuw a wɔyera.
english:
At the breath of God they perish;
    at the blast of his anger they are no more.

twi: Gyata betumi abobɔ mu na wɔaworo so,nanso wɔabubu gyata akɛse no se.
english:
The lions may roar and growl,
    yet the teeth of the great lions are broken.

twi: Gyata annya hanam a owu,na gyatabere mma no bɔ hwete.
english:
The lion perishes for lack of prey,
    and the cubs of the lioness are scattered.

twi: “Wɔbɛkaa kokoamsɛm bi kyerɛɛ mena mʼaso tee no sɛ asomsɛm.
english:
“A word was secretly brought to me,
    my ears caught a whisper of it.

twi: Wɔ anadwo daeso basabasa mu,bere a nnipa adeda nnahɔɔ no,
english:
Amid disquieting dreams in the night,
    when deep sleep falls on people,

twi: ehu ne nketenkete kyeree meɛmaa me nnompe nyinaa wosowee.
english:
fear and trembling seized me
    and made all my bones shake.

twi: Honhom bi twaa mʼani so,na me ho nwi sɔre gyinae.
english:
A spirit glided past my face,
    and the hair on my body stood on end.

twi: Egyinae,nanso, manhu nʼabɔsu.Biribi begyinaa mʼanim,na metee nne bɔkɔɔ bi a ɛrebisa se,
english:
It stopped,
    but I could not tell what it was.
A form stood before my eyes,
    and I heard a hushed voice:

twi: ‘Onipa desani betumi ateɛ asen Onyankopɔn?Na mpo ɔhoɔdenfo betumi ayɛ kronkron asen ne Yɛfo ana?
english:
‘Can a mortal be more righteous than God?
    Can even a strong man be more pure than his Maker?

twi: Sɛ Onyankopɔn ntumi mfa ne ho nto nʼankasa asomfo so,sɛ ɔka nʼabɔfo mfomso kyerɛ wɔn a,
english:
If God places no trust in his servants,
    if he charges his angels with error,

twi: na nkantom wɔn a wɔtete dɔte afi mu,wɔn a wɔn fapem sisi mfutuma muna wɔdwerɛw wɔn ntɛm so sen abubummaba!
english:
how much more those who live in houses of clay,
    whose foundations are in the dust,
    who are crushed more readily than a moth!

twi: Efi anɔpahema kosi anwummere wobubu wɔn mu nketenkete;na wɔyera korakora a obiara nhu wɔn bio.
english:
Between dawn and dusk they are broken to pieces;
    unnoticed, they perish forever.

twi: So wommiamia wɔn ntamadan ahama mu,a ɛno nti wowuwu a wonni nyansa ana?’
english:
Are not the cords of their tent pulled up,
    so that they die without wisdom?’

twi: “Wobɛfrɛ a frɛ, na hena na obegye wo so?Akronkronfo no mu hena nkyɛn na wobɛkɔ?
english:
“Call if you will, but who will answer you?
    To which of the holy ones will you turn?

twi: Ahisɛm kum ɔkwasea,na anibere kum atetekwaa.
english:
Resentment kills a fool,
    and envy slays the simple.

twi: Mʼankasa mahu ɔkwasea a ɔrefefɛw,nanso mpofirim, wɔdomee ne fi.
english:
I myself have seen a fool taking root,
    but suddenly his house was cursed.

twi: Ne mma ne bammɔ ntam kwan ware,wɔdwerɛw wɔn wɔ asennii a wonni ɔkamafo.
english:
His children are far from safety,
    crushed in court without a defender.

twi: Nea ɔkɔm de no no di ne nnɔbae,na ɔfa fi nsɔe mu mpo,na nea osukɔm de no no pere di nʼahode akyi.
english:
The hungry consume his harvest,
    taking it even from among thorns,
    and the thirsty pant after his wealth.

twi: Ahokyere mpue mmfi dɔte muna ɔhaw nso mfifi mmfi fam.
english:
For hardship does not spring from the soil,
    nor does trouble sprout from the ground.

twi: Nanso wɔwo nnipa to ɔhaw mumpɛn dodow a gyaframa turuw kɔ soro no.
english:
Yet man is born to trouble
    as surely as sparks fly upward.

twi: “Nanso sɛ ɛyɛ me a, anka meguan atoa Onyankopɔn;na mede mʼasɛm ato nʼanim.
english:
“But if I were you, I would appeal to God;
    I would lay my cause before him.

twi: Ɔyɛ anwonwade a wontumi nhwehwɛ mu,ne nsɛnkyerɛnne a wontumi nkan ne dodow.
english:
He performs wonders that cannot be fathomed,
    miracles that cannot be counted.

twi: Ɔtɔ osu gu asase so;na ɔde kɔ wuram.
english:
He provides rain for the earth;
    he sends water on the countryside.

twi: Ɔde ahobrɛasefo si nea ɛkorɔn,na ɔma wɔn a wodi awerɛhow nya asomdwoe.
english:
The lowly he sets on high,
    and those who mourn are lifted to safety.

twi: Ɔsɛe aniferefo nhyehyɛe,ma wɔn nsa si fam.
english:
He thwarts the plans of the crafty,
    so that their hands achieve no success.

twi: Ɔkyere anyansafo wɔ wɔn anifere mu,na ɔbɔ anitewfo nhyehyɛe gu.
english:
He catches the wise in their craftiness,
    and the schemes of the wily are swept away.

twi: Sum duru wɔn awia ketee;na wɔkeka wɔ owigyinae mu te sɛ anadwo.
english:
Darkness comes upon them in the daytime;
    at noon they grope as in the night.

twi: Ogye ahiafo fi afoa a ɛhyɛ wɔn anom;ogye wɔn fi ahoɔdenfo nkyehama mu.
english:
He saves the needy from the sword in their mouth;
    he saves them from the clutches of the powerful.

twi: Enti ahiafo wɔ anidaso,na ntɛnkyew ka nʼano to mu.
english:
So the poor have hope,
    and injustice shuts its mouth.

twi: “Nhyira ne onipa a Onyankopɔn teɛ no,enti mmu Otumfo nteɛteɛ no animtiaa.
english:
“Blessed is the one whom God corrects;
    so do not despise the discipline of the Almighty.

twi: Efisɛ ɔno na opira na ɔno ara akyekyere;opira nanso ne nsa sa yare.
english:
For he wounds, but he also binds up;
    he injures, but his hands also heal.

twi: Obegye wo afi ɔhaw ahorow asia mu;ason so no, bɔne biara renka wo.
english:
From six calamities he will rescue you;
    in seven no harm will touch you.

twi: Ɔkɔm ba a, obegye wo afi owu mu,na ɔko mu nso, obegye wo afi afoa ano.
english:
In famine he will deliver you from death,
    and in battle from the stroke of the sword.

twi: Wɔbɛbɔ wo ho ban afi ntwirii hona sɛ ɔsɛe ba a ɛnsɛ sɛ wusuro.
english:
You will be protected from the lash of the tongue,
    and need not fear when destruction comes.

twi: Wobɛserew ɔsɛe ne ɔkɔm;na ɛnsɛ sɛ wusuro asase so mmoa.
english:
You will laugh at destruction and famine,
    and need not fear the wild animals.

twi: Wo ne afuw so abo bɛyɛ apam,na emu nkekaboa nso ne wo bɛtena asomdwoe mu.
english:
For you will have a covenant with the stones of the field,
    and the wild animals will be at peace with you.

twi: Wubehu sɛ wo ntamadan wɔ bammɔ;na sɛ wosese wʼahode a wubehu sɛ hwee nyeraa ɛ.
english:
You will know that your tent is secure;
    you will take stock of your property and find nothing missing.

twi: Wubehu sɛ wo mma bɛyɛ bebree;na wʼase bɛfɛe sɛ asase so sare.
english:
You will know that your children will be many,
    and your descendants like the grass of the earth.

twi: Wode ahoɔden bɛkɔ ɔda mu,te sɛ afiafi a wɔaboa ano wɔ otwabere mu.
english:
You will come to the grave in full vigor,
    like sheaves gathered in season.

twi: “Yɛahwehwɛ eyi mu, na ɛyɛ nokwareɛno nti tie na fa toto wʼabrabɔ ho.”
english:
“We have examined this, and it is true.
    So hear it and apply it to yourself.”

twi: Hiob Bua ElifasNa Hiob buae se,
english: Then Job replied:

twi: “Sɛ wobetumi akari mʼawerɛhowdina me haw nso wɔde agu nsania so a,
english:
“If only my anguish could be weighed
    and all my misery be placed on the scales!

twi: anka emu bɛyɛ duru asen nwea a ɛwɔ po mu nyinaa,enti ɛnyɛ nwonwa sɛ me nsɛm ayɛ hagyahagya.
english:
It would surely outweigh the sand of the seas—
    no wonder my words have been impetuous.

twi: Otumfo agyan no wɔ me mu,me honhom nom ano bɔre no;wɔahyehyɛ Onyankopɔn ahunahuna nyinaa atia me.
Wuram afurum su wɔ bere a wanya sare ana,na nantwi nso su wɔ bere a wanya nʼaduan ana?
english:
Does a wild donkey bray when it has grass,
    or an ox bellow when it has fodder?

twi: So wodi aduan a nkyene nni mu?Na ɔdɛ bi wɔ nkesua mu fufu mu ana?
english:
Is tasteless food eaten without salt,
    or is there flavor in the sap of the mallow?

twi: Mempɛ sɛ mede me nsa ka;aduan a ɛte saa no bɔ me yare.
english:
I refuse to touch it;
    such food makes me ill.

twi: “Ao sɛ me nsa bɛka mʼabisade,sɛ Onyankopɔn bɛyɛ nea mʼani da so no ama me,
english:
“Oh, that I might have my request,
    that God would grant what I hope for,

twi: sɛ Onyankopɔn bɛpɛ sɛ ɔdwerɛw mesɛ ɔbɛtwe ne nsa na wakum me,
english:
that God would be willing to crush me,
    to let loose his hand and cut off my life!

twi: ɛne anka mɛkɔ so anya saa awerɛkyekye yi,a ɛyɛ anigye a mewɔ wɔ ɔyaw a entwa da yi mu,ne Ɔkronkronni no nsɛm a mimmuu so yi.
english:
Then I would still have this consolation—
    my joy in unrelenting pain—
    that I had not denied the words of the Holy One.

twi: “Ahoɔden bɛn na mewɔ a enti ɛsɛ sɛ minya anidaso?Daakye nneɛma pa bɛn nti na ɛsɛ sɛ minya ntoboase?
english:
“What strength do I have, that I should still hope?
    What prospects, that I should be patient?

twi: Mewɔ ahoɔden sɛ ɔbo ana?Me honam yɛ kɔbere mfrafrae ana?
english:
Do I have the strength of stone?
    Is my flesh bronze?

twi: So mewɔ tumi bi a mede bɛboa me hosaa bere yi a nkonimdi apare me yi ana?
english:
Do I have any power to help myself,
    now that success has been driven from me?

twi: “Obiara a ɔbɔ nʼadamfo ayamye sɛn nogyaw Otumfo no ho suro.
english:
“Anyone who withholds kindness from a friend
    forsakes the fear of the Almighty.

twi: Nanso ahotoso nni me nuanom mu sɛ nsuwansuwa a eyiri na ɛyow,sɛ nsuwansuwa a eyiri
english:
But my brothers are as undependable as intermittent streams,
    as the streams that overflow

twi: bere a sukyerɛmma renanna mparuwbo nso redan nsu,
english:
when darkened by thawing ice
    and swollen with melting snow,

twi: nanso owiabere mu no ɛsen biona ɔhyew nti nsu no tu yera.
english:
but that stop flowing in the dry season,
    and in the heat vanish from their channels.

twi: Akwantufo man fi wɔn akwan so;wɔforo kɔ nsase a awuwu so ma wowuwu.
english:
Caravans turn aside from their routes;
    they go off into the wasteland and perish.

twi: Tema akwantufo hwehwɛ nsu,Seba aguadifo akwantufo de anidaso hwehwɛ nsu.
english:
The caravans of Tema look for water,
    the traveling merchants of Sheba look in hope.

twi: Wɔn ho yeraw wɔn, efisɛ na wɔwɔ awerehyɛmu;woduu hɔ, na wɔn anidaso yɛ ɔkwa.
english:
They are distressed, because they had been confident;
    they arrive there, only to be disappointed.

twi: Afei, wo nso woakyerɛ sɛ wo so nni mfaso;wuhu biribi a ɛyɛ hu na wusuro.
english:
Now you too have proved to be of no help;
    you see something dreadful and are afraid.

twi: So maka pɛn se, ‘Me nti momma biribi,sɛ mumfi mo ahode mu ntua me ti so sika,
english:
Have I ever said, ‘Give something on my behalf,
    pay a ransom for me from your wealth,

twi: sɛ munnye me mfi mʼatamfo nsam,ne atirimɔdenfo nkyehama mu ana?’
english:
deliver me from the hand of the enemy,
    rescue me from the clutches of the ruthless’?

twi: “Monkyerɛkyerɛ me, na mɛyɛ komm;monkyerɛ me mfomso a mayɛ.
english:
“Teach me, and I will be quiet;
    show me where I have been wrong.

twi: Nokwareka yɛ yaw,na mo adwenkyerɛ no kosi dɛn?
english:
How painful are honest words!
    But what do your arguments prove?

twi: So mokyerɛ sɛ mubesiesie sɛ nea meka no,na moafa mʼahometew nsɛm sɛ mframa ana?
english:
Do you mean to correct what I say,
    and treat my desperate words as wind?

twi: Mpo mobɛbɔ ayisaa so ntonto,na mode mo adamfo adi nsesagua.
english:
You would even cast lots for the fatherless
    and barter away your friend.

twi: “Afei momfa ahummɔbɔ nhwɛ me.Metumi adi atoro wɔ mo anim ana?
english:
“But now be so kind as to look at me.
    Would I lie to your face?

twi: Montɔ mo bo ase, mummu ntɛnkyew;monsan nnwen ho, efisɛ eyi fa me pɛpɛyɛ ho.
english:
Relent, do not be unjust;
    reconsider, for my integrity is at stake.

twi: Amumɔyɛsɛm wɔ mʼano ana?Minnim papa ne bɔne ntam nsonoe ana?
english:
Is there any wickedness on my lips?
    Can my mouth not discern malice?

twi: “Asase so som nyɛ den mma onipa ana?Ne nkwanna nte sɛ ɔpaani de?
english:
“Do not mortals have hard service on earth?
    Are not their days like those of hired laborers?

twi: Sɛnea akoa ani gyina anwummere sunsuma,anaasɛ ɔpaani ho pere no nʼakatua ho no,
english:
Like a slave longing for the evening shadows,
    or a hired laborer waiting to be paid,

twi: saa ara na wɔatwa asram hunu ato me hɔ,ne anadwo a ɔhaw wɔ mu ama me.
english:
so I have been allotted months of futility,
    and nights of misery have been assigned to me.

twi: Sɛ meda a, midwen bisa se, ‘Bere bɛn na ade bɛkye?’Nanso anadwo twa mu nkakrankakra, na mepere kosi ahemadakye.
english:
When I lie down I think, ‘How long before I get up?’
    The night drags on, and I toss and turn until dawn.

twi: Asunson ne aporɔporɔw afura me nipadua,me were atetew na ɛrefi nsu.
english:
My body is clothed with worms and scabs,
    my skin is broken and festering.

twi: “Me nna kɔ ntɛm sen ɔnwemfo akurokurowa,na ɛkɔ awiei a anidaso biara nni mu.
english:
“My days are swifter than a weaver’s shuttle,
    and they come to an end without hope.

twi: Ao, Onyankopɔn, kae sɛ me nkwanna te sɛ ɔhome;na mʼani renhu anigye bio da.
english:
Remember, O God, that my life is but a breath;
    my eyes will never see happiness again.

twi: Ani a ehu me mprempren no renhu me bio;mobɛhwehwɛ me, nanso na minni hɔ bio.
english:
The eye that now sees me will see me no longer;
    you will look for me, but I will be no more.

twi: Sɛnea omununkum yera na etu kɔ,saa ara na nea ɔkɔ ɔda mu no nsan mma bio.
english:
As a cloud vanishes and is gone,
    so one who goes down to the grave does not return.

twi: Ɔrensan mma ne fi da biara da bio;nʼatenae renkae no bio.
english:
He will never come to his house again;
    his place will know him no more.

twi: “Ɛno nti meremmua mʼano;mifi me honhom ahoyeraw mu akasa,mefi me kra ɔyaw mu anwiinwii.
So meyɛ ɛpo anaa aboa kɛse a ɔwɔ bun mu,na mode me ahyɛ ɔwɛmfo nsa yi?
english:
Am I the sea, or the monster of the deep,
    that you put me under guard?

twi: Sɛ midwen sɛ minya awerɛkyekye wɔ me mpa so,na mʼakongua adwudwo mʼanwiinwii ano a,
english:
When I think my bed will comfort me
    and my couch will ease my complaint,

twi: ɛno mpo na wode adaeso yi me huna wode anisoadehu hunahuna me,
english:
even then you frighten me with dreams
    and terrify me with visions,

twi: ɛno nti mepɛ ɔsɛn ne owu,sen me nipadua yi.
english:
so that I prefer strangling and death,
    rather than this body of mine.

twi: Mimmu me nkwa; mentena ase afebɔɔ.Munnyaa me; na me nna nka hwee.
english:
I despise my life; I would not live forever.
    Let me alone; my days have no meaning.

twi: “Ɔdesani ne hena a ne ho hia wo sɛɛ,na wʼani ku ne ho,
english:
“What is mankind that you make so much of them,
    that you give them so much attention,

twi: na wohwehwɛ ne mu anɔpa biarana wosɔ no hwɛ bere biara?
english:
that you examine them every morning
    and test them every moment?

twi: Worennyi wʼani mfi me so da,anaasɛ worennyaa me bere tiaa bi mpo ana?
english:
Will you never look away from me,
    or let me alone even for an instant?

twi: Sɛ mayɛ bɔne a, dɛn na mayɛ wo,Ao adesamma so wɛmfo?Adɛn nti na watu wʼani asi me so?Mayɛ adesoa ama wo ana?
english:
If I have sinned, what have I done to you,
    you who see everything we do?
Why have you made me your target?
    Have I become a burden to you?

twi: Adɛn nti na wonkata me mmarato sona womfa me bɔne nkyɛ me?Ɛrenkyɛ biara, mɛda mfutuma mu.Wobɛhwehwɛ me nanso na minni hɔ bio.”
english:
Why do you not pardon my offenses
    and forgive my sins?
For I will soon lie down in the dust;
    you will search for me, but I will be no more.”

twi: Bildad Asɛnka A Edi KanNa Suhini Bildad buae se:
english: Then Bildad the Shuhite replied:

twi: “Wobɛkɔ so aka saa nsɛm yi akosi da bɛn?Wo nsɛm yɛ mframa huhuw.
english:
“How long will you say such things?
    Your words are a blustering wind.

twi: Onyankopɔn kyea atɛntrenee ana?Otumfo kyea nea ɛteɛ ana?
english:
Does God pervert justice?
    Does the Almighty pervert what is right?

twi: Bere a wo mma yɛɛ bɔne tiaa no no,ogyaw wɔn maa wɔn bɔne so akatua.
english:
When your children sinned against him,
    he gave them over to the penalty of their sin.

twi: Nanso sɛ wode wʼani bɛto Onyankopɔn sona woabɔ Otumfo no mpae,
english:
But if you will seek God earnestly
    and plead with the Almighty,

twi: sɛ woyɛ kronkron, na woteɛ a,wo nti, ɔbɛma ne ho so mpremprenna wama wo asi wo dedaw mu.
Wo mfiase bɛyɛ nkakrankakrana daakye woanya ama abu so.
english:
Your beginnings will seem humble,
    so prosperous will your future be.

twi: “Bisa awo ntoatoaso a atwa mu no,na hwehwɛ nea wɔn agyanom hui,
english:
“Ask the former generation
    and find out what their ancestors learned,

twi: na wɔwoo yɛn nkyɛe na yennim hwee,yɛn nna wɔ asase yi so te sɛ sunsuma.
english:
for we were born only yesterday and know nothing,
    and our days on earth are but a shadow.

twi: Wɔrenkyerɛkyerɛ wo na wɔrenka nkyerɛ wo ana?Wɔremfi wɔn ntease mu nka nsɛm bi ana?
english:
Will they not instruct you and tell you?
    Will they not bring forth words from their understanding?

twi: So paparɔso betumi anyin akɔ soro wɔ baabi a ɛnyɛ ɔwora?Demmire betumi afifi baabi a nsu nni ana?
english:
Can papyrus grow tall where there is no marsh?
    Can reeds thrive without water?

twi: Bere a ɛrenyin a wontwae no,ɛhyew ntɛm so sen sare.
english:
While still growing and uncut,
    they wither more quickly than grass.

twi: Saa na wɔn a wɔn werɛ fi Onyankopɔn no awiei te;saa ara na wɔn a wonni nyamesu no anidaso nkosi hwee.
english:
Such is the destiny of all who forget God;
    so perishes the hope of the godless.

twi: Biribiara a nʼani da so no nni ahoɔden;nea ɔde ne ho to so no yɛ ananse ntontan.
english:
What they trust in is fragile;
    what they rely on is a spider’s web.

twi: Otweri ne ntontan, nanso ɛtetew;oso mu dennen, nanso ɛnyɛ yie.
english:
They lean on the web, but it gives way;
    they cling to it, but it does not hold.

twi: Ɔte sɛ afifide a wogugu so nsu yiye a esi owia mu,ɛtrɛtrɛw ne mman mu wɔ turo no so;
english:
They are like a well-watered plant in the sunshine,
    spreading its shoots over the garden;

twi: Ne ntin nyin fa abotan ho,na ɛhwehwɛ ɔkwan kɔ abo mu.
english:
it entwines its roots around a pile of rocks
    and looks for a place among the stones.

twi: Nanso sɛ wotu fi ne sibea a,saa beae no nnim no bio na ɛka se, ‘Minhuu wo da.’
english:
But when it is torn from its spot,
    that place disowns it and says, ‘I never saw you.’

twi: Ampa ara ne nkwa twa mu,na afifide foforo nyin asase no so.
english:
Surely its life withers away,
    and from the soil other plants grow.

twi: “Ampa ara Onyankopɔn mpo onipa a ne ho nni asɛmna ɔnhyɛ amumɔyɛfo nsa mu den.
english:
“Surely God does not reject one who is blameless
    or strengthen the hands of evildoers.

twi: Ɔbɛma woaserew bio,na wode ahosɛpɛw ateɛteɛ mu.
english:
He will yet fill your mouth with laughter
    and your lips with shouts of joy.

twi: Wɔde aniwu befura wɔn a wɔtan wo,na amumɔyɛfo ntamadan bɛsɛe.”
english:
Your enemies will be clothed in shame,
    and the tents of the wicked will be no more.”

twi: Hiob Bua BildadNa Hiob kasaa bio se:
english: Then Job replied:

twi: “Yiw, minim sɛ eyi yɛ nokware.Na ɛbɛyɛ dɛn na ɔdesani bɛteɛ wɔ Onyankopɔn anim?
english:
“Indeed, I know that this is true.
    But how can mere mortals prove their innocence before God?

twi: Sɛ obi pɛ sɛ ɔne Onyankopɔn yiyi ano a,ɔrentumi nyi nsɛm apem mu baako mpo ano.
english:
Though they wished to dispute with him,
    they could not answer him one time out of a thousand.

twi: Ne nyansa mu dɔ, na ne tumi so.Hena na ɔne no adi asi na ne ho baabiara anti?
english:
His wisdom is profound, his power is vast.
    Who has resisted him and come out unscathed?

twi: Otutu mmepɔw a wonnim ho hweeobubu wɔn fa so wɔ nʼabufuw mu.
english:
He moves mountains without their knowing it
    and overturns them in his anger.

twi: Ɔwosow asase fi ne sibea,na ɔma ne nnyinaso wosow biribiri.
english:
He shakes the earth from its place
    and makes its pillars tremble.

twi: Ɔkasa kyerɛ owia na ɛnhyerɛn,na ɔsɔw nsoromma hyerɛn ano.
english:
He speaks to the sun and it does not shine;
    he seals off the light of the stars.

twi: Ɔno nko ara na ɔtrɛw ɔsoro mu,na ɔnantew po asorɔkye so.
english:
He alone stretches out the heavens
    and treads on the waves of the sea.

twi: Ɔno ne Nyankrɛnte, Akokɔbeatan ne ne mma Yɛfo;anafo fam nsorommakuw no.
english:
He is the Maker of the Bear and Orion,
    the Pleiades and the constellations of the south.

twi: Ɔyɛ anwonwade a wontumi nte ase,nsɛnkyerɛnne a wontumi nkan.
english:
He performs wonders that cannot be fathomed,
    miracles that cannot be counted.

twi: Sɛ ɔnam me ho a, minhu no;sɛ ɔsen a, minhu no.
english:
When he passes me, I cannot see him;
    when he goes by, I cannot perceive him.

twi: Sɛ ohwim kɔ a, hena na osiw no kwan?Hena na obetumi abisa no se, ‘Dɛn na woreyɛ yi?’
english:
If he snatches away, who can stop him?
    Who can say to him, ‘What are you doing?’

twi: Onyankopɔn nkora nʼabufuw so;Rahab aboafo mpo ho popo wɔ nʼanim.
english:
God does not restrain his anger;
    even the cohorts of Rahab cowered at his feet.

twi: “Na me ne hena a mene no beyiyi ano?Mɛyɛ dɛn anya nsɛm a me ne no de begye akyinnye?
english:
“How then can I dispute with him?
    How can I find words to argue with him?

twi: Sɛ minnim ho hwee mpo a, merentumi nyi nʼano;ɛno ara ne sɛ mɛsrɛ ahummɔbɔ afi me temmufo nkyɛn.
english:
Though I were innocent, I could not answer him;
    I could only plead with my Judge for mercy.

twi: Mpo, sɛ mefrɛ no na ɔba a,minnye nni sɛ obetie mʼasɛm.
english:
Even if I summoned him and he responded,
    I do not believe he would give me a hearing.

twi: Ɔde asorɔkye bɛhwe meama mʼapirakuru adɔɔso kwa.
english:
He would crush me with a storm
    and multiply my wounds for no reason.

twi: Ɔremma minnya mʼahome, bio,ɔde awerɛhow bɛhyɛ me ma tɔ.
english:
He would not let me catch my breath
    but would overwhelm me with misery.

twi: Sɛ ɛyɛ ahoɔden asɛm a, ɔyɛ ɔhoɔdenfo!Na sɛ ɛba atɛntrenee nso a, hena na ɔne no bedi asi?
english:
If it is a matter of strength, he is mighty!
    And if it is a matter of justice, who can challenge him?

twi: Sɛ midi bem mpo a, mʼano bebu me kumfɔ;sɛ me ho nni asɛm a, ebebu me fɔ.
english:
Even if I were innocent, my mouth would condemn me;
    if I were blameless, it would pronounce me guilty.

twi: “Ɛwɔ mu sɛ midi bem de,nanso mimmu me ho;abrabɔ afono me.
Ne nyinaa yɛ pɛ; ɛno nti na meka se,‘Ɔsɛe nea ne ho nni asɛm ne omumɔyɛfo.’
english:
It is all the same; that is why I say,
    ‘He destroys both the blameless and the wicked.’

twi: Bere a amanehunu de owu aba no,ɔserew nea ne ho nni asɛm no abawpa.
english:
When a scourge brings sudden death,
    he mocks the despair of the innocent.

twi: Bere a asase akɔ amumɔyɛfo nsam no,ofura ɛso atemmufo ani.Sɛ ɛnyɛ ɔno a, na ɛyɛ hena?
english:
When a land falls into the hands of the wicked,
    he blindfolds its judges.
    If it is not he, then who is it?

twi: “Me nna ho yɛ hare sen ommirikatufo;ɛsen kɔ a anigye kakra mpo nni mu.
english:
“My days are swifter than a runner;
    they fly away without a glimpse of joy.

twi: Etwa mu kɔ sɛ akorow a wɔde paparɔso ayɛte sɛ akɔre a wɔretow akyere wɔn hanam.
english:
They skim past like boats of papyrus,
    like eagles swooping down on their prey.

twi: Sɛ meka se, ‘Me werɛ mfi mʼanwiinwii,mɛsakra me nsɛnka, na maserew a,’
english:
If I say, ‘I will forget my complaint,
    I will change my expression, and smile,’

twi: me yaw ahorow no bɔ me hu ara.Na minim sɛ, woremmu me bem.
english:
I still dread all my sufferings,
    for I know you will not hold me innocent.

twi: Woabu me fɔ dedaw nti,adɛn na ɛsɛ sɛ mehaw me ho kwa?
english:
Since I am already found guilty,
    why should I struggle in vain?

twi: Mpo sɛ ɛba sɛ mede samina guarena mede samina hohoro me nsa ho a,
english:
Even if I washed myself with soap
    and my hands with cleansing powder,

twi: wobɛtow me akyene dontori amoa mu,ama mʼatade mpo akyi me.
english:
you would plunge me into a slime pit
    so that even my clothes would detest me.

twi: “Ɔnyɛ onipa te sɛ me na mayi nʼano,na yɛakogyina asennii abobɔ yɛn nkuro.
english:
“He is not a mere mortal like me that I might answer him,
    that we might confront each other in court.

twi: Sɛ anka obi wɔ hɔ a obesiesie yɛn ntamna waka yɛn baanu abɔ mu,
english:
If only there were someone to mediate between us,
    someone to bring us together,

twi: obi a obeyi Onyankopɔn abaa afi me so,na nʼahunahuna ammɔ me hu bio.
english:
someone to remove God’s rod from me,
    so that his terror would frighten me no more.

twi: Anka mɛkasa a merensuro no,nanso saa tebea a mewɔ mu yi de, mintumi.
english:
Then I would speak up without fear of him,
    but as it now stands with me, I cannot.

twi: “Abrabɔ afono me;enti mɛka mʼasɛm a meremfa hwee nsiena mɛkasa afi me kra yawdi mu.
Mɛka akyerɛ Onyankopɔn se: Mmu me kumfɔ,na mmom kyerɛ kwaadu a wobɔ me.
english:
I say to God: Do not declare me guilty,
    but tell me what charges you have against me.

twi: Ɛyɛ wo fɛ sɛ wohyɛ me so,de po wo nsa ano adwuma,na woserew hwɛ amumɔyɛfo nhyehyɛe?
english:
Does it please you to oppress me,
    to spurn the work of your hands,
    while you smile on the plans of the wicked?

twi: Wowɔ ɔhonam mu ani ana?Wuhu ade te sɛ ɔdesani ana?
english:
Do you have eyes of flesh?
    Do you see as a mortal sees?

twi: Wo nkwanna te sɛ ɔdesanianaa wo mfe te sɛ onipa hoɔdenfo,
english:
Are your days like those of a mortal
    or your years like those of a strong man,

twi: a enti ɛsɛ sɛ wohwehwɛ me mfomsona wopɛɛpɛɛ me bɔne mu?
english:
that you must search out my faults
    and probe after my sin—

twi: Ɛwɔ mu, wunim sɛ minni fɔ,na obiara nso ntumi nnye me mfi wo nsam.
english:
though you know that I am not guilty
    and that no one can rescue me from your hand?

twi: “Wo nsa na ɛnwenee me na ɛbɔɔ me.Afei wobɛdan wo ho asɛe me ana?
english:
“Your hands shaped me and made me.
    Will you now turn and destroy me?

twi: Kae sɛ wonwen me sɛ dɔte.Na wobɛdan me ayɛ me mfutuma bio ana?
english:
Remember that you molded me like clay.
    Will you now turn me to dust again?

twi: So woanhwie me sɛ nufusuna woammɔ me toa sɛ srade,
english:
Did you not pour me out like milk
    and curdle me like cheese,

twi: amfa were ne honam ankata me hoankeka nnompe ne ntin antoatoa mu ana?
english:
clothe me with skin and flesh
    and knit me together with bones and sinews?

twi: Womaa me nkwa, yii ayamye kyerɛɛ me,na ɔhwɛsie mu wohwɛɛ me honhom so.
english:
You gave me life and showed me kindness,
    and in your providence watched over my spirit.

twi: “Nanso eyi na wode siee wo koma mu,na minim sɛ na eyi wɔ wʼadwene mu.
english:
“But this is what you concealed in your heart,
    and I know that this was in your mind:

twi: Sɛ meyɛɛ bɔne a anka wobɛhwɛ mena wobɛma me so asotwe.
english:
If I sinned, you would be watching me
    and would not let my offense go unpunished.

twi: Na sɛ midi fɔ a, nnome nka me!Na sɛ mpo midi bem a, merentumi mma me ti so,efisɛ aniwu ahyɛ me mana mʼamanehunu amene me.
english:
If I am guilty—woe to me!
    Even if I am innocent, I cannot lift my head,
for I am full of shame
    and drowned in my affliction.

twi: Na sɛ mema me ti so a, wodɛɛdɛɛ me sɛ gyata,na bio woda wʼanwonwatumi no adi tia me.
english:
If I hold my head high, you stalk me like a lion
    and again display your awesome power against me.

twi: Wode nnansefo foforo betia mena woma wʼabufuw ano yɛ den wɔ me so;wʼasraafo tu ba me so bere biara.
“Adɛn nti na woma wɔwoo me?Ɛkaa me nko a anka miwui ansa na ani bi rehu me.
english:
“Why then did you bring me out of the womb?
    I wish I had died before any eye saw me.

twi: Sɛ anka mamma nkwa yi mu,anaasɛ wɔsoaa me fi awotwaa mu de me kɔɔ ɔda mu tee!
english:
If only I had never come into being,
    or had been carried straight from the womb to the grave!

twi: So ɛnkaa kakraa bi na me nna kakraa no to ntwaa ana?Gyaa me na minya anigye bere tiaa bi
english:
Are not my few days almost over?
    Turn away from me so I can have a moment’s joy

twi: ansa na makɔ koransankusuuyɛ ne sunsuma kabii asase so,
english:
before I go to the place of no return,
    to the land of gloom and utter darkness,

twi: asase a ɛyɛ anadwo sum kabii,sum kabii ne sakasaka,baabi a ɛhɔ hann mpo te sɛ sum.”
english:
to the land of deepest night,
    of utter darkness and disorder,
    where even the light is like darkness.”

twi: Sofar Mmuae A Edi KanNa Naamani Sofar buae se,
english: Then Zophar the Naamathite replied:

twi: “Ɛnsɛ sɛ woyi saa nsɛm yi ano ana?Ɛsɛ sɛ wobu saa ɔkasafo yi bem ana?
english:
“Are all these words to go unanswered?
    Is this talker to be vindicated?

twi: Wo nsɛm hunu no bɛma nnipa ayɛ komm ana?Sɛ wudi fɛw a obiara nka wʼanim ana?
english:
Will your idle talk reduce others to silence?
    Will no one rebuke you when you mock?

twi: Woka kyerɛ Onyankopɔn se, ‘Me gyidi ho nni asɛmna meyɛ pɛ wɔ wʼani so.’
english:
You say to God, ‘My beliefs are flawless
    and I am pure in your sight.’

twi: Ao, anka mepɛ sɛ Onyankopɔn kasa,anka ɔnkasa ntia wo
english:
Oh, how I wish that God would speak,
    that he would open his lips against you

twi: na ommue nyansa mu ahintasɛm so nkyerɛ wo,efisɛ nyansa turodoo yɛ afanu.Hu sɛ Onyankopɔn werɛ afi wo bɔne no bi mpo.
english:
and disclose to you the secrets of wisdom,
    for true wisdom has two sides.
    Know this: God has even forgotten some of your sin.

twi: “Wubetumi ate Onyankopɔn anwonwade ase ana?Wubetumi abɔre ahu nea Otumfo no tumi kɔpem ana?
english:
“Can you fathom the mysteries of God?
    Can you probe the limits of the Almighty?

twi: Ɛkorɔn sen ɔsoro, dɛn na wubetumi ayɛ?Emu dɔ sen ɔda ase tɔnn, dɛn na wubetumi ahu?
english:
They are higher than the heavens above—what can you do?
    They are deeper than the depths below—what can you know?

twi: Ne nsusuwii mu ware sen asasena ɛtrɛw sen po.
english:
Their measure is longer than the earth
    and wider than the sea.

twi: “Sɛ ɔba de wo bɛto afiaseansa na osi nkongua a, hena na obetumi asiw no kwan?
english:
“If he comes along and confines you in prison
    and convenes a court, who can oppose him?

twi: Ampa ara ohu nnipa nnaadaafo;na sɛ ohu bɔne a, ɔnhyɛ ne nsow ana?
english:
Surely he recognizes deceivers;
    and when he sees evil, does he not take note?

twi: Nanso ogyimifo rentumi nyɛ onyansafo dana wɔawo afurum ba sɛ onipa.
english:
But the witless can no more become wise
    than a wild donkey’s colt can be born human.

twi: “Na sɛ wode wo koma ma nona wopagyaw wo nsa kyerɛ no,
english:
“Yet if you devote your heart to him
    and stretch out your hands to him,

twi: sɛ wugyaa bɔne a wukura no muna woamma amumɔyɛ antena wo ntamadan mu a
english:
if you put away the sin that is in your hand
    and allow no evil to dwell in your tent,

twi: ɛno de, bɔne nni wo ho, wobɛma wo ti so;wubegyina pintinn a worensuro.
english:
then, free of fault, you will lift up your face;
    you will stand firm and without fear.

twi: Wo werɛ befi wʼahokyere,na wɔbɛkae no sɛ nsu a asen kɔ.
english:
You will surely forget your trouble,
    recalling it only as waters gone by.

twi: Abrabɔ bɛhyerɛn asen owigyinae,na sum bɛyɛ sɛ adekyee hann.
english:
Life will be brighter than noonday,
    and darkness will become like morning.

twi: Wubenya bammɔ, efisɛ anidaso wɔ hɔ;wobɛhwɛ wo ho ahyia, na wahome asomdwoe mu.
english:
You will be secure, because there is hope;
    you will look about you and take your rest in safety.

twi: Wobɛda ahome, na obi renhunahuna wo,na bebree bɛhwehwɛ mmoa afi wo nkyɛn.
english:
You will lie down, with no one to make you afraid,
    and many will court your favor.

twi: Amumɔyɛfo ani befura,wɔrentumi nguan;na wɔn anidaso bɛdan owu ahomegu.”
Hiob Bua SofarNa Hiob buae se,
english: Then Job replied:

twi: “Akyinnye nni ho, mo ne nnipa nona muwu a na nyansa asa!
english:
“Doubtless you are the only people who matter,
    and wisdom will die with you!

twi: Nanso mewɔ adwene sɛ mo aramonnsen me.Hena na onnim saa nneɛma yi nyinaa?
“Mayɛ aserewde ama me nnamfonom,mefrɛɛ Onyankopɔn na obuae,aserewde teta bi, nanso meteɛ na me ho nni asɛm.
english:
“I have become a laughingstock to my friends,
    though I called on God and he answered—
    a mere laughingstock, though righteous and blameless!

twi: Nnipa a wɔn ho tɔ wɔn no bu amanehunu animtiaasɛnea wobu wɔn a wɔn nan rewatiri no awiei animtiaa no.
english:
Those who are at ease have contempt for misfortune
    as the fate of those whose feet are slipping.

twi: Wɔmmfa wɔn nsa nka akorɔmfo ntamadan,na wɔn a woyi Onyankopɔn abufuw wɔ bammɔna Onyankopɔn bɔ nea ɔde ma wɔn ho ban.
english:
The tents of marauders are undisturbed,
    and those who provoke God are secure—
    those God has in his hand.

twi: “Bisa mmoa no, na wɔbɛkyerɛ woanaasɛ wim nnomaa no, na wɔbɛka akyerɛ wo
english:
“But ask the animals, and they will teach you,
    or the birds in the sky, and they will tell you;

twi: anaasɛ kasa kyerɛ asase, na ɛbɛkyerɛ wo,anaasɛ ma po mu mpataa nka nkyerɛ wo.
english:
or speak to the earth, and it will teach you,
    or let the fish in the sea inform you.

twi: Wɔn nyinaa mu hena na onnim sɛAwurade nsa na ayɛ eyi.
english:
Which of all these does not know
    that the hand of the Lord has done this?

twi: Ne nsam na abɔde nyinaa home wɔne adesamma nyinaa home.
english:
In his hand is the life of every creature
    and the breath of all mankind.

twi: So aso nsɔ nsɛm nhwɛsɛnea tɛkrɛma ka aduan hwɛ no ana?
english:
Does not the ear test words
    as the tongue tastes food?

twi: Wonnya nyansa mfi mpanyin nkyɛn,na ɛnyɛ onyinkyɛ na ɛde ntease ba ana?
english:
Is not wisdom found among the aged?
    Does not long life bring understanding?

twi: “Nyansa ne tumi yɛ Onyankopɔn de;afotu ne ntease yɛ ne dea.
english:
“To God belong wisdom and power;
    counsel and understanding are his.

twi: Nea obubu gu no, obiara rentumi nsi;nea ɔde no to afiase no, obiara rentumi nyi no.
english:
What he tears down cannot be rebuilt;
    those he imprisons cannot be released.

twi: Sɛ ɔma osu gyae tɔ a, asase no so yɛ wosee;sɛ ogyaa osutɔ mu a, ɛsɛe asase no.
english:
If he holds back the waters, there is drought;
    if he lets them loose, they devastate the land.

twi: Ahoɔden ne nkonimdi yɛ ne deosisifo ne nea wosisi no no nso yɛ ne de.
english:
To him belong strength and insight;
    both deceived and deceiver are his.

twi: Ɔpa afotufo ho ntama ma wɔkɔna ɔma atemmufo yɛ nkwasea.
english:
