He leads rulers away stripped
    and makes fools of judges.

twi: Ɔworɔw ahemfo nkyehamana ɔde abɔso bɔ wɔn asen.
english:
He takes off the shackles put on by kings
    and ties a loincloth around their waist.

twi: Ɔpa asɔfo ho ntama,na otu nnipa a wɔn ase atim akyɛ gu.
english:
He leads priests away stripped
    and overthrows officials long established.

twi: Ɔka afotufo a wogye wɔn di no kasaboa hyɛ,na ogye mpanyimfo nhumu.
english:
He silences the lips of trusted advisers
    and takes away the discernment of elders.

twi: Ɔde animguase gu atitiriw sona otintim gye ahoɔdenfo nsam akode.
english:
He pours contempt on nobles
    and disarms the mighty.

twi: Ɔda sum mu nneɛma a ahintaw adina ɔde sum kabii ba hann mu.
english:
He reveals the deep things of darkness
    and brings utter darkness into the light.

twi: Ɔyɛ aman akɛse, na ɔsɛe wɔn;ɔtrɛw aman mu, na ɔhwete wɔn mu.
english:
He makes nations great, and destroys them;
    he enlarges nations, and disperses them.

twi: Ogye wiase akannifo adwene fi wɔn nsam;na ɔma wokyinkyin asase wosee a ɔkwan nna so so.
english:
He deprives the leaders of the earth of their reason;
    he makes them wander in a trackless waste.

twi: Wɔkeka wɔ sum mu a wonni kanea;na ɔma wɔtɔ ntintan sɛ asabowfo.”
english:
They grope in darkness with no light;
    he makes them stagger like drunkards.

twi: “Mʼani ahu eyinom nyinaa,mʼaso ate, na ate ase.
english:
“My eyes have seen all this,
    my ears have heard and understood it.

twi: Nea wunim no, me nso minim;wonyɛ abomfiaa mma me.
english:
What you know, I also know;
    I am not inferior to you.

twi: Nanso mepɛ sɛ mekasa kyerɛ Otumfo nona mekyerɛkyerɛ mʼasɛm mu kyerɛ Onyankopɔn.
english:
But I desire to speak to the Almighty
    and to argue my case with God.

twi: Mode atoro mmom na asra me ho;mo nyinaa moyɛ ayaresafo a munsi hwee!
english:
You, however, smear me with lies;
    you are worthless physicians, all of you!

twi: Sɛ mobɛyɛ komm koraa aɛno na ɛbɛyɛ nyansa ama mo!
english:
If only you would be altogether silent!
    For you, that would be wisdom.

twi: Afei muntie mʼano asɛm;muntie mʼanoyi.
english:
Hear now my argument;
    listen to the pleas of my lips.

twi: Mobɛka amumɔyɛsɛm ama Onyankopɔn ana?Mobɛka nnaadaasɛm ama no ana?
english:
Will you speak wickedly on God’s behalf?
    Will you speak deceitfully for him?

twi: Mobɛkyea mo aso ama no?Mobɛka Onyankopɔn asɛm ama no ana?
english:
Will you show him partiality?
    Will you argue the case for God?

twi: Sɛ ɔhwehwɛ mo mu a, ebesi mo yiye ana?Mubetumi adaadaa no sɛnea modaadaa nnipa no ana?
english:
Would it turn out well if he examined you?
    Could you deceive him as you might deceive a mortal?

twi: Sɛ mokyeaa mo aso wɔ kokoa mu a,sɛnea ɛte biara, ɔbɛka mo anim
english:
He would surely call you to account
    if you secretly showed partiality.

twi: Nʼanuonyam mmɔ mo hu ana?Ne ho suro ntɔ mo so ana?
english:
Would not his splendor terrify you?
    Would not the dread of him fall on you?

twi: Mo kasatɔmmɛ yɛ mmɛbu a ɛte sɛ nsõ;mo anoyi yɛ dɔte twann anoyi.
english:
Your maxims are proverbs of ashes;
    your defenses are defenses of clay.

twi: “Monyɛ komm mma menkasa;na nea ɛbɛyɛ me biara mmra me so.
english:
“Keep silent and let me speak;
    then let come to me what may.

twi: Adɛn nti na mede me ho to amane muna mede me nkwa to me nsam?
english:
Why do I put myself in jeopardy
    and take my life in my hands?

twi: Ɛwɔ mu sɛ okum me de, nanso ne so na mʼani bɛda;ampa ara medi mʼakwan ho adanse wɔ nʼanim.
english:
Though he slay me, yet will I hope in him;
    I will surely defend my ways to his face.

twi: Nokware, eyi na ɛbɛyɛ me nkwagye,efisɛ nea onsuro Onyankopɔn no rentumi nkɔ nʼanim!
english:
Indeed, this will turn out for my deliverance,
    for no godless person would dare come before him!

twi: Muntie me nsɛm yi yiye;monyɛ aso mma nea meka.
english:
Listen carefully to what I say;
    let my words ring in your ears.

twi: Afei a masiesie me nkurobɔ yi,minim sɛ medi bem.
english:
Now that I have prepared my case,
    I know I will be vindicated.

twi: Obi betumi abɔ me kwaadu ana?Sɛ ɛte saa de a, anka mɛyɛ komm na mawu.
english:
Can anyone bring charges against me?
    If so, I will be silent and die.

twi: “Onyankopɔn, yɛ saa nneɛma abien yi pɛ ma me,na afei meremfa me ho nhintaw wo:
english:
“Only grant me these two things, God,
    and then I will not hide from you:

twi: Yi wo nsa fi me so kɔ akyirikyiri,na gyae wo ho hu a wode hunahuna me no.
english:
Withdraw your hand far from me,
    and stop frightening me with your terrors.

twi: Ɛno de, samena me na mɛba,anaa ma menkasa na bua me.
english:
Then summon me and I will answer,
    or let me speak, and you reply to me.

twi: Mfomso ne bɔne dodow ahe na mayɛ?Kyerɛ me me mfomso ne me bɔne.
english:
How many wrongs and sins have I committed?
    Show me my offense and my sin.

twi: Adɛn nti na wode wʼanim asie mena wudwen sɛ meyɛ wo tamfo?
english:
Why do you hide your face
    and consider me your enemy?

twi: Wobɛyɛ ahaban a mframa rebɔ no ayayade ana?Wobɛtaa ntɛtɛ a awo ana?
english:
Will you torment a windblown leaf?
    Will you chase after dry chaff?

twi: Wokyerɛw sobo a ɛyɛ yaw tia me,na woka me mmabunmmere mu bɔne nyinaa gu me so.
english:
For you write down bitter things against me
    and make me reap the sins of my youth.

twi: Wode nkyehama gu mʼanan;wohwɛ mʼanammɔnkwan nyinaa so yiyena wode agyiraehyɛde ayeyɛ mʼanammɔn mu.
“Enti onipa nkwa sa te sɛ ade a aporɔw,te sɛ atade a nwewee adi.
english:
“So man wastes away like something rotten,
    like a garment eaten by moths.

twi: “Nnipa a ɔbea awo wɔnnna yɛ tiaa bi na ɔhaw ahyɛ mu mma.
english:
“Mortals, born of woman,
    are of few days and full of trouble.

twi: Ɔfefɛw te sɛ nhwiren na etwintwam;ɔte sɛ sunsuma a ɛretwa mu akɔ, ɔntena hɔ nkyɛ.
english:
They spring up like flowers and wither away;
    like fleeting shadows, they do not endure.

twi: Woma wʼani kɔ saa onipa yi so?Wode no bɛba wʼanim abebu no atɛn ana?
english:
Do you fix your eye on them?
    Will you bring them before you for judgment?

twi: Hena na obetumi ayi nea ɛyɛ kronkron afi fi mu?Obiara nni hɔ.
english:
Who can bring what is pure from the impure?
    No one!

twi: Woahyehyɛ onipa nkwa nna;woahyɛ nʼasram dodow ato hɔna woahyɛ no bere a ɔrentumi ntra.
Enti yi wʼani fi ne so na ɔnyɛ nea ɔpɛ,kosi sɛ obewie nʼadwuma sɛ ɔpaani.
english:
So look away from him and let him alone,
    till he has put in his time like a hired laborer.

twi: “Dua mpo anidaso wɔ hɔ ma no:Sɛ wotwa a, ɛbɛfefɛw bio,na ne mman foforo no rempenpan.
english:
“At least there is hope for a tree:
    If it is cut down, it will sprout again,
    and its new shoots will not fail.

twi: Ne ntin betumi anyin akyɛ asase muna ne dunsin nso awu wɔ dɔte mu,
english:
Its roots may grow old in the ground
    and its stump die in the soil,

twi: nanso, onya nsu a ɛfefɛw,na eyiyi mman sɛ dua a wɔatɛw.
english:
yet at the scent of water it will bud
    and put forth shoots like a plant.

twi: Nanso sɛ nnipa wu a wɔde no hyɛ fam;ɔhome nea etwa to a, na afei onni hɔ bio.
english:
But a man dies and is laid low;
    he breathes his last and is no more.

twi: Sɛnea nsu tu yera wɔ po mu no,anaa sɛnea suka mu yowee no,
english:
As the water of a lake dries up
    or a riverbed becomes parched and dry,

twi: saa ara na onipa tɔ fam na ɔnsɔre bio;enkosi sɛ ɔsoro betwa mu no, nnipa rensɔrena wɔrennyan wɔn mfi wɔn nna mu.
“Sɛ anka wode me besie ɔda mude me ahintaw kosi sɛ wʼabufuw betwa mu!Sɛ anka wobɛhyɛ me berena afei woakae me!
english:
“If only you would hide me in the grave
    and conceal me till your anger has passed!
If only you would set me a time
    and then remember me!

twi: Sɛ onipa wu a ɔbɛba nkwa mu bio ana?Mʼaperedi nna mu nyinaamɛtwɛn akosi sɛ me foforoyɛ bɛba.
english:
If someone dies, will they live again?
    All the days of my hard service
    I will wait for my renewal to come.

twi: Wobɛfrɛ na megye wo so;wʼani begyina abɔde a wo nsa ayɛ.
english:
You will call and I will answer you;
    you will long for the creature your hands have made.

twi: Afei wobɛkan mʼanammɔntuna worenni me bɔne akyi.
english:
Surely then you will count my steps
    but not keep track of my sin.

twi: Wɔbɛsɔ me bɔne ano wɔ kotoku mu,na woakata mʼamumɔyɛ so.
english:
My offenses will be sealed up in a bag;
    you will cover over my sin.

twi: “Nanso sɛnea mmepɔw so hohoro na ɛpomponona ɔbotan nso twe fi ne sibea no,
english:
“But as a mountain erodes and crumbles
    and as a rock is moved from its place,

twi: sɛnea nsu yiyi abo hona osuhweam twe dɔte kɔ nosaa ara na wosɛe onipa anidaso.
english:
as water wears away stones
    and torrents wash away the soil,
    so you destroy a person’s hope.

twi: Wutintim ne so prɛko pɛ, na otwa mu kɔ;wosakra ne nipasu na wugya no kwan.
english:
You overpower them once for all, and they are gone;
    you change their countenance and send them away.

twi: Sɛ wɔhyɛ ne mmabarima anuonyam a, onnim;na sɛ wɔbrɛ wɔn ase a, onhu.
english:
If their children are honored, they do not know it;
    if their offspring are brought low, they do not see it.

twi: Ɔno ara were mu yaw na ɔteena ɔno ara ne ho na ogyam.”
english:
They feel but the pain of their own bodies
    and mourn only for themselves.”

twi: Elifas Mmuae A Ɛto So AbienNa Temanni Elifas buae se,
english: Then Eliphaz the Temanite replied:

twi: “Enti onyansafo de nsɛm a aba biara nni mu beyi nʼanoanaasɛ ɔde apuei mframa a emu yɛ hyew bɛhyɛ nʼafuru ma?
english:
“Would a wise person answer with empty notions
    or fill their belly with the hot east wind?

twi: Ɔde nsɛm huhuw begye akyinnye,aka nsɛm a mfaso biara nni so ana?
english:
Would they argue with useless words,
    with speeches that have no value?

twi: Wototo onyamesuro ase mmomna wusiw Onyankopɔn som ho kwan.
english:
But you even undermine piety
    and hinder devotion to God.

twi: Wo bɔne kyerɛ wʼano nea ɔnka;na woafa anitew tɛkrɛma.
english:
Your sin prompts your mouth;
    you adopt the tongue of the crafty.

twi: Wʼankasa wʼano bu wo kumfɔ, ɛnyɛ me de;wʼankasa wʼano di adanse tia wo.
english:
Your own mouth condemns you, not mine;
    your own lips testify against you.

twi: “Wone onipa a wɔwoo wo dii kan ana?Wɔwoo wo ansa na wɔrewo nkoko ana?
english:
“Are you the first man ever born?
    Were you brought forth before the hills?

twi: Wutie Onyankopɔn afotu ana?Wo nko ara na wunim nyansa ana?
english:
Do you listen in on God’s council?
    Do you have a monopoly on wisdom?

twi: Dɛn na wunim a, yennim?Nhumu bɛn na wowɔ a yenni?
english:
What do you know that we do not know?
    What insights do you have that we do not have?

twi: Nea wafuw dwen ne akwakoraa wɔ yɛn afawɔn a wɔanyinyin sen wʼagya mpo.
english:
The gray-haired and the aged are on our side,
    men even older than your father.

twi: Onyankopɔn awerɛkyekyene nsɛm a wɔka no brɛoo kyerɛ wo no sua ma wo ana?
english:
Are God’s consolations not enough for you,
    words spoken gently to you?

twi: Adɛn nti na wo koma atwe wo akɔadɛn nti na wʼani asɔ gya,
english:
Why has your heart carried you away,
    and why do your eyes flash,

twi: na woadan wʼabufuw agu Onyankopɔn sona woma saa nsɛm yi pue fi wʼano?
english:
so that you vent your rage against God
    and pour out such words from your mouth?

twi: “Ɔdesani ne hena a obetumi ayɛ pɛ,anaasɛ nea ɔbea awo no bɛn na obetumi ayɛ ɔtreneeni?
english:
“What are mortals, that they could be pure,
    or those born of woman, that they could be righteous?

twi: Onyankopɔn nni ahotoso wɔ nʼakronkronfo muɔsorosoro mpo nyɛ kronkron wɔ nʼani so,
english:
If God places no trust in his holy ones,
    if even the heavens are not pure in his eyes,

twi: na me ne onipa debɔneyɛfo ne omumɔyɛfo aɔnom bɔne sɛ nsu.
english:
how much less mortals, who are vile and corrupt,
    who drink up evil like water!

twi: “Tie me, na mɛkyerɛ wo mu;ma menka nea mahu nkyerɛ wo,
english:
“Listen to me and I will explain to you;
    let me tell you what I have seen,

twi: nea anyansafo apae mu aka,a wɔamfa biribiara a wonya fii wɔn agyanom hɔ no ansie
english:
what the wise have declared,
    hiding nothing received from their ancestors

twi: (wɔn nko ara na wɔde asase no maa wɔnbere a ananafo biara nni wɔn mu):
english:
(to whom alone the land was given
    when no foreigners moved among them):

twi: Omumɔyɛfo kɔ ahohia mu, ne nkwanna nyinaa,na basabasayɛni nso, ne mfe a wɔahyehyɛ ama no nyinaa.
english:
All his days the wicked man suffers torment,
    the ruthless man through all the years stored up for him.

twi: Nnyigyei a ɛyɛ hu hyɛ nʼasom ma;na sɛ ɛyɛ sɛ nneɛma rekɔ yiye ma no a, akorɔmfo tow hyɛ ne so.
english:
Terrifying sounds fill his ears;
    when all seems well, marauders attack him.

twi: Ɔpa abaw sɛ obeguan afi sum mu;wɔabɔ no ato hɔ ama afoa.
english:
He despairs of escaping the realm of darkness;
    he is marked for the sword.

twi: Okyinkyin hwehwɛ aduan;onim sɛ sum da no abɛn.
english:
He wanders about for food like a vulture;
    he knows the day of darkness is at hand.

twi: Ɔhaw ne ahoyeraw yi no hu;ɛhyɛ ne so sɛ ɔhene a wasiesie ne ho ama ɔko,
english:
Distress and anguish fill him with terror;
    troubles overwhelm him, like a king poised to attack,

twi: efisɛ ɔteɛteɛ ne nsa kyerɛ Onyankopɔnna ɔma ne ho so tia Otumfo,
english:
because he shakes his fist at God
    and vaunts himself against the Almighty,

twi: wɔde nkatabo a mu piw na ɛyɛ denkɔ ne so a, onsuro obiara.
english:
defiantly charging against him
    with a thick, strong shield.

twi: “Ɛwɔ mu sɛ srade ama nʼafono atotɔna nʼasen mu nam abubu agu so de,
english:
“Though his face is covered with fat
    and his waist bulges with flesh,

twi: nanso ɔbɛtena nkurow a agu sona watena afi a obi nte mu,afi a ɛrebubu mu.
english:
he will inhabit ruined towns
    and houses where no one lives,
    houses crumbling to rubble.

twi: Ɔrenkɔ so nyɛ ɔdefo bio, na nʼahonya rennyina,na nʼagyapade so bɛtew na ayera wɔ asase so.
english:
He will no longer be rich and his wealth will not endure,
    nor will his possessions spread over the land.

twi: Ɔrenguan sum no;ogyaframa bɛhyew ne mman,na Onyankopɔn anom ahomegu bɛsoa no akɔ.
Ɛnsɛ sɛ ɔde ne ho to nneɛma huhuw so de daadaa ne ho,efisɛ ɔrennya hwee mfi mu.
english:
Let him not deceive himself by trusting what is worthless,
    for he will get nothing in return.

twi: Ansa na ne da bedu no, wobetua no ka a bi nka,na ne mman renyɛ frɔmfrɔm.
english:
Before his time he will wither,
    and his branches will not flourish.

twi: Ɔbɛyɛ sɛ bobedua a wɔaporow so aba a ennyin ɛ,te sɛ ngodua a ne nhwiren reporow gu fam.
english:
He will be like a vine stripped of its unripe grapes,
    like an olive tree shedding its blossoms.

twi: Na abɔnefo fekuw a wonnim Onyankopɔn no rensow aba,na ogya bɛhyew wɔn a wɔdɔ kɛtɛasehyɛ no ntamadan.
english:
For the company of the godless will be barren,
    and fire will consume the tents of those who love bribes.

twi: Wonyinsɛn ɔhaw na wɔwo bɔne;wɔn awotwaa siesie nnaadaa.”
english:
They conceive trouble and give birth to evil;
    their womb fashions deceit.”

twi: Hiob MmuaeAfei Hiob buae se,
english: Then Job replied:

twi: “Mate nsɛm bebree a ɛte sɛ eyinom;na mo nyinaa moyɛ ogyamserewfo!
english:
“I have heard many things like these;
    you are miserable comforters, all of you!

twi: So mo kasa tenten no remma awiei ana?Dɛn na ɛhaw mo nti a mugu so regye akyinnye yi?
english:
Will your long-winded speeches never end?
    What ails you that you keep on arguing?

twi: Anka me nso metumi akasa sɛ mo,sɛ mo na mowɔ me tebea yi mu a,anka metumi akeka nsɛm a ɛyɛ dɛ atia mona mabu mo animtiaa.
english:
I also could speak like you,
    if you were in my place;
I could make fine speeches against you
    and shake my head at you.

twi: Nanso anka mɛhyɛ mo den;anka awerɛkyekye nsɛm a ebefi mʼanom no bɛma mo ahotɔ.
english:
But my mouth would encourage you;
    comfort from my lips would bring you relief.

twi: “Nanso sɛ mekasa a ɔyaw a mete no remmrɛ ase;na sɛ mankasa nso a, ɛrennyae.
english:
“Yet if I speak, my pain is not relieved;
    and if I refrain, it does not go away.

twi: Onyankopɔn, ampa ara woama mabrɛwoasɛe me fi pasaa.
english:
Surely, God, you have worn me out;
    you have devastated my entire household.

twi: Woakyekyere me, ama abɛyɛ adansedi;me so tew ara na ɛtew na edi adanse tia me.
english:
You have shriveled me up—and it has become a witness;
    my gauntness rises up and testifies against me.

twi: Onyankopɔn tow hyɛ me so tetew me wɔ nʼabufuw muna ɔtwɛre ne se gu me so;nea ɔne me anya no pɔkyere nʼani hwɛ me.
Nnipa bue wɔn ano di me ho fɛw;wɔbɔ me sotɔre de bu me animtiaana wɔka wɔn ho bɔ mu de tia me.
Onyankopɔn de me ama abɔnefowatow me ato amumɔyɛfo nsam.
english:
God has turned me over to the ungodly
    and thrown me into the clutches of the wicked.

twi: Na biribiara kɔ yiye ma me, nanso ɔdwerɛw me;osoo me kɔn mu, tow me hwee hɔ.Ɔde me asi nʼani so;
nʼagyantowfo atwa me ho ahyia,ohwirew mʼasaabo mu a wanhu me mmɔbɔmaa me bɔnwoma petee fam.
english:
his archers surround me.
Without pity, he pierces my kidneys
    and spills my gall on the ground.

twi: Ɔba me so bere biara;na ɔtow hyɛ me so sɛ ɔkofo.
english:
Again and again he bursts upon me;
    he rushes at me like a warrior.

twi: “Mapam atweaatam akata me were sona masie mʼanintɔn wɔ mfutuma mu.
english:
“I have sewed sackcloth over my skin
    and buried my brow in the dust.

twi: Agyaadwotwa ama mʼani ayɛ kɔɔ;sunsuma kabii atwa mʼani ho ahyia,
english:
My face is red with weeping,
    dark shadows ring my eyes;

twi: nanso me nsa nyɛɛ basabasayɛ biarana me mpaebɔ yɛ kann.
english:
yet my hands have been free of violence
    and my prayer is pure.

twi: “Asase, nkata me mogya so;na mma me sufrɛ to ntwa da!
english:
“Earth, do not cover my blood;
    may my cry never be laid to rest!

twi: Mprempren mpo, me danseni wɔ ɔsoro;me kamafo wɔ soro hɔ.
english:
Even now my witness is in heaven;
    my advocate is on high.

twi: Me dimafo yɛ mʼadamfobere a mʼaniwa tew nisu gu Onyankopɔn so yi;
english:
My intercessor is my friend
    as my eyes pour out tears to God;

twi: ogyina onipa anan mu di ma no wɔ Onyankopɔn animsɛnea obi di ma nʼadamfo no.
english:
on behalf of a man he pleads with God
    as one pleads for a friend.

twi: “Mfe kakraa bi akyiansa na metu kwan akɔ koransan.
english:
“Only a few years will pass
    before I take the path of no return.

twi: Me honhom atɔ beraw,me nna so atwa,na ɔda retwɛn me.
english:
My spirit is broken,
    my days are cut short,
    the grave awaits me.

twi: Ampa ara fɛwdifo atwa me ho ahyia;ɛsɛ sɛ mehwɛ wɔn atutuwpɛ.
english:
Surely mockers surround me;
    my eyes must dwell on their hostility.

twi: “Ao Onyankopɔn, hyɛ me bɔ a wuhia.Hena bio na ɔbɛma me bammɔ?
english:
“Give me, O God, the pledge you demand.
    Who else will put up security for me?

twi: Wɔato wɔn adwene mu a wɔnte asɛm ase;enti woremma wonni nkonim.
english:
You have closed their minds to understanding;
    therefore you will not let them triumph.

twi: Sɛ obi sopa ne nnamfonom de gye akatua a,ɛbɛhwere ne mma aniwa.
english:
If anyone denounces their friends for reward,
    the eyes of their children will fail.

twi: “Onyankopɔn de me ayɛ asɛm a ɛda obiara ano,obi a wɔte ntasu gu nʼani so.
english:
“God has made me a byword to everyone,
    a man in whose face people spit.

twi: Awerɛhow ama mʼani ayɛ siamoome nipadua nyinaa yɛ sunsuma.
english:
My eyes have grown dim with grief;
    my whole frame is but a shadow.

twi: Ɛyɛ atreneefo nwonwa;wɔn a wodi bem tia wɔn a wonni nyamesu.
english:
The upright are appalled at this;
    the innocent are aroused against the ungodly.

twi: Nanso atreneefo bɛkɔ wɔn anim,na wɔn a wɔn nsa ho tew no bɛkɔ so anya ahoɔden.
english:
Nevertheless, the righteous will hold to their ways,
    and those with clean hands will grow stronger.

twi: “Mo nyinaa monsan mmra mmɛsɔ nhwɛ!Na merennya onyansafo wɔ mo mu.
english:
“But come on, all of you, try again!
    I will not find a wise man among you.

twi: Me nna atwa mu, me nhyehyɛe apansam.Nanso me koma apɛde
english:
My days have passed, my plans are shattered.
    Yet the desires of my heart

twi: ma anadwo dan awia;sum mu koraa no hann bɛn.
english:
turn night into day;
    in the face of the darkness light is near.

twi: Sɛ ofi a mʼani da so nkutoo ne ɔda,sɛ mesɛw me kɛtɛ wɔ sum mu,
english:
If the only home I hope for is the grave,
    if I spread out my bed in the realm of darkness,

twi: sɛ meka kyerɛ porɔwee se, ‘Wo yɛ mʼagya,’ne osunson se, ‘Me na’ anaa ‘Me nuabea’ a,
english:
if I say to corruption, ‘You are my father,’
    and to the worm, ‘My mother’ or ‘My sister,’

twi: na afei mʼanidaso wɔ he?Hena na obetumi anya anidaso bi ama me?
english:
where then is my hope—
    who can see any hope for me?

twi: Ebesian akɔ owu pon ano ana?Yɛn nyinaa besian akɔ mfutuma mu ana?”
english:
Will it go down to the gates of death?
    Will we descend together into the dust?”

twi: Bildad Mmuae A Ɛto So AbienNa Suhini Bildad buae se,
english: Then Bildad the Shuhite replied:

twi: “Bere bɛn na wubegyae kasa tenten yi?Dwene ho yiye, na afei yebetumi akasa.
english:
“When will you end these speeches?
    Be sensible, and then we can talk.

twi: Adɛn nti na wofa yɛn sɛ anantwina wususuw sɛ yennim nyansa yi?
english:
Why are we regarded as cattle
    and considered stupid in your sight?

twi: Wo a wode abufuw tetew wo mu nketenkete,wo nti na yemfi asase soanaasɛ wonnwiriw abotan mfi wɔn sibea ana?
english:
You who tear yourself to pieces in your anger,
    is the earth to be abandoned for your sake?
    Or must the rocks be moved from their place?

twi: “Omumɔyɛfo kanea adum;na ne gya nnɛw bio.
english:
“The lamp of a wicked man is snuffed out;
    the flame of his fire stops burning.

twi: Hann a ɛwɔ ne ntamadan mu duru sum;kanea a esi ne ho no dum.
english:
The light in his tent becomes dark;
    the lamp beside him goes out.

twi: Nʼanammɔntu mu ahoɔden ano bɛbrɛ ase;nʼankasa nhyehyɛe hwe no ase.
english:
The vigor of his step is weakened;
    his own schemes throw him down.

twi: Nʼanammɔn de no kɔ afiri mu,na okyinkyin kɔtɔ ne tan mu.
english:
His feet thrust him into a net;
    he wanders into its mesh.

twi: Afiri so ne nantinna eso ne mu dennen.
english:
A trap seizes him by the heel;
    a snare holds him fast.

twi: Wɔasum no afiri ahintaw wɔ fam;afiri wɔ ne kwan mu.
english:
A noose is hidden for him on the ground;
    a trap lies in his path.

twi: Ahunahuna ma ɔbɔ huboa wɔ ne ho nyinaana ɛhaw no wɔ nʼanammɔntu biara mu.
english:
Terrors startle him on every side
    and dog his every step.

twi: Atoyerɛnkyɛm kɔn dɔ no;na sɛ ɔhwe ase a, amanehunu retwɛn no.
english:
Calamity is hungry for him;
    disaster is ready for him when he falls.

twi: Ɛwewe ne honam ani baabi;na owu di kan sɛe nʼakwaa.
english:
It eats away parts of his skin;
    death’s firstborn devours his limbs.

twi: Wɔtwe no fi ne ntamadan bammɔ muna wɔde no brɛ ahunahunahene.
english:
He is torn from the security of his tent
    and marched off to the king of terrors.

twi: Ogya te ne ntamadan mu;na wɔabɔ sufre a ɛredɛw apete nʼatenae.
english:
Fire resides in his tent;
    burning sulfur is scattered over his dwelling.

twi: Ne ntin wuwu wɔ asena ne mman nso wu wɔ soro.
english:
His roots dry up below
    and his branches wither above.

twi: Wɔnnkae no asase so bio;na onni din wɔ asase so.
english:
The memory of him perishes from the earth;
    he has no name in the land.

twi: Wɔka no fi hann mu kɔ sum muna wɔpam no fi wiase.
english:
He is driven from light into the realm of darkness
    and is banished from the world.

twi: Onni mma anaa nananom wɔ ne nkurɔfo mu,na nʼaseni biara renka wɔ baabi a ɔtenae.
english:
He has no offspring or descendants among his people,
    no survivor where once he lived.

twi: Nnipa a wofi atɔe fam ho adwiriw wɔn wɔ nea ato no no ho;na aninyanne bunkam wɔn a wɔwɔ apuei fam no so.
english:
People of the west are appalled at his fate;
    those of the east are seized with horror.

twi: Ampa ara, sɛɛ na omumɔyɛfo atenae te;sɛɛ ne beae a nea onnim Onyankopɔn no te.”
english:
Surely such is the dwelling of an evil man;
    such is the place of one who does not know God.”

twi: Hiob Bua BildadNa Hiob buae se,
english: Then Job replied:

twi: “Mobɛhyɛ me ɔyawna mode nsɛm abubu me akosi da bɛn?
english:
“How long will you torment me
    and crush me with words?

twi: Mpɛn du ni a moasopa me;mo ani nwu sɛ motow hyɛ me so.
english:
Ten times now you have reproached me;
    shamelessly you attack me.

twi: Sɛ ɛyɛ nokware sɛ mafom ɔkwan a,me mfomso yɛ me nko ara asɛm.
english:
If it is true that I have gone astray,
    my error remains my concern alone.

twi: Sɛ ampa sɛ mobɛma mo ho so asen mena mode mʼanimguase ayɛ adanse atia me a,
english:
If indeed you would exalt yourselves above me
    and use my humiliation against me,

twi: ɛno de munhu sɛ Onyankopɔn ayɛ me bɔnena ɔde ne tan atwa me ho ahyia.
english:
then know that God has wronged me
    and drawn his net around me.

twi: “Ɛwɔ mu, misu se, ‘Wɔafom me’ de, nanso obiara mmua me;meteɛ mu pɛ mmoa, nanso atɛntrenee biara nni hɔ.
english:
“Though I cry, ‘Violence!’ I get no response;
    though I call for help, there is no justice.

twi: Wasiw me kwan enti mintumi nsen;ɔde sum aduru mʼakwan so.
english:
He has blocked my way so I cannot pass;
    he has shrouded my paths in darkness.

twi: Wayi mʼanuonyam afi me sona watu mʼahenkyɛw afi me ti so.
english:
He has stripped me of my honor
    and removed the crown from my head.

twi: Wasɛe me akwannuasa nyinaa so de awie me;watu mʼanidaso ase te sɛ dua.
english:
He tears me down on every side till I am gone;
    he uproots my hope like a tree.

twi: Nʼabufuw huru tia me;na wakan me afra nʼatamfo mu.
english:
His anger burns against me;
    he counts me among his enemies.

twi: Nʼakofo ba anibere so;wosisi mpie de tia mena wotwa me ntamadan ho hyia.
“Wayi me nuabarimanom afi me ho;na mʼamanifo atwe wɔn ho koraa.
english:
“He has alienated my family from me;
    my acquaintances are completely estranged from me.

twi: Mʼabusuafo kɔ;na me nnamfonom werɛ afi me.
english:
My relatives have gone away;
    my closest friends have forgotten me.

twi: Mʼahɔho ne me mmaawa bu me sɛ ɔhɔho;mete sɛ ɔnanani ma wɔn.
english:
My guests and my female servants count me a foreigner;
    they look on me as on a stranger.

twi: Mefrɛ me somfo, na ommua;mpo, metew mʼano srɛ no.
english:
I summon my servant, but he does not answer,
    though I beg him with my own mouth.

twi: Me home bɔn me yere;me ho afono mʼankasa nuabarimanom.
english:
My breath is offensive to my wife;
    I am loathsome to my own family.

twi: Mpo, mmarimaa nkumaa bu me animtiaa;sɛ mipue a wodi me ho fɛw.
english:
Even the little boys scorn me;
    when I appear, they ridicule me.

twi: Me nnamfo ankasa nyinaa kyi me;mʼadɔfo asɔre atia me.
english:
All my intimate friends detest me;
    those I love have turned against me.

twi: Maka were ne nnompe,nea mede aguan nkutoo ne me se akyi nam.
english:
I am nothing but skin and bones;
    I have escaped only by the skin of my teeth.

twi: “Munhu me mmɔbɔ, me nnamfonom, munhu mmɔbɔ,na Onyankopɔn nsa abɔ me.
english:
“Have pity on me, my friends, have pity,
    for the hand of God has struck me.

twi: Adɛn nti na motaa me sɛnea Onyankopɔn yɛ no?Na mommfa me honam yi saa ara?
english:
Why do you pursue me as God does?
    Will you never get enough of my flesh?

twi: “Ao, sɛ anka wɔde me nsɛm bɛhyɛ nhoma mu,anka wɔbɛkyerɛw wɔ nhoma mmobɔwee so,
english:
“Oh, that my words were recorded,
    that they were written on a scroll,

twi: anka wɔde dade pɛe bɛkyerɛw wɔ sumpii so,anaa wobekuruakyerɛw wɔ ɔbotan so afebɔɔ!
english:
that they were inscribed with an iron tool on lead,
    or engraved in rock forever!

twi: Minim sɛ me dimafo te ase,na awiei no ɔbɛsɔre agyina asase so.
english:
I know that my redeemer lives,
    and that in the end he will stand on the earth.

twi: Na wɔasɛe me were awie no,mefi me were mu ahu Onyankopɔn.
english:
And after my skin has been destroyed,
    yet in my flesh I will see God;

twi: Me ara mehu nomede mʼani, na ɛnyɛ obi foforo ani, behu no.Sɛnea me koma ho pere wɔ me mu!
english:
I myself will see him
    with my own eyes—I, and not another.
    How my heart yearns within me!

twi: “Sɛ moka se, ‘Yɛbɛteetee no,efisɛ ɔhaw no fi ɔno ara a,’
english:
“If you say, ‘How we will hound him,
    since the root of the trouble lies in him,’

twi: ɛsɛ sɛ mo ankasa musuro afoa nona abufuw nam afoa so de asotwe bɛba,na mubehu sɛ atemmu wɔ hɔ.”
Sofar Mmuae A Ɛto So AbienNa Naamani Sofar buae se,
english: Then Zophar the Naamathite replied:

twi: Me tirim mu ntew me, na ɛhyɛ me sɛ mimmuaefisɛ me ho yeraw me yiye.
english:
“My troubled thoughts prompt me to answer
    because I am greatly disturbed.

twi: Mate animka bi a egu me ho fi,na ntease a minya no hyɛ me sɛ mimmua.
english:
I hear a rebuke that dishonors me,
    and my understanding inspires me to reply.

twi: “Ampa ara wunim sɛnea nneɛma te fi tete,efi bere a wɔde nnipa duaa asase so no,
english:
“Surely you know how it has been from of old,
    ever since mankind was placed on the earth,

twi: sɛ amumɔyɛfo ani gye bere tiaa bi mu,na wɔn a wonsuro nyame nso anigye nkyɛ.
english:
that the mirth of the wicked is brief,
    the joy of the godless lasts but a moment.

twi: Ɛwɔ mu sɛ nʼahohoahoa kodu ɔsoro,na ne ti kɔpem omununkum koraa a,
english:
Though the pride of the godless person reaches to the heavens
    and his head touches the clouds,

twi: ɔbɛyera afebɔɔ te sɛ nʼankasa nʼagyanan;na wɔn a wohuu no no bebisa se, ‘Ɔwɔ he?’
english:
he will perish forever, like his own dung;
    those who have seen him will say, ‘Where is he?’

twi: Otu kɔ te sɛ ɔdae, na wɔrenhu no bio,wɔn werɛ fi te sɛ anadwo mu anisoadehu.
english:
Like a dream he flies away, no more to be found,
    banished like a vision of the night.

twi: Ani a ehuu no no renhu no bio;na ne sibea nso renhu no bio.
english:
The eye that saw him will not see him again;
    his place will look on him no more.

twi: Ne mma bɛpata ahiafo;ɛsɛ sɛ nʼankasa de nʼahonya san ma.
english:
His children must make amends to the poor;
    his own hands must give back his wealth.

twi: Ne mmerantebere mu ahoɔden a ahyɛ ne nnompe ma none no bɛkɔ mfutuma mu.
english:
The youthful vigor that fills his bones
    will lie with him in the dust.

twi: “Ɛwɔ mu sɛ bɔne yɛ nʼanom dɛna ɔde sie ne tɛkrɛma ase,
english:
“Though evil is sweet in his mouth
    and he hides it under his tongue,

twi: ɛwɔ mu sɛ ontumi nnyaa muna ɔma ɛka ne dudom,
english:
though he cannot bear to let it go
    and lets it linger in his mouth,

twi: nanso, nʼaduan bɛyɛ nwen wɔ ne yafunu mu;ɛbɛyɛ ɔwɔ ano bɔre wɔ ne mu.
english:
yet his food will turn sour in his stomach;
    it will become the venom of serpents within him.

twi: Ɔbɛfe ahonyade a ɔmenee no;Onyankopɔn bɛma ne yafunu apuw agu.
english:
He will spit out the riches he swallowed;
    God will make his stomach vomit them up.

twi: Ɔbɛfefe awɔ bɔre;Ɔnanka se bekum no.
english:
He will suck the poison of serpents;
    the fangs of an adder will kill him.

twi: Ɔrennya nsuwansuwa no nnomnsubɔnten a nufusu ne ɛwo sen wɔ mu no.
english:
He will not enjoy the streams,
    the rivers flowing with honey and cream.

twi: Ɔbɛdan nea ɔbrɛ nyae no aba a ɔrenni bi;ɔremfa nʼaguadi mu mfaso nnye nʼani.
english:
What he toiled for he must give back uneaten;
    he will not enjoy the profit from his trading.

twi: Efisɛ ɔhyɛɛ ahiafo so ma wodii ohia buruburoo;ɔde ne nsa ato afi a ɛnyɛ ɔno na osii so.
english:
For he has oppressed the poor and left them destitute;
    he has seized houses he did not build.

twi: “Ampa ara ɔrennya ahomegye mfi nea wapere anya no mu;ɔrentumi mfa nʼademude nnye ne ho nkwa.
english:
“Surely he will have no respite from his craving;
    he cannot save himself by his treasure.

twi: Wafom nneɛma nyinaa awie;ne nkɔso nnu baabiara.
english:
Nothing is left for him to devour;
    his prosperity will not endure.

twi: Nʼadedodow nyinaa mu no, ɔbɛkɔ ɔhaw mu;na amanehunu a emu yɛ den bɛto no.
english:
In the midst of his plenty, distress will overtake him;
    the full force of misery will come upon him.

twi: Bere a nʼafuru ayɛ ma no,Onyankopɔn bɛtɔ nʼabufuw gya agu ne sona wabobɔ no basabasa.
english:
When he has filled his belly,
    God will vent his burning anger against him
    and rain down his blows on him.

twi: Ɛwɔ mu sɛ oguan fi dade akode anonanso bɛmma a ano yɛ kɔbere mfrafrae bɛwɔ no.
english:
Though he flees from an iron weapon,
    a bronze-tipped arrow pierces him.

twi: Ɔtwe bɛmma no fi nʼakyi,ano hyɛnhyɛn no fi ne brɛbo mu.Ehu bɛba ne so;
sum kabii retwɛn nʼademude.Ogya a ɛnnɛw mu bɛhyew no,na asɛe nea aka wɔ ne ntamadan mu.
english:
total darkness lies in wait for his treasures.
A fire unfanned will consume him
    and devour what is left in his tent.

twi: Ɔsoro bɛda nʼafɔdi adi,na asase asɔre atia no.
english:
The heavens will expose his guilt;
    the earth will rise up against him.

twi: Nsuyiri bɛtwe ne fi akɔ,saa ara na asuworo bɛyɛ Onyankopɔn abufuwhyew da no.
english:
A flood will carry off his house,
    rushing waters on the day of God’s wrath.

twi: Eyi ne nkrabea a Onyankopɔn de ma amumɔyɛfo,agyapade a Onyankopɔn de ato hɔ ama wɔn ne no.”
english:
Such is the fate God allots the wicked,
    the heritage appointed for them by God.”

twi: Na Hiob buae se,
english: Then Job replied:

twi: Muntie me nsɛm no yiye.Momma eyi nyɛ awerɛkyekye a mode ma me.
english:
“Listen carefully to my words;
    let this be the consolation you give me.

twi: Munnya ntoboase mma me bere a merekasa,na sɛ mekasa wie a, monkɔ so nni fɛw.
english:
Bear with me while I speak,
    and after I have spoken, mock on.

twi: “Minwiinwii hyɛ onipa ana?Adɛn nti na ɛsɛ sɛ minya ntoboase?
english:
“Is my complaint directed to a human being?
    Why should I not be impatient?

twi: Monhwɛ me, na mo ho nnwiriw mo;momfa mo nsa nkata mo ano.
english:
Look at me and be appalled;
    clap your hand over your mouth.

twi: Sɛ midwen eyi ho a, mebɔ hu;na me ho popo.
english:
When I think about this, I am terrified;
    trembling seizes my body.

twi: Adɛn nti na amumɔyɛfo tena nkwa mu?Wonyin kyɛ na wɔkɔ so di tumi.
english:
Why do the wicked live on,
    growing old and increasing in power?

twi: Wohu wɔn mma a atwa wɔn ho ahyia no nkɔso,wohu wɔn nenanom.
english:
They see their children established around them,
    their offspring before their eyes.

twi: Ɔhaw nni wɔn afi mu, na ehu nni hɔ;Onyankopɔn asotwe mma wɔn so.
english:
Their homes are safe and free from fear;
    the rod of God is not on them.

twi: Wɔn anantwinini nnyɛ asaadwe;na wɔn anantwibere nwo a wɔmpɔn.
english:
Their bulls never fail to breed;
    their cows calve and do not miscarry.

twi: Wɔka wɔn mma bɔ mu te sɛ nguankuw;na emu mmotafowa no huruhuruw.
english:
They send forth their children as a flock;
    their little ones dance about.

twi: Wɔto nnwom wɔ akasae ne sanku so;na wɔde atɛntɛbɛn nnyigyei gye wɔn ani.
english:
They sing to the music of timbrel and lyre;
    they make merry to the sound of the pipe.

twi: Wodi yiye wɔn nkwanna muna wɔkɔ ɔdae mu asomdwoe mu.
english:
They spend their years in prosperity
    and go down to the grave in peace.

twi: Nanso wɔka kyerɛ Onyankopɔn se, ‘Fi yɛn so!Yɛmpɛ sɛ yehu wʼakwan.
english:
Yet they say to God, ‘Leave us alone!
    We have no desire to know your ways.

twi: Hena ne otumfo no a ɛsɛ sɛ yɛsom no?Sɛ yɛbɔ no mpae a mfaso bɛn na yebenya?’
english:
Who is the Almighty, that we should serve him?
    What would we gain by praying to him?’

twi: Nanso wɔn nkɔso no nni wɔn nsam,enti metwe me ho fi amumɔyɛfo afotu ho.
english:
But their prosperity is not in their own hands,
    so I stand aloof from the plans of the wicked.

twi: “Nanso mpɛn ahe na wodum amumɔyɛfo kanea?Mpɛn ahe na amanehunu ba wɔn so,nea Onyankopɔn fi nʼabufuw mu de ba no?
english:
“Yet how often is the lamp of the wicked snuffed out?
    How often does calamity come upon them,
    the fate God allots in his anger?

twi: Mpɛn ahe na wɔyɛ sɛ sare wɔ mframa ano,te sɛ ntɛtɛ a mframaden bi apra wɔn?
english:
How often are they like straw before the wind,
    like chaff swept away by a gale?

twi: Wɔka se, ‘Onyankopɔn kora onipa asotwe so de twɛn ne mma.’Ɛsɛ sɛ ɔtwe onipa no ankasa aso ma ohu.
english:
It is said, ‘God stores up the punishment of the wicked for their children.’
    Let him repay the wicked, so that they themselves will experience it!

twi: Ma ɔno ankasa ani nhu ne sɛe;ma Otumfo abufuwhyew no nka nʼani.
english:
Let their own eyes see their destruction;
    let them drink the cup of the wrath of the Almighty.

twi: Dɛn na ɛfa wɔn ho fa wɔn abusuafo a woagyaw wɔn akyi no hobere a asram a wɔatwa ama no aba awiei no?
english:
For what do they care about the families they leave behind
    when their allotted months come to an end?

twi: “Obi betumi akyerɛ Onyankopɔn nyansa,wɔ bere a obu atitiriw mpo atɛn?
english:
“Can anyone teach knowledge to God,
    since he judges even the highest?

twi: Obi wu wɔ bere a ɔwɔ ahoɔdenne ho tɔ no na nʼaso mu adwo no,
english:
One person dies in full vigor,
    completely secure and at ease,

twi: na ne nipadua ayɛ frɔmfrɔm,na hon ahyɛ ne nnompe ma.
english:
well nourished in body,
    bones rich with marrow.

twi: Ɔfoforo nso de ɔkra mu yawdi wu,a wanka asetena pa anhwɛ da.
english:
Another dies in bitterness of soul,
    never having enjoyed anything good.

twi: Wosie wɔn nyinaa wɔ mfutuma koro mu,ma asunson nnunu wɔn nyinaa.
english:
Side by side they lie in the dust,
    and worms cover them both.

twi: “Mahu mo adwene,ɔkwan a mobɛfa so afom me.
english:
“I know full well what you are thinking,
    the schemes by which you would wrong me.

twi: Moka se, ‘Onipa kɛse no fi wɔ he,ntamadan a omumɔyɛfo no tenaa mu no?’
english:
You say, ‘Where now is the house of the great,
    the tents where the wicked lived?’

twi: So mummmisaa wɔn a wotu kwan no asɛm da?Wɔn amanneɛbɔ mu nsɛm ho nhiaa mo
english:
Have you never questioned those who travel?
    Have you paid no regard to their accounts—

twi: sɛ onipa bɔne nya ne ti didi mu amanehunu da,na wogye wɔn abufuwhyew da no ana?
english:
that the wicked are spared from the day of calamity,
    that they are delivered from the day of wrath?

twi: Hena na ɔde ne suban si nʼanim?Hena na otua no nea wayɛ so ka?
english:
Who denounces their conduct to their face?
    Who repays them for what they have done?

twi: Wɔsoa no kɔ ɔda mu,na wɔwɛn nʼaboda.
english:
They are carried to the grave,
    and watch is kept over their tombs.

twi: Obon mu dɔte yɛ no dɛ;nnipa nyinaa di nʼakyi,na dɔm a wontumi nkan wɔn di nʼanim.
“Enti ɛbɛyɛ dɛn na mode mo nsɛnhunu bɛkyekye me werɛ?Mo mmuae nyɛ hwee sɛ atoro!”
english:
“So how can you console me with your nonsense?
    Nothing is left of your answers but falsehood!”

twi: Elifas Mmuae A Ɛto So AbienNa Temanni Elifas buae se,
english: Then Eliphaz the Temanite replied:

twi: “Onyankopɔn benya onipa so mfaso ana?Mpo onyansafo so bɛba no mfaso ana?
english:
“Can a man be of benefit to God?
    Can even a wise person benefit him?

twi: Sɛ woyɛ ɔtreneeni a, anigye bɛn na Otumfo no benya?Sɛ wʼakwan ho nni asɛm a, mfaso bɛn na obenya?
english:
What pleasure would it give the Almighty if you were righteous?
    What would he gain if your ways were blameless?

twi: “Wo kronkronyɛ nti na ɔka wʼanimna ɔbɔ wo kwaadu ana?
english:
“Is it for your piety that he rebukes you
    and brings charges against you?

twi: Ɛnyɛ wʼamumɔyɛ na ɛso?Ɛnyɛ wo bɔne na ɛdɔɔso dodo?
english:
Is not your wickedness great?
    Are not your sins endless?

twi: Wopɛɛ bammɔ fii wo nuanom nkyɛn a emfi hwee so;wopaa nnipa ho ntama ma wɔdaa adagyaw.
english:
You demanded security from your relatives for no reason;
    you stripped people of their clothing, leaving them naked.

twi: Woamma abrɛfo nsu annomna wode aduan kamee nea ɔkɔm de no,
english:
You gave no water to the weary
    and you withheld food from the hungry,

twi: nanso na woyɛ obi a ɔwɔ tumi, wɔ nsase,onuonyamfo a ɔte so.
english:
though you were a powerful man, owning land—
    an honored man, living on it.

twi: Wopam akunafo ma wɔkɔɔ nsapanna womaa ayisaa nso ahoɔden sae.
english:
And you sent widows away empty-handed
    and broke the strength of the fatherless.

twi: Ɛno nti na mfiri atwa wo ho ahyia,na amanehunu a ɛba ntɛm so bɔ wo hu yi,
english:
That is why snares are all around you,
    why sudden peril terrifies you,

twi: ɛno nti na sum kabii aduru a wunhu ade,na asorɔkye akata wo so yi.
english:
why it is so dark you cannot see,
    and why a flood of water covers you.

twi: “So Onyankopɔn nni ɔsoro akyirikyiri ana?Hwɛ sɛnea ɔsoro akyirikyiri nsoromma korɔn!
english:
“Is not God in the heights of heaven?
    And see how lofty are the highest stars!

twi: Nanso woka se, ‘Dɛn na Onyankopɔn nim?Sum yi mu na obu atɛn ana?
english:
Yet you say, ‘What does God know?
    Does he judge through such darkness?

twi: Omununkum kabii akata nʼanim nti onhu yɛnbere a ɔnenam ɔsoro kontonkurowi mu.’
english:
Thick clouds veil him, so he does not see us
    as he goes about in the vaulted heavens.’

twi: So wobɛkɔ so afa ɔkwan dedaw aabɔnefo anantew so no so ana?
english:
Will you keep to the old path
    that the wicked have trod?

twi: Wɔpraa wɔn kɔe ansa na wɔn bere reso,na nsuyiri hohoroo wɔn fapem.
english:
They were carried off before their time,
    their foundations washed away by a flood.

twi: Na wɔka kyerɛɛ Onyankopɔn se, ‘Gyaa yɛn!Dɛn na Otumfo betumi ayɛ yɛn?’
english:
They said to God, ‘Leave us alone!
    What can the Almighty do to us?’

twi: Nanso ɛyɛ ɔno na ɔde nnepa hyɛɛ wɔn afi mu,nti metwe me ho fi amumɔyɛfo afotu ho.
english:
Yet it was he who filled their houses with good things,
    so I stand aloof from the plans of the wicked.

twi: Atreneefo hu wɔn asehwe ma wɔn ani gye;na wɔn a wɔn ho nni asɛm serew wɔn ka se,
english:
The righteous see their ruin and rejoice;
    the innocent mock them, saying,

twi: ‘Wɔasɛe yɛn atamfo,na ogya ahyew wɔn agyapade.’
english:
‘Surely our foes are destroyed,
    and fire devours their wealth.’

twi: “Fa wo ho ma Onyankopɔn na nya asomdwoe wɔ ne mu;saa ɔkwan yi so na yiyedi bɛfa ayɛ wo kyɛfa.
english:
“Submit to God and be at peace with him;
    in this way prosperity will come to you.

twi: Tie akwankyerɛ a efi nʼanom,na fa ne nsɛm sie wo koma mu.
english:
Accept instruction from his mouth
    and lay up his words in your heart.

twi: Sɛ wosan kɔ Otumfo no nkyɛn a obegye wo ato mu bio:sɛ wuyi amumɔyɛsɛm fi wo ntamadan mu
english:
If you return to the Almighty, you will be restored:
    If you remove wickedness far from your tent

twi: na wotow wo sika mpɔw gu mfutuma mune Ofir sikakɔkɔɔ gu abotan a ɛwɔ abon mu no so a,
english:
and assign your nuggets to the dust,
    your gold of Ophir to the rocks in the ravines,

twi: ɛno de Otumfo bɛyɛ wo sikakɔkɔɔɔbɛyɛ dwetɛ ankasa ama wo.
english:
then the Almighty will be your gold,
    the choicest silver for you.

twi: Afei nokware wubenya anigye wɔ Otumfo muna wobɛpagyaw wʼani akyerɛ Onyankopɔn.
english:
Surely then you will find delight in the Almighty
    and will lift up your face to God.

twi: Wobɛbɔ no mpae, na obetie wo,na wubedi wo bɔhyɛ so.
english:
You will pray to him, and he will hear you,
    and you will fulfill your vows.

twi: Nea woyɛ wʼadwene sɛ wobɛyɛ no bɛba mu,na hann bɛtɔ wʼakwan so.
english:
What you decide on will be done,
    and light will shine on your ways.

twi: Sɛ nnipa hwe ase na woka se, ‘Ma wɔn so!’ a,obegye wɔn a wɔahwe ase no nkwa.
english:
When people are brought low and you say, ‘Lift them up!’
    then he will save the downcast.

twi: Obegye abɔnefo mpo,ɔnam wo nsa a ɛho nni fi so begye wɔn.”
english:
He will deliver even one who is not innocent,
    who will be delivered through the cleanness of your hands.”

twi: Hiob MmuaeNa Hiob buae se,
english: Then Job replied:

twi: “Nnɛ mpo, mʼanwiinwii mu da so yɛ den;ne nsa ayɛ den, mʼapinisi nyinaa akyi.
english:
“Even today my complaint is bitter;
    his hand is heavy in spite of my groaning.

twi: Sɛ minim baabi a mehu no;anaasɛ metumi akɔ ne tenabea a
english:
If only I knew where to find him;
    if only I could go to his dwelling!

twi: anka mɛka mʼasɛm wɔ nʼanimna magye akyinnye bebree.
english:
I would state my case before him
    and fill my mouth with arguments.

twi: Anka mɛte mmuae a ɔde bɛma me,na madwen nea ɔbɛka ho.
english:
I would find out what he would answer me,
    and consider what he would say to me.

twi: Ɔbɛsɔre atia me dennen ana?Dabi, ɔremmɔ me kwaadu.
english:
Would he vigorously oppose me?
    No, he would not press charges against me.

twi: Ɛhɔ de, nnipa trenee betumi aka nʼasɛm wɔ nʼanim,na wobegye me afi me temmufo nsam afebɔɔ.
english:
There the upright can establish their innocence before him,
    and there I would be delivered forever from my judge.

twi: “Nanso sɛ mekɔ apuei fam a onni hɔ;sɛ mekɔ atɔe fam nso a minhu no.
english:
“But if I go to the east, he is not there;
    if I go to the west, I do not find him.

twi: Sɛ ɔreyɛ adwuma wɔ atifi fam a minhu no;sɛ ɔdan ne ho kɔ anafo fam a, mʼani nhye ne ho.
english:
When he is at work in the north, I do not see him;
    when he turns to the south, I catch no glimpse of him.

twi: Nanso onim ɔkwan a menam so;na sɛ ɔsɔ me hwɛ a mepue sɛ sikakɔkɔɔ.
english:
But he knows the way that I take;
    when he has tested me, I will come forth as gold.

twi: Madi nʼanammɔn akyi pɛɛ;na manantew nʼakwan so a mamman.
english:
My feet have closely followed his steps;
    I have kept to his way without turning aside.

twi: Mentwee me ho mfii mmara nsɛm a efi nʼanom no ho,mama asɛm a efi nʼanom ho ahia me asen me daa aduan.
english:
I have not departed from the commands of his lips;
    I have treasured the words of his mouth more than my daily bread.

twi: “Nanso obiara nni hɔ ka ne ho, na hena na obetumi atia no?Ɔyɛ biribiara a ɔpɛ.
english:
“But he stands alone, and who can oppose him?
    He does whatever he pleases.

twi: Ɔde ne mmaransɛm di dwuma tia me;ɔda so kora nhyehyɛe a ɛte sɛɛ bebree.
english:
He carries out his decree against me,
    and many such plans he still has in store.

twi: Ɛno nti na mebɔ hu wɔ nʼanim;na sɛ midwen eyinom nyinaa ho a, misuro no.
english:
That is why I am terrified before him;
    when I think of all this, I fear him.

twi: Onyankopɔn ama me koma abotow;Otumfo ama mabɔ huboa.
english:
God has made my heart faint;
    the Almighty has terrified me.

twi: Nanso sum no mma menka mʼano nto mu,sum kabii a ɛkata mʼanim no.
english:
Yet I am not silenced by the darkness,
    by the thick darkness that covers my face.

twi: “Adɛn nti na Onyankopɔn nhyɛ bere mma atemmu?Adɛn nti na ɛsɛ sɛ wɔn a wonim no no hwɛ saa da no anim nanso ɛmma da?
english:
“Why does the Almighty not set times for judgment?
    Why must those who know him look in vain for such days?

twi: Nnipa yiyi abo a wɔde ato ɔhye;na wɔde nguankuw a wɔawia kɔ hɔ adidi.
english:
There are those who move boundary stones;
    they pasture flocks they have stolen.

twi: Wɔpam ayisaa mfurumna wogye akunafo anantwi sɛ awowaside.
english:
They drive away the orphan’s donkey
    and take the widow’s ox in pledge.

twi: Wosum ahiafo fi kwan sona wɔhyɛ asase no so ahiafo ma wɔkɔtetɛw.
english:
They thrust the needy from the path
    and force all the poor of the land into hiding.

twi: Sɛnea sare so mfurum yɛ nosaa ara na ahiafo no yɛ wɔn adwuma de pɛ aduan;asase kesee no so na wonya aduan ma wɔn mma.
Wɔboaboa mmoa aduan ano wɔ mfuw no sona wodi mpɛpɛ wɔ amumɔyɛfo bobe nturo mu.
english:
They gather fodder in the fields
    and glean in the vineyards of the wicked.

twi: Wonni ntama, na wɔda adagyaw anadwo;wonni hwee a wɔde kata wɔn ho wɔ awɔw mu.
english:
Lacking clothes, they spend the night naked;
    they have nothing to cover themselves in the cold.

twi: Mmepɔw so osu tɔ fɔw wɔn kyamna wɔtetare abotan no ho, efisɛ wonni nnae.
english:
They are drenched by mountain rains
    and hug the rocks for lack of shelter.

twi: Wɔtew ayisaa fi nufu ano;na wɔfa ohiani abotafowa de si ne ka anan mu.
english:
The fatherless child is snatched from the breast;
    the infant of the poor is seized for a debt.

twi: Wɔnenam adagyaw a wonni ntama;wɔsoa awi afiafi, nanso ɔkɔm de wɔn ara.
english:
Lacking clothes, they go about naked;
    they carry the sheaves, but still go hungry.

twi: Wokyi ngo wɔn adan mu;wotiatia nsakyiamoa mu, nanso osukɔm de wɔn.
english:
They crush olives among the terraces;
    they tread the winepresses, yet suffer thirst.

twi: Wɔn a wɔrewuwu no apinisi fi kuropɔn no mu,na apirafo kra su pɛ mmoa.Nanso Onyankopɔn mfa bɔne nto obiara so.
english:
The groans of the dying rise from the city,
    and the souls of the wounded cry out for help.
    But God charges no one with wrongdoing.

twi: “Ebinom wɔ hɔ a wɔsɔre tia hann no,wɔn a wonnim nʼakwananaasɛ wɔnnantew nʼatempɔn so no.
english:
“There are those who rebel against the light,
    who do not know its ways
    or stay in its paths.

twi: Sɛ adekyee hann no kɔ a, owudifo no sɔrena okum ohiani ne mmɔborɔni;anadwo, mu owiawia ne ho sɛ ɔkorɔmfo.
english:
When daylight is gone, the murderer rises up,
    kills the poor and needy,
    and in the night steals forth like a thief.

twi: Ɔwaresɛefo twɛn bere a anim rebiribiri;ɔka se, ‘obiara renhu me,’na ɔde nʼanim hintaw.
Sum mu na nnipa bubu apon wura afi mu,na adekyee, wɔtoto wɔn ho apon mu;wɔne hann nni hwee yɛ.
Sum kabii yɛ adekyee ma wɔn nyinaa;wɔne sum mu nneɛma a ɛyɛ hu fa nnamfo.
english:
For all of them, midnight is their morning;
    they make friends with the terrors of darkness.

twi: “Nanso wɔte sɛ ahuru a ɛte nsu ani;wɔadome wɔn kyɛfa wɔ asase no so,enti obiara nkɔ bobe nturo no mu.
Sɛnea ɔhyew ne ɔpɛ hwim sukyerɛmma a anan kɔ no,saa ara na ɔda de wɔn a wɔayɛ bɔne kɔ ne no.
english:
As heat and drought snatch away the melted snow,
    so the grave snatches away those who have sinned.

twi: Awotwaa werɛ fi wɔn,na osunson di wɔn nam;nnipa bɔne de wɔnnkae wɔn biona mmom wobubu te sɛ dua.
english:
The womb forgets them,
    the worm feasts on them;
the wicked are no longer remembered
    but are broken like a tree.

twi: Wɔde ɔbea bonin a onni ba yɛ hanam,na wonhu akunafo mmɔbɔ.
english:
They prey on the barren and childless woman,
    and to the widow they show no kindness.

twi: Onyankopɔn nam ne tumi so twe atumfo kɔ;ɛwɔ mu sɛ wonya asetena pa de, nanso wonni nkwa ho bɔhyɛ.
english:
But God drags away the mighty by his power;
    though they become established, they have no assurance of life.

twi: Otumi ma wɔn tena ase asomdwoe mu,nanso nʼani wɔ wɔn akwan so.
english:
He may let them rest in a feeling of security,
    but his eyes are on their ways.

twi: Wɔma wɔn so bere tiaa bi, na afei wonni hɔ bio;wɔbrɛ wɔn ase boaboa wɔn ano sɛ nnipa nyinaa;wotwitwa wɔn gu te sɛ aburow ti.
“Sɛ eyi nte saa a, hena na obetumi agye me akyinnyena ama nea maka no ayɛ nsɛnhunu?”
english:
“If this is not so, who can prove me false
    and reduce my words to nothing?”

twi: Bildad Mmuae A Ɛto So AbiɛsaNa Suhini Bildad buae se,
english: Then Bildad the Shuhite replied:

twi: “Tumi ne suro wɔ Onyankopɔn;ɔno na ɔhyehyɛ pɛpɛyɛ wɔ ɔsorosoro.
english:
“Dominion and awe belong to God;
    he establishes order in the heights of heaven.

twi: Wobetumi akan nʼakofo ana?Hena na ne hann nhyerɛn wɔ ne so?
english:
Can his forces be numbered?
    On whom does his light not rise?

twi: Ɛno de, ɛbɛyɛ dɛn na ɔdesani betumi ateɛ wɔ Onyankopɔn anim?Ɛbɛyɛ dɛn na nea ɔbea awo no no bɛyɛ kronn?
english:
How then can a mortal be righteous before God?
    How can one born of woman be pure?

twi: Mpo sɛ ɔsram nhyerɛnna nsoromma nyɛ kronn wɔ nʼani so a,
english:
If even the moon is not bright
    and the stars are not pure in his eyes,

twi: na nkantom onipa a ɔte sɛ nsaammoa,onipa ba a ɔyɛ osunson bi kɛkɛ!”
english:
how much less a mortal, who is but a maggot—
    a human being, who is only a worm!”

twi: Hiob Kyerɛ Nyankopɔn KɛseyɛNa Hiob kasaa bio se,
english: Then Job replied:

twi: “Woaboa nea onni tumi!Woagye basa a enni ahoɔden!
english:
“How you have helped the powerless!
    How you have saved the arm that is feeble!

twi: Woatu nea onnim nyansa fo!Na woada nhumu pa ara adi!
english:
What advice you have offered to one without wisdom!
    And what great insight you have displayed!

twi: Hena na ɔboaa wo ma wokaa saa nsɛm yi?Hena honhom na ɛkasa faa wo mu?
english:
Who has helped you utter these words?
    And whose spirit spoke from your mouth?

twi: “Awufo wɔ ahoyeraw kɛse mu,wɔn a wɔwɔ nsu ase ne nea ɛte mu nyinaa.
english:
“The dead are in deep anguish,
    those beneath the waters and all that live in them.

twi: Asaman da adagyaw Onyankopɔn anim;Ɔsɛe nso nni nkataso.
english:
The realm of the dead is naked before God;
    Destruction lies uncovered.

twi: Ɔtrɛw wim atifi fam kata nea ɛda mpan so;na ɔde asase sensɛn ohunu so.
english:
He spreads out the northern skies over empty space;
    he suspends the earth over nothing.

twi: Ɔbɔ nsu boa hyɛ ne omununkum mu,nanso nsu no mu duru ntumi mpae no.
english:
He wraps up the waters in his clouds,
    yet the clouds do not burst under their weight.

twi: Ɔtrɛw ne omununkum mude kata ɔsram ani.
english:
He covers the face of the full moon,
    spreading his clouds over it.

twi: Ɔhyɛ agyirae wɔ nsu sode to ɔhye wɔ hann ne sum ntam.
english:
He marks out the horizon on the face of the waters
    for a boundary between light and darkness.

twi: Ɔsoro nnyinaso wosow,na nʼanimka ma wɔn ho dwiriw wɔn.
english:
The pillars of the heavens quake,
    aghast at his rebuke.

twi: Ɔde ne tumi wosow pone nyansa mu, otwitwaa Rahab mu asinasin.
english:
By his power he churned up the sea;
    by his wisdom he cut Rahab to pieces.

twi: Ɔde ne home maa wim tewee;na ne nsa wɔɔ ɔwɔ a ɔrewea.
english:
By his breath the skies became fair;
    his hand pierced the gliding serpent.

twi: Eyinom yɛ ne nnwuma kakraa bi;ne tumi kakraa bi kɛkɛ!Na hena na obetumi ate ne tumi mmubomu no ase?”
Hiob toaa nʼasɛm so se,
english: And Job continued his discourse:

twi: “Sɛ Onyankopɔn te ase yi, nea wammu me atɛntrenee no,Otumfo a wama madi me kra mu awerɛhow,
english:
“As surely as God lives, who has denied me justice,
    the Almighty, who has made my life bitter,

twi: mmere dodow a nkwa wɔ me mu,na Onyankopɔn home wɔ me mu yi,
english:
as long as I have life within me,
    the breath of God in my nostrils,

twi: mʼano renka amumɔyɛsɛm,na me tɛkrɛma rentwa nkontompo.
english:
my lips will not say anything wicked,
    and my tongue will not utter lies.

twi: Merennye nto mu da sɛ nea woka no yɛ nokware;merenka me mudi nhyɛ, kosi sɛ mewu.
english:
I will never admit you are in the right;
    till I die, I will not deny my integrity.

twi: Mekura me trenee mu, merennyaa mu;sɛ mete ase yi, me tiboa remmu me fɔ.
english:
I will maintain my innocence and never let go of it;
    my conscience will not reproach me as long as I live.

twi: “Ma mʼatamfo nyɛ sɛ amumɔyɛfo,na wɔn a wokyi me nyɛ sɛ atorofo.
english:
“May my enemy be like the wicked,
    my adversary like the unjust!

twi: Anidaso bɛn na wɔn a wonni nyamesu no wɔ wɔ wɔn wu akyi,bere a Onyankopɔn agye wɔn nkwa afi wɔn nsam no?
english:
For what hope have the godless when they are cut off,
    when God takes away their life?

twi: So Onyankopɔn tie wɔn sufrɛbere a amanehunu aba wɔn so no ana?
english:
Does God listen to their cry
    when distress comes upon them?

twi: So wɔn ani begye wɔ Otumfo no mu?Wobesu afrɛ Onyankopɔn bere biara ana?
english:
Will they find delight in the Almighty?
    Will they call on God at all times?

twi: “Mɛma mo Onyankopɔn tumi ho nkyerɛkyerɛ;meremfa Otumfo no akwan nhintaw.
english:
“I will teach you about the power of God;
    the ways of the Almighty I will not conceal.

twi: Mo ankasa moahu eyinom nyinaa.Afei nsɛnhunu yi ase ne dɛn?
english:
You have all seen this yourselves.
    Why then this meaningless talk?

twi: “Eyi ne nea Onyankopɔn ahyɛ ato hɔ ama omumɔyɛfo,agyapade a otirimɔdenfo nya fi Otumfo no nkyɛn:
english:
“Here is the fate God allots to the wicked,
    the heritage a ruthless man receives from the Almighty:

twi: Sɛ ɔwɔ mma dodow dɛn ara, wɔn nkrabea ne afoa;na nʼasefo rennidi mmee da.
english:
However many his children, their fate is the sword;
    his offspring will never have enough to eat.

twi: Ɔyaredɔm besie wɔn a wɔbɛka wɔ nʼakyi,na wɔn akunafo rensu wɔn.
english:
The plague will bury those who survive him,
    and their widows will not weep for them.

twi: Ɛwɔ mu sɛ ɔhɔre dwetɛ te sɛ mfutumana ɔboa ntama ano sɛ dɔte,
english:
Though he heaps up silver like dust
    and clothes like piles of clay,

twi: nea ɔpɛ gu hɔ no, atreneefo na wobefurana pɛpɛyɛfo no nso akyekyɛ dwetɛ no.
english:
what he lays up the righteous will wear,
    and the innocent will divide his silver.

twi: Ofi a osi no te sɛ ananse abubummaba,ɛte sɛ pata bi a ɔwɛmfo abɔ.
english:
The house he builds is like a moth’s cocoon,
    like a hut made by a watchman.

twi: Ɔda hɔ te sɛ ɔdefo, nanso ɔrenna saa bio;ɔbɛtew nʼani no na ne nyinaa atu ayera.
english:
He lies down wealthy, but will do so no more;
    when he opens his eyes, all is gone.

twi: Ahunahuna ba ne so sɛ nsuyiri;ahum hwim no kɔ anadwo.
english:
Terrors overtake him like a flood;
    a tempest snatches him away in the night.

twi: Apuei mframa soa no kɔ, na onni hɔ bio;ɛtwe no fi ne tenabea.
english:
The east wind carries him off, and he is gone;
    it sweeps him out of his place.

twi: Ɛbɔ no a ahummɔbɔ nni mubere a ɔreguan afi ne tumi ase.
english:
It hurls itself against him without mercy
    as he flees headlong from its power.

twi: Ɔde fɛw bɔ ne nsamna ɔpam no fi ne tenabea.”
english:
It claps its hands in derision
    and hisses him out of his place.”

twi: “Beae a wotu dwetɛ wɔ hɔne beae a wɔnan sika kɔkɔɔ.
english:
There is a mine for silver
    and a place where gold is refined.

twi: Wotu dade fi fam,na wɔnan kɔbere fi dadebo mu.
english:
Iron is taken from the earth,
    and copper is smelted from ore.

twi: Onipa ma sum ba awiei;na ɔhwehwɛ kɔ akyirikyiri asase mukɔhwehwɛ dadebo wɔ sum kabii mu.
Wɔde fagudetu afiri hyɛ beae a ɛmmɛn ɔdesani atenae,mmeae a nnipa anan nsii hɔ da,baabi a ɛmmɛn nnipa no, ɛhɔ na wodi aforosian.
Asase a ɛbɔ aduan no,wɔdan ase no te sɛ nea wɔde ogya na ayɛ;
english:
The earth, from which food comes,
    is transformed below as by fire;

twi: hoabo fi nʼabotan muna sikakɔkɔɔ mpɔw nso wɔ ne mfutuma mu.
english:
lapis lazuli comes from its rocks,
    and its dust contains nuggets of gold.

twi: Ɔkɔre biara nnim saa kwan a ahintaw no,akoroma biara ani nhuu ɛ.
english:
No bird of prey knows that hidden path,
    no falcon’s eye has seen it.

twi: Mmoa ahantanfo nsi hɔna gyata nkɔdɛɛdɛɛ wɔ hɔ.
english:
Proud beasts do not set foot on it,
    and no lion prowls there.

twi: Onipa nsa paapae abotan dennenna ɔma mmepɔw ase da hɔ.
english:
People assault the flinty rock with their hands
    and lay bare the roots of the mountains.

twi: Otwa aka fa abotan mu,na ohu nʼademude nyinaa.
english:
They tunnel through the rock;
    their eyes see all its treasures.

twi: Ɔhwehwɛ baabi a nsubɔnten ti wɔna ɔda nneɛma a ahintaw adi.
english:
They search the sources of the rivers
    and bring hidden things to light.

twi: “Nanso ɛhe na yebehu nea nyansa hyɛ?Ɛhe na ntease te?
english:
But where can wisdom be found?
    Where does understanding dwell?

twi: Onipa renhu ne bo a ɛsom;wɔrenhu wɔ ateasefo asase so.
english:
No mortal comprehends its worth;
    it cannot be found in the land of the living.

twi: Na ebun ka se, ‘Enni me mu’;na po nso se, ‘Enni me nkyɛn.’
english:
The deep says, “It is not in me”;
    the sea says, “It is not with me.”

twi: Wɔrentumi mfa sikakɔkɔɔ ankasa ntɔ,na wɔrentumi mfa dwetɛ nkari ne bo.
english:
It cannot be bought with the finest gold,
    nor can its price be weighed out in silver.

twi: Wɔrentumi mfa Ofir sikakɔkɔɔ ntɔapopobibiribo anaa hoabo nso saa ara.
english:
It cannot be bought with the gold of Ophir,
    with precious onyx or lapis lazuli.

twi: Wɔrentumi mfa ahwehwɛ anaa sikakɔkɔɔ ntoto ho,na wɔrentumi mfa sikakɔkɔɔ nnwinne nsesa.
english:
Neither gold nor crystal can compare with it,
    nor can it be had for jewels of gold.

twi: Ɛnsɛ sɛ yɛbɔ ahene panyin ne ahwehwɛbo din;nyansa bo sen nhene pa.
english:
Coral and jasper are not worthy of mention;
    the price of wisdom is beyond rubies.

twi: Etiopia akraatebo ne no nsɛ;wɔrentumi mfa sikakɔkɔɔ kronkron ntɔ.
english:
The topaz of Cush cannot compare with it;
    it cannot be bought with pure gold.

twi: “Ɛno de, na ɛhe na nyansa fi?Ɛhe na ntease te?
english:
Where then does wisdom come from?
    Where does understanding dwell?

twi: Wɔde asie abɔde biara ani,wɔde asie wim nnomaa mpo.
english:
It is hidden from the eyes of every living thing,
    concealed even from the birds in the sky.

twi: Ɔsɛe ne Owu ka se,‘Yɛate no huhuhuhu kɛkɛ.’
english:
Destruction and Death say,
    “Only a rumor of it has reached our ears.”

twi: Onyankopɔn te ɔkwan a ɛkɔ hɔ ase,na ɔno nko ara na onim faako a ɛte,
english:
God understands the way to it
    and he alone knows where it dwells,

twi: efisɛ ɔhwɛ kodu nsase anona ohu biribiara a ɛwɔ ɔsoro ase.
english:
for he views the ends of the earth
    and sees everything under the heavens.

twi: Bere a ɔhyɛɛ mframa ano den too hɔna osusuw nsuwa no,
english:
When he established the force of the wind
    and measured out the waters,

twi: bere a ɔkaa no ɔhyɛ so kyerɛɛ osutɔna otwaa kwan maa aprannaa no,
english:
when he made a decree for the rain
    and a path for the thunderstorm,

twi: afei ɔhwɛɛ nyansa na ɔkarii no hwɛe;na ogyee no too mu na ɔsɔɔ no hwɛe.
english:
then he looked at wisdom and appraised it;
    he confirmed it and tested it.

twi: Na ɔka kyerɛɛ onipa se,‘Awurade suro, ɛno ne nyansa;na sɛ wokyi bɔne, yɛ ntease.’ ”
english:
And he said to the human race,
    “The fear of the Lord—that is wisdom,
    and to shun evil is understanding.”

twi: Hiob toaa so se,
english: Job continued his discourse:

twi: “Mʼani agyina asram a atwa mu no,nna a Onyankopɔn hwɛɛ me so no,
english:
“How I long for the months gone by,
    for the days when God watched over me,

twi: bere a ne kanea hyerɛn mʼatifina mede ne kanea nantewee sum mu no!
english:
when his lamp shone on my head
    and by his light I walked through darkness!

twi: Ao, nna a misii so no,bere a Onyankopɔn adamfofa a emu yɛ den hyiraa me fi,
english:
Oh, for the days when I was in my prime,
    when God’s intimate friendship blessed my house,

twi: bere a na Otumfo no da so ka me hona me mma atwa me ho ahyia no,
english:
when the Almighty was still with me
    and my children were around me,

twi: bere a na nufusu mu srade afɔw mʼakwanna abotan hwiee ngo sɛ nsu maa me no.
english:
when my path was drenched with cream
    and the rock poured out for me streams of olive oil.

twi: “Bere a na mekɔ kuropɔn pon anomekɔtena mʼagua so wɔ ɔmanfo aguabɔbea,
english:
“When I went to the gate of the city
    and took my seat in the public square,

twi: mmerante hu me a, wogyina nkyɛnna mpanyimfo sɔre gyina hɔ;
english:
the young men saw me and stepped aside
    and the old men rose to their feet;

twi: atitiriw gyae kasana wɔde wɔn nsa kata wɔn ano;
english:
the chief men refrained from speaking
    and covered their mouths with their hands;

twi: mmapɔmma tɛm dinn,na wɔn tɛkrɛma ka wɔn dudom.
english:
the voices of the nobles were hushed,
    and their tongues stuck to the roof of their mouths.

twi: Wɔn a wɔte me nka nyinaa ka me ho asɛmpa,na wɔn a wohu me nyinaa kamfo me,
english:
Whoever heard me spoke well of me,
    and those who saw me commended me,

twi: efisɛ meboaa ahiafo a wosu pɛɛ mmoa,ne ayisaa a wonni aboafo.
english:
because I rescued the poor who cried for help,
    and the fatherless who had none to assist them.

twi: Onipa a na ɔrewu no hyiraa me;na memaa akunafo ani gyee wɔn koma mu.
english:
The one who was dying blessed me;
    I made the widow’s heart sing.

twi: Mede trenee furaa sɛ mʼadurade;atɛntrenee yɛɛ me nkataso ne mʼabotiri.
english:
I put on righteousness as my clothing;
    justice was my robe and my turban.

twi: Meyɛɛ aniwa maa anifuraefo,ne anan maa mmubuafo.
english:
I was eyes to the blind
    and feet to the lame.

twi: Meyɛɛ ahiafo agya;na mekaa ahɔho asɛm maa wɔn.
english:
I was a father to the needy;
    I took up the case of the stranger.

twi: Mibubuu amumɔyɛfo sena mihwim wɔn a wodi wɔn nya no fii wɔn anom.
english:
I broke the fangs of the wicked
    and snatched the victims from their teeth.

twi: “Medwenee sɛ, ‘Mewu wɔ mʼankasa me fi mu,na me nna dɔɔso sɛ nwea.
english:
“I thought, ‘I will die in my own house,
    my days as numerous as the grains of sand.

twi: Me ntin beduu nsu ano,na obosu agugu me mman so anadwo mu nyinaa.
english:
My roots will reach to the water,
    and the dew will lie all night on my branches.

twi: Mʼanuonyam rempa da,na agyan ayɛ foforo wɔ me nsam daa.’
english:
My glory will not fade;
    the bow will be ever new in my hand.’

twi: “Nnipa hwehwɛɛ sɛ wotie me,wɔyɛɛ dinn, twɛn mʼafotu.
english:
“People listened to me expectantly,
    waiting in silence for my counsel.

twi: Sɛ mekasa wie a wɔnnkasa bio,efisɛ me nsɛm tɔɔ wɔn asom yiye.
english:
After I had spoken, they spoke no more;
    my words fell gently on their ears.

twi: Wɔtwɛn me sɛnea wɔtwɛn osu a ɛpete,na wɔmenee me nsɛm sɛ osutɔ bere nsu.
english:
They waited for me as for showers
    and drank in my words as the spring rain.

twi: Sɛ meserew mekyerɛ wɔn a, wɔntaa nnye nni;mʼanimtew som bo ma wɔn.
english:
When I smiled at them, they scarcely believed it;
    the light of my face was precious to them.

twi: Mebɔɔ kwan maa wɔn na metenaa ase sɛ wɔn hene;metenaa ase sɛ ɔhene a ɔwɔ nʼasraafo mu;meyɛɛ sɛ obi a ɔkyekye agyaadwotwafo werɛ.
“Nanso mprempren wɔserew me,nnipa a manyin sen wɔn,na wɔn agyanom mfata sɛwɔne me nguan ho akraman tena.
english:
“But now they mock me,
    men younger than I,
whose fathers I would have disdained
    to put with my sheep dogs.

twi: Mfaso bɛn na wɔn nsa mu ahoɔden wɔ ma me,bere a wɔn ahoɔden afi wɔn mu?
english:
Of what use was the strength of their hands to me,
    since their vigor had gone from them?

twi: Ohia ne ɔkɔm ama wɔn ho atetew,wɔnantew asase keseene asase bonin so anadwo.
english:
Haggard from want and hunger,
    they roamed the parched land
    in desolate wastelands at night.

twi: Wɔboaboaa nkyenhaban ano wɔ nkyɛkyerɛ mu,na wɔde sare so nnua ntin yɛɛ wɔn aduan.
english:
In the brush they gathered salt herbs,
    and their food was the root of the broom bush.

twi: Wɔn mfɛfo pam wɔn fii wɔn mu,na wohuroo wɔn sɛ akorɔmfo.
english:
They were banished from human society,
    shouted at as if they were thieves.

twi: Wɔhyɛɛ wɔn ma wɔtenaa suka a emu awo,abotan ne fam ntokuru mu,
english:
They were forced to live in the dry stream beds,
    among the rocks and in holes in the ground.

twi: wosuu sɛ mfurum wɔ wuramna wɔfofɔree so wɔ ɔdɔtɔ ase.
english:
They brayed among the bushes
    and huddled in the undergrowth.

twi: Kuw a wɔmfra na wonni din,wɔpam wɔn fii asase no so.
english:
A base and nameless brood,
    they were driven out of the land.

twi: “Na nnɛ yi wɔn mmabarima de dwom bɔ me akutia;mayɛ abusude wɔ wɔn mu.
english:
“And now those young men mock me in song;
    I have become a byword among them.

twi: Wokyi me na wontwiw mmɛn me;wɔmmfɛre sɛ wɔtete ntasu gu mʼanim.
english:
They detest me and keep their distance;
    they do not hesitate to spit in my face.

twi: Afei a Onyankopɔn abubu me tadua na ɔde amanehunu aba me so yi,wɔyɛ nea wɔpɛ wɔ mʼanim.
english:
Now that God has unstrung my bow and afflicted me,
    they throw off restraint in my presence.

twi: Abusuakuw no tow hyɛ me so wɔ me nifa so;wosum mʼanan mfiri,na wosisi mpie tia me.
Wosisiw mʼakwan;na wonya me sɛe mena obiara mmoa me.
Wɔba te sɛ nea wofi ntokuru a ano abae mu;wɔnam mmubui no mu munumunum ba.
english:
They advance as through a gaping breach;
    amid the ruins they come rolling in.

twi: Ahunahuna ma me ho dwiriw me;mʼanuonyam atu kɔ sɛnea mframa abɔ agu,me bammɔ atu ayera sɛ omununkum.
“Na mprempren, me nkwa resa;na amanehununna akyekyere me.
english:
“And now my life ebbs away;
    days of suffering grip me.

twi: Anadwo wowɔ me nnompe mu;ɔyaw a ɛwe me no nnyae.
english:
Night pierces my bones;
    my gnawing pains never rest.

twi: Onyankopɔn fi ne tumi mu yɛ sɛ adurade ma me;omia me te sɛ mʼatade kɔn.
english:
In his great power God becomes like clothing to me;
    he binds me like the neck of my garment.

twi: Ɔtow me kyene dontori muna ɔma me yɛ sɛ mfutuma ne nsõ.
english:
He throws me into the mud,
    and I am reduced to dust and ashes.

twi: “Onyankopɔn, misu mefrɛ wo, nanso wummua me.Mesɔre gyina, nanso wohwɛ me kɛkɛ.
english:
“I cry out to you, God, but you do not answer;
    I stand up, but you merely look at me.

twi: Woba me so anibere so;wode wʼabasa mu tumi tow hyɛ me so.
english:
You turn on me ruthlessly;
    with the might of your hand you attack me.

twi: Wuhwim me na wode mframa pia me;wudenkyidenkyi me wɔ ahum mu.
english:
You snatch me up and drive me before the wind;
    you toss me about in the storm.

twi: Minim sɛ wode me bɛkɔ owu mu,faako a woahyɛ ama ateasefo nyinaa no.
english:
I know you will bring me down to death,
    to the place appointed for all the living.

twi: “Ampa ara obiara mfa ne nsa nka onipa a ɔrebrɛbere a ɔresu pɛ mmoa wɔ nʼamanehunu mu.
english:
“Surely no one lays a hand on a broken man
    when he cries for help in his distress.

twi: Mansu amma wɔn a wɔwɔ ɔhaw mu ana?Me kra werɛ anhow amma ahiafo ana?
english:
Have I not wept for those in trouble?
    Has not my soul grieved for the poor?

twi: Nanso bere a mʼani da papa so no, bɔne bae;bere a mepɛɛ hann no sum na edurui.
english:
Yet when I hoped for good, evil came;
    when I looked for light, then came darkness.

twi: Me yafunu mu a ɛwowɔ me no nnyae da;na nna a amanehunu wɔ mu da mʼanim.
english:
The churning inside me never stops;
    days of suffering confront me.

twi: Menenam a mabiri, nanso ɛnyɛ sɛ owia na ahyew me;migyina aguabɔbea na misu pɛ mmoa.
english:
I go about blackened, but not by the sun;
    I stand up in the assembly and cry for help.

twi: Madan nnompo nuabarima,me ne mpatu na ɛbɔ.
english:
I have become a brother of jackals,
    a companion of owls.

twi: Me honam ani biri na ehuanhuan;atiridii ama me ho adɔ.
english:
My skin grows black and peels;
    my body burns with fever.

twi: Me sanku bɔ kwadwom,na mʼatɛntɛbɛn ma agyaadwotwa nnyigyei.
english:
My lyre is tuned to mourning,
    and my pipe to the sound of wailing.

twi: “Me ne mʼani yɛɛ apam sɛmeremfi akɔnnɔ mu, nhwɛ ababaa.
english:
“I made a covenant with my eyes
    not to look lustfully at a young woman.

twi: Dɛn ne onipa kyɛfa a efi ɔsoro Nyankopɔn nkyɛn?Dɛn ne nʼagyapade a efi ɔsoro Tumfo no nkyɛn?
english:
For what is our lot from God above,
    our heritage from the Almighty on high?

twi: Ɛnyɛ ɔsɛe mma amumɔyɛfo,atoyerɛnkyɛm mma wɔn a wɔyɛ bɔne ana?
english:
Is it not ruin for the wicked,
    disaster for those who do wrong?

twi: Onhu mʼakwanna ɔnkan anammɔn biara a mitu ana?
english:
Does he not see my ways
    and count my every step?

twi: “Sɛ manantew wɔ nkontompo muanaasɛ matu mmirika adi nnaadaasɛm akyi a,
english:
“If I have walked with falsehood
    or my foot has hurried after deceit—

twi: ma Onyankopɔn nkari me wɔ nsania papa sona obehu sɛ me ho nni asɛm;
english:
let God weigh me in honest scales
    and he will know that I am blameless—

twi: sɛ mʼanammɔntu afom ɔkwan,sɛ me koma adi mʼani akyi,anaasɛ me nsa ho agu fi a
ɛno de ma afoforo nni nea madua,na ma wontutu me nnɔbae ngu.
english:
then may others eat what I have sown,
    and may my crops be uprooted.

twi: “Sɛ ɔbea bi atɔ me koma so,anaasɛ matɛw me yɔnko bi pon akyi a,
english:
“If my heart has been enticed by a woman,
    or if I have lurked at my neighbor’s door,

twi: ɛno de, me yere nyam ɔbarima foforo aduan,na mmarima afoforo ne no nna.
english:
then may my wife grind another man’s grain,
    and may other men sleep with her.

twi: Efisɛ anka ɛno na ɛbɛyɛ aniwusɛmne bɔne a ɛsɛ sɛ wɔtwe aso wɔ so.
english:
For that would have been wicked,
    a sin to be judged.

twi: Ɛyɛ ogya a ɛhyew kodu Ɔsɛe mu;na ebetumi atutu me nnɔbae ase.
english:
It is a fire that burns to Destruction;
    it would have uprooted my harvest.

twi: “Sɛ mabu mʼasomfo mmarima ne mmea ntɛnkyew,bere a wɔne me nyaa asɛm,
english:
“If I have denied justice to any of my servants,
    whether male or female,
    when they had a grievance against me,

twi: sɛ Onyankopɔn de si mʼanim a dɛn na mɛyɛ?Sɛ wɔfrɛ me akontaabu a, mmuae bɛn na mɛma?
english:
what will I do when God confronts me?
    What will I answer when called to account?

twi: Ɛnyɛ nea ɔbɔɔ me wɔ ɔyafunu mu no na ɔbɔɔ wɔn?Ɛnyɛ onipa koro no na ɔyɛɛ yɛn baanu wɔ yɛn nanom yafunu mu?
english:
Did not he who made me in the womb make them?
    Did not the same one form us both within our mothers?

twi: “Sɛ mamma ahiafo nea wɔn koma pɛanaa mama akunafo ani ayɛ wɔn yaw,
english:
“If I have denied the desires of the poor
    or let the eyes of the widow grow weary,

twi: sɛ mabɔ mʼaduan ho atirimɔden amamma ayisaa bi,
english:
if I have kept my bread to myself,
    not sharing it with the fatherless—

twi: nanso efi mmerantebere mu matetew no sɛnea agya bɛyɛ,na efi ɔyafunu mu, mahwɛ akunafo.
english:
but from my youth I reared them as a father would,
    and from my birth I guided the widow—

twi: Sɛ mahu obi a onni adurade na ɔrebrɛ,anaa ohiani bi a onni atade,
english:
if I have seen anyone perishing for lack of clothing,
    or the needy without garments,

twi: na sɛ wɔamfi koma mu anhyira mesɛ mede me nguan ho nwi kaa wɔn hyew,
english:
and their hearts did not bless me
    for warming them with the fleece from my sheep,

twi: sɛ mama me nsa so atia ayisaa bi,esiane sɛ mewɔ tumi wɔ asennii nti a,
english:
if I have raised my hand against the fatherless,
    knowing that I had influence in court,

twi: ɛno de, ma me basa mpan mfi me mmati,ma emmubu mfi nʼapɔw so.
english:
then let my arm fall from the shoulder,
    let it be broken off at the joint.

twi: Misuroo ɔsɛe a efi Onyankopɔn nkyɛn,na nʼanuonyam ho suro nti mantumi anyɛ saa nneyɛe no.
english:
For I dreaded destruction from God,
    and for fear of his splendor I could not do such things.

twi: “Sɛ mede me werɛ ahyɛ sikakɔkɔɔ muanaasɛ maka akyerɛ sikakɔkɔɔ ankasa se, ‘Wo na wobɔ me ho ban,’
english:
“If I have put my trust in gold
    or said to pure gold, ‘You are my security,’

twi: sɛ masɛpɛw me ho wɔ mʼahode bebrebe nti,ahode a me nsa aka yi,
english:
if I have rejoiced over my great wealth,
    the fortune my hands had gained,

twi: sɛ mahwɛ owia ne ne hyerɛnanaa ɔsram a ɔnam anuonyam mu,
english:
if I have regarded the sun in its radiance
    or the moon moving in splendor,

twi: ama aka me koma a obiara nnimna me nsa yɛɛ wɔn atuu de nidi maa wɔn a,
english:
so that my heart was secretly enticed
    and my hand offered them a kiss of homage,

twi: ɛno de, na eyinom nso bɛyɛ bɔne a wobu ho atɛn,efisɛ na manni Onyankopɔn a ɔte ɔsoro no nokware.
english:
then these also would be sins to be judged,
    for I would have been unfaithful to God on high.

twi: “Sɛ mʼani gyee wɔ me tamfo amanehunu ntianaa mesrew no wɔ ɔhaw a aba ne so nti,
english:
“If I have rejoiced at my enemy’s misfortune
    or gloated over the trouble that came to him—

twi: memmaa mʼano nyɛɛ bɔnesɛ mɛdome ne nkwa,
english:
I have not allowed my mouth to sin
    by invoking a curse against their life—

twi: sɛ nnipa a wɔwɔ me fi mu nkaa da sɛ,‘Hena na Hiob pon so nam mmee no da?’
english:
if those of my household have never said,
    ‘Who has not been filled with Job’s meat?’—

twi: Ɔhɔho biara anna abɔnten so da,efisɛ me pon ano daa hɔ da biara maa akwantufo,
english:
but no stranger had to spend the night in the street,
    for my door was always open to the traveler—

twi: Makata me bɔne so sɛnea nnipa yɛde mʼafɔdi ahyɛ me koma mu
english:
if I have concealed my sin as people do,
    by hiding my guilt in my heart

twi: esiane sɛ misuroo nnipadɔmne ahohora a efi mmusua hɔ no ntina meyɛɛ komm a mamfi adi.
english:
because I so feared the crowd
    and so dreaded the contempt of the clans
    that I kept silent and would not go outside—

twi: (“Ao, sɛ anka mewɔ obi a obetie me.Mede me din ahyɛ mʼanoyi ase, ma Otumfo no mmua me;ma nea ɔbɔ me kwaadu no nkyerɛw ne sobobɔ.
Ampa ara, mɛhyɛ wɔ me mmati,mɛhyɛ sɛ ahenkyɛw.
english:
Surely I would wear it on my shoulder,
    I would put it on like a crown.

twi: Mebu mʼanammɔntu biara ho akontaa akyerɛ no;mɛkɔ nʼanim sɛ ɔheneba.)
english:
I would give him an account of my every step;
    I would present it to him as to a ruler.)—

twi: “Sɛ mʼasase teɛ mu tia mena nusu fɔw ne nkɔ nyinaa,
english:
“if my land cries out against me
    and all its furrows are wet with tears,

twi: sɛ madi so aba a mintuaa kaanaasɛ mabu so apaafo no aba mu a,
english:
if I have devoured its yield without payment
    or broken the spirit of its tenants,

twi: ma nsɔe mfifi nsi awi anan muna wura mfuw nsi atoko anan mu.”Hiob nsɛm no asi.
english:
then let briers come up instead of wheat
    and stinkweed instead of barley.”
The words of Job are ended.

twi: Elihu AdwenkyerɛEnti saa mmarima baasa yi ammua Hiob bio, efisɛ na ɔteɛ wɔ ɔno ara ani so.
english: So these three men stopped answering Job, because he was righteous in his own eyes.

twi: Na Busini Barakel babarima Elihu a ofi Ram abusua mu no bo fuw Hiob yiye sɛ obu ne ho bem na ommu Onyankopɔn mmom bem.
english: But Elihu son of Barakel the Buzite, of the family of Ram, became very angry with Job for justifying himself rather than God.

twi: Ne bo fuw nnamfonom baasa no sɛ wɔantumi anya nnyinaso bi ammɔ Hiob nsɛm no angu, nanso wobuu no fɔ.
english: He was also angry with the three friends, because they had found no way to refute Job, and yet had condemned him.

twi: Elihu twɛn sɛ afoforo no bɛkasa akyerɛ Hiob, efisɛ na wɔanyinyin sen no.
english: Now Elihu had waited before speaking to Job because they were older than he.

twi: Na ohuu sɛ nnipa baasa no nni asɛm biara ka bio no, nʼabufuw no sɔree.
english: But when he saw that the three men had nothing more to say, his anger was aroused.

twi: Enti Busini Barakel babarima Elihu kae se,“Meyɛ abofra,na moyɛ mpanyimfo;ɛno nti na misuroo sɛmɛka nea minim akyerɛ mo.
english:
So Elihu son of Barakel the Buzite said:
“I am young in years,
    and you are old;
that is why I was fearful,
    not daring to tell you what I know.

twi: Medwenee sɛ, ‘Ɛsɛ sɛ mpanyimfo kasa;ɛsɛ sɛ wɔn a wɔn ani afi kyerɛ nyansa.’
english:
I thought, ‘Age should speak;
    advanced years should teach wisdom.’

twi: Nanso honhom a ɛte onipa mu,Otumfo no home no na ɛma ntease.
english:
But it is the spirit in a person,
    the breath of the Almighty, that gives them understanding.

twi: Ɛnyɛ mpanyimfo nko na wɔyɛ anyansafo,ɛnyɛ wɔn a wɔn ani afi nko na wɔte nea eye ase.
english:
It is not only the old who are wise,
    not only the aged who understand what is right.

twi: “Enti mise: Muntie me;me nso mɛka mʼadwene.
english:
“Therefore I say: Listen to me;
    I too will tell you what I know.

twi: Metwɛn wɔ bere a na morekasa,mitiee mo adwenkyerɛ;bere a na munhu nea monka no,
meyɛɛ aso maa mo pa ara,nanso mo mu biara antumi ankyerɛ sɛ Hiob ayɛ mfomso;mo mu biara anyi ne nsɛm no ano.
Monnka se, ‘Yɛahu nyansa;momma Onyankopɔn mmɔ nʼasɛm no ngu, na ɛnyɛ onipa.’
english:
Do not say, ‘We have found wisdom;
    let God, not a man, refute him.’

twi: Nanso Hiob nkasa ntia me,na merennyina mo adwenkyerɛ so mmua no.
english:
But Job has not marshaled his words against me,
    and I will not answer him with your arguments.
