twi: “Wɔn ho adwiriw wɔn, wonni hwee ka bio;wɔn nsɛm asa.
english:
“They are dismayed and have no more to say;
    words have failed them.

twi: So ɛsɛ sɛ metwɛn wɔ bere a wɔayɛ komm yi,saa bere yi a wogyinagyina ha yi a wonni mmuae biara no?
english:
Must I wait, now that they are silent,
    now that they stand there with no reply?

twi: Me nso mɛka bime nso mɛka mʼadwene.
english:
I too will have my say;
    I too will tell what I know.

twi: Efisɛ nsɛm ahyɛ mʼanom ma,na honhom a ɛte me mu no hyɛ me sɛ menka;
english:
For I am full of words,
    and the spirit within me compels me;

twi: Me mu no, mete sɛ nsa a ɛhyɛ toa mute sɛ nsa kotoku foforo a ɛrebɛpae.
english:
inside I am like bottled-up wine,
    like new wineskins ready to burst.

twi: Ɛsɛ sɛ mekasa na me ho tɔ me;ɛsɛ sɛ mibue mʼano na mema mmuae.
english:
I must speak and find relief;
    I must open my lips and reply.

twi: Merenyɛ nhwɛanimna merennɛfɛdɛfɛ obiara;
english:
I will show no partiality,
    nor will I flatter anyone;

twi: na sɛ makwadaw adɛfɛdɛfɛ mu a,anka me Yɛfo beyi me afi hɔ ntɛm so.
english:
for if I were skilled in flattery,
    my Maker would soon take me away.

twi: “Na afei, Hiob, tie me nsɛm;yɛ aso ma biribiara a mɛka.
english:
“But now, Job, listen to my words;
    pay attention to everything I say.

twi: Merebebue mʼano;me nsɛm aba me tɛkrɛma so.
english:
I am about to open my mouth;
    my words are on the tip of my tongue.

twi: Me nsɛm fi koma a ɛteɛ mu;na mʼano de ahonim pa ka nea minim.
english:
My words come from an upright heart;
    my lips sincerely speak what I know.

twi: Onyankopɔn Honhom na abɔ me;Otumfo no home ma me nkwa.
english:
The Spirit of God has made me;
    the breath of the Almighty gives me life.

twi: Sɛ wubetumi a, ma me mmuae;siesie wo ho, na ka si mʼanim.
english:
Answer me then, if you can;
    stand up and argue your case before me.

twi: Wo ne me nyinaa yɛ pɛ wɔ Onyankopɔn anim;me nso wɔbɔɔ me fii dɔte mu.
english:
I am the same as you in God’s sight;
    I too am a piece of clay.

twi: Ɛnsɛ sɛ wusuro me,na ɛnsɛ sɛ me nsa yɛ den wɔ wo so.
english:
No fear of me should alarm you,
    nor should my hand be heavy on you.

twi: “Nanso woaka ama mate,mete saa nsɛm no, na wokae se,
english:
“But you have said in my hearing—
    I heard the very words—

twi: ‘Meyɛ kronkron na minni bɔne;me ho tew na afɔdi biara nni me ho.
english:
‘I am pure, I have done no wrong;
    I am clean and free from sin.

twi: Nanso Onyankopɔn anya me ho mfomsowafa me sɛ ne tamfo.
english:
Yet God has found fault with me;
    he considers me his enemy.

twi: Ɔde me nan hyɛ mpokyerɛ mu;na nʼani wɔ mʼakwan nyinaa so.’
english:
He fastens my feet in shackles;
    he keeps close watch on all my paths.’

twi: “Nanso meka mekyerɛ wo se, eyi mu de woayɛ mfomso,efisɛ Onyankopɔn so sen ɔdesani.
english:
“But I tell you, in this you are not right,
    for God is greater than any mortal.

twi: Na adɛn nti na wunwiinwii hyɛ nosɛ ommua onipa nsɛm biara ana?
english:
Why do you complain to him
    that he responds to no one’s words?

twi: Nanso Onyankopɔn kasa wɔ akwan ahorow so,na ebia nnipa nte.
english:
For God does speak—now one way, now another—
    though no one perceives it.

twi: Ɔkasa wɔ daeso ne anadwo anisoadehu mu,bere a nna afa nnipana wɔada hatee wɔ wɔn mpa so no,
english:
In a dream, in a vision of the night,
    when deep sleep falls on people
    as they slumber in their beds,

twi: otumi kasa gu wɔn asomna ɔde kɔkɔbɔ yi wɔn hu,
english:
he may speak in their ears
    and terrify them with warnings,

twi: sɛ ɔbɛdan onipa afi nneyɛe bɔne hona watwe no afi ahantan ho,
english:
to turn them from wrongdoing
    and keep them from pride,

twi: sɛ ɔmma ne kra nkɔ amoa muna ɔnhwere ne nkwa wɔ afoa ano.
english:
to preserve them from the pit,
    their lives from perishing by the sword.

twi: Anaasɛ wotumi de mpa so yaw twe onipa asonnompe mu yaw a ennyae da,
english:
“Or someone may be chastened on a bed of pain
    with constant distress in their bones,

twi: kosi sɛ ne kɔn nnɔ aduanna ne kra nso po aduan a ɛyɛ akɔnnɔ pa ara;
english:
so that their body finds food repulsive
    and their soul loathes the choicest meal.

twi: ɔfɔn yɛ basaa,na ne nnompe a anka ɛho akata no, ho da hɔ.
english:
Their flesh wastes away to nothing,
    and their bones, once hidden, now stick out.

twi: Ne kra bɛn ɔda,na ne nkwa bɛn owu abɔfo.
english:
They draw near to the pit,
    and their life to the messengers of death.

twi: “Nanso sɛ ɔbɔfo bi wɔ nʼafasɛ odimafo a, ɛyɛ apem mu baako,na ɔbɛkyerɛ no nea eye ma no,
english:
Yet if there is an angel at their side,
    a messenger, one out of a thousand,
    sent to tell them how to be upright,

twi: obehu no mmɔbɔ na waka se,‘Munnyaa no na wankɔ ɔda mu;na manya mpatade ama no,’
afei ne were yɛ foforo sɛ abofra;na esi ne dedaw mu yɛ sɛ mmerantebere mu de.
english:
let their flesh be renewed like a child’s;
    let them be restored as in the days of their youth’—

twi: Ɔbɔ Onyankopɔn mpae na onya adom fi ne hɔ,ohu Onyankopɔn anim na ɔde ahosɛpɛw teɛ mu;na Onyankopɔn gye no bio sɛ ɔtreneeni.
Afei ɔba nnipa mu bɛka se,‘Meyɛɛ bɔne na mekyeaa nea ɛteɛ,nanso mannya nea ɛfata me.
english:
And they will go to others and say,
    ‘I have sinned, I have perverted what is right,
    but I did not get what I deserved.

twi: Ogyee me kra na wamma no ankɔ ɔda mu,enti mɛtena ase na madi hann no mu dɛ.’
english:
God has delivered me from going down to the pit,
    and I shall live to enjoy the light of life.’

twi: “Onyankopɔn yɛ eyinom nyinaa ma onipa,mprenu ne ne mprɛnsa so,
english:
“God does all these things to a person—
    twice, even three times—

twi: sɛnea ne kra renkɔ ɔda mu,na nkwa hann no ahyerɛn ne so.
english:
to turn them back from the pit,
    that the light of life may shine on them.

twi: “Yɛ aso, Hiob, na tie me;yɛ dinn na menkasa.
english:
“Pay attention, Job, and listen to me;
    be silent, and I will speak.

twi: Na sɛ wowɔ biribi ka a, bua me;kasa, na mepɛ sɛ wobu wo bem.
english:
If you have anything to say, answer me;
    speak up, for I want to vindicate you.

twi: Sɛ ɛnte saa nso a, ɛno de tie me.Yɛ dinn na mɛkyerɛ wo nyansa.”
english:
But if not, then listen to me;
    be silent, and I will teach you wisdom.”

twi: Afei Elihu kae se,
english: Then Elihu said:

twi: “Mo anyansafo, muntie me nsɛm;mo nimdefo monyɛ aso mma me.
english:
“Hear my words, you wise men;
    listen to me, you men of learning.

twi: Efisɛ aso sɔ nsɛm hwɛsɛnea tɛkrɛma ka aduan hwɛ no.
english:
For the ear tests words
    as the tongue tastes food.

twi: Momma yɛnsese, nhu nea eye ma yɛn.Momma yɛn nyinaa mmɔ mu nsua nea eye.
english:
Let us discern for ourselves what is right;
    let us learn together what is good.

twi: “Hiob ka se, ‘Me ho nni asɛm,nanso Onyankopɔn abu me ntɛnkyew.
english:
“Job says, ‘I am innocent,
    but God denies me justice.

twi: Ɛwɔ mu sɛ mʼasɛm da kwan mu,nanso wobu me ɔtorofo;ɛwɔ mu sɛ menyɛɛ bɔne biara,nanso ne bɛmma no ama me apirakuru a enwu da.’
english:
Although I am right,
    I am considered a liar;
although I am guiltless,
    his arrow inflicts an incurable wound.’

twi: Onipa bɛn na ɔte sɛ Hiob aɔnom animtiaabu sɛ nsu?
english:
Is there anyone like Job,
    who drinks scorn like water?

twi: Ɔne amumɔyɛfo nantew;na ɔne atirimɔdenfo nso bɔ.
english:
He keeps company with evildoers;
    he associates with the wicked.

twi: Efisɛ ɔka se, ‘Sɛ onipa bɔ mmɔden sɛ ɔbɛsɔ Onyankopɔn ani aonnya so mfaso biara.’
english:
For he says, ‘There is no profit
    in trying to please God.’

twi: “Enti mo mmarima a mowɔ ntease muntie me.Ɛmpare Onyankopɔn sɛ ɔbɛyɛ bɔne,sɛ Otumfo no bɛyɛ mfomso.
english:
“So listen to me, you men of understanding.
    Far be it from God to do evil,
    from the Almighty to do wrong.

twi: Nnipa nneyɛe so na ɔhwɛ tua wɔn ka;nea ɛfata ne nneyɛe na ɔma ɛba ne so.
english:
He repays everyone for what they have done;
    he brings on them what their conduct deserves.

twi: Ɛmfata sɛ wɔde mfomso susuw Onyankopɔn,na ɛmfata sɛ wɔde ntɛnkyew susuw Otumfo.
english:
It is unthinkable that God would do wrong,
    that the Almighty would pervert justice.

twi: Hena na ɔde no sii asase so?Hena na ɔde wiase nyinaa hyɛɛ ne nsa?
english:
Who appointed him over the earth?
    Who put him in charge of the whole world?

twi: Sɛ ɛyɛɛ ne pɛna oyii ne Honhom ne nʼahome a,
english:
If it were his intention
    and he withdrew his spirit and breath,

twi: anka adesamma nyinaa bɛbɔ mu ayera,na onipa bɛsan akɔ mfutuma mu.
english:
all humanity would perish together
    and mankind would return to the dust.

twi: “Sɛ mowɔ nhumu a, muntie eyi;muntie nea meka.
english:
“If you have understanding, hear this;
    listen to what I say.

twi: So obi a okyi atɛntrenee betumi adi nnipa so?Mubetumi abu Ɔtreneeni kɛse no fɔ ana?
english:
Can someone who hates justice govern?
    Will you condemn the just and mighty One?

twi: Ɛnyɛ Ɔno na ɔka kyerɛ ahemfo se, ‘Mo so nni mfaso,’na ɔka kyerɛɛ atitiriw se, ‘Moyɛ atirimɔdenfo,’
english:
Is he not the One who says to kings, ‘You are worthless,’
    and to nobles, ‘You are wicked,’

twi: nea ɔnhwɛ mmapɔmma animna onyiyi adefo ne ahiafo mu,efisɛ wɔn nyinaa yɛ ne nsa ano adwuma.
english:
who shows no partiality to princes
    and does not favor the rich over the poor,
    for they are all the work of his hands?

twi: Wowuwu mmere tiaa bi mu, wɔ anadwo dasu mu;nnipa no ho wosow na wɔsen kɔ;ahoɔdenfo totɔ a emfi nipa.
“Nʼani hwɛ nnipa akwan;na ohu wɔn anammɔntu biara.
english:
“His eyes are on the ways of mortals;
    he sees their every step.

twi: Baabiara nni hɔ a aduru sum, sum kabii,a amumɔyɛfo betumi ahintaw.
english:
There is no deep shadow, no utter darkness,
    where evildoers can hide.

twi: Ɛho nhia Onyankopɔn sɛ ɔbɛhwehwɛ nnipa mu bio,a enti ɛsɛ sɛ wɔba nʼanim begye atemmu.
english:
God has no need to examine people further,
    that they should come before him for judgment.

twi: Ɔbobɔ abirɛmpɔn gu a ɔnyɛ nhwehwɛmu biara,na ɔde afoforo sisi wɔn anan mu.
english:
Without inquiry he shatters the mighty
    and sets up others in their place.

twi: Efisɛ ohu wɔn nneyɛe,otu wɔn gu anadwo na wɔdwerɛw wɔn.
english:
Because he takes note of their deeds,
    he overthrows them in the night and they are crushed.

twi: Otua wɔn amumɔyɛsɛm so kawɔ faako a obiara betumi ahu wɔn,
english:
He punishes them for their wickedness
    where everyone can see them,

twi: efisɛ wɔman fii nʼakyi kɔena wɔampɛ nʼakwan biara anhwɛ.
english:
because they turned from following him
    and had no regard for any of his ways.

twi: Wɔmaa ahiafo sufrɛ duu nʼanimna ɛma ɔtee mmɔborɔni su.
english:
They caused the cry of the poor to come before him,
    so that he heard the cry of the needy.

twi: Nanso sɛ ɔyɛ komm a, hena na obetumi abu no fɔ?Sɛ ɔde nʼanim hintaw nso a, hena na obehu no?Nanso odi onipa ne ɔman so pɛpɛɛpɛ,
english:
But if he remains silent, who can condemn him?
    If he hides his face, who can see him?
Yet he is over individual and nation alike,

twi: ɔmma onipa a onnim Nyame nni hene,sɛnea ɔrensum nnipa no mfiri.
english:
to keep the godless from ruling,
    from laying snares for the people.

twi: “Sɛ ɛba sɛ onipa ka kyerɛ Onyankopɔn se,‘Mayɛ bɔne na merenyɛ bɔne bio.
english:
“Suppose someone says to God,
    ‘I am guilty but will offend no more.

twi: Kyerɛ me na minhu;na sɛ mayɛ bɔne a, merenyɛ saa bio.’
english:
Teach me what I cannot see;
    if I have done wrong, I will not do so again.’

twi: So ɛsɛ sɛ Onyankopɔn gyina nea woka so tua wo ka,wɔ bere a woayɛ sɛ worennu wo ho ana?Ɛsɛ sɛ wusi gyinae, ɛnyɛ me;enti ka nea wunim kyerɛ me.
english:
Should God then reward you on your terms,
    when you refuse to repent?
You must decide, not I;
    so tell me what you know.

twi: “Nnipa a wɔwɔ ntease pae mu ka,nimdefo a wotie me ka kyerɛ me se,
english:
“Men of understanding declare,
    wise men who hear me say to me,

twi: ‘Hiob nkasa nimdeɛ kwan so;aba biara nni ne kasa mu.’
english:
‘Job speaks without knowledge;
    his words lack insight.’

twi: Ao, sɛ wɔsɔɔ Hiob hwɛ kɔɔ akyiri a anka eye,efisɛ oyiyii nsɛm ano sɛ omumɔyɛfo!
english:
Oh, that Job might be tested to the utmost
    for answering like a wicked man!

twi: Ɔde atuatew ka ne bɔne ho;ɔde ahantan bɔ ne nsam gu yɛn sona ɔma ne nsɛm a ɔka tia Onyankopɔn no dɔɔso.”
Afei, Elihu kae se:
english: Then Elihu said:

twi: “Wugye di sɛ, eyi fata?Woka se, ‘Onyankopɔn betwitwa agye me.’
english:
“Do you think this is just?
    You say, ‘I am in the right, not God.’

twi: Nanso wubisa no se, ‘Mfaso bɛn na menya,na sɛ manyɛ bɔne a, mfaso bɛn na menya?’
english:
Yet you ask him, ‘What profit is it to me,
    and what do I gain by not sinning?’

twi: “Mepɛ sɛ mibua wone wo nnamfonom nyinaa.
english:
“I would like to reply to you
    and to your friends with you.

twi: Ma wʼani so kyerɛ soro na hwɛ;hwɛ omununkum a ɛwɔ wʼatifi sorosoro nohɔ.
english:
Look up at the heavens and see;
    gaze at the clouds so high above you.

twi: Sɛ woyɛ bɔne a, ɔkwan bɛn so na ɛfa haw no?Mpo sɛ wo bɔne dɔɔso a, nsunsuanso bɛn na enya wɔ ne so?
english:
If you sin, how does that affect him?
    If your sins are many, what does that do to him?

twi: Sɛ woteɛ a, dɛn na wode ma noanaasɛ dɛn na onya fi wo nsam?
english:
If you are righteous, what do you give to him,
    or what does he receive from your hand?

twi: Wʼamumɔyɛ ka onipa a ɔte sɛ wona wo trenee ka nnipa mma nko ara.
english:
Your wickedness only affects humans like yourself,
    and your righteousness only other people.

twi: “Nnipa su bere a wɔhyɛ wɔn so;na wɔsrɛ mmoa fi nea ɔwɔ tumi nsam.
english:
“People cry out under a load of oppression;
    they plead for relief from the arm of the powerful.

twi: Nanso obi mmisa se, ‘Ɛhe na Onyankopɔn, me Yɛfo no wɔ,nea ɔma nnwom anadwo no,
english:
But no one says, ‘Where is God my Maker,
    who gives songs in the night,

twi: nea ɔkyerɛ yɛn nimdeɛ bebree sen asase so mmoana ɔma yehu nyansa sen wim nnomaa no?’
english:
who teaches us more than he teaches the beasts of the earth
    and makes us wiser than the birds in the sky?’

twi: Sɛ nnipa su teɛ mu a, ommua,amumɔyɛfo ahantan nti.
english:
He does not answer when people cry out
    because of the arrogance of the wicked.

twi: Ampa ara Onyankopɔn rentie wɔn nkotosrɛ hunu no;na Otumfo remmu.
english:
Indeed, God does not listen to their empty plea;
    the Almighty pays no attention to it.

twi: Ɛno de adɛn na ɔrentiebere a woka se wunhu no,na woka se wʼasɛm wɔ nʼanimenti ɛsɛ sɛ wotwɛn no,
english:
How much less, then, will he listen
    when you say that you do not see him,
that your case is before him
    and you must wait for him,

twi: na bio, nʼabufuw mmfa asotwe mmana nʼani nni amumɔyɛsɛm akyi pii?
english:
and further, that his anger never punishes
    and he does not take the least notice of wickedness.

twi: Enti Hiob bue nʼano ka nsɛnhunu;nimdeɛ a onni nti, ɔkeka nsɛm bebree.”
english:
So Job opens his mouth with empty talk;
    without knowledge he multiplies words.”

twi: Elihu toaa ne kasa so se,
english: Elihu continued:

twi: “Montɔ mo bo ase kakra mma me, na mɛkyerɛ mo sɛaka bebree a ɛsɛ sɛ yɛka ma Onyankopɔn.
english:
“Bear with me a little longer and I will show you
    that there is more to be said in God’s behalf.

twi: Minya me nimdeɛ fi akyirikyiri;mɛka se me Yɛfo bu atɛntrenee.
english:
I get my knowledge from afar;
    I will ascribe justice to my Maker.

twi: Munnye nto mu sɛ me nsɛm yɛ nokware turodoo;na meyɛ obi a ne nimdeɛ so wɔ mo mu.
english:
Be assured that my words are not false;
    one who has perfect knowledge is with you.

twi: “Onyankopɔn so, nanso, ontwiri nnipa;ɔkorɔn na osi pi wɔ ne botae mu.
english:
“God is mighty, but despises no one;
    he is mighty, and firm in his purpose.

twi: Ɔmma amumɔyɛfo ntena nkwa mu,na ɔde amanehunufo kyɛfa ma wɔn.
english:
He does not keep the wicked alive
    but gives the afflicted their rights.

twi: Onnyi nʼani mfi ɔtreneeni so,ɔma wɔne ahemfo di adena ɔma wɔn so afebɔɔ.
Na sɛ wɔde mpokyerɛ gu nnipana amanehunu hama akyekyere wɔn papee a,
english:
But if people are bound in chains,
    held fast by cords of affliction,

twi: ɔka nea wɔayɛ kyerɛ wɔnsɛ wɔnam ahantan so ayɛ bɔne.
english:
he tells them what they have done—
    that they have sinned arrogantly.

twi: Ɔma wotie nteɛsona ɔhyɛ wɔn sɛ wonnu wɔn ho wɔ wɔn bɔne ho.
english:
He makes them listen to correction
    and commands them to repent of their evil.

twi: Sɛ wɔyɛ osetie na wɔsom no a,wobedi yiye wɔ wɔn nna a aka no muna wɔn mfe nyinaa ayɛ anisɔ ama wɔn.
english:
If they obey and serve him,
    they will spend the rest of their days in prosperity
    and their years in contentment.

twi: Na sɛ wɔantie no a, wɔbɛyera wɔ afoa ano,na wɔawuwu a wonni nimdeɛ.
english:
But if they do not listen,
    they will perish by the sword
    and die without knowledge.

twi: “Wɔn a wonnim Nyame no kora abufuw so;mpo sɛ ogu wɔn nkɔnsɔnkɔnsɔn a wonsu mpɛ mmoa.
english:
“The godless in heart harbor resentment;
    even when he fetters them, they do not cry for help.

twi: Wowuwu wɔ wɔn mmabunmmere mu,wɔ mmarima nguamanfo a wɔtete abosonnan mu.
english:
They die in their youth,
    among male prostitutes of the shrines.

twi: Nanso wɔn a wohu amane no, ogye wɔn;na ɔkasa kyerɛ wɔn wɔ wɔn haw mu.
english:
But those who suffer he delivers in their suffering;
    he speaks to them in their affliction.

twi: “Ɔregye wo afi ahohia mude wo akɔ beae a hɔ bae a ahokyere nni,nea wowɔ asomdwoe, na nnuan pa ayɛ wo pon so ma.
english:
“He is wooing you from the jaws of distress
    to a spacious place free from restriction,
    to the comfort of your table laden with choice food.

twi: Nanso mprempren, atemmu a ɛfata amumɔyɛfo na aba wo so;atemmu ne atɛntrenee aso wo mu.
english:
But now you are laden with the judgment due the wicked;
    judgment and justice have taken hold of you.

twi: Hwɛ yiye na obi amfa ahonya annaadaa wo;mma adanmude kɛse bi ntwe wo.
english:
Be careful that no one entices you by riches;
    do not let a large bribe turn you aside.

twi: Wʼahonya anaasɛ mpowʼahohia bebrebe nyinaa nti,worenkɔ amanehunu mu ana?
english:
Would your wealth or even all your mighty efforts
    sustain you so you would not be in distress?

twi: Mpere anadwo ho,sɛ ammɛpra nnipa mfi wɔn afi mu.
english:
Do not long for the night,
    to drag people away from their homes.

twi: Hwɛ na woannan ankɔ bɔne ho,nea ayɛ sɛ wopɛ sen amanehunu.
english:
Beware of turning to evil,
    which you seem to prefer to affliction.

twi: “Onyankopɔn yɛ ɔkɛse wɔ ne tumi mu.Hena na ɔyɛ ɔkyerɛkyerɛfo sɛ ɔno?
english:
“God is exalted in his power.
    Who is a teacher like him?

twi: Hena na wahyehyɛ nʼakwan ama noanaa waka akyerɛ no se, ‘Woayɛ mfomso.’
english:
Who has prescribed his ways for him,
    or said to him, ‘You have done wrong’?

twi: Kae na kamfo nʼadwuma annipa de nnwonto akamfo no.
english:
Remember to extol his work,
    which people have praised in song.

twi: Adesamma nyinaa ahu;nnipa fi akyirikyiri hwɛ no haa.
english:
All humanity has seen it;
    mortals gaze on it from afar.

twi: Onyankopɔn yɛ ɔkɛse, ɛboro yɛn ntease so!Ne mfe dodow mu nni hwehwɛbea.
english:
How great is God—beyond our understanding!
    The number of his years is past finding out.

twi: “Ɔtwetwe nsu a ɛsosɔ,ma ɛdan osu gu nsuten mu;
english:
“He draws up the drops of water,
    which distill as rain to the streams;

twi: na omununkum tɔ obosu gu famna osu pete mmoroso gu adesamma so.
english:
the clouds pour down their moisture
    and abundant showers fall on mankind.

twi: Hena na obetumi ate sɛnea ɔtrɛtrɛw omununkum mu no ase,sɛnea ɔbobɔ mu fi ne suhyɛ ase no?
english:
Who can understand how he spreads out the clouds,
    how he thunders from his pavilion?

twi: Hwɛ sɛnea ɔhwete nʼanyinam mu wɔ ne homa ɛkɔ po bun mu.
english:
See how he scatters his lightning about him,
    bathing the depths of the sea.

twi: Eyi ne ɔkwan a ɔfa so di amanaman no sona ɔma aduan bu wɔn so.
english:
This is the way he governs the nations
    and provides food in abundance.

twi: Ɔde anyinam hyɛ ne nsam mana ɔhyɛ no sɛ ɛmpa nʼagyiraehyɛ.
english:
He fills his hands with lightning
    and commands it to strike its mark.

twi: Nʼaprannaa bɔ ahum a ɛreba no ho nkae;na anantwi mpo ma wohu sɛ ɛreba.
english:
His thunder announces the coming storm;
    even the cattle make known its approach.

twi: “Eyi ma me koma bɔ kitirikitirina ehuruw fi nʼatenae.
english:
“At this my heart pounds
    and leaps from its place.

twi: Tie! Tie ne nne mmubomu,ne huuyɛ a efi nʼanom reba no.
english:
Listen! Listen to the roar of his voice,
    to the rumbling that comes from his mouth.

twi: Ogyaa nʼanyinam mu wɔ ɔsoro ase nyinaana ɔma ekodu asase ano.
english:
He unleashes his lightning beneath the whole heaven
    and sends it to the ends of the earth.

twi: Ɛno akyi na ne mmubomu no ba;ɔde nne kɛse bobɔ mu.Sɛ ɔkasa a,biribiara nsianka no.
english:
After that comes the sound of his roar;
    he thunders with his majestic voice.
When his voice resounds,
    he holds nothing back.

twi: Onyankopɔn nne bobɔ mu ma no yɛ nwonwa;ɔyɛ nneɛma akɛse a ɛboro yɛn adwene so.
english:
God’s voice thunders in marvelous ways;
    he does great things beyond our understanding.

twi: Ɔka kyerɛ sukyerɛmma se, ‘Tɔ gu asase so,’ne osu nso se, ‘Yɛ osutɔ kɛse.’
english:
He says to the snow, ‘Fall on the earth,’
    and to the rain shower, ‘Be a mighty downpour.’

twi: Sɛnea nnipa a wabɔ wɔn nyinaa behu nʼadwuma nti,ɔma nnipa nyinaa gyae wɔn adwumayɛ.
english:
So that everyone he has made may know his work,
    he stops all people from their labor.

twi: Wuram mmoa kɔtetɛw;wɔkɔhyehyɛ wɔn abon mu.
english:
The animals take cover;
    they remain in their dens.

twi: Ahum tu fi ne pia mu,na awɔw nso fi mframa a ɛrebɔ mu.
english:
The tempest comes out from its chamber,
    the cold from the driving winds.

twi: Onyankopɔn home de sukyerɛmma ba,na nsu tamaa no kyen.
english:
The breath of God produces ice,
    and the broad waters become frozen.

twi: Ɔde fuonwini hyɛ omununkum ma;na otwa nʼanyinam fa mu.
english:
He loads the clouds with moisture;
    he scatters his lightning through them.

twi: Ɔhyɛ ma wokyinkyinfa asase so nyinaa hyiayɛ nea ɔhyɛ sɛ wɔnyɛ biara.
english:
At his direction they swirl around
    over the face of the whole earth
    to do whatever he commands them.

twi: Ɔde omununkum ba bɛtwe nnipa aso,anaasɛ ɔma ɛtɔ gu asase so de kyerɛ nʼadɔe.
english:
He brings the clouds to punish people,
    or to water his earth and show his love.

twi: “Tie eyi, Hiob;gyae na dwene Onyankopɔn anwonwade ho.
english:
“Listen to this, Job;
    stop and consider God’s wonders.

twi: Wunim sɛnea Onyankopɔn si fa di omununkum so,na ɔma nʼanyinam twa?
english:
Do you know how God controls the clouds
    and makes his lightning flash?

twi: Wunim sɛnea omununkum si fa sensɛn wim,nea ɔwɔ nimdeɛ a so nni no anwonwade no?
english:
Do you know how the clouds hang poised,
    those wonders of him who has perfect knowledge?

twi: Mo a mufi fifiri wɔ mo ntade mubere a anafo mframa ma asase no yɛ dinn no,
english:
You who swelter in your clothes
    when the land lies hushed under the south wind,

twi: wubetumi aboa no ama watrɛw wim,a ɛyɛ den sɛ kɔbere mfrafrae ahwehwɛ?
english:
can you join him in spreading out the skies,
    hard as a mirror of cast bronze?

twi: “Kyerɛ yɛn nea ɛsɛ sɛ yɛka kyerɛ no;yɛrentumi nka yɛn asɛm, efisɛ yennim.
english:
“Tell us what we should say to him;
    we cannot draw up our case because of our darkness.

twi: Ɛsɛ sɛ wɔka nea mepɛ sɛ meka kyerɛ no ana?Onipa bi wɔ hɔ a ɔbɛpɛ sɛ wɔbɛmene no ana?
english:
Should he be told that I want to speak?
    Would anyone ask to be swallowed up?

twi: Obiara rentumi nhwɛ owia,sɛnea ɛhyerɛn wɔ wimbere a mframa abɔ ama wim atew.
english:
Now no one can look at the sun,
    bright as it is in the skies
    after the wind has swept them clean.

twi: Ofi atifi fam ba wɔ anuonyam sononko mu;Onyankopɔn ba wɔ ahenni nwonwaso mu.
english:
Out of the north he comes in golden splendor;
    God comes in awesome majesty.

twi: Otumfo no korɔn wɔ yɛn so na wɔpagyaw no wɔ tumi mu;nʼatɛntrenee ne treneeyɛ kɛse akyi no mpo, ɔnyɛ nhyɛso.
english:
The Almighty is beyond our reach and exalted in power;
    in his justice and great righteousness, he does not oppress.

twi: Ɛno nti nnipa de nidi ma no,efisɛ onnwen koma mu anyansafo nyinaa ho ana?”
english:
Therefore, people revere him,
    for does he not have regard for all the wise in heart?”

twi: Awurade Bisa Hiob NsɛmAfei, Awurade fi ahum mu buaa Hiob se,
english: Then the Lord spoke to Job out of the storm. He said:

twi: “Hena ne nea ɔde nsɛm a nimdeɛ nni mukata me nhyehyɛe so?
english:
“Who is this that obscures my plans
    with words without knowledge?

twi: Hyɛ wo ho den sɛ ɔbarima;mebisa wo nsɛm,na wubebua me.
“Bere a metoo asase fapem no, na wowɔ he?Sɛ wote ase, ka ɛ.
english:
“Where were you when I laid the earth’s foundation?
    Tell me, if you understand.

twi: Hena na osusuw ne tenten ne ne trɛw? Ampa ara wunim!Hena na ɔtwee susuhama faa ani?
english:
Who marked off its dimensions? Surely you know!
    Who stretched a measuring line across it?

twi: Dɛn so na egyina,anaa hena na ɔtoo ne tweatibo no,
english:
On what were its footings set,
    or who laid its cornerstone—

twi: bere a anɔpa nsoromma bɔɔ mu too dwom,na abɔfo nyinaa de anigye teɛɛ mu no?
english:
while the morning stars sang together
    and all the angels shouted for joy?

twi: “Hena na ɔkaa po hyɛɛ apon akyi,bere a epue fii ɔyafunu mu,
english:
“Who shut up the sea behind doors
    when it burst forth from the womb,

twi: bere a mede omununkum yɛɛ nʼaduradena mede sum kabii kyekyeree no,
english:
when I made the clouds its garment
    and wrapped it in thick darkness,

twi: bere a metoo ɔhye maa nona misisii nʼapon ne nʼadaban,
english:
when I fixed limits for it
    and set its doors and bars in place,

twi: bere a mekae se, ‘Ɛha ara na wubedu na worentra ha;ɛha na wʼahantan asorɔkye no bɛso no?’
english:
when I said, ‘This far you may come and no farther;
    here is where your proud waves halt’?

twi: “So woahyɛ mmara ama adekyee da?Na woakyerɛ ahemadakye nso afa,
english:
“Have you ever given orders to the morning,
    or shown the dawn its place,

twi: sɛ ɛnkɔka asase anona ontu amumɔyɛfo mfi so?
english:
that it might take the earth by the edges
    and shake the wicked out of it?

twi: Asase fa ne bɔbea sɛ dɔte a ɛhyɛ nsɔwano ase;na ɛsow tebea da wɔn ho adi te sɛ atade.
english:
The earth takes shape like clay under a seal;
    its features stand out like those of a garment.

twi: Wɔde amumɔyɛfo hann akame wɔn,na wɔn abasa a wɔama so no mu abu.
english:
The wicked are denied their light,
    and their upraised arm is broken.

twi: “So woapɛɛpɛɛ mu ahu nea po aniwa wɔanaa woanantew ne bun mu pɛn?
english:
“Have you journeyed to the springs of the sea
    or walked in the recesses of the deep?

twi: So wɔde owu apon akyerɛ wo?Woahu owu sunsuma apon ana?
english:
Have the gates of death been shown to you?
    Have you seen the gates of the deepest darkness?

twi: Woate wiase a ɛda hɔ tamaa no ase ana?Sɛ wunim eyinom nyinaa a, ka kyerɛ me.
english:
Have you comprehended the vast expanses of the earth?
    Tell me, if you know all this.

twi: “Ɔkwan bɛn na ɛkɔ hann atenae?Na ɛhe na sum te?
english:
“What is the way to the abode of light?
    And where does darkness reside?

twi: Wubetumi de wɔn akɔ wɔn sibea?Wunim akwan a ɛkɔ wɔn atenae?
english:
Can you take them to their places?
    Do you know the paths to their dwellings?

twi: Ampa ara wunim, efisɛ na wɔawo wo dedaw.Woanyin yiye!
english:
Surely you know, for you were already born!
    You have lived so many years!

twi: “Woakɔ sukyerɛmma adekoradan mu daanaa woahu mparuwbo adekoradan
english:
“Have you entered the storehouses of the snow
    or seen the storehouses of the hail,

twi: a makora so ama ahohia bere,ɔsa ne akodi nna?
english:
which I reserve for times of trouble,
    for days of war and battle?

twi: Ɔkwan bɛn na ɛkɔ faako a anyinam fi ba,anaa faako a apuei mframa fi na ɛbɔ fa asase so?
english:
What is the way to the place where the lightning is dispersed,
    or the place where the east winds are scattered over the earth?

twi: Hena na otwaa ɛka maa osuhweam,ne ɔkwan maa aprannaa mmubomu,
english:
Who cuts a channel for the torrents of rain,
    and a path for the thunderstorm,

twi: sɛ ɛbɛtɔ agu asase a obiara nte so so,nweatam a obiara nni so,
english:
to water a land where no one lives,
    an uninhabited desert,

twi: na ama asase kesee a ɛda mpan afɔwna sare afifi wɔ so?
english:
to satisfy a desolate wasteland
    and make it sprout with grass?

twi: Osu wɔ agya ana?Hena na ɔyɛ agya ma obosu a ɛsosɔ?
english:
Does the rain have a father?
    Who fathers the drops of dew?

twi: Hena yafunu mu na sukyerɛmma fi?Hena na ɔwoo sukyerɛmma mporoporowa fi soro
english:
From whose womb comes the ice?
    Who gives birth to the frost from the heavens

twi: bere a nsu kyen dan sɛ ɔbo,na bun ani kyen?
english:
when the waters become hard as stone,
    when the surface of the deep is frozen?

twi: “Wubetumi de hama akyekyere Akokɔbeatan ne ne mma?Wubetumi asan Nyankrɛnte hama ana?
english:
“Can you bind the chains of the Pleiades?
    Can you loosen Orion’s belt?

twi: Wubetumi de anɔpa nsoromma aba wɔ ne bere muanaasɛ wubetumi ayi sisi ne ne mma afi hɔ?
english:
Can you bring forth the constellations in their seasons
    or lead out the Bear with its cubs?

twi: So wunim mmara a ɛfa ɔsoro ho?Wubetumi de Onyankopɔn ahenni aba asase so ana?
english:
Do you know the laws of the heavens?
    Can you set up God’s dominion over the earth?

twi: “Wubetumi ama wo nne adu omununkum sona wode nsu akata wo ho ana?
english:
“Can you raise your voice to the clouds
    and cover yourself with a flood of water?

twi: Wutumi ma anyinam twa?Wɔka kyerɛ wo se, ‘Yenni’ ana?
english:
Do you send the lightning bolts on their way?
    Do they report to you, ‘Here we are’?

twi: Hena na ɔde nyansa ma komaanaasɛ ɔde ntease hyɛ adwene mu?
english:
Who gives the ibis wisdom
    or gives the rooster understanding?

twi: Hena na ɔwɔ nyansa a wɔde kan omununkum?Hena na obetumi akyea ɔsoro nsu nkotoku,
english:
Who has the wisdom to count the clouds?
    Who can tip over the water jars of the heavens

twi: bere a mfutuma ayɛ denama dɔte atɔwatɔw keka bɔ mu.
english:
when the dust becomes hard
    and the clods of earth stick together?

twi: “Wokɔ ahayɛ ma gyataberema gyata didi mee
english:
“Do you hunt the prey for the lioness
    and satisfy the hunger of the lions

twi: bere a wobutubutuw wɔn abon anoanaasɛ wɔtetɛw adɔtɔ ase?
english:
when they crouch in their dens
    or lie in wait in a thicket?

twi: Hena na ɔma kwaakwaadabi aduanbere a ne mma su frɛ Onyankopɔnna wonni aduan nti wokyinkyin?
english:
Who provides food for the raven
    when its young cry out to God
    and wander about for lack of food?

twi: “So wunim bere a bepɔw so mmirekyi wowo?Woahwɛ, ahu bere a ɔforote nyinsɛn ne ba?
english:
“Do you know when the mountain goats give birth?
    Do you watch when the doe bears her fawn?

twi: So woakan asram dodow a wɔde nyinsɛn?Wunim bere a wɔwo ana?
english:
Do you count the months till they bear?
    Do you know the time they give birth?

twi: Wɔkotow wowo wɔn mma;wɔn awoko yaw to twa.
english:
They crouch down and bring forth their young;
    their labor pains are ended.

twi: Wɔn mma nyin ahoɔden so wɔ wuram;na wogyaw wɔn awofo hɔ a wɔnnsan nkɔ wɔn nkyɛn bio.
english:
Their young thrive and grow strong in the wilds;
    they leave and do not return.

twi: “Hena na ɔma wuram afurum fa ne ho di?Hena na ɔsan ne hama?
english:
“Who let the wild donkey go free?
    Who untied its ropes?

twi: Mede asase kesee maa no sɛ ne fi,ne nkyene asase tamaa sɛ nʼatenae.
english:
I gave it the wasteland as its home,
    the salt flats as its habitat.

twi: Ɔserew kurom gyegyeegyeyɛ;na ɔnte ɔkafo nteɛteɛmu.
english:
It laughs at the commotion in the town;
    it does not hear a driver’s shout.

twi: Okyinkyin mmepɔw no so sɛ ne didibeaɛhɔ na okyin hwehwɛ wura amono biara.
english:
It ranges the hills for its pasture
    and searches for any green thing.

twi: “Ɛko bɛpene sɛ ɔbɛsom wo ana?Ɔbɛtena wo mmoa adididaka nkyɛn anadwo ana?
english:
“Will the wild ox consent to serve you?
    Will it stay by your manger at night?

twi: Wubetumi asa no wɔ funtumfiri so ana?Ɔbɛfɛntɛm aku a ɛda wʼakyi no ana?
english:
Can you hold it to the furrow with a harness?
    Will it till the valleys behind you?

twi: Wubetumi de wo ho ato no so esiane nʼahoɔden dodo nti?Wubegyaw wʼadwuma a ɛyɛ den no ama no ana?
english:
Will you rely on it for its great strength?
    Will you leave your heavy work to it?

twi: Wugye di sɛ ɔde wʼaburow bɛbana waboa ano de akɔ awiporowbea ana?
english:
Can you trust it to haul in your grain
    and bring it to your threshing floor?

twi: “Sohori bɔ ne ntaban mu anigye so,nanso wontumi mfa ntoto asukɔnkɔn de ho.
english:
“The wings of the ostrich flap joyfully,
    though they cannot compare
    with the wings and feathers of the stork.

twi: Ɔtow ne nkesua gu asase soma mfutuma ka no hyew,
english:
She lays her eggs on the ground
    and lets them warm in the sand,

twi: ɛmfa ne ho sɛ ɛnan bi bɛpɛtɛw no,sɛ wuram aboa bi betiatia so.
english:
unmindful that a foot may crush them,
    that some wild animal may trample them.

twi: Ɔbɔ ne mma atirimɔden sɛnea wɔnyɛ ne dea;ɛmfa ne ho sɛ nʼadwuma bɛyɛ ɔkwa,
english:
She treats her young harshly, as if they were not hers;
    she cares not that her labor was in vain,

twi: efisɛ Onyankopɔn amma no nyansawamma no nhumu biara.
english:
for God did not endow her with wisdom
    or give her a share of good sense.

twi: Nanso sɛ ɔtrɛw ne ntaban mu tu mmirika a,ɔserew ɔpɔnkɔ ne ne sotefo.
english:
Yet when she spreads her feathers to run,
    she laughs at horse and rider.

twi: “Wo na woma ɔpɔnkɔ no nʼahoɔdenanaa woma ne kɔn mu nwi kuhaa no?
english:
“Do you give the horse its strength
    or clothe its neck with a flowing mane?

twi: Wo na woma no huruw te sɛ mmoadabi,na ɔde ne nkotɔ hunahuna ana?
english:
Do you make it leap like a locust,
    striking terror with its proud snorting?

twi: Ɔde ne nan tintim fam dennen, na nʼani gye nʼahoɔden mu,na afei ɔbɔ wura ɔko mu.
english:
It paws fiercely, rejoicing in its strength,
    and charges into the fray.

twi: Ɔmmɔ hu, na onsuro biribiara;ohu afoa a onguan.
english:
It laughs at fear, afraid of nothing;
    it does not shy away from the sword.

twi: Bɛmma wosow wɔ ne nkyɛn mu boha mu,na peaw ne pɛmɛ nso di ahim wɔ ne ho.
english:
The quiver rattles against its side,
    along with the flashing spear and lance.

twi: Ofi ahopere mu de nʼano sisi fam;na sɛ wɔhyɛn torobɛnto a ontumi nnyina faako.
english:
In frenzied excitement it eats up the ground;
    it cannot stand still when the trumpet sounds.

twi: Sɛ torobɛnto hyɛn a ɔka se, ‘Wiɛ!’ɔte ɔko ho hua fi akyirikyiri,ɔsahene no nteɛmu ne ɔko mu osebɔ.
english:
At the blast of the trumpet it snorts, ‘Aha!’
    It catches the scent of battle from afar,
    the shout of commanders and the battle cry.

twi: “Wo nyansa na ɛma akoroma tuna ɔtrɛw ne ntaban mu fa anafo?
english:
“Does the hawk take flight by your wisdom
    and spread its wings toward the south?

twi: Wo na wohyɛ ɔkɔre ma no tu kɔ sorosorokɔyɛ ne berebuw wɔ hɔ?
english:
Does the eagle soar at your command
    and build its nest on high?

twi: Ɔbotan mu na ɔte na ɛhɔ na ɔda;ɔbotan sorɔnsorɔn yɛ nʼabandennen.
english:
It dwells on a cliff and stays there at night;
    a rocky crag is its stronghold.

twi: Ɛhɔ na ofi kɔhwehwɛ nʼaduan;nʼani hu ade a ɛwɔ akyirikyiri.
english:
From there it looks for food;
    its eyes detect it from afar.

twi: Mogya yɛ ne mma aduan,na faako a atɔfo wɔ no, ɛhɔ na ɔwɔ.”
english:
Its young ones feast on blood,
    and where the slain are, there it is.”

twi: Afei Awurade buaa Hiob se,
english: The Lord said to Job:

twi: “Nea ɔne Otumfo no wɔ asɛm no bɛteɛ ne so ana?Ma nea ɔbɔ Onyankopɔn kwaadu no mmua no ɛ!”
english:
“Will the one who contends with the Almighty correct him?
    Let him who accuses God answer him!”

twi: Na Hiob buaa Awurade se,
english: Then Job answered the Lord:

twi: “Mensɛ na memfata, ɛbɛyɛ dɛn na matumi anya mmuae?Mede me nsa mua mʼano.
english:
“I am unworthy—how can I reply to you?
    I put my hand over my mouth.

twi: Makasa baako, nanso minni mmuaemprenu so, na merenkasa bio.”
english:
I spoke once, but I have no answer—
    twice, but I will say no more.”

twi: Afei, Awurade fi ahum mu buaa Hiob se,
english: Then the Lord spoke to Job out of the storm:

twi: “Hyɛ wo ho den sɛ ɔbarima;mebisa wo nsɛm,na ɛsɛ sɛ wubua me.
“Wobɛka mʼatemmu ho asɛm bɔne ana?Wubebu me fɔ de abu wo ho bem ana?
english:
“Would you discredit my justice?
    Would you condemn me to justify yourself?

twi: Wowɔ abasa te sɛ Onyankopɔn de,na wo nne betumi abobɔ mu sɛ ne de ana?
english:
Do you have an arm like God’s,
    and can your voice thunder like his?

twi: Ɛno de fa anuonyam ne ɔhyerɛn hyehyɛ wo ho,na fura nidi ne kɛseyɛ.
english:
Then adorn yourself with glory and splendor,
    and clothe yourself in honor and majesty.

twi: Hwie wʼabufuwhyew mmoroso no gu,hwɛ ɔhantanni biara na brɛ no ase,
english:
Unleash the fury of your wrath,
    look at all who are proud and bring them low,

twi: hwɛ ɔhantanni biara na si no famna tiatia amumɔyɛfo so wɔ faako a wogyina hɔ.
english:
look at all who are proud and humble them,
    crush the wicked where they stand.

twi: Sie wɔn nyinaa bɔ mu wɔ mfutuma mu;kata wɔn anim wɔ ɔda mu.
english:
Bury them all in the dust together;
    shroud their faces in the grave.

twi: Na afei mʼankasa megye ato mu sɛwo ara wo basa nifa betumi agye wo nkwa.
english:
Then I myself will admit to you
    that your own right hand can save you.

twi: “Hwɛ susono,nea meyɛɛ no kaa wo hona ɔwe sare te sɛ nantwi.
english:
“Look at Behemoth,
    which I made along with you
    and which feeds on grass like an ox.

twi: Hwɛ ahoɔden a ɔwɔ wɔ nʼasen mune ahoɔden a ɛwɔ ne yafunu so were mu!
english:
What strength it has in its loins,
    what power in the muscles of its belly!

twi: Ne dua hinhim sɛ sida;ne srɛ mu ntin yɛ peperee.
english:
Its tail sways like a cedar;
    the sinews of its thighs are close-knit.

twi: Ne nnompe te sɛ kɔbere mfrafrae dorobɛn,nʼabasa ne ne nʼanan te sɛ nnade praban.
english:
Its bones are tubes of bronze,
    its limbs like rods of iron.

twi: Odi Onyankopɔn nsa ano adwuma mu kan,nanso ne Yɛfo betumi de nʼafoa akɔ ne so.
english:
It ranks first among the works of God,
    yet its Maker can approach it with his sword.

twi: Nkoko fifi wɔn nnɔbae ma no,na wuram mmoa nyinaa goru bɛn hɔ.
english:
The hills bring it their produce,
    and all the wild animals play nearby.

twi: Nsɔensɔe nnua ase na ɔda,na dontori mu demmire akata no so.
english:
Under the lotus plants it lies,
    hidden among the reeds in the marsh.

twi: Nsɔensɔe nwini no kata ne so;na nsunoa nnua twa ne ho hyia.
english:
The lotuses conceal it in their shadow;
    the poplars by the stream surround it.

twi: Nsu nworoso nhaw no;mpo sɛ Yordan bobɔ ba nʼano a, onni ɔhaw.
english:
A raging river does not alarm it;
    it is secure, though the Jordan should surge against its mouth.

twi: Obi betumi akyere no animono;anaa obi betumi de afiri ayi no na wabɔre ne hwene mu ana?
english:
Can anyone capture it by the eyes,
    or trap it and pierce its nose?

twi: “So wubetumi de darewa atwe ɔdɛnkyɛmmirampɔnanaa wubetumi de hama akyekyere ne tɛkrɛma?
english:
“Can you pull in Leviathan with a fishhook
    or tie down its tongue with a rope?

twi: So wubetumi de hama afa ne hwenem,anaasɛ wubetumi de darewa aso nʼabogye mu?
english:
Can you put a cord through its nose
    or pierce its jaw with a hook?

twi: Ɔbɛkɔ so asrɛ wo sɛ hu no mmɔbɔ ana?Ɔne wo bɛkasa brɛoo ana?
english:
Will it keep begging you for mercy?
    Will it speak to you with gentle words?

twi: Ɔbɛpene ne wo ayɛ apamama wode no ayɛ wʼakoa afebɔɔ ana?
english:
Will it make an agreement with you
    for you to take it as your slave for life?

twi: Wubetumi de no ayɛ abɛbɛ te sɛ anomaaanaa wubetumi asa no hama de no ama wo mmabea?
english:
Can you make a pet of it like a bird
    or put it on a leash for the young women in your house?

twi: So aguadifo bɛpɛ sɛ wode no bedi nsesagua?Wɔbɛkyekyɛ ne mu ama aguadifo ana?
english:
Will traders barter for it?
    Will they divide it up among the merchants?

twi: Wubetumi de mpeaw awowɔ ne were muanaasɛ wode mpataa mpɛmɛ bɛwowɔ ne ti ho?
english:
Can you fill its hide with harpoons
    or its head with fishing spears?

twi: Wode wo nsa ka no a,wobɛkae sɛnea ɔbɛwosow ne ho, nti worenyɛ saa bio!
english:
If you lay a hand on it,
    you will remember the struggle and never do it again!

twi: Ɔkwan biara nni hɔ a wobɛfa so akyere no;ani a ɛbɔ ne so kɛkɛ no ma nnipa dwudwo.
english:
Any hope of subduing it is false;
    the mere sight of it is overpowering.

twi: Obiara ntumi nsi ne bo nhwanyan no.Afei hena na obetumi ne me adi asi?
english:
No one is fierce enough to rouse it.
    Who then is able to stand against me?

twi: Hena na mede no ka a ɛsɛ sɛ mitua?Biribiara a ɛhyɛ ɔsoro ase no yɛ me de.
english:
Who has a claim against me that I must pay?
    Everything under heaven belongs to me.

twi: “Me werɛ remfi sɛ mɛka nʼakwaa,nʼahoɔden ne ne bɔbea fɛfɛ no ho asɛm.
english:
“I will not fail to speak of Leviathan’s limbs,
    its strength and its graceful form.

twi: Hena na obetumi aworɔw ne ho ahama,na hena na ɔde nnareka bɛkɔ ne ho?
english:
Who can strip off its outer coat?
    Who can penetrate its double coat of armor?

twi: Hena na obetumi abue nʼabogye,a ɛse a ɛyɛ hu ayɛ no ma no?
english:
Who dares open the doors of its mouth,
    ringed about with fearsome teeth?

twi: Nʼakyi wɔ bona a ɛsesa so,ɛtetare so a ɔkwan nna mu koraa;
english:
Its back has rows of shields
    tightly sealed together;

twi: sɛnea ɛtetare so fa no nti,mframa biara mfa ntam.
english:
each is so close to the next
    that no air can pass between.

twi: Ɛtoatoa mu denneennen aemu ntumi ntetew.
english:
They are joined fast to one another;
    they cling together and cannot be parted.

twi: Sɛ ɔnwansi a, ɛpepa gya;nʼaniwa aba te sɛ adekyeenim hann.
english:
Its snorting throws out flashes of light;
    its eyes are like the rays of dawn.

twi: Agyatɛn turuw fi nʼanomna nsramma turuturuw fi mu.
english:
Flames stream from its mouth;
    sparks of fire shoot out.

twi: Wusiw sen fi ne hwene mute sɛ ɔsɛn a esi gya so.
english:
Smoke pours from its nostrils
    as from a boiling pot over burning reeds.

twi: Ne home ma gyabiriw ano sɔ,na ogyaframa tu fi nʼanom.
english:
Its breath sets coals ablaze,
    and flames dart from its mouth.

twi: Ne kɔn mu wɔ ahoɔden ankasa;wɔn a wohu no no aba mu bu.
english:
Strength resides in its neck;
    dismay goes before it.

twi: Ne were a abubu agu so no yɛ peperee;ayɛ pemee a ɛnka ne ho.
english:
The folds of its flesh are tightly joined;
    they are firm and immovable.

twi: Ne koko so yɛ den sɛ ɔbotanɛyɛ den sɛ awiyammo.
english:
Its chest is hard as rock,
    hard as a lower millstone.

twi: Sɛ ɔsɔre a, ahoɔdenfo bɔ huboa;sɛ ɔwosow ne ho a woguan.
english:
When it rises up, the mighty are terrified;
    they retreat before its thrashing.

twi: Afoa wɔ no a, ɛnka no,peaw, pɛmɛ ne agyan nso saa ara.
english:
The sword that reaches it has no effect,
    nor does the spear or the dart or the javelin.

twi: Ɔfa dade sɛ wura bina kɔbere mfrafrae te sɛ dua a awu bi ma no.
english:
Iron it treats like straw
    and bronze like rotten wood.

twi: Agyan mma no nguan;ahwimmo mu aboa yɛ ntɛtɛ ma no.
english:
Arrows do not make it flee;
    slingstones are like chaff to it.

twi: Kontibaa te sɛ sare wɔ nʼani so;na ɔserew pɛmɛ nnyigyei.
english:
A club seems to it but a piece of straw;
    it laughs at the rattling of the lance.

twi: Abon a ano yɛ nnam tuatua ne yafunu so.Ɔtwe ne ho ase wɔ fam fa dontori mu a, eyiyi akam.
english:
Its undersides are jagged potsherds,
    leaving a trail in the mud like a threshing sledge.

twi: Ɔma bun mu huru sɛ nsu a ɛwɔ ɛsɛn muna onunu po mu sɛ srade a ɛwɔ kuku mu.
english:
It makes the depths churn like a boiling caldron
    and stirs up the sea like a pot of ointment.

twi: Nea ɔbɛfa no, ɛhɔ nsu no pa yerɛw yerɛw;na obi besusuw sɛ po bun adan ayɛ dwen.
english:
It leaves a glistening wake behind it;
    one would think the deep had white hair.

twi: Asase so biribiara ne no nsɛ.Ɔyɛ abɔde a onsuro hwee.
english:
Nothing on earth is its equal—
    a creature without fear.

twi: Ommu wɔn a wɔyɛ ahantan no mu biara;ɔyɛ wɔn a wɔyɛ ahomaso no nyinaa so hene.”
english:
It looks down on all that are haughty;
    it is king over all that are proud.”

twi: Hiob Bua AwuradeNa Hiob buaa Awurade se,
english: Then Job replied to the Lord:

twi: “Minim sɛ wutumi yɛ nneɛma nyinaa;obiara rentumi nsɛe wo nhyehyɛe.
english:
“I know that you can do all things;
    no purpose of yours can be thwarted.

twi: Wubisa se, ‘Hena ni a onni nimdeɛ nso osiw mʼafotu ho kwan?’Ampa ara mekaa nneɛma a mente ase no ho nsɛm,nneɛma a ɛyɛ nwonwa ma me.
english:
You asked, ‘Who is this that obscures my plans without knowledge?’
    Surely I spoke of things I did not understand,
    things too wonderful for me to know.

twi: “Wokae se, ‘Tie na menkasa;mebisa wo nsɛmna ɛsɛ sɛ woma me mmuae.’
Mate wo nka pɛn,na mprempren de, mʼani ahu wo.
english:
My ears had heard of you
    but now my eyes have seen you.

twi: Ɛno nti mibu me ho animtiaana mete mfutuma ne nsõ mu de kyerɛ mʼahonu.”
english:
Therefore I despise myself
    and repent in dust and ashes.”

twi: AwieiNa Awurade kaa nsɛm yi kyerɛɛ Hiob wiei no, Awurade ka kyerɛɛ Temanni Elifas se, “Me bo afuw wo ne wo nnamfonom baanu no, efisɛ moanka me ho asɛm a ɛyɛ nokware sɛnea me somfo Hiob kae no.
english: After the Lord had said these things to Job, he said to Eliphaz the Temanite, “I am angry with you and your two friends, because you have not spoken the truth about me, as my servant Job has.

twi: Afei, momfa anantwi ason ne adwennini ason, na monkɔ me somfo Hiob nkyɛn, na monkɔbɔ ɔhyew afɔre mma mo ho. Me somfo Hiob bɛbɔ mpae ama mo, na metie ne mpaebɔ no na merenyɛ mo sɛnea ɛfata mo nkwaseasɛm no, nsɛm a moka faa me ho no nyɛ nokware sɛnea me somfo Hiob yɛe no.”
english: So now take seven bulls and seven rams and go to my servant Job and sacrifice a burnt offering for yourselves. My servant Job will pray for you, and I will accept his prayer and not deal with you according to your folly. You have not spoken the truth about me, as my servant Job has.”

twi: Enti Temanni Elifas ne Suhini Bildad ne Naamani Sofar yɛɛ sɛnea Awurade hyɛɛ wɔn no; na Awurade tiee Hiob mpaebɔ.
english: So Eliphaz the Temanite, Bildad the Shuhite and Zophar the Naamathite did what the Lord told them; and the Lord accepted Job’s prayer.

twi: Hiob bɔɔ mpae maa ne nnamfonom akyi no, Awurade san yɛɛ no ɔdefo bio na ɔde nʼahode a na ɔwɔ kan no mmɔho abien maa no.
english: After Job had prayed for his friends, the Lord restored his fortunes and gave him twice as much as he had before.

twi: Afei, ne nuabarimanom, ne nuabeanom nyinaa ne obiara a na onim no dedaw no baa ne fi ne no bedidii. Wɔkyekyee ne werɛ wɔ amanehunu a Awurade ma ɔkɔɔ mu no ho, na wɔn mu biara brɛɛ no dwetɛ ne sikakɔkɔɔ kaa.
english: All his brothers and sisters and everyone who had known him before came and ate with him in his house. They comforted and consoled him over all the trouble the Lord had brought on him, and each one gave him a piece of silver and a gold ring.

twi: Awurade hyiraa Hiob nkwa awiei sen ne mfiase. Onyaa nguan mpem dunan, yoma mpem asia, anantwinini mpamho apem ne mfurum abere apem.
english: The Lord blessed the latter part of Job’s life more than the former part. He had fourteen thousand sheep, six thousand camels, a thousand yoke of oxen and a thousand donkeys.

twi: Bio onyaa mmabarima baason ne mmabea baasa.
english: And he also had seven sons and three daughters.

twi: Ɔtoo ne babea piesie no din Yemima, na nea odi so no Kesia na nea ɔto so abiɛsa no de Keren-Hapuk.
english: The first daughter he named Jemimah, the second Keziah and the third Keren-Happuch.

twi: Asase no so nyinaa, na mmaa biara nni hɔ a wɔn ho yɛ fɛ sɛ Hiob mmabea no, na wɔn agya de wɔn kaa wɔn nuabarimanom no ho maa wɔn agyapade.
english: Nowhere in all the land were there found women as beautiful as Job’s daughters, and their father granted them an inheritance along with their brothers.

twi: Eyi akyi no, Hiob dii mfirihyia ɔha aduanan; ohuu ne mma ne ne nenanom awo ntoatoaso anan.
english: After this, Job lived a hundred and forty years; he saw his children and their children to the fourth generation.

twi: Afei owui a na wabɔ akwakoraa pa ara.
english: And so Job died, an old man and full of years.

twi: Onyankopɔn Yɛ Yosua ƆkannifoMose a ɔyɛ Awurade somfo no wu akyi no, Awurade ka kyerɛɛ Nun babarima Yosua, Mose boafo no se,
english: After the death of Moses the servant of the Lord, the Lord said to Joshua son of Nun, Moses’ aide:

twi: “Afei a me somfo Mose awu no, ɛsɛ sɛ wudi me nkurɔfo no anim kotwa Asubɔnten Yordan kɔ asase a mede rema wɔn no so.
english: “Moses my servant is dead. Now then, you and all these people, get ready to cross the Jordan River into the land I am about to give to them—to the Israelites.

twi: Sɛnea mehyɛɛ Mose bɔ no, baabiara a wode wo nan besi no, mede bɛma wo.
english: I will give you every place where you set your foot, as I promised Moses.

twi: Efi Negeb sare a ɛwɔ anafo fam kosi Lebanon mmepɔw a ɛwɔ atifi fam, efi Asubɔnten Eufrate a ɛwɔ apuei fam kosi Ntam Po a ɛwɔ atɔe fam, ne Hetifo asase nyinaa.
english: Your territory will extend from the desert to Lebanon, and from the great river, the Euphrates—all the Hittite country—to the Mediterranean Sea in the west.

twi: Obiara rentumi nsɔre ntia wo, wo nkwanna nyinaa. Sɛnea na mekaa Mose ho no, saa ara na mɛka wo ho. Merennyaw wo na merempa wʼakyi da.
english: No one will be able to stand against you all the days of your life. As I was with Moses, so I will be with you; I will never leave you nor forsake you.

twi: Wo ho nyɛ den na yɛ nnam, efisɛ wubedi me nkurɔfo yi anim akɔfa asase a mekaa ntam sɛ mede bɛma wɔn agyanom no nyinaa.
english: Be strong and courageous, because you will lead these people to inherit the land I swore to their ancestors to give them.

twi: “Wo ho nyɛ den na yɛ nnam. Di mmara a Mose de maa wo no nyinaa so. Mfi ho, na wubedi nkonim biribiara a woyɛ mu.
english: “Be strong and very courageous. Be careful to obey all the law my servant Moses gave you; do not turn from it to the right or to the left, that you may be successful wherever you go.

twi: Sua saa Mmara Nhoma yi bere biara. Dwen ho awia ne anadwo, sɛnea ɛbɛma woayɛ biribiara a wɔakyerɛw wɔ mu no. Saa na ɛbɛma asi wo yiye.
english: Keep this Book of the Law always on your lips; meditate on it day and night, so that you may be careful to do everything written in it. Then you will be prosperous and successful.

twi: Mehyɛ wo sɛ, yɛ den na yɛ nnam! Nsuro, na mma wʼaba mu mmu, na Awurade wo Nyankopɔn ka wo ho baabiara a wobɛkɔ.”
english: Have I not commanded you? Be strong and courageous. Do not be afraid; do not be discouraged, for the Lord your God will be with you wherever you go.”

twi: Yosua Kyerɛ Nea Israelfo NyɛAfei, Yosua hyɛɛ Israel ntuanofo no se,
english: So Joshua ordered the officers of the people:

twi: “Momfa atenae no mu na monka nkyerɛ nnipa no ma wonsiesie wɔn nnuan. Nnansa akyi no, mubetwa Asubɔnten Yordan na moakɔfa asase a Awurade, mo Nyankopɔn, de ama mo no.”
english: “Go through the camp and tell the people, ‘Get your provisions ready. Three days from now you will cross the Jordan here to go in and take possession of the land the Lord your God is giving you for your own.’”

twi: Afei Yosua frɛɛ Ruben ne Gad mmusuakuw ne Manase abusua no fa. Ɔka kyerɛɛ wɔn se,
english: But to the Reubenites, the Gadites and the half-tribe of Manasseh, Joshua said,

twi: “Monkae ahyɛde a Awurade somfo Mose maa mo no: ‘Awurade, mo Nyankopɔn, rema mo ɔhome na ɔde asase yi ama mo.’
english: “Remember the command that Moses the servant of the Lord gave you after he said, ‘The Lord your God will give you rest by giving you this land.’

twi: Mo yerenom, mo mma ne mo anantwi bɛtena Yordan apuei fam ha. Nanso, mo akofo a wɔasiesie wɔn ho ama ɔkɔ no bedi mmusuakuw a aka no anim atwa Yordan, na wɔaboa ma wɔafa asase no. Mo ne wɔn ntena hɔ
english: Your wives, your children and your livestock may stay in the land that Moses gave you east of the Jordan, but all your fighting men, ready for battle, must cross over ahead of your fellow Israelites. You are to help them

twi: nkosi sɛ Awurade bɛma wɔn ɔhome sɛnea wayɛ ama mo no. Na wɔn nso bedi asase a Awurade, mo Nyankopɔn de rema wɔn no so. Ɛno ansa na mode Yordan apuei fam ha asase a Mose a ɔyɛ Awurade somfo de maa mo no, bɛyɛ mo atenae.”
english: until the Lord gives them rest, as he has done for you, and until they too have taken possession of the land the Lord your God is giving them. After that, you may go back and occupy your own land, which Moses the servant of the Lord gave you east of the Jordan toward the sunrise.”

twi: Wobuaa Yosua se, “Nea woahyɛ yɛn sɛ yɛnyɛ nyinaa yɛbɛyɛ, na baabiara a wobɛsoma yɛn nso, yɛbɛkɔ.
english: Then they answered Joshua, “Whatever you have commanded us we will do, and wherever you send us we will go.

twi: Yɛbɛyɛ osetie ama wo sɛnea yɛyɛ maa Mose no. Awurade wo Nyankopɔn, nni wʼakyi sɛnea odii Mose akyi no.
english: Just as we fully obeyed Moses, so we will obey you. Only may the Lord your God be with you as he was with Moses.

twi: Obiara a ɔbɛtew wʼasɛm so atua na wanni wʼahyɛde mu biara so no, wonkum no. Enti, hyɛ wo ho den na nya akokoduru!”
english: Whoever rebels against your word and does not obey it, whatever you may command them, will be put to death. Only be strong and courageous!”

twi: Rahab Bɔ Akwansrafo Ho BanAfei, Yosua somaa akwansrafo baanu wɔ kokoa mu fii Israelfo atenae a ɛwɔ Sitim. Ɔka kyerɛɛ wɔn se, “Monkɔsra asase a ɛda Yordan agya no, ne titiriw nea atwa Yeriko ho ahyia no.” Enti, mmarima baanu no sii mu koduu oguamanfo bi a ne din de Rahab fi, na wɔtenaa hɔ anadwo no.
english: Then Joshua son of Nun secretly sent two spies from Shittim. “Go, look over the land,” he said, “especially Jericho.” So they went and entered the house of a prostitute named Rahab and stayed there.

twi: Obi kɔka kyerɛɛ Yerikohene se, “Anadwo yi ara, Israelfo no bi aba ha a wɔrebɛsra asase yi.”
english: The king of Jericho was told, “Look, some of the Israelites have come here tonight to spy out the land.”

twi: Enti Yerikohene soma kɔɔ Rahab nkyɛn kɔka kyerɛɛ no se, “Fa mmarima a wɔabɛsoɛ wo no ma yɛn. Wɔyɛ akwansrafo a wɔrebɛsra yɛn asase yi ahwehwɛ ɔkwan a wɔbɛfa so atow ahyɛ yɛn so.”
english: So the king of Jericho sent this message to Rahab: “Bring out the men who came to you and entered your house, because they have come to spy out the whole land.”

twi: Rahab a na ɔde mmarima baanu no asie no buae se, “Mmarima no baa me ha de, nanso minnim faako a wofi bae.
english: But the woman had taken the two men and hidden them. She said, “Yes, the men came to me, but I did not know where they had come from.

twi: Ade reyɛ asa a wɔrebɛtoto kuropɔn no apon mu no na wɔkɔe, nso manhu faako a wɔfae. Sɛ moyɛ ntɛm tiw wɔn a, ebia, mobɛto wɔn.”
english: At dusk, when it was time to close the city gate, they left. I don’t know which way they went. Go after them quickly. You may catch up with them.”

twi: (Nanso, na ɔde wɔn akɔhyɛ ɔdan atifi, akohintaw ɔfo a waboa ano akuwakuw ase.)
english: (But she had taken them up to the roof and hidden them under the stalks of flax she had laid out on the roof.)

twi: Enti, ɔhene asomafo no sii mu sɛ wɔrekɔhwehwɛ akwansrafo no wɔ ɔkwan a ɛkɔ Asubɔnten Yordan asutwabea hɔ. Asomafo no fi hɔ ara pɛ na wɔtotoo kuropɔn no apon mu.
english: So the men set out in pursuit of the spies on the road that leads to the fords of the Jordan, and as soon as the pursuers had gone out, the gate was shut.

twi: Ansa na akwansrafo no rebɛda anadwo no, Rahab kɔɔ ɔdan no atifi ne wɔn kɔkasae se,
english: Before the spies lay down for the night, she went up on the roof

twi: “Minim sɛ Awurade de saa asase yi ama mo. Yɛn nyinaa suro mo. Yɛn mu biara abɔ huboa.
english: and said to them, “I know that the Lord has given you this land and that a great fear of you has fallen on us, so that all who live in this country are melting in fear because of you.

twi: Yɛate sɛnea Awurade maa Po Kɔkɔɔ no yow ma munyaa kwan faa mu bere a mufii Misraim no. Na yenim sɛnea moyɛɛ Sihon ne Og a na wɔyɛ Amorifo ahemfo wɔ Asubɔnten Yordan apuei fam no ne sɛnea mosɛee wɔn nkurɔfo pasaa no.
english: We have heard how the Lord dried up the water of the Red Sea for you when you came out of Egypt, and what you did to Sihon and Og, the two kings of the Amorites east of the Jordan, whom you completely destroyed.

twi: Ɛnyɛ nwonwa sɛ yɛn koma atu na yɛabɔ huboa. Obiara nni akokoduru a sɛ ɔte nsɛm a ɛte sɛɛ a, ɔbɛko. Na Awurade, mo Nyankopɔn no, ne otumfo Nyankopɔn a ɔwɔ ɔsorosoro ne asase ase.
english: When we heard of it, our hearts melted in fear and everyone’s courage failed because of you, for the Lord your God is God in heaven above and on the earth below.

twi: “Enti momfa Awurade nka ntam nkyerɛ me se, esiane sɛ maboa mo nti, mobɛyɛ me ne mʼabusuafo adom. Momfa biribi nsi mo bɔhyɛ so se,
english: “Now then, please swear to me by the Lord that you will show kindness to my family, because I have shown kindness to you. Give me a sure sign

twi: moko fa Yeriko a, morenkum me ne mʼagya ne me na, me nuabarimanom ne nuabeanom ne wɔn ho nnipa nyinaa.”
english: that you will spare the lives of my father and mother, my brothers and sisters, and all who belong to them—and that you will save us from death.”

twi: Mmarima no penee so kae se, “Yɛde yɛn nkwa si yɛn bɔhyɛ so. Sɛ woanyi yɛn amma na sɛ Awurade de asase no ma yɛn a, yebedi yɛn bɔhyɛ so.”
english: “Our lives for your lives!” the men assured her. “If you don’t tell what we are doing, we will treat you kindly and faithfully when the Lord gives us the land.”

twi: Esiane sɛ wosii Rahab fi sii kurow no fasu so nti, ɔde hama sian wɔn faa mfɛnsere mu maa wosii fam.
english: So she let them down by a rope through the window, for the house she lived in was part of the city wall.

twi: Afei ɔka kyerɛɛ wɔn se, “Munguan mfa bepɔw so man no so. Momfa mo ho nsie nnansa kosi sɛ atiwfo no a wɔrehwehwɛ mo no bɛsan wɔn akyi ansa na moakɔ mo kwan.”
english: She said to them, “Go to the hills so the pursuers will not find you. Hide yourselves there three days until they return, and then go on your way.”

twi: Ansa na mmarima no bɛkɔ no, wɔka kyerɛɛ no se, “Yɛbɛbɔ mo nkwa ho ban
english: Now the men had said to her, “This oath you made us swear will not be binding on us

twi: na mmom, gyaw hama kɔkɔɔ a ɛsɛn wo mfɛnsere ano no na ma wʼabusuafo a ɛyɛ wʼagya, wo na, wo nuabarimanom ne wɔn abusuafo nyinaa mmɛhyɛ ofi no mu a wɔnnkɔ baabiara.
english: unless, when we enter the land, you have tied this scarlet cord in the window through which you let us down, and unless you have brought your father and mother, your brothers and all your family into your house.

twi: Sɛ wopue si abɔnten a, wobekum wɔn nyinaa na obi ntumi mmɔ yɛn sobo sɛ yɛabu yɛn ntam so. Na yɛka ntam sɛ, obiara a ɔhyɛ ofi yi mu no, wɔrenkum no. Obiara nso renteɛ ne nsa wɔ wɔn so.
english: If any of them go outside your house into the street, their blood will be on their own heads; we will not be responsible. As for those who are in the house with you, their blood will be on our head if a hand is laid on them.

twi: Na sɛ wudi yɛn huammɔ de a, ntam yi nnkyekyere yɛn ɔkwan biara so.”
english: But if you tell what we are doing, we will be released from the oath you made us swear.”

twi: Ɔbea no buae se, “Mepene mo nhyehyɛe no nyinaa so.”Ogyaa wɔn kwan, bere a hama kɔkɔɔ no sɛn ofi no mfɛnsere no ano.
english:
“Agreed,” she replied. “Let it be as you say.”
So she sent them away, and they departed. And she tied the scarlet cord in the window.

twi: Akwansrafo no kɔɔ bepɔw asase no so kɔtenaa hɔ nnansa. Atiwfo no hwehwɛɛ ɔkwan no so baabiara, san kɔɔ wɔn kurom a wɔanhu akwansrafo no wɔ baabiara.
english: When they left, they went into the hills and stayed there three days, until the pursuers had searched all along the road and returned without finding them.

twi: Afei akwansrafo baanu no sian fii bepɔw asase no so twaa Asubɔnten Yordan bɛkaa nsɛm a ɛtoo wɔn nyinaa kyerɛɛ Yosua.
english: Then the two men started back. They went down out of the hills, forded the river and came to Joshua son of Nun and told him everything that had happened to them.

twi: Wɔkae se, “Ampa ara Awurade de asase no nyinaa bɛma yɛn, efisɛ yɛn ho hu atɔ nnipa a wɔwɔ asase no so nyinaa so.”
english: They said to Joshua, “The Lord has surely given the whole land into our hands; all the people are melting in fear because of us.”

twi: Israelfo Twa Asubɔnten YordanAde kyee anɔpahema no, Yosua ne Israelfo no nyinaa tu fii Sitim koduu Asubɔnten Yordan nsunoa, baabi a wɔtenaa nna kakra ansa na wɔretwa.
english: Early in the morning Joshua and all the Israelites set out from Shittim and went to the Jordan, where they camped before crossing over.

twi: Nnansa akyi no, Israelfo ntuanofo no faa atenae hɔ nyinaa
english: After three days the officers went throughout the camp,

twi: maa nnipa no akwankyerɛ sɛ, “Sɛ muhu sɛ Lewifo asɔfo no so Awurade, mo Nyankopɔn Apam Adaka no a, munni wɔn akyi.
english: giving orders to the people: “When you see the ark of the covenant of the Lord your God, and the Levitical priests carrying it, you are to move out from your positions and follow it.

twi: Esiane sɛ momfaa ha da no nti, wɔbɛkyerɛ mo kwan. Momma ɔkwansin fa nna mo ne wɔn ntam, na moammɛn Apam Adaka no. Monhwɛ na moammɛn ho.”
english: Then you will know which way to go, since you have never been this way before. But keep a distance of about two thousand cubits between you and the ark; do not go near it.”

twi: Yosua ka kyerɛɛ nkurɔfo no se, “Munnwira mo ho, efisɛ, ɔkyena Awurade bɛyɛ anwonwade wɔ mo mu.”
english: Joshua told the people, “Consecrate yourselves, for tomorrow the Lord will do amazing things among you.”

twi: Anɔpa no, Yosua ka kyerɛɛ asɔfo no se, “Mompagyaw Apam Adaka no na momfa nni nnipa no anim ntwa asubɔnten no.” Ɛno nti wosii mu.
english: Joshua said to the priests, “Take up the ark of the covenant and pass on ahead of the people.” So they took it up and went ahead of them.

twi: Awurade ka kyerɛɛ Yosua se, “Nnɛ, mefi ase ayɛ wo ɔkɛse wɔ Israelfo no nyinaa ani so. Na ɛbɛma wɔahu sɛ, meka wo ho sɛnea na meka Mose ho no.
english: And the Lord said to Joshua, “Today I will begin to exalt you in the eyes of all Israel, so they may know that I am with you as I was with Moses.

twi: Fa saa akwankyerɛ yi ma asɔfo a wɔso Apam Adaka no: ‘Sɛ mudu Asubɔnten Yordan nsunoa hɔ a, monnantew nkɔ nsu no mu kakra na munnyina.’ ”
english: Tell the priests who carry the ark of the covenant: ‘When you reach the edge of the Jordan’s waters, go and stand in the river.’”

twi: Na Yosua ka kyerɛɛ Israelfo no se, “Mommra mmetie asɛm a Awurade, mo Nyankopɔn aka.
english: Joshua said to the Israelites, “Come here and listen to the words of the Lord your God.

twi: Nnɛ mubehu sɛ Onyankopɔn teasefo no ka mo ho. Ampa ara ɔbɛpam Kanaanfo, Hetifo, Hewifo, Perisifo, Girgasifo, Amorifo ne Yebusifo.
english: This is how you will know that the living God is among you and that he will certainly drive out before you the Canaanites, Hittites, Hivites, Perizzites, Girgashites, Amorites and Jebusites.

twi: Munnwen ho! Apam Adaka a ɛyɛ Awurade a asase nyinaa yɛ ne de no bedi mo anim de mo atwa Asubɔnten Yordan.
english: See, the ark of the covenant of the Lord of all the earth will go into the Jordan ahead of you.

twi: Afei, munyiyi nnipa dumien a ɔbaako biara fi mmusuakuw dumien no mu.
english: Now then, choose twelve men from the tribes of Israel, one from each tribe.

twi: Asɔfo no bɛsoa Awurade a ɔyɛ asase nyinaa wura no Adaka no. Sɛ wɔn nan nya si asu no mu ara pɛ, nsu no betwa afi atifi ama ano aboa wɔ hɔ.”
english: And as soon as the priests who carry the ark of the Lord—the Lord of all the earth—set foot in the Jordan, its waters flowing downstream will be cut off and stand up in a heap.”

twi: Bere a nnipa no sɔree sɛ wɔrekotwa Yordan no, asɔfo a na wɔso Apam Adaka no dii wɔn anim.
english: So when the people broke camp to cross the Jordan, the priests carrying the ark of the covenant went ahead of them.

twi: Na ɛyɛ otwabere mu nti na Yordan no ayiri aba nsunoa. Nanso, asɔfo a wɔso Adaka no anan sii nsu no ano pɛ,
english: Now the Jordan is at flood stage all during harvest. Yet as soon as the priests who carried the ark reached the Jordan and their feet touched the water’s edge,

twi: nsu no ano fitii ase boaa wɔ nʼatifi fam, baabi a wɔfrɛ hɔ Adam a ɛbɛn Saretan. Na nsu a ɛwɔ anafo no nso sen koguu Nkyene Po no mu kosii sɛ asu no subon no yowee. Enti, nnipa no nyinaa twaa wɔ beae bi a ɛbɛn Yeriko kuropɔn no.
english: the water from upstream stopped flowing. It piled up in a heap a great distance away, at a town called Adam in the vicinity of Zarethan, while the water flowing down to the Sea of the Arabah (that is, the Dead Sea) was completely cut off. So the people crossed over opposite Jericho.

twi: Saa bere no mu, asɔfo a wɔso Awurade Apam Adaka no gyinaa asase kesee so wɔ subon no mfimfini maa nnipa no nyinaa twaa mu. Wɔtwɛn wɔ hɔ kosii sɛ obiara faa asase kesee so twaa Yordan.
english: The priests who carried the ark of the covenant of the Lord stopped in the middle of the Jordan and stood on dry ground, while all Israel passed by until the whole nation had completed the crossing on dry ground.

twi: Abo Dumien NkaedumBere a ɔman no nyinaa twaa Yordan wiei no, Awurade ka kyerɛɛ Yosua se,
english: When the whole nation had finished crossing the Jordan, the Lord said to Joshua,

twi: “Yiyi mmarima dumien fi ɔmanfo no mu a ɔbaako biara fi abusuakuw no bi mu,
english: “Choose twelve men from among the people, one from each tribe,

twi: na ka kyerɛ wɔn se, wɔmfa abo dumien mfi Yordan mfimfini nifa so wɔ faako a na asɔfo no gyina hɔ, na wɔnsoa mfa ntwa mmra mmegu faako a mobɛtena anadwo yi.”
english: and tell them to take up twelve stones from the middle of the Jordan, from right where the priests are standing, and carry them over with you and put them down at the place where you stay tonight.”

twi: Ɛnna Yosua frɛɛ mmarima dumien a oyii wɔn fii Israelfo no mu no a ɔbaako biara fi abusuakuw bi mu no,
english: So Joshua called together the twelve men he had appointed from the Israelites, one from each tribe,

twi: na ɔka kyerɛɛ wɔn se, “Munkodi Awurade, mo Nyankopɔn, adaka no anim mfa nkɔ Yordan mfimfini. Ɔbaako biara mfa ɔbo nto ne bati so sɛnea Israelfo mmusuakuw no dodow te,
english: and said to them, “Go over before the ark of the Lord your God into the middle of the Jordan. Each of you is to take up a stone on his shoulder, according to the number of the tribes of the Israelites,

twi: na ɛnyɛ nsɛnkyerɛnne wɔ mo mu. Sɛ daakye bi, mo mma bisa mo se, ‘Saa abo yi ase kyerɛ dɛn’ a,
english: to serve as a sign among you. In the future, when your children ask you, ‘What do these stones mean?’

twi: monka nkyerɛ wɔn se, Yordan gyaee sen, gyinae wɔ Awurade apam adaka no anim, bere a Awurade apam adaka no retwa Yordan asubɔnten no. Saa abo yi bɛyɛ nkae ade ama Israelfo daa nyinaa.”
english: tell them that the flow of the Jordan was cut off before the ark of the covenant of the Lord. When it crossed the Jordan, the waters of the Jordan were cut off. These stones are to be a memorial to the people of Israel forever.”

twi: Enti, mmarima no yɛɛ sɛnea Yosua kyerɛɛ wɔn no. Wɔfaa abo dumien fii Asubɔnten Yordan mfimfini a ɔbo baako biara gyina hɔ ma abusuakuw baako, sɛnea Awurade hyɛɛ Yosua no. Wɔsoa de kɔɔ faako a wɔtenaa hɔ anadwo no na wosii nkaedum wɔ hɔ.
english: So the Israelites did as Joshua commanded them. They took twelve stones from the middle of the Jordan, according to the number of the tribes of the Israelites, as the Lord had told Joshua; and they carried them over with them to their camp, where they put them down.

twi: Yosua nso de abo dumien sii nkaedum wɔ Yordan mfimfini wɔ faako a na asɔfo a wɔso apam Adaka no gyinae no. Ɛwɔ hɔ de besi nnɛ.
english: Joshua set up the twelve stones that had been in the middle of the Jordan at the spot where the priests who carried the ark of the covenant had stood. And they are there to this day.

twi: Asɔfo a na wɔso adaka no gyinaa asu no mfimfini hɔ ara kosii sɛ wɔyɛɛ Awurade ahyɛde a ɔnam Mose so de maa Yosua no nyinaa. Saa bere no, nnipa no yɛɛ ntɛm twaa asu no koduu ne konkɔn so.
english: Now the priests who carried the ark remained standing in the middle of the Jordan until everything the Lord had commanded Joshua was done by the people, just as Moses had directed Joshua. The people hurried over,

twi: Na bere a obiara duu asu no fa hɔ no, asɔfo no nso de Awurade adaka no twa kɔɔ hɔ bi.
english: and as soon as all of them had crossed, the ark of the Lord and the priests came to the other side while the people watched.

twi: Na akofo a wɔahyɛ wɔn akode a wofi Ruben abusuakuw mu, Gad abusuakuw mu ne Manase abusuakuw fa mu akofo no dii Israelfo no anim twaa Yordan sɛnea Mose kyerɛɛ wɔn no pɛpɛɛpɛ.
english: The men of Reuben, Gad and the half-tribe of Manasseh crossed over, ready for battle, in front of the Israelites, as Moses had directed them.

twi: Saa akofo yi, na wɔn dodow bɛyɛ mpem aduanan a wɔasiesie wɔn ho ama ɔko. Wotwa kɔɔ Yeriko asase so wɔ Awurade anim.
english: About forty thousand armed for battle crossed over before the Lord to the plains of Jericho for war.

twi: Saa da no, Awurade yɛɛ Yosua kɛse wɔ Israelfo no nyinaa anim; na Yosua nna a aka no nyinaa, Israelfo de obu ne nidi maa no sɛnea wɔde obu ne nidi maa Mose no.
english: That day the Lord exalted Joshua in the sight of all Israel; and they stood in awe of him all the days of his life, just as they had stood in awe of Moses.

twi: Na Awurade ka kyerɛɛ Yosua se,
english: Then the Lord said to Joshua,

twi: “Hyɛ asɔfo a Awurade apam adaka no so wɔn no sɛ, womfi nsubon no mu hɔ mmra.”
english: “Command the priests carrying the ark of the covenant law to come up out of the Jordan.”

twi: Enti, Yosua hyɛɛ wɔn.
english: So Joshua commanded the priests, “Come up out of the Jordan.”

twi: Na bere a asɔfo a wɔso Awurade apam adaka no fii nsubon no mu ara pɛ na Asubɔnten Yordan san ka sram so tɛnn te sɛ kan no.
english: And the priests came up out of the river carrying the ark of the covenant of the Lord. No sooner had they set their feet on the dry ground than the waters of the Jordan returned to their place and ran at flood stage as before.

twi: Ɔsram a edi kan no da ɛto so du no nnipa no foro fii Yordan kɔbɔɔ atenae wɔ Gilgal, Yeriko apuei fam hye so.
english: On the tenth day of the first month the people went up from the Jordan and camped at Gilgal on the eastern border of Jericho.

twi: Gilgal hɔ na Yosua boaa abo dumien a wɔde fi Asubɔnten Yordan mu bae no ano.
english: And Joshua set up at Gilgal the twelve stones they had taken out of the Jordan.

twi: Afei, Yosua ka kyerɛɛ Israelfo no se, “Daakye bi mo mma bebisa se, ‘Saa abo yi kyerɛ dɛn?’
english: He said to the Israelites, “In the future when your descendants ask their parents, ‘What do these stones mean?’

twi: Na mo nso moaka akyerɛ wɔn se, ‘Ɛha ne beae a Israelfo twaa Yordan wɔ asase wosee so no.’
english: tell them, ‘Israel crossed the Jordan on dry ground.’

twi: Awurade, mo Nyankopɔn, maa asu no yowee wɔ mo anim, na ɔkɔɔ so ma ɛyowee ara kosii sɛ mo nyinaa twae, sɛnea ɔyɛɛ Po Kɔkɔɔ no. Ɔmaa no yowee ara kosii sɛ yɛn nyinaa twae.
english: For the Lord your God dried up the Jordan before you until you had crossed over. The Lord your God did to the Jordan what he had done to the Red Sea when he dried it up before us until we had crossed over.

twi: Ɔyɛɛ eyi sɛnea aman a wɔwɔ wiase nyinaa behu Awurade tumi na mo nso moasuro Awurade, mo Nyankopɔn, daa nyinaa.”
english: He did this so that all the peoples of the earth might know that the hand of the Lord is powerful and so that you might always fear the Lord your God.”

twi: Bere a Amorifo ahemfo nyinaa a wɔwɔ Yordan atɔe fam ne Kanaanfo ahemfo a wɔwɔ Po Kɛse no mpoano tee sɛ Awurade ama Asubɔnten Yordan ayow wɔ Israelfo anim ama wɔatwa no, wɔn koma tui, na ehu kyekyeree wɔn.
english: Now when all the Amorite kings west of the Jordan and all the Canaanite kings along the coast heard how the Lord had dried up the Jordan before the Israelites until they had crossed over, their hearts melted in fear and they no longer had the courage to face the Israelites.

twi: Israelfo San Yɛ Apam No Ho AmanneSaa bere no, Awurade ka kyerɛɛ Yosua se, “Yɛ kyerɛwbo asekan na fa twa Israelfo no twetia bio.”
english: At that time the Lord said to Joshua, “Make flint knives and circumcise the Israelites again.”

twi: Enti, Yosua yɛɛ kyerɛwbo asekan no de twitwaa Israelfo nyinaa twetia wɔ Aaralot koko so.
english: So Joshua made flint knives and circumcised the Israelites at Gibeath Haaraloth.

twi: Na ɛsɛ sɛ Yosua twitwa wɔn twetia, efisɛ mmarima a na wɔanyinyin a wotumi ko bere a wofii Misraim no nyinaa awuwu wɔ sare no so.
english: Now this is why he did so: All those who came out of Egypt—all the men of military age—died in the wilderness on the way after leaving Egypt.

twi: Nnipa a wotu fii Misraim bae no, na wɔatwitwa wɔn nyinaa twetia, nanso wɔn a wɔwowoo wɔn wɔ sare no so wɔ akwantu bere no mu no de, na wontwitwaa wɔn twetia ɛ.
english: All the people that came out had been circumcised, but all the people born in the wilderness during the journey from Egypt had not.

twi: Israelfo no kyinkyinii wɔ sare no so mfe aduanan kosii sɛ mmarima a wotumi ko bere a wɔrefi Misraim no nyinaa wuwui. Efisɛ wɔyɛɛ asoɔden maa Awurade, na ɔkaa ntam sɛ ɔremma wɔn ani nhu asase a waka ntam sɛ ɔde bɛma wɔn no so, asase a nufusu ne ɛwo sen wɔ so no.
english: The Israelites had moved about in the wilderness forty years until all the men who were of military age when they left Egypt had died, since they had not obeyed the Lord. For the Lord had sworn to them that they would not see the land he had solemnly promised their ancestors to give us, a land flowing with milk and honey.

twi: Enti Yosua twitwaa wɔn mmabarima a wontwaa wɔn twetia no twetia bere a na wɔrekɔ Bɔhyɛ Asase no so no. Eyinom yɛ wɔn a na wɔanyinyin a wotumi si wɔn agyanom anan mu no.
english: So he raised up their sons in their place, and these were the ones Joshua circumcised. They were still uncircumcised because they had not been circumcised on the way.

twi: Otwaa mmarima no nyinaa twetia wiei no, wogyee wɔn ahome wɔ atenae hɔ kosii sɛ wɔn ho tɔɔ wɔn.
english: And after the whole nation had been circumcised, they remained where they were in camp until they were healed.

twi: Afei, Awurade ka kyerɛɛ Yosua se, “Nnɛ mayi mo nkoayɛ wɔ Misraim ho animguase no afi mo so.” Ɛno nti, wɔfrɛ beae hɔ Gilgal de besi nnɛ.
english: Then the Lord said to Joshua, “Today I have rolled away the reproach of Egypt from you.” So the place has been called Gilgal to this day.

twi: Bere a Israelfo no wɔ Gilgal atenae hɔ wɔ Yeriko asase pradada no so no, wodii Twam Afahyɛ no wɔ ɔsram a edi kan no da a ɛto so dunan no anwummere. Saa ɔsram no na wɔde kae bere a wotu fii Misraim no.
english: On the evening of the fourteenth day of the month, while camped at Gilgal on the plains of Jericho, the Israelites celebrated the Passover.

twi: Da no ara, wofii ase dii apiti ne aburow a wɔatoto a wotwa fii asase no so.
english: The day after the Passover, that very day, they ate some of the produce of the land: unleavened bread and roasted grain.

twi: Mana amma da no na wɔanhu bi nso bio. Enti, efi saa bere no, Israelfo no dii Kanaan asase no so nnɔbae.
english: The manna stopped the day after they ate this food from the land; there was no longer any manna for the Israelites, but that year they ate the produce of Canaan.

twi: Awurade Sahene Hyia YosuaBere a Yosua rebɛn Yeriko kuropɔn mu no, ɔpagyaw nʼani huu ɔbarima bi a okura afoa rehyia no. Yosua kɔɔ ne nkyɛn bisaa no se, “Wowɔ yɛn afa anaa woyɛ ɔtamfo?”
english: Now when Joshua was near Jericho, he looked up and saw a man standing in front of him with a drawn sword in his hand. Joshua went up to him and asked, “Are you for us or for our enemies?”

twi: Na ɔbarima no buaa se, “Menyɛ wɔn mu biara, meyɛ Awurade nsraadɔm so safohene.” Yosua tee eyi no, ɔdaa hɔ de nʼanim butuu fam wɔ nidi mu na ɔkae se, “Kyerɛ me nea menyɛ, dɛn na wopɛ sɛ wo somfo yɛ?”
english: “Neither,” he replied, “but as commander of the army of the Lord I have now come.” Then Joshua fell facedown to the ground in reverence, and asked him, “What message does my Lord have for his servant?”

twi: Awurade nsraadɔm safohene no buae se, “Yi wo mpaboa na ɛha yɛ asase kronkron.” Na Yosua yɛɛ nea ɔkyerɛɛ no sɛ ɔnyɛ no.
english: The commander of the Lord’s army replied, “Take off your sandals, for the place where you are standing is holy.” And Joshua did so.

twi: Wɔfa YerikoWɔtotoo Yeriko apon mu papee, efisɛ na wosuro Israelfo no. Wɔamma obiara kwan ma wankɔ mu anaa wamfi adi.
english: Now the gates of Jericho were securely barred because of the Israelites. No one went out and no one came in.

twi: Awurade ka kyerɛɛ Yosua se, “Mede Yeriko, ɛhɔ hene ne ɛhɔ akofo nyinaa ahyɛ wo nsa.
english: Then the Lord said to Joshua, “See, I have delivered Jericho into your hands, along with its king and its fighting men.

twi: Ma wo nsraadɔm no nyinaa mmɔ nsra ntwa kuropɔn no ho nhyia pɛnkoro da biara nnansia.
english: March around the city once with all the armed men. Do this for six days.

twi: Asɔfo baason a wokurakura adwennini mmɛn abɛn bedi Adaka no anim. Da a ɛto so ason no, ɛsɛ sɛ mobɔ nsra twa kuropɔn no ho mpɛn ason, a asɔfo no rehyɛn mmɛn no.
english: Have seven priests carry trumpets of rams’ horns in front of the ark. On the seventh day, march around the city seven times, with the priests blowing the trumpets.

twi: Sɛ mote sɛ asɔfo no hyɛn mmɛn no denneennen ma ɛkyɛ a, nnipa no nyinaa mmɔ nnye so. Afei kuropɔn no afasu nyinaa bedwiriw agu fam, na nnipa no betumi atow ahyɛ kuropɔn no so.”
english: When you hear them sound a long blast on the trumpets, have the whole army give a loud shout; then the wall of the city will collapse and the army will go up, everyone straight in.”

twi: Na Yosua frɛɛ asɔfo no ka kyerɛɛ wɔn se, “Momfa Apam Adaka no na mo mu baason nni anim a wokurakura mmɛn.”
english: So Joshua son of Nun called the priests and said to them, “Take up the ark of the covenant of the Lord and have seven priests carry trumpets in front of it.”

twi: Enti, ɔhyɛɛ nnipa no se, “Mommɔ nsra mfa kuropɔn no ho na wɔn a wokurakura akode no bedi Awurade adaka no anim.”
english: And he ordered the army, “Advance! March around the city, with an armed guard going ahead of the ark of the Lord.”

twi: Yosua kasa kyerɛɛ nnipa no wiei no, asɔfo baason a wokurakura mmɛn no fii ase bɔɔ nsra wɔ Awurade anim a wɔrehyɛn mmɛn no. Na asɔfo a wɔso Awurade Apam Adaka no dii wɔn akyi.
english: When Joshua had spoken to the people, the seven priests carrying the seven trumpets before the Lord went forward, blowing their trumpets, and the ark of the Lord’s covenant followed them.

twi: Wɔn a wokurakura akode no bi bɔɔ nsra wɔ asɔfo no a wɔrehyɛn mmɛn no anim, na bi nso bɔɔ nsra wɔ asɔfo a wɔso Adaka no akyi, bere a asɔfo no gu so rehyɛn mmɛn no.
english: The armed guard marched ahead of the priests who blew the trumpets, and the rear guard followed the ark. All this time the trumpets were sounding.
