twi: Mose yɛɛ sɛnea Awurade hyɛɛ no no, na wohyiaa wɔ Ahyiae Ntamadan kwan no ano.
english: Moses did as the Lord commanded him, and the assembly gathered at the entrance to the tent of meeting.

twi: Mose ka kyerɛɛ wɔn se, “Ade a merebɛyɛ yi, Awurade na wahyɛ me sɛ menyɛ.”
english: Moses said to the assembly, “This is what the Lord has commanded to be done.”

twi: Afei, Mose de Aaron ne ne mmabarima no baa anim, na ɔde nsu hohoroo wɔn ho.
english: Then Moses brought Aaron and his sons forward and washed them with water.

twi: Ɔde Aaron atade sononko bi a ne mmeamu ka ho ne batakari a asɔfotade a wɔde tam a ɛyɛ fɛ ayɛ nʼabɔso hyɛɛ no.
english: He put the tunic on Aaron, tied the sash around him, clothed him with the robe and put the ephod on him. He also fastened the ephod with a decorative waistband, which he tied around him.

twi: Afei, Mose de adɛbo fam Aaron bo de Urim ne Tumim a ase ne hann ne pɛyɛ no hyɛɛ mu.
english: He placed the breastpiece on him and put the Urim and Thummim in the breastpiece.

twi: Ɔbɔɔ Aaron abotiri kɛse bi a ɛwɔ sika abɔanim sɛnea Awurade hyɛɛ no sɛ ɔnyɛ no ara pɛ.
english: Then he placed the turban on Aaron’s head and set the gold plate, the sacred emblem, on the front of it, as the Lord commanded Moses.

twi: Afei, Mose faa ɔsra ngo no de bi petee Ahyiae Ntamadan no ankasa ne biribiara a ɛwɔ mu ho de tew ne nyinaa ho.
english: Then Moses took the anointing oil and anointed the tabernacle and everything in it, and so consecrated them.

twi: Ɔpetee afɔremuka no so mpɛn ason. Afei, ɔpetee nkuku a ɛwɔ afɔremuka no so no ne hweaseammɔ ne ne ntaamu ho de tew ho.
english: He sprinkled some of the oil on the altar seven times, anointing the altar and all its utensils and the basin with its stand, to consecrate them.

twi: Afei, ohwiee ɔsra ngo no guu Aaron tirim de tew ne ho sɛ omfiti nʼadwuma ase.
english: He poured some of the anointing oil on Aaron’s head and anointed him to consecrate him.

twi: Nea edi hɔ ne sɛ, Mose de batakari hyehyɛɛ Aaron mmabarima a nkyekyeremu ne kyɛw ka ho, sɛnea Awurade hyɛɛ no sɛ ɔnyɛ no.
english: Then he brought Aaron’s sons forward, put tunics on them, tied sashes around them and fastened caps on them, as the Lord commanded Moses.

twi: Afei, ɔfaa nantwinini ba sɛ ɔde no rekɔbɔ bɔne ho afɔre. Aaron ne ne mmabarima de wɔn nsa guu aboa no apampam.
english: He then presented the bull for the sin offering, and Aaron and his sons laid their hands on its head.

twi: Mose kum no. Ɔde ne nsateaa baako bɔɔ ne mogya mu de yɛɛ afɔremuka mmɛn nan no ho ne afɔremuka no ankasa ho de tew ho, na ohwiee mogya no nkae no guu afɔremuka no ase de tew ho sɛ mpata.
english: Moses slaughtered the bull and took some of the blood, and with his finger he put it on all the horns of the altar to purify the altar. He poured out the rest of the blood at the base of the altar. So he consecrated it to make atonement for it.

twi: Ɔfaa nʼayamde ho srade ne ne mmerɛbo ho srade ne nʼasaabo abien no ne ɛho srade hyew ne nyinaa wɔ afɔremuka no so.
english: Moses also took all the fat around the internal organs, the long lobe of the liver, and both kidneys and their fat, and burned it on the altar.

twi: Nanso ɔhyew nantwinini ba no ne ne nwoma ne ne nsono wɔ nsraban no akyi sɛnea Awurade hyɛɛ Mose no.
english: But the bull with its hide and its flesh and its intestines he burned up outside the camp, as the Lord commanded Moses.

twi: Afei, ɔde odwennini no maa Awurade sɛ ɔhyew afɔre. Aaron ne ne mmabarima de wɔn nsa guu aboa no apampam.
english: He then presented the ram for the burnt offering, and Aaron and his sons laid their hands on its head.

twi: Na Mose kum no de ne mogya no bi petee afɔremuka no ho nyinaa.
english: Then Moses slaughtered the ram and splashed the blood against the sides of the altar.

twi: Otwitwaa odwennini no nam na ɔhyew asinasin no a ne ti ne ne srade ka ho.
english: He cut the ram into pieces and burned the head, the pieces and the fat.

twi: Na ɔde nsu hohoroo nʼayamde ne nʼanan no ho hyew no wɔ afɔremuka no so maa ne nyinaa hyew dwerɛbee. Na ɛyɛ ɔhyew afɔre, ehua a ɛsɔ ani, aduan afɔre a wɔbɔ maa Awurade, sɛnea Awurade hyɛɛ Mose no.
english: He washed the internal organs and the legs with water and burned the whole ram on the altar. It was a burnt offering, a pleasing aroma, a food offering presented to the Lord, as the Lord commanded Moses.

twi: Afei, Mose de odwennini baako a ɔyɛ asɔfohyɛ dwennini no bae. Aaron ne ne mmabarima de wɔn nsa guu nʼapampam.
english: He then presented the other ram, the ram for the ordination, and Aaron and his sons laid their hands on its head.

twi: Mose kum no na ɔde mogya no bi kaa Aaron aso nifa ase ne ne nsa nifa kokurobeti ne ne nan nifa kokurobeti.
english: Moses slaughtered the ram and took some of its blood and put it on the lobe of Aaron’s right ear, on the thumb of his right hand and on the big toe of his right foot.

twi: Ɔde mogya no bi yɛɛ Aaron mmabarima no nso aso nifa ase ne wɔn nsa nifa kokurobeti ne wɔn anan nifa kokurobeti. Ɔde mogya no nkae petee afɔremuka no ho nyinaa.
english: Moses also brought Aaron’s sons forward and put some of the blood on the lobes of their right ears, on the thumbs of their right hands and on the big toes of their right feet. Then he splashed blood against the sides of the altar.

twi: Afei, ɔfaa srade no, ne dua, ne ne mu srade, ne bɔnwoma kotoku, nʼasaabo abien no ne ɛho srade ne ne srɛ nifa no.
english: After that, he took the fat, the fat tail, all the fat around the internal organs, the long lobe of the liver, both kidneys and their fat and the right thigh.

twi: Na ɔde saa brodo ntrantraa a mmɔkaw nni mu no baako nso ne brodo ntrantraa no baako a wɔde ngo agu so ne brodo ntrantraa baako a wɔfaa ne nyinaa fii kɛntɛn a wɔde besii hɔ wɔ Awurade anim no mu guguu eyinom nyinaa so.
english: And from the basket of bread made without yeast, which was before the Lord, he took one thick loaf, one thick loaf with olive oil mixed in, and one thin loaf, and he put these on the fat portions and on the right thigh.

twi: Wɔde eyinom nyinaa hyɛɛ Aaron ne ne mmabarima nsa na wonhim no wɔ Awurade anim sɛ ohim afɔrebɔ.
english: He put all these in the hands of Aaron and his sons, and they waved them before the Lord as a wave offering.

twi: Mose gyee ne nyinaa fii wɔn nsam hyew no wɔ afɔremuka no so wɔ ɔhyew afɔre no so sɛ asɔfohyɛ afɔrebɔ, ehua a ɛsɔ ani, aduan afɔre a wɔbɔ ma Awurade.
english: Then Moses took them from their hands and burned them on the altar on top of the burnt offering as an ordination offering, a pleasing aroma, a food offering presented to the Lord.

twi: Afei Mose nso faa ne yan no a na ɛyɛ ne kyɛfa wɔ asɔfohyɛ dwennini nam no mu no hinhim wɔ Awurade anim sɛ ohim afɔrebɔ, sɛnea Awurade hyɛɛ no sɛ ɔnyɛ no.
english: Moses also took the breast, which was his share of the ordination ram, and waved it before the Lord as a wave offering, as the Lord commanded Moses.

twi: Afei ɔfaa ɔsra ngo no ne mogya a ɔde apete afɔremuka no so no bi de petee Aaron ne ne mmabarima ntade mu de tew Aaron ne ne mmabarima ne wɔn ntade ho maa Awurade dwumadi.
english: Then Moses took some of the anointing oil and some of the blood from the altar and sprinkled them on Aaron and his garments and on his sons and their garments. So he consecrated Aaron and his garments and his sons and their garments.

twi: Mose ka kyerɛɛ Aaron ne ne mmabarima no se, “Monnoa nam no wɔ Ahyiae Ntamadan no kwan ano na momfa nni brodo a ɛwɔ kɛntɛn a asɔfohyɛ afɔrebɔde wɔ mu no sɛnea meka kyerɛɛ mo no.
english: Moses then said to Aaron and his sons, “Cook the meat at the entrance to the tent of meeting and eat it there with the bread from the basket of ordination offerings, as I was commanded: ‘Aaron and his sons are to eat it.’

twi: Nam ne brodo biara a ɛbɛka no, monhyew.
english: Then burn up the rest of the meat and the bread.

twi: Bio, ɔka kyerɛɛ wɔn se wɔntena Ahyiae Ntamadan no ano nnanson, mfa nwie asɔfohyɛ dwumadi no.
english: Do not leave the entrance to the tent of meeting for seven days, until the days of your ordination are completed, for your ordination will last seven days.

twi: Mose kaa bio se nea ɔyɛɛ no da no nyinaa no, Awurade na ɔhyɛɛ no sɛ ɔnyɛ mfa nyɛ mpata mma wɔn.
english: What has been done today was commanded by the Lord to make atonement for you.

twi: Ɔsan hyɛɛ Aaron ne ne mmabarima no sɛ wɔntena Ahyiae Ntamadan no ano anadwo ne awia nnanson. Ɔka kyerɛɛ wɔn se, ‘Sɛ mufi hɔ a, mubewuwu. Eyi ne asɛm a Awurade aka.’ ”
english: You must stay at the entrance to the tent of meeting day and night for seven days and do what the Lord requires, so you will not die; for that is what I have been commanded.”

twi: Enti Aaron ne ne mmabarima dii nsɛm a Awurade nam Mose so hyɛɛ wɔn sɛ wɔnyɛ no nyinaa so.
english: So Aaron and his sons did everything the Lord commanded through Moses.

twi: Asɔfo No Fi Wɔn Dwumadi AseAhodwira no akyi da a ɛto so awotwe no, Mose frɛɛ Aaron ne ne mmabarima ne Israel mpanyimfo nyinaa.
english: On the eighth day Moses summoned Aaron and his sons and the elders of Israel.

twi: Ɔka kyerɛɛ Aaron se ɔnkɔkyere nantwinini ba mfi anantwi no mu na ɔmfa no mmɔ bɔne afɔre, na ɔnkyere odwennini a ne ho nni dɛm mfa no mmɔ ɔhyew afɔre. Ɔka kyerɛɛ no se ɔmmɔ saa afɔre yi nyinaa wɔ Awurade anim.
english: He said to Aaron, “Take a bull calf for your sin offering and a ram for your burnt offering, both without defect, and present them before the Lord.

twi: Afei Mose ka kyerɛɛ wɔn se, “Monka nkyerɛ Israelfo na wonyi ɔpapo mfa no mmɔ bɔne afɔre mma wɔn ho, na wɔmfa nantwi a wadi afe ne oguamma a wadi afe a wɔn ho nni dɛm biara mmɔ wɔn ɔhyew afɔre no,
english: Then say to the Israelites: ‘Take a male goat for a sin offering, a calf and a lamb—both a year old and without defect—for a burnt offering,

twi: na wɔmfa nantwinini ne odwennini mmɔ asomdwoe afɔre na wɔmfa asikresiam a wɔde ngo afra mmɔ aduan afɔre mma Awurade, efisɛ nnɛ, Awurade beyi ne ho adi akyerɛ mo.”
english: and an ox and a ram for a fellowship offering to sacrifice before the Lord, together with a grain offering mixed with olive oil. For today the Lord will appear to you.’”

twi: Enti wɔde saa nneɛma yi nyinaa baa Ahyiae Ntamadan no kwan ano sɛnea Mose hyɛe no. Nnipa no nyinaa begyinagyinaa Awurade anim.
english: They took the things Moses commanded to the front of the tent of meeting, and the entire assembly came near and stood before the Lord.

twi: Mose ka kyerɛɛ wɔn se, “Eyi na Awurade ahyɛ mo sɛ monnyɛ na Awurade anuonyam ada ne ho adi akyerɛ mo.”
english: Then Moses said, “This is what the Lord has commanded you to do, so that the glory of the Lord may appear to you.”

twi: Mose ka kyerɛɛ Aaron se ɔnkɔ afɔremuka no so na ɔnkɔbɔ bɔne ne ɔhyew afɔre no mfa nyɛ mpata mma ne ho ansa na ato nnipa no sɛnea Awurade hyɛe no.
english: Moses said to Aaron, “Come to the altar and sacrifice your sin offering and your burnt offering and make atonement for yourself and the people; sacrifice the offering that is for the people and make atonement for them, as the Lord has commanded.”

twi: Enti Aaron foro kɔɔ afɔremuka no so. Okum nantwi ba no de bɔɔ ɔno ara ne bɔne ho afɔre.
english: So Aaron came to the altar and slaughtered the calf as a sin offering for himself.

twi: Ne mmabarima no de mogya no brɛɛ no na ɔde ne nsateaa baako bɔɔ mu sraa mmɛn a ɛwɔ afɔremuka no ho no na ohwiee nkae no guu afɔremuka no ase.
english: His sons brought the blood to him, and he dipped his finger into the blood and put it on the horns of the altar; the rest of the blood he poured out at the base of the altar.

twi: Afei, ɔhyew srade, asaabo, bɔnwoma, bɔnwoma nkotoku a efi bɔne afɔrebɔde no mu sɛnea Awurade hyɛɛ Mose no.
english: On the altar he burned the fat, the kidneys and the long lobe of the liver from the sin offering, as the Lord commanded Moses;

twi: Na nam no de, ɔhyew ne ne nwoma wɔ nsraban no akyi.
english: the flesh and the hide he burned up outside the camp.

twi: Nea edi hɔ ne sɛ, okum ɔhyew afɔre aboa no maa ne mmabarima sɔw mogya no ma ɔde petee afɔremuka no ho nyinaa,
english: Then he slaughtered the burnt offering. His sons handed him the blood, and he splashed it against the sides of the altar.

twi: Wɔde aboa no brɛɛ no asinasin a ne ti ka ho. Ɔhyew aboa no akwaa biara wɔ afɔremuka no so.
english: They handed him the burnt offering piece by piece, including the head, and he burned them on the altar.

twi: Afei, ɔhoroo aboa no ayamde ne ne nan ho hyew wɔ afɔremuka no so sɛ ɔhyew afɔre.
english: He washed the internal organs and the legs and burned them on top of the burnt offering on the altar.

twi: Afei, ɔbɔɔ afɔre maa ɔmanfo. Okum abirekyi nanso ɔfaa ɔkwan koro a ɔfaa so bɔɔ bɔne afɔre maa ne ho no so bɔɔ afɔre maa ne ho.
english: Aaron then brought the offering that was for the people. He took the goat for the people’s sin offering and slaughtered it and offered it for a sin offering as he did with the first one.

twi: Saa ɔkwan no so na ɔfa bɔɔ wɔn ɔhyew afɔre de maa Awurade sɛnea Onyankopɔn mmara kyerɛ no.
english: He brought the burnt offering and offered it in the prescribed way.

twi: Afei, ɔbɔɔ atoko afɔre no, ɔfaa ne nsa mma na ɔhyew wɔ afɔremuka no so de kaa anɔpa ɔhyew afɔrebɔ no ho.
english: He also brought the grain offering, took a handful of it and burned it on the altar in addition to the morning’s burnt offering.

twi: Okum nantwi ne odwennini no a ɛyɛ nnipa no asomdwoe afɔrebɔde no. Aaron mmabarima no de mogya no brɛɛ no ma ɔde petee afɔremuka no ho nyinaa.
english: He slaughtered the ox and the ram as the fellowship offering for the people. His sons handed him the blood, and he splashed it against the sides of the altar.

twi: Oyii nantwi no ne odwennini no srade. Oyii wɔn dua mu srade ne wɔn ayamde srade, ne wɔn asaabo ne wɔn bɔnwoma kotoku no.
english: But the fat portions of the ox and the ram—the fat tail, the layer of fat, the kidneys and the long lobe of the liver—

twi: Wɔde srade no guu mmoa no yan so na Aaron hyew wɔ afɔremuka no so.
english: these they laid on the breasts, and then Aaron burned the fat on the altar.

twi: Na ohim yan no ne mmoa no mmati nifa no wɔ Awurade anim de kyerɛɛ sɛ afɔre no yɛ ne dea, sɛnea Mose hyɛe no.
english: Aaron waved the breasts and the right thigh before the Lord as a wave offering, as Moses commanded.

twi: Afei, Aaron trɛw ne nsam wɔ nnipa no so hyiraa wɔn, na osian fii afɔremuka no ho sii fam.
english: Then Aaron lifted his hands toward the people and blessed them. And having sacrificed the sin offering, the burnt offering and the fellowship offering, he stepped down.

twi: Mose ne Aaron kɔɔ Ahyiae Ntamadan mu hɔ na wɔsan baa bio no, wohyiraa nnipa no na Awurade anuonyam baa nnipa no nyinaa so.
english: Moses and Aaron then went into the tent of meeting. When they came out, they blessed the people; and the glory of the Lord appeared to all the people.

twi: Na ogya fi Awurade nkyɛn bɛhyew ɔhyew afɔrebɔde no ne srade a ɛwɔ afɔremuka no so no. Na nnipa no huu eyi no, wɔn nyinaa teɛteɛɛ mu butubutuw fam wɔ Awurade anim.
english: Fire came out from the presence of the Lord and consumed the burnt offering and the fat portions on the altar. And when all the people saw it, they shouted for joy and fell facedown.

twi: Nadab Ne Abihu WuNa Aaron mma Nadab ne Abihu de ogya guu wɔn aduhuamyɛfo ade mu. Wɔde aduhuam no petee ogya no so ma wɔnam saa kwan yi so buu Awurade mmara so, efisɛ wɔde ogya a ɛnyɛ nea Awurade ahyɛ baa nʼanim.
english: Aaron’s sons Nadab and Abihu took their censers, put fire in them and added incense; and they offered unauthorized fire before the Lord, contrary to his command.

twi: Enti ogya dɛw fii Awurade nkyɛn bɛhyew wɔn.
english: So fire came out from the presence of the Lord and consumed them, and they died before the Lord.

twi: Mose ka kyerɛɛ Aaron se, Awurade kae se,“ ‘Mɛda me ho kronkronyɛ adi akyerɛwɔn a wɔba me nkyɛn;wɔbɛhyɛ me anuonyam wɔ nnipa nyinaa anim no,na nea ɔrekyerɛ nen.’”Na asɛm no tɔɔ Aaron mum.
english:
Moses then said to Aaron, “This is what the Lord spoke of when he said:
“‘Among those who approach me
    I will be proved holy;
in the sight of all the people
    I will be honored.’”
Aaron remained silent.

twi: Mose soma ma wɔkɔfrɛɛ Misael ne Elsafan a wɔyɛ Aaron agya nuabarima mma brɛɛ no. Ɔka kyerɛɛ wɔn se, “Monkɔtwe nnipa a wɔahyew no nyinaa mfi Ahyiae Ntamadan no anim mfa wɔn nkɔ nsraban no akyi.”
english: Moses summoned Mishael and Elzaphan, sons of Aaron’s uncle Uzziel, and said to them, “Come here; carry your cousins outside the camp, away from the front of the sanctuary.”

twi: Na wɔkɔsoaa wɔn wɔ wɔn ntade mu sɛnea Mose aka akyerɛ wɔn no.
english: So they came and carried them, still in their tunics, outside the camp, as Moses ordered.

twi: Mose ka kyerɛɛ Aaron ne ne mmabarima Eleasar ne Itamar se, “Munnsu. Mommma mo tinwi nsensɛn hɔ yuu mmfa nkyerɛ sɛ moretwa agyaadwo. Munnsunsuane mo ntade mu nso. Sɛ moyɛ saa a, Onyankopɔn bekum mo nso na nʼabufuw bɛba Israelfo nyinaa so. Nanso Israelfo a wɔaka no de, esiane ogya a Awurade de bae no nti, wotumi di Nadab ne Abihu wu no ho awerɛhow, tumi su wɔn nso.
english: Then Moses said to Aaron and his sons Eleazar and Ithamar, “Do not let your hair become unkempt and do not tear your clothes, or you will die and the Lord will be angry with the whole community. But your relatives, all the Israelites, may mourn for those the Lord has destroyed by fire.

twi: Na mummfi Ahyiae Ntamadan no ano, anyɛ saa a mubewuwu, efisɛ Awurade ngosra wɔ mo so.” Na wodii asɛm a Mose kae no so.
english: Do not leave the entrance to the tent of meeting or you will die, because the Lord’s anointing oil is on you.” So they did as Moses said.

twi: Afei, Awurade hyɛɛ Aaron se,
english: Then the Lord said to Aaron,

twi: “Sɛ wokɔ Ahyiae Ntamadan no mu a, nnom bobesa anaa nsa a ano yɛ den. Woyɛ saa a, wubewu. Saa mmara yi bɛtena hɔ afebɔɔ ama awo ntoatoaso a ɛbɛba no nyinaa,
english: “You and your sons are not to drink wine or other fermented drink whenever you go into the tent of meeting, or you will die. This is a lasting ordinance for the generations to come,

twi: na ama moatumi ahu nsonoe a ɛda kronkron ne nea ɛyɛ teta, nea ɛho tew ne nea ɛho ntew no tam,
english: so that you can distinguish between the holy and the common, between the unclean and the clean,

twi: na woatumi akyerɛkyerɛ Israelfo mmara a Awurade nam Mose so de ama mo no nyinaa.”
english: and so you can teach the Israelites all the decrees the Lord has given them through Moses.”

twi: Mose ka kyerɛɛ Aaron ne ne mmabarima Eleasar ne Itamar se, “Momfa atoko afɔrebɔde nkae wɔ aduan afɔrebɔ a mmɔkaw nni mu a wɔde brɛɛ Awurade no na munni wɔ afɔremuka no ho, efisɛ ɛyɛ kronkron koraa.
english: Moses said to Aaron and his remaining sons, Eleazar and Ithamar, “Take the grain offering left over from the food offerings prepared without yeast and presented to the Lord and eat it beside the altar, for it is most holy.

twi: Munni wɔ kronkronbea hɔ. Ɛyɛ wo ne wo mmabarima no dea, na ɛyɛ wo ne wo mmabarima no kyɛfa a efi aduan afɔrebɔ a wɔde brɛɛ Awurade no mu; efisɛ saa na wɔahyɛ sɛ menyɛ.
english: Eat it in the sanctuary area, because it is your share and your sons’ share of the food offerings presented to the Lord; for so I have been commanded.

twi: Nanso ne yan ne ne srɛ a muhim no Awurade anim no, mutumi we no beae biara a amanne kwan so no ɛhɔ tew. Ɛyɛ wo, wo mmabarima ne wo mmabea kyɛfa wɔ Israelfo Asomdwoe afɔrebɔde no mu.
english: But you and your sons and your daughters may eat the breast that was waved and the thigh that was presented. Eat them in a ceremonially clean place; they have been given to you and your children as your share of the Israelites’ fellowship offerings.

twi: Ne srɛ ne ne yan a wohim no, ɛsɛ sɛ wɔde ka srade afɔrebɔde a wɔhyew de ma Awurade no ho. Eyi bɛyɛ wo ne wʼasefo kyɛfa daa, sɛnea Awurade ahyɛ no.”
english: The thigh that was presented and the breast that was waved must be brought with the fat portions of the food offerings, to be waved before the Lord as a wave offering. This will be the perpetual share for you and your children, as the Lord has commanded.”

twi: Bere a Mose bisaa nea ayɛ abirekyi a wɔde no bɛbɔ bɔne afɔre no ho asɛm no, ohuu sɛ wɔahyew no. Ɛno nti, ne bo fuw Eleasar ne Itamar a na wɔyɛ Aaron mmabarima no, bisae se,
english: When Moses inquired about the goat of the sin offering and found that it had been burned up, he was angry with Eleazar and Ithamar, Aaron’s remaining sons, and asked,

twi: “Adɛn nti na moanwe bɔne afɔrebɔde no wɔ kronkronbea hɔ? Ɛyɛ afɔrebɔde kronkron! Wɔde maa mo sɛ momfa nyi nnipa no afɔdi na ɛnyɛ mpata mma wɔn wɔ Awurade anim.
english: “Why didn’t you eat the sin offering in the sanctuary area? It is most holy; it was given to you to take away the guilt of the community by making atonement for them before the Lord.

twi: Esiane sɛ wɔamfa ne mogya ankɔ kronkronbea hɔ no nti, anka mubetumi awe wɔ hɔ ara sɛnea mehyɛe no.”
english: Since its blood was not taken into the Holy Place, you should have eaten the goat in the sanctuary area, as I commanded.”

twi: Aaron buaa Mose se, “Nnɛ wɔbɔɔ wɔn bɔne afɔre ne ɔhyew afɔre maa Awurade. Nanso hwɛ asɛm yi a ato me. Sɛ mewee bɔne afɔre nam yi bi nnɛ a, anka Awurade ani bɛsɔ ana?”
english: Aaron replied to Moses, “Today they sacrificed their sin offering and their burnt offering before the Lord, but such things as this have happened to me. Would the Lord have been pleased if I had eaten the sin offering today?”

twi: Na Mose tee saa no, ne bo dwoe.
english: When Moses heard this, he was satisfied.

twi: Mmoa A Wɔn Ho Tew Ne Wɔn A Wɔn Ho NtewAfei, Awurade ka kyerɛɛ Mose ne Aaron se,
english: The Lord said to Moses and Aaron,

twi: “Monka nkyerɛ Israelfo no se, ‘eyi ne mmoa a mubetumi awe wɔ asase so mmoa no mu.
english: “Say to the Israelites: ‘Of all the animals that live on land, these are the ones you may eat:

twi: Mutumi we aboa biara a ne tɔte mu apae kosi nea opuw wosaw so.
english: You may eat any animal that has a divided hoof and that chews the cud.

twi: “ ‘Monnnwe mmoa a wodidi so yi. Yoma, efisɛ opuw wosaw nanso ne tɔte mu mpae; ne ho ntew mma mo.
english: “‘There are some that only chew the cud or only have a divided hoof, but you must not eat them. The camel, though it chews the cud, does not have a divided hoof; it is ceremonially unclean for you.

twi: Atwaboa, efisɛ opuw wosaw nanso ne tɔte mu mpae; ne ho ntew mma mo.
english: The hyrax, though it chews the cud, does not have a divided hoof; it is unclean for you.

twi: Adanko, efisɛ opuw wosaw nanso ne tɔte mu mpae; ne ho ntew mma mo.
english: The rabbit, though it chews the cud, does not have a divided hoof; it is unclean for you.

twi: Prako, efisɛ ne tɔte mu apae nanso ompuw nwosaw; ne ho ntew mma mo.
english: And the pig, though it has a divided hoof, does not chew the cud; it is unclean for you.

twi: Monnnwe wɔn nam anaa mommfa mo nsa nka wɔn funu; wɔn ho ntew mma mo.
english: You must not eat their meat or touch their carcasses; they are unclean for you.

twi: “ ‘Munni nsumnam biara a ɛwɔ ntɛtɛ ne abon a efi nsubɔnten anaa po mu.
english: “‘Of all the creatures living in the water of the seas and the streams you may eat any that have fins and scales.

twi: Nanso nsumnam a aka no de, mukyi.
english: But all creatures in the seas or streams that do not have fins and scales—whether among all the swarming things or among all the other living creatures in the water—you are to regard as unclean.

twi: Ɛnsɛ sɛ mowe wɔn nam anaa mode mo nsa ka wɔn afunu; wɔn ho ntew.
english: And since you are to regard them as unclean, you must not eat their meat; you must regard their carcasses as unclean.

twi: Miti mu sɛ, nsumnam biara a enni ntɛtɛ anaa abon no, mukyi, wɔn ho ntew.
english: Anything living in the water that does not have fins and scales is to be regarded as unclean by you.

twi: “ ‘Nnomaa a ɛsɛ sɛ mubu wɔn sɛ wɔn ho ntew nti mukyi no korakora nso ne: ɔkɔre, ne opete ne opetebiri,
english: “‘These are the birds you are to regard as unclean and not eat because they are unclean: the eagle, the vulture, the black vulture,

twi: ɔkompete, ɔsansa,
english: the red kite, any kind of black kite,

twi: kwaakwaadabi,
english: any kind of raven,

twi: sohori, patukɛse, po so akorɔma, akorɔma,
english: the horned owl, the screech owl, the gull, any kind of hawk,

twi: patu, sare so patu, patukɛse,
english: the little owl, the cormorant, the great owl,

twi: bakanoma, nantwinoma, opete,
english: the white owl, the desert owl, the osprey,

twi: asukɔnkɔn, asuɔkwaa ne ampan.
english: the stork, any kind of heron, the hoopoe and the bat.

twi: “ ‘Mmoawa a wotu a wɔn anan yɛ anan no nso nyɛ mmoa a wɔn ho tew; ɛnsɛ sɛ mowe.
english: “‘All flying insects that walk on all fours are to be regarded as unclean by you.

twi: Mmom, wɔn a wɔn anan bɔ mu a wɔde huruwhuruw wɔ fam no de mutumi we.
english: There are, however, some flying insects that walk on all fours that you may eat: those that have jointed legs for hopping on the ground.

twi: Ebi ne mmoadabi ahorow nyinaa, nketekre, ne tɛwtɛw nyinaa mutumi we.
english: Of these you may eat any kind of locust, katydid, cricket or grasshopper.

twi: Nanso mmoawa a wotu na wɔwɔ anan anan no de, munhu sɛ wɔn ho ntew.
english: But all other flying insects that have four legs you are to regard as unclean.

twi: “ ‘Obiara a ɔde ne nsa bɛka wɔn funu no mpo ho begu fi kosi anwummere.
english: “‘You will make yourselves unclean by these; whoever touches their carcasses will be unclean till evening.

twi: Obiara a ɔbɛfa bi no ɛsɛ sɛ ɔhoro ne ntama na ɔtwe ne ho fi nnipa mu kosi anwummere de kyerɛ sɛ ne ho agu fi.
english: Whoever picks up one of their carcasses must wash their clothes, and they will be unclean till evening.

twi: “ ‘Obiara a ɔde ne nsa bɛka aboa biara a ne tɔte mu mpae nwiei anaa aboa a ompuw nwosaw no, wagu ne ho fi.
english: “‘Every animal that does not have a divided hoof or that does not chew the cud is unclean for you; whoever touches the carcass of any of them will be unclean.

twi: Aboa biara a nʼanan yɛ anan na ɔnam nʼawerɛw so no, mukyi ne nam. Obiara a ɔde ne nsa bɛka aboa a ɔte saa funu no ho begu fi kosi anwummere; ɛyɛ mo akyiwade.
english: Of all the animals that walk on all fours, those that walk on their paws are unclean for you; whoever touches their carcasses will be unclean till evening.

twi: Obiara a ɔbɛfa saa aboa no funu no, ɛsɛ sɛ ɔhoro ne ntama na ne ho rentew ara kosi anwummere.
english: Anyone who picks up their carcasses must wash their clothes, and they will be unclean till evening. These animals are unclean for you.

twi: “ ‘Mmoa a wɔwea wɔ fam a wɔn ho ntew no ni: Ahweaa, okisi, ɔketew abusua a wɔsoso,
english: “‘Of the animals that move along the ground, these are unclean for you: the weasel, the rat, any kind of great lizard,

twi: opo, ɔmampam, ɔdan ne na, ɔketew, ne ɔbosomaketew.
english: the gecko, the monitor lizard, the wall lizard, the skink and the chameleon.

twi: Wɔn a wɔwea no nyinaa ho ntew mma mo, obiara a ɔde ne nsa bɛka wɔn mu bi funu no ho begu fi akosi anwummere
english: Of all those that move along the ground, these are unclean for you. Whoever touches them when they are dead will be unclean till evening.

twi: Biribiara a wɔn funu no bɛka no nso ho begu fi, sɛ ɛyɛ dua, ntama, kuntu, kotoku; biribiara a ɛbɛka no, wɔmfa ngu nsu mu nkosi anwummere. Ɛno akyi no, ɛho bɛtew.
english: When one of them dies and falls on something, that article, whatever its use, will be unclean, whether it is made of wood, cloth, hide or sackcloth. Put it in water; it will be unclean till evening, and then it will be clean.

twi: Kuku biara a bi bɛtɔ mu no, nea ɛwɔ mu biara ho begu fi enti ɛsɛ sɛ wɔbɔ saa kuku no.
english: If one of them falls into a clay pot, everything in it will be unclean, and you must break the pot.

twi: Nsu a wɔde bɛhohoro nneɛma a ɛho ntew no ho wɔ kuku no mu no, sɛ bi ka aduan bi a, ebegu aduan no ho fi. Na nsã biara a ɛwɔ kuku a ɛho agu fi no mu no nso ho begu fi saa ara.
english: Any food you are allowed to eat that has come into contact with water from any such pot is unclean, and any liquid that is drunk from such a pot is unclean.

twi: Sɛ aboa biara a ne ho agu fi funu ka fononoo a wɔde ɔbo anwen a, na ɛno nso ho agu fi enti ɛsɛ sɛ wobubu gu.
english: Anything that one of their carcasses falls on becomes unclean; an oven or cooking pot must be broken up. They are unclean, and you are to regard them as unclean.

twi: Sɛ aboa no tew hwe asuti anaa abura bi a nsu wɔ mu a, nsu no ho rengu fi, na mmom, onipa a obeyi aboa no ho na ebegu fi.
english: A spring, however, or a cistern for collecting water remains clean, but anyone who touches one of these carcasses is unclean.

twi: Na sɛ aboa no funu ka aduan a wobedua wɔ afum a, ɛho rengu fi,
english: If a carcass falls on any seeds that are to be planted, they remain clean.

twi: Nanso sɛ wɔfɔw aba no nsu na funu no tɔ so a, aba no ho begu fi.
english: But if water has been put on the seed and a carcass falls on it, it is unclean for you.

twi: “ ‘Sɛ ɔyare bi kum aboa a wɔama wo ho kwan sɛ we ne nam a, obi a ɔde ne nsa bɛka ne funu no no ho begu fi akosi anwummere.
english: “‘If an animal that you are allowed to eat dies, anyone who touches its carcass will be unclean till evening.

twi: Saa ara nso na onipa a ɔbɛwe ne nam no bɛhoro ne ntama na ne ho agu fi akosi anwummere.
english: Anyone who eats some of its carcass must wash their clothes, and they will be unclean till evening. Anyone who picks up the carcass must wash their clothes, and they will be unclean till evening.

twi: “ ‘Monnnwe mmoa a wɔwea wɔ fam no nam.
english: “‘Every creature that moves along the ground is to be regarded as unclean; it is not to be eaten.

twi: Wɔn a wɔtwe wɔn ho ase fa wɔn afuru so ne wɔn a wɔnam wɔn anan anan so nyinaa ka ho. Monnnwe wɔn a wɔwɔ anan bebree na wɔwea no nam nso, efisɛ wɔn ho agu fi.
english: You are not to eat any creature that moves along the ground, whether it moves on its belly or walks on all fours or on many feet; it is unclean.

twi: Mfa wo ho nka wɔn na wo ho angu fi.
english: Do not defile yourselves by any of these creatures. Do not make yourselves unclean by means of them or be made unclean by them.

twi: Mene Awurade wo Nyankopɔn. Momma mo ho ntew wɔ saa nneɛma yi nyinaa ho na monyɛ kronkron, efisɛ meyɛ kronkron. Eyi nti, mommfa mo nsa nkɔka mmoa a wɔwea wɔ fam yi mu biara mfa ngu mo ho fi.
english: I am the Lord your God; consecrate yourselves and be holy, because I am holy. Do not make yourselves unclean by any creature that moves along the ground.

twi: Mene Awurade a miyii mo fii Misraim de mo bɛyɛɛ mo Nyankopɔn no. Ɛno nti, ɛsɛ sɛ moyɛ kronkron, efisɛ meyɛ kronkron.
english: I am the Lord, who brought you up out of Egypt to be your God; therefore be holy, because I am holy.

twi: “ ‘Eyi ne mmara a ɛfa mmoa, nnomaa, nsumnam ne wɔn a wɔwea asase so no ho.
english: “‘These are the regulations concerning animals, birds, every living thing that moves about in the water and every creature that moves along the ground.

twi: Eyi ne nsonoe a ɛda mmoa a wɔn ho tew a ɛsɛ sɛ wɔwe wɔn nam ne wɔn a wɔn ho ntew a ɛnsɛ sɛ wɔwe wɔn nam wɔ mmoa a wɔwɔ asase so no ntam.’ ”
english: You must distinguish between the unclean and the clean, between living creatures that may be eaten and those that may not be eaten.’”

twi: Awo Akyi AhodwiraAwurade ka kyerɛɛ Mose se, “Ka kyerɛ Israelfo no se,
english: The Lord said to Moses,

twi: ‘Sɛ ɔbea bi wo ɔbabarima a, ne ho ntew nnanson, te sɛ nea ɔkɔ afikyiri a ne ho ntew no ara.
english: “Say to the Israelites: ‘A woman who becomes pregnant and gives birth to a son will be ceremonially unclean for seven days, just as she is unclean during her monthly period.

twi: Ne nnaawɔtwe so no, ɛsɛ sɛ wotwa abarimaa no twetia.
english: On the eighth day the boy is to be circumcised.

twi: Na nnafua aduasa abiɛsa a ɛda nʼanim a ɔde retew ne ho no, ɛnsɛ sɛ oso biribiara a ɛyɛ kronkron mu na onni ho kwan sɛ ɔkɔ hyiadan mu nso.
english: Then the woman must wait thirty-three days to be purified from her bleeding. She must not touch anything sacred or go to the sanctuary until the days of her purification are over.

twi: Sɛ ɔbea bi wo ɔbabea a, ne ho ntew nnaawɔtwe abien, te sɛ nea ɔkɔ afikyiri a ne ho ntew no ara. Afei ɛsɛ sɛ ɔtwɛn nnafua aduosia asia ma ne ho twa.
english: If she gives birth to a daughter, for two weeks the woman will be unclean, as during her period. Then she must wait sixty-six days to be purified from her bleeding.

twi: “ ‘Sɛ saa ahotew nna yi twa mu a, ɛsɛ sɛ ɔde oguamma a wadi afe bɛbɔ ɔhyew afɔre na ɔde aborɔnoma anaa aturukuku ba bɛbɔ bɔne ho afɔre. Ɛsɛ sɛ ɔde wɔn kɔ Ahyiae Ntamadan no ano kɔma ɔsɔfo no.
english: “‘When the days of her purification for a son or daughter are over, she is to bring to the priest at the entrance to the tent of meeting a year-old lamb for a burnt offering and a young pigeon or a dove for a sin offering.

twi: Na ɔsɔfo no de wɔn bɛma Awurade de ayɛ mpata ama ɛna no; ɛba saa a, ne ho tew bio wɔ nʼawo mu mogyagugu ho.“ ‘Eyinom ne awo akyi ahyɛde.
english:
He shall offer them before the Lord to make atonement for her, and then she will be ceremonially clean from her flow of blood.
“‘These are the regulations for the woman who gives birth to a boy or a girl.

twi: Na sɛ ɔyɛ ohiani a ɔrennya oguamma no a, ɛno de, ɛsɛ sɛ ɔde mmorɔnoma abien anaa nturukuku mma abien ba. Wɔde ɔbaako bɛbɔ ɔhyew afɔre na wɔde ɔbaako abɔ bɔne ho afɔre. Ɔsɔfo no bɛfa saa kwan yi so ayɛ mpata ama no, sɛnea ɛbɛyɛ a ne ho bɛtew bio.’ ”
english: But if she cannot afford a lamb, she is to bring two doves or two young pigeons, one for a burnt offering and the other for a sin offering. In this way the priest will make atonement for her, and she will be clean.’”

twi: Ɔhonam Ani Nsanyare Ho NsɛnkyerɛnneAwurade ka kyerɛɛ Mose ne Aaron se,
english: The Lord said to Moses and Aaron,

twi: “Sɛ obi hu sɛ biribi ahon ne honam ani, anaa pɔmpɔ anaa atape asi no na adidi akɔ ne honam mu a, onhu sɛ ɛyɛ kwata. Ɛsɛ sɛ wɔde saa onipa no kɔma ɔsɔfo Aaron anaa ne mmabarima no mu baako
english: “When anyone has a swelling or a rash or a shiny spot on their skin that may be a defiling skin disease, they must be brought to Aaron the priest or to one of his sons who is a priest.

twi: na ɔhwɛ kuru no. Sɛ nwi a esi kuru no hɔ dan yɛ fitaa na kuru no atu atɔ ɔhonam no mu a, na ɛyɛ kwata a ɛsɛ sɛ ɔsɔfo no da no adi sɛ ɔyarefo no yɛ ɔkwatani.
english: The priest is to examine the sore on the skin, and if the hair in the sore has turned white and the sore appears to be more than skin deep, it is a defiling skin disease. When the priest examines that person, he shall pronounce them ceremonially unclean.

twi: Na sɛ kuru no ntɔɔ ɔhonam no mu na sɛ kuru no hɔ nwi no nso nyɛɛ fitaa a, ɛsɛ sɛ ɔsɔfo no yi ɔyarefo no fi nnipa mu nnanson.
english: If the shiny spot on the skin is white but does not appear to be more than skin deep and the hair in it has not turned white, the priest is to isolate the affected person for seven days.

twi: Nnanson no du a, ɔsɔfo no bɛhwɛ no bio na sɛ kuru no nsakrae na ɛntrɛwee wɔ ɔhonam no ani a, ɔsɔfo no bɛsan atwa no asu nnanson bio.
english: On the seventh day the priest is to examine them, and if he sees that the sore is unchanged and has not spread in the skin, he is to isolate them for another seven days.

twi: Afei ne nnanson so no, ɔsɔfo no bɛhwɛ ne honam ani bio, na sɛ ohu sɛ ɔyare no ano abrɛ ase a ɛntrɛwee a, ɔsɔfo no bɛka ato gua sɛ, ɔyarefo no ho atɔ no; ɔbɛkyerɛ mu sɛ ɛyɛ ntwom bi na eguu no bere tiaa bi mu. Enti sɛ ɔyarefo no horo ne ntama a, wɔbɛfa no sɛ wanya ayaresa awie.
english: On the seventh day the priest is to examine them again, and if the sore has faded and has not spread in the skin, the priest shall pronounce them clean; it is only a rash. They must wash their clothes, and they will be clean.

twi: Na sɛ nso ɔyarefo no ba ɔsɔfo no nkyɛn ma ɔhwɛ no na ɔyare no atrɛtrɛw a, ɛsɛ sɛ ɔsan ba ɔsɔfo no nkyɛn bio
english: But if the rash does spread in their skin after they have shown themselves to the priest to be pronounced clean, they must appear before the priest again.

twi: na ɔhwɛ no na sɛ ɔyare no atrɛtrɛw wɔ ɔhonam no ani a, afei, ɔbɛpae mu aka sɛ amanne kwan so no, ne ho ntew na ɛyɛ ɔhonam ani nsanyare.
english: The priest is to examine that person, and if the rash has spread in the skin, he shall pronounce them unclean; it is a defiling skin disease.

twi: “Sɛ obi nya ɔhonam ani nsanyare a, ɛsɛ sɛ wɔde no kɔkyerɛ ɔsɔfo na ɔhwɛ no.
english: “When anyone has a defiling skin disease, they must be brought to the priest.

twi: Sɛ ɔsɔfo no hu sɛ nwi no bi ayɛ fitaa na kuru atɔ saa beae hɔ a,
english: The priest is to examine them, and if there is a white swelling in the skin that has turned the hair white and if there is raw flesh in the swelling,

twi: na ɛkyerɛ sɛ ɛyɛ ɔhonam ani nsanyare, na ɛsɛ sɛ ɔsɔfo no de to gua sɛ amanne kwan so no, onipa no ho ntew. Ɛba saa a, wɔnhwehwɛ ɔyare no mu bio, efisɛ ɛda adi pefee sɛ ɔhonam no ayɛ kwata.
english: it is a chronic skin disease and the priest shall pronounce them unclean. He is not to isolate them, because they are already unclean.

twi: “Nanso sɛ ɔsɔfo no hu sɛ kwata no adidi ne honam nyinaa fi ne ti so kosi ne nan ase nyinaa a,
english: “If the disease breaks out all over their skin and, so far as the priest can see, it covers all the skin of the affected person from head to foot,

twi: ɔsɔfo no bɛpae mu aka se ne ho tew, efisɛ ne honam nyinaa adan ayɛ fitaa.
english: the priest is to examine them, and if the disease has covered their whole body, he shall pronounce them clean. Since it has all turned white, they are clean.

twi: Na sɛ akuru no bi pue ne honam no baabi foforo a, wɔbɛpae mu aka sɛ onipa no yɛ ɔkwatani.
english: But whenever raw flesh appears on them, they will be unclean.

twi: Ɛsɛ sɛ ɔsɔfo no pae mu ka ntɛm ara a ohu kuru wɔ honam no fa baabi, efisɛ akuru no kyerɛ sɛ kwata wɔ ɔhonam no mu.
english: When the priest sees the raw flesh, he shall pronounce them unclean. The raw flesh is unclean; they have a defiling disease.

twi: Na sɛ akuru no wu na ɛdan yɛ fitaa sɛ ɔhonam a aka no a, ɔkwatani no bɛkɔ ɔsɔfo no hɔ bio.
english: If the raw flesh changes and turns white, they must go to the priest.

twi: Ɔsɔfo no bɛhwɛ no na sɛ ɔhonam no fa hɔ ayɛ fitaa de a, ɔsɔfo no bɛpae mu aka sɛ ne ho atɔ no.
english: The priest is to examine them, and if the sores have turned white, the priest shall pronounce the affected person clean; then they will be clean.

twi: “Sɛ pɔmpɔ si obi na agyae
english: “When someone has a boil on their skin and it heals,

twi: na sɛ baabi a pɔmpɔ no sii no biribi hyerɛnn bi, anaa nea ɛbere kakra hon wɔ hɔ a, ɛsɛ sɛ ɔde ne ho kɔkyerɛ ɔsɔfo.
english: and in the place where the boil was, a white swelling or reddish-white spot appears, they must present themselves to the priest.

twi: Na sɛ ɔsɔfo no hwɛ na ɔyare no adidi kɔ ne honam mu na nwi a ɛwɔ ɔhonam no hɔ no ayɛ fitaa a, ɔsɔfo no bɛpae mu aka se ɔyarefo no ho ntew, efisɛ kwata apue afi pɔmpɔ no mu.
english: The priest is to examine it, and if it appears to be more than skin deep and the hair in it has turned white, the priest shall pronounce that person unclean. It is a defiling skin disease that has broken out where the boil was.

twi: Nanso sɛ ɔsɔfo no hwɛ na ohu sɛ nwi fitaa biara nni baabi a ɔyare no wɔ hɔ no, na ɔyare no nnidi nkɔɔ honam no mu, na ahosu no yɛ nsonso a ɔsɔfo no beyi no afi nnipa mu nnanson.
english: But if, when the priest examines it, there is no white hair in it and it is not more than skin deep and has faded, then the priest is to isolate them for seven days.

twi: Saa bere no mu sɛ beae hɔ no trɛtrɛw a, ɔsɔfo no bɛpae mu aka se, onipa no yare kwata.
english: If it is spreading in the skin, the priest shall pronounce them unclean; it is a defiling disease.

twi: Na sɛ beae a ɛhɔ ayɛ hyerɛnn no anhon bio na antrɛtrɛw a, na ɛyɛ pɔmpɔ no twa kɛkɛ enti ɔsɔfo no bɛpae mu aka se ne ho tew.
english: But if the spot is unchanged and has not spread, it is only a scar from the boil, and the priest shall pronounce them clean.

twi: “Sɛ obi hyehyew na sɛ ɔhyehyew no mu yɛ kɔkɔɔ ne fitaa anaa fitaa a,
english: “When someone has a burn on their skin and a reddish-white or white spot appears in the raw flesh of the burn,

twi: ɛsɛ sɛ ɔsɔfo no hwɛ faako a ɔhyehyew no wɔ. Sɛ nwi a ɛwɔ beae a ɛhɔ nnii dɛm biara no dan yɛ fitaa na sɛ ɛyɛ ade a adidi kɔ ɔhonam no mu a, na ɛyɛ kwata na apue afi ɔhyehyew no mu, enti ɛsɛ sɛ ɔsɔfo no pae mu ka sɛ onipa no yɛ ɔkwatani.
english: the priest is to examine the spot, and if the hair in it has turned white, and it appears to be more than skin deep, it is a defiling disease that has broken out in the burn. The priest shall pronounce them unclean; it is a defiling skin disease.

twi: Na sɛ ɔsɔfo no hwɛ hu sɛ nwi fitaa nni beae a ɛhɔ yɛ hyerɛnn no, na sɛ hyerɛnn no nnidi nkɔɔ ɔhonam no mu, na ɔyare no regyae a, ɔsɔfo no beyi no afi nnipa mu nnanson
english: But if the priest examines it and there is no white hair in the spot and if it is not more than skin deep and has faded, then the priest is to isolate them for seven days.

twi: na wahwɛ no ne nnanson so bio. Sɛ ɔyare no trɛw fa ɔhonam no ani a, ɛsɛ sɛ ɔsɔfo no pae mu ka se kwata ayɛ onipa no.
english: On the seventh day the priest is to examine that person, and if it is spreading in the skin, the priest shall pronounce them unclean; it is a defiling skin disease.

twi: Nanso sɛ ɔhonam no fa hɔ a ayɛ hyerɛnn no antrɛtrɛw ɔhonam no ani, na sɛ ɛyɛ sɛ nea ɛhɔ retwintwam no a, wɔbɛfa no sɛ ɛyɛ ɔhyehyew twa bi, enti ɔsɔfo no bɛda no adi sɛ ɔnyare kwata.
english: If, however, the spot is unchanged and has not spread in the skin but has faded, it is a swelling from the burn, and the priest shall pronounce them clean; it is only a scar from the burn.

twi: “Sɛ kuru da ɔbarima anaa ɔbea bi tirim anaa nʼafono ho a,
english: “If a man or woman has a sore on their head or chin,

twi: ɛsɛ sɛ ɔsɔfo no hwɛ; sɛ ɔhwɛ na ohu sɛ ɔyare no adidi kɔ ɔhonam no mu na ɔsan hu nwi a ɛte sɛ akokɔsrade wɔ kuru no mu a, ɛsɛ sɛ ɔpae mu ka se onipa no yare kwata.
english: the priest is to examine the sore, and if it appears to be more than skin deep and the hair in it is yellow and thin, the priest shall pronounce them unclean; it is a defiling skin disease on the head or chin.

twi: Na sɛ ɔsɔfo no hwɛ na ohu sɛ ɔyare no nnidi nkɔɔ ɔhonam no mu, na mmom, ɛwɔ ɔhonam no ani a nwi tuntum wɔ mu a, ɛsɛ sɛ woyi onipa no fi nnipa mu nnanson,
english: But if, when the priest examines the sore, it does not seem to be more than skin deep and there is no black hair in it, then the priest is to isolate the affected person for seven days.

twi: na ne nnanson so no, wɔsan hwɛ no bio. Sɛ ɔyare no ntrɛtrɛwee, na nwi a ɛte sɛ akokɔsrade nnaa ne ho adi wɔ mu na ennidi nkɔɔ ɔhonam no mu a,
english: On the seventh day the priest is to examine the sore, and if it has not spread and there is no yellow hair in it and it does not appear to be more than skin deep,

twi: ɔbɛtwerɛw nwi a atwa kuru no ho ahyia nyinaa (na mmom ɛnyɛ kuru no mu ankasa) na ɔsɔfo no ayi no afi nnipa mu nnanson bio.
english: then the man or woman must shave themselves, except for the affected area, and the priest is to keep them isolated another seven days.

twi: Ne nnanson so no, ɔbɛsan ahwɛ no, na sɛ ɔyare no ntrɛtrɛw nnidi nkɔɔ ɔhonam no mu a, ɔsɔfo no bɛpae mu aka se onipa no ho atew na sɛ ɔhoro ne ntama wie a, na afei wadi mu.
english: On the seventh day the priest is to examine the sore, and if it has not spread in the skin and appears to be no more than skin deep, the priest shall pronounce them clean. They must wash their clothes, and they will be clean.

twi: Na sɛ akyiri no saa ɔyare no trɛtrɛw a,
english: But if the sore does spread in the skin after they are pronounced clean,

twi: ɛsɛ sɛ ɔsɔfo no hwɛ no bio a ɔhwɛ sɛ nwi a ɛte sɛ akokɔsrade fra ɔyare no mu na ɔpae mu ka se, onipa no yare kwata.
english: the priest is to examine them, and if he finds that the sore has spread in the skin, he does not need to look for yellow hair; they are unclean.

twi: Na sɛ ɔyare no trɛw a ɛtrɛtrɛw no gyae na sɛ nwi tuntum fuw wɔ beae hɔ a, na ɛkyerɛ sɛ, ne ho atɔ no a kwata biara nni ne ho enti ɛsɛ sɛ ɔsɔfo no pae mu ka se ne ho atew.
english: If, however, the sore is unchanged so far as the priest can see, and if black hair has grown in it, the affected person is healed. They are clean, and the priest shall pronounce them clean.

twi: “Sɛ ɔbarima anaa ɔbea bi honam ani yɛ fitaa hanahana,
english: “When a man or woman has white spots on the skin,

twi: na akyiri no ɔhonam no ani dum ara na ɛredum a, na ɛnkyerɛ sɛ kwata ayɛ onipa no, na mmom, ɛyɛ ɔyare foforo bi.
english: the priest is to examine them, and if the spots are dull white, it is a harmless rash that has broken out on the skin; they are clean.

twi: “Sɛ obi ti so pa a, ɛwɔ mu sɛ ne ti so apa de, nanso ɛno nkyerɛ sɛ ɔyɛ ɔkwatani!
english: “A man who has lost his hair and is bald is clean.

twi: Sɛ obi ti so pa fi ne moma so a, na ne moma so ara na apa, na ɛnkyerɛ sɛ ɛyɛ kwata.
english: If he has lost his hair from the front of his scalp and has a bald forehead, he is clean.

twi: Na mmom, sɛ nsisii akɔkɔɔ a fitaa frafra mu wɔ tipae no so a, na ɛkyerɛ sɛ ebia kwata pɛ sɛ ɛyɛ saa onipa no.
english: But if he has a reddish-white sore on his bald head or forehead, it is a defiling disease breaking out on his head or forehead.

twi: Sɛ ɛba saa a, ɔsɔfo no bɛhwɛ no na sɛ biribi kɔkɔɔ aboa ne ho baabi te sɛ kwata a,
english: The priest is to examine him, and if the swollen sore on his head or forehead is reddish-white like a defiling skin disease,

twi: na ɛkyerɛ sɛ, kwata ayɛ no, enti ɛsɛ sɛ ɔsɔfo no pae mu ka se, onipa no yare kwata.
english: the man is diseased and is unclean. The priest shall pronounce him unclean because of the sore on his head.

twi: “Onipa biara a wobehu sɛ ɔyare kwata no, ɛsɛ sɛ ofura ntama a atetew na ɔma ne tinwi fuw, twa mpɛsɛmpɛsɛ na ɔkata nʼanim fa na ɔnam a ɔteɛteɛ mu se, ‘Me ho ntew! Me ho ntew!’
english: “Anyone with such a defiling disease must wear torn clothes, let their hair be unkempt, cover the lower part of their face and cry out, ‘Unclean! Unclean!’

twi: Na nna dodow a ɔyare no nkɔe no de, wɔbɛfa ɔyarefo no sɛ ne ho ntew enti ɛsɛ sɛ ɔtena kurow no akyi baabi.
english: As long as they have the disease they remain unclean. They must live alone; they must live outside the camp.

twi: “Sɛ kwata ho nsɛnkyerɛnne bi ka atade,
english: “As for any fabric that is spoiled with a defiling mold—any woolen or linen clothing,

twi: kuntutam anaa nweratam, aboa nhoma anaa biribiara a wɔde aboa nwoma ayɛ mu,
english: any woven or knitted material of linen or wool, any leather or anything made of leather—

twi: na sɛ nsisii ahabammono anaa kɔkɔɔ wɔ mu a, ebia na ɛyɛ kwata, enti ɛsɛ sɛ wɔde kɔma ɔsɔfo na ɔhwɛ.
english: if the affected area in the fabric, the leather, the woven or knitted material, or any leather article, is greenish or reddish, it is a defiling mold and must be shown to the priest.

twi: Ɔsɔfo no de bɛkɔ akosie nnanson.
english: The priest is to examine the affected area and isolate the article for seven days.

twi: Nnanson so no, wasan ahwɛ bio. Na sɛ ohu sɛ nsisii no atrɛtrɛw a, na ɛkyerɛ sɛ, ɛyɛ kwata a etumi san nnipa.
english: On the seventh day he is to examine it, and if the mold has spread in the fabric, the woven or knitted material, or the leather, whatever its use, it is a persistent defiling mold; the article is unclean.

twi: Ɛsɛ sɛ ɔde ogya hyew ntama, kuntu ne ntadetam ne aboa nwoma no nyinaa, efisɛ, ɛnam eyinom so betumi ama ɔyare no asan nnipa.
english: He must burn the fabric, the woven or knitted material of wool or linen, or any leather article that has been spoiled; because the defiling mold is persistent, the article must be burned.

twi: “Na sɛ ne nnanson so no ɔhwɛ na sɛ nsisii no ntrɛtrɛwee a,
english: “But if, when the priest examines it, the mold has not spread in the fabric, the woven or knitted material, or the leather article,

twi: ɔsɔfo no bɛhyɛ ama wɔahoro nneɛma a wodwen sɛ ɔyare no bi wɔ mu no no nyinaa na wɔakora no baabi bio nnanson.
english: he shall order that the spoiled article be washed. Then he is to isolate it for another seven days.

twi: Sɛ nnanson bio akyi faako a ɔyare no wɔ hɔ no nsesaa nʼahosu na ɛntrɛwee a, wɔbɛfa no sɛ ɛyɛ kwata nti ɛsɛ sɛ wɔhyew ade no, efisɛ ɔyare no adidi kɔ mu ara yiye.
english: After the article has been washed, the priest is to examine it again, and if the mold has not changed its appearance, even though it has not spread, it is unclean. Burn it, no matter which side of the fabric has been spoiled.

twi: Na sɛ ɔsɔfo no hu sɛ nneɛmahoro no akyi, nsisii no ano abrɛ ase a, obetwa hɔ afi ntama anaa aboa nwoma a wɔde adi dwuma bi no mu.
english: If, when the priest examines it, the mold has faded after the article has been washed, he is to tear the spoiled part out of the fabric, the leather, or the woven or knitted material.

twi: Na sɛ ɛsan ba bio de a, na ɛyɛ kwata enti ɛsɛ sɛ wɔhyew no.
english: But if it reappears in the fabric, in the woven or knitted material, or in the leather article, it is a spreading mold; whatever has the mold must be burned.

twi: Sɛ wɔhoro na asɛm biara amma ho a, wotumi de di dwuma biara bere a wɔasan ahoro no.”
english: Any fabric, woven or knitted material, or any leather article that has been washed and is rid of the mold, must be washed again. Then it will be clean.”

twi: Eyinom ne mmara a ɛfa kwata a ɛwɔ ntama anaa biribiara a wɔde aboa nhoma ayɛ a wɔnam so da no adi sɛ kwata wɔ dekode no mu anaa bi nni mu no ho.
english: These are the regulations concerning defiling molds in woolen or linen clothing, woven or knitted material, or any leather article, for pronouncing them clean or unclean.

twi: Akwatafo AhodwiraOnyankopɔn ka kyerɛɛ Mose se,
english: The Lord said to Moses,

twi: “Da a wobedwira ɔkwatani ho no, ɛho mmara ni: Wɔde no bɛkɔ akɔma ɔsɔfo,
english: “These are the regulations for any diseased person at the time of their ceremonial cleansing, when they are brought to the priest:

twi: na ɔsɔfo no ahwɛ no wɔ nsraban no akyi. Na sɛ ɔsɔfo no hu sɛ kwata no agyae a,
english: The priest is to go outside the camp and examine them. If they have been healed of their defiling skin disease,

twi: obebisa nnomaa abien bi a wɔwe, na afei wɔde sida dua, koogyan hama ne adwerɛ mman a wɔde bɛyɛ ahodwira ahyɛde ama ɔkwatani no abrɛ no.
english: the priest shall order that two live clean birds and some cedar wood, scarlet yarn and hyssop be brought for the person to be cleansed.

twi: Ɔsɔfo no bɛka ama wɔakum nnomaa no mu baako wɔ asanka a nsu wɔ mu so.
english: Then the priest shall order that one of the birds be killed over fresh water in a clay pot.

twi: Na anomaa a wonnya nkum no no nso, wɔde ɔno ne sida dua no ne koogyan hama no ne adwerɛ mman no bɛhyɛ anomaa a wokum no no mogya no mu.
english: He is then to take the live bird and dip it, together with the cedar wood, the scarlet yarn and the hyssop, into the blood of the bird that was killed over the fresh water.

twi: Na ɔsɔfo no apete mogya no agu ɔkwatani a ne ho afi no so mpɛn ason, na wapae mu aka se ne ho atew na wagyaa anomaa a wonkum no no.
english: Seven times he shall sprinkle the one to be cleansed of the defiling disease, and then pronounce them clean. After that, he is to release the live bird in the open fields.

twi: “Na ɔyarefo a ne ho atɔ no no bɛhoro ne ntama nyinaa. Obeyi ne ho nwi nyinaa nso. Obeguare na wasan abɛtena faako a kan no na ɔte hɔ no bio; nanso ɛsɛ sɛ ɔtena ne ntamadan akyi nnanson.
english: “The person to be cleansed must wash their clothes, shave off all their hair and bathe with water; then they will be ceremonially clean. After this they may come into the camp, but they must stay outside their tent for seven days.

twi: Nnanson no so no, obeyi ne ho nwi nyinaa bio, obeyi nʼabogyesɛ ayi nʼanintɔn nwi na wayi ne ho nwi a aka nyinaa, na waguare, na afei wɔapae mu aka sɛ ne ho atew.
english: On the seventh day they must shave off all their hair; they must shave their head, their beard, their eyebrows and the rest of their hair. They must wash their clothes and bathe themselves with water, and they will be clean.

twi: “Da a edi so a ɛyɛ nnaawɔtwe so no, ɔbɛfa adwennini abien a wɔn ho nni dɛm ne oguamma bere baako a ɔno nso ho nni dɛm, asikresiam muhumuhu lita asia ne fa a wɔde ngo afra ne ngo a wɔmfa mfraa hwee lita fa.
english: “On the eighth day they must bring two male lambs and one ewe lamb a year old, each without defect, along with three-tenths of an ephah of the finest flour mixed with olive oil for a grain offering, and one log of oil.

twi: Afei ɔsɔfo a ɔbɛhwehwɛ ɔyarefo no ho ahwɛ sɛ ne ho atɔ no no de onipa no ne nʼafɔrebɔde bɛba Awurade anim wɔ Ahyiae Ntamadan no ano.
english: The priest who pronounces them clean shall present both the one to be cleansed and their offerings before the Lord at the entrance to the tent of meeting.

twi: “Ɔsɔfo no bɛfa nguantenmma no baako ne ngotoa baako no na ɔde ama Awurade sɛ afɔdi afɔrebɔ a wohim no wɔ afɔremuka no anim.
english: “Then the priest is to take one of the male lambs and offer it as a guilt offering, along with the log of oil; he shall wave them before the Lord as a wave offering.

twi: Afei, wobekum oguamma no wɔ beae a wɔbɔ bɔne ne ɔhyew afɔre no wɔ kronkronbea hɔ. Wɔde saa afɔdi afɔrebɔde yi bɛma ɔsɔfo no sɛnea wɔyɛ no bɔne afɔrebɔ mu no ara pɛ. Ɛyɛ afɔrebɔ a ɛyɛ kronkron ankasa.
english: He is to slaughter the lamb in the sanctuary area where the sin offering and the burnt offering are slaughtered. Like the sin offering, the guilt offering belongs to the priest; it is most holy.

twi: Ɔsɔfo no bɛfa saa afɔdi afɔrebɔde mogya na ɔde akeka ɔyarefo a wɔretew ne ho no aso nifa ase ne ne nsa nifa kokurobeti ne ne nan nifa kokurobeti.
english: The priest is to take some of the blood of the guilt offering and put it on the lobe of the right ear of the one to be cleansed, on the thumb of their right hand and on the big toe of their right foot.

twi: Afei, ɔsɔfo no bɛfa ngo no bi ahwie agu ne nsa benkum mu
english: The priest shall then take some of the log of oil, pour it in the palm of his own left hand,

twi: na ɔde ne nsa nifa abɔ mu, na watu apete mpɛn ason wɔ Awurade anim.
english: dip his right forefinger into the oil in his palm, and with his finger sprinkle some of it before the Lord seven times.

twi: Ngo no a ɛbɛka ne nsa benkum mu no, ɔsɔfo no de bɛka onipa no aso nifa ase ne ne nsa nifa kokurobeti ne ne nan nifa kokurobeti sɛnea ɔde afɔdi mogya yɛe wɔ afɔdi afɔrebɔ no mu no ara pɛ.
english: The priest is to put some of the oil remaining in his palm on the lobe of the right ear of the one to be cleansed, on the thumb of their right hand and on the big toe of their right foot, on top of the blood of the guilt offering.

twi: Ɔde ngo no nkae a ɛwɔ ne nsam no bɛfɔw ɔbarima no ti ho. Eyi bɛkyerɛ sɛ, ɔsɔfo no de ne ho ayɛ mpata ama onipa no wɔ Awurade anim.
english: The rest of the oil in his palm the priest shall put on the head of the one to be cleansed and make atonement for them before the Lord.

twi: “Afei, ɛsɛ sɛ ɔsɔfo no bɔ bɔne afɔre na ɔsan yɛ mpata ho ade ma onipa a wɔrehohoro ne ho afi ne kwata mu no ho; ɛno akyi no, ɔsɔfo no bekum ɔhyew afɔrebɔde no
english: “Then the priest is to sacrifice the sin offering and make atonement for the one to be cleansed from their uncleanness. After that, the priest shall slaughter the burnt offering

twi: na ɔde abɔ ɛne atoko afɔre wɔ afɔremuka no so de ayɛ mpata ama ɔbarima no na afei, wapae mu aka sɛ ne ho afi no.
english: and offer it on the altar, together with the grain offering, and make atonement for them, and they will be clean.

twi: “Sɛ ɔyɛ ohiani a ɔrentumi ntɔ nguamma abien no a, ɛno de, ɔde oguamma nini baako bɛbɔ afɔdi afɔre no de ama Awurade sɛ mpata a wohim wɔ afɔremuka no anim; na wɔde asikresiam fitaa muhumuhu lita abien ne fa a wɔde ngo afra de abɔ atoko afɔre no a ngo tumpan ka ho.
english: “If, however, they are poor and cannot afford these, they must take one male lamb as a guilt offering to be waved to make atonement for them, together with a tenth of an ephah of the finest flour mixed with olive oil for a grain offering, a log of oil,

twi: Ɛno akyi no, ɔde mmorɔnoma abien anaa nturukuku mma abien mu biara a obenya no mu baako bɛbɔ bɔne afɔre na ɔde baako a ɛbɛka no nso abɔ ɔhyew afɔre.
english: and two doves or two young pigeons, such as they can afford, one for a sin offering and the other for a burnt offering.

twi: “Da a ɛto so awotwe no, ɔde ne nyinaa bɛkɔ akɔma ɔsɔfo no wɔ Ahyiae Ntamadan no ano na ɔsɔfo no de adwira no wɔ Awurade anim.
english: “On the eighth day they must bring them for their cleansing to the priest at the entrance to the tent of meeting, before the Lord.

twi: Ɔsɔfo no bɛfa oguamma no de abɔ afɔdi afɔre. Ɔde ngo tumpan ma bɛka ho na wahim wɔ afɔremuka no anim de akyerɛ sɛ, wɔde rema Awurade.
english: The priest is to take the lamb for the guilt offering, together with the log of oil, and wave them before the Lord as a wave offering.

twi: Afei, wobekum oguamma no de no abɔ afɔdi afɔre na ɔde ne mogya no bi akeka ɔbarima a wɔredwira no no aso nifa ase. Ɔde mogya no bi bɛka ne nsa nifa kokurobeti ne ne nan nifa kokurobeti.
english: He shall slaughter the lamb for the guilt offering and take some of its blood and put it on the lobe of the right ear of the one to be cleansed, on the thumb of their right hand and on the big toe of their right foot.

twi: Ɔsɔfo no behwie ngo agu ɔno ara ne nsa benkum mu
english: The priest is to pour some of the oil into the palm of his own left hand,

twi: na ɔde ne nsateaa nifa abɔ mu apete bi mpɛn ason wɔ Awurade anim.
english: and with his right forefinger sprinkle some of the oil from his palm seven times before the Lord.

twi: Na ɛsɛ sɛ ɔde ngo a ɛwɔ ne nsam no bi ka ɔbarima no aso nifa ase ne ne nsa nifa kokurobeti ne ne nan nifa kokurobeti sɛnea ɔyɛɛ mogya no, bere a ɔrebɔ afɔdi afɔre no.
english: Some of the oil in his palm he is to put on the same places he put the blood of the guilt offering—on the lobe of the right ear of the one to be cleansed, on the thumb of their right hand and on the big toe of their right foot.

twi: Ngo no a ɛbɛka wɔ ne nsam no, ɛsɛ sɛ ɔde fɔw ɔbarima a wɔredwira no no ti ho de yɛ mpata wɔ Awurade anim.
english: The rest of the oil in his palm the priest shall put on the head of the one to be cleansed, to make atonement for them before the Lord.

twi: Afei, ɛsɛ sɛ ɔde nturukuku abien anaa mmorɔnoma abien no mu biara a otumi tɔe no ba.
english: Then he shall sacrifice the doves or the young pigeons, such as the person can afford,

twi: Wɔde abien a onyae no mu baako bɛbɔ bɔne afɔre na baako a aka no, ɔde abɔ ɔhyew afɔre a saa bere no ara mu wɔbɛbɔ atoko afɔre nso, na ɔsɔfo no bɛyɛ mpata ama ɔbarima no wɔ Awurade anim.”
english: one as a sin offering and the other as a burnt offering, together with the grain offering. In this way the priest will make atonement before the Lord on behalf of the one to be cleansed.”

twi: Eyinom ne mmara a ɛfa wɔn a wɔtew wɔn ho ma wɔn ho fi kwata mu nanso wontumi mfa afɔrebɔde a ɛho hia no nyinaa mma no.
english: These are the regulations for anyone who has a defiling skin disease and who cannot afford the regular offerings for their cleansing.

twi: Afei, Awurade ka kyerɛɛ Mose ne Aaron se,
english: The Lord said to Moses and Aaron,

twi: “Sɛ mudu Kanaan asase a mede ama mo no so, na sɛ mede kwata kɔ afi bi mu a,
english: “When you enter the land of Canaan, which I am giving you as your possession, and I put a spreading mold in a house in that land,

twi: ɛno de, ofiwura no nyi ne ho adi nkyerɛ ɔsɔfo no na ɔnka se, ‘Ɛyɛ me sɛ kwata wɔ me fi ha!’
english: the owner of the house must go and tell the priest, ‘I have seen something that looks like a defiling mold in my house.’

twi: Ɔsɔfo no bɛhyɛ ama wɔatu ofie hɔ nneɛma nyinaa ansa na wahwɛ hɔ sɛnea ɛbɛyɛ a, sɛ ɔka se kwata wɔ fie hɔ a, ɛrengu biribi foforo ho fi wɔ hɔ.
english: The priest is to order the house to be emptied before he goes in to examine the mold, so that nothing in the house will be pronounced unclean. After this the priest is to go in and inspect the house.

twi: Sɛ ohu nsensansensan ahabammono anaa kɔkɔɔ wɔ ofie no afasu ho a anonom kɔ afasu no mu a,
english: He is to examine the mold on the walls, and if it has greenish or reddish depressions that appear to be deeper than the surface of the wall,

twi: ɔbɛto ofi no mu nnanson
english: the priest shall go out the doorway of the house and close it up for seven days.

twi: na ne nnanson so no, wasan aba bio abɛhwɛ. Na sɛ nsensansensan awurawura afasu no mu a,
english: On the seventh day the priest shall return to inspect the house. If the mold has spread on the walls,

twi: ɛno de, ɔsɔfo no bɛhyɛ ama wɔawerɛwerɛw nsisii no afi hɔ na wɔatow nwerɛwerɛwee no agu baabi a ɛhɔ ntew wɔ kurow no akyi baabi.
english: he is to order that the contaminated stones be torn out and thrown into an unclean place outside the town.

twi: Afei, ɔbɛhyɛ ama afasu a ɛwɔ ofi no mu no, wɔawerɛwerɛw no yiye na wɔatow nwerɛwerɛwee no agu baabi a ɛhɔ ntew wɔ kurow no akyi baabi.
english: He must have all the inside walls of the house scraped and the material that is scraped off dumped into an unclean place outside the town.

twi: Na wɔde abo foforo bi abɛhyɛ nea wɔwerɛwerɛw no anan na wɔde dɔte foforo asra ofi no ho.
english: Then they are to take other stones to replace these and take new clay and plaster the house.

twi: “Na sɛ nsisii no ba bio a,
english: “If the defiling mold reappears in the house after the stones have been torn out and the house scraped and plastered,

twi: ɔsɔfo no bɛba bio abɛhwɛ na sɛ ohu sɛ nsisii no atrɛtrɛw a, na ɛyɛ kwata na ɛkyerɛ sɛ ofi no ho ntew.
english: the priest is to go and examine it and, if the mold has spread in the house, it is a persistent defiling mold; the house is unclean.

twi: Sɛ ɛba saa a, ɔbɛhyɛ ama wɔabubu ofi no agu. Wɔbɛtwe mmubui no mu abo, nnua ne dɔte no nyinaa afi kurow no mu de akogu kurow no akyi baabi a ɛhɔ ntew.
english: It must be torn down—its stones, timbers and all the plaster—and taken out of the town to an unclean place.

twi: “Obiara a obewura ofi a wɔato mu no mu no ho ntew kosi anwummere.
english: “Anyone who goes into the house while it is closed up will be unclean till evening.

twi: Na obiara a ɔbɛda hɔ anaa obedidi wɔ fie hɔ no bɛhoro ne nneɛma nyinaa.
english: Anyone who sleeps or eats in the house must wash their clothes.

twi: “Na sɛ wɔsra ofi no ho bio na ɔsɔfo no bɛhwɛ na nsisii no mmaa bio a, ɔbɛpae mu aka se wɔatew ofi no ho na kwata no nso kɔ.
english: “But if the priest comes to examine it and the mold has not spread after the house has been plastered, he shall pronounce the house clean, because the defiling mold is gone.

twi: Obedi ofi no ahodwira ho dwuma. Ɔde nnomaa abien, sida dua, asaawa kɔkɔɔ ne adwerɛ mman na ebedi saa dwuma no.
english: To purify the house he is to take two birds and some cedar wood, scarlet yarn and hyssop.

twi: Obekum nnomaa no baako wɔ nsu pa a ɛwɔ asanka mu so,
english: He shall kill one of the birds over fresh water in a clay pot.

twi: na ɔde sida dua no ne adwerɛ mman ne hama kɔkɔɔ ne anomaa a wonkum no no anu anomaa a wɔakum no nsu pa no so no mogya mu na wɔde apete ofi no mpɛn ason.
english: Then he is to take the cedar wood, the hyssop, the scarlet yarn and the live bird, dip them into the blood of the dead bird and the fresh water, and sprinkle the house seven times.

twi: Wɔyɛ eyi de tew ofi no ho.
english: He shall purify the house with the bird’s blood, the fresh water, the live bird, the cedar wood, the hyssop and the scarlet yarn.

twi: Afei, obegyaa anomaa a onwui no ama watu akɔ kurow no akyi baabi. Eyi ne ɔkwan a wɔfa so de yɛ mpata de ma ofi san de dwira ho no.”
english: Then he is to release the live bird in the open fields outside the town. In this way he will make atonement for the house, and it will be clean.”

twi: Eyinom ne mmara a ɛfa mmeaemmeae a kwata ba hɔ no ho.
english: These are the regulations for any defiling skin disease, for a sore,

twi: Sɛ ɛyɛ atade mu anaa ofi mu,
english: for defiling molds in fabric or in a house,

twi: anaa ɔhonam ani ahonhon, anaa ɔhyehyew mu mpumpunnya anaa ɔhonam ani baabi a ɛhɔ ayɛ hyerɛnn.
english: and for a swelling, a rash or a shiny spot,

twi: Saa ɔkwan yi so na wɔbɛfa ahu sɛ ɛyɛ kwata anaa ɛnyɛ kwata.Eyi nti na wɔhyɛɛ saa mmara yi.
english:
to determine when something is clean or unclean.
These are the regulations for defiling skin diseases and defiling molds.

twi: Awurade ka kyerɛɛ Mose ne Aaron se,
english: The Lord said to Moses and Aaron,

twi: “Monhyɛ saa mmara yi mma Israelfo: ‘Ɔbarima biara a ne ho bɛsen nsu no, saa nsu no yɛ fi.
english: “Speak to the Israelites and say to them: ‘When any man has an unusual bodily discharge, such a discharge is unclean.

twi: Sɛ ɛkɔ so sen o, egyae o, agu ne ho fi. Fi a nsu a egu no no de bɛba ni:
english: Whether it continues flowing from his body or is blocked, it will make him unclean. This is how his discharge will bring about uncleanness:

twi: “ ‘Mpa a ɔbɛda so ne biribiara a ɔbɛtena so nso ho gu fi.
english: “‘Any bed the man with a discharge lies on will be unclean, and anything he sits on will be unclean.

twi: Obiara a ɔde ne ho ka ɔbarima no mpa ho gu fi kosi anwummere, enti ɛsɛ sɛ ɔhoro ne ntama na oguare.
english: Anyone who touches his bed must wash their clothes and bathe with water, and they will be unclean till evening.

twi: Obiara a ɔbɛtena akongua a ɔbarima no atena so so ho gu fi kosi anwummere, enti ɛsɛ sɛ ɔhoro ne ntama na oguare.
english: Whoever sits on anything that the man with a discharge sat on must wash their clothes and bathe with water, and they will be unclean till evening.

twi: “ ‘Saa mmara yi ka obiara a ɔde ne ho bɛka ɔbarima no.
english: “‘Whoever touches the man who has a discharge must wash their clothes and bathe with water, and they will be unclean till evening.

twi: “ ‘Obiara a ɔbarima no bɛte ntasu agu ne so no ho ntew kosi anwummere, enti ɛsɛ sɛ onii no horo ne ntama na oguare.
english: “‘If the man with the discharge spits on anyone who is clean, they must wash their clothes and bathe with water, and they will be unclean till evening.

twi: “ ‘Ɔpɔnkɔ agua biara a ɔbɛtena so no ho agu fi.
english: “‘Everything the man sits on when riding will be unclean,

twi: Obiara a ne ho bɛka biribiara a aka saa onipa no ase no ho ntew kosi anwummere, enti ɛsɛ sɛ ɔhoro ne ntama na oguare.
english: and whoever touches any of the things that were under him will be unclean till evening; whoever picks up those things must wash their clothes and bathe with water, and they will be unclean till evening.

twi: “ ‘Sɛ onipa a ne ho ntew no koso obi mu na wanhohoro ne nsa ansa a, ɛsɛ sɛ onipa ko no horo ne ntama, guare, efisɛ ne ho ntew kosi anwummere.
english: “‘Anyone the man with a discharge touches without rinsing his hands with water must wash their clothes and bathe with water, and they will be unclean till evening.

twi: “ ‘Sɛ saa onipa no so asanka biara mu a, ɛsɛ sɛ wɔbɔ no na sɛ ɛyɛ mukaase biribi a wɔde dua na asen de a, ɛsɛ sɛ wɔde nsu hohoro ho.
english: “‘A clay pot that the man touches must be broken, and any wooden article is to be rinsed with water.

twi: “ ‘Sɛ nʼahosen no twa a, ɛsɛ sɛ ɔde nnanson fi ahodwira ho ahosiesie ase na ɔhoro ne ntama na okoguare wɔ asubɔnten mu.
english: “‘When a man is cleansed from his discharge, he is to count off seven days for his ceremonial cleansing; he must wash his clothes and bathe himself with fresh water, and he will be clean.

twi: Da a ɛto so awotwe no, ɔde nturukuku abien anaa mmorɔnomamma abien bɛba Awurade anim wɔ Ahyiae Ntamadan no ano na ɔde ama ɔsɔfo no.
english: On the eighth day he must take two doves or two young pigeons and come before the Lord to the entrance to the tent of meeting and give them to the priest.

twi: Ɔsɔfo no de wɔn bɛbɔ afɔre a baako yɛ bɔne ho afɔre na baako no nso yɛ ɔhyew afɔre; na ɛkyerɛ sɛ, ɔsɔfo no bɛyɛ mpata wɔ Awurade anim ama ɔbarima no, esiane nʼahosen no nti.
english: The priest is to sacrifice them, the one for a sin offering and the other for a burnt offering. In this way he will make atonement before the Lord for the man because of his discharge.

twi: “ ‘Sɛ ɔbarima biara ho nsu gu a, ɛsɛ sɛ oguare ne ho nyinaa, efisɛ ne ho nso ntew kosi anwummere.
english: “‘When a man has an emission of semen, he must bathe his whole body with water, and he will be unclean till evening.

twi: Ntama anaa mpasotam biara a ho nsu no bi begu mu no, ɛsɛ sɛ wɔhoro, efisɛ ɛho ntew kosi anwummere.
english: Any clothing or leather that has semen on it must be washed with water, and it will be unclean till evening.

twi: Sɛ ɔbarima fa ɔbea a, wɔn nna no akyi, ɛsɛ sɛ ɔbea no ne ɔbarima no nyinaa guare, efisɛ wɔn ho ntew kosi anwummere.
english: When a man has sexual relations with a woman and there is an emission of semen, both of them must bathe with water, and they will be unclean till evening.

twi: “ ‘Sɛ ɔbea kɔ afikyiri a, ne ho ntew nnanson mu. Saa bere no mu, obiara a ɔde ne ho bɛka no no nso ho ntew kosi anwummere.
english: “‘When a woman has her regular flow of blood, the impurity of her monthly period will last seven days, and anyone who touches her will be unclean till evening.

twi: “ ‘Biribiara a ɔbɛda so anaa ɔbɛtena so saa bere no mu no nso ho agu fi.
english: “‘Anything she lies on during her period will be unclean, and anything she sits on will be unclean.

twi: Obiara a ɔde ne nsa bɛka ne mpa anaa biribiara a ɔtena so no bɛhoro ne ntama, aguare, efisɛ onipa no ho agu fi kosi anwummere.
english: Anyone who touches her bed will be unclean; they must wash their clothes and bathe with water, and they will be unclean till evening.

twi: Sɛ obi so biribi a watena so mu nso a, ɛsɛ sɛ ɔhoro ne ntama na oguare, efisɛ ne ho agu fi kosi anwummere.
english: Anyone who touches anything she sits on will be unclean; they must wash their clothes and bathe with water, and they will be unclean till evening.

twi: Sɛ ɛyɛ ne mpasotam anaa nʼakongua, obiara a ne ho bɛka no ho begu fi akosi anwummere.
english: Whether it is the bed or anything she was sitting on, when anyone touches it, they will be unclean till evening.

twi: “ ‘Sɛ ɔbarima ne no da saa bere yi mu a, ɔbarima no ho gu fi nnanson; na mpa biara a ɔbarima no bɛda so no nso ho gu fi.
english: “‘If a man has sexual relations with her and her monthly flow touches him, he will be unclean for seven days; any bed he lies on will be unclean.

twi: “ ‘Sɛ bere du sɛ ofi nanso mogya da so ba anaasɛ mogya ba bere a ɛnsɛ mu wɔ ɔsram no mu a, mmara koro no ara na wɔde ka ho asɛm,
english: “‘When a woman has a discharge of blood for many days at a time other than her monthly period or has a discharge that continues beyond her period, she will be unclean as long as she has the discharge, just as in the days of her period.

twi: na ɛkyerɛ sɛ, biribiara a ɔbɛda so saa bere no ho agu fi te sɛ nea nʼafikyikɔ bere mu ɔtena biribi so a, ɛho gu fi no ara pɛ.
english: Any bed she lies on while her discharge continues will be unclean, as is her bed during her monthly period, and anything she sits on will be unclean, as during her period.

twi: Obiara a ɔde ne nsa bɛka ne mpa anaa biribiara a ɔtena so no ho agu fi a ɛsɛ sɛ ɔhoro ne ntama, san guare, efisɛ ne ho ntew kosi anwummere.
english: Anyone who touches them will be unclean; they must wash their clothes and bathe with water, and they will be unclean till evening.

twi: “ ‘Nnanson akyi, sɛ afikyikɔ no twa a, na onni efi mu bio.
english: “‘When she is cleansed from her discharge, she must count off seven days, and after that she will be ceremonially clean.

twi: Da a ɛto so awotwe no, ɔde nturukuku abien anaa mmorɔnomamma abien bɛkɔ akɔma ɔsɔfo no wɔ Ahyiae Ntamadan no kwan ano.
english: On the eighth day she must take two doves or two young pigeons and bring them to the priest at the entrance to the tent of meeting.

twi: Ɛsɛ sɛ ɔsɔfo no de baako bɔ bɔne ho afɔre na ɔde baako bɔ ɔhyew afɔre na ayɛ mpata ama ɔbea no wɔ Awurade anim wɔ nʼafikyikɔ mu no ho.
english: The priest is to sacrifice one for a sin offering and the other for a burnt offering. In this way he will make atonement for her before the Lord for the uncleanness of her discharge.

twi: “ ‘Saa ɔkwan yi so na sɛ Israelfo no bi ho gu fi a, mobɛfa de atew wɔn ho; anyɛ saa a, esiane sɛ wɔagu mʼAhyiae Ntamadan a esi wɔn mu no ho fi nti, wobewuwu.’ ”
english: “‘You must keep the Israelites separate from things that make them unclean, so they will not die in their uncleanness for defiling my dwelling place, which is among them.’”

twi: Eyinom ne mmara a ɛwɔ hɔ ma ɔbarima a ne ho sen
english: These are the regulations for a man with a discharge, for anyone made unclean by an emission of semen,

twi: ne ɔbea a wakɔ afikyiri ne obiara a ɔde ne ho ka ɔsakyimafo wɔ bere a ne ho ntew no mu no.
english: for a woman in her monthly period, for a man or a woman with a discharge, and for a man who has sexual relations with a woman who is ceremonially unclean.

twi: Mpata DaAaron mmabarima baanu a wowuwuu wɔ Awurade anim no wu akyi no, Awurade ka kyerɛɛ Mose se,
english: The Lord spoke to Moses after the death of the two sons of Aaron who died when they approached the Lord.

twi: “Bɔ wo nua Aaron kɔkɔ sɛ, ɔnnkɔ kronkronbea hɔ wɔ ntwamtam no akyi; beae a apam adaka no si ne mmɔborɔhunu beae hɔ kwa. Ɔkɔ hɔ a obewu, efisɛ mʼankasa mewɔ omununkum a ɛkata mpata beae so no mu.
english: The Lord said to Moses: “Tell your brother Aaron that he is not to come whenever he chooses into the Most Holy Place behind the curtain in front of the atonement cover on the ark, or else he will die. For I will appear in the cloud over the atonement cover.

twi: “Sɛ ɔpɛ sɛ ɔkɔ hɔ a, nea ɛsɛ sɛ ɔyɛ ni: Ɛsɛ sɛ ɔde nantwinini ba ba ma wɔde bɔ bɔne ho afɔre na ɔde odwennini nso ba ma wɔde bɔ ɔhyew afɔre.
english: “This is how Aaron is to enter the Most Holy Place: He must first bring a young bull for a sin offering and a ram for a burnt offering.

twi: Ɛsɛ sɛ oguare na ɔhyɛ atade hanahana ne ne nhyɛase na ɔbɔ nkyekyeremu ne abotiri.
english: He is to put on the sacred linen tunic, with linen undergarments next to his body; he is to tie the linen sash around him and put on the linen turban. These are sacred garments; so he must bathe himself with water before he puts them on.

twi: Afei, Israelfo bɛbrɛ no mmirekyi abien a wɔde bɛbɔ wɔn bɔne ho afɔre ne odwennini a wɔde bɛbɔ wɔn ɔhyew afɔre.
english: From the Israelite community he is to take two male goats for a sin offering and a ram for a burnt offering.

twi: “Ɛsɛ sɛ Aaron de nantwi ba no bɛma Awurade sɛ bɔne ho afɔre a ɔrebɔ ama ne ho de ayɛ mpata ama ne ho ne ne fifo.
english: “Aaron is to offer the bull for his own sin offering to make atonement for himself and his household.

twi: Afei, ɔde mmirekyi abien no bɛba Awurade anim wɔ Ahyiae Ntamadan no ano.
english: Then he is to take the two goats and present them before the Lord at the entrance to the tent of meeting.

twi: Ɛsɛ sɛ ɔbɔ mmirekyi no so ntonto hu Awurade de, ne nea ɛsɛ sɛ wɔsan de no kɔ.
english: He is to cast lots for the two goats—one lot for the Lord and the other for the scapegoat.

twi: Aaron de abirekyi a wɔde no rebɛbɔ Awurade afɔre no bɛbɔ bɔne ho afɔre.
english: Aaron shall bring the goat whose lot falls to the Lord and sacrifice it for a sin offering.

twi: Wɔrenkum abirekyi baako a waka no na wɔde no aba Awurade anim. Wɔbɛyɛ mpata ho dwumadi bi agu ne so na wɔde no akɔ sare so akogyaw no wɔ hɔ sɛ mpata guan.
english: But the goat chosen by lot as the scapegoat shall be presented alive before the Lord to be used for making atonement by sending it into the wilderness as a scapegoat.

twi: “Aaron de nantwinini ba no bɛbɔ bɔne ho afɔre ama ne ho ne ne fifo.
english: “Aaron shall bring the bull for his own sin offering to make atonement for himself and his household, and he is to slaughter the bull for his own sin offering.

twi: Ɛsɛ sɛ ɔfa ade a wɔhyew aduhuam wɔ mu a nnyansramma a wɔfaa wɔ Awurade afɔremuka no so ayɛ no ma. Afei ɔde aduhuam a wɔayam no muhumuhu bɛyɛ ne nsam na ɔde akɔ ntwamtam no akyi.
english: He is to take a censer full of burning coals from the altar before the Lord and two handfuls of finely ground fragrant incense and take them behind the curtain.

twi: Ɛhɔ na ɔde aduhuam no begu ogya no so wɔ Awurade anim na ayɛ wusiw kumɔnn wɔ mpata beae apam ne adaka (a abo apon a wɔakyerɛw Mmaransɛm Du agu so wɔ mu) no so nyinaa sɛnea ɛbɛyɛ a ɔrenwu.
english: He is to put the incense on the fire before the Lord, and the smoke of the incense will conceal the atonement cover above the tablets of the covenant law, so that he will not die.

twi: Na ɔde nantwinini ba no mogya no bi bɛba na ɔde ne nsateaa baako abɔ mu apete mpata beae hɔ apuei fam na wapete no mpɛn ason wɔ anim.
english: He is to take some of the bull’s blood and with his finger sprinkle it on the front of the atonement cover; then he shall sprinkle some of it with his finger seven times before the atonement cover.

twi: “Afei, ɛsɛ sɛ ofi adi na ɔde abirekyi no kɔbɔ ɔmanfo no bɔne ho afɔre na wɔde ne mogya no ba ntwamtam no akyi na wɔpete gu mpata hɔ ne anim sɛnea ɔde nantwinini ba no mogya no yɛe no ara pɛ.
english: “He shall then slaughter the goat for the sin offering for the people and take its blood behind the curtain and do with it as he did with the bull’s blood: He shall sprinkle it on the atonement cover and in front of it.

twi: Na ɛkyerɛ sɛ wayɛ mpata ama beae kronkron hɔ, efisɛ Israelfo bɔne ama efi aka beae hɔ ne Ahyiae Ntamadan no a wɔasi wɔ wɔn mfimfini hɔ no.
english: In this way he will make atonement for the Most Holy Place because of the uncleanness and rebellion of the Israelites, whatever their sins have been. He is to do the same for the tent of meeting, which is among them in the midst of their uncleanness.

twi: Sɛ Aaron wura Ahyiae Ntamadan no mu kɔ kronkronbea hɔ rekɔyɛ mpata adwuma no a, ɛnsɛ sɛ obiara kɔ hɔ bi, gye sɛ ɔyɛ mpata no ma ne ho ne ne fifo ne Israelfo nyinaa wie.
english: No one is to be in the tent of meeting from the time Aaron goes in to make atonement in the Most Holy Place until he comes out, having made atonement for himself, his household and the whole community of Israel.

twi: “Afei, ɔbɛkɔ afɔremuka no ho wɔ Awurade anim akɔyɛ mpata ama afɔremuka no. Ɛsɛ sɛ ɔde nantwinini ba no ne abirekyi mogya no sra mmɛn a etuatua afɔremuka no ho no ho.
english: “Then he shall come out to the altar that is before the Lord and make atonement for it. He shall take some of the bull’s blood and some of the goat’s blood and put it on all the horns of the altar.

twi: Na ɔde ne nsateaa baako bɛpete mogya no mpɛn ason agu afɔremuka no so de atew ho afi Israelfo bɔne no ho ayɛ no kronkron.
english: He shall sprinkle some of the blood on it with his finger seven times to cleanse it and to consecrate it from the uncleanness of the Israelites.

twi: “Sɛ owie mpata a ɛfa kronkronbea hɔ ne Ahyiae Ntamadan no ho nsɛm nyinaa ne afɔremuka no ho a, ɔde abirekyi no bɛba anikann.
english: “When Aaron has finished making atonement for the Most Holy Place, the tent of meeting and the altar, he shall bring forward the live goat.

twi: Na ɔde ne nsa abien agu aboa no apampam, na waka atirimɔden ne atuatew a Israelfo ayɛ, wɔn bɔne nyinaa de agu abirekyi no apampam, na obi a wɔayi no sɛ ɔnyɛ saa adwuma no de aboa no bɛkɔ sare so.
english: He is to lay both hands on the head of the live goat and confess over it all the wickedness and rebellion of the Israelites—all their sins—and put them on the goat’s head. He shall send the goat away into the wilderness in the care of someone appointed for the task.
