english: I will set my face against you so that you will be defeated by your enemies; those who hate you will rule over you, and you will flee even when no one is pursuing you.

twi: “ ‘Na sɛ mokɔ so yɛ asoɔden a, mɛtwe mo bɔne no so aso mmɔho ason.
english: “‘If after all this you will not listen to me, I will punish you for your sins seven times over.

twi: Mɛsɛe mo ahantan tumi no na mayɛ mo soro sɛ dade ne mo fam sɛ kɔbere.
english: I will break down your stubborn pride and make the sky above you like iron and the ground beneath you like bronze.

twi: Mobɛsɛe mo ahoɔden kwa, na mo asase rennya nnɔbae biara, na ɛso nnua nso rensow aba.
english: Your strength will be spent in vain, because your soil will not yield its crops, nor will the trees of your land yield their fruit.

twi: “ ‘Na sɛ tie ara na morentie me a, mo bɔne nti, mede ɔyaredɔm mmɔho ason a ɛfata mo bɔne no begu mo so.
english: “‘If you remain hostile toward me and refuse to listen to me, I will multiply your afflictions seven times over, as your sins deserve.

twi: Mɛma nkekaboa abekunkum mo mma na wɔakunkum mo anantwi, na matew mo dodow so, na mo akwan bɛda mpan a obi mfa so bio.
english: I will send wild animals against you, and they will rob you of your children, destroy your cattle and make you so few in number that your roads will be deserted.

twi: “ ‘Na sɛ eyi antumi ansakra mo, na mokɔ so tia mʼapɛde a,
english: “‘If in spite of these things you do not accept my correction but continue to be hostile toward me,

twi: me nso, metia mo apɛde, na me ara mʼankasa mɛtwe mo aso mpɛn ason wɔ mo bɔne ho.
english: I myself will be hostile toward you and will afflict you for your sins seven times over.

twi: Menam ɔko so bebu mʼapam so ako atia mo de atua mo so ka. Mubeguan akɔ mo nkurow mu, na mede nyarewa bɛtoa mo wɔ hɔ. Na mo atamfo bedi mo so.
english: And I will bring the sword on you to avenge the breaking of the covenant. When you withdraw into your cities, I will send a plague among you, and you will be given into enemy hands.

twi: Mɛsɛe mo nnuan a mubenya nyinaa akosi sɛ mpo, fononoo baako brodo a ɛbɛto no na mmusuakuw du bedi. Aduan kakra a mubedi no akyi, ɔkɔm bɛde mo.
english: When I cut off your supply of bread, ten women will be able to bake your bread in one oven, and they will dole out the bread by weight. You will eat, but you will not be satisfied.

twi: “ ‘Na sɛ mokɔ so yɛ asoɔden a,
english: “‘If in spite of this you still do not listen to me but continue to be hostile toward me,

twi: mo bɔne nti, me bo befuw mo na matwe mo aso a emu yɛ den mmɔho ason.
english: then in my anger I will be hostile toward you, and I myself will punish you for your sins seven times over.

twi: Mobɛwe mo mmabarima ne mo mmabea nam.
english: You will eat the flesh of your sons and the flesh of your daughters.

twi: Mɛsɛe mo sorɔnsorɔmmea. Metwitwa mo aduhuam afɔremuka agu, na mahyehyɛ mo afunu wɔ mo ahoni a enni nkwa no so; na mɛpo mo.
english: I will destroy your high places, cut down your incense altars and pile your dead bodies on the lifeless forms of your idols, and I will abhor you.

twi: Mɛma mo nkurow ayɛ amamfo na masɛe baabi a mosom nyinaa, na mapo mo ohuam afɔrebɔ no.
english: I will turn your cities into ruins and lay waste your sanctuaries, and I will take no delight in the pleasing aroma of your offerings.

twi: Ampa ara, mɛma mo asase so ada mpan na mo atamfo atena so, na nea mɛyɛ mo no ayɛ mo nwonwa.
english: I myself will lay waste the land, so that your enemies who live there will be appalled.

twi: Mɛbɔ mo apete aman no a morekɔ so nyinaa so, na mede ɔko asɛe mo. Mo asase bɛda mpan na wɔasɛe mo nkurow.
english: I will scatter you among the nations and will draw out my sword and pursue you. Your land will be laid waste, and your cities will lie in ruins.

twi: Akyiri no, asase no bɛda hɔ ahome de asi mfe dodow a moamma anhome no anan; ɛbɛda hɔ wɔ mmere a mowɔ atamfo nsam wɔ wɔn nsase so no nyinaa. Na asase no ahome, na anya ne home nna nso.
english: Then the land will enjoy its sabbath years all the time that it lies desolate and you are in the country of your enemies; then the land will rest and enjoy its sabbaths.

twi: Bere a asase no da mpan nyinaa, ebenya home a moamma annya wɔ Homeda dodow a motenaa so no.
english: All the time that it lies desolate, the land will have the rest it did not have during the sabbaths you lived in it.

twi: “ ‘Wɔn a wogyaw wɔn hɔ a wonwui no nso, mɛma wɔatwe wɔn akɔ akyirikyiri nsase so sɛ ɔko mu nneduafo ne nkoa. Ɛhɔ na wɔbɛtena daa wɔ ehu mu. Wɔte sɛ mframa rebɔ ahaban koraa a, wobeguan te sɛ nea obi a okura afoa repam wɔn; wɔbɛhwehwe ase wɔ bere a obi ntaa wɔn.
english: “‘As for those of you who are left, I will make their hearts so fearful in the lands of their enemies that the sound of a windblown leaf will put them to flight. They will run as though fleeing from the sword, and they will fall, even though no one is pursuing them.

twi: Obiara rentaa wɔn nanso ehu nti, wobehintihintiw wɔn ho wɔn ho te sɛnea wɔreguan afi akono a wonni tumi biara a wɔde begyina wɔn atamfo anim no.
english: They will stumble over one another as though fleeing from the sword, even though no one is pursuing them. So you will not be able to stand before your enemies.

twi: Mobɛyera wɔ aman mu, na mo atamfo asɛe mo.
english: You will perish among the nations; the land of your enemies will devour you.

twi: Wɔn a wɔbɛka no, wɔn bɔne nti, wɔn ho bɛyeraw wɔn wɔ atamfo nsase so, bɔne a wɔn agyanom yɛe no nti.
english: Those of you who are left will waste away in the lands of their enemies because of their sins; also because of their ancestors’ sins they will waste away.

twi: “ ‘Nanso akyiri no, me nkurɔfo bɛka wɔn bɔne ne wɔn agyanom bɔne. Wɔbɛka sɛnea wodii me huammɔ na wotiaa me no.
english: “‘But if they will confess their sins and the sins of their ancestors—their unfaithfulness and their hostility toward me,

twi: Sɛ me nso mitia wɔn sɛ nea ɛsɛ na mede wɔn kɔ wɔn atamfo asase so a, afei, wɔn komaden no ano bɛbrɛ ase, na wobetua wɔn bɔne so ka.
english: which made me hostile toward them so that I sent them into the land of their enemies—then when their uncircumcised hearts are humbled and they pay for their sin,

twi: Afei, mɛkae apam a mene Yakob, Isak ne Abraham ayɛ, na mɛkae asase no.
english: I will remember my covenant with Jacob and my covenant with Isaac and my covenant with Abraham, and I will remember the land.

twi: Asase no da hɔ dinn no, ebedi ne homeda. Nanso akyiri no, wobenya wɔn asotwe sɛ wɔanni me nhyehyɛe so na wɔpoo mʼahyɛde.
english: For the land will be deserted by them and will enjoy its sabbaths while it lies desolate without them. They will pay for their sins because they rejected my laws and abhorred my decrees.

twi: Na nea wɔyɛɛ no nyinaa akyi no, merensɛe wɔn ne mʼapam no korakora, efisɛ mene Awurade wɔn Nyankopɔn.
english: Yet in spite of this, when they are in the land of their enemies, I will not reject them or abhor them so as to destroy them completely, breaking my covenant with them. I am the Lord their God.

twi: Mɛkae tete apam a me ne wɔn agyanom a miyii wɔn fii Misraim, bere a amanaman nyinaa rehwɛ no yɛe no. Me Awurade ne wɔn Nyankopɔn.’ ”
english: But for their sake I will remember the covenant with their ancestors whom I brought out of Egypt in the sight of the nations to be their God. I am the Lord.’”

twi: Eyinom ne mmara ne ahyɛde a Awurade nam Mose so de maa Israelfo no wɔ Sinai Bepɔw so no.
english: These are the decrees, the laws and the regulations that the Lord established at Mount Sinai between himself and the Israelites through Moses.

twi: Sɛnea Wogye Nea Ɛyɛ Awurade De NoAwurade ka kyerɛɛ Mose se,
english: The Lord said to Moses,

twi: “Ka kyerɛ Israelfo no se, ‘Sɛ onipa bi hyɛ bɔ sɛ ɔde obi bɛma Awurade a, na sɛ ɔpɛ sɛ otua sika mmom a,
english: “Speak to the Israelites and say to them: ‘If anyone makes a special vow to dedicate a person to the Lord by giving the equivalent value,

twi: obetua dwetɛ gram ahannum ne aduoson () ama ɔbarima a wadi mfe aduonu kosi mfe aduosia,
english: set the value of a male between the ages of twenty and sixty at fifty shekels of silver, according to the sanctuary shekel;

twi: sɛ ɔyɛ ɔbea a wadi mfe aduonu kosi aduosia a, wobetua dwetɛ gram ahaasa ne aduanan (),
english: for a female, set her value at thirty shekels;

twi: abarimaa a wadi mfe anum kosi aduonu no nso wobetua dwetɛ gram ahannu ne aduasa (). Sɛ ɔyɛ ɔbea a, wobetua dwetɛ gram ɔha ne dunum ().
english: for a person between the ages of five and twenty, set the value of a male at twenty shekels and of a female at ten shekels;

twi: Abarimaa a wadi ɔsram kosi mfe anum no wobetua dwetɛ gram ; na ɔbabea nso wɔatua dwetɛ gram .
english: for a person between one month and five years, set the value of a male at five shekels of silver and that of a female at three shekels of silver;

twi: Ɔbarima a wadi boro mfe aduosia no wobetua dwetɛ gram ɔha aduoson (); na ɔbea nso wɔatua dwetɛ gram ɔha ne dunum ().
english: for a person sixty years old or more, set the value of a male at fifteen shekels and of a female at ten shekels.

twi: Na sɛ obi yɛ ohiani a ɔrentumi ntua saa sika yi a, ɔde saa onipa no bɛba ɔsɔfo anim, na ɔsɔfo no akyerɛ no sika a obetumi atua.
english: If anyone making the vow is too poor to pay the specified amount, the person being dedicated is to be presented to the priest, who will set the value according to what the one making the vow can afford.

twi: “ ‘Sɛ ɔde aboa hyɛ bɔ sɛ afɔrebɔde a ɛfata ma Awurade a, saa aboa no a ɔde ama Awurade no bɛyɛ kronkron.
english: “‘If what they vowed is an animal that is acceptable as an offering to the Lord, such an animal given to the Lord becomes holy.

twi: Ɛnsɛ sɛ ɔsesa saa aboa no. Ɛnsɛ sɛ ɔde nea eye sesa nea enye anaa sɛ ɔde nea enye sesa nea eye. Sɛ ɛba sɛ wɔyɛ saa nsesae yi a, wɔbɛfa no sɛ mmoa abien no nyinaa ho tew.
english: They must not exchange it or substitute a good one for a bad one, or a bad one for a good one; if they should substitute one animal for another, both it and the substitute become holy.

twi: Sɛ aboa a ɔde rema Awurade no ho ntew na ɛmfata sɛ wɔde yɛ afɔrebɔde ma Awurade a, ɛsɛ sɛ ne wura no de brɛ ɔsɔfo,
english: If what they vowed is a ceremonially unclean animal—one that is not acceptable as an offering to the Lord—the animal must be presented to the priest,

twi: na wahwɛ sɛ aboa no di mu anaa sɛ onni mu, na wakyerɛ sika dodow a ɛsɛ sɛ otua de si aboa no anan.
english: who will judge its quality as good or bad. Whatever value the priest then sets, that is what it will be.

twi: Sɛ aboa no yɛ nea ɛsɛ sɛ wɔde no bɔ afɔre nanso onipa a ɔde no reba no pɛ sɛ ɔsan gye nʼade a, obetua sika ɔha mu nkyɛmu aduonu aka bo a ɔsɔfo no betwa ama no sɛ ontua no ho.
english: If the owner wishes to redeem the animal, a fifth must be added to its value.

twi: “ ‘Sɛ obi de ne fi ma Awurade na sɛ ɔpɛ sɛ ɔsan gye a, ɔsɔfo no bɛsese ahu sɛ eye anaasɛ enye. Bo biara a ɔsɔfo no bɛkyerɛ no na ɛsɛ sɛ wotua.
english: “‘If anyone dedicates their house as something holy to the Lord, the priest will judge its quality as good or bad. Whatever value the priest then sets, so it will remain.

twi: Sɛ nea ɔde ofi no mae no pɛ sɛ ɔsan gye a ɛsɛ sɛ otua ne bo no nkyɛmu ɔha mu aduonu ka ho na ama ofi no asan abɛyɛ ne de.
english: If the one who dedicates their house wishes to redeem it, they must add a fifth to its value, and the house will again become theirs.

twi: “ ‘Sɛ ɔbarima bi pɛ sɛ ɔde nʼabusua asase fa bi bɔ afɔre ma Awurade a, wobegyina aba kɛntɛnma dodow a ebehia sɛ wobedua wɔ so no so atwa asase no bo; aba kɛntɛnma biara bo yɛ dwetɛ gram ahannum ne aduoson ().
english: “‘If anyone dedicates to the Lord part of their family land, its value is to be set according to the amount of seed required for it—fifty shekels of silver to a homer of barley seed.

twi: Mfirihyia Aduonum Afahyɛ mu no, sɛ obi de nʼafuw kyɛ a, ne bo no rensesa.
english: If they dedicate a field during the Year of Jubilee, the value that has been set remains.

twi: Na sɛ ɔde asase no ma wɔ Mfirihyia Aduonum Afahyɛ no akyi a, ɔsɔfo no begyina mfe a aka ansa na Mfirihyia Aduonum Afahyɛ a edi so no so asese ne bo no, na wobetumi atew so.
english: But if they dedicate a field after the Jubilee, the priest will determine the value according to the number of years that remain until the next Year of Jubilee, and its set value will be reduced.

twi: Na sɛ ɔbarima no pɛ sɛ ogye nʼasase a, ɔsɔfo no bo a ɔbɛbɔ no, obetua ɔha mu nkyɛmu aduonu aka ho ansa na asase no abɛyɛ ne dea bio.
english: If the one who dedicates the field wishes to redeem it, they must add a fifth to its value, and the field will again become theirs.

twi: Na sɛ nso ɔyɛ nʼadwene sɛ ɔmpɛ sɛ ogye asase no bio, anaasɛ sɛ watɔn asase no ama obi foforo a, ɛno de, wɔrentumi nnye bio.
english: If, however, they do not redeem the field, or if they have sold it to someone else, it can never be redeemed.

twi: Sɛ wɔdan asase no ma wɔ Mfirihyia Aduonum Afahyɛ no mu a, ɛbɛyɛ asase kronkron. Wɔde bɛto hɔ ama Awurade. Ɛbɛyɛ asɔfo no agyapade.
english: When the field is released in the Jubilee, it will become holy, like a field devoted to the Lord; it will become priestly property.

twi: “ ‘Sɛ obi de asase a watɔ ma Awurade, na sɛ asase no nyɛ nʼabusua asase a,
english: “‘If anyone dedicates to the Lord a field they have bought, which is not part of their family land,

twi: ɔsɔfo no begyina mfe a aka ama wɔadi Mfirihyia Aduonum Afahyɛ no so asese ne bo. Ɛsɛ sɛ onipa ko no tua ka no da no ara, na ɛyɛ afɔrebɔde kronkron ma Awurade.
english: the priest will determine its value up to the Year of Jubilee, and the owner must pay its value on that day as something holy to the Lord.

twi: Mfirihyia Aduonum Afahyɛ no du so a, asase no bɛsan akɔ nea ɔtɔnee no anaasɛ nea na ɔyɛ asase no wura no nkyɛn.
english: In the Year of Jubilee the field will revert to the person from whom it was bought, the one whose land it was.

twi: Wɔbɛsese ho ka no nyinaa wɔ nnwetɛbona a wogye wɔ hyiadan mu no ho, a ɛyɛ gram dubaako.
english: Every value is to be set according to the sanctuary shekel, twenty gerahs to the shekel.

twi: “ ‘Ɛnsɛ sɛ obiara de aboa bi abakan ma Awurade, efisɛ abakan biara, sɛ ɔyɛ nantwi anaa oguan no, yɛ Awurade de dedaw.
english: “‘No one, however, may dedicate the firstborn of an animal, since the firstborn already belongs to the Lord; whether an ox or a sheep, it is the Lord’s.

twi: Sɛ ɔyɛ mmoa a wɔn ho ntew no bi a, onipa no betumi atua ne bo no, na ɔde ɛbo no ɔha mu nkyɛmu aduonu aka ho. Sɛ onipa no antɔ bio de a, wɔbɛtɔn aboa no sɛnea ne bo te.
english: If it is one of the unclean animals, it may be bought back at its set value, adding a fifth of the value to it. If it is not redeemed, it is to be sold at its set value.

twi: “ ‘Ade biara a wɔde ama Awurade no, sɛ ɛyɛ nnipa, mmoa anaa abusuasase no, ɛnsɛ sɛ wɔtɔn anaa wɔsan gye, efisɛ biribiara a ɛte saa no yɛ kronkron ma Awurade.
english: “‘But nothing that a person owns and devotes to the Lord—whether a human being or an animal or family land—may be sold or redeemed; everything so devoted is most holy to the Lord.

twi: “ ‘Onipa biara a Awurade ayi no ama ɔsɛe no, wɔmmfa biribi ntua ne ti ka. Ɛsɛ sɛ wokum no.
english: “‘No person devoted to destruction may be ransomed; they are to be put to death.

twi: “ ‘Asase no so nnɔbae nkyɛmu du mu baako, sɛ ɛyɛ aburow anaa aduaba no yɛ Awurade dea. Ɛyɛ kronkron.
english: “‘A tithe of everything from the land, whether grain from the soil or fruit from the trees, belongs to the Lord; it is holy to the Lord.

twi: Sɛ obi pɛ sɛ ɔsan tɔ saa aduaba anaa aburow no a, ɛsɛ sɛ ɔde ne bo nkyɛmu anum mu baako ka ho.
english: Whoever would redeem any of their tithe must add a fifth of the value to it.

twi: Anantwi ne nguan no ntotoso du du nyinaa, aboa biara a ɔto so du a ɔfa oguanhwɛfo nsam no yɛ kronkron ma Awurade.
english: Every tithe of the herd and flock—every tenth animal that passes under the shepherd’s rod—will be holy to the Lord.

twi: Aboa a ɔto so du a wɔde bɛma Awurade no, wɔnnhwɛ sɛ oye anaa onye, na wɔmmfa biribiara nsi nʼanan mu, efisɛ sɛ wɔde biribiara si anan mu a, ne nyinaa bɛyɛ kronkron, a obiara rentumi nnye bio.’ ”
english: No one may pick out the good from the bad or make any substitution. If anyone does make a substitution, both the animal and its substitute become holy and cannot be redeemed.’”

twi: Eyinom ne ahyɛde a Awurade de maa Mose wɔ Sinai Bepɔw so sɛ ɔnka nkyerɛ Israelfo no.
english: These are the commands the Lord gave Moses at Mount Sinai for the Israelites.

twi: Yesu Kristo MpanyimfoYesu Kristo a ofi Ɔhene Dawid ne Abraham abusua mu no mpanyimfo din na edidi so yi:
english: This is the genealogy of Jesus the Messiah the son of David, the son of Abraham:

twi: Abraham ba ne Isak,Isak ba ne Yakob;Yakob nso mma ne Yuda ne ne nuanom.
english:
Abraham was the father of Isaac,
Isaac the father of Jacob,
Jacob the father of Judah and his brothers,

twi: Yuda mma ne Peres ne Sera. Wɔn na ne Tamar.Peres ba ne Hesronna Hesron nso ba ne Ram.
english:
Judah the father of Perez and Zerah, whose mother was Tamar,
Perez the father of Hezron,
Hezron the father of Ram,

twi: Ram woo Aminadab,Aminadab woo Nahson,Nahson nso woo Salmon.
english:
Ram the father of Amminadab,
Amminadab the father of Nahshon,
Nahshon the father of Salmon,

twi: Salmon ne ne yere Rahab woo Boas,Boas ne ne yere Rut woo Obed,Obed nso woo Yisai.
english:
Salmon the father of Boaz, whose mother was Rahab,
Boaz the father of Obed, whose mother was Ruth,
Obed the father of Jesse,

twi: Yisai ba ne Ɔhene Dawid.Dawid ba ne Salomo. Dawid ne Batseba a na anka ɔyɛ Uria yere no na wɔwoo Salomo.
english:
and Jesse the father of King David.
David was the father of Solomon, whose mother had been Uriah’s wife,

twi: Salomo woo Rehoboam,Rehoboam woo Abia,Abia woo Asa.
english:
Solomon the father of Rehoboam,
Rehoboam the father of Abijah,
Abijah the father of Asa,

twi: Asa woo Yehosafat,Yehosafat woo Yoram,Yoram nso woo Usia
english:
Asa the father of Jehoshaphat,
Jehoshaphat the father of Jehoram,
Jehoram the father of Uzziah,

twi: Usia ba ne Yotam,Yotam ba ne Ahas:Ahas ba ne Hiskia.
english:
Uzziah the father of Jotham,
Jotham the father of Ahaz,
Ahaz the father of Hezekiah,

twi: Hiskia ba ne Manase,Manase ba ne Amon,Amon nso ba ne Yosia.
english:
Hezekiah the father of Manasseh,
Manasseh the father of Amon,
Amon the father of Josiah,

twi: Yosia woo Yekonia ne ne nuanom. Wɔwoo wɔn bere a na Yudafo te nnommum mu wɔ Babilon no.
english: and Josiah the father of Jeconiah and his brothers at the time of the exile to Babylon.

twi: Wɔn a wofi Babilon nnommum mu bae no akyi awo ntoatoaso ni:Yekonia woo Sealtiel,Sealtiel woo Serubabel.
english:
After the exile to Babylon:
Jeconiah was the father of Shealtiel,
Shealtiel the father of Zerubbabel,

twi: Serubabel woo Abihud,Abihud woo Eliakim,Eliakim nso woo Asor.
english:
Zerubbabel the father of Abihud,
Abihud the father of Eliakim,
Eliakim the father of Azor,

twi: Asor ba ne Sadok,Sadok ba ne Akim,Akim ba ne Elihud.
english:
Azor the father of Zadok,
Zadok the father of Akim,
Akim the father of Elihud,

twi: Elihud ba ne Eleasar,Eleasar ba ne Matan.Matan nso ba ne Yakob,
english:
Elihud the father of Eleazar,
Eleazar the father of Matthan,
Matthan the father of Jacob,

twi: Yakob woo Yosef a ɔwaree Maria no. Saa Maria yi na ɔwoo Yesu Kristo.
english: and Jacob the father of Joseph, the husband of Mary, and Mary was the mother of Jesus who is called the Messiah.

twi: Awo ntoatoaso a efi Abraham so de besi Ɔhene Dawid so yɛ dunan. Efi Ɔhene Dawid so de besi bere a wɔfaa ɔman no nnommum kɔɔ Babilon no nso awo ntoatoaso yɛ dunan saa ara. Saa ara nso na efi bere a wotu fii Babilon san baa wɔn man mu bio no de besi Kristo awo so nso yɛ awo ntoatoaso dunan.
english: Thus there were fourteen generations in all from Abraham to David, fourteen from David to the exile to Babylon, and fourteen from the exile to the Messiah.

twi: Yesu AwoSɛnea Yesu Kristo awo ho nsɛm te ni: Wɔde ne na Maria maa Yosef sɛ ɔnware no, nanso ansa na wobehyia mu sɛ awarefo no, ohuu sɛ wanyinsɛn; nea efi Honhom Kronkron.
english: This is how the birth of Jesus the Messiah came about: His mother Mary was pledged to be married to Joseph, but before they came together, she was found to be pregnant through the Holy Spirit.

twi: Ɛbaa saa no, ne kunu Yosef a odi ne ho ni no ampɛ sɛ obegu Maria anim ase nti ɔyɛɛ nʼadwene sɛ obegyaa no aware wɔ kokoa mu.
english: Because Joseph her husband was faithful to the law, and yet did not want to expose her to public disgrace, he had in mind to divorce her quietly.

twi: Bere a asɛm no ayɛ Yosef dadwen no, Awurade bɔfo beyii ne ho adi kyerɛɛ no wɔ dae mu. Ɔbɔfo no kae se, “Yosef, Dawid ba, nsuro sɛ wobɛfa Maria sɛ wo yere efisɛ ne nyinsɛn no fi Honhom Kronkron.
english: But after he had considered this, an angel of the Lord appeared to him in a dream and said, “Joseph son of David, do not be afraid to take Mary home as your wife, because what is conceived in her is from the Holy Spirit.

twi: Ɔbɛwo ɔbarima na woato no din Yesu, ase ne Agyenkwa, efisɛ ɔno na obegye ne nkurɔfo nkwa afi wɔn bɔne mu.”
english: She will give birth to a son, and you are to give him the name Jesus, because he will save his people from their sins.”

twi: Eyi nyinaa baa mu de hyɛɛ nea Awurade nam odiyifo no so kae no ma se:
english: All this took place to fulfill what the Lord had said through the prophet:

twi: “Ɔbabun no benyinsɛn, na wawo ɔbabarima, na wɔato no din Immanuel” a ase ne sɛ, “Onyankopɔn ne yɛn wɔ hɔ.”
english: “The virgin will conceive and give birth to a son, and they will call him Immanuel” (which means “God with us”).

twi: Bere a Yosef nyan no, ɔyɛɛ sɛnea ɔbɔfo no hyɛɛ no sɛ ɔnyɛ no. Enti ɔkɔfaa Maria baa ne fi ma ɔbɛyɛɛ ne yere.
english: When Joseph woke up, he did what the angel of the Lord had commanded him and took Mary home as his wife.

twi: Nanso Yosef ne Maria anhyia da kosii sɛ Maria woo ɔbabarima maa Yosef too ne din “Yesu.”
english: But he did not consummate their marriage until she gave birth to a son. And he gave him the name Jesus.

twi: Anyansafo A Wofi Apuei NoBere a Ɔhene Herode di ade no na wɔwoo Yesu wɔ Betlehem a ɛwɔ Yudea.
english: After Jesus was born in Bethlehem in Judea, during the time of King Herod, Magi from the east came to Jerusalem

twi: Saa bere no ara mu na anyansafo bi fi apuei baa Yerusalem bebisae se, “Ɛhe na Yudafo hene a wɔawo no no wɔ? Yehuu ne nsoromma wɔ apuei nohɔ, nti na yɛaba sɛ yɛrebɛsom no.”
english: and asked, “Where is the one who has been born king of the Jews? We saw his star when it rose and have come to worship him.”

twi: Ɔhene Herode tee saa asɛm yi no, ɛhaw ɔne Yerusalemfo nyinaa adwene yiye.
english: When King Herod heard this he was disturbed, and all Jerusalem with him.

twi: Ɔhene Herode frɛɛ ɔman no mu asɔfo mpanyin ne Kyerɛwsɛm no akyerɛkyerɛfo behyiae. Obisaa wɔn se, “Ɛhefa na wɔbɛwo Kristo no?”
english: When he had called together all the people’s chief priests and teachers of the law, he asked them where the Messiah was to be born.

twi: Wobuaa no se, “Betlehem a ɛwɔ Yudea. Na eyi ne nea odiyifo no kae:
english: “In Bethlehem in Judea,” they replied, “for this is what the prophet has written:

twi: “ ‘Ao kurow Betlehem, wo awoyɛ otitiriw wɔ Yudaman mu,wo mu na meyi nea obedime man Israel anim ahwɛ wɔn so.’ ”
english:
“‘But you, Bethlehem, in the land of Judah,
    are by no means least among the rulers of Judah;
for out of you will come a ruler
    who will shepherd my people Israel.’”

twi: Ɔhene Herode frɛɛ anyansafo no kokoa mu bisaa wɔn bere pɔtee a wohuu nsoromma no. Ɔtoaa so ka kyerɛɛ wɔn se,
english: Then Herod called the Magi secretly and found out from them the exact time the star had appeared.

twi: “Monkɔ Betlehem nkɔhwehwɛ abofra no. Sɛ muhu no a, mommɛka nkyerɛ me, na me nso menkɔsom no bi.”
english: He sent them to Bethlehem and said, “Go and search carefully for the child. As soon as you find him, report to me, so that I too may go and worship him.”

twi: Anyansafo no tiee ɔhene no asɛm no wiei no, wɔkɔe. Wɔrekɔ no, nsoromma a wohuu wɔ apuei no san yii ne ho adi bio kyerɛɛ wɔn. Edii wɔn anim kosii faako a wɔawo abofra no wɔ Betlehem hɔ.
english: After they had heard the king, they went on their way, and the star they had seen when it rose went ahead of them until it stopped over the place where the child was.

twi: Bere a wohuu nsoromma no, wɔn ani gyee mmoroso.
english: When they saw the star, they were overjoyed.

twi: Woduu ofi a abofra no ne ne na Maria wɔ mu no, wɔkotow sɔree no. Wɔde wɔn akyɛde a ɛyɛ sikakɔkɔɔ, aduhuam ne kurobow yɛɛ no ayɛ.
english: On coming to the house, they saw the child with his mother Mary, and they bowed down and worshiped him. Then they opened their treasures and presented him with gifts of gold, frankincense and myrrh.

twi: Onyankopɔn soo wɔn dae bɔɔ wɔn kɔkɔ se wɔnnsan nkɔ Herode nkyɛn bio wɔ Yerusalem. Enti wɔfaa ɔkwan foforo so kɔɔ wɔn kurom.
english: And having been warned in a dream not to go back to Herod, they returned to their country by another route.

twi: Wɔbɔ Wɔn Ho Aguaa Wɔ MisraimAnyansafo no kɔ akyi no, Awurade bɔfo soo Yosef dae se, “Sɔre fa abofra no ne ne na na monkɔ Misraim nkɔtena hɔ nkosi sɛ mɛkyerɛ mo bere a mobɛsan aba. Efisɛ Ɔhene Herode rehwehwɛ abofra no akum no.”
english: When they had gone, an angel of the Lord appeared to Joseph in a dream. “Get up,” he said, “take the child and his mother and escape to Egypt. Stay there until I tell you, for Herod is going to search for the child to kill him.”

twi: Anadwo no ara Yosef faa abofra no ne Maria sii mu kɔɔ Misraim,
english: So he got up, took the child and his mother during the night and left for Egypt,

twi: ma wɔtenaa hɔ kosii sɛ Ɔhene Herode wui. Eyi na ɛmaa nea Awurade nam odiyifo no so kae se, “Mafrɛ me Ba afi Misraim” no baa mu.
english: where he stayed until the death of Herod. And so was fulfilled what the Lord had said through the prophet: “Out of Egypt I called my son.”

twi: Betlehem Mmofra No KumHerode huu sɛ anyansafo no adaadaa no no, ne bo fuw mmoroso. Ɔsomaa nʼasraafo se wɔnkɔ Betlehem ne nkurow a atwa ho ahyia no nyinaa mu nkokunkum nkokoaa mmarimaa kosi wɔn a wɔadi mfe abien so, sɛnea anyansafo no bere a wɔkae sɛ wɔwoo abofra no wɔ mu no kyerɛ no.
english: When Herod realized that he had been outwitted by the Magi, he was furious, and he gave orders to kill all the boys in Bethlehem and its vicinity who were two years old and under, in accordance with the time he had learned from the Magi.

twi: Nea wɔnam odiyifo Yeremia so kae no baa mu se,
english: Then what was said through the prophet Jeremiah was fulfilled:

twi: “Wɔte nne bi wɔ Rama.Ɛyɛ osu ne agyaadwo;Rahel resu ne mma;na ɔmpɛ sɛ wɔkyekye ne werɛ,efisɛ wɔnte ase bio.”
english:
“A voice is heard in Ramah,
    weeping and great mourning,
Rachel weeping for her children
    and refusing to be comforted,
    because they are no more.”

twi: Wɔsan Ba NasaretHerode wu akyi no, Awurade bɔfo yii ne ho adi kyerɛɛ Yosef wɔ dae mu wɔ Misraim ka kyerɛɛ no se,
english: After Herod died, an angel of the Lord appeared in a dream to Joseph in Egypt

twi: “Sɔre na fa abofra no ne ne na kɔ Israel asase so, efisɛ wɔn a wɔpɛe sɛ wokum abofra no awuwu.”
english: and said, “Get up, take the child and his mother and go to the land of Israel, for those who were trying to take the child’s life are dead.”

twi: Yosef faa abofra no ne ne na san kɔɔ Israel asase so bio.
english: So he got up, took the child and his mother and went to the land of Israel.

twi: Yosef tee sɛ Arkelao a ɔyɛ Herode ba na odi hene wɔ Yudea saa bere no mu no, osuroo sɛ ɔbɛkɔ hɔ. Awurade san soo no dae foforo bio sɛ ɔnnkɔ Yudea, na mmom, ɔnkɔ Galilea.
english: But when he heard that Archelaus was reigning in Judea in place of his father Herod, he was afraid to go there. Having been warned in a dream, he withdrew to the district of Galilee,

twi: Enti wɔkɔtenaa kurow Nasaret mu. Eyi nso maa nea adiyifo no kae se, “Wɔbɛfrɛ no Nasareni” no baa mu.
english: and he went and lived in a town called Nazareth. So was fulfilled what was said through the prophets, that he would be called a Nazarene.

twi: Osuboni Yohane AsɛnkaBere a Yesu ne nʼawofo wɔ Nasaret no, Osuboni Yohane bɛkaa asɛm wɔ Yudea sare so se,
english: In those days John the Baptist came, preaching in the wilderness of Judea

twi: “Monsakra mo adwene; momfa mo ho mma Onyankopɔn na ɔsoro ahenni no abɛn”
english: and saying, “Repent, for the kingdom of heaven has come near.”

twi: Yohane ne nea odiyifo Yesaia kaa ne ho asɛm se,“Obi nne reteɛ mu wɔ sare so se,‘Mommɔ kwan mma Awurade;momma nʼatempɔn nteɛ!’ ”
english:
This is he who was spoken of through the prophet Isaiah:
“A voice of one calling in the wilderness,
‘Prepare the way for the Lord,
    make straight paths for him.’”

twi: Saa bere no na Yohane fura yoma ho nwi ntama bɔ aboa nhoma abɔso. Na nʼaduan yɛ mmoadabi ne ɛwo.
english: John’s clothes were made of camel’s hair, and he had a leather belt around his waist. His food was locusts and wild honey.

twi: Yerusalemfo ne Yudeafo ne nnipa a wɔte Asubɔnten Yordan ho no nyinaa kɔɔ ne nkyɛn wɔ sare no so hɔ kotiee asɛm no bi.
english: People went out to him from Jerusalem and all Judea and the whole region of the Jordan.

twi: Wɔkaa wɔn bɔne ma ɔbɔɔ wɔn asu wɔ Asubɔnten Yordan mu.
english: Confessing their sins, they were baptized by him in the Jordan River.

twi: Yohane huu sɛ Farisifo ne Sadukifo pii reba ne nkyɛn ma wabɔ wɔn asu no, ɔka kyerɛɛ wɔn se, “Awɔ mma! Hena na ɔka kyerɛɛ mo se munguan mfi Onyankopɔn abufuw a ɛreba no ano?
english: But when he saw many of the Pharisees and Sadducees coming to where he was baptizing, he said to them: “You brood of vipers! Who warned you to flee from the coming wrath?

twi: Monkɔbɔ ɔbra pa mfa nkyerɛ sɛ moasakra ampa.
english: Produce fruit in keeping with repentance.

twi: Na monnhoahoa mo ho sɛ moyɛ Abraham asefo, efisɛ Onyankopɔn betumi ama saa abo yi adan nnipa ma wɔabɛyɛ Abraham asefo.
english: And do not think you can say to yourselves, ‘We have Abraham as our father.’ I tell you that out of these stones God can raise up children for Abraham.

twi: Onyankopɔn de nʼabonnua ato dua biara a ɛnsow aba pa ntin so sɛ ɔde betwa na ɔde agu gya mu ahyew no.
english: The ax is already at the root of the trees, and every tree that does not produce good fruit will be cut down and thrown into the fire.

twi: “Me de, mede nsu na ɛrebɔ wɔn a wɔasakra wɔn su no asu. Nanso nea odi mʼakyi reba no de, ɔso sen me a ne mpaboa mpo mensɛ sɛ mikura. Ɔno de, sɛ ɔba a, ɔde Honhom Kronkron ne ogya na ɛbɛbɔ mo asu.
english: “I baptize you with water for repentance. But after me comes one who is more powerful than I, whose sandals I am not worthy to carry. He will baptize you with the Holy Spirit and fire.

twi: Obehuhuw aburow no so ayiyi mu aba pa no afi ntɛtɛ no mu, na ɔde aba pa no akosie, na ɔde ogya a ennum da ahyew ntɛtɛ no pasaa.”
english: His winnowing fork is in his hand, and he will clear his threshing floor, gathering his wheat into the barn and burning up the chaff with unquenchable fire.”

twi: Yesu AsubɔYesu tee Osuboni Yohane nka no, ofii Galilea baa Asubɔnten Yordan ho sɛ Yohane mmɔ no asu.
english: Then Jesus came from Galilee to the Jordan to be baptized by John.

twi: Yohane huu sɛ ɔmfata sɛ ɔbɔ Yesu asu nti ɔkae se, “Wo na ɛsɛ sɛ wobɔ me asu na ɛnyɛ me.”
english: But John tried to deter him, saying, “I need to be baptized by you, and do you come to me?”

twi: Yesu nso ka kyerɛɛ no se, “Otwa ara na etwa sɛ wobɔ me asu sɛnea ɛbɛyɛ a nea Onyankopɔn ahyɛ ato hɔ no bɛba mu.” Yesu asɛm a ɔkae no nti, Yohane bɔɔ no asu.
english: Jesus replied, “Let it be so now; it is proper for us to do this to fulfill all righteousness.” Then John consented.

twi: Wɔbɔɔ Yesu asu wiei no, ofii asu no mu, na hwɛ, ɔsoro buei. Ohuu Onyankopɔn Honhom sɛ ɛresian ba ne so sɛ aborɔnoma.
english: As soon as Jesus was baptized, he went up out of the water. At that moment heaven was opened, and he saw the Spirit of God descending like a dove and alighting on him.

twi: Ɛhɔ ara, nne bi fi ɔsoro kae se, “Oyi ne me Dɔba a ɔsɔ mʼani.”
english: And a voice from heaven said, “This is my Son, whom I love; with him I am well pleased.”

twi: Ɔbonsam Sɔ Yesu HwɛEyi akyi no, Honhom Kronkron faa Yesu kɔɔ sare so sɛ ɔbonsam nkɔsɔ no nhwɛ.
english: Then Jesus was led by the Spirit into the wilderness to be tempted by the devil.

twi: Saa bere no mu, Yesu dii mmuada adaduanan; awia ne anadwo. Eyi maa ɔkɔm dee no.
english: After fasting forty days and forty nights, he was hungry.

twi: Ɔbonsam baa Yesu nkyɛn bɛka kyerɛɛ no se, “Sɛ wone Onyankopɔn Ba no a, ka na saa abo yi nnan aduan.”
english: The tempter came to him and said, “If you are the Son of God, tell these stones to become bread.”

twi: Yesu buaa no se, “Wɔakyerɛw se, ‘Ɛnyɛ aduan nko ara na ɛho hia onipa wɔ nʼasetena mu, na mmom asɛm biara a efi Awurade anom.’ ”
english: Jesus answered, “It is written: ‘Man shall not live on bread alone, but on every word that comes from the mouth of God.’”

twi: Afei ɔbonsam de Yesu kɔɔ Yerusalem de no kogyinaa asɔredan a ɛwɔ hɔ no atifi pɛɛ,
english: Then the devil took him to the holy city and had him stand on the highest point of the temple.

twi: na ɔka kyerɛɛ no se, “Sɛ wone Onyankopɔn Ba no ampa ara a, huruw fi nea wugyina hɔ si fam, efisɛ, wɔakyerɛw se,“ ‘Onyankopɔn bɛsoma nʼabɔfo abeso wo mu,wɔde wɔn nsa bɛma wo so,na wo nan ampem ɔbo.’ ”
english:
“If you are the Son of God,” he said, “throw yourself down. For it is written:
“‘He will command his angels concerning you,
    and they will lift you up in their hands,
    so that you will not strike your foot against a stone.’”

twi: Yesu buaa bio se, “Wɔakyerɛw se, ‘Nsɔ Awurade wo Nyankopɔn nhwɛ.’ ”
english: Jesus answered him, “It is also written: ‘Do not put the Lord your God to the test.’”

twi: Eyi akyi no, ɔbonsam de Yesu kɔɔ bepɔw tenten bi apampam. Ɔde nʼani kari kyerɛɛ no wiase ahenni ahorow ne mu anuonyam nyinaa.
english: Again, the devil took him to a very high mountain and showed him all the kingdoms of the world and their splendor.

twi: Afei ɔka kyerɛɛ Yesu se, “Sɛ wobɛkotow asom me a, mede nea wuhu yi nyinaa bɛma wo.”
english: “All this I will give you,” he said, “if you will bow down and worship me.”

twi: Ɛhɔ ara na Yesu buae se, “Fi me so, Satan! Hu sɛ wɔakyerɛw se, ‘Kotow som Awurade, wo Nyankopɔn, na ɔno nko ara na som no.’ ”
english: Jesus said to him, “Away from me, Satan! For it is written: ‘Worship the Lord your God, and serve him only.’”

twi: Yesu ano sii no, ɔbonsam gyaw no hɔ kɔe. Ɛno akyi no abɔfo baa Yesu nkyɛn bɛsom no.
english: Then the devil left him, and angels came and attended him.

twi: Yesu Fi Nʼadwuma Ase Wɔ GalileaYesu tee sɛ wɔakyere Yohane no, ɔkɔɔ Galilea.
english: When Jesus heard that John had been put in prison, he withdrew to Galilee.

twi: Oduu Galilea no, wantena Nasaret, na mmom otwaa mu wɔ Nasaret hɔ kɔtenaa Kapernaum a ɛwɔ Galilea mpoano no, Sebulon ne Naftali ahye so.
english: Leaving Nazareth, he went and lived in Capernaum, which was by the lake in the area of Zebulun and Naphtali—

twi: Eyi maa nea Odiyifo Yesaia kae no baa mu sɛ,
english: to fulfill what was said through the prophet Isaiah:

twi: “Sebulon asase ne Naftali asase,ɛpo kwan so, Yordan agya,Galilea a amanamanmufo te hɔ,
english:
“Land of Zebulun and land of Naphtali,
    the Way of the Sea, beyond the Jordan,
    Galilee of the Gentiles—

twi: nnipa a wɔte sum mu no,Hann kɛse bi apue ama wɔn.Hann no apue amawɔn a wɔte owu asase so.”
english:
the people living in darkness
    have seen a great light;
on those living in the land of the shadow of death
    a light has dawned.”

twi: Efi saa bere no, Yesu fii nʼasɛnka ase se, “Monsakra mo adwene, momfa mo ho mma Onyankopɔn na ɔsoro ahenni no abɛn.”
english: From that time on Jesus began to preach, “Repent, for the kingdom of heaven has come near.”

twi: Yesu Frɛ Asuafo BaananDa bi a Yesu nam Galilea mpoano no, ohuu anuanom baanu bi a wɔn nyinaa yɛ apopofo sɛ wɔregu asau wɔ po no mu. Saa anuanom yi mu baako din de Simon a ne din foforo nso de Petro. Ɔbaako no nso din de Andrea.
english: As Jesus was walking beside the Sea of Galilee, he saw two brothers, Simon called Peter and his brother Andrew. They were casting a net into the lake, for they were fishermen.

twi: Yesu ka kyerɛɛ wɔn se, “Mummedi mʼakyi na mɛsoma mo ama moakoyi nnipa kra.”
english: “Come, follow me,” Jesus said, “and I will send you out to fish for people.”

twi: Ɛhɔ ara wogyaw wɔn asau no guu hɔ kodii nʼakyi ne no kɔe.
english: At once they left their nets and followed him.

twi: Ɔkɔɔ nʼanim kakra no, ohuu Sebedeo mma baanu a wɔfrɛ ɔbaako Yohane na ɔbaako nso din de Yakobo sɛ wɔne wɔn agya te ɔkorow mu repempam wɔn asau mu. Yesu frɛɛ wɔn nso se wommedi nʼakyi.
english: Going on from there, he saw two other brothers, James son of Zebedee and his brother John. They were in a boat with their father Zebedee, preparing their nets. Jesus called them,

twi: Ntɛm ara, wogyaw wɔn agya ne ɔkorow no hɔ kodii nʼakyi.
english: and immediately they left the boat and their father and followed him.

twi: Galilea Asɛnka Ne AyaresaYesu kyinkyinii Galileaman mu nyinaa kaa ahenni no ho asɛmpa wɔ Yudafo hyiadan mu. Ɔsaa nyarewa ahorow a wɔde baa nʼanim nyinaa nso.
english: Jesus went throughout Galilee, teaching in their synagogues, proclaiming the good news of the kingdom, and healing every disease and sickness among the people.

twi: Yesu anwonwade a ɔyɛe yi trɛw koduu Siriaman mu nyinaa. Eyi ma wɔde wɔn a ahonhommɔne wɔ wɔn so, wɔn a wotwa, wɔn a wɔyare mmubui ne wɔn a nyarewa ahorow haw wɔn no nyinaa fi Siriaman mu brɛɛ no ma ɔsaa wɔn nyinaa yare.
english: News about him spread all over Syria, and people brought to him all who were ill with various diseases, those suffering severe pain, the demon-possessed, those having seizures, and the paralyzed; and he healed them.

twi: Anwonwade a Yesu yɛɛ yi maa nnipakuw a wofi Galilea ne nkurow “Dekapoli” no mu ne Yerusalem ne Yordan agya tu dii nʼakyi.
english: Large crowds from Galilee, the Decapolis, Jerusalem, Judea and the region across the Jordan followed him.

twi: Nhyira NsɛmOhuu nnipakuw no saa no, ɔkɔɔ bepɔw bi so. Ɔtenaa ase no, nʼasuafo no kɔɔ ne nkyɛn.
english: Now when Jesus saw the crowds, he went up on a mountainside and sat down. His disciples came to him,

twi: Na ofii ase kyerɛkyerɛɛ wɔn se,
english:
and he began to teach them.
He said:

twi: “Nhyira ne wɔn a wonim sɛ wɔyɛ ahiafo wɔ honhom mu,na wɔn na ɔsoro ahenni yɛ wɔn dea.
english:
“Blessed are the poor in spirit,
    for theirs is the kingdom of heaven.

twi: Nhyira ne wɔn a wɔn werɛ ahow,na wɔn na Onyankopɔn bɛkyekye wɔn werɛ.
english:
Blessed are those who mourn,
    for they will be comforted.

twi: Nhyira ne ahobrɛasefo,na wɔn na Onyankopɔn bɛma wɔadi asase so.
english:
Blessed are the meek,
    for they will inherit the earth.

twi: Nhyira ne wɔn a wɔn pɛ ne sɛ wɔbɛyɛ Onyankopɔn apɛde,na wɔn na Onyankopɔn bɛma wɔn nea ehia wɔn.
english:
Blessed are those who hunger and thirst for righteousness,
    for they will be filled.

twi: Nhyira ne wɔn a wohu mmɔbɔ,na wɔn na Onyankopɔn behu wɔn mmɔbɔ.
english:
Blessed are the merciful,
    for they will be shown mercy.

twi: Nhyira ne wɔn a wɔn koma mu tew,na wɔn na wobehu Onyankopɔn.
english:
Blessed are the pure in heart,
    for they will see God.

twi: Nhyira ne apatafo,na wɔn na Onyankopɔn bɛfrɛ wɔn ne mma.
english:
Blessed are the peacemakers,
    for they will be called children of God.

twi: Nhyira ne wɔn a esiane sɛ wɔyɛ Onyankopɔn apɛde nti, wɔtaa wɔn,na wɔn na Ɔsoro Ahenni no yɛ wɔn dea.
english:
Blessed are those who are persecuted because of righteousness,
    for theirs is the kingdom of heaven.

twi: “Nhyira ne mo a me din mu nti, wɔyaw mo, taa mo, twa atoro, ka asɛmmɔne to mo so.
english: “Blessed are you when people insult you, persecute you and falsely say all kinds of evil against you because of me.

twi: Momma mo ani nnye na monsɛpɛw mo ho, efisɛ mowɔ akatua a ɛso wɔ ɔsoro. Munhu sɛ saa ara na wɔtaa adiyifo a wodii mo kan no.”
english: Rejoice and be glad, because great is your reward in heaven, for in the same way they persecuted the prophets who were before you.

twi: Nkyene Ne Kanea“Mone asase yi so nkyene. Sɛ nkyene dɛ yera a, ɔkwan bɛn so na wɔbɛfa ama ayɛ nkyene bio? Enye mma hwee bio, gye sɛ wohwie gu na nnipa tiatia so.
english: “You are the salt of the earth. But if the salt loses its saltiness, how can it be made salty again? It is no longer good for anything, except to be thrown out and trampled underfoot.

twi: “Mone wiase kanea. Kurow a ɛda bepɔw so no ntumi nhintaw.
english: “You are the light of the world. A town built on a hill cannot be hidden.

twi: Wɔnnsɔ kanea mfa nsie, na mmom wɔde si petee mu na ahyerɛn ama wɔn a wɔwɔ ofi no mu no nyinaa.
english: Neither do people light a lamp and put it under a bowl. Instead they put it on its stand, and it gives light to everyone in the house.

twi: Saa ara na momma mo nneyɛe pa nna adi mma nnipa nhu na wɔafa so ahyɛ mo Agya a ɔwɔ soro no anuonyam.”
english: In the same way, let your light shine before others, that they may see your good deeds and glorify your Father in heaven.

twi: Mmara No Mu Denhyɛ“Munnsusuw sɛ maba sɛ merebɛsɛe Mmara no anaa Adiyifo no nkyerɛkyerɛ no. Na mmom maba sɛ merebɛhyɛ no ma sɛnea ne nyinaa bɛba mu pɛpɛɛpɛ.
english: “Do not think that I have come to abolish the Law or the Prophets; I have not come to abolish them but to fulfill them.

twi: Munhu sɛ ɔsoro ne asase da so wɔ hɔ yi, Mmara no mu biribiara rensakra da kosi sɛ ne nyinaa bɛba mu.
english: For truly I tell you, until heaven and earth disappear, not the smallest letter, not the least stroke of a pen, will by any means disappear from the Law until everything is accomplished.

twi: Eyi nti, obiara a obebu mmara nsɛm no mu fa bi so na ɔbɛkyerɛkyerɛ afoforo ama wɔn nso abu mmara nsɛm no mu fa bi so no bɛyɛ akumaa ɔsoro ahenni mu. Na obiara a obedi mmara no so, na ɔbɛkyerɛkyerɛ afoforo ama wɔn nso adi mmara no so no bɛyɛ ɔkɛse Ɔsoro Ahenni mu.
english: Therefore anyone who sets aside one of the least of these commands and teaches others accordingly will be called least in the kingdom of heaven, but whoever practices and teaches these commands will be called great in the kingdom of heaven.

twi: Enti merebɔ mo kɔkɔ sɛ, sɛ mopɛ sɛ mokɔ ɔsoro ahenni mu de a, gye sɛ moyɛ Onyankopɔn apɛde sen nea Kyerɛwsɛm no akyerɛkyerɛfo no ne Farisifo no yɛ.
english: For I tell you that unless your righteousness surpasses that of the Pharisees and the teachers of the law, you will certainly not enter the kingdom of heaven.

twi: Abufuw Ho Mmara“Mose mmara no ka se, ‘Nea odi awu no, ɔno nso ɛsɛ sɛ wokum no bi.’
english: “You have heard that it was said to the people long ago, ‘You shall not murder, and anyone who murders will be subject to judgment.’

twi: Na me de, nea mereka ne sɛ, obiara a ne bo befuw ne nua no, wobebu no atɛn. Bio, obiara a ɔbɛyeyaw ne nua no, wɔbɛfrɛ no wɔ mpanyin anim. Afei obiara a ɔbɛka akyerɛ ne nua se, ‘Ogyimifo’ no bɛkɔ amanehunu gya mu.
english: But I tell you that anyone who is angry with a brother or sister will be subject to judgment. Again, anyone who says to a brother or sister, ‘Raca,’ is answerable to the court. And anyone who says, ‘You fool!’ will be in danger of the fire of hell.

twi: “Enti sɛ ɛba sɛ worekɔbɔ afɔre na wokae sɛ wo ne wo nua wɔ asɛm a,
english: “Therefore, if you are offering your gift at the altar and there remember that your brother or sister has something against you,

twi: gyae afɔre no bɔ, na kɔ na wo ne wo nua no nkɔbɔ mu ansa na woakɔbɔ wʼafɔre no.
english: leave your gift there in front of the altar. First go and be reconciled to them; then come and offer your gift.

twi: “Sɛ wo ne obi nya asɛm a, wo ne no mmɔ mu ntɛm, na wamfa wo ankɔ asennii ankɔma otemmufo, na otemmufo no amfa wo anhyɛ afiasehwɛfo nsa, na afiasehwɛfo no amfa wo ankɔto afiase.
english: “Settle matters quickly with your adversary who is taking you to court. Do it while you are still together on the way, or your adversary may hand you over to the judge, and the judge may hand you over to the officer, and you may be thrown into prison.

twi: Mereka no nokware akyerɛ mo se, ansa na wubefi asennii hɔ no, gye sɛ woatua sika biara a wɔregye afi wo hɔ no.
english: Truly I tell you, you will not get out until you have paid the last penny.

twi: Aguamammɔ“Mose mmara no ka se, ‘Nsɛe aware.’
english: “You have heard that it was said, ‘You shall not commit adultery.’

twi: Na me de, nea mereka ne sɛ: Obiara a ohu ɔbea na ne kɔn dɔ no ne koma mu no, abɔ aguaman.
english: But I tell you that anyone who looks at a woman lustfully has already committed adultery with her in his heart.

twi: Sɛ wʼani baako a eye to wo hintidua a, eye sɛ wubetu atow akyene. Efisɛ eye sɛ wobɛhwere wʼakwaa fa bi sen sɛ wɔbɛtow wo nipadua no nyinaa akyene amanehunu gya mu.
english: If your right eye causes you to stumble, gouge it out and throw it away. It is better for you to lose one part of your body than for your whole body to be thrown into hell.

twi: Saa ara nso na sɛ wo nsa a eye to wo hintidua a, eye sɛ wubetwa atow akyene. Efisɛ eye sɛ wobɛhwere wʼakwaa fa bi sen sɛ wɔbɛtow wo nipadua nyinaa akyene amanehunu gya mu.
english: And if your right hand causes you to stumble, cut it off and throw it away. It is better for you to lose one part of your body than for your whole body to go into hell.

twi: Awaregyae“Mose mmara no ka se, ‘Obiara a obegyaa ne yere no mma no awaregyae krataa.’
english: “It has been said, ‘Anyone who divorces his wife must give her a certificate of divorce.’

twi: Na me de, nea mereka ne sɛ, sɛ ɔbarima bi gyaa ne yere a ɛnyɛ sɛ ɔbea no abɔ aguaman na ɔbea no san kɔware bio a, na ɔbarima a ogyaa no no ama ɔbea no asɛe aware. Ɔbarima foforo a ɔbɛware ɔbea no nso asɛe aware saa ara.
english: But I tell you that anyone who divorces his wife, except for sexual immorality, makes her the victim of adultery, and anyone who marries a divorced woman commits adultery.

twi: Ɔkasa Mu Nokwaredi“Bio, Mose mmara no ka se, ‘Mmu bɔ a woahyɛ Onyankopɔn no so, na mmom di bɔ a woahyɛ no no so.’
english: “Again, you have heard that it was said to the people long ago, ‘Do not break your oath, but fulfill to the Lord the vows you have made.’

twi: Na me de, nea mereka ne sɛ: Monnka ntam mmfa nhyɛ bɔ. Monnnɔ ɔsoro, efisɛ ɛyɛ Onyankopɔn ahengua.
english: But I tell you, do not swear an oath at all: either by heaven, for it is God’s throne;

twi: Monnnɔ fam, efisɛ ɛyɛ Onyankopɔn nan ase agua. Monnnɔ Yerusalem, efisɛ ɛyɛ ɔhenkɛse kuropɔn.
english: or by the earth, for it is his footstool; or by Jerusalem, for it is the city of the Great King.

twi: Mfa wo ti nka ntam, efisɛ worentumi nnan tinwi baako mpo mma ɛnyɛ fitaa anaa tuntum.
english: And do not swear by your head, for you cannot make even one hair white or black.

twi: Momma mo nsɛm nyɛ ‘Yiw’ anaa ‘Dabi.’ Asɛm biara a wobɛka a ɛnyɛ Yiw anaa dabi no fi ɔbonsam.
english: All you need to say is simply ‘Yes’ or ‘No’; anything beyond this comes from the evil one.

twi: Aweretɔ“Mose mmara no ka se, ‘Sɛ obi tu wʼani a, tu ne de bi. Sɛ obi tu wo se nso a, tu ne de bi.’
english: “You have heard that it was said, ‘Eye for eye, and tooth for tooth.’

twi: Na me de, nea mereka ne se: Mommfa bɔne ntua bɔne so ka! Sɛ obi bɔ wʼaso nifa mu a, dan benkum no nso ma no na ɔmmɔ mu.
english: But I tell you, do not resist an evil person. If anyone slaps you on the right cheek, turn to them the other cheek also.

twi: Sɛ obi ne wo di asɛm gye wʼatade nhyɛase a, worɔw wʼatade nguguso ka ho ma no.
english: And if anyone wants to sue you and take your shirt, hand over your coat as well.

twi: Sɛ obi hyɛ wo sɛ, wo ne no nnantew ɔkwansin baako a, wo ne no nkɔ akwansin abien.
english: If anyone forces you to go one mile, go with them two miles.

twi: Sɛ obi srɛ wo biribi a, fa ma no; obi pɛ sɛ ɔfɛm wo hɔ biribi a, fa fɛm no.
english: Give to the one who asks you, and do not turn away from the one who wants to borrow from you.

twi: Dɔ Wʼatamfo“Moate sɛ wɔaka se, ‘Dɔ wo yɔnko na tan wo tamfo.’
english: “You have heard that it was said, ‘Love your neighbor and hate your enemy.’

twi: Na me de, nea mereka ne sɛ: monnɔ mo atamfo na mommɔ mpae mma wɔn a wɔhaw mo.
english: But I tell you, love your enemies and pray for those who persecute you,

twi: Eyi bɛma moayɛ mo Agya a ɔwɔ ɔsoro no mma, efisɛ ɔma ne owia pue, ma ne osu tɔ ma nnipa bɔne ne nnipa pa nyinaa pɛ.
english: that you may be children of your Father in heaven. He causes his sun to rise on the evil and the good, and sends rain on the righteous and the unrighteous.

twi: Sɛ modɔ wɔn a wɔdɔ mo no nko ara a, akatua bɛn na mubenya? Ɛnyɛ saa ara na nnebɔneyɛfo nso yɛ?
english: If you love those who love you, what reward will you get? Are not even the tax collectors doing that?

twi: Sɛ mukyia wɔn a munim wɔn nko ara a, nsonoe bɛn na ɛda mo ne afoforo ntam? Ɛnyɛ saa ara na nnebɔneyɛfo nso yɛ?
english: And if you greet only your own people, what are you doing more than others? Do not even pagans do that?

twi: Enti monyɛ pɛ sɛnea mo Agya a ɔwɔ ɔsoro no yɛ pɛ no.
english: Be perfect, therefore, as your heavenly Father is perfect.

twi: Nyaatwom Papayɛ Ho Kɔkɔbɔ“Monhwɛ yiye na moanyɛ papa ankyerɛ nnipa amfa ampɛ anuonyam. Sɛ moyɛ saa a, morennya mfaso biara mfi mo Agya a ɔwɔ ɔsoro no nkyɛn.
english: “Be careful not to practice your righteousness in front of others to be seen by them. If you do, you will have no reward from your Father in heaven.

twi: “Sɛ woyɛ papa a mmɔ no dawuru sɛnea nyaatwomfo yɛ wɔ asɔredan mu ne mmɔnten so no. Merema mo ate sɛ saa nnipa no anya wɔn akatua dedaw.
english: “So when you give to the needy, do not announce it with trumpets, as the hypocrites do in the synagogues and on the streets, to be honored by others. Truly I tell you, they have received their reward in full.

twi: Sɛ woyɛ papa a, mma obiara nhu, mpo sɛ wode wo nsa nifa yɛ papa a, mma wo nsa benkum nhu,
english: But when you give to the needy, do not let your left hand know what your right hand is doing,

twi: na wʼagya a onim kokoa mu nsɛm nyinaa no betua wo ka.
english: so that your giving may be in secret. Then your Father, who sees what is done in secret, will reward you.

twi: Nyaatwom Mpaebɔ Ho Kɔkɔbɔ“Na sɛ morebɔ mpae a, mommmɔ mpae sɛnea nyaatwomfo gyina asɔredan mu ne mmɔnten so bɔ mpae de pɛ nnipa anim anuonyam no. Merema moate ase sɛ, saa nnipa no anya wɔn akatua dedaw.
english: “And when you pray, do not be like the hypocrites, for they love to pray standing in the synagogues and on the street corners to be seen by others. Truly I tell you, they have received their reward in full.

twi: Sɛ wobɔ mpae a, hyɛn wo dan mu, na to wo pon mu, na bɔ wʼAgya a wonhu no no mpae, na wʼAgya a onim kokoa mu nsɛm no betua wo ka.
english: But when you pray, go into your room, close the door and pray to your Father, who is unseen. Then your Father, who sees what is done in secret, will reward you.

twi: Sɛ mobɔ mpae a, monnkasakasa bebree, nti nsɛm mu nsusuw sɛ, sɛ moyɛ saa a na Onyankopɔn betie mo.
english: And when you pray, do not keep on babbling like pagans, for they think they will be heard because of their many words.

twi: Mo Agya Nyankopɔn nim nea ehia mo nyinaa ansa na mubisa no.
english: Do not be like them, for your Father knows what you need before you ask him.

twi: “Enti saa ɔkwan yi so na momfa mmɔ mpae:“ ‘Yɛn Agya a wowɔ ɔsoro,wo din ho ntew.
english:
“This, then, is how you should pray:
“‘Our Father in heaven,
hallowed be your name,

twi: Wʼahenni mmra.Nea wopɛ nyɛ wɔ asase so,sɛnea ɛyɛ wɔ ɔsoro.
english:
your kingdom come,
your will be done,
    on earth as it is in heaven.

twi: Ma yɛn, yɛn daa aduan nnɛ,
english: Give us today our daily bread.

twi: na fa yɛn aka kyɛ yɛn,sɛnea yɛde kyɛ wɔn a wɔde yɛn aka.
english:
And forgive us our debts,
    as we also have forgiven our debtors.

twi: Nnyaa yɛn nkɔ sɔhwɛ mu.Na yi yɛn fi ɔbɔnefo no nsam.’
english:
And lead us not into temptation,
    but deliver us from the evil one.’

twi: Sɛ mode wɔn a wɔfom mo mfomso kyɛ wɔn a, mo nso mo ɔsoro Agya no de mo mfomso bɛkyɛ mo.
english: For if you forgive other people when they sin against you, your heavenly Father will also forgive you.

twi: Nanso sɛ moamfa wɔn a wɔfom mo mfomso ankyɛ wɔn a, mo ɔsoro Agya no nso remfa mo mfomso nkyɛ mo.”
english: But if you do not forgive others their sins, your Father will not forgive your sins.

twi: Nyaatwom Mmuadadi Ho Kɔkɔbɔ“Sɛ mudi mmuada a, monnyɛ mo anim mmɔbɔmmɔbɔ sɛnea nyaatwomfo di mmuada a wɔyɛ de pɛ nnipa anim anuonyam no. Merema mo ate ase sɛ, saa nnipa no anya wɔn akatua dedaw.
english: “When you fast, do not look somber as the hypocrites do, for they disfigure their faces to show others they are fasting. Truly I tell you, they have received their reward in full.

twi: Sɛ wudi mmuada a, serɛn wo ti, na hohoro wʼanim, na ma wʼanim nyɛ frɔmfrɔm,
english: But when you fast, put oil on your head and wash your face,

twi: na mma nnipa nhu sɛ woredi mmuada, gye wʼAgya a ohu nea woyɛ wɔ kokoa mu nyinaa no nko ara; na wʼAgya a onim kokoa mu nsɛm nyinaa no betua wo ka.
english: so that it will not be obvious to others that you are fasting, but only to your Father, who is unseen; and your Father, who sees what is done in secret, will reward you.

twi: “Monnhyehyɛ mo agyapade wɔ asase yi so, nea ntɛferɛw betumi awe, na ebetumi agye nkannare na asɛe, na akorɔmfo betumi awia.
english: “Do not store up for yourselves treasures on earth, where moths and vermin destroy, and where thieves break in and steal.

twi: Mmom monhyehyɛ mo agyapade wɔ ɔsoro, nea ntɛferɛw ntumi nwe, na entumi nnye nkannare nsɛe, na akorɔmfo ntumi nwia.
english: But store up for yourselves treasures in heaven, where moths and vermin do not destroy, and where thieves do not break in and steal.

twi: Na nea wʼagyapade wɔ no, ɛhɔ na wo koma nso wɔ.
english: For where your treasure is, there your heart will be also.

twi: “Wʼani yɛ wo nipadua kanea. Ɛno nti sɛ wʼani ye a, na wo nipadua nyinaa yɛ hann.
english: “The eye is the lamp of the body. If your eyes are healthy, your whole body will be full of light.

twi: Nanso sɛ wʼaniwa nye a, ɛma wo nipadua no nyinaa dan sum tumm. Enti sɛ hann a ɛwɔ wo mu no yɛ sum a, na wo nipadua no yɛ sum kabii.
english: But if your eyes are unhealthy, your whole body will be full of darkness. If then the light within you is darkness, how great is that darkness!

twi: “Obiara ntumi nsom awuranom baanu, efisɛ ɔyɛ saa a, ɔbɛdɔ ɔbaako na watan ɔbaako anaasɛ, ɔbɛsom ɔbaako yiye na wabu ɔbaako animtiaa. Morentumi nsom Onyankopɔn ne ahonyade.
english: “No one can serve two masters. Either you will hate the one and love the other, or you will be devoted to the one and despise the other. You cannot serve both God and money.

twi: “Eyi nti na mitu mo fo se, munnnwinnwen nea mubedi anaa nea mobɛnom anaa nea mubefura ho. Mowɔ ɔkra ne nipadua a ɛsom bo sen nea mubedi ne nea mubefura.
english: “Therefore I tell you, do not worry about your life, what you will eat or drink; or about your body, what you will wear. Is not life more than food, and the body more than clothes?

twi: Monhwɛ wim nnomaa, wonnua aba na wontwa aba mmoaboa ano mfa nsie, nanso mo Agya a ɔwɔ ɔsoro no ma wɔn aduan di. Monnsom bo nsen wɔn ana?
english: Look at the birds of the air; they do not sow or reap or store away in barns, and yet your heavenly Father feeds them. Are you not much more valuable than they?

twi: Mo mu hena na ɔdwene a adwennwene no betumi ato ne nkwa nna so simmasin mpo?
english: Can any one of you by worrying add a single hour to your life?

twi: “Adɛn nti na mudwinnwen ntama ho? Monhwɛ afifide bi sɛ wuram nhwiren, wɔnnwene ntama ho.
english: “And why do you worry about clothes? See how the flowers of the field grow. They do not labor or spin.

twi: Nanso Salomo ahonya ne nʼanuonyam nyinaa akyi no, na nʼahoɔfɛ nnu wuram nhwiren yi.
english: Yet I tell you that not even Solomon in all his splendor was dressed like one of these.

twi: Na sɛ Onyankopɔn tumi fura afifide a ɛwɔ hɔ nnɛ na ɔkyena enni hɔ ntama a, mo a mo gyidi sua, ɛbɛyɛ dɛn na ɔrentumi mma mo nea ehia mo?
english: If that is how God clothes the grass of the field, which is here today and tomorrow is thrown into the fire, will he not much more clothe you—you of little faith?

twi: Enti munnnwinnwen nea mubedi, nea mobɛnom anaasɛ nea mubefura ho.
english: So do not worry, saying, ‘What shall we eat?’ or ‘What shall we drink?’ or ‘What shall we wear?’

twi: Na wɔn a wonni gyidi no na bere biara wodwen saa nneɛma no ho. Na mo de, mo Agya a ɔwɔ ɔsoro no nim sɛ eyinom nyinaa ho hia mo.
english: For the pagans run after all these things, and your heavenly Father knows that you need them.

twi: Enti monhwehwɛ Onyankopɔn Ahenni ne ne trenee kan, na ɔde nea ehia mo nyinaa bɛka mo ho.
english: But seek first his kingdom and his righteousness, and all these things will be given to you as well.

twi: Enti munnnwinnwen ɔkyena ho. Onyankopɔn no ara de nea ehia mo no bɛma mo. Ɛda biara ne mu nsɛm.
english: Therefore do not worry about tomorrow, for tomorrow will worry about itself. Each day has enough trouble of its own.

twi: Atɛnyi“Mummmu ntɛn, na afoforo ammu mo ntɛn.
english: “Do not judge, or you too will be judged.

twi: Nea mode yɛ afoforo no, ɛno ara na wɔde bɛyɛ mo.
english: For in the same way you judge others, you will be judged, and with the measure you use, it will be measured to you.

twi: “Adɛn na woma dua ntɛtɛ a ɛda wo nua ani so no haw wo, bere a mpuran a ɛda wo de so no mfa wo ho?
english: “Why do you look at the speck of sawdust in your brother’s eye and pay no attention to the plank in your own eye?

twi: Ɛbɛyɛ dɛn na woatumi aka akyerɛ wo nua se, ‘Ma minyi ntɛtɛ a ɛda wʼani so no mma wo,’ bere a mpuran da wʼani so daa.
english: How can you say to your brother, ‘Let me take the speck out of your eye,’ when all the time there is a plank in your own eye?

twi: Nyaatwomni! Di kan yi mpuran a ɛda wʼankasa ani so no ansa na woatumi ahu ntɛtɛ a ɛda wo nua ani so no yiye na woayi ama no.
english: You hypocrite, first take the plank out of your own eye, and then you will see clearly to remove the speck from your brother’s eye.

twi: “Mommfa nea ɛho tew mma akraman. Saa ara nso na monntow mo nhene pa ngu mprako anim! Wobetiatia so, na wɔadan wɔn ho atow ahyɛ mo so.
english: “Do not give dogs what is sacred; do not throw your pearls to pigs. If you do, they may trample them under their feet, and turn and tear you to pieces.

twi: Bisa, Hwehwɛ, Pem“Mummisa, na wɔbɛma mo; monhwehwɛ, na mubehu; mompem, na wobebue mo.
english: “Ask and it will be given to you; seek and you will find; knock and the door will be opened to you.

twi: Na obiara a obisa no, onya. Obiara a ɔhwehwɛ no, ohu; na nea ɔpem no, wobue no.
english: For everyone who asks receives; the one who seeks finds; and to the one who knocks, the door will be opened.

twi: “Na hena na ne ba bisa no brodo a ɔbɛma no ɔbo?
english: “Which of you, if your son asks for bread, will give him a stone?

twi: Anaasɛ obisa no nsumnam a ɔbɛma no ɔwɔ? Ɛremma saa da!
english: Or if he asks for a fish, will give him a snake?

twi: Na sɛ mo a moyɛ abɔnefo mpo nim sɛnea moma mo mma nnepa a, ɛbɛyɛ dɛn na mo Agya a ɔwɔ ɔsoro no mfa nnepa mma ne mma wɔn a wobisa no no?
english: If you, then, though you are evil, know how to give good gifts to your children, how much more will your Father in heaven give good gifts to those who ask him!

twi: Enti sɛnea mmara no ne adiyifo no ka no, ade biara a mopɛ sɛ nnipa nyɛ mma mo no, mo nso monyɛ mma wɔn saa ara.
english: So in everything, do to others what you would have them do to you, for this sums up the Law and the Prophets.

twi: Ɔpon Ne Ɔkwan Hiahiaa No“Ɔkwan teateaa no nko ara so na wubetumi afa akɔ ɔsoro! Ɔkwan a ɛkɔ ɔbonsam kurom no trɛw, na nʼapon nso mu bae ma nnipadɔm a wɔfa so kɔ ɔsɛe mu.
english: “Enter through the narrow gate. For wide is the gate and broad is the road that leads to destruction, and many enter through it.

twi: Ɔpon a wowura mu de kɔ nkwa mu no yɛ hiahiaa na ɔkwan a wɔfa so no nso yɛ teateaa, na nnipa kakraa bi na wohu fa so.
english: But small is the gate and narrow the road that leads to life, and only a few find it.

twi: “Monhwɛ mo ho yiye wɔ atoro akyerɛkyerɛfo a wɔba mo nkyɛn ahobrɛase mu sɛ nguan, nanso wɔyɛ mpataku a wonya mo a, wɔbɛtetew mo pasaa no ho.
english: “Watch out for false prophets. They come to you in sheep’s clothing, but inwardly they are ferocious wolves.

twi: Wɔn nneyɛe na mode behu wɔn, sɛnea mutumi de dua bi aba hu dua ko a ɛyɛ no. Worentumi ntew bobe wɔ nsɔe so; saa ara nso na worentumi ntew borɔdɔma wɔ nnɛnkyɛnse so.
english: By their fruit you will recognize them. Do people pick grapes from thornbushes, or figs from thistles?

twi: Dua a ɛwɔ nnyinaso pa no tumi sow aba pa; na dua a enni nnyinaso pa no nso sow aba bɔne.
english: Likewise, every good tree bears good fruit, but a bad tree bears bad fruit.

twi: Dua pa ntumi nsow aba bɔne; saa ara nso na dua bɔne ntumi nsow aba pa.
english: A good tree cannot bear bad fruit, and a bad tree cannot bear good fruit.

twi: Dua biara a ɛnsow aba pa no, wotwa de gu gya mu hyew no.
english: Every tree that does not bear good fruit is cut down and thrown into the fire.

twi: Onipa nneyɛe na ɛma wohu ne suban.
english: Thus, by their fruit you will recognize them.

twi: “Ɛnyɛ obiara a ɔbɔ me din ‘Awurade, Awurade’ no na ɔbɛkɔ ɔsoro ahemman mu.
english: “Not everyone who says to me, ‘Lord, Lord,’ will enter the kingdom of heaven, but only the one who does the will of my Father who is in heaven.

twi: Atemmu da no, nnipa pii bɛka akyerɛ me se, ‘Awurade, yɛkaa wo ho asɛm kyerɛɛ afoforo. Yɛnam wo din nso so tuu ahonhommɔne, san yɛɛ anwonwade, ahorow.’
english: Many will say to me on that day, ‘Lord, Lord, did we not prophesy in your name and in your name drive out demons and in your name perform many miracles?’

twi: Na mabua wɔn se, ‘Minnim mo da. Mumfi me so nkɔ, nnebɔneyɛfo!’
english: Then I will tell them plainly, ‘I never knew you. Away from me, you evildoers!’

twi: “Wɔn a wotie nea meka, na wodi so no te sɛ onyansafo a osi ne dan si ɔbotan so.
english: “Therefore everyone who hears these words of mine and puts them into practice is like a wise man who built his house on the rock.

twi: Osu tɔe, na osuframa bɔe, na nsu yirii, na emu biara kaa ɔdan no nanso ammu da, efisɛ wosi sii ɔbotan so.
english: The rain came down, the streams rose, and the winds blew and beat against that house; yet it did not fall, because it had its foundation on the rock.

twi: Nanso wɔn a wotie nea meka na wonni so no te sɛ ɔkwasea bi a osii ne dan sii nwea so.
english: But everyone who hears these words of mine and does not put them into practice is like a foolish man who built his house on sand.

twi: Osu tɔe, na osuframa bɔe, na nsu yirii, na emu biara kaa ɔdan no. Na edwiriw guu fam, bubuu pasaa.”
english: The rain came down, the streams rose, and the winds blew and beat against that house, and it fell with a great crash.”

twi: Yesu asɛnka no maa nnipadɔm a wotiee no no nyinaa ho dwiriw wɔn,
english: When Jesus had finished saying these things, the crowds were amazed at his teaching,

twi: efisɛ ɔkyerɛkyerɛɛ te sɛ obi a okura tumi, na ne nkyerɛkyerɛ no nte sɛ nea Kyerɛwsɛm no akyerɛkyerɛfo no kyerɛ no.
english: because he taught as one who had authority, and not as their teachers of the law.

twi: Yesu Sa NyarewaBere a Yesu sian bepɔw no, dɔm dii nʼakyi.
english: When Jesus came down from the mountainside, large crowds followed him.

twi: Ɔkwatani bi baa Yesu nkyɛn bɛkotow no srɛɛ no se, “Me wura, mesrɛ wo, sɛ ɛyɛ wo pɛ a, sa me yare.”
english: A man with leprosy came and knelt before him and said, “Lord, if you are willing, you can make me clean.”

twi: Yesu teɛɛ ne nsa de kaa ɔkwatani no kae se, “Mɛsa wo yare. Wo ho mfi!” Amono mu hɔ ara, kwata no fii ne ho.
english: Jesus reached out his hand and touched the man. “I am willing,” he said. “Be clean!” Immediately he was cleansed of his leprosy.

twi: Yesu ka kyerɛɛ no se, “Wo ne obiara nni wʼayaresa yi ho nkɔmmɔ. Kɔ na fa wo ho kɔkyerɛ ɔsɔfo, na bɔ afɔre a Mose hyɛɛ sɛ wɔmmɔ sɛ adansede no.”
english: Then Jesus said to him, “See that you don’t tell anyone. But go, show yourself to the priest and offer the gift Moses commanded, as a testimony to them.”

twi: Yesu kɔɔ Kapernaum. Oduu hɔ no, Roma asraafo ɔha so panyin bi baa ne kyɛn bebuu no nkotodwe kae se,
english: When Jesus had entered Capernaum, a centurion came to him, asking for help.

twi: “Awurade, mʼabofra abubu gu hɔ a ɔrehu amane; mesrɛ wo, bɛsa no yare ma me.”
english: “Lord,” he said, “my servant lies at home paralyzed, suffering terribly.”

twi: Yesu ka kyerɛɛ no se, “Mɛba abɛsa no yare.”
english: Jesus said to him, “Shall I come and heal him?”

twi: Asraafo ha so panyin no tee Yesu asɛm a ɔkae no, ɔkae se, “Awurade, memfata sɛ woba me fi. Ka biribi na mʼabofra no ho bɛyɛ no den.
english: The centurion replied, “Lord, I do not deserve to have you come under my roof. But just say the word, and my servant will be healed.

twi: Meyɛ obi a mehyɛ tumi ase, na mesan wɔ asraafo a wɔhyɛ mʼase. Meka kyerɛ wɔn mu bi sɛ ɔnkɔ a, ɔkɔ. Meka kyerɛ ɔfoforo se ɔmmra a, ɔba. Saa ara nso na mehyɛ me somfo sɛ ɔnyɛ biribi a, ɔyɛ ara ne no.”
english: For I myself am a man under authority, with soldiers under me. I tell this one, ‘Go,’ and he goes; and that one, ‘Come,’ and he comes. I say to my servant, ‘Do this,’ and he does it.”

twi: Yesu tee saa asɛm no, ɛyɛɛ no nwonwa. Ɔdan nʼani, ka kyerɛɛ nnipadɔm a wodi nʼakyi no se, “Israelman mu nyinaa, minhuu gyidi a ɛte sɛɛ da.
english: When Jesus heard this, he was amazed and said to those following him, “Truly I tell you, I have not found anyone in Israel with such great faith.

twi: Na mereka akyerɛ mo se, nnipa pii befi apuei ne atɔe aba na wɔne Abraham, Isak ne Yakob abɛtena ase wɔ ɔsoro Ahenni no mu.
english: I say to you that many will come from the east and the west, and will take their places at the feast with Abraham, Isaac and Jacob in the kingdom of heaven.

twi: Na Israelfo a wosiesiee ɔsoro ahenni maa wɔn no mu pii wɔ hɔ a wɔde wɔn nsa begu wɔn ti atwa agyaadwo na wɔatow wɔn agu sum kabii mu ama ɔyaw.”
english: But the subjects of the kingdom will be thrown outside, into the darkness, where there will be weeping and gnashing of teeth.”

twi: Yesu ka kyerɛɛ asraafo so panyin no se, “Kɔ fie. Nea wugye di no mmra mu saa mma wo!” Abofra no ho tɔɔ no saa bere no ara mu!
english: Then Jesus said to the centurion, “Go! Let it be done just as you believed it would.” And his servant was healed at that moment.

twi: Yesu Sa Petro Ase YareYesu kɔɔ Petro fi. Ɔkɔtoo sɛ atiridii akyere Petro asebea ma ɔda hɔ.
english: When Jesus came into Peter’s house, he saw Peter’s mother-in-law lying in bed with a fever.

twi: Yesu soo ne nsa mu maa atiridii no tu fii no so. Ɔsɔre noaa aduan maa wɔn.
english: He touched her hand and the fever left her, and she got up and began to wait on him.

twi: Saa da no anwummere no, wɔde wɔn a wɔwɔ ahonhommɔne pii brɛɛ Yesu. Nʼanom asɛm a ɔkae no maa ahonhommɔne no nyinaa tu yerae, na wɔn a wɔyare no nyinaa nso ho tɔɔ wɔn.
english: When evening came, many who were demon-possessed were brought to him, and he drove out the spirits with a word and healed all the sick.

twi: Eyi maa nea Odiyifo Yesaia kae se,“Ɔfaa yɛn ahoɔmmerɛw,na ɔsoaa yɛn nyarewa nyinaa” no baa mu.
english:
This was to fulfill what was spoken through the prophet Isaiah:
“He took up our infirmities
    and bore our diseases.”

twi: Yesu AkyidiYesu huu sɛ dɔm no redɔɔso no, ɔka kyerɛɛ nʼasuafo no se, wontwa ɔtare no nkɔ nʼagya nohɔ.
english: When Jesus saw the crowd around him, he gave orders to cross to the other side of the lake.

twi: Ɛhɔ ara Yudani kyerɛkyerɛfo bi ka kyerɛɛ Yesu se, “Kyerɛkyerɛfo, baabiara a wobɛkɔ no, medi wʼakyi!”
english: Then a teacher of the law came to him and said, “Teacher, I will follow you wherever you go.”

twi: Yesu buaa no se, “Sakraman wɔ wɔn abon, wim nnomaa nso wɔ mmerebuw, nanso me, Onipa Ba no de, minni baabi a mede me ti to!”
english: Jesus replied, “Foxes have dens and birds have nests, but the Son of Man has no place to lay his head.”

twi: Asuafo no mu baako bɛka kyerɛɛ no se, “Owura, ma me kwan na minkosie mʼagya ansa na mabedi wʼakyi.”
english: Another disciple said to him, “Lord, first let me go and bury my father.”

twi: Nanso Yesu ka kyerɛɛ no se, “Di mʼakyi. Wɔn a wɔawu no nsie wɔn awufo.”
english: But Jesus told him, “Follow me, and let the dead bury their own dead.”

twi: Yesu Brɛ Ahum AseYesu saa nyarewa no wiee no, ɔkɔtenaa ɔkorow mu na nʼasuafo no dii nʼakyi.
english: Then he got into the boat and his disciples followed him.

twi: Prɛko pɛ, ahum kɛse bi tu maa asorɔkye bu bɛkataa ɔkorow no so. Nanso na Yesu de, wada.
english: Suddenly a furious storm came up on the lake, so that the waves swept over the boat. But Jesus was sleeping.

twi: Nʼasuafo no de nteɛteɛmu kɔɔ ne nkyɛn, konyan no kae se, “Awurade! Gye yɛn na yɛreyɛ amem!”
english: The disciples went and woke him, saying, “Lord, save us! We’re going to drown!”

twi: Yesu nyanee no, ɔka kyerɛɛ wɔn se, “Mo a mo gyidi sua, adɛn na moabɔ hu saa?” Ɛhɔ ara, ɔsɔre teɛteɛɛ ahum ne asorɔkye no ma ɛyɛɛ dinn.
english: He replied, “You of little faith, why are you so afraid?” Then he got up and rebuked the winds and the waves, and it was completely calm.

twi: Asuafo no ho dwiriw wɔn yiye. Wobisabisaa wɔn ho wɔn ho se, “Onipa bɛn mpo ni a ahum ne ɛpo tie no yi?”
english: The men were amazed and asked, “What kind of man is this? Even the winds and the waves obey him!”

twi: Yesu Tu AhohommɔneYesu ne nʼasuafo no duu asuogya wɔ Gadarafo asase so no, nnipa baanu bi a ahonhommɔne wɔ wɔn so fii amusiei behyiaa no. Esiane sɛ na saa nnipa yi yɛ keka nti, na obiara ntumi mfa faako a wɔwɔ hɔ.
english: When he arrived at the other side in the region of the Gadarenes, two demon-possessed men coming from the tombs met him. They were so violent that no one could pass that way.

twi: Wohuu no pɛ, wofii ase teɛteɛɛ mu se, “Onyankopɔn Ba, dɛn na worehwehwɛ afi yɛn nkyɛn? Woaba ha sɛ worebɛyɛ yɛn ayayade wɔ bere a mmere no nsoe ana?”
english: “What do you want with us, Son of God?” they shouted. “Have you come here to torture us before the appointed time?”

twi: Saa bere koro no ara mu, na mprakokuw bi redidi wɔ nkyɛn baabi.
english: Some distance from them a large herd of pigs was feeding.

twi: Ahonhommɔne no srɛɛ Yesu se, “Sɛ wutu yɛn a, fa yɛn kɔhyɛ mprakokuw yi mu.”
english: The demons begged Jesus, “If you drive us out, send us into the herd of pigs.”

twi: Yesu teɛɛ wɔn se, “Mumfi!” Ɛhɔ ara ahonhommɔne no fii nnipa no mu, kowuraa mprako no mu. Mprakokuw no nyinaa de mmirika sian bepɔw no, koguu ɛpo no mu ma ɛfaa wɔn.
english: He said to them, “Go!” So they came out and went into the pigs, and the whole herd rushed down the steep bank into the lake and died in the water.

twi: Ntɛm ara, wɔn a wɔhwɛ mprako no so no tuu mmirika kɔɔ kurom, kɔkaa nea asi no kyerɛɛ nkurɔfo.
english: Those tending the pigs ran off, went into the town and reported all this, including what had happened to the demon-possessed men.

twi: Kurom hɔfo no tee nea aba no, wɔbɔɔ twi kɔɔ nea Yesu wɔ hɔ no. Wohuu Yesu no, wɔsrɛɛ no sɛ omfi wɔn man mu hɔ nkɔ.
english: Then the whole town went out to meet Jesus. And when they saw him, they pleaded with him to leave their region.

twi: Yesu De Obubuafo Bi Bɔne Kyɛ No Sa No YareEyi akyi no, Yesu kɔtenaa ɔkorow bi mu kɔɔ Kapernaum, kurow a ɔte mu no mu.
english: Jesus stepped into a boat, crossed over and came to his own town.

twi: Oduu hɔ no, ankyɛ biara na nnipa bi de obubuafo bi brɛɛ no sɛ ɔnsa no yare. Na Yesu huu gyidi a wɔwɔ wɔ ne mu no, ɔka kyerɛɛ obubuafo no se, “Ɔba, ma wʼani nnye, wɔde wo bɔne nyinaa akyɛ wo.”
english: Some men brought to him a paralyzed man, lying on a mat. When Jesus saw their faith, he said to the man, “Take heart, son; your sins are forgiven.”

twi: Ɛhɔ ara na Kyerɛwsɛm no akyerɛkyerɛfo a na wɔwɔ hɔ no bi teɛɛ mu se, “Ɔbarima yi ka abususɛm. Ɔkyerɛ sɛ ɔyɛ Onyankopɔn!”
english: At this, some of the teachers of the law said to themselves, “This fellow is blaspheming!”

twi: Yesu huu nea ɛwɔ wɔn adwene mu no, obisaa wɔn se, “Adɛn nti na modwene bɔne wɔ mo koma mu saa?
english: Knowing their thoughts, Jesus said, “Why do you entertain evil thoughts in your hearts?

twi: Me Onipa Ba no, mewɔ tumi wɔ asase yi so sɛ mede bɔne kyɛ. Nea ɛwɔ he na ɛyɛ den, sɛ obi bɛka se, ‘Mede wo bɔne akyɛ wo’ anaasɛ ɔbɛka se, ‘Sɔre na nantew?’ ”
english: Which is easier: to say, ‘Your sins are forgiven,’ or to say, ‘Get up and walk’?

twi: Nanso sɛnea ɛbɛyɛ na mubehu sɛ Onipa Ba no wɔ tumi sɛ ɔde bɔne kyɛ nti. Ɔka kyerɛɛ obubuafo no se, “Sɔre na bobɔw wo kɛtɛ, na kɔ fie efisɛ masa wo yare.”
english: But I want you to know that the Son of Man has authority on earth to forgive sins.” So he said to the paralyzed man, “Get up, take your mat and go home.”

twi: Amono mu hɔ ara, obubuafo no sɔre bobɔw ne kɛtɛ, sii mu kɔɔ ne fi!
english: Then the man got up and went home.

twi: Nnipadɔm no huu anwonwade yi no, wɔn ho dwiriw wɔn yiye. Wɔkamfoo Onyankopɔn sɛ ɔde tumi a ɛte saa ama onipa.
english: When the crowd saw this, they were filled with awe; and they praised God, who had given such authority to man.

twi: Yesu Frɛ MateoYesu fi nea ɔsaa obubuafo no yare hɔ rekɔ no, ohuu ɔbarima towgyeni bi a ɔte atowgyei. Wɔfrɛ saa ɔbarima no Mateo. Yesu huu no no, ɔka kyerɛɛ no se, “Bedi mʼakyi.” Ɛhɔ ara, Mateo sɔre dii Yesu akyi.
english: As Jesus went on from there, he saw a man named Matthew sitting at the tax collector’s booth. “Follow me,” he told him, and Matthew got up and followed him.

twi: Ɛbae sɛ Yesu ne nʼasuafo no kɔɔ Mateo fi kodidii. Wɔredidi no, towgyefo ne nnebɔneyɛfo bebree baa hɔ ne no ne nʼasuafo no too nsa didii.
english: While Jesus was having dinner at Matthew’s house, many tax collectors and sinners came and ate with him and his disciples.

twi: Farisifo no huu sɛ ɔne nnebɔneyɛfo ato nsa redidi no, anyɛ wɔn dɛ. Wobisaa nʼasuafo no se, “Adɛn nti na mo kyerɛkyerɛfo no de ne ho abɔ nnebɔneyɛfo a wɔte sɛɛ yi?”
english: When the Pharisees saw this, they asked his disciples, “Why does your teacher eat with tax collectors and sinners?”

twi: Yesu tee no, obuaa wɔn se, “Nnipa a wɔnyare no, ɔyaresafo ho nhia wɔn, na nnipa a wɔyare no na ɔyaresafo ho hia wɔn.”
english: On hearing this, Jesus said, “It is not the healthy who need a doctor, but the sick.

twi: Ɔsan kaa bio se, “Monkɔhwehwɛ eyi ase wɔ Kyerɛw Kronkron no mu. Wɔakyerɛw se, ‘Ɛnyɛ mo afɔre ne ayɛyɛde na mepɛ, na mmom ahummɔbɔ.’ Mammɛfrɛ atreneefo, na mmom, mebɛfrɛɛ nnebɔneyɛfo sɛ wɔnsakra mmra Onyankopɔn nkyɛn.”
english: But go and learn what this means: ‘I desire mercy, not sacrifice.’ For I have not come to call the righteous, but sinners.”

twi: Mmuadadi Ho AsɛmmisaDa bi Osuboni Yohane asuafo baa Yesu nkyɛn bebisaa no se, “Adɛn nti na wʼasuafo no nni mmuada, sɛnea yɛne Farisifo di mmuada no?”
english: Then John’s disciples came and asked him, “How is it that we and the Pharisees fast often, but your disciples do not fast?”

twi: Yesu buaa wɔn se, “Mugye di sɛ, sɛ ayeforokunu ne ne nnamfonom te hɔ a, ɛsɛ sɛ ne nnamfonom no werɛ how, na wobua da ana? Bere bi bɛba a wɔbɛfa me afi wɔn nkyɛn. Saa bere no na wobedi mmuada.
english: Jesus answered, “How can the guests of the bridegroom mourn while he is with them? The time will come when the bridegroom will be taken from them; then they will fast.

twi: “Hena na ɔde ntama foforo bɛtare ntama dedaw mu? Saa ntaremu no besunsuan dedaw no mu ama tokuru kɛse abɛda hɔ.
english: “No one sews a patch of unshrunk cloth on an old garment, for the patch will pull away from the garment, making the tear worse.

twi: Hena na ɔde nsa foforo begu aboa nhoma nsa nkotoku dedaw mu? Sɛ ɔyɛ saa a, nsa no bɛpae nkotoku no ama nsa no ahwie agu, na nkotoku no nso asɛe. Nsa nkotoku foforo mu nko ara na ɛsɛ sɛ wɔde nsa foforo gugu na amma nkotoku no ne nsa no mu biara ansɛe.”
english: Neither do people pour new wine into old wineskins. If they do, the skins will burst; the wine will run out and the wineskins will be ruined. No, they pour new wine into new wineskins, and both are preserved.”

twi: Ɔbea Bi Ayaresa Ne Ababaa Bi WunyanYesu gu so rekasa no, Yudafo panyin bi ba bɛkotow, sɔree no. Ɔde nʼadesrɛ too Yesu anim se, “Me babea awu mprempren ara. Minim sɛ, sɛ woba de wo nsa bɛka no pɛ a, obenyan.”
english: While he was saying this, a synagogue leader came and knelt before him and said, “My daughter has just died. But come and put your hand on her, and she will live.”

twi: Yesu ne nʼasuafo no ne ɔpanyin no sii mu sɛ wɔrekɔ ɔpanyin no fi.
english: Jesus got up and went with him, and so did his disciples.

twi: Wɔrekɔ no, ɔbea bi a mogya atu no mfirihyia dumien faa nʼakyi, soo nʼatade ano.
english: Just then a woman who had been subject to bleeding for twelve years came up behind him and touched the edge of his cloak.

twi: Ɔkaa wɔ ne tirim se, “Sɛ mede me nsa ka no nko ara a, me ho bɛyɛ me den.”
english: She said to herself, “If I only touch his cloak, I will be healed.”

twi: Yesu dan nʼani ka kyerɛɛ no se, “Ɔbabea, ma wo bo ntɔ wo yam. Wo gyidi agye wo. Wo ho atɔ wo.” Efi saa bere no mu no, ne ho tɔɔ no.
english: Jesus turned and saw her. “Take heart, daughter,” he said, “your faith has healed you.” And the woman was healed at that moment.

twi: Yesu duu ɔpanyin no fi hɔ a ohuu sɛ nkurɔfo no bi resu na ebinom reto ayiase nnwom no,
english: When Jesus entered the synagogue leader’s house and saw the noisy crowd and people playing pipes,

twi: ɔkae se, “Obiara mfi adi. Ababaa no nwui. Wada!” Yesu asɛm a ɔkae yi maa nnipa no serew no.
english: he said, “Go away. The girl is not dead but asleep.” But they laughed at him.

twi: Nnipa no nyinaa fii adi no, Yesu kɔɔ faako a ababaa no da hɔ no. Osoo ne nsa. Prɛko pɛ, ababaa no nyanee.
english: After the crowd had been put outside, he went in and took the girl by the hand, and she got up.

twi: Saa anwonwade a Yesu yɛe yi trɛw wɔ mpɔtam hɔ nyinaa.
english: News of this spread through all that region.

twi: Anifuraefo Baanu Bi AyaresaYesu fi nea onyan ababaa no hɔ rekɔ no, anifuraefo baanu bi dii nʼakyi teɛteɛɛ mu se, “Dawid ba, hu yɛn mmɔbɔ!”
english: As Jesus went on from there, two blind men followed him, calling out, “Have mercy on us, Son of David!”

twi: Yesu duu fie no, anifuraefo no baa ne nkyɛn. Yesu bisaa wɔn se, “Mugye di sɛ metumi ama moahu ade?”Wobuaa no se, “Yiw, Awurade, yegye di!”
english:
When he had gone indoors, the blind men came to him, and he asked them, “Do you believe that I am able to do this?”
“Yes, Lord,” they replied.

twi: Yesu de ne nsa kaa wɔn ani kae se, “Mo gyidi nyɛ nea mohwehwɛ mma mo!”
english: Then he touched their eyes and said, “According to your faith let it be done to you”;

twi: Amono mu hɔ ara na wɔn ani buebuei. Yesu bɔɔ wɔn ano se, “Monnka saa ayaresa yi ho asɛm nkyerɛ obiara.”
english: and their sight was restored. Jesus warned them sternly, “See that no one knows about this.”

twi: Nanso nnipa no fii hɔ pɛ na wɔbɔɔ asɛm no dawuru.
english: But they went out and spread the news about him all over that region.

twi: Mum Nifuraefo Bi AyaresaYesu ne nʼasuafo refi adi no, wɔde mum bi a honhommɔne wɔ ne so brɛɛ no.
english: While they were going out, a man who was demon-possessed and could not talk was brought to Jesus.

twi: Yesu tuu honhommɔne no na prɛko pɛ, mum no kasae. Saa honhommɔnetu yi yɛɛ nnipa a wɔwɔ hɔ no nyinaa nwonwa ma wɔkae se, “Yenhuu saa anwonwade yi bi da wɔ Israelman mu ha!”
