english: When the other servants saw what had happened, they were outraged and went and told their master everything that had happened.

twi: “Ɔhene no tee no, ɔfrɛɛ saa ɔpaani a ɔde ne ho kyɛɛ no no baa nʼanim. Ɔka kyerɛɛ no se, ‘Onipa bɔne ne otirimɔdenfo! Wosrɛɛ me no, mede ka kɛse a wode me no nyinaa kyɛɛ wo;
english: “Then the master called the servant in. ‘You wicked servant,’ he said, ‘I canceled all that debt of yours because you begged me to.

twi: ɛnsɛ wo sɛ wo nso wuhu wo yɔnko mmɔbɔ sɛnea mihuu wo mmɔbɔ no ana?’
english: Shouldn’t you have had mercy on your fellow servant just as I had on you?’

twi: Ɔhene no de abufuw ma wɔde ɔpaani yi kɔtoo afiase kae se, gye sɛ watua ka a ɔde no no nyinaa ansa na ɔbɛma wɔayi no.
english: In anger his master handed him over to the jailers to be tortured, until he should pay back all he owed.

twi: “Saa ara na sɛ moamfa mo nuanom mfomso ankyɛ wɔn a, me soro Agya nso remfa mo mfomso nkyɛ mo.”
english: “This is how my heavenly Father will treat each of you unless you forgive your brother or sister from your heart.”

twi: AwaregyaeYesu wiee nʼasɛnka no, ɔkɔɔ Galilea. Ofi Galilea no, otwaa Asubɔnten Yordan baa Yudea.
english: When Jesus had finished saying these things, he left Galilee and went into the region of Judea to the other side of the Jordan.

twi: Nnipadɔm tu dii nʼakyi, ma ɔsaa wɔn yare.
english: Large crowds followed him, and he healed them there.

twi: Farisifo bi ba bebisaa no nsɛm bi pɛɛ sɛ wɔnam wɔn nsɛmmisa no so ma ɔka asɛm bi a ɛde no bɛkɔ sɔhwɛ mu. Wobisaa no se, “Wopene awaregyae so ana?”
english: Some Pharisees came to him to test him. They asked, “Is it lawful for a man to divorce his wife for any and every reason?”

twi: Yesu nso bisaa wɔn se, “Gyama monkenkan Kyerɛw Kronkron no? Wɔakyerɛw wɔ mu se, ‘Mfiase no, Onyankopɔn bɔɔ ɔbarima ne ɔbea.
english: “Haven’t you read,” he replied, “that at the beginning the Creator ‘made them male and female,’

twi: Eyi nti na ɔbarima begyaw nʼagya ne ne na hɔ de ne ho akɔbɔ ne yere ho daa nyinaa no.’
english: and said, ‘For this reason a man will leave his father and mother and be united to his wife, and the two will become one flesh’?

twi: Enti na wɔnyɛ baanu bio, na mmom wɔabɛyɛ ɔhonam koro. Enti nea Onyankopɔn aka abɔ mu no, ɛnsɛ sɛ obiara tetew mu.”
english: So they are no longer two, but one flesh. Therefore what God has joined together, let no one separate.”

twi: Farisifo no kɔɔ so bisaa no se, “Adɛn nti na Mose kae se, sɛ ɔbarima bi pɛ sɛ ogyaa ne yere a otumi kyerɛw no krataa kɛkɛ, de gyaa no?”
english: “Why then,” they asked, “did Moses command that a man give his wife a certificate of divorce and send her away?”

twi: Yesu buaa wɔn se, “Esiane sɛ na mo koma apirim no nti na Mose maa awaregyae ho kwan, na ɛnyɛ ade a Onyankopɔn hyehyɛe.
english: Jesus replied, “Moses permitted you to divorce your wives because your hearts were hard. But it was not this way from the beginning.

twi: Na mereka akyerɛ mo se, obiara a obegyaa ne yere, a ɛnyɛ sɛ ɔbea no abɔ aguaman, na ɔbɛsan aware ɔbea foforo no asɛe aware.”
english: I tell you that anyone who divorces his wife, except for sexual immorality, and marries another woman commits adultery.”

twi: Yesu asuafo no kae se, “Sɛ saa na ɛte de a, na ɛnsɛ sɛ obiara ware.”
english: The disciples said to him, “If this is the situation between a husband and wife, it is better not to marry.”

twi: Yesu buaa wɔn se, “Ɛnyɛ obiara na obetumi agye asɛm yi ato mu, gye wɔn a Onyankopɔn hyɛ wɔn den no nko ara.
english: Jesus replied, “Not everyone can accept this word, but only those to whom it has been given.

twi: Nnipa bi wɔ hɔ a wonni mmarimayɛ mu ahoɔden fi awo mu, ebinom nso wɔ hɔ a nnipa na wɔyɛɛ wɔn saa; ebinom nso ɔsoro Ahenni no nti, wɔpo aware. Obiara a obetumi no, nni mʼasɛm a maka yi so.”
english: For there are eunuchs who were born that way, and there are eunuchs who have been made eunuchs by others—and there are those who choose to live like eunuchs for the sake of the kingdom of heaven. The one who can accept this should accept it.”

twi: Yesu Hyira Mmofra NkumaaWɔde mmofra nkumaa brɛɛ Yesu sɛ ɔmfa ne nsa ngu wɔn so, na ɔmmɔ mpae mma wɔn. Nanso asuafo no kaa wɔn anim.
english: Then people brought little children to Jesus for him to place his hands on them and pray for them. But the disciples rebuked them.

twi: Yesu kae se, “Momma mmofra no kwan na wɔmmra me nkyɛn, na munnsiw wɔn kwan, na eyinom sɛɛ na Ɔsoro Ahenni no yɛ wɔn dea.”
english: Jesus said, “Let the little children come to me, and do not hinder them, for the kingdom of heaven belongs to such as these.”

twi: Na ɔde ne nsa guu wɔn so, hyiraa wɔn ansa na ɔrefi hɔ akɔ.
english: When he had placed his hands on them, he went on from there.

twi: Ahonya Ne Onyankopɔn Ahenni NoƐno mu na ɔbarima bi baa Yesu nkyɛn bebisaa no se, “Ɔkyerɛkyerɛfo, ade pa bɛn na menyɛ na manya nkwa a enni awiei?”
english: Just then a man came up to Jesus and asked, “Teacher, what good thing must I do to get eternal life?”

twi: Yesu buaa no se, “Adɛn nti na wubisa me nea ɛyɛ papa ho asɛm? Ɔbaako pɛ na ɔyɛ papa. Sɛ wopɛ sɛ wokɔ nkwa mu de a, di mmara nsɛm no so.”
english: “Why do you ask me about what is good?” Jesus replied. “There is only One who is good. If you want to enter life, keep the commandments.”

twi: Aberante no nso bisaa no se, “Mmaransɛm no mu nea ɛwɔ he?”Yesu buaa no se, “Nni awu. Nsɛe aware. Mmɔ korɔn. Nni atoro.
english:
“Which ones?” he inquired.
Jesus replied, “‘You shall not murder, you shall not commit adultery, you shall not steal, you shall not give false testimony,

twi: Di wʼagya ne wo na ni, na dɔ wo yɔnko sɛ wo ho!”
english: honor your father and mother,’ and ‘love your neighbor as yourself.’”

twi: Aberante no nso kae se, “Midi eyinom nyinaa so pɛpɛɛpɛ. Afei menyɛ dɛn?”
english: “All these I have kept,” the young man said. “What do I still lack?”

twi: Yesu ka kyerɛɛ no se, “Sɛ wopɛ sɛ woyɛ pɛ a kɔ na kɔtɔn biribiara a wowɔ, na fa sika a wubenya afi mu no ma ahiafo. Ɛno ansa na wubenya ademude wɔ ɔsoro. Afei bedi mʼakyi.”
english: Jesus answered, “If you want to be perfect, go, sell your possessions and give to the poor, and you will have treasure in heaven. Then come, follow me.”

twi: Esiane sɛ na saa aberante yi wɔ ahonyade bebree nti, ɔtee saa nsɛm no, anyɛ no dɛ maa ɔde awerɛhow fii hɔ kɔe.
english: When the young man heard this, he went away sad, because he had great wealth.

twi: Afei Yesu ka kyerɛɛ nʼasuafo no se, “Meka mo nokware se ɛyɛ den ma osikani sɛ ɔbɛkɔ Ɔsoro Ahenni no mu.
english: Then Jesus said to his disciples, “Truly I tell you, it is hard for someone who is rich to enter the kingdom of heaven.

twi: Meka ti mu se, ɛyɛ mmerɛw sɛ yoma bewura pane aniwa mu sen sɛ osikani bɛkɔ Onyankopɔn Ahenni mu!”
english: Again I tell you, it is easier for a camel to go through the eye of a needle than for someone who is rich to enter the kingdom of God.”

twi: Asuafo no tee saa asɛm no, wɔn adwene mu yɛɛ wɔn naa. Wobisae se, “Na ɛno de, hena na wiase mu ha wobegye no nkwa?”
english: When the disciples heard this, they were greatly astonished and asked, “Who then can be saved?”

twi: Yesu hwɛɛ wɔn buae se, “Onipa fam de, ɛyɛ den, na Onyankopɔn fam de, biribiara betumi aba mu.”
english: Jesus looked at them and said, “With man this is impossible, but with God all things are possible.”

twi: AhopakyiPetro nso kae se, “Yagyaw biribiara hɔ abedi wʼakyi; na mfaso bɛn na yebenya afi wʼakyidi no mu?”
english: Peter answered him, “We have left everything to follow you! What then will there be for us?”

twi: Yesu buae se, “Me, Agyenkwa no, sɛ metena mʼanuonyam ahengua no so a, nokware, mo mʼasuafo yi nso bɛtena ahengua dumien no so na moabu Israel mmusuakuw dumien no atɛn.
english: Jesus said to them, “Truly I tell you, at the renewal of all things, when the Son of Man sits on his glorious throne, you who have followed me will also sit on twelve thrones, judging the twelve tribes of Israel.

twi: Na obiara a obegyaw ne fi, ne nuabarimanom, ne nuabeanom, nʼagya, ne na, ne yere, ne mma anaa nʼagyapade abedi mʼakyi no, obenya no ho mmɔho ɔha, na wanya nkwa a enni awiei nso.
english: And everyone who has left houses or brothers or sisters or father or mother or wife or children or fields for my sake will receive a hundred times as much and will inherit eternal life.

twi: Na wɔn a wɔadi kan no mu pii bedi akyi, na wɔn a wodi akyi no nso mu bi abedi kan.”
english: But many who are first will be last, and many who are last will be first.

twi: Afum Adwumayɛfo Ho BɛYesu san buu wɔn bɛ foforo bi se, “Ɔsoro Ahenni te sɛ okuafo bi a ofii adi anɔpa bi sɛ ɔrekɔhwehwɛ nnipa abɔ wɔn paa.
english: “For the kingdom of heaven is like a landowner who went out early in the morning to hire workers for his vineyard.

twi: Ne nsa kaa apaafo no, ɔne wɔn hyehyɛɛ sɛ obetua wɔn da koro adwuma so akatua.
english: He agreed to pay them a denarius for the day and sent them into his vineyard.

twi: “Ankyɛ ofii adi bio kohuu nnipa bi nso, sɛ wogyinagyina hɔ a wɔnyɛ hwee.
english: “About nine in the morning he went out and saw others standing in the marketplace doing nothing.

twi: Ɔfaa wɔn nso de wɔn kɔɔ nʼafuw no mu. Ɔka kyerɛɛ wɔn nso se, obetua wɔn nea eye.
english: He told them, ‘You also go and work in my vineyard, and I will pay you whatever is right.’

twi: Enti wɔkɔe.“Ɔsan kɔɔ owigyinae ne nnɔn abiɛsa bere mu kɔbɔɔ nnipa foforo paa ne wɔn yɛɛ nhyehyɛe koro no ara bi.
english:
So they went.
“He went out again about noon and about three in the afternoon and did the same thing.

twi: Ɔsan fii adi bɛyɛ nnɔnnum bere mu, kohuu sɛ nnipa bi gyinagyina hɔ. Obisaa wɔn se, ‘Adɛn nti na da mu yi nyinaa mugyinagyina ha a monyɛ hwee?’
english: About five in the afternoon he went out and found still others standing around. He asked them, ‘Why have you been standing here all day long doing nothing?’

twi: “Wobuae se, ‘Obi mmɛbɔɔ yɛn paa ɛ.’“Ɛhɔ ara na ɔka kyerɛɛ wɔn se, ‘Ɛno de, mo nso monkɔyɛ adwuma wɔ mʼafum.’
english:
“‘Because no one has hired us,’ they answered.
“He said to them, ‘You also go and work in my vineyard.’

twi: “Eduu anwummere no, ɔfrɛɛ nea otua nʼapaafo no ka no ka kyerɛɛ no se, ‘Hwɛ na tua wɔn ka, fi wɔn a wɔbaa akyiri yi no so kosi wɔn a wɔbaa kan no so.’
english: “When evening came, the owner of the vineyard said to his foreman, ‘Call the workers and pay them their wages, beginning with the last ones hired and going on to the first.’

twi: “Apaafo a ɔfaa wɔn akyiri no nyinaa, otuaa wɔn da koro apaade.
english: “The workers who were hired about five in the afternoon came and each received a denarius.

twi: Wɔn a wɔfaa wɔn kan no nso bae. Wosusuw sɛ wobenya sika a ɛboro wɔn a wɔfaa wɔn akyiri no de no. Nanso wɔn nso wotuaa wɔn sɛnea wotuaa wɔn a wɔbaa akyiri no ara pɛ.
english: So when those came who were hired first, they expected to receive more. But each one of them also received a denarius.

twi: Wɔn nsa kaa wɔn apaade no, anyɛ wɔn dɛ.
english: When they received it, they began to grumble against the landowner.

twi: Wɔka kyerɛɛ afuw wura no se, ‘Nnipa a wɔbaa akyiri no yɛɛ adwuma dɔnhwerew baako pɛ, nanso yɛn a yɛyɛɛ adwuma fi anɔpa maa owia hyee yɛn no, womaa yɛne wɔn nyinaa akatua pɛ.’
english: ‘These who were hired last worked only one hour,’ they said, ‘and you have made them equal to us who have borne the burden of the work and the heat of the day.’

twi: “Obuaa wɔn mu baako se, ‘Damfo, menyɛɛ wo bɔne biara. Me ne wo anni ano sɛ, metua wo da koro adwuma so akatua ana?
english: “But he answered one of them, ‘I am not being unfair to you, friend. Didn’t you agree to work for a denarius?

twi: Fa sika a wo nsa aka no na kɔ. Efi me pɛ mu na meretua wɔn a wɔbaa kan ne wɔn a wɔbaa akyiri no nyinaa ka pɛ.
english: Take your pay and go. I want to give the one who was hired last the same as I gave you.

twi: Mmara bi siw me ho kwan sɛ mede me sika yɛ nea mepɛ? Anaasɛ mʼayamye nti na wʼani abere yi?’
english: Don’t I have the right to do what I want with my own money? Or are you envious because I am generous?’

twi: “Asɛm a Yesu ka de wiee ne sɛ, ‘Saa ara na wɔn a wodi akyi no bedi kan, na wɔn a wodi kan no nso bedi akyi.’ ”
english: “So the last will be first, and the first will be last.”

twi: Yesu Hyɛ Ne Wu Ho Nkɔm A Ɛto So AbiɛsaYesu sii mu sɛ ɔrekɔ Yerusalem no, ɔde nʼasuafo no kaa ne ho.
english: Now Jesus was going up to Jerusalem. On the way, he took the Twelve aside and said to them,

twi: Wɔrekɔ no, ɔtwee nʼasuafo no gyinaa nkyɛn baabi ka kyerɛɛ wɔn se, “Yɛrekɔ Yerusalem. Wobeyi me ama asɔfo mpanyin ne kyerɛwsɛm no akyerɛkyerɛfo, na wɔabu me kumfɔ.
english: “We are going up to Jerusalem, and the Son of Man will be delivered over to the chief priests and the teachers of the law. They will condemn him to death

twi: Wɔde me bɛhyɛ Roma aban nsa, na wɔadi me ho fɛw, abɔ me asennua mu, na ne nnansa so no, mɛsɔre afi awufo mu.”
english: and will hand him over to the Gentiles to be mocked and flogged and crucified. On the third day he will be raised to life!”

twi: Ɛna Bi AdesrɛSebedeo mma Yakobo ne Yohane ne wɔn na baa Yesu nkyɛn. Ɔbea yi de adesrɛde bi bɛtoo Yesu anim.
english: Then the mother of Zebedee’s sons came to Jesus with her sons and, kneeling down, asked a favor of him.

twi: Yesu bisaa no se, “Dɛn na wopɛ sɛ menyɛ mma wo?”Obuaa no se, “Mepɛ sɛ, sɛ wokɔ wʼahenni mu a, me mma baanu yi mu baako tena wo nifa so, na ɔbaako nso tena wo benkum so.”
english:
“What is it you want?” he asked.
She said, “Grant that one of these two sons of mine may sit at your right and the other at your left in your kingdom.”

twi: Nanso Yesu ka kyerɛɛ no se, “Wunnim nea worebisa no.” Afei ɔdan ne ho bisaa Yakobo ne Yohane se, “Mubetumi anom kuruwa a merebɛnom ano no bi ana?”Wobuaa no se, “Yebetumi!”
english:
“You don’t know what you are asking,” Jesus said to them. “Can you drink the cup I am going to drink?”
“We can,” they answered.

twi: Yesu ka kyerɛɛ wɔn se, “Me kuruwa ano de, mubetumi anom, nanso minni tumi sɛ miyi wɔn a wɔbɛtena me nifa anaa me benkum so. Saa afa no wɔ hɔ ma wɔn a mʼAgya ayi wɔn no.”
english: Jesus said to them, “You will indeed drink from my cup, but to sit at my right or left is not for me to grant. These places belong to those for whom they have been prepared by my Father.”

twi: Asuafo du a aka no tee nea Yakobo ne Yohane akobisa no, wɔn bo fuwii.
english: When the ten heard about this, they were indignant with the two brothers.

twi: Yesu frɛɛ wɔn nyinaa ka kyerɛɛ wɔn se, “Munim sɛ ahene ne atumfo di wɔn a wɔhyɛ wɔn ase no so. Saa ara nso na wɔn a wodi wɔn so no nso di afoforo so.
english: Jesus called them together and said, “You know that the rulers of the Gentiles lord it over them, and their high officials exercise authority over them.

twi: Nanso mo de, ɛnte saa wɔ mo mu. Mmom, obiara a ɔpɛ sɛ ɔyɛ ɔkɛse wɔ mo mu no, ɛsɛ sɛ ɔyɛ mo somfo.
english: Not so with you. Instead, whoever wants to become great among you must be your servant,

twi: Obiara a ɔpɛ sɛ ɔyɛ odikanfo wɔ mo mu no, ɔnyɛ mo akoa.
english: and whoever wants to be first must be your slave—

twi: Onipa Ba no amma sɛ wɔnsom no, na mmom ɔbɛsomee, na ɔde ne kra too hɔ sɛ mpata maa nnipa nyinaa.”
english: just as the Son of Man did not come to be served, but to serve, and to give his life as a ransom for many.”

twi: Anifuraefo Baanu Hu AdeYesu ne nʼasuafo fi Yeriko rekɔ no, nnipadɔm tu dii wɔn akyi.
english: As Jesus and his disciples were leaving Jericho, a large crowd followed him.

twi: Wɔrekɔ no, wɔkɔfaa baabi a anifuraefo baanu bi tete. Anifuraefo yi tee sɛ Yesu retwa mu no, wɔteɛteɛɛ mu se, “Awurade, Dawid Ba, hu yɛn mmɔbɔ!”
english: Two blind men were sitting by the roadside, and when they heard that Jesus was going by, they shouted, “Lord, Son of David, have mercy on us!”

twi: Nnipadɔm a wodi Yesu akyi no teɛteɛɛ wɔn se wommua wɔn ano. Nanso anifuraefo no kɔɔ so teɛteɛɛ mu se, “Awurade, Dawid Ba, hu yɛn mmɔbɔ!”
english: The crowd rebuked them and told them to be quiet, but they shouted all the louder, “Lord, Son of David, have mercy on us!”

twi: Yesu duu nea wɔtete hɔ no, ogyina bisaa wɔn se, “Dɛn na mopɛ sɛ meyɛ ma mo?”
english: Jesus stopped and called them. “What do you want me to do for you?” he asked.

twi: Wɔka kyerɛɛ no se, “Awurade, yɛpɛ sɛ yehu ade!”
english: “Lord,” they answered, “we want our sight.”

twi: Anifuraefo no yɛɛ Yesu mmɔbɔ. Ɔde ne nsa kekaa wɔn ani, na prɛko pɛ wohuu ade, na wodii nʼakyi.
english: Jesus had compassion on them and touched their eyes. Immediately they received their sight and followed him.

twi: Yesu Kɔ Yerusalem Sɛ ƆhempɔnAka kakra na Yesu ne nʼasuafo no adu Yerusalem no, wɔbɛn kurow bi a wɔfrɛ no Betfage a ɛwɔ Ngo Bepɔw no so hɔ no. Ɛhɔ na Yesu somaa nʼasuafo no mu baanu se, wonni kan nkɔ.
english: As they approached Jerusalem and came to Bethphage on the Mount of Olives, Jesus sent two disciples,

twi: Ɔka kyerɛɛ wɔn se, “Sɛ mudu hɔ a, mubehu sɛ wɔasa afurum bi ne ne ba hama. Monsan wɔn, na momfa wɔn mmrɛ me.
english: saying to them, “Go to the village ahead of you, and at once you will find a donkey tied there, with her colt by her. Untie them and bring them to me.

twi: Sɛ obi ka asɛm bi kyerɛ mo a, monka nkyerɛ onipa ko no se, ‘Wɔn ho hia Awurade,’ na ntɛm ara ɔbɛma mo de wɔn aba.”
english: If anyone says anything to you, say that the Lord needs them, and he will send them right away.”

twi: Wɔyɛɛ eyi de hyɛɛ tete nkɔmhyɛ a ɛka se,
english: This took place to fulfill what was spoken through the prophet:

twi: “Monka nkyerɛ Ɔbabea Sion sewo hene reba wo nkyɛn.Odwo, na ɔte afurum neafurum ba so” no mu den.
english:
“Say to Daughter Zion,
    ‘See, your king comes to you,
gentle and riding on a donkey,
    and on a colt, the foal of a donkey.’”

twi: Asuafo baanu no yɛɛ nea Yesu ka kyerɛɛ wɔn no.
english: The disciples went and did as Jesus had instructed them.

twi: Wɔde mmoa no brɛɛ no no, wɔde wɔn ntama sesɛw afurum no so, maa Yesu tenaa no so.
english: They brought the donkey and the colt and placed their cloaks on them for Jesus to sit on.

twi: Nnipadɔm a wɔwɔ hɔ no bi de wɔn ntama sesɛw ɔkwan a ɔde aboa no nam so no so. Ebinom nso bubuu nnua mman de sesɛw ɔkwan no mu saa ara.
english: A very large crowd spread their cloaks on the road, while others cut branches from the trees and spread them on the road.

twi: Dɔm no tu teɛe de osebɔ teɛteɛɛ mu se,“Hosiana Dawid Ba!”“Nhyira ne nea ɔnam Awurade din mu reba no.”“Hosiana wɔ ɔsoro nohɔ!”
english:
The crowds that went ahead of him and those that followed shouted,
“Hosanna to the Son of David!”
“Blessed is he who comes in the name of the Lord!”
“Hosanna in the highest heaven!”

twi: Bere a oduu Yerusalem no, kurow no nyinaa bɔɔ twi. Ɛhɔfo no bisae se, “Na hena ni?”
english: When Jesus entered Jerusalem, the whole city was stirred and asked, “Who is this?”

twi: Nnipadɔm no buae se, “Ɛyɛ Yesu, Odiyifo a ofi Nasaret a ɛwɔ Galileaman mu no.”
english: The crowds answered, “This is Jesus, the prophet from Nazareth in Galilee.”

twi: Yesu Kɔ Hyiadan MuYesu fii hɔ no, ɔkɔɔ hyiadan mu. Oduu hɔ no, ɔpam aguadifo a wɔwɔ hɔ no nyinaa, kaa sikasesafo apon nyinaa guu fam, bubuu pata a wɔtɔn mmorɔnoma wɔ mu no nyinaa gui.
english: Jesus entered the temple courts and drove out all who were buying and selling there. He overturned the tables of the money changers and the benches of those selling doves.

twi: Yesu ka kyerɛɛ wɔn se, “Kyerɛwsɛm no ka se, ‘Mʼasɔrefi yɛ beae a wɔbɔ mpae.’ Nanso mo de, mode hɔ ayɛ adwowtwafo atenae.”
english: “It is written,” he said to them, “‘My house will be called a house of prayer,’ but you are making it ‘a den of robbers.’”

twi: Afei anifuraefo ne mmubuafo baa ne nkyɛn wɔ hyiadan mu hɔ ma ɔsaa wɔn nyinaa yare.
english: The blind and the lame came to him at the temple, and he healed them.

twi: Nanso bere a asɔfo mpanyin ne Yudafo mpanyin bi huu anwonwade yi na wɔtee nso sɛ mmofra nkumaa a wɔwɔ hyiadan mu hɔ reteɛteɛ mu se, “Nhyira nka Dawid Ba no” no, anyɛ wɔn dɛ.
english: But when the chief priests and the teachers of the law saw the wonderful things he did and the children shouting in the temple courts, “Hosanna to the Son of David,” they were indignant.

twi: Enti wobisaa Yesu se, “Wote nsɛm a mmofra no reka no ana?”Yesu bua se, “Yiw. Na monkenkan saa Kyerɛwsɛm a ɛka se,“ ‘Mmofra ne nkokoaa mpode wɔn ano kamfo wo’ no da, ana?”
english:
“Do you hear what these children are saying?” they asked him.
“Yes,” replied Jesus, “have you never read,
“‘From the lips of children and infants
    you, Lord, have called forth your praise’?”

twi: Afei ofii hɔ san kɔɔ Betania kɔdaa hɔ.
english: And he left them and went out of the city to Bethany, where he spent the night.

twi: Yesu Dome Borɔdɔma Dua BiAde kyee anɔpa a ɔresan akɔ Yerusalem no, ɔkɔm dee no.
english: Early in the morning, as Jesus was on his way back to the city, he was hungry.

twi: Ohuu sɛ borɔdɔma dua bi si ɔkwan ho baabi. Ɔkɔɔ hɔ kɔhwɛɛ sɛ borɔdɔma no bi wɔ so, nanso oduu hɔ no, ohuu sɛ nhaban nko ara na ɛwɔ so. Ɔdomee borɔdɔma dua no se, “Efi nnɛ, worensow aba bio!” Ɛhɔ ara borɔdɔma dua no wui.
english: Seeing a fig tree by the road, he went up to it but found nothing on it except leaves. Then he said to it, “May you never bear fruit again!” Immediately the tree withered.

twi: Asɛm yi yɛɛ Yesu asuafo no nwonwa ma wobisaa no se, “Na ɛyɛɛ dɛn nti na borɔdɔma dua no so nhaban poo ntɛm saa?”
english: When the disciples saw this, they were amazed. “How did the fig tree wither so quickly?” they asked.

twi: Yesu nso buaa wɔn se, “Nokware, sɛ mowɔ gyidi na munnhinhim a, mubetumi ayɛ ade koro yi ara bi, anaa nea ɛkyɛn saa mpo. Anka mubetumi aka akyerɛ Ngo Bepɔw yi se, ‘Tutu kogu po mu,’ na ebetutu akogu mu nso.
english: Jesus replied, “Truly I tell you, if you have faith and do not doubt, not only can you do what was done to the fig tree, but also you can say to this mountain, ‘Go, throw yourself into the sea,’ and it will be done.

twi: Biribiara a mode gyidi bebisa wɔ mpaebɔ mu no, mo nsa bɛka.”
english: If you believe, you will receive whatever you ask for in prayer.”

twi: Yesu Tumi Ho AsɛmmisaYesu san kɔɔ hyiadan mu hɔ a ɔrekyerɛkyerɛ no, asɔfo mpanyin ne Yudafo mpanyin baa ne kyɛn bebisaa no tumi ko a ogyina so pam aguadifo ne sikasesafo no fii hyiadan mu hɔ no.
english: Jesus entered the temple courts, and, while he was teaching, the chief priests and the elders of the people came to him. “By what authority are you doing these things?” they asked. “And who gave you this authority?”

twi: Yesu kae se, “Merebebisa mo asɛm baako bi, na mummua me ansa.
english: Jesus replied, “I will also ask you one question. If you answer me, I will tell you by what authority I am doing these things.

twi: Onyankopɔn na ɔsomaa Osuboni Yohane anaa ɛnyɛ ɔno?”Wodwinnwen ho kae se, “Sɛ yɛka sɛ ‘Efi Onyankopɔn’ a, wobebisa yɛn nea enti a yɛannye nea Yohane kae no anni?
english:
John’s baptism—where did it come from? Was it from heaven, or of human origin?”
They discussed it among themselves and said, “If we say, ‘From heaven,’ he will ask, ‘Then why didn’t you believe him?’

twi: Na sɛ yɛka se, ‘Ɛnyɛ Onyankopɔn na ɔsomaa no’ nso a, dɔm no bɛhaw yɛn efisɛ, wɔn nyinaa nim sɛ Yohane yɛ odiyifo.”
english: But if we say, ‘Of human origin’—we are afraid of the people, for they all hold that John was a prophet.”

twi: Enti wɔn mmuae a wɔmae ara ne sɛ, “Yennim!”Ɛhɔ ara na Yesu nso kae se, “Sɛ munnim de a, me nso meremmua mo.”
english:
So they answered Jesus, “We don’t know.”
Then he said, “Neither will I tell you by what authority I am doing these things.

twi: Mmabarima Baanu Ho BɛYesu kae se, “Saa asɛm a merebɛka yi mudwen ho dɛn? Ɔbarima bi wɔ mmabarima baanu. Ɔka kyerɛɛ wɔn mu panyin no se, ‘Me ba, nnɛ kɔ mʼafum na kɔyɛ adwuma wɔ hɔ.’
english: “What do you think? There was a man who had two sons. He went to the first and said, ‘Son, go and work today in the vineyard.’

twi: “Ne ba no kae se, ‘Merenkɔ,’ nanso akyiri no, ɔsesaa nʼadwene na ɔkɔe.
english: “‘I will not,’ he answered, but later he changed his mind and went.

twi: “Afei agya no ka kyerɛɛ akumaa no se, ‘Wo nso kɔ.’ Ɔno nso kae se, ‘Agya, mate, mɛkɔ.’ Nanso wankɔ.
english: “Then the father went to the other son and said the same thing. He answered, ‘I will, sir,’ but he did not go.

twi: “Saa mmofra baanu yi mu hena na otie nʼagya asɛm?”Wobuae se, “Ɛyɛ ne ba panyin no.”Yesu see wɔn se, “Akyinnye biara nni ho sɛ abɔnefo ne nguamanfo bɛkɔ Ɔsoro Ahenni mu ansa na moakɔ.
english:
“Which of the two did what his father wanted?”
“The first,” they answered.
Jesus said to them, “Truly I tell you, the tax collectors and the prostitutes are entering the kingdom of God ahead of you.

twi: Efisɛ Yohane baa mo nkyɛn sɛ ɔrebɛkyerɛ mo trenee kwan, na moannye no anni. Nanso towgyefo ne nguamanfo gyee no dii. Na muhuu eyi mpo no, moansakra mo adwene, na moannye no anni.”
english: For John came to you to show you the way of righteousness, and you did not believe him, but the tax collectors and the prostitutes did. And even after you saw this, you did not repent and believe him.

twi: Apaafo Ho BɛYesu buu wɔn bɛ foforo bi se, “Da bi, ɔbarima bi a ɔwɔ bobeturo a wagye ban afa ho, na watu amoa a wokyi nsa wɔ mu, de afuw no gyaw akuafo bi. Eyi akyi no, otuu kwan kɔɔ ɔman foforo bi so.
english: “Listen to another parable: There was a landowner who planted a vineyard. He put a wall around it, dug a winepress in it and built a watchtower. Then he rented the vineyard to some farmers and moved to another place.

twi: Eduu bere a bobe no beree a ɛsɛ sɛ wɔtew no, ɔsomaa ne ho nnipa baa akuafo no hɔ sɛ wommegye ne kyɛfa mmrɛ no.
english: When the harvest time approached, he sent his servants to the tenants to collect his fruit.

twi: “Woduu hɔ ara pɛ na akuafo no tow hyɛɛ nnipa no so, boroo ɔbaako, kum ɔbaako na wosiw ɔbaako nso abo.
english: “The tenants seized his servants; they beat one, killed another, and stoned a third.

twi: Afei ɔsan somaa nnipa a wɔn dodow sen wɔn a ɔsomaa wɔn kan no se wɔnkɔ akuafo no nkyɛn, nanso asɛm koro no ara bi na esii.
english: Then he sent other servants to them, more than the first time, and the tenants treated them the same way.

twi: Eyi akyi no ɔsomaa ɔno nʼankasa ne ba kɔɔ akuafo no nkyɛn susuwii sɛ, wɔde nidi bɛma no.
english: Last of all, he sent his son to them. ‘They will respect my son,’ he said.

twi: “Nanso akuafo no huu sɛ ne ba no apue reba pɛ, wɔfaa ne ho adwene kae se, ‘Ɔdedifo no na ɔreba no; momma yenkum no, na yɛmfa afuw no!’
english: “But when the tenants saw the son, they said to each other, ‘This is the heir. Come, let’s kill him and take his inheritance.’

twi: Ɛhɔ ara na wɔtwee no fii afuw no mu, kokum no too baabi.
english: So they took him and threw him out of the vineyard and killed him.

twi: “Sɛ afuw wura no san ba a, mugye di sɛ dɛn na ɔbɛyɛ saa akuafo no?”
english: “Therefore, when the owner of the vineyard comes, what will he do to those tenants?”

twi: Yudafo mpanyin no buae se, “Ɔno nso bekum saa atirimɔdenfo no na ɔde afuw no ama akuafo foforo a wɔde ne kyɛfa bɛma no bere a ɛsɛ mu.”
english: “He will bring those wretches to a wretched end,” they replied, “and he will rent the vineyard to other tenants, who will give him his share of the crop at harvest time.”

twi: Yesu bisaa wɔn bio se, “Monkenkan Kyerɛwsɛm no mu da sɛ,“ ‘Ɔbo a adansifo apo noɛno ara na abɛyɛ ɔdan no twea so tibo.Awurade na wayɛ eyi,na ɛyɛ nwonwa wɔ yɛn ani so?’
english:
Jesus said to them, “Have you never read in the Scriptures:
“‘The stone the builders rejected
    has become the cornerstone;
the Lord has done this,
    and it is marvelous in our eyes’?

twi: “Nea mereka ara ne sɛ, wobegye Onyankopɔn Ahenni no afi mo nsam de akɔma ɔman foforo a wobebu ne nnɔbae no ho nkontaa pa akyerɛ no.
english: “Therefore I tell you that the kingdom of God will be taken away from you and given to a people who will produce its fruit.

twi: Wɔn a wɔbɛhwe saa ɔbotan yi so no mu bebubu, na nea ɔbo no bɛhwe ne so no nso bɛpɛtɛw.”
english: Anyone who falls on this stone will be broken to pieces; anyone on whom it falls will be crushed.”

twi: Bere a asɔfo mpanyin ne Yudafo mpanyin no tee ase sɛ Yesu asɛm a ɔreka no fa wɔn ho no,
english: When the chief priests and the Pharisees heard Jesus’ parables, they knew he was talking about them.

twi: wɔpɛɛ sɛ wɔyɛ no bɔne, nanso na wosuro dɔm no efisɛ na wɔagye Yesu ato mu sɛ ɔyɛ Odiyifo.
english: They looked for a way to arrest him, but they were afraid of the crowd because the people held that he was a prophet.

twi: Ayeforohyia Aponto Ho BɛYesu de mmebu ahorow kyerɛɛ sɛnea Ɔsoro Ahenni no te.
english: Jesus spoke to them again in parables, saying:

twi: Ose, “Ɔsoro Ahenni no te sɛ ɔhene bi a ne babarima hyiaa ayeforo na ɔtoo pon maa no.
english: “The kingdom of heaven is like a king who prepared a wedding banquet for his son.

twi: Ɔtoo nsa frɛɛ nnipa pii. Bere no dui no, ɔnam tumi so somaa nʼasomfo sɛ wɔnkɔfrɛfrɛ nnipa no na wɔmmra. Nanso nnipa no amma.
english: He sent his servants to those who had been invited to the banquet to tell them to come, but they refused to come.

twi: “Ɔsan somaa nʼasomfo afoforo se, ‘Monkɔka nkyerɛ wɔn se, wɔawie biribiara. Wɔakum mʼanantwi ne me nyɛmmoa de anoa aduan awie. Mommra ayeforo no ase mmedidi!’
english: “Then he sent some more servants and said, ‘Tell those who have been invited that I have prepared my dinner: My oxen and fattened cattle have been butchered, and everything is ready. Come to the wedding banquet.’

twi: “Nanso wɔammua no. Obi kɔɔ nʼafum. Ɔfoforo nso kodii ne gua.
english: “But they paid no attention and went off—one to his field, another to his business.

twi: Afoforo nso kyeree nʼasomfo no hwee wɔn, pirapiraa wɔn, kunkum ebinom nso.
english: The rest seized his servants, mistreated them and killed them.

twi: Ɔhene no tee nea nnipa no ayɛ nʼasomfo no, ne bo fuwii. Ɔsomaa nʼasraafo ma wokokunkum awudifo no, hyew wɔn kurow no pasaa.
english: The king was enraged. He sent his army and destroyed those murderers and burned their city.

twi: “Ɔsan frɛɛ nʼasomfo ka kyerɛɛ wɔn se, ‘Wɔawie ayeforo aduan no. Nanso wɔn a mefrɛɛ wɔn no mfata sɛ wɔba aponto no ase.
english: “Then he said to his servants, ‘The wedding banquet is ready, but those I invited did not deserve to come.

twi: Enti monkɔ mmɔnten so na obiara a mubehu no no, momfrɛ no mmra aponto no ase.’
english: So go to the street corners and invite to the banquet anyone you find.’

twi: Asomfo no fii adi kɔɔ mmɔnten so kɔfrɛɛ nnipa dodow a wohuu wɔn no nyinaa. Wɔfrɛɛ nnipa pa ne nnipa bɔne, maa ɔdan a wɔtoo pon wɔ mu no yɛɛ ma.
english: So the servants went out into the streets and gathered all the people they could find, the bad as well as the good, and the wedding hall was filled with guests.

twi: “Ɔhene no baa hɔ sɛ ɔrebɛhwɛ nnipa a wɔaba no, ohuu obi a ɔnhyɛ ayeforohyia atade wɔ hɔ.
english: “But when the king came in to see the guests, he noticed a man there who was not wearing wedding clothes.

twi: Obisaa no se, ‘Damfo, ɛyɛɛ dɛn na wonhyɛ ayeforohyia atade, na wutumi baa ha?’ Nanso damfo no antumi ammua.
english: He asked, ‘How did you get in here without wedding clothes, friend?’ The man was speechless.

twi: “Afei ɔhene no ka kyerɛɛ nʼasomfo no se, ‘Monkyekyere ne nan ne ne nsa na monkɔtow no nkyene akyirikyiri sum mu, nea osu ne setwɛre wɔ no.’
english: “Then the king told the attendants, ‘Tie him hand and foot, and throw him outside, into the darkness, where there will be weeping and gnashing of teeth.’

twi: “Wɔafrɛ bebree, nanso kakraa bi na wɔpaw wɔn.”
english: “For many are invited, but few are chosen.”

twi: Towyi Ho AsɛmmisaFarisifo no tuu Yesu ho agyina, pɛɛ ɔkwan bi a wɔbɛfa nʼanom asɛm so anya no akyere no.
english: Then the Pharisees went out and laid plans to trap him in his words.

twi: Wosii no gyinae se, wɔbɛsoma wɔn nnipa bi ne Herodefo aba Yesu nkyɛn abebisa no se, “Owura, yenim sɛ woyɛ ɔnokwafo, na wonam nokware kwan so kyerɛ nnipa kwan a ɛkɔ Onyankopɔn nkyɛn a wunsuro akyi asɛm, efisɛ wonhwɛ nnipa anim.
english: They sent their disciples to him along with the Herodians. “Teacher,” they said, “we know that you are a man of integrity and that you teach the way of God in accordance with the truth. You aren’t swayed by others, because you pay no attention to who they are.

twi: Ka ma yentie. Eye sɛ woyi tow ma Roma Hempɔn Kaesare anaa enye?”
english: Tell us then, what is your opinion? Is it right to pay the imperial tax to Caesar or not?”

twi: Yesu huu wɔn adwemmɔne no ma ɔka kyerɛɛ wɔn se, “Mo nyaatwomfo! Adɛn nti na mopɛ sɛ mode nnaadaa sɔ me hwɛ?
english: But Jesus, knowing their evil intent, said, “You hypocrites, why are you trying to trap me?

twi: Momfa sika a wɔde yi tow no bi nkyerɛ me.” Wɔde bi kyerɛɛ no.
english: Show me the coin used for paying the tax.” They brought him a denarius,

twi: Obisaa wɔn se, “Hena mfoni na ɛda so, na hena din nso na ɛwɔ so?”
english: and he asked them, “Whose image is this? And whose inscription?”

twi: Wobuaa se, “Kaesare.”Yesu ka kyerɛɛ wɔn se, “Ɛno de, momfa Kaesare de mma Kaesare, na momfa Onyankopɔn de mma Onyankopɔn.”
english:
“Caesar’s,” they replied.
Then he said to them, “So give back to Caesar what is Caesar’s, and to God what is God’s.”

twi: Ne mmuae a ɔmaa wɔn no maa wɔn ho dwiriw wɔn ma wogyaw no hɔ kɔe.
english: When they heard this, they were amazed. So they left him and went away.

twi: Owusɔre Mu AwareDa no ara, Sadukifo a wonnye owusɔre nni no baa Yesu nkyɛn bebisaa no se,
english: That same day the Sadducees, who say there is no resurrection, came to him with a question.

twi: “Owura, Mose kae se, ‘Sɛ ɔbarima bi anwo na owu a, ne nuabarima mfa ne yere no kunabea na ɔne no nwo mma owufo no.
english: “Teacher,” they said, “Moses told us that if a man dies without having children, his brother must marry the widow and raise up offspring for him.

twi: Anuanom baason bi ne yɛn tenaa ha. Ɔpanyin no waree a wanwo ba na owui. Enti ne nua a ɔto so abien no faa ne yere no kunabea.
english: Now there were seven brothers among us. The first one married and died, and since he had no children, he left his wife to his brother.

twi: Nea ɔto so abien no nso wui, maa nea ɔto so abiɛsa no faa ɔbea no kunabea. Ɔno nso wui a wanwo ba, maa ɔfoforo nso faa ɔbea no kunabea. Eyi toaa so ara kosii sɛ anuanom baason no nyinaa waree ɔbea no.
english: The same thing happened to the second and third brother, right on down to the seventh.

twi: Nea edi akyi ne sɛ, ɔbea no nso wui.
english: Finally, the woman died.

twi: Ɛno nti, owusɔrebere no, nnipa baason yi mu hena na ɔbea no bɛyɛ ne yere? Efisɛ wɔn nyinaa waree no!’ ”
english: Now then, at the resurrection, whose wife will she be of the seven, since all of them were married to her?”

twi: Yesu buaa wɔn se, “Mo mfomso a moayɛ no fi nim a munnim Kyerɛwsɛm no ne Onyankopɔn tumi a ɔwɔ no!
english: Jesus replied, “You are in error because you do not know the Scriptures or the power of God.

twi: Na owusɔrebere no, aware nni hɔ; obiara bɛyɛ sɛ abɔfo a wɔwɔ ɔsoro no.
english: At the resurrection people will neither marry nor be given in marriage; they will be like the angels in heaven.

twi: Nea ɛfa owusɔre no ho no nso, monkenkan nea Onyankopɔn aka afa ho no pɛn? Munhu sɛ Onyankopɔn kasa kyerɛɛ mo bere a ɔkae se,
english: But about the resurrection of the dead—have you not read what God said to you,

twi: ‘Mene Abraham Nyankopɔn, Isak Nyankopɔn ne Yakob Nyankopɔn no?’ Eyi kyerɛ sɛ, Onyankopɔn nyɛ awufo Nyankopɔn na mmom, ateasefo Nyankopɔn.”
english: ‘I am the God of Abraham, the God of Isaac, and the God of Jacob’? He is not the God of the dead but of the living.”

twi: Nnipadɔm no tee ne nkyerɛkyerɛ no, ɛyɛɛ wɔn nwonwa.
english: When the crowds heard this, they were astonished at his teaching.

twi: Mmaransɛm No Mu Nea Ɛkyɛn Ne NyinaaFarisifo no tee sɛ Yesu abu afa Sadukifo no so no, wokohyiaa Yesu.
english: Hearing that Jesus had silenced the Sadducees, the Pharisees got together.

twi: Wɔn mu baako a ɔyɛ mmaranimfo bisaa Yesu se,
english: One of them, an expert in the law, tested him with this question:

twi: “Owura, Mose mmaransɛm no mu nea ɛwɔ he koraa na ɛkyɛn ne nyinaa?”
english: “Teacher, which is the greatest commandment in the Law?”

twi: Yesu buaa no se, “ ‘Dɔ Awurade, wo Nyankopɔn, wo koma nyinaa mu ne wo kra nyinaa mu ne wʼadwene nyinaa mu.’
english: Jesus replied: “‘Love the Lord your God with all your heart and with all your soul and with all your mind.’

twi: Eyi ne mmaransɛm no mu nea edi kan na ɛkyɛn ne nyinaa.
english: This is the first and greatest commandment.

twi: Nea ɛto so abien no te sɛ ɛno ara: ‘Dɔ wo yɔnko sɛ wo ho.’
english: And the second is like it: ‘Love your neighbor as yourself.’

twi: Mose mmaransɛm ne adiyifo no nkyerɛkyerɛ no nyinaa gyina saa mmaransɛm abien yi so.”
english: All the Law and the Prophets hang on these two commandments.”

twi: Hena Ba Ne Agyenkwa No?Farisifo no twaa Yesu ho hyiae no, obisaa wɔn se,
english: While the Pharisees were gathered together, Jesus asked them,

twi: “Dɛn na mususuw fa Agyenkwa no ho? Hena ba ne no?”Wobuaa no se, “Dawid Ba.”
english:
“What do you think about the Messiah? Whose son is he?”
“The son of David,” they replied.

twi: Yesu bisaa wɔn se “Ɛno de, adɛn na Dawid nam Honhom Kronkron so frɛ no ‘Awurade?’ Efisɛ Dawid kae se,
english: He said to them, “How is it then that David, speaking by the Spirit, calls him ‘Lord’? For he says,

twi: “ ‘Awurade ka kyerɛɛ me wura se,“Tena me nifakosi sɛ mɛma woadiwʼatamfo nyinaa so.” ’
english:
“‘The Lord said to my Lord:
    “Sit at my right hand
until I put your enemies
    under your feet.”’

twi: Sɛ Dawid frɛ no ‘Awurade’ a, ɛno de, ɛyɛɛ dɛn na Kristo no yɛ ne ba?”
english: If then David calls him ‘Lord,’ how can he be his son?”

twi: Obiara antumi ammua. Eyi akyi nso, obiara antumi ammisa no nsɛm bio.
english: No one could say a word in reply, and from that day on no one dared to ask him any more questions.

twi: Nyaatwomyɛ Ho KɔkɔbɔAfei, Yesu ka kyerɛɛ nnipadɔm no ne nʼasuafo no se,
english: Then Jesus said to the crowds and to his disciples:

twi: “Kyerɛwsɛm no Akyerɛkyerɛfo ne Farisifo no na wɔkyerɛ Mose mmara no ase.
english: “The teachers of the law and the Pharisees sit in Moses’ seat.

twi: Eyi nti, ɛsɛ sɛ mutie wɔn, na moyɛ biribiara a wɔkyerɛ mo. Nanso monnyɛ nea wɔyɛ no bi efisɛ nea wɔka no, ɛnyɛ ɛno na wɔyɛ.
english: So you must be careful to do everything they tell you. But do not do what they do, for they do not practice what they preach.

twi: Wɔhyɛ mo ma mudi mmara a ɛyɛ den so a wɔn ankasa mpɛ sɛ wodi so.
english: They tie up heavy, cumbersome loads and put them on other people’s shoulders, but they themselves are not willing to lift a finger to move them.

twi: “Biribiara a wɔyɛ no yɛ ɔyɛkyerɛ. Wɔde sɛbɛ a kyerɛw nsɛm bi hyɛ mu sɛn wɔn nsa, hyɛ ntade yuu kyerɛ sɛ wɔyɛ atreneefo.
english: “Everything they do is done for people to see: They make their phylacteries wide and the tassels on their garments long;

twi: Na wɔkɔ aponto ase nso a, wɔpɛ sɛ daa wɔtena mpanyin tenabea; wɔkɔ asɔre nso a wɔpɛ sɛ wɔtena mpanyin tenabea pa.
english: they love the place of honor at banquets and the most important seats in the synagogues;

twi: Sɛ wode obu kyia wɔn wɔ abɔnten so na wofrɛ wɔn ‘Rabi’ anaa ‘Owura’ a ɛyɛ wɔn dɛ.
english: they love to be greeted with respect in the marketplaces and to be called ‘Rabbi’ by others.

twi: “Mommma obiara mmfrɛ mo sa. Efisɛ Onyankopɔn nko ara na ɔyɛ Owura. Mo nyinaa moyɛ pɛ sɛ anuanom.
english: “But you are not to be called ‘Rabbi,’ for you have one Teacher, and you are all brothers.

twi: Mommfrɛ obiara wɔ asase so ha sɛ ‘Agya,’ efisɛ Onyankopɔn a ɔwɔ ɔsoro no nko ara na ɛsɛ sɛ wɔfrɛ no saa.
english: And do not call anyone on earth ‘father,’ for you have one Father, and he is in heaven.

twi: Na mommma wɔmmfrɛ mo ‘Owura,’ efisɛ ɔbaako pɛ na ɔyɛ mo wura a ɔne Agyenkwa no.
english: Nor are you to be called instructors, for you have one Instructor, the Messiah.

twi: Wobrɛ wo ho ase som afoforo a, wobɛyɛ ɔkɛse. Wopɛ sɛ woyɛ ɔkɛse a, yɛ ɔsomfo.
english: The greatest among you will be your servant.

twi: Na obiara a ɔbɛma ne ho so no, wɔbɛbrɛ no ase; saa ara nso na obiara a ɔbɛbrɛ ne ho ase no, wɔbɛma no so.
english: For those who exalt themselves will be humbled, and those who humble themselves will be exalted.

twi: Yesu Kasa Tia Nyaatwomyɛ“Munnue! Mo Farisifo ne Kyerɛwsɛm no akyerɛkyerɛfo nyaatwomfo, efisɛ musiw afoforo Ɔsoro Ahenni ho kwan. Mo a, monkɔ mu. Mo nso a, momma afoforo a wɔpɛ sɛ wɔkɔ mu no kwan.
english: “Woe to you, teachers of the law and Pharisees, you hypocrites! You shut the door of the kingdom of heaven in people’s faces. You yourselves do not enter, nor will you let those enter who are trying to.

twi: Nyaatwomfo! Mobɔ mpae atenten wɔ mmɔnten so de kyerɛ sɛ moyɛ atreneefo wɔ bere a mutu akunafo fi wɔn afi mu.
“Munnue! Mo Farisifo ne Kyerɛwsɛm no akyerɛkyerɛfo nyaatwomfo! Mokɔ wiase afanan nyinaa sɛ mubenya onipa baako abɛfra mo mu. Na sɛ munya obi saa a, mosɛe no ma ɔyɛ ɔbonsam ba sen sɛnea mote no.
english: “Woe to you, teachers of the law and Pharisees, you hypocrites! You travel over land and sea to win a single convert, and when you have succeeded, you make them twice as much a child of hell as you are.

twi: “Munnue! Akwankyerɛfo anifuraefo a moka se, sɛ obi de asɔredan ka ntam a, ɛno de, ɛnyɛ hwee. Na sɛ ɔde sikakɔkɔɔ a ɛwɔ asɔredan no mu ka ntam de a, ɛno de, ntam no kyekyere onii no.
english: “Woe to you, blind guides! You say, ‘If anyone swears by the temple, it means nothing; but anyone who swears by the gold of the temple is bound by that oath.’

twi: Anifuraefo nkwaseafo! Asɔredan no ne emu sikakɔkɔɔ no mu nea ɛwɔ he na ɛsom bo; sikakɔkɔɔ no anaa asɔredan no a ɛtew sikakɔkɔɔ no ho no?
english: You blind fools! Which is greater: the gold, or the temple that makes the gold sacred?

twi: Na moka se, ‘Sɛ obi ka afɔremuka no ntam a, ɛnyɛ hwee. Na mmom, sɛ ɔka ayɛyɛde a egu afɔremuka no so ntam de a, ɛkyekye onii! no’
english: You also say, ‘If anyone swears by the altar, it means nothing; but anyone who swears by the gift on the altar is bound by that oath.’

twi: Anifuraefo! Afɔremuka a ɛtew ayɛyɛde a egu so no ho no, ne ayɛyɛde a egu so no mu nea ɛwɔ he na ɛsom bo?
english: You blind men! Which is greater: the gift, or the altar that makes the gift sacred?

twi: Sɛ woka afɔremuka no ntam a, woka afɔremuka no ne ɛso ayɛyɛde no nyinaa ntam,
english: Therefore, anyone who swears by the altar swears by it and by everything on it.

twi: na sɛ woka asɔredan no ntam a, woka asɔredan no ne Onyankopɔn a ɔte mu no nyinaa ntam.
english: And anyone who swears by the temple swears by it and by the one who dwells in it.

twi: Na sɛ woka ɔsoro ntam a, na woreka Onyankopɔn ahengua ne Onyankopɔn no ankasa ntam.
english: And anyone who swears by heaven swears by God’s throne and by the one who sits on it.

twi: “Munnue! Mo Farisifo ne Kyerɛwsɛm no akyerɛkyerɛfo nyaatwomfo! Muyi ntotoso du du wɔ afifide a ɛwɔ mo mfikyifuw mu no ho, nanso mugyaw nneɛma a ɛsom bo te sɛ atɛntrenee, ahummɔbɔ ne nokwaredi. Ɛwɔ mu sɛ ɛsɛ sɛ muyiyi ntotoso du du no de, nanso ɛnsɛ sɛ mugyaw nneɛma a ɛsom bo no.
english: “Woe to you, teachers of the law and Pharisees, you hypocrites! You give a tenth of your spices—mint, dill and cumin. But you have neglected the more important matters of the law—justice, mercy and faithfulness. You should have practiced the latter, without neglecting the former.

twi: Akwankyerɛfo anifuraefo! Mosɔn nea monom so, yi mu nwansena nanso momene yoma!
english: You blind guides! You strain out a gnat but swallow a camel.

twi: “Munnue! Mo Farisifo ne Kyerɛwsɛm no akyerɛkyerɛfo nyaatwomfo! Mutwiw mo kuruwa ne mo asanka ho fɛfɛɛfɛ nanso emu no de, amim ne pɛsɛmenkominya ahyɛ no ma tɔ.
english: “Woe to you, teachers of the law and Pharisees, you hypocrites! You clean the outside of the cup and dish, but inside they are full of greed and self-indulgence.

twi: Farisifo anifuraefo! Muntwiw kuruwa no mu kan, na kuruwa no ho nyinaa bɛtew!
english: Blind Pharisee! First clean the inside of the cup and dish, and then the outside also will be clean.

twi: “Munnue! Mo Farisifo ne Kyerɛwsɛm no akyerɛkyerɛfo! Mote sɛ ɔda a wɔasra ho fɛfɛɛfɛ nanso awufo nnompe ne nneɛma funu ahyɛ mu ma tɔ.
english: “Woe to you, teachers of the law and Pharisees, you hypocrites! You are like whitewashed tombs, which look beautiful on the outside but on the inside are full of the bones of the dead and everything unclean.

twi: Moyɛ mo anim sɛ atreneefo, nanso bɔne ahorow ahyɛ mo mu ma tɔ.
english: In the same way, on the outside you appear to people as righteous but on the inside you are full of hypocrisy and wickedness.

twi: “Munnue! Mo Farisifo ne Kyerɛwsɛm no akyerɛkyerɛfo nyaatwomfo! Musisi ada akɛse ma adiyifo a mo ara mo agyanom kunkum wɔn, na mode nhwiren gugu atreneefo a wokunkum wɔn no nna so,
english: “Woe to you, teachers of the law and Pharisees, you hypocrites! You build tombs for the prophets and decorate the graves of the righteous.

twi: na mutwa mo ho ka se, ‘Sɛ na yɛte ase saa bere no a, anka yɛrenyɛ bɔne a yɛn agyanom yɛe no.’
english: And you say, ‘If we had lived in the days of our ancestors, we would not have taken part with them in shedding the blood of the prophets.’

twi: Sɛ moka saa a, mubu mo ho fɔ sɛ moyɛ atirimɔdenfo mma.
english: So you testify against yourselves that you are the descendants of those who murdered the prophets.

twi: Munni wɔn anammɔn akyi nyɛ saa bɔne koro no ara bi pɛpɛɛpɛ.
english: Go ahead, then, and complete what your ancestors started!

twi: “Awɔ! Nhurutoa mma! Mobɛyɛ dɛn aguan amanehunu gya mu atemmu no?
english: “You snakes! You brood of vipers! How will you escape being condemned to hell?

twi: Mɛsoma adiyifo ne anyansafo ne akyerɛkyerɛfo aba mo nkyɛn. Mobɛbɔ wɔn mu bi asennua mu akum wɔn. Mobɛbɔ ebinom akyi mmaa wɔ mo asɔredan mu, na moataa bi afi nkurow so akɔ nkurow so.
english: Therefore I am sending you prophets and sages and teachers. Some of them you will kill and crucify; others you will flog in your synagogues and pursue from town to town.

twi: Na atreneefo mogya a moahwie agu asase so nyinaa, efi Habel so de kosi Barakia ba Sakaria a mukum no asɔredan ne afɔremuka ntam no, bɛba mo so.
english: And so upon you will come all the righteous blood that has been shed on earth, from the blood of righteous Abel to the blood of Zechariah son of Berekiah, whom you murdered between the temple and the altar.

twi: Mereka akyerɛ mo se, atemmu a wɔaboaboa ano no nyinaa bɛba nnɛmma yi so.
english: Truly I tell you, all this will come on this generation.

twi: “Ao Yerusalem, Yerusalem, wo a wukum adiyifo, na wusiw wɔn a wɔasoma wɔn wo nkyɛn abo, mpɛn ahe na anka mepɛɛ sɛ meboaboa wo mma ano, sɛnea akokɔbeatan boaboa ne mma ano wɔ ne ntaban ase, nanso moampɛ!
english: “Jerusalem, Jerusalem, you who kill the prophets and stone those sent to you, how often I have longed to gather your children together, as a hen gathers her chicks under her wings, and you were not willing.

twi: Wobegyaw mo fi ofituw ama mo.
english: Look, your house is left to you desolate.

twi: Na mise mo sɛ, efi sesɛɛ morenhu me bio kosi sɛ mobɛka se, ‘Nhyira ne nea ɔnam Awurade din mu reba no.’ ”
english: For I tell you, you will not see me again until you say, ‘Blessed is he who comes in the name of the Lord.’”

twi: Asɔredansɛe Ho Nkɔmhyɛ Ne Awiei Mmere NsɛnkyerɛnneYesu refi faako a asɔredan no si hɔ akɔ no, nʼasuafo no baa ne nkyɛn pɛɛ sɛ wɔtwe nʼadwene kɔ adan ahorow a ɛwɔ asɔredan no mu no so.
english: Jesus left the temple and was walking away when his disciples came up to him to call his attention to its buildings.

twi: Nanso ɔka kyerɛɛ wɔn se, “Wobedwiriw saa dan yi agu pasaa!”
english: “Do you see all these things?” he asked. “Truly I tell you, not one stone here will be left on another; every one will be thrown down.”

twi: Ɔhaw Ne ƆtaaYesu kɔɔ Ngo Bepɔw no so. Ɔte hɔ no, nʼasuafo no baa ne nkyɛn bebisaa no se, “Bere bɛn na nea woreka yi bɛba? Na nsɛnkyerɛnne bɛn na ɛbɛma yɛahu wo ba a wobɛsan aba bio no ne wiase awiei a ɛbɛba no?”
english: As Jesus was sitting on the Mount of Olives, the disciples came to him privately. “Tell us,” they said, “when will this happen, and what will be the sign of your coming and of the end of the age?”

twi: Yesu ka kyerɛɛ wɔn se, “Monhwɛ na obi annaadaa mo.
english: Jesus answered: “Watch out that no one deceives you.

twi: Nnipa bebree de me din bɛba abɛka se, wɔne Agyenkwa no, na wɔadaadaa mo mu pii.
english: For many will come in my name, claiming, ‘I am the Messiah,’ and will deceive many.

twi: Sɛ mote sɛ wɔafi akodi ase a, ɛnkyerɛ me ba a mɛsan aba no ho nsɛnkyerɛnne. Ɛsɛ sɛ eyinom ba, nanso awiei no de, ennya mmae.
english: You will hear of wars and rumors of wars, but see to it that you are not alarmed. Such things must happen, but the end is still to come.

twi: Aman bɛsɔre wɔ aman so, na ahenni asɔre wɔ ahenni so, na ɔkɔm ne asasewosow bɛba mmeaemmeae.
english: Nation will rise against nation, and kingdom against kingdom. There will be famines and earthquakes in various places.

twi: Eyinom nyinaa bɛyɛ nneɛma a ɛyɛ hu a ɛbɛba no mfiase.
english: All these are the beginning of birth pains.

twi: “Sɛ moyɛ me de nti, wɔbɛyɛ mo ayayade, na wɔakunkum mo wɔ wiase afanan nyinaa,
english: “Then you will be handed over to be persecuted and put to death, and you will be hated by all nations because of me.

twi: na mo mu pii bɛsan akɔ bɔne mu, na moayiyi mo ho mo ho ama, na moatentan mo ho mo ho.
english: At that time many will turn away from the faith and will betray and hate each other,

twi: Atoro adiyifo bebree bɛsɔre, na wɔadaadaa mo mu pii.
english: and many false prophets will appear and deceive many people.

twi: Bɔne bɛdɔɔso wɔ wiase, na abrɛ nnipa dɔ a wɔwɔ no ase.
english: Because of the increase of wickedness, the love of most will grow cold,

twi: Nanso wɔn a wobegyina pintinn akodu awiei no, wobegye wɔn nkwa.
english: but the one who stands firm to the end will be saved.

twi: Na wɔbɛka asɛmpa a ɛfa Ahenni no ho no wɔ wiase mmaa nyinaa, na wɔate. Ɛno akyi ansa na awiei no bɛba.”
english: And this gospel of the kingdom will be preached in the whole world as a testimony to all nations, and then the end will come.

twi: Ahohia A Ɛyɛ Hu“Enti sɛ muhu ‘abusude a ɛde ɔsɛe ba’ a Odiyifo Daniel kaa ho asɛm sɛ egyina kronkronbea hɔ no a, ma nea ɔkenkan no nte ase,
english: “So when you see standing in the holy place ‘the abomination that causes desolation,’ spoken of through the prophet Daniel—let the reader understand—

twi: na wɔn a wɔte Yudea no nguan nkɔ Yuda mmepɔw so.
english: then let those who are in Judea flee to the mountains.

twi: Mma obiara a ɔwɔ ne fi dan atifi no nsian nkɔfa biribiara mfi ne fi hɔ.
english: Let no one on the housetop go down to take anything out of the house.

twi: Wɔn a wɔwɔ mfuw so no nso nnsan wɔn akyi mmɛfa wɔn ntama.
english: Let no one in the field go back to get their cloak.

twi: Ɛbɛyɛ hu ama wɔn a wɔafa afuru ne wɔn a woturu mma saa bere no mu!
english: How dreadful it will be in those days for pregnant women and nursing mothers!

twi: Na mommɔ mpae na bere a ɛsɛ sɛ muguan no anyɛ awɔwbere anaa Homeda.
english: Pray that your flight will not take place in winter or on the Sabbath.

twi: Efisɛ awerɛhowdi a ɛbɛba no, bi nsii wɔ wiase abakɔsɛm mu da, na bi nso rensi da.
english: For then there will be great distress, unequaled from the beginning of the world until now—and never to be equaled again.

twi: “Nokware, sɛ wɔantwa saa nna no so a, ɛrenka obi.
english: “If those days had not been cut short, no one would survive, but for the sake of the elect those days will be shortened.

twi: Sɛ obi ka kyerɛ mo se, ‘Agyenkwa no wɔ ha anaasɛ ɔwɔ nohɔ anaa wayi ne ho adi wɔ ha anaa ɛhɔ’ a, munnnye nni.
english: At that time if anyone says to you, ‘Look, here is the Messiah!’ or, ‘There he is!’ do not believe it.

twi: Atoro agyenkwanom ne atoro adiyifo bɛsɔre, na wɔayɛ anwonwade ahorow na sɛ ebetumi a, wɔadaadaa wɔn a Onyankopɔn ayi wɔn no mpo.
english: For false messiahs and false prophets will appear and perform great signs and wonders to deceive, if possible, even the elect.

twi: Monhwɛ yiye, efisɛ maka biribiara akyerɛ mo!
english: See, I have told you ahead of time.

twi: “Enti sɛ obi ka kyerɛ mo se, ‘Agyenkwa no asan aba na ɔwɔ sare so a,’ monnhaw mo ho sɛ mobɛkɔ hɔ akɔhwehwɛ no. Anaasɛ nso wose, ‘Ɔde ne ho asie baabi a,’ munnnye nni!
english: “So if anyone tells you, ‘There he is, out in the wilderness,’ do not go out; or, ‘Here he is, in the inner rooms,’ do not believe it.

twi: Na sɛnea anyinam twa fi apuei kɔ atɔe no, saa ara na sɛ Onipa Ba no reba a, ɛbɛyɛ ne no.
english: For as lightning that comes from the east is visible even in the west, so will be the coming of the Son of Man.

twi: Na nea funu wɔ no, ɛhɔ na apete bɛboaboa wɔn ho ano.
english: Wherever there is a carcass, there the vultures will gather.

twi: “Saa mmere no awerɛhowdi no akyi pɛ“ ‘owia beduru sum,na ɔsram renhyerɛn;na nsoromma befi wim atetew ahwe,na wim abɔde behinhim.’
english:
“Immediately after the distress of those days
“‘the sun will be darkened,
    and the moon will not give its light;
the stars will fall from the sky,
    and the heavenly bodies will be shaken.’

twi: “Afei Onipa Ba no ho nsɛnkyerɛnne bɛda adi wɔ ɔsoro. Na asase sofo nyinaa betwa agyaadwo bere a wobehu Onipa Ba no sɛ ɔde tumi ne anuonyam nam ɔsoro omununkum mu reba.
english: “Then will appear the sign of the Son of Man in heaven. And then all the peoples of the earth will mourn when they see the Son of Man coming on the clouds of heaven, with power and great glory.

twi: Na mɛsoma mʼabɔfo na wɔde torobɛnto a ano yɛ den aba abɛboaboa wɔn a mayi wɔn no ano fi ɔsoro ano akɔka asase ano.
english: And he will send his angels with a loud trumpet call, and they will gather his elect from the four winds, from one end of the heavens to the other.

twi: “Afei munsua biribi mfi borɔdɔma dua no ho asɛm no mu. Sɛ eyi mman foforo, san yi nhaban foforo a, na ɛkyerɛ sɛ asusow abɛn.
english: “Now learn this lesson from the fig tree: As soon as its twigs get tender and its leaves come out, you know that summer is near.

twi: Saa ara nso na sɛ muhu sɛ saa nneɛma yi nyinaa afi ase resisi a, mubehu sɛ me ba a mɛsan aba no abɛn, adu ɔpon ano.
english: Even so, when you see all these things, you know that it is near, right at the door.

twi: Nokware mise mo sɛ, awo ntoatoaso yi rentwa mu, gye sɛ saa nneɛma yi nyinaa aba mu ansa.
english: Truly I tell you, this generation will certainly not pass away until all these things have happened.

twi: Ɔsoro ne asase betwa mu akɔ, nanso me nsɛm de, ɛbɛtena hɔ daa.
english: Heaven and earth will pass away, but my words will never pass away.

twi: “Nanso da anaa dɔn ko a awiei no bɛba de, obiara nnim. Ɔsoro abɔfo ne Onyankopɔn Ba no mpo nnim. Agya no nko na onim.
english: “But about that day or hour no one knows, not even the angels in heaven, nor the Son, but only the Father.

twi: Onipa Ba no ba a ɔbɛba no bɛyɛ sɛnea Noa bere so ɛyɛɛ no ara pɛ.
english: As it was in the days of Noah, so it will be at the coming of the Son of Man.

twi: Na sɛnea nna a edi nsuyiri no anim no nnipa didii, na wɔnomee, warewaree, de kosii da a Noa kɔɔ hyɛn no mu,
english: For in the days before the flood, people were eating and drinking, marrying and giving in marriage, up to the day Noah entered the ark;

twi: na nnipa annye nea ɛbɛba anni, kosii sɛ nsuyiri bɛfaa wɔn nyinaa kɔe no, saa ara na me ba a mɛsan aba no bɛyɛ.
english: and they knew nothing about what would happen until the flood came and took them all away. That is how it will be at the coming of the Son of Man.

twi: Saa bere no, wɔbɛfa mmarima baanu a wɔreyɛ adwuma wɔ afum no mu baako akɔ, na wɔagyaw ɔbaako.
english: Two men will be in the field; one will be taken and the other left.

twi: Saa ara nso na mmea baanu a wɔwɔ fie renoa aduan no nso, wɔbɛfa ɔbaako agyaw ɔbaako.
english: Two women will be grinding with a hand mill; one will be taken and the other left.

twi: “Enti monwɛn, efisɛ munnim da ko a Awurade bɛba.
english: “Therefore keep watch, because you do not know on what day your Lord will come.

twi: Sɛnea sɛ ofiwura nim bere a owifo bɛba a anka ɔbɛwɛn de abɔ ne ho ban afi akorɔmfo ho no,
english: But understand this: If the owner of the house had known at what time of night the thief was coming, he would have kept watch and would not have let his house be broken into.

twi: saa ara na ɛsɛ sɛ musiesie mo ho, efisɛ Onipa Ba no bɛba bere a mo ani nna so sɛ ɔbɛba.
english: So you also must be ready, because the Son of Man will come at an hour when you do not expect him.

twi: Akoa Pa Anaa Akoa Bɔne“Hena ne ɔsomfo nokwafo nyansafo no, nea ne wura de ne fi mu asomfo ahyɛ ne nsa sɛ ɔmma wɔn aduan wɔ bere a ɛsɛ mu?
english: “Who then is the faithful and wise servant, whom the master has put in charge of the servants in his household to give them their food at the proper time?

twi: Nhyira ne ɔsomfo a ne wura no bɛba abɛto no sɛ wayɛ nʼadwuma pɛpɛɛpɛ.
english: It will be good for that servant whose master finds him doing so when he returns.

twi: Meka mo nokware se ɔde nea ɔwɔ nyinaa bɛhyɛ ne nsa na wahwɛ so!
english: Truly I tell you, he will put him in charge of all his possessions.

twi: Na sɛ ɔkɔyɛ ɔsomfo tirimuɔdenfo, na ɔka kyerɛ ne ho se, ‘Me Wura nnya mmae,’
english: But suppose that servant is wicked and says to himself, ‘My master is staying away a long time,’

twi: na ofi ase boro ne mfɛfo nkoa, na ɔne akɔwensafo didi, bow nsa a,
english: and he then begins to beat his fellow servants and to eat and drink with drunkards.

twi: Ɔsomfo no wura no bɛba da a nʼani nna so.
english: The master of that servant will come on a day when he does not expect him and at an hour he is not aware of.

twi: Ɔbɛtwe nʼaso dennen, na ɔde no akɔ baabi a wobu nyaatwomfo atɛn; ɛhɔ na osu ne setwɛre wɔ.
english: He will cut him to pieces and assign him a place with the hypocrites, where there will be weeping and gnashing of teeth.

twi: Mmabaa Du No Ho Bɛ“Ɔsoro Ahenni te sɛ mmabaa du bi a wɔfaa wɔn akanea se wɔrekohyia ayeforokunu.
english: “At that time the kingdom of heaven will be like ten virgins who took their lamps and went out to meet the bridegroom.

twi: Na mmabaa no mu baanum yɛ anyansafo na baanum nso yɛ nkwaseafo.
english: Five of them were foolish and five were wise.

twi: Wɔn mu nkwaseafo no rekɔ no, wɔfaa wɔn akanea nanso wɔamfa ngo anka ho.
english: The foolish ones took their lamps but did not take any oil with them.

twi: Nanso wɔn mu anyansafo no de, wɔrekɔ no wɔfaa ngo kaa wɔn akanea ho kɔe.
english: The wise ones, however, took oil in jars along with their lamps.

twi: Ayeforokunu no amma ntɛm, enti wofii ase totɔɔ nko dedae.
english: The bridegroom was a long time in coming, and they all became drowsy and fell asleep.

twi: “Ɔdasu mu na wɔtee nteɛteɛmu se, ‘Ayeforokunu no reba! Mumfi adi nkohyia no!’
english: “At midnight the cry rang out: ‘Here’s the bridegroom! Come out to meet him!’

twi: “Mmabaa yi nyinaa sɔre buebuee wɔn akanea no.
english: “Then all the virgins woke up and trimmed their lamps.

twi: Nkwaseafo no srɛɛ anyansafo no se, ‘Momma yɛn mo ngo no bi ngu yɛn akanea no mu na ɛredunnum.’
english: The foolish ones said to the wise, ‘Give us some of your oil; our lamps are going out.’

twi: “Anyansafo no ka kyerɛɛ wɔn se, ‘Ngo a yɛwɔ no sua. Monkɔ kurom nkɔtɔ bi.’
english: “‘No,’ they replied, ‘there may not be enough for both us and you. Instead, go to those who sell oil and buy some for yourselves.’

twi: “Wɔrekɔ akɔtɔ ngo no pɛ, na ayeforokunu no bae. Enti wɔn a wɔasiesie wɔn ho no ne ayeforokunu no kɔɔ nʼaponto no ase, na wɔtoo ɔpon no mu.
english: “But while they were on their way to buy the oil, the bridegroom arrived. The virgins who were ready went in with him to the wedding banquet. And the door was shut.

twi: “Akyiri no a baanum no san bae no, wogyinaa ɔpon no akyi frɛe se, ‘Owura, hiɛ yɛn!’
english: “Later the others also came. ‘Lord, Lord,’ they said, ‘open the door for us!’

twi: “Nanso ɔka kyerɛɛ wɔn se, ‘Mumfi hɔ nkɔ. Minnim mo!’
english: “But he replied, ‘Truly I tell you, I don’t know you.’

twi: “Enti monwɛn na munnim da anaa dɔn ko no.
english: “Therefore keep watch, because you do not know the day or the hour.

twi: Sika Nkotoku No Ho Bɛ“Bio, Ɔsoro Ahenni te sɛ ɔbarima bi a ɔretu kwan akɔ ɔman foforo bi so. Ɔrekɔ no, ɔfrɛɛ ne nkoa na ɔde nʼahode maa wɔn.
english: “Again, it will be like a man going on a journey, who called his servants and entrusted his wealth to them.

twi: Ɔmaa ɔbaako sika nkotoku anum. Ɔmaa ɔfoforo nkotoku abien na ɔfoforo, kotoku baako, sɛnea obiara ahoɔden te.
english: To one he gave five bags of gold, to another two bags, and to another one bag, each according to his ability. Then he went on his journey.

twi: Nea ɔmaa no nkotoku anum no de sika no kɔyɛɛ adwuma, nyaa mfaso nkotoku anum kaa ho.
english: The man who had received five bags of gold went at once and put his money to work and gained five bags more.

twi: Saa ara na nea onyaa sika nkotoku abien no nso nyaa abien kaa ho,
english: So also, the one with two bags of gold gained two more.

twi: Nanso nea onyaa kotoku baako no de, okotuu fam de ne wura sika no siee hɔ.
english: But the man who had received one bag went off, dug a hole in the ground and hid his master’s money.

twi: “Mmere bi akyi na wɔn wura no fi akwantu mu bae ne wɔn bebuu akontaa.
english: “After a long time the master of those servants returned and settled accounts with them.

twi: Nea onyaa sika nkotoku anum no de anum kaa ho bae. Ɔkae se, ‘Me wura, womaa me sika nkotoku anum. Hwɛ, manya anum aka ho.’
english: The man who had received five bags of gold brought the other five. ‘Master,’ he said, ‘you entrusted me with five bags of gold. See, I have gained five more.’

twi: “Ne wura no ka kyerɛɛ no se, ‘Mo, akoa pa ne ɔnokwafo, woadi kakra yi ho nokware, mede wo besi nneɛma pii so panyin. Bra, na me ne wo nni dɛw!’
english: “His master replied, ‘Well done, good and faithful servant! You have been faithful with a few things; I will put you in charge of many things. Come and share your master’s happiness!’

twi: “Akoa a ɔmaa no sika nkotoku abien no nso bae. Ɔka kyerɛɛ ne wura no se, ‘Worekɔ no, womaa me sika nkotoku abien, hwɛ, manya abien aka ho.’
english: “The man with two bags of gold also came. ‘Master,’ he said, ‘you entrusted me with two bags of gold; see, I have gained two more.’

twi: “Ne wura no ka kyerɛɛ no se, ‘Mo, akoa pa ne ɔnokwafo, woadi kakra yi ho nokware, mede wo besi nneɛma pii so panyin. Bra, wo wura anigye mu!’
english: “His master replied, ‘Well done, good and faithful servant! You have been faithful with a few things; I will put you in charge of many things. Come and share your master’s happiness!’

twi: “Akoa a onyaa sika kotoku baako no nso bae. Ɔka kyerɛɛ ne wura no se, ‘Owura, minim sɛ woyɛ onipa a wo ho yɛ nwonwa. Wutumi twa wɔ nea wunnuae ɛ, na wutumi boaboa ano wɔ nea wompetee ɛ;
english: “Then the man who had received one bag of gold came. ‘Master,’ he said, ‘I knew that you are a hard man, harvesting where you have not sown and gathering where you have not scattered seed.

twi: enti misuroi, na mede wo sika no kɔhyɛɛ fam, enti wʼade ni!’
english: So I was afraid and went out and hid your gold in the ground. See, here is what belongs to you.’

twi: “Ne wura no ka kyerɛɛ no se, ‘Akoa bɔne ne onihawfo! So wunim sɛ mitumi twa wɔ nea minnuae, na mitumi boaboa ano wɔ nea mempetee?
english: “His master replied, ‘You wicked, lazy servant! So you knew that I harvest where I have not sown and gather where I have not scattered seed?

twi: Saa de a anka ɛsɛ sɛ wode sika no kɔto sikakorabea nya nsiho to hɔ ma me.
english: Well then, you should have put my money on deposit with the bankers, so that when I returned I would have received it back with interest.

twi: “ ‘Munnye sika kotoku no mfi ne nsam, na momfa nkɔma nea onyaa nkotoku du no.
english: “‘So take the bag of gold from him and give it to the one who has ten bags.

twi: Obiara a ɔwɔ no, wɔde bi bɛka ho ama no anya aboro so. Na obiara a onni no, nea ɔwɔ no mpo, wobegye afi ne nsam.
english: For whoever has will be given more, and they will have an abundance. Whoever does not have, even what they have will be taken from them.

twi: Na wɔatow saa akoa a ne so nni mfaso no akyene sum kabii mu; ɛhɔ na osu ne setwɛre wɔ.’ ”
english: And throw that worthless servant outside, into the darkness, where there will be weeping and gnashing of teeth.’

twi: Nguanten Ne Mmirekyi No“Na sɛ Onipa Ba no ba nʼanuonyam mu a abɔfo nyinaa ka ne ho a, saa bere no na ɔbɛtena nʼanuonyam ahengua no so.
english: “When the Son of Man comes in his glory, and all the angels with him, he will sit on his glorious throne.

twi: Na wɔbɛboaboa aman nyinaa ano wɔ nʼanim. Na ɔbɛpaw nnipa no mu sɛnea oguanhwɛfo paw nguan fi mmirekyi mu;
english: All the nations will be gathered before him, and he will separate the people one from another as a shepherd separates the sheep from the goats.

twi: na ɔde nguan no begyina ne nifa so, na ɔde mmirekyi no agyina ne benkum so.
english: He will put the sheep on his right and the goats on his left.

twi: “Ɛno na Ɔhene no bɛka akyerɛ wɔn a wogyina ne nifa so no se, ‘Mo a mʼagya ahyira mo, mommra mmɛfa ahenni a wɔasiesie ama mo fi abɔde mfiase no nni!
english: “Then the King will say to those on his right, ‘Come, you who are blessed by my Father; take your inheritance, the kingdom prepared for you since the creation of the world.

twi: Ɔkɔm dee me, na momaa me aduan dii. Osukɔm dee me, na momaa me nsu nomee. Meyɛɛ ɔhɔho, na mode me kɔɔ mo fi.
english: For I was hungry and you gave me something to eat, I was thirsty and you gave me something to drink, I was a stranger and you invited me in,

twi: Medaa adagyaw na mufuraa me ntama. Meyaree, na mobɛsraa me. Medaa afiase, na mobɛhwɛɛ me.’
english: I needed clothes and you clothed me, I was sick and you looked after me, I was in prison and you came to visit me.’

twi: “Saa bere no mu na atreneefo bebisa se, ‘Owura, da bɛn na yehuu wo sɛ ɔkɔm de wo a, yɛmaa wo aduan, na osukɔm de wo a yɛmaa wo nsu nomee?
english: “Then the righteous will answer him, ‘Lord, when did we see you hungry and feed you, or thirsty and give you something to drink?

twi: Afei da bɛn na yehuu sɛ woyɛɛ ɔhɔho, a yɛde wo kɔɔ yɛn fi, anaasɛ wodaa adagyaw a, yefuraa wo ntama?
english: When did we see you a stranger and invite you in, or needing clothes and clothe you?

twi: Afei da bɛn na yehuu sɛ woyaree a, yɛbɛsraa wo, anaasɛ wodaa afiase a, yɛbɛhwɛɛ wo?’
english: When did we see you sick or in prison and go to visit you?’

twi: “Na Ɔhene no, bebua wɔn se, ‘Sɛ moayɛ ama me nuanom nkumaa yi mu baako yi, moayɛ ama me!’
english: “The King will reply, ‘Truly I tell you, whatever you did for one of the least of these brothers and sisters of mine, you did for me.’

twi: “Afei mɛka akyerɛ wɔn a wogyina me benkum so no se, ‘Mo a wɔadome mo, mumfi me so nkɔ ogyatannaa a ennum da a wɔasɔ ama ɔbonsam ne nʼabɔfo no mu.
english: “Then he will say to those on his left, ‘Depart from me, you who are cursed, into the eternal fire prepared for the devil and his angels.

twi: Na ɔkɔm dee me, moamma me aduan anni, osukɔm dee me, moamma me nsu annom.
english: For I was hungry and you gave me nothing to eat, I was thirsty and you gave me nothing to drink,

twi: Meyɛɛ ɔhɔho, moamfa me ankɔ mo fi. Medaa adagyaw, moamfura me ntama. Meyaree, moammɛsra me. Medaa afiase, moammɛhwɛ me.’
english: I was a stranger and you did not invite me in, I needed clothes and you did not clothe me, I was sick and in prison and you did not look after me.’

twi: “Wɔn nso bebua no se, ‘Awurade, da bɛn na yehuu wo sɛ ɔkɔm dee wo, anaasɛ osukɔm dee wo, anaasɛ woyɛɛ ɔhɔho, anaasɛ wodaa adagyaw, anaasɛ woyaree, anaasɛ wodaa afiase, na yɛammoa wo?’
english: “They also will answer, ‘Lord, when did we see you hungry or thirsty or a stranger or needing clothes or sick or in prison, and did not help you?’

twi: “Na obebua wɔn se, ‘Sɛ moanyɛ amma nkumaa yi mu baako nti, moanyɛ amma me.’
english: “He will reply, ‘Truly I tell you, whatever you did not do for one of the least of these, you did not do for me.’

twi: “Na wɔbɛkɔ asotwe a ɛto ntwa da mu, na atreneefo akɔ nkwa a enni awiei mu.”
english: “Then they will go away to eternal punishment, but the righteous to eternal life.”

twi: Wɔbɔ Yesu Ho PɔwYesu wiee nsɛm yi nyinaa ka no, ɔka kyerɛɛ nʼasuafo no se,
english: When Jesus had finished saying all these things, he said to his disciples,

twi: “Sɛnea munim no aka nnaanu na Twam Afahyɛ no adu, na wobeyi Onipa Ba no ama, na wɔabɔ no asennua mu.”
english: “As you know, the Passover is two days away—and the Son of Man will be handed over to be crucified.”

twi: Saa bere no ara na asɔfo mpanyin ne Yudafo mpanyin bi ahyia mu wɔ Ɔsɔfopanyin Kaiafa fi,
english: Then the chief priests and the elders of the people assembled in the palace of the high priest, whose name was Caiaphas,

twi: retu agyina ahwehwɛ ɔkwan a wɔbɛfa so akyere Yesu, akum no a obiara renhu akyi.
english: and they schemed to arrest Jesus secretly and kill him.

twi: Nanso wɔkae se, “Ɛnsɛ sɛ wɔkyere no Twam Afahyɛ no mu, anyɛ saa a, ɛde basabasayɛ bɛba ɔman no mu.”
english: “But not during the festival,” they said, “or there may be a riot among the people.”

twi: Wɔsra Yesu Ngo Wɔ BetaniaAfei Yesu kɔɔ Betania na ɔkɔɔ Simon ɔkwatani fi.
english: While Jesus was in Bethany in the home of Simon the Leper,

twi: Ɔwɔ hɔ redidi no, ɔbea bi a okura ngo huamhuam bi a ne bo yɛ den yiye toa ma baa hɔ, behwie guu Yesu tirim.
english: a woman came to him with an alabaster jar of very expensive perfume, which she poured on his head as he was reclining at the table.

twi: Asuafo no hui no, anyɛ wɔn dɛ. Wɔkae se, “Adesɛe yi ase ne dɛn?
english: When the disciples saw this, they were indignant. “Why this waste?” they asked.

twi: Anka wobetumi atɔn srade huamhuam yi anya sika bebree de ama ahiafo.”
english: “This perfume could have been sold at a high price and the money given to the poor.”

twi: Yesu huu wɔn adwene na ɔka kyerɛɛ wɔn se, “Adɛn na mohaw ɔbea yi? Wayɛ ade pa ama me.
english: Aware of this, Jesus said to them, “Why are you bothering this woman? She has done a beautiful thing to me.

twi: Mo ne ahiafo wɔ ha daa na me de, me ne mo nni hɔ daa.
english: The poor you will always have with you, but you will not always have me.

twi: Wahwie ngo huamhuam yi agu me so de asiesie me nipadua ama me sie.
english: When she poured this perfume on my body, she did it to prepare me for burial.

twi: Nokware, mise mo sɛ, wɔbɛka nea ɔyɛe yi wɔ wiase baabiara a wɔka asɛmpa no de akae no.”
english: Truly I tell you, wherever this gospel is preached throughout the world, what she has done will also be told, in memory of her.”

twi: Yuda Pene So Sɛ Obeyi Yesu AmaAfei Yuda Iskariot a ɔyɛ asuafo dumien no mu baako kɔɔ asɔfo mpanyin no nkyɛn
english: Then one of the Twelve—the one called Judas Iscariot—went to the chief priests

twi: kobisaa wɔn se, “Sɛ miyi Yesu ma mo a, ahe na mode bɛma me?” Wɔmaa no dwetɛ mpɔw aduasa.
english: and asked, “What are you willing to give me if I deliver him over to you?” So they counted out for him thirty pieces of silver.

twi: Efi saa bere no, Yuda hwehwɛɛ ɔkwan a ɔbɛfa so ayi no ama wɔn.
english: From then on Judas watched for an opportunity to hand him over.

twi: Adidi A Edi AkyiriApiti Afahyɛ da a edi kan no, asuafo no baa Yesu nkyɛn bebisaa no se, “Ɛhe na wopɛ sɛ yekodi Twam Afahyɛ no?”
english: On the first day of the Festival of Unleavened Bread, the disciples came to Jesus and asked, “Where do you want us to make preparations for you to eat the Passover?”

twi: Obuaa wɔn se, “Monkɔ kurow no mu nkohu ɔpanyin asiamasi nka nkyerɛ no se, ‘Kyerɛkyerɛfo no se, Me bere abɛn, na wo fi na me ne nʼasuafo no bedi Twam Afahyɛ no.’ ”
english: He replied, “Go into the city to a certain man and tell him, ‘The Teacher says: My appointed time is near. I am going to celebrate the Passover with my disciples at your house.’”

twi: Asuafo no dii nea ɔka kyerɛɛ wɔn no so, yɛɛ Twam Afahyɛ aduan no.
english: So the disciples did as Jesus had directed them and prepared the Passover.

twi: Anwummere no na ɔne Dumien no te adidii.
english: When evening came, Jesus was reclining at the table with the Twelve.

twi: Wɔredidi no ɔkae se, “Mereka mo nokware, mo mu baako beyi me ama.”
english: And while they were eating, he said, “Truly I tell you, one of you will betray me.”

twi: Asɛm yi maa wɔn werɛ howee yiye, na wofii ase bisabisaa mmaako mmaako se, “Awurade, ɛyɛ me ana?”
english: They were very sad and began to say to him one after the other, “Surely you don’t mean me, Lord?”

twi: Yesu buae se, “Nea ɔne me nsa da asanka baako mu no, ɔno na obeyi me ama.
english: Jesus replied, “The one who has dipped his hand into the bowl with me will betray me.

twi: Onipa Ba no rekɔ sɛnea wɔakyerɛw afa ne ho de, nanso onipa a obeyi no ama no, nnue! Sɛ wɔanwo saa onipa no mpo a, anka eye.”
english: The Son of Man will go just as it is written about him. But woe to that man who betrays the Son of Man! It would be better for him if he had not been born.”

twi: Yuda a obeyi no ama nso bisaa no se, “Kyerɛkyerɛfo, ɛyɛ me ana?”Yesu buaa no se, “Woaka.”
english:
Then Judas, the one who would betray him, said, “Surely you don’t mean me, Rabbi?”
Jesus answered, “You have said so.”

twi: Adidi KronkronBere a wɔredidi no. Yesu faa brodo, na ohyiraa so bubuu mu, de maa nʼasuafo no kae se: “Munnye nni, eyi ne me nipadua.”
english: While they were eating, Jesus took bread, and when he had given thanks, he broke it and gave it to his disciples, saying, “Take and eat; this is my body.”

twi: Na ɔfaa kuruwa no, na ɔdaa ase no, ɔde maa wɔn kae se, “Mo nyinaa monnom bi,
english: Then he took a cup, and when he had given thanks, he gave it to them, saying, “Drink from it, all of you.

twi: na eyi ne me mogya a ɛhyɛ Apam Foforo no mu den, a wohwie gu ma nnipa bebree nya bɔnefakyɛ.
english: This is my blood of the covenant, which is poured out for many for the forgiveness of sins.

twi: Mise mo sɛ, merennom saa nsa yi bi bio da, de bɛkɔ akosi da a me ne mo bɛnom bi bio wɔ mʼAgya Ahenni no mu.”
english: I tell you, I will not drink from this fruit of the vine from now on until that day when I drink it new with you in my Father’s kingdom.”

twi: Na wɔtoo dwom wiee no, wofii adi kɔɔ Ngo Bepɔw no so.
english: When they had sung a hymn, they went out to the Mount of Olives.

twi: Yesu Hyɛ Petro Pa A Ɔbɛpa No No Ho NkɔmYesu ka kyerɛɛ wɔn se, “Anadwo yi, mo nyinaa beguan agya me. Na wɔakyerɛw se,“ ‘wɔbɛbɔ oguanhwɛfo no,na nguankuw no abɔ apete.’
english:
Then Jesus told them, “This very night you will all fall away on account of me, for it is written:
“‘I will strike the shepherd,
    and the sheep of the flock will be scattered.’

twi: Na sɛ miwu sɔre a, medi mo kan akɔ Galilea.”
english: But after I have risen, I will go ahead of you into Galilee.”

twi: Petro buae se, “Sɛ nnipa nyinaa beguan agya wo a, me de, merenguan nnya wo da.”
english: Peter replied, “Even if all fall away on account of you, I never will.”

twi: Yesu buae se, “Nokware mise wo sɛ, ansa na akokɔ bɛbɔn no, na woapa me mprɛnsa!”
english: “Truly I tell you,” Jesus answered, “this very night, before the rooster crows, you will disown me three times.”

twi: Petro pae mu kae se, “Mpo sɛ etwa sɛ me ne wo wu a, merempa wo da!” Asuafo no nyinaa nso kaa saa asɛm koro yi ara.
english: But Peter declared, “Even if I have to die with you, I will never disown you.” And all the other disciples said the same.

twi: Yesu Bɔ Mpae Wɔ GetsemaneYesu de wɔn kɔɔ baabi a wɔfrɛ hɔ Getsemane. Woduu hɔ no, ɔka kyerɛɛ wɔn se, “Montena ha na merekɔ hɔ akɔbɔ mpae.”
english: Then Jesus went with his disciples to a place called Gethsemane, and he said to them, “Sit here while I go over there and pray.”

twi: Ɔfaa Petro ne Sebedeo mma baanu no kaa ne ho, na ne werɛ fii ase howee, na ne ho nso yeraw no.
english: He took Peter and the two sons of Zebedee along with him, and he began to be sorrowful and troubled.

twi: Ɔka kyerɛɛ wɔn se, “Awerɛhow ahyɛ me kra so de kɔ owu mu. Montena ha na mo ne me nwɛn.”
english: Then he said to them, “My soul is overwhelmed with sorrow to the point of death. Stay here and keep watch with me.”

twi: Na ɔkɔɔ nʼanim kakra, de nʼanim kobutuw fam bɔɔ mpae se, “MʼAgya, sɛ ebetumi a, ma wonyi kuruwa yi mfi me so. Nanso nea wopɛ na ɛnyɛ na ɛnyɛ nea mepɛ.”
english: Going a little farther, he fell with his face to the ground and prayed, “My Father, if it is possible, may this cup be taken from me. Yet not as I will, but as you will.”

twi: Na ɔsan baa asuafo baasa no nkyɛn behuu sɛ wɔadeda. Ɔfrɛɛ Petro bisaa no se, “Petro, woantumi antena ase ne me anwɛn dɔnhwerew baako pɛ mpo?
english: Then he returned to his disciples and found them sleeping. “Couldn’t you men keep watch with me for one hour?” he asked Peter.

twi: Monwɛn na mommɔ mpae, na moankɔ sɔhwɛ mu. Honhom no pɛ de, nanso ɔhonam no yɛ mmerɛw!”
english: “Watch and pray so that you will not fall into temptation. The spirit is willing, but the flesh is weak.”

twi: Ɔsan gyaw wɔn hɔ nea ɛto so abien kɔbɔɔ mpae se, “MʼAgya, sɛ wɔrenyi kuruwa yi mfi me so, na nom ara na ɛsɛ sɛ menom a, nea wopɛ nyɛ.”
english: He went away a second time and prayed, “My Father, if it is not possible for this cup to be taken away unless I drink it, may your will be done.”

twi: Ɔsan baa wɔn nkyɛn bio behuu wɔn sɛ wɔadeda efisɛ na wɔn ani kum yiye.
english: When he came back, he again found them sleeping, because their eyes were heavy.

twi: Ɔsan kɔɔ mpaebɔ a ɛto so abiɛsa so kɔbɔɔ mpae kaa asɛm koro no ara.
english: So he left them and went away once more and prayed the third time, saying the same thing.

twi: Ɔsan baa asuafo no nkyɛn bɛka kyerɛɛ wɔn se, “Afei de, monna na monhome. Nanso dɔn no adu. Wɔrebeyi Onipa Ba no ahyɛ nnebɔneyɛfo nsa!
english: Then he returned to the disciples and said to them, “Are you still sleeping and resting? Look, the hour has come, and the Son of Man is delivered into the hands of sinners.

twi: Monsɔre na yɛnkɔ! Monhwɛ! Nea ɔreyi me ama no na ɔreba no!”
english: Rise! Let us go! Here comes my betrayer!”

twi: Wɔkyere YesuOgu so rekasa no, Yuda a ɔyɛ asuafo dumien no mu baako ne dɔm a Yudafo mpanyin asoma wɔn a wokurakura afoa ne nkontimmaa baa hɔ.
english: While he was still speaking, Judas, one of the Twelve, arrived. With him was a large crowd armed with swords and clubs, sent from the chief priests and the elders of the people.

twi: Na Yuda aka akyerɛ wɔn se, “Nea mefew nʼafono no ne onipa no; mokyere no”
english: Now the betrayer had arranged a signal with them: “The one I kiss is the man; arrest him.”

twi: Yuda baa Yesu nkyɛn bɛbam no kae se, “Me wura!” Na ofew nʼafono.
english: Going at once to Jesus, Judas said, “Greetings, Rabbi!” and kissed him.

twi: Yesu ka kyerɛɛ no se, “Damfo, nea wobaa ha se worebɛyɛ no, yɛ no ntɛm.”Ɛhɔ ara, wɔn a wɔne Yuda nam no kyeree Yesu.
english:
Jesus replied, “Do what you came for, friend.”
Then the men stepped forward, seized Jesus and arrested him.

twi: Wɔn a wɔka Yesu ho no mu baako twee nʼafoa de twaa Ɔsɔfopanyin no akoa bi aso.
english: With that, one of Jesus’ companions reached for his sword, drew it out and struck the servant of the high priest, cutting off his ear.

twi: Yesu ka kyerɛɛ no se, “Fa wʼafoa no to nea ɛda. Na wɔn a wɔtwe afoa no, afoa ano na wobewu.
english: “Put your sword back in its place,” Jesus said to him, “for all who draw the sword will die by the sword.

twi: Munnim sɛ metumi aka akyerɛ mʼAgya na wasoma nʼabɔfo mpempem aba ntɛm so, na wɔabɛbɔ yɛn ho ban?
english: Do you think I cannot call on my Father, and he will at once put at my disposal more than twelve legions of angels?

twi: Nanso sɛ meyɛ saa a, ɛbɛyɛ dɛn na nea Kyerɛwsɛm no ka se ɛsɛ sɛ esi wɔ eyi ho no bɛba mu?”
