english: Then they are to place on it all the utensils used for ministering at the altar, including the firepans, meat forks, shovels and sprinkling bowls. Over it they are to spread a covering of the durable leather and put the poles in place.

twi: “Sɛ Aaron ne ne mma mmarima no wie kronkronbea hɔ nneɛma no anoboa a, Kohat ne nʼabusuafo bɛba abɛsoa akɔ baabiara a wɔretu nneɛma akɔ. Nanso wonni ho kwan sɛ wɔde wɔn nsa ka nneɛma a ɛho tew no bi. Wɔyɛ saa a, wobewuwu. Ɛsɛ sɛ Kohat mmabarima no soa nneɛma a ɛwɔ Ahyiae Ntamadan no mu no.
english: “After Aaron and his sons have finished covering the holy furnishings and all the holy articles, and when the camp is ready to move, only then are the Kohathites to come and do the carrying. But they must not touch the holy things or they will die. The Kohathites are to carry those things that are in the tent of meeting.

twi: “Aaron babarima Eleasar a ɔyɛ ɔsɔfo no na ɔbɛhwɛ ngo a wɔde bɛsɔ kanea, nnuhuam, daa aduan a wɔde bɔ afɔre, ɔsra ngo ne Ahyiae Ntamadan no nyinaa so. Biribiara a ɛwɔ Ahyiae Ntamadan no mu no nso, ɔbɛhwɛ so.”
english: “Eleazar son of Aaron, the priest, is to have charge of the oil for the light, the fragrant incense, the regular grain offering and the anointing oil. He is to be in charge of the entire tabernacle and everything in it, including its holy furnishings and articles.”

twi: Afei, Awurade ka kyerɛɛ Mose ne Aaron se,
english: The Lord said to Moses and Aaron,

twi: “Monhwɛ sɛ wɔrentwa Kohatfo abusuakuw no mfi Lewifo mu.
english: “See that the Kohathite tribal clans are not destroyed from among the Levites.

twi: Sɛ wɔresoa nneɛma a ɛho tew no a, nea ɛsɛ sɛ wɔyɛ a wɔrenwuwu ni: Ɛsɛ sɛ Aaron ne ne mma mmarima no ne wɔn kɔ hɔ kɔkyerɛ wɔn ade a ɛsɛ sɛ wɔn mu biara soa.
english: So that they may live and not die when they come near the most holy things, do this for them: Aaron and his sons are to go into the sanctuary and assign to each man his work and what he is to carry.

twi: Ɛnsɛ sɛ Kohatfo no kɔ hɔ kɔhwɛ akronkronne no koraa, na wɔanwuwu.”
english: But the Kohathites must not go in to look at the holy things, even for a moment, or they will die.”

twi: Gerson MmabarimaAwurade ka kyerɛɛ Mose se,
english: The Lord said to Moses,

twi: “Kan Gerson asefo a wɔfra Lewifo abusua mu no,
english: “Take a census also of the Gershonites by their families and clans.

twi: fi mmarima a wɔadi mfe aduasa kosi aduonum a wobetumi ayɛ adwuma kronkron wɔ Ahyiae Ntamadan mu hɔ no so.
english: Count all the men from thirty to fifty years of age who come to serve in the work at the tent of meeting.

twi: “Gerson mmusua no dwuma a wobedi ni:
english: “This is the service of the Gershonite clans in their carrying and their other work:

twi: Wɔbɛsoa ntama a etwa Ahyiae Ntamadan mu hɔ, Ahyiae Ntamadan no ankasa ne nea ɛkata ho, abirekyi nhoma nkuruso ne ntama a ɛsɛn Ahyiae Ntamadan no ano no.
english: They are to carry the curtains of the tabernacle, that is, the tent of meeting, its covering and its outer covering of durable leather, the curtains for the entrance to the tent of meeting,

twi: Afei, wɔbɛsoa nkataho a ɛkata adiwo hɔ fasu no ho no. Wɔbɛsoa ntama a etwa adiwo hɔ kwan no ano ne afɔremuka ne Ahyiae Ntamadan no ntam no. Wɔbɛsoa afɔremuka no, ntampehama ne nea ɛkeka ho nyinaa. Wɔn na ɛsɛ sɛ wɔhwɛ twe eyinom nyinaa.
english: the curtains of the courtyard surrounding the tabernacle and altar, the curtain for the entrance to the courtyard, the ropes and all the equipment used in the service of the tent. The Gershonites are to do all that needs to be done with these things.

twi: Aaron anaa ne mmabarima no bi tumi ma Gerson asefo no bi dwuma di.
english: All their service, whether carrying or doing other work, is to be done under the direction of Aaron and his sons. You shall assign to them as their responsibility all they are to carry.

twi: Eyi ne Gersonfo no adwuma wɔ Ahyiae Ntamadan no mu. Ɛsɛ sɛ wodi Aaron ba Itamar a ɔyɛ ɔsɔfo no nan ase.
english: This is the service of the Gershonite clans at the tent of meeting. Their duties are to be under the direction of Ithamar son of Aaron, the priest.

twi: Merari Mmabarima“Kan Merari asefo a wɔfra Lewifo abusua mu no.
english: “Count the Merarites by their clans and families.

twi: Kan mmarima a wɔadi mfe aduasa kosi aduonum so a wobetumi ayɛ adwuma wɔ Ahyiae Ntamadan mu hɔ.
english: Count all the men from thirty to fifty years of age who come to serve in the work at the tent of meeting.

twi: Sɛ wɔpagyaw Ahyiae Ntamadan no a, wɔn na ɛsɛ sɛ wɔsoa ne nnyinaso, nnua a esisi mu, ne nsisiso,
english: As part of all their service at the tent, they are to carry the frames of the tabernacle, its crossbars, posts and bases,

twi: mpuran a wɔde yɛɛ adiwo hɔ afasu no ne ne nsisiso, nnyinaso, ntampehama ne biribiara a wɔde di ho dwuma. Fa dwumadi ahorow no hyɛ nnipa a wobɛbobɔ wɔn din no nsa.
english: as well as the posts of the surrounding courtyard with their bases, tent pegs, ropes, all their equipment and everything related to their use. Assign to each man the specific things he is to carry.

twi: Merari asefo no, Aaron babarima Itamar na ɔbɛhwɛ wɔn so.”
english: This is the service of the Merarite clans as they work at the tent of meeting under the direction of Ithamar son of Aaron, the priest.”

twi: Enti Mose ne Aaron ne mpanyimfo no bi kɔkan Kohatfo
english: Moses, Aaron and the leaders of the community counted the Kohathites by their clans and families.

twi: a mmarima a wɔadi mfe aduasa kosi aduonum nyinaa a wobetumi ayɛ Ahyiae Ntamadan mu adwuma ka ho,
english: All the men from thirty to fifty years of age who came to serve in the work at the tent of meeting,

twi: na wohuu sɛ wɔn nyinaa dodow yɛ mpem abien ne ahanson aduonum.
english: counted by clans, were 2,750.

twi: Eyinom ne Kohat asefo dodow a na wɔsom wɔ Ahyiae Ntamadan no mu Wɔyɛɛ eyinom nyinaa de dii Awurade ahyɛde a ɔmaa Mose no so.
english: This was the total of all those in the Kohathite clans who served at the tent of meeting. Moses and Aaron counted them according to the Lord’s command through Moses.

twi: Wɔkan Gersonfo no mmusua ne wɔn mmusuakuw.
english: The Gershonites were counted by their clans and families.

twi: Wɔkan mmarima a wɔadi mfe aduasa kosi aduonum a wobetumi ayɛ adwuma wɔ Ahyiae Ntamadan no mu.
english: All the men from thirty to fifty years of age who came to serve in the work at the tent of meeting,

twi: Wɔn nyinaa dodow yɛɛ mpem abien ahansia ne aduasa.
english: counted by their clans and families, were 2,630.

twi: Enti na Gersonfo a wɔfata sɛ wɔsom wɔ Ahyiae Ntamadan no mu no nyinaa dodow ne no. Mose ne Aaron na wɔkan wɔn sɛnea Awurade hyɛɛ wɔn no.
english: This was the total of those in the Gershonite clans who served at the tent of meeting. Moses and Aaron counted them according to the Lord’s command.

twi: Merarifo no nso, wɔkan wɔn mmusua ne wɔn mmusuakuw.
english: The Merarites were counted by their clans and families.

twi: Wɔkan wɔn mmarima a wɔadi mfe aduasa kosi aduonum a wɔfata sɛ wɔyɛ adwuma wɔ Ahyiae Ntamadan no mu.
english: All the men from thirty to fifty years of age who came to serve in the work at the tent of meeting,

twi: Wɔn nyinaa dodow yɛɛ mpem abiɛsa ne ahannu.
english: counted by their clans, were 3,200.

twi: Enti Merarifo a wɔfata sɛ wɔsom wɔ Ahyiae Ntamadan no mu no nyinaa dodow ne no. Mose ne Aaron na wɔkan wɔn sɛnea Awurade hyɛɛ Mose no.
english: This was the total of those in the Merarite clans. Moses and Aaron counted them according to the Lord’s command through Moses.

twi: Enti Mose ne Aaron ne Israel mpanyimfo nam Lewifo no mmusua ne wɔn afi so kan wɔn nyinaa.
english: So Moses, Aaron and the leaders of Israel counted all the Levites by their clans and families.

twi: Mmarima a na wɔadi fi mfe aduasa kosi mfe aduonum no nyinaa a na wɔfata sɛ wɔyɛ adwuma wɔ Ahyiae Ntamadan no mu hɔ no ne wɔn a wɔbɛsoa akɔ no
english: All the men from thirty to fifty years of age who came to do the work of serving and carrying the tent of meeting

twi: dodow yɛ mpem ahanwɔtwe ahannum ne aduɔwɔtwe.
english: numbered 8,580.

twi: Awurade hyɛ a ɔhyɛɛ Mose no nti na wɔnam so kan nnipa no.
english:
At the Lord’s command through Moses, each was assigned his work and told what to carry.
Thus they were counted, as the Lord commanded Moses.

twi: Israelfo Atenae Hɔ KronkronyɛEyi ne mmara a Awurade san hyɛ maa Mose:
english: The Lord said to Moses,

twi: “Ka kyerɛ Israelfo no se, ɛsɛ sɛ wɔpam akwatafo nyinaa fi atenae hɔ. Wɔn a kuru atutu wɔn ne wɔn a wɔde wɔn nsa akɔka funu nti wɔn ho agu fi nyinaa no, ɛsɛ sɛ wɔpam wɔn.
english: “Command the Israelites to send away from the camp anyone who has a defiling skin disease or a discharge of any kind, or who is ceremonially unclean because of a dead body.

twi: Mmarima ne mmea nyinaa ka ho. Yi wɔn nyinaa fi hɔ, sɛnea ɛbɛyɛ na atenae a me ne mo bɛtena no ho rengu fi.”
english: Send away male and female alike; send them outside the camp so they will not defile their camp, where I dwell among them.”

twi: Wodii Awurade mmara no so.
english: The Israelites did so; they sent them outside the camp. They did just as the Lord had instructed Moses.

twi: Afei, Awurade ka kyerɛɛ Mose se,
english: The Lord said to Moses,

twi: “Ka kyerɛ Israelfo no se, sɛ ɔbarima o, ɔbea o, odi Awurade huammɔ a, ɛyɛ bɔne.
english: “Say to the Israelites: ‘Any man or woman who wrongs another in any way and so is unfaithful to the Lord is guilty

twi: Ɛsɛ sɛ ɔka ne bɔne na ade a owiae no, otua ho ka nyinaa na ɔsan de ɛho ka no nkyɛmu ɔha mu aduonu ka ho de ma onipa ko a ɔbɔɔ no korɔn no.
english: and must confess the sin they have committed. They must make full restitution for the wrong they have done, add a fifth of the value to it and give it all to the person they have wronged.

twi: Na sɛ onipa ko a wɔyɛɛ no bɔne no awu na onni obusuani biara a ɔbɛn no a wobetua ho ka ama no, na ɛsɛ sɛ wotua ma ɔsɔfo a, ɛsɛ sɛ wɔde odwennini ka ho sɛ mpatade. Ɛyɛ Awurade de.
english: But if that person has no close relative to whom restitution can be made for the wrong, the restitution belongs to the Lord and must be given to the priest, along with the ram with which atonement is made for the wrongdoer.

twi: Akyɛde kronkron a Israelfo de bɛkyɛ ɔsɔfo no yɛ ne de.
english: All the sacred contributions the Israelites bring to a priest will belong to him.

twi: Ɔsɔfo biara bɛfa akyɛde kronkron biara a ne nsa bɛka.”
english: Sacred things belong to their owners, but what they give to the priest will belong to the priest.’”

twi: Awurade ka kyerɛɛ Mose se,
english: Then the Lord said to Moses,

twi: “Ka kyerɛ Israelfo no se, sɛ ɔbarima bi yere kɔbɔ aguaman
english: “Speak to the Israelites and say to them: ‘If a man’s wife goes astray and is unfaithful to him

twi: nanso onhu asɛm no mu nokware na onya ɔdanseni
english: so that another man has sexual relations with her, and this is hidden from her husband and her impurity is undetected (since there is no witness against her and she has not been caught in the act),

twi: na ɔtwe ho ninkunu na ɔnte ne ho ase a,
english: and if feelings of jealousy come over her husband and he suspects his wife and she is impure—or if he is jealous and suspects her even though she is not impure—

twi: ɔbarima no de ne yere no bɛkɔ ɔsɔfo anim a ɔbea no ho afɔrebɔde a ɛyɛ atokosiam a wɔmfaa ohuam ngo mfrae lita abien ka ho. Efisɛ ɛyɛ ninkutwe afɔrebɔ. Ɛno na ɛbɛma nokware ada adi ama wɔahu sɛ ɔbea no di fɔ anaa odi bem.
english: then he is to take his wife to the priest. He must also take an offering of a tenth of an ephah of barley flour on her behalf. He must not pour olive oil on it or put incense on it, because it is a grain offering for jealousy, a reminder-offering to draw attention to wrongdoing.

twi: “Ɔsɔfo no de ɔbea no bɛba Awurade anim,
english: “‘The priest shall bring her and have her stand before the Lord.

twi: na wasaw Ahyiae Ntamadan no mu mfutuma de afra nsu kronkron a egu asuhina kɛse bi mu no.
english: Then he shall take some holy water in a clay jar and put some dust from the tabernacle floor into the water.

twi: Ɔbɛsan ne ti a wakyekyere no na ɔde ninkunu afɔrebɔde no agu ne nsam de ahwɛ sɛ ɔbarima no nsusuwii no yɛ nokware ampa ara anaasɛ ɛnyɛ nokware. Ɔsɔfo no begyina nʼanim a okura nsu nwenweenwen a ɛde mmusu ba no.
english: After the priest has had the woman stand before the Lord, he shall loosen her hair and place in her hands the reminder-offering, the grain offering for jealousy, while he himself holds the bitter water that brings a curse.

twi: -Ɔbɛma no aka ntam sɛ onnim asɛm no ho hwee na waka akyerɛ no se, sɛ wo ne ɔbarima biara nnae ka wo kunu nko ara ho de a, ɛno de, wo ho ntew mfi nsu nwenweenwen a ɛde mmusu ba yi ho. Na sɛ woabɔ aguaman a, ɛno de, Awurade bɛdome wo wɔ wo nkurɔfo mu. Ɔbɛma wo srɛ aporɔw na wo yafunu ahon. Na ɔbea no bɛka se, ‘Yiw, saa na ɛsɛ sɛ ɛba.’
english: Then the priest shall put the woman under oath and say to her, “If no other man has had sexual relations with you and you have not gone astray and become impure while married to your husband, may this bitter water that brings a curse not harm you.

twi: “Ɔsɔfo no bɛkyerɛw nnome yi nyinaa agu nhoma bi mu na wahohoro agu nsu nwenweenwen no mu.
english: “‘The priest is to write these curses on a scroll and then wash them off into the bitter water.

twi: Sɛ ɛsɛ sɛ ɔbea no nom nsu no na sɛ ɔnom wɔ bere a wayɛ bɔne a, ɛyɛ nwenweenwen wɔ ne mu.
english: He shall make the woman drink the bitter water that brings a curse, and this water that brings a curse and causes bitter suffering will enter her.

twi: Afei, ɔsɔfo no begye ninkunu afɔrebɔde no afi ɔbea no nsam na wahinhim wɔ Awurade anim na ɔde akɔ afɔremuka no so.
english: The priest is to take from her hands the grain offering for jealousy, wave it before the Lord and bring it to the altar.

twi: Ɔbɛsaw ne nsa ma de asi ne nyinaa anan na wahyew no wɔ afɔremuka no so na wama ɔbea no anom nsu no.
english: The priest is then to take a handful of the grain offering as a memorial offering and burn it on the altar; after that, he is to have the woman drink the water.

twi: Sɛ ne ho agu fi na wabɔ aguaman atia ne kunu a, nsu a wanom no bɛyɛ nwenweenwen wɔ ne mu na ne yafunu ahon na ne srɛ aporɔw na wayɛ nnome wɔ ne nkurɔfo mu.
english: If she has made herself impure and been unfaithful to her husband, this will be the result: When she is made to drink the water that brings a curse and causes bitter suffering, it will enter her, her abdomen will swell and her womb will miscarry, and she will become a curse.

twi: Sɛ ɔyɛ kronkron a ɔmmɔɔ aguaman a, wɔrenhaw no, na ɛrenkyɛ, obenyinsɛn.
english: If, however, the woman has not made herself impure, but is clean, she will be cleared of guilt and will be able to have children.

twi: “Eyi ne mmara a ɛfa ɔbea a ne bra nye na ne kunu twe ne ho ninkunu
english: “‘This, then, is the law of jealousy when a woman goes astray and makes herself impure while married to her husband,

twi: de hwehwɛ mu hu sɛ odi ne kunu nokware anaa onni no nokware no ho. Ɔde no bɛba Awurade anim na ɔsɔfo no adi dwuma a wɔabobɔ so no nyinaa.
english: or when feelings of jealousy come over a man because he suspects his wife. The priest is to have her stand before the Lord and is to apply this entire law to her.

twi: Wɔrenni ne kunu no asɛm wɔ baabiara sɛ wama ɔyare bɔne bi aba ne yere so, efisɛ ɛyɛ ɔno ara na ɔma ɛbaa saa.”
english: The husband will be innocent of any wrongdoing, but the woman will bear the consequences of her sin.’”

twi: Ahotuafo MmaraAwurade san ka kyerɛɛ Mose se,
english: The Lord said to Moses,

twi: “Ka kyerɛ Israelfo no se, sɛ ɔbarima anaa ɔbea kɔyɛ Nasareni de tew ne ho wɔ Awurade anim a,
english: “Speak to the Israelites and say to them: ‘If a man or woman wants to make a special vow, a vow of dedication to the Lord as a Nazirite,

twi: ɛno akyi, saa bere a ɔwɔ ahotew no mu no, onni ho kwan sɛ ɔnom nsa a ɛyɛ den anaa bobesa anaa nsa a emu kaw.
english: they must abstain from wine and other fermented drink and must not drink vinegar made from wine or other fermented drink. They must not drink grape juice or eat grapes or raisins.

twi: Saa bere no mu no, onni ho kwan sɛ odi biribiara a efi bobe mu, sɛ ɛyɛ nʼaba anaa ne hono.
english: As long as they remain under their Nazirite vow, they must not eat anything that comes from the grapevine, not even the seeds or skins.

twi: “Saa bere no mu no, ɛnsɛ sɛ oyi ne tinwi, efisɛ ɔyɛ kronkron na wɔatew ne ho ama Awurade; ɛno nti na ɛsɛ sɛ ɔma ne tinwi fuw no.
english: “‘During the entire period of their Nazirite vow, no razor may be used on their head. They must be holy until the period of their dedication to the Lord is over; they must let their hair grow long.

twi: “Ne bɔhyɛ no nna no mu a watew ne ho ama Awurade no, onni ho kwan sɛ ɔkɔ owufo ho.
english: “‘Throughout the period of their dedication to the Lord, the Nazirite must not go near a dead body.

twi: Sɛ owufo no yɛ nʼagya, ne na, ne nuabarima anaa ne nuabea koraa a, ɔnnkɔ ne ho, efisɛ ɔda so hyɛ ne bɔ a ɔhyɛ de tew ne ho maa Onyankopɔn no ase.
english: Even if their own father or mother or brother or sister dies, they must not make themselves ceremonially unclean on account of them, because the symbol of their dedication to God is on their head.

twi: Saa bere no mu nyinaa, wɔatew ne ho ama Awurade.
english: Throughout the period of their dedication, they are consecrated to the Lord.

twi: “Sɛ obi wu tɔ ne nkyɛn de gu ne ho fi a, nnanson akyi no, ɛsɛ sɛ oyi ne tinwi a ɛho agu fi no. Afei, wobedwira ne ho afi fi a owufo no de aka no no ho.
english: “‘If someone dies suddenly in the Nazirite’s presence, thus defiling the hair that symbolizes their dedication, they must shave their head on the seventh day—the day of their cleansing.

twi: Nʼadekyee a ɛyɛ da a ɛto so awotwe no, ɛsɛ sɛ ɔde nturukuku abien anaa mmorɔnoma mma abien brɛ ɔsɔfo wɔ Ahyiae Ntamadan no kwan ano.
english: Then on the eighth day they must bring two doves or two young pigeons to the priest at the entrance to the tent of meeting.

twi: Ɔsɔfo no de nnomaa no mu baako bɛbɔ bɔne ho afɔre na ɔde ɔbaako abɔ ɔhyew afɔre, na ayɛ mpata ama nea ne ho agu fi no. Na da no ara, ɛsɛ sɛ oti ne bɔhyɛ mu na ɔsan ma ne tinwi no fuw bio.
english: The priest is to offer one as a sin offering and the other as a burnt offering to make atonement for the Nazirite because they sinned by being in the presence of the dead body. That same day they are to consecrate their head again.

twi: Nna dodow a odii wɔ ne bɔhyɛ a edi kan no mu no nyinaa ahyew agu. Ɔbɛhyɛ Awurade bɔ foforo de afi ase, na ɔde odwennini ba a wadi afe bɛba abɛbɔ afɔdi ho afɔre.
english: They must rededicate themselves to the Lord for the same period of dedication and must bring a year-old male lamb as a guilt offering. The previous days do not count, because they became defiled during their period of dedication.

twi: “Da a ne bɔhyɛ a ɛtew ɔno ne Awurade ntam no wie du no, ɛsɛ sɛ ɔkɔ Ahyiae Ntamadan no ano.
english: “‘Now this is the law of the Nazirite when the period of their dedication is over. They are to be brought to the entrance to the tent of meeting.

twi: Ɛhɔ na ɔbɛbɔ ɔhyew afɔre ama Awurade. Ɔde oguan ba a wadi afe a onnii dɛm na ɛbɛbɔ saa afɔre no. Ɛsɛ sɛ ɔde oguammere a wadi afe a onnii dɛm bɔ bɔne ho afɔre na ɔde odwennini a onnii dɛm bɔ asomdwoe afɔre.
english: There they are to present their offerings to the Lord: a year-old male lamb without defect for a burnt offering, a year-old ewe lamb without defect for a sin offering, a ram without defect for a fellowship offering,

twi: Nneɛma a ɔde bɛka ho no ne brodo a mmɔkaw mfra mu, asikresiam tetare a wɔde ngo afra; brodo ntrantraa bi a mmɔkaw mfra mu a wɔde ngo ayɛ so a aduan ne nsa afɔrebɔde ka ho.
english: together with their grain offerings and drink offerings, and a basket of bread made with the finest flour and without yeast—thick loaves with olive oil mixed in, and thin loaves brushed with olive oil.

twi: “Ɛsɛ sɛ Ɔsɔfo no de saa afɔrebɔde yi nyinaa ba Awurade anim na wabɛbɔ bɔne ho afɔre ne ɔhyew afɔre.
english: “‘The priest is to present all these before the Lord and make the sin offering and the burnt offering.

twi: Ɛsɛ sɛ ɔde odwennini a wɔde no bɛbɔ asomdwoe afɔre a brodo kɛntɛnma a mmɔkaw nni mu nso ka ho na ɔde abɛbɔ aduan ne nsa afɔre.
english: He is to present the basket of unleavened bread and is to sacrifice the ram as a fellowship offering to the Lord, together with its grain offering and drink offering.

twi: “Afei, ɔhotuafo no beyi ne tinwi a afuw kuhaa no; ɛno ne nsɛnkyerɛnne a ɛkyerɛ sɛ ɔnhyɛ bɔhyɛ no ase bio. Wɔbɛyɛ eyi wɔ Ahyiae Ntamadan no ano, na wɔde nwi no agu asomdwoe afɔre a wɔrebɔ no wɔ gya mu no ahyew no.
english: “‘Then at the entrance to the tent of meeting, the Nazirite must shave off the hair that symbolizes their dedication. They are to take the hair and put it in the fire that is under the sacrifice of the fellowship offering.

twi: “Wɔayi ɔbarima no tinwi no awie no, ɔsɔfo no de odwennini no basa a wɔatoto tetare a mmɔkaw nni mu no baako ne brodo ntrantraa a mmɔkaw nni mu bɛhyɛ ɔbarima no nsam.
english: “‘After the Nazirite has shaved off the hair that symbolizes their dedication, the priest is to place in their hands a boiled shoulder of the ram, and one thick loaf and one thin loaf from the basket, both made without yeast.

twi: Ɔsɔfo no behim akɔ nʼanim aba nʼakyi wɔ Awurade anim a ɛkyerɛ ma a ɔde rema Awurade. Ne nyinaa yɛ kyɛfa a ɛho tew ma ɔsɔfo no. Wɔbɛyɛ no sɛnea wɔyɛ odwennini no basa mu mfe mparow a wohim no wɔ Awurade anim no. Eyi akyi no, ɔhotuafo no tumi nom bobesa a ɛkyerɛ sɛ wɔayi no afi ne bɔhyɛ no mu.
english: The priest shall then wave these before the Lord as a wave offering; they are holy and belong to the priest, together with the breast that was waved and the thigh that was presented. After that, the Nazirite may drink wine.

twi: “Eyinom ne mmara a ɛda hɔ ma Nasareni a wahyɛ nʼahofama ho bɔ awie, na ɔde afɔrebɔ ahorow brɛ Awurade. Saa afɔrebɔ yi akyi no, otumi de afɔrebɔde biara a ɔrebɛyɛ Nasareni no, ɔhyɛɛ ho bɔ sɛ ɔde bɛba no ba.”
english: “‘This is the law of the Nazirite who vows offerings to the Lord in accordance with their dedication, in addition to whatever else they can afford. They must fulfill the vows they have made, according to the law of the Nazirite.’”

twi: Afei, Awurade ka kyerɛɛ Mose se,
english: The Lord said to Moses,

twi: “Ka kyerɛ Aaron ne ne mmabarima no se, ɛsɛ sɛ wohyira Israelfo yi sononko sɛ:
english: “Tell Aaron and his sons, ‘This is how you are to bless the Israelites. Say to them:

twi: “ ‘Awurade nhyira mona ɔnhwɛ mo so.
english:
“‘“The Lord bless you
    and keep you;

twi: Awurade ntew nʼanim nkyerɛ mona ɔnnom mo.
english:
the Lord make his face shine on you
    and be gracious to you;

twi: Awurade mma nʼani so nhwɛ mona ɔmma mo asomdwoe.’
english:
the Lord turn his face toward you
    and give you peace.”’

twi: “Saa na ɛsɛ sɛ Aaron ne ne mmabarima hyira Israelfo, na mʼankasa nso mehyira wɔn.”
english: “So they will put my name on the Israelites, and I will bless them.”

twi: Da a Mose wiee Ahyiae Ntamadan no hyehyɛ no, ɔsraa ho nyinaa ngo, tew mu nneɛma nyinaa ho. Ɔsan sraa afɔremuka ne ho nkuku ne nkaka nyinaa ngo, tew ho nso.
english: When Moses finished setting up the tabernacle, he anointed and consecrated it and all its furnishings. He also anointed and consecrated the altar and all its utensils.

twi: Afei, Israel mpanyimfo ne mmusuakuw no mu mpanyin a wɔhwɛɛ nnipakan no so no nyinaa de wɔn afɔrebɔde bae.
english: Then the leaders of Israel, the heads of families who were the tribal leaders in charge of those who were counted, made offerings.

twi: Wɔde nteaseɛnam asia a wɔakatakata ho ne anantwi dumien na ɛbae. Na nteaseɛnam no baako biara yɛ mpanyimfo baanu de, a nantwi baako yɛ wɔn mu biara de. Wɔde ne nyinaa maa Awurade wɔ Ahyiae Ntamadan no anim.
english: They brought as their gifts before the Lord six covered carts and twelve oxen—an ox from each leader and a cart from every two. These they presented before the tabernacle.

twi: Awurade ka kyerɛɛ Mose se,
english: The Lord said to Moses,

twi: “Gye wɔn akyɛde no na fa nteaseɛnam no yɛ Ahyiae Ntamadan no ho adwuma. Fa ma Lewifo no na obiara mfa nni dwuma biara a ɛsɛ sɛ odi.”
english: “Accept these from them, that they may be used in the work at the tent of meeting. Give them to the Levites as each man’s work requires.”

twi: Enti Mose de nteaseɛnam no ne anantwi no maa Lewifo no.
english: So Moses took the carts and oxen and gave them to the Levites.

twi: Ɔmaa Gerson ne ne nkurɔfo nteaseɛnam abien ne anantwi anan sɛnea na ehia ma wɔn dwumadi,
english: He gave two carts and four oxen to the Gershonites, as their work required,

twi: na ɔmaa Merari ne ne nkurɔfo nso nteaseɛnam anan ne anantwi awotwe a Aaron babarima Itamar na na odi so panyin.
english: and he gave four carts and eight oxen to the Merarites, as their work required. They were all under the direction of Ithamar son of Aaron, the priest.

twi: Wɔamma Kohat nkurɔfo nteaseɛnam no bi, efisɛ na ɛsɛ sɛ wɔsoa wɔn kyɛfa a ɛfa Ahyiae Ntamadan no ho nneɛma no ho no wɔ wɔn mmati so.
english: But Moses did not give any to the Kohathites, because they were to carry on their shoulders the holy things, for which they were responsible.

twi: Mpanyimfo a wodi anim no nso de nsrabɔ akyɛde beguu afɔremuka no anim da a wɔresra afɔremuka no ngo no.
english: When the altar was anointed, the leaders brought their offerings for its dedication and presented them before the altar.

twi: Awurade ka kyerɛɛ Mose se, “Kyekyɛ nna a obiara de nʼafɔrebɔde bɛba afɔremuka no so.”
english: For the Lord had said to Moses, “Each day one leader is to bring his offering for the dedication of the altar.”

twi: Aminadab babarima Nahson a ofi Yuda abusuakuw mu na ɔde nʼafɔrebɔde baa da a edi kan no.
english: The one who brought his offering on the first day was Nahshon son of Amminadab of the tribe of Judah.

twi: Nneɛma a ɔde bae no yɛ:dwetɛ prɛte baako a emu duru yɛ kilogram baako ne fa, dwetɛ kuruwa kɛse bi a ɛbɛyɛ kilogram baako a ne nyinaa na wɔde asikresiam muhumuhu a wɔde ngo afra ahyɛ no amaama;
english: His offering was one silver plate weighing a hundred and thirty shekels and one silver sprinkling bowl weighing seventy shekels, both according to the sanctuary shekel, each filled with the finest flour mixed with olive oil as a grain offering;

twi: sikakɔkɔɔ adaka baako a ɛkari gram ɔha ne dunan () a wɔde aduhuam ahyɛ no ma;
english: one gold dish weighing ten shekels, filled with incense;

twi: ɔde nantwinini ba, odwennini ne oguamma a wadi afe bae sɛ ɔhyew afɔrebɔde.
english: one young bull, one ram and one male lamb a year old for a burnt offering;

twi: Wɔde ɔpapo bae sɛ bɔne ho afɔrebɔde
english: one male goat for a sin offering;

twi: ne anantwi abien, adwennini anum, mmirekyi anum ne nguantenmma a wɔn mu biara adi afe, anum bae sɛ wɔn asomdwoe afɔrebɔde.Eyi ne Nahson, Aminadab ba afɔrebɔde.
english: and two oxen, five rams, five male goats and five male lambs a year old to be sacrificed as a fellowship offering. This was the offering of Nahshon son of Amminadab.

twi: Da a ɛto so abien no, Suar babarima Netanel a ɔda Isakar abusuakuw ano no de nʼafɔrebɔde bae.
english: On the second day Nethanel son of Zuar, the leader of Issachar, brought his offering.

twi: Na nʼafɔrebɔde no yɛ:dwetɛ prɛte a ɛyɛ kilogram baako ne fa ne dwetɛ hweaseammɔ a emu duru yɛ kilogram baako a wɔde atoko afɔrebɔde a ɛyɛ asikresiam muhumuhu a wɔde ngo afra ahyehyɛ no amaama.
english: The offering he brought was one silver plate weighing a hundred and thirty shekels and one silver sprinkling bowl weighing seventy shekels, both according to the sanctuary shekel, each filled with the finest flour mixed with olive oil as a grain offering;

twi: Sikakɔkɔɔ nnwetɛbona baako a ɛkari gram ɔha ne dunan () a wɔde aduhuam ahyɛ no ma;
english: one gold dish weighing ten shekels, filled with incense;

twi: nantwi ba, odwennini ne oguamma a wɔadi afe bae sɛ ɔhyew afɔre,
english: one young bull, one ram and one male lamb a year old for a burnt offering;

twi: ɔpapo sɛ bɔne ho afɔre
english: one male goat for a sin offering;

twi: ne anantwi abien, adwennini anum, mpapo anum ne nguantenmma anum a wɔn mu biara adi afe sɛ asomdwoe afɔre.Eyi ne afɔre a Suar babarima Netanel de bae.
english: and two oxen, five rams, five male goats and five male lambs a year old to be sacrificed as a fellowship offering. This was the offering of Nethanel son of Zuar.

twi: Ne nnansa so no, Helon babarima Eliab a ɔda Sebulon abusuakuw ano no de nʼafɔrebɔde bae.
english: On the third day, Eliab son of Helon, the leader of the people of Zebulun, brought his offering.

twi: Na nʼafɔrebɔde no yɛ:dwetɛ prɛte a ɛyɛ kilogram baako ne fa ne dwetɛ hweaseammɔ a emu duru yɛ kilogram baako. Na wɔde atoko afɔrebɔde a ɛyɛ asikresiam a wɔayam no muhumuhu a wɔde ngo afra ahyɛ no amaama;
english: His offering was one silver plate weighing a hundred and thirty shekels and one silver sprinkling bowl weighing seventy shekels, both according to the sanctuary shekel, each filled with the finest flour mixed with olive oil as a grain offering;

twi: sikakɔkɔɔ akorade a emu duru yɛ gram ɔha ne dunan () a wɔde aduhuam ahyɛ no ma;
english: one gold dish weighing ten shekels, filled with incense;

english: one young bull, one ram and one male lamb a year old for a burnt offering;

english: one male goat for a sin offering;

english: and two oxen, five rams, five male goats and five male lambs a year old to be sacrificed as a fellowship offering. This was the offering of Eliab son of Helon.

twi: Ne nnaanan so no, Sedeur babarima Elisur a ɔda Ruben abusuakuw ano no de nʼafɔrebɔde bae.
english: On the fourth day Elizur son of Shedeur, the leader of the people of Reuben, brought his offering.

english: and two oxen, five rams, five male goats and five male lambs a year old to be sacrificed as a fellowship offering. This was the offering of Elizur son of Shedeur.

twi: Ne nnaanum so no, Surisadai babarima Selumiel a ɔda Simeon abusuakuw ano no de nʼafɔrebɔde bae.
english: On the fifth day Shelumiel son of Zurishaddai, the leader of the people of Simeon, brought his offering.

english: and two oxen, five rams, five male goats and five male lambs a year old to be sacrificed as a fellowship offering. This was the offering of Shelumiel son of Zurishaddai.

twi: Ne nnansia so no, Deguel babarima Eliasaf a ɔda Gad abusuakuw ano no de nʼafɔrebɔde bae.
english: On the sixth day Eliasaph son of Deuel, the leader of the people of Gad, brought his offering.

english: and two oxen, five rams, five male goats and five male lambs a year old to be sacrificed as a fellowship offering. This was the offering of Eliasaph son of Deuel.

twi: Ne nnanson so no, Amihud babarima Elisama a ɔda Efraim abusuakuw ano no de nʼafɔrebɔde bae.
english: On the seventh day Elishama son of Ammihud, the leader of the people of Ephraim, brought his offering.

english: and two oxen, five rams, five male goats and five male lambs a year old to be sacrificed as a fellowship offering. This was the offering of Elishama son of Ammihud.

twi: Ne nnaawɔtwe so no, Pedahsur babarima Gamaliel a ɔda Manase abusuakuw ano no de nʼafɔrebɔde bae.
english: On the eighth day Gamaliel son of Pedahzur, the leader of the people of Manasseh, brought his offering.

english: His offering was one silver plate weighing a hundred and thirty shekels and one silver sprinkling bowl weighing seventy shekels, both according to the sanctuary shekel, each filled with the finest flour mixed with olive oil as a grain offering;

twi: sikakɔkɔɔ akorade bi a ɛkari nnwetɛbona du a wɔde aduhuam ahyɛ no ma;
english: one gold dish weighing ten shekels, filled with incense;

english: and two oxen, five rams, five male goats and five male lambs a year old to be sacrificed as a fellowship offering. This was the offering of Gamaliel son of Pedahzur.

twi: Ne nnankron so no, Gideoni babarima Abidan a ɔda Benyamin abusuakuw ano no de nʼafɔrebɔde bae.
english: On the ninth day Abidan son of Gideoni, the leader of the people of Benjamin, brought his offering.

english: and two oxen, five rams, five male goats and five male lambs a year old to be sacrificed as a fellowship offering. This was the offering of Abidan son of Gideoni.

twi: Ne nnadu so no, Amisadai babarima Ahieser a ɔda Dan abusuakuw ano no de nʼafɔrebɔde bae.
english: On the tenth day Ahiezer son of Ammishaddai, the leader of the people of Dan, brought his offering.

english: His offering was one silver plate weighing a hundred and thirty shekels and one silver sprinkling bowl weighing seventy shekels, both according to the sanctuary shekel, each filled with the finest flour mixed with olive oil as a grain offering;

english: and two oxen, five rams, five male goats and five male lambs a year old to be sacrificed as a fellowship offering. This was the offering of Ahiezer son of Ammishaddai.

twi: Ne nna dubaako so no, Okran babarima Pagiel a ɔda Aser abusuakuw ano no de nʼafɔrebɔde bae.
english: On the eleventh day Pagiel son of Okran, the leader of the people of Asher, brought his offering.

twi: Na nʼafɔrebɔde no yɛ:dwetɛ prɛte a ɛyɛ kilogram baako ne fa ne dwetɛ hweaseammɔ a emu duru yɛ kilogram baako. Na wɔde atoko afɔrebɔde a ɛyɛ asikresiam a wɔayam no muhumuhu a wɔde ngo afra ahyehyɛ no amaama;
english: His offering was one silver plate weighing a hundred and thirty shekels and one silver sprinkling bowl weighing seventy shekels, both according to the sanctuary shekel, each filled with the finest flour mixed with olive oil as a grain offering;

twi: sikakɔkɔɔ akorade a ɛkari gram ɔha ne dunan () a wɔde aduhuam ahyɛ no ma;

english: one young bull, one ram and one male lamb a year old for a burnt offering;

english: and two oxen, five rams, five male goats and five male lambs a year old to be sacrificed as a fellowship offering. This was the offering of Pagiel son of Okran.

twi: Ne nnadumien so no, Enan babarima Ahira a ɔda Naftali abusuakuw ano no de nʼafɔrebɔde bae.
english: On the twelfth day Ahira son of Enan, the leader of the people of Naphtali, brought his offering.

twi: Na nʼafɔrebɔde no yɛ:dwetɛ prɛte a ɛyɛ kilogram baako ne fa ne dwetɛ hweaseammɔ a emu duru yɛ kilogram baako. Na wɔde atoko afɔrebɔde a ɛyɛ asikresiam a wɔayam no muhumuhu a wɔde ngo afra ahyehyɛ no amaama;
english: His offering was one silver plate weighing a hundred and thirty shekels and one silver sprinkling bowl weighing seventy shekels, both according to the sanctuary shekel, each filled with the finest flour mixed with olive oil as a grain offering;

twi: sikakɔkɔɔ akorade a ɛkari gram ɔha ne dunan () a wɔde aduhuam ahyɛ no ma;
english: one gold dish weighing ten shekels, filled with incense;

twi: nantwi ba, odwennini ne oguamma onini a wadi afe bae sɛ ɔhyew afɔre;
english: one young bull, one ram and one male lamb a year old for a burnt offering;

english: one male goat for a sin offering;

twi: ne anantwi abien, adwennini anum, mpapo anum ne nguantenmma anum a wɔn mu biara adi afe sɛ asomdwoe afɔre.Eyi ne afɔre a Enan babarima Ahira de bae.
english: and two oxen, five rams, five male goats and five male lambs a year old to be sacrificed as a fellowship offering. This was the offering of Ahira son of Enan.

twi: Eyinom ne afɔremuka no afɔrebɔde a Israel mpanyimfo de ba bɛsraa afɔremuka no, nam so bɔɔ no atenase:dwetɛ mprɛte dumien, dwetɛ hweaseammɔ dumien ne sikakɔkɔɔ aduhuam nnwetɛbona dumien.
english: These were the offerings of the Israelite leaders for the dedication of the altar when it was anointed: twelve silver plates, twelve silver sprinkling bowls and twelve gold dishes.

twi: Ne nyinaa mu, na dwetɛ nneɛma no kari bɛyɛ kilogram aduasa, na prɛte biara kari bɛyɛ kilogram baako ne fa, na hweaseammɔ no nso mu duru yɛ kilogram baako.
english: Each silver plate weighed a hundred and thirty shekels, and each sprinkling bowl seventy shekels. Altogether, the silver dishes weighed two thousand four hundred shekels, according to the sanctuary shekel.

twi: Sikakɔkɔɔ a wɔde bɛkyɛe no mu duru yɛɛ bɛyɛ kilogram baako ne fa a ɛkyerɛ sɛ, sikakɔkɔɔ no akorade no mu biara duru yɛ nnwetɛbona du a wɔde aduhuam ahyɛ no ma.
english: The twelve gold dishes filled with incense weighed ten shekels each, according to the sanctuary shekel. Altogether, the gold dishes weighed a hundred and twenty shekels.

twi: Wɔde anantwi dumien ne adwennini a wɔn mu biara adi afe na ɛbɛbɔɔ ɔhyew afɔre no a atoko afɔrebɔ nso ka ho. Wɔde mpapo bɛbɔɔ bɔne ho afɔre.
english: The total number of animals for the burnt offering came to twelve young bulls, twelve rams and twelve male lambs a year old, together with their grain offering. Twelve male goats were used for the sin offering.

twi: Asomdwoe afɔre nneɛma a wɔde bae ni: nantwininimma aduonu anan, adwennini aduosia, mmirekyi aduosia, adwennini a wɔn mu biara adi afe aduosia.
english: The total number of animals for the sacrifice of the fellowship offering came to twenty-four oxen, sixty rams, sixty male goats and sixty male lambs a year old. These were the offerings for the dedication of the altar after it was anointed.

twi: Bere a Mose kɔɔ Ahyiae Ntamadan no mu sɛ ɔne Awurade rekɔkasa no, ɔtee nne bi fi soro a ɛrekasa kyerɛ no fi Mpata Beae no atifi hɔ, wɔ adaka no ho baabi a kerubim abien no sisi no ntam. Awurade faa saa kwan yi so kasa kyerɛɛ no.
english: When Moses entered the tent of meeting to speak with the Lord, he heard the voice speaking to him from between the two cherubim above the atonement cover on the ark of the covenant law. In this way the Lord spoke to him.

twi: Awurade ka kyerɛɛ Mose se,
english: The Lord said to Moses,

twi: “Ka kyerɛ Aaron se, ‘Sɛ wosɔ akanea ason a ɛwɔ kaneadua no so no a, sɔ no sɛnea ɛbɛyɛ a, ɛbɛtow ne hann no akɔ kaneadua no nʼanim.’ ”
english: “Speak to Aaron and say to him, ‘When you set up the lamps, see that all seven light up the area in front of the lampstand.’”

twi: Aaron yɛɛ saa; ɔsɔɔ akanea no ma ɛtow hann kɔɔ kaneadua no anim, sɛnea Awurade hyɛɛ Mose no.
english: Aaron did so; he set up the lamps so that they faced forward on the lampstand, just as the Lord commanded Moses.

twi: Sɛnea Wosi yɛɛ kaneadua no ni: Sikakɔkɔɔ a wɔaboro na wɔde yɛ fii nʼase kosi ne soro. Wɔyɛɛ no sɛnea Awurade kyerɛɛ Mose sɛ wɔnyɛ no ara pɛ.
english: This is how the lampstand was made: It was made of hammered gold—from its base to its blossoms. The lampstand was made exactly like the pattern the Lord had shown Moses.

twi: Na Awurade ka kyerɛɛ Mose se,
english: The Lord said to Moses:

twi: “Yi Lewifo no fi Israelfo no mu na tew wɔn ho.
english: “Take the Levites from among all the Israelites and make them ceremonially clean.

twi: Sɛ ɛbɛyɛ a wɔn ho ni yɛ eyi: Fa ahodwira nsu pete wɔn so. Ma wonyi wɔn ho nwi nyinaa, na wɔnhoro wɔn nneɛma nyinaa, na ama wɔn ho atew.
english: To purify them, do this: Sprinkle the water of cleansing on them; then have them shave their whole bodies and wash their clothes. And so they will purify themselves.

twi: Afei, ma wɔmfa nantwinini ba ne aduan afɔrebɔde a ɛyɛ asikresiam a wɔayam no muhumuhu a wɔde ngo afra a nantwinini ba baako ka ho a wɔde no bɛbɔ bɔne ho afɔre mmra.
english: Have them take a young bull with its grain offering of the finest flour mixed with olive oil; then you are to take a second young bull for a sin offering.

twi: Frɛ Israelfo no nyinaa hyia na fa Lewifo no bra Ahyiae Ntamadan no pon ano.
english: Bring the Levites to the front of the tent of meeting and assemble the whole Israelite community.

twi: Ɛhɔ na mpanyimfo a wotuatua mmusuakuw no ano no de wɔn nsa begu wɔn so.
english: You are to bring the Levites before the Lord, and the Israelites are to lay their hands on them.

twi: Ɛsɛ sɛ Aaron yɛ nsɛnkyerɛnne bi sɛ ɔde wɔn rema Awurade sɛ akyɛde a efi Israel manfo nyinaa nkyɛn, na asiesie Lewifo no ama wɔayɛ Awurade adwuma.
english: Aaron is to present the Levites before the Lord as a wave offering from the Israelites, so that they may be ready to do the work of the Lord.

twi: “Afei, Lewifo mpanyimfo no de wɔn nsa begu nantwimma no apampam na wɔde wɔn ama Awurade. Wɔde ɔbaako bɛbɔ bɔne ho afɔre na wɔde ɔbaako nso abɔ ɔhyew afɔre de ayɛ mpata ama Lewifo no.
english: “Then the Levites are to lay their hands on the heads of the bulls, using one for a sin offering to the Lord and the other for a burnt offering, to make atonement for the Levites.

twi: Afei, wɔde Lewifo no bɛma Aaron ne ne mma te sɛnea wɔde afɔrebɔde biara fa asɔfo so de ma Awurade no.”
english: Have the Levites stand in front of Aaron and his sons and then present them as a wave offering to the Lord.

twi: Mobɛfa saa kwan yi so ayi Lewifo no afi Israelfo no mu ama me, na wɔayɛ me dea.
english: In this way you are to set the Levites apart from the other Israelites, and the Levites will be mine.

twi: “Sɛ motew wɔn ho na mofa saa kwan yi so de wɔn ma me a, afei, wobedi ahyɛmfiri wɔ Ahyiae Ntamadan no mu, adi wɔn dwuma.
english: “After you have purified the Levites and presented them as a wave offering, they are to come to do their work at the tent of meeting.

twi: Israelfo mu nyinaa, wɔn na wɔyɛ me nkurɔfo, na magye wɔn ato mu asi Israelfo mmakan nyinaa anan, Israelni bea biara abakan barima.
english: They are the Israelites who are to be given wholly to me. I have taken them as my own in place of the firstborn, the first male offspring from every Israelite woman.

twi: Israel abakan biara yɛ me de; nnipa ne mmoa nyinaa. Bere a mikunkum Misraimfo mmakan nyinaa no ara na mefaa wɔn de wɔn yɛɛ me nkurɔfo.
english: Every firstborn male in Israel, whether human or animal, is mine. When I struck down all the firstborn in Egypt, I set them apart for myself.

twi: Mafa Lewifo no asi Israelfo mmakan nyinaa anan mu.
english: And I have taken the Levites in place of all the firstborn sons in Israel.

twi: Na mede Lewifo no bɛkyɛ Aaron ne ne mmabarima. Lewifo no na wɔbɛyɛ Ahyiae Ntamadan no mu nnwuma kronkron a anka ɛsɛ sɛ Israelfo no na wɔyɛ, na wɔn na wɔbɛbɔ afɔre ama nkurɔfo de ayɛ mpata ama wɔn sɛnea sɛ Israelfo no kɔ kronkronbea hɔ a ɔyaredɔm biara renka wɔn.”
english: From among all the Israelites, I have given the Levites as gifts to Aaron and his sons to do the work at the tent of meeting on behalf of the Israelites and to make atonement for them so that no plague will strike the Israelites when they go near the sanctuary.”

twi: Mose ne Aaron ne Israelfo no nyinaa faa ɔkwan a Awurade kyerɛɛ Mose no so pɛpɛɛpɛ de Lewifo no maa Awurade.
english: Moses, Aaron and the whole Israelite community did with the Levites just as the Lord commanded Moses.

twi: Lewifo no dwiraa wɔn ho, horoo wɔn nneɛma. Na Aaron de wɔn hyɛɛ Awurade nsa sɛ ohim afɔre na ɔyɛɛ wɔn ho mpata adwuma de tew wɔn ho.
english: The Levites purified themselves and washed their clothes. Then Aaron presented them as a wave offering before the Lord and made atonement for them to purify them.

twi: Ɛno akyi no, Lewifo no kɔyɛɛ adwuma wɔ Ahyiae Ntamadan no mu a na Aaron ne ne mmabarima no hwɛ wɔn so Wɔyɛɛ biribiara sɛnea Awurade hyɛɛ Mose sɛ wɔnyɛ no.
english: After that, the Levites came to do their work at the tent of meeting under the supervision of Aaron and his sons. They did with the Levites just as the Lord commanded Moses.

twi: Awurade ka kyerɛɛ Mose se,
english: The Lord said to Moses,

twi: “Eyi kɔ ma Lewifo no: Sɛ Lewini barima biara di mfe aduonu anum a, ma no nsom wɔ Ahyiae Ntamadan mu,
english: “This applies to the Levites: Men twenty-five years old or more shall come to take part in the work at the tent of meeting,

twi: na sɛ wodi mfe aduonum a, ɛsɛ sɛ wɔapɔn fi adwuma mu a wɔnnyɛ adwuma bio.
english: but at the age of fifty, they must retire from their regular service and work no longer.

twi: Sɛ wɔpɔn a, wotumi adi dwuma wɔ Ahyiae Ntamadan mu hɔ de boa wɔn nuanom, mmom wɔn ankasa de, ɛnsɛ sɛ wɔhyɛ da yɛ adwuma. Eyi ne ɔkwan a momfa so mma Lewifo no adwuma nyɛ.”
english: They may assist their brothers in performing their duties at the tent of meeting, but they themselves must not do the work. This, then, is how you are to assign the responsibilities of the Levites.”

twi: Twam AfahyɛƆsram a edi kan no mu afe a ɛto so abien no mu a wɔafi Misraim no na Awurade kaa saa asɛm yi kyerɛɛ Mose bere a ɔne Israelfo wɔ Sinai sare no so no se,
english: The Lord spoke to Moses in the Desert of Sinai in the first month of the second year after they came out of Egypt. He said,

twi: “Ma Israelfo no nni Twam Afahyɛ no wɔ ne bere ano.
english: “Have the Israelites celebrate the Passover at the appointed time.

twi: Munni no wɔ ne bere ano, na mofa ne mmara akwan ahorow no nyinaa so nni wɔ ɔsram yi da a ɛto so dunan no anwummere.”
english: Celebrate it at the appointed time, at twilight on the fourteenth day of this month, in accordance with all its rules and regulations.”

twi: Enti Mose ka kyerɛɛ Israelfo no se wonni Twam Afahyɛ no,
english: So Moses told the Israelites to celebrate the Passover,

twi: na wɔyɛɛ saa wɔ Sinai Nweatam no so wɔ ɔsram a edi kan no da a ɛto so dunan no anwummere. Na Israelfo no yɛɛ biribiara pɛpɛɛpɛ sɛnea Awurade hyɛɛ Mose no.
english: and they did so in the Desert of Sinai at twilight on the fourteenth day of the first month. The Israelites did everything just as the Lord commanded Moses.

twi: Nanso na nnipa no bi fi ayi aba a esiane sɛ wɔde wɔn ho aka owufo nti na wɔn ho agu fi. Eyi nti wɔantumi anni Twam Afahyɛ no bi. Enti wɔbaa Mose ne Aaron nkyɛn da no ara
english: But some of them could not celebrate the Passover on that day because they were ceremonially unclean on account of a dead body. So they came to Moses and Aaron that same day

twi: bɛka kyerɛɛ Mose se, “Yɛde yɛn ho aka funu ama yɛn ho agu fi, nanso dɛn nti na yɛne Israelfo nyinaa rentumi mfa yɛn afɔrebɔde mmrɛ Awurade sɛnea nhyehyɛe no te no?”
english: and said to Moses, “We have become unclean because of a dead body, but why should we be kept from presenting the Lord’s offering with the other Israelites at the appointed time?”

twi: Mose buaa wɔn se, “Montwɛn mma mimmisa sɛnea Awurade mmara no ka fa mo ho.”
english: Moses answered them, “Wait until I find out what the Lord commands concerning you.”

twi: Na Awurade ka kyerɛɛ Mose se,
english: Then the Lord said to Moses,

twi: “Ka kyerɛ Israelfo no se, Obiara a obeso funu mu, sɛ ɔyɛ nnɛmma anaa ofi awo ntoatoaso a ɛreba no mu wɔ Twam Afahyɛ bere a ɛbɛma ne ho agu fi anaa ɔnam akwantu so nti wɔantumi amma no tumi di Awurade Twam Afahyɛ no,
english: “Tell the Israelites: ‘When any of you or your descendants are unclean because of a dead body or are away on a journey, they are still to celebrate the Lord’s Passover,

twi: nanso ɔsram a ɛto so abien no da a ɛto so dunan no anwummere na ɛsɛ sɛ wodi. Saa bere no na ɛsɛ sɛ wɔwe oguamma no a brodo a mmɔkaw nni mu ka ho a naban nweenwen ka ho.
english: but they are to do it on the fourteenth day of the second month at twilight. They are to eat the lamb, together with unleavened bread and bitter herbs.

twi: Ɛnsɛ sɛ wogyaw bi ma ade kye so, anaa wɔbɔ ne dompe mu. Na ɛsɛ sɛ wodi Twam Afahyɛ no mmara no nyinaa so pɛpɛɛpɛ.
english: They must not leave any of it till morning or break any of its bones. When they celebrate the Passover, they must follow all the regulations.

twi: Nanso obiara a ne ho nguu fi anaa obi a ontuu kwan nanso wanni Twam Afahyɛ no wɔ ne bere ano no, ɛsɛ sɛ wotwa no asu afi Israelfo no mu wɔ afɔre a wamma ammɛbɔ amma Awurade bere a ɛsɛ mu no nti. Wɔbɛsoa wɔn afɔdi ho sodi.
english: But if anyone who is ceremonially clean and not on a journey fails to celebrate the Passover, they must be cut off from their people for not presenting the Lord’s offering at the appointed time. They will bear the consequences of their sin.

twi: “Ɛsɛ sɛ ɔhɔho a ɔfra mo mu no fa mmara koro no ara so di Awurade Twam Afahyɛ no. Ɛsɛ sɛ ɔhɔho ne okuroni nyinaa di mmara koro no so.”
english: “‘A foreigner residing among you is also to celebrate the Lord’s Passover in accordance with its rules and regulations. You must have the same regulations for both the foreigner and the native-born.’”

twi: OgyamununkumDa a wɔmaa Ahyiae Ntamadan no so sii hɔ no, omununkum kataa so. Anwummere no ara, omununkum no dan yɛɛ sɛ ogya na ɛyɛɛ saa ara anadwo mu no nyinaa de kosii adekyee.
english: On the day the tabernacle, the tent of the covenant law, was set up, the cloud covered it. From evening till morning the cloud above the tabernacle looked like fire.

twi: Saa ara na ɛte bere biara, na edu anadwo a, mununkum no dan yɛ sɛ ogya.
english: That is how it continued to be; the cloud covered it, and at night it looked like fire.

twi: Omununkum no maa ne ho so no, Israelfo no dii akyi kosii baabiara a ɛkɔ kogyina ma wɔbɔɔ hɔ atenae.
english: Whenever the cloud lifted from above the tent, the Israelites set out; wherever the cloud settled, the Israelites encamped.

twi: Eyi kyerɛ sɛ, sɛ Awurade ka se wɔnkɔ a, wɔkɔ, na sɛ ɔka se wonnyina a, wogyina. Na sɛ Omununkum no gyina a, wɔn nso gyina mmere dodow a egyina hɔ no nyinaa.
english: At the Lord’s command the Israelites set out, and at his command they encamped. As long as the cloud stayed over the tabernacle, they remained in camp.

twi: Sɛ egyina baabi kyɛ a, wɔn nso gyina hɔ kyɛ. Na sɛ egyina hɔ nna kakraa bi a, wɔn nso gyina hɔ nna kakraa bi saa ara, efisɛ saa na Awurade ahyɛ wɔn sɛ wɔnyɛ.
english: When the cloud remained over the tabernacle a long time, the Israelites obeyed the Lord’s order and did not set out.

twi: Ɛtɔ da bi a, omununkum no tena Ahyiae Ntamadan no so nna kakraa bi. Sɛ ɛba saa a, nnipa no nso tena nna kakraa bi. Na Awurade nhyɛ mu, wotu fii wɔn atenae.
english: Sometimes the cloud was over the tabernacle only a few days; at the Lord’s command they would encamp, and then at his command they would set out.

twi: Ɛtɔ da bi nso a, omununkum no tena anadwo na akɔ adekyee. Nanso sɛ ɛyɛ awia anaa anadwo na omununkum no ma ne ho so a, nnipa no tu fi atenae hɔ di akyi.
english: Sometimes the cloud stayed only from evening till morning, and when it lifted in the morning, they set out. Whether by day or by night, whenever the cloud lifted, they set out.

twi: Sɛ omununkum no ba Ahyiae Ntamadan no atifi na edi nnaanu, ɔsram anaa afe a, saa nna no ara so na Israelfo no hwɛ de tena hɔ. Nanso enya tu ara pɛ a, na wɔn nso atu.
english: Whether the cloud stayed over the tabernacle for two days or a month or a year, the Israelites would remain in camp and not set out; but when it lifted, they would set out.

twi: Eyi kyerɛ sɛ, wɔn nsrabɔ ne wɔn akwantu nyinaa gyina Awurade mmara a ɔhyɛ ma wɔn no so; na biribiara a Awurade ka kyerɛɛ Mose sɛ wɔnyɛ no, wɔyɛe.
english: At the Lord’s command they encamped, and at the Lord’s command they set out. They obeyed the Lord’s order, in accordance with his command through Moses.

twi: Dwetɛ Ntorobɛnto NoAfei, Awurade ka kyerɛɛ Mose se,
english: The Lord said to Moses:

twi: “Fa dwetɛ a wɔaboro yɛ ntorobɛnto abien, na ɛyɛ a wɔahyɛn de afrɛ nnipa no, na edu ntamadan no tu so nso a, wɔahyɛn.
english: “Make two trumpets of hammered silver, and use them for calling the community together and for having the camps set out.

twi: Sɛ wɔhyɛn ntorobɛnto abien no a, nnipa no behu sɛ, ɛsɛ sɛ wɔboa wɔn ho ano wɔ Ahyiae Ntamadan no ano.
english: When both are sounded, the whole community is to assemble before you at the entrance to the tent of meeting.

twi: Na sɛ wɔhyɛn baako pɛ a, na ɛkyerɛ sɛ Israel mmusua no mu mpanyimfo na ɛsɛ sɛ wɔba wo nkyɛn.
english: If only one is sounded, the leaders—the heads of the clans of Israel—are to assemble before you.

twi: Sɛ mohyɛn de kyerɛ sɛ monkɔ mo anim a, mmusuakuw a wɔwɔ Ahyiae Ntamadan apuei fam no betu afi wɔn atenae hɔ na wɔakɔ.
english: When a trumpet blast is sounded, the tribes camping on the east are to set out.

twi: Sɛ mohyɛn nea ɛto so abien no a, mmusuakuw a wɔwɔ anafo fam no bedi so. Monhyɛn no ntiantia mu mfa nkyerɛ sɛ wɔnkɔ.
english: At the sounding of a second blast, the camps on the south are to set out. The blast will be the signal for setting out.

twi: Na sɛ mofrɛ nnipa no ama wɔabehyia a, momfa ɔkwan foforo so nhyɛn ntorobɛnto no.
english: To gather the assembly, blow the trumpets, but not with the signal for setting out.

twi: “Aaron mmabarima asɔfo nko ara na wɔbɛma wɔn kwan ama wɔahyɛn ntorobɛnto no. Eyi yɛ mmara a ɛbɛtena hɔ daa ama awo ntoatoaso a ɛbɛba no nyinaa.
english: “The sons of Aaron, the priests, are to blow the trumpets. This is to be a lasting ordinance for you and the generations to come.

twi: Sɛ mudu Bɔhyɛ Asase no so na mo ne mo atamfo a wɔhyɛ mo so no ko a mohyɛn ntorobɛnto no. Na, Awurade, mo Nyankopɔn bɛkae mo na wagye mo afi mo atamfo nsam.
english: When you go into battle in your own land against an enemy who is oppressing you, sound a blast on the trumpets. Then you will be remembered by the Lord your God and rescued from your enemies.

twi: Anigyebere mu nso, monhyɛn ntorobɛnto no. Afe mu dapɔnna nso, monhyɛn. Ɔsram biara mfiase nso, monhyɛn mfa nnye mo ani wɔ ɔhyew afɔre ne asomdwoe afɔre ho. Sɛ moyɛ saa a, ɛbɛkae Onyankopɔn apam a ɔne mo wɔ no. Na mene Awurade mo Nyankopɔn.”
english: Also at your times of rejoicing—your appointed festivals and New Moon feasts—you are to sound the trumpets over your burnt offerings and fellowship offerings, and they will be a memorial for you before your God. I am the Lord your God.”

twi: Ɔsram a ɛto so abien no da a ɛto so aduonu no a ɛyɛ mfe abien a Israelfo fii Misraim no, omununkum no pagyaw ne ho fii Ahyiae Ntamadan no so,
english: On the twentieth day of the second month of the second year, the cloud lifted from above the tabernacle of the covenant law.

twi: enti Israelfo no fii Sinai sare so hɔ dii omununkum no akyi kosii sɛ ekogyinaa Paran sare so.
english: Then the Israelites set out from the Desert of Sinai and traveled from place to place until the cloud came to rest in the Desert of Paran.

twi: Bere a ɛsɛ sɛ wotu no duu no, Awurade nam Mose so ka kyerɛɛ wɔn.
english: They set out, this first time, at the Lord’s command through Moses.

twi: Akwantu no mu no, mmusua a wɔhyɛ Yuda abusuakuw no ase, a Aminadab babarima Nahson tua ano na otuu wɔn frankaa ma wodii kan.
english: The divisions of the camp of Judah went first, under their standard. Nahshon son of Amminadab was in command.

twi: Wɔn a wodii so ne Isakar abusuakuw a Suar babarima Netanel di wɔn anim.
english: Nethanel son of Zuar was over the division of the tribe of Issachar,

twi: Sebulon abusuakuw na wodii hɔ a Helon babarima Eliab na na odi wɔn anim.
english: and Eliab son of Helon was over the division of the tribe of Zebulun.

twi: Wotutuu Ahyiae Ntamadan no, na Gerson ne Merari mmusua a wofi Lewifo mu no soaa Ahyiae Ntamadan no dii wɔn afa wɔ santen no mu.
english: Then the tabernacle was taken down, and the Gershonites and Merarites, who carried it, set out.

twi: Ruben abusuakuw tuu wɔn frankaa de dii so a Sedeur babarima Elisur di wɔn anim.
english: The divisions of the camp of Reuben went next, under their standard. Elizur son of Shedeur was in command.

twi: Wɔn a na wodi so ne Simeon abusuakuw a Surisadai babarima Selumiel di wɔn anim;
english: Shelumiel son of Zurishaddai was over the division of the tribe of Simeon,

twi: Gad abusuakuw nso, na Deguel babarima Eliasaf na odi wɔn anim.
english: and Eliasaph son of Deuel was over the division of the tribe of Gad.

twi: Na Kohatfo no nso na na wodi hɔ a wɔsoso kronkronbea hɔ nneɛma. Na ɛsɛ sɛ wɔhyehyɛ Ahyiae Ntamadan no wɔ beae foforo hɔ ansa na wɔadu hɔ.
english: Then the Kohathites set out, carrying the holy things. The tabernacle was to be set up before they arrived.

twi: Wɔn a na wodi so ne Efraim abusuakuw a na wodi wɔn frankaa no akyi a Amihud babarima Elisama na odi wɔn anim;
english: The divisions of the camp of Ephraim went next, under their standard. Elishama son of Ammihud was in command.

twi: Wɔn a na wodi so ne Manase abusuakuw a Pedahsur babarima Gamaliel di wɔn anim;
english: Gamaliel son of Pedahzur was over the division of the tribe of Manasseh,

twi: na Benyamin abusuakuw na na wodi so a Gideoni babarima Abidan di wɔn anim.
english: and Abidan son of Gideoni was over the division of the tribe of Benjamin.

twi: Wɔn a na wotwa to koraa no ne Dan abusuakuw a wɔyɛ wɔn nyinaa awɛmfo na Amisadai babarima Ahieser da wɔn ano na frankaa di wɔn anim.
english: Finally, as the rear guard for all the units, the divisions of the camp of Dan set out under their standard. Ahiezer son of Ammishaddai was in command.

twi: Okran babarima Pagiel na na odi Aser abusuakuw anim,
english: Pagiel son of Okran was over the division of the tribe of Asher,

twi: na Enan babarima Ahira nso di Naftali abusuakuw anim.
english: and Ahira son of Enan was over the division of the tribe of Naphtali.

twi: Saa nhyehyɛe yi na Israel mmusuakuw yi faa so tuu wɔn kwan no.
english: This was the order of march for the Israelite divisions as they set out.

twi: Afei, Mose ka kyerɛɛ nʼase Hobab, Midiani Reuel ba se, “Eyi nyinaa akyi no, yɛrekɔ beae a Awurade kae se, ‘Mede bɛma mo no.’ Bra na yɛnkɔ na yɛbɛhwɛ wo so yiye; efisɛ Awurade ahyɛ Israelfo nnepa ho bɔ.”
english: Now Moses said to Hobab son of Reuel the Midianite, Moses’ father-in-law, “We are setting out for the place about which the Lord said, ‘I will give it to you.’ Come with us and we will treat you well, for the Lord has promised good things to Israel.”

twi: Obuae se, “Dabi, merenkɔ; merekɔ mʼasase so ne mʼabusuafo nkyɛn.”
english: He answered, “No, I will not go; I am going back to my own land and my own people.”

twi: Nanso Mose kae se, “Mesrɛ wo, nnyaw yɛn. Wo na wunim faako a ɛsɛ sɛ yɛtena wɔ sare no so, na wubetumi ayɛ yɛn kwankyerɛfo.
english: But Moses said, “Please do not leave us. You know where we should camp in the wilderness, and you can be our eyes.

twi: Sɛ wo ne yɛn kɔ a, nneɛma pa a Awurade de bɛma yɛn no nyinaa, wubenya bi.”
english: If you come with us, we will share with you whatever good things the Lord gives us.”

twi: Enti wofi Awurade Bepɔw so nantew nnansa. Awurade Apam Adaka no dii wɔn anim hwehwɛɛ baabi a wɔbɛsoɛ maa wɔn.
english: So they set out from the mountain of the Lord and traveled for three days. The ark of the covenant of the Lord went before them during those three days to find them a place to rest.

twi: Wofii wɔn akwantu no ase awia a wɔrekɔ no nyinaa na Awurade mununkum no di wɔn anim.
english: The cloud of the Lord was over them by day when they set out from the camp.

twi: Bere biara a wɔbɛma adaka no so asi mu no, Mose teɛ mu se,“Awurade, sɔre!Ma wʼatamfo nhwete;ma wɔn nyinaa nguan mfi wʼanim.”
english:
Whenever the ark set out, Moses said,
“Rise up, Lord!
    May your enemies be scattered;
    may your foes flee before you.”

twi: Bere biara a wɔbɛsoɛ adaka no, ɔka se,“Awurade, san braIsraelfo mpempem a wontumi nkan wɔn no mu.”
english:
Whenever it came to rest, he said,
“Return, Lord,
    to the countless thousands of Israel.”

twi: Israelfo AnwiinwiiAnkyɛ biara na nnipa no fii ase nwiinwii sɛ nneɛma nkɔ yiye mma wɔn, na Awurade tee. Nʼabufuw sɔree wɔ wɔn anwiinwii no ho. Eyi nti, Awurade maa ogya bɛhyew beae a na wɔte hɔ no mfikyiri baabi.
english: Now the people complained about their hardships in the hearing of the Lord, and when he heard them his anger was aroused. Then fire from the Lord burned among them and consumed some of the outskirts of the camp.

twi: Wɔteɛteɛɛ mu frɛɛ Mose sɛ ommegye wɔn no, ɔbɔɔ mpae srɛɛ Awurade maa wɔn na ogya no dumii.
english: When the people cried out to Moses, he prayed to the Lord and the fire died down.

twi: Efi saa bere no, wɔtoo beae hɔ din se Tabera a ne nkyerɛase ne “Ahyewee,” efisɛ ogya a efi Awurade nkyɛn no hyew wɔn atenae hɔ.
english: So that place was called Taberah, because fire from the Lord had burned among them.

twi: Misraimfo a na wɔwɔ wɔn ntam no kɔn dɔɔ nneɛma pa a na ɛwɔ Misraim no. Eyi amma Israelfo no ani ansɔ baabi a na wɔwɔ hɔ no, enti wosui se, “Hena na ɔbɛma yɛn aduan adi?
english: The rabble with them began to crave other food, and again the Israelites started wailing and said, “If only we had meat to eat!

twi: Yɛkae nsumnam a yɛwee wɔ Misraim mpoano no. Saa ara nso na na yenya kokumba, ɛfere, gyeene ne galik di no.
english: We remember the fish we ate in Egypt at no cost—also the cucumbers, melons, leeks, onions and garlic.

twi: Nanso mprempren de, yɛn anom ato; yenhu hwee sɛ mana nko ara.”
english: But now we have lost our appetite; we never see anything but this manna!”

twi: Na mana no kɛse te sɛ wusa aba na ɛsɛ ɛhyɛ a awaawae afi dubona ho agu fam.
english: The manna was like coriander seed and looked like resin.

twi: Nnipa no tase fii fam na wɔayam anaa wɔasiw wɔ ɔwaduru mu ma adan esiam. Wowie a, wɔnoa de bi yɛ tetare. Woka wʼano a, ɛte sɛ tetare a wɔakyew wɔ nhabamma ngo mu.
english: The people went around gathering it, and then ground it in a hand mill or crushed it in a mortar. They cooked it in a pot or made it into loaves. And it tasted like something made with olive oil.

twi: Obosu tɔ wɔ wɔn atenae hɔ Anadwo a na mana no nso tɔ.
english: When the dew settled on the camp at night, the manna also came down.

twi: Mose tee sɛ mmusuakuw no nyinaa gyinagyina, atwa wɔn ntamadan ho ahyia resu. Eyi hyɛɛ Awurade abufuw yiye, na ɛhaw Mose nso.
english: Moses heard the people of every family wailing at the entrance to their tents. The Lord became exceedingly angry, and Moses was troubled.

twi: Mose bisaa Awurade se, “Adɛn nti na wode ɔhaw sɛɛ aba wʼakoa so? Dɛn na mayɛ atia wo a na wode saa nnipa a wɔte sɛɛ yi nyinaa adesoa abɛsoa me?
english: He asked the Lord, “Why have you brought this trouble on your servant? What have I done to displease you that you put the burden of all these people on me?

twi: Me na minyinsɛn nnipa yi nyinaa? Me na mewoo wɔn? Adɛn nti na wuse minturu wɔn wɔ me nsa so sɛ nkokoaa nkosi sɛ yebedu asase a wohyɛɛ wɔn agyanom ho bɔ no so?
english: Did I conceive all these people? Did I give them birth? Why do you tell me to carry them in my arms, as a nurse carries an infant, to the land you promised on oath to their ancestors?

twi: Ɛhefa na merekɔfa nam abrɛ nnipa yi? Wosu kyerɛ me se, ‘Ma yɛn nam nwe!’
english: Where can I get meat for all these people? They keep wailing to me, ‘Give us meat to eat!’

twi: Me nko ara rentumi nsoa ɔman yi! Adesoa no mu yɛ duru ma me dodo!
english: I cannot carry all these people by myself; the burden is too heavy for me.

twi: Na sɛ saa na wo ne me bedi no de a, mesrɛ, kum me, sɛ manya wʼanim anuonyam a, na mma minnhyia mʼankasa me sɛe.”
english: If this is how you are going to treat me, please go ahead and kill me—if I have found favor in your eyes—and do not let me face my own ruin.”

twi: Awurade ka kyerɛɛ Mose se, “Frɛ Israelfo mpanyimfo no mu aduɔson ma me; fa wɔn bra Ahyiae Ntamadan no mu na wo ne wɔn nnyina hɔ.
english: The Lord said to Moses: “Bring me seventy of Israel’s elders who are known to you as leaders and officials among the people. Have them come to the tent of meeting, that they may stand there with you.

twi: Mɛba hɔ na me ne wo abɛkasa na honhom a ɛwɔ wo so no, mɛfa na mede akogu wɔn nso so bi; ɛba saa a, wɔne wo bɛsoa nnipa no adesoa sɛnea ɛrenyɛ wo nko ara wʼadesoa.
english: I will come down and speak with you there, and I will take some of the power of the Spirit that is on you and put it on them. They will share the burden of the people with you so that you will not have to carry it alone.

twi: “Ka kyerɛ nnipa no se: Munnwira mo ho na ɔkyena, mubenya nam awe. Ka kyerɛ wɔn se, ‘Awurade ate mo sufrɛ a ɛfa nneɛma a mugyaw no Misraim no ho na ɔrebɛma mo nam na mobɛwe.
english: “Tell the people: ‘Consecrate yourselves in preparation for tomorrow, when you will eat meat. The Lord heard you when you wailed, “If only we had meat to eat! We were better off in Egypt!” Now the Lord will give you meat, and you will eat it.

twi: Ɛnyɛ da koro anaa nnaanu anaa nnaanum anaa nnadu anaa aduonu!
english: You will not eat it for just one day, or two days, or five, ten or twenty days,

twi: Na ɔsram baako mu, mobɛwe nam ara ama afono mo ama afa mo hwene mu. Efisɛ moapo Awurade a ɔka mo ho wɔ ha no, na moasu wɔ nʼanim se, adɛn nti na yefii Misraim?’ ”
english: but for a whole month—until it comes out of your nostrils and you loathe it—because you have rejected the Lord, who is among you, and have wailed before him, saying, “Why did we ever leave Egypt?”’”

twi: Mose kae se, “Mmarima nko ara mpem ahansia na wɔwɔ ha, ɛno na woahyɛ wɔn bɔ sɛ wobɛma wɔn nam awe ara ɔsram!
english: But Moses said, “Here I am among six hundred thousand men on foot, and you say, ‘I will give them meat to eat for a whole month!’

twi: Sɛ yekum nguan ne anantwi ma wɔn a ɛbɛso wɔn ana? Sɛ wɔkyere po mu nam nyinaa ma wɔn a ɛbɛso wɔn ana?”
english: Would they have enough if flocks and herds were slaughtered for them? Would they have enough if all the fish in the sea were caught for them?”

twi: Na Awurade bisaa Mose se, “So Awurade basa yɛ tiaa dodo ana? Afei wubehu sɛ mʼasɛm yɛ nokware anaa ɛnyɛ nokware.”
english: The Lord answered Moses, “Is the Lord’s arm too short? Now you will see whether or not what I say will come true for you.”

twi: Enti Mose fii Ahyiae Ntamadan no mu hɔ kɔkaa nsɛm a Awurade ka kyerɛɛ no no nyinaa kyerɛɛ nnipa no. Ɔboaboaa mpanyimfo aduɔson ano ma wotwaa Ahyiae Ntamadan no ho hyiae.
english: So Moses went out and told the people what the Lord had said. He brought together seventy of their elders and had them stand around the tent.

twi: Na Awurade nam omununkum mu baa fam ne Mose kasae, na ɔfaa honhom a ɛwɔ Mose so no de guu mpanyimfo aduɔson no so. Bere a honhom no baa wɔn so kakra no, wɔhyɛɛ nkɔm mmere tiaa bi mu.
english: Then the Lord came down in the cloud and spoke with him, and he took some of the power of the Spirit that was on him and put it on the seventy elders. When the Spirit rested on them, they prophesied—but did not do so again.

twi: Nanso na mpanyimfo aduɔson no mu baanu a wɔfrɛ wɔn Eldad ne Medad da so wɔ wɔn atenae hɔ. Na bere a honhom no baa wɔn so wɔ hɔ no, wɔhyɛɛ nkɔm wɔ hɔ.
english: However, two men, whose names were Eldad and Medad, had remained in the camp. They were listed among the elders, but did not go out to the tent. Yet the Spirit also rested on them, and they prophesied in the camp.

twi: Mmerante bi tuu mmirika kɔbɔɔ Mose asɛm a asi no ho amanneɛ
english: A young man ran and told Moses, “Eldad and Medad are prophesying in the camp.”

twi: na Nun babarima Yosua a na wɔayi no sɛ ɔnyɛ Mose boafo no ampene so, na ɔkae se, “Me wura Mose, ma wonnyae!”
english: Joshua son of Nun, who had been Moses’ aide since youth, spoke up and said, “Moses, my lord, stop them!”

twi: Mose bisaa no se, “Me ho na woretwe ninkunu yi? Ɛkaa me nko a, na anka Awurade nkurɔfo nyinaa yɛ adiyifo a Awurade de ne honhom agu wɔn nyinaa so!”
english: But Moses replied, “Are you jealous for my sake? I wish that all the Lord’s people were prophets and that the Lord would put his Spirit on them!”

twi: Na Mose ne Israel mpanyimfo no san kɔɔ wɔn atenae hɔ.
english: Then Moses and the elders of Israel returned to the camp.

twi: Na Awurade bɔɔ ahum maa ɛde mmoko fi po mu beguu atenae hɔ ne ɛho mmaa nyinaa. Baabiara a obi bɛfa no, na nnomaa yi bi atu nenam asase ani bɛyɛ anammɔn anan.
english: Now a wind went out from the Lord and drove quail in from the sea. It scattered them up to two cubits deep all around the camp, as far as a day’s walk in any direction.

twi: Enti da mu no nyinaa, nnipa kyekyeree mmoko no bi kunkum wɔn awia ne anadwo ne nʼadekyee nso. Nea wannya bi no koraa na onyaa susukoraa ɔha! Mmoko buu so wɔ atenae hɔ nyinaa.
english: All that day and night and all the next day the people went out and gathered quail. No one gathered less than ten homers. Then they spread them out all around the camp.

twi: Na nnipa no fii ase wee mmoa no bi no, Awurade bo san fuw wɔn maa ɔde ɔyaredɔm kum wɔn mu fa kɛse no ara.
english: But while the meat was still between their teeth and before it could be consumed, the anger of the Lord burned against the people, and he struck them with a severe plague.

twi: Enti wɔtoo beae hɔ din se Kibrot-Hataawa a nkyerɛase ne, “Akɔnnɔ ɔda” efisɛ wɔn a na wɔn ani bere nam na wɔn kɔn adɔ Misraim tena no na wosiee wɔn wɔ hɔ.
english: Therefore the place was named Kibroth Hattaavah, because there they buried the people who had craved other food.

twi: Ɔman no tu fii Kibrot-Hataawa hɔ kɔtenaa Haserot.
english: From Kibroth Hattaavah the people traveled to Hazeroth and stayed there.

twi: Miriam Ne Aaron Tia MoseMiriam ne Aaron kasa tiaa Mose sɛ ne yere yɛ Etiopiani.
english: Miriam and Aaron began to talk against Moses because of his Cushite wife, for he had married a Cushite.

twi: Wɔkae se, “Mose nko ara na Awurade akasa afa ne so ana? Na yɛn nso ɔnkasa mfa yɛn so bi ana?” Na Awurade tee wɔn anwiinwii no.
english: “Has the Lord spoken only through Moses?” they asked. “Hasn’t he also spoken through us?” And the Lord heard this.

twi: Na Mose yɛ ɔhobrɛaseni sen obiara a ɔte asase yi so.
english: (Now Moses was a very humble man, more humble than anyone else on the face of the earth.)

twi: Ntɛm so, Awurade frɛɛ Mose, Aaron ne Miriam kɔɔ Ahyiae Ntamadan no mu. Ɔhyɛɛ wɔn se, “Mo baasa no mommra Ahyiae Ntamadan mu ha.” Enti wobegyinagyinaa Awurade anim.
english: At once the Lord said to Moses, Aaron and Miriam, “Come out to the tent of meeting, all three of you.” So the three of them went out.

twi: Afei, Awurade nam omununkum fadum mu sian ba begyinaa Ahyiae Ntamadan no kwan ano, na ɔfrɛɛ Aaron ne Miriam. Bere a wotwiw kɔɔ wɔn anim no,
english: Then the Lord came down in a pillar of cloud; he stood at the entrance to the tent and summoned Aaron and Miriam. When the two of them stepped forward,

twi: ɔkae se, “Muntie me nsɛm:“Sɛ odiyifo wɔ mo mu a,Me, Awurade, menam anisoadehu so da me ho adi kyerɛ no,me kasa kyerɛ no wɔ dae mu.
english:
he said, “Listen to my words:
“When there is a prophet among you,
    I, the Lord, reveal myself to them in visions,
    I speak to them in dreams.

twi: Nanso ɛnte saa wɔ me somfo Mose ho.Me fi nyinaa mu no, ɔyɛ ɔnokwafo.
english:
But this is not true of my servant Moses;
    he is faithful in all my house.

twi: Me ne no kasa anim ne anim,kasa a emu da hɔ na ɛnyɛ abisae mu.Na ohu Awurade sɛnea ɔte.Adɛn nti na moansurosɛ mobɛkasa atia me somfo Mose?”
english:
With him I speak face to face,
    clearly and not in riddles;
    he sees the form of the Lord.
Why then were you not afraid
    to speak against my servant Moses?”

twi: Awurade bo fuw wɔn dennen pa ara na ofii hɔ kɔe.
english: The anger of the Lord burned against them, and he left them.

twi: Bere a omununkum no fii Ahyiae Ntamadan no atifi no, kwata beduruu Miriam ho fitaa sɛ sukyerɛmma. Aaron twaa nʼani huu sɛ ɔwɔ ɔhonam ani yare a ɛyɛ fi no,
english: When the cloud lifted from above the tent, Miriam’s skin was leprous—it became as white as snow. Aaron turned toward her and saw that she had a defiling skin disease,

twi: ɔka kyerɛɛ Mose se, “Me wura, mesrɛ wo, nnyina saa bɔne a yɛnam nkwaseasɛm so adi yi so ntwe yɛn aso.
english: and he said to Moses, “Please, my lord, I ask you not to hold against us the sin we have so foolishly committed.

twi: Mma no nyɛ sɛ akokoaa a wawu wɔ ne yam a ne fa aporɔw.”
english: Do not let her be like a stillborn infant coming from its mother’s womb with its flesh half eaten away.”

twi: Na Mose teɛɛ mu frɛɛ Awurade se, “Onyankopɔn, mesrɛ wo sɛ sa no yare!”
english: So Moses cried out to the Lord, “Please, God, heal her!”

twi: Awurade buaa Mose se, “Sɛ nʼagya tew ntasu guu nʼanim a, anka nʼanim rengu ase nnanson? Munyi no mfi atenae ha nkɔhyɛ baabi nnanson na akyiri no, obetumi asan aba.”
english: The Lord replied to Moses, “If her father had spit in her face, would she not have been in disgrace for seven days? Confine her outside the camp for seven days; after that she can be brought back.”

twi: Enti wotwaa Miriam asu fii atenae hɔ ma okodii nnanson. Nnipa no twɛn kosii sɛ wɔsan de no bae ansa na wɔretu kwan no bio.
english: So Miriam was confined outside the camp for seven days, and the people did not move on till she was brought back.

twi: Ɛno akyi no, wofii Haserot bɛbɔɔ atenae wɔ Paran sare so.
english: After that, the people left Hazeroth and encamped in the Desert of Paran.

twi: Akwansrafo Kɔ Kanaan Asase SoNa Awurade ka kyerɛɛ Mose se,
english: The Lord said to Moses,

twi: “Soma akwansrafo na wɔnkɔ Kanaan asase so; asase a mede rema Israelfo no. Soma mmusuakuw dumien no mu biara ntuanoni.”
english: “Send some men to explore the land of Canaan, which I am giving to the Israelites. From each ancestral tribe send one of its leaders.”

twi: Enti Mose yɛɛ sɛnea Awurade hyɛɛ no no. Ɔsomaa mmarima dumien a wɔn nyinaa yɛ mmusuakuw ntuanofo fi wɔn atenae wɔ Paran sare so.
english: So at the Lord’s command Moses sent them out from the Desert of Paran. All of them were leaders of the Israelites.

twi: Saa mmusuakuw no ne wɔn mpanyimfo no din na edidi so yi:Ruben abusuakuw no ntuanoni ne Sakur babarima Samua;
english:
These are their names:
from the tribe of Reuben, Shammua son of Zakkur;

twi: Simeon abusuakuw no ntuanoni ne Hori babarima Safat;
english: from the tribe of Simeon, Shaphat son of Hori;

twi: Yuda abusuakuw no ntuanoni ne Yefune babarima Kaleb;
english: from the tribe of Judah, Caleb son of Jephunneh;

twi: Isakar abusuakuw no ntuanoni ne Yosef babarima Igal;
english: from the tribe of Issachar, Igal son of Joseph;

twi: Efraim abusuakuw no ntuanoni ne Nun babarima Hosea;
english: from the tribe of Ephraim, Hoshea son of Nun;

twi: Benyamin abusuakuw no ntuanoni ne Rafu babarima Palti;
english: from the tribe of Benjamin, Palti son of Raphu;

twi: Sebulon abusuakuw no ntuanoni ne Sodi babarima Gadiel;
english: from the tribe of Zebulun, Gaddiel son of Sodi;

twi: Manase abusuakuw (a ɛyɛ Yosef abusuakuw no mu fa) no ntuanoni ne Susi babarima Gadi;
english: from the tribe of Manasseh (a tribe of Joseph), Gaddi son of Susi;

twi: Dan abusuakuw no ntuanoni ne Gemali babarima Amiel;
english: from the tribe of Dan, Ammiel son of Gemalli;

twi: Aser abusuakuw no ntuanoni ne Mikael babarima Setur;
english: from the tribe of Asher, Sethur son of Michael;

twi: Naftali abusuakuw no ntuanoni ne Wofsi babarima Nahbi;
english: from the tribe of Naphtali, Nahbi son of Vophsi;

twi: Gad abusuakuw no ntuanoni ne Maki babarima Geuel.
english: from the tribe of Gad, Geuel son of Maki.

twi: Nnipa yi na Mose somaa wɔn ma wɔkɔsraa Kanaan asase no. Mose na ɔmaa Nun ba Hosea din Yosua.
english: These are the names of the men Moses sent to explore the land. (Moses gave Hoshea son of Nun the name Joshua.)

twi: Mose ka kyerɛɛ wɔn se, “Monkɔ atifi fam wɔ Negeb bepɔw no so.
english: When Moses sent them to explore Canaan, he said, “Go up through the Negev and on into the hill country.

twi: Monhwɛ sɛnea ɛhɔ asase no te; na monhwɛ wɔn a wɔte hɔ no nso tebea sɛ wɔwɔ ahoɔden anaa wɔyɛ mmerɛw, sɛ wɔdɔɔso anaa wosua.
english: See what the land is like and whether the people who live there are strong or weak, few or many.

twi: Asasesu bɛn na wɔte so? Eye anaasɛ enye? Nkurowsu bɛn na wɔtete mu? Ɛdeda hɔ petee anaasɛ afasu wowɔ ho?
english: What kind of land do they live in? Is it good or bad? What kind of towns do they live in? Are they unwalled or fortified?

twi: Dɔte no te dɛn? Srade wɔ mu anaasɛ ɛyɛ kwaboo? Nnua wɔ so anaasɛ nnua nni so? Mommɔ mmɔden na momfa ɛhɔ nnɔbae no bi mmra.” Saa bere no na wɔretew bobe aba kan.
english: How is the soil? Is it fertile or poor? Are there trees in it or not? Do your best to bring back some of the fruit of the land.” (It was the season for the first ripe grapes.)

twi: Enti wɔkɔsraa asase no fi Sin sare so kosii Rehob a ɛbɛn Hamat no.
english: So they went up and explored the land from the Desert of Zin as far as Rehob, toward Lebo Hamath.

twi: Wɔfaa atifi fam kɔfaa Negeb beduu Hebron. Ɛhɔ na wohuu Anak asefo a wɔfrɛ wɔn Ahiman, Sesai ne Talmai. Hebron yɛ kurow dedaw. Wɔkyekyeree saa kurow no mfe ason ansa na wɔrekyekyere Soan a ɛwɔ Misraim no.
english: They went up through the Negev and came to Hebron, where Ahiman, Sheshai and Talmai, the descendants of Anak, lived. (Hebron had been built seven years before Zoan in Egypt.)

twi: Woduu Eskol bon mu no, wotwaa mman a bobe kasiaw wɔ so. Mmarima baanu na wɔworaa no dua soa kaa borɔdɔma aba ho de kɔe.
english: When they reached the Valley of Eshkol, they cut off a branch bearing a single cluster of grapes. Two of them carried it on a pole between them, along with some pomegranates and figs.

twi: Saa bere no, Israelfo no too subon hɔ din sɛ “Eskol bon mu” a nkyerɛase ne “Kasiaw,” efisɛ wohuu bobe kasiaw pii wɔ hɔ.
english: That place was called the Valley of Eshkol because of the cluster of grapes the Israelites cut off there.

twi: Adaduanan akyi no, wofii wɔn akwansra no mu bae.
english: At the end of forty days they returned from exploring the land.

twi: Wɔkaa nea wokohui nyinaa kyerɛɛ Mose ne Aaron ne nnipa a wɔwɔ Israel nyinaa ne wɔn a wɔwɔ Paran sare so wɔ Kades na wɔde aduaba a wɔde bae no kyerɛe.
english: They came back to Moses and Aaron and the whole Israelite community at Kadesh in the Desert of Paran. There they reported to them and to the whole assembly and showed them the fruit of the land.

twi: Asɛm a wɔbɛkae ne sɛ, “Yeduu asase a wosomaa yɛn sɛ yɛnkɔsra so no so, na ɛwo ne nufusu sen wɔ so ampa! Ɛso aduaba a yɛde bae ni.
english: They gave Moses this account: “We went into the land to which you sent us, and it does flow with milk and honey! Here is its fruit.

twi: Nanso na nnipa a wɔtete hɔ no yɛ den. Wɔn nkurow no soso na wɔabɔ ho ban nso. Yehuu Anak asefo wɔ hɔ mpo.
english: But the people who live there are powerful, and the cities are fortified and very large. We even saw descendants of Anak there.

twi: Amalekfo te anafo na Hetifo, Yebusifo ne Amorifo nso tete mmepɔw so. Na Kanaanfo nso tete Ntam Po no ne Yordan subon ho.”
english: The Amalekites live in the Negev; the Hittites, Jebusites and Amorites live in the hill country; and the Canaanites live near the sea and along the Jordan.”

twi: Na Kaleb bɔɔ nnipa no ano wɔ Mose anim kae se, “Momma yɛmforo nkɔ hɔ prɛko pɛ na yɛnkɔfa asase no, efisɛ yebetumi adi wɔn so nkonim.”
english: Then Caleb silenced the people before Moses and said, “We should go up and take possession of the land, for we can certainly do it.”

twi: Nanso mmarima a wɔne no kɔe no kae se, “Yɛrentumi nkɔtoa saa nnipa yi; wɔn ho yɛ den sen yɛn.”
english: But the men who had gone up with him said, “We can’t attack those people; they are stronger than we are.”

twi: Na wɔde asɛm a ɛmma akomatɔyam fa asase a wɔkɔsraa so no ho tene faa Israelfo no mu nyinaa. Wose, “Asase a yɛkɔsraa so no sofo no yɛ awudifo nkutoo. Nnipa a yehuu wɔn wɔ hɔ no yɛ abran.
english: And they spread among the Israelites a bad report about the land they had explored. They said, “The land we explored devours those living in it. All the people we saw there are of great size.

twi: Yehuu Anakfo no bi a efi awo ntoatoaso mu wɔyɛ abran no. Sɛ yɛne wɔn gyina hɔ a, na yɛayɛ te sɛ nketekre wɔ yɛn ani so. Na saa ara nso na yɛyɛɛ wɔ wɔn ani so.”
english: We saw the Nephilim there (the descendants of Anak come from the Nephilim). We seemed like grasshoppers in our own eyes, and we looked the same to them.”

twi: Nnipa No Tew AtuaSaa anadwo no, nnipa no nyinaa fii ase suu denneennen.
english: That night all the members of the community raised their voices and wept aloud.

twi: Wɔde nne koro nwiinwii tiaa Mose ne Aaron. Wɔkae se, “Sɛ yewuwuu wɔ Misraim anaa sare so ha a, anka eye.
english: All the Israelites grumbled against Moses and Aaron, and the whole assembly said to them, “If only we had died in Egypt! Or in this wilderness!
