twi: Wofii Po Kɔkɔɔ no ho, kɔbɔɔ atenae wɔ Sin nweatam so.
english: They left the Red Sea and camped in the Desert of Sin.

twi: Wotu fii Sin sare so kɔbɔɔ atenae Dofka.
english: They left the Desert of Sin and camped at Dophkah.

twi: Wofii Dofka kɔbɔɔ atenae wɔ Alus.
english: They left Dophkah and camped at Alush.

twi: Wofii Alus kɔbɔɔ atenae wɔ Refidim, baabi a na wonnya nsu mma nnipa no nnom.
english: They left Alush and camped at Rephidim, where there was no water for the people to drink.

twi: Wofii Refidim no, wɔkɔbɔɔ atenae wɔ Sinai sare so.
english: They left Rephidim and camped in the Desert of Sinai.

twi: Wofii Sinai sare so no, wɔkɔɔ atenae wɔ Kibrot-Hataawa.
english: They left the Desert of Sinai and camped at Kibroth Hattaavah.

twi: Wofii Kibrot-Hataawa no, wɔkɔbɔɔ atenae wɔ Haserot.
english: They left Kibroth Hattaavah and camped at Hazeroth.

twi: Wofii Haserot kɔbɔɔ atenae wɔ Ritma.
english: They left Hazeroth and camped at Rithmah.

twi: Wofii Ritma kɔbɔɔ atenae wɔ Rimon Peres.
english: They left Rithmah and camped at Rimmon Perez.

twi: Wofii Rimon Peres kɔbɔɔ atenae wɔ Libna.
english: They left Rimmon Perez and camped at Libnah.

twi: Wofii Libna kɔbɔɔ atenae wɔ Risa.
english: They left Libnah and camped at Rissah.

twi: Wofii Risa kɔbɔɔ atenae wɔ Kahelata.
english: They left Rissah and camped at Kehelathah.

twi: Wofii Kahelata kɔbɔɔ atenae wɔ Sefer Bepɔw so.
english: They left Kehelathah and camped at Mount Shepher.

twi: Wofii Sefer Bepɔw so kɔbɔɔ atenae wɔ Harada.
english: They left Mount Shepher and camped at Haradah.

twi: Wofii Harada kɔbɔɔ atenae wɔ Makhelot.
english: They left Haradah and camped at Makheloth.

twi: Wofii Makhelot kɔbɔɔ atenae wɔ Tahat.
english: They left Makheloth and camped at Tahath.

twi: Wofii Tahat kɔbɔɔ atenae wɔ Tera.
english: They left Tahath and camped at Terah.

twi: Wofii Tera kɔbɔɔ atenae wɔ Mitka.
english: They left Terah and camped at Mithkah.

twi: Wofii Mitka kɔbɔɔ atenae wɔ Hasmona.
english: They left Mithkah and camped at Hashmonah.

twi: Wofii Hasmona kɔbɔɔ atenae wɔ Moserot.
english: They left Hashmonah and camped at Moseroth.

twi: Wofii Moserot kɔbɔɔ atenae wɔ Beneyaakan.
english: They left Moseroth and camped at Bene Jaakan.

twi: Wofii Beneyaakan kɔbɔɔ atenae wɔ Horhagidgad.
english: They left Bene Jaakan and camped at Hor Haggidgad.

twi: Wofii Horhagidgad kɔbɔɔ atenae wɔ Yotbata.
english: They left Hor Haggidgad and camped at Jotbathah.

twi: Wofii Yotbata kɔbɔɔ atenae wɔ Abrona.
english: They left Jotbathah and camped at Abronah.

twi: Wofii Abrona kɔbɔɔ atenae wɔ Esion-Geber.
english: They left Abronah and camped at Ezion Geber.

twi: Wofii Esion-Geber kɔbɔɔ atenae wɔ Kades, wɔ Sin sare so.
english: They left Ezion Geber and camped at Kadesh, in the Desert of Zin.

twi: Wofii Kades kɔbɔɔ atenae wɔ Bepɔw Hor so, wɔ Edom hye ano.
english: They left Kadesh and camped at Mount Hor, on the border of Edom.

twi: Bere a woduu Bepɔw Hor ase no, Awurade ka kyerɛɛ ɔsɔfo Aaron se ɔnkɔ bepɔw no atifi, na ɛhɔ na okowui. Asɛm yi sii mfe aduanan so a Israelfo tu fii Misraim no.
english: At the Lord’s command Aaron the priest went up Mount Hor, where he died on the first day of the fifth month of the fortieth year after the Israelites came out of Egypt.

twi: Aaron dii mfe ɔha aduonu abiɛsa, bere a owuu wɔ Bepɔw Hor so no.
english: Aaron was a hundred and twenty-three years old when he died on Mount Hor.

twi: Saa bere no ara mu na Kanaanhene Arad a ɔtenaa Negeb wɔ Kanaan asase so no tee sɛ Israelfo no reba nʼasase so.
english: The Canaanite king of Arad, who lived in the Negev of Canaan, heard that the Israelites were coming.

twi: Israelfo no toaa wɔn akwantu no so fi Bepɔw Hor so kɔbɔɔ atenae wɔ Salmona.
english: They left Mount Hor and camped at Zalmonah.

twi: Wofii Salmona kɔtenaa Punon.
english: They left Zalmonah and camped at Punon.

twi: Wofii Punon kɔtenaa Obot.
english: They left Punon and camped at Oboth.

twi: Wɔtoaa so kɔɔ Iye-Abarim, Moab hye so kɔtenaa hɔ.
english: They left Oboth and camped at Iye Abarim, on the border of Moab.

twi: Wofii hɔ no, wɔkɔtenaa Dibon Gad.
english: They left Iye Abarim and camped at Dibon Gad.

twi: Wofii Dibon Gad kɔtenaa Almon Diblataim.
english: They left Dibon Gad and camped at Almon Diblathaim.

twi: Wofii Almon Diblataim kɔtenaa Abarim mmepɔw a ɛbɛn Nebo no so.
english: They left Almon Diblathaim and camped in the mountains of Abarim, near Nebo.

twi: Akyiri no, wotutu fii hɔ twaa mu wɔ Yeriko kɔbɔɔ atenae wɔ Moab tataw so wɔ Asubɔnten Yordan ho.
english: They left the mountains of Abarim and camped on the plains of Moab by the Jordan across from Jericho.

twi: Wɔwɔ saa beae hɔ no, wɔtenaa mmeae bebree a ɛbɛn Asubɔnten Yordan ho—efi Bet-Yesimot kosi Abel Sitim a ɛwɔ Moab tataw so no.
english: There on the plains of Moab they camped along the Jordan from Beth Jeshimoth to Abel Shittim.

twi: Bere a wɔabɔ atenase wɔ hɔ no na Awurade nam Mose so kasa kyerɛɛ Israelfo no se,
english: On the plains of Moab by the Jordan across from Jericho the Lord said to Moses,

twi: “Sɛ mutwa Asubɔnten Yordan kodu Kanaan asase so a,
english: “Speak to the Israelites and say to them: ‘When you cross the Jordan into Canaan,

twi: mompam nnipa a wɔte hɔ no nyinaa na monsɛe wɔn abosom ne ahoni a wɔde abo ayɛ ne nsɔree a wɔasisi no petee mu wɔ mmepɔw so ne mmeae a wɔsom wɔn ahoni no nyinaa.
english: drive out all the inhabitants of the land before you. Destroy all their carved images and their cast idols, and demolish all their high places.

twi: Mede asase no ama mo. Momfa na montena so.
english: Take possession of the land and settle in it, for I have given you the land to possess.

twi: Munnyina ntontobɔ so nkyekyɛ asase no, sɛnea mo mmusua no te. Wɔn a wɔdɔɔso no, wɔbɛma wɔn asase kɛse na wɔn a wosua no nso benya asase ketewa. Sɛnea ntonto no besi abɔ biara no na ɛbɛyɛ wɔn de. Monhwɛ mo agyanom mmusua so mfa nkyekyɛ.
english: Distribute the land by lot, according to your clans. To a larger group give a larger inheritance, and to a smaller group a smaller one. Whatever falls to them by lot will be theirs. Distribute it according to your ancestral tribes.

twi: “Sɛ moampam nnipa a wɔte hɔ no a, wɔbɛyɛ mo ani ase mpe ne mo honam mu nsɔe. Wɔbɛhaw mo wɔ asase a mobɛtena so no so.
english: “‘But if you do not drive out the inhabitants of the land, those you allow to remain will become barbs in your eyes and thorns in your sides. They will give you trouble in the land where you will live.

twi: Na mede nea masusuw sɛ mɛyɛ wɔn no, bɛyɛ mo.”
english: And then I will do to you what I plan to do to them.’”

twi: Kanaan AhyeAwurade ka kyerɛɛ Mose se,
english: The Lord said to Moses,

twi: “Ka kyerɛ Israelfo no se: ‘Sɛ mubedu Kanaan asase no so a, asase a mede rema mo sɛ mo ankasa asase no a, sɛɛ na mo ahye bɛyɛ:
english: “Command the Israelites and say to them: ‘When you enter Canaan, the land that will be allotted to you as an inheritance is to have these boundaries:

twi: “ ‘Asase no anafo fam no bɛyɛ Sin sare so a ɛda Edom hye ano no fa bi. Anafo hye no ano befi apuei fam, Nkyene Po no anafo.
english: “‘Your southern side will include some of the Desert of Zin along the border of Edom. Your southern boundary will start in the east from the southern end of the Dead Sea,

twi: Ɛbɛtoa so akɔtra Akrabbim wɔ anafo hɔ a ɛrekɔ Sin no. Nʼanafo pa ara no bɛyɛ Kades-Barnea, na efi hɔ akosi Hasarada de akowie Asmon.
english: cross south of Scorpion Pass, continue on to Zin and go south of Kadesh Barnea. Then it will go to Hazar Addar and over to Azmon,

twi: Efi Asmon a, ɔhye no bɛkɔ ara akosi Misraim asuwa no mu na ano akɔpem Ntam Po no ano.
english: where it will turn, join the Wadi of Egypt and end at the Mediterranean Sea.

twi: Mo hye a ɛwɔ atɔe no bɛyɛ Ntam Po no ano.
english: “‘Your western boundary will be the coast of the Mediterranean Sea. This will be your boundary on the west.

twi: Mo hye a ɛda atifi no befi ase wɔ Ntam Po no ano na atoa so akosi bepɔw Hor,
english: “‘For your northern boundary, run a line from the Mediterranean Sea to Mount Hor

twi: de akɔ Lebo Hamat na akɔ Sedad
english: and from Mount Hor to Lebo Hamath. Then the boundary will go to Zedad,

twi: na atoa so akɔ Sifron na akowie wɔ Hasar-Enan.
english: continue to Ziphron and end at Hazar Enan. This will be your boundary on the north.

twi: Apuei hye no befi Hasar-Enan akɔ Sefam.
english: “‘For your eastern boundary, run a line from Hazar Enan to Shepham.

twi: Ɔhye no besian afi Sefam akosi Ribla wɔ Ain apuei fam. Efi hɔ a, ebesiansian afa mmepɔw no ase wɔ Galilea Po no apuei fam.
english: The boundary will go down from Shepham to Riblah on the east side of Ain and continue along the slopes east of the Sea of Galilee.

twi: Ɔhye no besian afa Asubɔnten Yordan ho na akɔpem Nkyene Po no.“ ‘Sɛnea mo nsase ne mo ahye te ni.’ ”
english:
Then the boundary will go down along the Jordan and end at the Dead Sea.
“‘This will be your land, with its boundaries on every side.’”

twi: Afei Mose hyɛɛ Israelfo no se, “Momfa ntontobɔ so nkyekyɛ asase yi sɛ mo agyapade. Awurade ahyɛ sɛ wɔmfa mma mmusua akron ne fa no,
english: Moses commanded the Israelites: “Assign this land by lot as an inheritance. The Lord has ordered that it be given to the nine and a half tribes,

twi: efisɛ Ruben ne Gad mmusuakuw no ne Manase abusua no fa no de, wɔanya wɔn agyapade dedaw.
english: because the families of the tribe of Reuben, the tribe of Gad and the half-tribe of Manasseh have received their inheritance.

twi: Saa mmusua abien ne fa yi anya wɔn agyapade wɔ Yeriko akyi, Yordan apuei fam a ɛhwɛ apuei no.”
english: These two and a half tribes have received their inheritance east of the Jordan across from Jericho, toward the sunrise.”

twi: Ntuanofo A Wɔbɛkyɛ Asase NoAwurade ka kyerɛɛ Mose se,
english: The Lord said to Moses,

twi: “Nnipa a wɔn din didi so yi na mayi wɔn sɛ wɔnkyekyɛ asase no mu mma mo sɛ mo agyapade: Ɔsɔfo Eleasar ne, Nun babarima Yosua.
english: “These are the names of the men who are to assign the land for you as an inheritance: Eleazar the priest and Joshua son of Nun.

twi: Yi abusua biara mu ɔpanyin baako na ɔmmoa nkyekyɛ asase no.
english: And appoint one leader from each tribe to help assign the land.

twi: “Wɔn din na edidi so yi:“Yefune babarima Kaleb, Yuda abusuakuw ntuanoni;
Amihud babarima Semuel, Simeon abusuakuw ntuanoni;
english:
Shemuel son of Ammihud,
from the tribe of Simeon;

twi: Kislon babarima Elidad, Benyamin abusuakuw ntuanoni;
english:
Elidad son of Kislon,
from the tribe of Benjamin;

twi: Yogli babarima Buki, Dan abusuakuw ntuanoni;
english:
Bukki son of Jogli,
the leader from the tribe of Dan;

twi: Efod babarima Haniel, Yosef babarima Manase abusuakuw ntuanoni;
english:
Hanniel son of Ephod,
the leader from the tribe of Manasseh son of Joseph;

twi: Siftan babarima Kemuel, Yosef babarima Efraim abusuakuw ntuanoni;
english:
Kemuel son of Shiphtan,
the leader from the tribe of Ephraim son of Joseph;

twi: Parknak babarima Elisafan, Sebulon abusuakuw ntuanoni;
english:
Elizaphan son of Parnak,
the leader from the tribe of Zebulun;

twi: Asan babarima Paltiel, Isakar abusuakuw ntuanoni;
english:
Paltiel son of Azzan,
the leader from the tribe of Issachar;

twi: Selomi babarima Ahihud, Aser abusuakuw ntuanoni;
english:
Ahihud son of Shelomi,
the leader from the tribe of Asher;

twi: Amihud babarima Pedahel, Naftali abusuakuw ntuanoni.”
english:
Pedahel son of Ammihud,
the leader from the tribe of Naphtali.”

twi: Saa nnipa yi na Awurade yii wɔn sɛ wɔnhwɛ nkyekyɛ agyapade no mu mma Israelfo no wɔ Kanaan asase so no.
english: These are the men the Lord commanded to assign the inheritance to the Israelites in the land of Canaan.

twi: Lewifo NkurowBere a Israelfo bɔɔ atenase wɔ Yordan ho, Moab tataw so wɔ Yeriko akyi no, Awurade ka kyerɛɛ Mose se,
english: On the plains of Moab by the Jordan across from Jericho, the Lord said to Moses,

twi: “Ka kyerɛ Israelfo no na wɔmfa wɔn agyapade no mu bi a ɛyɛ nkurow ne ɛho mmoa adidibea mma Lewifo no.
english: “Command the Israelites to give the Levites towns to live in from the inheritance the Israelites will possess. And give them pasturelands around the towns.

twi: Nkurow no mu na wɔbɛtena na wɔn anantwi, wɔn nguan ne wɔn mmoa a aka no nso akɔ adidi wɔ adidibea hɔ.
english: Then they will have towns to live in and pasturelands for the cattle they own and all their other animals.

twi: “Wɔn mmoa adidibea no kɛse befi kurow no afasu ho a ne fa biara trɛw yɛ anammɔn apem ne ahannum.
english: “The pasturelands around the towns that you give the Levites will extend a thousand cubits from the town wall.

twi: Munsusuw anammɔn mpensa mfi kurow no afasu no ho wɔ nʼafanan nyinaa. Eyi bɛyɛ mmoa adidibea kɛse ama nkurow no.
english: Outside the town, measure two thousand cubits on the east side, two thousand on the south side, two thousand on the west and two thousand on the north, with the town in the center. They will have this area as pastureland for the towns.

twi: Guankɔbea Nkuropɔn“Nkurow a mode bɛma Lewifo no no mu asia bɛyɛ guankɔbea nkuropɔn, baabi a obi a wafom akum ɔfoforo no, betumi aguan akɔ. Momfa nkurow aduanan abien nka ho mma wɔn.
english: “Six of the towns you give the Levites will be cities of refuge, to which a person who has killed someone may flee. In addition, give them forty-two other towns.

twi: Ne nyinaa bɛyɛ nkurow aduanan awotwe ne ho mmoa adidibea.
english: In all you must give the Levites forty-eight towns, together with their pasturelands.

twi: Saa nkurow yi befi Israelfo no agyapade mu. Mmusuakuw no mu akɛse bɛma Lewifo no nkurow bebree na mmusuakuw nketewa no ama kakraa bi. Abusuakuw biara bɛma sɛnea nʼagyapade kɛse te.”
english: The towns you give the Levites from the land the Israelites possess are to be given in proportion to the inheritance of each tribe: Take many towns from a tribe that has many, but few from one that has few.”

twi: Awurade ka kyerɛɛ Mose se,
english: Then the Lord said to Moses:

twi: “Ka kyerɛ Israelfo no se, ‘Sɛ mutwa Yordan du Kanaan a,
english: “Speak to the Israelites and say to them: ‘When you cross the Jordan into Canaan,

twi: mompaw nkurow bi mfa nyɛ guankɔbea nkurow a, obiara a ɔbɛfom akum onipa no betumi aguan akɔ hɔ.
english: select some towns to be your cities of refuge, to which a person who has killed someone accidentally may flee.

twi: Saa nkurow yi bɛyɛ guankɔbea a ebegye no afi owufo no abusuafo a wɔpɛ sɛ wɔtɔ owufo no wu so were no nsa mu; na ɛnsɛ sɛ wokum owudifo no gye sɛ wɔadi nʼasɛm abu no kumfɔ ansa.
english: They will be places of refuge from the avenger, so that anyone accused of murder may not die before they stand trial before the assembly.

twi: Ɛsɛ sɛ wosisi guankɔbea nkurow yi mu abiɛsa wɔ Kanaan asase so
english: These six towns you give will be your cities of refuge.

twi: na wosisi abiɛsa nso wɔ Asubɔnten Yordan apuei fam.
english: Give three on this side of the Jordan and three in Canaan as cities of refuge.

twi: Ɛnyɛ Israelfo nko na ɛhɔ bɛyɛ wɔn guankɔbea, na mmom, ɛbɛyɛ guankɔbea ama ahɔho ne akwantufo nyinaa.
english: These six towns will be a place of refuge for Israelites and for foreigners residing among them, so that anyone who has killed another accidentally can flee there.

twi: “ ‘Nanso sɛ obi de dade pema sin bi bɔ obi kum no a, wɔfa no sɛ wadi awu enti ɛsɛ sɛ wokum owudifo no.
english: “‘If anyone strikes someone a fatal blow with an iron object, that person is a murderer; the murderer is to be put to death.

twi: Anaasɛ, sɛ wɔde ɔbo kɛse bi bɔ obi ma owu a, ɛyɛ awudi enti ɛsɛ sɛ wokum owudifo no.
english: Or if anyone is holding a stone and strikes someone a fatal blow with it, that person is a murderer; the murderer is to be put to death.

twi: Saa ara nso na sɛ wɔde dua na ekum no a ɛte ara ne no.
english: Or if anyone is holding a wooden object and strikes someone a fatal blow with it, that person is a murderer; the murderer is to be put to death.

twi: Sɛ ɔweretɔni no hyia owudifo no wɔ baabiara a, ɔwɔ ho kwan sɛ okum no bi.
english: The avenger of blood shall put the murderer to death; when the avenger comes upon the murderer, the avenger shall put the murderer to death.

twi: Enti sɛ obi nam ɔtan so tow biribi bɔ obi, anaa, sɛ ɔtetɛw no,
english: If anyone with malice aforethought shoves another or throws something at them intentionally so that they die

twi: anaa ɔde abufuw bɔ no kuturuku na onii no wu a, ɔyɛ owudifo nti ɛsɛ sɛ wokum no.
english: or if out of enmity one person hits another with their fist so that the other dies, that person is to be put to death; that person is a murderer. The avenger of blood shall put the murderer to death when they meet.

twi: “ ‘Na sɛ emfi ɔtan so na obi sum ɔfoforo, anaa wanhyɛ da na ɔtow biribi ma ɛkɔbɔ obi,
english: “‘But if without enmity someone suddenly pushes another or throws something at them unintentionally

twi: anaasɛ wanhu no na ogyaa ɔbo bi a ɛso a ebetumi akum no mu ma ekokum no a, esiane sɛ saa onipa no nyɛ ɔtamfo na onkura adwene bɔne bi nti,
english: or, without seeing them, drops on them a stone heavy enough to kill them, and they die, then since that other person was not an enemy and no harm was intended,

twi: ɛyɛ bagua no asɛde sɛ wodi asɛm na wɔfa saa mmarakwan yi so bu ɔweretɔni no nea ne nsa apa no ntam atɛn.
english: the assembly must judge between the accused and the avenger of blood according to these regulations.

twi: Ɛsɛ sɛ bagua no bɔ nea ne nsa apa no ho ban fi ɔweretɔni no nsam na wɔde nea ne nsa apa no san kɔ guankɔbea kuropɔn a oguan kɔɔ mu no mu. Ɛsɛ sɛ nea ne nsa apa no tena hɔ ara kosi sɛ ɔsɔfopanyin a wɔsraa no ngo bewu.
english: The assembly must protect the one accused of murder from the avenger of blood and send the accused back to the city of refuge to which they fled. The accused must stay there until the death of the high priest, who was anointed with the holy oil.

twi: “ ‘Nanso sɛ nea ne nsa apa no no fi guankɔbea kuropɔn a waguan akɔ mu no no ahye so
english: “‘But if the accused ever goes outside the limits of the city of refuge to which they fled

twi: na ɔweretɔni no hu no wɔ hɔ a obetumi akum no a ɔrenni awudi ho fɔ.
english: and the avenger of blood finds them outside the city, the avenger of blood may kill the accused without being guilty of murder.

twi: Ɛsɛ sɛ nea ne nsa apa no tena guankɔbea kuropɔn no mu ara kosi sɛ ɔsɔfopanyin bewu. Ɔsɔfopanyin wu akyi nkutoo na obetumi asan akɔ nʼankasa agyapade ho.
english: The accused must stay in the city of refuge until the death of the high priest; only after the death of the high priest may they return to their own property.

twi: “ ‘Ɛsɛ sɛ eyi yɛ mmara a mudi so wɔ awo ntoatoaso a ɛbɛba no nyinaa mu wɔ baabiara a mobɛtena.
english: “‘This is to have the force of law for you throughout the generations to come, wherever you live.

twi: “ ‘Ɛsɛ sɛ wokum obiara a obekum obi, nanso gye sɛ nnansefo a wɔboro onipa baako di tia no ansa na ɛsɛ sɛ wokum no. Sɛ onipa baako pɛ na odi adanse tia no de a, ɛno de, ɛnsɛ sɛ wokum no.
english: “‘Anyone who kills a person is to be put to death as a murderer only on the testimony of witnesses. But no one is to be put to death on the testimony of only one witness.

twi: “ ‘Munnnye owudifo a ɛsɛ sɛ owu no ti mpata, nnyina so nnyaa no. Ɛsɛ sɛ wokum no.
english: “‘Do not accept a ransom for the life of a murderer, who deserves to die. They are to be put to death.

twi: “ ‘Munnnye obi a waguan akɔ guankɔbea kuropɔn mu no ti mpata nnyina so mma no nsan mmɛtena nʼasase so bere a ɔsɔfopanyin bi nwui.
english: “‘Do not accept a ransom for anyone who has fled to a city of refuge and so allow them to go back and live on their own land before the death of the high priest.

twi: “ ‘Munngu asase a mote so no ho fi. Awudi gu asase ho fi, na wɔrentumi nyɛ mpata foforo biara mma asase a wɔahwie mogya agu so gye sɛ wɔde nea ohwiee mogya gui no mogya yɛ okum owudifo no.
english: “‘Do not pollute the land where you are. Bloodshed pollutes the land, and atonement cannot be made for the land on which blood has been shed, except by the blood of the one who shed it.

twi: Munngu asase a mote so ne faako a mete no ho fi, efisɛ Me, Awurade no, mete Israelfo no mu.’ ”
english: Do not defile the land where you live and where I dwell, for I, the Lord, dwell among the Israelites.’”

twi: Mmabea Bi AgyapadeGilead abusua no ntuanofo, Makir a ɔyɛ Manase babarima ne Yosef nena asefo, kɔɔ Mose ne Israel mmusua ntuanofo no nkyɛn de adesrɛde kɔtoo wɔn anim.
english: The family heads of the clan of Gilead son of Makir, the son of Manasseh, who were from the clans of the descendants of Joseph, came and spoke before Moses and the leaders, the heads of the Israelite families.

twi: Wɔkae se, “Awurade hyɛɛ wo se bɔ ntonto na gyina so kyekyɛ asase no ma Israelfo no. Awurade ɔhyɛɛ wo se fa yɛn nuabarima Selofehad agyapade ma ne mmabea.
english: They said, “When the Lord commanded my lord to give the land as an inheritance to the Israelites by lot, he ordered you to give the inheritance of our brother Zelophehad to his daughters.

twi: Na sɛ ɛba sɛ wɔn mu bi kɔware wɔ abusua foforo mu a, ɔde asase a wɔde ama no no bɛkɔ aware. Sɛ ɛba saa a, yɛn abusua no asase a wɔde ama yɛn no so bɛtew.
english: Now suppose they marry men from other Israelite tribes; then their inheritance will be taken from our ancestral inheritance and added to that of the tribe they marry into. And so part of the inheritance allotted to us will be taken away.

twi: Sɛ Israelfo Mfirihyia Aduonum Afahyɛ no du so a, wɔde wɔn agyapade no bɛka abusua a wɔkɔwaree wɔ mu no de ho, na wobeyi afi yɛn agyanom abusua agyapade mu.”
english: When the Year of Jubilee for the Israelites comes, their inheritance will be added to that of the tribe into which they marry, and their property will be taken from the tribal inheritance of our ancestors.”

twi: Enti Mose de saa ɔhyɛ nsɛm a efi Awurade yi maa Israelfo no: “Yosef abusuakuw mu nnipa no asɛm no yɛ nokware.
english: Then at the Lord’s command Moses gave this order to the Israelites: “What the tribe of the descendants of Joseph is saying is right.

twi: Nea Awurade rehyɛ ama Selofehad mmabea no ni: Wotumi ware ɔbarima biara a wɔpɛ a ofi wɔn agya abusuakuw mu.
english: This is what the Lord commands for Zelophehad’s daughters: They may marry anyone they please as long as they marry within their father’s tribal clan.

twi: Ɛnsɛ sɛ Israel agyapade biara fi abusuakuw bi mu kɔ abusuakuw foforo nsam, efisɛ ɛsɛ sɛ Israel agyanom abusuakuw biara agyapade tena hɔ sɛnea ɛte no.
english: No inheritance in Israel is to pass from one tribe to another, for every Israelite shall keep the tribal inheritance of their ancestors.

twi: Ɛsɛ sɛ mmabea a wɔwɔ Israel mmusuakuw mu nyinaa a agyapade tumi kɔ wɔn nsam no wareware wɔ wɔn agyanom mmusuakuw mu na Israel abusuakuw biara agyanom agyapade amfi wɔn abusuakuw mu.
english: Every daughter who inherits land in any Israelite tribe must marry someone in her father’s tribal clan, so that every Israelite will possess the inheritance of their ancestors.

twi: Ɛnsɛ sɛ agyapade biara fi abusuakuw bi nsam kodi ɔfoforo nsam, ɛsɛ sɛ Israel Abusuakuw biara asase a wanya no tena hɔ.”
english: No inheritance may pass from one tribe to another, for each Israelite tribe is to keep the land it inherits.”

twi: Selofehad mmabea no yɛɛ sɛnea Awurade hyɛɛ Mose no.
english: So Zelophehad’s daughters did as the Lord commanded Moses.

twi: Mahla, Tirsa, Hogla, Milka ne Noa nyinaa wareware wɔn agyanom nuabarimanom mma.
english: Zelophehad’s daughters—Mahlah, Tirzah, Hoglah, Milkah and Noah—married their cousins on their father’s side.

twi: Wɔwarewaree wɔ Yosef babarima Manase mmusua mu enti wɔn agyapade no kaa wɔn abusuakuw no mu.
english: They married within the clans of the descendants of Manasseh son of Joseph, and their inheritance remained in their father’s tribe and clan.

twi: Eyinom ne mmara ne nhyehyɛe a Awurade nam Mose so de maa Israelfo wɔ Moab tataw so no, wɔ Asubɔnten Yordan a na wɔafi Yeriko atwa no.
english: These are the commands and regulations the Lord gave through Moses to the Israelites on the plains of Moab by the Jordan across from Jericho.

twi: Edom Atemmu Ho NkɔmhyɛAnisoadehu a Awurade Nyankopɔn daa no adi faa Edom asase ho kyerɛɛ Obadia ni:Yɛate asɛm a efi Awurade nkyɛn.Wɔsomaa ɔnanmusini bi kɔɔ aman so kɔkae se,“Monsɔre na momma yɛnkɔko ntia Edom.”
english:
The vision of Obadiah.
This is what the Sovereign Lord says about Edom—
We have heard a message from the Lord:
    An envoy was sent to the nations to say,
“Rise, let us go against her for battle”—

twi: Awurade ka kyerɛ Edom se:“Hwɛ, mɛbrɛ wo ase.Mɛyɛ wo ketewa wɔ aman no mu,na wɔabu wo animtiaa.
english:
“See, I will make you small among the nations;
    you will be utterly despised.

twi: Wayɛ ahantan adaadaa wo ho,Wo a wote abotan ntokuru muna woayɛ wʼatenae wɔ mmepɔw so,na woka kyerɛ wo ho se,‘Hena na obetumi ayi me asi fam?’
english:
The pride of your heart has deceived you,
    you who live in the clefts of the rocks
    and make your home on the heights,
you who say to yourself,
    ‘Who can bring me down to the ground?’

twi: Sɛ wutu kɔ wim sɛ akɔre,na woyɛ wo berebuw wɔ nsoromma ntam mpo a,hɔ na mɛba abɛtwe wo adwira fam.”Sɛnea Awurade se ni.
english:
Though you soar like the eagle
    and make your nest among the stars,
    from there I will bring you down,”
declares the Lord.

twi: “Sɛ akorɔmfo ba wo so,anaa adwowtwafo ba wo so anadwo a,atoyerɛnkyɛm bɛn na ɛrento wo?Na wɔrennwia wo nneɛma dodow a wɔpɛ ana?Sɛ bobe abatewfo ba wo so a,ɛnyɛ bobe aba kakraa bi pɛ na wobegyaw ama wo ana?
english:
“If thieves came to you,
    if robbers in the night—
oh, what a disaster awaits you!—
    would they not steal only as much as they wanted?
If grape pickers came to you,
    would they not leave a few grapes?

twi: Na wo Esau de, wobewia wʼademudea wode asie na wɔayɛ wo dosodoso.
english:
But how Esau will be ransacked,
    his hidden treasures pillaged!

twi: Wɔn a wo ne wɔn wɔ nkabom nyinaabedi wo huammɔ.Wɔn a wʼadwene yɛ wo sɛwo ne wɔn te asomdwoe mu nobɛdaadaa wo adi wo so,wɔn a wodi wʼaduan no asum wo afiri,nanso, wunhui.
“Saa da no,” Awurade na ose,“Merensɛe anyansafo a wɔwɔ Edom ana,mmarima a wɔte asɛm asea wɔwɔ Esau mmepɔw so ana?
english:
“In that day,” declares the Lord,
    “will I not destroy the wise men of Edom,
    those of understanding in the mountains of Esau?

twi: Teman wʼakofo bɛbɔ hune obiara a ɔwɔ Esau bepɔw so no,wobetwitwa mo atɔre mo ase.
english:
Your warriors, Teman, will be terrified,
    and everyone in Esau’s mountains
    will be cut down in the slaughter.

twi: Esiane basabasayɛ a woyɛ tiaa wo nua Yakob no ntianiwu bɛka wo,na wɔbɛsɛe wo koraa.
Da a wugyinaa ntentenso hwɛɛ no haa,maa ananafo faa nʼahonyade kɔena ahɔho hyɛn ne kurow apon mu,na wɔbɔɔ Yerusalem so ntonto no,na wote sɛ wɔn mu baako.
english:
On the day you stood aloof
    while strangers carried off his wealth
and foreigners entered his gates
    and cast lots for Jerusalem,
    you were like one of them.

twi: Anka ɛnsɛ sɛ wubu wo nua animtiaabere a ɔwɔ asiane mu,anaa sɛ wudi ahurusi wɔ Yudafo sobere a wɔwɔ ɔsɛe mu,na mpo wohoahoa wo hobere a wɔwɔ ahohia mu no.
english:
You should not gloat over your brother
    in the day of his misfortune,
nor rejoice over the people of Judah
    in the day of their destruction,
nor boast so much
    in the day of their trouble.

twi: Anka ɛnsɛ sɛ wode nsrabɔhyɛn me nkurɔfo kurow apon no muwɔ wɔn amanehunuda,anka ɛnsɛ sɛ woserew wɔ bere awɔwɔ ɔhaw mu.Afei nso anka ɛnsɛ sɛwode wo nsa to wɔn ahode so gyewɔ bere a wɔwɔ amanehunu mu.
english:
You should not march through the gates of my people
    in the day of their disaster,
nor gloat over them in their calamity
    in the day of their disaster,
nor seize their wealth
    in the day of their disaster.

twi: Anka ɛnsɛ sɛ wotɛw wɔn nkwantanan sokunkum nʼaguanfoNa wuyi wɔn a aka no mawɔ wɔn amanehunuda no mu.
english:
You should not wait at the crossroads
    to cut down their fugitives,
nor hand over their survivors
    in the day of their trouble.

twi: “Awurade da no abɛnama amanaman nyinaa.Na hwɛ, Edom, sɛnea woyɛɛ nosaa ara na wɔbɛyɛ wo.Wo nneyɛe bɛsan abegu wʼapampam.
english:
“The day of the Lord is near
    for all nations.
As you have done, it will be done to you;
    your deeds will return upon your own head.

twi: Sɛnea mononom nsã wɔ me bepɔw kronkron so no,saa ara na amanaman no nyinaa bɛkɔ so anom,saa ara na ɛbɛkɔ so da biarana wɔbɛyɛ te sɛ nea wonni hɔ.
english:
Just as you drank on my holy hill,
    so all the nations will drink continually;
they will drink and drink
    and be as if they had never been.

twi: Na ogye bɛba Sion bepɔw sona ɛbɛyɛ kronkronbea,na Yakob nsabɛsan aka nʼagyapade.
Yakob bɛyɛ ogyana Yosef ayɛ ogyatannaa;Esau bɛyɛ adehunu bina wɔde no bɛto ogya so ahyew no aobiara renka wɔ Esau ase.”Nea Awurade se ni.
english:
Jacob will be a fire
    and Joseph a flame;
Esau will be stubble,
    and they will set him on fire and destroy him.
There will be no survivors
    from Esau.”
The Lord has spoken.

twi: Nkurɔfo a wofi Negeb nobɛtena Esau mmepɔw so,Na wɔn a wofi nkoko no ase no,bɛfa Filisti asase no,na wɔbɛfa Efraim ne Samaria mfuw atena so,na Benyamin nso afa Gilead.
english:
People from the Negev will occupy
    the mountains of Esau,
and people from the foothills will possess
    the land of the Philistines.
They will occupy the fields of Ephraim and Samaria,
    and Benjamin will possess Gilead.

twi: Nnipakuw yi a wɔyɛ Israelfo a wotwaa wɔn asu kɔɔ Kanaan nobɛfa Kanaan asase no akosi Sarefat;na Yerusalemfo a wotwaa wɔn asu awɔte Safarad no bɛfa Negeb nkurow no adi so.
english:
This company of Israelite exiles who are in Canaan
    will possess the land as far as Zarephath;
the exiles from Jerusalem who are in Sepharad
    will possess the towns of the Negev.

twi: Agyefo bɛkɔ Sion bepɔw so,akodi Edom mmepɔw no so.Na ahenni no bɛyɛ Awurade de!
english:
Deliverers will go up on Mount Zion
    to govern the mountains of Esau.
    And the kingdom will be the Lord’s.

twi: Botae Ne NsɛmpɔwDawid babarima Salomo, Israelhene, mmebusɛm ni:
english: The proverbs of Solomon son of David, king of Israel:

twi: Ne botae ne sɛ ɛbɛkyerɛ nnipa nyansa ne ahohyɛso;ne sɛ ɛbɛboa ama wɔate nsɛm a emu dɔ ase;
english:
for gaining wisdom and instruction;
    for understanding words of insight;

twi: sɛ wobenya akwankyerɛ wɔ abrabɔ pa mu,a ɛbɛma wɔayɛ ade pa, nea ɛteɛ na ho nni asɛm;
english:
for receiving instruction in prudent behavior,
    doing what is right and just and fair;

twi: sɛ ɛbɛma nea nʼadwene mu nnɔ anya nyansana mmabun anya nimdeɛ ne adwene,
english:
for giving prudence to those who are simple,
    knowledge and discretion to the young—

twi: anyansafo ntie na wɔmfa nka nea wonim ho,na nea ɔwɔ nhumu nya akwankyerɛ a
english:
let the wise listen and add to their learning,
    and let the discerning get guidance—

twi: ɛbɛma wate mmɛ ne kasammebu,anyansafo nsɛnka ne abisaa ase.
english:
for understanding proverbs and parables,
    the sayings and riddles of the wise.

twi: Awurade suro yɛ nimdeɛ mfiase,na nkwaseafo bu nyansa ne ahohyɛso animtiaa.
english:
The fear of the Lord is the beginning of knowledge,
    but fools despise wisdom and instruction.

twi: Nyansapɛ Ho AfotusɛmNnaadaa Ho KɔkɔbɔMe ba, tie wʼagya akwankyerɛna mpo wo na nkyerɛkyerɛ.
english:
Listen, my son, to your father’s instruction
    and do not forsake your mother’s teaching.

twi: Ɛbɛyɛ wo ti anuonyam abotirine wo kɔn mu atweaban.
english:
They are a garland to grace your head
    and a chain to adorn your neck.

twi: Me ba, sɛ nnebɔneyɛfo twetwe wo a,mma wɔn ho kwan.
english:
My son, if sinful men entice you,
    do not give in to them.

twi: Sɛ wɔka se, “Bra ma yɛnkɔ;ma yɛnkɔtetɛw na yenkum obi,ma yɛnkɔtɛw ntwɛn mmɔborɔni bi;
ma yɛmmemene wɔn anikann sɛ ɔda,koraa, te sɛ wɔn a wɔkɔ ɔda mu;
english:
let’s swallow them alive, like the grave,
    and whole, like those who go down to the pit;

twi: yebenya nneɛma a ɛsom bo ahorowna yɛde asade ahyɛ yɛn afi ma;
english:
we will get all sorts of valuable things
    and fill our houses with plunder;

twi: fa wo ho bɛhyɛ mu,na wubenya wo kyɛfa wɔ ahonyade no mu.”
english:
cast lots with us;
    we will all share the loot”—

twi: Me ba, wo ne wɔn nnantew,mfa wo nan nsi wɔn akwan so;
english:
my son, do not go along with them,
    do not set foot on their paths;

twi: Wɔn anan de ntɛmpɛ kɔ bɔne mu,na wɔde ahoɔhare ka mogya gu.
english:
for their feet rush into evil,
    they are swift to shed blood.

twi: So nni mfaso sɛ obi besum nnomaafiriwɔ beae a anomaa biara hu!
english:
How useless to spread a net
    where every bird can see it!

twi: Saa nnipa yi tetɛw pɛ wɔn ankasa mogya;wɔtetɛw wɔn ankasa wɔn ho!
english:
These men lie in wait for their own blood;
    they ambush only themselves!

twi: Saa na wɔn a wodi akorɔnne akyi no awiei te;ɛma wɔhwere wɔn nkwa!
english:
Such are the paths of all who go after ill-gotten gain;
    it takes away the life of those who get it.

twi: Nyansa A Wɔpo Ho KɔkɔbɔNyansa teɛ mu wɔ mmɔnten so,ɔma ne nne so wɔ aguabɔbea,
english:
Out in the open wisdom calls aloud,
    she raises her voice in the public square;

twi: ɔteɛ mu wɔ afasu no atifi,ɔkasa wɔ kuropɔn no apon ano se,
english:
on top of the wall she cries out,
    at the city gate she makes her speech:

twi: “Mo adwenharefo, mobɛyɛ adwenhare akosi da bɛn?Fɛwdifo bedi fɛw akosi da bɛn?Nkwaseafo bekyi nimdeɛ akosi da bɛn?
english:
“How long will you who are simple love your simple ways?
    How long will mockers delight in mockery
    and fools hate knowledge?

twi: Sɛ mutiee mʼanimka a,anka mekaa me koma mu nsɛm nyinaa kyerɛɛ moma muhuu me nsusuwii.
english:
Repent at my rebuke!
    Then I will pour out my thoughts to you,
    I will make known to you my teachings.

twi: Nanso sɛ muyii mo aso, bere a mefrɛɛ mona amfa obiara ho, bere a meteɛɛ me nsa mu,
english:
But since you refuse to listen when I call
    and no one pays attention when I stretch out my hand,

twi: sɛ mopoo mʼafotu,na moampɛ mʼanimka nti,
english:
since you disregard all my advice
    and do not accept my rebuke,

twi: me nso mɛserew mo wɔ mo amanehunu mu;sɛ abɛbrɛsɛ bi bu fa mo so a, midi mo ho fɛw,
english:
I in turn will laugh when disaster strikes you;
    I will mock when calamity overtakes you—

twi: sɛ abɛbrɛsɛ bi bu fa mo so te sɛ ahum,na amanehunu bi bɔ fa mo so sɛ mfɛtɛ,na awerɛhow ne ɔhaw mene mo a,
english:
when calamity overtakes you like a storm,
    when disaster sweeps over you like a whirlwind,
    when distress and trouble overwhelm you.

twi: “Afei wɔbɛfrɛ me, nanso meremmua;wɔbɛhwehwɛ me, nanso wɔrenhu me.
english:
“Then they will call to me but I will not answer;
    they will look for me but will not find me,

twi: Esiane sɛ wokyii nimdeɛna wɔampɛ sɛ wobesuro Awurade,
english:
since they hated knowledge
    and did not choose to fear the Lord.

twi: sɛ wɔpoo mʼafotu,na wobuu me nteɛso animtiaa nti,
english:
Since they would not accept my advice
    and spurned my rebuke,

twi: wobedi wɔn akwan so aba;na wɔn nhyehyɛe mu aduan bɛmee wɔn.
english:
they will eat the fruit of their ways
    and be filled with the fruit of their schemes.

twi: Na ntetekwaafo asoɔden bekum wɔn,na nkwaseafo tirimudɛ bɛsɛe wɔn;
english:
For the waywardness of the simple will kill them,
    and the complacency of fools will destroy them;

twi: Nanso obiara a obetie me no, ɔbɛtena ase asomdwoe muna ne ho bɛtɔ no a ɔrensuro ɔhaw biara.”
english:
but whoever listens to me will live in safety
    and be at ease, without fear of harm.”

twi: Nyansa So Mfaso Wɔ Abrabɔ MuMe ba, sɛ wutie me nsɛm,na woma me mmaransɛm tena wo mu a,
english:
My son, if you accept my words
    and store up my commands within you,

twi: sɛ wowɛn wʼaso ma nyansana wode wo koma ma ntease,
english:
turning your ear to wisdom
    and applying your heart to understanding—

twi: na woma wo nne so frɛ nhumuna wusu frɛ ntease,
english:
indeed, if you call out for insight
    and cry aloud for understanding,

twi: na sɛ wohwehwɛ no te sɛnea wohwehwɛ dwetɛna wohwehwɛ no sɛnea worepɛ ademude a ahintaw a,
english:
and if you look for it as for silver
    and search for it as for hidden treasure,

twi: ɛno na wobɛte Awurade suro asena woahu Onyankopɔn ho nimdeɛ.
english:
then you will understand the fear of the Lord
    and find the knowledge of God.

twi: Awurade ma nimdeɛ,na nʼanom na nyansa ne ntease fi ba.
english:
For the Lord gives wisdom;
    from his mouth come knowledge and understanding.

twi: Ɔkora nkonimdi ma wɔn a wɔteɛ,ɔyɛ kyɛm ma wɔn a wɔn akwan yɛ pɛ,
english:
He holds success in store for the upright,
    he is a shield to those whose walk is blameless,

twi: ɔwɛn nea ɔyɛ pɛ kwan,na ɔbɔ wɔn a wodi no nokware no akwan ho ban.
english:
for he guards the course of the just
    and protects the way of his faithful ones.

twi: Ɛno na wobɛte nea eye ne nea ɛyɛ pɛ,ne nea ɛfata, ɔkwan biara a eye ase.
english:
Then you will understand what is right and just
    and fair—every good path.

twi: Afei nyansa bewura wo koma mu,na nimdeɛ ayɛ ahomeka ama wo kra.
english:
For wisdom will enter your heart,
    and knowledge will be pleasant to your soul.

twi: Adwene bɛbɔ wo ho banna ntease ahwɛ wo so.
english:
Discretion will protect you,
    and understanding will guard you.

twi: Nyansa beyi wo afi amumɔyɛfo akwan mu,ebeyi wo afi nnipa a wɔn nsɛm yɛ basabasa nsam,
english:
Wisdom will save you from the ways of wicked men,
    from men whose words are perverse,

twi: wɔn a wɔaman afi akwan pa soakɔnantew sum akwan so no,
english:
who have left the straight paths
    to walk in dark ways,

twi: wɔn a wɔn ani gye bɔneyɛ ho,na wodi ahurusi wɔ bɔne mu basabasayɛ ho,
english:
who delight in doing wrong
    and rejoice in the perverseness of evil,

twi: wɔn a wɔn akwan yɛ kɔntɔnkyena wɔyɛ abonsam wɔ wɔn akwan mu.
english:
whose paths are crooked
    and who are devious in their ways.

twi: Nimdeɛ begye wo afi ɔbea waresɛefo no nsam,afi ɔbea warefo huhuni a ɔka nnaadaasɛm ho,
english:
Wisdom will save you also from the adulterous woman,
    from the wayward woman with her seductive words,

twi: nea wagyaa ne mmabaabere mu kununa wapo apam a ɔyɛɛ wɔ Onyankopɔn anim no.
english:
who has left the partner of her youth
    and ignored the covenant she made before God.

twi: Ne fi yɛ ɔkwan a ɛkɔ owu muna nʼakwan kɔ awufo honhom nkyɛn.
english:
Surely her house leads down to death
    and her paths to the spirits of the dead.

twi: Obiara a ɔkɔ ne nkyɛn no nsan mmaanaasɛ ɔrensi nkwa akwan so.
english:
None who go to her return
    or attain the paths of life.

twi: Enti wubedi nnipa pa anammɔn akyina woanantew atreneefo akwan so.
english:
Thus you will walk in the ways of the good
    and keep to the paths of the righteous.

twi: Efisɛ wɔn a wɔteɛ bɛtena asase no so,na wɔn a asɛm nni wɔn ho no na wɔbɛka hɔ;
english:
For the upright will live in the land,
    and the blameless will remain in it;

twi: na wobetwa amumɔyɛfo afi asase no so,na wɔatɔre atorofo ase.
english:
but the wicked will be cut off from the land,
    and the unfaithful will be torn from it.

twi: Nyansa De Yiyedi BaMe ba, mma wo werɛ mfi me nkyerɛkyerɛ,kora me mmara wɔ wo koma mu,
english:
My son, do not forget my teaching,
    but keep my commands in your heart,

twi: na ɛbɛma wo nkwa aware, mfe bebreena ɛde yiyedi abrɛ wo.
english:
for they will prolong your life many years
    and bring you peace and prosperity.

twi: Mma adɔe ne nokware mmfi wo nkyɛnfa yan wo kɔn mukyerɛw gu wo koma pon so.
Na wubenya adom ne din pawɔ Onyankopɔn ne nnipa anim.
english:
Then you will win favor and a good name
    in the sight of God and man.

twi: Fa wo koma nyinaa to Awurade so,na mfa wo ho nto wʼankasa ntease so;
english:
Trust in the Lord with all your heart
    and lean not on your own understanding;

twi: hu no wʼakwan nyinaa mu,na ɔbɛteɛ wʼakwan.
english:
in all your ways submit to him,
    and he will make your paths straight.

twi: Nnye wo ho nni sɛ woyɛ onyansafo;suro Awurade na kyi bɔne.
english:
Do not be wise in your own eyes;
    fear the Lord and shun evil.

twi: Ɛde ahoɔden bɛbrɛ wo nipadua,na ayɛ aduan ama wo nnompe.
english:
This will bring health to your body
    and nourishment to your bones.

twi: Fa wʼahonya hyɛ Awurade anuonyam,ne wo nnɔbae a edi kan nyinaa;
english:
Honor the Lord with your wealth,
    with the firstfruits of all your crops;

twi: na ɛno na ɛbɛma wo pata ayɛ ma abu so,na nsa foforo abu afa wʼahina so.
english:
then your barns will be filled to overflowing,
    and your vats will brim over with new wine.

twi: Me ba, sɛ Awurade teɛ wo so a, tie no yiye,na mmu nʼanimka so,
english:
My son, do not despise the Lord’s discipline,
    and do not resent his rebuke,

twi: Efisɛ, obiara a Awurade pɛ nʼasɛm no, ɔtwe nʼaso,sɛnea agya teɛ ɔba a ɔdɔ no no.
english:
because the Lord disciplines those he loves,
    as a father the son he delights in.

twi: Nhyira nka onipa a ohu nyansa,onipa a onya ntease,
english:
Blessed are those who find wisdom,
    those who gain understanding,

twi: efisɛ, nimdeɛ so mfaso sen dwetɛ,na nea efi mu ba sen sikakɔkɔɔ.
english:
for she is more profitable than silver
    and yields better returns than gold.

twi: Ne bo yɛ den sen bota;na worentumi mfa wʼapɛde biara ntoto no ho.
english:
She is more precious than rubies;
    nothing you desire can compare with her.

twi: Nkwa tenten wɔ ne nsa nifa mu;ahonyade ne anuonyam wɔ ne nsa benkum mu.
english:
Long life is in her right hand;
    in her left hand are riches and honor.

twi: Nʼakwan yɛ ahomeka,na nʼanammɔnkwan nyinaa yɛ asomdwoe.
english:
Her ways are pleasant ways,
    and all her paths are peace.

twi: Ɔyɛ nkwadua ma wɔn a woso ne mu;wɔn a wokura no mu no benya nhyira.
english:
She is a tree of life to those who take hold of her;
    those who hold her fast will be blessed.

twi: Nyansa mu na Awurade yɛɛ asase fapem,na ntease mu na ɔde ɔsoro tim hɔ.
english:
By wisdom the Lord laid the earth’s foundations,
    by understanding he set the heavens in place;

twi: Efi ne nimdeɛ mu na ɔkyekyɛɛ ebun mu,na omununkum nso tɔɔ obosu.
english:
by his knowledge the watery depths were divided,
    and the clouds let drop the dew.

twi: Me ba, fa atemmu pa ne nhumu sie,na mma emfi wʼani so;
english:
My son, do not let wisdom and understanding out of your sight,
    preserve sound judgment and discretion;

twi: ɛbɛyɛ nkwa ama wo,nnwinne a ɛma wo kɔn anuonyam wie pɛyɛ.
english:
they will be life for you,
    an ornament to grace your neck.

twi: Afei wo kwan so bɛyɛ wo dwoodwoo,na wo nan renhintiw;
english:
Then you will go on your way in safety,
    and your foot will not stumble.

twi: sɛ woda a worensuro;sɛ woda a wʼani bekum.
english:
When you lie down, you will not be afraid;
    when you lie down, your sleep will be sweet.

twi: Nsuro mpofirim amanehunuanaa ɔsɛe a ɛba amumɔyɛfo so,
english:
Have no fear of sudden disaster
    or of the ruin that overtakes the wicked,

twi: efisɛ Awurade bɛwɔ wʼafana ɔbɛkora wo nan afi afiri mu.
english:
for the Lord will be at your side
    and will keep your foot from being snared.

twi: Mfa ade pa nkame wɔn a wɔfata,bere a tumi wɔ wo nsam.
english:
Do not withhold good from those to whom it is due,
    when it is in your power to act.

twi: Nka nkyerɛ wo yɔnko se:“Kɔ na bra; mede bɛma wo ɔkyena”wɔ bere a wowɔ no saa bere no.
english:
Do not say to your neighbor,
    “Come back tomorrow and I’ll give it to you”—
    when you already have it with you.

twi: Mpam ɔhaw mma wo yɔnkobere a ɔne wo te yiye.
english:
Do not plot harm against your neighbor,
    who lives trustfully near you.

twi: Mmɔ obi sobo kwabere a ɔnyɛɛ wo bɔne biara ɛ.
english:
Do not accuse anyone for no reason—
    when they have done you no harm.

twi: Mma wʼani mmere basabasayɛfo,na mfa nʼakwan no mu biara,
english:
Do not envy the violent
    or choose any of their ways.

twi: efisɛ Awurade kyi basabasayɛfona ɔde ne werɛ hyɛ ɔtreneeni mu.
english:
For the Lord detests the perverse
    but takes the upright into his confidence.

twi: Awurade nnome wɔ omumɔyɛfo fi so,na ohyira ɔtreneeni fi.
english:
The Lord’s curse is on the house of the wicked,
    but he blesses the home of the righteous.

twi: Odi fɛwdifo a wɔyɛ ahantan no ho fɛw,na ɔdom ahobrɛasefo ne wɔn a wɔhyɛ wɔn so no.
english:
He mocks proud mockers
    but shows favor to the humble and oppressed.

twi: Anyansafo benya anuonyam adi,nanso nkwaseafo de, ɔma wɔn anim gu ase.
english:
The wise inherit honor,
    but fools get only shame.

twi: Pere Hwehwɛ NyansaMe mma, muntie me, muntie agya nkyerɛkyerɛ;monyɛ aso na moanya ntease.
english:
Listen, my sons, to a father’s instruction;
    pay attention and gain understanding.

twi: Mema mo adesua a ɛkɔ anim,enti munnnyaa me nkyerɛkyerɛ mu.
english:
I give you sound learning,
    so do not forsake my teaching.

twi: Efisɛ na me nso, meyɛ mʼagya babarima,meda so yɛ akokoaa no, na me na ani gye me ho.
english:
For I too was a son to my father,
    still tender, and cherished by my mother.

twi: Na ɔkyerɛkyerɛɛ me se,“Ma me nsɛm nni wo koma mu dɛm,di me nkyerɛkyerɛ so na wubenya nkwa.
Nya nyansa, nya ntease;mma wo werɛ mfi me nsɛm anaa ntwe wo ho mfi ho.
english:
Get wisdom, get understanding;
    do not forget my words or turn away from them.

twi: Nnyaw nyansa hɔ, na ɛbɛbɔ wo ho ban;dɔ no, na ɛbɛhwɛ wo so.
english:
Do not forsake wisdom, and she will protect you;
    love her, and she will watch over you.

twi: Nyansa boro biribiara so; enti hwehwɛ nyansa.Ɛwɔ mu sɛ ne bo te sɛ wʼahode nyinaa de, nanso nya ntease.
english:
The beginning of wisdom is this: Get wisdom.
    Though it cost all you have, get understanding.

twi: Di no ni na ɛbɛma wo so;yɛ no atuu, na ɛbɛhyɛ wo anuonyam.
english:
Cherish her, and she will exalt you;
    embrace her, and she will honor you.

twi: Ɔde nkonimdi nhwiren hankare begu wo ti sona wama wo ahenkyɛw a ɛyɛ fɛ.”
english:
She will give you a garland to grace your head
    and present you with a glorious crown.”

twi: Me ba, tie na fa nea meka no,na wo nkwanna bɛyɛ bebree.
english:
Listen, my son, accept what I say,
    and the years of your life will be many.

twi: Mɛkyerɛ wo nyansa kwan sona mede wo afa akwan a ɛteɛ so.
english:
I instruct you in the way of wisdom
    and lead you along straight paths.

twi: Sɛ wonantew a, wʼanammɔntu bɛkɔ waana sɛ wutu mmirika a, worenhintiw.
english:
When you walk, your steps will not be hampered;
    when you run, you will not stumble.

twi: Di nkyerɛkyerɛ so; na nnyaa mu,bɔ ho ban yiye, efisɛ ɛyɛ wo nkwa.
english:
Hold on to instruction, do not let it go;
    guard it well, for it is your life.

twi: Ntu wo nan nsi amumɔyɛfo kwan sona nnantew abɔnefo kwan so.
english:
Do not set foot on the path of the wicked
    or walk in the way of evildoers.

twi: Kwati no, ntu kwan mfa so;dan fi so na kɔ wo kwan.
english:
Avoid it, do not travel on it;
    turn from it and go on your way.

twi: Efisɛ wɔnyɛɛ bɔne a wontumi nna;na wɔn nna tew yera kosi sɛ wɔbɛma obi ahwe ase.
english:
For they cannot rest until they do evil;
    they are robbed of sleep till they make someone stumble.

twi: Wodi amumɔyɛsɛm brodo,na wɔnom kitikitiyɛ nsa.
english:
They eat the bread of wickedness
    and drink the wine of violence.

twi: Atreneefo kwan te sɛ adekyee hann a edi kan,ɛkɔ so hyerɛn yiye kodu awia ketee.
english:
The path of the righteous is like the morning sun,
    shining ever brighter till the full light of day.

twi: Nanso amumɔyɛfo kwan te sɛ sum kabii;wonnim nea ɛma wohintiw.
english:
But the way of the wicked is like deep darkness;
    they do not know what makes them stumble.

twi: Me ba, yɛ aso ma nea meka;tie me nsɛm no yiye.
english:
My son, pay attention to what I say;
    turn your ear to my words.

twi: Mma emfi wʼani so,fa sie wo koma mu;
english:
Do not let them out of your sight,
    keep them within your heart;

twi: efisɛ, ɛyɛ nkwa ma wɔn a wohune akwahosan ma nipadua no nyinaa.
english:
for they are life to those who find them
    and health to one’s whole body.

twi: Ne nyinaa akyi, bɔ wo koma ho ban,efisɛ, ɛno ne wo nkwa asuti.
english:
Above all else, guard your heart,
    for everything you do flows from it.

twi: Mma oburu kasa mfi wʼano;mma nkontomposɛm mmɛn wʼano koraa.
english:
Keep your mouth free of perversity;
    keep corrupt talk far from your lips.

twi: Hwɛ wʼanim tee,na ma wʼani nkɔ nea ɛwɔ wʼanim no so.
english:
Let your eyes look straight ahead;
    fix your gaze directly before you.

twi: Bɔ ɔkwan tamaa ma wʼananna fa akwan a atim so.
english:
Give careful thought to the paths for your feet
    and be steadfast in all your ways.

twi: Mman mfa nifa anaa benkum;twe wo nan fi bɔne ho.
english:
Do not turn to the right or the left;
    keep your foot from evil.

twi: Aguamammɔ Ho KɔkɔbɔMe ba, yɛ aso ma me nyansa;tie me nhumu nsɛm no yiye,
english:
My son, pay attention to my wisdom,
    turn your ear to my words of insight,

twi: sɛnea ɛbɛma woahwɛ yiye,na wʼano akora nimdeɛ.
english:
that you may maintain discretion
    and your lips may preserve knowledge.

twi: Efisɛ ɔbea aguaman ano sosɔ ɛwo,na ne kasa yɛ fɔmm sen ngo;
english:
For the lips of the adulterous woman drip honey,
    and her speech is smoother than oil;

twi: nanso awiei no, ɛyɛ nwen sen bɔnwoma,ɛyɛ nam sɛ afoa anofanu.
english:
but in the end she is bitter as gall,
    sharp as a double-edged sword.

twi: Nʼanan kɔ owu mu;nʼanammɔntutu kɔ ɔda mu tee.
english:
Her feet go down to death;
    her steps lead straight to the grave.

twi: Onsusuw ɔkwan a ɛkɔ nkwa mu ho;nʼakwan yɛ kɔntɔnkye, nanso onnim.
english:
She gives no thought to the way of life;
    her paths wander aimlessly, but she does not know it.

twi: Enti afei, me mma, muntie me;Monntwe mo ho mmfi nea meka ho.
english:
Now then, my sons, listen to me;
    do not turn aside from what I say.

twi: Ɔkwan a ɛmmɛn no no na momfa so;mommmɛn ne fi pon ano,
english:
Keep to a path far from her,
    do not go near the door of her house,

twi: anyɛ saa a, mode mo ahoɔden bɛma afoforona mode mo mfe ama otirimɔdenfo,
english:
lest you lose your honor to others
    and your dignity to one who is cruel,

twi: anyɛ saa a, ahɔho bɛfom mo ahonyadena mo brɛ de ahonya akɔ afoforo fi.
english:
lest strangers feast on your wealth
    and your toil enrich the house of another.

twi: Mo nkwanna akyi, mubesi apini,bere a mo honam ne mo nipadua asa no.
english:
At the end of your life you will groan,
    when your flesh and body are spent.

twi: Na moaka se, “Na mikyi ahohyɛso!Me koma ampɛ nteɛso!
english:
You will say, “How I hated discipline!
    How my heart spurned correction!

twi: Manyɛ osetie amma mʼakyerɛkyerɛfona mantie me kwankyerɛfo asɛm.
english:
I would not obey my teachers
    or turn my ear to my instructors.

twi: Madu ɔsɛe anowɔ asafo no nyinaa mu.”
english:
And I was soon in serious trouble
    in the assembly of God’s people.”

twi: Nom nsu fi wʼankasa ahina mu,nsu a ɛteɛ fi wʼankasa abura mu.
english:
Drink water from your own cistern,
    running water from your own well.

twi: So ɛsɛ sɛ wʼasuti yiri fa mmɔnten sona wo nsuwa kokɔ ɔman aguabɔbea ana?
english:
Should your springs overflow in the streets,
    your streams of water in the public squares?

twi: Ma ɛnyɛ wo nko ara de,a wo ne ahɔho nkyɛ da.
english:
Let them be yours alone,
    never to be shared with strangers.

twi: Nhyira nka wʼasuburana wʼani nnye wo mmrantebere mu yere ho.
english:
May your fountain be blessed,
    and may you rejoice in the wife of your youth.

twi: Ɔte sɛ ɔtwe bere dɔfo, ɔwansan nuonyamfo;ma ne nufu nsɔ wʼani daana ne dɔ nkyekyere wo.
english:
A loving doe, a graceful deer—
    may her breasts satisfy you always,
    may you ever be intoxicated with her love.

twi: Me ba, adɛn nti na woma ɔbea aguaman kyekyere wo?Adɛn nti na woda ɔbarima foforo bi yere kokom?
english:
Why, my son, be intoxicated with another man’s wife?
    Why embrace the bosom of a wayward woman?

twi: Awurade hu onipa akwan nyinaa,na ɔhwehwɛ ne nyinaa mu.
english:
For your ways are in full view of the Lord,
    and he examines all your paths.

twi: Omumɔyɛfo nnebɔne sum no afiri;na ne bɔne ahama kyekyere no papee.
english:
The evil deeds of the wicked ensnare them;
    the cords of their sins hold them fast.

twi: Wobewu, esiane ahohyɛso a wonni nti,na wɔayera, esiane wɔn agyennyentwisɛm nti.
english:
For lack of discipline they will die,
    led astray by their own great folly.

twi: Agyimisɛm Ho KɔkɔbɔMe ba, sɛ woadi akagyinamu ama ɔyɔnko bi,sɛ wode wo biribi asi awowa ama obi,
english:
My son, if you have put up security for your neighbor,
    if you have shaken hands in pledge for a stranger,

twi: sɛ nea wokae ayi ka ama wona sɛ wʼano asɛm afiri ayi wo a,
english:
you have been trapped by what you said,
    ensnared by the words of your mouth.

twi: ɛno de yɛ eyi, me ba, na fa tetew wo ho,sɛ ɔyɔnko nsa aka wo no nti:fa ahobrɛase kɔ nʼanim;na kɔ so pa wo yɔnko no kyɛw!
english:
So do this, my son, to free yourself,
    since you have fallen into your neighbor’s hands:
Go—to the point of exhaustion—
    and give your neighbor no rest!

twi: Mma wʼani nkumna ntɔ nko.
english:
Allow no sleep to your eyes,
    no slumber to your eyelids.

twi: Gye wo ho, sɛnea ɔforote guan fi ɔbɔmmɔfo nsamanaa sɛnea anomaa guan fi ofirisumfo afiri mu no.
english:
Free yourself, like a gazelle from the hand of the hunter,
    like a bird from the snare of the fowler.

twi: Ɔkwadwofo, kɔ ɔtɛtea nkyɛn;hwɛ nʼakwan, na hu nyansa!
english:
Go to the ant, you sluggard;
    consider its ways and be wise!

twi: Onni ɔsahene,onni ɔhwɛfo anaa sodifo bi,
english:
It has no commander,
    no overseer or ruler,

twi: nanso ɔde aduan sie wɔ ahuhurubere mu,ɔboaboa nnuan ano wɔ twabere.
english:
yet it stores its provisions in summer
    and gathers its food at harvest.

twi: Wo, ɔkwadwofo, wobɛda akosi da bɛn?Wubenyan bere bɛn?
english:
How long will you lie there, you sluggard?
    When will you get up from your sleep?

twi: Nna kakra, nkotɔ kakra,nsa a woabobɔw de rehome kakra,
english:
A little sleep, a little slumber,
    a little folding of the hands to rest—

twi: ɛbɛma ohia aba wo so sɛ ɔkwanmukafona ahokyere atow akyere wo sɛnea okura otuo.
english:
and poverty will come on you like a thief
    and scarcity like an armed man.

twi: Onipa teta ne ohuhuni aodi atoro kyin,
english:
A troublemaker and a villain,
    who goes about with a corrupt mouth,

twi: nea obu nʼani,na ɔde ne nan yɛ nsɛnkyerɛnnena ɔde ne nsateaa kyerɛkyerɛ ade,
english:
who winks maliciously with his eye,
    signals with his feet
    and motions with his fingers,

twi: nea ɔde ne koma mu nnaadaa bɔ pɔw bɔne,na ɔde mpaapaemu ba bere biara.
english:
who plots evil with deceit in his heart—
    he always stirs up conflict.

twi: Ɛno nti amanehunu bɛba no so prɛko pɛ;wɔbɛsɛe no mpofirim, a wɔrenya ano aduru.
english:
Therefore disaster will overtake him in an instant;
    he will suddenly be destroyed—without remedy.

twi: Nneɛma asia na Awurade mpɛ,nneɛma ason na ɛyɛ nʼakyiwade:
english:
There are six things the Lord hates,
    seven that are detestable to him:

twi: ani a ɛtra ntɔn,atoro tɛkrɛma,nsa a ɛka mogya a edi bem gu,
english:
haughty eyes,
        a lying tongue,
        hands that shed innocent blood,

twi: koma a edwen amumɔyɛ ho,anan a etutu mmirika kɔyɛ bɔne,
english:
a heart that devises wicked schemes,
        feet that are quick to rush into evil,

twi: ɔdansekurumni a odi atorone onipa a ɔde mpaapaemu ba anuanom mu.
english:
a false witness who pours out lies
        and a person who stirs up conflict in the community.

twi: Aguamammɔ Ho KɔkɔbɔMe ba, tie wʼagya ahyɛdena nnyaa wo na nkyerɛkyerɛ mu.
english:
My son, keep your father’s command
    and do not forsake your mother’s teaching.

twi: Fa kyekyere wo koma ho daa;na fa kyekyere wɔ kɔn mu.
english:
Bind them always on your heart;
    fasten them around your neck.

twi: Wonantew a, ɛbɛkyerɛ wo kwan;sɛ woda a, ɛbɛwɛn wo;sɛ wunyan a, ɛbɛkasa akyerɛ wo.
Na saa ahyɛde yi yɛ kaneasaa nkyerɛkyerɛ yi yɛ hann,na ahohyɛso nteɛso yiyɛ nkwa kwan,
english:
For this command is a lamp,
    this teaching is a light,
and correction and instruction
    are the way to life,

twi: ɛtwe wo fi ɔbea a onni suban pa no ho,fi ɔbeawarefo huhuni tɛkrɛmadɛ ho.
english:
keeping you from your neighbor’s wife,
    from the smooth talk of a wayward woman.

twi: Mma wo kɔn nnɔ nʼahoɔfɛ,mma nʼani akyideda no ntwetwe wo,
english:
Do not lust in your heart after her beauty
    or let her captivate you with her eyes.

twi: efisɛ oguamanfo ma wʼanuonyam yɛ sɛ brodosin,na obi yere gyigye wo kɔ owu mu.
english:
For a prostitute can be had for a loaf of bread,
    but another man’s wife preys on your very life.

twi: Obi betumi asɔ gya agu ne srɛ so anhyew nʼatade ana?
english:
Can a man scoop fire into his lap
    without his clothes being burned?

twi: Obi betumi anantew nnyansramma so ampumpunnya mmobɔ nʼanan ho ana?
english:
Can a man walk on hot coals
    without his feet being scorched?

twi: Saa na ɔbarima a ɔne ɔbarima foforo yere da no te;obiara a ɔde ne nsa bɛka no no, remfa ne ho nni da.
english:
So is he who sleeps with another man’s wife;
    no one who touches her will go unpunished.

twi: Nnipa mmu ɔkorɔmfo a wakowia ade animtiaasɛ ɔkɔm de no na ɔde rekodwudwo ano nti.
english:
People do not despise a thief if he steals
    to satisfy his hunger when he is starving.

twi: Mmom, sɛ wɔkyere no a, ɛsɛ sɛ otua mmɔho ason;sɛ ɛbɛma wahwere ne fi agyapade nyinaa mpo a.
english:
Yet if he is caught, he must pay sevenfold,
    though it costs him all the wealth of his house.

twi: Ɔbarima a ɔsɛe aware no nni adwene;obiara a ɔyɛ saa no sɛe ne ho.
english:
But a man who commits adultery has no sense;
    whoever does so destroys himself.

twi: Ɔhwe ne animguase na obenya,na nʼahohora rempepa da.
english:
Blows and disgrace are his lot,
    and his shame will never be wiped away.

twi: Ninkutwe hwanyan okunu abufuwna sɛ ɔtɔ were a, ahummɔbɔ biara nni mu.
english:
For jealousy arouses a husband’s fury,
    and he will show no mercy when he takes revenge.

twi: Ɔrennye mpata biara;na ɔbɛpo adanmude, sɛ ɛso sɛ dɛn mpo a.
english:
He will not accept any compensation;
    he will refuse a bribe, however great it is.

twi: Ɔbeawaresɛefo Ho KɔkɔbɔMe ba, fa me nsɛm siena kora mʼahyɛde wɔ wo mu.
english:
My son, keep my words
    and store up my commands within you.

twi: Di mʼahyɛde so na wubenya nkwa;bɔ me nkyerɛkyerɛ ho ban sɛ nea wodɔ no.
english:
Keep my commands and you will live;
    guard my teachings as the apple of your eye.

twi: Kyekyere bɔ wo nsateaa ho;kyerɛw no yiye gu wo koma pon so.
english:
Bind them on your fingers;
    write them on the tablet of your heart.

twi: Ka kyerɛ nyansa se, “Woyɛ me nuabea,”na frɛ ntease wo busuani;
english:
Say to wisdom, “You are my sister,”
    and to insight, “You are my relative.”

twi: Wɔbɛtwe wo afi ɔbeawaresɛefo ho,afi ɔbeawarefo huhuni nsɛmmɔdɛ ho.
english:
They will keep you from the adulterous woman,
    from the wayward woman with her seductive words.

twi: Me fi mfɛnsere ano,mede mʼani faa mfɛnsere mu.
english:
At the window of my house
    I looked down through the lattice.

twi: Mihuu wɔ ntetekwaafo mu,mehyɛɛ mmerante no mu baako nsow,ɔbabun a onni adwene.
english:
I saw among the simple,
    I noticed among the young men,
    a youth who had no sense.

twi: Na ɔnam borɔn a ɛbɛn ɔbea no fi soa nʼani kyerɛ ɔbea no fi
english:
He was going down the street near her corner,
    walking along in the direction of her house

twi: bere a onwini redwo,na anim rebiribiri no.
english:
at twilight, as the day was fading,
    as the dark of night set in.

twi: Afei ɔbea bi fi behyiaa no awasiesie ne ho sɛ oguamanfo a nnaadaa wɔ ne koma mu.
english:
Then out came a woman to meet him,
    dressed like a prostitute and with crafty intent.

twi: (Ɔyɛ hyirenn na hwee mfa ne ho,ɔntena fie koraa;
english:
(She is unruly and defiant,
    her feet never stay at home;

twi: nnɛ wohu no mmɔnten so, ɔkyena na ɔte aguabɔbea,ɔtetɛw wɔ mmantwea mmantwea.)
english:
now in the street, now in the squares,
    at every corner she lurks.)

twi: Osoo ne mu few nʼano,wamfɛre, na ɔkae se,
english:
She took hold of him and kissed him
    and with a brazen face she said:

twi: “Mewɔ asomdwoe afɔrebɔde wɔ fie;nnɛ madi me bɔhyɛ so.
english:
“Today I fulfilled my vows,
    and I have food from my fellowship offering at home.

twi: Enti mebae sɛ merebehyia wo;mehwehwɛɛ wo na mahu wo!
english:
So I came out to meet you;
    I looked for you and have found you!

twi: Mato me mpa,mede nwera a wɔahyɛ no aduru a efi Misraim.
english:
I have covered my bed
    with colored linens from Egypt.

twi: Mede nnuhuam apete me mpa so:kurobow, pɛprɛ ne dupapo.
english:
I have perfumed my bed
    with myrrh, aloes and cinnamon.

twi: Bra, ma yɛmfa ɔdɔ mmɔ ɔdɔ mu nkosi anɔpa;
english:
Come, let’s drink deeply of love till morning;
    let’s enjoy ourselves with love!

twi: Me kunu nni fie;watu kwan na ɔbɛkyɛ.
english:
My husband is not at home;
    he has gone on a long journey.

twi: Ɔde sika a ɛdɔɔso hyɛɛ ne sika kotoku mana ɔremma kosi ɔsram no kurokumatwa bere mu.”
english:
He took his purse filled with money
    and will not be home till full moon.”

twi: Ɔde tɛkrɛmakyene bɔɔ no adafa;ɔde nnaadaa nyaa no ne no dae.
english:
With persuasive words she led him astray;
    she seduced him with her smooth talk.

twi: Odii nʼakyi prɛko pɛte sɛ nantwi a ɔrekɔ akumii,anaa ɔwansan a ɔde ne ti rekɔhyɛ hankare fi mu
english:
All at once he followed her
    like an ox going to the slaughter,
like a deer stepping into a noose

twi: kosi sɛ bɛmma bɛwɔ ne brɛbo mu,te sɛ anomaa a ɔrekɔtɔ anomaa afiri muna onnim sɛ ɔbɛhwere ne nkwa.
english:
till an arrow pierces his liver,
like a bird darting into a snare,
    little knowing it will cost him his life.

twi: Na afei, me mma, muntie me;monyɛ aso mma nea meka.
english:
Now then, my sons, listen to me;
    pay attention to what I say.

twi: Mommma mo koma mpatiri nkɔ no sona momman mmfa nʼakwan so.
english:
Do not let your heart turn to her ways
    or stray into her paths.

twi: Bebree na wɔnam no so ahwehwe ase;wɔn a wakum wɔn dɔɔso pa ara.
english:
Many are the victims she has brought down;
    her slain are a mighty throng.

twi: Ne fi yɛ ɔda tempɔn aɛkɔ owu pia mu.
english:
Her house is a highway to the grave,
    leading down to the chambers of death.

twi: Nyansa FrɛTie: Nyansa refrɛ.Ntease ma ne nne so.
english:
Does not wisdom call out?
    Does not understanding raise her voice?

twi: Ɔkwan no so, sorɔnsorɔmmea hɔ,nkwantanan no so, ɛhɔ na egyina,
english:
At the highest point along the way,
    where the paths meet, she takes her stand;

twi: apon a ɛkɔ kuropɔn no mu no ho,ɛteɛ mu wɔ abobow ano hɔ se,
english:
beside the gate leading into the city,
    at the entrance, she cries aloud:

twi: “Ao, mo nnipa na meteɛ mu refrɛ;meteɛ mu frɛ adesamma nyinaa.
english:
“To you, O people, I call out;
    I raise my voice to all mankind.

twi: Mo a moyɛ ntetekwaa, momma mo ani ntew;mo a moyɛ nkwaseafo, munnya ntease.
english:
You who are simple, gain prudence;
    you who are foolish, set your hearts on it.

twi: Muntie, na mewɔ nsɛm pa bi ka kyerɛ mo;mibue mʼano ka nea eye.
english:
Listen, for I have trustworthy things to say;
    I open my lips to speak what is right.

twi: Mʼano ka nea ɛyɛ nokware,efisɛ mʼanofafa kyi amumɔyɛsɛm.
english:
My mouth speaks what is true,
    for my lips detest wickedness.

twi: Mʼanom nsɛm nyinaa yɛ pɛ;biara nni mu a ɛyɛ nkontompo anaa nnaadaasɛm.
english:
All the words of my mouth are just;
    none of them is crooked or perverse.

twi: Ne nyinaa mu da hɔ ma nea ɔwɔ nhumu;ɛho nni asɛm ma wɔn a wɔwɔ nimdeɛ.
english:
To the discerning all of them are right;
    they are upright to those who have found knowledge.

twi: Mompo dwetɛ na momfa mʼakwankyerɛ,momfa nimdeɛ na mompo sikakɔkɔɔ ankasa.
english:
Choose my instruction instead of silver,
    knowledge rather than choice gold,

twi: Efisɛ nimdeɛ som bo sen bota,na worentumi mfa nea wopɛ biara ntoto no ho.
english:
for wisdom is more precious than rubies,
    and nothing you desire can compare with her.

twi: “Me, nyansa, mene anitew na ɛte;nimdeɛ ne nhumu wɔ me.
english:
“I, wisdom, dwell together with prudence;
    I possess knowledge and discretion.

twi: Sɛ wosuro Awurade ɛne sɛ wokyi bɔne;mikyi ahantan ne ahomaso,ɔbra bɔne ne nnaadaasɛm.
Afotu ne atemmu pa wɔ me;mewɔ ntease ne tumi.
english:
Counsel and sound judgment are mine;
    I have insight, I have power.

twi: Me so na ahemfo nam di adena sodifo nam me so hyehyɛ mmara a ɛyɛ pɛ;
english:
By me kings reign
    and rulers issue decrees that are just;

twi: Mmapɔmma de me bu ɔmanne atitiriw nyinaa a wodi asase so hene.
english:
by me princes govern,
    and nobles—all who rule on earth.

twi: Medɔ wɔn a wɔdɔ me,na wɔn a wɔhwehwɛ me no hu me.
english:
I love those who love me,
    and those who seek me find me.

twi: Ahonyade ne anuonyam wɔ me nkyɛn,ahode a ɛkyɛ ne yiyedi nso saa ara.
english:
With me are riches and honor,
    enduring wealth and prosperity.

twi: Mʼaba ye sen sikakɔkɔɔ ankasa;nea efi me mu boro dwetɛ a wɔasɔn so so.
english:
My fruit is better than fine gold;
    what I yield surpasses choice silver.

twi: Trenee akwan so na menam,atɛntrenee akwan so,
english:
I walk in the way of righteousness,
    along the paths of justice,

twi: mede ahode ma wɔn a wɔdɔ mena mehyɛ wɔn adekoradan amaama.
english:
bestowing a rich inheritance on those who love me
    and making their treasuries full.

twi: “Awurade bɔɔ me sɛ nʼabɔde mu abakandii ne tete nneyɛe anim;
english:
“The Lord brought me forth as the first of his works,
    before his deeds of old;

twi: oyii me sii hɔ fi tete,ansa na wiase refi ase.
english:
I was formed long ages ago,
    at the very beginning, when the world came to be.

twi: Wɔwoo me ansa na wɔrebɔ po kakraka no,ansa na wɔreyɛ nsuti a nsu ahyɛ no ma no,
english:
When there were no watery depths, I was given birth,
    when there were no springs overflowing with water;

twi: ansa na wɔde mmepɔw resisi hɔ;wɔwoo me ansa na nkoko reba,
english:
before the mountains were settled in place,
    before the hills, I was given birth,

twi: ansa na ɔbɔɔ asase ne ne mfuwanaa dɔte biara a ɛwɔ asase so.
english:
before he made the world or its fields
    or any of the dust of the earth.

twi: Mewɔ hɔ ansa na wɔbɔɔ ɔsoro,bere a otwaa ɔhye too ebun no ani no,
english:
I was there when he set the heavens in place,
    when he marked out the horizon on the face of the deep,

twi: bere a ɔbɔɔ omununkum wɔ sorona ɔde ebun mu nsuti tintim hɔ dennen no;
english:
when he established the clouds above
    and fixed securely the fountains of the deep,

twi: bere a otwaa ɔhye maa posɛnea nsu no rentra ne hye,ne bere a otwaa asase fapem no,
english:
when he gave the sea its boundary
    so the waters would not overstep his command,
and when he marked out the foundations of the earth.

twi: na meyɛ odwumfo a mete ne nkyɛn.Anigye hyɛɛ me ma daana midii ahurusi wɔ nʼanim bere biara,
english:
Then I was constantly at his side.
I was filled with delight day after day,
    rejoicing always in his presence,

twi: na mʼani gye wɔ ne wiase nyinaa muna mʼani ka wɔ adesamma mu.
english:
rejoicing in his whole world
    and delighting in mankind.

twi: “Enti me mma, muntie me;nhyira ne wɔn a wɔnantew mʼakwan so.
english:
“Now then, my children, listen to me;
    blessed are those who keep my ways.

twi: Muntie mʼakwankyerɛ na munhu nyansa;mummmu mo ani ngu so.
english:
Listen to my instruction and be wise;
    do not disregard it.

twi: Nhyira ne onipa a otie me,ɔwɛn mʼabobow ano daa,na ɔtwɛn wɔ hɔ.
english:
Blessed are those who listen to me,
    watching daily at my doors,
    waiting at my doorway.

twi: Na obiara a ohu me no nya nkwa,na onya anisɔ fi Awurade nkyɛn.
english:
For those who find me find life
    and receive favor from the Lord.

twi: Na nea wanhwehwɛ me no haw ne hona wɔn a wɔtan me no dɔ owu.”
english:
But those who fail to find me harm themselves;
    all who hate me love death.”

twi: Nyansa Ne Nkwaseasɛm FrɛNyansa asi ne fi;wasisi nʼafadum ason.
english:
Wisdom has built her house;
    she has set up its seven pillars.

twi: Wasiesie ne nam de afra ne nsa,wato ne pon.
english:
She has prepared her meat and mixed her wine;
    she has also set her table.

twi: Wasoma ne mmaawa, na ɔfrɛfi kuropɔn no sorɔnsorɔmmea hɔ se,
english:
She has sent out her servants, and she calls
    from the highest point of the city,

twi: “Momma ntetekwaafo nyinaa mmra ha!”Ɔka kyerɛ wɔn a wonni atemmu se,
english:
“Let all who are simple come to my house!”
To those who have no sense she says,

twi: “Mommra mmedi mʼaduanna monnom nsa a mafra no.
english:
“Come, eat my food
    and drink the wine I have mixed.

twi: Munnyaw mo ntetekwaasɛm no na mubenya nkwa;monnantew ntease akwan so.”
english:
Leave your simple ways and you will live;
    walk in the way of insight.”

twi: Nea ɔteɛteɛ ɔfɛwdifo no frɛ ahohorabɔ;na nea ɔka amumɔyɛfo anim no nya ɔyaw.
english:
Whoever corrects a mocker invites insults;
    whoever rebukes the wicked incurs abuse.

twi: Ɛno nti, nka ɔfɛwdifo anim na ɔmmɛtan wo;ka onyansafo anim na ɔbɛdɔ wo.
english:
Do not rebuke mockers or they will hate you;
    rebuke the wise and they will love you.

twi: Ma onyansafo akwankyerɛ na ɔbɛkɔ so ahu nyansa;kyerɛkyerɛ ɔtreneeni na ɔde bɛka nʼadesua ho.
english:
Instruct the wise and they will be wiser still;
    teach the righteous and they will add to their learning.

twi: Awurade suro yɛ nyansa mfiaseƆkronkronni no ho nimdeɛ yɛ ntease.
english:
The fear of the Lord is the beginning of wisdom,
    and knowledge of the Holy One is understanding.

twi: Me mu na wo nna bɛdɔɔso,na wɔde mfe bɛka wo nkwa ho.
english:
For through wisdom your days will be many,
    and years will be added to your life.

twi: Sɛ woyɛ onyansafo a, wubenya wo nyansa so mfaso;sɛ woyɛ ɔfɛwdifo a, wo nko ara na wubehu amane.
english:
If you are wise, your wisdom will reward you;
    if you are a mocker, you alone will suffer.

twi: Ɔbea ɔkwasea yɛ ɔkasafo;onni ahohyɛso na onni nimdeɛ.
english:
Folly is an unruly woman;
    she is simple and knows nothing.

twi: Ɔte ne fi pon ano,na ɔte akongua a esi kuropɔn no sorɔnsorɔmmea,
english:
She sits at the door of her house,
    on a seat at the highest point of the city,

twi: na ɔfrɛfrɛ wɔn a wotwa mu wɔ hɔ,wɔn a wɔnam wɔn kwan so tee se,
english:
calling out to those who pass by,
    who go straight on their way,

twi: “Momma ntetekwaafo nyinaa mmra ha”ɔka kyerɛ wɔn a wonni atemmu se,
english:
“Let all who are simple come to my house!”
To those who have no sense she says,

twi: “Nsu a wowia no yɛ fremfremna aduan a wodi no ahintawee no yɛ dɛ!”
english:
“Stolen water is sweet;
    food eaten in secret is delicious!”

twi: Nanso wonnim koraa sɛ awufo wɔ hɔsɛ nʼahɔho wɔ ɔda no ase tɔnn.
english:
But little do they know that the dead are there,
    that her guests are deep in the realm of the dead.

twi: Salomo MmebusɛmSalomo mmebusɛm:Ɔba nyansafo ma nʼagya ani gye,na ɔba kwasea brɛ ne na awerɛhow.
english:
The proverbs of Solomon:
A wise son brings joy to his father,
    but a foolish son brings grief to his mother.

twi: Ɔkwan bɔne so ahonya nni bo,nanso trenee gye onipa fi owu mu.
english:
Ill-gotten treasures have no lasting value,
    but righteousness delivers from death.

twi: Awurade remma ɔkɔm nne ɔtreneenina omumɔyɛfo de, ɔka nʼadepa gu.
english:
The Lord does not let the righteous go hungry,
    but he thwarts the craving of the wicked.

twi: Nsa a ɛnyɛ adwuma ma onipa di hia,nanso nsiyɛfo nsa de ahonya ba.
english:
Lazy hands make for poverty,
    but diligent hands bring wealth.

twi: Nea ɔboaboa nnɔbae ano wɔ ahuhurubere no yɛ ɔba nyansafona nea ɔda wɔ twabere mu no yɛ ɔba nimguaseni.
english:
He who gathers crops in summer is a prudent son,
    but he who sleeps during harvest is a disgraceful son.

twi: Atreneefo hyɛ nhyira kyɛwna akakabensɛm ayɛ omumɔyɛfo anom ma.
english:
Blessings crown the head of the righteous,
    but violence overwhelms the mouth of the wicked.

twi: Ɔtreneeni nkae yɛ nhyira,na omumɔyɛfo din bɛporɔw.
english:
The name of the righteous is used in blessings,
    but the name of the wicked will rot.

twi: Koma mu nyansafo tie ɔhyɛ nsɛm,na ɔkwasea kasafo hwe ase.
english:
The wise in heart accept commands,
    but a chattering fool comes to ruin.

twi: Ɔnokwafo nantew dwoodwoo,na nea ɔfa akwan kɔntɔnkye so no ho bɛda adi.
english:
Whoever walks in integrity walks securely,
    but whoever takes crooked paths will be found out.

twi: Nea ɔde nitan bu nʼani no de ɔhaw ba,na ɔkwasea kasafo hwe ase.
english:
Whoever winks maliciously causes grief,
    and a chattering fool comes to ruin.

twi: Ɔtreneeni anom yɛ nkwa asuti,na akakabensɛm ayɛ omumɔyɛfo anom ma.
english:
The mouth of the righteous is a fountain of life,
    but the mouth of the wicked conceals violence.

twi: Ɔtan kanyan mpaapaemu,nanso ɔdɔ kata mfomso nyinaa so.
english:
Hatred stirs up conflict,
    but love covers over all wrongs.

twi: Wohu nyansa wɔ nhumufo anom,na abaa fata nea onni adwene akyi.
english:
Wisdom is found on the lips of the discerning,
    but a rod is for the back of one who has no sense.

twi: Anyansafo kora nimdeɛ,nanso ɔkwasea ano frɛfrɛ ɔsɛe.
english:
The wise store up knowledge,
    but the mouth of a fool invites ruin.

twi: Adefo ahonya yɛ wɔn kuropɔn a wɔabɔ ho ban,nanso ahiafo hia yɛ wɔn asehwe.
english:
The wealth of the rich is their fortified city,
    but poverty is the ruin of the poor.

twi: Atreneefo akatua de nkwa brɛ wɔn,na nea amumɔyɛfo nya no de asotwe brɛ wɔn.
english:
The wages of the righteous is life,
    but the earnings of the wicked are sin and death.

twi: Nea otie ntetew pa no kyerɛ nkwa kwan,na nea ɔpo nteɛso no di afoforo anim yera kwan.
english:
Whoever heeds discipline shows the way to life,
    but whoever ignores correction leads others astray.

twi: Nea ɔkata nitan so no yɛ ɔtorofo,na nea odi nseku no yɛ ɔkwasea.
english:
Whoever conceals hatred with lying lips
    and spreads slander is a fool.

twi: Mfomso mpa ɔkasa bebree mu,na nea ɔkora ne tɛkrɛma no yɛ onyansafo.
english:
Sin is not ended by multiplying words,
    but the prudent hold their tongues.

twi: Ɔtreneeni tɛkrɛma yɛ dwetɛ ankasananso omumɔyɛfo koma nni bo.
english:
The tongue of the righteous is choice silver,
    but the heart of the wicked is of little value.

twi: Atreneefo ano ma bebree aduan,na atemmu a nkwaseafo nni nti wowuwu.
english:
The lips of the righteous nourish many,
    but fools die for lack of sense.

twi: Awurade nhyira de ahonya ba,na ɔmfa ɔbrɛ mmata ne nya ho.
english:
The blessing of the Lord brings wealth,
    without painful toil for it.

twi: Bɔneyɛ yɛ anigyede ma ɔkwasea,nanso nea ɔwɔ nimdeɛ anigye wɔ nyansa mu.
english:
A fool finds pleasure in wicked schemes,
    but a person of understanding delights in wisdom.

twi: Nea amumɔyɛfo suro no bɛba wɔn so;na nea atreneefo pɛ no, wɔde bɛma wɔn.
english:
What the wicked dread will overtake them;
    what the righteous desire will be granted.

twi: Sɛ ahum no betwa mu a, amumɔyɛfo yera,nanso atreneefo gyina hɔ pintinn afebɔɔ.
english:
When the storm has swept by, the wicked are gone,
    but the righteous stand firm forever.

twi: Sɛnea nsa keka ɛse, na wusiw kɔ aniwa no,saa ara na ɔkwadwofo yɛ ma wɔn a wɔsoma no.
english:
As vinegar to the teeth and smoke to the eyes,
    so are sluggards to those who send them.

twi: Awurade suro ma nkwa tenten,nanso wotwa amumɔyɛfo nkwa so.
english:
The fear of the Lord adds length to life,
    but the years of the wicked are cut short.

twi: Atreneefo anidaso de ahotɔ ba,nanso amumɔyɛfo anidaso nkosi hwee.
english:
The prospect of the righteous is joy,
    but the hopes of the wicked come to nothing.

twi: Awurade kwan yɛ guankɔbea ma ɔtreneeni,nanso ɛyɛ ɔsɛe ma wɔn a wɔyɛ bɔne.
english:
The way of the Lord is a refuge for the blameless,
    but it is the ruin of those who do evil.

twi: Wɔrentɔre atreneefo ase da,nanso amumɔyɛfo renka asase no so.
english:
The righteous will never be uprooted,
    but the wicked will not remain in the land.

twi: Nyansa fi ɔtreneeni anom bananso tɛkrɛma a ɛdaadaa no, wobetwa akyene.
english:
From the mouth of the righteous comes the fruit of wisdom,
    but a perverse tongue will be silenced.

twi: Ɔtreneeni ano nim ade a ɛfatana omumɔyɛfo ano nim nea ɛyɛ nnaadaasɛm nko ara.
english:
The lips of the righteous know what finds favor,
    but the mouth of the wicked only what is perverse.

twi: Awurade kyi asisi nsania,na nʼani gye nokware nkaribo ho.
english:
The Lord detests dishonest scales,
    but accurate weights find favor with him.

twi: Ahantan ba a, animguase na edi so,nanso ahobrɛase de nyansa ba.
english:
When pride comes, then comes disgrace,
    but with humility comes wisdom.

twi: Teefo nokwaredi kyerɛ wɔn kwan;nanso nkontompofo ano ntanta sɛe wɔn.
english:
The integrity of the upright guides them,
    but the unfaithful are destroyed by their duplicity.

twi: Ahonya nka hwee wɔ abufuwhyew da no,nanso trenee gye nkwa fi owu mu.
english:
Wealth is worthless in the day of wrath,
    but righteousness delivers from death.

twi: Wɔn a wonni bɔne no trenee bɔ kwan tee ma wɔn,nanso amumɔyɛfo amumɔyɛsɛm brɛ wɔn ase.
english:
The righteousness of the blameless makes their paths straight,
    but the wicked are brought down by their own wickedness.

twi: Pɛyɛfo treneeyɛ gye wɔn,nanso akɔnnɔ bɔne afiri yi nkontompofo.
english:
The righteousness of the upright delivers them,
    but the unfaithful are trapped by evil desires.

twi: Sɛ omumɔyɛfo wu a, nʼanidaso yera;nea osusuw sɛ obenya afi ne tumi mu nyinaa no yɛ ɔkwa.
english:
Hopes placed in mortals die with them;
    all the promise of their power comes to nothing.

twi: Wogye ɔtreneeni fi amane mu,na ɛba omumɔyɛfo so mmom.
english:
The righteous person is rescued from trouble,
    and it falls on the wicked instead.

twi: Nea onsuro Onyame de nʼano sɛe ne yɔnko,nanso ɔtreneeni nam nimdeɛ so fi mu.
english:
With their mouths the godless destroy their neighbors,
    but through knowledge the righteous escape.

twi: Sɛ atreneefo di yiye a, kuropɔn no di ahurusi;nanso amumɔyɛfo wu a, wɔbɔ ose.
english:
When the righteous prosper, the city rejoices;
    when the wicked perish, there are shouts of joy.

twi: Pɛyɛfo nhyira ma kuropɔn no kɔ so,nanso amumɔyɛfo ano ma ɛbɔ.
english:
Through the blessing of the upright a city is exalted,
    but by the mouth of the wicked it is destroyed.

twi: Onipa a onni adwene no bu ne yɔnko animtiaa,nanso nea ɔwɔ nhumu no to ne tɛkrɛma nnareka.
english:
Whoever derides their neighbor has no sense,
    but the one who has understanding holds their tongue.

twi: Nsekudi sɛe ahotoso,nanso nea wɔwɔ ne mu ahotoso no kora ahintasɛm.
english:
A gossip betrays a confidence,
    but a trustworthy person keeps a secret.

twi: Ɔman a enni akwankyerɛ no bɔ,nanso afotufo dodow ma nkonimdi ba.
english:
For lack of guidance a nation falls,
    but victory is won through many advisers.

twi: Nea odi akagyinamu ma ɔfoforo no behu amane,na nea ɔmmfa ne nsa nhyɛ awowasi ase no aso mu dwo no.
english:
Whoever puts up security for a stranger will surely suffer,
    but whoever refuses to shake hands in pledge is safe.

twi: Ɔbea a ne yam ye no, wɔde obu ma no,nanso mmarima atirimɔdenfo nya ahode nkutoo.
english:
A kindhearted woman gains honor,
    but ruthless men gain only wealth.

twi: Ɔyamyefo ye ma ne ho,na otirimɔdenfo de ɔhaw ba nʼankasa so.
english:
Those who are kind benefit themselves,
    but the cruel bring ruin on themselves.

twi: Omumɔyɛfo nya akatua a ennyina,nanso nea ogu trenee aba no twa aba a edi mu.
english:
A wicked person earns deceptive wages,
    but the one who sows righteousness reaps a sure reward.

twi: Nea ɔyɛ nokware treneeni no nya nkwa,nanso nea ɔkɔ so yɛ bɔne no kɔ owu mu.
english:
Truly the righteous attain life,
