    but whoever pursues evil finds death.

twi: Awurade kyi nnipa a wɔn koma akyea,na nʼani gye wɔn a wɔn akwan ho nni asɛm no ho.
english:
The Lord detests those whose hearts are perverse,
    but he delights in those whose ways are blameless.

twi: Gye to mu sɛ, amumɔyɛfo benya wɔn akatua,na atreneefo benya wɔn ti adidi mu.
english:
Be sure of this: The wicked will not go unpunished,
    but those who are righteous will go free.

twi: Ɔbea hoɔfɛfo a ontumi nsi gyinae note sɛ sika kaa a ɛhyɛ prako hwene mu.
english:
Like a gold ring in a pig’s snout
    is a beautiful woman who shows no discretion.

twi: Atreneefo apɛde wie yiye,nanso amumɔyɛfo anidaso wie abufuwhyew.
english:
The desire of the righteous ends only in good,
    but the hope of the wicked only in wrath.

twi: Obi yɛ adɔe, na onya ne ho bebree;obi nso yɛ pɛpɛe, nanso ehia no.
english:
One person gives freely, yet gains even more;
    another withholds unduly, but comes to poverty.

twi: Ɔyamyefo bɛkɔ so anya ne ho;na nea ɔma ebinom mee no nso bɛmee.
english:
A generous person will prosper;
    whoever refreshes others will be refreshed.

twi: Nnipa dome nea ɔde atoko sie,na nhyira ba nea ɔtɔn ne de so.
english:
People curse the one who hoards grain,
    but they pray God’s blessing on the one who is willing to sell.

twi: Nea ɔhwehwɛ papa akyi kwan no nya anisɔ,na nea ɔhwehwɛ bɔne no, bɔne ba ne so.
english:
Whoever seeks good finds favor,
    but evil comes to one who searches for it.

twi: Nea ɔde ne ho to nʼahonyade so no bɛhwe ase,na ɔtreneeni bɛyɛ frɔmfrɔm sɛ ahabammono.
english:
Those who trust in their riches will fall,
    but the righteous will thrive like a green leaf.

twi: Nea ɔde ɔhaw bɛto nʼabusua so no bedi mframa ade,na ɔkwasea bɛyɛ onyansafo somfo.
english:
Whoever brings ruin on their family will inherit only wind,
    and the fool will be servant to the wise.

twi: Ɔtreneeni aba yɛ nkwadua,na nea ogye akra no yɛ onyansafo.
english:
The fruit of the righteous is a tree of life,
    and the one who is wise saves lives.

twi: Kyerɛwsɛm no ka se, “Ɛyɛ den sɛ wobegye onipa pa nkwa;na wɔn a wonnye asɛm no nni ne nnebɔneyɛfo no de, dɛn na ɛbɛba wɔn so?”
english:
If the righteous receive their due on earth,
    how much more the ungodly and the sinner!

twi: Obiara a ɔpɛ ahohyɛso no pɛ nimdeɛ,na nea okyi nteɛso no yɛ ogyimifo.
english:
Whoever loves discipline loves knowledge,
    but whoever hates correction is stupid.

twi: Nnipa pa nya Awurade nkyɛn adom,na Awurade bu amumɔyɛfo fɔ.
english:
Good people obtain favor from the Lord,
    but he condemns those who devise wicked schemes.

twi: Amumɔyɛsɛm rentumi mma onipa ase ntim,na wɔrentumi ntu ɔtreneeni ase.
english:
No one can be established through wickedness,
    but the righteous cannot be uprooted.

twi: Ɔyere a ɔwɔ suban pa yɛ ne kunu ahenkyɛw,nanso ɔyere nimguasefo te sɛ porɔwee wɔ ne kunu nnompe mu.
english:
A wife of noble character is her husband’s crown,
    but a disgraceful wife is like decay in his bones.

twi: Atreneefo nhyehyɛe yɛ pɛ,na amumɔyɛfo afotu yɛ nnaadaa.
english:
The plans of the righteous are just,
    but the advice of the wicked is deceitful.

twi: Amumɔyɛfo nsɛm da hɔ twɛn mogya,na ɔtreneeni kasa yi wɔn fi mu.
english:
The words of the wicked lie in wait for blood,
    but the speech of the upright rescues them.

twi: Wotu amumɔyɛfo gu na wɔyera,nanso atreneefo fi gyina pintinn.
english:
The wicked are overthrown and are no more,
    but the house of the righteous stands firm.

twi: Wɔkamfo onipa sɛnea ne nyansa tena nnipa a wɔn adwene yɛ kɔntɔnkye de, wobu wɔn animtiaa.
english:
A person is praised according to their prudence,
    and one with a warped mind is despised.

twi: Eye sɛ wobɛyɛ wo ho sɛ ɔteta nanso wowɔ ɔsomfo,sen sɛ wobɛyɛ wo ho sɛ obi, nanso wunni aduan.
english:
Better to be a nobody and yet have a servant
    than pretend to be somebody and have no food.

twi: Ɔtreneeni ma ne nyɛmmoa nea wɔpɛ,na amumɔyɛfo nneyɛe a eye pa ara yɛ atirimɔden.
english:
The righteous care for the needs of their animals,
    but the kindest acts of the wicked are cruel.

twi: Nea ɔyɛ nʼasase so adwuma no benya aduan bebree,na nea odi nsɛm huhuw akyi no nni adwene.
english:
Those who work their land will have abundant food,
    but those who chase fantasies have no sense.

twi: Amumɔyɛfo pɛ abɔnefo asade,nanso ɔtreneeni ase dɔ.
english:
The wicked desire the stronghold of evildoers,
    but the root of the righteous endures.

twi: Ɔbɔnefo anosɛm yi no sɛ afiri,nanso ɔtreneeni nya ne ho tetew wɔ ahohia mu.
english:
Evildoers are trapped by their sinful talk,
    and so the innocent escape trouble.

twi: Nneɛma pa fi onipa anom aba mu hyɛ no masɛnea ne nsa ano adwuma ma no akatua no.
english:
From the fruit of their lips people are filled with good things,
    and the work of their hands brings them reward.

twi: Ɔkwasea akwan teɛ nʼani so,na onyansafo tie afotu.
english:
The way of fools seems right to them,
    but the wise listen to advice.

twi: Nkwaseafo bo nkyɛ fuw,nanso mmadwemma bu wɔn ani gu animka so.
english:
Fools show their annoyance at once,
    but the prudent overlook an insult.

twi: Ɔdanseni nokwafo di adanse turodoo,na nea odi adansekurum no twa nkontompo.
english:
An honest witness tells the truth,
    but a false witness tells lies.

twi: Nsɛm hunu keka wowɔ te sɛ afoananso onyansafo tɛkrɛma ma abodwo.
english:
The words of the reckless pierce like swords,
    but the tongue of the wise brings healing.

twi: Ano a ɛka nokware no tim hɔ daa,na atoro tɛkrɛma renkyɛ koraa.
english:
Truthful lips endure forever,
    but a lying tongue lasts only a moment.

twi: Nnaadaa hyɛ wɔn a wodwen bɔne ho no koma mu,na wɔn a wɔpɛ asomdwoe nya ahosɛpɛw.
english:
Deceit is in the hearts of those who plot evil,
    but those who promote peace have joy.

twi: Ɔhaw biara rento ɔtreneeni,nanso amanehunu mee amumɔyɛfo.
english:
No harm overtakes the righteous,
    but the wicked have their fill of trouble.

twi: Awurade kyi ano a etwa atoro,na nʼani gye nnipa a wodi nokware ho.
english:
The Lord detests lying lips,
    but he delights in people who are trustworthy.

twi: Ɔtreneeni mmɔ ne nimdeɛ ho dawurunanso ɔkwasea koma da agyimisɛm adi.
english:
The prudent keep their knowledge to themselves,
    but a fool’s heart blurts out folly.

twi: Nsa a ɛyɛ adwuma no bedi tumi,nanso akwadworɔ wie nkoasom mu.
english:
Diligent hands will rule,
    but laziness ends in forced labor.

twi: Koma a ɛpere ade ho ma onipa botow,nanso nkuranhyɛsɛm bi hyɛ no den.
english:
Anxiety weighs down the heart,
    but a kind word cheers it up.

twi: Ɔtreneeni wɔ ntoboase wɔ ayɔnkofa mu,nanso amumɔyɛfo kwan ma wɔfom.
english:
The righteous choose their friends carefully,
    but the way of the wicked leads them astray.

twi: Onihawfo ntoto ne hanam,nanso nsiyɛfo ahonyade som bo ma wɔn.
english:
The lazy do not roast any game,
    but the diligent feed on the riches of the hunt.

twi: Trenee kwan mu wɔ nkwa;na owu nni saa kwan no so.
english:
In the way of righteousness there is life;
    along that path is immortality.

twi: Ɔba nyansafo tie nʼagya nkyerɛkyerɛ;na ɔfɛwdifo ntie animka.
english:
A wise son heeds his father’s instruction,
    but a mocker does not respond to rebukes.

twi: Nneɛma pa a efi onipa anom no ma no anigye,na wɔn a wonni nokware no kɔn dɔ kitikitiyɛ.
english:
From the fruit of their lips people enjoy good things,
    but the unfaithful have an appetite for violence.

twi: Nea ɔkora nʼano no kora ne nkwa so,nanso nea ɔkasa a onsusuw ho no bɛba ɔsɛe mu.
english:
Those who guard their lips preserve their lives,
    but those who speak rashly will come to ruin.

twi: Onihawfo pere hwehwɛ nanso onya hwee,na nea ɔyɛ adwuma no nya nea ɔpɛ biara.
english:
A sluggard’s appetite is never filled,
    but the desires of the diligent are fully satisfied.

twi: Atreneefo kyi nea ɛnyɛ nokware,nanso amumɔyɛfo de aniwu ne ahohora ba.
english:
The righteous hate what is false,
    but the wicked make themselves a stench
    and bring shame on themselves.

twi: Trenee bɔ ɔnokwafo ho ban,na amumɔyɛsɛm tu ɔbɔnefo gu.
english:
Righteousness guards the person of integrity,
    but wickedness overthrows the sinner.

twi: Obi yɛ ne ho sɛ ɔdefo, a nso onni hwee,ɔfoforo yɛ ne ho sɛ ohiani, nso ɔwɔ ahonya bebree.
english:
One person pretends to be rich, yet has nothing;
    another pretends to be poor, yet has great wealth.

twi: Obi ahonya betumi agye no nkwa,nanso ohiani nte ahunahuna biara.
english:
A person’s riches may ransom their life,
    but the poor cannot respond to threatening rebukes.

twi: Atreneefo kanea hyerɛn pa ara,nanso wodum amumɔyɛfo kanea.
english:
The light of the righteous shines brightly,
    but the lamp of the wicked is snuffed out.

twi: Ahantan de ntɔkwaw nko ara na ɛba,na wohu nyansa wɔ wɔn a wotie afotu mu.
english:
Where there is strife, there is pride,
    but wisdom is found in those who take advice.

twi: Ahonya a ɛnam ɔkwammɔne so no hwere ntɛm so,na nea ɔboa sika ano nkakrankakra no ma ɛdɔɔso.
english:
Dishonest money dwindles away,
    but whoever gathers money little by little makes it grow.

twi: Anidaso a wotu hyɛ da no bɔ koma ɔyare,nanso anigyinade a nsa aka no yɛ nkwadua.
english:
Hope deferred makes the heart sick,
    but a longing fulfilled is a tree of life.

twi: Nea otwiri akwankyerɛ no betua so ka,nanso wɔma nea ɔde obu ma mmara no akatua.
english:
Whoever scorns instruction will pay for it,
    but whoever respects a command is rewarded.

twi: Onyansafo nkyerɛkyerɛ te sɛ nkwa asuti,eyi onipa fi owu afiri mu.
english:
The teaching of the wise is a fountain of life,
    turning a person from the snares of death.

twi: Nhumu pa de adom ba,nanso atorofo akwan so yɛ den.
english:
Good judgment wins favor,
    but the way of the unfaithful leads to their destruction.

twi: Ɔbadwemma biara yɛ nʼade wɔ nimdeɛ mu,nanso ɔkwasea da nʼagyimisɛm adi.
english:
All who are prudent act with knowledge,
    but fools expose their folly.

twi: Ɔsomafo mumɔyɛfo tɔ amane mu,nanso ɔnanmusini nokwafo de abodwo ba.
english:
A wicked messenger falls into trouble,
    but a trustworthy envoy brings healing.

twi: Nea ɔpo nteɛso no kɔ ohia ne animguase mu,na wɔhyɛ nea otie nteɛso no anuonyam.
english:
Whoever disregards discipline comes to poverty and shame,
    but whoever heeds correction is honored.

twi: Akɔnnɔde a nsa aka ma ɔkra ani gye,nanso nkwaseafo kyi sɛ wɔtwe wɔn ho fi bɔne ho.
english:
A longing fulfilled is sweet to the soul,
    but fools detest turning from evil.

twi: Nea ɔne onyansafo nantew no hu nyansa,na nea ɔne nkwaseafo bɔ no hu amane.
english:
Walk with the wise and become wise,
    for a companion of fools suffers harm.

twi: Ɔhaw di ɔbɔnefo akyi,na nkɔso yɛ ɔtreneeni akatua.
english:
Trouble pursues the sinner,
    but the righteous are rewarded with good things.

twi: Onipa pa de agyapade gyaw ne nenanom,na wɔkora ɔbɔnefo ahonyade so ma ɔtreneeni.
english:
A good person leaves an inheritance for their children’s children,
    but a sinner’s wealth is stored up for the righteous.

twi: Ohiani afum nnɔbae tumi ba pii,nanso ntɛnkyew pra kɔ.
english:
An unplowed field produces food for the poor,
    but injustice sweeps it away.

twi: Nea ɔkyɛe nʼabaa so no tan ne ba,na nea ɔdɔ no no hwɛ sɛ ɔbɛteɛ no.
english:
Whoever spares the rod hates their children,
    but the one who loves their children is careful to discipline them.

twi: Atreneefo didi ma wɔn koma mee,nanso ɔkɔm de amumɔyɛfo.
english:
The righteous eat to their hearts’ content,
    but the stomach of the wicked goes hungry.

twi: Ɔbea nyansafo si ne dan,nanso ɔbea kwasea de nʼankasa ne nsa dwiriw ne de gu fam.
english:
The wise woman builds her house,
    but with her own hands the foolish one tears hers down.

twi: Nea ne nantew teɛ no suro Awurade,na nea nʼakwan kyea no bu no animtiaa.
english:
Whoever fears the Lord walks uprightly,
    but those who despise him are devious in their ways.

twi: Ɔkwasea kasa ma wɔbɔ nʼakyi abaa,nanso anyansafo ano bɔ wɔn ho ban.
english:
A fool’s mouth lashes out with pride,
    but the lips of the wise protect them.

twi: Faako a anantwi nni no, adididaka no mu da mpan,na nantwi ahoɔden mu na nnɔbae pii fi ba.
english:
Where there are no oxen, the manger is empty,
    but from the strength of an ox come abundant harvests.

twi: Ɔdanseni nokwafo rennaadaa,ɔdansekurumni hwie atoro gu hɔ.
english:
An honest witness does not deceive,
    but a false witness pours out lies.

twi: Ɔfɛwdifo hwehwɛ nyansa nanso onya,nanso wɔn a wɔwɔ nhumu nya nimdeɛ ntɛm.
english:
The mocker seeks wisdom and finds none,
    but knowledge comes easily to the discerning.

twi: Twe wo ho fi ɔkwasea ho,efisɛ, worennya nimdeɛ mfi nʼano.
english:
Stay away from a fool,
    for you will not find knowledge on their lips.

twi: Anitewfo nyansa ne sɛ wɔbɛdwene wɔn akwan ho,na nkwaseafo agyimisɛm yɛ nnaadaa.
english:
The wisdom of the prudent is to give thought to their ways,
    but the folly of fools is deception.

twi: Nkwaseafo de bɔne ho adwensakra di fɛw,na wɔn a wɔteɛ mu na anisɔ wɔ.
english:
Fools mock at making amends for sin,
    but goodwill is found among the upright.

twi: Koma biara nim ɔyaw wɔ ne mu,na obi foforo rentumi ne no nkyɛ nʼanigye.
english:
Each heart knows its own bitterness,
    and no one else can share its joy.

twi: Wɔbɛsɛe amumɔyɛfo fi,nanso teefo ntamadan bɛyɛ frɔmfrɔm.
english:
The house of the wicked will be destroyed,
    but the tent of the upright will flourish.

twi: Ɔkwan bi wɔ hɔ a ɛteɛ wɔ onipa ani so,nanso awiei no, ɛkɔ owu mu.
english:
There is a way that appears to be right,
    but in the end it leads to death.

twi: Ɔserew mu mpo, koma tumi di yaw,na anigye tumi wie awerɛhow.
english:
Even in laughter the heart may ache,
    and rejoicing may end in grief.

twi: Akyirisanfo benya akatua sɛnea wɔn akwan te,na onipa pa nso benya ne de.
english:
The faithless will be fully repaid for their ways,
    and the good rewarded for theirs.

twi: Atetekwaa gye biribiara di,nanso onitefo dwene nʼanammɔntu ho.
english:
The simple believe anything,
    but the prudent give thought to their steps.

twi: Onyansafo suro Awurade na oguan bɔne,nanso ɔkwasea yɛ asowui ne basabasa.
english:
The wise fear the Lord and shun evil,
    but a fool is hotheaded and yet feels secure.

twi: Onipa a ne bo nkyɛ fuw no yɛ nkwaseade,na wɔtɔn nea ɔpam apam bɔne no.
english:
A quick-tempered person does foolish things,
    and the one who devises evil schemes is hated.

twi: Ntetekwaafo agyapade ne gyimi,na wɔde nimdeɛ bɔ anitewfo abotiri.
english:
The simple inherit folly,
    but the prudent are crowned with knowledge.

twi: Nnipa bɔnefo bɛkotow nnipa pa anim,na amumɔyɛfo akotow atreneefo apon ano.
english:
Evildoers will bow down in the presence of the good,
    and the wicked at the gates of the righteous.

twi: Ahiafo de, wɔn yɔnkonom mpo mpɛ wɔn anim ahwɛ,nanso adefo wɔ nnamfonom bebree.
english:
The poor are shunned even by their neighbors,
    but the rich have many friends.

twi: Nea obu ne yɔnko animtiaa yɛ bɔne,na nhyira nka nea ne yam ye ma ohiani.
english:
It is a sin to despise one’s neighbor,
    but blessed is the one who is kind to the needy.

twi: So wɔn a wɔbɔ pɔw bɔne nyera kwan ana?Nanso wɔn a wɔhyehyɛ nea eye no nya adɔe ne nokware.
english:
Do not those who plot evil go astray?
    But those who plan what is good find love and faithfulness.

twi: Adwumadenyɛ nyinaa de mfaso ba,na kasahunu de, ɛkɔ ohia mu.
english:
All hard work brings a profit,
    but mere talk leads only to poverty.

twi: Anyansafo ahonya ne wɔn abotiri,na nkwaseafo agyimisɛm sow gyimi aba.
english:
The wealth of the wise is their crown,
    but the folly of fools yields folly.

twi: Ɔdanseni nokwafo gye nkwa,nanso ɔdansekurumni yɛ ɔdaadaafo.
english:
A truthful witness saves lives,
    but a false witness is deceitful.

twi: Nea osuro Awurade no wɔ bammɔ a mu yɛ den,na ɛbɛyɛ guankɔbea ama ne mma.
english:
Whoever fears the Lord has a secure fortress,
    and for their children it will be a refuge.

twi: Awurade suro yɛ nkwa asuti,eyi onipa fi owu afiri mu.
english:
The fear of the Lord is a fountain of life,
    turning a person from the snares of death.

twi: Ɔman mu nnipa dodow yɛ ɔhene anuonyam,nanso sɛ asomfo nni hɔ a mmapɔmma no sɛe.
english:
A large population is a king’s glory,
    but without subjects a prince is ruined.

twi: Onipa a ɔwɔ abodwokyɛre wɔ ntease a mu dɔ,na nea ne bo fu ntɛm no da agyimisɛm adi.
english:
Whoever is patient has great understanding,
    but one who is quick-tempered displays folly.

twi: Koma mu asomdwoe ma nipadua nkwa,na anibere ma nnompe porɔw.
english:
A heart at peace gives life to the body,
    but envy rots the bones.

twi: Nea ɔhyɛ ahiafo so no bu wɔn Yɛfo animtiaa,nanso nea ohu ohiani mmɔbɔ no hyɛ Onyankopɔn anuonyam.
english:
Whoever oppresses the poor shows contempt for their Maker,
    but whoever is kind to the needy honors God.

twi: Sɛ amanehunu ba a amumɔyɛfo hwe ase,nanso owu mu mpo atreneefo wɔ guankɔbea.
english:
When calamity comes, the wicked are brought down,
    but even in death the righteous seek refuge in God.

twi: Nyansa te ntease koma mu,na nkwaseafo mu mpo, oyi ne ho adi.
english:
Wisdom reposes in the heart of the discerning
    and even among fools she lets herself be known.

twi: Trenee pagyaw ɔman,na bɔne yɛ animguase ma nnipa nyinaa.
english:
Righteousness exalts a nation,
    but sin condemns any people.

twi: Ɔhene ani sɔ ɔsomfo nyansani,na ɔsomfo nimguasefo hyɛ no abufuw.
english:
A king delights in a wise servant,
    but a shameful servant arouses his fury.

twi: Mmuae pa sianka abufuwhyew,nanso asɛm a ano yɛ den hwanyan abufuw mu.
english:
A gentle answer turns away wrath,
    but a harsh word stirs up anger.

twi: Onyansafo tɛkrɛma yi nimdeɛ ayɛ,nanso ɔkwasea ano woro agyimisɛm.
english:
The tongue of the wise adorns knowledge,
    but the mouth of the fool gushes folly.

twi: Awurade ani hu baabiara,na ɛhwɛ amumɔyɛfo ne apapafo.
english:
The eyes of the Lord are everywhere,
    keeping watch on the wicked and the good.

twi: Tɛkrɛma a ɛde abodwo ba yɛ nkwadua,nanso nnaadaa tɛkrɛma dwerɛw honhom.
english:
The soothing tongue is a tree of life,
    but a perverse tongue crushes the spirit.

twi: Ɔkwasea mfa nʼagya nteɛso nyɛ hwee,na nea otie nteɛso no kyerɛ sɛ ɔyɛ onitefo.
english:
A fool spurns a parent’s discipline,
    but whoever heeds correction shows prudence.

twi: Ahonya bebree wɔ ɔtreneeni fi,nanso amumɔyɛfo adenya de ɔhaw brɛ wɔn.
english:
The house of the righteous contains great treasure,
    but the income of the wicked brings ruin.

twi: Anyansafo ano trɛtrɛw nimdeɛ mu,nanso ɛnyɛ saa na nkwaseafo koma te.
english:
The lips of the wise spread knowledge,
    but the hearts of fools are not upright.

twi: Awurade kyi amumɔyɛfo afɔrebɔ,nanso teefo mpaebɔ sɔ nʼani.
english:
The Lord detests the sacrifice of the wicked,
    but the prayer of the upright pleases him.

twi: Awurade kyi amumɔyɛfo akwan,nanso ɔdɔ wɔn a wotiw trenee.
english:
The Lord detests the way of the wicked,
    but he loves those who pursue righteousness.

twi: Asotwe dennen wɔ hɔ ma nea ɔman fi ɔkwan no so,nea ɔtan nteɛso no bewu.
english:
Stern discipline awaits anyone who leaves the path;
    the one who hates correction will die.

twi: Owu ne Ɔsɛe da Awurade anim,na nnipa koma mu de, onim ma ɛboro so.
english:
Death and Destruction lie open before the Lord—
    how much more do human hearts!

twi: Ɔfɛwdifo mpɛ nteɛso;onkobisa anyansafo hwee.
english:
Mockers resent correction,
    so they avoid the wise.

twi: Anigye koma ma anim yɛ sereserew,na koma a abotow dwerɛw honhom.
english:
A happy heart makes the face cheerful,
    but heartache crushes the spirit.

twi: Nhumufo koma hwehwɛ nimdeɛ,nanso ɔkwasea ano ka agyimisɛm.
english:
The discerning heart seeks knowledge,
    but the mouth of a fool feeds on folly.

twi: Wɔn a wɔhyɛ wɔn so nna nyinaa yɛ mmɔbɔmmɔbɔ,nanso anigye koma wɔ daa ahosɛpɛw mu.
english:
All the days of the oppressed are wretched,
    but the cheerful heart has a continual feast.

twi: Ketewa bi a yenya a Awurade suro ka ho no yesen ahonyade bebree a ɔhaw bata ho.
english:
Better a little with the fear of the Lord
    than great wealth with turmoil.

twi: Nhabamma aduan a ɔdɔ wɔ mu no yesen nantwi sradenam a ɔtan bata ho.
english:
Better a small serving of vegetables with love
    than a fattened calf with hatred.

twi: Nea ne bo fuw ntɛm no de mpaapaemu ba,nanso nea ɔwɔ ntoboase pata ntɔkwaw.
english:
A hot-tempered person stirs up conflict,
    but the one who is patient calms a quarrel.

twi: Nsɔe ama onihawfo kwan asiw,nanso teefo kwan yɛ ɔtempɔn.
english:
The way of the sluggard is blocked with thorns,
    but the path of the upright is a highway.

twi: Ɔba nyansafo ma nʼagya ani gye,nanso ɔba kwasea bu ne na animtiaa.
english:
A wise son brings joy to his father,
    but a foolish man despises his mother.

twi: Agyimisɛm ma nea onni adwene ani gye,nanso nea ɔwɔ ntease no fa ɔkwan a ɛteɛ so.
english:
Folly brings joy to one who has no sense,
    but whoever has understanding keeps a straight course.

twi: Nhyehyɛe a enni afotu no sɛe,nanso afotufo bebree ma ɛyɛ yiye.
english:
Plans fail for lack of counsel,
    but with many advisers they succeed.

twi: Onipa a ɔma mmuae a ɛfata no ani gye,asɛm a ɛba bere pa mu no nso ye.
english:
A person finds joy in giving an apt reply—
    and how good is a timely word!

twi: Onyansafo asetena mu kwan ma no nkɔso,esiw ne da mukɔ ho kwan.
english:
The path of life leads upward for the prudent
    to keep them from going down to the realm of the dead.

twi: Awurade sɛe ɔhantanni fi,na ɔma akunafo ahye yɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ.
english:
The Lord tears down the house of the proud,
    but he sets the widow’s boundary stones in place.

twi: Awurade kyi amumɔyɛfo nsusuwii,nanso nʼani sɔ wɔn a wɔyɛ kronkron no de.
english:
The Lord detests the thoughts of the wicked,
    but gracious words are pure in his sight.

twi: Odifudepɛfo de ɔhaw brɛ nʼabusua,nanso nea okyi kɛtɛasehyɛ no benya nkwa.
english:
The greedy bring ruin to their households,
    but the one who hates bribes will live.

twi: Ɔtreneeni koma kari ne mmuae,nanso omumɔyɛfo ano woro bɔne.
english:
The heart of the righteous weighs its answers,
    but the mouth of the wicked gushes evil.

twi: Awurade mmɛn amumɔyɛfo koraa,nanso ɔte ɔtreneeni mpaebɔ.
english:
The Lord is far from the wicked,
    but he hears the prayer of the righteous.

twi: Anim a ɛtew ma koma nya ahomeka,na asɛm pa ma nnompe ahoɔden.
english:
Light in a messenger’s eyes brings joy to the heart,
    and good news gives health to the bones.

twi: Nea otie animka a ɛma nkwa none anyansafo bɛbɔ mu atena ase.
english:
Whoever heeds life-giving correction
    will be at home among the wise.

twi: Nea ɔmfa ahohyɛso no bu ne ho animtiaa,na nea otie nteɛso no nya nhumu.
english:
Those who disregard discipline despise themselves,
    but the one who heeds correction gains understanding.

twi: Awurade suro kyerɛ onipa nyansa,ahobrɛase di anuonyam anim.
english:
Wisdom’s instruction is to fear the Lord,
    and humility comes before honor.

twi: Koma mu nhyehyɛe yɛ onipa de,na tɛkrɛma mmuae fi Awurade.
english:
To humans belong the plans of the heart,
    but from the Lord comes the proper answer of the tongue.

twi: Ɛyɛ onipa sɛ nʼakwan nyinaa yɛ kronkron,nanso Awurade na ɔpɛɛpɛɛ adwene mu.
english:
All a person’s ways seem pure to them,
    but motives are weighed by the Lord.

twi: Fa nea woyɛ nyinaa hyɛ Awurade nsam,na wo nhyehyɛe besi yiye.
english:
Commit to the Lord whatever you do,
    and he will establish your plans.

twi: Awurade yɛ biribiara ma nʼankasa botae,mpo, ɔhwɛ omumɔyɛfo so kosi amanehunu da.
english:
The Lord works out everything to its proper end—
    even the wicked for a day of disaster.

twi: Awurade kyi koma mu ahantanfo nyinaa.Nya saa ntease yi sɛ, wɔremfa wɔn ho nni.
english:
The Lord detests all the proud of heart.
    Be sure of this: They will not go unpunished.

twi: Wɔnam ɔdɔ ne nokware so pata bɔne;onipa nam Awurade suro so yi bɔne akwa.
english:
Through love and faithfulness sin is atoned for;
    through the fear of the Lord evil is avoided.

twi: Sɛ onipa akwan sɔ Awurade ani a,ɔma nʼatamfo mpo ne no tena asomdwoe mu.
english:
When the Lord takes pleasure in anyone’s way,
    he causes their enemies to make peace with them.

twi: Kakraa bi a wɔnam trenee kwan so nya no yesen mfaso pii a wɔnam ntɛnkyew so nya.
english:
Better a little with righteousness
    than much gain with injustice.

twi: Onipa yɛ ne nhyehyɛe wɔ ne koma mu,nanso Awurade na ɔhwɛ nʼanammɔntu.
english:
In their hearts humans plan their course,
    but the Lord establishes their steps.

twi: Ɔhene anom kasa te sɛ nkɔmhyɛ,enti ɛnsɛ sɛ nʼano ka nea ɛnyɛ atɛntrenee.
english:
The lips of a king speak as an oracle,
    and his mouth does not betray justice.

twi: Nsania ne abrammo a asisi nni mu fi Awurade;nkaribo a ɛwɔ kotoku mu no, ɔno na ɔyɛe.
english:
Honest scales and balances belong to the Lord;
    all the weights in the bag are of his making.

twi: Ahemfo kyi bɔneyɛ,efisɛ ahengua si trenee so.
english:
Kings detest wrongdoing,
    for a throne is established through righteousness.

twi: Ahemfo ani sɔ ano a ɛka nokware;na wobu onipa a ɔka nokware.
english:
Kings take pleasure in honest lips;
    they value the one who speaks what is right.

twi: Ɔhene abufuwhyew yɛ owu somafo,nanso onyansafo bedwudwo ano.
english:
A king’s wrath is a messenger of death,
    but the wise will appease it.

twi: Sɛ ɔhene anim tew a, ɛyɛ nkwa,nʼadom te sɛ asusowbere mu omununkum.
english:
When a king’s face brightens, it means life;
    his favor is like a rain cloud in spring.

twi: Eye sɛ wubenya nyansa sen sɛ wubenya sikakɔkɔɔ,sɛ wubenya nhumu sen sɛ wubenya dwetɛ!
english:
How much better to get wisdom than gold,
    to get insight rather than silver!

twi: Ɔtreneeni tempɔn kwati bɔne;nea ɔhwɛ nʼakwan yiye no bɔ ne nkwa ho ban.
english:
The highway of the upright avoids evil;
    those who guard their ways preserve their lives.

twi: Ahantan di ɔsɛe anim,na ahomaso honhom nso di asehwe anim.
english:
Pride goes before destruction,
    a haughty spirit before a fall.

twi: Eye sɛ wobɛyɛ honhom mu hiani wɔ wɔn a wɔhyɛ wɔn so musen sɛ wo ne ahantanfo bɛkyɛ asade.
english:
Better to be lowly in spirit along with the oppressed
    than to share plunder with the proud.

twi: Nea ɔyɛ osetie ma nkyerɛkyerɛ no nya nkɔso;nhyira nka nea ɔde ne ho to Awurade so.
english:
Whoever gives heed to instruction prospers,
    and blessed is the one who trusts in the Lord.

twi: Wɔfrɛ koma mu anyansafo se nhumufo,na kasa pa ma nkyerɛkyerɛ kɔ so.
english:
The wise in heart are called discerning,
    and gracious words promote instruction.

twi: Ntease yɛ nkwa asuti ma wɔn a wɔwɔ bi,nanso agyimisɛm de asotwe brɛ nkwaseafo.
english:
Prudence is a fountain of life to the prudent,
    but folly brings punishment to fools.

twi: Onyansafo koma kyerɛ nʼano kwan,na nʼanofafa ma nkyerɛkyerɛ kɔ so.
english:
The hearts of the wise make their mouths prudent,
    and their lips promote instruction.

twi: Abodwosɛm te sɛ ɛwokyɛm;ɛyɛ ɔkra dɛ, na ɛsa nnompe yare.
english:
Gracious words are a honeycomb,
    sweet to the soul and healing to the bones.

twi: Ɔkwan bi wɔ hɔ a ɛteɛ wɔ onipa ani so,nanso awiei no, ɛkɔ owu mu.
english:
There is a way that appears to be right,
    but in the end it leads to death.

twi: Apaafo akɔnnɔ ma wɔyɛ adwumaden;efisɛ wɔpɛ sɛ wokum wɔn kɔm.
english:
The appetite of laborers works for them;
    their hunger drives them on.

twi: Ohuhuni bɔ pɔw bɔne,ne kasa te sɛ ogya a ɛhyew ade.
english:
A scoundrel plots evil,
    and on their lips it is like a scorching fire.

twi: Onipa kɔntɔnkye de mpaapaemu ba,na ɔsututufo tetew nnamfonom ntam.
english:
A perverse person stirs up conflict,
    and a gossip separates close friends.

twi: Kitikitiyɛni daadaa ne yɔnko,na ɔde no fa ɔkwammɔne so.
english:
A violent person entices their neighbor
    and leads them down a path that is not good.

twi: Nea obu nʼani no redwene bɔneyɛ ho;na nea omua nʼano no ani wɔ bɔne so.
english:
Whoever winks with their eye is plotting perversity;
    whoever purses their lips is bent on evil.

twi: Dwen yɛ anuonyam abotiri;trenee mu asetena na ɛde ba.
english:
Gray hair is a crown of splendor;
    it is attained in the way of righteousness.

twi: Nea ɔwɔ abodwokyɛre no ye sen ɔkofo,na nea ɔmfa abufuw ye sen nea ɔko fa kuropɔn.
english:
Better a patient person than a warrior,
    one with self-control than one who takes a city.

twi: Wɔbɔ ntonto de hwehwɛ nea Awurade pɛ,nanso ne gyinaesi biara fi Awurade.
english:
The lot is cast into the lap,
    but its every decision is from the Lord.

twi: Aduan sakoo a asomdwoe wɔ hoye sen ofi a aponto ahyɛ no ma nanso basabasayɛ wɔ mu.
english:
Better a dry crust with peace and quiet
    than a house full of feasting, with strife.

twi: Ɔsomfo nyansafo bedi ɔba nimguasefo so,na obenya ne kyɛfa wɔ agyapade no mu sɛ anuanom no mu baako.
english:
A prudent servant will rule over a disgraceful son
    and will share the inheritance as one of the family.

twi: Kyɛmfɛre wɔ hɔ ma dwetɛ na fononoo wɔ hɔ ma sikakɔkɔɔnanso Awurade na ɔsɔ koma hwɛ.
english:
The crucible for silver and the furnace for gold,
    but the Lord tests the heart.

twi: Omumɔyɛfo tie nsusuwii bɔne;ɔtorofo yɛ aso ma adwene bɔne tɛkrɛma.
english:
A wicked person listens to deceitful lips;
    a liar pays attention to a destructive tongue.

twi: Nea odi ahiafo ho fɛw no bu wɔn Yɛfo animtiaa;na nea ɔfoa amanehunu so no benya asotwe.
english:
Whoever mocks the poor shows contempt for their Maker;
    whoever gloats over disaster will not go unpunished.

twi: Nananom yɛ mmasiriwa anuonyam,na awofo yɛ wɔn mma ahohoahoa.
english:
Children’s children are a crown to the aged,
    and parents are the pride of their children.

twi: Anotew nye mma ɔkwasea,saa ara na ano a edi atoro mfata ɔhene.
english:
Eloquent lips are unsuited to a godless fool—
    how much worse lying lips to a ruler!

twi: Nea ɔma adanmude no hu sɛ ɛyɛ suman;osusuw sɛ nkonimdi bɛba bere biara.
english:
A bribe is seen as a charm by the one who gives it;
    they think success will come at every turn.

twi: Nea obu nʼani gu mfomso so no ma ɔdɔ kwan,na nea ɔkɔ so bɔ so no tetew nnamfonom ntam.
english:
Whoever would foster love covers over an offense,
    but whoever repeats the matter separates close friends.

twi: Animka sɔ onipa a ɔwɔ nhumu anisen mmaa ɔha a wɔbɔ ɔkwasea.
english:
A rebuke impresses a discerning person
    more than a hundred lashes a fool.

twi: Onipa bɔnefo ani wɔ atuatew nko ara sona wɔbɛsoma odwumayɛni tirimuɔdenfo akɔ no so.
english:
Evildoers foster rebellion against God;
    the messenger of death will be sent against them.

twi: Eye sɛ wubehyia sisi a wɔawia ne mmasen ɔkwasea a ɔregyimi.
english:
Better to meet a bear robbed of her cubs
    than a fool bent on folly.

twi: Sɛ obi de bɔne tua papa so ka a,bɔne rempa ne fi da.
english:
Evil will never leave the house
    of one who pays back evil for good.

twi: Ntɔkwaw mfiase te sɛ nea wɔretue suka;enti gyae ma ɛnka na ankɔfa ɔham amma.
english:
Starting a quarrel is like breaching a dam;
    so drop the matter before a dispute breaks out.

twi: Sɛ wobegyaa nea odi fɔ ne sɛ wobebu nea odi bem kumfɔ no,Awurade kyi nʼabien no nyinaa.
english:
Acquitting the guilty and condemning the innocent—
    the Lord detests them both.

twi: Sika a ɛwɔ ɔkwasea nsam so nni mfaso,efisɛ onni botae biara sɛ obehu nyansa.
english:
Why should fools have money in hand to buy wisdom,
    when they are not able to understand it?

twi: Adamfo kyerɛ ɔdɔ bere nyinaa mu,wɔwo onuabarima ma ahokyere bere.
english:
A friend loves at all times,
    and a brother is born for a time of adversity.

twi: Obi a onni adwene no na ɔde ne nsa hyɛ krataa ase di akagyinamunam so de si awowa ma ne yɔnko.
english:
One who has no sense shakes hands in pledge
    and puts up security for a neighbor.

twi: Nea ɔpɛ ntɔkwaw no dɔ bɔne;nea osi ɔpon tenten no frɛfrɛ ɔsɛe.
english:
Whoever loves a quarrel loves sin;
    whoever builds a high gate invites destruction.

twi: Onipa a ɔwɔ porɔwee koma no nnya nkɔso;nea ɔwɔ nnaadaa tɛkrɛma no tɔ amane mu.
english:
One whose heart is corrupt does not prosper;
    one whose tongue is perverse falls into trouble.

twi: Nea ɔwo ɔbakwasea no di awerɛhow,ɔbakwasea agya nni anigye.
english:
To have a fool for a child brings grief;
    there is no joy for the parent of a godless fool.

twi: Koma mu anigye yɛ aduru, ɛsa ɔyare,nanso honhom a abotow no yoyow nnompe.
english:
A cheerful heart is good medicine,
    but a crushed spirit dries up the bones.

twi: Omumɔyɛfo gye adanmude wɔ sum asede kyea atɛntrenee.
english:
The wicked accept bribes in secret
    to pervert the course of justice.

twi: Onipa a ɔwɔ nhumu no ani kɔ nyansa so,na ɔkwasea toto nʼani kosi asase ano.
english:
A discerning person keeps wisdom in view,
    but a fool’s eyes wander to the ends of the earth.

twi: Ɔbakwasea hyɛ nʼagya awerɛhow,na ɔma nea onyinsɛn no no di yaw.
english:
A foolish son brings grief to his father
    and bitterness to the mother who bore him.

twi: Enye sɛ wɔtwe nea odi bem aso,anaasɛ wotwa adwumayɛfo mmaa wɔ wɔn nokwaredi nti.
english:
If imposing a fine on the innocent is not good,
    surely to flog honest officials is not right.

twi: Onimdefo dwene nʼanom kasa ho,na nea ɔwɔ nhumu no wɔ abodwo.
english:
The one who has knowledge uses words with restraint,
    and whoever has understanding is even-tempered.

twi: Mpo sɛ ɔkwasea yɛ dinn a wobu no sɛ onyansafo,na sɛ omua nʼano a wobu no sɛ ɔwɔ nhumu.
english:
Even fools are thought wise if they keep silent,
    and discerning if they hold their tongues.

twi: Ɔhonamkani yɛ pɛsɛmenkominya;na nea ɛmfa atɛntrenee mma no turuw ɔham.
english:
An unfriendly person pursues selfish ends
    and against all sound judgment starts quarrels.

twi: Ɔkwasea nni nhumu ho anigye,na mmom nea ɔpɛ ara ne sɛ ɔde nʼadwene bɛto gua.
english:
Fools find no pleasure in understanding
    but delight in airing their own opinions.

twi: Sɛ amumɔyɛsɛm ba a animtiaabu di so,na aniwu nso di animguase akyi.
english:
When wickedness comes, so does contempt,
    and with shame comes reproach.

twi: Onipa anom nsɛm yɛ nsu a emu dɔ,na nyansa asuti yɛ asuwa a ɛrefi ahuru.
english:
The words of the mouth are deep waters,
    but the fountain of wisdom is a rushing stream.

twi: Enye sɛ wodi ma omumɔyɛfoanaasɛ wobu nea odi bem ntɛnkyew.
english:
It is not good to be partial to the wicked
    and so deprive the innocent of justice.

twi: Nkwaseafo ano de akasakasa ba,na wɔn ano frɛfrɛ ɔhwe.
english:
The lips of fools bring them strife,
    and their mouths invite a beating.

twi: Nkwaseafo ano yɛ wɔn ara wɔn sɛe,na wɔn anofafa yɛ wɔn ara wɔn kra afiri.
english:
The mouths of fools are their undoing,
    and their lips are a snare to their very lives.

twi: Osekuni ano asɛm te sɛ aduan a ɛyɛ dɛ;ɛhyɛnhyɛn onipa akwaa mu nyinaa.
english:
The words of a gossip are like choice morsels;
    they go down to the inmost parts.

twi: Nea ɔtoto nʼadwuma ase noyɛ ɔsɛefo nuabarima.
english:
One who is slack in his work
    is brother to one who destroys.

twi: Awurade din yɛ abantenten a ɛyɛ den;ahotefo guan kɔtoa na wonya bammɔ.
english:
The name of the Lord is a fortified tower;
    the righteous run to it and are safe.

twi: Adefo ahonyade ne wɔn kuropɔn a wɔabɔ ho banwɔfa no sɛ ɔfasu tenten a wontumi mforo.
english:
The wealth of the rich is their fortified city;
    they imagine it a wall too high to scale.

twi: Ansa na onipa bɛhwe ase no onya ahomaso koma,na ahobrɛase di anuonyam anim.
english:
Before a downfall the heart is haughty,
    but humility comes before honor.

twi: Nea ontie asɛm ansa na wama mmuae no,ɛno ne ne gyimi ne nʼanimguase.
english:
To answer before listening—
    that is folly and shame.

twi: Onipa honhom na ɛhyɛ no den wɔ ɔyare muna honhom a abotow de, hena na ɔpɛ?
english:
The human spirit can endure in sickness,
    but a crushed spirit who can bear?

twi: Nhumu koma nya nimdeɛ;na anyansafo aso nso hwehwɛ.
english:
The heart of the discerning acquires knowledge,
    for the ears of the wise seek it out.

twi: Akyɛde bue kwan ma nea ɔde mana ɛde no ba atitiriw anim.
english:
A gift opens the way
    and ushers the giver into the presence of the great.

twi: Ɛyɛ nea ɔbɔ ne nkuro kan no sɛ nʼasɛm yɛ dɛ,kosi sɛ ɔfoforo bɛba abebisa no nsɛm no mu.
english:
In a lawsuit the first to speak seems right,
    until someone comes forward and cross-examines.

twi: Ntontobɔ twa akyinnyegye so,na ɛpata atamfo.
english:
Casting the lot settles disputes
    and keeps strong opponents apart.

twi: Onua a wɔafom no no asɛm yɛ den sen kuropɔn a ɛwɔ bammɔ,akyinnyegye te sɛ abankɛse apon a wɔabram akyi.
english:
A brother wronged is more unyielding than a fortified city;
    disputes are like the barred gates of a citadel.

twi: Onipa anom asɛm so aba ma ɔyafunu mee,nnɔbae a nʼanofafa twa no mee no.
english:
From the fruit of their mouth a person’s stomach is filled;
    with the harvest of their lips they are satisfied.

twi: Tɛkrɛma kura nkwa ne owu tumi,na wɔn a wɔdɔ no no bedi nʼaba.
english:
The tongue has the power of life and death,
    and those who love it will eat its fruit.

twi: Nea wanya yere no anya ade pana onya adom fi Awurade hɔ.
english:
He who finds a wife finds what is good
    and receives favor from the Lord.

twi: Ohiani srɛ ahummɔbɔ,nanso ɔdefo de kasaden bua no.
english:
The poor plead for mercy,
    but the rich answer harshly.

twi: Ɔbarima a ne nnamfonom dɔɔso betumi ahwe ase,nanso adamfo bi wɔ hɔ a ɔbɛfam ne ho asen onua.
english:
One who has unreliable friends soon comes to ruin,
    but there is a friend who sticks closer than a brother.

twi: Ohiani a ne nantew ho nni asɛm noye sen ɔkwasea a nʼasɛm mfa kwan mu.
english:
Better the poor whose walk is blameless
    than a fool whose lips are perverse.

twi: Mmɔdemmɔ a nimdeɛ nka ho no nye,saa ara na ntɛmpɛ a ɛma obi yera kwan nso nye.
english:
Desire without knowledge is not good—
    how much more will hasty feet miss the way!

twi: Onipa agyimisɛm sɛe nʼabrabɔ,nanso ne koma huru tia Awurade.
english:
A person’s own folly leads to their ruin,
    yet their heart rages against the Lord.

twi: Ahonya frɛfrɛ nnamfonom bebree;nanso ohiani adamfo gyaw no hɔ.
english:
Wealth attracts many friends,
    but even the closest friend of the poor person deserts them.

twi: Adansekurumni benya nʼakatua,na nea otwa nkontompo remfa ne ho nni.
english:
A false witness will not go unpunished,
    and whoever pours out lies will not go free.

twi: Nnipa pii pɛ adom fi sodifo nkyɛn,na nea ɔkyɛ ade yɛ obiara adamfo.
english:
Many curry favor with a ruler,
    and everyone is the friend of one who gives gifts.

twi: Ohiani abusuafo nyinaa po no,na saa ara na ne nnamfonom po no!Mpo ɔhwehwɛ wɔn, pɛ sɛ ɔpa wɔn kyɛw,nanso onhu wɔn baabiara.
english:
The poor are shunned by all their relatives—
    how much more do their friends avoid them!
Though the poor pursue them with pleading,
    they are nowhere to be found.

twi: Nea onya nyansa no dɔ ne kra;nea ɔpɛ nhumu no nya nkɔso.
english:
The one who gets wisdom loves life;
    the one who cherishes understanding will soon prosper.

twi: Adansekurumni benya asotwe,na nea otwa nkontompo no bɛyera.
english:
A false witness will not go unpunished,
    and whoever pours out lies will perish.

twi: Ɛmfata sɛ ɔkwasea bedi taamu,anaasɛ akoa bedi mmapɔmma so!
english:
It is not fitting for a fool to live in luxury—
    how much worse for a slave to rule over princes!

twi: Onipa nyansa ma no ntoboase;ɛyɛ anuonyam ma obi sɛ obebu nʼani gu mfomso bi so.
english:
A person’s wisdom yields patience;
    it is to one’s glory to overlook an offense.

twi: Ɔhene abufuw te sɛ gyata mmubomu,na nʼadom te sɛ sare so bosu.
english:
A king’s rage is like the roar of a lion,
    but his favor is like dew on the grass.

twi: Ɔba kwasea yɛ nʼagya ɔsɛe,ɔyere tɔkwapɛfo te sɛ ɔdan a ne nwini to ntwa da.
english:
A foolish child is a father’s ruin,
    and a quarrelsome wife is like
    the constant dripping of a leaky roof.

twi: Afi ne ahonyade yɛ agyapade a efi awofo,na ɔyere nimdefo fi Awurade.
english:
Houses and wealth are inherited from parents,
    but a prudent wife is from the Lord.

twi: Akwadworɔ de nnahɔɔ ba,na ɔkɔm de ɔkwadwofo.
english:
Laziness brings on deep sleep,
    and the shiftless go hungry.

twi: Nea odi nkyerɛkyerɛ so no bɔ ne nkwa ho ban,na nea ogyaagyaa ne ho no bewu.
english:
Whoever keeps commandments keeps their life,
    but whoever shows contempt for their ways will die.

twi: Nea ɔyɛ adɔe ma ohiani no yɛ de fɛm Awurade,na obetua no nea ɔyɛ no so ka.
english:
Whoever is kind to the poor lends to the Lord,
    and he will reward them for what they have done.

twi: Teɛ wo ba, na ɛno mu na anidaso wɔ,na nyɛ wɔn a wɔde no kɔ owu mu no mu baako.
english:
Discipline your children, for in that there is hope;
    do not be a willing party to their death.

twi: Ɛsɛ sɛ onipa a ne koma haw no no nya so asotwe;sɛ woka ma no a, wobɛyɛ bio.
english:
A hot-tempered person must pay the penalty;
    rescue them, and you will have to do it again.

twi: Tie afotu na gye nkyerɛkyerɛ to mu,na awiei no, wubehu nyansa.
english:
Listen to advice and accept discipline,
    and at the end you will be counted among the wise.

twi: Nhyehyɛe bebree wɔ onipa koma mu,nanso nea Awurade pɛ no na ɛba mu.
english:
Many are the plans in a person’s heart,
    but it is the Lord’s purpose that prevails.

twi: Nea onipa pɛ ne nokware dɔ;eye sɛ wobɛyɛ ohiani sen sɛ wobɛyɛ ɔtorofo.
english:
What a person desires is unfailing love;
    better to be poor than a liar.

twi: Awurade suro kɔ nkwa mu;na onipa de abotɔyam home a ɔhaw bi nni mu.
english:
The fear of the Lord leads to life;
    then one rests content, untouched by trouble.

twi: Ɔkwadwofo de ne nsa si aduan mu,na ɛyɛ no anihaw sɛ obeyi akɔ nʼano.
english:
A sluggard buries his hand in the dish;
    he will not even bring it back to his mouth!

twi: Twa ɔfɛwdifo mmaa, na atetekwaa bɛfa adwene;ka nea ɔwɔ nhumu anim, na obenya nimdeɛ.
english:
Flog a mocker, and the simple will learn prudence;
    rebuke the discerning, and they will gain knowledge.

twi: Nea ɔbɔ nʼagya korɔn na ɔpam ne na noyɛ ɔba a ɔde aniwu ne animguase ba.
english:
Whoever robs their father and drives out their mother
    is a child who brings shame and disgrace.

twi: Me ba, sɛ wugyae nkyerɛkyerɛ tie a,wobɛman afi nimdeɛ nsɛm ho.
english:
Stop listening to instruction, my son,
    and you will stray from the words of knowledge.

twi: Adansekurumni di atɛntrenee ho fɛw;na omumɔyɛfo ano mene bɔne.
english:
A corrupt witness mocks at justice,
    and the mouth of the wicked gulps down evil.

twi: Wɔasiesie asotwe ama fɛwdifo,ne mmaabɔ ama nkwaseafo akyi.
english:
Penalties are prepared for mockers,
    and beatings for the backs of fools.

twi: Nsa yɛ ɔfɛwdifo na nsaden yɛ ɔtɔkwapɛfo;na obiara a nsa bɛma wafom kwan no nyɛ onyansafo.
english:
Wine is a mocker and beer a brawler;
    whoever is led astray by them is not wise.

twi: Ɔhene abufuwhyew te sɛ gyata mmubomu;na nea ɔhyɛ no abufuw no de nkwa twa so.
english:
A king’s wrath strikes terror like the roar of a lion;
    those who anger him forfeit their lives.

twi: Ɛyɛ onipa anuonyam sɛ ɔbɛkwati akasakasa,nanso ogyimifo biara pɛ ntɔkwaw.
english:
It is to one’s honor to avoid strife,
    but every fool is quick to quarrel.

twi: Onihawfo mfuntum nʼasase wɔ ne bere mu;enti edu twabere a onya hwee.
english:
Sluggards do not plow in season;
    so at harvest time they look but find nothing.

twi: Onipa koma botae yɛ asubun,nanso nea ɔwɔ nhumu no twetwe ma epue.
english:
The purposes of a person’s heart are deep waters,
    but one who has insight draws them out.

twi: Nnipa dodow no ara ka se wɔwɔ ɔdɔ a ɛnsa da,na hena na obetumi ahu ɔnokwafo?
english:
Many claim to have unfailing love,
    but a faithful person who can find?

twi: Ɔtreneeni bu ɔbra kronkron;nhyira nka ne mma a wɔba wɔ nʼakyi.
english:
The righteous lead blameless lives;
    blessed are their children after them.

twi: Sɛ ɔhene tena nʼahengua so bu atɛn a,ɔde nʼani huhuw bɔne nyinaa so gu.
english:
When a king sits on his throne to judge,
    he winnows out all evil with his eyes.

twi: Hena na obetumi aka se, “Mapra me koma mu;meyɛ kronkron na minni bɔne?”
english:
Who can say, “I have kept my heart pure;
    I am clean and without sin”?

twi: Nkaribo ne susudua a ɛnyɛ papa no,Awurade kyi nʼabien no nyinaa.
english:
Differing weights and differing measures—
    the Lord detests them both.

twi: Mpo wɔnam abofra nketewa nneyɛe so hu wɔn,saa ara na ne suban yɛ kronkron ne papa no.
english:
Even small children are known by their actions,
    so is their conduct really pure and upright?

twi: Aso a wɔde te asɛm ne ani a wɔde hu ade,Awurade na wayɛ nʼabien no nyinaa.
english:
Ears that hear and eyes that see—
    the Lord has made them both.

twi: Mma nna nyɛ wo dɛ, na woanni hia;nna, na wubenya aduan ama abu so.
english:
Do not love sleep or you will grow poor;
    stay awake and you will have food to spare.

twi: Adetɔni ka se, “Enye, enye!”nanso sɛ ɔkɔ a ɔde nea watɔ no hoahoa ne ho.
english:
“It’s no good, it’s no good!” says the buyer—
    then goes off and boasts about the purchase.

twi: Sika kɔkɔɔ wɔ hɔ, na nhene pa nso abu so,na ano a ɛka nimdeɛ nsɛm yɛ ɔbohemaa a ɛho yɛ na.
english:
Gold there is, and rubies in abundance,
    but lips that speak knowledge are a rare jewel.

twi: Fa obi a odi ɔhɔho akagyinamu atade;sɛ ɔregyina ɔbea huhufo akyi a, fa si awowa.
english:
Take the garment of one who puts up security for a stranger;
    hold it in pledge if it is done for an outsider.

twi: Aduan a wonya no ɔkwan bɔne so no yɛ onipa anom dɛ,nanso akyiri no, ɛdan mmosea wɔ nʼanom.
english:
Food gained by fraud tastes sweet,
    but one ends up with a mouth full of gravel.

twi: Pɛ afotu yɛ wo nhyehyɛe;sɛ wutu ɔsa a, nya ho akwankyerɛ.
english:
Plans are established by seeking advice;
    so if you wage war, obtain guidance.

twi: Osekuni da kokoamsɛm adi;enti twe wo ho fi onipa a ɔkasa bebree ho.
english:
A gossip betrays a confidence;
    so avoid anyone who talks too much.

twi: Sɛ obi dome nʼagya anaasɛ ne na a,wobedum ne kanea wɔ sum kabii mu.
english:
If someone curses their father or mother,
    their lamp will be snuffed out in pitch darkness.

twi: Agyapade a wɔpere ho nya no,renyɛ nhyira akyiri no.
english:
An inheritance claimed too soon
    will not be blessed at the end.

twi: Nka se, “Metua wo saa bɔne yi so ka!”Twɛn Awurade, na obegye wo.
english:
Do not say, “I’ll pay you back for this wrong!”
    Wait for the Lord, and he will avenge you.

twi: Awurade kyi nkaribo a ɛnyɛ papa,na asisi nsania nso nsɔ nʼani.
english:
The Lord detests differing weights,
    and dishonest scales do not please him.

twi: Awurade na ɔkyerɛ onipa anammɔntu.Na ɛbɛyɛ dɛn na obi bɛte nʼankasa akwan ase?
english:
A person’s steps are directed by the Lord.
    How then can anyone understand their own way?

twi: Obi pɛ ntɛm hyɛ bɔ, ansa na wadwene ho a,osum ne ho afiri.
english:
It is a trap to dedicate something rashly
    and only later to consider one’s vows.

twi: Ɔhene nyansafo hu amumɔyɛfo;na ɔde awiyam afiri hankare fa wɔn so.
english:
A wise king winnows out the wicked;
    he drives the threshing wheel over them.

twi: Awurade kanea hwehwɛ onipa honhom mu,ɛhwehwɛ ne mu baabiara.
english:
The human spirit is the lamp of the Lord
    that sheds light on one’s inmost being.

twi: Ɔdɔ ne nokwaredi bɔ ɔhene ho ban;nʼadɔe ma nʼahengua tim.
english:
Love and faithfulness keep a king safe;
    through love his throne is made secure.

twi: Mmerante anuonyam ne wɔn ahoɔden,tidwen nso ne mmasiriwa anuonyam.
english:
The glory of young men is their strength,
    gray hair the splendor of the old.

twi: Ɔhwe ne apirakuru hohoro amumɔyɛ,mmaatwa tew koma mu.
english:
Blows and wounds scrub away evil,
    and beatings purge the inmost being.

twi: Ɔhene koma da Awurade nsam;ɔkyerɛ no ɔkwan te sɛ asuten ma ɔkɔ baabiara a ɔpɛ.
english:
In the Lord’s hand the king’s heart is a stream of water
    that he channels toward all who please him.

twi: Onipa akwan nyinaa teɛ wɔ nʼani so,nanso Awurade na ɔkari koma.
english:
A person may think their own ways are right,
    but the Lord weighs the heart.

twi: Sɛ woyɛ ade pa ne ade a ɛteɛ a,ɛsɔ Awurade ani sen afɔrebɔ.
english:
To do what is right and just
    is more acceptable to the Lord than sacrifice.

twi: Ani a ɛtra ntɔn ne ahomaso koma,ne amumɔyɛfo asetena nyinaa yɛ bɔne!
english:
Haughty eyes and a proud heart—
    the unplowed field of the wicked—produce sin.

twi: Nsiyɛfo nhyehyɛe de mfaso ba,sɛnea ntɛmpɛ kowie ohia no.
english:
The plans of the diligent lead to profit
    as surely as haste leads to poverty.

twi: Ahonya a nkontompo tɛkrɛma de ba no,ɛyɛ omununkum a etwa mu kɔ, na ɛsan yɛ owu afiri.
english:
A fortune made by a lying tongue
    is a fleeting vapor and a deadly snare.

twi: Amumɔyɛfo basabasayɛ bɛtwe wɔn akɔ,efisɛ wɔmpɛ sɛ wɔyɛ nea ɛteɛ.
english:
The violence of the wicked will drag them away,
    for they refuse to do what is right.

twi: Onipa a odi fɔ no akwan yɛ kɔntɔnkye,na nea ne ho nni asɛm no nneyɛe teɛ.
english:
The way of the guilty is devious,
    but the conduct of the innocent is upright.

twi: Suhyɛ twɔtwɔw ase baabi tenaye sen sɛ wo ne ɔyere tɔkwapɛfo bɛtena fie.
english:
Better to live on a corner of the roof
    than share a house with a quarrelsome wife.

twi: Omumɔyɛfo kɔn dɔ bɔne;onni ahummɔbɔ mma ne yɔnko.
english:
The wicked crave evil;
    their neighbors get no mercy from them.

twi: Sɛ wɔtwe ɔfɛwdifo aso a, ntetekwaafo hu nyansa,sɛ wɔkyerɛkyerɛ onyansafo a, onya nimdeɛ.
english:
When a mocker is punished, the simple gain wisdom;
    by paying attention to the wise they get knowledge.

twi: Ɔtreneeni no hu nea ɛrekɔ so wɔ omumɔyɛfo fi,na ɔde omumɔyɛfo no kɔ ɔsɛe mu.
english:
The Righteous One takes note of the house of the wicked
    and brings the wicked to ruin.

twi: Sɛ onipa sisiw nʼaso wɔ mmɔborɔni su ho a,ɔno nso besu afrɛ, na wɔrennye no so.
english:
Whoever shuts their ears to the cry of the poor
    will also cry out and not be answered.

twi: Kokoa mu adekyɛ dwudwo koma,kɛtɛasehyɛ nso pata abufuwhyew.
english:
A gift given in secret soothes anger,
    and a bribe concealed in the cloak pacifies great wrath.

twi: Sɛ wubu atɛntrenee a, atreneefo ani gye,nanso ɛyɛ ahunahuna ma abɔnefo.
english:
When justice is done, it brings joy to the righteous
    but terror to evildoers.

twi: Onipa a ɔman fi nhumu kwan so nobɛhome wɔ awufo fekuw mu.
english:
Whoever strays from the path of prudence
    comes to rest in the company of the dead.

twi: Nea odi ahosɛpɛw akyi no bɛyɛ ohiani;nea ɔpɛ nsa ne ngo no rennya ne ho da.
english:
Whoever loves pleasure will become poor;
    whoever loves wine and olive oil will never be rich.

twi: Amumɔyɛfo de wɔn nkwa to hɔ ma atreneefo,na atorofo yɛ saa ma wɔn a wɔyɛ pɛ.
english:
The wicked become a ransom for the righteous,
    and the unfaithful for the upright.

twi: Eye sɛ wobɛtena sare so,sen sɛ wo ne ɔyere tɔkwapɛfo a ne koma haw no no bɛtena.
english:
Better to live in a desert
    than with a quarrelsome and nagging wife.

twi: Nnuan pa ne ngo ayɛ onyansafo fi ma,nanso ɔkwasea di nea ɔwɔ nyinaa.
english:
The wise store up choice food and olive oil,
    but fools gulp theirs down.

twi: Nea otiw trenee ne ɔdɔ nonya nkwa, yiyedi ne anuonyam.
english:
Whoever pursues righteousness and love
    finds life, prosperity and honor.

twi: Onyansafo tow hyɛ ahoɔdenfo kuropɔn so,na odwiriw abandennen a wɔn werɛ hyɛ mu no gu fam.
english:
One who is wise can go up against the city of the mighty
    and pull down the stronghold in which they trust.

twi: Nea ɔkora nʼano ne ne tɛkrɛma notwe ne ho fi amanenya ho.
english:
Those who guard their mouths and their tongues
    keep themselves from calamity.

twi: Ɔhantanni a ɔma ne ho so no, ne din ne “Ɔfɛwdifo”ɔde ahantan ntraso yɛ ade.
english:
The proud and arrogant person—“Mocker” is his name—
    behaves with insolent fury.

twi: Nea ɔkwadwofo kɔn dɔ no bɛyɛ owu ama no,efisɛ ne nsa mpɛ adwumayɛ.
english:
The craving of a sluggard will be the death of him,
    because his hands refuse to work.

twi: Da mu nyinaa ɔpere sɛ obenya bebree,nanso ɔtreneeni de, ɔma a ɔnnodow ho.
english:
All day long he craves for more,
    but the righteous give without sparing.

twi: Omumɔyɛfo afɔrebɔ yɛ akyiwade,ne titiriw ne sɛ ɔde adwemmɔne bata ho.
english:
The sacrifice of the wicked is detestable—
    how much more so when brought with evil intent!

twi: Ɔdansekurumni bɛyera,na wɔbɛsɛe obiara a otie no no nso.
english:
A false witness will perish,
    but a careful listener will testify successfully.

twi: Amumɔyɛfo di akakabensɛm,na ɔtreneeni de, osusuw nʼakwan ho.
english:
The wicked put up a bold front,
    but the upright give thought to their ways.

twi: Nyansa, nhumu ne nhyehyɛe biara nni hɔ aebetumi ayɛ yiye atia Awurade.
english:
There is no wisdom, no insight, no plan
    that can succeed against the Lord.

twi: Wosiesie apɔnkɔ ma ɔko da,nanso nkonimdi yɛ Awurade dea.
english:
The horse is made ready for the day of battle,
    but victory rests with the Lord.

twi: Din pa ye sen ahonya bebrebe;sɛ wobedi wo ni ye sen dwetɛ anaa sikakɔkɔɔ.
english:
A good name is more desirable than great riches;
    to be esteemed is better than silver or gold.

twi: Ɔdefo ne ohiani wɔ ade baako,Awurade ne wɔn nyinaa Yɛfo.
english:
Rich and poor have this in common:
    The Lord is the Maker of them all.

twi: Onitefo hu amanehunu a ɛreba na ohintaw ne ho,nanso atetekwaa kɔ nʼanim konya amane.
english:
The prudent see danger and take refuge,
    but the simple keep going and pay the penalty.

twi: Ahobrɛase ne Awuradesuroɛma ahonya ne anuonyam ne nkwa.
english:
Humility is the fear of the Lord;
    its wages are riches and honor and life.

twi: Nsɔe ne mfiri wɔ amumɔyɛfo akwan so,nanso nea ɔbɔ ne kra ho ban no mmɛn ho.
english:
In the paths of the wicked are snares and pitfalls,
    but those who would preserve their life stay far from them.

twi: Kyerɛ abofra ɔkwan a ɔmfa so,na sɛ onyin a ɔremfi so.
english:
Start children off on the way they should go,
    and even when they are old they will not turn from it.

twi: Adefo di ahiafo so,na boseagyefo yɛ nea ɔde fɛm somfo.
english:
The rich rule over the poor,
    and the borrower is slave to the lender.

twi: Nea odua amumɔyɛsɛm no twa ɔhawna wɔbɛsɛe nʼabufuwhyew abaa.
english:
Whoever sows injustice reaps calamity,
    and the rod they wield in fury will be broken.

twi: Ɔyamyefo benya nhyiraefisɛ ɔne ahiafo kyɛ nʼaduan.
english:
The generous will themselves be blessed,
    for they share their food with the poor.

twi: Pam ɔfɛwdifo na basabasayɛ nso bɛkɔ;ntɔkwaw ne animka to atwa.
english:
Drive out the mocker, and out goes strife;
    quarrels and insults are ended.

twi: Obi a ɔdɔ koma a mu tew na ne kasa ho yɛ nyam no,benya ɔhene afa no adamfo.
english:
One who loves a pure heart and who speaks with grace
    will have the king for a friend.

twi: Awurade ani wɛn nimdeɛ,na ɔsɛe ɔtorofo nsɛm.
english:
The eyes of the Lord keep watch over knowledge,
    but he frustrates the words of the unfaithful.

twi: Ɔkwadwofo ka se, “Gyata bi wɔ mfikyiri hɔ!”anaasɛ, “Wobekum me wɔ mmɔnten so.”
english:
The sluggard says, “There’s a lion outside!
    I’ll be killed in the public square!”

twi: Ɔbea waresɛefo anom yɛ amoa donkudonku;nea ɔhyɛ Awurade abufuw ase no bɛtɔ mu.
english:
The mouth of an adulterous woman is a deep pit;
    a man who is under the Lord’s wrath falls into it.

twi: Agyimisɛm kyekyere abofra koma ho,nanso nteɛso abaa bɛpam no akɔ akyiri.
english:
Folly is bound up in the heart of a child,
    but the rod of discipline will drive it far away.

twi: Obi besisi ohiani de apɛ ahonya,anaa ɔbɛkyɛ ɔdefo ade, ne nyinaa de no kɔ ohia mu.
english:
One who oppresses the poor to increase his wealth
    and one who gives gifts to the rich—both come to poverty.

twi: AnyansasɛmYɛ aso na tie anyansasɛm yi;fa wo koma di me nkyerɛkyerɛ akyi,
english:
Pay attention and turn your ear to the sayings of the wise;
    apply your heart to what I teach,

twi: efisɛ eye sɛ wokora saa nsɛm yi wɔ wo koma mu,na ne nyinaa ada wʼano.
english:
for it is pleasing when you keep them in your heart
    and have all of them ready on your lips.

twi: Sɛ ɛbɛyɛ a wode wo ho bɛto Awurade so,merekyerɛkyerɛ wo nnɛ, yiw ɛyɛ wo.
english:
So that your trust may be in the Lord,
    I teach you today, even you.

twi: Menkyerɛw mmɛ aduasa mmaa wo,nea ɛyɛ afotusɛm ne nimdeɛ,
english:
Have I not written thirty sayings for you,
    sayings of counsel and knowledge,

twi: a ɛkyerɛkyerɛ wo nokware ne nea akyinnye nni ho,sɛnea wubenya mmuae pa ama nea ɔsomaa wo no ana?
english:
teaching you to be honest and to speak the truth,
    so that you bring back truthful reports
    to those you serve?

twi: Mmɔ ahiafo korɔn, sɛ wɔyɛ ahiafo nti,na nsisi wɔn a wonni bi wɔ asennii,
english:
Do not exploit the poor because they are poor
    and do not crush the needy in court,

twi: efisɛ Awurade bedi wɔn asɛm ama wɔn,na wafom afa wɔn a wɔfom ahiafo fa.
english:
for the Lord will take up their case
    and will exact life for life.

twi: Mfa obi a ne koma yɛ den no adamfo,na mfa wo ho mmɔ nea ne bo nkyɛ fuw,
english:
Do not make friends with a hot-tempered person,
    do not associate with one easily angered,

twi: anyɛ saa a, wubesua nʼakwanna woakɔtɔ afiri mu.
english:
or you may learn their ways
    and get yourself ensnared.

twi: Nyɛ nea ɔde ne nsa hyɛ krataa ase di akagyinamuanaasɛ odi akagyinamu;
english:
Do not be one who shakes hands in pledge
    or puts up security for debts;

twi: na sɛ wunni nea wɔde tua awobehuam wo mpa mpo afi wʼase.
english:
if you lack the means to pay,
    your very bed will be snatched from under you.

twi: Ntutu tete abo a wɔde ato hye,nea wo nenanom de sisii hɔ no.
english:
Do not move an ancient boundary stone
    set up by your ancestors.

twi: Wuhu obi a ne nsa akokwaw nʼadwuma ho ana?Ahemfo anim na ɔbɛsom,na ɔrensom wɔ mpapahwekwa anim.
Sɛ wo ne ɔhene bi to nsa didi a,hwɛ nea esi wʼanim no yiye,
english:
When you sit to dine with a ruler,
    note well what is before you,

twi: Sɛ woyɛ adidibrada a,hyɛ wo ho so.
english:
and put a knife to your throat
    if you are given to gluttony.

twi: Nni nʼaduan akɔnnɔ akɔnnɔ no akyi,efisɛ saa aduan no daadaa nnipa.
english:
Do not crave his delicacies,
    for that food is deceptive.

twi: Mmiri wo mogya ani mpɛ sika;hu nyansa na tɔ wo bo ase.
english:
Do not wear yourself out to get rich;
    do not trust your own cleverness.

twi: Wʼani bɔɔ sika so ara pɛ, na atu ayera,ampa ara ebefuw ntabanna atu akɔ wim sɛ ɔkɔre.
english:
Cast but a glance at riches, and they are gone,
    for they will surely sprout wings
    and fly off to the sky like an eagle.

twi: Nni obi a ɔyɛ pɛpɛe aduan,nni nʼakɔnnɔ aduan akyi;
english:
Do not eat the food of a begrudging host,
    do not crave his delicacies;

twi: efisɛ ɔyɛ obi abere biara osusuw sika ho.Ɔka se, “Didi na nom,”nanso ɛnyɛ ne koma mu.
english:
for he is the kind of person
    who is always thinking about the cost.
“Eat and drink,” he says to you,
    but his heart is not with you.

twi: Kakra a woadi no wobɛfe,na ɛno nti wo nkamfo so remma mfaso.
english:
You will vomit up the little you have eaten
    and will have wasted your compliments.

twi: Nkasa nkyerɛ ɔkwasea,efisɛ ɔremfa nyansa a ɛwɔ wo kasa mu no.
english:
Do not speak to fools,
    for they will scorn your prudent words.

twi: Ntutu tete abo a wɔde ato hye ngu,na ntra ɔhye nkɔ ayisaa mfuw mu,
english:
Do not move an ancient boundary stone
    or encroach on the fields of the fatherless,

twi: efisɛ wɔn Gyefo yɛ den,na obedi wɔn asɛm ama wɔn.
english:
for their Defender is strong;
    he will take up their case against you.

twi: Ma wo koma mmra nkyerɛkyerɛ so,na wɛn wʼaso tie nimdeɛ.
english:
Apply your heart to instruction
    and your ears to words of knowledge.

twi: Ntwentwɛn abofra nteɛso so;sɛ wode abaa teɛ no a, ɔrenwu.
english:
Do not withhold discipline from a child;
    if you punish them with the rod, they will not die.

twi: Fa abaa twe nʼasona gye ne kra fi owu mu.
english:
Punish them with the rod
    and save them from death.

twi: Me ba, sɛ wo koma hu nyansa a,ɛno de, me koma ani begye;
english:
My son, if your heart is wise,
    then my heart will be glad indeed;

twi: sɛ wʼano ka nea ɛteɛ ame mu ade nyinaa ani begye.
english:
my inmost being will rejoice
    when your lips speak what is right.

twi: Mma wʼani mmere abɔnefo,mmom bɔ Awurade suro ho mmɔden bere biara.
english:
Do not let your heart envy sinners,
    but always be zealous for the fear of the Lord.

twi: Ampa ara anidaso wɔ hɔ ma wo daakye,na wʼanidaso renyɛ ɔkwa.
english:
There is surely a future hope for you,
    and your hope will not be cut off.

twi: Me ba, tie, na hu nyansa,ma wo koma mfa ɔkwantrenee so.
english:
Listen, my son, and be wise,
    and set your heart on the right path:

twi: Mfa wo ho mmɔ akɔwensafoanaasɛ wɔn a wɔpɛ nam mmoroso ho,
english:
Do not join those who drink too much wine
    or gorge themselves on meat,

twi: efisɛ, akɔwensafo ne adidibradafo bɛyɛ ahiafo,na anikum fura wɔn ntamagow.
english:
for drunkards and gluttons become poor,
    and drowsiness clothes them in rags.

twi: Tie wʼagya a ɔwoo wo no,na sɛ wo na bɔ aberewa a, mmu no animtiaa.
english:
Listen to your father, who gave you life,
    and do not despise your mother when she is old.

twi: Tɔ nokware na ntɔn da;nya nyansa, ahohyɛso ne nhumu.
english:
Buy the truth and do not sell it—
    wisdom, instruction and insight as well.

twi: Ɔtreneeni agya wɔ anigye bebree;nea ɔwɔ ɔba nyansafo no ani gye ne ho.
english:
The father of a righteous child has great joy;
    a man who fathers a wise son rejoices in him.

twi: Ma wʼagya ne wo na ani nnye;ma ɔbea a ɔwoo wo no nnya ahosɛpɛw.
english:
May your father and mother rejoice;
    may she who gave you birth be joyful!

twi: Me ba, fa wo koma ma mena ma wʼani nkɔ mʼakwan ho,
english:
My son, give me your heart
    and let your eyes delight in my ways,

twi: na oguamanfo yɛ amoa donkudonkuɔyere huhuni yɛ ɔdaadaafo.
english:
for an adulterous woman is a deep pit,
    and a wayward wife is a narrow well.

twi: Ɔtɛw, twɛn, te sɛ ɔkwanmukafo,na ɔma mmarima mu atorofo dɔɔso.
english:
Like a bandit she lies in wait
    and multiplies the unfaithful among men.

twi: Hena na wɔadome no? Hena na odi awerɛhow?Hena na odi aperepere? Hena na onwiinwii?Hena na ɔwɔ atape nko ara? Hena na mogya ada nʼani so?
english:
Who has woe? Who has sorrow?
    Who has strife? Who has complaints?
    Who has needless bruises? Who has bloodshot eyes?

twi: Wɔn a wɔkyɛ nsa ho,na wɔka nsa a wɔafrafra hwɛ.
english:
Those who linger over wine,
    who go to sample bowls of mixed wine.

twi: Nhwɛ nsa ani kɔkɔɔ no haa,bere a ɛretwa yerɛw yerɛw wɔ kuruwa mu,na ɛkɔ yɔɔ no.
english:
Do not gaze at wine when it is red,
    when it sparkles in the cup,
    when it goes down smoothly!

twi: Awiei no, ɛka te sɛ ɔwɔna ɛwɔ bɔre te sɛ ahurutoa.
english:
In the end it bites like a snake
    and poisons like a viper.

twi: Wʼani behu nneɛma a wunhuu da,na woadwene nneɛma basabasa ho.
english:
Your eyes will see strange sights,
    and your mind will imagine confusing things.

twi: Wobɛtɔ ntintan te sɛ hyɛn mu dwumayɛni a,okura hyɛn dua a, ɛrehinhim mu den, na ehinhim wɔ po so.
english:
You will be like one sleeping on the high seas,
    lying on top of the rigging.

twi: Na wobɛka se, “Wɔbɔ me, nanso mimpira.Wɔboro me, nanso mente ɔyaw biara.Bere bɛn na menyanakɔpɛ nsa anom bio?”
english:
“They hit me,” you will say, “but I’m not hurt!
    They beat me, but I don’t feel it!
When will I wake up
    so I can find another drink?”

twi: Mma wʼani mmere amumɔyɛfo,mfa wo ho mmɔ wɔn;
english:
Do not envy the wicked,
    do not desire their company;

twi: Efisɛ wɔn koma dwene atirimɔdensɛm ho,na wɔn ano ka nea ɛde basabasayɛ ba ho asɛm.
english:
for their hearts plot violence,
    and their lips talk about making trouble.

twi: Wɔde nyansa na esi fi,na nhumu mu na wɔma etim;
english:
By wisdom a house is built,
    and through understanding it is established;

twi: ɛnam nimdeɛ so na wonya ademude a ɛho yɛ nana ɛyɛ fɛ hyehyɛ nʼadan mu.
english:
through knowledge its rooms are filled
    with rare and beautiful treasures.

twi: Onyansafo wɔ tumi a ɛso,na onimdefo nyin ahoɔden mu;
english:
The wise prevail through great power,
    and those who have knowledge muster their strength.

twi: nea ɔretu sa hia akwankyerɛ,nea ɔrehwehwɛ nkonimdi no hia afotufo pii.
english:
Surely you need guidance to wage war,
    and victory is won through many advisers.

twi: Nyansa wɔ soro dodo ma ɔkwasea;wɔ apon ano aguabɔ mu no, ɛnsɛ sɛ wobue wɔn ano.
english:
Wisdom is too high for fools;
    in the assembly at the gate they must not open their mouths.

twi: Onipa a ɔbɔ pɔw bɔne no,wɔbɛfrɛ no ɔkɔtwebrɛfo.
english:
Whoever plots evil
    will be known as a schemer.

twi: Ogyimifo nhyehyɛe yɛ bɔne,nnipa kyi ɔfɛwdifo.
english:
The schemes of folly are sin,
    and people detest a mocker.

twi: Sɛ wʼaba mu gow wɔ ɔhaw mu a,na wʼahoɔden sua!
english:
If you falter in a time of trouble,
    how small is your strength!

twi: Gye wɔn a wɔde wɔn rekɔ akokum wɔn no nkwa;na sianka wɔn a wɔtɔ ntintan kɔ akumii.
english:
Rescue those being led away to death;
    hold back those staggering toward slaughter.

twi: Sɛ woka se, “Na yennim eyi ho hwee a,”nea ɔkari koma hwɛ no nhu ana?Nea ɔbɔ wo nkwa ho ban no nnim ana?Ɔrentua nea obiara ayɛ so ka ana?
english:
If you say, “But we knew nothing about this,”
    does not he who weighs the heart perceive it?
Does not he who guards your life know it?
    Will he not repay everyone according to what they have done?

twi: Me ba, di ɛwo, efisɛ eye;ɛwokyɛm mu wo yɛ wʼanom dɛ.
english:
Eat honey, my son, for it is good;
    honey from the comb is sweet to your taste.

twi: Hu nso sɛ nyansa yɛ wo kra dɛ;sɛ wunya a, wowɔ anidaso ma daakye,na wʼanidaso renyɛ ɔkwa.
english:
Know also that wisdom is like honey for you:
    If you find it, there is a future hope for you,
    and your hope will not be cut off.

twi: Nkɔtɛw ɔtreneeni fi sɛ ɔkwanmukafo,na nkɔtow nhyɛ nʼatenae so,
english:
Do not lurk like a thief near the house of the righteous,
    do not plunder their dwelling place;

twi: Ɛwɔ mu sɛ ɔtreneeni hwe ase mpɛn ason de, nanso ɔsɔre bio,na amumɔyɛfo de amanehunu baako ma wɔhwe ase.
english:
for though the righteous fall seven times, they rise again,
    but the wicked stumble when calamity strikes.

twi: Sɛ wo tamfo hwe ase a mma ɛnyɛ wo dɛ;na sɛ ohintiw a mma wo koma nni ahurusi,
english:
Do not gloat when your enemy falls;
    when they stumble, do not let your heart rejoice,

twi: efisɛ Awurade behu wʼadwene na ɔrempɛna obeyi nʼabufuwhyew afi no so.
english:
or the Lord will see and disapprove
    and turn his wrath away from them.

twi: Nhaw wo ho wɔ abɔnefo nti,na mma wʼani mmere amumɔyɛfo nso,
english:
Do not fret because of evildoers
    or be envious of the wicked,

twi: efisɛ, ɔbɔnefo nni anidaso biara daakye,na wobedum amumɔyɛfo kanea.
english:
for the evildoer has no future hope,
    and the lamp of the wicked will be snuffed out.

twi: Me ba, suro Awurade ne ɔhene,na mfa wo ho mmɔ atuatewfo ho,
english:
Fear the Lord and the king, my son,
    and do not join with rebellious officials,

twi: efisɛ saa baanu yi de, ɔsɛe bɛba wɔn so mpofirim;na hena na onim amanehunu ko a wobetumi de aba?
english:
for those two will send sudden destruction on them,
    and who knows what calamities they can bring?

twi: Anyansafo Nsɛnka A Ɛkeka HoEyinom nso yɛ anyansafo Nsɛnka:Atemmu a nhwɛanim wɔ mu no nye:
english:
These also are sayings of the wise:
To show partiality in judging is not good:

twi: Obiara a ɔbɛka akyerɛ nea odi fɔ se, “Wo ho nni asɛm” no,nnipa bɛdome no na amanaman remmɔ no din pa.
english:
Whoever says to the guilty, “You are innocent,”
    will be cursed by peoples and denounced by nations.

twi: Na wɔn a wobu afɔdifo fɔ no, ebesi wɔn yiye,na nhyira bɛba wɔn so.
english:
But it will go well with those who convict the guilty,
    and rich blessing will come on them.

twi: Mmuae pate sɛ mfewano.
english:
An honest answer
    is like a kiss on the lips.

twi: Wie wo mfikyidwumana siesie wo mfuw;ɛno akyi, si wo fi.
Nni adanse ntia ɔyɔnko a ɔnyɛɛ wo hwee,na mfa wʼano nnaadaa.
english:
Do not testify against your neighbor without cause—
    would you use your lips to mislead?

twi: Nka se, “Nea wayɛ me no me nso mɛyɛ no bi;nea ɔyɛe no mitua no so ka.”
english:
Do not say, “I’ll do to them as they have done to me;
    I’ll pay them back for what they did.”

twi: Menantew faa onihawfo afuw ho,twaa mu wɔ nea onni adwene bobeturo nso ho;
english:
I went past the field of a sluggard,
    past the vineyard of someone who has no sense;

twi: nsɔe afuw wɔ baabiara,wura afuw akata asase no so,na abo afasu no nso abubu.
english:
thorns had come up everywhere,
    the ground was covered with weeds,
    and the stone wall was in ruins.

twi: Mede me koma kɔɔ nea mihuu no sona misuaa biribi fii mu:
english:
I applied my heart to what I observed
    and learned a lesson from what I saw:

twi: nna kakra, nkotɔ kakra,nsa a woabobɔw de rehome kakra
english:
A little sleep, a little slumber,
    a little folding of the hands to rest—

twi: bɛma ohia aba wo so sɛ ɔkwanmukafo,na nneɛma ho nna bɛba wo so sɛ obi a okura akode. Na ohia bɛtow akyere wo sɛ ɔkwanmukafo; ahokyere bɛtoa wo sɛ ɔkorɔmfowerɛmfo.
english:
and poverty will come on you like a thief
    and scarcity like an armed man.

twi: Salomo Mmebusɛm NkekahoEyinom yɛ Salomo mmebusɛm nkekaho a Yudahene Hesekia afotufo kyerɛwee:
english: These are more proverbs of Solomon, compiled by the men of Hezekiah king of Judah:

twi: Ɛyɛ Onyankopɔn anuonyamhyɛ sɛ wɔde asɛm sie;sɛ wɔpɛɛpɛɛ asɛm mu nso hyɛ ahemfo anuonyam.
english:
It is the glory of God to conceal a matter;
    to search out a matter is the glory of kings.

twi: Sɛnea ɔsoro korɔn na asase mu dɔ no,saa ara na wɔrentumi nhwehwɛ ahemfo koma mu.
english:
As the heavens are high and the earth is deep,
    so the hearts of kings are unsearchable.

twi: Sɛ woyi dwetɛ ho fi a,na ato nea ɛkɔ dwetɛdwumfo nsam;
english:
Remove the dross from the silver,
    and a silversmith can produce a vessel;

twi: Yi amumɔyɛfo fi ɔhene anim,na trenee bɛma nʼahengua atim.
english:
remove wicked officials from the king’s presence,
    and his throne will be established through righteousness.

twi: Mma wo ho so wɔ ɔhene anim,na mpere dibea wɔ atitiriw mu;
english:
Do not exalt yourself in the king’s presence,
    and do not claim a place among his great men;

twi: Eye ma no sɛ ɔbɛka akyerɛ wo se, “Bra soro ha,”sen sɛ ɔbɛbrɛ wo ase wɔ otitiriw bi anim.Nea wode wʼani ahu no
english:
it is better for him to say to you, “Come up here,”
    than for him to humiliate you before his nobles.
What you have seen with your eyes

twi: mpɛ ntɛm mfa nkɔ asennii,na sɛ awiei no wo yɔnko gu wʼanim ase adɛn na wobɛyɛ?
english:
do not bring hastily to court,
for what will you do in the end
    if your neighbor puts you to shame?

twi: Sɛ wo ne wo yɔnko di asɛm anna obi foforo ahintasɛm adi,
english:
If you take your neighbor to court,
    do not betray another’s confidence,

twi: anyɛ saa a, nea ɔbɛte no begu wʼanim asena din bɔne a wubenya no rempepa da.
english:
or the one who hears it may shame you
    and the charge against you will stand.

twi: Asɛm a wɔka no sɛnea ɛfata note sɛ sika kɔkɔɔ a wɔabɔ sɛ aprɛde atuatua dwetɛ nsiesiei mu.
english:
Like apples of gold in settings of silver
    is a ruling rightly given.

twi: Sikakɔkɔɔ asokaa anaa sikakɔkɔɔ ankasa ahyehyɛdete sɛ onyansafo animka a ɔde ma nea ɔyɛ aso ma no.
english:
Like an earring of gold or an ornament of fine gold
    is the rebuke of a wise judge to a listening ear.

twi: Sɛnea sukyerɛmma ma wim dwo wɔ otwabere mu no,saa ara na ɔsomafo nokwafo te ma wɔn a wɔsoma no no;na ɔma ne wuranom akomatɔyam.
Omununkum ne mframa a ɛmfa osu mma note sɛ onipa a ɔde akyɛde a ɔmmfa mma hoahoa ne ho.
english:
Like clouds and wind without rain
    is one who boasts of gifts never given.

twi: Ntoboase ma sodifo ti da,na tɛkrɛmabere tumi bu dompe mu.
english:
Through patience a ruler can be persuaded,
    and a gentle tongue can break a bone.

twi: Sɛ wunya ɛwo a, nni ntra so,ne bebrebe bɛma woafe.
english:
If you find honey, eat just enough—
    too much of it, and you will vomit.

twi: Ntaa nkɔ wo yɔnko fi,wo ho fono no a, ɔbɛtan wo.
english:
Seldom set foot in your neighbor’s house—
    too much of you, and they will hate you.

twi: Onipa a odi adansekurum tia ne yɔnko note sɛ kontibaa, afoa anaa bɛmma a ano yɛ nnam.
english:
Like a club or a sword or a sharp arrow
    is one who gives false testimony against a neighbor.

twi: Ɛse a ɛyare ɔkekaw anaa nan a ɛyɛ apakyete sɛ nea wode wo ho to ɔtorofo so hiada mu.
english:
Like a broken tooth or a lame foot
    is reliance on the unfaithful in a time of trouble.

twi: Nea ɔto dwom kyerɛ ɔwerɛhowni no,te sɛ nea ɔpa ntama gu awɔwbere muanaa te sɛ nsa nyinyanyinya a wohwie gu apirakuru so.
english:
Like one who takes away a garment on a cold day,
    or like vinegar poured on a wound,
    is one who sings songs to a heavy heart.

twi: Sɛ ɔkɔm de wo tamfo a, ma no aduan nni;sɛ osukɔm de no a, ma no nsu nnom.
english:
If your enemy is hungry, give him food to eat;
    if he is thirsty, give him water to drink.

twi: Sɛ woyɛ saa a, wobɛsosɔ nnyansramma agu nʼatifi,na Awurade bɛma wo akatua.
english:
In doing this, you will heap burning coals on his head,
    and the Lord will reward you.

twi: Sɛnea atifi fam mframa de osu ba no,saa ara na tɛkrɛma a edi nseku de omuna ba.
english:
Like a north wind that brings unexpected rain
    is a sly tongue—which provokes a horrified look.

twi: Eye sɛ wobɛtena suhyɛ twɔtwɔw ase baabi,sen sɛ wo ne ɔyere tɔkwapɛfo bɛtena fie.
english:
Better to live on a corner of the roof
    than share a house with a quarrelsome wife.

twi: Nsuonwini a ɔkra a atɔ beraw nya note sɛ anigyesɛm a efi akyirikyiri.
english:
Like cold water to a weary soul
    is good news from a distant land.

twi: Asuti a afono anaa abura a ayɛ pɔtɔɔte sɛ ɔtreneeni a ogyaa ne ho ma amumɔyɛfo.
english:
Like a muddied spring or a polluted well
    are the righteous who give way to the wicked.

twi: Enye sɛ wodi ɛwo ntraso,saa ara na ɛnyɛ anuonyam sɛ obi bɛhwehwɛ nsɛm a mu dɔ mu.
english:
It is not good to eat too much honey,
    nor is it honorable to search out matters that are too deep.

twi: Onipa a onni ahohyɛso note sɛ kuropɔn a nʼafasu abubu agu fam.
english:
Like a city whose walls are broken through
    is a person who lacks self-control.

twi: Sɛnea sukyerɛmma te ahuhurubere anaasɛ osu wɔ otwabere no,saa ara na anuonyam mfata ɔkwasea.
english:
Like snow in summer or rain in harvest,
    honor is not fitting for a fool.

twi: Sɛnea apatuprɛw tu anaasɛ asomfena tu dannan ne ho no,saa ara na nnuabɔ hunu nsi hwee.
english:
Like a fluttering sparrow or a darting swallow,
    an undeserved curse does not come to rest.

twi: Ɔkafo abaa wɔ hɔ ma ɔpɔnkɔ, nnareka wɔ hɔ ma afurum,na abaa wɔ hɔ ma nkwaseafo akyi.
english:
A whip for the horse, a bridle for the donkey,
    and a rod for the backs of fools!

twi: Nhwɛ ɔkwasea agyimisɛm so mma no mmuae,anyɛ saa a wo nso bɛyɛ sɛ ɔno.
english:
Do not answer a fool according to his folly,
    or you yourself will be just like him.

twi: Gyina ɔkwasea agyimisɛm so ma no mmuae,anyɛ saa a ɛbɛyɛ no sɛ onim nyansa.
english:
Answer a fool according to his folly,
    or he will be wise in his own eyes.

twi: Sɛ wode nkra bi soma ɔkwasea a,ɛte sɛ wutwitwa wʼankasa wʼanan anaasɛ wonom awuduru.
english:
Sending a message by the hands of a fool
    is like cutting off one’s feet or drinking poison.

twi: Apakye nan a awu na ɛsensɛn hɔ no,yɛ mmebusɛm a ɛda ɔkwasea ano.
english:
Like the useless legs of one who is lame
    is a proverb in the mouth of a fool.

twi: Ɔbo a wɔakyekyere afam ahwimmo sote sɛ anuonyam a wɔde ama ɔkwasea.
english:
Like tying a stone in a sling
    is the giving of honor to a fool.

twi: Nsɔe dua a ɔkɔwensani kita note sɛ mmebusɛm a ɛda ɔkwasea ano.
english:
Like a thornbush in a drunkard’s hand
    is a proverb in the mouth of a fool.

twi: Nea ɔbɔ ɔkwasea anaa obi hunu paa note sɛ agyantowni a opira nnipa kwa.
english:
Like an archer who wounds at random
    is one who hires a fool or any passer-by.

twi: Sɛnea ɔkraman san kɔ ne fe ho no,saa ara na ɔkwasea ti nʼagyimisɛm mu.
english:
As a dog returns to its vomit,
    so fools repeat their folly.

twi: Wuhu obi a ɔyɛ onyansafo wɔ nʼankasa ani so ana?Anidaso pii wɔ ɔkwasea mu sen no.
english:
Do you see a person wise in their own eyes?
    There is more hope for a fool than for them.

twi: Ɔkwadwofo ka se, “Gyata wɔ ɔkwan no mu,gyatakeka nenam mmɔnten no so!”
english:
A sluggard says, “There’s a lion in the road,
    a fierce lion roaming the streets!”

twi: Sɛnea ɔpon di akɔneaba wɔ ne mpontare so no,saa ara na ɔkwadwofo twa ne ho wɔ ne mpa so.
english:
As a door turns on its hinges,
    so a sluggard turns on his bed.

twi: Ɔkwadwofo de ne nsa si aduan mu,na ɛyɛ no anihaw sɛ obeyi akɔ nʼano.
english:
A sluggard buries his hand in the dish;
    he is too lazy to bring it back to his mouth.

twi: Ɔkwadwofo yɛ onyansafo wɔ ɔno ankasa ani sosen nnipa baason a wodwen asɛm ho na wɔabua.
english:
A sluggard is wiser in his own eyes
    than seven people who answer discreetly.

twi: Obi a oso ɔkraman aso twe no note sɛ obi a ɔretwa mu na ɔde ne ho kɔfra ntɔkwaw a ɛmfa ne ho mu.
english:
Like one who grabs a stray dog by the ears
    is someone who rushes into a quarrel not their own.

twi: Ɔbɔdamfo a ɔtotow atuoanaa agyanwerɛmfo no
english:
Like a maniac shooting
    flaming arrows of death

twi: te sɛ obi a, ɔdaadaa ne yɔnkona ɔka se, “Na mede redi agoru!”
english:
is one who deceives their neighbor
    and says, “I was only joking!”

twi: Nnyansin hi a ogya dum;nseku nni hɔ a ntɔkwaw to twa.
english:
Without wood a fire goes out;
    without a gossip a quarrel dies down.

twi: Sɛnea gyabiriw dan nnyansramma na nnyina dan ogya no,saa ara na ɔtɔkwapɛfo hyɛ ntɔkwaw mu takramugya.
english:
As charcoal to embers and as wood to fire,
    so is a quarrelsome person for kindling strife.

twi: Osekuni ano asɛm te sɛ aduan a ɛyɛ dɛ;ɛhyɛnhyɛn onipa akwaa mu nyinaa.
english:
The words of a gossip are like choice morsels;
    they go down to the inmost parts.

twi: Sɛnea ama kata asankagow ho nosaa ara na tɛkrɛmadɛ kata amumɔyɛ koma so.
english:
Like a coating of silver dross on earthenware
    are fervent lips with an evil heart.

twi: Onipa bɔne kasa te sɛ nea oye,nanso nnaadaa ahyɛ ne koma ma.
english:
Enemies disguise themselves with their lips,
    but in their hearts they harbor deceit.

twi: Ɛwɔ mu sɛ ne kasa yɛ dɛ de, nanso nnye no nni,efisɛ abususɛm ason ahyɛ ne koma ma.
english:
Though their speech is charming, do not believe them,
    for seven abominations fill their hearts.

twi: Ebia nnaadaa bɛkata nʼadwemmɔne so,nanso nʼamumɔyɛsɛm bɛda adi wɔ bagua mu.
english:
Their malice may be concealed by deception,
    but their wickedness will be exposed in the assembly.

twi: Sɛ onipa tu amoa a, ɔbɛtɔ mu;sɛ onipa pirew ɔbo a, ɛbɛsan aba no so.
english:
Whoever digs a pit will fall into it;
    if someone rolls a stone, it will roll back on them.

twi: Atoro tɛkrɛma kyi wɔn a ogu wɔn ho fi,na adɛfɛdɛfɛ ano de ɔsɛe ba.
english:
A lying tongue hates those it hurts,
    and a flattering mouth works ruin.

twi: Mfa ɔkyena nhoahoa wo ho,na wunnim nea ɛda bi de bɛba.
english:
Do not boast about tomorrow,
    for you do not know what a day may bring.
